title: fix(story): causa-embed mount-fn-for returns nil — per-panel embed never mounts
description:
PR #1566 (rf2-v1ach) introduced `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/causa_embed.cljs` with a per-panel embed: `panel-host-component` calls `(mount-fn-for panel-id)` and uses the returned mount-fn to mount the Causa panel into a `<div data-test=\"story-causa-panel-host\">`. In practice the panel-host is always empty — the Causa Event-detail / App-db / etc. panels never render.

Root cause: `resolve-fn` in causa_embed.cljs uses `find-ns-obj` + `aget` to look up the mount-fn symbol (`day8.re-frame2-causa.panels/mount-event-detail!`). In shadow-cljs's namespace organisation the symbol's munged name (`mount_event_detail_BANG_`) is NOT exposed as a property of the parent `day8.re_frame2_causa.panels` JS object — that object only carries SUB-namespace references (`app_db_diff`, `event_detail`, etc.). The mount fns live in the namespace module's own scope and are not reachable via the goog-symbol walk.

Reproduction (worker `worker/fix-tig7u-rhs-smoke` worktree):
1. `npm run test:examples --filter causa-rhs-smoke` (or just open `http://127.0.0.1:8030/causa-rhs-smoke/` and click `/loaded`).
2. Inspect the RHS: `[data-test=\"story-causa-embed\"]` renders, chip-row + 7 chips visible, panel-host present.
3. Panel-host `innerHTML === \"\"` — Causa panel never paints.
4. JS console: `window.re_frame.story.ui.causa_embed.mount_fn_for(cljs.core.keyword.call(null, 'event-detail'))` returns `null`.

This was missed because PR #1566's targeted Story/Causa browser gate (`test:causa-feature-gate` + `test:story-static` + `test:story-feature-load` + `test:story-play-scripts`) does NOT include `test:examples` / the causa-rhs-smoke spec. The `Examples (browser)` gate was SKIPPED on the merge because the surface classifier didn't flag examples for Story-only diffs. Now this is biting the Examples gate on `main`.

Fix options (worker chooses):
- Direct require: replace the `find-ns-obj` lookup with a direct `(:require [day8.re-frame2-causa.panels :as panels])` and `(case panel-id :event-detail panels/mount-event-detail! …)`. This is the simplest and cleanest; feature-detect-safe at compile time via existing classpath/preload.
- Carry the mount-fn refs on a hash-map registered by Causa's preload at runtime (preload-time registration of `panel-id → mount-fn`), keyed by panel-id. Embed reads from the map.

Test gates to verify:
- `npm run test:examples --filter causa-rhs-smoke` — the `causa-rhs-smoke` spec should be able to assert `[data-testid=\"rf-causa-event-detail\"]` after a variant focus.
- Re-run a full `npm run test:examples` sweep.

Found by rf2-tig7u worker while investigating the spec.cjs selector regression. The selector regression is fixed in PR #<N>; this is the underlying per-panel embed bug surfaced during that investigation.
close_reason: PR #1577 opened — fix is option (a) direct require of day8.re-frame2-causa.panels with case dispatch; Causa-in-Story panel-host now actually paints (verified via extended causa-rhs-smoke smoke asserting rf-causa-event-detail and rf-causa-app-db-diff visible inside [data-test=story-causa-panel-host]). 21/21 example specs pass; bundle-isolation clean.

title: story-mcp: include-sensitive? schema property key violates Anthropic tools API pattern
description:
The wire-surface property key colon-include-sensitive-questionmark in tool input schemas violates the Anthropic Messages API tool-schema pattern caret-bracket-aA-zZ0-9-underscore-period-hyphen-bracket-curly-1-comma-64-curly-dollar (specifically the trailing question-mark is rejected). Any Claude Code session that loads story-mcp returns 400 on every tool call (Claude Code re-sends the full tools array each turn), so the session is effectively bricked.

Exact API error from a live session today:

  API Error: 400 tools.32.custom.input_schema.properties: Property keys should match pattern caret-bracket-a-A-zZ0-9-underscore-period-hyphen-bracket-curly-1-comma-64-curly-dollar

Root cause: tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/schemas.cljc line 60 the with-include-sensitive helper assoc-es :include-sensitive? into the property map. Every tool that calls (s/with-include-sensitive ...) advertises that property key.

Tools that use the helper (per grep on tools/story-mcp):
- testing.cljc line 166 (preview-variant or run-variant region)
- Several others use the helper or destructure the arg

Call sites that read the arg (must also change if the wire-key changes):
- helpers.cljc line 97 (defn include-sensitive?) and line 117 (get arguments :include-sensitive?)
- testing.cljc line 67, 144
- dev.cljc line 94
- registry.cljc lines 50, 58, 59 (strips the slot when sensitive-reads gate is closed)
- Test references in tools_test.clj (about 22 sites)
- Spec docs API.md and 002-Tool-Registry.md (about 13 sites)

Suggested fix shapes (operator decision):
1. Drop the trailing question-mark everywhere. Rename :include-sensitive? to :include-sensitive across schema, helper fn, handlers, tests, spec docs. Loses the Clojure boolean-naming idiom but the wire and the source line up.
2. Keep the internal Clojure name include-sensitive? as a function/boolean idiom but advertise the wire key as include-sensitive. The schema helper would assoc into the property map under :include-sensitive while the arg-reader helper does (get arguments :include-sensitive). Spec docs need updating to call out the wire shape.

Option 1 is the smaller diff and removes the asymmetry; option 2 preserves the Clojure idiom at the cost of a wire-name vs. fn-name split.

Acceptance:
- A Claude Code session that loads story-mcp does not return 400 on tool invocations.
- The tools/list output for any tool using with-include-sensitive has a property key matching the Anthropic pattern caret-bracket-aA-zZ0-9-underscore-period-hyphen-bracket-1-comma-64-curly-dollar.
- Existing tests pass after the rename or wire-name split (the test file references the slot symbolically about 22 times; mechanical sed).

Filed from sibling pitch8.com.au mayor session on operator instruction; the re-frame2 mayor should own the fix. Originating repo: pitch8 worked around the issue by avoiding the story-mcp surface today.
notes: OPERATOR DECISION (mayor 2026-05-18 21:35 AUSEST): Option 1 — rename :include-sensitive? → :include-sensitive on the wire key + arg destructure everywhere. Rationale (pre-alpha posture): wire MUST drop ? per Anthropic schema; introducing a wire/source-name split (Option 2) creates a hidden serialization asymmetry. Predicate fn name include-sensitive? keeps its ? — the idiom belongs on the predicate, not on a data key whose wire form disallows ?. Smaller diff, no back-compat shims.
close_reason: PR #1494 - option-1 rename shipped

title: bug(story+causa): Open-in-editor chip doesn't open VSCode despite URI scheme allowlist + chip rendering
description:
Mike reports the per-variant Open-in-editor chip in Story (also affects Causa's parallel surface) is NOT launching VSCode when clicked. The chip renders (so source-coord :file is present + scheme is allowed), but the OS handler chain isn't picking up the URI.

## Repro
1. Start Story testbed: cd implementation && npx shadow-cljs watch :testbeds/panel-gallery
2. Open http://localhost:8765
3. Pick any variant (e.g. :story.causa.app-db)
4. Click the Open-in-editor chip in the variant header
5. Expected: VSCode (Mike's configured editor) opens the variant body's source file at the line
6. Actual: nothing happens / silent failure

## Surface
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/open_in_editor.cljs (the chip; sets window.location.href)
- tools/source-coords/editor-uri/editor-uri (the URI builder + allowed-uri? gate)
- Causa's parallel surface: day8.re-frame2-causa.open-in-editor

## Likely root causes to investigate
1. Configured editor name not set — defaults to a no-op or wrong scheme
2. URI scheme not registered with OS (vscode://path/to/file:line works only when VSCode handler is registered)
3. Browser security blocking custom-scheme navigation from non-user-gesture
4. URI percent-encoding issue (Windows paths with backslashes; spaces in path)
5. allowed-uri? gate rejecting the URI despite scheme being in allowlist
6. set-href! seam succeeding silently when window.open would have surfaced an error
7. Windows-specific URI handler quirk (Mike is on Windows 11)

## Diagnostic steps
- Run the testbed live + click the chip with browser devtools open: any console errors? any navigation blocked?
- Verify the editor config is set (story/configure!)
- Inspect the actual URI that's being assigned to window.location.href (log it before assignment)
- Try clicking the equivalent Causa chip — same failure?
- Try pasting the URI directly into the browser address bar — does the OS handler fire then?

## Acceptance
Clicking the chip in Story (and the parallel Causa chip) opens VSCode (or whichever configured editor) at the captured source-coord. Or a clear actionable error surfaces when the OS handler isn't available.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #1433 (merged 2026-05-18). Open-in-editor chip now uses explicit .assign() instead of property-setter form; Chromium on Windows was silently no-op'ing property assignment for non-http(s) schemes.

title: fix(core): delete redundant runtime alias of inject-cofx that clobbers CLJ macro var
description:
rf2-s60vj probe (2026-05-16 21:xx AUSEST) confirmed: implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc has TWO definitions of inject-cofx.

Line 405: #?(:clj (defmacro inject-cofx ...)) — stamps :rf.trace/call-site source-coords via csm/build-inject-cofx-form
Line 572: (def inject-cofx cofx/inject-cofx) — UNGUARDED plain alias

Line 572 runs in BOTH CLJ and CLJS:
- CLJ: macros and fns share the var; line 572 CLOBBERS the macro. JVM callers of rf/inject-cofx get the bare interceptor with NO source-coord stamping. SSR pipelines (ssr/, ssr-ring/) + JVM tests affected. Error events emitted from inside cofx bodies lose source-coord attribution.
- CLJS: the macro lives in the JVM compile-time ns; CLJS user code resolves rf/inject-cofx to the macro via :require-macros self-import (line 74). Hence CLJS tests pass.

inject-cofx* already exists at line 342 as the documented HoF/programmatic form. Line 572 is REDUNDANT — pure regression.

spec/API.md:557 documents inject-cofx as M (macro) — contradicted by the alias's existence in CLJ.

## Fix
1. Delete line 572 outright.
2. Add CLJ regression in implementation/core/test/re_frame/source_coord_test.cljc asserting (meta #'re-frame.core/inject-cofx) reports {:macro true}.

## Risk
LOW. 1-line delete, 1 test add. Restores documented contract.

## Discovered
rf2-s60vj audit (P1) — broader API reconcile parent. This P0 is the tight correctness bug; the broader reconcile stays at P1 for separate dispatch.

## Refs
- core.cljc:404-418 (macro)
- core.cljc:572 (the redundant alias)
- core.cljc:342-348 (inject-cofx* HoF — already documented surface)
- spec/API.md:557
- source_coord_test.cljc:129-139
notes: PR #1307 opened — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1307. Deleted core.cljc:572 (def inject-cofx cofx/inject-cofx) — the ungated runtime alias that clobbered the CLJ macro at line 405 with no source-coord stamping. Added CLJ regression in source_coord_test.cljc asserting (:macro (meta #'re-frame.core/inject-cofx)). Gates: clojure -M:test 523/2718 green; npm run test:cljs 2281/6488 green.

title: [causa] Wire panel source-coord chips to open-chip — currently dispatching to stub event, editor never opens
description:
## The bug

Causa's four panels render their own `[:button]` with an `on-click` that dispatches `[:rf.causa/open-in-editor ...]` — which is a STUB `reg-event-db` that just records the coord into `app-db`. **Clicking the source-coord chip in any Causa panel does NOT open the editor.**

The `open-chip` helper at `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/open_in_editor.cljs:136-171` exists, is tested, and has the full rf2-cm93v positive-allowlist gating. But it's not invoked by any panel.

`shell.cljs:70` imports `open-in-editor` namespace but never calls anything from it.

## Affected files

- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/trace.cljs:307-320` — inline `[:button]` dispatches stub
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/issues_ribbon.cljs:261-278` — inline `[:button]` dispatches stub
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/mcp_server.cljs:343-358` — inline `[:button]` dispatches stub
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/hydration_debugger.cljs:298-308` — inline `[:button]` dispatches stub
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/hydration_debugger.cljs:562-564` — the stub `(rf/reg-event-db :rf.causa/open-in-editor ...)`

## Fix

Replace each panel's inline button with `(open-in-editor/open-chip source-coord)` — that helper renders `[:a {:href "vscode://..."}]` and fires the OS handler via `(set! (.-location js/window) uri)` with the positive-allowlist gate.

Delete the stub `:rf.causa/open-in-editor` event-db handler in `hydration_debugger.cljs:562-564` (and update `014-Registry-Catalogue.md:223` accordingly).

Update affected panel tests in `tools/causa/test/.../panels/*_view_cljs_test.cljs` — the click contract changes from "dispatches event" to "renders an `<a href>` chip".

Update `spec/016-Auxiliary-Panels.md:66-69` to drop the "non-interactive in v1" disclaimer.

## Context

Per rf2-3vucz audit (`ai/findings/source-coord-clickability-audit-2026-05-14.md`). rf2-evgf5 closed 2026-05-12 as "implementation complete" but only Story's panels were wired; Causa shipped the helper plus a shell-stub demo only. This is a load-bearing UX gap: every Causa source-coord chip is a no-op for the user.

## Acceptance

- Clicking a source-coord chip in any Causa panel (trace / issues-ribbon / mcp-server / hydration-debugger) renders an `<a href="vscode://..." />` (or whichever editor is configured) and `window.location` is set on click.
- The stub `:rf.causa/open-in-editor` event-db handler is gone.
- Panel view tests assert the chip is an `<a>` with an editor-URI `href` rather than a button dispatching an event.
- Existing `open_in_editor_cljs_test.cljs` keeps passing.
notes: Rebased onto post-#1105 main; conflicts resolved (src + test). Local quality gates green: test:cljs (1994 tests / 5651 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors) + test:bundle-isolation (PASS). Force-pushed via --force-with-lease. PR #1106 now reports mergeable=MERGEABLE; ready for admin-merge.

- Impl emit site: `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:365-380` — builds `base-tags` with `:where :app-db`, `:path leaf-path`, `:registered-path reg-path`, `:value leaf-value`, `:frame frame-id`, `:explain explanation`, `:reason (reason-string ...)`, `:rollback? true`, `:recovery :no-recovery`, plus `:failing-id` (when event-id known).
- `trace/emit-error!` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:388-462) hoists `:recovery` from tags to top level. Adds `:category` if not present.
- Fixture expects: `:tags {:category :rf.error/schema-validation-failure :failing-id ... :where :app-db :path ... :value ... :rollback? true :reason "App-db at path [:count] failed schema [:int], got string."}` at top level `{:operation :rf.error/schema-validation-failure :op-type :error :tags {...} :recovery :no-recovery}`.

**Likely root cause**:
1. `:reason` text format mismatch — `reason-string` may produce different prose than fixture expects
2. OR impl adds extra fields (e.g. `:explain`, `:registered-path`, `:frame`) the fixture matcher doesn't allow (if it's an exact-match shape rather than superset)

**Fix**:
- Compare actual emit (run the failing case locally) vs fixture
- Either update fixture `:reason` text to match what `reason-string` emits, or simplify impl's tag set
- May also need to update `:explain` / `:registered-path` handling

**Files**: `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:154` (reason-string fn), `spec/conformance/fixtures/error-schema-failure.edn`, `spec/conformance/fixtures/schema-app-db-slice-validates.edn`

**State**: branch pushed to origin; worktree at `/c/Users/miket/code/rf2-schemas-cluster-work`. Other gates green; only this conformance check failing.

title: feat(elision): Path D — collapse declaration surface to schema-first (rf2-j40u7 impl)
description:
Path D impl bead for rf2-j40u7 (CLOSED — decision). Docs preview landed at https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/958 (this bead's mirror in docs).

# Goal

Collapse the privacy + size declaration surface from 6 sites to 2:

1. Per-slot Malli schema meta (`{:sensitive? true}` / `{:large? true}`) — canonical truth for both axes.
2. Handler-meta `:sensitive?` — single escape hatch for cross-cutting handlers whose sensitivity claim isn't owned by any one slot.

Composes with rf2-ynnq0 Option A (already decided): schemas owns the deep walker, elision consumes `:schemas/extract-large-paths-from-schema` and writes the registry slot. Schema is the single source feeding the elision pipe.

Pre-alpha; no back-compat. Masterpiece-grade Zen-of-Python.

# Deltas

## spec/

- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` — mark deleted APIs as deleted; document the new single-source mechanism (schema-first ONLY); add the dev-only `:rf.warning/large-value-unschema'd` trace event spec (once-per-slot-per-session, compiles away under goog.DEBUG=false).
- `spec/010-Schemas.md` — promote schema-slot `:large?` / `:sensitive?` from one-of-three to THE declaration site for each axis; the per-slot props map is the canonical surface. Cross-link to 009 + 014.

## implementation/

DELETE (not deprecate — pre-alpha):
- The runtime `pr-str` byte-counting walker that auto-flagged values over the 16KB threshold.
- The `:rf.size/declare-large` fx and the `[:rf/elision :runtime-flagged]` slot it wrote into.
- The `rf/declare-large-path!` REPL convenience and its `rf/clear-large-path!` pair.
- The `with-redacted` interceptor as a USER-FACING API. The auto-install-from-schema path replaces it: when a schema slot declares `:sensitive? true`, the runtime auto-installs the scrub for handlers that read/write that slot (no user-side interceptor lines).
- The `:rf.warning/runtime-large-elision` trace — replaced by the dev-only `:rf.warning/large-value-unschema'd` (next bullet).

ADD:
- `:rf.warning/large-value-unschema'd` — dev-only trace event, fires once per (slot, session) when the walker would elide an over-threshold value at a path with NO schema declaration. Emit-site evaporates under `goog.DEBUG=false`. The trace carries the slot's path, the byte count, and a hint string ("Add `{:large? true}` to the schema slot for this path.").
- Schema-based auto-install of the redaction interceptor for every handler that reads/writes a `:sensitive?` slot. The handler body sees the unredacted value; the trace surface sees `:rf/redacted`.

REFACTOR:
- The handler-meta `:sensitive?` path stays — but reframe as "the single escape hatch for cross-cutting handlers." Tests covering the handler-meta path stay; tests covering it as the PRIMARY declaration site need to be migrated (their migration target is the schema-slot meta path).

## docs/

DONE in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/958:
- `docs/guide/23-privacy-and-elision.md` — full rewrite.
- `docs/guide/04a-schemas.md` — cross-ref update.
- `docs/guide/README.md` — chapter row trim.

## skills/

Audit every leaf under `skills/` for references to the deleted APIs (`with-redacted`, `:rf.size/declare-large`, `rf/declare-large-path!`, the runtime auto-detect threshold) and migrate them to the schema-first vocabulary. Recent skill-leaf landing rf2-xas97 is the touchstone.

## tests

- Retire tests that pin the deleted APIs:
  - Tests for the runtime byte-counting walker.
  - Tests for `:rf.size/declare-large` fx + `rf/declare-large-path!` REPL form.
  - Tests asserting the user-facing `with-redacted` shape (replaced by tests asserting the auto-install-from-schema behaviour).
- Migrate `:rf.warning/runtime-large-elision` tests to `:rf.warning/large-value-unschema'd`.
- Add tests for the schema-auto-install path: handler reads/writes a `:sensitive?` slot ⇒ trace shows `:rf/redacted`; no interceptor was written by the test author.
- Add tests for cross-cutting handler-meta `:sensitive?` (the escape hatch) — handler whose slots are individually non-sensitive but the handler scope is.

## conformance corpus

Update fixtures under spec/conformance/ that exercise the deleted APIs. Validate against the new schema-first contract.

# Sequencing

Hot-zone files touched: spec/009-Instrumentation.md, spec/010-Schemas.md, implementation/core/* (privacy.cljc, elision.cljc, events.cljc, frame.cljc). Sequential dispatch — must not run in parallel with rf2-ynnq0 Option A's impl (which also touches schemas.cljc + elision.cljc + spec/010).

# Acceptance

- `npm run test:cljs` green from `implementation/`.
- `npm run test:browser` green.
- conformance suite green.
- `mkdocs build --strict` green.
- skill-leaf audit clean (no references to deleted APIs).
- No `with-redacted` / `:rf.size/declare-large` / `rf/declare-large-path!` / runtime-byte-counter symbols in `implementation/` source.

Source: Mike, 2026-05-14 ~10:08 AUSEST (Path D decision on rf2-j40u7).

title: refactor(mcp-conformance): split pair2-mcp source-text pin to grep actual emit files
description:
**Source:** refactor-audit r2 of \`tools/mcp-conformance\` (rf2-azk9c), finding **F-VOCAB-1** (with F-VOCAB-3 folded in).

## The bug

\`wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/wire_vocab_test.clj:507-509\` lists pair2-mcp's source files as:

\`\`\`clojure
:pair2-mcp [\"tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs\"
            \"tools/pair2-mcp/spec/Principles.md\"
            \"tools/pair2-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md\"]
\`\`\`

The literal-presence test uses \`some\` across the three. **For 4 of the 5 markers, the literal exists ONLY in the spec doc — not in any pair2-mcp source code.** The gate passes via prose in \`Principles.md\`, not via emission grep.

Verified with \`grep -c\` against \`tools.cljs\`:
- \`:rf.mcp/overflow\` → 1 (line 109, in a docstring)
- \`:rf.mcp/summary\` → 0
- \`:rf.mcp/dedup-table\` → 0
- \`:rf.mcp/diff-from\` → 0
- \`:rf.size/large-elided\` → 0

Real emission lives in \`tools/cap.cljs\` (overflow), \`tools/summary.cljs\` (summary), \`tools/dedup.cljs\` (dedup), \`tools/elision.cljs\` (large-elided), \`cache.cljs\`, \`wire_pipeline.cljs\` — none of which are grepped.

A rename of \`:rf.mcp/summary\` to \`:rf.mcp/summarize\` in \`tools/summary.cljs\` does NOT trip this test today.

## Fix

Split \`server-source-files :pair2-mcp\` into two slots:

- \`:pair2-mcp-emit\` — actual source \`.cljs\` files: \`tools/{cap,summary,dedup,elision}.cljs\` + \`cache.cljs\` + \`wire_pipeline.cljs\`.
- \`:pair2-mcp-doc\` — \`Principles.md\` + \`003-Tool-Catalogue.md\`.

Make \`marker-literal-appears-in-every-contracted-server-source\` assert the literal appears in the EMIT slot. The DOC slot can be a separate (looser) consistency gate or left as documentation.

Per-marker emit files (might want a per-marker map, since not every marker is emitted from every file):

- \`:rf.mcp/overflow\` → \`tools/cap.cljs\` + \`cache.cljs\`
- \`:rf.mcp/summary\` → \`tools/summary.cljs\`
- \`:rf.mcp/dedup-table\` → \`tools/dedup.cljs\`
- \`:rf.mcp/diff-from\` → \`tools/dedup.cljs\` (verify) or \`tools.cljs\`
- \`:rf.size/large-elided\` → \`tools/elision.cljs\`

Verify emit-file claims by grepping before encoding the table.

## Severity

P0 — the gate's load-bearing claim ('the literal MUST appear in each contracted server's source') is provably weaker than advertised. The cross-server vocabulary contract is precisely what this artefact exists to enforce; the pin currently has a hole.

## Under-appreciated win to propagate

\`strip-comments-and-strings\` (rf2-7dnct, rf2-xx42k) cleanly distinguishes docstring mentions from emissions. Apply it here on the emit-side pin to be defensive — a future commit that leaves the literal only inside a docstring inside an emit file would otherwise pass.

## Time estimate

30-45 min (grep verification + table encoding + test update).

## Coordination

Bundled with F-VOCAB-3 (which would resolve when this lands). Touches \`wire-vocab/test/.../wire_vocab_test.clj\` — isolated surface, parallel-safe.
close_reason: Landed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1017

title: refactor(mcp-conformance): wire JVM wire-vocab tests into CI
description:
**Source:** refactor-audit r2 of `tools/mcp-conformance` (rf2-azk9c), finding **F-CI-1**.

## The gap

`.github/workflows/test.yml` registers `mcp-conformance-pair2`, `mcp-conformance-story`, `mcp-conformance-causa` jobs that run the Node-side `npm run test:...`. **No job runs the JVM-side `clojure -M:test` from `tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/`.**

A grep across `.github/workflows/` for `wire-vocab` or `wire_vocab` returns zero hits. Verified.

Affected tests (all rich, all this-session-fresh):

- `wire_vocab_test.clj` — cross-server wire-marker vocabulary (rf2-j2z7o).
- `indicator_field_test.clj` — envelope-slot parity (rf2-6m8tq).
- `slot_name_test.clj` — tool-arg slot-name parity (rf2-zvv65).

These gates only fire when Mike manually runs them locally. Every PR ships without them.

## Fix

Add `mcp-conformance-wire-vocab` job to `.github/workflows/test.yml`:

- `working-directory: tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab`
- JDK 21 (already provisioned by sibling jobs)
- Step: `clojure -M:test`
- Maven cache key on `wire-vocab/deps.edn`

Per `wire-vocab/README.md:71` — total cold-JVM run time ~3-5s; near-zero CI cost.

## Severity

P0 — three contract gates that the artefact exists to enforce currently fire only at Mike's discretion. The cross-server vocabulary, envelope-slot parity, and slot-name parity contracts can regress in a PR and the merge proceeds green.

## Pre-alpha rule

This is masterpiece-grade work currently behind a manual run gate. Wiring it into CI is the load-bearing fix.

## Coordination

`.github/workflows/test.yml` is hot-zone — sequence behind any other workflow-touching beads in flight.

## Time estimate

10-15 min (single workflow YAML block + cache key).

title: refactor(epoch): capture-event! filter set missing :rf.epoch/db-replaced and reset-frame-db-* ops (correctness)
description:
Per refactor-audit r2 (rf2-lwn4t): `capture-event!` filter set at `epoch.cljc:277-284` excludes `:rf.epoch/snapshotted` / `:rf.epoch/restored` / the five `:rf.epoch/restore-*` ops, but MISSES `:rf.epoch/db-replaced`, `:rf.epoch/reset-frame-db-during-drain`, `:rf.epoch/reset-frame-db-schema-mismatch`. These three are emitted by `reset-frame-db!` (success path + two failure paths), carry `:frame` tags, and fire OUTSIDE any cascade. Therefore they accrete into `capture-buffers[frame-id]` and leak into the next drain's harvested record for that frame — silent correctness bug. The next epoch record would carry phantom events; `find-trigger-event`'s fallback arm would pick the leaked `:epoch-id`; `project-effects` would silently include them.

Fix: lift the set to a private module-level def, add the three missing ops, AND consider filtering by op-type prefix (`:rf.epoch`) instead of op enumeration so this stays right by construction.

Add a regression test: drive a cascade on a frame, call `reset-frame-db!`, drive a second cascade, assert the second record's `:trace-events` excludes the `:rf.epoch/db-replaced` event AND `:trigger-event` is the new event vector (not `[:rf.epoch/db-replaced]`).

Findings doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-epoch-2026-05-14.md` §F1.1.
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/953. capture-event! skip-ops catalogue now includes :rf.epoch/db-replaced, :rf.epoch/reset-frame-db-during-drain, :rf.epoch/reset-frame-db-schema-mismatch. Lifted to module-level private def (rf2-5xrvl). Three regression tests pin the cross-contamination shape; a fourth catalogue test pins the skip-ops set itself. Enumeration over prefix-filter chosen deliberately so future in-cascade :rf.epoch/* ops continue to surface in records.

title: refactor(mcp-base): lift apply-cap pipeline to mcp-base (drop ~100 LoC of duplication)
description:
## What

Lift the cap-enforcement pipeline (`max-tokens-arg`, `sum-text-tokens`, `overflow-result`, `apply-cap`) from `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/cap.cljs` and `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cap.cljc` into shared mcp-base machinery.

Today `re-frame.mcp-base.overflow` owns the *overflow-marker map shape* — but the actual cap-enforcement *algorithm* (token-count the result, compare against cap, swap payload for marker, build a fresh result) duplicates across both consumers (~95 LoC in pair2-mcp, ~60 LoC in story-mcp).

## Why

Round-2 audit (rf2-n4q62 / `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-tools-mcp-base-2026-05-14.md`, F7 — top finding) identified this as the highest-payoff remaining cross-MCP drift. Drain-wave rf2-vw4sq landed the *constants* and the *helpers*; the cap pipeline (the highest-volume duplicated surface across the triplet) is still per-consumer.

## How

Sketch (in mcp-base):

```clojure
;; re-frame.mcp-base.cap
(defprotocol ResultIO
  (content-texts [_ result] "Seq of strings from the result's :text slots.")
  (build-overflow-result [_ marker original-result] "Build a result carrying marker."))

(defn max-tokens [raw] ...)  ;; resolves the :max-tokens MCP arg → int / nil

(defn apply-cap [io result {:keys [tool cap hint]}] ...)
```

- pair2-mcp ships a `js-io` reifying the protocol over `#js {:content #js [...]}`.
- story-mcp ships a `clj-io` reifying it over CLJ maps.
- Per-tool `overflow-hints` tables stay local.

## Estimated impact

- mcp-base: +~40 LoC (new ns + protocol).
- pair2-mcp: -~80 LoC (delete duplicate impl, keep ResultIO).
- story-mcp: -~50 LoC (same).
- **Net: -~90 LoC across the triplet**, plus the wire-shape invariant pinned in one place.

## Tests

- New `mcp-base/test/.../cap_test.clj` unit tests via a mock ResultIO.
- pair2-mcp `wire_cap_test.cljs` and story-mcp `tools_test.clj` cap tests stay (they validate the IO instances + integration); should still pass without modification.

## Source

rf2-n4q62 round-2 audit, finding F7.
notes:
PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/990

Design — per-server specialisation via the new ResultIO protocol (defprotocol in re-frame.mcp-base.cap):

  (defprotocol ResultIO
    (content-texts [_io result])
    (build-overflow-result [_io marker original-result]))

pair2-mcp reifies over #js {:content #js [...]}-shaped JS results (js-interop accessors); story-mcp reifies over {:content [...] :structuredContent ...} CLJ maps. Per-tool hint table stays consumer-side; cap value, token rule, and marker shape stay in mcp-base.

LoC delta:
- pair2-mcp/cap.cljs: 140 -> 142 (IO reify + thin wrappers preserving test-facing API)
- story-mcp/cap.cljc: 132 -> 99 (-33)
- mcp-base/cap.cljc: 0 -> 192 (~50% docstrings; algorithm body ~50 LoC)
- mcp-base/cap_test.clj: 0 -> 160

Duplicated algorithm content ~45 LoC across the two consumers is single-sourced in mcp-base.

Gates: mcp-base JVM (85/211/0), story-mcp JVM (86/449/0), implementation CLJS (1816/5040/0), bundle-isolation green (mcp-base does not leak into counter production bundle).

title: refactor(causa): migrate per-panel registrations to install! (drops registry.cljs from 1912 to ~150 LoC)
description:
## Context

Filed from round-2 audit rf2-imynx (ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-tools-causa-2026-05-14.md, top finding P0-1).

## Problem

`tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/registry.cljs` is **1912 LoC** — ~7.5× the leaf-size ceiling (09f53791 codified ≤250L / ≤16KB). It holds every panel's subs/events/fxs in one monolithic `register-causa-handlers!` thunk gated by a single `registered?` sentinel.

The `ai-co-pilot` panel already proved the alternative shape: it exposes `(defn install! [] ...)` at `ai_co_pilot.cljs:465`, and the registry calls it from inside its own `compare-and-set!` gate (`registry.cljs:1903`). That pattern is the migration target.

## Scope

Migrate each of the remaining 15 panels' registration blocks into a per-panel `install!`:

  - app-db-diff, causality-graph, effects, event-detail, flows,
    hydration-debugger, issues-ribbon, machine-inspector, mcp-server,
    performance, routes, schema-violation-timeline, subscriptions,
    time-travel, trace

Each panel's existing `panel_name.cljs` ns gains an `(defn install! [] ...)` fn that takes its block out of registry.cljs verbatim. `registry.cljs` becomes a thin orchestrator:

```clj
(defn register-causa-handlers! []
  (when (compare-and-set! registered? false true)
    (rf/reg-sub :rf.causa/trace-buffer ...)  ;; cross-panel primitives
    (rf/reg-event-db :rf.causa/note-trace-event ...)
    ;; ... ~6 cross-panel primitives ...
    (event-detail/install!)
    (time-travel/install!)
    (causality-graph/install!)
    ;; ... 15 panels ...
    (ai-co-pilot/install!)))
```

Net delta: registry.cljs ~1912 LoC → ~150 LoC. Per-panel ns grows ~80–250 LoC but the code is colocated with the panel it serves.

## Safe to parallel-dispatch?

Each panel migration is independent — 16 sub-beads could parallelise. registry.cljs is a hot-zone in this work (every sub-bead touches it); sequence those, or move the cross-panel primitives to a tiny `registry/core` file FIRST and have each panel migration add its own `install!` call to a per-panel registration-order vector.

## Acceptance

- `registry.cljs` < 250 LoC
- Each panel ns exposes `install!` mirroring the ai-co-pilot pattern
- Existing tests pass unchanged (the sub-graph wires the same; only the registration call sites move)
close_reason: Migrated. registry.cljs: 1771 → 211 LoC (88% reduction). 15 panels each gained  mirroring the ai-co-pilot pattern. New  ns breaks the registry→panel→registry require cycle for  / . Tests green: 488 JVM, 1817 CLJS, bundle-isolation. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1011

title: refactor(routing): :rf/pending-navigation slot shape incomplete (missing :rejecting-route :rejecting-guard :reason :requested-url :requested-by-event)

title: refactor(routing): :rf/url-changed hardcodes :transition :idle; must compute from :on-match
description:
Per Spec 012 §URL changes are events the :rf/url-changed handler should set :transition (if (seq on-match-vec) :loading :idle). Currently routing.cljc:794 hardcodes :transition :idle, so URL-driven navigations with :on-match events never observe :loading during the drain.

Note: the sibling :rf.route/handle-url-change DOES compute this correctly (routing.cljc:851). The two handlers are 95% duplicate (see audit A1) — fixing either way will surface during the collapse refactor.

Audit: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-routing-2026-05-14.md A3.
Parent: rf2-yt2g2.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1020 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1020)

title: refactor(routing): :rf.route/handle-url-change omits :fragment and :nav-token from slice
description:
Per Spec 012 §The :rf/route slice the slice always carries {:id :params :query :fragment :transition :error :nav-token}. routing.cljc:847-852 writes only 5 keys: :fragment is computed via split-fragment but never assoc'd; :nav-token is never allocated. Spec §URL changes are events pseudocode explicitly allocates nav-token here.

Effect: URL-driven navigation (popstate, initial, SSR) produces a slice that diverges in shape from programmatic navigation. The Spec-Schemas :rf/route-slice schema will reject it.

Fix: thread alloc-nav-token, assoc :fragment + :nav-token into the slice write. Coordinate with A1 (handler collapse).

Audit: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-routing-2026-05-14.md A2.
Parent: rf2-yt2g2.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1020 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1020)

title: refactor(routing): :rf/url-changed must write :rf.route/not-found slice on unmatched URL
description:
Per Spec 012 §URL changes are events / §Route-not-found, an unmatched URL must update :rf/route to {:id :rf.route/not-found :params {:url url} :query {} :fragment ... :transition <idle|loading> :error nil :nav-token <fresh>}. Current impl (routing.cljc:800-809) only trace/emit-error!s and returns {} — the previous slice stays visible, so the user sees the previous route's UI after navigating to a nonexistent URL.

Also emit :rf.warning/no-not-found-route when :rf.route/not-found itself isn't registered (separate spec requirement; see S5 in audit).

Audit: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-routing-2026-05-14.md A4 + S5.
Parent: rf2-yt2g2.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1020 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1020)

title: refactor(core): with-debug-stamp helper for core_call_site_macros' 8 inline DCE gates
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-byut1 finding CQ-R2.3 (round-1 CQ2 leftover).

`core_call_site_macros.cljc` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_call_site_macros.cljc:50-104`) has 8 inlined `(if re-frame.interop/debug-enabled? <stamping-form> <plain-form>)` forms across the 4 `build-…-form` plain-CLJ fns. Each carries 2 arity branches; each branch emits the same gate-shape.

`grep -c "re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?" core_call_site_macros.cljc` returns 8.

Round-1 flagged this as CQ2 ('`with-debug-stamp` helper'); the carve-out from `core.cljc` (CQ1 / rf2-4rnui) shipped but the inlined-gate pattern travelled wholesale.

## Proposed shape

```clojure
(defn- gate
  "Emit (if interop/debug-enabled? stamped plain) — wraps each call-site
  macro's gate in a single shape so Closure-DCE still elides under
  goog.DEBUG=false (the gate must be OUTERMOST per Spec 009)."
  [stamped plain]
  `(if re-frame.interop/debug-enabled? ~stamped ~plain))
```

Then each `build-…-form` collapses from ~ 12 lines to ~ 5:

```clojure
(defn build-dispatch-form
  [form-meta ns-sym file event-vec opts-form]
  (let [cs-form  (call-site-form form-meta ns-sym file)
        stamped  (if opts-form
                   `(re-frame.core/dispatch* ~event-vec (assoc ~opts-form :rf.trace/call-site ~cs-form))
                   `(re-frame.core/dispatch* ~event-vec {:rf.trace/call-site ~cs-form}))
        plain    (if opts-form
                   `(re-frame.core/dispatch* ~event-vec ~opts-form)
                   `(re-frame.core/dispatch* ~event-vec))]
    (gate stamped plain)))
```

## Estimate

~ -35 LoC across the 4 builders. Low risk — macros are compile-time scaffolding; the Closure-DCE invariant (gate outermost) is enforced by construction.

## Related

- Round-2 audit doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-core-2026-05-14.md` §CQ-R2.3
- Round-1 origin: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-core-2026-05-14.md` §CQ2
- Carve-out that left this leftover: rf2-4rnui
- Parent audit bead: rf2-byut1
close_reason: Landed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/984. Single `gate` helper introduced; 8 inline (if re-frame.interop/debug-enabled? ...) forms across the 4 build-…-form fns collapsed to a single emission shape. LoC delta: +52/-40 (net +12 — bead's -35 estimate was optimistic; the per-arity stamped/plain let-bindings retain symmetry over the original 2-line ternary inlining). Production elision gate green first-try (rf.trace/call-site sentinel ABSENT in release, PRESENT in control). CLJS gate green (1816 tests). JVM core gate green (456 tests). No other inlined gates found beyond the listed 8.

title: refactor(core): factor frame/destroy-frame!'s 4 inline cleanup-hook fires
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-byut1 finding CQ-R2.2.

`frame/destroy-frame!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:427-451`) carries 3 consecutive `(when-let [hook-fn (late-bind/get-fn :X/Y)] (try (hook-fn id) (catch _ nil)))` blocks for:

- `:privacy/clear-suppression-cache!` (rf2-isdwf)
- `:ssr/on-frame-destroyed` (rf2-fcj33)
- `:machines/on-frame-destroyed!` (rf2-ysa94)

Plus the matching `notify-epoch-listeners!` helper at `frame.cljc:355-364` for `:epoch/on-frame-destroyed` — FOUR call sites of the same shape.

## Proposed shape

Either:

**Option A (helper fn):**
```clojure
(defn- safe-call-hook! [hook-key & args]
  (when-let [f (late-bind/get-fn hook-key)]
    (try (apply f args)
         (catch #?(:clj Throwable :cljs :default) _ nil))))
```
Then each fire is one line: `(safe-call-hook! :privacy/clear-suppression-cache!)`.

**Option B (data table):**
```clojure
(def ^:private destroy-hooks
  [{:hook :privacy/clear-suppression-cache! :args [] :bead "rf2-isdwf"}
   {:hook :ssr/on-frame-destroyed           :args [:frame-id] :bead "rf2-fcj33"}
   {:hook :machines/on-frame-destroyed!     :args [:frame-id] :bead "rf2-ysa94"}
   {:hook :epoch/on-frame-destroyed         :args [:frame-id] :bead "rf2-d656"}])
```

Option A is simpler (4 sites × 5 lines → 4 sites × 1 line). Option B unifies with rf2-d7vw8 (the test-support reset table) so both follow the same idiom; preferable if both land.

## Estimate

~ -15 LoC. Low risk (pure refactor, no behaviour change). 

## Related

- Round-2 audit doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-core-2026-05-14.md` §CQ-R2.2 / §A-R2.1
- Sibling: rf2-d7vw8 (the test_support reset table)
- Parent audit bead: rf2-byut1
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/985 — factored safe-call-hook! private helper; 4 call sites collapse from ~5-line when-let/try/catch blocks to 1-line calls. Order preserved exactly (privacy -> ssr -> machines -> emit-trace -> dissoc -> unregister -> notify-epoch). LoC delta on frame.cljc: +21/-18 = net +3 (helper docstring outweighs site savings; the win is call-site clarity + single-sourced late-bind+best-effort policy). All quality gates green: test:cljs (1816 tests), test:elision, JVM core (456 tests). No other safe-call-hook! candidates within scope — fx.cljc's call-frame-scoped-hook! is intentionally non-tolerant (different policy); test_support.cljc's late-bind calls are the rf2-d7vw8 sibling scope (already landed).

title: refactor(core): factor reset-runtime-fixture's 9-row late-bind table into data + driver
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-byut1 finding CQ-R2.1.

`test_support/reset-runtime-fixture` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:250-302`) carries 9 inline `(when-let [reset-X! (late-bind/get-fn :Y/reset-Z!)] (reset-X!))` forms — one per artefact (`:flows/reset-flows!`, `:flows/reset-last-inputs!`, `:machines/reset-timers!`, `:routing/reset-counters!`, `:http/clear-all-in-flight!`, `:epoch/clear-history!`, `:epoch/clear-epoch-cbs!`, `:adapter/clear-warn-once-caches!`, `:schemas/clear-by-frame!`). Each is decorated with 6-9 lines of prose explaining the artefact pedigree (rf2-* design beads).

Same shape as the `core_artefact/defwrapper` factory (rf2-h824v) — this is the SECOND instance of the 'late-bind dispatch via data table' idiom that hasn't been factored.

## Proposed shape

```clojure
(def ^:private reset-hooks
  [{:hook :flows/reset-flows!         :bead "rf2-tfw3" :doc "Drop per-frame flow registry"}
   {:hook :flows/reset-last-inputs!   :bead "rf2-tfw3" :doc "Drop dirty-check last-inputs map"}
   {:hook :machines/reset-timers!     :bead "rf2-ysa94" :doc "Cancel in-flight :after timers"}
   {:hook :routing/reset-counters!    :bead "rf2-k682"  :doc "Reset route reg-index counter"}
   {:hook :http/clear-all-in-flight!  :bead "rf2-5kpd"  :doc "Drop in-flight HTTP request registry"}
   {:hook :epoch/clear-history!       :bead "rf2-lt4e"  :doc "Drop per-frame epoch ring buffer"}
   {:hook :epoch/clear-epoch-cbs!     :bead "rf2-lt4e"  :doc "Drop epoch callback registry"}
   {:hook :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches! :bead "rf2-4edk" :doc "Clear warn-once caches"}])

(defn- run-reset-hooks! []
  (doseq [{:keys [hook]} reset-hooks]
    (when-let [f (late-bind/get-fn hook)]
      (f))))
```

The prose-rationale absorbs into a single ns-docstring block keyed by hook name. Adding a new artefact's reset becomes a one-row edit.

## Estimate

~ -65 LoC. Low risk (pure refactor, no behaviour change). The fixture is used by 50+ test files; one missed hook ripples loudly.

## Companion test

Consider an explicit test that registers sentinel hooks and asserts every hook fires exactly once per fixture invocation (round-2 audit TE-R2.2; could file separately as a P1 follow-on).

## Related

- Round-2 audit doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-core-2026-05-14.md` §CQ-R2.1
- Sibling pattern: `core_artefact/defwrapper` (rf2-h824v)
- Sibling pattern: `fx/reserved-fx-handlers` (rf2-b64yz)
- Parent audit bead: rf2-byut1
close_reason: Shipped via PR #977 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/977). 9 inline late-bind when-let forms collapse to a single 9-row data table (reset-hook-table) + filter-by-:phase driver (run-reset-hooks!). Body of reset-runtime-fixture shrinks from ~80 lines to ~25; 9 scattered prose blocks absorb into one consolidated table docstring. Order preserved verbatim (pre-dispose runs flows-resets + schemas-clear; post-dispose runs machines/routing/http/epoch/adapter-warn-once). Schemas clear-fn capture retained for the :clear-kinds [:app-schema] branch (rf2-0frdi). LoC delta: +19 net (+117/-98) — increase comes from the consolidated docstring carrying all 8 artefact rationales in one place. Tests: JVM 456/2439 + CLJS 1816/5040, zero failures.

title: refactor(schemas): collapse double-deref of validator-fn in run-validation + validate-app-db! hot path
description:
Source: rf2-whepe round-2 audit, 2026-05-14 09:40 AUSEST.

Round-1's run-validation refactor (rf2-s7s6j) unified the four meta-bearing validate-*! fns. Post-refactor a redundant atom-deref pattern is now stark in two places:

1. `schemas/validate.cljc:156` — run-validation:
   ```clojure
   (if @validator/validator-fn
     ...
     (if (validator/run-validator schema value) ...)  ;; <-- run-validator derefs again
   ```

2. `schemas/validate.cljc:207` — validate-app-db!:
   ```clojure
   (when @validator/validator-fn
     (doseq [[path m] (storage/frame-schema-entries frame-id)]
       ...
       (when-not (validator/run-validator schema val-at)  ;; <-- per-iter deref
         ...)))
   ```

`validator/run-validator` (`validator.cljc:253-261`) body:
```clojure
(defn run-validator [schema value]
  (if-let [f @validator-fn]
    (f schema value)
    true))
```

The outer-guard short-circuit is correct in both sites, but the per-validation deref inside the doseq + the second deref inside run-validator are redundant. For an app with 50 registered app-schemas, every committed handler does 51 atom derefs when one would suffice; for run-validation-using paths (event / cofx / fx / sub-return) it's 2 derefs per validation.

Recommend: snapshot @validator-fn once at the gate, pass the deref'd fn into a refactored `apply-validator [f schema value]` (or change run-validator to accept a non-nil fn directly). Same for run-explainer / run-printer.

Hot-path atom derefs are ~5-10 ns on JVM; not the bottleneck in absolute terms but the pattern smells — the schemas-artefact is otherwise pristine post-refactor and this is the load-bearing slip.

Net: -10 LoC, single-deref-per-dispatch contract, the substrate's validator-fn ownership story reads cleaner.

Architecturally this is the under-appreciated cleanup that the round-1 run-validation refactor MADE VISIBLE — before unification the gate-deref was inside three separate fns; you couldn't see the redundancy without tracing all three at once. Now it's a 2-line slip on a clean substrate.
close_reason: Option 2 (inline single-deref-and-bind at the call sites — no API change). Bind @validator-fn once via if-let/when-let in run-validation + validate-app-db!; invoke directly. Eliminates 1 deref per event/cofx/fx/sub-return validation and N derefs per validate-app-db! call (for N registered app-schemas in the frame). validator/run-validator keeps its public shape — boundary-validation seam still routes through it. PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/960. Tests: schemas JVM (133/383), CLJS full gate (1818/5056), elision probe — all green.

title: refactor(machines): introduce frame-db-swap! helper to collapse 6 read/write call sites
description:
**Round-2 audit finding · rf2-2ukxv · A-r2-1 helper**

The read-container/replace-container pattern appears 6 times in machines fx handlers:
- `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:60-63` (`destroy-single-actor!`).
- `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:90-94` (`destroy-invoke-all-children!` slot clear).
- `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:125-130` (`destroy-single!`).
- `lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:140-141` (`install-spawn!`).
- `lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:277-279` (`invoke-all-init-fx`).
- Plus read-only sites: `lifecycle_fx.cljc:87`, `destroy.cljc:76-77`, `timer.cljc:177-178`, `timer.cljc:300-301`.

Each spelled as:

    (when-let [container (frame/get-frame-db frame-id)]
      (let [old-db (adapter/read-container container)
            new-db (... transform ...)]
        (adapter/replace-container! container new-db)))

## Fix sketch

Two helpers modelled on `swap!`/`deref`:

    (defn swap-frame-db!
      "Mutate the frame's app-db via (f db & args). Returns the new-db."
      [frame-id f & args]
      (when-let [container (frame/get-frame-db frame-id)]
        (let [old (adapter/read-container container)
              new (apply f old args)]
          (adapter/replace-container! container new)
          new)))

    (defn read-frame-db
      "Return the frame's app-db, or nil if no frame."
      [frame-id]
      (when-let [container (frame/get-frame-db frame-id)]
        (adapter/read-container container)))

(Live somewhere reachable — possibly `re-frame.frame` itself, since the pattern is generic and not machines-specific. Open question: scope to machines or generalise.)

Each call site collapses to one line; the `(when container ...)` guards disappear; the contract for "mutate the frame's app-db atomically" gets a named home.

## Acceptance

- One `swap-frame-db!` + `read-frame-db` (or equivalent) helper exists somewhere reachable.
- All 6 read/write pairs + 4 read-only sites in machines reach through it.
- ~40 LoC saved.

## Links

- Audit: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-machines-2026-05-14.md`
- Parent audit bead: rf2-2ukxv
close_reason: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/968. Added frame/swap-frame-db! (paired with existing frame/frame-app-db-value as read helper). Swept 5 write sites (audit said 6 but only 5 replace-container! call sites existed) + 4 read sites. LoC delta: +14 net total (frame.cljc +18 for helper+docstring; machines -2). Adapter require drops from destroy/spawn/timer/lifecycle_fx. All 359 machines JVM assertions + 5040 CLJS assertions green.

title: refactor(machines): unify synthesise-initial-snapshot / compute-initial-snapshot
description:
**Round-2 audit finding · rf2-2ukxv · Q-r2-1 / A-r2-1**

Two near-identical fns derive a machine's initial snapshot:
- `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:30-69` — `synthesise-initial-snapshot` (singleton registration path).
- `lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:89-114` — `compute-initial-snapshot` (spawn path).

Both build the freshly-derived initial snapshot for a machine. Six steps in each: detect parallel?, build region-map-or-cascaded-leaf state, seed `:data`, seed `:meta` (registration path), seed `:rf/spawn-counter` (registration path only — spawn omits!), `commit-tags-parallel`, optional `:rf/bootstrap-pending?` stamp.

## The drift (real defect, not just duplication)

The spawn path **omits**:
- `:rf/spawn-counter {}` slot seeding (registration.cljc:67) — a child machine whose `:entry` declares its own `:invoke` lands on `allocate-spawned-id`'s `(fnil inc 0)` defensive backstop, NOT the contract path.
- `:meta` propagation (registration.cljc:68) — a spawned actor whose spec declares `:meta` won't have it on the snapshot's `:meta` slot. Any `^:rf.machine/wants-ctx` action introspecting `:meta` sees nil.

These are silent contract gaps. The fix is one helper.

## Fix sketch

Extract `(build-initial-snapshot machine-spec {:keys [bootstrap-pending?]})` — could live in `lifecycle-fx/init.cljc` or alongside `commit-tags-parallel` in `parallel.cljc`. Both call sites delegate.

## Tests to add (see also TE-r2-1)

- A spawned actor's initial snapshot at `[:rf/machines <spawned-id>]` carries `:rf/spawn-counter {}`.
- A spawned actor whose spec declares `:meta` carries it on the snapshot.

## Acceptance

- One canonical `build-initial-snapshot` helper used by both paths.
- New tests in `spawn_registry_test.clj` covering the contract.
- `-30 LoC`, behaviour bugs closed.

## Links

- Audit: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-machines-2026-05-14.md`
- Round-1 doc: `ai/findings/machines-refactor-audit-2026-05-14.md`
- Parent audit bead: rf2-2ukxv
close_reason: Unified into parallel/build-initial-snapshot. Both registration.cljc and spawn.cljc delegate; :rf/bootstrap-pending? is now opt-in. Spawn path now correctly carries :rf/spawn-counter and :meta. PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/995

title: fix(scripts): drift checker — story-mcp tool discovery broken after rf2-3ukix per-category split
description:
rf2-3ukix (#?) split tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools.cljc into per-category files under tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/{dev,docs,testing,write,recorder}.cljc — the parent tools.cljc is now a thin façade with zero {:name "..."} literals.

scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py MAPPINGS still points at the old tools.cljc, so both story-mcp <-> re-frame2 and story-mcp <-> re-frame-pair2 entries return server=0 tools. The gate now fires 17 phantom missing-in-server findings for the skill allow-lists.

Fix: scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py needs to handle a multi-file source for story-mcp. Either:

1. Switch server_src to a sequence (tuple of paths) so extract_server_tools concatenates lex results from every file.
2. Point each mapping at the new registry.cljc and have it (and the per-category files) reachable.

(1) is mechanically simpler and matches what the gate has always done — lex source for {:name "..."} literals.

Discovered during rf2-0l82a (the parallel pair2-mcp fix). Both refactors landed within an hour of each other so the gate has been red since rf2-3ukix went in.

Companion bead: rf2-0l82a closes the pair2-mcp side. This bead closes the story-mcp side.
close_reason: Fixed: Mapping.server_src generalised to tuple[Path,...]; story-mcp mappings now point at the five per-category leaves (dev/docs/testing/write/recorder). Local verify: 'python scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py --verbose --ci' reports server=17 tools for both story-mcp mappings, exit 0. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/946.

title: fix(core): path-interceptor-uses-reserved-namespace test failing post-rf2-mn0qc
description:
The JVM core CI gate went RED on the post-#875 (rf2-mn0qc) main run.

Failing assertion at `implementation/core/test/re_frame/interceptor_test.clj:92`:
```
FAIL in (path-interceptor-uses-reserved-namespace) (interceptor_test.clj:92)
expected: (= 11 (get-in (rf/get-frame-db :rf/default) [:foo :bar]))
```

The rf2-mn0qc agent reported "440 tests / 2364 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors" pre-merge — so the test passes in isolation but fails in the full-suite CI run. Likely fixture-lifecycle / test-ordering issue: a sibling test leaves `:rf/default` frame state polluted, or the path interceptor's slice-back doesn't reset across tests.

Investigation:
1. Run `clojure -M:test :includes interceptor-test` from `implementation/core/` — does it pass in isolation?
2. Run the full core suite locally — does it reproduce?
3. If yes: which sibling test is leaving state? Add `(use-fixtures :each ...)` reset, or use a fresh frame-id per test, OR fix the path-interceptor reset semantics if real.
4. If no (flake): note conditions, but don't suppress.

Pre-alpha: NO back-compat. Correctness paramount. Masterpiece-grade.

Discovered: post-#875 main CI run 25822497162.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #884. Root cause was a test-authoring bug introduced in rf2-mn0qc / #875: the regression test passed bare  as a reg-event-db handler, but reg-event-db invokes handlers as  (arity-2). On the JVM,  threw ArityException, the chain's :before catch recorded :rf/interceptor-error, and path's :after fell back to the unchanged :coeffects :db (= 10) — silently as data, because the handler exception is emitted as a trace event, not via clojure.test. Splice-back logic in std_interceptors.cljc is unchanged and correct. Fix: wrap inc as (fn [slice _] (inc slice)), matching the neighbouring path-interceptor test. Full core suite 444 tests / 2369 assertions / 0 failures.

title: fix(core): late-bind-drift-test failing for schemas/* directory entries after rf2-dgug5 split
description:
The `late-bind-drift-test` in `implementation/core/test/` fails on main after #842 (rf2-dgug5 split schemas.cljc into 7 sub-namespaces).

title: refactor(causa-mcp): unify count-of-things across spec (17 tools, 6 mechanisms, 10 locks)
description:
## Goal

Three count-of-things drift findings across  need a single coordinated edit.

## Findings (from audit rf2-m9yoi)

1. **Tool count: 'eighteen' vs upstream 'seventeen'** — Causa-MCP spec asserts 'eighteen tools' 13+ times; upstream source-of-truth at `tools/causa/spec/010-MCP-Server.md:15, :127, :279` consistently says **seventeen**. The Causa-MCP bands table at 000-Vision.md:93-100 enumerates Inspection (9) + Mutation (3) + Streaming (2) + Escape hatch (1) + Meta (2) + Compatibility (1 'phantom' band with 0 tools) = 18 only via a fictional sixth band.

2. **Mechanism count: 'five' vs 'six'** — Principles.md describes **six** mechanisms (§1-§6 at lines 306, 330, 347, 365, 387, 406; line 292: 'six normative mechanisms'). DESIGN-RATIONALE.md Lock #9 title still says 'Wire-protocol budget posture (five mechanisms)' and §Summary-table row 9 (line 744) says 'five mechanisms'. spec/README.md:12 advertises 'five-mechanism wire-protocol budget posture' missing the sixth (size elision, locked by Lock #10).

3. **Lock count: 'Nine' vs 'ten'** — spec/README.md:13 says 'Nine direction-setting decisions'; DESIGN-RATIONALE.md has ten locks (line 747: 'These ten locks define...').

## Proposed fix (single coordinated edit)

- Drop the phantom 'Compatibility' band from 000-Vision.md:100; total = 17 across 5 bands.
- Search-and-replace 'eighteen' → 'seventeen' across spec/ (13+ sites in 000-Vision.md, Principles.md, DESIGN-RATIONALE.md, README.md, spec/README.md).
- Rewrite Lock #5's enumeration arithmetic (DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:305): drop '+ 1 reserved'; result 9 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 17.
- Retitle Lock #9 (DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:530) to 'Wire-protocol budget posture (the mechanism cascade)' so future mechanisms don't churn the lock title.
- Update DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:744 §Summary-table row 9 to mention 'six mechanisms'.
- spec/README.md:12 parenthetical: add 'size elision (`:rf.size/large-elided`)' as mechanism #6.
- spec/README.md:13: 'Nine' → 'Ten'.
- Add a 'Canonical counts' subsection to spec/README.md naming: 17 tools, 5 bands, 6 mechanisms, 10 locks. Other files cite this subsection rather than restating.

Risk: zero — pure documentation. Total edit ~35-45 LoC.

## Why coordinated, not three separate beads

All three findings share a structural cause: the count is asserted in many places with no canonical home. A single PR fixes the staleness AND lands the canonical-counts subsection that prevents recurrence.

## Linked

- Findings: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-causa-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §P0 #1 / P0 #2 / P0 #3 / Q1 / Q6

title: fix(core): swap-fn side-effects race in subs/invalidate-sub-on-replace! and dispose-entry-now!
description:
Audit finding SU2 / SU6 from rf2-spr6q — CORRECTNESS BUG.

subs.cljc:619-644 (invalidate-sub-on-replace!) and subs.cljc:529-547 (dispose-entry-now!) both perform side-effecting (swap! conj) and (reset! ...) INSIDE the swap-fn body.

Per clojure.core/swap! contract, the swap-fn can re-run on CAS contention. Under JVM concurrency:
- The (swap! evictions conj r) in invalidate-sub-on-replace! can double-conj.
- The (reset! reaction-to-dispose ...) in dispose-entry-now! can fire twice.

Result: double-dispose of an already-disposed reaction, potential NPE.

Repro: drive 'a sub re-registers while N threads are simultaneously walking the cache'. JVM-only — CLJS is single-threaded so the race is invisible there.

Proposed fix shape — rewrite each as a pure swap-fn that returns:
  {:new-cache <m>
   :evicted-reactions [...]
   :evicted-timers [...]}

Then act on the returned value OUTSIDE the swap.

Example for dispose-entry-now!:

  (let [{:keys [m reaction]} (swap-vals! cache (fn [m] (if eligible? [...] [m nil])))]
    (when reaction (try (interop/dispose! reaction) (catch ...))))

Pair with a JVM concurrency test (using future + concurrent-atom) that drives contention through these swap sites. Without the test these correctness fixes would be invisibly re-broken on a future refactor.

Time-box: ~ 90 min for the fix + ~ 60 min for the test. Risk: medium (correctness; must verify the fix doesn't subtly change observable semantics on the happy path).

Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc + a new implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_cache_concurrency_test.clj.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #829. Three swap-fn side-effects sites in subs.cljc rewritten to use swap-vals! with side-effects derived from the [old new] diff post-CAS. JVM-only regression test added in sub_cache_concurrency_test.clj covering all three sites under N-thread contention. Core test suite: 440 tests / 2306 assertions, 0/0. CLJS suite: 1778 tests / 4937 assertions, 0/0.

title: refactor(core): factor trace/emit! and trace/emit-error! shared body into build-event + deliver!
description:

title: refactor(core): consolidate 5 *current-...* dynamic Vars into a single *handler-scope* record
description:
Audit finding A2 / RT2 from rf2-spr6q — and the 'under-appreciated win' for this audit.

trace.cljc:101-316 accumulates five dynamic Vars: *current-trigger-handler*, *current-call-site*, *current-dispatch-id*, *current-sensitive?*, *current-no-emit?*. Each is bound at every handler-scope site:

  1. router.cljc:466-471 — handler chain
  2. fx.cljc:320-325 — fx handler scope
  3. cofx.cljc:210-217 — cofx injector scope
  4. subs.cljc:252-257 — sub recompute scope
  5. views.cljs:232-235 — view render scope

Every site repeats: compute-from-meta (trigger-handler-from-meta + sensitive?-from-meta + no-emit?-from-meta) + emit a 3-key binding form.

The Vars are conceptually one bundle — 'what's the in-scope handler's reading?' — fragmented into 5 Vars + 5 compute helpers + 5 binding-form copies (~ 240 lines of comment-text not behaviour across the trace file alone).

Proposed:
1. HandlerScope record {:trigger-handler :call-site :dispatch-id :sensitive? :no-emit?} bound to ONE Var *handler-scope*.
2. (trace/with-handler-scope kind id meta & body) macro that wraps the binding.
3. Each site collapses from 6 lines to 1 line: (with-handler-scope :event event-id handler-meta (run-chain)).
4. emit! / emit-error! read (.-trigger-handler scope), (.-sensitive? scope) etc.

Benefits:
- ~ -80 LoC across binding sites.
- One binding-frame allocation per scope instead of 5 (perf — pushThreadBindings is non-trivial).
- Future 6th handler-scope concern lands in one record-field + one helper + one emit hoist (today: 5 sites + 1 Var + 1 helper + 5 hoists).
- Test ergonomics: one Var to mock per scope instead of 5.

Time-box: ~ 3 hr. Risk: medium — five binding-sites; correctness depends on emit! reading the bundle correctly. The change is mechanical once the record + macro shape is settled.

Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc, router.cljc, fx.cljc, cofx.cljc, subs.cljc, views.cljs.

THIS IS THE UNDER-APPRECIATED WIN — pairs with rf2-spr6q's report-back.
close_reason: Closed
