title: refactor(story): extract shared review-dialog ns from recorder + save-variant
description:
## Goal

Extract a shared `re-frame.story.review-dialog` ns owning the pure data + state machine for the "review-then-commit modal" pattern. Two save-as flows ship today with parallel duplication:

- recorder's "save recording as variant" (`recorder.cljs` + `recorder.cljc`)
- save-current-canvas-state's "save as variant" (`save_variant.cljs` + `save_variant.cljc`)

The second factored the pure dialog state machine into `.cljc` (open / close / set-draft-id / default-variant-id / initial-dialog-state). The first did NOT — its `ui-dialog` ratom, `default-variant-id`, `set-draft-id!`, `open-dialog!`, `close-dialog!`, `copy-to-clipboard!` all live in CLJS-only code.

## What to extract

A `re-frame.story.review-dialog` ns with:

- Pure data + transitions: `open` / `close` / `set-draft-id` / `initial-dialog-state` / `default-variant-id-with-prefix [source-id now-ms prefix]` / `parse-variant-id-string [s]`.
- A `.cljs` modal renderer parameterised by `{:title :hint :snippet-fn :draft-id :source-id :on-copy :on-discard :on-close}`.
- A shared `copy-to-clipboard!` helper.

Both flows consume the shared surface; ~120 LoC of CLJS duplication drops to ~30 LoC of glue + JVM-testable dialog transitions for the recorder.

## Future use

The pattern is reusable: save-as-workspace, save-as-snapshot, save-as-mode, save-as-anything. Each future flow becomes a ~20-line addition rather than a 100-line copy.

## Risk

Medium — the recorder's dialog has a richer state (snippet generation, picker overlay) than save-variant's. Take care to keep the rich state in the recorder while sharing the dialog core.

## Audit reference

Audit bead: rf2-dd5ze. Findings: Executive P0 #3, §Strongest design-taste opinion, also covers RU2/RU3/RU4.
close_reason: PR #830 opened. Extracted shared re-frame.story.review-dialog ns owning pure state machine + parse + derive + CLJS renderer. Both save-as flows migrated; -198 LoC across existing files; new JVM-testable seam. All gates pass.

title: refactor(core): unify db/fx/ctx handler->interceptor wrappers in events.cljc
description:
Audit finding P0 #3 from rf2-spr6q.

events.cljc:96-170 defines three private fns — db-handler->interceptor, fx-handler->interceptor, ctx-handler->interceptor — each ~15-30 LoC carrying the same :before shape: check :rf/skip-handler?, read coeffects, invoke handler, project return into effects. The three differ only in (a) which coeffect they pull, (b) which assoc shape they emit, (c) whether they police the closed-shape (only fx does).

The same triple appears in reg-event-db / reg-event-fx / reg-event-ctx at events.cljc:227-334 with three near-identical bodies.

Proposed: one wrap-event-handler primitive parameterised by {:event/kind :db|:fx|:ctx :read-coeffects fn :commit-effects fn :police? bool} plus a single register-event! that fans out by kind.

Bundle: also fix events.cljc:174-194 normalise-args 4-arity bug — the case-block goes 1/2/3 but the docstring promises (id metadata interceptors handler) as a 4-arity (EV2 in the findings doc).

Net: ~ -50 LoC + bug fix.

Time-box: ~ 2 hr. Risk: low. Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc.
close_reason: Landed via PR #855. Unified db/fx/ctx handler->interceptor wrappers in events.cljc into single wrap-event-handler primitive driven by kind-spec dispatch table; unified the three reg-event-* registration bodies into register-event! helper. Net LoC: +9 (135 insertions, 126 deletions) - slight net growth from comprehensive docstrings on the new dispatch table; behavioural code shrunk substantially. Tests: 1795/4975 CLJS assertions + 440/2309 core CLJ assertions all pass. Also cleaned up the misleading normalise-args error message (audit's EV2 claim of a missing 4-arity branch was a misread of the variadic shape - count is the tail's count, not including id).

title: refactor(core): defreg-macro helper for the 14 reg-* defmacros in core.cljc
description:
Audit finding P0 #2 from rf2-spr6q.

core.cljc:130-225 ships seven structurally identical defmacros (reg-event-db / reg-event-fx / reg-event-ctx / reg-sub / reg-fx / reg-cofx / reg-frame) and another four under flows/schemas/SSR (reg-flow, reg-app-schema, reg-app-schemas, reg-error-projector, reg-head). Each is a six-line wrapper:

  (defmacro reg-X [id & args]
    (with-coords-form (meta &form) *file* (symbol (str (ns-name *ns*)))
                      `(<delegate-ns>/<fn-name> ~id ~@args)))

The (symbol (str (ns-name *ns*))) literal repeats 18× across the file.

Proposed: a private 'defreg-macro' helper macro that takes (macro-name, delegate-sym, arglists, & docstring) and emits the canonical defmacro form. Each reg-* macro reduces to a 1-line declaration.

Net: ~ -100 LoC; adding a new artefact's reg-* macro becomes a one-line declaration.

Time-box: ~ 90 min. Risk: low — pure compile-time scaffolding. Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc.

Pairs with rf2-spr6q-#1 (the artefact-wrapper factory); shipping both together yields a clean core.cljc.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #836 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/836). defreg-macro helper now drives 13 reg-* defmacros (reg-machine stays bespoke). Net LoC: +6 (file 1162 -> 1168), but each reg-* declaration is now a one-line declarative form. Tests: 1778 CLJS / 4937 assertions + 440 JVM / 2306 assertions all pass. Zero behaviour change. (2026-05-14 02:35 AUSEST)

title: refactor(story): split test_mode.cljc (974 LoC) along its own banner lines
description:
## Goal

Split `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode.cljc` (974 LoC) into a sub-package mirroring the rf2-5hnn split pattern in machines/. The file is the single biggest readability tax in tools/story/ — 4× larger than the next-largest UI surface (recorder.cljs at 718). Breaches the just-shipped leaf-size ceiling (rf2-zkca8 — ≤250L / ≤16KB) by 4×.

## Six concerns the file's own docstring enumerates

1. Pure data helpers (`variant-has-tests?`, `aggregate-summary`, `assertion-row`, `play-step-statuses`, `epoch-id-slice`, `format-elapsed-ms`, `format-timestamp-ms`) — ~250 LoC, JVM-testable.
2. CLJS styles map — ~180 LoC.
3. CLJS local state (`results-atom`, `begin-run!`, `store-result!`, `select-step!`, `toggle-expanded!`, `run-variant-pane!`) — ~100 LoC.
4. Section renderers (`header`, `summary-section`, `scrubber-section`, `rows-section`, `empty-state`) — ~400 LoC.
5. Top-level component (`test-view`) — ~40 LoC.

## Recommended split

- `test_mode/pure.cljc` — concerns 1 (pure helpers).
- `test_mode/state.cljs` — concerns 3 (results-atom + mutators).
- `test_mode/view.cljs` — concerns 2 + 4 + 5 (styles + renderers + top-level).

Or, less aggressively, keep `test_mode.cljc` for the pure helpers and extract a sibling `test_mode/view.cljs` for the CLJS-only surface.

## Risk

Low — pure rearrange + `:require`. The downstream caller (shell.cljs:58) imports `[re-frame.story.ui.test-mode :as test-mode]` and calls `test-mode/test-view`. Either keep that fully-qualified path resolvable via a re-export, or update the one call site.

## Audit reference

Audit bead: rf2-dd5ze. Findings: Executive P0 #2.
close_reason: Split delivered in PR #833: pure.cljc / state.cljs / view.cljs under tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/. Mechanical split along banner lines per audit rf2-dd5ze P0 #2. Tests: tools/story 324/0/0, implementation cljs 1778/0/0.

title: refactor(core): collapse 7 core_*.cljc artefact-wrappers into a factory + per-artefact tables
description:
Audit finding P0 #1 from rf2-spr6q (see ai/findings/refactor-audit-core-2026-05-14.md).

The seven core_*.cljc wrappers (flows, routing, schemas, machines, ssr, epoch, http) are structurally identical: each defn does (if-let [f (late-bind/get-fn :hook/key)] (f args) (throw ex-info :rf.error/X-artefact-missing {...})). Across the seven files there are 26 artefact-missing ex-info literals each spelling the same skeleton:

- core_epoch.cljc:94
- core_flows.cljc:23
- core_http.cljc:24
- core_machines.cljc:23
- core_routing.cljc:24
- core_schemas.cljc:87
- core_ssr.cljc:31 + 19 siblings

The :reason strings are stencils with one substitution (the rf/symbol + the artefact coordinates).

Proposed:
1. Add late-bind/require-fn! helper that takes hook-key + 'rf/name symbol + artefact-coords, returns the fn or throws the structured error.
2. Add a small factory (e.g. re-frame.core-artefact/defwrapper) that takes a declarative table of (name :hook/key arglists absent-arm-policy).
3. Each core_X.cljc becomes a ~20-line declarative table + (run-factory!) invocation.

The variant the factory must support is the 'absent-artefact returns nil / [] / false' branch — epoch returns []/false for introspection arms; http/ssr/machines throw. The factory takes the absent-arm as data per row.

Net: ~ -450 LoC for zero behaviour change; produced error events stay byte-identical; adding a new artefact becomes a table-row edit.

Time-box: ~ 4 hr. Risk: Low. Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_*.cljc, implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind.cljc.

Hot-zone: NO — these files are isolated, no other agents likely touching them concurrently.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #850 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/850). Factory + per-artefact tables — 26 ex-info literals collapse to ONE template in late-bind/require-fn!. Pre-alpha: zero behaviour change. Tests: 1795 CLJS / 4975 assertions + 440 JVM / 2309 assertions + all 7 per-artefact suites pass. Net +94 LoC absolute (wrappers -84, central helpers +178); adding a new wrapper is now a one-row addition. (2026-05-14)

title: refactor(story): close snapshot-identity drift — add variant :decorators + view schema-digest to hash
description:
## Goal

Close the P0 spec-vs-impl drift surfaced by audit rf2-dd5ze.

Per spec/007-Stories.md:424-429 the snapshot-identity hash MUST include:
- the resolved (post-extends-merge) args, **decorators**, and tags
- the parent story's component id + decorators
- the *registered* schema digest of the view (per spec/011 §rf/schema-digest)

Impl in `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/identity.cljc:147-151` selects only `[:events :play :loaders :loaders-complete-when :tags :args->events :platforms :substrates]` from the variant body — **the variant's :decorators slot is missing**. And the view's schema-digest is **not consulted at all** — no late-bind lookup anywhere in the ns.

## Consequences

- watch-mode auto-rerun (shell.cljs:146-160) misses decorator-only edits.
- visual-regression keys against `[variant-id content-hash]` can return stale baselines after a view-schema change.

## Scope

1. Extend `variant-body-slice` to include `:decorators`.
2. Add a view-schema-digest lookup via the late-bind hook into `snapshot-tuple`. The framework already publishes `:rf.ssr/check-schema-digest` (rf2-69ad2 just landed); use the same registered slot.
3. Add JVM tests:
   - changing a variant-level decorator changes the content-hash.
   - changing the view's schema changes the content-hash.

## Out of scope

The sha-256 upgrade (currently 32-bit `hash`) — flagged as P3 in the audit.

## Audit reference

Audit bead: rf2-dd5ze. Findings: Executive P0 #1, Spec-vs-impl S1+S2, Test coverage TE2.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #825. Added :decorators to variant-body-slice and :view-schema-digest slot (via :schemas/app-schemas-digest late-bind hook) to snapshot-tuple. Two tests added: decorator-only edit perturbs hash, schema-digest change perturbs hash. tools/story full suite 326/0/0.

title: decision(schemas): resolve [:rf/elision] ownership — schemas-side vs elision-artefact double-writes
description:
Per Spec-Schemas §:rf/elision-registry line 1623-1665, the [:rf/elision] slot is runtime-owned, app-db-resident, schema-fed. The current implementation has **two write surfaces** that overlap:

1. re-frame.schemas ships populate-elision-declarations (schemas.cljc:862-903) and populate-sensitive-declarations (schemas.cljc:794-833) that directly write [:rf/elision :declarations] / [:rf/elision :sensitive-declarations].
2. re-frame.elision (core) ships populate-elision-from-schemas! (elision.cljc:329-348) that inlines a parallel walker (schema-large?) and writes the same slot.

re-frame.elision/populate-elision-from-schemas! does NOT call the schemas-side populate-* fns. They are reachable only via the late-bind hooks :schemas/populate-elision-declarations / :schemas/populate-sensitive-declarations, which have **no consumer** (per rf2-5q7r0).

This is the architectural confusion behind the seven dead hooks (rf2-5q7r0). Resolving the ownership:

Option A: schemas owns the walker; elision owns the registry. Delete the schemas-side populate-* fns. Elision consumes :schemas/extract-large-paths-from-schema and writes [:rf/elision] itself.

Option B: schemas owns BOTH walker and registry write. elision.cljc/populate-elision-from-schemas! delegates entirely to :schemas/populate-elision-declarations.

Option A is cleaner — re-frame.elision is the elision authority; schemas provides the data extraction. ~150 LoC deletable from schemas.

Decision unblocks rf2-5q7r0.

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (A3 / P0#2 details).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.
notes:
DECISION (Mike, 2026-05-14 ~10:00 AUSEST): **Option A** — schemas owns the walker; elision owns the registry.

Action:
- Delete schemas-side `populate-elision-declarations` (schemas.cljc:862-903) and `populate-sensitive-declarations` (schemas.cljc:794-833) — ~150 LoC out of schemas.
- elision/populate-elision-from-schemas! consumes `:schemas/extract-large-paths-from-schema` (and the sensitive analogue) and writes `[:rf/elision]` itself.
- elision's shallow `schema-large?` walker is removed; the deep walker from schemas wins. **Closes the correctness gap** rf2-whepe round-2 audit surfaced — `[:map [:logs {:large? true} [:vector :string]]]` will now get `:logs` caught by both dev-time redaction and boot-time elision-population.

Unblocks rf2-5q7r0 (delete 7 dead late-bind hooks).
close_reason: DECIDED Option A — schemas walker, elision registry. See notes. Unblocks rf2-5q7r0.

title: refactor(ssr): default-html-shell <title> duplicates head-fragment <title>
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §R10 / TC7.

`re-frame.ssr.ring/default-html-shell` (ssr-ring.clj:235-268) emits a hardcoded `<title>` tag from the `:title` opt (default "re-frame2 app"). The shell ALSO injects the head-fragment that `active-head` produced into `<head>` via the `(or head "")` slot.

`re-frame.ssr.head/head-model->html` emits a `<title>` tag from the model's `:title`. `active-head` resolves the active route's `:head` registration → model → HTML, and the Ring adapter at `resolve-head-html` (ssr-ring.clj:326-338) renders it.

Net: under the default shell, an app whose route declares `:head /...` gets **TWO** `<title>` tags in the document — the shell's hard-coded one and the head-fragment's one. HTML5 says the second wins, but the document is malformed (only one `<title>` per document).

## Fix

The shell should defer to the head fragment for `<title>`. Options:

A. **Suppress shell title when head-fragment carries title.** The shell calls `(when-not (str/includes? head "<title") (str "<title>" title "</title>"))`.

B. **Always defer to head fragment.** Remove the shell's `<title>` entirely; the head fragment is responsible. `default-head` already emits a sensible title from frame meta.

C. **Route the shell title through the head fragment.** The shell builds its own head-model `(merge default-head {:title title})` then renders.

Recommendation: **B** — simplest; the head/meta contract (Spec 011 §Head/meta) is the canonical source of `<title>`. The shell becomes a structural skeleton, not a competing title source.

## Test

```clojure
(deftest no-duplicate-title-tags
  (rf/reg-head :head/main (fn [_ _] {:title "From head fragment"}))
  (rf/reg-route :route/x {:head :head/main})
  (rf/reg-event-db :_/init (fn [db _] (assoc db :rf/route {:id :route/x})))
  (let [handler (ssr-ring/ssr-handler
                  {:on-create [:_/init]
                   :root-view [:div]})
        body    (:body (handler {:uri "/" :request-method :get}))
        title-count (count (re-seq #"<title" body))]
    (is (= 1 title-count)
        "exactly one <title> tag; head fragment is the canonical source")))
```

Will FAIL today.

## Risk

Low — shell-default behaviour change. Apps with custom `:html-shell` are unaffected. Apps using the bundled shell get correct HTML.
close_reason: Closed

title: refactor(ssr): :rf/response accumulator leaks into hydration payload (privacy / perf)
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §Q13 / R11 / A3 / S5 / P1.

The HTTP response accumulator lives at `[:rf/response]` in app-db (Spec 011 §HTTP response contract, line 343-353). The hydration payload at `ssr-ring/build-payload` ships the WHOLE app-db by default (line 280-288). Without explicit `:payload-keys` filtering, **the response accumulator (including server-only `:headers` / `:cookies` / `:redirect`) rides the hydration wire to the client.**

Spec 011 §Payload scope (line 60-80) does NOT mention `:rf/response` as a 'carry' key but doesn't explicitly say it must be stripped either — the spec is silent on the leak. The request-slot side-channel is explicitly excluded from app-db FOR THIS REASON (line 332-341: 'app-db is the hydration payload's source ... request maps routinely carry Host, Cookie, Authorization ... whose leakage to the client is a security incident'). The response is similarly server-only and similarly carrier of host secrets (Set-Cookie auth tokens, internal headers).

## Two-fold cost today

1. **Privacy / contract.** A default-config SSR request ships server-only response data to the client.
2. **Performance.** `swap-response!` allocates the **full app-db** per fx call (`(adapter/read-container container) → assoc → (replace-container! container ...)`). For a 7-fx response shape (typical login flow: set-status + set-cookie + delete-cookie + 3 headers + redirect), that's 7 full app-db replacements per request.

## Option A — move `:rf/response` to side-channel atom (preferred, masterpiece grade)

Add a `response-slots` defonce atom keyed by frame-id, mirroring `request-slots`. The `:rf.server/*` fxs swap that atom; `get-response` reads it; `on-frame-destroyed!` clears it.

Pros:
- Privacy boundary lives at the storage layer (cannot be misconfigured).
- Per-fx write is O(1) — small map swap, not full-app-db replacement.
- Spec 011 §Request storage substrate's own rationale applies symmetrically.
- The host adapter's API stays the same (`ssr/get-response` is the read).

Cons:
- Spec 011 §HTTP response contract update required. Migration: the `[:rf/response]` app-db path was conventionally accessible to user code (debugging? unlikely); the side-channel is host-adapter-only.

## Option B — explicit dissoc in `build-payload` (minimal)

`ssr-ring/build-payload` does `(-> app-db (dissoc :rf/response :rf/hydration))` before the slice. The cofx-perf cost (7 full-db swaps) is NOT addressed.

## Recommendation

Option A. The change is small (~50 LoC across response.cljc + frame teardown + a hook); the contract becomes self-enforcing rather than caller-vigilant.

## Acceptance

- Default payload does NOT contain `:rf/response` (test: assert payload's app-db has no `:rf/response` key).
- Per-fx response writes don't reallocate the full app-db.
- `get-response` returns the same shape it does today.
- Spec 011 §HTTP response contract is updated to reflect side-channel storage.
notes:
RESCUE NOTES (2026-05-14 ~04:40 AUSEST): A prior agent (a36b8203785ca5ff0) completed implementation + tests but lost work when their worktree was reaped by the hygiene sweep mid-task (they hadn't committed yet — pre-alpha audit/refactor agents often don't commit until the end). The design is VALIDATED; a fresh dispatch can re-apply the 10-step diff per audit doc §Q13 / R11 / A3 at ai/findings/refactor-audit-ssr-2026-05-14.md.

Implementation summary (re-apply this):

1. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc` — rewrite: drop response-path; introduce `defonce response-slots` atom keyed by frame-id (mirror request-slots). Add `clear-response!`. `swap-response!` becomes a swap on response-slots — O(small-map), no app-db ping-pong.

2. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/request.cljc` — `on-frame-destroyed!` adds `(response/clear-response! frame-id)`.

3. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc` (façade) — replace response-path re-export with ^:private response-slots re-export (tests reach via resolve).

4. `spec/011-SSR.md` — new §Response storage substrate under §HTTP response contract, mirror of §Request. Per-request frame teardown table: add `response-slots` allocation row. §Resolved decisions: rf2-jbcmt entry.

5. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` — `:ssr/on-frame-destroyed` description extended to mention response-slots.

6. 7 conformance fixtures (spec/conformance/fixtures/ssr-set-status.edn, ssr-cookie, ssr-redirect, ssr-error-known-mapping, ssr-error-sanitisation, cross-spec-route-not-found-ssr-status, cross-spec-ssr-machine-error) — drop `:rf/response` from `:final-app-db`.

7. 6 test files reset response-slots between fixtures via resolve pattern (mirror pending-error-traces): ssr_end_to_end_test, ssr_head_test, ssr_request_cofx_test, ssr_compatibility_checks_test, ssr_source_coord_test, ssr_teardown_load_test, ssr-ring/ring_test.

8. ssr_teardown_load_test extension: response-slots-snapshot probe + baseline/end-counts assertion across 2000 requests. Updated :load-test/server-init to fire `:rf.server/set-header`.

9. NEW test in ssr-ring/ring_test.clj: `hydration-payload-omits-rf-response-accumulator` — dispatches set-status + secret-header + leak-probe-cookie + append-header; asserts payload script (a) contains public app-db, (b) does NOT contain `:rf/response` literal, (c) does NOT contain secret values, (d) Set-Cookie + X-Secret-Header DO appear on response headers.

10. Docstring/comment refresh: ssr/emit.cljc, ssr-ring/ring.clj, ssr/deps.edn, core_ssr.cljc.

Verified test pass before worktree reaping:

- ssr-ring JVM: 12/59 (0 fail) including new privacy test

Re-applied the validated 10-step diff per rescue notes. response-path re-export removed; response-slots defonce side-channel atom keyed by frame-id introduced; on-frame-destroyed! clears it via :ssr/on-frame-destroyed hook. Spec 011 adds §Response storage substrate + teardown table row + §Resolved decisions entry. 7 conformance fixtures drop :rf/response from :final-app-db. 6 ssr/ssr-ring test files reset response-slots between fixtures. title: test(pair2-mcp): conformance test for :dropped-sensitive / :elided-large MUST-level indicator field
description:
Spec 009 §Indicator field on tool responses (line 1411) is a MUST-level row: tools that walk a tree-typed payload MUST carry an `:elided-large` count alongside `:dropped-sensitive`. After rf2-zjqh8 landed parity across all 5 emit sites, the MUST-level row is enforced by reviewers, not by tests.

## Coverage gap

No test asserts:

- (a) Every tool that walks a tree-typed payload includes BOTH `:dropped-sensitive` and `:elided-large` in its emit-path
- (b) The slot is omitted when count is zero (Conventions.md:154-155)
- (c) The slot's value matches what the walker actually dropped/elided

## Proposed test

`tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/indicator-field-test.cljc` or pair2-mcp/test addition. Per-tool, fabricate a payload with N sensitive items + M large-elided markers, dispatch via `invoke`, assert the envelope carries the right counts (or omits when zero).

## Why

The MUST-level row in Spec 009 stays MUST-level only if a test enforces it. Today an audit (rf2-7hie3) caught the parity gap that rf2-zjqh8 closed — that was reviewer-driven. The conformance test removes the dependence on reviewer vigilance.

Surface: new test file under `tools/pair2-mcp/test/` or `tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/`.

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §TE8.
close_reason: Conformance test landed via PR #866. New file  (8 deftests, 32 assertions) pins the three contract axes from audit §TE8: (a) every tree-walking tool routes through , (b) omit-when-zero semantics, (c) value passes through verbatim. Helper-source grep pin keeps the simulation byte-faithful with the CLJS implementation. Drive-by fix: corrected stale  path in  (post-rf2-vrbwx split moved emit literals to ). Follow-on bead rf2-xx42k filed for pre-existing story-mcp  tripwire (docstring references, unrelated).

title: refactor(schemas): split schemas.cljc (1471 LoC) into 7 sub-namespaces
description:
schemas.cljc carries eight independent concerns at 1471 LoC. Per the rf2-zkca8 leaf-size ceiling (≤250L / ≤16KB) the file is 6× over budget. Banner-comment-delimited sections already mark the natural split points.

Recommended sub-files (each falls under the leaf-size ceiling):

- schemas.cljc — public façade + late-bind table (~100 LoC)
- schemas/validator.cljc — pluggable validator/explainer atoms + set-schema-validator! / set-schema-explainer! / reset-schema-validator! (~165 LoC)
- schemas/storage.cljc — per-frame storage + reg-app-schema / app-schemas / app-schema-at (~210 LoC)
- schemas/walker.cljc — unified :large? / :sensitive? walker (~150 LoC, after the dedup in sibling bead)
- schemas/elision_feeder.cljc — populate-elision-declarations / populate-sensitive-declarations (~80 LoC) — OR delete if the dead-hooks bead lands as 'delete'
- schemas/validate.cljc — validate-event! / validate-cofx! / validate-app-db! / validate-sub-return! + redaction helpers (~280 LoC after run-validation factoring)
- schemas/digest.cljc — app-schemas-digest + canonicalise-schema-form + sha256 (~135 LoC)

Mirror of sibling rf2-3sbb6 (machines/lifecycle_fx.cljc split). Pure rearrange + declare; net LoC neutral.

Should land AFTER the unified-walker bead and the run-validation factoring bead — sequencing them avoids double-rework on the same surface.

title: refactor(pair2-mcp): stop hand-copying private fns in test nses (make public, require directly)
description:
Test files hand-copy private fns from `tools.cljs`. Each test ns prefixes with "Mirror of … private helpers in tools.cljs. Keep in lockstep" and re-implements ~30-50 LoC of helper code.

## Sites

- elision_test.cljs:34-46 (mirrors parse-elision-arg, elision-opts-edn)
- sensitive_filter_test.cljs:20-41 (mirrors sensitive-event?, sensitive-epoch?, strip-sensitive)
- subscribe_test.cljs:20-27, 58-65 (mirrors parse-filter-arg, subscribe-form)
- snapshot_test.cljs:19-46 (mirrors valid-slices, ->frame-keyword, parse-frames-arg, parse-include-arg)
- cursor_pagination_test.cljs (mirrors encode-cursor, decode-cursor)
- … and others

Total: ~250 LoC of duplicated helpers across the test corpus.

## Problems

- **Drift.** A bug fix in `tools.cljs` doesn't propagate to the mirror; tests test the mirror, not the source.
- **Mis-signal.** A passing test "proves" the mirror works, not production code.

## Proposed fix

Make the private fns public (`defn`, not `defn-`). Tests `require :as` them directly. Most of the helpers are pipeline functions that genuinely could be public; the privacy is reflexive, not load-bearing.

Tightly coupled to rf2-vrbwx (file split): once each fn moves to its own ns, the privacy decision is per-ns and obvious.

Surface: `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs` + every test ns under `tools/pair2-mcp/test/`.

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §TE1.
close_reason: Closed via PR #862 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/862). Eleven test nses now require fns directly from source ns (drop ~250 LoC of hand-copied mirrors). Promoted decode-all-frames from defn- to defn so nrepl_test can require it; every other lifted fn was already public post-rf2-vrbwx. Left eval-form composer mirrors alone where rf2-dpzpe's DSL keeps source counterparts inlined per-tool. Net -594 LoC; 289 tests / 686 assertions / 0 failures.

title: refactor(schemas): collapse :large? and :sensitive? walkers into one parameterised walker
description:
The :large? walker (schemas.cljc:362-574, ~125 LoC) and the :sensitive? walker (schemas.cljc:576-833, ~250 LoC) are **byte-identical** except for one predicate keyword. Every line of the sensitive-walker block is a copy-paste of the corresponding large-walker line with s/large/sensitive/g.

Structural duplicates:
- walk-map-children (:432-471) ≡ walk-sensitive-map-children (:616-638)
- walk-multi-children (:473-497) ≡ walk-sensitive-multi-children (:640-657)
- walk-positional-children (:499-507) ≡ walk-sensitive-positional-children (:659-661)
- walk-schema (:520-559) ≡ walk-sensitive-schema (:663-693)

Recommend: parameterise on the predicate key + declaration-builder:

`(walk-schema-for-predicate predicate-key schema base-path acc)`

Each of the two existing extract-*-paths-from-schema fns becomes a one-line closure.

Net deletion: ~150 LoC. Strategic win: future per-slot annotations (Spec-Schemas §:rf/app-schema-meta reserves additional slots) become one-line registrations instead of 250-LoC PRs.

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (P0 #3 + under-appreciated-win section).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.
close_reason: PR #824 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/824. Collapsed :large? and :sensitive? walkers (~472 LoC) into one parameterised walk-flagged-schema (~239 LoC, including all docstrings + module-level comment). Net -224 LoC file-wide. All 1778 CLJS tests + 116 JVM schemas tests pass. Public surface (extract-*-paths-from-schema, schema-has-sensitive?, frame-/populate- pairs, late-bind hooks) preserved; only the unused multi-arity walk-schema / walk-sensitive-schema entry points dropped (pre-alpha — no back-compat).

title: refactor(schemas): delete seven dead late-bind hooks (or wire elision to consume them)
description:
Seven late-bind hooks are published by schemas.cljc:1423-1443 but have **zero consumers** in the implementation tree:

- :schemas/extract-large-paths-from-schema
- :schemas/frame-elision-declarations
- :schemas/populate-elision-declarations
- :schemas/extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema
- :schemas/schema-has-sensitive?
- :schemas/frame-sensitive-declarations
- :schemas/populate-sensitive-declarations

`grep -rn "late-bind/get-fn :schemas/extract-large-paths-from-schema" implementation` returns zero hits outside directory.cljc (which only catalogues them). re-frame.core/elision.cljc:331-348 has its own walker (`schema-large?`) — completely parallel to the schemas-side walker.

Two paths:
(a) Delete the dead hooks and the schemas-side populate-* fns (~150-200 LoC). Walker fns are kept and reachable via direct require.
(b) Wire elision.cljc/populate-elision-from-schemas! to consume :schemas/populate-elision-declarations. Single walker, single writer. Schema owns the data-walk; elision owns the elision-slot write.

Option (b) is the cleaner architectural answer — see also rf2-x8x4p audit's A3 finding on "[:rf/elision]" ownership confusion. Architectural decision required before refactor.

title: refactor(pair2-mcp): name the wire-pipeline as a parameterised fn
description:
Today the same conceptual wire-pipeline runs three different ways:

- `snapshot-tool` (5-step: sensitive-strip → path-slice → diff-encode → dedup → summary → indicator-count → cap)
- `trace-window-tool` / `watch-epochs-tool` (3-step: sensitive-strip → diff-encode → dedup → indicator-count → cap)
- `get-path-tool` (minimal: server-side elide → indicator-count → cap)
- `subscribe-tool` per-tick (sensitive-strip → dedup → indicator-count → progress-emit)

None of these has a *name*. Ordering rules (dedup-BEFORE-summary, summary-BEFORE-cap, elision-count-AFTER-dedup-BEFORE-summary) are absorbed into the let-bindings of three tool bodies — three local-obvious copies of the same invariant.

## Proposed shape

```clojure
(defn run-wire-pipeline
  "Single named pipeline. Each tool calls one fn with its specific
   payload kind. Returns the value + indicator counts so the tool
   wraps the envelope."
  [payload {:keys [tool kind incl? mode dedup? elision? path slice-mode slice-modes]}]
  ...)
```

Kinds: `:snapshot-map`, `:epoch-vector`, `:scalar-value`, `:event-batch`. Returns `{:value v :indicators {:dropped N :elided N :path-status ...}}`.

## Why

- Encodes ordering invariant once,
- Reader verifies "dedup before summary?" in one place (today it's in `snapshot-tool`'s let-binding at lines 1654-1665),
- Per-tool envelope assembly becomes a 5-line tail rather than 50-line orchestration,
- Pairs naturally with rf2-7hie3's TE7 `invoke_test.cljs` recommendation.

This is the audit's "strongest design-taste opinion / under-appreciated win". See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §Strongest design-taste opinion / T6 / A2.

Surface: `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs` only.

Tightly coupled to rf2-vrbwx (file split): the pipeline lives in the new `wire_pipeline.cljs` ns.
close_reason: Refactor complete. run-wire-pipeline lives in tools/wire_pipeline.cljs, dispatched on :kind for the four tool bodies (snapshot/trace-window/watch-epochs/get-path). Ordering invariant encoded once. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/843. 270 tests / 660 assertions pass.

title: refactor(ssr): root-view fn invoked twice per request (render-body + render-hash-for)
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §P0 #3 / R2 / P4.

`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj`:

```clojure
(defn- render-body [frame-id root-view emit-hash?]
  (rf/with-frame frame-id
    (let [hiccup (cond
                   (vector? root-view) root-view
                   (fn?     root-view) (root-view)   ; <-- first call
                   ...)]
      (ssr/render-to-string hiccup ...))))

(defn- render-hash-for [frame-id root-view]
  (rf/with-frame frame-id
    (let [hiccup (if (fn? root-view) (root-view) root-view)]   ; <-- second call
      (ssr/render-tree-hash hiccup))))
```

For a **fn-form** root-view, the fn is invoked **twice per request** — once for the wire HTML and `data-rf-render-hash` attribute, once for the payload's `:rf/render-hash`.

## Two consequences

1. **2× cost.** The fn may run reagent/hooks setup logic, allocate hiccup, or read subs — paid twice.
2. **Correctness gap.** If the two `(root-view)` invocations return slightly different trees (unsorted map iteration, gensym'd keys, time-of-day props), the two hashes disagree on the wire — and `verify-hydration!` will fire `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` on a perfectly successful hydration. This silently breaks every hydration where root-view is non-idempotent.

## Fix

Compute hiccup once; pass it down.

```clojure
(defn- resolve-root [root-view]
  (cond
    (vector? root-view) root-view
    (fn?     root-view) (root-view)
    :else
    (throw (ex-info ":rf.error/invalid-root-view" {:received root-view}))))

;; In ring-handler:
(let [hiccup     (rf/with-frame frame-id (resolve-root root-view))
      body-html  (rf/with-frame frame-id (ssr/render-to-string hiccup {:emit-hash? emit-hash?}))
      hash-str   (ssr/render-tree-hash hiccup)
      ...])
```

## Test

```clojure
(deftest fn-form-root-view-invoked-once-per-request
  (let [calls (atom 0)
        view  (fn [] (swap! calls inc) [:div "once"])
        handler (ssr-ring/ssr-handler {:on-create [:_/init] :root-view view})]
    (rf/reg-event-fx :_/init (fn [_ _] {}))
    (handler {:uri "/" :request-method :get})
    (is (= 1 @calls))))
```

Will FAIL today.

## Risk

Low — adds a helper, removes duplication. Vector-form root-view path unchanged.
close_reason: fixed in PR #864 — root-view resolved exactly once per request; regression tests pin invocation count and wire==payload hash equality even for non-idempotent fn-form root-views

title: refactor(schemas): implement missing fx-args validation step (Spec 010 step 5)
description:

title: refactor(ssr): Ring adapter doesn't call set-request! — :rf.server/request cofx is broken
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §R13 / A4 / TC1.

Spec 011 §Server-only `reg-cofx` for request context (line 332-341) commits to:
> The substrate MUST NOT use a single dynamic Var / thread-local / module-level binding that could bleed across frames sharing a thread. Frame-id keying is the canonical implementation.

Spec also commits the **cofx reads from the per-frame slot via `set-request!` / `get-request`**.

`re-frame.ssr/cofx :rf.server/request` (ssr.cljc:1325-1349) reads from `request-slots` (the per-frame atom).

`re-frame.ssr.ring/ssr-handler` (ssr-ring.clj:444-510) **binds a dynamic Var `*current-request*`** for the request duration BUT NEVER calls `ssr/set-request!`.

Net effect: a handler that does `(inject-cofx :rf.server/request)` under the bundled Ring adapter gets **nil**, not the request map. The cofx is documented as the canonical read path; it's wired through to a slot the bundled adapter never populates.

## Why this slipped through

- The cofx tests (`ssr_request_cofx_test.clj`) call `ssr/set-request!` directly — they never drive the cofx through the Ring adapter.
- The Ring tests (`ssr/ring_test.clj`) test `*current-request*` directly via positional read — they never inject the cofx.
- No test crosses the boundary.

## Fix

In `ring-handler` after `make-frame` returns a frame-id:

```clojure
:else
(do
  (ssr/set-request! frame-id request)   ; <-- ADD
  (try
    (let [response (ssr/get-response frame-id)
          ...]
      ...)
    (catch ...)
    (finally
      (destroy-frame-quietly! frame-id))))  ; on-frame-destroyed! clears the slot
```

Then DROP the `*current-request*` dynamic Var (ssr-ring.clj:95-101) — it's a second read path for the same data, and Spec 011 §Request storage substrate explicitly forbids the dynamic-Var pattern.

## Test

```clojure
(deftest ring-adapter-surfaces-request-via-cofx
  (rf/reg-event-fx :test/capture-req
    [(rf/inject-cofx :rf.server/request)]
    (fn [{:keys [rf.server/request]} _]
      (reset! captured request) {}))
  (let [captured (atom :unset)
        handler  (ssr-ring/ssr-handler
                   {:on-create [:test/capture-req]
                    :root-view [:div]})
        request  {:uri "/articles/42" :request-method :get}]
    (handler request)
    (is (= request @captured)
        "the cofx surfaced the Ring request under the per-frame slot")))
```

Will FAIL today.

## Risk

Low — three lines of additive code in the Ring adapter; drop the dynamic Var (3 LoC + binding sites). Tests pin the new behaviour.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #839 — Ring adapter now calls ssr/set-request! before reg-frame's drain so the :rf.server/request cofx surfaces the active Ring request map. Dynamic *current-request* Var dropped (Spec 011 §Request storage substrate forbids it). Three boundary-crossing tests added; ssr-ring + ssr JVM suites pass.

description:
Six tools build CLJS eval forms by raw string concatenation. The longest is `trace-window` at tools.cljs:915-934 — 20 lines of un-indented CLJS source inside one `str` block. Tests parse the string back out to assert (`subscribe_test.cljs:96-98` does `read-string` on a substring).

title: refactor(pair2-mcp): with-indicators helper for :dropped-sensitive / :elided-large envelope tail
description:
The 5 emit sites for `:dropped-sensitive` / `:elided-large` are structurally identical after rf2-zjqh8. Extract a single helper.

## Sites

- trace-window: tools.cljs:981-982
- watch-epochs: tools.cljs:1074-1075
- snapshot: tools.cljs:1700-1701
- get-path: tools.cljs:1789-1790
- subscribe (final summary): tools.cljs:1983-1985
- subscribe (per-tick progress): tools.cljs:2053-2056

## Proposed helper

```clojure
(defn with-indicators
  "Splice cross-MCP indicator-field slots (Conventions §Cross-MCP
   indicator-field vocabulary, Spec 009 §Indicator field on tool
   responses — MUST-level) onto a tool's envelope map. Omit when zero
   per the MUST rule."
  [envelope {:keys [dropped elided]}]
  (cond-> envelope
    (pos? (or dropped 0)) (assoc :dropped-sensitive dropped)
    (pos? (or elided 0))  (assoc :elided-large elided)))
```

## Why

Centralises the MUST-level rule (Spec 009:1411). Today, drift across the 5 sites would silently violate the MUST. Future indicator slots (say `:dropped-redacted` per a `with-redacted` cousin) added once, not five times. Saves ~15 LoC; each tool's envelope-assembly reads as one line.

Surface: `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs` only.

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §P0 #2 / T3.
close_reason: Helper extracted into tools/wire.cljs; applied at all 5 emit sites (6 call sites incl. subscribe per-tick + final-summary). MUST-level omit-when-zero rule now lives in one place with Spec 009 / Conventions citations on the helper docstring. PR #838. Tests: 270 / 660 assertions, 0 failures.

title: refactor(ssr): :ssr opt documented but ssr-handler destructures :ssr-config
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §P0 #2 / R1 / TC8.

`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj`:

- Line 375 documents: `:ssr — per-frame :ssr config map (e.g. {:dev-error-detail? true :public-error-id :myapp/projector})`
- Line 427 destructures: `[{:keys [... ssr-config ...]}]`
- Line 453 plumbs: `(assoc :ssr ssr-config)`

A caller passing `{:ssr {...}}` per the docstring gets that opt **silently ignored** — `ssr-config` resolves to nil, the `cond->` doesn't assoc, the per-request frame has no `:ssr` metadata, and the default projector is used regardless of the caller's intent.

## Symptom

User configures `:dev-error-detail? true` in staging, deploys to prod, and the projector still falls back to default — no warning, no trace.

## Fix

Option A (preferred): destructure `{:keys [... ssr ...]}` and `(assoc :ssr ssr)`. Matches the docstring + matches `rf/make-frame`'s key.

Option B: rename the docstring to `:ssr-config` (uglier; doesn't match make-frame's key).

## Test

```clojure
(deftest ssr-handler-passes-through-ssr-config
  (testing "the :ssr opt reaches the per-request frame's :ssr metadata"
    (rf/reg-event-fx :test/capture
      (fn [{:keys [frame]} _]
        (reset! captured (:ssr (rf/frame-meta frame)))
        {}))
    (let [captured (atom :unset)
          handler  (ssr-ring/ssr-handler
                     {:on-create [:test/capture]
                      :root-view [:div]
                      :ssr       {:dev-error-detail? true}})]
      (handler {:uri "/" :request-method :get})
      (is (= {:dev-error-detail? true} @captured)))))
```

Will FAIL today.

## Risk

Trivial — one keyword rename.
notes: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/857. Destructure renamed :ssr-config → :ssr in ssr-handler (ring.clj L438+L473) to match the documented opt and rf/make-frame's frame-config key. Regression test handler-passes-through-ssr-opt-to-frame-meta in ring_test.clj pins the wiring: caller passes :ssr, on-create event reads (:ssr (rf/frame-meta frame)), supplied map round-trips. clojure -M:test from implementation/ssr-ring/ — 16 tests, 61 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors.

title: refactor(ssr): canonical-edn must prune nil per Spec 011 §Hydration-mismatch
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §Q3 / TC3 / A2.

`canonical-edn` (ssr.cljc:245-274) does NOT prune nil. Spec 011 §Hydration-mismatch detection (line 295) is explicit: 'depth-first traversal; attribute maps in sorted-key order; **nil pruned**.'

The fn falls through to `(:else (pr-str x))` which renders `nil` as `"nil"`. Two render trees `[:div {:class nil}]` and `[:div {}]` hash differently — but the spec says they're structurally equivalent.

## Symptom

Spurious `:rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch` traces whenever the server emits a nil attr value and the client emits an absent key. The shape `{:class (when condition? :selected)}` is common.

## Fix

```clojure
(defn- canonical-edn [x]
  (cond
    (nil? x) nil                                    ;; pruned at parent
    (map? x)
    (str "{"
         (clojure.string/join
           ","
           (->> x
                (remove (comp nil? val))
                (sort-by (comp str key))
                (map (fn [[k v]] (str (canonical-edn k) " " (canonical-edn v))))))
         "}")
    (vector? x)
    (str "[" (clojure.string/join " " (keep canonical-edn x)) "]")
    ;; ... same for sequential / set
    ))
```

## Test

```clojure
(deftest canonical-edn-prunes-nil
  (is (= (render-tree-hash [:div {:class nil}])
         (render-tree-hash [:div {}])))
  (is (= (render-tree-hash [:p "text" nil])
         (render-tree-hash [:p "text"]))))
```

Will FAIL today, which is the lock.

## Risk

Low — hash values change for previously-mismatching trees. The change is forward-only (no apps depend on the buggy hash). Update conformance fixtures if any pin pre-fix hash strings.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #841 — canonical-edn now prunes nil per Spec 011 §Hydration-mismatch (line 295). Pruning at three levels: nil input returns nil (sentinel), map entries with nil values removed pre-sort, vector/list/set children walked with keep instead of map. Byte-identity preserved for nil-free trees (JVM↔CLJS parity hash 9d7457ef unchanged). New ns re-frame.ssr-hash-test pins the four pruning rules + 3 end-to-end render-tree-hash equivalences. Gates: ssr clojure -M:test 76/235 0/0, core clojure -M:test 440/2309 0/0, npm test:cljs 1795/4975 0/0.

title: refactor(http): canned-stub fxs ship in CLJS production builds — gate on interop/debug-enabled? in both branches
description:
Audit finding from rf2-wui5v (refactor-audit-http-2026-05-14.md §P0 #3 / M2).

In http_managed.cljc:231-244 the :rf.http/managed-canned-success and :rf.http/managed-canned-failure fxs are registered conditionally on JVM but UNCONDITIONALLY on CLJS:

  #?(:clj  (when interop/debug-enabled?
             (fx/reg-fx :rf.http/managed-canned-success ...)
             (fx/reg-fx :rf.http/managed-canned-failure ...))
     :cljs (do
             (fx/reg-fx :rf.http/managed-canned-success ...)
             (fx/reg-fx :rf.http/managed-canned-failure ...)))

The CLJS branch has NO debug-enabled? gate. Yet the ns docstring at line 30 says 'The canned stub fxs gate on interop/debug-enabled? so they elide in production.'

This is either:
(a) A real bug — production CLJS bundles ship the canned-stub fxs, contradicting Spec 014 §Testing ('Don't ship the canned-stub fxs as production-eligible') and the docstring; OR
(b) Intentional asymmetry that needs documentation.

Verification step: run npm run test:elision (and npm run test:bundle-isolation if applicable) to confirm whether the canned-stub fxs leak into the production CLJS bundle. If they do, this is escalated to a P0 contract violation.

Recommend treat the docstring as the contract: gate both branches:
  (when interop/debug-enabled?
    (fx/reg-fx :rf.http/managed-canned-success ...)
    (fx/reg-fx :rf.http/managed-canned-failure ...))

-16 LoC, fixes the elision leak.

Source: ai/findings/refactor-audit-http-2026-05-14.md §P0 #3 / M2 + S3.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #853. CLJS branch was unconditional; collapsed reader-conditional to single (when interop/debug-enabled? ...) gate. Added two elision sentinels (rf.http/managed-canned-success, rf.http/managed-canned-failure) to lock the contract. Elision tests + http JVM tests + cljs tests all green.

title: refactor(ssr): split ssr.cljc (1380 LoC) along its banner-line concerns
description:
## Context

title: refactor(http): unify origin-event resolution into a single helper (3 call-sites, 5 reads)
description:
Audit finding from rf2-wui5v (refactor-audit-http-2026-05-14.md §P0 #2).

The shape (or (:event frame-ctx) (:rf.http/origin-event args-map) [:rf.http/managed]) appears verbatim 3 times:

- http_managed.cljc:139-141 (normalise-args)
- http_managed.cljc:193-195 (managed-handler)
- http_machine_wrapper.cljc:53-57 (origin-event-from helper)

In http_managed.cljc the SAME shape is computed in adjacent fns: managed-handler computes it (line 193), then calls normalise-args (line 202) which computes it AGAIN (line 139). The resolved value is built twice per request.

Recommend a resolve-origin-event fn in http_encoding.cljc, called once in managed-handler, with the result threaded into normalise-args via the ctx map.

title: refactor(http): collapse http_transport_cljs.cljc + http_transport_jvm.cljc onto shared http_transport.cljc (~440 LoC duplication)
description:
Audit finding from rf2-wui5v (refactor-audit-http-2026-05-14.md §P0 #1).

The two transport files (http_transport_cljs.cljc 361 LoC, http_transport_jvm.cljc 359 LoC) share ~440 LoC of structurally-identical code:

- dispatch-reply!: transport-cljs:95-108 ≡ transport-jvm:111-124
- finalise-success!: transport-cljs:110-124 ≡ transport-jvm:126-143 (CLJS uses (case (first (keys accepted))), JVM uses cond — divergent and CLJS form is fragile)
- finalise-failure!: transport-cljs:127-158 ≡ transport-jvm:146-177
- maybe-retry!: transport-cljs:160-210 ≡ transport-jvm:179-227 (differs only in backoff sleep mechanism)
- run-attempt! response-cascade (4xx/5xx/2xx/else): transport-cljs:299-357 ≡ transport-jvm:304-356
- content-type header merge (cond-> + or-default-{}): transport-cljs:244-247 ≡ transport-jvm:254-257

Concrete consequences:
- The rf2-lxd3 supersede-suppression fix landed twice
- Future bug fixes must land twice
- Silent drift over time
- Real platform divergence is ~150 LoC (cljs-fetch + classify-cljs-error + fetch-headers->map; jvm-fetch + classify-jvm-error + jvm-build-request + jvm-headers->map + check-cljs-only-keys!)

Recommend a defprotocol HttpTransport with (do-fetch [_ ctx]) + (classify-error [_ throwable]), backed by a shared http_transport.cljc core module owning run-attempt!/finalise-*/maybe-retry!/dispatch-reply!. Platform-specific extends via #?(:cljs ...) / #?(:clj ...) at the extend-protocol site.

~440 LoC saved, drift eliminated. Pre-alpha: back-compat not a concern.

Source: ai/findings/refactor-audit-http-2026-05-14.md §P0 #1 + TR1.
close_reason: PR #826 opened. Collapsed http_transport_cljs.cljc (361 LoC) + http_transport_jvm.cljc (359 LoC) onto shared re-frame.http-transport (493 LoC); net -225 LoC. JVM tests: 134/369/0/0. CLJS tests: 1778/4937/0/0. Bundle-isolation OK. Also collapsed: (a) the rf2-lxd3 supersede-suppression fix is now one block; (b) the CLJS finalise-success! :failure branch (silently broken — referenced ctx :decoded that wasn't there) routes through the JVM-style path that stamps :decoded; (c) retry scheduling unified onto interop/set-timeout! (Thread+sleep eliminated); (d) check-cljs-only-keys! now a no-op CLJS stub so the façade callsite no longer needs #?(:clj ...) wrapping. PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/826

title: refactor(flows): regression test for cycle-rollback on reg-flow replacement
description:
Per audit rf2-o3hok finding TE2. Pin the regression behaviour from rf2-7csri.

Scenario:
1. Register flow :a with non-cyclic shape — succeeds.
2. Register flow :b reading :a's output — succeeds.
3. RE-register flow :b with inputs that close a cycle with :a — should throw.
4. Assert the PRIOR :b definition is still in the registry (not silently deleted).

The bug currently silently deletes the prior :b. The test should fail today; lock the contract once rf2-7csri lands.

LoC: ~+25 (test only). Risk: trivial.

Parent: rf2-o3hok (flows refactor audit).

title: refactor(flows): resolve cycle-error data-shape drift (spec or impl)
description:
Per audit rf2-o3hok finding Exec#3 / S1. Three drifts in one ex-info contract:

1. Spec 013:149 says cycle path lives under `:tags`; impl (flows.cljc:93-94) puts it at top of ex-data.
2. Spec 013:155 example shows `{:cycle [:a :b :a]}` (path); impl returns `(vec (keys @remaining))` (unsorted set of remaining ids).
3. Spec implies a cycle PATH for tooling to render; impl returns a SET of remaining ids.

Spec 009:968 documents `:cycle` at top of ex-data (no `:tags`) — so the spec 013 `:tags` reference is at minimum a spec bug.

Decision required:
- (a) Spec edit only — drop `:tags` reference, change 013:155 example to `{:cycle [<remaining-ids>]}`; align with current impl.
- (b) Impl edit — extract actual cycle path via DFS from any remaining node; store under `:cycle` at ex-data top level (Spec 009:968 implies top-level).

I lean (b): tools like Causa will want the cycle path to render the offending chain. ~+15 LoC for DFS extraction.

Parent: rf2-o3hok (flows refactor audit).
notes: PR #858 opened. Direction: align impl to spec (option b in the bead). Extract a real cycle path via DFS over stuck nodes; throw ex-info with :cycle as a closing-repeat path. Spec 013 §Cycle detection rewritten to drop the :tags wording bug and restate the path contract. Regression test pins two- and three-flow cycle shapes. Tests: 28 / 115 / 0F0E.

title: refactor(flows): cycle-rollback on reg-flow REPLACEMENT discards prior registration
description:
Per audit rf2-o3hok finding Exec#2 (flows.cljc:144-151). When `reg-flow` re-registers an existing id and the new registration introduces a cycle, the rollback does:

```clojure
(swap! flows update frame-id dissoc flow-id)
(registrar/unregister! :flow flow-id)
```

— which DELETES both the just-written entry AND the prior definition under the same id. A hot-reload that accidentally introduces a cycle therefore vacates the previously-working flow registration.

Fix: detect-before-write. Run cycle detection on a *prospective* flow-map (current map `assoc`ed with the new entry) BEFORE mutating the atom; only commit if it passes.

LoC: +10 net (refactor). No test covers this regression today — see TE2 / sibling bead for the regression test.

Parent: rf2-o3hok (flows refactor audit).
close_reason: fix shipped in PR #837 — reg-flow now runs cycle detection on a prospective map before any mutation; cyclic replacements no longer vacate the prior registration. The sibling regression test rf2-cdh9h (PR #828) had its ^:expected-fail metadata dropped and now passes in the default sweep. clojure -M:test in implementation/flows/: 27 tests / 105 assertions / 0 failures, 0 errors.

title: refactor(flows): rewrite topo-sort as pure loop/recur (kill three local atoms)
description:
Per audit rf2-o3hok finding Q1/PF1 (flows.cljc:65-95). `topo-sort` is currently written with three local atoms (`order`, `ready`, `remaining`) in a `while` loop with `swap!`/`@deref` calls. The state never escapes the fn — it's a pure-functional Kahn fold and reads cleanly as `loop`/`recur` over immutable state (or transients).

Per-call cost today: ~6 `swap!` + 4 `@deref` per emitted node. Called on every event drain.

Win: ~30% shorter, zero atom allocation, reads as the algorithm. The cheapest 'good code looks like this' win in the artefact.

LoC: -10. Risk: low (well-covered behaviour). Audit calls this out as the under-appreciated win.

Parent: rf2-o3hok (flows refactor audit).
close_reason: PR #847 — topo-sort rewritten as pure loop/recur, three local atoms gone. Flows tests (105 assertions) and full CLJS suite (4975 assertions) green.

title: refactor(machines): unify the destroy-cascade dance across 3 call-sites into one teardown-actor helper
description:
Per findings rf2-ra1he §P0 #3 / §L2 / §L7 / §L8 / §L12: the actor-teardown app-db dance is duplicated three times across `lifecycle_fx.cljc` with subtle order-of-operations divergence.

## Duplicated sites

1. `finalize-machine` tail (lifecycle_fx.cljc:706-729) — final-state auto-destroy
2. `destroy-single-actor!` (lifecycle_fx.cljc:1285-1296) — keyword/iterated destroy
3. `destroy-machine-fx-single` (lifecycle_fx.cljc:1392-1407) — declarative-:invoke / legacy destroy

All three perform the same five-step dance:
- dissoc snapshot at `[:rf/machines actor-id]`
- release `:system-id` reverse-index entry
- update `[:rf/spawned parent-id]` (declarative case only)
- prune empty parent map
- prune empty `:rf/spawned` root

Plus the `(some (fn [[sid mid]] (when (= mid actor-id) sid)) (get db :rf/system-ids))` reverse-lookup repeats three times (lifecycle_fx.cljc:691-695, 1278-1283, 1373-1378).

## Proposed surface

```clojure
(defn teardown-actor
  "Per Spec 005 §Cancellation cascade. Apply the full teardown projection
   to db: dissoc snapshot, release system-id reverse-index, clear/prune
   :rf/spawned slot. Returns new-db + the released system-id (or nil) for
   trace emission."
  [db {:keys [actor-id parent-id invoke-id]}]
  ...)

(defn find-system-id-for-actor [db actor-id] ...)
```

Each call-site shrinks from a 15-line `cond->` chain to one helper call. The 50 LoC savings is dwarfed by the clarity / single-source-of-truth win — currently a contract change (e.g., `:rf/spawned` key rename) requires 3 grep-and-edits with high chance of inconsistency.

## Risk

Medium. `destroy-single-actor!` and `destroy-machine-fx-single` order operations subtly differently around the registrar unregister step. Need to verify ordering preserves the 'in-flight trace consumers see destroy signal while handler still resolves' invariant (lifecycle_fx.cljc:696-705). Test coverage: spawn_registry_test, invoke_all_test, final_state_cljs_test.

## Acceptance

- One `teardown-actor` helper used by 3 call-sites.
- One `find-system-id-for-actor` helper used by 3 call-sites.
- All machines tests green (`npm run test:cljs`).
- Order-sensitive trace tests still pass.

## Sequencing

Best sequenced as: this lands first, then rf2-3sbb6 (split lifecycle_fx) lands cleanly because `spawn-destroy.cljc` becomes substantially smaller. Either order works but landing the unification first gives the split cleaner boundaries.
close_reason: Landed via PR #852. Extracted teardown-actor helper into new lifecycle-fx.teardown namespace; consumed by all 4 destroy paths (finalize-machine, destroy-single-actor!, destroy-single!, destroy-invoke-all-children!). Also extracted find-system-id-for-actor. All 332 machines + 4975 full CLJS assertions green. Conformance fixture :machine/destroy-machine-clears-system-id-index preserved (pruning policy keeps :rf/machines and :rf/system-ids present-but-empty). LoC: -37 across destroy.cljc + finalize.cljc, +91 new teardown.cljc (mostly docstring). Win: single-source-of-truth on the 5-step teardown contract.

title: refactor(machines): introduce Result ADT replacing the ::action-failed sentinel across 6 call-sites
description:
Per findings rf2-ra1he §P0 #2 / §T1 / §T4 / §T8: the machine engine uses a hand-rolled sum type to distinguish success from action-failure. Each call-site spells the same disambiguation guard:

```clojure
(if (and (vector? result)
         (= ::action-failed (first result)))
  (handle-failure (second result))
  (let [[snap fx] result] (handle-success snap fx)))
```

Six call-sites carry this dance:
- `transition.cljc:830` (`apply-transition-once`)
- `transition.cljc:901` (`apply-transition-once` spawn branch)
- `transition.cljc:1060` (`machine-transition-single` post-event)
- `transition.cljc:1094` (`machine-transition-single` :always branch)
- `lifecycle_fx.cljc:848` (boot cascade)
- `lifecycle_fx.cljc:881` (post-event transition)
- `parallel.cljc:181` (`apply-initial-entry-cascade`)
- `parallel.cljc:245` (`parallel-machine-transition`)

Plus two additional micro-ADTs for the same concept:
- `run-action` returns a `{:rf.machine/action-failure ...}` map (transition.cljc:443-453)
- `materialise-data` returns `[:ok data]` / `[:fail e]` (transition.cljc:487-500)

Three sentinel shapes for one logical concept.

## Proposed surface

A tiny `re-frame.machines.result` ns (~30 LoC) with:

```clojure
(defn ok [snap fx] {::tag :ok ::snap snap ::fx fx})
(defn fail [info] {::tag :fail ::info info})
(defn ok? [r] (= ::ok (::tag r)))
(defn fail? [r] (= ::fail (::tag r)))
(defn map-ok [r f] (if (ok? r) (f (::snap r) (::fx r)) r))
```

(Or use a defrecord if perf matters; benchmark before choosing.)

Each call-site becomes `(if (result/fail? r) (handle-fail (::info r)) (let [{::keys [snap fx]} r] ...))`.

## Risk

Low. Mechanical refactor; existing test suite (machine_transition_purity_test, three_arity_guards, etc.) pins behaviour. Watch for shape pinning in tests (rf2-ra1he §TE1).

## Acceptance

- `::action-failed` keyword and `:rf.machine/action-failure` map shape vanish from src files.
- All 6+ call-sites read with `result/ok?` / `result/fail?` / `::keys` destructure.
- `npm run test:cljs` green.
- Bundle-isolation test (`npm run test:bundle-isolation`) unaffected — the result ns is internal.
close_reason: PR opened: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/846. Result ADT introduced; six sentinel call-sites collapsed; tests + docs + example updated; JVM machines 119/0, JVM core 440/0, npm test:cljs 1795/0, bundle-isolation PASS.

title: refactor(machines): split lifecycle_fx.cljc (1439 LoC) into 4 sub-files (registration / join / finalize / spawn_destroy)
description:
Per findings rf2-ra1he §P0 #1 / §L1: `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx.cljc` is 1439 LoC across four independent concerns (the file's own opening docstring lists three; the fourth is the final-state orchestrator). It is 4-5x the size of the next-largest sibling and exceeds the rf2-zkca8 leaf-size ceiling (250 LoC / 16KB).

The rf2-5hnn split worked beautifully for the other three sub-namespaces (`transition.cljc` 1102, `parallel.cljc` 278, `timer.cljc` 302) — each a crisp single-responsibility file. lifecycle_fx alone wasn't split far enough.

## Recommended split

Four flat sub-namespaces under `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.*` matching the rf2-5hnn X.Y convention:

- `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.registration` — `validate-machine!`, `validate-parallel!`, `validate-invoke-all!`, `validate-final-state!`, `validate-no-invoke-timeout-ms!`, `walk-state-nodes`, `synthesise-initial-snapshot`, `create-machine-handler`, `reg-machine*` (~480 LoC)

- `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx` becomes a thin façade re-exporting the public surface, matching how `re-frame.machines` is structured today (machines.cljc:129-139).

title: [conformance] Reconcile fixture :actor/spawn vs spec :actor/spawn-destroy vocabulary (needs Mike-decision)
description:
## Direct AI-implementability blocker

The spec corpus and the conformance fixture corpus DISAGREE on the actor capability vocabulary, which means an AI port author cannot reliably claim conformance.

### Spec says

The authoritative capability list is enumerated three times — all three name `:actor/spawn-destroy`, `:actor/own-state`, `:actor/cross-actor-fx`:

- `spec/005-StateMachines.md:2828` — "Imperative spawn / destroy" row, manifest example `#{:actor/spawn-destroy ...}`
- `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:470` — actor axis enumeration `(:actor/own-state, :actor/spawn-destroy, :actor/cross-actor-fx, :actor/invoke, :actor/spawn-and-join, :actor/system-id)`
- `spec/conformance/README.md:148` — same list

### Fixtures use

14 fixtures tag with `:actor/spawn` — none use `:actor/spawn-destroy`, `:actor/own-state`, or `:actor/cross-actor-fx`. The README's worked example also shows `:core/trace` and `:core/frame` capability tags but no fixtures carry those either.

### Why it bites AI one-shot

An AI implementor following 005 + Implementor-Checklist declares `:actor/spawn-destroy` in its harness manifest. The harness then filters fixtures via `(subset? fixture-capabilities claimed-capabilities)`. Since `:actor/spawn` is not in the claimed set, ALL 14 spawn fixtures are skipped as "not exercised". Conversely a port that declares `:actor/spawn` matching the fixtures has its claim diverge from the spec's vocabulary.

This is the canonical SA-6 violation under SPEC-AUTHORING — harness MUST honour the claim.

### Affected fixtures

`cross-actor-send`, `destroy-clears-snapshot`, `destroy-machine-clears-system-id-index`, `invoke-all-{join-all-completes, join-any-fails-cancels, n-of-cancels-extras}`, `invoke-spawn-on-entry-destroy-on-exit`, `machine-actor-isolation`, `spawn-{from-action, on-spawn-callback, tracked-without-data-pending, with-system-id-then-lookup-resolves, without-system-id-leaves-index-empty}`, `system-id-collision-warns-and-rebinds`.

## Proposed fix

Pick one vocabulary as canonical and align the other:

- **(a) Preferred:** rename all fixture tags `:actor/spawn` → `:actor/spawn-destroy` to match the spec's normative capability list. The spec is the contract.
- **(b) Alternative:** reword 005 / Implementor-Checklist / conformance/README.md to use `:actor/spawn`.

Also reconcile the README example's `:core/trace` and `:core/frame` mentions — either fix the README example, or add those tags to appropriate fixtures.

## Needs Mike's decision

Pick (a) spec-wins or (b) fixtures-win.

## Source

- `ai/findings/sweep-spec-completeness-2026-05-13.md` §Bucket 1 / Finding 1.1 — flagged HIGH, the only P0 in stream 4.
notes: PR #624 (rename + claim-set updates) + follow-on bead rf2-3pnob (core/trace + core/frame tagging)

title: Fix baseline 23F/8E test failures on main — blocking merge queue
description:
## Symptom

The CLJS test suite on `origin/main` has **23 failures + 8 errors**
that pre-date this session's recent worker PRs. Every worker since
~22:00 AUSEST has noted them as "pre-existing baseline." They're
blocking the merge queue — required-checks gates fail on PRs
whose diff is structurally unrelated to the failing surface.

Confirmed instances of workers flagging:
- rf2-tvu99 (PR #2200) — "same pre-existing 23+8 in xray panel-gallery tests, all unrelated"
- rf2-kducz (PR #2202) — "Pre-existing failures in panels/epoch/*, badge_cljs_test, registry_cljs_test are untouched"
- rf2-u69j7 (PR #2203) — "Failures/errors identical to baseline (23F/8E — all pre-existing)"
- rf2-mrnur (PR #2204) — "pre-existing failures in day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/* (app-db-diff projection work in flight per rf2-rrykz)"
- rf2-ezqpm (PR #2205) — "pre-existing CLJS failures (registry-snapshot, panels/epoch projection)"

## Likely root cause

Mike's recent fix commits (ee9def224 / adaabb8aa / eccb6db1b)
retired the APP-DB DIFF + CHILD DISPATCHES sections from the
Epoch panel. Tests under `panels/epoch/*` likely still reference
those sections. Plus `registry_cljs_test` likely lost a snapshot
key when Mike retired the toggle event.

## Fix scope

Worker investigates the 23F + 8E:
1. Run `npm run test:cljs` from `implementation/` against `origin/main`
   HEAD to capture the exact failure list.
2. Categorise: each failure → cause + fix shape.
3. Most likely fixes:
   - Drop tests referencing retired sections (CHILD DISPATCHES, APP-DB DIFF)
   - Update registry snapshot to current event-id set
   - Update badge_cljs_test for any badge-taxonomy drift
4. Anything genuinely broken (vs orphan tests against retired surface)
   gets surgical fixes.

## Acceptance

1. `npm run test:cljs` from `implementation/` shows 0 failures, 0 errors.
2. `npm run test:browser` similarly clean.
3. No test deleted unless the surface it tested was deliberately retired
   (commit references the retiring PR).
4. `npm run test:bundle-isolation` green.

## What does NOT change

- Don't fix the pre-existing failures by introducing new bugs.
- Don't relax the regression coverage; if a test should stay,
  update it to the new shape.
- Don't touch the Epoch panel itself — it's in flight (PR #2203).

## Coordination

This bead's surface (tests under `panels/epoch/*` + registry +
badge) may overlap with in-flight PRs #2203 (Epoch redesign) +
#2205 (machine topology). Dispatch AFTER #2203 + #2205 merge,
or work cleanly around their commits.

## Priority

**P0 — blocks merge queue.** All non-spec-only PRs get blocked
by the failing required checks. Fixing this unblocks the entire
queue.

title: fix(xray/cancellation-cascade): dispatch-id grouping reads :dispatch-id instead of canonical :rf.trace/dispatch-id — deterministic correlation degraded to flaky wall-clock heuristic
description:
**Severity: HIGH** — surfaced by audit rf2-33cqr.

**Symptom.** The cancellation-cascade visualiser's primary correlation pivot ("aborts that share the same dispatch-id as the destroy anchor are gathered into one cascade") returns nil for every event, so the deterministic correlation always falls through to the wall-clock proximity heuristic (`default-actor-destroy-window-ms 100`). Aborts may scatter across cascades; the visualiser's "this destroy caused these aborts" mental model is unreliable on busy frames.

**Root cause.** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/cancellation_cascade_helpers.cljc:228` AND `:243` read `(:dispatch-id tags)`. The substrate stamps the canonical `:rf.trace/dispatch-id` per spec 009 §Dispatch correlation (line 51-67) and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1664`. Cross-check: `tools/xray/src/.../panels/trace_helpers.cljc:691-692` reads `(get-in ev [:tags :rf.trace/dispatch-id])` correctly — so the canonical-name pattern IS used elsewhere in xray; this is local drift in the cancellation-cascade helpers.

**Recommended fix.**
- cancellation_cascade_helpers.cljc:228 → `(:rf.trace/dispatch-id tags)`.
- cancellation_cascade_helpers.cljc:243 → `(:rf.trace/dispatch-id tags)`.

(The local row-shape map-value can keep the bare `:dispatch-id` key — that's the row schema's internal choice. Only the read off the trace tags needs to use the canonical name.)

**Acceptance.** A real-substrate cancellation cascade (a destroy that aborts in-flight HTTP via `:rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy`) correlates by dispatch-id rather than wall-clock window; the visualiser's row association is deterministic.

**Sequential after rf2-33cqr (this audit) closes; safe to parallel with HIGH-1/2/3/4 — different file.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2202. Reader sites at cancellation_cascade_helpers.cljc:228+243 now read canonical :rf.trace/dispatch-id. Test co-bug at extract-wall-clock-fallback dissoc fixed. Two new regression tests pin both directions.

title: fix(xray/epoch): COEFFECT step per-row durations always nil — reads :duration-ms instead of canonical :rf.cofx/elapsed-ms, AND cofx-steps flattening drops the duration slot entirely
description:
**Severity: HIGH** — surfaced by audit rf2-33cqr. Two stacked defects.

**Symptom.** Every COEFFECT step shows nil duration even when the substrate stamps a real elapsed-ms.

**Root causes (two stacked).**

1. `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:173` (inside `coeffect-rows-from-runs`) reads `:duration-ms`. Substrate emits `:rf.cofx/elapsed-ms` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:296`); spec 009:243.
2. Even if (1) is fixed, the `cofx-steps` flattening at projection.cljc:902-908 (inside the top-level `project` fn) drops the `:duration-ms` slot — it builds each cofx-step with only `:id` and `:value`. So the duration never reaches the numbered cascade.

**Recommended fix.**
1. projection.cljc:173 — `(or (common/tag-of ev :rf.cofx/elapsed-ms) (common/tag-of ev :duration-ms))`.
2. projection.cljc:902-908 — extend the `cofx-steps` map construction to thread `:duration-ms` from each row: `(mapv (fn [{:keys [id value duration-ms]}] {:step :coeffect :badge :COEFFECT :id id :value value :duration-ms duration-ms}) cofx-rows)`.

**Acceptance.** Every focused epoch's COEFFECT steps show non-nil durations against real substrate-driven traces; `(long-step? cofx-step)` predicate works correctly (the cofx step participates in the long-step chrome detection).

**Sequential after rf2-33cqr (this audit) closes; safe to parallel with the other tag-name HIGH beads.
close_reason: Landed in PR #2210 (cluster: epoch-projection-tag-drift).

title: fix(xray/epoch): FX step per-row durations always nil — reads :duration-ms instead of canonical :rf.fx/elapsed-ms
description:

**Symptom.** Every fx-handler row in the FX step shows nil duration. (Also contributes to a wrong cascade-summary total — see rf2-slnce.)

**Root cause.** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:502` reads `:duration-ms`. Substrate emits `:rf.fx/elapsed-ms` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:368` — `(some? elapsed-ms) (assoc :rf.fx/elapsed-ms elapsed-ms)`); spec 009:241.

**Recommended fix.**

title: fix(xray/epoch): HANDLER step duration always nil — reads :duration-ms / :rf.event/duration-ms instead of canonical :rf.event/elapsed-ms
description:
**Severity: HIGH** — surfaced by audit rf2-33cqr.

**Symptom.** The HANDLER row in the Epoch panel's numbered cascade shows nil/em-dash duration. The cascade-summary chip ("cascade total") becomes the sum of the (also-broken — see rf2-bbg83) FX durations plus the (correct) sub/view durations. Operator's first-glance perf read is wrong.

**Root cause.** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:384-386` reads `:duration-ms` and `:rf.event/duration-ms` off the `:rf.event/run-end` tag-map. The substrate emits `:rf.event/elapsed-ms` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1060`); spec 009:238 documents the canonical name (it's the per-op duration the Trace panel's DURATION column reads — rf2-hhh92).

**Recommended fix.**
projection.cljc:384-386 — primary read should be `(:rf.event/elapsed-ms run-end)`. Keep `:duration-ms` / `:rf.event/duration-ms` / `(some-> db-changed :tags :duration-ms)` as legacy fixture-compat fallbacks (or drop the last two entirely if no fixture relies on them — see rf2-33cqr LOW-2 about test-fixture cleanup).

**Acceptance.** Every focused epoch's HANDLER row shows a non-nil duration; the cascade-summary chip's total matches the sum of per-step durations.

title: fix(xray/epoch): FLOW step reads wrong op-name + tag-names; never renders against real substrate traces
description:
**Severity: HIGH** — surfaced by audit rf2-33cqr.

**Symptom.** A cascade that fires one or more flows shows NO FLOW row in the Epoch panel's numbered pipeline. The conditional-cascade contract says: "present iff one or more flow-recompute events surfaced this epoch" — and the reader looks for events the substrate never emits.

**Root cause.** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:413` reads `(filter-op events :rf.flow/recomputed)`. The substrate emits `:rf.flow/computed` (`implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:234`); spec 009 §Flow trace events (line 286) is the canonical reference. Same drift on every tag-name read at lines 416-420 — the projection reads `:rf.flow/id`, `:rf.flow/path`, `:rf.flow/before`, `:rf.flow/after` but the substrate stamps bare `:flow-id`, `:path`, `:before`, `:result` under `:tags`. Every slot returns nil.
