title: Xray: Reagent lazy-seq deref tracking failure (SUPERSEDES rf2-tvu99 — was misdiagnosed as React-click-frame-leak)
description:
## Why — corrected diagnosis supersedes rf2-tvu99's hypothesis

rf2-tvu99 (filed earlier this session) attributed the recurring
"click-fires-but-view-doesn't-update" pattern to React synthetic-
event frame leaking — based on the assumption that dispatches were
landing in `:rf/default` instead of `:rf/xray`. Pair-debug 2026-05-26
followed-up with a more careful diagnostic:

1. **Dispatch IS landing in `:rf/xray`.** Direct verification:
   `(re-frame.core/dispatch-sync [:rf.xray.epoch/set-db-view-mode :all])`
   from `eval-cljs` with `--frame :rf/xray` updates the sub value
   correctly — `(re-frame.core/subscribe [:rf.xray.epoch/db-view-mode])`
   returns `:all`. State IS being mutated; sub IS reading the right
   slot.
2. **The view doesn't re-render even when state changes.** DOM
   probe after the sub returned `:all` shows `data-db-view-mode="diff"`
   — the rendered hiccup is stale. Reagent isn't detecting the
   sub-value change → no Panel re-render → operator sees no effect.
3. **External re-render forces correct state to surface.**
   Switching focused epoch (which forces the Panel to re-render
   from scratch) reads the sub fresh and shows the correct value
   that's been there all along. Confirms the issue is rendering,
   not state.

So the bug is purely a Reagent reactive-tracking failure. Frame
routing is fine; rf2-tvu99's hypothesis was wrong.

## Root cause — lazy-seq deref outside reactive scope

The Epoch panel's `pipeline-view` builds the per-step hiccup via
`(for [[i step] (map-indexed vector steps)] [step-hiccup])`. The
`for` returns a LAZY SEQ. Hiccup is realized when Reagent walks
it AFTER the Panel reg-view's render fn returns.

Inside that lazy seq, deep helpers (`handler-db-diff-block`,
`db-view-mode-toggle`) deref subscriptions like
`@(rf/subscribe [:rf.xray.epoch/db-view-mode])`. For Reagent to
track these derefs, they must happen DURING the Panel's render
phase (when Reagent's reactive scope is live). Because the lazy
seq realizes AFTER the render phase, the derefs happen OUTSIDE
the reactive scope → Reagent doesn't watch them → sub-value
changes don't trigger re-render.

A Reagent warning fires for this exact pattern:

    "Reactive deref not supported in lazy seq, it should be
    wrapped in doall: ([:div {:data-testid ...} ...])"

(Mike observed this warning on entry to the Epoch tab during
pair-debug 2026-05-26.)

## Reach — affects multiple beads' "fixed" symptoms

Several beads filed this session attribute the same recurring
symptom to React-click-frame-leak. They are likely ALL actually
this lazy-seq tracking issue:

| Bead | Filed for | Likely actual cause |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-7sdja | popup-affordance click | lazy-seq deref tracking |
| rf2-kcaiz | zoom-affordance click | lazy-seq deref tracking |
| rf2-p56sk | "Show unchanged" toggle | lazy-seq deref tracking |
| rf2-tvu99 | Epoch `:db` toggle | THIS bead — lazy-seq deref tracking |

Worker should investigate whether each of those four call sites
sits inside a similar lazy `for` / `map` / `filter` deref chain
without a `doall` to force realization inside the reactive scope.
If yes — the simple `doall` wrap is the canonical fix; per-call-
site `with-frame :rf/xray` envelope wrapping (per rf2-tvu99's
prior recommendation) is unnecessary.

## Fix — three options, pick one per the panel author's preference

### Option A — `doall` the lazy seq

Wrap the `for` in `doall` at each call site that produces hiccup
containing sub-derefs:

    (doall
      (for [[i step] (map-indexed vector steps)]
        ^{:key (str ...)}
        [:div {...} (render-step step ctx)]))

This is the minimum-change, most-Reagent-idiomatic fix. The
`doall` realizes the lazy seq INSIDE the render scope; all derefs
inside the realized elements register on Reagent's reactive
tracking.

### Option B — Replace `for` with `mapv`

`mapv` returns an eager vector. Same effect as `doall` over `for`,
slightly more readable:

    (mapv
      (fn [[i step]]
        (with-meta
          [:div {...} (render-step step ctx)]
          {:key (str ...)}))
      (map-indexed vector steps))

Pre-alpha posture might prefer `mapv` over `for` + `doall` as the
canonical eager-realization pattern.

### Option C — Move sub-derefs UP to the reg-view body

Read all subs at the top of the Panel reg-view's render body, pass
the values as props down to plain-fn helpers. This is the most
robust but requires threading every sub-value through the call
graph.

Recommendation: **Option A or B** for the Epoch panel; same
treatment for the other three filed beads (rf2-7sdja / rf2-kcaiz
/ rf2-p56sk) — audit + apply.

## Acceptance

1. Lazy seqs in panel renderers that contain `@(rf/subscribe ...)`
   derefs are realized eagerly via `doall` (option A) or replaced
   with `mapv` (option B).
2. No more "Reactive deref not supported in lazy seq" warnings in
   the browser console during Epoch panel render.
3. Clicking the `[diff][all]` toggle visibly flips the mode + the
   `:db` sub-section re-renders accordingly (no manual focus-
   change needed).
4. Same fix applied at the other three filed call sites (popup
   affordance, zoom affordance, Show unchanged toggle) — verify
   each by clicking + observing immediate visible update.
5. rf2-tvu99 is closed as duplicate of this bead (its hypothesis
   was wrong; its symptom is real and addressed here).

## What does NOT change

- The framework's dispatch routing — it was always correct
- The `with-frame` / `bound-fn` / explicit-envelope patterns —
  they remain valid for legitimate frame-context concerns, just
  weren't the right tool for this symptom
- The reducer / sub registration mechanics

## What DOES change

- Panel render fns that produce hiccup-with-sub-derefs via lazy
  `for` get `doall`'d or rewritten as `mapv`
- rf2-tvu99 closed as superseded
- rf2-7sdja / rf2-kcaiz / rf2-p56sk's "fixes" reviewed under this
  diagnosis lens — likely simpler than the patches that shipped

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce: open the Epoch panel, click the `[all]` button,
   observe no visible change. Then probe via eval-cljs:
   confirm the sub value DID flip to `:all` in `:rf/xray`. The
   gap between "state changed" and "view re-rendered" IS the bug.
2. Look at the panel's `pipeline-view` `for` — confirm it's a lazy
   seq containing hiccup whose descendants deref subs.
3. Wrap in `doall` (or rewrite as `mapv`). Verify the click
   immediately re-renders.
4. Audit the other three call sites (rf2-7sdja / rf2-kcaiz /
   rf2-p56sk source) — if they're in the same lazy-seq pattern,
   apply the same fix. Document findings.
5. Audit broader: search the Xray codebase for other `for` forms
   producing hiccup. Each is a candidate for the same bug.
6. Close rf2-tvu99 as duplicate; note the corrected diagnosis.
7. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Live diagnosis: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Mike's observation: "if I clicked the button there was no
  change. But if I changed events (got the view to refresh) then
  the click had happened. In effect, the event is getting through
  but the view is not updating."
- Reagent warning (observed in console): "Reactive deref not
  supported in lazy seq, it should be wrapped in doall: (...)"
- Affected file: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`
  `pipeline-view` (worker locates the exact for-loop)
- Related (wrongly-diagnosed) beads:
  - rf2-tvu99 — close as superseded by THIS bead
  - rf2-7sdja (popup) — re-audit
  - rf2-kcaiz (zoom) — re-audit
  - rf2-p56sk (show-unchanged) — re-audit
EOF
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2212 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2212). Single-site doall on pipeline-view's outer step-seq (epoch/view.cljs:2351) realises the lazy (for …) inside the reg-view's reactive scope so every transitive @(rf/subscribe …) deref reached by ender-step (handler-db-diff-block / render-subscriptions-step) fires while Reagent's tracking is live. Audit confirmed single-site root cause — every other panel (for …) is either already realised via into [:<>] … / into [:div …] or its body is pure hiccup with no transitive sub derefs. Regression test pipeline-view-realises-step-seq-rf2-atqkg-test pins the structural invariant; spec/006 §Lazy-seq deref tracking (Reagent adapter; rf2-atqkg) documents the pattern. Quality gates green: test:cljs 4799/15586 0 fail, test:browser 124/353 0 fail, test:bundle-isolation pass.

title: Framework: React click handlers don't route dispatches to surrounding frame — 4th instance of same root-cause pattern
description:
## Symptom

Every recently-shipped Xray UI toggle that dispatches from a React
click handler exhibits the same failure mode: the click fires, the
dispatch executes without exception, but the reducer never lands
in the surrounding `:rf/xray` frame's app-db. The sub (also in
`:rf/xray`) never sees the change. The UI shows no effect.

Confirmed instances this session (pair-debug 2026-05-26):

| Bead | Affordance | Status |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-7sdja | popup-affordance `↗` | closed; fix shipped a `{:frame :rf/xray}` envelope on the dispatch |
| rf2-kcaiz | zoom-affordance `⊙` | open; same pattern |
| rf2-p56sk | SUBSCRIPTIONS "Show unchanged" toggle | open; same pattern |
| (this bead) | Epoch HANDLER `:db` `[diff][all]` toggle | this session |

Each instance was diagnosed independently and fixed (or attempted-
fixed) at the call site with the `{:frame :rf/xray}` envelope or
the `(rf/with-frame :rf/xray (rf/dispatch [...]))` lexical wrapper.
NEITHER pattern reliably routes dispatches from React synthetic-
event callbacks to `:rf/xray`.

This is a recurring framework-level concern. The per-call-site
patches treat the symptom; the root cause needs investigation.

## What's been verified for the latest instance

- Click handler attached (`onClick` present on the DOM button)
- Click invocation executes without exception ("ok" returned)
- Code path:
  ```clj
  (rf/with-frame :rf/xray
    (rf/dispatch [:rf.xray.epoch/set-db-view-mode m]))
  ```
- Compiled JS shows the `*current-frame*` dynamic var IS bound to
  `:rf/xray` via `binding` synchronously, dispatch fires inside
  that binding, var is restored in `finally`.
- Direct `dispatch-sync` from `eval-cljs` (outside React) WITH
  `--frame :rf/xray` arg works correctly — sub updates.
- The reducer + sub are correctly registered (verified via
  `registrar/lookup`).
- After click, mode stays `:diff` in `:rf/xray` AND in `:rf/default`
  AND in `:step-deck` (the dispatch lands NOWHERE that the sub
  reads).

## Hypotheses (not yet eliminated)

1. **Dynamic-var unwind timing** — somewhere in the
   `dispatch* → router/dispatch! → build-envelope` chain there's
   a deferred read of `*current-frame*` that happens after the
   `binding` unwinds. The compiled JS shows `binding` is synchronous
   around the dispatch call, but if dispatch internally hands off
   to an async tick that reads the dyn var AGAIN, that read would
   see the restored (default / `:step-deck`) value.

2. **React synthetic-event context** — React's `flushSync` /
   `batchedUpdates` may run the click handler inside a different
   stack frame that interferes with Clojure's `binding` semantics.
   The same dispatch from a non-React context works.

3. **Frame-resolution layered race** — Spec 002's 3-tier resolution
   (dynamic var → React Context → `:rf/default`) might be reading
   from a tier that's NOT the `binding`-set dynamic var when called
   from inside a React event handler. The React Context tier
   (per `:adapter/current-frame` late-bind hook) may resolve to
   the host app's frame (`:step-deck`) instead of `:rf/xray`.

4. **Queue-time read** — `dispatch!` enqueues the envelope, but
   maybe `:frame` is resolved at DEQUEUE time (when the router
   drains the queue), not at enqueue time. By dequeue time the
   binding has unwound. If the router resolves `:frame` again
   from the dynamic var on drain, the wrong frame wins.

Worker investigation should:
1. Add a temporary `js/console.log` inside `build-envelope` logging
   the resolved `:frame` value
2. Add a log inside the click handler right before the dispatch
   showing `(frame/resolve-current-frame)` value
3. Compare the two — if they differ, the dispatch chain is
   re-resolving frame mid-flight.

## Recommended framework-level fix path

If hypothesis #1 / #4 holds:
- Make `build-envelope`'s `:frame` resolution happen at the SAME
  synchronous moment as the binding. Verify the dispatch chain
  has no deferred frame read.

If hypothesis #2 holds:
- Document a working pattern for React click handlers in
  spec/002-Frames.md. Likely `bound-fn` at render-time captures
  the surrounding frame and re-binds it inside the callback. The
  `bound-fn` macro (core.cljc:783) is the canonical mechanism per
  its docstring: "Return a fn that captures the current frame and
  re-binds `*current-frame*` inside its body. Per Spec 002
  §bound-fn."

If hypothesis #3 holds:
- The React Context tier needs to NOT override `:rf/xray`-frame
  panels mounted inside a host app. Per rf2-d4sf the resolution
  chain is `dynamic var → React Context → :rf/default`. If
  `*current-frame*` is :rf/xray via with-frame, that tier should
  win. Confirm the order is honoured.

## Direct attempt that worked elsewhere

The `core.cljs` `set-target-frame!` fn uses the same pattern:
```clj
(rf/with-frame :rf/xray
  (rf/dispatch [:rf.xray/set-target-frame frame-id]))
```

This fn is called from imperative code (not React handlers). It
DOES work. So `with-frame` works fine OUTSIDE the React click
context. The bug is specifically inside React synthetic-event
callbacks.

## Workaround for v1

Until framework fix lands, every Xray UI toggle should use
**`bound-fn`** to capture the surrounding frame at render-time
and re-bind it inside the callback:

```clj
;; in the reg-view'd component body:
(let [click-fn (rf/bound-fn [e mode]
                 (.stopPropagation e)
                 (rf/dispatch [:rf.xray.epoch/set-db-view-mode mode]))]
  ;; in the button hiccup:
  [:button {:on-click #(click-fn % :all)} "all"])
```

The `bound-fn` macro captures `*current-frame*` at the let-
binding moment (during render, while the reg-view body has
:rf/xray bound) and re-binds it inside the fn body each time the
fn is called. The captured frame survives React's event-handler
timing.

Worker tries this pattern for the toggle's onClick + confirms it
works. If yes → ALL the broken-toggle call sites

title: Epoch panel: route ALL value rendering through edn-inspector (currently plain text across DISPATCH/HANDLER/SUBSCRIPTIONS/VIEWS)
description:
## Symptom

Live audit (pair-debug 2026-05-26) of the Epoch panel — probing for
`[data-rf-mount-id]` / `[data-rf-type]` / `[data-rf-mini]` elements
across every step:

| Step | edn-inspector mounts | typed scalars | mini renders |
|---|---|---|---|
| DISPATCH | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| COEFFECT | 0 | 1 | 1 |
| HANDLER | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| SUBSCRIPTIONS | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| VIEWS | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The Epoch panel renders almost ALL of its value-shaped data as
plain text. The COEFFECT step is the lone partial (one `mini`
render — which is the cofx result row that itself shows `nil`, per
rf2-mmlgk).

Compare to other Xray panels (App-DB, Handler, Trace, Machines,
Issues, Routing) — they ALL route value rendering through the
edn-inspector. The Epoch panel is the outlier.

## Why it matters

Beyond visual consistency (the operator sees the SAME value styled
differently in DIFFERENT panels of the same tool), the
edn-inspector brings:

- Per-token syntax colours (rf2-79ojx palette — keywords purple,
  strings green, numbers orange, etc.)
- Sentinel chrome (`:rf/redacted`, `:rf.size/large-elided` per
  rf2-ndb13)
- Width-aware inline-vs-tree (rf2-kbdk8 — short fits inline; long
  expands)
- Sticky expansion (rf2-pvsxs — operator's expand choices persist)
- Click-to-zoom + breadcrumbs (rf2-h71e0)
- Click-to-toggle expand (post-rf2-y59tb / rf2-kcaiz frame-leak
  fixes)
- Card chrome + header ribbon (rf2-63ie5 + rf2-okq7p, where
  applicable)

Plain-text rendering means NONE of this — for every value-shaped
data point in the Epoch panel the operator gets unstyled, static,
non-interactive text.

## Specific data points to route through edn-inspector

### DISPATCH step (rf2-nszcv already filed for this specific case)

- Event vector: `[:counter/inc]` — currently plain text

### COEFFECT step

- Cofx-id keyword: e.g. `:testdeck/now` — currently plain text
- Cofx result value: e.g. the timestamp number — currently
  rendered via `mini` but the value is `nil` (rf2-mmlgk)
- Cofx args (when present) — likely plain text

### HANDLER step

- Event-id keyword: e.g. `:counter/inc` — currently plain text
- Handler-type label: e.g. `reg-event-db` / `reg-event-fx` /
  `reg-machine` — could remain plain text (it's a label, not a
  value), but consistent treatment with edn-inspector tokens for
  keywords would help

(Source code rendering via `code-block` is CORRECT — that's source
text, not a value; the inspector wouldn't help.)

### SUBSCRIPTIONS step

- Sub-id vectors: e.g. `[:counter/value]` `[:counter/last-clicked]`
  `[:counter/parity]` — currently plain text
- Input source (e.g. `app-db`) — could stay plain (it's a label)
- Before/after values: e.g. `0 → 1`, `1779785519293`,
  `:counter/value` (for derived subs) — currently plain text;
  should be edn-inspector mini renders so:
  - Numbers render in syntax-number colour
  - Keywords render in syntax-keyword colour
  - Long values truncate via width-aware
  - Sentinels render their chrome

### VIEWS step

- View-id keyword: e.g. `:testdeck.panel/counter-tab` — currently
  plain text
- Subs consumed list: `[:counter/value] [:counter/last-clicked]
  [:counter/show-parity?]` — currently plain text; each sub-id
  should be a `mini` render

### Future steps (when they land per other beads)

- **DB diff** (rf2-rrykz, rf2-93436) — diff rendering MUST route
  through edn-inspector diff mode (consistency with App-DB panel
  diff, Machine snapshot Before/After)
- **FX** (rf2-uffov) — per-fx args render via edn-inspector
- **Schema violations** (rf2-17vxj) — failing data via
  edn-inspector
- **Machine handler details** (rf2-9c27r) — :data deltas,
  snapshot diff, etc. — all via edn-inspector

## Fix

Audit each step's render code in
`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`.
Identify every plain-text emit of a CLJS value. Replace each with
an `[ei/edn-inspector value opts]` or `[ei/mini value]` mount.

Decision matrix:
- Single-line context (table cell, inline row item) → `[ei/mini value]`
- Multi-line / expandable context (top-level value, may need
  drill-down) → `[ei/edn-inspector value opts]`
- Source code → KEEP as `code-block` (not a value)
- Labels (`from ui`, `app-db`, section headers) → KEEP as plain
  text (not values)

The audit + bulk-replace can ship as one PR (no behaviour change,
just renderer swap) OR split per-step. Worker picks.

## Acceptance

1. DOM probe across the panel: every plain-text rendering of a
   CLJS-value has been replaced with an edn-inspector or `mini`
   mount. Each step has `> 0` typed-spans / mounts in its DOM.
2. Per-token syntax colouring visible across the panel for
   keywords, numbers, strings, booleans, nil.
3. Sentinels render their chrome where applicable.
4. Width-aware behaviour kicks in for long values.
5. Visual consistency vs other Xray panels — App-DB, Handler,
   etc.

## What does NOT change

- The handler source rendering (`code-block` is correct)
- Section labels (`DISPATCH`, `COEFFECT`, etc.)
- Step header text ("from ui", "1 coeffect injected", etc.)
- Pipeline structure

## What DOES change

- Every value-shaped data point in the Epoch panel routes through
  edn-inspector or `mini`
- Per-step row renderers updated to mount the widget
- Consistent visual treatment across the panel

## Out of scope

- Adding NEW data points to the panel (other beads cover what data
  to ADD; this bead is purely about HOW existing data renders)
- Renaming testids
- Layout/structure changes

## Coordination

Subsumes rf2-nszcv (DISPATCH event-vector — same root cause,
narrower scope; worker can close rf2-nszcv as part of this bead's
PR with reference).

Coordinates with every other open Epoch bead that ADDS new data
(rf2-93436 db-diff, rf2-uffov FX, rf2-17vxj schema, rf2-9c27r
machine details) — those beads should land their data USING the
inspector from the start.

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Read `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`
   end-to-end.
2. Probe live (pair-debug session reproduction):
   `[data-rf-mount-id]` count per step → confirm audit data above.
3. Decide per-step: bulk-replace in one PR or split.
4. Confirm `views.edn-inspector` (renamed per rf2-h4fce) is already
   `:require`'d in the view ns; if not, add the alias.
5. Test post-change: every step renders with visible syntax
   colours; sub-ids click through (where the inspector supports
   that — `:zoomable? true` would be useful per step's affordance
   decision).
6. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Pair-debug 2026-05-26 — DOM probe of every step
- Inspector source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs`
- Code-block source (for handler source — DO NOT replace this with
  inspector): `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget/widget.cljs`
  (`code-block` fn)
- Parent: rf2-sc3r1 (Epoch panel)
- Subsumes: rf2-nszcv (DISPATCH event-vector — narrower)
- Coordinates with: rf2-mmlgk (cofx result nil), rf2-93436
  (db-diff), rf2-uffov (FX), rf2-17vxj (schema), rf2-9c27r
  (machine details)
EOF
close_reason: All value-shaped Epoch-panel emits route through ei/edn-inspector + ei/mini; DISPATCH/COEFFECT/HANDLER/FLOW/FX/SUBSCRIPTIONS/VIEWS/SCHEMA-VIOLATIONS/APP-DB-DIFF/CHILD-DISPATCHES all covered. PR #2198.

title: Epoch panel: 'Show unchanged' toggle in SUBSCRIPTIONS does nothing (frame-leak class)
description:
## Symptom

The Epoch panel's SUBSCRIPTIONS step renders a "Show unchanged"
toggle (per rf2-kfh1v) but clicking it does NOTHING. The unchanged
rows remain hidden; toggling has no visible effect.

Live (pair-debug 2026-05-26) for `:counter/inc` cascade:
- Step header: `4 SUBSCRIPTIONS 7 recomputed (3 changed, 4 unchanged) Show unchanged`
- Body lists 3 changed rows only
- Clicking "Show unchanged" → no rows added; the 4 unchanged subs
  remain hidden

The toggle infrastructure landed (per the epoch_panel.cljs source
showing `:rf.xray.epoch/subs-show-unchanged?` sub +
`:rf.xray.epoch/toggle-subs-show-unchanged` event registered), but
either:

- The click handler isn't dispatching, OR
- The dispatch fires but the sub isn't updating, OR
- The sub updates but the renderer doesn't read it to gate
  unchanged-row inclusion

## Likely root cause (pattern-match)

This is the same class of bug as rf2-7sdja (popup affordance), rf2-
kcaiz (zoom affordance), rf2-y59tb (triangle toggle): a React click
handler dispatches via the lexical `dispatch-fn` but the surrounding
frame context has been popped — dispatch leaks to `:rf/default`
instead of `:rf/xray`. The reducer mutates `:rf/default`'s app-db;
the sub running in `:rf/xray` doesn't see the change.

Verify by:

1. Click the "Show unchanged" toggle
2. Probe `@(rf/subscribe {:frame :rf/default}
   [:rf.xray.epoch/subs-show-unchanged?])` — if true, dispatch is
   leaking
3. `dispatch-sync` the toggle event explicitly with
   `{:frame :rf/xray}` envelope — if THAT updates the
   `:rf/xray`-frame sub + the rows appear, confirms the click-leak
   hypothesis

## Fix

Same fix pattern as rf2-7sdja: wrap the toggle button's onClick
dispatch with explicit `{:frame :rf/xray}` envelope.

Worker should ALSO audit every other Epoch-panel-internal dispatch
(per-row expand toggle, any future filter chips, etc.) for the same
class of bug — apply the envelope-wrapping pattern uniformly.

## Acceptance

1. Clicking "Show unchanged" → the 4 unchanged-input rows appear in
   the SUBSCRIPTIONS step body.
2. Clicking again → the unchanged rows hide.
3. Toggle state persists across re-renders (sub correctly tracks).
4. State sits on `:rf/xray`'s app-db at
   `:epoch-panel-subs-show-unchanged?` (per the epoch_panel.cljs
   reducer).

## References

- Same bug class: rf2-7sdja (popup), rf2-kcaiz (zoom), rf2-y59tb
  (triangle toggle) — all React-click frame-leak bugs
- Parent: rf2-kfh1v (SUBSCRIPTIONS — sub names + changed + hide
  unchanged; landed but toggle broken)
- Pair-debug 2026-05-26 (Mike: "'Show unchanged' subscriptions does
  nothing")
- Source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch_panel.cljs`
  line 139-145 (sub + event registration)
EOF

title: Epoch panel: HANDLER step missing :db diff sub-section (per design doc §Section 1+2)
description:
## Symptom

The Epoch panel's HANDLER step renders the handler source code but
does NOT show the `:db` diff produced by the handler. For
`:counter/inc` (reg-event-fx that mutates `[:counter :value]`), the
operator can see the handler's source but not what the handler
ACTUALLY DID to app-db this cascade. Critical debug information
absent.

## Design-doc reference

`ai/findings/epoch-panel-handler-section-design.md` §Section 1 +
§Section 2 — both `reg-event-db` and `reg-event-fx` HANDLER
sections include a **DB DIFF sub-section** showing the path-changes
the handler produced:

    HANDLER (reg-event-db :counter/inc)
    ─────────────────────────────────────────
    SOURCE                  counter.cljs:42  [open]
      (fn [db _ev]
        (update db :value inc))

    DB DIFF
      [:counter :value]  5 → 6

The spec places DB DIFF AS A SUB-SECTION OF HANDLER (not as a
separate top-level pipeline step). This is intentional: it tells
the operator "this is what the handler we just showed you DID".

## Relationship to existing beads

rf2-rrykz ("Epoch panel: add app-db diff section") is OPEN. The
filed bead currently positions the diff as a SEPARATE top-level
pipeline step. Per the design doc, it should be a SUB-SECTION of
HANDLER. Worker on rf2-rrykz should be made aware of this design
intent — file as either:

- (a) **Update rf2-rrykz** if still open + unclaimed, clarifying
  position as sub-section of HANDLER (not separate step)
- (b) **New focused bead** documenting the specific
  HANDLER-sub-section requirement, with rf2-rrykz as parent

Worker for THIS bead checks rf2-rrykz status first; choose path
accordingly.

## Fix

Add DB DIFF as a sub-section UNDER the HANDLER step (vertically
nested inside HANDLER's body, between the SOURCE block and where
the FX sub-section would go). For machine handlers, the position
changes — see design doc §Section 3 (DB DIFF folds into SNAPSHOT
DIFF).

Source data: existing `:rf.xray/selected-epoch-diff` sub (the same
sub the App-DB panel + Event panel consume).

Render via edn-inspector diff mode (consistency with the App-DB
panel diff treatment) or the flat `~ [path] old → new` projection
(consistency with the Event panel diff treatment) — worker picks;
edn-inspector mode is preferred for visual consistency with
Machine snapshot Before/After.

## Acceptance

1. HANDLER step body shows a DB DIFF sub-section between SOURCE
   and (eventual) FX sub-section.
2. For `:counter/inc` → operator sees `[:counter :value] 0 → 1`
   under HANDLER.
3. For a cascade with no app-db changes (e.g. a reg-event-fx
   returning only `:fx`, no `:db`), DB DIFF renders `— (no
   changes)` per design doc §Empty-edge-case-rendering table.
4. For machine cascades, DB DIFF folds into SNAPSHOT DIFF (per
   design doc §Section 3b §DB DIFF — single-line "see SNAPSHOT
   DIFF" when only the machine slot changed).

## References

- Design doc: `ai/findings/epoch-panel-handler-section-design.md`
  §Section 1 + §Section 2
- Related (open): rf2-rrykz — app-db diff section position
- Pair-debug 2026-05-26 (Mike: "No diff for :db under handler")
EOF

title: Xray edn-inspector: zoom-affordance click leaks to :rf/default (same class as rf2-7sdja popup fix)
description:
**The defect.** The zoom-affordance button (`⊙` glyph, top-right of each container when `:zoomable? true`, shipped in rf2-h71e0) is rendered with an onClick handler that does nothing visible — the dispatch leaks to `:rf/default` instead of `:rf/xray` because React's synthetic-event timing pops the frame context before the lexically-captured `dispatch-fn` fires.

**Acceptance:**
1. Clicking the zoom-affordance `⊙` button updates `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/zoom` sub in `:rf/xray` frame.
2. No leak to `:rf/default`.
3. No regression of rf2-7sdja popup-affordance or rf2-y59tb triangle toggle.
4. Test added that mirrors the rf2-7sdja test shape for popup-affordance.

**Resolution:** Fixed via PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2190. Zoom-affordance click now dispatches with explicit `{:frame :rf/xray}` envelope at call time. New regression test `zoom-affordance-button-onclick-dispatches-against-xray-frame` asserts the envelope; existing tests refactored to use `with-redefs rf/dispatch*` spy pattern matching the rf2-7sdja shape.

title: Epoch panel: add FX section (per-fx + outcome + per-action attribution)
description:

The Epoch panel doesn't show which fx fired. For a handler that
returned `:fx [[:http/get ...] [:dispatch [:other]]]`, no way to see

title: Epoch panel: add app-db diff section (what changed in app-db this cascade)
description:

title: Epoch panel: VIEWS step missing view name + view's consumed subs
description:
## Symptom

VIEWS step shows `1 view re-rendered` but does NOT show the view
name OR which subs the view depends on. Operator sees a count
with no identification — can't tell WHICH view re-rendered or WHY.

## Fix

Per-view row showing:
- View name / id (rendered hiccup component name or the registered
  view-id when reg-view'd)
- Which subs the view consumed (the dependency list — same data
  the Subscriptions panel uses)
- Optionally: render count (was this view re-rendered 1 time or 50
  this cascade?)

Source data: framework records render events with the view-id +
deps per Spec 009. The render-events projection is already on the
epoch-record.

## Acceptance

1. VIEWS step body lists one row per view with the view-id +
   the subs the view consumed.
2. View-id rendered as a clear label (file:line if available via

description:

title: Xray data-display: width-aware expansion heuristic (don't auto-expand when inline fits)
description:
## Symptom

The data-display widget's auto-expansion heuristic is depth-based (`:default-expanded-depth 2`), not width-aware. Any collection within the depth limit auto-expands, regardless of whether its inline form would trivially fit in the available column width. Result: short values get rendered as multi-row trees and waste massive vertical real-estate.

Measured live this session (pair-debug 2026-05-26) on the Handler panel dispatch-section mount:

- Available column width: **966px**
- Value text content: **81 chars** (`[:ws/connection [:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed 2501 [:active :authenticating]]]`)
- Inline render would be: ~570px (about 60% of available)
- Actual rendered height: **148px** (8-9 rows of tree)

That value would fit inline in roughly one line at 17px height — instead it takes ~9× the vertical space for no good reason. Operator's eye has to walk a tree where a glance at one line would suffice.

This is pervasive across every panel that mounts the widget: Handler, Trace, Issues, Machine snapshots — anywhere a short event vector or compact collection auto-expands when inline rendering would read better.

## Why the current heuristic is wrong

Current logic (data_display.cljs): `resolve-expanded?` returns `true` when `depth < default-expanded-depth`. The `default-expanded-depth` opt (typically 2-3) treats expansion as a "how deep should I auto-open?" question — depth-first, width-blind.

The `:max-inline-width 60` opt that exists today is a CHARACTER threshold used only when ALREADY rendering inline (e.g. previews on collapsed nodes). It does NOT enter the "should this expand or not?" decision.

What the right heuristic looks like:

> **Render inline if the value's inline form fits in the available column width (with a small margin). Otherwise expand to tree.**

Matches the convention every mainstream inspector uses (cljs-devtools, Chrome devtools, vscode debug "variables", react-inspector). Short values stay inline; long ones expand. Operator's sticky override always wins.

## Proposed heuristic

For each candidate node, decide expansion in this order:

1. **Sticky operator override exists?** → use the override (current behaviour; persists across re-renders)
2. **Diff mode + this node is on an ancestor-chain over a changed descendant?** → expand (current behaviour; eye follows the diff)
3. **Inline form fits in available width?** → render inline. Compute `would-fit-inline?` by estimating inline-render width (`char-count * mono-char-width` is good enough; ~7px per char in JetBrains Mono 12px). If the estimate is ≤ `available-width - safety-margin`, inline.
4. **Otherwise** → expand to tree.

The `default-expanded-depth` opt becomes a CEILING (don't expand past depth N even if it doesn't fit — at that depth, show as truncated preview with a click-to-expand affordance) rather than the primary heuristic.

The `:max-inline-width` opt remains useful for the COLLAPSED-PREVIEW formatting (when a node is collapsed and shows a one-line summary like `{:counter {…} :async {…} :machine-ui {…}}` — that preview line still respects 60 chars).

## How "available width" is determined

The widget knows its container element via the React ref / mount-id container. On render, walk up to find the effective container width (the panel's main column, post-card-chrome padding). Cache per mount; recompute on resize via ResizeObserver. Cheap.

Estimation rule: `inline-fit? = (estimated-inline-width + safety-margin) <= available-width`. Use `safety-margin = 16px` to avoid edge-case wraps.

For a vector of N items where each item is itself a collection, the inline width estimation recursively computes children's inline widths and aggregates. Caps at a reasonable max-depth so the heuristic itself stays cheap (matches current `:max-depth 16`).

## Composes with existing features

- **Sticky overrides** (rf2-pvsxs) — operator clicks ▾ or ▸; that wins regardless of fit. Persists.
- **Diff mode** — ancestor chain over changed nodes still force-expands. Diff readability > fit.
- **Default-expanded-depth** becomes a ceiling, NOT the trigger. Worker decides the right default ceiling (probably 8 or so — basically "never auto-expand into a binary-tree-of-doom case").
- **Card chrome** (rf2-63ie5) — the width measurement happens AFTER the card's padding, so the inline form fits inside the card's actual content area, not outside it.

## Acceptance

1. Short collections (inline-fits-in-width) render INLINE by default, not expanded. Verified live: the Handler panel dispatch event renders on one line at ~570px wide, not as a 9-row tree.
2. Long collections (inline-overflows-width) STILL render expanded as today.
3. Operator clicking ▾ on an auto-inlined collection expands it; clicking ▸ on an auto-expanded one collapses it. Sticky override mechanism unchanged.
4. The `:max-inline-width 60` opt continues to govern the collapsed-preview one-liner formatting (no regression in how a collapsed `{…}` summary reads).
5. The `:default-expanded-depth` opt repurposed as a CEILING (don't auto-expand past depth N even if it doesn't fit; truncate with click-to-expand). Worker picks the new default; document the change.
6. Resize the panel — wider → more collections inline; narrower → more expand. Verified via window resize triggering a re-render via ResizeObserver.
7. No regression in panels that intentionally want everything expanded (worker identifies any; likely none — but check the Machine snapshot panels which have their own conventions).
8. Diff mode still force-expands ancestor chains over changed descendants. Tested via a diff with deep changes.

## What does NOT change

- The widget's data-render logic (token colours, scalar formatting, sentinels, etc.)
- The expansion-state mechanics (sticky overrides via `:rf.xray.data-display/expansion`)
- The triangle interaction
- The popup affordance
- The diff-mode gutter glyphs and `← changed from X` annotations

## What DOES change

- `resolve-expanded?` (or equivalent) gains a width-aware branch
- A new `would-fit-inline?` helper that estimates inline width recursively
- A new `available-width` capture per mount (via ResizeObserver)
- `default-expanded-depth` semantics shift from "auto-open this deep" → "ceiling beyond which never auto-open"

## Out of scope

- Animation on auto-expand/collapse
- Per-token-type sizing (e.g. treat strings vs numbers differently)
- Operator-tunable inline-width budget per mount (default 60 should suffice; can add later if needed)

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: load http://localhost:8031/counter → Handler tab → dispatch section. Probe the dispatch event mount: panel-width 966px, content 81 chars, render height 148px. Confirm the value would trivially inline.
2. Test in multiple panels — Handler, Trace, Issues. Each should benefit; identify any panel where inline-by-default would HURT (probably none — but check Machine snapshots which may have their own conventions).
3. Decide the `safety-margin` constant. 16px is a starting point; tune by eyeballing the visual against the running app.
4. Decide the new `default-expanded-depth` ceiling. Today's 2-3 is too low (treats it as a trigger); the new semantic wants something like 8 (only kicks in for genuinely huge trees).
5. Confirm the estimation function (`char-count * mono-char-width`) is accurate enough. Render a few candidates with a probe + measure actual width; calibrate.
6. Test ResizeObserver lifecycle — cleanup on unmount, throttling on rapid resize, no leaks.
7. Test composition with rf2-card-chrome, rf2-alignment, rf2-popup-fix beads (likely all land separately; integration test once they're in).
8. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Live measurement + diagnosis: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Widget render: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs`
- Current `resolve-expanded?` logic: `views/data_display.cljs:155-164`
- Existing `:max-inline-width` opt: defaults to 60 chars; used for collapsed-preview one-liner formatting
- Existing `:default-expanded-depth` opt: defaults to 2; current trigger to be repurposed as ceiling
- Convention reference: cljs-devtools, Chrome devtools' "object inspector", react-inspector — all width-aware

title: Xray data-display: popup-affordance fix + drop from App-DB + glyph ⊕→↗
description:
## Symptom

Clicking the `⊕` popup-affordance button in the top-right of a data-display mount does NOTHING. The button registers `cursor: pointer`, the React onClick handler is attached, but the popup never opens. Reproducible on every panel that mounts data-display with `:popup-affordance? true`.

Confirmed live this session (pair-debug 2026-05-26):
- The popup-open reducer IS registered (`re-frame.registrar/lookup :event :rf.xray.data-display-popup/open` returns a handler)
- The popup stack subscribe IS registered
- Dispatching the open event via `dispatch-sync` from `eval-cljs` (inside `:rf/xray` frame) makes the popup render correctly — `[role='dialog']` element appears with backdrop + content. So the popup MACHINERY is fully working.
- Invoking the button's React onClick handler directly (via probe) does NOT land the dispatch. Stack stays empty in every frame (`:rf/default`, `:step-deck`, `:rf/xray`).

The widget IS `reg-view`-registered (line 1412 in `views/data_display.cljs`) and the popup-affordance-button receives the lexically-captured `dispatch-fn`. Same `dispatch-fn` is used by the triangle toggle (which works fine). So the dispatcher itself isn't the problem — something specific to the popup event-dispatch silently fails.

Strong hint at `data_display_popup.cljs:195-199` — the `install-events!` docstring says:

> *Every dispatch carries the `{:frame :rf/xray}` envelope at call time so React's click/keydown context pop doesn't leak the event to `:rf/default` (same fix as the App-DB segment-inspector + settings popup).*

OTHER consumers of these popup events (settings-popup, segment-inspector) explicitly wrap with `{:frame :rf/xray}` envelope. The data-display's popup-affordance-button does NOT — it relies only on the reg-view-captured dispatch-fn closure. That implicit reliance evidently isn't sufficient for the popup-open event class.

## Fix — two parts

### Part 1 — Popup-affordance dispatch carries explicit `{:frame :rf/xray}` envelope

In `popup-affordance-button` at `views/data_display.cljs:1378`, change the onClick from:

    (dispatch-fn
      [:rf.xray.data-display-popup/open popup-mount-id payload])

to use the same envelope pattern other popup consumers use. Worker confirms exactly which envelope syntax matches the framework convention by inspecting how settings-popup + segment-inspector dispatch — likely either:

    (rf/dispatch {:frame :rf/xray}
      [:rf.xray.data-display-popup/open popup-mount-id payload])

OR a metadata variant on the event vector. Use the established pattern; don't invent a new shape.

Why the triangle works without the envelope but the popup-open doesn't: worker investigates as part of the fix and documents the difference. Hypothesis: the popup-open event's reducer mutates a slot the popup stack-view subscribes against via the `:rf/xray` frame-provider; if the dispatch leaks to `:rf/default`, the mutation lands in the wrong frame's app-db and the stack view never sees it. The triangle's toggle reducer mutates the data-display expansion slot — possibly that slot ends up in the same frame regardless of where dispatch lands (e.g. because the sub is in `:rf/default` too, or via shared state). Worker resolves the asymmetry — if it's an accidental difference, also fix the triangle path to use the envelope so the next consumer doesn't trip the same trap.

### Part 2 — Drop popup affordance from App-DB panel

The App-DB panel has plenty of horizontal room — the popup is unnecessary there. The popup design (`app_db_diff_state.cljs:147` comment) calls App-DB "the canonical cramped in the side panel case" — that framing is wrong; the side panel is wide enough for App-DB's whole-tree without help.

Remove `:popup-affordance? true` from the App-DB panel mounts at `app_db_diff_state.cljs:142,146`. Keep the affordance on panels where the side-panel IS cramped (Handler panel's event-detail mounts, Trace expanded payloads, Machine snapshot inspector). Worker audits and decides per-panel.

### Part 3 — Glyph change `⊕` → `↗`

In `popup-affordance-button` at `views/data_display.cljs:1410`, change the glyph from `⊕` (circled plus — reads as "add" or "expand-all") to `↗` (north-east arrow — established UX convention for "open in new pane / external"). Aria-label and title stay "Open in popup".

## Acceptance

1. Clicking the `⊕` (now `↗`) popup-affordance button on a data-display mount opens the popup overlay. Verified manually + via probe (invoke the button's React onClick; stack count goes from 0 → 1; dialog renders).
2. The popup-open dispatch lands in the `:rf/xray` frame's app-db — measured via `[:rf.xray.data-display-popup/stack]` sub on `:rf/xray`, NOT `:rf/default`.
3. App-DB panel mounts NO LONGER carry the affordance button — verified live (no `[data-testid^='rf-xray-data-display-popup-affordance-']` elements in the App-DB panel).
4. Other panels (Handler, Trace, etc.) still carry the affordance and it still works.
5. Glyph in the button is `↗`, not `⊕`. Title + aria-label unchanged.
6. The mystery about WHY the triangle dispatch worked without the envelope but the popup didn't is documented in the PR description — either fixed (use envelope everywhere for symmetry) or explained.

## What does NOT change

- The popup widget itself (`views/data_display_popup.cljs`) — events, subs, stack management all unchanged
- The popup's modal chrome / backdrop / Esc handling
- The `:popup-affordance?` opt's name + default (false)
- Consumer panels other than App-DB still pass `:popup-affordance? true`

## What DOES change

- `popup-affordance-button`'s onClick wraps dispatch with `{:frame :rf/xray}` envelope (or equivalent established pattern)
- App-DB panel call sites drop `:popup-affordance? true`
- Glyph in the button: `⊕` → `↗`
- PR description documents the dispatch-asymmetry investigation

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: load http://localhost:8031/counter → App-DB → click `⊕` → confirm nothing happens. Then via `eval-cljs` dispatch-sync the same event into `:rf/xray` and confirm the popup DOES render. This isolates the bug to the dispatch path.
2. Inspect how `settings-popup` and `app_db_segment_inspector` dispatch their popup-open events. Match the envelope pattern they use.
3. Audit every panel that currently passes `:popup-affordance? true`. Decide which keep it (cramped panels) and which lose it (room-y panels). App-DB definitely loses it. Worker confirms others case by case.
4. Test the `↗` glyph in both light + dark themes — confirm it's visible against the inspector card chrome.
5. Investigate the triangle-vs-popup dispatch asymmetry. Either fix triangles to also use the envelope (defensive symmetry) or document why their reducer survives the leak.
6. Report findings before pushing implementation.

## References

- Bug repro: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Popup widget: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display_popup.cljs`
- Popup-affordance button render: `views/data_display.cljs:1378-1410`
- Reg-view registration: `views/data_display.cljs:1412`
- App-DB call-sites to drop affordance: `panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:142,146`
- Established envelope-wrapping pattern: `settings/popup.cljs`, `panels/app_db_segment_inspector.cljs`
- Install-events docstring hint: `views/data_display_popup.cljs:195-199`

title: Xray data-display: click-toggle broken (frame leak + first-click logic)
description:
## Symptom

In the App-DB panel (and any other surface using the new `views.data-display` widget), clicking a ▾ / ▸ triangle does NOTHING. Triangles look interactive (`cursor: pointer`, real React onClick handler attached, dispatch event fires without exception) but the visible state never changes. Confirmed live this session via DOM probes against the running step-deck testbed.

This is the rf2-oqa60 Phase 1 widget — not the pre-rebuild cljs-devtools facade. The infrastructure landed clean (mount-id keying, drop of binaryage/cljs-devtools, Spec 015 sentinels first-class, diff mode subsumed in Phase 5). Per-token colours in the expanded body are correct (numbers → `:syntax-number`, booleans → `:syntax-keyword`, strings → `:syntax-string`, etc.). The interactive toggle, the panel's whole-point feature, is the missing piece.

## Diagnosis (live source review + DOM probes, pair-debug session 2026-05-25)

Two independent root causes, both confirmed:

### Bug A — Frame leak via missing `reg-view`

`data-display` (the widget's public entry) is registered as a plain `defn` (line 1117) — NOT `rf/reg-view`:

    (defn data-display
      ([value] (data-display value nil))
      ([_value _opts]
       (let [mount-id (gen-mount-id)]
         (fn [value opts]
           ...))))

Plain Reagent fns do NOT capture the surrounding frame-provider's frame via React Context. Spec 002 / Spec 006 are explicit: only `reg-view`-registered views participate in frame-aware dispatch/subscribe routing.

So when the widget is mounted under `:rf/xray` (App-DB panel's frame) and a triangle's click handler runs:

    (rf/dispatch [:rf.xray.data-display/toggle-node panel-id mount-id path])   ; line 717

… the dispatch DOES NOT carry the surrounding `:rf/xray` frame. It routes to `:rf/default`. The toggle reducer runs against `:rf/default`'s app-db; the expansion-slot mutation lands in `:rf/default`'s slot.

Meanwhile, render-time `@(rf/subscribe [expansion-slot])` (line 1159) runs inside the `:rf/xray` reactive context and reads `:rf/xray`'s expansion-slot. The mutation in `:rf/default`'s slot is invisible to the sub running in `:rf/xray`'s frame.

→ Click fires, event dispatches, reducer mutates… wrong frame's db. Sub never sees a change. View never re-renders. Operator sees nothing happen.

This is the same `:rf.warning/plain-fn-under-non-default-frame-once` class previously surfaced for `ribbon-theme-toggle` (rf2-uu3lp). Confirm by opening DevTools console while the App-DB panel is mounted under `:rf/xray` — a warning should be emitted for `day8.re-frame2-xray.views.data-display/data-display`.

### Bug B — First-click logic is wrong for default-expanded paths

Toggle reducer at lines 131-144:

    (rf/reg-event-db :rf.xray.data-display/toggle-node
      (fn [db [_ panel-id mount-id path]]
        (let [k       (expansion-key panel-id mount-id path)
              current (get-in db [expansion-slot k])
              next?   (if (contains? current :expanded?)
                        (not (boolean (:expanded? current)))
                        true)] ;; "first click opens — common case"
          (assoc-in db [expansion-slot k] {:expanded? next?}))))

When no override exists for a path, the reducer ALWAYS sets `{:expanded? true}` (the "first click opens" path). But the widget's `:default-expanded-depth` is 2 — so top-level paths (the most-visible triangles) START EXPANDED before any click.

Flow for a default-expanded triangle:

1. Path renders expanded (no override, default-expanded? = true) → triangle ▾
2. User clicks → reducer reads "no override", stores `{:expanded? true}` ⟵ same value the path already had; visible state unchanged
3. User clicks AGAIN → reducer reads override `:expanded? true`, inverts to `:expanded? false` → collapses
4. From the operator's perspective: "first click does nothing; second click works"

For default-COLLAPSED paths (deep nodes past `default-expanded-depth`), the "first click opens" intent IS correct — those paths start collapsed, and first click sets `:expanded? true` → opens. The bug is one-sided: visible only on default-expanded paths, which is most of what the operator sees.

Even if Bug A were fixed in isolation, top-level triangles would still appear non-functional because of Bug B.

## Fixes

### Fix A — Register `data-display` via `reg-view`

The cleanest fix: make the component frame-aware so dispatches inherit the surrounding frame:

    (rf/reg-view :rf.xray/data-display
      ([{:keys [value]}] [data-display-inner value nil])
      ([{:keys [value opts]}] [data-display-inner value opts]))

… where `data-display-inner` is the form-2 fn currently called `data-display`. Or wrap `data-display` itself via `reg-view`.

Alternative (less invasive but more friction): keep `data-display` as a plain fn and explicitly capture the current frame at mount time, threading it through every dispatch:

    (defn data-display
      ([value] (data-display value nil))
      ([_value _opts]
       (let [mount-id (gen-mount-id)
             frame-id (rf/current-frame-id)]   ; capture once at mount
         (fn [value opts]
           ... (rf/dispatch {:frame frame-id} [:rf.xray.data-display/toggle-node ...])))))

The `reg-view` approach is preferable for symmetry with the rest of the framework, and so subscribes (`@(rf/subscribe [expansion-slot])`) also inherit the right frame for free.

Audit and update every call-site that mounts the widget to use the registered view rather than the plain fn — the App-DB panel `[dd/data-display ...]` at `panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:142,146` is the primary one; check the diff convenience `data-display-diff`, the popup `data_display_popup`, and any other consumers.

### Fix B — Pass current `default?` into the toggle dispatch; flip from it on no-override

Reducer should know whether the path is currently rendered as expanded (per default or override) so it can flip correctly even when no override exists:

    (rf/reg-event-db :rf.xray.data-display/toggle-node
      (fn [db [_ panel-id mount-id path current-rendered-expanded?]]
        (let [k       (expansion-key panel-id mount-id path)
              current (get-in db [expansion-slot k])
              next?   (if (contains? current :expanded?)
                        (not (boolean (:expanded? current)))
                        (not (boolean current-rendered-expanded?)))]   ; flip the actual rendered state
          (assoc-in db [expansion-slot k] {:expanded? next?}))))

Dispatch payload at line 717 updates to thread the current state:

    (rf/dispatch [:rf.xray.data-display/toggle-node
                  panel-id mount-id path expanded?])

where `expanded?` is the value `resolve-expanded?` returned for this path on the current render. The renderer already has this value in scope at the click-handler emit site.

`set-node` (line 146) is fine as-is — it takes the explicit `expanded?` flag from the caller, no inference needed.

## Acceptance

1. `data-display` is `reg-view`-registered (or equivalent frame-capture happens at mount time so dispatch/subscribe both target the surrounding frame).
2. Opening the App-DB panel and clicking any ▾ triangle visibly collapses it ON THE FIRST CLICK. Clicking the resulting ▸ visibly expands it ON THE FIRST CLICK. Repeat at every depth.

title: feat(flows): run flows immediately after the event handler (before rest of :after + before db-install/fx) — spec + impl + tracing
description: Mike-directed 2026-05-24. CHANGE the flow-execution point in the event pipeline. I.e. flows move from the current post-install drain step (today: full interceptor chain -> db commit -> run-flows! mutates live app-db -> fx) to an INNERMOST :after :db-effect transform right after the handler, before the other :after interceptors and before db-install. PRESERVED: :fx still sees flow outputs (flows step 2, fx step 4). CHANGES (intended): after-interceptors now see flow output; run-flows! transforms the pending :db effect rather than mutating installed app-db; trace db-changed now fires at install (after flows) not before. SPEC-FIRST (all hot-zone): spec/002-Frames.md (drain-loop pseudocode — relocate the run-flows! step), spec/013-Flows.md (Drain-integration section + the Trace-stream-ordering-on-flow-throw section ~155, rewrite so flows precede db-changed/install), spec/009-Instrumentation.md (trace ordering / emit points — define the canonical per-event trace sequence with flow :rf.flow/computed emitted after :rf.event/run-end and before :rf.event/db-changed[install]; db-changed reflects the flow-augmented db). TRACING must RECOGNISE the new ordering (Mike): emit flow + db-changed at the new points so the sequence is observable + Causa Trace panel can place flows right after the handler. IMPL: core/src/re_frame/router.cljc (drain loop ~line 469 — relocate the :flows/run-flows! invocation); flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc (run-flows! ~295 — transform pending :db effect in context vs mutate installed app-db); the do-fx/effects-install interceptor (install :db after flows + after-interceptors); epoch/trace emit. DOWNSTREAM (separate): Causa Trace-panel doc flow placement moves to right-after-handler.

title: fix(machines): guarded candidate-vector :after silently no-ops (only single-map/keyword resolved)
description: pick-after-transition in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc normalises the resolved :after value with only (if (keyword? t) {:target t} t) at lines 454 and 476. When the :after value is a guarded candidate-vector [{:guard g :target s} {:target s2}] (the same shape :on supports via normalize-on-clause lines 317-325), the vector is passed whole to resolve-hit: (:guard vector) returns nil so the guard passes vacuously, and :transition becomes the whole vector so downstream :target/:action read nil. Net: the after-elapsed timer fires with outcome :ok but no state change and no effects; the machine is stranded. Live repro: step-deck :ws/connection machine stuck in [:active :authenticating] (authenticating :after is the guarded form; connecting :after is single-map and transitions fine). Fix: resolve a guarded candidate-vector :after the same way :on does (walk candidates leaf order, first guard-pass wins; all-fail = guard-suppressed per Spec 005 multi-stage interaction with guard). Add regression test for guarded :after reaching both the pass target and the fallback target. Cross-check Spec 005 documents guarded :after.
acceptance_criteria: Fix resolves a guarded candidate-vector :after via the same candidate-walk semantics as :on (first guard-pass wins; all-fail with no unguarded fallback = guard-suppressed, no transition, sibling timers continue). Broaden machines unit tests to cover :after value forms exhaustively: (a) bare keyword target, (b) single map no guard, (c) single map guard-pass, (d) single map guard-fail = suppressed, (e) guarded vector first-guard-pass -> first target, (f) guarded vector first-fail -> unguarded fallback target + action, (g) guarded vector all-fail no fallback = suppressed, plus hierarchical (leaf vs parent epoch) and parallel-region-scoped guarded :after. Prefer one shared candidate-resolution helper between :after and :on. All machines tests green; clj-kondo clean.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2053 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2053). pick-after-transition now routes guarded candidate-vector :after values through the shared normalise-candidates + select-passing-candidate helpers used by :on, so the two slots cannot drift. Exhaustive :after value-form unit sweep added (re-frame.after-value-forms-test, cases a-i + on/after shared-walk proof; cases e-i reproduce the bug pre-fix), plus JVM + CLJS integration counterparts. spec/005 §Value shape tightened to document the guarded candidate-vector form normatively parallel to :on. title: fix(ci): pass github-token to all setup-clojure steps — stop anonymous GitHub-API rate-limit flakes
description: The recurring CI flakiness (re-run ~6-8x today, worsening) is NOT a flaky test — it is the DeLaGuardo/setup-clojure action hitting GitHub's ANONYMOUS API rate limit. ROOT CAUSE confirmed: 43 setup-clojure steps across .github/workflows/*.yml, ZERO pass a github-token. setup-clojure downloads tools (clojure/clj-kondo/etc.) via the GitHub releases API; unauthenticated calls hit the 60-req/hr anonymous limit, failing with 'Bad credentials' at the 'Set up Clojure CLI' step (and cascading to actions/checkout 'could not read Username for github.com'). It gets MORE frequent as more CI runs fire — matches the observed pattern all session. FIX: add 'github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}' to EVERY setup-clojure step (its supported input for authenticated API calls). Files: .github/workflows/test.yml (most steps), lint.yml, expensive-tests.yml, release.yml, release-causa.yml, template-release.yml — 43 steps total. ALSO investigate the actions/checkout 'could not read Username' failures (likely the same rate-limit cascade; if a separate checkout/submodule/ref-fetch config issue, note it). HOT-ZONE (.github/workflows/*) — SOLO, no other workflow worker. Verify YAML validity (actionlint if available). High value: removes the per-PR re-run tax that has slowed every merge today.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2047 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2047): added github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} to all 43 DeLaGuardo/setup-clojure steps across the 6 workflows. title: fix(testbed/step-deck): tab clicks don't navigate + navigate never updates the URL
description:
Mike found via the live step-deck testbed: clicking the feature tabs (Counter/Machine/Routing/Async) does NOTHING — no route change, URL stays http://localhost:8031/. Diagnosed with re-frame2-pair — TWO distinct bugs.

EVIDENCE:
- epoch-history :step-deck shows ONLY the 3 boot events; ZERO :rf.route/navigate events from tab clicks.
- A PROGRAMMATIC re-frame2-pair dispatch of [:rf.route/navigate :testdeck/machine] DID change the route slice (:rf/route :id -> :testdeck/machine) but the URL STAYED "/" (machine's :path is /machine; boot's :testdeck/counter /counter also never pushed).
- Tab inventory is correct: counter->/counter, machine->/machine, routing->/routing, async->/async.

BUG A — tab clicks don't dispatch:
testdeck/panel.cljs tab-bar (~line 319-329) does :on-click that dispatches [:rf.route/navigate id] via the frame-provider's INJECTED dispatch. In the step-deck single-frame mount (step_deck/core.cljs frame-provider ~line 218, [rf/frame-provider {:frame frame-id}]) the click fires no event. Root-cause how panel.cljs binds its dispatch vs how step_deck provides it (the two-frame testbed injects a per-frame dispatch; the step-deck mount may not, leaving the tab-bar's dispatch unbound / a no-op). NOTE: dispatching TO :step-deck works (the programmatic navigate landed) — so the bug is specifically the click->dispatch path in this mount, not the navigate handler.

BUG B — navigate doesn't update the URL:
The step-deck content frame is the NON-DEFAULT frame :step-deck. Per Spec 012, non-default frames default :url-bound? FALSE -> route changes are in-memory only, the URL is untouched. The step_deck/core.cljs comment (~line 49) WRONGLY assumes the default is :url-bound? true. The step-deck is single-frame and "owns the URL" per its own README, so it must be url-bound. FIX: pass :url-bound? true to the step-deck frame-provider (or mount the content in :rf/default).

VERIFY (re-frame2-pair; build examples/step-deck, nREPL port 51708, SHADOW_CLJS_BUILD_ID=examples/step-deck): after the fix, clicking a tab fires [:rf.route/navigate <id>] AND js/location updates to the tab's :path (/machine etc.); the browser back button works.

Disjoint from rf2-ad7zx.13 (theme/colour). Surfaces: tools/causa/testbeds/step_deck/core.cljs + possibly tools/causa/testbeds/testdeck/panel.cljs (the shared tab-bar dispatch).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2045 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2045). Root cause: :step-deck is a non-default frame, default :url-bound? false, so navigate stayed in-memory and URL never moved. Reported BUG A (clicks dont dispatch) does not exist - real-browser probe shows clicks DO navigate the slice; only the URL sync (BUG B) was broken. Fix: :rf/default opts out of URL ownership + :step-deck :url-bound? true. Made routing/url-owner-frame-id public + added ownership-transfer regression test.
