title: Spec: port the Causa visual design into tools/causa/spec (orange tokens · 5-region layout · 7 panel designs · visual encoding)
description:
# Causa UI — design brief (for Figma)

> Working draft. Purpose: a tight, unambiguous description of the Causa UI's shape so a
> designer (Figma) can lay it out. Causa is an information-dense ClojureScript developer
> tool (a re-frame2 inspector) — refined, utilitarian, high-density; not a marketing page.

## For the design tool (Figma Make)

**This brief is self-contained — you don't need (and can't use) the source repo.** Everything
needed to design Causa is in this document; design from this prompt. (A repo pointer wouldn't
help — the tool can't read a private/local codebase.) If you can, attach **screenshots of the
current Causa UI** as a "here's the starting point, redesign it" reference.

- **Medium:** a **desktop developer-tool panel** (docked sidecar or pop-out window), not a
  web page. Information-dense, keyboard-friendly. Support **dark and light themes**.
- **Aesthetic references** (tools you likely know): **re-frame-10x** and **Redux DevTools**
  for the inspector feel; the **Stately / xstate visualizer** for the Machine topology.
  Refined, utilitarian, high-density — *not* a marketing site, *not* generic AI styling.
- **Use the palette + type scale below — don't invent a generic one.**

### Palette (both themes; ship as CSS custom properties)

| token | role | dark | light |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bg-1` | deepest surface | `#15171B` | `#F1F3F6` |
| `bg-2` | panel surface | `#1B1E24` | `#FFFFFF` |
| `bg-3` | raised/strip | `#232730` | `#E6E9EE` |
| `border-subtle` | hairlines | `#232730` | `#E6E9EE` |
| `border-default` | controls | `#2F3441` | `#CFD4DC` |
| `text-primary` | body text | `#E8EAF0` | `#15171B` |
| `text-secondary` | labels/hints | `#A8AEC0` | `#4B5160` |
| `accent` | **brand + Dynamic** mode — **orange** (the dominant identity) | `#F97316` | `#EA580C` |
| `accent-static` | **Static** mode — cool complement (keeps the two modes legible) | `#43C3D0` | `#2A8B96` |
| `yellow` | filters / warnings | `#FBBF24` | `#B07A05` |

**Orange-forward identity:** `accent` (orange) is the brand colour — the **logo/wordmark, the
active tab, primary buttons, and the Dynamic-mode signal**. Surfaces stay neutral-dark so the
orange pops (optionally warm them a hair for cohesion). Keep `yellow` (warnings/filters)
clearly distinct from `accent` — they're close on the wheel; if they blur, cool the warning
toward gold (`#EAB308`). The export's generic GitHub-blue (`--devtools-active: #0969da`) must
become this orange. **All accents are single tokens** — `accent` (orange = Dynamic),
`accent-static` (cyan = Static) — so swapping the colour identity is a **one-line edit per
token, by design** (decision: keep cyan for Static, but make it that easy to change).

### Type scale (anchored at 13px)
`body` 13px · `body-tight` ~12px (header chrome) · `caption` ~11px (hints/labels) · `micro`
~10px (badges/tabs). Sans-serif for UI; **monospace for code / EDN values**.

## What Causa is

Causa is a **devtools sidecar for re-frame2** — an inspector/debugger that runs alongside a
live re-frame2 application and shows the developer *what the app is doing*, event by event.
It's the re-frame2 analogue of re-frame-10x / Redux DevTools, rebuilt around re-frame2's
model.

**re-frame2 in one paragraph (for designers who don't know it):** re-frame2 is a
ClojureScript UI framework with **unidirectional data flow**. All app state lives in one map
called **app-db**. **Events** (e.g. `[:counter-inc]`) are dispatched and handled to produce a
new app-db. **Subscriptions** ("subs") derive values from app-db; **views** (components)
render from subs and re-render when their subs' values change. re-frame2 also has **state
machines**, **routing**, and **flows** (declarative derived values). Each dispatched event is
processed to completion as one unit — Causa calls that unit an **epoch**.

**What Causa shows:** it observes the app's **trace stream** (every event, sub re-run, view
render, fx, machine transition, route change, error) plus app-db, groups it per epoch, and
presents it so a developer can answer: *what did this event do? what changed? what
re-rendered, and why? what's wrong?*

## Core mental model

- **The focused event (epoch) is the spine of the whole UI.** You pick one event in the
  **Event list** (Region 3); almost every tab below is a **lens on that one event** — its
  handler pipeline (Event), the resulting state (app-db), the reactive fallout (Views), the
  raw timeline (Trace), the machine transition (Machine), the navigation (Routes), the
  problems (Issues). Change the focused event and every lens updates together.
- **Dynamic vs Static** (the chrome-ribbon dropdown): **Dynamic** is the live, event-coupled
  inspection described above (focused-epoch lenses). **Static** is a registry-browse mode
  (explore the app's declared events / subs / machines / routes without a live event). **This
  brief describes the Dynamic surface.**
- **Frames.** A re-frame2 app can run multiple isolated **frames** (independent app-db +
  event loop). The **Frame dropdown** picks which frame you're inspecting — one at a time.
  Causa itself runs in its own `:rf/causa` frame, kept separate from the app's.

## Visual encoding (applies to every panel)

Carry meaning through the **strongest channel first**; treat little pictographic icons as at
most *secondary* reinforcement, never the primary signal:

- **Node state** (e.g. a sub recomputed vs unchanged) → **colour + emphasis on the node**:
  recomputed = bright/accent/filled; unchanged = dimmed/greyed/outline. A short text tag only
  if colour alone is ambiguous.
- **A relationship / short-circuit** → **edge style**: a cut/short-circuited dependency is a
  *dashed + greyed* (or visibly severed) edge — not a glyph beside it.
- **A count / sharing fact** (e.g. a sub read by N views) → the **topology** (multiple edges)
  plus a small **`×N`** number.
- **Naming something** (source kind, ids, labels) → **text, spelled out** (e.g. the event
  list's Source column reads `view` / `fx` / `timer`, not icons).
- **Accessibility:** never rely on a lone glyph *or* a lone colour — pair colour with
  shape/weight/text so meaning survives colour-blindness and unfamiliar symbols.

The ASCII sketches below use bracketed words like `[changed]` / `[no change]` only because
ASCII can't show colour — in the real design those are colour/emphasis per the above.

## Overall shape (top → bottom)

A single panel, stacked vertically:

```
┌ Chrome ribbon ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ❖ Causa   [Frame ▾]  [Dynamic / Static ▾]                        [⚙]   [✕]    │
├ Events ribbon ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Events:  [◀ ▶ ⏭]  [🎯 focus]   [pill] [pill] [+]            [Clear Filters]    │
├ Event list  (6 rows default, drag bottom edge ↕ to resize) ────────────────────┤
│  source │ event id          │ timestamp      │ duration                         │
├ Tabs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ [Event]  app-db   Views   Trace   Machine   Routes   Issues                     │
├ Panel content (active tab) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│   (… to be described …)                                                          │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Region 1 — Chrome ribbon (top, compact)
The thin top strip. Houses global selectors + window controls; deliberately short.
- **Left:** the **Causa logo / wordmark** (top-left brand anchor), then a **Frame**
  single-select dropdown, then a **Dynamic / Static** single-select dropdown (compact,
  understated — occasional use).
- **Right:** `⚙` settings, `✕` close.

### Region 2 — Events ribbon (just below)
Header bar for the event list.
- **Left:** the label `Events:`, then the nav cluster `[◀ ▶ ⏭]` (prev / next / fast-forward),
  then the focus-chip `🎯`, then the active filter pills (and a `[+]` to add one).
- **Right:** `Clear Filters`.

### Region 3 — Event list
A compact, scannable **table** — one row per event, newest at the bottom. **6 rows
visible by default; the bottom edge is a drag handle for vertical resize** (drag down to
show more history).

Columns, left → right:

| Column | Contents |
|---|---|
| **Source** | what triggered the event, written as a short **text label** (not an icon) — `view` · `fx` · `timer` · `machine` · … |
| **Event id** | the dispatched event keyword, e.g. `:title/flow`. |
| **Timestamp** | when it fired. |
| **Duration** | how long the event took to process. |

```
┌ Event list  (6 rows default · drag bottom edge ↕ to resize) ───────────┐
│ source │ event id          │ timestamp      │ duration │
│ fx     │ :title/flow       │ 12:30:05.123   │  1.2 ms  │
│ view   │ :counter-inc      │ 12:30:06.456   │  0.4 ms  │
│ timer  │ :poll/tick        │ 12:30:07.001   │  0.2 ms  │
│  …                                          ↕ resize edge │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Region 4 — Tab strip
A horizontal strip of tabs that selects which detail panel shows below. One active at a
time. Tabs, left → right:

  **Event · app-db · Views · Trace · Machine · Routes · Issues**

```
┌ Tabs ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ [Event]  app-db   Views   Trace   Machine   Routes   Issues             │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Region 5 — Panel content (the active tab's panel)
Each tab renders its own panel into the content area. Walking through each:

#### Event tab — "how the event got handled"
A vertical sequence of sections, top → bottom:

1. **Dispatch** — shows the **entire** event vector, in full, e.g. `[:something {…}]` (all
   of it, not truncated). And the event's **source**: a label + click-to-source coord —
   e.g. `source: view [source.code.cljs:34]`.

2. **Before Interceptors** *(optional — only when present)* — the non-standard interceptors
   in the chain (the `:before` phase, e.g. coeffect injection): each by **name** + a
   **↗source link**, plus the **coeffects they injected** (id + value). Bookends with
   **After Interceptors** below. *(Per-interceptor context diffs are NOT available — see
   Data availability.)*

3. **DB Handler** / **FX Handler** — the event handler's **syntax-highlighted code**, shown
   in a code block. Includes a **button to jump to the source code** (opens the handler's
   source file).

4. **DB Changes** — a **diff-like view** of the changes the event handler made to app-db.

5. **After Interceptors** *(optional — only when non-standard interceptors ran)* — lists
   the non-standard interceptors, each with its **name** and a **source-code link**.

6. **Flows** *(optional)* — outlines what **flows** ran and the **DB changes** they made.

7. **FX** — lists the **fx handlers** that ran (the effects the event produced).

**Outcome badge + halted/error state.** The panel header carries an **outcome badge** —
`ok` · **`error`** · `rolled-back` · `flow-error`. When a step **throws or rolls back**, the
pipeline **halts there**: that section renders the **exception inline** (message + ↗source to
the throwing line) and the **downstream sections are shown *not-run*** (dimmed / "skipped —
cascade halted"), not merely absent. Example — a throwing handler: Dispatch + Before-Interceptors
shown, **Handler shows the exception**, then **DB Changes / After-Interceptors / Flows / FX =
not-run**, badge **`error`**. This is what makes a failed event legible vs. a clean one.
(Data: `:rf.error/*` carries the exception + responsible-handler coord; the epoch carries the
outcome.)

```
┌ Event panel ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ DISPATCH                                                  │
│   [:something {…}]                                        │
│   source: view  [source.code.cljs:34]                    │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ BEFORE INTERCEPTORS      (optional)                       │
│   :inject-now [icpt.cljs:8 ↗]    coeffects: :now = …      │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ DB HANDLER                               [ ↗ source ]     │
│   (rf/reg-event-db :something  …)    ← syntax-highlighted │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ DB CHANGES                                                │
│   - [:a :b] 1 → 2     + [:c] "new"     (diff view)        │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ AFTER INTERCEPTORS       (optional)                       │
│   :my-interceptor   [interceptors.cljs:12 ↗]             │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ FLOWS                    (optional)                       │
│   :totals-flow  → [:totals] recomputed                   │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ FX                                                        │
│   :dispatch → [:title/flow …]    :http-xhrio → …         │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data availability (Event panel)** — what the trace actually supports, so nobody designs
for data that isn't there:
- **Fully traced:** Dispatch (event vector + source), DB Changes (diff), FX (handlers +
  returned vector), Flows (what ran + `:path` + new value).
- **Interceptors are registry-derived** (the chain), shown as name + ↗source. There is **no
  per-interceptor runtime trace and no per-interceptor context diff.** The Before section's
  real substance is the **coeffects injected** (id + value), which IS traced. (re-frame
  interceptors are one chain with optional `:before`/`:after` phases — the Before/After
  split is presentational, not two separate runtime lists.)
- **Handler source code** rides `:rf.handler/source` (rf2-xgfuy, in flight) — a
  `<source not yet captured>` placeholder shows until it lands; the jump-to-source coord
  works now.

#### app-db tab — the current app-db, sectioned by area
The complete app-db rendered as **vertical sections, each a cljs-devtools widget**
(collapsible tree). Sectioned by reserved `:rf/*` area (per Conventions §Reserved app-db
keys):

- **App state** (TOP) — the app-db **minus** every reserved `:rf/*` key (the application's
  own state).
- **Machines** — `:rf/machines` **fans out: one section per machine**, headed by the
  machine id (e.g. `:title/flow`). (Each machine separate, as you said.)
- **Spawned** — `:rf/spawned` fans out the same way, one section per spawned instance.
- **Route** — `:rf/route` is a **single section** (singleton — the current-route slice; NOT
  fanned out).
- **Other reserved singletons** — `:rf/system-ids`, `:rf/pending-navigation`,
  `:rf/elision` — one section each.
- Every reserved area renders **even when absent/empty** (empty-state placeholder).

**Every** section's value renders as a cljs-devtools-style collapsible inspector widget —
App state, **each machine**, Route, and every reserved singleton alike (not just App state).

> Note: Machines and Route also have their own dedicated tabs (richer, specialized views).
> The app-db tab is deliberately the **raw, complete state** view — it shows everything,
> sectioned, including those reserved areas.

```
┌ app-db panel  (every ▸ value is a cljs-devtools widget) ───┐
│ APP STATE                                                 │
│   ▸ {:counter 2, :user {…}}                               │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ MACHINE :title/flow                                       │
│   ▸ {:state :loaded, …}                                   │
│ MACHINE :other/flow                                       │
│   ▸ {…}                                                   │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ ROUTE                                                     │
│   ▸ {:id :home, :params {…}}                              │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ SYSTEM-IDS · PENDING-NAVIGATION · ELISION   (one each)    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### Views tab — what re-rendered, and why
**This tab is about the Views.** For the focused epoch it answers: **which views re-rendered
and why** — backed by the reactive graph that caused them (`app-db → Level-1 subs →
(optional) Level-2 subs → Views`). It also shows **where the cascade short-circuited** (a sub
whose value didn't change stops everything downstream) and **which subscriptions are shared
across multiple views**.

**Layout — a left → right graph:**
- **app-db** — a **single source node** labelled `app-db`, with an **arrow to each Level-1
  sub** (every Level-1 sub reads app-db). No path detail — just the fan-out.
- **Level-1 subs** (extractors): the ones that re-ran, each with changed/unchanged state.
- **Level-2 subs** (derived via `:<-`; *optional* layer).
- **Views** (right-most — **the focus**): each component, tagged re-rendered + *why*.

Edges `Level-1 → Level-2 → View` are precise (`:<-` topology / `:rf.sub/cause-sub` /
`:rf.sub/reader-render-key`). **Shared subscriptions fall out of the graph:** a sub with edges
to **two or more views** is a shared sub — highlight it (the "one sub drives N views"
insight). **Flows** (where present) keep precise `app-db-path → flow` edges since flows
declare `:inputs`.

**Node state — what each node did this epoch (the crux):**
- **Recomputed** (value changed) → highlighted/active; propagation continues downstream.
- **Unchanged / skipped** → dimmed + a "no change" marker, and its **downstream edges are
  visually cut** — this is the "Level-1 didn't change, so nothing below re-ran" story.
- **Not involved** this epoch → omitted or very faint.

**Views column** also says *why* each view re-rendered: **reactive** (a sub it derefs
changed — name those subs) vs **parent re-render** (structural — no own sub changed).

```
┌ Views panel  (what re-rendered & why · focused epoch) ─────────────────────┐
│  app-db ─┬─► ::counter [changed] ──► ::counter-parity ─► counter-view (reactive) │
│          └─► ::title-state [no change] ╌╌╌  (downstream short-circuited)    │
│                                                                            │
│  app-db ───► ::session [changed] ─┬─► header-view (reactive)   ×2 (shared) │
│                                   └─► sidebar-view (reactive)              │
│                                                                            │
│  Views (right) are the focus — each: re-rendered + why (a sub it reads     │
│  changed = reactive · parent re-render = structural).                      │
│  Real UI (colour/edge, NOT glyphs): [changed]=bright/accent ·             │
│  [no change]=dimmed · short-circuit=dashed-grey edge · ×N=shared sub       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data availability** (live-verified — `:rf.*` names, post-migration):
- **Recomputed subs:** `:rf.sub/run` — `:rf.sub/value-changed?`, `:rf.sub/prev-value` /
  `:rf.sub/value`, **`:rf.sub/cause-sub`** (sub→sub edge; **nil ⇒ Level-1**, non-nil ⇒
  Level-2), **`:rf.sub/reader-render-key`** (sub→view edge).
- **app-db source:** `:rf.event/db-changed` + the epoch db-diff (the changed paths).
- **Views:** `:rf.view/rendered` — `:rf.view/render-key` / `:rf.view/id` / `:rf.view/mount?`.
- **Per-epoch aggregate:** `:rf.cascade/captured` (subs recomputed/skipped, flows
  computed/skipped, views rendered).

**Constraints (the design above is shaped around these):**
1. **app-db → Level-1 is a plain fan-out, not path-wired.** re-frame subs read app-db
   imperatively; nothing records which paths a sub reads (`sub-topology` `:inputs` is empty
   for Level-1; the trace records re-runs + value-changes, not paths). So `app-db` is one
   node with an arrow to each Level-1 sub. Only **flows** declare `:inputs` paths → precise
   app-db-path → flow.
2. **`:rf.view/rendered` carries no deref-subs list** (live: only render-key/id/frame/
   mount?). The sub→view link comes from `:rf.sub/reader-render-key`, which names only the
   **triggering** view of a recompute — **not all readers**. So BOTH the per-view
   "reactive-vs-parent" reason AND **shared-subscription detection** (which views read a
   given sub) need the deref-subs sink (spec'd, absent in the build) or sub-cache reader
   introspection. **Candidate bead — it now blocks two Views-tab features.**
3. **`:rf.sub/skip`** (explicit "considered, didn't recompute") fired 0× in the testbed run
   — skip-nodes appear only when skips happen; `:rf.sub/value-changed? false` carries the
   changed/not story regardless.

#### Trace tab — the complete raw timeline (focused epoch)
**Purpose:** Event is the curated story; Views is the reactive DAG; **Trace is the complete,
chronological, timed raw stream** for the focused epoch — the firehose you drop to when the
curated views don't answer the question. Its value is **completeness + order + timing +
raw-detail access**, not re-structuring (that's Event's job).

**Design:**
1. **Readable lines, not raw op-types.** Each event rendered as plain language —
   `dispatched [:counter-inc]` · `db changed [:counter] 1→2` · `sub ::counter recomputed
   1→2` · `view counter-view rendered` · `fx :dispatch → [:title/flow]` · `machine
   :title/flow idle→loading`. The raw `:operation` + tag-map is **expandable detail**, not
   the default line.
2. **Colour-band by op-family** (per Visual encoding): event-dominoes · reactive (sub/view)
   · machine · flow · fx · error — so you can scan the epoch's shape at a glance.
3. **Timing is the payoff** Event doesn't give: relative timestamp + per-op duration, in
   true chronological order — sequence *and* cost.
4. **Collapse noise, don't filter.** The reactive aftermath (the many `:rf.sub/run` /
   `:rf.view/render`) collapses under one expandable group — `▸ reactive aftermath
   (12 subs, 7 renders)` — so the core dominoes stand out. (No filter chrome — collapsible
   groups, consistent with the #1958 rework that removed Trace filtering.)
5. **Causal nesting.** Indent child dispatches under their parent (the cascade tree) so
   structure is visible even in the raw view.

```
┌ Trace panel  (raw timeline · focused epoch) ──────────────────────────────┐
│ t+0.0ms   dispatched  [:counter-inc]                          0.4 ms      │
│ t+0.1ms   db changed  [:counter] 1 → 2                                     │
│ t+0.2ms   fx :dispatch → [:title/flow [:rf/init]]                          │
│ t+0.3ms   ▸ reactive aftermath (2 subs, 1 render)         ← collapsible    │
│ t+0.5ms   machine :title/flow  idle → loading                             │
│           └─ dispatched [:title/loaded]   (child cascade, indented)        │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│  colour-banded by op-family · click a row → expand raw :operation + tags  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data availability** — the panel just renders the focused epoch's `:trace-events`, so it is
inherently **complete**. Every event carries `:time` (→ chronological order + relative
timestamps) and `:op-type` (→ family colour); the readable line is a per-op-type template
over the event's tags. **Per-op duration** is available for the event-emit / `:rf.fx/do-fx`
steps (they carry elapsed timing); reactive ops (`:rf.sub/run`, `:rf.view/render`) are
point-in-time emits with no duration — show a timestamp, not a bar, for those.

#### Machine tab — the focused event's state-machine lens (event-driven)
**Aim:** **xstate / Stately-level topology rendering** of the state machine — including
**nested (compound) states**, **guards**, **actions**, and the live transition. This is a
**lens on the focused event**, not a machine browser.

**Behaviour (event-driven only):**
- **BLANK** when the focused event is **not** machine-related (silent-by-default).
- **When the focused event triggered a transition** → one section **per machine involved**.
- **prev/next** walks the epoch-history to the prior/next event **for the focused machine**
  (not the full spine).

**The topology chart (the centrepiece) — xstate/Stately quality:**
- **All states as a hierarchical graph** — sized nodes, arrowheads, ELK layout.
- **Nested / compound states** drawn as **containers** (parent boxes enclosing children),
  with initial-state markers.
- **FROM → TO transition highlighted** for the focused event (dashed-origin / bold-landing);
  the current/active state marked.
- **Guards & actions on the edges** — the guard condition + whether it passed, the actions
  that ran — plus per-transition guard/action result lists below.
- **Cancellation cascade** inline (when the transition triggered one); **`:after` countdown
  rings** overlay (when armed timers exist).
- **It must fill the available panel height** — the topology is the point; no fixed small box.

```
┌ Machine panel  (focused event = :title/flow [:rf/init]) ──────────────────┐
│  machine :title/flow                       ◀ prev   next ▶  (this machine) │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │  ┌─ active (compound) ─────────────────────┐                        │  │
│  │  │  (idle) ═FROM═► ((loading)) ──► (loaded) │   ← nested container   │  │
│  │  │           guard token? [pass] · do fetch!│                        │  │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘  ──► (error)          │  │
│  │       large ELK graph · fills the panel · FROM→TO highlighted        │  │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│  guards: token? [pass]    actions: [fetch!]    after: ◴ ring 5s → :timeout │
│                                                                           │
│  (BLANK when the focused event isn't machine-related)                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Live defects (filed rf2-zdfbm):** the panel currently (1) **inverts visibility** — blank
on machine events, shows on non-machine (opposite of the spec above; likely tied to the
rf2-rly4a epoch-correlation regression), and (2) caps the topology at a **fixed 320px**
leaving whitespace. The design above is the target once those land.

#### Routes tab — current route, this-epoch navigation, the route map
Routing's analogue of the Machine tab: a **map of routes** plus the live navigation. Unlike
the pure event-driven panels, most of this is **persistent context** (current route + table)
with one **event-driven** section (the navigation that happened this epoch).

**Three stacked sections:**
1. **Current route** (always shown) — the active route **id**, its **params**, and the
   **matched path / URL**. The "where am I."
2. **Navigation this epoch** (event-driven lens) — when the focused event navigated, show
   **FROM route → TO route**, the **params diff**, and the **outcome**: *transitioned* ·
   *blocked* (+ reason) · *cancelled* · *not-found*. Quiet/absent when the focused event
   isn't a navigation.
3. **Route table** — all **registered routes** (id → path pattern), drawn as a **tree when
   routes are nested** (else a flat list), with the **current route highlighted** and the
   focused navigation's FROM→TO marked on it (parallels the Machine topology's transition
   highlight). Click a route → its definition / source coord.

```
┌ Routes panel ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ CURRENT ROUTE                                                             │
│   :user/profile    params {:id 42}    /users/42                           │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ NAVIGATION THIS EPOCH        (event-driven · quiet when not a nav)        │
│   :dashboard ──► :user/profile   params {:id 42}   outcome: transitioned  │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ ROUTE TABLE    (registered · current highlighted · tree when nested)      │
│   :home                /                                                   │
│   :dashboard           /dashboard                                         │
│   ▸ :users             /users                                             │
│       :user/profile    /users/:id          ◀ current                      │
│   :settings            /settings                                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data availability** — fully supported (Spec 012 routing + Spec 009 route traces):
- **Current route + params:** `[:rf.route/id]` / `[:rf.route/params]` subs + the `:rf/route`
  app-db slice.
- **Registered routes:** the route registry (`:rf.causa/registered-routes`).
- **This-epoch navigation:** route trace ops in the focused epoch — `:rf.route/activated` /
  `:rf.route/deactivated` (FROM→TO), `:rf.route/navigation-blocked` / `:rf.route/not-found` /
  `:rf.route/cancel` (outcomes), `:rf.route/transitioned` (success).

#### Issues tab — "what's wrong in this epoch?"
A focused-epoch lens on **errors, warnings, and advisories**: reads only the focused epoch's
`:trace-events`, projects the issue subset. Silent-by-default — a clean epoch shows a calm
positive state, not an error look.

**Rows** — one per issue, **severity-coded by colour** (per Visual encoding):
`severity · category · short description · timestamp · ↗source`
- **error** — handler/sub/fx exception, no-such-sub, flow-eval, etc. (strongest colour).
- **warning** — plain-fn-under-non-default-frame, missing-doc, etc.
- **advisory** — fx skipped-on-platform, SSR hydration mismatch, cofx skipped, etc.

**Interactions:**
- **Click a row** → selects the parent dispatch and **pivots to the Event panel** (see the
  full cascade that produced the issue).
- **Click the ↗source coord** → opens the responsible handler at `file:line`.

**Empty / edge states (silent-by-default):**
- **No issues** → "No issues in this epoch." (calm, positive — not an error look).
- **Epoch evicted** → "Epoch evicted from buffer. Increase `:epoch-history` to retain more."
- **No epoch focused** → cold-start placeholder.

**Cross-epoch:** this panel is the *per-epoch* detail — there is **no aggregate-across-epochs
list**. Instead the **L2 event list carries a subtle issue marker** on rows whose epoch has
issues (a row tint / small dot, not a new column), so you can navigate to the troubled epoch
and open Issues there.

```
┌ Issues panel  ("what's wrong in this epoch?") ────────────────────────────┐
│ ERROR     handler-exception   :counter-inc threw …          12:30:05  ↗   │
│ WARNING   missing-doc         sub ::counter has no :doc      12:30:05  ↗   │
│ ADVISORY  fx-skipped          :rf.nav/scroll skipped (node)  12:30:05  ↗   │
│ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────│
│  click a row → Event panel (the cascade)  ·  click ↗ → source file:line   │
│                                                                           │
│  clean epoch →  "No issues in this epoch."                                 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Data availability** — fully traced: `:error` / `:warning` op-types, with the specific
identity in `:operation` (`:rf.error/*`, `:rf.warning/*`) and advisories (`:rf.fx/skipped-
on-platform`, `:rf.ssr/*`, `:rf.cofx/*`). Each error carries the responsible handler's source
coord (`:rf.trace/trigger-handler`) for jump-to-source, and rides the cascade's `:dispatch-id`
so the row → Event pivot works.

title: Causa Machines panel: inverted visibility (blank on machine events, shows on non-machine) + topology surface fixed at 320px (whitespace)
description:
Two defects in the Dynamic Machines panel (`machine_inspector.cljs`), observed live in the
parallel-frames testbed.

## 1. Inverted visibility (P1)
Per the panel's own spec (`machine_inspector.cljs:4-15`, Mike's 2026-05-19 redesign) the
Dynamic Machines panel is **event-driven only**:
- **BLANK** when the focused event is **not** machine-related (silent-by-default), and
- **shows the machine** (topology + FROM/TO transition highlight, guards/actions,
  cancellation cascade, `:after` rings) **when the focused event triggered a transition**.

Observed: the **inverse** — the panel shows content on events that are NOT machine-related,
and is blank on events that ARE (e.g. `:title/flow`).

Likely cause: the machine-detection is **focused-epoch-scoped** (it reads the focused
epoch's `:trace-events` for machine transitions). It is very likely entangled with the
**focus.epoch-id correlation regression (rf2-rly4a)** — if focus resolves to the wrong/nil
epoch, "did a transition fire this epoch?" misfires, producing the inverted/off-by-one
behaviour. Also check whether `machine_inspector` actually gates on "machine-related?"
before rendering the topology, vs always rendering `topology_view`'s Case-B blank-state
topology (which would explain "shows on non-machine events").

**Verify after rf2-rly4a lands**; if it persists, the inversion is local to the panel's
machine-relatedness gate.

## 2. Topology surface too small (P2)
`topology_view.cljs` renders the chart at a **fixed `height "320px"`** (default at :119,
applied at :174). The Machines panel has plenty of vertical space, so the chart sits in a
small box with whitespace around it. The topology is the centrepiece (xstate/Stately-level)
— it should **fill the available panel height** (flex / 100% within the panel), not a fixed
320px. Caller (`machine_inspector`) should pass a fill height or the chart should flex.

## Files
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/machine_inspector.cljs` (visibility gate)
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/machines/topology_view.cljs:119/174` (height)
- `:rf.causa/machine-inspector-data` sub (the focused-machine detection)

## Repro
parallel-frames → focus a machine event (`:title/flow`): panel is blank (should show the
machine). Focus a non-machine event (`:counter-inc`): panel shows content (should be blank).
Topology, when shown, is a small 320px box with whitespace below.

## Acceptance
- Blank on non-machine events; on a machine-transition event, the focused machine's topology
  renders with FROM→TO highlight.
- The topology chart fills the panel's available height (no dead whitespace).
close_reason: Landed in PR #1978: inversion was a LOCAL gate bug (rf2-t5wp9 #1757 made blank-state render an all-machines topology, surfacing content on non-machine events) — NOT rly4a-residual. Restored truly-blank affordance; focused-event chart + topology_view now flex to fill panel height (320px->100% + min-height floor). +gate-polarity tests incl. migrated :rf.machine/transition op detection. test:cljs 0 fail, causa-feature-gate 13/13.

title: Causa regression: Views + Trace panels empty after refresh — focus.epoch-id correlation returns nil (epoch-scoped panels starved)
description:
## Symptom

After a page refresh, Causa's **Views and Trace panels show nothing** (parallel-frames
testbed). The app itself works (epochs land, app-db updates).

## NOT the keyword migration

Ruled out: the running build's trace op-types are still the OLD set (`:sub/run`,
`:view/render`, `:event`, …) — the in-flight rf2-y4qpy.2 substrate rename is NOT in the
build. So the `:rf.*` migration is not the cause.

## Root cause (mechanism, live-verified port 51708)

Views/Trace are epoch-scoped: `:rf.causa/reactive-data` and `:rf.causa/trace-feed` read
the **focused epoch RECORD** via `focus.epoch-id`. The break:

- `:rf.causa/focus` = `{:dispatch-id 5, :epoch-id nil, :frame :below, :head? true, …}` —
  **`:epoch-id` is nil**. The cascade→epoch-history correlation in the `:rf.causa/focus`
  sub (spine.cljs) is returning nil.
- Consequently `:rf.causa/reactive-data` = `{:has-cascade? false, :subs-ran 0,
  :views-rendered 0, :view-rows 0, …}` → Views renders empty; Trace likewise.

The substrate side is HEALTHY:
- `(epoch-history :below)` = epoch-ids `[3 4]`, trace-counts `[6 19]` — records intact,
  reactive events folded into them by the harvest.
- `:rf.epoch/snapshotted` events present with `{:frame :epoch-id :event-id}` (no
  `:dispatch-id`, which is per Spec 009 — not the issue).

Earlier THIS session the same focus correctly bridged dispatch-id 5 → epoch-id 4 and the
panels populated — so this is a regression introduced by a merge that landed during the
session.

### Secondary (by-design, NOT the bug — documented to prevent a wrong fix)
`group-cascades` (projection.cljc:137) keys cascades purely on `:dispatch-id`
(`(or (dispatch-id ev) :ungrouped)`). Reactive sub/run + view/render events fire post-RtC
with **nil dispatch-id**, so they correctly land in `:ungrouped` (observed: `:ungrouped`
holds 17 subs / 9 renders; cascades 2–5 hold 0). This is expected — the panels read the
epoch RECORD, not the grouped cascade, so don't "fix" group-cascades. The fix is the
`focus.epoch-id` correlation.

## Suspect merges (this session) — bisect to confirm
- **rf2-avvwm** (orphan `:frame/created` attribution) — changed the epoch settle/harvest
  (epoch-record assembly). PRIME suspect: if it altered the epoch-record shape/keys the
  focus sub correlates against, the cascade→epoch match breaks.
- **rf2-2qaqh / #1964** (tool-frame trace gate) — `:rf/causa` now has 0 epochs/0 trace.
  Its trace.cljc diff only changes the emit GUARD (adds the frame-disabled `or`), not
  tag-merging — so less likely, but in scope.
- **rf2-j8m01** (counter-inc cascade) — verify it didn't touch the focus/projection path
  (didn't appear in `git log` of core trace files; may have closed as dup of avvwm).

avvwm/j8m01 did NOT touch `re-frame/trace*` / `subs/memo` / `router` (per git log of those
files) — so the regression is most plausibly avvwm's epoch-record change interacting with
the `:rf.causa/focus` correlation, OR a Causa-side focus-sub assumption broken by the new
record shape.

## Fix locus
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/spine.cljs` — `:rf.causa/focus` sub (~724) and its
  epoch-id derivation (cascade ↔ epoch-history correlation). Identify what key it matches
  on and why it now yields nil.
- Cross-check the epoch-record shape produced after rf2-avvwm vs what the focus sub expects.
- `tools/causa/src/.../panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs` (`project-record`) +
  `panels/trace.cljs` (trace-feed) read the record by epoch-id — confirm once focus is fixed.

## Repro + acceptance
1. parallel-frames testbed → refresh → leave focus on the head (LIVE).
2. `@(rf/subscribe [:rf.causa/focus])` in the `:rf/causa` frame should have a **non-nil
   `:epoch-id`**; today it's nil.
3. `@(rf/subscribe [:rf.causa/reactive-data])` should have `:has-cascade? true` with
   non-zero `:subs-ran` / `:views-rendered`; today all zero.
4. Views + Trace panels render rows.

## Bisect plan
Against the repro above, revert/inspect rf2-avvwm first (epoch-record change), then #1964.
The check is a one-liner: focus `:epoch-id` non-nil + reactive-data `:has-cascade? true`.

## Evidence (live, port 51708, parallel-frames)
- focus: `{:dispatch-id 5 :epoch-id nil :frame :below :head? true}`
- reactive-data: `{:has-cascade? false :subs-ran 0 :views-rendered 0 :view-rows 0}`
- cascades: `[:ungrouped 2 3 4 5]`; subs/renders: ungrouped 17/9, cascades 2–5 all 0/0.
- below epoch-history: epoch-ids `[3 4]`, trace-counts `[6 19]`.
- below sub/run tags: `[:cause-sub :frame :cascade? :prev-value :value :sub-id

title: Causa: redesign top two ribbons (chrome + events) + frame-as-view-scope + mode dropdown
description:
# Causa — redesign the top two ribbons (chrome + events), frame-as-view-scope, fix the X

## TL;DR

Reshape the top of the Causa Dynamic shell into **two clean strata** and make it look
genuinely good (use the `frontend-design` skill — see Design direction):

1. **Chrome ribbon** (top, made shorter): on the LEFT, a **Frame** single-select
   dropdown and a **Dynamic / Static** single-select dropdown. On the RIGHT, the `⚙`
   settings button and the `✕` close button — **and make the `✕` actually work** (it's
   currently a no-op).
2. **Events ribbon** (below it): on the LEFT, the label `Events:` then the
   `[◀ ▶ ⏭]` nav cluster, the focus-chip, and the active filter pills (+ the add-pill
   widget). On the far RIGHT, a **Clear Filters** button.
3. **Frame is a view scope, not a filter** — single frame at a time, defaulted, chosen
   from the dropdown; never a filter pill, never counted as "hidden", never reset by
   Clear Filters.

This supersedes the earlier `ai/prompt/causa-events-filter-ribbon.md` (delete that). It
refines **rf2-jvghz** (the hidden-by-filters indicator) and must sequence after
**rf2-swclw** (persistence — see Coordination).

Pre-alpha masterpiece posture: breaking changes fine, **no shims**. Correctness +
elegance. Stay inside Causa's existing token system and the density-is-binding rule
(`tools/causa/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §0) — do NOT import a generic web
aesthetic.

---

## Desired end state (layout)

```
┌ Chrome ribbon  (compact — shorter than today) ───────────────────────────────┐
│ [Frame ▾]  [Dynamic ▾]                                          [⚙]   [✕]     │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌ Events ribbon ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Events:  [◀ ▶ ⏭]  [🎯 focus-chip]  [+pill] [×pill] [+]      2 hidden  [Clear Filters] │
│   (the "2 hidden" message + Clear Filters appear ONLY when filters are active)         │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌ Event list — rows for the SELECTED frame ─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  …                                                                             │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Left = state/selectors + navigation; Right = actions. No "Frame:" chip anywhere in the
filter chrome. The **"N events hidden by filters" message (rf2-jvghz) is kept and valued**
— Mike likes it. Retain its prominent yellow-accented styling; it appears in the events
ribbon whenever `N > 0` (placement in Decisions). It must reflect ONLY pill/mute
filtering now, never frame scope.

---

## Workstream A — Chrome ribbon (the top strip)

Current L1 `ribbon` defn: `shell.cljs` ~682-760. Today it carries mode-pill,
nav-cluster, focus-chip, frame-picker, AND the filter pills. New composition:

- **LEFT cluster:**
  - **Frame dropdown** — the existing single-select picker (`frame_switcher.cljs`,
    `rf-causa-ribbon-frame-picker`, `:rf.causa/select-frame` / `:rf.causa/current-frame`
    / `:rf.causa/available-frames`). Keep its behaviour; restyle per Design direction.
  - **Dynamic / Static dropdown** — convert `static/mode_pill.cljs` from its two-button
    pill (`rf-causa-mode-pill-<mode>`, lines ~116/129) into a single-select `<select>`
    with options `Dynamic` / `Static` (labels already exist, lines 65-66). Reuse the
    existing mode-switch dispatch; only the control shape changes. **DESIGN INTENT
    (Mike):** the current pill is *too dominant for an occasional-use control* — the
    dropdown must be compact and understated, matching the frame picker's weight, not a
    prominent element. **Keep the mode accent signal** — the left-edge ribbon stripe
    (rf2-o5f5f.1, `stripe-hex-for-mode`, `shell.cljs` ~741) stays as the
    violet(Dynamic)/cyan(Static) cue (that quiet stripe carries the signal so the control
    itself can recede).
- **RIGHT cluster** — the right-icons group (`shell.cljs` ~637-667):
  - `⚙` settings (`rf-causa-icon-settings` → `:rf.causa/settings-open`) — keep.
  - `✕` close (`rf-causa-icon-close` → `:rf.causa/close-shell`) — **FIX (see below)**.
- **MOVE OUT to the events ribbon:** nav-cluster (`ribbon-nav-cluster`), focus-chip
  (`ribbon-focus-chip`, ~554-565), and the filter pills (`ribbon-filter-pills`,
  508-520, removed from line 757).
- **Reduce height** — the strip is much emptier now. Lower `(:top-strip-height layout)`
  (theme/layout) to a compact value; reclaim the vertical space for the event list.

### The `✕` bug (must fix)
`:rf.causa/close-shell` (`registry.cljs:420-425`) only does `(assoc db :close-requested?
true)` — a reactive flag with a comment claiming "mount.cljs reads the slot to drive the
CSS-only hide", but **nothing consumes it**, so the X does nothing. `mount.cljs` already
has a real hide (`hide-shell`, ~535; the `display:none` mechanism at ~215; the toggle at
~546). Wire the X to it: e.g. make `:rf.causa/close-shell` a `reg-event-fx` that fires a
`:rf.causa/hide-shell` effect calling `mount/hide-shell`, OR have mount observe
`:close-requested?` and hide. Keep the reactive flag for tests. Verify the
`Ctrl+Shift+C` keybinding path closes too. (Also sanity-check the `⚙` button — note
there are two settings events, `:rf.causa/open-settings` in registry.cljs:415 and
`:rf.causa/settings-open` in settings/events.cljs:53; make sure the button hits the live
one. The user reports settings works — don't change behaviour, just don't regress it.)

---

## Workstream B — Events ribbon

Repurpose `filters-hidden-indicator` (`shell.cljs:1346`, mounted ~1502 in the
`event-list` view above the scroll container) into the always-present **events ribbon**.
Rename it (e.g. `events-ribbon`; container testid `rf-causa-events-ribbon`). Render
order, left → right:

1. `Events:` label.
2. `[◀ ▶ ⏭]` nav cluster (`ribbon-nav-cluster`, moved from chrome — it already drives
   `:rf.causa/focus-cascade-prev/next/head` over the filtered list).
3. focus-chip (`ribbon-focus-chip`, moved from chrome — `🎯 <pivot> ✕`,
   `:rf.causa/clear-focus`).
4. active filter pills + trailing `[+]` add-pill — the interactive `filter-pills/
   pills-view` (`filters/pills.cljs`), moved down. This REPLACES the old read-only
   cause-chips (don't render both).
6. **Right-side action cluster** (far right) — the **`N events hidden by filters`
   message** immediately left of the **Clear Filters** button (`:rf.causa/clear-all-
   filters`). Visibility (Mike):
   - **Both are absent when there are no active filters** (no pills, no mutes) — the
     right side is empty in the clean/default state.
   - When filters ARE active, the Clear Filters button shows; the message shows beside it
     **only when `N > 0`** (an active filter that hides nothing → button present, message
     absent). Keep the rf2-jvghz yellow-accent styling on the message; it counts pill/mute
     suppression only (frame scope excluded per Workstream C).

Pure hiccup (Causa panel contract, rf2-tijr). Update tests keyed on
`rf-causa-filters-hidden-indicator` / `rf-causa-mode-pill-*`.

---

## Workstream C — Frame is a view scope, not a filter

### The trap (read first)
`[:focus :frame]` is written by TWO paths: the picker (`:rf.causa/select-frame` →
`spine/set-frame-reducer`) AND the epoch-focus reducer auto-aligning it to the focused
epoch's frame (`epoch.cljs:56-79`, rf2-ulpp8). `:rf.causa/filtered-cascades` reads
`(:frame focus-slot)` and applies `matcher/filter-cascades-by-frame` (`filters.cljs:
176-185`) — so LIVE auto-tracking onto a `:below` epoch silently turned the list into a
`:below`-only filtered view the user never asked for. That conflation is the bug.

### Required behaviour
- The list scopes to the **dropdown's** selected frame as a *view scope*, decoupled from
  the filter chain and from epoch-focus alignment driving the list scope.
- Frame is NOT in the filter chain conceptually: remove `:frame` from
  `:rf.causa/hidden-by-filters` (`filters.cljs:212-225`) — and fix the count baseline so
  it's computed **within the selected frame** (today `raw-n` counts across all frames, so
  switching frames inflates "hidden"). Drop the frame cause from `filters/hidden.cljc`
  (+ `hidden_test.cljc`). Delete the `rf-causa-filters-hidden-frame` chip
  (`shell.cljs` ~1386-1392).
- `:rf.causa/clear-all-filters` (`filters.cljs:356-378`): remove the
  `[:dispatch [:rf.causa/select-frame nil]]` — Clear Filters must not change the frame.
- **Default the view-scope frame on load to the head (most recent) epoch's frame**
  (Mike's call; single frame, no "all merged"). **Persistence itself is owned by rf2-swclw**
  (decided: reset transient filters incl. frame-pin on load) — do NOT re-implement it
  here; reconcile so the net result is "frame is a non-persisted, single-select view
  scope," not "a non-persisted filter."
- Preserve any legitimate non-list use of epoch→frame alignment (rf2-ulpp8); only the
  list-scope-as-filter coupling is wrong.

---

## Design direction (use the `frontend-design` skill)

Invoke the `frontend-design` skill and apply its **refined / industrial-utilitarian**
branch — this is an information-dense developer tool, so the win is precision, rhythm,
and hierarchy, NOT distinctive fonts, motion, or maximalism. Hard constraints: stay
within `theme/tokens.cljc` (no new colours/fonts), honour density-is-binding (spec/021
§0), keep pure hiccup. Concretely:

- **Two distinct strata.** The chrome ribbon and events ribbon must read as separate
  layers. Give them different backgrounds from the token ramp (e.g. chrome `:bg-1`,
  events `:bg-2`, list `:bg-2`/`:bg-3`) with a `:border-subtle` hairline between. The
  mode-accent left stripe (violet/cyan) anchors the chrome strip.
- **Alignment & rhythm.** Left = selectors/state/nav; right = actions (`⚙`/`✕`;
  `Clear Filters`). One consistent horizontal gap unit, one consistent control height,
  vertically centered. Make the chrome ribbon visibly shorter than today — it's the
  reward for moving nav/pills out.
- **Typography.** Labels `Events:` / `Frame:` in `:body-tight` or `:caption`,
  `:text-secondary`; chips/badges `:micro`. The two dropdowns share one control style
  (the frame picker's `<select>` is the reference — compact, `:bg-2`, `:border-default`,
  4px radius).
- **Controls & affordances.** `⚙`/`✕` as ghost icon-buttons: `:text-secondary` resting →
  `:text-primary` on hover; the `✕` gets an unmistakable destructive hover (a `:yellow`
  or red-tinted bg/border) so "close" reads as deliberate. Pills keep their semantic
  tones (IN green, OUT magenta); the `[+]` add-pill is a quiet dashed/ghost affordance.
  `Clear Filters` is a restrained outline button (not loud) — present, not shouting.
- **Restraint.** No gratuitous motion. At most a subtle hover transition on controls.
  Elegance here is exact spacing, consistent metrics, and a clean two-row silhouette that
  gives the event list more room.

Treat the skill's output as direction to execute precisely against the tokens — show
what a meticulously-refined devtool chrome looks like.

---

## Decisions (resolved by Mike — 2026-05-22)
1. **Default frame on load** — the **head (most recent) epoch's frame**. Single frame; no
   "all merged".
2. **`N hidden` message placement** — beside the **Clear Filters** button on the right
   (see Workstream B step 6).
3. **Clear Filters + `N hidden` visibility** — both **absent when no filters are active**;
   button appears when filters exist, message appears beside it only when `N > 0`.
4. **Dynamic/Static control** — a **dropdown**, deliberately compact/understated (the
   current pill is too dominant for occasional use); drop the two-button pill; the mode
   accent stripe stays as the signal.

---

## Coordination / sequencing (in-flight worker)
- **rf2-swclw is IN_PROGRESS** and touches `frame_switcher.cljs`, `filters/
  persistence.cljs`, `mount.cljs` (transient-filter reset, incl. frame-pin). **Do not
  dispatch this work until rf2-swclw merges** — shared files + the frame concern.
- Order: **rf2-2qaqh → rf2-swclw → this work.** After rf2-swclw lands, re-read
  `frame_switcher.cljs` + the persistence layer before starting.
- `shell.cljs` + `filters.cljs` are shared Causa hot files — never parallel another
  Causa worker on them.

---

## Files in play
- `shell.cljs` — L1 `ribbon` (~682-760), right-icons (~637-667), `ribbon-nav-cluster`,
  `ribbon-focus-chip` (~554-565), `ribbon-filter-pills` (508-520),
  `filters-hidden-indicator` (1346-1415) + mount (1502), mode stripe (~741).
- `static/mode_pill.cljs` — button-pair → dropdown.
- `frame_switcher.cljs` — frame dropdown + write surface.
- `registry.cljs:420-425` — `:rf.causa/close-shell` (wire to real hide).
- `mount.cljs` — `hide-shell` (~535), display:none (~215), toggle (~546).
- `filters.cljs` — `:rf.causa/filtered-cascades` (176-185), `:rf.causa/hidden-by-filters`
  (212-225), `:rf.causa/clear-all-filters` (356-378).
- `filters/hidden.cljc` (+ `hidden_test.cljc`), `filters/pills.cljs`,
  `filters/matcher.cljc` (`filter-cascades-by-frame`).
- `epoch.cljs:56-79` (focus→frame trap), `spine.cljs` (`set-frame-reducer`).
- `theme/tokens.cljc`, `theme/layout` (`top-strip-height`), `settings/events.cljs`.

## Out of scope (don't fold in)
- Filter/frame persistence (rf2-swclw). Buffer pollution (rf2-2qaqh). Orphan-attribution
  (rf2-avvwm). Machine-pill causal matching (rf2-jvghz #2 / `:rf.*` epic).

## Verification
- `npm run test:cljs`, `npm run test:causa-feature-gate`, and `cd tools/causa && clojure
  -M:test` (incl. `hidden_test.cljc`) green.
- Manual (parallel-frames): chrome ribbon shows only Frame + Dynamic/Static dropdowns
  (left) and `⚙`/`✕` (right), and is visibly shorter; **`✕` actually closes Causa** (and
  Ctrl+Shift+C); switching Dynamic/Static via the dropdown works + the accent stripe
  follows; events ribbon shows `Events:` + nav + focus-chip + pills + `[+]` and
  `Clear Filters` right; no `Frame:` chip; switching frames re-scopes the list WITHOUT a
  "hidden by filters" count; adding a pill shows the count; Clear Filters resets

## Working agreement (background worker)
- Run `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/assert-worker-worktree.ps1` from

- No AI attribution in commits/PRs.

title: Substrate: orphan trace events (:frame/created) emitted outside a dequeued-event cascade are mis-attributed into the next epoch's :trace-events (regression from #1952 epoch-per-event)
description:
## Summary

Under the per-event epoch model (#1952 / rf2-nj6p7), a trace event emitted OUTSIDE any
dequeued-event cascade — `:frame/created` is the visible instance — is mis-attributed into
the next dequeued event's `:rf/epoch-record :trace-events`, instead of staying uncorrelated.

## Expected (the contract)

Frame boot for `:below` produces exactly TWO epochs:
- `:initialise` (the `:on-create` event) — its own dequeued event → epoch 1.
- `:title/flow [:rf/init]` — dispatched by `:initialise`'s `:fx [[:dispatch …]]`, a separately
  dequeued child → epoch 2.

`:frame/created` is NOT a dequeued event (no handler, no cascade). Per Spec 009
§Dispatch-correlation, a trace event emitted outside any in-flight cascade carries NO
`:dispatch-id` and stays uncorrelated in the raw trace stream. It must therefore be
**neither a third epoch nor folded into either epoch's `:trace-events`**.

## Actual

`frame.cljc` (lines 304–328) runs `:on-create` via `dispatch-sync` FIRST, then emits
`:frame/created` AFTER:

```clojure
;; Run :on-create events BEFORE emitting :frame/created (Spec 002 §Frame creation)
(when-let [on-create (:on-create config)]
  ...
  (dispatch-sync on-create {:frame id}))   ; :initialise → :title/flow run AND settle their epochs here
(trace/emit! :frame :frame/created          ; emitted AFTER both epochs already settled
             {:frame id :config config}))
```

Under per-event epochs, epoch 1 and epoch 2 each settle and harvest their cascade buffer
right there. `:frame/created` is then emitted with no frame-creation settle to harvest it,
so it lingers ORPHANED in the capture buffer until the NEXT dequeued event settles — and
that event's harvest vacuums it in as the FIRST `:trace-events` entry.

Observed (parallel-frames, `:below`): clicking `+` increments the counter and creates
epoch eid 8, whose `:trace-events` begin with `[:frame :frame/created]` followed by the
real counter-inc ops (`:event/dispatched`, `:event/db-changed`, 5×`:sub/run`, render).
"frame created" appears as the bottom (first) line of an epoch that is actually a counter
increment. Note it lands in the NEWEST epoch, never the first — confirming it was stranded
and swept forward, not simply mis-ordered.

## Root cause

Pre-#1952 the whole frame boot was ONE drain-settle epoch, so the trailing `:frame/created`
emit was harvested correctly. The per-event boundary (#1952) leaves any emit that occurs
between the last settled event and the next dequeued event orphaned; the next epoch's
harvest sweeps it up. General defect class: ALL out-of-cascade emits (frame lifecycle, and
by the same logic registry-time emits) are exposed, not just `:frame/created`.

## Fix direction

Ensure out-of-cascade emits never join a later epoch's harvest — e.g. flush/close the
capture buffer immediately after the `:frame/created` emit so the event stays uncorrelated
(no `:dispatch-id`, in no epoch's `:trace-events`). Do NOT reorder `:frame/created` before
`:on-create` (Spec 002 deliberately orders it after) and do NOT give it a synthetic third
epoch (the contract is two epochs).

## Likely-downstream symptom (verify after fix)

The counter-inc epoch (eid 8) landed but did NOT surface as a cascade in Causa's L2 event
list (focus stayed on eid 4) — so the `+` click produced no visible new event row. Strong
hypothesis: eid 8's leading `:frame/created` makes Causa's cascade-grouping misclassify the
epoch as frame-lifecycle rather than a user event and drop it. Confirm whether fixing the
orphan-attribution restores the row.

## Separate observation (candidate for its own bead)

The raw trace ring (`re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer`, 200-cap here) was observed
100% saturated by `:rf/causa`-frame `:sub/run` + `:view/render` events — Causa's own UI
reactivity had evicted every application event from the shared buffer (`:n-app 0`). Causa
keeps its own cascade accumulator so cascades survive, but this is a heap/pollution concern
for any consumer reading the raw buffer.

## Repro

parallel-frames testbed → refresh → click `+` on the below frame → read the `:below`
frame epoch-history: the newest epoch's `:trace-events` begins with `[:frame :frame/created]`.

## Files

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:304-328` (emit ordering)
- Epoch harvest: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` (~1058 harvest), `core_epoch.cljc`,
  `late_bind/directory.cljc` (`:epoch/settle!`, ~505-509).
close_reason: Landed in PR #1961: orphans (no :dispatch-id) dropped at the epoch capture-site so they stay uncorrelated, not folded into the next epoch's :trace-events

title: Complete the :rf.* single-root migration for trace op-types, operations, and framework tag-keys
description:
# Complete the `:rf.*` single-root migration for trace op-types, operations, and framework tag-keys

## Why

`spec/Conventions.md` §single-root (locked) reserves ONE root namespace `:rf/*` for every
framework-owned id and names **"trace operations"** explicitly. The v2 migration collapsed
the old 14 prefixes (`:machine/*`, `:route/*`, `:registry/*`, …) into `:rf.machine/*`,
`:rf.route/*`, `:rf.registry/*` — but **the core domino trace ops were left behind.** The
live trace buffer (parallel-frames, observed) carries a half-migrated vocabulary:

- `:op-type` values: `:sub/run`, `:view`, `:event`, `:rf.epoch` — only the last is migrated.
- `:operation` values: `:sub/run`, `:view/render`, `:rf.view/rendered`, `:event/dispatched`,
  `:event`, `:event/db-changed`, `:rf.epoch/snapshotted`, `:rf.view/unmounted` — the `view`
  family alone carries THREE forms (`:view/render` old, `:rf.view/rendered` + `:rf.view/unmounted`
  new), the clearest tell of an interrupted migration.
- tag keys: `:sub-id :query-v :frame :value-changed? :prev-value :value :cascade? :cause-sub
  :render-key :view-id :mount? :deref-subs :event :origin :sync? :dispatch-id :event-id
  :trace-id :phase :epoch-id :outcome :reader-render-key` — all bare; only `:rf/dispatch-origin`
  is namespaced. Framework-emitted tags share the `:tags` map with potential user tags, so
  bare names are both a convention violation and a collision risk.

This is a conformance violation against a locked convention, internally inconsistent in the
spec itself (Spec 009 §op-type vocabulary + Spec-Schemas `:rf/trace-event`). Pre-alpha:
breaking changes are fine, no shims — goal is correctness and elegance.

## Canonical target (the pattern the already-migrated families set)

op-type = `:rf.<family>` ; operation = `:rf.<family>/<op>` (matching `:rf.machine`/`:rf.machine/transition`,
`:rf.epoch`/`:rf.epoch/snapshotted`).

| Family | Current (wrong) | Target |
|---|---|---|
| event | `:op-type :event` · `:event/dispatched` · `:event/db-changed` · bare `:event` | `:op-type :rf.event` · `:rf.event/dispatched` · `:rf.event/db-changed` |
| sub | `:op-type :sub/run` · `:sub/run` · `:sub/create` | `:op-type :rf.sub` · `:rf.sub/run` · `:rf.sub/create` (skip already `:rf.sub/skip`) |
| view | `:op-type :view` · `:view/render` | `:op-type :rf.view` · `:rf.view/render` (rendered/unmounted already `:rf.view/*`) |
| fx | `:op-type :fx` · `:event/do-fx` | `:op-type :rf.fx` · `:rf.fx/do-fx` (or `:rf.event/do-fx` — decide in spec child) |
| registry | `:op-type :registry` | `:op-type :rf.registry` (operations already `:rf.registry/*`) |
| machine | `:op-type :machine` | `:op-type :rf.machine` (operations already `:rf.machine/*`) |

NOTE: the op VALUES live in the per-family `:rf.<family>` namespace, NOT `:rf.trace/*`.
`:rf.trace/*` stays reserved for the trace ENVELOPE's structural keys (`:rf.trace/trigger-handler`,
`:rf.trace/call-site`).

## Open design decision (resolved in the spec child)

**Tag-key naming scheme.** Each framework-emitted tag key needs a home. Proposed (for Mike to
confirm): route per concern — `:sub-id`→`:rf.sub/id`, `:query-v`→`:rf.sub/query-v`,
`:render-key`→`:rf.view/render-key`, `:view-id`→`:rf.view/id`, `:epoch-id`→`:rf.epoch/id`,
`:dispatch-id`→`:rf.trace/dispatch-id`, `:event-id`→`:rf.trace/event-id`,
`:frame`→`:rf/frame`, `:phase`/`:outcome`/`:trace-id`→`:rf.trace/*`. The cross-cutting trace
correlation keys (`:dispatch-id`, `:parent-dispatch-id`, `:trace-id`) belong under `:rf.trace/*`;
domain tags under their family. Final scheme is the one normative decision here.

**Envelope fields** (`:id` `:operation` `:op-type` `:time` `:tags`) — Spec 009 line 222 keeps
these stable/bare as the record shape. Recommendation: LEAVE bare (they're the trace-event
record's own fields, not "operations"); namespacing the record schema itself is noise, not
elegance. Flagged for a conscious call.

## Correctness constraint — atomicity

This is a breaking rename with NO shims. Substrate emit-sites and ALL consumers branch on the
same vocabulary, so `main` must never carry a substrate/consumer mismatch. Land the substrate
+ three consumer changes coordinated (a single PR, or back-to-back on an integration branch
gated together) — NOT as independent merges. The `npm run test:cljs` contract tests +
`npm run test:causa-feature-gate` + Story/pair suites are the safety net; they must be green
across the whole set, not per-bead.

## Scope (hot-zone + consumers)

- Spec (hot-zone, sequential): `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md`
  (§op-type vocabulary, per-op operation values, error/flow catalogues), `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`
  (`:rf/trace-event`).
- Substrate: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace*`, `subs/memo`, `views`, `router`,
  fx/do-fx emit, `registrar` + core trace tests.
- Consumers: Story (`group-cascades` + op-type branching), Causa (Trace/Reactive/Event-detail
  panels, filters typed-predicates, projection), re-frame2-pair (`runtime.cljs`, `ops.clj`,
  MCP tool surface).

## Children
1. Spec: canonical rename table + tag-key scheme decision (Conventions / 009 / Spec-Schemas). FIRST.
2. Substrate: emit-site migration + core trace tests. Depends on 1.
3. Causa: read-site migration + tests. Depends on 1; lands coordinated with 2.
4. Story: read-site migration + tests. Depends on 1; lands coordinated with 2.
5. re-frame2-pair: read-site migration (runtime/ops/MCP). Depends on 1; lands coordinated with 2.
notes: Naming contract DECIDED 2026-05-22 (Mike: go-with-recommendation). See y4qpy.1 notes + ai/findings/2026-05-22-rf-star-trace-naming-contract.md. .1 (spec) dispatched; .2-.5 follow once .1 merges.

title: Causa L2 list: persisted filters silently hide events (no hidden-count indicator); machine-pill loses parent-event match under epoch-per-event
description:
## Symptom

After the epoch-per-event merges (#1952), Causa's L2 event list appeared broken: on a
fresh page load it rendered exactly ONE row and ignored subsequent events. Clicking the
counter `+` in the `:below` frame incremented the counter (data correct) but produced no
new rows. It read as "Causa lost all events / only catches the first."

## Root cause — persisted filters, EXPOSED (not caused) by epoch-per-event

The defect is NOT a reactivity, epoch, or front-of-queue regression. The data layer is
healthy: raw `:rf.causa/cascades` held all 4 event cascades. The L2 list reads
`:rf.causa/filtered-cascades`, which on the affected load applied two persisted filters
left over from an earlier debugging session:

- `re-frame2.causa.filters.v1` = `{:in [{:kind :machine :params {:machine-id :title/flow}}]}`
  — an active machine IN-pill.
- `re-frame2.causa.frame-switcher.v1` = `{:frame :below}` — frame picker pinned to `:below`.

Both survive page reload via localStorage. Stacked: frame filter keeps `:below` cascades
(`:initialise` did 4 + `:title/flow` did 5); the machine-pill then keeps only cascades
that actually run `:title/flow` → drops `:initialise` → one surviving row (did 5).

epoch-per-event EXPOSED this:
- Before: `:initialise` and its child `:dispatch [:title/flow ...]` were ONE cascade. It
  contained the machine, so the machine-pill kept it — everything looked normal.
- After: `:initialise` (did 4) and `:title/flow` (did 5) are SEPARATE cascades. The pill
  now matches only did 5 and drops the parent `:initialise`.
- Counter `+` clicks produced no new rows because `:counter-inc` doesn't run the machine,
  so the pill filtered every increment out.

## Two defects to address

### 1. Persisted filters silently hide events with no visible indicator (primary)
A reload into a filtered-empty (or filtered-to-one) L2 list is indistinguishable from a
broken tool. This fooled the project author. The L2 list needs an unmistakable signal when
active filters are suppressing rows — e.g. an "N events hidden by filters" affordance with
a one-click clear, and clearly-visible active pills + frame pin. (Open question: should
filter pills / frame pin persist across reloads at all, or reset to unfiltered on load?)

### 2. Machine-pill causal matching under epoch-per-event (secondary / design)
A `:machine` pill now matches only the machine's own epoch, not the parent event that
spawned it. Arguably "show me everything about `:title/flow`" should follow the causal link
upstream so the `:initialise` (or any event) that kicked off the machine is still included.
This is a design question for how typed pills (`:machine`, `:http-correlation`, `:fx`)
should relate cascades to their causal parents now that each dequeued event is its own
epoch. May warrant a sibling bead once direction is set.

## Repro
1. In the parallel-frames Causa testbed, add a `:machine :title/flow` IN-pill and pin the
   frame picker to `:below`.
2. Reload the page.
3. Observe the L2 list shows one row; new `:below` events that don't run the machine never
   appear.

## Evidence (live, port 51708, parallel-frames build)
- `:rf.causa/cascades` (raw): 4 event cascades (did 2/3 above, did 4/5 below) + ungrouped.
- DOM `rf-causa-event-list`: 1 `<li>` (`rf-causa-event-row-5`).
- `:rf.causa/focus-slot` = `{:frame :below}`; `:rf.causa/active-filters` =
  `{:in [{:kind :machine :params {:machine-id :title/flow}}], :out []}`; muted = `#{}`.
- `:rf.causa/filtered-cascades` = `[{:did 5 :ev :title/flow :frame :below}]`.

## Files
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/filters.cljs` (`:rf.causa/filtered-cascades` sub,
  ~L176).
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/filters/typed_predicates.cljs` (machine pill matcher).
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/shell.cljs` (L2 list reads `:rf.causa/filtered-cascades`, ~L1327/L1386).
- Persistence keys: `re-frame2.causa.filters.v1`, `re-frame2.causa.frame-switcher.v1`.
notes: defect #1 (indicator) landed in PR #1962; defect #2 + persist question split to rf2-a1eld (typed-pill causal-parent matching) and rf2-swclw (persist-vs-reset design, Mike). This bead stays in_progress for defect #2 (tracked in rf2-a1eld).
close_reason: defect #1 (the 'N hidden by filters' indicator + Clear) landed in PR #1962. Defect #2 (machine-pill causal matching) split to rf2-a1eld; persist-vs-reset design split to rf2-swclw. Both Mike-decisions.

title: bug(instrumentation): :sub/run attribution lags one cascade — Views subs-table value-changed? checkmark wrong (rf2-qs6dl sibling; #1935 fixed renders only)
description:
The new per-cascade subs table (#1934) + value-change attribution (#1933) shows the 'changed' checkmark against the WRONG subs — most visibly, every sub appears changed on the first cascade after a (re)load.

ROOT CAUSE: :sub/run ops are attributed to the next cascade (one-epoch lag) — the SAME defect as rf2-qs6dl, which #1935 fixed for :rf.view/rendered ONLY. #1935's back-fill in epoch/capture.cljc handles render ops (:view/render / :rf.view/rendered / :rf.view/rendered-cap-reached) that arrive post-settle with no in-flight cascade, re-attributing them to the most-recently-settled epoch. :sub/run has the identical post-settle (lazy deref at render) timing but is NOT back-filled, so its value/value-changed?/prev-value land on cascade N+1.

The :value-changed? boolean itself is computed correctly per-recompute in subs/memo.cljc (not= prev-value validated); the bug is purely WHICH epoch the :sub/run is filed under.

CLEAN REPRODUCTION (single tab, DOM clicks on :below counter):
  epoch 11  counter-inc  db 0->1  -> counter {changed? true, prev nil, value 0}; ALL title subs {changed? true, prev nil}   <- displaying the MOUNT recomputes (first runs, prev nil) shoved forward by the lag
  epoch 15  counter-inc  db 1->2  -> counter {changed? true, prev 0, value 1}; title subs {changed? false}                  <- :value 1 for a 1->2 click betrays the one-cascade lag
  Note :value consistently equals the epoch's db-BEFORE counter, i.e. the prior cascade's result.

FIX DIRECTION: extend #1935's post-settle back-fill (epoch/capture.cljc + epoch/state.cljc) to cover :sub/run (and :sub/skip) ops, not just render ops — re-attribute a sub-run arriving with no in-flight cascade to the most-recently-settled causing epoch. Consider whether eager-in-cascade sub recompute would be a cleaner fix than back-fill.

IMPACT: user-visible correctness bug in the freshly-shipped Reactive/Views value-changed feature (rf2-l1jz8 #1933 + rf2-isun6 #1934). Diagnosed live via re-frame2-pair on the parallel-frames testbed.
close_reason: Could not reproduce in clean conditions — closing as invalid. Re-tested on a fresh single-tab page after the L2 ::counter-parity addition: :sub/run value-changed?/prev-value/value are all correct (e.g. epoch 10 counter-inc 1->2 reports counter :value 2 changed? true; title subs changed? false; ::counter-parity correctly skips on title-only changes). The earlier 'value=db-before / all-changed' evidence was confounded by that session's multiple browser tabs + a dozen hot-reloads (reads were hitting a stale/dead runtime — confirmed at the time by 'I don't see yours' and stale-epoch peeks). No genuine one-cascade :sub/run lag. Reopen if it resurfaces with a clean single-runtime repro.

title: bug(instrumentation): :rf.view/rendered attributed to NEXT cascade (one-epoch lag) — epoch :renders shows the previous cascade's renders
description:
Confirmed live on the parallel-frames testbed via re-frame2-pair, with a falsifiable prediction that held.

SYMPTOM: each epoch's :renders projection lists the renders caused by the PREVIOUS cascade, not its own. Causa's Views tab therefore systematically shows the wrong cascade's re-renders.

REPRODUCTION (foregrounded tab, single deliberate clicks on :below):
  epoch 17  reply->:loaded  -> reports [title-view]   (its own)
  epoch 19  counter-inc     -> reports [title-view]   <- 17's lagged render; IMPOSSIBLE from a counter-inc (title-view doesn't read ::counter)
  epoch 22  counter-inc     -> reports [counter-view] <- 19's lagged render (predicted in advance, confirmed)

The smoking gun: epoch 19 is a counter-inc but reports title-view rendered — a counter-inc cannot cause title-view to render, so the render must belong to a prior (title) cascade. Predicted epoch 22 would then report the lagged counter-view; it did.

ROOT CAUSE (hypothesis): :rf.view/rendered fires at React commit, which lands AFTER the causing cascade's run-to-completion has settled (same timing that makes dispatch-and-collect return :n-trace 0). By commit time the cause-attribution / epoch-capture window has advanced to the next in-flight epoch, so the render is filed against cascade N+1. Investigate the rf2-25zo2 cause-event-id stamp in core views.cljs and the render bucketing in the epoch-capture artefact (epoch/capture.cljc).

SCOPE: shared instrumentation — affects every consumer of epoch :renders (Causa Views/Reactive panel, Story, re-frame2-pair). Distinct from rf2-p1qas (panel op-name fix, merged) and rf2-l1jz8 (value-changed/cascaded attribution). Note this undermines the per-cascade accuracy of the Views tab fixed in rf2-p1qas: subs-ran is correct, but views-rendered is off-by-one-cascade.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1935

title: fix(causa): Views/Reactive panel reads structured :sub-runs/:renders projections (subs-ran was always 0)
description: The Causa Views (Reactive) panel showed 0 subs-ran/subs-skipped no matter how many subs ran. Root cause: panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs project-trace-events grouped epoch :trace-events by phantom op names :rf.sub/computed / :rf.sub/skipped, but the substrate emits canonical :sub/run / :rf.sub/skip (Spec 009 §:op-type vocabulary; emit sites subs.cljc:457, subs/memo.cljc:160). Only :rf.view/rendered matched, so views-rendered worked while subs were pinned to 0. Fix: replaced project-trace-events with project-record reading the structured :sub-runs (split on :recomputed?) and :renders (:render-key->:view-id) projections directly; flow counts still tallied from :trace-events with canonical :rf.flow/computed / :rf.flow/skip. Tests rewritten (old suite encoded the buggy contract). Diagnosed live via re-frame2-pair on the parallel-frames testbed; verified end-to-end post-refresh (SUBS RAN (5) with real ids).
close_reason: Fixed + merged in PR #1930 (commit 47051e731). Views/Reactive panel now reads structured :sub-runs/:renders projections; subs-ran shows real counts. Verified live + gate green (4090 tests, 0 failures).

title: audit(story): snapshot identity hash omits play body (stale :play slot)
description: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/identity.cljc:164 — variant-body-slice selects :play, a key REMOVED by rf2-0wrud (2026-05-20). title: audit(machines-viz): delete dead *chart* dynamic Var + its test (renderer threads :chart via :data, never binds it)

title: testcov(pair-mcp): fix false-green async tests + cover port discovery/transport/registry-drift
description:

title: skill(setup): reconcile day-one shape with deps-new template (schemas+causa+init)
description:
skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:30-33 claims the skill and the generator template 'end up at the same canonical shape', but they no longer do. The deps-new template (rf2-dolpf, landed 2026-05-20) emits a richer day-one shape than the skill describes:

title: review(machines): parent :after timer wrongly invalidated by child sibling-leaf transition
description:
Single per-machine :rf/after-epoch advances whenever ANY exited/entered node declares :after (transition.cljc compute-cascade-paths epoch-bumps?, ~L969-971). When a parent state declares :after AND a child also declares :after, a sibling-leaf transition under that parent (LCA at parent) bumps the epoch (child :a is exited and has :after) WITHOUT exiting the parent and WITHOUT rescheduling the parent's timer (build-after-fx only schedules entered-pairs). Result: parent's in-flight timer (prior epoch) is now permanently stale and silently never fires.

Violates Spec 005 §Hierarchy interaction §Normative rule (005-StateMachines.md:1638): leaf-only sibling transitions inside the same parent MUST NOT make that parent's pending :after fire stale; implementations that can't satisfy both clauses with a single per-machine epoch MUST track per-level and selectively reschedule.

Reproduced (JVM pure-fn): parent {:after {30000 ..}}, child {:after {5000 ..}}, snapshot {:state [:P :a] :data {:rf/after-epoch 2}}, transition :a->:b => epoch 2->3, fx carries after-cancel for [:P :a] only, no [:P] reschedule.

No test exercises :after on parent AND child simultaneously, hence undetected.

Fix: per-level epoch / selective reschedule (spec sketch) or per-:after-entry epoch keying.
Files: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc (compute-cascade-paths, commit-snapshot, build-after-fx, build-after-cancel-fx).

title: review(core): spine derived values over-fire + glitch on multi-input subs
description:
Spine (UIx/Helix) make-derived-value-fn wires one watch per source container. A layer-2+ sub with N inputs installs N independent watches; when app-db changes, each upstream reaction fires its watch synchronously and independently, so the downstream derived value's watch fires once per changed source. This (a) recomputes against a half-updated input set producing an intermediate GLITCH value delivered to views, and (b) notifies downstream up to N times instead of once.

Violates Spec 006 §Invalidation algorithm (lines 461-503): topological cascade with single Phase-3 notification per dirty entry; "Non-CLJS implementations must satisfy the contract explicitly." Reagent is immune (native batched reactions); plain-atom JVM adapter is immune (deref-on-demand, no notify). The subs.memo =-dedup does NOT save it (cannot suppress the half-updated recompute's genuinely-different value, nor coalesce notifications).

File: implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:125-197 (make-derived-value-fn), :139-165 (notify + per-source watch wiring).

Direction: coalesce per-source watches so one app-db change recomputes the derived value at most once after all upstream sources settle (per-cascade dirty-flag + flush, or recompute-once-after-batch keyed off drain settle), matching the Phase 1/2/3 ordering the spec writes for explicit substrates.

It does NOT satisfy Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle MUST 2 (release host-specific resources: unmount active roots) nor MUST 3 (discard internal caches: clear the hiccup-emitter defonce at reagent_slim.cljs:67). The render fn (lines 53-65) never tracks the React root in an active-roots set — it closes the root into the per-mount unmount thunk only — so there is nothing for dispose to drain.
