title: ssr-ring frame-id keyword violates EDN identifier grammar (rejected by clojure.edn + cljs.tools.reader.edn)
description:
Surfaced by rf2-j3dlc (live-SSR browser smoke).

`re-frame.ssr.ring.pipeline/setup-request-frame!` builds the per-request frame-id via:

    (keyword "rf.frame" (str (gensym "")))

`(str (gensym ""))` returns a pure-digit string (e.g. `"5401"`), producing keyword `:rf.frame/5401`. `clojure.core/keyword` does not validate, but per the EDN spec (https://github.com/edn-format/edn) identifier names (and thus keyword local-parts) must begin with a non-numeric character.

**Consequence:**

- `clojure.edn/read-string` on the JVM rejects with `Invalid token: :rf.frame/5401`.
- `cljs.tools.reader.edn/read-string` in the browser rejects with `Invalid keyword: :rf.frame/5401.`
- The example's `ssr.core/run` reads the embedded `__rf_payload` via `cljs.reader/read-string` and crashes on hydration → no hydration, no interactivity.

**Why not caught before rf2-j3dlc:**

The only browser-driven SSR smoke prior to rf2-j3dlc was `examples/reagent/ssr/ssr.spec.cjs`, which exercised PRE-BAKED HTML (hand-written `index.html`) that didn't ship a `pipeline/setup-request-frame!`-shaped frame-id. The JVM-side `ring_e2e_validator_test.clj` reads the response body as a string and asserts on substrings — never round-trips through any EDN reader.

**Workaround in rf2-j3dlc:**

`examples/reagent/ssr/server.clj`'s custom `:html-shell` does a regex substitution on the payload-EDN string before emission:

    #":rf\.frame/(\d+)"  →  ":rf.frame/f$1"

This keeps the frame-id unique per request, namespaced, and EDN-spec-compliant. The workaround documents the issue at the call site and unblocks the live-SSR smoke.

**Fix:**

Change `pipeline/setup-request-frame!` to prefix the gensym counter with a letter, e.g.:

    (keyword "rf.frame" (str (gensym "f")))

`(str (gensym "f"))` → `"f5401"` — still unique, still readable. Add a regression test in `ring_test.clj` that round-trips a response body's `__rf_payload` through `clojure.edn/read-string` and asserts the read succeeds.

Hot zone: `implementation/ssr-ring/`. Coordinate with rf2-o6ndb (`ssr-shell-trust-contract`).
notes: PR #1261 — 1-line fix in pipeline.clj setup-request-frame!: (gensym 'f') instead of (gensym ''). Removed band-aid workaround in examples/reagent/ssr/server.clj (-65 lines, no shim). Regression test hydration-payload-frame-id-keyword-is-edn-readable verifies round-trip. 40 example specs pass (incl. live-SSR). ssr-ring suite: 59 tests / 305 assertions / 0 fail.
close_reason: Merged

title: test(causa): use Story as a Causa panel-state gallery
description:
# Why

Use Story as a UI/component-state coverage layer for Causa. Causa's browser feature gate should continue to prove real observer behaviour, but Story can give Causa a deterministic panel gallery: one story per panel, variants for meaningful panel states, and reusable fixture builders for panel-shaped data.

# Design Direction

1. Build a Causa panel gallery using Story: one story per Causa panel, many variants per panel state.
2. Seed each Story variant with deterministic Causa-shaped data, preferably via shared fixture builders reused by unit tests and browser tests.
3. Keep this as UI/component/state coverage, not the only Causa test layer.
4. Keep the Causa feature gate responsible for live observer behaviour: trace collection, epoch history, frame isolation, preload/mount, pop-out, and 20-event load.

# Initial Scope

Land the first usable slice, not the full gallery. The first slice should establish the pattern with enough coverage to prove the approach:
- A Story-backed Causa gallery testbed or fixture namespace in the appropriate Causa/Story testbed tree.
- Shared deterministic Causa fixture builders for at least one or two high-value panels.
- Story registrations that render Causa panel UI states without requiring live tracing.
- A focused test or runner hook proving the gallery compiles/renders and does not replace the Causa feature gate.

# Constraints

- Causa and Story must coexist without shared app-db contamination: Causa retains `:rf/causa`; Story variants retain per-variant frames.
- Do not make the full Story browser shell a mandatory Causa CI dependency by default unless deliberately promoted later.
- Avoid recursive Causa-tracing-Causa noise in the gallery. Prefer seeded data over live trace collection unless explicitly testing observer behaviour.
- Preserve the Causa feature/load matrix as the canonical end-to-end observer test.

# Acceptance

- A Causa-in-Story gallery foundation exists and documents the intended layering.
- At least one Causa panel has multiple deterministic Story variants that render distinct panel states.
- Fixture builders are reusable outside Story.
- Relevant focused tests pass, and no default CI promotion happens accidentally.
acceptance_criteria: First usable Causa panel gallery slice lands: Story variants render deterministic Causa panel state from reusable fixtures, while live observer behaviour remains owned by the Causa feature gate.

title: feat(causa): default left inline side panel launch mode
description:
Causa should open automatically on application load in dev/debug usage, but the default panel must be a true inline left-hand side panel, not a viewport overlay and not merely a body-padding approximation.

Product decision:
- Best developer experience means the host app provides an explicit Causa layout host in its page/app layout.
- Causa mounts into that host by default once the application/Causa runtime is ready.
- The app remains visible and usable beside the panel because normal flex/grid/layout flow owns the relationship.
- If Causa cannot find the configured/default host element, it must fail loudly but safely with an actionable dev diagnostic that explains exactly what element/config is missing and shows a minimal snippet to add.
- Prefer console.error plus a small dev-only diagnostic status exposed through the Causa API/state; avoid blocking alert() because it disrupts app startup and tests.
- Width resizing is desirable if low-risk, but not mandatory for the first cut.
- Pop-out remains documented and available. Pop-out must stay in-process/same-runtime where possible so app/Causa state sharing does not require serialization.
- Overlay/floating/body-padding modes may remain as optional fallback/debug modes, but must not be described as the primary/default developer experience.

Context:
- day8/re-frame-10x defaults visible and persists width, but its main panel is a fixed overlay; useful ideas are default-visible state, persisted width/resizer, and possible Shadow DOM isolation, not its layout model.
- PR #1213 exposed pop-out/dock/inline surfaces; PR #1220 added launch-mode load coverage. This bead should now turn the product default into explicit true-inline host mounting and update docs/skills accordingly.
acceptance_criteria:
- A documented app layout host contract exists for Causa, including the default selector/attribute, example markup, configuration override, and missing-host diagnostic behaviour.
- Loading a Causa-enabled testbed with the host element shows the Causa panel by default without a keyboard shortcut.
- The default panel is on the LHS and participates in normal layout; app controls remain visible/clickable to the RHS without body-padding tricks.
- Loading without the host emits an actionable dev diagnostic with the missing selector/config and snippet; no blocking alert and no silent failure.
- Pop-out is still available and documented as same-runtime/in-process where possible; tests or explicit verification cover the entry point.
- Causa launch-mode docs/specs and relevant skills describe true-inline host mounting as required for the best/default developer experience.
- Relevant Causa tests are quiet on success and report actionable diagnostics on failure.
notes: 2026-05-16 decision: true inline host is required for the primary Causa developer experience. Do not implement body-padding dock as the default. Missing host should produce console/error-state diagnostics, not alert().
close_reason: Merged PR #1222 (83f7c1e5): Causa default dev launch now uses true inline left host mounting, actionable missing-host diagnostics, Story-only auto-open suppression, updated docs/specs/skills/templates, and green targeted Story/Causa browser gate.

title: fix(machines-viz): align Mermaid emitter with state-machine grammar
description:
Follow-up from read-only audit bead `rf2-77mz1`.

Goal: align `tools/machines-viz` Mermaid output with the state-machine grammar in `spec/005-StateMachines.md` and `spec/CP-5-MachineGuide.md`. Pre-alpha posture applies: prefer complete, correct grammar handling over preserving omission-lock tests.

Actionable findings to address in this slice:

- P1 vector-path compound targets can crash the emitter because `transition-target` returns vector targets unchanged and `sanitise-id` calls `name`.
- P1 nested states are keyed by local keyword only, so repeated child names under different compound parents collapse into identical Mermaid ids.
- P1 `:after` transitions are silently omitted even though the API text says lossy timer semantics still render the target edge.
- P1 parallel-region machines are rejected because `emit` requires top-level `:initial` and `:states`, while the spec makes `:type :parallel` / `:regions` first-class.
- P2 multiple-candidate transition vectors are dropped; guarded branch topology disappears.
- P2 wildcard transitions are intentionally dropped and tests lock that in, despite spec treating `:*` as real transition topology.
- P3 top-level fallback `:on` is ignored; either render it explicitly or reject/comment unsupported topology.

Acceptance:

- Mermaid state ids are path-qualified enough to disambiguate duplicate nested leaves.
- Vector-path targets, `:after`, `:always`, wildcard, top-level fallback, and candidate-vector transitions render or produce explicit unsupported diagnostics.
- Parallel-region machines render with documented lossy semantics.
- Tests assert spec alignment rather than omission-lock behaviour.
- `clojure -M:test` passes in `tools/machines-viz`.
notes: Dispatched as independent machines-viz worker. Owns tools/machines-viz and its tests; avoid unrelated implementation/spec edits except minimal references needed for grammar alignment.

- P1 URL-bound frame exclusivity is reported but not enforced; duplicate URL-bound frames can still affect navigation.
- P2 `route-url` skips query-schema validation for empty query maps, so required query params are not enforced.
- P2 scroll restoration capture is incomplete; restore helpers exist, but navigation does not reliably save the current position before leaving.
- P2 route pattern grammar is not enforced at registration; non-canonical patterns are accepted contrary to spec.
- P2 `:rf.route/continue` and `:rf.route/cancel` ignore the supplied pending-nav id.
- P3 query-key cap implementation and spec disagree: implementation caps raw pair count before unique-key semantics.

Acceptance:

- Routing behaviour and tests match `spec/012-Routing.md` for the cases above.
- The navigation path has one clear guard-aware decision flow instead of parallel bypasses.
- Public route APIs keep canonical query-vector semantics.
- Invalid route patterns fail early with actionable errors.
- JVM routing tests pass; add CLJS/browser coverage where behaviour is browser-specific.

title: fix(http): JVM abort does not cancel the underlying CompletableFuture — double-reply on slow servers
description:
Found by audit bead rf2-wui5v.

## Issue

`http_transport.cljc:593-599` — the JVM abort-fn body is just

    (finalise-failure! ctx-no-handle {:kind :rf.http/aborted ...})

No `.cancel cf`. The underlying `CompletableFuture` from `HttpClient.sendAsync` continues running. When the server eventually responds (or the socket errors), the `.whenComplete` BiConsumer fires `handle-response!` / `maybe-retry!`, which calls `finalise-success!` / `finalise-failure!` — a SECOND reply dispatch for the SAME request.

User-observable symptom: an event handler with explicit `:on-success` / `:on-failure` will receive TWO replies for one request — first the synthesised aborted-reply (immediate, from abort-fn), then the natural-completion reply (much later, from the latent in-flight future).

## CLJS path: symmetric concern

`.abort internal-controller` cancels Fetch, but the rejection rides through `.catch → maybe-retry! → finalise-failure!` for a second pass after the abort-fn closure already called `finalise-failure!`.

## Why tests don't notice

The existing `jvm-abort-by-request-id` test (http_managed_test.clj:456) ends before the latch is released; the second reply fires after assertions complete. The supersede tests work because supersede's `:request-id-superseded` skips the dispatch (the only reason path that does).

## Suggested fix

1. Add `finalised? (atom false)` on the request handle stamped at `record-in-flight!` time.
2. `finalise-success!` / `finalise-failure!` check + CAS the flag before dispatching; bail if already finalised.
3. JVM abort-fn additionally calls `(.cancel cf true)` to interrupt the underlying HTTP send.

## Regression-pin test

JVM blocked-server scenario: dispatch :rf.http/managed with :request-id :x, latch the server, fire :rf.http/managed-abort :x, assert reply count == 1 EVEN AFTER releasing the server latch and waiting for the future to complete.

## Surface

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc` — abort-fn closures + finalise-* + run-attempt!

## Discovered through

Audit bead rf2-wui5v (http slice). Pre-alpha-blocking severity: double-dispatch corrupts event-handler state machines.

title: fix(story): watch-mode cache key must include cell-overrides
description:
Watch-mode hash cache (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/shell.cljs:124-164) keys on [registrar-mutation-tick, active-modes, substrate]. The namespace docstring justifies omitting :cell-overrides by claiming snapshot-identity's public surface drops it. That's wrong: identity.cljc:213 calls (args/resolve-args variant-id {... :cell-overrides cell-overrides}), and args.cljc:125-134 makes cell-overrides the last layer of the deep-merge.

Result: when the user edits a control on a :test-tagged variant under watch-mode, the 500ms detector hits the cache (key unchanged), gets pre-edit hashes, sees no drift, fires no re-run. The canvas re-renders (because :cell-overrides flows through args/resolve-args independently) but the test widget stays stale.

Fix: include the :cell-overrides slot in the cache key. The map is small (one entry per actively-edited variant, mostly empty). Alternatively, strip overrides at snapshot-identity's boundary — loses fidelity, not recommended.

title: refactor(mcp-conformance): conformance gate for notifications/progress streaming (F-GAP-1)
description:
## Source

rf2-i3ffz audit, finding F-GAP-1.

## What

`end-to-end-pair2.js` exercises `subscribe` only in degraded mode (returns `isError: true, nrepl-port-not-found`). The live path (`live-pair2-overflow.js`) only exercises `eval-cljs`. **Neither test ever observes a `notifications/progress` frame from the server.**

This is the streaming wire surface — pair2-mcp's `subscribe` tool returns exactly one `notifications/progress` per matching batch (per `NAMING.md:38`). The MCP SDK's `Client` carries handlers via `client.setNotificationHandler(schema, handler)`.

Today: tool dispatch is asserted (degraded), streaming wire-shape is not (live).

## Fix

Extend the hermetic orchestrator (`scripts/run-live-pair2-overflow-hermetic.cjs`) with a second inner test (`test/live-pair2-subscribe.js`):
1. Subscribe to `:trace` topic.
2. Dispatch a known event.
3. Assert at least one `notifications/progress` frame arrives.
4. Validate the frame body against a Malli schema cross-encoded against `wire-vocab/` (mirror posture of OverflowBody).
5. Unsubscribe; assert clean teardown.

## LoC

~150 LoC (new test file + orchestrator wiring + Malli schema + cross-encoding gate).

## Severity

title: fix(flows): :fx must not run after a flow throws (Spec 013 §Failure semantics rule 3)
description:
Spec 013 §Failure semantics rule 3 + §rationale (line 202) state the cascade halts at a failing flow and downstream `:fx` does NOT run — because the rationale for halting is "downstream `:fx` and tooling rely on to skip work that depended on a now-invalid derived state."

Current impl in `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:684-693` (process-effects!):

```
(when (commit-db-effect! ...)
  (run-flows! ...)                ;; catches+swallows; emits :rf.error/flow-eval-exception
  (run-fx-effects! ...))          ;; runs UNCONDITIONALLY
```

`run-flows!` (router.cljc:481-545) catches the throw, fans out to error-emit substrate + trace, returns nil. Control flows on to `run-fx-effects!` — `:fx` walks even though one of its preconditions (post-commit derived state) is invalid.

The flows artefact side correctly re-throws (`flows.cljc:run-flows!` line 244). The swallow is in the router wrapper.

Impact: A handler emitting `[:dispatch [:react-to-area-change]]` from `:fx` (Spec 013 line 136 example) fires the child dispatch even when the source flow threw. Child handler runs on stale/partial derived state. Side effects (HTTP, navigation, analytics) escape.

Fix shape (small, surgical, no back-compat shim):
- Make `run-flows!` signal success/failure (return-or-throw).
- In `process-effects!`: `(when (commit-db-effect! ...) (when (run-flows! ...) (run-fx-effects! ...)))`.
- Add regression test: register a throwing flow, register `[:dispatch [:must-not-fire]]` `:fx`, assert `:must-not-fire` did not run.

Audit: ai/findings/flows-slice-audit-2026-05-15.md §C1.
Reference: Spec 013 line 202; sibling pattern at `emit-handler-exception!` halting `:fx`.

title: fix(epoch): build-record must not emit :event-id nil on halt paths (schema drift)
description:
## Finding

Parent audit: rf2-3391t (round-3 epoch audit). See `ai/findings/epoch-slice-audit-2026-05-15.md` §F1.

**Severity:** MED — correctness drift between schema and impl. The live router halt paths short-circuit via `(when (seq events) ...)` in `settle!` (epoch.cljc:735), but the `on-frame-destroyed!` `:halted-destroy` path at `epoch.cljc:384` calls `build-record` directly with whatever buffered events are present. If those events have no `:event/run-start` AND no `:event-id` tag (e.g. the buffer holds only `:frame/created` registration emits), `find-trigger-event` returns nil and the record lands with `:event-id nil`.

## Spec citation

`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2194` declares:

```
[:event-id      :keyword]                                                ;; the event that triggered the cascade
```

Required (no `{:optional true}`), non-maybe (no `[:maybe :keyword]`). `nil` is not a `:keyword` — a schema-validating consumer would reject the record.

## Impl citation

`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:667-686` — `build-record`:

```clojure
(let [{:keys [event-id event]} (find-trigger-event events)]
  (cond-> {:epoch-id      (next-epoch-id)
           :frame         frame-id
           :committed-at  (interop/now-ms)
           :event-id      event-id        ;; nil when find-trigger-event returns nil
           :trigger-event event           ;; nil ditto
           ...}
          halt-reason (assoc :halt-reason halt-reason)))
```

The `settle!` docstring at `epoch.cljc:706-709` claims the schema tolerates the absent slot via open-map semantics — but the slots are present with nil values, not absent.

## Fix

Smallest change: emit `:event-id` / `:trigger-event` only when non-nil. Replace the unconditional `cond->` slot with conditional assoc:

```clojure
(cond-> {:epoch-id      (next-epoch-id)
         :frame         frame-id
         :committed-at  (interop/now-ms)
         ...}
        event-id     (assoc :event-id event-id)
        event        (assoc :trigger-event event)
        halt-reason  (assoc :halt-reason halt-reason))
```

Alternative: widen the schema to `{:optional true} [:maybe :keyword]` — but that's a Spec-Schemas hot-zone edit and changes the spec for a degenerate path. The impl-side fix is the right one.

## Test

Add a test under the `destroyed-frame-*` cluster (`epoch_test.clj` around line 1700+) that drives the `on-frame-destroyed!` `:halted-destroy` path with a buffer that contains no `:event/run-start` and no `:event-id` tag, and asserts the emitted record does NOT carry `:event-id` as a key (verify via `(not (contains? record :event-id))`).

title: fix(routing): cap keyword interning on URL query keys + :keyword-typed values
description:
Security audit follow-up (rf2-y5vy9 F1; ai/findings/routing-security-audit-2026-05-15.md).

## Action

`match-url` at `routing.cljc:418-431` keywordises every query key from any URL via `(keyword (url-decode k))` at line 428 — **before** any route pattern match.

`coerce-by-type-form` at `routing.cljc:317-329` calls `(keyword v)` for any `:keyword`-typed declared query slot.

Identical accident class to **rf2-wu1n5** (HTTP-side keyword-interning cap): JVM `Keyword/table` is process-global + never GC'd → unbounded memory growth under hostile / compromised partner URL streams (especially SSR JVMs).

## Direction (per pragmatic-stance audit)

The right fix shape per the audit:
- Parse raw query keys as **strings** first.
- Only convert to keywords for a **bounded declared set** derived from the route's schema/defaults.
- Unknown keys: stay strings, drop, or fail-closed validation (decide at impl time).
- For `:keyword`-typed values: convert only after the value matches an allowed enum/whitelist; otherwise stay string + let validator decide.

## Concrete steps

1. Refactor `match-url` to parse query into a string-keyed map (don't keyword right away).
2. After route-match succeeds, walk the declared query schema and selectively keyword the keys that have a declared slot. Unknown keys stay as string keys (decide on drop vs validation-failed at impl time).
3. Refactor `coerce-by-type-form` `:keyword` branch: require an allowlist/enum constraint or keep string.
4. Add per-route or per-frame config knob (mirror `:rf.http/max-decoded-keys`) — name TBD, e.g. `:rf.route/max-keyword-keys`. Symmetric default.
5. Spec/012 cross-ref: align with the spec's normative contract for query parsing.
6. Regression tests:
   - 10000-unique-key URL doesn't grow the keyword table beyond the cap.
   - Declared schema slots still get keywords.
   - Unknown query keys come back as strings (or dropped, per chosen direction).
   - Malformed enum value for `:keyword` slot fails validation rather than interning.

## Acceptance

- Routing keyword-table-growth bounded.
- Symmetric pattern with rf2-wu1n5.
- Spec/012 updated to reflect the new contract.
- All routing tests green.

## Cross-refs

- rf2-y5vy9 (parent audit bead).
- rf2-wu1n5 (HTTP-side cap — pattern reference).
- Security.md §DoS by input.
- Spec/012 §Query-string coercion.

title: fix(machines/invoke-all): reject forged child-id on :on-child-done/:on-child-error
description:
Security audit follow-up (rf2-s9tf8 F1; ai/findings/machines-security-audit-2026-05-15.md).

## Action

`intercept-invoke-all-event` at `machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc:224-267` trusts the inbound `child-id` from the event vector and directly adds it to `:done` / `:failed` via `update ... (fnil conj #{})` at lines 258-260. No `contains?` check against the seeded `(:children join-state)` set.

`join-condition-met?` (lines 79-104) resolves purely from set-count vs `n-total`. Unknown ids count toward resolution → silent state machine corruption.

Accident class: any path that can dispatch `[parent-id [:on-child-done <bogus-id>]]` or `[:on-child-error <bogus-id> ...]` — including typo, mis-typed sibling, or cascaded event from a destroyed-but-still-listening child — collapses the join early and fires phony resolution events.

## Concrete steps

1. Edit `intercept-invoke-all-event` (`join.cljc:255-267`) — before the `case kind` update at line 258, guard:
   ```clojure
   (not (contains? (:children join-state) child-id))
   (do (trace/emit-error! :rf.error/invoke-all-unknown-child-id
                          {:machine-id parent-id
                           :invoke-id invoke-id
                           :child-id child-id
                           :children (:children join-state)
                           :kind kind})
       {:db db :fx []})
   ```
2. The new `:rf.error/invoke-all-unknown-child-id` event:
   - Goes under the `:rf.error/*` reserved prefix per Spec/009 §Error contract.
   - Carries the bogus id + the legitimate children set + the resolution kind for forensics.
3. Regression tests in `invoke_all_test.clj`:
   - Forged id with no live children → join unchanged + error emitted.
   - Repeated forged completions → each emits error; join still doesn't resolve.
   - Child-id that matches a DIFFERENT invoke-all sibling in same parent → not counted.
   - Legitimate child-id flow remains unchanged.

## Acceptance

- New test cases pin behaviour.
- No legitimate `:invoke-all` path regressed.
- The error trace shows up in the always-on error-emit substrate (verify symmetric with handler-exception classification).

title: fix(core): consume :interceptor-overrides — currently accepted but dead
description:
Spec/002 §Per-frame and per-call overrides (lines 1108-1139) specifies replace-by-`:id` interceptor substitution: per-call `{:interceptor-overrides {:my-app/logging nil}}` or per-frame `reg-frame {:interceptor-overrides {...}}` MUST walk the chain and substitute interceptors by their `:id`, with nil-substituted entries removed and per-call winning over per-frame on key conflict.

CURRENT IMPL IS DEAD CODE. `build-envelope` accepts `:interceptor-overrides` in opts (router.cljc:78, 133) and stores on the envelope. Per-frame `:interceptor-overrides` rides the frame config (frame.cljc handles it). But NO CODE PATH CONSUMES THE STORED VALUE: `apply-overrides` (router.cljc:230-252) merges `:fx-overrides` only; `prepare-handler-ctx` (router.cljc:521-541) builds chain from `extra-interceptors` (per-frame `:interceptors` prepend) + handler's own `:interceptors` — NO substitution-by-id walk.

```clojure
(defn- apply-icpt-overrides [chain overrides]
  (->> chain
       (mapv #(if (contains? overrides (:id %)) (get overrides (:id %)) %))
       (filter some?)))
```
Honor per-frame + per-call merge with per-call winning (matches `:fx-overrides` precedence in `apply-overrides`).

title: [spec+impl] Emit partial epoch records on drain-halt — devtools need cascade context for failing cascades
description:
## Problem

The current epoch-record emission contract silently DROPS the record on any drain-halting error, eliminating the devtools' view into the exact cascades developers most need to inspect.

**Current behavior** (per `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc`):
- `:rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded` → `handle-depth-exceeded!` calls `:epoch/discard-buffer!`; **no record committed, no listener fire** (rationale: "a misleading partial-cascade record")
- `:rf.frame/drain-interrupted` (frame destroyed mid-drain) → `handle-drain-interrupted!`; **epoch settle skipped** (rationale: "a half-cascade settle record would mislead time-travel consumers")
- `handle-drain-settled!` gated on `(pos? depth)` — only fires when at least one event processed cleanly

Trace events DO fire via the always-on error-emit substrate (rf2-vnjfg / rf2-rirbq), so `register-trace-cb!` listeners see the raw error. But `register-epoch-cb!` consumers (Causa epoch-panel, re-frame-pair2 cascade-of, post-mortem dashboards) get NOTHING — exactly when they're most needed.

## Why this is wrong for devtools

Causa and re-frame-pair2 exist to surface "what just happened in this cascade". The failing cascades ARE the bug. Silently dropping them means:
- Pair2's epoch panel shows nothing for a depth-exceeded cascade
- Causa can't render trace-up-to-halt with the error highlighted
- Time-travel "go to the failing epoch" is impossible
- Devs have to fall back to scanning the raw trace stream and rebuilding the cascade context manually — undoing the whole `:sub-runs` / `:renders` / `:effects` projection Spec 009 provides

The original "discard misleading record" rationale was protecting `restore-epoch` semantics — a valid concern, but addressable without hiding the data.

## Proposal

**Emit a partial epoch record on every halt**, with new schema slots distinguishing the outcome:

```clojure
;; Additive to spec/Spec-Schemas.md :rf/epoch-record
[:outcome      [:enum :ok :halted-depth :halted-destroy :halted-handler-exception]]
[:halt-reason  {:optional true} :any]   ;; pointer to the error trace by :id
;; :db-after carries whatever state the runtime actually settled to:
;;   - :ok                          → post-cascade db
;;   - :halted-depth                → pre-drain snapshot (atomic rollback)
;;   - :halted-destroy              → state at the moment of destroy
;;   - :halted-handler-exception    → impl-dependent (rollback if applied, else partial)
```

Schema is additive — existing consumers ignore `:outcome` and continue to work. Open maps per `spec/Principles.md`.

## Restore safety

`restore-epoch` refuses non-`:ok` records, emitting `:rf.epoch/restore-non-ok-record`:
```clojure
(when (not= :ok (:outcome epoch-record))
  (trace/emit-error! :rf.epoch/restore-non-ok-record
                     {:outcome     (:outcome epoch-record)
                      :halt-reason (:halt-reason epoch-record)
                      :reason      "Cannot restore a halted-cascade epoch."}))
```

That preserves the original "time-travel never lands you in a misleading state" invariant.

## Cascade-listener behaviour

`register-epoch-cb!` listeners receive EVERY epoch record — `:ok` and halted alike. Pair2 / Causa interpret `:outcome` and `:halt-reason` to render the partial cascade with the failure highlighted.

## Impl notes

- `handle-depth-exceeded!` should COMMIT a `:halted-depth` record (with `:db-after = db-before`, the rolled-back state) BEFORE clearing the queue
- `handle-drain-interrupted!` should COMMIT a `:halted-destroy` record before discarding
- `commit-and-flow!` handler-exception path: emit `:halted-handler-exception` only if the cascade actually halts the drain (currently the impl proceeds through commit-db / flows / fx after the error — this may itself be ambiguous per Spec 010 §line 140 "cascade halts"). Worth resolving as part of this bead.
- `register-epoch-cb!` cb-invocation path unchanged.
- Spec 009 §`register-epoch-cb!` (lines 220-252) gets a new "Halted cascades" paragraph documenting the contract.
- Spec-Schemas `:rf/epoch-record` (lines 2189-2236) gains the `:outcome` / `:halt-reason` rows.
- Conformance fixtures `drain-depth-limit.edn` + `cross-spec-machine-action-throws.edn` need updates to assert the new partial-record emission.

## Files touched

- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (epoch-cb spec)
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (epoch record schema)
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/drain-depth-limit.edn`

title: fix(http): JSON keyword-interning DoS — cap or string-key by default
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P1.4.

## Surface

- implementation/http/src/re_frame/util_json.cljc:112-133 (`read-object` — fallback reader)
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/util_json.cljc:171 (Cheshire branch — `json-parse` passes `true` for keywordize)

## Evidence

Both readers produce keyword keys from arbitrary JSON object keys. JVM keywords are interned and never GC'd. Long-running SSR JVM is the worst case.

## Exploit sketch

An app uses `:rf.http/managed` to call a third-party JSON API. Attacker compromises the upstream and returns 100k unique-key JSON objects per response. Each key becomes a permanent interned keyword. Particularly dangerous on the SSR JVM (long-running) — a compromised webhook recipient burns the box.

Note also: webhook receivers + agent-controlled fetches are real production exposure.

## Recommendation — DECISION required (audit Q3)

Three options:

**Option A** — keep keys as strings by default; offer `:keywordize? true` as an opt-in via the request map. Cheshire supports a `:key-fn` callback. Pro: zero exploit surface. Con: breaks idiomatic re-frame2 `(:foo response)` accessor pattern for every consumer.

**Option B** — cap JSON object cardinality and key length, throwing `:rf.http/decode-failure` on overflow. Cheaper, preserves keywordize-by-default convenience. Con: false-positive risk on legitimate large responses.

**Option C** — keywordize-by-default but with intern-budget per request (e.g. WeakHashMap of seen-strings, fall back to string keys after budget exhausted). Most complex; cleanest semantics.

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P1.4.
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1042 — Option B (cap) chosen. Cap is :rf.http/max-decoded-keys (default 10000). Both readers (Cheshire + pure-Clojure fallback) and CLJS path enforce; overflow throws :rf.http/decode-failure :reason :too-many-keys. Spec 014 §Keyword-interning cap documents.

title: fix(ssr): CRLF injection in set-header-fx / redirect-fx / Location header
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P1.3.

## Surface

- implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc:174-189 (`set-header-fx`, `append-header-fx`)
- implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc:213-243 (`redirect-fx`)
- implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/response.clj:21-24 (Location header materialisation)

## Evidence

Header values flow from event-handler input through `:rf.server/set-header` / `:rf.server/redirect` straight to the Ring response map. Nothing strips/rejects CRLF along the path.

## Exploit sketch

A redirect handler reads a `next` query param, dispatches `[:rf.server/redirect {:location next-param}]`. Attacker sends `?next=https://example.com%0d%0aSet-Cookie:%20stolen=1`. URL-decoding produces literal CRLF → header-splitting on the wire (assuming the host doesn't reject).

## Recommendation

Validate header values at the `set-header-fx` / `redirect-fx` boundary — reject CR/LF/NUL with structured error rather than host-specific 500.

**Mike decision point** (audit Q4): fail-fast (reject with `:rf.error/header-invalid`) or strip + warn? Lean fail-fast — more discoverable.

Note: also covers the Location-header materialisation site downstream; a single boundary check makes the wire-side immune.

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P1.3.
close_reason: Fixed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1043 (batched ssr security sweep — 5 P1 + 2 P2 + 1 structure)

title: fix(ssr-ring): CRLF injection in Set-Cookie attributes (:domain/:path/:name/:max-age/:same-site)
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P1.2.

## Surface

implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/cookie.clj:79-101 (`cookie->set-cookie-header`)

## Evidence

`:domain`, `:path`, `:max-age`, `:same-site` are concatenated raw into the Set-Cookie header. `:name` is concatenated raw via `(clojure.core/name name)`. Only `:value` is URL-encoded.

## Exploit sketch

Multi-tenant app that includes a tenant-controlled subdomain in `:domain`. Attacker registers `"evil.com\r\nSet-Cookie: admin=1; Path=/"`. The framework emits a Set-Cookie with embedded CRLF and a second forged Set-Cookie. Jetty 11+ rejects, but the framework should not rely on the host's defence.

## Recommendation

Reject cookie attribute values containing CR/LF/NUL with `:rf.error/cookie-invalid-attribute` at serialise time. Same for `:name` (no whitespace, controls, `=`/`;`/`,`).

Sibling P2 from same audit: cookie name not validated for RFC 6265 grammar (§P2.4) — fold into this fix.

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P1.2 + §P2.4.
close_reason: Fixed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1043 (batched ssr security sweep — 5 P1 + 2 P2 + 1 structure)

title: fix(ssr): JSON-LD <script> body injection — escape < as backslash-u003c in ld-json string values
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P1.1. Sibling vector to rf2-7ksyr.

## Surface

implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/emit.cljc:49-92 (`ld-json-string`, `emit-json-ld`)

## Evidence

`ld-json-string` escapes only `\` and `"` inside string values. The result is dropped raw inside `<script type="application/ld+json">…</script>`. A string value containing `</script>` closes the script tag and lets attacker HTML follow.

## Exploit sketch

An app writes user-controlled content (review body, listing title, author bio) into a JSON-LD slot via `reg-head`. Attacker submits `"</script><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>"`. The closing tag in the data terminates the JSON-LD block early; the second `<script>` runs in the document context. This is the exact rf2-7ksyr vector applied to JSON-LD instead of the hydration payload.

## Recommendation

When emitting a string inside a `<script>` body, escape `<` (or specifically `</`) as `<` inside JSON string literals. Keeps the JSON valid AND prevents tag-close. Same fix applies to the hydration payload (rf2-7ksyr) and any future `<script>`-embedded EDN.

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P1.1.
close_reason: Fixed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1043 (batched ssr security sweep — 5 P1 + 2 P2 + 1 structure)

title: fix(ssr-ring): ensure-content-type case-insensitive normalisation
description:
Split from rf2-dvnop audit.

`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/headers.clj` documents `ensure-content-type` as case-insensitive, but only checks `"content-type"` and `"Content-Type"`. A mixed-case existing header like `"CONTENT-TYPE"` or `"CoNtEnT-TyPe"` would currently duplicate the header instead of preserving it.

Same shape as rf2-6hbo8 (http Content-Type case-insensitivity, already shipped PR #963). Apply the same pattern here.

## Fix

Normalise header names to lower-case at the boundary (matches CLJS Fetch behaviour AND the http-side fix from rf2-6hbo8). Or: factor a small case-insensitive header lookup helper if normalisation is unsafe in some path.

## Acceptance

Test with mixed-case preexisting Content-Type header; assert no duplication.

Sourced from: rf2-dvnop §Robustness risks.
close_reason: Fixed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1043 (batched ssr security sweep — 5 P1 + 2 P2 + 1 structure)

title: fix(ssr-ring): escape </script> in __rf_payload injection — XSS / payload break risk
description:
Split from rf2-dvnop audit.

**implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj** injects `payload-edn` **raw** into:

    <script id="__rf_payload" type="application/edn">...</script>

There is no escaping. If user-controlled data reaches app-db and the payload string contains:
- `</script>` — breaks out of the script tag (XSS vector)
- `<script>` — could open a nested context
- Other parser-breaking content

This is a **real correctness bug**, not just a missing test. EDN serialisation of user data into app-db is common (any string field that round-trips).

## Fix

Escape `</script>` in the EDN payload before injection. The standard approach for inline JSON/EDN script tags is to backslash-escape `</script>` → `<\/script>` (or split the literal into `<\/scrip\\"t>`). Either pattern works because the EDN parser accepts both.

## Acceptance

- A regression test with payload containing `</script>` and `<script>` strings.
- Payload still round-trips through EDN reader unchanged.
- No XSS path remains.

Sourced from: rf2-dvnop §Robustness risks / Highest priority.
close_reason: Fixed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1043 (batched ssr security sweep — 5 P1 + 2 P2 + 1 structure)

title: refactor(routing): on-match :on-error trap + :transition :error (rf2-pm9pk follow-on)
description:
Follow-on from rf2-pm9pk. The settle portion (:transition :loading → :idle after on-match drain) landed in PR <TBD> via :rf.route/settle-transition. The :on-error trap remains:

  - Trap exceptions thrown by :on-match event handlers.
  - On exception: set :rf.route/transition :error, populate :rf.route/error with the structured error map (per Spec 009 §error contract).
  - If the route declares :on-error, dispatch it. The handler reads (:error (:rf/route db)) for the error context.

Implementation approach options:
  1. Register an error-emit listener (per re-frame.error-emit) and discriminate "is this exception from an :on-match dispatch?" via a frame-level tag.
  2. Add a new dispatch variant :rf.route/dispatch-on-match that wraps the inner event execution with try/catch; rewrite on-match :fx entries to use this wrapper.

Approach 2 is cleaner but requires invoking the registered handler directly. Approach 1 is fragile but needs no new event surface.

Audit: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-routing-2026-05-14.md S3.
Parent: rf2-yt2g2.

UPDATED: 2026-05-14 — split from pm9pk after the settle half landed standalone.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1047 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1047): on-match :on-error trap via corpus-wide error-emit listener; nav-token-guarded :rf.route/on-match-error event flips :transition :error + populates :rf.route/error + dispatches :on-error.

title: fix(ssr-ring): make default-html-shell honor :html-attrs and :body-attrs
description:

1. Thread `:html-attrs` / `:body-attrs` from the resolved head model into the default shell.
2. Reuse a shared attr-emission helper so shell and head emitter stay consistent.
3. Add an SSR regression test covering both attribute bags on the default shell path.

Note: an earlier bead on this topic appears closed, but the current code still fails the contract check in this audit pass.

title: fix(flows): route flow trace payloads through rf/elide-wire-value
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec 013 explicitly inherits the managed-effects elision contract for wire-bearing trace payloads.
Implementation: flow traces emit raw `:input-values`, raw `:result`, and raw failure `:inputs`; `trace/emit!` does not apply elision centrally.

Preserve: current `:rf.flow/computed` / `:rf.flow/failed` payload shape and per-flow attribution.

Options:
1. Elide `:input-values`, `:result`, and failure `:inputs` at the flow emit site with frame-aware opts.
2. Introduce a small helper for flow-trace payload shaping so computed and failed paths stay consistent.
3. Add a test with `:sensitive?` or `:large?` data proving trace output is redacted/elided.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1014 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1014. Flow trace payloads now ride through elision/elide-wire-value per Spec 009 §Size elision in traces. Both :rf.flow/computed (:input-values, :result) and :rf.flow/failed (:inputs) walk under their declared paths. Three new tests in flows_trace_test pin the routing.

title: fix(routing): implement schema validation for match-url, route-url, and :rf.route/navigate
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: route params/query can be schema-validated in `match-url`, `route-url`, and `:rf.route/navigate`; navigation should reject invalid values rather than silently substituting a fallback URL.
Implementation: `match-url` hardcodes `:validation-failed? false`, `route-url` never validates params/query, and `:rf.route/navigate` catches route-url exceptions and falls back to `"/"`.

Preserve: current path/query parsing, simple query coercion, and pure `match-url` / `route-url` API shape.

Options:
1. Add route-schema validation in `match-url` with `:validation-failed?` / `:validation-error`.
2. Make `route-url` throw `:rf.error/route-url-validation` with explain data.
3. Route `:rf.route/navigate` through the normal validation path instead of swallowing failures to `"/"`.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1020 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1020)

title: fix(routing): make :rf.route/navigate write fragment/nav-token and emit nav-token trace
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: programmatic navigation must allocate a fresh nav-token, write both `:fragment` and `:nav-token` into `:rf/route`, and emit `:rf.route.nav-token/allocated`.
Implementation: `:rf.route/navigate` writes `:id`, `:params`, `:query`, `:transition`, and `:error`, but omits `:fragment`, `:nav-token`, and the allocation trace.

Preserve: target resolution, route-id vs URL-string handling, state-first ordering, and current scroll-fx emission shape.

Options:
1. Add a shared nav-state builder used by both `:rf.route/navigate` and `:rf/url-changed`.
2. Thread nav-token allocation into programmatic navigation only.
3. Add regression tests that assert slice contents and `:rf.route.nav-token/allocated`.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1020 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1020)

title: fix(adapters): complete dispose-adapter! conformance across browser adapters
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: Spec 006 adapter disposal lifecycle requires browser adapters to cancel reactive subscriptions, release host resources, discard caches, and unmount active roots where relevant.
Implementation: browser adapters currently implement `dispose-adapter!` as a no-op. Existing open issues cover some adapters already, but the audit confirmed the contract is still incomplete across the browser-adapter surface, especially Helix and reagent-slim.

Preserve: current per-render unmount thunks and the cheap no-op path when nothing was mounted.

Options:
1. Track active roots / unmount fns inside each browser adapter and drain them in `dispose-adapter!`.
2. Centralize root tracking in a shared substrate helper used by all browser adapters.
3. If caller-owned teardown is the intended model, weaken the spec explicitly and document the new responsibility split.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1041 — adapters shared batch cluster

title: spec(substrate): resolve internal contradictions in Spec 006 adapter semantics
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: spec weakness.
Spec 006 contradicts itself: early normative text says CLJS-headless `subscribe-container` is unsupported / returns nil, plain-atom has no listeners, and derived containers cache on input equality; later adapter sections and the reference implementation use `add-watch` listeners and recompute-on-deref derived containers.

Preserve: the later adapter-specific behavior already shared by the implementation and the later reference-adapter sections.

Options:
1. Rewrite the early normative text to match the later adapter sections.
2. Change the implementations to the early contract and update the later examples.
3. Split generic contract from reference-adapter permitted variants so the exceptions are explicit.
close_reason:
Resolved via PR #988 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/988

Chose Option 1: rewrite early normative text to match the later adapter sections and the shipped reference implementations. Surgical edits — 4 spots in spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md, 7 lines added / 7 removed, no section headings renamed, no renumbering, all 30+ inbound cross-refs to Spec 006 intact. The early text was not describing a generic substrate-agnostic minimum (which would have justified Option 3); it was wrong about what the shipped adapters actually do (Reagent, UIx, Helix, plain-atom all use add-watch listeners and recompute-on-deref derived containers, with =-equality enforced by the per-frame sub-cache). Pre-alpha; the spec is the artefact; top-down readers should not hit a contradiction half a screen apart.

Cross-cut flagged for follow-up: implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/plain_atom.cljc ns docstring (lines 4-7) still carries the old contradictory prose; file a follow-up impl bead if rf2-nz3f1 doesn't catch it.

title: fix(adapters): pair UIx/Helix use-subscribe with unsubscribe cleanup
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: hook-based adapter subscriptions must dispose/unsubscribe on cleanup.
Implementation: UIx and Helix `use-subscribe` memoize `subs/subscribe`, but cleanup only removes an `add-watch` listener; the sub-cache ref-count is never decremented on unmount or key change.

Preserve: one stable reaction per `(frame, query)` during component lifetime and the existing `useSyncExternalStore` watch bridge.

Options:
1. Add cleanup that calls `subs/unsubscribe` for the memoized subscription.
2. Wrap the memoized subscription in a disposable handle and dispose it from hook cleanup.
3. Factor the hook lifecycle into a shared helper used by both UIx and Helix.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1041 — adapters shared batch cluster

title: fix(schemas): make schema-validation failure paths precise and sensitivity-aware
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: ambiguous (lean implementation drift).
Spec: schema-validation failure traces should report the failing path and apply sensitivity logic to that path's schema.
Implementation: `validate-app-db!` always emits the registered schema root as `:path`, then falls back to coarse whole-value redaction whenever any nested slot is sensitive.

Preserve: the current conservative privacy posture when exact path extraction is unavailable.

Options:
1. Derive the failing leaf path from Malli explain data and emit that as `:path`.
2. Keep conservative whole-value redaction only as a fallback when no path can be extracted.
3. Add a second field like `:registered-path` if tools still need root registration context.
close_reason: Landed: validate-app-db! now derives the failing leaf path from the registered explainer's :in slot (concat'd with the registration root) and applies path-targeted sensitivity (ancestor- or descendant-sensitive at the leaf). Trace tags: :path = leaf path; new :registered-path = registration root; :value = the failing leaf's value (narrowed via get-in :in). Conservative fallback to whole-schema sensitivity when explainer absent/non-Malli. Tests: implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_failure_paths_test.clj (15 deftests). Spec 010 §All-validation-points text updated to document :path / :registered-path; conformance fixture schema-app-db-slice-validates.edn updated to assert leaf [:user :id].

title: fix(schemas): roll back app-db on schema-validation failure
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Related context: there is already an open decision bead about this contract drift.
Spec: Spec 010 says a post-handler `app-db` schema failure restores the pre-handler db and treats the dispatch as failed.
Implementation: the runtime commits `:db`, emits `:event/db-changed`, and only then traces `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure`.

Preserve: structured schema-failure trace emission with the triggering handler id.

Options:
1. Capture pre-commit db in the router and restore it on any failing path.
2. Have `validate-app-db!` return structured failures so the router can decide rollback deterministically.
3. Move validation before durable commit if that produces a simpler integration.
close_reason: Closed via PR #1054 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1054). Implements the rf2-wkxng decision: validate-app-db! returns boolean; router rolls back :db + skips flows/fx on failure; trace tag carries :rollback? true.

title: fix(core+machines): run machine exit/disposal cascades during destroy-frame
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: ambiguous (lean implementation drift).
Spec: Cross-Spec Interactions requires destroying a frame with active machines to run machine exit/disposal cascades in reverse creation order before sub-cache / adapter teardown.
Implementation: destroy-frame aborts HTTP and emits destroy traces, but does not run machine exit cascades.

Preserve: current HTTP-abort hook and per-machine destroy tracing.

Options:
1. Delegate frame-destroy machine teardown to the machines artefact.
2. Track spawn order so reverse-creation disposal is possible.
3. If v1 cannot support this, narrow the spec explicitly instead of silently under-implementing it.
notes: PR #1089 opened (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1089). Option 1 implementation — :machines/teardown-on-frame-destroy! late-bind hook; reverse-creation walk via process-side spawn-order channel; exit cascade + unified teardown projection + handler unregister; singleton handlers stay registered (Spec 005 v1-partial).
close_reason: Landed via PR #1089 (already merged). Option 1 implementation: :machines/teardown-on-frame-destroy! late-bind hook + reverse-creation walk via spawn-order channel. Bead state was stuck in_progress.

title: fix(core): queue child-frame :on-create asynchronously inside handler-created frames
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: Spec 002 says top-level frame creation dispatches `:on-create` synchronously, but `reg-frame` / `make-frame` inside a handler must queue the child frame's `:on-create` asynchronously on the child router.
Implementation: `reg-frame` always calls `dispatch-sync`, causing cross-frame interleaving during a parent drain.

Preserve: synchronous `:on-create` for ordinary top-level frame creation.

Options:
1. Detect in-drain creation and switch child-frame `:on-create` to `dispatch!`.
2. Route through an internal helper that chooses sync vs async by context.
3. Keep the current top-level fast path unchanged.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #1018 — reg-frame branches on frame/*current-frame*: bound = async-queue via :router/dispatch!, unbound = dispatch-sync. make-frame inherits the fix. Three new tests in frame_lifecycle_test.clj.

title: fix(core): interrupt active frame drains on destroy
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: Spec 002 / Spec 009 require `destroy-frame` to interrupt an active drain before the next dequeue, drop the remaining queue once, and emit `:rf.frame/drain-interrupted`.
Implementation: the router keeps dequeuing after frame removal and surfaces repeated `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` errors instead.

Preserve:
- the already-dequeued event should still run to completion
- the current single-drainer locking

Options:
1. Add the destroyed-frame check before each dequeue in `run-one-pass!`.
2. Clear the remaining queue and emit one lifecycle event with `:dropped-count`.
3. Reuse the existing epoch discard path so aborted drains still record nothing.
notes: Follow-up: CI-only JVM test flake in destroy-from-handler-interrupts-drain-and-emits-interrupted. The test pre-seeds 4 async dispatches then dispatch-sync's a self-destruct seed at the front; on JVM, interop/next-tick runs on a separate single-thread executor, racing the main thread. On fast CI runners the async drain processed the 4 ticks BEFORE dispatch-sync reached drain-lock, leaving an empty queue and yielding :dropped-count 0. CLJS next-tick is a microtask in the same JS task (no race). Fix: wrap the four async dispatches + dispatch-sync in (with-redefs [interop/next-tick ...]) to capture the scheduled drains so dispatch-sync deterministically wins the drain-lock with all 4 ticks still queued. Captured ticks are discarded — frame is destroyed before they would dequeue and rf2-dpny says a drain on an already-destroyed frame is a silent no-op. Implementation untouched; the run-one-pass! disposed-check works correctly on both runtimes once the test removes the race.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #1018 — new frame/frame-disposed-for-drain? predicate; router/run-one-pass! checks before each dequeue and on detect handle-drain-interrupted! drops queue + emits one :rf.frame/drain-interrupted. Run-to-completion preserved; rf2-dpny contract unaffected.

title: fix(machines): forward decisive child payload through invoke-all join resolution
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: Spec 005 `:invoke-all` join resolution payload forwarding.
Implementation: join interception discards the decisive child payload and emits the join event without the child `& extra` data; the failure trace also omits the spec's `:reason` payload.

Why it matters:
- Parent join handlers cannot inspect the forwarded child result/error payload as specified.
- Useful current behavior to preserve: current join bookkeeping, cancellation timing, and single-fire resolution behavior.

Options:
1. Append the intercepted child `& extra` onto the dispatched join event.
2. Persist decisive payload in join state and project it into the join event / trace.
3. Enrich `:rf.machine.invoke-all/any-failed` with failure reason and add fixture coverage.
close_reason: Closed

title: fix(machines): run child :exit on all destroy paths
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: Spec 005 state-machine destroy/final-state semantics.
Implementation: machine destroy/finalize paths tear down actor state without executing the active state's `:exit` action.

Why it matters:
- Explicit `:rf.machine/destroy`, `:invoke` exit teardown, `:invoke-all` cancellation, and final-state auto-destroy can skip child cleanup that the spec promises.
- Useful current behavior to preserve: synchronous teardown, existing `:system-id` release ordering, and current snapshot/registrar cleanup.

Options:
1. Route destroy/finalize through one helper that resolves and executes the active leaf's `:exit` before teardown.
2. Reuse the transition-layer exit-cascade logic directly from destroy/finalize.
3. Add regression coverage for explicit destroy, `:invoke-all` cancellation, and final-state auto-destroy.
close_reason: Closed

title: test(adapters): add use-subscribe unit coverage (Helix + UIx)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-w0u2w (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/helix`, 2026-05-14).
**Findings doc:** `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-helix-2026-05-14.md` §T-1.

## Problem

Grep for `use-subscribe` and `use-current-frame` in `adapters/helix/test/**` and `adapters/uix/test/**` returns zero hits. The hook is published as the canonical Helix subscribe surface (per Decision 1 of rf2-2qit, rf2-3yij), documented in README, spec/API.md, and spec/MIGRATION.md, used by `examples/helix/counter_helix` — but exercised only via Playwright (browser smoke), not the unit-test runner.

If `use-subscribe`'s React.useSyncExternalStore wiring regresses (e.g. `subscribe-fn`'s add-watch keying breaks, snapshot fn returns stale-on-tear, the deps vec for use-memo* drops a dep), headless tests stay green and only Playwright catches it.

## Recommendation

Add a node-runnable test in each adapter's test tree (`helix_use_subscribe_cljs_test.cljs`, `uix_use_subscribe_cljs_test.cljs`) that:

1. Sets up a JSDOM-y container (or uses `React/act` with a manually-driven createRoot).
2. Registers a sub.
3. Renders a component that calls `use-subscribe` and writes the value to a side-channel atom.
4. Dispatches an event that mutates the source.
5. Calls `flush-views!` (once that's fixed — see rf2-jk7hr).
6. Asserts the side-channel reflects the post-dispatch value.
7. Repeats with the 2-arg form pinning an explicit frame.

The Reagent adapter's `scenario-7-concurrent-renders-survive-act-flush` test in `adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/frame_provider_context_cljs_test.cljs` is a template.

## Estimate

~+40 LoC per adapter (~+80 total).

## Severity

P1 — substantial unit-test gap on the publicly-documented primary subscribe surface for both function-component adapters.

## Coordination

Depends on rf2-jk7hr (flush-views! fix) for clean test plumbing.

title: refactor(adapters): fix flush-views! fallback + add coverage (Helix + UIx)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-w0u2w (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/helix`, 2026-05-14).
**Findings doc:** `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-helix-2026-05-14.md` §CQ-1.

## Problem

In both `adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs:289-304` and `adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:283-298`, `flush-views!` ships:

```clojure
(when-let [act (or (.-act React)
                   ;; React 18 moved act into react-dom/test-utils;
                   ;; if not on React directly, swallow gracefully.
                   nil)]
  (act f))
```

Two issues:

1. The `(or X nil)` collapses to `(.-act React)` — the literal `nil` in the `or` is a no-op fallback. The comment promises a `react-dom/test-utils` fallback the body does not implement. A user on React 18.x where `act` still lives in `react-dom/test-utils` gets a silent no-op.
2. No test in either `adapters/helix/test/**` or `adapters/uix/test/**` references `flush-views!` or `React/act` — the published surface is uncovered.

The Reagent adapter's test helper at `adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/frame_provider_context_cljs_test.cljs:473-477` has a working fallback to model after.

## Recommendation

In both `helix.cljs` and `uix.cljs`:

1. Port the Reagent-test `act-fn` pattern: `(or (when (exists? (.-act React)) (.-act React)) (try (let [tu (js/require "react-dom/test-utils")] (.-act tu)) (catch :default _ nil)))`.
2. Add a `flush-views!` smoke test in each adapter's test tree (call with no-arg, call with a thunk, assert nil return shape, assert React.act invocation).

## Estimate

~+12 LoC code, +30 LoC tests across both adapters.

## Severity

P1 — published surface that silently no-ops on common React versions; users following MIGRATION advice ("Reagent tests calling r/flush become Helix tests calling (flush-views!)") get no flush.

## Cross-adapter

Helix and UIx have the bug byte-for-byte; one PR can fix both. Reagent doesn't ship `flush-views!` (its tests use r/flush directly).
notes: Agent killed at ~12:00 AUSEST after 44+ min stall (0 bytes output). Stuck on browser test infrastructure — agent had reported 'Port 8021 clear. Run browser test in background — keep it streamable' before going silent. Browser-test hangs are a recurring pattern (same recipe as the rf2-e9s81 stall before its retry). Next attempt should either skip the browser-test gate (the fix is well-typed enough to verify via JVM/cljs gates alone) or use a more aggressive timeout/headless config.
close_reason: Subsumed into PR #1015 (rf2-3vwbx). The flush-views! react-dom/test-utils fallback is implemented in re-frame.substrate.spine.

title: refactor(uix): implement dispose-adapter! per Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle (or update spec) — UIx side
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-0fgm8 (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/uix`, 2026-05-14).
**Findings doc:** `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-uix-2026-05-14.md` (local-only).
**Sibling:** rf2-a47kq (reagent side).

## Problem

`dispose-adapter!` in uix.cljs lines 418–422 is a no-op with a "nothing special to do" justification comment, but Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle (lines 208–227) lists FOUR MUSTs:

1. Cancel all in-flight reactive subscriptions.
2. Release host-specific resources (DOM event listeners, websocket subscribers, timers).
3. Discard internal caches.
4. Make subsequent calls to other adapter functions return `:rf.error/adapter-disposed` (or throw, host-dependent).

The UIx no-op covers none of (1)–(4). Same drift exists in Helix (`implementation/adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs` lines 425–429) and in Reagent (covered by rf2-a47kq).

## Recommendation

Decide cross-adapter: either

A. Expand each adapter's `dispose-adapter!` to:
   - (a) clear adapter-side `hiccup-emitter` defonce
   - (b) clear adapter-side `warned-non-dom-roots` defonce
   - (c) install a sentinel on the adapter map's other fns so subsequent calls throw `:rf.error/adapter-disposed` (matches the spec MUST contract).

B. Update Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle to say React-shaped substrates need none of (1)–(3) because React unmounts handle listener teardown, and only (4) is normative.

Pick A for masterpiece-grade conformance, B if (1)–(3) are genuinely no-ops given React's lifecycle.

## Severity

P1 — spec drift on a MUST-list. Coordinated decision with rf2-a47kq + a Helix-side companion.

## Coordination

Same decision and same PR shape as rf2-a47kq. Recommend the PR covers UIx + Helix + Reagent in one go; the decision is global to the React-shaped adapter family.
close_reason: Landed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1051

description:

No duplication remained at PR #1058 dispatch time.

title: refactor(reagent-slim): dedup class-names (template) vs class-string (server) in same artefact
description:
Per audit rf2-bgnin (A-1, Top-3 finding #3).

reagent2.impl.template/class-names (template.cljs:268-284) and reagent2.dom.server/class-string (server.cljs:250-257) both do the same coercion: coll value → space-joined names; named value → name; string → passthrough. Structurally identical.

The SSR ns docstring (server.cljs:53, 92-97) claims this duplication is intentional 'because bundle isolation forbids :require between artefacts.' But template.cljs and server.cljs are BOTH inside the day8/reagent-slim artefact; bundle isolation only forbids :require between artefacts (re-frame.ssr is a separate artefact). The cited rf2-6phn note doesn't apply here.

Fix: keep template/class-names (broader: 0/1/2 arities). Add :require [reagent2.impl.template] to server.cljs (already there for parse-tag). Delete server.cljs class-string; rewrite the two callers (named->str on line 257, and merge-shorthand on line 268) to use template/class-names.

Net LoC: ~-15.

Risk: low — template/class-names handles all the same cases class-string handles (verified by reading both).
close_reason: template/class-names promoted to public; server.cljs class-string deleted; merge-shorthand uses template/class-names directly. -15 LoC.

title: refactor(reagent-slim): collapse force-update 2-arity (silent :deep? no-op)
description:
Per audit rf2-bgnin (CQ-3).

In implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/core.cljs, force-update (lines 133-146) has a 2-arity [^js this _deep?] that silently ignores the :deep? flag and does identical work to the 1-arity. The comment (lines 140-144) admits no production caller relies on the deep behaviour.

Pre-alpha rule: back-compat is not a concern. Silent semantic divergence is a footgun: a migrating user passes :deep? true expecting deep re-render, gets shallow, no warning.

Two acceptable fixes:
A) Drop the 2-arity entirely. (fn force-update [^js this] ...). Cleanest.
B) Keep the 2-arity but throw :rf.error/force-update-deep-unsupported with a migration message. More honest about the failure mode.

Slim adapter's elsewhere-discipline (the Class B throw-on-call shims for React-19-removed surfaces in dom.cljs, core.cljs lines 184+) suggests option B is the in-house pattern. Decision likely B.

Either way: net LoC ~-8 (option A) or ±0 (option B with throw).

Test: add a reagent2.core/force-update test (per follow-on T-1). Covers 1-arity calls .forceUpdate; 2-arity throws-or-drops-cleanly.

title: refactor(mcp-conformance): add JS-vs-Malli OverflowBody schema cross-encoding sanity test
description:
**Source:** refactor-audit r2 of \`tools/mcp-conformance\` (rf2-azk9c), finding **F-EMIT-1**.

## The gap

\`test/live-pair2-overflow.js:106-161\` hand-rolls \`assertOverflowBody(body, ctx)\` as a JS re-encoding of the JVM \`OverflowBody\` Malli schema. The comment at line 104 claims:

> A drift between the two pins is a vocabulary bug: the marker MUST validate against both encodings identically.

But **nothing tests that.** If the Malli schema tightens (e.g. \`:cap-tokens\` becomes required), the JS form silently lags. If the JS form gains a check (e.g. \`:hint\` must be ≤200 chars), the Malli form silently lags.

## Fix options (pick during impl)

**(a) Minimal — comment-driven sanity:** add a fat block comment to both forms listing every field both must check, with a date stamp; demand any change updates both pins.

**(b) Belt-and-braces — a JVM gate that asserts the JS hand-rolled form:** read \`live-pair2-overflow.js\` from JVM (\`slurp\`) and grep for the literal substrings each Malli schema field requires (\`:cap-tokens\` int check, etc.). When the Malli schema gains a field, the grep test fails and forces the JS update.

**(c) Heavy — generate the JS from the Malli schema at test time.** Probably not worth it.

Probably (b) is the sweet spot — one deftest in \`wire_vocab_test.clj\` that grep-asserts the JS body. ~10 LoC.

## Severity

P1 — silent divergence risk; the two encodings can quietly disagree on what 'the contract' means.

## Time estimate

20-40 min (depending on fix option chosen).

## Coordination

Touches \`wire_vocab_test.clj\` (option b) and/or \`live-pair2-overflow.js\` (option a). Isolated.
close_reason: Landed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1017

title: refactor(mcp-conformance): extract repo-root + read-source helper to dedupe JVM test boilerplate
description:

title: refactor(mcp-conformance): tighten OverflowBody schema to forbid empty-bodied marker
description:
**Source:** refactor-audit r2 of \`tools/mcp-conformance\` (rf2-azk9c), finding **F-VOCAB-2**.

## The gap

\`wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/wire_vocab_test.clj:213-225\`:

\`\`\`clojure
(def OverflowBody
  [:map
   {:closed false}
   [:limit [:enum :reached]]                                   ;; pair2-mcp
   [:tool   {:optional true} [:or :string :keyword]]
   [:cap-tokens   {:optional true} :int]
   [:cap          {:optional true} :int]
   [:token-count  {:optional true} :int]
   [:would-be     {:optional true} :int]
   [:hint         {:optional true} [:or :string :keyword]]
   [:continuation {:optional true} [:map ...]]])
\`\`\`

Every slot except \`:limit\` is optional. \`{:rf.mcp/overflow {:limit :reached}}\` alone — no \`:cap-tokens\`, \`:token-count\`, \`:tool\`, \`:hint\`, \`:cap\`, \`:would-be\`, OR \`:continuation\` — validates.

The cross-server contract intends EITHER:
- **pair2-mcp shape:** \`:cap-tokens\` + \`:token-count\` + \`:tool\` + \`:hint\` required.
- **causa-mcp shape:** \`:cap\` + \`:would-be\` + \`:hint\` (+ optional \`:continuation\`) required.

An empty-bodied marker shipped by a future regression slips through.

## Fix

Replace with \`[:or pair2-shape causa-shape]\`. Both existing fixtures still validate; an empty-bodied marker fails loud.

\`\`\`clojure
(def Pair2OverflowBody
  [:map {:closed false}
   [:limit       [:enum :reached]]
   [:tool        [:or :string :keyword]]
   [:cap-tokens  :int]
   [:token-count :int]
   [:hint        [:or :string :keyword]]])

(def CausaOverflowBody
  [:map {:closed false}
   [:limit        [:enum :reached]]
   [:cap          :int]
   [:would-be     :int]
   [:hint         [:or :string :keyword]]
   [:continuation {:optional true} [:map [:cursor {:optional true} [:or :string :nil]]
                                          [:next-args {:optional true} [:maybe :map]]]]])

(def OverflowBody [:or Pair2OverflowBody CausaOverflowBody])
\`\`\`

(Sketch — refine when implementing.)

## Severity

P1 — the schema under-constrains the contract by accepting a degenerate marker. The two fixtures in \`canonical-markers\` document the intended shapes; the schema should pin them.

## Coordination

Touches \`wire_vocab_test.clj\` only. Isolated, parallel-safe with other mcp-conformance beads that don't touch this file.

## Time estimate

15-30 min (schema rewrite + verify both fixtures + check live-pair2-overflow's hand-rolled JS form still agrees).

title: refactor(epoch): fold rf2-t0hq history-narration in malli-validate-fn docstring
description:
Per refactor-audit r2 (rf2-lwn4t): `malli-validate-fn` docstring (`epoch.cljc:480-499`) carries history narration:

    Per rf2-t0hq the CLJS runtime `resolve` is a compile-time analyzer
    affordance, not a runtime fn — the historical `:cljs (resolve
    'malli.core/validate)` arm silently returned nil, so the
    schema-mismatch failure-mode predicate at epoch-restore time treated
    every recorded db as conforming on CLJS.

The 'historical `:cljs (resolve ...)` arm silently returned nil' clause is pure post-mortem narration about a deprecated arm. Fold to:

    Per rf2-t0hq — CLJS has no runtime `resolve`, so the lookup order on
    CLJS is: late-bind hook then nil. Returning nil is treated as
    soft-pass by callers ('cannot disprove, treat as valid').

title: refactor(epoch): on-frame-destroyed! restructure — let body or hoist; indentation lies about scope
description:
Per refactor-audit r2 (rf2-lwn4t): in `on-frame-destroyed!` (`epoch.cljc:199-222`), the parens balance such that `(swap! histories dissoc frame-id)` on line 222 is INSIDE the `when` but OUTSIDE the `let` body. The `let` closes on line 217 at `m))))` (four parens close: if, let, inner-fn, then the FOURTH closes the outer let). Lines 218-222 are at `when` body level.

BUT the indentation of lines 218-222 is 4 spaces, matching the `(let` keyword's column — so a reader would think they're inside the `let` body. The indentation lies about scope.

Fix: restructure either:

1. Move `(swap! histories dissoc frame-id)` INSIDE the `let` so indentation matches.
2. OR hoist the `silenced-cbs` computation, use a `do` for the sequence of side-effects:

    (when interop/debug-enabled?
      (let [silenced-cbs (->> @observed-frames-by-cb ...)]
        (doseq [cb-id silenced-cbs]
          (trace/emit! ...)))
      (swap! observed-frames-by-cb prune-frame frame-id)
      (swap! histories dissoc frame-id))

The `reduce-kv` block on lines 209-217 can also extract to a private `(defn- drop-frame-from-cb-observations [m frame-id] ...)` for clarity.

Findings doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-epoch-2026-05-14.md` §F1.8.
close_reason: Resolved in PR #983. on-frame-destroyed! restructured per option 2 — closed the let after the doseq emit-loop; both swap!s now sit at when body level with honest indentation. Hoisted the reduce-kv block into private drop-frame-from-cb-observations helper. 62 JVM + 1816 CLJS tests green. PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/983

title: refactor(epoch): notify-listeners! guards record-observation! swap to avoid per-listener churn
description:
Per refactor-audit r2 (rf2-lwn4t): `notify-listeners!` (`epoch.cljc:172-181`) calls `record-observation!` for every listener on every drain-settle. `record-observation!` does a `swap!` on `observed-frames-by-cb` unconditionally — even when the listener has already observed that frame.

For a long-lived app with stable frame-id-per-listener (the common case), this is N swap!s per settle for ZERO state change. Pure churn.

Fix: guard the swap with a contains-check, or batch the observation update into a single swap! that derives the new state from `record` and `@listeners` (one swap per settle instead of one per listener):

    (defn- record-observation! [cb-id frame-id]
      (when frame-id
        (swap! observed-frames-by-cb
               (fn [m]
                 (if (contains? (get m cb-id) frame-id)
                   m
                   (update m cb-id (fnil conj #{}) frame-id))))))

Findings doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-epoch-2026-05-14.md` §F1.7.
close_reason: PR #979 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/979 — guard-inside chosen over batched-swap (preserves notify-listeners! shape, zero steady-state alloc); regression test uses atom watcher counter (Clojure persistent maps can return identical instances for value-equal updates, so identity-equality is too weak). Pre-fix: 5 swaps across 4 cascades; post-fix: 2 swaps.

title: refactor(epoch): collapse double-walk of missing-references / machine-version-mismatch / failing-paths-for in check-restore-preconditions!
description:

title: refactor(reagent): fix render-to-string :rf.error/no-hiccup-emitter-bound :reason text (cross-adapter)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-z3oab.
**Findings doc:** \`ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-reagent-2026-05-14.md\`.

## Problem

The error message at `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:91-93`:

```clojure
(throw (ex-info \":rf.error/no-hiccup-emitter-bound\"
                {:reason \"use the plain-atom adapter on the JVM for SSR, or install via set-hiccup-emitter!\"
                 :render-tree render-tree}))
```

steers users wrong:

1. **CLJS context.** This is the CLJS-side adapter; a CLJS app cannot \"use the plain-atom adapter on the JVM\" without context-switching to the JVM build.
2. **Outdated guidance.** Per rf2-uo7v, SSR moved to `day8/re-frame2-ssr`, not the plain-atom adapter. The correct guidance is \"require `re-frame.ssr` so its ns-load resolves the `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!` late-bind hook, or call `set-hiccup-emitter!` directly\".

The same wrong text duplicates in:
- `adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:91-93`
- `adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:142-144`
- `adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:161-163`
- `adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs:165-167`

## Recommendation

Replace the `:reason` field across all four adapters with: `\"require re-frame.ssr (the SSR ns-load resolves the :reagent/set-hiccup-emitter! late-bind hook automatically), or call set-hiccup-emitter! directly\"`.

If/when the cross-adapter dedup bead lands (rf2-3vwbx), the `render-to-string` body collapses into a shared helper and this fix lands at one site.

Add a regression test pinning the :reason field — see the sibling bead for the test gap.

## Severity

P1 — debug-time pitfall; users hitting this error during SSR-bring-up are pointed at the wrong fix.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1058: :reason text in :rf.error/no-hiccup-emitter-bound updated across spine + Reagent + reagent-slim to point users at (require '[re-frame.ssr]) instead of the JVM plain-atom adapter (CLJS-context-wrong) and the pre-rf2-uo7v SSR shape.

title: refactor(epoch): lift drain-check + frame-exists preconditions to a helper; share between restore-epoch and reset-frame-db!

The data-shape factoring of `check-restore-preconditions!` is excellent; the same lift to `reset-frame-db!` would harmonise the two paths.
