title: refactor(reagent): implement dispose-adapter! per Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle (or update spec)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-z3oab.
**Findings doc:** \`ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-reagent-2026-05-14.md\`.

## Problem

`re-frame.adapter.reagent/dispose-adapter!` at `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:107-110` is a no-op with a comment saying \"Reagent's reaction caches GC themselves when their owners go away. Nothing special to do here.\"

Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle (lines 216-222) requires:

1. Cancel all in-flight reactive subscriptions.
2. Release any host-specific resources (DOM event listeners, websocket subscribers, timers).
3. Discard internal caches.
4. Make subsequent calls to other adapter functions return `:rf.error/adapter-disposed` (or throw).

Spec 006 lines 700-708 (bridging pseudocode) names three concrete calls: `(sub-cache/dispose-all!)`, `(fc/dispose-providers!)`, `(ratom/flush!)`.

The comment captures only the production-path GC observation. Two concerns:

- **Test-fixture path:** `reset-runtime-fixture` calls `dispose-adapter!` between tests. The per-frame sub-cache holds Reaction references on a defonce frame registry; without explicit `(ratom/flush!)` pending reactions can survive across test boundaries. This is the same shape `warn_once_fixture_isolation_cljs_test` defends against in the warn-once tier.
- **Spec drift:** the spec carries a four-item MUST and a three-call bridging pseudocode; the impl no-ops both. Either the impl is wrong or the spec is.

## Decisions for Mike

Option A: implement the three-call bridging shape in the adapter (calls `sub-cache/dispose-all!`, `fc/dispose-providers!`, `ratom/flush!`). Spec is right; impl was lazy.

Option B: update Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle to note that for adapters built on Reagent's reaction-cache GC, the four-item MUST list reduces to a no-op IFF the test fixture documents this. Impl was right; spec was overspec'd.

Decision belongs to Mike; the audit cannot tell which is intended.

## Severity

P1 — normative spec MUST is currently a no-op; impl-vs-spec drift visible to anyone reading both.
close_reason: Closed by PR #1048 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1048). Hybrid Option A + B per pre-alpha rule: strengthened dispose-adapter! to walk-and-dispose per-frame sub-caches across all live frames (closes the test-fixture / headless path gap); rewrote Spec 006 bridging pseudocode to reflect what actually ships (frame-provider is stateless per rf2-4y60; Reagent's reaction caches GC on last-watcher-drop).

title: refactor(reagent): extract substrate-spine helpers; collapse cross-adapter duplication
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-z3oab (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/reagent`, 2026-05-14).
**Findings doc:** `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-reagent-2026-05-14.md` (local-only).

## Problem

The substrate-contract spine (`make-state-container`, `read-container`, `replace-container!`, `subscribe-container`, `render`, `render-to-string` + emitter glue) is duplicated byte-for-byte (modulo gensym prefix) across all four React-shaped adapter ns's:

- `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs`
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs`
- `implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs`
- `implementation/adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs`

The `(satisfies? ratom/IReactiveAtom ^js x)` predicate hook is duplicated 4x verbatim with a copy-pasted (incorrect) `^js` hint.

## Recommendation

Extract a shared helpers namespace — likely `re-frame.substrate.adapter-helpers` in core — that exports:

- `make-state-container` (Reagent ratom shape; plain `atom` shape; takes the underlying `atom-ctor` fn)
- `read-container`, `replace-container!` (one-liners; could move to substrate.adapter directly)
- `subscribe-container` (parameterised on gensym-prefix)
- `make-react-root-renderer` (the createRoot+render / hydrateRoot shape; parameterised on `react-dom/client` ns)
- `make-late-bind-render-to-string` (the hiccup-emitter atom + set!-er + thrower)

Each adapter ns then becomes ~30 LoC of "this is the substrate-bindings map I supply to the shared helpers", plus its substrate-unique surface (uix's `use-subscribe`, helix's `use-subscribe`, reagent-slim's `wrap-render`-via-reagent2-internals, …).

## Estimate

~120 LoC removed across the four adapters. Reagent shrinks 188 → ~110 LoC.

## Audit context

This is the dominant cross-adapter finding in the audit; six other audit findings collapse under this refactor as the same code stops being duplicated. Mike should decide if this is one PR or four (one per adapter), and whether the helpers ns lives under `core/` or under a new shared `adapters/shared/` artefact.

## Severity

P1 — high-yield refactor; pre-alpha rule applies (no back-compat constraint).
notes: Resolved via PR #1015 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1015). Extracted re-frame.substrate.spine (513 LoC) containing the React-shaped substrate spine. helix.cljs 516->204, uix.cljs 508->201. Net -104 LoC; ~620 LoC of previously duplicated body consolidated. rf2-jk7hr subsumed (flush-views! fallback now correctly probes react-dom/test-utils). Gates: cljs 1817/0/0, browser 1817/0/0, elision PASS, bundle-isolation PASS. CQ-4 hoist also incorporated.
close_reason: Resolved via PR #1015; helix/uix duplication eliminated. rf2-jk7hr subsumed.

title: refactor(mcp-base): pin diff-encode patch grammar via Malli schema
description:
## What

Define a Malli schema for the patch grammar emitted by `re-frame.mcp-base.diff-encode`:

```clojure
[:or
 [:tuple [:vector :any] [:= :assoc] :any]
 [:tuple [:vector :any] [:= :dissoc]]]
```

Pin via a unit test that validates a sample of `(collect-patches a b [])` outputs against the schema.

Optionally publish the schema as a public def for downstream consumers (causa-mcp's spec/004-Wire-Pipeline.md already plans a Malli-based decoder).

## Why

`diff_encode.cljc` produces `{:rf.mcp/diff-from :db-before :patches [...]}`. The `wire-vocab` conformance test (`tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test/.../wire_vocab_test.clj`) pins the OUTER marker shape — but the patch grammar lives only inside the encoder. A future consumer pinning the decoder needs the grammar pinned somewhere; `diff_encode.cljc` is the right home.

Caught by round-2 audit (rf2-n4q62, F9).

## Estimated impact

- +~15 LoC in `diff_encode.cljc` (def the schema).
- +2 tests in `diff_encode_test.clj`.

## Source

rf2-n4q62 round-2 audit, finding F9.
close_reason: Pinned via Malli schema. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/972

title: refactor(mcp-base): add :rf/redacted constant to vocab.cljc (vocab-completeness)
description:
## What

Add `redacted-key :rf/redacted` (and probably `redacted-sentinel :rf/redacted` if it appears as a literal value, not just a key) to `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/vocab.cljc`. Update `vocab_test.clj` to pin the constant.

## Why

`vocab.cljc`'s opening doctrine: *"One place to learn — and pin — the namespaced keys that the agent learns once and recognises across every MCP tool in the re-frame2 triplet."*

But the spec/Tool-Pair.md §Direct-read privacy posture (line 552) reserves `:rf/redacted` as the sensitive-drop sentinel emitted by `elide-wire-value` at the wire boundary — and `vocab.cljc` does NOT carry a constant for it. Every consumer that wants to test against the sentinel pins the literal keyword in-line. The catalogue mandate is violated by absence.

Caught by round-2 audit (rf2-n4q62, F8).

## Scope check

Stay within `vocab.cljc` — don't pull `:rf.elision/declarations` or `:rf.elision/runtime-flagged` (those are framework-internal app-db registry keys, not wire markers).

## Estimated impact

- +4 LoC in `vocab.cljc` (the def + docstring).
- +2 LoC in `vocab_test.clj` (one new pin).

## Source

rf2-n4q62 round-2 audit, finding F8.
close_reason: Shipped via https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1025 — added redacted-sentinel :rf/redacted to vocab.cljc with docstring distinguishing the in-place scalar sentinel from :rf.size/large-elided's map marker, and pinned in vocab_test.clj. All quality gates green (mcp-base, test:cljs, test:bundle-isolation).

title: refactor(mcp-base): move count-elided-markers out of vocab.cljc into its own ns
description:

title: refactor(causa-mcp): Lock #9 needs Date-amended header re Lock #10 mechanism promotion
description:
Parent audit: rf2-c33xi. Source: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-tools-causa-mcp-2026-05-14.md §SI3.

DESIGN-RATIONALE Lock #9 (line 605-716) headlines "Five normative mechanisms" and the body enumerates cap / slicing / pagination / lazy-summary / dedup. Same-day Lock #10 (line 718-815, 2026-05-13) **promoted** size-elision to mechanism #6. The summary table at line 1163 correctly says "Six mechanisms ... mechanism #6 added by Lock #10" — but Lock #9's body wasn't amended to reflect the promotion.

Lock #5 has the right pattern (when Lock #12 grew the catalogue from 17 to 18, Lock #5 grew a clean `### Date amended` header). Lock #9 should adopt the same:

- Add `### Date amended` subsection after the existing `### Date locked` (line 692-696).
- Note: "2026-05-13 (Mike). Same-day Lock #10 (rf2-knshj) promoted `:rf.size/large-elided` to mechanism #6 in 004-Wire-Pipeline.md. The five-mechanism framing in §Pick and §Why bullets is historical (the lock as first written). The current normative count is six; see Lock #10 for the sixth mechanism and the summary table line 1163."

Alternatively rewrite §Pick + §Why to say "six" throughout — but the Date-amended pattern is the lighter touch and matches Lock #5's precedent (historical lock text + amendment header). Reader's mental model: cold-read Lock #9 needs to get the right count.

Internal-consistency fix. Small edit. Filed as P1 because a future contributor reading Lock #9 cold gets the wrong mechanism count.

title: refactor(story-mcp): thread tool-name through assert-writes-allowed — fix lying :structuredContent :tool slot
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-w8jxf (findings R2-W1; carryover from round-1 T12).

tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/write.cljc:23-34 — the write-gate predicate.

Today the error result's :structuredContent slot hardcodes :tool "register-variant":

  (defn assert-writes-allowed []
    (when-not (config/writes-allowed?)
      (h/error-result
        (str "Write surface disabled. ...")
        {:gated true :tool "register-variant"})))

Called from three sites:
- tool-register-variant (write.cljc:46) — correct
- tool-unregister-variant (write.cljc:87) — :tool slot LIES
- tool-record-as-variant (recorder.cljc:95) — :tool slot LIES

Two of three callsites produce error responses whose structured-content claims the wrong tool produced the gate. An agent inspecting the gated error's :tool field gets misinformation.

Fix (+1 LoC):

  (defn assert-writes-allowed
    [tool-name]
    (when-not (config/writes-allowed?)
      (h/error-result
        (str "Write surface disabled. ...")
        {:gated true :tool tool-name})))

Update three callsites:
- write.cljc:46 → (assert-writes-allowed "register-variant")
- write.cljc:87 → (assert-writes-allowed "unregister-variant")
- recorder.cljc:95 → (write/assert-writes-allowed "record-as-variant")

Risk: zero. The :tool slot today is wrong; the fix makes it accurate.
close_reason: Fixed via PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/981. assert-writes-allowed now takes tool-name; 3 callsites pass their own MCP name; regression test pins the :tool slot for all 3 callers. Tests + drift checker green.

title: refactor(causa-mcp): Principles.md "Tool verbs" enum missing list-subscriptions
description:

title: fix(mcp-conformance): hermetic nREPL port-file timeout (post-rf2-papcw)
description:
After rf2-papcw (#950) fixed the catalogue-mismatch deterministic regression, the `MCP conformance tools/pair2-mcp` CI step still fails — different failure mode:

```
[hermetic] FAIL: timeout after 360000ms waiting for: nREPL port file
```

Six minutes elapsed before the nREPL port file appeared. Either:
- shadow-cljs `:server-test` build takes too long on CI / never starts
- the port-file path the harness watches is wrong
- a race between port-file creation and the harness wait

Investigation:
1. Find the hermetic harness (likely `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/` or `tools/pair2-mcp/scripts/`).
2. Reproduce locally to confirm or rule out CI-specific timing.
3. Add diagnostics: log path being watched, log shadow-cljs startup output.
4. Fix at root cause.

Pre-alpha: NO back-compat. Correctness paramount; don't suppress.

Discovered: 2026-05-14 ~10:05 AUSEST on main run 25832571514 (commit 74fa1526). rf2-papcw fixed the catalogue check; this is the next layer.
notes:
Fixed in PR #962 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/962

Three layered failures behind the 360s timeout:

1) Fixture classpath dropped re-frame.core. shadow-cljs.edn declared its own :dependencies parallel to a deps.edn with :local/root entries; shadow honours its own slot and silently ignored deps.edn. Runtime preload failed to compile, build errored before binding nREPL. Flipped fixture to :deps true (same idiom as tools/pair2-mcp/shadow-cljs.edn, rf2-obpa9).

2) Orchestrator watched the legacy port-file path. shadow-cljs 3.x writes .shadow-cljs/nrepl.port (not target/shadow-cljs/nrepl.port). Now walks all three standard candidates in lockstep with tools/pair2-mcp/src/.../nrepl.cljs port-file-candidates.

3) Two missing waits between boot and live test. (a) Bundle gate: dev-http returns SPA-fallback HTML 200 for /out/main.js BEFORE the first compile finishes; Chromium loaded too early. New probe checks Content-Type and body prefix. (b) Runtime gate: browser CLJS runtime takes a moment to register with shadow's :app build; pair2-mcp's runtime-preloaded? .catches that transient error to false, surfacing as :runtime-not-preloaded. New probe round-trips the same cljs-eval :app pair2-mcp uses, so the harness hands off only after the runtime is addressable.

Local hermetic: 22s end-to-end on warm Maven cache. All six OK checks pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: refactor(story-mcp): symmetric tools.recorder/descriptors vec — collapse registry concat asymmetry
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-w8jxf (findings R2-R1 / win #3).

tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/registry.cljc:31-36 builds the canonical tool registry with an asymmetric concat:

  (def tool-registry
    (-> []
        (into cat [dev/descriptors docs/descriptors
                   testing/descriptors write/descriptors])
        (conj recorder/descriptor)))

Four namespaces ship a vector named descriptors; tools.recorder ships a single map named descriptor. The docstring (registry.cljc:13) justifies the asymmetry as 'avoid a load-time cycle (recorder requires write for the gate fn)'. The rationale doesn't survive scrutiny — descriptor is a top-level def map; constructing it requires no recursive load. Wrapping in a one-element vec changes nothing about loading.

Fix:
1. tools/recorder.cljc:147 — rename def descriptor → def descriptors with [<the-one-map>].
2. tools/registry.cljc:31 — collapse to:
   (def tool-registry
     (into [] cat [dev/descriptors docs/descriptors testing/descriptors
                   write/descriptors recorder/descriptors]))

Risk: zero. Single-element vec construct/destructure is round-trip-stable; the descriptor map identity survives.

Win: removes a load-bearing-but-unjustified asymmetry every registry reader has to learn about.
close_reason: Resolved via PR #973 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/973. Recorder ships descriptors vec; registry collapses to single into-cat. Gates green: story-mcp 85/85, cljs 1816/1816, drift checker exit 0.

title: refactor(story-mcp): elide-app-db include? branch — avoid no-op walk on opt-in
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-w8jxf (findings R2-H1 / win #2).

tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/helpers.cljc:141-154 — the wire-egress scrubber for live frame state.

Today the include? true branch passes both :rf.size/include-sensitive? true and :rf.size/include-large? true to rf/elide-wire-value. The walker then traverses the entire app-db but yields v unchanged at every step (both inclusion knobs short-circuit per-node).

For preview-variant / run-variant with a 100 KB app-db on the :include-sensitive? true escape-hatch path:
- full walk (pure cost)
- no edits (zero benefit)
- followed by full pr-str + cap measurement

The walk is microseconds per node but the work is genuinely pointless. The escape hatch should be free.

Fix (3 LoC delta):

  (defn elide-app-db [app-db variant-id include?]
    (cond
      (nil? app-db) app-db
      include?      app-db
      :else         (rf/elide-wire-value app-db {:frame variant-id})))

Risk: zero. With both inclusion knobs true the walker's contract IS that v rides through unchanged; returning app-db directly produces byte-identical wire output. The existing privacy tests (preview-variant-app-db-includes-sensitive-when-opted-in tools_test.clj:984-994 and friends) pin the contract via the wire shape, not via 'must walk through elide-wire-value'.
close_reason:
PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/992

Refactor: skip the no-op walk on include? true. Verified elide-wire-value's contract — sensitive? and large? branches both return v with no side-effects when their inclusion flag is on; safe to bypass entirely.

LoC delta: +18/-7 in helpers.cljc (mostly docstring), +40/-0 regression test.

Perf note: ~100 KB app-db with :include-sensitive? true previously did O(node-count) walker dispatches (reduce-kv + mapv allocations per container) for zero edits, then pr-str + cap. Now skips the walk entirely; savings scale linearly with db size. Free escape hatch.

Regression test (elide-app-db-include?-true-bypasses-walker, in tools_test.clj) pins two invariants: (1) identical? — the bypass returns the SAME object ref (walker would rebuild maps, breaking identity); (2) value-equal to walking-with-both-knobs-on. If a future refactor reintroduces walker work the identical? assertion fires.

No unexpected side-effects of elide-wire-value on the include? true path — confirmed by re-reading the walker. Quality gates: clojure -M:test (87/453 green) and npm run test:cljs (1816/5040 green).

title: refactor(story-mcp): drop tools.cljc façade — 130 LoC pure indirection post-split

title: refactor(routing): (or (get path-params k) (throw ...)) masks false/0/empty-string params
description:
routing.cljc:471-473 and :480-482 in route-url:

  v (or (get path-params k)
        (throw (ex-info ":rf.error/missing-route-param" ...)))

(or x throw) treats false, 0, "" as missing. A user passing {:enabled false} or {:slug ""} to a route like /page/:enabled or /articles/:slug gets a spurious :rf.error/missing-route-param throw.

Use (get path-params k ::not-found) + ::not-found sentinel comparison, or if-some. Empty-string slug is the most realistic case in production.

While here, consider whether route-url should validate against :params / :query Malli schemas (Spec 012 throws :rf.error/route-url-validation for non-conforming caller args — currently only presence-checked; see S6 in audit). Coordinate the two fixes — they touch the same lines.

Audit: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-routing-2026-05-14.md CQ3 + S6.
Parent: rf2-yt2g2.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1020 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1020)

title: perf(routing): match-url replaces keep+sort with single-pass max-rank reduce; pre-sort the route table on registration
description:
Two coupled perf wins on the navigation hot path:

  P1. match-url (routing.cljc:354-383) builds candidates via keep, then sort-by :rank descending, then first. In production each URL matches one route in the overwhelming majority of cases. Replace with reduce that tracks the max-rank match — saves the sort + the keep-seq realisation. Single-pass.

  P2. (registrar/handlers :route) walks the entire route table on every match-url call. For a 100-route app on a navigation-heavy session this is many MBs of metadata reads. Maintain a pre-sorted [id meta rank] vector inside reg-route; match-url iterates in pre-sorted order and CAN short-circuit on first match (since pre-sorted).

  Cache invalidation: register a registrar replacement-hook (already exists per registrar.cljc:55-66) to rebuild the pre-sorted vector on reg-route replacements.

Audit: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-routing-2026-05-14.md P1 + P2.
Parent: rf2-yt2g2.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1020 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1020)

title: refactor(causa): hoist private tag helper to panels.common-helpers
description:
## Context

Filed from round-2 audit rf2-imynx (P2-1).

## Problem

title: refactor(routing): match-url should return :fragment; route-url 4-arity (fragment) per spec
description:
Two paired spec contracts on the pure helpers:

  1. match-url result shape per Spec 012 §Bidirectional URL ↔ params:
     {:route-id :params :query :fragment :validation-failed?}
     Impl returns :route-id :rank :params :query :validation-failed? — :fragment missing. Callers like :rf.route/handle-url-change work around with split-fragment manually.

  2. route-url 4-arity (route-id path-params query-params fragment) per Spec 012 §Bidirectional URL ↔ params and §Fragments. Impl tops out at 3-arity. route-link-render currently bolts a #fragment on after via (str base-url "#" fragment) at routing.cljc:1005-1007; :rf.route/navigate doesn't append fragment to the pushed URL at all.

Fix both — they're a coupled correctness gap. After the fix, route-link-render and the handlers can drop their ad-hoc fragment splicing.

Tests cover URL → match-url → route-url → URL round-trip with fragment. Conformance fixtures + JVM/CLJS runners updated so the fragment round-trip property is locked across every conforming implementation.

title: perf(causa): share group-cascades projection across event-detail / causality / performance composites
description:
## Context

Filed from round-2 audit rf2-imynx (P1-4 / lens 3).

## Problem

`projection/group-cascades` is called THREE times per trace-buffer push:

  - `registry.cljs:272` — `:rf.causa/event-detail` composite
  - `registry.cljs:374` — `:rf.causa/causality-graph-data` composite
  - `registry.cljs:1494` — `:rf.causa/performance-data` composite

Each composite reads `:rf.causa/trace-buffer` and runs a full O(buffer) pass through `group-cascades`. At the 1000-event default depth, that's 3× full-buffer work per push.

## Fix

Introduce one intermediate sub:

```clj
(rf/reg-sub :rf.causa/cascades
  :<- [:rf.causa/trace-buffer]
  (fn [buffer _query]
    (projection/group-cascades buffer)))
```

The three composites change to `:<- [:rf.causa/cascades]` and consume the projected vector directly.

## Bonus

`cg-helpers/enrich-cascades` could fold into the same upstream sub — the causality graph's enrichment step (walking the raw buffer for `:event/dispatched` traces) shares state with the projection. Out of scope here; a follow-on once this lands.

## Impact

3× perf reduction on cascade projection per trace push. The sub-graph stays correct because each downstream composite already declares the dependency through `:<-`.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/991

title: refactor(routing): :on-match error trapping + :on-error dispatch + :transition :error / :idle settle
description:
Per Spec 012 §Per-route error handling + §Per-route data loading:

  - :on-match handlers may throw or downstream-fail; runtime must set :transition :error and populate :rf.route/error with the structured error.
  - If route declares :on-error, the runtime dispatches it.
  - :transition transitions :loading → :idle when :on-match drain settles.

UPDATE 2026-05-14: The settle half (:loading → :idle via :rf.route/settle-transition) landed in PR #1020. Conformance fixtures depended on it. Remaining: :on-match error trapping + :on-error dispatch. Split out as rf2-ye7sh.

ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION:
Today: no error-trap, no :on-error read from route metadata, no settle-to-idle. Routes with :on-match observe :loading forever (S4) and errors silently lose. The whole transition FSM is half-implemented.

Implementation sketch:
  - inject an interceptor on each :on-match dispatch that traps + writes :rf.route/error on throw
  - a 'route nav settled' marker — likely an extra :fx step the cascade emits after the last :on-match dispatch — writes :idle back
  - read :on-error from route-meta in the trap

Coordinate with Spec 005 / drain semantics. Possibly leverage Spec 002 §Run-to-completion drain end hook if such exists.

Audit: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-routing-2026-05-14.md S3 + S4.
Parent: rf2-yt2g2.
close_reason: Settle half landed in PR #1020 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1020); :on-error trap deferred to follow-on rf2-ye7sh.

title: refactor(routing): register :rf.route/with-nav-token fx (currently spec-only; production has no staleness-suppression path)
description:
Spec 012 §Effects (reg-fx) lists :rf.route/with-nav-token as a universal-platform fx and §Navigation tokens §Threading documents the canonical usage:

    {:fx [[:rf.route/with-nav-token
           {:do        [:dispatch [:cart/items-loaded items]]
            :nav-token (:nav-token cofx)}]]}

Impl ships only :rf.test/simulate-http-resolution (a test-only event). Production code has no production-grade way to wrap an async completion with the nav-token check — users would hand-roll the staleness compare from app-db, which defeats the contract.

Build:
  - :rf.route/with-nav-token fx: read carried nav-token vs current from app-db (via frame? or via cofx?); on match, run the :do (dispatch / fx); on mismatch, emit :rf.route.nav-token/stale-suppressed and drop
  - Wire the carry side too: :on-match handlers need a :nav-token cofx injected at scheduling time (Spec 012 §Mechanism §2)

Audit: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-routing-2026-05-14.md A8.
Parent: rf2-yt2g2.
close_reason:
Resolved via PR #986 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/986

Contract: :rf.route/with-nav-token registered as a universal-platform fx in implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc. Match → routes inner :do fx entry through fx/handle-one-fx (so :dispatch, :rf.http/managed et al all work uniformly); mismatch → emits :rf.route.nav-token/stale-suppressed with canonical {:carried-token :current-token :event-id} tags and suppresses the inner fx.

Decision: silent-suppress + trace emit (per Spec 012 §Mechanism step 4 and §Trace events). Same trace shape as :rf.test/simulate-http-resolution so a single conformance assertion covers both production and test paths.

handle-one-fx promoted defn- → defn so the inner re-entry doesn't double-emit the :event/do-fx boundary marker the epoch six-domino projection keys off.

Regression test (routing_test.clj :: with-nav-token-fx-suppresses-stale-do-and-commits-fresh) pins both branches against the production fx.

title: refactor(routing): register missing framework subs — :rf.route/fragment, :rf.route/chain, :rf/pending-navigation

Spec 012 §Subscriptions normative table lists 9 framework subs. Impl registers 6 (:rf/route, :rf.route/{id,params,query,transition,error}). Missing:
  - :rf.route/fragment  → reads (:fragment (:rf/route db))
  - :rf.route/chain     → walks (:parent route-meta) up to the root, returns [parent-most ... current]

:rf.route/chain is non-trivial — it must walk the :route registrar following :parent meta until nil. Pin a cycle-detection guard.

title: refactor(routing): :rf.route/continue should re-issue :rf/url-requested, not :rf/url-changed + :rf.nav/push-url
description:
Per Spec 012 §Navigation blocking: continue 'clears :rf/pending-navigation and re-dispatches the original navigation request *without* re-running the leave guard'.

Impl (routing.cljc:691-697) bypasses the URL-requested layer: dispatches :rf/url-changed directly AND emits :rf.nav/push-url separately. Side effects:
  (a) :rf/url-requested policy interceptors (auth-guard, modifier-key, frame-policy) DON'T fire on continue
  (b) :rf.nav/push-url races with the :rf/url-changed slice write

Right model: re-issue :rf/url-requested with a one-shot :bypass-leave-guard? flag (or threaded through the request map).

title: test(core): explicit coverage for reset-runtime-fixture + destroy-frame hook cascades
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-byut1 findings TE-R2.2 + TE-R2.3.

Two parallel test gaps that share the same shape:

## TE-R2.2 — reset-runtime-fixture hook coverage

If rf2-d7vw8 (factor `reset-runtime-fixture` into a data table) lands, add a test that registers sentinel hooks under each `late-bind` key and asserts every hook is called exactly once per fixture invocation. Locks the 'no hook gets dropped during refactor' property.

## TE-R2.3 — destroy-frame hook coverage

If rf2-ggkay (factor `destroy-frame!`'s 4 cleanup-hook fires) lands, add a parallel test:

- Register sentinel hooks under `:privacy/clear-suppression-cache!`, `:ssr/on-frame-destroyed`, `:machines/on-frame-destroyed!`, `:epoch/on-frame-destroyed`.
- Destroy a frame.
- Assert all four sentinel hooks fired exactly once.

## Why these matter

Both refactors are pure-shape (data → call) but the call-set is implicit in the inline forms today. Without explicit coverage, a future edit that drops a hook silently breaks the cascade. The fixture is exercised by 50+ test files (so one dropped hook ripples loudly), but the destroy-frame cascade has narrower coverage and is harder to catch.

## Estimate

~ +50 LoC test code (split across two test files: `test_support_test.clj` and `frame_lifecycle_test.clj`).

title: fix(core): std_interceptors/path skips :db write when handler emits no :db effect
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-byut1 finding CQ-R2.5.

`std_interceptors.cljc:43-55` — the `path` interceptor's `:after` arm unconditionally writes `:effects :db` even when the handler emitted no `:db` effect:

```clojure
:after
(fn [ctx]
  (let [stack       (:rf/path-stack ctx [])
        original-db (peek stack)
        new-stack   (pop stack)
        ;; The handler may or may not have produced a new :db;
        ;; if it didn't, the slice didn't change.
        new-slice   (or (get-in ctx [:effects :db])
                        (get-in ctx [:coeffects :db]))]
    (-> ctx
        (assoc :rf/path-stack new-stack)
        (assoc-in [:effects :db]
                  (assoc-in original-db path-vec new-slice)))))
```

The comment on line 48 says 'if it didn't, the slice didn't change' — but the impl writes `:db` either way. Idempotent (substrate writes the same value), but:

1. Allocates `(assoc-in original-db path-vec new-slice)` per path-walk-step.
2. Creates a spurious `:db` effect when the handler returned none, breaking the 'no `:db` effect = no DB write' contract that downstream tools may rely on.

## Proposed fix

`cond->` the `:db` write on whether the handler actually produced one:

```clojure
:after
(fn [ctx]
  (let [stack       (:rf/path-stack ctx [])
        original-db (peek stack)
        new-stack   (pop stack)
        handler-emitted-db? (contains? (:effects ctx) :db)]
    (cond-> (assoc ctx :rf/path-stack new-stack)
      handler-emitted-db?
      (assoc-in [:effects :db]
                (assoc-in original-db path-vec (get-in ctx [:effects :db]))))))
```

Now: handler emits no `:db` → no `:db` effect (the path interceptor passes through cleanly). Handler emits `:db` → slice spliced back. Matches the docstring intent.

## Estimate

~ 3 LoC. Low risk. May surface a downstream test that was implicitly relying on the always-written `:db` (unlikely — the value would have been identical to the pre-handler one); review the path-interceptor test corpus during the fix.

## Related

- Round-2 audit doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-core-2026-05-14.md` §CQ-R2.5
- Parent audit bead: rf2-byut1
close_reason: Shipped in PR #1018 — std_interceptors/path :after gates splice-back on (contains? (:effects ctx) :db); two new tests in interceptor_test.clj.

title: refactor(core): cache trace/emit! in registrar's 4 :registry op-type sites
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-byut1 finding CQ-R2.4.

`registrar.cljc` has 4 call sites of the same `(when interop/debug-enabled? (when-let [emit! (late-bind/get-fn :trace/emit!)] (emit! :registry … {…})))` shape:

- `registrar.cljc:105-109` (handler-replaced trace)
- `registrar.cljc:114-117` (handler-registered trace)
- `registrar.cljc:129-133` (unregister trace)
- `registrar.cljc:143-148` (clear-kind trace)

Each is correctly gated outermost (per Closure-DCE rule) and uses the late-bind hook (per cycle-avoidance rule). The repetition is structural — Closure-DCE wants the OUTERMOST form to be `(when interop/debug-enabled? …)`, not a fn call — but the late-bind `get-fn` lookup can collapse.

## Proposed shape

```clojure
(defonce ^:private emit!-cache (atom nil))
(defn- emit! [op tags]
  (when interop/debug-enabled?
    (when-let [f (or @emit!-cache
                     (reset! emit!-cache (late-bind/get-fn :trace/emit!)))]
      (f :registry op tags))))
```

Each call site collapses to `(emit! :rf.registry/handler-registered {:kind kind :id id})` etc. The cache survives the lookup overhead but the outer `(when interop/debug-enabled? …)` MUST stay inlined at each call site (NOT moved into the helper) for Closure-DCE to elide.

Actually — since the gate-outermost requirement makes the helper less clean than expected, a cleaner alternative is just to cache the fn at ns-load via late-bind hook installation order. Or accept the cost and just lift the 3-level nesting into a 2-arg macro that emits the if/let/let triple inline.

## Estimate

~ -10 LoC. Low risk. Must preserve the Closure-DCE invariant — the gate must stay OUTERMOST per Spec 009 §Production builds.

## Related

- Round-2 audit doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-core-2026-05-14.md` §CQ-R2.4
- Parent audit bead: rf2-byut1
close_reason: Done — PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/959. Used gate-outside-helper shape from the start: the four call sites keep their (when interop/debug-enabled? …) outer gate (load-bearing for Closure DCE), the helper just memoises the late-bind lookup. Elision gate passed first try — no iteration needed.

title: perf(core): indexed-vec walk in execute-chain (no seq reverse)
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-byut1 finding PE-R2.1 (round-1 IC1 leftover).

`interceptor.cljc:169` still allocates a fresh seq per dispatch:

```clojure
ctx-after-afters  (reduce invoke-after ctx-after-befores (reverse interceptors))
```

`(reverse seq)` allocates a fresh lazy-seq per call. Replace with an indexed-vec walk so the :after pass walks the interceptors vector in reverse without a fresh allocation:

```clojure
(loop [i   (dec (count interceptors))
       ctx ctx-after-befores]
  (if (neg? i)
    ctx
    (recur (dec i) (invoke-after ctx (nth interceptors i)))))
```

## Estimate

~ 3 LoC. Low risk. One allocation per dispatch saved (and `invoke-after` runs unconditionally for teardown even on failure, so the cost is paid every drain).

## Related

- Round-2 audit doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-core-2026-05-14.md` §PE-R2.1
- Round-1 origin: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-core-2026-05-14.md` §IC1
- Parent audit bead: rf2-byut1
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/966 — replaced (reverse interceptors) with backward indexed-vec loop in execute-chain. interceptors is always a vector (router.cljc builds full-chain via vec), so (nth … i) is O(1) and the right-to-left walk produces identical invoke-after order against the same accumulating context. One per-dispatch lazy-seq allocation eliminated on the unconditional :after teardown path. Existing chain-composition tests (interceptor_test.clj) pin reverse-order across happy, single-throw, multi-error and short-circuit cases — all green; no new test needed. CLJS gate green (1816 tests). Bundle +49 chars (loop slightly larger than reduce, within budget).

title: feat(ssr-ring): default-html-shell honours :html-attrs / :body-attrs from head model
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-cegm7 §P1 #3 (`ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-ssr-2026-05-14.md`).

Spec 011 §477-479 documents the head model as carrying `:html-attrs` and `:body-attrs`:

```clojure
{:title       "Article: re-frame2 SSR"
 :meta        [...]
 ...
 :html-attrs  {:lang "en"}
 :body-attrs  {:class "page-article"}}
```

`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/emit.cljc:111-113` correctly documents these two keys as 'consumed by host shells that stamp them onto `<html>` / `<body>`.' But the bundled `default-html-shell` (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:316-336`) does NOT stamp them. It hardcodes:

```clojure
(str "<!DOCTYPE html>"
     "<html lang=\"" lang "\">"          ;; ← lang opt only, no :html-attrs merge
     ...
     "<body>"                              ;; ← no :body-attrs merge
     ...)
```

A route that registers `:head/article` with `{:html-attrs {:lang "fr" :data-theme "dark"} :body-attrs {:class "page-article"}}` gets NONE of those on the wire under the default shell — silent contract violation. A first-time user reading Spec 011 §477 and using the bundled adapter would only discover the gap by reading their HTML output.

Recommendation:

  - Honour them in `default-html-shell` — merge into the `<html>` and `<body>` opening tags via the existing `attr-string` helper.

title: spec(011-SSR): hash-injection mechanism — document structural-hiccup as canonical (post rf2-lxwse)
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-cegm7 §P1 #2 (`ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-ssr-2026-05-14.md`).

`spec/011-SSR.md:303` still describes post-emit regex injection as the hash-injection mechanism:

> When `render-to-string` is called with `:emit-hash? true`, the attribute is injected on the **first `<tag` opener** in the emitted body string (a regex of shape `<[a-zA-Z][^\s>/]*` — i.e. an opener whose tag-name starts with an ASCII letter). The letter-prefix lookahead is deliberate: it skips a leading `<!DOCTYPE html>` if `:doctype?` was also set, so the attribute lands on the root element rather than on the doctype.

The implementation (per rf2-lxwse, shipped) does NOT do regex injection. `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:225-250` threads a `root-attrs` map through `emit-element` and merges it onto the FIRST DOM-tag element of the hiccup tree BEFORE stringification — past view-refs, fragments (`:<>`), Reagent-native heads (`:>`), and fn-headed components on the root path.

The spec is the artefact; the code is downstream. A port engineer reading Spec 011 §303 today would implement regex injection, mismatching the CLJS reference on edge cases the regex misses (e.g. a non-DOM root, where the impl correctly no-ops and a regex-based implementation would over-inject).

Recommended spec edit:
  - §Hydration-mismatch detection should describe **structural injection on the hiccup root** as the canonical mechanism.
  - The exempt-keyword enumeration (already at §242-251) governs the skip-list.
  - Post-emit regex can survive as a 'valid alternative for ports lacking a hiccup-walk' footnote; the structural form is the contract.

Related minor: `spec/011-SSR.md:829` (Resolved decisions) says 'two re-frame.ssr defonce side-channel atoms'; should be **three** after rf2-jbcmt (response-slots joined request-slots + pending-error-traces). Line 784's table is already correct; line 829 lags.

Linked from rf2-cegm7. Spec-only change; no impl modification needed. Hot-zone: spec/011-SSR.md is sequential — coordinate with any open spec edits on the same file.

Estimated: ~10 LoC spec change.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/976 — spec/011-SSR.md §303 + §829 updated (4 +, 2 -). §303 rewrites injection-point as structural hiccup-walk (matching shipped rf2-lxwse impl in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:225-250); post-emit regex demoted to footnote with documented divergence cost. §829 corrects defonce count two → three after rf2-jbcmt (response-slots joined request-slots + pending-error-traces); §784 table was already correct.

title: refactor(machines): Result-unwrap macro/fn for terser call sites
description:
Round-2 audit finding · rf2-2ukxv · Q-r2-7.

result.cljc itself is clean (66 LoC), BUT call sites that thread Results read repetitively:

   (let [{snap ::result/snap fx ::result/fx} step-result] ...)
   ...or...
   (::result/snap r) / (::result/fx r)

This pattern appears 30+ times across transition.cljc, parallel.cljc, lifecycle_fx/*.cljc.

Options:
A. (defn unwrap-ok [r] [(::snap r) (::fx r)]) — terse but loses the names at the call site.
B. (defmacro with-ok [[snap fx] r & body] ...) — preserves names + reduces by 1 line per site.
C. Status quo, accept the verbosity — Result IS supposed to be transparent.

Recommend option B — let-binding-shape macro. Or, alternatively, give Result a (defrecord Result [tag snap fx info]) so destructuring is by field name without the ::result/ ns prefix:

   (let [{:keys [snap fx]} step-result] ...)

The defrecord adds JVM class generation overhead but lets call sites read as plain maps.

Risk: low. Mechanical change across 30+ sites.

Links: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-machines-2026-05-14.md · Parent: rf2-2ukxv
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/956 — picked option B (with-ok macro) plus snap/fx/info single-slot accessor fns. Swept 17 production call sites (13 pair-destructure → with-ok, 4 single-slot → accessor fn) across transition/parallel/registration.cljc. CLJS macro plumbing added via :include-macros true in each consumer require. Test gates green: npm run test:cljs (1818 tests) + machines JVM tests (124 tests including full conformance corpus).

title: spec(005): unified Spawn lifecycle ordering subsection (:on-spawn / :rf.machine/spawn fx / [:rf.machine/spawned] event / :entry / :start)
description:
Round-2 audit finding · rf2-2ukxv · S-r2-7.

The spawn lifecycle is well-spec'd individually but scattered across rf2-t07u, rf2-ijm7, rf2-6vmw. Specifically: what fires when, and against what context, between the moment a parent state with :invoke is entered and the moment the spawned child processes its first user event.

Two 'spawn' surfaces:
- :on-spawn (advisory action on the parent's :data, declared per-invoke-spec, runs INSIDE the transition reducer at allocate-time).
- :rf.machine/spawned (synthetic event dispatched into the spawned child, fires after spawn-fx if :start absent).

Add to Spec 005 a §Spawn lifecycle subsection enumerating the order:
1. parent enters :invoke-bearing state (in the entry cascade).
2. :on-spawn advisory callback runs against parent :data with the freshly-allocated spawned-id.
3. :rf.machine/spawn fx emitted into the fx vector.
4. fx handler: child's spec resolved; reg-event-fx registers child; initial snapshot installed at [:rf/machines <id>] with :rf/bootstrap-pending? true.
5. Child's first event: either the supplied :start, or the synthetic [:rf.machine/spawned] when :start absent.
6. Child's initial-entry cascade fires (the :entry actions along the :initial path).
7. Child processes the event.

References to wire in: rf2-t07u (declarative :invoke via :rf/spawned tracking), rf2-ijm7 (synthetic :rf.machine/spawned + parent-id/self-id stamping), rf2-6vmw (invoke-all child-side wiring).

Risk: spec edit only.

title: refactor(pair2-mcp): :scalar-value pipeline arm — name scalar vs envelope
description:

Option 2 is cleaner; option 1 is mechanical.

title: refactor(story): consolidate duplicated micro-fns into re-frame.story.predicates.cljc leaf ns
description:
## Context

From round-2 refactor audit rf2-cgqam (see `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-tools-story-2026-05-14.md` P1 #3 + under-appreciated win).

## The pattern

Five 'mirrored here because the JVM target can't require X' comments across the tree right now. Each is justified locally -- the dependency graph genuinely forbids the require. But sit them next to each other:

- **`parent-story-id`** (×4 sites, same 3-line body):
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/args.cljc:66`
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/state.cljc:323`
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/docs.cljc:169`
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/pure.cljc:34`

- **`assertion-event?`** (×2 sites):
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/assertions.cljc:506`
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/pure.cljc:25` (private mirror)

- **`(= "rf.assert" (namespace id))`** literal (×3):
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/assertions.cljc:513`
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/recorder.cljc:302`
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/pure.cljc:30`

That's ~30 LoC of duplicated pure data -> data across 9 sites, with the wave's new pure namespaces (test_mode/pure.cljc, schema_validation.cljc) adding fresh mirrors each cycle.

## Fix — `re-frame.story.predicates.cljc` (or `.utils.cljc`) leaf ns

A single 60-80 LoC pure leaf namespace that depends on nothing but `clojure.core`:

```clojure
(ns re-frame.story.predicates
  "Story-internal pure data -> data helpers shared across the tree.
  Lives at the leaf of the require graph (depends on clojure.core only)
  so any sibling ns can :require it without cycle risk.")

(def reserved-assertion-ns
  "The reserved namespace string for assertion event ids per Conventions.md."
  "rf.assert")

(defn parent-story-id
  "Derive a variant's parent story id by stripping the variant's name.
  Pure; nil for keywords without a namespace."
  [variant-id]
  (when (and (keyword? variant-id) (namespace variant-id))
    (keyword (namespace variant-id))))

(defn assertion-id?
  "True iff `id` is an `:rf.assert/*` event id."
  [id]
  (and (keyword? id) (= reserved-assertion-ns (namespace id))))

(defn assertion-event?
  "True iff `event` is a vector whose head is an `:rf.assert/*` keyword."
  [event]
  (let [id (when (sequential? event) (first event))]
    (assertion-id? id)))
```

Every existing ns that needs them `:require`s the leaf. No cycle (the leaf has no Story deps). The 'mirrored here because...' comments come out alongside the duplicate definitions.

## Why this is worth doing

Round 1's pattern was 'each individual duplication looks justified locally'. Round 2's wave landed two new pure namespaces (test_mode/pure.cljc, schema_validation.cljc) and each added fresh mirrors -- the pattern is self-propagating. The next pure pane to land (Story has more in the SOTA backlog) costs one `:require` instead of one fresh mirror.

This is the masterpiece-grade refactor signal: 'find the shape that wants to exist' applied to the *repeat* of round-1's discovery.

## Implementation

1. Create `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/predicates.cljc`.
2. Replace the duplicate definitions site-by-site with `(:require [re-frame.story.predicates :as pred])` + `pred/parent-story-id` / `pred/assertion-event?` etc.
3. Drop the 'mirrored here' explanatory comments.
4. Run `npm run test:cljs` -- pure rearrange; behaviour unchanged.

## Notes

- Companion ns to `re-frame.story.late-bind` (which just shipped) -- both are pure leaves the rest of Story consumes.
- Net: -30 LoC of duplication, +80 LoC of new leaf, ~50 LoC net + a cycle-immune home for tiny pure fns.
- Bead parent: rf2-cgqam.

## Related

The Malli schema-walker dup (filed separately) follows the same shape -- another tiny pure leaf ns. Could be folded into this bead if convenient, but the rationale + the surface differ enough to keep them separate.

title: refactor(story): extract Malli schema-walker helpers shared by controls.cljs + schema_validation.cljc
description:
## Context

From round-2 refactor audit rf2-cgqam (see `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-tools-story-2026-05-14.md` P1 #2).

## Duplication

The recent round-1 wave introduced `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/schema_validation.cljc` (575 LoC). It carries its own private copies of FIVE Malli schema-walking helpers:

```clojure
;; schema_validation.cljc:163-184
(defn- properties? [x] (map? x))
(defn- schema-op [s] (when (vector? s) (first s)))
(defn- schema-children [s] ...)
(defn- map-entry-key [entry] (first entry))
(defn- map-entry-schema [entry] ...)
```

`controls.cljs:141-184` carries the same five helpers with identical bodies.

The schema_validation.cljc docstring at line 159 acknowledges the duplication explicitly:

> *'Mirrors the helpers in `re-frame.story.ui.controls` -- but kept in-namespace so this file stands on its own under the JVM test target.'*

The justification is real: `controls.cljs` is `.cljs`-only, so a `.cljc` namespace cannot `:require` it for the pure walkers without bifurcating the require graph.

## Fix

Extract the five helpers into a new `re-frame.story.malli-schema-utils.cljc` pure leaf ns:

```clojure
(ns re-frame.story.malli-schema-utils
  "Pure Malli-schema introspection helpers. Shared between the controls
  panel's widget-derivation and the schema-validation panel's args-
  violation walk.")

(defn properties?     [x] (map? x))
(defn schema-op       [s] (when (vector? s) (first s)))
(defn schema-children [s] ...)
(defn map-entry-key   [entry] (first entry))
(defn map-entry-schema [entry] ...)
```

Both `controls.cljs` and `schema_validation.cljc` `:require` it. Net: -25 LoC of dup, one canonical home for the Malli-shape walking, JVM-testable in one place.

## Notes

- Round 1 didn't flag this because schema_validation.cljc didn't exist yet -- it was filed and shipped in the round-1 wave.
- This is a small but elegant cleanup -- the file's own docstring already acknowledged the duplication.
- Bead parent: rf2-cgqam.

## Test

The existing CLJS tests against `controls/infer-widget` + the JVM tests against `schema_validation/args-violations` cover the walkers' behaviour; the extraction is a pure rearrange. Confirm no test changes are needed beyond the require updates.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1019

title: refactor(story): fix :argtypes key drift — spec uses :control, impl uses :widget
description:
## Context

From round-2 refactor audit rf2-cgqam (see `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-tools-story-2026-05-14.md` P1 #1).

## The drift

`spec/007-Stories.md:212-222` shows the canonical authoring example:

```clojure
{:argtypes
 {:placeholder  {:control :text}
  :variant      {:control {:type :select :options [:primary :secondary]}}
  :disabled?    {:control :boolean}}}
```

The slot key is `:control`. Vocabulary names are `:text` / `:textarea` / `:number` / `:boolean` / `:select` / `:radio` / `:date` / `:color`.

The impl (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/controls.cljs:262-280, 303-345, 466`) dispatches on `:widget` keys exclusively:

```clojure
(case (:widget widget-spec)
  :group    [group-widget    ...]
  :repeater [repeater-widget ...]
  :tuple    [tuple-widget    ...]
  [scalar-widget ...])
```

`resolve-argtypes` (controls.cljs:303-345) consumes user-supplied `:argtypes` raw without translating `:control` -> `:widget`. So a spec-conformant `{:placeholder {:control :text}}` lands at `scalar-widget` with `widget = nil` -> the 'unsupported widget' fallback span.

The schema (`schemas.cljc:160-163`) is `ArgtypesMap = [:map-of :keyword :any]` -- no validation gate catches this.

## Decision required

Two paths:

### Option A (impl accepts `:control` as canonical, `:widget` as legacy alias)

In `resolve-argtypes` translate user-supplied `{:control X ...}` -> `{:widget X ...}`. Keep `:widget` as the internal dispatch key (the inferred descriptors from `infer-widget` / `infer-value-shape` use it). The author-facing surface stays `:control`; the internal dispatch stays `:widget`.

Est: +15 LoC in `resolve-argtypes` + a translation helper.

### Option B (spec example updates to `:widget`)

Edit `spec/007-Stories.md:212-222` to use `{:widget :text}` shape. Aligns spec with the existing impl. Risk: existing user docs / external articles citing `:control` go stale. Pre-alpha, so manageable.

Est: -2 LoC of spec edit; no impl change.

## Recommendation

**Option A.** `:control` is the more obvious authoring slot name (a 'control' is what the user sees in the UI; `:widget` is an implementation term). The translation cost is trivial. The internal dispatch can remain `:widget` so `infer-widget` / `infer-value-shape` don't need changes.

## Test

After the refactor add a unit test asserting:

- `(resolve-argtypes :story.foo/bar)` against a variant with `{:argtypes {:k {:control :textarea}}}` returns `{:k {:widget :textarea}}`.
- Render-time dispatch produces the `:textarea` widget (not the fallback span).

## Notes

- Round 1 missed this: CT3 / S3 focused on the missing widget *types*, not the slot-key mismatch.
- This bead supersedes nothing -- it's a fresh round-2 finding.
- Bead parent: rf2-cgqam.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1019

title: refactor(machines): extract reduce-regions helper from parallel.cljc duplication
description:
**Round-2 audit finding · rf2-2ukxv · Q-r2-4 + TE-r2-2** (under-appreciated win)

Two near-identical reducers in `parallel.cljc` encode the parallel-region threading invariant:
- `apply-initial-entry-cascade` (lines 160-190).
- `parallel-machine-transition` (lines 223-255).

Both:
- iterate `ordered-regions`,
- thread `cur-data` and `cur-counter`,
- build `region-spec` via `region-machine`,
- build `region-snap` with `:state` + `:data` + optional `:rf/spawn-counter`,
- call a per-region step (the differ),
- handle `result/fail?` short-circuit,
- destructure region's result,
- prefix region-name onto per-region fx via `prefix-region-invoke-id`,
- recur with new state-map / data / counter / accumulated fx.

The two functions differ in only ONE line: the inner step (`apply-initial-entry-cascade-single` vs `machine-transition`).

## Why this is THE round-2 win

The parallel-region broadcast invariant — "data and counter thread through regions in declaration order; fx-prefix per region" — is what defines parallel regions in Spec 005 §Parallel regions. Yet the invariant has no named home; you have to assemble the rule from two near-identical reducers.

This is the same kind of win as round-1's `path_walk/walk-path-leaf-to-root` (which named the deepest-wins rule once). `reduce-regions` would name the broadcast rule once.

## Fix sketch

    (defn reduce-regions
      "Broadcast  across 's regions in declaration order,
      threading shared  and . Each region's
      returned fx is prefixed via . Returns a
       Result with the merged snapshot or a  from
      any region's step."
      [machine snapshot region-fn]
      ...)

Then:
- `apply-initial-entry-cascade` → `(reduce-regions machine snapshot apply-initial-entry-cascade-single)` (after A-r2-2 inlines the wrapper).
- `parallel-machine-transition` → `(reduce-regions machine snapshot machine-transition)`.

## Tests (TE-r2-2)

A pure-fn unit test for the helper:
- Two-region machine; first region's `:data` write is visible to the second region's reducer.
- `:rf/spawn-counter` bump propagates.
- `prefix-region-invoke-id` applied per-region.

## Acceptance

- `reduce-regions` helper exists in `parallel.cljc` (or a sibling).
- Both reducers delegate.
- Unit test for the helper.
- ~30 LoC saved + named invariant.

## Links

- Audit: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-machines-2026-05-14.md` (the under-appreciated-win section)
- Parent audit bead: rf2-2ukxv
- Inline `apply-initial-entry-cascade-single` first (A-r2-2) for the cleanest landing.
close_reason: Closed

title: refactor(machines): consolidate :rf.machine/destroyed + :system-id-released trace-emit sites
description:
**Round-2 audit finding · rf2-2ukxv · Trace-r2-3**

Three sites emit `:rf.machine/destroyed` with near-identical argument maps:
- `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:80-87` (`destroy-invoke-all-children!` per-child).
- `lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:113-120` (`destroy-single!`).

The `teardown.cljc` ns is the natural home since it already owns the unified app-db projection that these traces are paired with.

## Why this matters

Per Spec 009 §:op-type vocabulary, the `:rf.machine/destroyed` trace IS the contract surface — tools (Causa, story, re-frame-10x) key on its shape. Three independent emission sites = three chances to drift in argument keys.

title: refactor(flows): align :rf.flow/failed cascade behaviour — spec + code + tests
description:
Cluster from audit rf2-0b2eh (findings CQ-1 / TC-1 / SVI-3).

## Problem

`evaluate-flow!` (implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:95-153) has a docstring that lies. The docstring says:

> 'On the failure path the in-flight db is returned unchanged and dirty? is false so downstream flows still walk.'

The body actually `(throw e)`s after emitting `:rf.flow/failed`. The throw aborts `run-flows!`'s loop. Real consequences:

1. Downstream flows scheduled later in topo order **do not execute** on that drain.
2. If any flow earlier in the cascade succeeded (wrote to local `db`), its write is **silently dropped** — the `replace-container!` at flows.cljc:172 is bypassed by the throw. The `:rf.flow/computed` trace still fired with the new `:result`, so tools claim the write happened. Real-world bug surface.

Spec 013 §Flow tracing is silent on which behaviour is the contract.

## Work

Three pieces, sequenced:

1. **Spec decision** (Spec 013): pin one of:
   - **(a)** Cascade halts on first `:rf.flow/failed`. Re-throw bubbles through router → `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception`. Prior-flow writes in the same drain are **discarded** (current impl behaviour).
   - **(b)** Cascade halts on first `:rf.flow/failed`. Prior-flow writes are **preserved** (`replace-container!` runs first, then re-throw).
   - **(c)** Cascade continues; downstream flows see the failing flow's prior cached output unchanged. Most isolation, most surprising.

   Recommendation: **(b)** — strongest 'no work is silently lost' guarantee; matches the run-to-completion principle in Spec 002; cascade-level error still surfaces.

2. **Impl alignment** — update `evaluate-flow!` + `run-flows!` to match the chosen contract. Drop the misleading docstring; replace with what the code actually does.

3. **Test pin** — `flows_trace_test.clj` currently only exercises single-flow failure. Add a deftest with two flows (A succeeds, B downstream of A throws) that verifies the chosen behaviour:
   - app-db after the drain — does A's write survive?
   - downstream flow C (after B in topo order) — does it fire?
   - what trace events appear in what order?

## Files

- spec/013-Flows.md — add 'Failure semantics' subsection or extend 'Flow tracing'.
- implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:95-175 — `evaluate-flow!` docstring + body, `run-flows!` if option (b)/(c).
- implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_trace_test.clj — new deftest.

## Estimate

~5 LoC code change in flows.cljc, ~25 LoC new test, ~10-line spec subsection.

Pre-alpha; no back-compat concern.

Source: audit rf2-0b2eh §CQ-1 / TC-1 / SVI-3.
close_reason: Landed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1044 (commit 48c710a5). Spec 013 §Failure semantics added with four-rule contract + worked example; run-flows! wraps evaluate-flow! in try/catch that flushes replace-container! before re-throwing; evaluate-flow! docstring rewritten to match behaviour. New deftest failed-cascade-preserves-prior-flow-writes pins the three observable rules (A's :path lands, B's :path absent, C's :path absent, trace stream as expected).

title: refactor(http): :rf.http/cors spec-vs-impl drift — never emitted
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 4.1.

Spec 014 §Failure categories closed set documents `:rf.http/cors` with `:message`, `:url` tags. **Grepping http sources for \`:rf.http/cors\`: zero occurrences in src/.** \`classify-cljs-error\` at \`http_transport.cljc:101-121\` maps Fetch errors to one of \`:rf.http/timeout\` / \`:rf.http/aborted\` / \`:rf.http/transport\` — CORS errors silently land at \`:rf.http/transport\`.

The spec promises a discrimination that is not present in the impl. Two options:

1. **Spec amendment** — soften the row: \"emitters MAY classify when detectable; otherwise falls through to \`:rf.http/transport\`.\" (The likely fix, since the JS Fetch API gives no signal beyond \"TypeError\" for CORS — distinguishing is fragile.)
2. **Impl change** — detect via message-string + cross-origin URL check, emit \`:rf.http/cors\`.

Mike decides direction. ~spec doc edit OR ~30 LoC impl.

Either way, a test should be added that \`:retry :on #{:rf.http/cors}\` is a valid configuration (idempotent retry-set membership), per audit finding 5.1.
close_reason: fixed in PR #1053 — CORS heuristic emission landed on CLJS (TypeError + cross-origin URL); 3 classifier tests + retry-set membership test added

title: refactor(http): case-insensitive Content-Type lookup (encoding/transport)
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Top finding #1.

`http_encoding.cljc:164-165`:

```clojure
(let [content-type (or (get headers \"content-type\")
                       (get headers \"Content-Type\")) ...]
```

Spec 014 §Request envelope line 102 says header names are case-insensitive. The decode-defaulting path only checks two exact spellings. A response with `\"CONTENT-TYPE: application/json\"` (or any non-canonical casing) yields nil → `sniff-decoder` falls to `:blob`, so JSON arrives as raw text. The CLJS Fetch path normalises (lower-case in `fetch-headers->map`); the JVM `jvm-headers->map` preserves the casing the server emits. **Real correctness bug on JVM.**

Same pattern at `http_transport.cljc:419-420` for the request-side `Content-Type` clash check.

**Fix:** factor a `content-type-of` helper into `http-encoding` (or normalise headers to lower-case at the transport boundary on JVM). ~15 LoC.

**Test:** add a JVM test that a server returning `\"Content-type: application/json\"` (lowercase 't') correctly resolves the JSON decoder.

4. Either: (a) fix the regression, OR (b) loosen the perf-budget tolerance if the test is intrinsically flaky.

Pre-alpha: NO back-compat. Correctness paramount. Don't suppress the test — diagnose first.

Discovered: 2026-05-14 ~04:35 AUSEST on run 25817752366. Pre-existing failures on the same run: rf2-cum40 (MCP conformance) and rf2-lyj0 (Examples browser).
notes:
Diagnosed: timing-precision flake, not algorithmic regression. CI ratio 50.00000000044775 ≈ 50.0 + 4.4e-10 — mathematically straddles the slack ceiling on float-precision wobble. project-feed is genuinely O(n); the algorithm is sound.

Root cause: (1) no JIT warm-up — small t1 measurement paid V8 compile/optimise overhead that t10 then ran free, compressing the t1 baseline; (2) ratio noise-floor at 0.5ms was below Chromium's performance.now clamp granularity (~0.1ms non-isolated, up to ~1ms under privacy-mode / CI container scheduling jitter), so both t1 and t10 round to the same clamped grid and land on an exact small-integer ratio.

Fix in PR #869: timed now does one discarded warm-up call; ratio noise-floor lifted to 2.0ms (extracted as ratio-noise-floor-ms with rationale doc). Slack constant unchanged — a true O(n²) at 10× input would still be ~100×, far outside the 50× slack. Improves signal, not threshold.

Verified locally: JVM (clojure -M:test) + CLJS (npm run test:cljs + npm run test:browser) all green.

PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/869
close_reason: Diagnosed as timing-precision flake (NOT regression). project-feed is genuinely O(n); CI ratio 50.0+1e-10 straddled the slack ceiling on float-precision wobble. Fix in PR #869: warm-up call in timed + raise ratio noise-floor 0.5ms → 2.0ms. All test targets green locally.

title: refactor(story-mcp): thread :origin :story-mcp through register-variant / record-as-variant writes (or amend spec)
description:

spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md:87 claims:

  'tools/story-mcp/ — does not ship dispatch directly, but its register-variant / record-as-variant writes carry :origin :story-mcp'

The implementation does NOT do this:
- tool-register-variant (tools.cljc:486-526) invokes `(story/reg-variant* vk body-v)`; no `:origin` is threaded.
- tool-record-as-variant (tools.cljc:576-678) invokes `start-recording!` + `stop-recording!` + `reg-variant*`; no `:origin`.

Two paths to resolution:

a) IMPL CHANGE — extend `story/reg-variant*` to accept `:origin` slot, propagate to the registrar's `:event/registered` trace stream so post-mortem filters work. Same for the recorder's `start-recording!`. This is the right move per the cross-MCP origin-tagging convention (spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md §5).

b) SPEC AMENDMENT — strike the claim from Cross-Cutting-Designs.md:87; document that story-mcp writes inherit the host process's default `:origin :app` because Story's registrar doesn't currently distinguish.

Recommend (a) — the convention is the lock; story-mcp should honour it.

close_reason: PR #844 — stamped :origin :story-mcp on register-variant and record-as-variant write-back per spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md §5. Pinned config/origin as single source of truth. 7 new tests, 95/95 pass.

title: refactor(story-mcp): route :app-db slices through mcp-base sensitive scrubber at egress
description:
Per audit rf2-1sdzn (findings doc: ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-story-mcp-2026-05-14.md, S3 / S4-S5).

spec/Tool-Pair.md:550-554 is unambiguous: a pair-shaped tool that surfaces live frame state MUST route the value through the wire-egress walker before crossing into the agent surface. Spec/API.md:458 carries the same MUST for `:sensitive?` egress filtering at framework-published forwarders.

Today `preview-variant` (tools.cljc:204-213) and `run-variant` (tools.cljc:391-398) return the variant frame's `:app-db` slot verbatim. `read-failures` (tools.cljc:461) similarly returns the variant frame's `:rf.story/assertions` accumulator. Neither is routed through any privacy / size walker.

Note: re-frame.mcp-base.sensitive ships:
- `strip-sensitive` (filters `:sensitive? true` events from collections)
- `scrub-snapshot` (scrubs `:traces` / `:epochs` slices on a per-frame snapshot map)

For `:app-db` payloads the broader `rf/elide-wire-value` walker (per spec/API.md §Size-elision wire-boundary walker) is the framework-side primitive. Story-mcp depends on tools/story which depends on implementation/, so the walker is in reach.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Every tool returning `:app-db` routes through `rf/elide-wire-value` (or `scrub-snapshot` if no app-db).
2. Every tool surfacing accumulated traces / assertions runs `strip-sensitive` with `(include-sensitive? args)` by default-off.
3. Every such tool accepts a `:include-sensitive?` arg per the cross-MCP convention (sensitive.cljc:79-85 is the spec'd reader).
4. Tests pin: (a) a tagged-`:sensitive?` event accumulator is stripped by default; (b) `:include-sensitive? true` preserves it; (c) the scrubber composes with the token cap (rf2-zavp5).

Linked-from: rf2-1sdzn (audit). Sequence after rf2-u5z3x (mcp-base consolidation) and rf2-zavp5 (token cap).
close_reason: Landed in PR #877. Wire-egress scrubbers added at three surfaces: preview-variant + run-variant route :app-db through re-frame.core/elide-wire-value with :frame variant-id; read-failures filters assertion accumulator through mcp-base/strip-sensitive. Cross-MCP :include-sensitive? opt-in surfaced on all three input schemas (default false). Regression tests pin redaction at default + raw-value passthrough on opt-in for both surface categories. clojure -M:test from tools/story-mcp: 102 tests / 478 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors.

- Exercises all three MCP servers (pair2-mcp today, causa-mcp at impl-pass time, story-mcp likewise) over a small fixture surface.

title: refactor(causa-mcp): decide subscription-info parity with pair2-mcp (17 + bundle, or 18 with subscription-info)
description:
## Goal

Causa-MCP's catalogue is 17 (per upstream `tools/causa/spec/010-MCP-Server.md`). pair2-mcp ships a `subscription-info` tool that surfaces metadata about open subscriptions. Causa-MCP's catalogue doesn't include it, nor does the spec say it's bundled. Decision needed.

## Finding (from audit rf2-m9yoi)

Causa-MCP's streaming pair is `subscribe` / `unsubscribe` (per 000-Vision.md:97). pair2-mcp's streaming surface has three tools: `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`, and `subscription-info` (per `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs`). The audit's cross-MCP-symmetry posture (per Principles.md §Privacy / §Token budget) implies an agent learning the slot on one server gets the same surface on the others.

Either:
- **Causa-MCP genuinely lacks the `subscription-info` surface** (likely oversight) → add it as the eighteenth tool, retaining "eighteen" arithmetic and reframing the phantom 'Compatibility' band as Streaming (3 tools instead of 2).
- **Causa-MCP bundles `subscription-info` into another tool** (e.g. `subscribe` with `:mode :info`) → spec needs to say so; today it doesn't.

This decision is upstream of the count-of-things bead (rf2-22my5). If the answer is "18 + name the eighteenth", the count-drift fix changes shape.

## Recommendation

Add a question to `ai/map.md` for Mike. Don't dispatch the impl until the answer is locked. If 18: amend rf2-22my5 to land "seventeen + subscription-info" as the eighteenth tool name in band Streaming.

title: refactor(causa-mcp): reconcile coord-shape divergence from pair2-mcp (lock #6 silent on the difference)
description:
## Goal

Causa-MCP and pair2-mcp coord shapes disagree on where the `2` lives. The audit-finding-time spec doesn't reconcile.

## Finding (from audit rf2-m9yoi)

Lock #6 (DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:349-413) picks `@day8/re-frame2-causa-mcp` and cites `@day8/re-frame-pair2-mcp` as precedent. The two shapes disagree:
- pair2: `re-frame-pair2-mcp` (framework bare `re-frame`, tool name carries the `2` as `pair2`)
- causa: `re-frame2-causa-mcp` (framework carries the `2` as `re-frame2`, tool name bare `causa`)

The Lock's "Why §brand consistency" cites Day8 brand but doesn't reconcile the diverging shape.

Today this contradicts the cross-server symmetry posture (per Principles.md §Privacy / §Token budget — agents "learn the slot on one server, get the same on the others") because the maven/npm coord IS one of the slots agents learn.

## Proposed fix

Add to Lock #6's "Why" subsection a paragraph naming the divergence:

> pair2-mcp pre-dates re-frame2's rename; its coord `re-frame-pair2-mcp` reflects the v1 framework name. Causa-MCP launches post-rename and picks `re-frame2-causa-mcp` to match the framework's current name. The shape is intentionally different from pair2-mcp's; future MCP artefacts (story-mcp, when it lands) inherit Causa-MCP's shape, not pair2-mcp's.

If story-mcp's coord has already been picked and disagrees, fix that instead.

Optionally: file a separate bead to rename pair2-mcp's coord to `re-frame2-pair-mcp` at v1.0-major-bump time, eliminating the divergence permanently.

- Findings: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-causa-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §Q3

title: refactor(causa-mcp): split MCP-server-ns from injected-runtime-ns (currently conflated)
description:
## Goal

Causa-MCP spec uses a single namespace `re-frame2-causa-mcp.runtime` for two distinct roles, conflating what pair2-mcp splits into two.

## Finding (from audit rf2-m9yoi)

`tools/causa-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:166` says:
| Runtime ns | `re-frame-pair2.runtime` | `re-frame2-causa-mcp.runtime` |

In pair2-mcp the **injected runtime namespace** is `re-frame-pair2.runtime` (lives in `skills/re-frame-pair2/preload/re_frame_pair2/runtime.cljs`), distinct from the **MCP server's own code** which lives in `re-frame-pair2-mcp.*` (per `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/{tools,cache,nrepl,server}.cljs`). Two namespaces, two roles.

Causa-MCP's spec uses the single namespace `re-frame2-causa-mcp.runtime` for both roles:
- Principles.md:26 — "The eighteen tools route through the existing `re-frame2-causa-mcp.runtime` namespace via `cljs-eval`."
- Vision.md:62 — "a small sentinel namespace (`re-frame2-causa-mcp.runtime`) re-ships on browser reload."

The pair2 split is meaningful: the MCP server is the Node-side process; the injected runtime is what reaches the browser.

## Proposed fix

Pick one and write it down:
- **Option A (split):** spec the MCP server's code namespace separately from the injected runtime ns. E.g. server code at `re-frame2-causa-mcp.*`, injectable runtime at `re-frame2-causa.runtime` (matching the `re-frame2-causa` maven coord pattern).
- **Option B (collapse):** keep the single namespace but document the dual role explicitly — "the same namespace is loaded server-side (in the Node MCP process) and runtime-side (in the consumer app's browser); the runtime-side functions are gated by environment-detection".

Recommendation: Option A. Mirroring pair2-mcp's split costs nothing at the spec level and avoids an impl-time "wait, which side am I writing?" pause.

## Linked
- Parent audit: rf2-m9yoi
- Findings: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-causa-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §Q2
close_reason: Spec-only split landed. PR #880 introduces (a) Vision §'Two namespaces, two sides' with full table, (b) Principles §'MCP-server-ns and injected-runtime-ns are distinct' as the tie-breaker principle, (c) DESIGN-RATIONALE Lock #11 capturing the Option A pick with rationale citing pair2-mcp precedent + bundle-isolation rule. Naming locked: day8.re-frame2-causa-mcp.* (Node) vs day8.re-frame2-causa.runtime (browser, rides Causa-the-panel's preload). Five conflated references updated. Mirrors pair2-mcp's re-frame-pair2-mcp.* / re-frame-pair2.runtime split.
