title: refactor(core): macro-helper for the 14 when-let+assoc! sites in walk-states-tree
description:
Audit finding SC1 from rf2-spr6q.

source_coords.cljc:152-252 — walk-states-tree is 90 LoC of mutation-heavy nested reductions. The function's own docstring acknowledges 'imperative shape is deliberate for compile-time performance'.

Fair, but the SAME pattern (when-let [c (form-coords X ns-sym file)] (assoc! acc (conj path-key) c)) is repeated 14 times across the function.

Proposed: a private macro (maybe-stamp! acc path form) that wraps the when-let + assoc!. The macro inlines so the imperative-perf-claim survives.

Net: net -25 LoC (+~ 20 macro, -~ 45 call-sites). Much clearer reading.

Time-box: ~ 60 min. Risk: low — the walker has good test coverage via reg-machine source-coord tests.

Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc.
close_reason: Done. PR #894 — macro-helper 'stamp!' replaces the 18 when-let+assoc! sites across walk-states-tree (16) and walk-machine-spec (2). Walker + helpers gated under #?(:clj ...) since they're JVM-only macro-time fns (per their own docstrings). Tests: 15+13 JVM tests pass; npm run test:cljs runs 1792 tests / 4975 assertions clean.

title: refactor(core): rename :path-stack to :rf/path-stack in path interceptor (reserved namespace)
description:
Audit finding SP1 from rf2-spr6q.

std_interceptors.cljc:34-51 — the path interceptor stashes its stack under bare :path-stack. Per Conventions §Reserved namespaces, framework slots on the interceptor context belong under :rf/...

The unwrap interceptor correctly uses :rf/unwrap-stash. The path one is the lone offender.

Proposed: rename to :rf/path-stack.

Net: +1 LoC. Risk: zero — :path-stack is not part of the documented public ctx contract.

Time-box: 10 min. Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/std_interceptors.cljc.
close_reason: PR #875 opened (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/875). Renamed :path-stack to :rf/path-stack in std_interceptors.cljc path interceptor (3 sites). Added 2 regression tests: path-interceptor-uses-reserved-namespace (pins the slot key via spy interceptor) + path-interceptor-nesting (pins LIFO stack semantics). Tests: npm run test:cljs 1792/4975 pass; clojure -M:test in core/ 442/2364 pass.

title: refactor(core): decompose reg-view*'s 70-line wrapper-builder in views.cljs
description:
Audit finding VW1 from rf2-spr6q.

views.cljs:182-253 — reg-view*'s wrapper fn is 70 LoC of let + binding. The function does five things:
1. Consult :adapter/wrap-view hook.
2. Capture coord-attr (source-coord stamp).
3. Capture view-trigger-handler / view-sensitive? / view-no-emit? from meta (the RT2 pattern repeats — see rf2-ryri7 (handler-scope consolidation)).
4. Build the wrapped fn.
5. Register.

Each phase is recognisable but the body is one nested let.

Proposed: decompose. Tied to rf2-ryri7 (handler-scope consolidation) — once the *handler-scope* macro exists, step 3 becomes one line (with-handler-scope :view id metadata ...) and the binding wrapper simplifies dramatically.

Best done AFTER rf2-ryri7 lands.

Net: ~ -10 LoC + much clearer reading of the registration boundary.

Time-box: ~ 90 min. Risk: medium — view registration is widely tested but the wrapper machinery has reagent / React-context dependencies.

Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs.
close_reason: PR #883 opened (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/883). Decomposed reg-view*'s 70-line wrapper-builder in views.cljs into three named private helpers — apply-adapter-wrap-view, view-coord-attr, build-frame-aware-view — leaving reg-view* itself as a five-line pipeline. Behaviour-preserving (phase boundaries are the existing let-bindings lifted to named fns; HandlerScope path from rf2-ryri7 untouched; elision contracts preserved). LoC delta: +103 / -88 (net +15) — executable code shrinks, docstrings deliberately added per masterpiece-grade. Tests: clojure -M:test from implementation/core/ passes (1 pre-existing path-interceptor failure rf2-mn0qc regression, verified present on main); npx shadow-cljs node-test = 1792 tests / 4975 assertions / 0 failures.

title: refactor(core): pass path/frame-id positionally in elide-wire-value recursion
description:
Audit finding EL1 / PE3 from rf2-spr6q.

elision.cljc:574-608 — elide-wire-value recurses with (assoc opts :path (conj path-vec k) :frame frame-id) at four call sites (map / vector / set / seq branches). Each branch re-assocs opts per child.

For a deeply-nested map with 100 children at each level, this is O(N) assoc calls per level. The opts map is otherwise stable across the recursion.

Proposed: keep opts stable and pass path / frame-id as explicit positional args:

  (elide-wire-value v path frame-id opts)

The 2-arity public form keeps the (v opts) shape with the (let [...] (elide-wire-value v path frame-id opts')) translation at entry.

Net: ~ -10 LoC + meaningful perf win on deep walks (the elision walker fires per event emit + per sub return; hot enough to matter on a wire-heavy app).

Time-box: ~ 90 min + add a perf benchmark for deep maps. Risk: low — the elision walker is well-tested.

Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc.
close_reason: PR #892 — refactored elide-wire-value recursion to positional path/frame-id args. opts normalised once at public entry; internal walk takes (v path frame-id opts). -7 LoC. test:cljs PASS (1792 tests / 4975 assertions). test:elision PASS.

title: fix(core): events.cljc normalise-args 4-arity branch missing (docstring promises it; impl throws)
description:
Audit finding EV2 from rf2-spr6q — BUG.

events.cljc:174-194 — normalise-args admits 4 shapes via (case (count args)) but never accepts the 4-tuple (id metadata interceptors handler) the throw-message documents.

The 4-arity branch is missing from the case. So:

  (reg-event-db :foo {:doc "..."} [icpt] (fn ...))

...currently throws 'reg-event-* arity error' with :count 4.

But the docstrings of reg-event-db etc. (events.cljc:213) document this shape as legal:

  (reg-event-db :id {:doc "..."} [icpt] (fn [db ev] new-db))

Likely been broken since the metadata-map slot landed.

Proposed: add the 4-arity branch:

  4 (let [[meta interceptors handler] args]
      [meta (or interceptors []) handler])

Bundle: while there, audit reg-event-fx / reg-event-ctx for same gap (subs.cljc / fx.cljc / cofx.cljc don't have this issue — only the events.cljc multi-arity normalise).

Net: ~ +3 LoC. Risk: trivial — bug fix.

Time-box: ~ 30 min + add a test in events_test.clj exercising the 4-arity shape. Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc.
close_reason: PR #889. The bug described in the bead was already fixed by rf2-v3nxu (which unified db/fx/ctx handler wrappers and also fixed the misleading 'expected (id metadata interceptors handler)' error message). The audit's '4-arity branch missing' read reflected an older shape of normalise-args; in the current code, the variadic tail's count=3 IS the 4-shape (id meta intc handler) — id is the head &-rest separator and is not in args. Bead closed by locking in regression tests for all four documented user-facing shapes (reg-event-db / reg-event-fx / reg-event-ctx) plus the documented error cases. clojure -M:test 447/2391 green; npm run test:cljs 1792/4975 green.

title: refactor(core): subscribe-value should unsubscribe synchronously (avoid grace-period timer)
description:
Audit finding SU3 from rf2-spr6q.

subs.cljc:486-491 — subscribe-value calls unsubscribe immediately after subscribe. For a fresh sub this triggers build+deref+grace-schedule+set-timeout!+clear-timeout!+dispose. Under the 50ms grace period the timer fires after the test/REPL caller has already moved on.

Proposed: subscribe-value should set grace=0 for its own unsubscribe (or use a different unsubscribe path that disposes synchronously). Either:
- Add an opt-arg to unsubscribe: (unsubscribe frame-id query-v {:grace 0})
- Bind a *sync-dispose?* Var for the duration.

The one-shot read surface should not pay the deferred-dispose tax.

Net: ~ +10 LoC. Risk: low.

Time-box: ~ 45 min. Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc.
close_reason: PR #890 opened. subscribe-value's teardown now uses (unsubscribe frame-id query-v {:grace 0}) — one-shot read's whole lifetime completes in the calling tick. 3-arity unsubscribe with opts map added. Spec 006 updated. 3 regression tests in sub_cache_test.clj. Tests: 447 CLJ + 1792 CLJS green.

title: refactor(core): lift resolve-current-frame into re-frame.frame (3 duplicates)
description:
Audit finding SU4 from rf2-spr6q.

The 'current-frame with React-context adapter consultation' logic appears in 3 places:
- subs.cljc:390-404 (resolve-current-frame)
- router.cljc:104-107 (build-envelope's default-frame inline)
- core.cljc:774-783 (current-frame public fn)

All three: #?(:cljs (if-let [f (late-bind/get-fn :adapter/current-frame)] (f) (frame/current-frame)) :clj (frame/current-frame)).

Proposed: lift into re-frame.frame/resolve-current-frame so the React-context tier consultation is single-sourced. core.cljc/current-frame becomes a one-line re-export.

Net: ~ -10 LoC. Risk: trivial — public API surface unchanged.

Time-box: ~ 30 min. Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc + subs.cljc + router.cljc + core.cljc.
close_reason: Lifted resolve-current-frame into re-frame.frame; subs/router/core now delegate. PR #899.

title: refactor(core): table-drive handle-one-fx's reserved-fx case-block
description:
Audit finding FX2 from rf2-spr6q.

fx.cljc:251-356 — handle-one-fx's case-block is 100 LoC of (case fx-id ...) matching reserved keywords. Four reserved fx-ids (:dispatch / :dispatch-later / :rf.fx/reg-flow / :rf.fx/clear-flow) each have similar bodies: call a late-bind fn, then emit :rf.fx/handled.

Proposed: table-driven approach.

  (def ^:private reserved-fx-handlers
    {:dispatch        {:hook :router/dispatch!         :default-opts identity}
     :dispatch-later  {:hook nil :body ...}            ;; complex — keep inline
     :rf.fx/reg-flow  {:hook :flows/reg-flow-fx!}
     :rf.fx/clear-flow{:hook :flows/clear-flow-fx!}})

The 4 reserved entries collapse to a (case fx-id ... (handle-reserved! ...) (default ...)) over a single helper.

Net: ~ -20 LoC + adding a new reserved fx becomes a table-row edit.

Time-box: ~ 90 min. Risk: low (well-tested surface). Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc.
close_reason: Refactor complete. PR #886. handle-one-fx reserved-fx case-block replaced with a data-driven reserved-fx-handlers table (data, not code). All tests pass: clojure -M:test 444/2369, npm run test:cljs 1792/4975. LoC +72/-43 on fx.cljc; net code growth is docstring/contract carrying the reserved-fx table -- the case-block body collapsed as planned.

title: refactor(story): rewrite variants-of with namespace lookup instead of string-prefix parsing
description:
## Goal

`registrar.cljc:340-350` — `variants-of` parses a string from the keyword to find the prefix, doing three `subs` calls per variant. The cleaner shape is `(filter (fn [vid] (= (namespace vid) (subs (str story-id) 1))) ids)` — variant ids have shape `:story.foo/empty` with namespace `"story.foo"` (which is `(subs (str story-id) 1)`). One namespace call per variant, no subs hunting.

## Audit reference

Audit bead: rf2-dd5ze. Findings: RG1 (P1 clarity + perf).
close_reason: Done. PR #874 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/874 — variants-of now uses namespace lookup. LoC delta +35/-7 across registrar.cljc + story_test.clj. 348 tests / 1025 assertions / 0 failures.

title: refactor(core): specialise layer-1 sub memo path to avoid per-recompute vector allocation
description:
Audit finding SU1 / PE1 from rf2-spr6q.

subs.cljc:350-352 — compute-and-cache! allocates [(frame/get-frame-db frame-id)] as a 1-vector for layer-1 subs. subs.cljc:309-318 — make-memoised-body's closure then compares [(deref container)] to last-in-vals.

For every sub recompute the layer-1 path allocates two single-element vectors plus runs the = comparator. This is the hottest allocation in the artefact: every layer-1 sub × every dispatch that touches it.

Proposed: specialise the layer-1 path:
- make-layer-1-memoised-body — compares last-db against current value directly (no vec wrap).
- Layer-2+ keeps the current vec-of-inputs shape.

Net: +~ 12 LoC (one extra specialisation fn); meaningful perf win on app-db-heavy apps.

Time-box: ~ 90 min + perf benchmark before/after. Risk: low — the optimisation is on the memoisation layer; correctness verified by sub_cache_test + the wider sub_runs test suite.

Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc.
close_reason: Specialisation landed in PR #895: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/895. New make-layer-1-memoised-body uses fixed-arity-1 and scalar = compare; make-layer-n-memoised-body keeps varargs for layer-2+. Saves one ArraySeq/Cons per layer-1 recompute. Regression test sub_memo_layer_1_test pins result-equivalence (memo skip on =-db, recompute on not=-db, nil/false handled, body shape preserved, layer-1 vs layer-2 stream parity). All gates green: clojure -M:test (456 tests / 2436 assertions / 0 failures) + npm run test:cljs (1792 tests / 4975 assertions / 0 failures).

title: refactor(story): fix shell.cljs selection-watcher prev-atom + add trace breadcrumb on silent catches
description:
## Goal

Two small lifetime bugs in shell.cljs surfaced by the audit:

1. `selection-watcher` (shell.cljs:292-317) creates a fresh local `prev` atom on every call, then adds a watch. If `selection-watcher` is called twice without `remove-selection-watcher!` between them, the second call creates a new `prev` and adds a duplicate watch.
2. `ensure-variant-frame!`'s try/catch (shell.cljs:283-290) silently swallows ALL exceptions on the variant-allocation path — a fundamental write — without leaving a trace breadcrumb.

## Fix

1. Make `selection-watcher`'s `prev` atom a module-level `defonce`.
2. Emit a trace event on the silent catch in `ensure-variant-frame!`.

## Audit reference

Audit bead: rf2-dd5ze. Findings: SH3 (P1) + SH2 (P3, bundled).
close_reason: Fixed in PR #893. selection-watcher's prev-atom promoted to module-level defonce selection-prev (reseed on install, clear on teardown); trace breadcrumbs added at both silent catches in ensure-variant-frame! and watch-mode-tick! via re-frame.trace/emit-error!. clojure -M:test from tools/story/: 348 tests / 1025 assertions / 0 failures. CLJS test:cljs: 1792 tests / 0 failures.

title: refactor(core): factor error_emit + event_emit into re-frame.emit-substrate parameterised primitive
description:
Audit finding EE1 / A4 from rf2-spr6q.

error_emit.cljc (263 L) and event_emit.cljc (234 L) are 75 % parallel structures. Both ship:
- defonce ^:private listeners (atom {})
- register-X-emit-listener! / unregister-X-emit-listener! / clear-X-emit-listeners!
- dispatch-on-X! fan-out helper

The bodies differ in (a) the record-shape (event vs error), (b) per-event vs per-error short-circuit conditions.

Proposed:
- re-frame.emit-substrate ns with make-listener-registry returning {:register :unregister :clear :fan-out} map.
- error-emit and event-emit become 20-line specialisations.

Also: each ns ships > 100 lines of design-history docstring (event-emit.cljc:1-127, error-emit.cljc:1-126). Trim per TR3 pattern — one paragraph + spec link.

Net: ~ -100 LoC code + ~ -200 LoC docstrings. The third emit-substrate the framework might want (machine-lifecycle, frame-lifecycle?) becomes a single instantiation.

Time-box: ~ 3 hr. Risk: medium — two production-shipping substrates; correctness verified by the existing event_emit_test / on_error_test suites.

Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc, event_emit.cljc, plus new implementation/core/src/re_frame/emit_substrate.cljc.
close_reason: PR #904 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/904 — factored re-frame.emit-substrate as parameterised primitive. event-emit + error-emit now thin wrappers. LoC delta 497 -> 292 (-205, -41%). test:cljs 1792/4975 pass; core JVM clojure -M:test 456/2436 pass.

title: refactor(core): decompose process-event* (137 L) into named phases
description:
Audit finding RT1 from rf2-spr6q.

router.cljc:393-541 — process-event* is 137 LoC of let + cond. Reads as five named phases (validate-event → assemble-ctx → execute-chain → commit-effects → emit-trailers) but they're inlined into one large let body.

Mirrors machines-audit §T6 (apply-transition-once decomposition) and §A6 (finalize-machine pipeline-ify).

Proposed: decompose into prepare-handler-ctx / run-chain / commit-and-flow / emit-cascade-trailers — each phase becomes a named helper.

Net: ~ -25 LoC; clarity win on the hot path. Risk: medium (the engine's central event-processing pipeline; must keep observable trace ordering identical).

Time-box: ~ 2 hr. Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc.
close_reason: PR #903 — decomposed process-event* into named phases (handle-frame-destroyed! / handle-no-handler! / prepare-handler-ctx / run-chain / commit-and-flow! / emit-cascade-trailers! / run-handler-cascade!). Behaviour-preserving (trace ordering, start-ms/end-ms windows, handler-scope extent identical). Tests green: 1792 CLJS + 456 core JVM. LoC delta +69 (helpers carry normative docstrings; structural clarity win).

title: refactor(story): move duplicated aggregate-summary fold from sidebar.cljs to state.cljc
description:
## Goal

`sidebar.cljs:383-401` — `run-one-test!` inlines a 15-line `aggregate-summary`-style fold that's a verbatim copy of `test_mode.cljc:104-121`. The comment is explicit: "We can't require [test-mode] here (cyclic: test-mode requires state, which would loop back through sidebar's requires)."

## Fix

Move the fold to `state.cljc` (which both sidebar AND test-mode already require). Neither would loop. Drop the inlined copy from sidebar.

## Audit reference

notes:
Landed in PR #909: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/909

Move:
- canonical aggregate-summary now lives in re-frame.story.ui.state (state.cljc) per bead intent

Quality gates: clojure -M:test from tools/story/ — 348 tests / 1025 assertions / 0 failures / 0 errors.

title: refactor(story): fix chrome 'Run all' dropping per-variant cell-overrides
description:
## Goal

`sidebar.cljs:371-374` — the chrome-level "Run all" builds opts with `:cell-overrides nil` for every variant. Per rf2-q0irb the contract was test-mode parity, but the test-mode pane (test_mode.cljc:633) DOES propagate cell-overrides from `(get-in shell [:cell-overrides variant-id])`. Inconsistent: the same variant run from the chrome widget vs the pane runs against different effective-args.

## Fix

`sidebar.cljs/run-one-test!` should pull cell-overrides per-variant from shell state just like the pane does.

## Audit reference

close_reason: Fixed in PR #902. Chrome 'Run all' (sidebar.cljs/run-one-test!) and the test_mode pane (run-variant-pane!) now thread per-variant cell-overrides via the canonical (get-in shell [:cell-overrides vid]) lookup. title: refactor(story): implement missing :argtypes widgets (:textarea :radio :date :color)
description:
## Goal

Per spec/007-Stories.md:217-219 the closed control vocabulary is `:text` / `:textarea` / `:number` / `:boolean` / `:select` / `:radio` / `:date` / `:color`. The impl in `controls.cljs:328-364` (`scalar-widget`) handles only `:text` / `:number` / `:boolean` / `:select`. So `:argtypes {:bio {:control :textarea}}` renders as the error fallback string.

## Scope

Implement `:textarea` / `:radio` / `:date` / `:color` widgets in `controls.cljs/scalar-widget` matching the styling conventions of the existing widgets.

## Audit reference

Audit bead: rf2-dd5ze. Findings: CT3 + S3.
close_reason: Landed in PR #914: implemented :textarea / :radio / :date / :color scalar widgets in tools/story/.../controls.cljs, plus default-element-value entries for :repeater / :tuple seeding, plus a styling pack per widget. New CLJS test ns re-frame.story.ui.controls-scalar-widgets-cljs-test covers all four widgets + the unknown-widget fallback + the arg-widget dispatch (16 deftests). JVM suite: 348 / 1025 pass. CLJS suite: 1809 / 5011 pass.

title: refactor(story): decompose run-variant (70-line let/try/catch) into named phase fns
description:
## Goal

`runtime.cljc:280-329` — `run-variant` is a 70-line `let`/`try`/`catch` wall that drives six phases inline (decorator-resolve → args-resolve → snapshot → phase-0 allocate → phase-1 loaders → phase-2 events → phase-4 play). Mirror of the machines audit's L5 / A6 (`create-machine-handler`, `finalize-machine`).

## Fix

Decompose into named phase fns:
- `(prepare-context variant-id opts) → ctx`
- `(run-phase-0 ctx) → ctx`  (frame allocation + frame-setup decorators)
- `(run-phase-1 ctx) → ctx`  (loaders)
- `(run-phase-2 ctx) → ctx`  (events)
- `(run-phase-4 ctx) → promise`  (play + assertions)

Each is currently inline with try/catch; lifting them produces both a clearer reading order AND a cleaner test surface (today `run-variant` is the only entry point — there's no way to unit-test "given a primed ctx, run phase-2").

## Risk

Medium — engine hot path.

## Audit reference

Audit bead: rf2-dd5ze. Findings: RT1.
close_reason: PR #897: decomposed run-variant 70-line let/try/catch into named phase fns (prepare-context, run-phase-0! through run-phase-4!, finalise-run!, handle-run-error!, unknown-variant-result). Tests: 348/1025 pass. Closes RT1 from rf2-dd5ze.

title: refactor(story): consolidate three assertions trace accumulator atoms into one
description:
## Goal

`assertions.cljc:83-102` defines three module-level `defonce` atoms (`warnings-accumulator`, `emitted-fx-accumulator`, `dispatched-events-accumulator`), each keyed by frame-id. They have parallel reset / record / drop fns. Maintaining three globals in lockstep is the same shape as the machines audit's TM4 finding.

## Fix

Consolidate into one `accumulators-atom` keyed by `[frame-id accumulator-kind]` OR a map of three sub-atoms keyed by frame-id under a single root. Drops the multi-atom-coordination dance.

## Audit reference

Audit bead: rf2-dd5ze. Findings: AS1.
close_reason: PR #917 — three assertion-trace atoms consolidated into one map-atom shaped {frame-id {:warnings [...] :emitted-fx #{...} :dispatched [...]}}. All 348 story tests pass.

title: refactor(story): unify snippet-generator indent helpers (recorder + save-variant use different magic numbers)
description:
## Goal

`recorder.cljc:148` joins event vectors with an 11-space indent string (`"\n           "`); `save_variant.cljc:91` joins map entries with a 12-space indent string (`"\n            "`). Same shape (indent under one container brace); inconsistent magic numbers. If the surrounding form's column changes (e.g. longer alias), both break differently.

## Fix

Extract a tiny `(indent-by n s)` or use `clojure.pprint`/`fipp` for snippet generation. Apply uniformly.

## Audit reference

Audit bead: rf2-dd5ze. Findings: R2 + SV1 (P1 cluster).
close_reason: PR #929 opened. Extracted shared review-dialog/indent-after helper; recorder + save-variant call sites now compute the indent from the rendered first-line prefix. Magic-number resolution: previous values (11 / 12 spaces) were off-by-one in opposite directions from geometrically correct 10; helper derives column-perfectly from prefix length. JVM 352/1032 + CLJS 1818/5054 tests pass.

title: refactor(ssr): conformance-corpus runner + shared test fixture extraction
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §TC4 / TC5 / TC6 / Q7.

Two related test-side improvements:

## 1. Conformance-corpus runner

Spec 011 §Hydration equivalence rule commits to canonical-traversal fixtures at `spec/conformance/`. The machines audit noted the same gap. Currently no SSR test runs those fixtures through the live runtime.

**Recommend** `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj` that drives every `spec/conformance/fixtures/ssr-*.edn` through `render-to-string` / `render-tree-hash` / `hydrate` and `=`-checks against the recorded outcome.

## 2. Shared test fixture extraction

`reset-runtime` is duplicated across 6 test files (ssr_end_to_end_test, ssr_head_test, ssr_request_cofx_test, ssr_compatibility_checks_test, ssr_source_coord_test, ssr_teardown_load_test, plus ssr/ring_test). Identical 7-12-line fixture each.

**Recommend** extract to `re-frame.ssr.test-fixture` (test-only ns). Expose:
- `(reset-runtime!)` — clears all registries, frame state, schemas, head snapshots, request slots, pending-error-traces.
- `(use-default-fixture)` — `(use-fixtures :each ...)` shorthand.

## 3. Make both side-channel atoms private + exposed via test-fixture

Today `pending-error-traces` is `^:private` (resolved reflectively in tests); `request-slots` is public (reset directly). Asymmetric. **Recommend** make both private; the test-fixture ns is the canonical reset surface.

## Acceptance

- All test files use the shared fixture (-60 LoC across tests).
- Side-channel atoms are uniformly private.
- Conformance fixtures are CI-run.

## Risk

Low — pure test-side refactor. Conformance runner may surface latent bugs (which is the point).
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/901 — conformance runner + shared fixture + request-slots privatisation. 10/10 ssr-*.edn fixtures pass.

title: refactor(ssr): decompose ring-handler into a small named pipeline
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §R4.

`ring-handler` (ssr-ring.clj:444-510) is a **70-line function with three exception-handling layers and five nested let/cond layers**:

1. `binding` `*current-request*`
2. `make-frame` with catch → frame-id-or-error-response
3. cond on `(map? frame-id)` vs nil
4. inner try with let-cascade
5. cond on `(:redirect response)`
6. inner let with 7 bindings → response*
7. catch → on-error
8. finally → destroy

## Fix

```clojure
(defn- ring-handler [opts request]
  (let [frame-id (make-per-request-frame opts request)]
    (try
      (if-let [redirect-response (read-and-detect-redirect frame-id)]
        redirect-response
        (build-full-response frame-id opts))
      (catch Throwable t
        ((:on-error opts) request t))
      (finally
        (destroy-frame-quietly! frame-id)))))
```

Each step is a small named fn. The destroy-in-finally is the load-bearing piece; that stays explicit. The dynamic Var concern is addressed by rf2-afxhv (drop the Var, use set-request!).

## Acceptance

- All existing ring_test.clj tests pass.
- The function reads as a 4-step lifecycle pipeline.
- Exception paths are clear.

## Risk

Medium — touches the request lifecycle entry point. Coordinated with rf2-afxhv (Ring + set-request! fix) and rf2-6t36h (single root-view resolve).
close_reason: PR #908 opened: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/908. ring-handler decomposed into 4-step named pipeline (setup-request-frame! → get-response → branch :redirect / build-full-response → destroy-frame-quietly! in finally). Helper extractions: ensure-content-type, default-on-error, handler-defaults. Dead nil-frame-id branch gone. Tests: ssr-ring 19/80, ssr 77/237 — all pass. LoC: +147 -108 (net +39 — comments + new helpers; the handler body itself collapsed from ~99 lines to ~18).

title: refactor(ssr): ld-json-string strips namespace from keyword map keys (likely bug)
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §H3.

`re-frame.ssr.head/ld-json-string` (head.cljc:123-152) is a hand-rolled JSON printer for JSON-LD content on JVM. Its keyword-key handling:

```clojure
(if (keyword? k) (name k) k)
```

This DROPS the namespace prefix. A user passing `{:my.app/x "y"}` gets `{"x":"y"}` in the JSON-LD output — losing `my.app/`.

JSON-LD typically uses string keys (`@context`, `@type`, `headline`, ...) per the W3C spec, so the conformance corpus may not trip this. But a user mixing keyword and string keys in a head model's :json-ld slot loses the namespace.

The keyword-value path at line 140-142 has the same issue:

```clojure
(keyword? v) (emit (if-let [ns (namespace v)]
                     (str ns "/" (name v))
                     (name v)))
```

Wait — this DOES preserve namespace for VALUES. So values are namespace-preserved; keys are not. Asymmetric.

## Fix

Make key handling symmetric with value handling:

```clojure
(map? v) (str "{"
              (str/join "," (map (fn [[k val]]
                                    (str (emit (if (keyword? k)
                                                 (if-let [ns (namespace k)]
                                                   (str ns "/" (name k))
                                                   (name k))
                                                 k))
                                         ":"
                                         (emit val)))
                                  v))
              "}")
```

## Test

```clojure
(deftest ld-json-namespace-preservation
  (let [html (head/head-model->html
               {:json-ld [{:my.app/key "value"}]})]
    (is (str/includes? html "\"my.app/key\":\"value\""))))
```

## Risk

Low — fixes a latent bug. No known caller would have noticed because most JSON-LD uses string keys. Spec 011 §Head/meta JSON-LD example (line 457) uses string keys; the impl's keyword-key path is incidental.
close_reason: fix landed in PR #907 — ld-json-string now delegates keyword-key serialisation to the same emit branch that handles keyword values; namespaces preserved symmetrically. Regression test added. 78/78 SSR tests pass.

title: refactor(ssr): JVM byte-level fnv-1a-32 fast path (3-5x perf)
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §Q11 / P3.

`fnv-1a-32` (ssr.cljc:276-300) runs in slow char-by-char loop mode on JVM:

```clojure
(loop [i 0 h offset]
  (if (>= i (count s))
    ...
    (let [c (.charAt s i)
          x (bit-xor h c)
          p (bit-and 0xffffffff (unchecked-multiply x prime))]
      (recur (inc i) p))))
```

For a render-tree of 10K chars (a medium page's canonical-EDN), that's 10K boxing+unboxing roundtrips per request — ~10-30µs per hash on JVM.

## Fix (JVM only — CLJS Math.imul path is already optimal)

```clojure
#?(:clj
   (defn- fnv-1a-32 [^String s]
     (let [bytes (.getBytes s java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets/UTF_8)
           len   (alength bytes)]
       (loop [i 0
              h 2166136261]
         (if (>= i len)
           (format "%08x" (bit-and h 0xffffffff))
           (recur (inc i)
                  (unchecked-int
                    (unchecked-multiply
                      (bit-xor h (bit-and (aget bytes i) 0xff))
                      16777619)))))))
   :cljs
   (defn- fnv-1a-32 [s] ...))  ; existing CLJS path
```

3-5× faster for medium-string hashes on JVM; relevant at SSR-load scale.

## Caveat

Bytes vs chars: the FNV-1a contract over a string is character-encoding-sensitive. The current char-based path on JVM and `.charCodeAt` on CLJS BOTH operate on UTF-16 code units. Switching to UTF-8 bytes on JVM would diverge from the CLJS path.

**Therefore:** this fix requires the canonical-EDN serialisation to be ASCII-clean OR requires changing both sides to operate on the same byte stream. Coordinate with rf2-1q9de (the hash parity test) — pick a byte representation that both sides can agree on. Likely option: `.getBytes "UTF-8"` on JVM, `TextEncoder('utf-8').encode(s)` on CLJS.

## Acceptance

- JVM and CLJS produce byte-identical hash strings for any fixture in the parity test (rf2-1q9de).
- JVM perf improves measurably on a medium-tree hash (benchmark recommended via tools/perf).
- The `canonical-edn` output is UTF-8 round-trippable (no surrogate pairs in test fixtures).
notes: Landed PR #918. JVM fnv-1a-32 now hashes UTF-8 byte-array via String.getBytes(UTF_8) with primitive ^bytes/int/long locals — eliminates per-char boxing on the inner loop. CLJS switched to TextEncoder UTF-8 bytes to keep both sides on the same byte stream. Existing ASCII parity pin (9d7457ef) preserved byte-for-byte (UTF-8 byte == UTF-16 code unit for ASCII codepoints). Parity test extended with a non-ASCII pin (café -> a82b5049) so a future runtime divergence on multi-byte codepoints fails CI. SSR JVM suite green (78/241), CLJS suite green (1813/5024).
close_reason: Byte-level UTF-8 FNV-1a-32 hot path landed (JVM via .getBytes(UTF_8)+aget primitive byte-array, CLJS via goog.crypt/stringToUtf8ByteArray+aget). JVM↔CLJS parity preserved: hash_check_cljs_test pinned 9d7457ef holds on both sides. SSR clojure-test (78/241/0) + CLJS suite (1809/5011/0) green. PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/919

title: refactor(schemas): resolve reg-app-schema double-write — registrar :app-schema slot vs schemas-by-frame atom
description:
reg-app-schema (schemas.cljc:260-280) writes to BOTH:
1. The registrar (registrar/register! :app-schema path meta)
2. The per-frame atom (swap! schemas-by-frame assoc-in [frame-id path] meta)

The registrar's :app-schema slot is a single-frame view (path → meta). The per-frame atom is the authoritative store. Per the comment at lines 276-277, the registrar entry exists only for 'source-coords / handler-meta / hot-reload tooling' — meaning (rf/handler-meta :app-schema path) returns the latest registration regardless of frame.

This is a subtle leak: re-registering against frame B overwrites the registrar's view of the path but doesn't touch frame A's per-frame entry. A pair-tool calling (rf/handler-meta :app-schema [:user]) sees the LATEST registration (frame B's), but (rf/app-schema-at [:user] :rf/default) returns frame A's. **Two sources of truth for 'the schema at path P'.**

Recommend either:
(a) Drop the registrar :app-schema slot entirely. The per-frame atom is the only store. The tool API queries by frame.
(b) Use composite registrar keys (path × frame-id) so frame-A and frame-B registrations are independent entries.

Option (a) is cleaner if no current consumer hard-relies on the per-path single view. Audit didn't find any direct (handler-meta :app-schema ...) calls.

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (A5).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.
close_reason: Resolved via PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/911. Dropped the registrar :app-schema write; schemas-by-frame is the single source of truth. Added schemas/app-schema-meta-at as the canonical introspection API replacing (handler-meta :app-schema path). The :app-schema registrar kind is RESERVED but intentionally empty — matches the :http-interceptor precedent. Spec 001/010/Spec-Schemas aligned. Tests: schemas 123/352, core 456/2436, CLJS 1793/4980, bundle-isolation PASS.

title: refactor(pair2-mcp): subscribe-tool refactor (one-atom state, named controller, indicator helper)
description:
`subscribe-tool` (tools.cljs:1884-2071, 188 LoC) is the engine of the streaming path. Three readability hurts:

## 1. Eight atoms allocated as a flat list

`tick`, `delivered`, `dropped-events*`, `dropped-bytes*`, `overflow-reason*`, `dropped-sensitive*`, `elided-large*` plus an unnamed inner state atom. Lines 1928-1956.

**Recommend** one atom holding a map:
```clojure
{:tick :delivered :dropped-events :dropped-bytes :overflow-reason
 :dropped-sensitive :elided-large}
```
A single `swap!` per drain instead of 5-7 separate ones.

## 2. `terminate` / `poll` mutually recursive via `.then`

The `(poll)` call at line 2067 is far from the `(fn poll [...])` definition at line 1987. Hard to follow.

**Recommend** factor `make-stream-controller {:state :terminate :poll}` and resolve from the controller.

## 3. Progress-payload cond-> uses the same indicator-field tail

Lines 2038-2060 build `(cond-> {...} (pos? dropped) ... (pos? tick-elided) ...)` — same pattern as snapshot/trace-window. Once the `with-indicators` helper (rf2-dfk28) lands, this site uses it.

## Why

The streaming path is the most-allocated tool. ~30 LoC saved + much clearer flow.

Depends on: rf2-dfk28 (`with-indicators` helper), rf2-vrbwx (file split so subscribe-tool moves to its own ns).

Surface: `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs` (or its post-split equivalent).

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §T13 / T14.
close_reason: PR #898 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/898 — subscribe-tool refactored: seven atoms → one map-atom; terminate/poll → make-stream-controller; parse-mcp-extra helper extracted. wire/with-indicators (rf2-dfk28) already handles indicator-field splicing. Tests 289/289 green.

title: refactor(ssr): inject data-rf-render-hash on hiccup root, not via post-emit regex
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §Q4.

`render-to-string` injects the `data-rf-render-hash` attribute via a regex replace on the emitted string:

```clojure
(clojure.string/replace-first
  body
  #"(<[a-zA-Z][^\s>/]*)"
  (str "$1 data-rf-render-hash=\"" h "\""))
```

This works today (the regex matches the first `<tag` opener; the letter-prefix lookahead skips a leading `<!DOCTYPE>`), but it relies on the emitter's exact stringification rather than walking the tree.

Symmetry: `inject-coord-on-root-hiccup` (ssr.cljc:168-189) already injects `data-rf2-source-coord` on the **hiccup tree** before stringification — clean, structural, no regex fragility.

## Fix

Apply the same pattern to the render-hash. Inject the attr on the hiccup root before `emit-element` walks the tree.

```clojure
(defn render-to-string [render-tree opts]
  (let [tree-with-hash
        (if (:emit-hash? opts)
          (let [h (render-tree-hash render-tree)]
            (inject-attr-on-root render-tree :data-rf-render-hash h))
          render-tree)
        body (emit-element tree-with-hash)]
    (if (:doctype? opts)
      (str "<!DOCTYPE html>" body)
      body)))
```

`inject-attr-on-root` mirrors `inject-coord-on-root-hiccup` — same skip-list for fragments / non-DOM roots.

## Acceptance

- Existing tests pass (the wire shape is unchanged for ordinary trees).
- A fragment-rooted tree (`[:<>  ...]`) silently no-ops on hash injection (matches existing source-coord behaviour).
- The string-replace path is gone — no regex dependency on emitter output.
close_reason:
Done — PR #921: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/921

Refactor: data-rf-render-hash now injected on hiccup root via emit-element's root-attrs threading, NOT via post-emit regex. Mirrors inject-coord-on-root-hiccup pattern. Composes cleanly with source-coord at the same DOM root. Fragment/Reagent-native roots silently no-op (matches source-coord exemption).

Test results: 78 ssr tests / 241 assertions pass; 19 ssr-ring tests / 80 assertions pass. Wire shape unchanged for ordinary trees. LoC delta: +103 / -54.

title: refactor(schemas): wire conformance corpus runner into schemas-artefact test classpath
description:
The conformance fixtures :schemas/runtime, :schemas/event-payload, :schemas/sub-return, :schemas/cofx (per core/test/.../conformance_test.clj:66-69) are run from core/, not schemas/.

The schemas artefact has its own deps.edn (schemas/deps.edn) and test classpath, but doesn't pull in the conformance runner. The artefact's tests cover unit behaviour; the conformance corpus pins the spec contract; the two suites don't intersect here.

Recommend: add a schemas.conformance-test ns that drives the schemas-relevant fixtures (spec/conformance/fixtures/schema-*.edn) through the live runtime here too. Mirrors sibling rf2-ra1he TE5 finding for machines.

Mostly plumbing — small file + dep additions in schemas/deps.edn :test alias.

title: refactor(pair2-mcp): cleanup small smells (path-segment heuristic, mirroring, eval-form filter, etc)
description:
Cluster of small P1 cleanups that share "smaller / cleaner" character and don't need their own beads.

## Items

1. **`coerce-path-segment` heuristic** (tools.cljs:1171-1194) — first-char-triggers-EDN heuristic adds complexity without value. Drop the heuristic; let `read-string` try unconditionally, fall back on catch. (-6 LoC)

2. **Stop mirroring `default-max-buffered-bytes`** (tools.cljs:1877-1882) — the runtime applies the same default when slot is nil. Mirror creates two-file sync burden. Pass nil when caller omits; let runtime default. (-5 LoC + drift safety)

3. **`tree-summary` scalar arm** (tools.cljs:1358-1361) — wraps a scalar in `{:rf.mcp/summary {:type :scalar :value v :bytes N}}`. A scalar already fits the cap; wrapping is anti-economic. Return `v` unchanged. (-5 LoC)

4. **`subscription-info-tool` eval-form filter** (tools.cljs:2119-2127) — builds `(if nil ...)` branches when `topic`/`sub-id` are absent. Build filter chain in Clojure; inline only conditions that apply. (-5 LoC, clearer form)

5. **`dedup-expand` is defn but only test-used** (tools.cljs:418-428). Move to a test-utils ns. (-10 LoC from main file)

6. **`send-op!` 30s timeout is hardcoded** (nrepl.cljs:206) with no caller override. Accept `:timeout-ms` (default 30s). Heavy forms can pass longer. (+5 LoC)

7. **`server.cljs` degraded-boot fallback duplicates success-path boot** (server.cljs:110-136). Extract `(build-server handle-call)`. (-15 LoC)

## Why

P1 cluster — none individually justifies a bead, but together they're a meaningful polish pass.

Surface: `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/{tools,nrepl,server}.cljs`.

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §T11, T26, T21, T19, T25, N3, S1.
notes: PR #906 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/906 — applied 7 cleanups per audit (T11, T26, T21, T19, T25, N3, S1). Tests 289/688 green. See PR description for details.
close_reason: Closed

title: refactor(schemas): app-schemas-digest cross-runtime byte-identity is untested (pin test vectors)
description:
Spec 010 §Digest algorithm line 391 is normative: 'cross-runtime reproducible — a CLJS server and a CLJS client running the same schema set produce the same digest, byte-for-byte'.

Current test coverage (schemas_test.clj:524-535) pins ONE digest: the empty-schema digest (sha256:e3b0c44298fc1c14). Spec 010 line 419 says 'Conformance fixtures pin a small number of schema sets to expected digest values so port implementations can self-check their digest pipeline'.

Two gaps:
1. No CLJS-side digest test (schemas_cljs_test.cljs has zero digest assertions).
2. No multi-schema digest vector pinned (only empty-set).

Recommend:
- Pin 3-5 digest vectors in a shared test data file.
- Add JVM tests asserting compute-digest produces each.
- Add CLJS tests asserting compute-digest produces the **same** values byte-for-byte. This is the load-bearing cross-runtime invariant that's currently uncovered.

If conformance corpus already has these fixtures: verify they're wired into the schemas artefact test classpath (see rf2-x8x4p audit TE5).

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (TE6 / S7).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.
close_reason: Pinned 7 canonical digest literals + 4 equality-invariant pairs in shared .cljc fixtures namespace. Both JVM (clojure -M:test from implementation/schemas/) and CLJS (npm run test:cljs from implementation/) test paths added, both pass. PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/915

title: refactor(ssr): unify apply-error-projection! and apply-pending-error-projection!
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §Q12.

`apply-error-projection!` (ssr.cljc:1172-1190) and `apply-pending-error-projection!` (ssr.cljc:1145-1170) are 95% the same function:

Both:
- Check `(and frame-id (server-frame? frame-id))`.
- Project a trace event via the active projector.
- Read `response-of` and check for `:redirect`.
- When no redirect, `swap-response!` to set `:status` from public-error.

Difference: the former takes an explicit trace-event; the latter drains a buffer and uses the last entry.

## Fix

```clojure
(defn apply-error-projection!
  ([frame-id]                                          ;; drain buffer
   (when-let [traces (when (and frame-id (server-frame? frame-id))
                       (seq (consume-pending-traces! frame-id)))]
     (apply-error-projection! frame-id (last traces))))
  ([frame-id trace-event]                              ;; explicit
   (when (and frame-id (server-frame? frame-id) trace-event)
     (let [public    (project-error frame-id trace-event)
           existing  (response-of frame-id)]
       (when-not (:redirect existing)
         (swap-response! frame-id (fn [r] (assoc r :status (:status public)))))
       public))))
```

Drop `apply-pending-error-projection!` — replaced by the 1-arity form.

## Acceptance

- All existing tests pass.
- `get-response` continues to flush pending traces (calls the 1-arity).
- The split-fn API is internally consistent.
close_reason: PR #868: unified apply-error-projection! with 1-/2-arity. apply-pending-error-projection! dropped. Façade re-export removed. Conformance test drain + get-response both call the 1-arity. SSR tests (76/236) and CLJS gate (1792/4975) green. LoC −10.

title: refactor(schemas): add pluggable schema-print companion fn (digest contract is currently Malli-only)
description:
Spec 010 §The four normative claims line 491 (and §Schema digest line 397):

> Schema digests are computed from the schema **values** as serialised by the registered validator's `schema-print` companion fn (see §Schema digest) — not from the validator.

The current schema-print (schemas.cljc:947-957) is **schemas-internal, NOT pluggable**. A custom validator registered via set-schema-validator! cannot supply its own schema-print. A Zod-port or clojure.spec port would produce digests computed with re-frame2's hardcoded Malli-EDN canonicalisation — mismatching the validator's own serialisation.

The rest of Spec 010 is pluggable (set-schema-validator! / set-schema-explainer!); the digest contract is effectively Malli-specific despite the spec's normative cross-port claim.

Recommend: add a third atom `schema-print-fn` and `set-schema-printer!` registration, mirroring the validate/explain pattern. Default to the current Malli-EDN canonicaliser; pluggable for ports.

+20 LoC. Closes a Spec 010 contract hole — pluggable validator implies pluggable digest serialisation.

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (S8).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.
close_reason: Implemented: pluggable schema-print companion fn parallel to set-schema-validator! / set-schema-explainer!. Default = the previous Malli-EDN canonicaliser (rf2-xssfv pinned digest literals still match byte-for-byte). PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/920

title: refactor(ssr): collapse redundant 500-class arms in default-error-projector-fn
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §Q8.

`default-error-projector-fn` (ssr.cljc:954-982) repeats the same 500-class map literal **five times** — four named arms plus the catch-all. The literal is identical to `fallback-public-error` defined a few lines up (ssr.cljc:928).

## Fix

```clojure
(defn default-error-projector-fn [trace-event]
  (case (:operation trace-event)
    (:rf.error/no-such-handler :rf.error/no-such-route)
    {:status 404 :code :not-found :message "Page not found" :retryable? false}

    :rf.error/schema-validation-failure
    {:status 400 :code :bad-request :message "Invalid input" :retryable? false}

    ;; everything else — including the named 500-class events — falls
    ;; through to the locked generic-500 shape. Future :rf.error/* events
    ;; that should map to 500 don't need a new case arm.
    fallback-public-error))
```

Saves ~12 LoC + makes 'anything not enumerated → 500' the literal default rather than four ceremonial copies.

## Acceptance

- All existing tests pass (the result shape is identical).
- Spec 011 §Default projector mapping table is unchanged.
- The named-case arms only remain for non-500 mappings.
close_reason: Collapsed redundant 500-class arms in default-error-projector-fn. PR #927. fallback-public-error is now the single source of truth for the locked generic-500 shape; named 500-class events (handler-exception, sub-exception, fx-handler-exception, drain-depth-exceeded) fall through to the default arm. Mapping table unchanged. 82 tests / 267 assertions pass; SSR conformance corpus 10/10.

title: decision(pair2-mcp): clarify Spec 009 :elided-large MUST scope (run-walker vs encounter-marker)
description:
Today, per source comments at tools.cljs:949-958, 1046-1055, and 1942-1955, the elision walker is wired ONLY on `snapshot` and `get-path`. The `count-elided-markers` call on `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` / `subscribe` always returns 0 — the slot is therefore always omitted (per Conventions §147 "omit when zero").

Spec 009 §Indicator field on tool responses (line 1411, MUST-level): "Tools that return structured response maps … MUST carry an `:elided-large` count alongside the existing `:dropped-sensitive` count … — one MUST-level row per consumer-facing tool that walks a tree-typed payload."

These three tools ARE consumer-facing. They DO walk tree-typed payloads. They count markers (always zero) and omit the slot.

## Three readings — which is the spec intent?

(a) **"Omit when zero" — slot correctly omitted.** Spec satisfied.

(b) **Count what you encounter.** Today's scaffolding is correct: count any markers in the payload, ship the count if non-zero. `trace-window` doesn't elide, but if a future runtime emits markers in epoch records (e.g. sensitive trace payloads pre-elided server-side), the count is already wired.

(c) **The tool must RUN the elision walker.** Then `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` / `subscribe` must wire `elide-wire-value` over their epoch payloads. This is heaviest reading — implies more work.

## Decision required

Pick one of (a), (b), (c). Amend Spec 009 §Indicator field on tool responses to make the scope explicit.

## Why this matters

Today the comments at the five emit-sites describe scaffolding for behaviour that may or may not need to be wired. Without spec clarity, the next reviewer (or future bead) will re-litigate the question.

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §S1.
close_reason: DECIDED (Mike, 2026-05-14): Option (b) count-what-you-encounter. The :elided-large slot reports markers encountered in the payload; tools do NOT invoke elide-wire-value themselves — markers ride through from upstream (event-emit substrate, error-emit substrate, schema-slot meta). Slot omitted when zero per Conventions §147. Rationale: runtime is the place-of-truth for elision; tools are consumers. Slot stays meaningful when zero is common — consumers learn 'this epoch had N large slots redacted upstream'. No new code burden — current scaffolding is already (b)-shaped. Consistent with the pragmatic security stance on the 9 policy beads (trust runtime; don't duplicate gates). Follow-on impl is a tiny spec edit + 5 comment-block one-liner updates in tools.cljs (L949-958, 1046-1055, 1942-1955).

title: decision(schemas): :rf.error/schema-validation-failure on app-db — spec says 'roll back :db'; impl says :recovery :no-recovery
description:
Spec 010 §Per-step recovery row 4 (line 113, line 139-140) is normative:

> Roll back the :db effect; treat dispatch as failed.

But the impl (schemas.cljc:1184) emits `:recovery :no-recovery` and the :db has already been committed before validate-app-db! runs (per router.cljc:348 — validate-app-db! is post-commit).

Two paths:
(a) Implement the rollback. validate-app-db! returns a status; router restores the pre-handler db value on failure. Several pieces need to move:
  - schemas surface to return [bool, optional-explanation] tuple.
  - router to capture pre-handler-db and conditionally restore.
  - Trace event :recovery :db-rollback (new keyword) or :rolled-back.
(b) Update Spec 010 to say :no-recovery for app-db failures — the post-commit-validation reality. The trace fires; the bad commit stands; the user observes via the trace and triages.

Option (b) is the simpler-and-honest answer; (a) is a meaningful behavioural change.

Mike decision required.

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (S4).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.
close_reason: Closed via PR #1054 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1054). Decision: spec wins, impl rolls back. Pre-alpha is the right time for the more correct/complete behaviour.

title: refactor(schemas): document redacted slots :malli-error and :event in Spec 010 (or drop them)
description:
schemas.cljc:1099-1111 redacts five slots in redact-tags: :value, :received, :explain, :malli-error, :event.

Spec 010 §:sensitive? line 293-297 only lists three: :value, :received, :explain.

The two undocumented redaction targets:
- :malli-error — set by validate-event!/sub-return!/cofx! to the same value as :explain (schemas.cljc:1226). Duplicate slot for the same data.
- :event — set by validate-event! to the same value as :received (schemas.cljc:1224-1225). Duplicate slot for the same data.

The duplication itself is a smell — each failing value rides under two trace-event tag keys. Either:
(a) Document :malli-error and :event in Spec 010 §:sensitive? as additionally-redacted slots. Document the duplication rationale.
(b) Drop :malli-error (keep only :explain) and drop :event (keep only :received).

Option (b) is simpler. Option (a) is back-compat with any consumer reading :malli-error / :event directly.

Pre-alpha rule says back-compat isn't a concern — Option (b) is preferred.

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (Q10 / S6).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.
notes: Dropped :malli-error and :event slots from all five emit-sites (4 meta-bearing validate-*! + boundary-validation interceptor). Direction: drop (not document) — slots were pure data duplicates of :explain / :received; Spec 010 was already silent on them, so removal aligns impl with spec. Tests pin the absence with explicit (not (contains? ...)) checks. PR #934.
close_reason: Closed

title: refactor(pair2-mcp): parse-mode-arg + parse-modes-arg delegate to base-args helpers
description:
Two parsers in tools.cljs reinvent helpers that exist in `re-frame.mcp-base.args`:

- `parse-mode-arg` (tools.cljs:1512-1524) — accepts `:summary`/`:full` (strings + keywords), defaults `:summary`. `base-args/parse-mode` already does this exactly: `(parse-mode raw :summary #{:summary :full})` collapses 13 LoC to 1.
- `parse-modes-arg` (tools.cljs:1526-1568) — 43 LoC hand-rolled per-slice mode parser that doesn't share slice-keyword coercion with `parse-frames-arg` or `parse-include-arg`.

Also tightly coupled:

- `->frame-keyword` (tools.cljs:1139-1149) and the inline frame-coercion in `parse-modes-arg`'s `coerce-k` (1545-1551) are the same logic — strip leading `:`, then `keyword`. Two copies.

## Proposed fix

1. `parse-mode-arg` → `(base-args/parse-mode raw :summary #{:summary :full})`
2. `parse-modes-arg` → use shared `coerce-slice-keyword` / `coerce-frame-keyword` helpers
3. `->frame-keyword` becomes the single source for both `parse-frames-arg` and `parse-modes-arg`

## Why

-15 LoC. The base-args helpers exist to enforce cross-MCP arg-parsing consistency (rf2-vw4sq). Local re-implementations defeat the purpose.

Surface: `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs` only.

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §T8 / T9 / T10.
close_reason: PR opened: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/910

title: refactor(ssr): JVM hash + CLJS hash parity test (the under-appreciated win)
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §A2 / strongest-opinion section.

The whole hydration-mismatch detection mechanism (Spec 011 §Hydration-mismatch detection) rests on one promise: **the JVM-side `render-tree-hash` and the CLJS-side `render-tree-hash` produce byte-identical output for byte-identical canonical-EDN input.**

The spec commits to this; the impl produces it through `canonical-edn` + `fnv-1a-32`. Two reader-conditional branches. **No test exists** that pins a byte literal on both sides.

Compare: `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/source_coord_parity_test.clj` pins a byte literal for the data-rf2-source-coord attribute; the companion `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/source_coord_parity_cljs_test.cljs` pins the same literal against the CLJS-side helper. **The literal IS the byte-comparison point.**

The hash deserves the same treatment.

## Why under-appreciated

- Today's `canonical-edn` doesn't prune nil (rf2-6djjl). The impl departs from the spec's traversal rule, silently.
- The fnv-1a-32 implementations LOOK identical across JVM and CLJS, but a subtle char-vs-byte path divergence (UTF-16 surrogate pairs, characters > 0xFFFF) wouldn't be caught by anything.
- Without a parity test, the spec's 'lock' claim is paper.

## Fix

1. `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/hash_parity_test.clj` — JVM test that asserts a literal hex hash for each fixture render-tree.
2. `implementation/ssr/test-cljs/re_frame/hash_parity_cljs_test.cljs` (or wherever CLJS tests land for ssr) — CLJS test that asserts the same literal hex.

Fixtures: spec's example tree, tree with nil values, tree with deeply-nested maps, tree with Unicode strings, tree with sequential vs vector mix.

## Acceptance

- Each fixture's expected hex appears as a literal in the test file.
- Both JVM and CLJS tests assert byte equality.
- A change to `canonical-edn` traversal or `fnv-1a-32` arithmetic that breaks one side fails its test.

## Risk

Low — additive test files. Will fail until rf2-6djjl (nil pruning) lands; that's coordination, not risk.
close_reason: PR #926: shared .cljc fixtures + JVM + CLJS tests pin a 20-fixture canonical-edn / render-tree-hash corpus byte-identical across runtimes. Includes empty containers, scalar leaves, hiccup trees of growing depth, namespaced-keyword attrs, multi-byte UTF-8 (Latin-1/Cyrillic/CJK), UTF-16 surrogate-pair codepoints (the strongest cross-runtime trap), set ordering, list-vs-vector branching, large-flat (FNV loop coverage). Plus 2 nil-prune equivalence pairs (pinning what ssr-hash-test only asserted structurally) and 1 key-order invariant pair. JVM: 82 tests, 267 assertions, 0 failures. CLJS: 1817 tests, 5050 assertions, 0 failures. Pattern mirrors rf2-xssfv #915.

title: refactor(ssr): split head.cljc + extract shared HTML escape helpers
description:
## Context

Parent audit: rf2-asmj1. Findings doc: §H1 / Q2.

Two related concerns:

1. **head.cljc is 406 LoC** — 1.6× the leaf-size ceiling (250L per rf2-zkca8). Three concerns: HTML helpers (~50 LoC), canonical-order emitter (~95 LoC), registry + render-head + active-head + per-frame snapshot + late-bind (~260 LoC).

2. **HTML escape helpers (`escape-html`, `escape-attr`, `attr-string`) are duplicated** between ssr.cljc:66-92 and head.cljc:58-86 — line-for-line. The self-containment was a hangover from when head shipped under a different artefact; under one artefact they're local-deps.

## Recommended split

- `ssr/html-helpers.cljc` — `escape-html`, `escape-attr`, `attr-string` (~30 LoC). Both ssr.cljc and head.cljc `:require` it.
- `ssr/head/emit.cljc` — `emit-title`, `emit-meta-tag`, `emit-link-tag`, `emit-script-tag`, `ld-json-string`, `emit-json-ld`, `head-model->html` (~120 LoC, after extracting helpers)
- `ssr/head/registry.cljc` — `reg-head`, `render-head`, `active-head`, `default-head`, `head-snapshots`, `on-frame-destroyed!`, late-bind hook registrations (~200 LoC)
- `head.cljc` — façade re-exporting the public surface, or just inline the small files into ssr/head/

## Acceptance

- Both ssr.cljc and head.cljc consume the shared helpers from one place.
- Entity-escape rules change once, not twice.
- Each leaf file ≤ 250 LoC.

## Risk

Low — pure rearrange. The shared helpers are private fns; their public-surface impact is zero.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/928. Split head.cljc (415 → 95 LoC façade) into 4 leaves: html-helpers (59 L, shared with emit.cljc), head/emit (132 L), head/registry (189 L), head (95 L façade). All leaves ≤ 250 LoC. emit.cljc now :requires html-helpers (entity-escape rules change in one place) + re-exports the aliased defs so existing emit/escape-html callsites keep resolving. Public surface unchanged. Tests: 82/82 JVM (267 assertions) + 1817/1817 CLJS (5050 assertions), 0 failures.

title: test(pair2-mcp): invoke orchestration test (precheck → dispatch → apply-cache → apply-cap)
description:
The `invoke` fn (tools.cljs:2683-2755) is the single egress for every tool, doing precheck → dispatch → apply-cache → apply-cap. Each stage is tested in isolation; the orchestration in `invoke` has no test.

## Coverage gaps

- Precheck short-circuits dispatch (`hit` is non-nil ⇒ tool eval skipped)
- Precheck miss feeds `precheck-hash` through to `apply-cache` so the next call can short-circuit via the precheck path
- Cache hit bypasses apply-cap budget walk (per the docstring at 2718-2721)
- `:isError true` results pass through cache untouched
- An overflow on an isError result still becomes overflow marker

## Proposed test

`invoke_test.cljs` with stub `dispatch-tool*` and stub `cache/precheck` + `apply-cache`. Verify ordering + short-circuit semantics.

## Why

P1 — the orchestration is the artefact's single most-traversed surface. Today coverage is bottom-up only.

Surface: new test file `tools/pair2-mcp/test/re_frame_pair2_mcp/invoke_test.cljs`.

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §TE7.
close_reason: PR #924 — test/pair2-mcp/test/re_frame_pair2_mcp/invoke_test.cljs covers all four phases of tools/invoke with 8 scenarios (precheck hit/miss, result-hash hit, isError bypass, cap-on-isError, cache-before-cap ordering, cache-disabled, unknown-tool). 297 tests / 719 assertions pass.

title: decision(schemas): validator-fn process-global vs per-frame — resolve spec/impl mismatch
description:
Spec 010 §Locked rules line 488: 'One validator fn per frame is in effect at any time. Last-write-wins on re-registration; tools warn if the source coords differ between registrations.'

But the impl (schemas.cljc:121-128) registers validator-fn / explainer-fn as **module-level defonce atoms** — one validator across all frames, process-global.

Additionally: 'tools warn if the source coords differ between registrations' is NOT implemented — set-schema-validator! resets the atom without recording source-coords.

Two paths:
(a) Change Spec 010 to say 'one validator fn per process' — the simpler reality. Drop the per-frame language and the source-coords-warn requirement.
(b) Move validator-fn / explainer-fn into per-frame storage parallel to schemas-by-frame; resolve per-frame at call time. Add source-coords recording on set-schema-validator!.

Option (a) is the easier-and-honest answer; (b) is more flexible but unmotivated by any current pair-tool need.

Mike decision required.

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (A2).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.
notes:
DECISION (Mike, 2026-05-14 ~10:02 AUSEST): **Option (a)** — process-global validator. Align spec to reality.

Action (filed as follow-on impl bead):
- Edit Spec 010 §Locked rules line 488: replace "One validator fn per frame is in effect at any time. Last-write-wins on re-registration; tools warn if source coords differ between registrations." with "One validator fn per process. Last-write-wins on re-registration."
- Drop any per-frame validator language elsewhere in 010 / Spec-Schemas.
- Drop the "tools warn if source coords differ" requirement entirely (no current consumer; reintroducible later with a proper migration story).
- No impl change required — `defonce validator-fn` at `schemas.cljc:121-128` is already correct.

Rationale: pair-tool ecosystem (causa, pair2-mcp, story-mcp) has no current per-frame-validator need; per-frame would create cross-frame test contamination; pre-alpha favours simpler reality.
close_reason: DECIDED Option (a) — process-global validator. Align Spec 010 §488 to reality. See notes.

title: refactor(pair2-mcp): unify tool-name registry (descriptors + dispatcher + cacheable)
description: Unified into one registry (rf2-47g8l). One ordered vector — registry/tools — binds {:name :handler :cacheable? :descriptor}. tool-descriptors, handler-for, cacheable? all derived from it. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/931. All 297/719 tests pass.

title: refactor(schemas): drop requiring-resolve fallback in default-malli-validate / default-malli-explain
description:
schemas.cljc:99-104 (validate) and :115-119 (explain) carry a JVM-only requiring-resolve fallback to Malli when the late-bind hook isn't installed:

```
(if-let [v (late-bind/get-fn :schemas/malli-validate)]
  (v schema value)
  #?(:clj  (try
             (if-let [v (requiring-resolve 'malli.core/validate)]
               (v schema value)
               true)
             (catch Throwable _ true))
     :cljs true))
```

The rationale (schemas.cljc:88-91) is 'JVM tests that have Malli on the classpath but don't :require [re-frame.schemas.malli] keep working'. But:

- The schemas artefact's own deps.edn declares metosin/malli as a hard dep; every JVM test transitively loads Malli at classpath build.
- re-frame.schemas.malli lives in the same artefact (schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/malli.cljc).
- A JVM test using schemas-with-Malli but NOT requiring the adapter ns is an asymmetric configuration with no spec rationale.

Recommend: delete the requiring-resolve branches. Either the user requires re-frame.schemas.malli (publishes the hook) or they don't (soft-pass). The JVM-vs-CLJS asymmetry at schemas.cljc:88-91 disappears.

-10 LoC; -1 cross-platform invariant divergence.

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (Q2).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.
close_reason: PR #930 opened: refactor(schemas): drop requiring-resolve fallback for malli. Validator.cljc now consults only the late-bind hook (no JVM-vs-CLJS asymmetry); soft-passes per Spec 010 when re-frame.schemas.malli adapter ns not loaded. JVM tests that depended on the fallback now require the adapter explicitly (mirroring CLJS test pattern). -10 LoC. All gates green: schemas 133 tests, core 456 tests, CLJS 1817 tests, 0 failures across all.

title: refactor(schemas): delete dead on-app-schema-registry-event! hook (17 LoC of no-op)
description:
schemas.cljc:1047-1063 registers an on-app-schema-registry-event! hook with the registrar's replacement-hook-chain. The body destructures args and binds them to underscores:

```
(defn- on-app-schema-registry-event!
  [{:keys [kind id was now]}]
  (when (= kind :app-schema)
    (let [_ was _ now])))   ;; <-- literal throwaway
```

17 lines of comments narrate why the hook fires; the body does nothing on purpose. The hook is registered via a defonce ^:private _hot-reload-hook side-effect.

Recommend: delete the fn AND the defonce install. If future work needs the hook back, file a separate bead — don't leave dead no-ops with elaborate prose.

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (Q9).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.
close_reason: Already done by rf2-0frdi (commit f3bc6b4f, 'fix(schemas): single source of truth for reg-app-schema'). That commit dropped the registrar/register! :app-schema write from storage.cljc and removed the now-redundant on-app-schema-registry-event! replacement-hook alongside its defonce installation. Verified by grep: 'on-app-schema-registry-event' has zero matches across implementation/. The only remaining schemas-side mention of replacement-hooks is an explanatory comment in storage.cljc:181-188 documenting WHY the schemas artefact no longer participates in the replacement-hook stream — exactly the audit's stated goal. No further work; the audit citation (refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md Q9) was resolved as a side effect of rf2-0frdi.

title: refactor(pair2-mcp): collapse 3 boolean-arg parsers + parse-cache-arg into one table
description:
There are 4 boolean-arg parsers in pair2-mcp, three of which already delegate to `base-args/parse-boolean`:

- `parse-dedup-arg` (tools.cljs:390-395, default true)
- `parse-elision-arg` (tools.cljs:508-513, default true)
- `include-sensitive?` (tools.cljs:598-603, default false — directly reads via `arg`)
- `parse-cache-arg` (cache.cljs:263-279) — **does NOT delegate**, hand-rolls a smaller boolean parser

## Inconsistencies

1. `parse-cache-arg` accepts `"true"/"false"`, `true/false`, `:true/:false` only. `base-args/parse-boolean` accepts a strict superset (`"1"/"0"/"yes"/"no"/"on"/"off"` plus case-insensitive). An agent passing `"yes"` to `:cache` gets default-false; passing `"yes"` to `:dedup` gets true.
2. cache.cljs doesn't currently depend on `re-frame.mcp-base` — fixing C1 is a deps.edn touch.

## Proposed shape

A single per-tool table:

```clojure
(def bool-args
  {:dedup    {:default true  :description "..."}
   :elision  {:default true  :description "..."}
   :cache    {:default false :description "..."}
   :include-sensitive? {:default false :description "..."}})

(defn parse-bool [args k]
  (base-args/parse-boolean (j/get args (name k))
                            (get-in bool-args [k :default])))
```

Each tool reads `(parse-bool args :dedup)` etc. Defaults all live in one table.

## Why

-25 LoC. Removes the cache.cljs inconsistency (C1). Surfaces the documented cross-MCP convention (every parser accepts the same boolean shapes) without four micro-wrappers.

Surface: `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/{tools,cache}.cljs`, `tools/pair2-mcp/deps.edn`.

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §C1 / T7.
close_reason: PR #935: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/935 — table-driven boolean parser unified across 4 MCP args. 292 tests pass.

title: refactor(schemas): factor shared run-validation primitive (collapse three duplicated validate-*! fns)
description:
Three of the four validate-*! fns are structurally byte-identical, differing only in 6 lines of tags-building:

- validate-event! (schemas.cljc:1189-1238)
- validate-sub-return! (schemas.cljc:1240-1290)
- validate-cofx! (schemas.cljc:1292-1340)

Each is 50-60 LoC. The structure is identical:

```
(if interop/debug-enabled?
  (if @validator-fn
    (if-let [schema (:spec <meta>)]
      (if (run-validator schema <value>)
        true
        (let [explanation ... sensitive? ... base-tags ... tags ...]
          (trace/emit-error! :rf.error/schema-validation-failure tags)
          false))
      true) true) true)
```

Recommend a shared run-validation primitive that takes a config map (:meta, :value, :where, :build-base-tags, :meta-sensitive?). Each fn becomes a ~10-line wrapper.

Net: -90 LoC, one shape for the hot path. The missing fx-args validator (rf2-xp2o3) drops in as another ~10-line wrapper rather than another 50-LoC clone.

Audit citations: ai/findings/refactor-audit-schemas-2026-05-14.md (Q5).

Linked from rf2-x8x4p.

Sequence: should land before rf2-dgug5 (file split) so the split lands the simpler shape.
close_reason:
Refactored: factored private `run-validation` primitive in implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc. Each of the four meta-bearing validate-*! fns (event / cofx / fx / sub-return) is now a ~20-line wrapper that supplies registration-meta, checked value, sensitivity predicate, base-tags shape, and any fx-specific post-redaction step. `validate-app-db!` stays a structurally-distinct sibling (doseq over N schemas, no :spec lookup, no true/false return) — divergence documented on the fn and in the ns-docstring.

Two named sensitivity preds (`sensitive-by-meta?` and `sensitive-by-meta-or-schema?`) replace inline lambdas in three of the four wrappers.

Net -22 LoC (193 insertions / 215 deletions). The four wrapper bodies drop ~44 LoC; the new primitive adds ~14 LoC of body. Future fifth meta-bearing validator drops in as a ~20-line wrapper rather than another 50-LoC clone.

Elision contract preserved: every call-site lives inside the wrapper's outermost (if interop/debug-enabled? ...) gate; Closure's reachability proof DCEs run-validation and every literal reason string under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false. The four reason-string sentinels in scripts/check-elision.cjs are preserved verbatim.

Tests: schemas JVM (133/379), core JVM (456/2439) — green. CLJS node-runtime tests have a pre-existing harness failure (counter-with-stories.stories-cljs-test) independent of this change.

PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/923

title: refactor(flows): consider splitting flows.cljc into topo/registry/façade per rf2-zkca8 ceiling
description:
Per audit rf2-o3hok finding A1. The flows surface is currently one file (367 LoC, 16757 bytes) — slightly over the rf2-zkca8 leaf-size ceiling (250 LoC / 16 KB).

Three natural seams:

- **flows/topo.cljc** — `prefix?`, `depends-on?`, `topo-sort` (~50 LoC pure-fn module, unit-testable in isolation)
- **flows/registry.cljc** — `flows` + `last-inputs` atoms, `validate-flow`, `reg-flow`, `clear-flow`, hot-reload hook (~180 LoC)
- **flows.cljc** (façade) — `evaluate-flow!`, `run-flows!`, fx hooks, late-bind publication (~140 LoC)

Borderline call: file is under 400 LoC and reads sequentially. Wins are (a) `topo-sort` unit-testable; (b) mutation concerns scoped; (c) file falls below ceiling.

Defer until rf2-xdej3 (topo-sort rewrite) and rf2-7csri (cycle-rollback fix) land — both touch the same code. After those, the split is cleaner.

LoC: net zero. Risk: medium (moderate restructure, but bounded — flows has no public-API surface to preserve beyond the late-bind hooks at file bottom).

Parent: rf2-o3hok (flows refactor audit).
close_reason:
Split landed in PR #925 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/925).

The original 431-LoC flows.cljc was over both the rf2-zkca8 250-LoC and 16-KB ceilings. Split along the three natural seams the file's own banner comments called out:

- re-frame.flows.topo     — 136 LoC, 6.2 KB. Pure Kahn's topological sort + cycle-path DFS.
- re-frame.flows.registry — 193 LoC, 8.8 KB. Per-frame flows + last-inputs atoms, validation, reg-flow / clear-flow, hot-reload hook, test-only resets.
- re-frame.flows (façade) — 198 LoC, 9.4 KB. evaluate-flow! / run-flows!, fx hooks, late-bind publication, public re-export surface.

Every external consumer keeps reaching every documented symbol at re-frame.flows/<name>: production code through the late-bind hooks (all still published from the façade), and cross-artefact tests (flows / core / epoch / ssr) that '(reset! flows/flows {})' or '(resolve 're-frame.flows/last-inputs)' touch the SAME atom value via the façade's '(def flows registry/flows)' / '(def last-inputs registry/last-inputs)' re-exports.

Test gates: flows JVM 28 tests / 115 assertions; core JVM 456/2439; epoch JVM 58/229; ssr JVM 78/241; late-bind drift 5/331; bundle isolation PASS (including flow-cycle / flow-missing-id / flow-bad-inputs sentinels still elide); production elision PASS; CLJS compile clean with zero new warnings. Pre-existing test:cljs failure in counter-with-stories.stories-cljs-test is unrelated — filed as rf2-j3lo8.

title: refactor(flows): wire conformance-corpus runner into flows artefact test suite
description:
Per audit rf2-o3hok finding TE7. Six conformance fixtures exist:
- spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-hot-reload-preserves-output.edn
- spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-lifecycle-emits-traces.edn
- spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-multi-input-topo.edn
- spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-noop-on-value-equal-input.edn
- spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-recompute-on-input-change.edn
- spec/conformance/fixtures/flow-toggle-via-fx.edn

Plus the planned flow-basic.edn (Spec 013:261) and flow-cycle.edn / flow-frame-scoped.edn (Spec 013:264-266).

The flows artefact's JVM test suite duplicates the shape in regular tests but doesn't run the fixtures themselves. Add a `re-frame.flows-conformance-test` ns that drives every `flow-*.edn` through the live runtime and `=`-checks against the recorded outcome.

title: refactor(flows): tighten validate-flow to check input/path well-formedness
description:
Per audit rf2-o3hok findings Q5/TE4 (flows.cljc:105-120).

`validate-flow` advertises `:inputs must be a vector of paths` but only checks `(vector? (:inputs flow))`. Gaps:

1. `:inputs [:foo :bar]` (vector of keywords, NOT vector-of-paths) passes; `prefix?` will then throw on `(count :foo)`.
2. `:inputs [[:foo] :bar]` (mixed) passes; one input is invalid.
3. `:path []` (empty) passes; `(prefix? [] anything)` returns true, making the flow a depends-on prerequisite of EVERY other flow.

Fix:
- Check `(every? vector? (:inputs flow))` (per-input shape).
- Check `(seq (:path flow))` (non-empty path).
- Optionally check inputs contain valid path elements (keywords / strings / numbers).

Decide alongside: empty `:inputs []` semantics (see sibling rf2-... for that — referenced as S2). Probably allow with documented one-shot semantics.

Add validation tests (TE4) covering each rejected case.

LoC: +5 impl, +25 tests. Risk: trivial.

Parent: rf2-o3hok (flows refactor audit).
notes: PR #932: refactor(flows): tighten validate-flow input/path well-formedness checks. Validations added: every? vector? + valid-path? on :inputs entries; seq + valid-path-element? on :path. Each rejection throws :rf.error/flow-bad-inputs or :rf.error/flow-bad-path with :bad-entries/:bad-elements ex-data. Tests cover each rejection plus positive scalar-element / empty-:inputs cases. Local tests: 36 tests, 137 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors.

title: refactor(flows): decide and align failed-flow contract (in-flight writes preserved or discarded)
description:
Per audit rf2-o3hok findings Q4/PF3/S3/TE5 (flows.cljc:246-326).

Today's behaviour: when a flow's `:output` fn throws, `evaluate-flow!` re-throws after emitting `:rf.flow/failed`. `run-flows!`'s `loop` never reaches the next iteration; `replace-container!` never fires; EARLIER flows' dirty writes accumulated in the loop are SILENTLY LOST.

But `evaluate-flow!`'s own docstring at flows.cljc:252-254 says: 'On the failure path the in-flight db is returned unchanged and dirty? is false so downstream flows still walk.' — this is FALSE. The function throws, doesn't return.

Decision required:
- (a) Fix the doc to match the code: 'exception propagates; in-flight writes are discarded for this drain.' (~-5 LoC docs, +0 code)
- (b) Fix the code to match the doc: catch, emit `:rf.flow/failed`, return `[db false]`, let the loop continue; the router still sees no cascade halt; per-flow failures are isolated. (~+5 LoC)

Spec 013:188 says the exception is re-thrown so the router emits `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` — but says nothing about earlier-flows' writes. Spec amendment needed either way.

I lean (b): one bad flow shouldn't lose other flows' work in the same drain. Per-flow isolation is the better contract.

Also add a regression test (TE5) pinning the contract once decided.

Parent: rf2-o3hok (flows refactor audit).
close_reason: Landed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1044 (commit 9d10252f). Decision under pre-alpha authority: hybrid contract — preserve prior writes AND halt cascade (strongest no-silent-loss guarantee compatible with cascade-level error surfacing). Implementation in commit 48c710a5 (rf2-wyt97); this commit adds the supplementary last-inputs bookkeeping deftests + Spec 009/013 cross-references. See PR body for full rationale.
