title: test(machines): loosen shape-pinning assertions and wire conformance corpus into artefact CI
description:
Per findings rf2-ra1he §TE1 / §TE5: two test-coverage issues to fix together.

## (1) Shape-pinning relaxation (rf2-ra1he §TE1)

`machine_transition_purity_test.clj:62-75` asserts the entire spawn-fx map by literal `=`:

```clojure
(is (= [[:rf.machine/spawn {:machine-id :http/post
                            :id-prefix :http/post
                            :data {:url "/api/login"}
                            :start [:begin]
                            :rf/spawned-id :http/post#1
                            :rf/parent-id :rf/transition-pure
                            :rf/invoke-id [:authenticating]}]]
       fx1))
```

The contract that should be pinned:
- `:rf/spawned-id` is `:http/post#1` (allocator deterministic)
- `:rf/parent-id` is `:rf/transition-pure` (sentinel for pure-call surface)
- `:rf/invoke-id` is the state-path (`[:authenticating]`)

The implementation detail pinned:
- exact key-set on the spawn-args map (currently 8 keys)
- the presence of `:id-prefix` (could be derived from `:machine-id`)

Refactors that touch spawn-args shape (e.g., rf2-peox8 unifying `:invoke` and `:invoke-all`) churn this test for no contract reason. **Recommend** rewrite the asserts as per-key:

```clojure
(let [[[fx-id args]] fx1]
  (is (= :rf.machine/spawn fx-id))
  (is (= :http/post#1 (:rf/spawned-id args)))
  (is (= :rf/transition-pure (:rf/parent-id args)))
  (is (= [:authenticating] (:rf/invoke-id args))))
```

Audit other tests for similar map-equality pinning (likely candidates: invoke_all_test, spawn_registry_test, after_test).

## (2) Conformance corpus runner in machines artefact (rf2-ra1he §TE5)

`spec/conformance/fixtures/machines-*.edn` and `spec/conformance/fixtures/parallel-*.edn` exist as the normative behaviour corpus, runnable per Spec 005. The machines test suite covers the impl extensively but DOESN'T drive the EDN fixtures.

Need to verify: does any artefact run these fixtures today? If not (likely), wire a `machines.conformance-test` ns that reads each fixture, drives it through `machine-transition`, and `=`-checks against the recorded outcome. This is the canonical contract surface and should be a gate.

## Acceptance

- (1) Shape-pinning audit complete; per-key asserts in machine_transition_purity_test + any others surfaced.
- (2) `re-frame.machines.conformance-test` runs every `machines-*.edn` and `parallel-*.edn` fixture.
- (2) `npm run test:cljs` includes the new runner.

## Risk

Low. The corpus is authoritative; if a fixture fails, it likely surfaces a real impl bug (good — pre-alpha).

## Sequencing

Best sequenced BEFORE the major refactors (rf2-aa2rw / lha2t / 8sz7f / 2zzyg / peox8) so the corpus is the gate they pass against.

description:

## Reserved snapshot-internal :rf/* keys

These keys appear in snapshots that pass through user code (Causa renders them, tests inspect them, the conformance corpus pins them) but Spec 005 §Snapshot shape (line 37-64) describes only `:state`, `:data`, `:tags`, `:meta`:

- `:rf/spawn-counter` — per-machine-id integer map; rf2-gr8q
- `:rf/finished?` — final-state marker (transient, lifecycle-handler-only); rf2-gn80
- `:rf/bootstrap-pending?` — initial-entry cascade flag; rf2-0z73
- `:rf/after-epoch` — per-machine :after timer epoch; rf2-3y3y
- `:rf/after-epoch-by-region` — per-region :after epoch for parallel machines; rf2-l67o
- (Plus runtime-stamped on machine spec, not snapshot, but related: `:rf/frame`, `:rf/platform`, `:rf/parent-id`, `:rf/region`)

Spec 005 should add a §Reserved snapshot-internal keys subsection documenting each, with read/write rules and visibility (the `:rf/finished?` slot is deliberately NOT set by pure transition — see code at transition.cljc:912-921; that invariant should be spec'd).

## 3-arity dispatch rule

Spec 005 §3-arity escape hatch (~line 421) says guards/actions admit 2-arity OR 3-arity opt-in. It does NOT say HOW the runtime decides. Currently the rule lives in code (`declares-3-arity?`, transition.cljc:75-116) — Java reflection on JVM, `cljs$lang$maxFixedArity` on CLJS, variadics route through 2-arity.

Spec 005 should state the rule explicitly. If rf2-2yupx lands (replace reflection with metadata), the rule simplifies to 'opt-in via `^::rf.machine/wants-ctx` metadata' — much easier to spec and reason about.

## Other minor spec gaps surfaced by the audit (P2)

- `intercept-invoke-all-event` pure-call no-op (§S2)
- Lazy `synthesise-initial-snapshot` timing (§S3)
- `:rf.machine/spawned` synthetic event (§S4)
- `:rf.machine.timer/after-elapsed` carrier-event format (§S5)

Bundle into a single spec PR with the P1 items above for review density.

## Risk

Zero — pure spec amendments. Pre-alpha latitude applies.

## Acceptance

- New §Reserved snapshot-internal keys subsection lands in spec/005-StateMachines.md.
- 3-arity dispatch rule explicit (whichever wins per rf2-2yupx).
- Cross-references from Conventions.md §reserved namespaces to the new section.

Plus a sibling note on the four runtime-stamped machine-spec keys (:rf/frame, :rf/platform, :rf/parent-id, :rf/region) — not snapshot-internal but related. 3-arity dispatch rule finalised in 005 as a new normative #### Dispatch rule subsection naming the (:rf.machine/wants-ctx (meta f)) metadata check as the one-line contract; ctx projection pinned as the closed {:state :meta} pair; four named consequences (explicit intent, no platform reflection, variadic safety, chase-ref preservation). Cross-reference added from 005 §Snapshot shape to the new Conventions catalogue. Tests pass (npm test:cljs 1792/4975 0F, machines clojure -M:test 123/352 0F). No mkdocs warnings on changed files.

title: refactor(machines.timer): frame-scope the after-timers atom (last remaining process-global)
description:
Per findings rf2-ra1he §TM4: `re-frame.machines.timer/after-timers` (timer.cljc:38-52) is the LAST remaining piece of module-level mutable state in the machines artefact after rf2-gr8q. Two consequences:

1. **Frame isolation broken.** Two test frames running in parallel race against the same atom. The keying `[frame-id parent-id invoke-id delay-key]` partitions correctly, BUT `reset-timers!` (machines.cljc:141-154) is process-global, not frame-scoped.

2. **`after-cancel-fx` does a linear scan** (timer.cljc:283-287) over the entire atom on every state-exit-with-:after, including all OTHER frames' timers. Performance bug at scale.

## Proposed structure

Move the timer table inside the frame metadata, analogous to how `:rf/spawn-counter` was moved per rf2-gr8q. Either:

- Add a `:rf.machine/after-timers` slot to `frame/frame-meta` (an atom per frame, keyed by `[parent-id invoke-id delay-key]`).
- Or thread the table through cofx into the timer fxs.

Option 1 preserves the current 'fire-and-forget' fx semantics (the fx handler doesn't need to read back the table from a cofx). Option 2 makes the table a value rather than a singleton — testability win, more invasive.

## Acceptance

- `reset-timers!` becomes frame-scoped (with a process-global variant for tests).
- Two test fixtures running parallel in different frames don't see each other's timers.
- `after-cancel-fx` no longer scans across frames.
- All after_test / final_state tests green.

## Risk

Medium. The fix surface touches the host-clock handle lifecycle. The trace-events emitted by `schedule-after-timer!` and `on-sub-changed!` reference the timer state — must preserve.

## Sequencing

Standalone. Lower priority than rf2-3sbb6/aa2rw/lha2t (the P0 trio) but matters for the rf2-gr8q purity promise.
close_reason: Frame-scoped the after-timers atom — outer key is now frame-id, inner table is keyed by [parent-id invoke-id-vec delay-key]. Added 1-arity reset-timers! / cancel-all-timers! and wired :machines/on-frame-destroyed! late-bind hook into frame/destroy-frame!. after-cancel-fx now scans only the active frame's entries (O(timers-this-frame), no more cross-frame linear scan). Regression test exercises two frames with overlapping timer ids stay isolated, plus the 1-arity reset + destroy-frame cleanup paths. All gates green: machines (123/352), http (134/369), core (440/2312), drift test. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/872

title: refactor(machines): replace declares-3-arity? reflection with explicit ::wants-ctx opt-in metadata
description:
Per findings rf2-ra1he §T3 / §P3 / §P4 / §S1: `declares-3-arity?` (transition.cljc:75-116) introspects each guard / action fn on every invocation to decide whether to pass the optional ctx map. JVM walks Java reflection (`getDeclaredMethods`); CLJS reads `cljs` + `unchecked-get`.

Cost: ~80-200ns per fn per invocation on JVM. With 10 guards/actions × 1000 transitions/sec = 1-2ms/sec of pure introspection. Not catastrophic, but pure overhead for the 99%-case 2-arity user.

Cost: complexity. The fn is ~40 LoC of subtle dispatch (regular fn vs variadic vs multi-arity fn vs RestFn), with a recently-fixed CLJS bug (rf2-l04j) showing the dispatch is fragile.

## Proposed surface

Explicit opt-in via metadata:

```clojure
;; user-side
(defn my-guard
  {::rf.machine/wants-ctx true}
  [data event ctx]
  (... use :state, :meta ...))

;; OR via a helper wrapper:
(rf.machines/guard-with-ctx (fn [data event ctx] ...))
```

Engine becomes:

```clojure
(defn- wants-ctx? [f] (-> f meta ::wants-ctx))

(defn- call-guard [g snap event]
  (if (wants-ctx? g)
    (g (:data snap) event {:state (:state snap) :meta (:meta snap)})
    (g (:data snap) event)))
```

## Migration

Single `grep`-able pattern. The 3-arity opt-in is uncommon (Spec 005 §3-arity escape hatch describes it as 'opt-in introspection'). Existing 3-arity users adopt the metadata; the engine errors clearly if a 3-fixed-arity fn lacks the metadata ('did you mean to opt in via ^::rf.machine/wants-ctx?').

## Alternative

If we want to keep the auto-detection, memoise the dispatch per-fn (WeakHashMap on JVM, simple atom-cache on CLJS). Eliminates the per-call cost. Lower migration cost, higher residual complexity. Estimate ~10 LoC.

## Risk

Low — both alternatives are isolated to `call-guard` / `call-action`. Tests: three_arity_guards_cljs_test pins the dispatch.

## Spec amendment

Spec 005 §3-arity escape hatch (~line 421) needs to describe whichever rule wins. Currently the spec is silent on HOW dispatch decides — code-comment-only (T3 in audit).

## Sequencing

Standalone; no dependencies on other refactors.
notes: Replaced declares-3-arity? reflection with explicit :rf.machine/wants-ctx metadata opt-in. wants-ctx? is now a one-line meta lookup. Public wants-ctx helper added to re-frame.machines. Spec 005 §3-arity escape hatch updated. No production callers needed migration. Tests: 119 JVM + 1792 CLJS, all green. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/867
close_reason: completed

title: refactor(machines): decompose create-machine-handler returned-fn into 4-step pipeline
description:
Per findings rf2-ra1he §L5 / §A6: `create-machine-handler`'s returned fn (lifecycle_fx.cljc:771-934, 165 LoC) is the 'event arrives → drive a machine' boundary — the most-executed path in the whole artefact. It is a single wall of let-bindings + cond branches that conceptually does four things:

1. **Prepare machine context** (lines 772-794): stamp frame-id / platform / parent-id, look up existing snapshot, decide `needs-bootstrap?`.
2. **Boot-if-pending** (lines 836-851): if bootstrap-pending, run initial-entry cascade; project boot-failure or extract `post-boot-snap`.
3. **Step** (lines 878-902): call `parallel/machine-transition`; project action-failure.
4. **Commit-or-finalize** (lines 904-933): build new-db, emit traces, route to `finalize-machine` if `finished?`.

Plus the cross-cutting branch: `intercept-invoke-all-event` short-circuits the pipeline (line 835, 853).

## Proposed structure

```clojure
(defn- prepare-machine-ctx [db frame event machine] ...)
(defn- maybe-boot [machine ctx] ...)             ;; → Result {:snap :fx}
(defn- run-step [machine ctx boot-result inner-event] ...) ;; → Result {:next-snap :fx :finished?}
(defn- commit [machine ctx step-result inner-event] ...)   ;; → {:db :fx}

(defn create-machine-handler [machine]
  (validate-machine! machine)
  (let [base-initial (delay (synthesise-initial-snapshot machine))]
    (fn [{:keys [db frame]} event]
      (let [ctx          (prepare-machine-ctx db frame event machine base-initial)
            intercepted  (intercept-invoke-all-event ...)]
        (if intercepted
          intercepted
          (-> (maybe-boot machine ctx)
              (result/and-then (run-step machine ctx ...))
              (commit machine ctx ...)))))))
```

## Wins

- Each step ≤ 30 LoC, named, individually testable.
- Spec 005 §Drain semantics §Level 3 reads onto the pipeline directly.
- The intercept short-circuit becomes a single visible branch.

## Risk

Medium. Hot path; lots of trace-emit sequencing (`:rf.machine/event-received` → boot fx → `:rf.machine/transition` → optional `:rf.machine/snapshot-updated` → finalize). Must preserve trace ordering. Tests: every machines test file exercises this; `machine_transition_trigger_handler_test` specifically pins trace shape.

## Sequencing

After rf2-aa2rw (Result ADT) — the failure-projection branches collapse cleanly with the type.
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/870 — 4-step pipeline (prepare-machine-ctx / maybe-boot / run-step / commit-or-finalize). Each step <=30 LoC. Trace ordering preserved. clojure -M:test (machines): 338/338. npm test:cljs: 4975/4975.

title: refactor(machines): decompose apply-transition-once into named cascade phases
description:
Per findings rf2-ra1he §T6: `apply-transition-once` (transition.cljc:783-921, 139 LoC) is the engine's heart and the most-executed code path in the machines artefact. It deserves to read as cleanly as Spec 005 §Entry/exit cascading along the LCA describes.

## Specific friction

1. `exit-refs` / `entry-refs` / `action-refs` / `all-refs` build the cascade ordering with `concat` (transition.cljc:818-828). Reading the let-bindings you have to reconstruct the spec's 'exit shallowest-first … action at LCA … entry shallowest-first' rule from the local code.

2. `nodes-along-path` is called twice for src-path (transition.cljc:819, 843) and twice for target-leaf (transition.cljc:824, 847). Same path-walk runs twice; only the projection differs. Compute once.

3. `new-state` is a 4-branch `cond` (transition.cljc:861-867) that mostly maps onto `denormalise-state` but with bespoke logic. Read once to understand.

4. `snap-final` is a 3-branch `cond` (transition.cljc:868-880) interleaved with the epoch-bump logic.

5. The spawn-reducer at the tail (transition.cljc:885-900) is logically a separate phase but shares the `let` scope.

## Proposed structure

```clojure
(defn- compute-cascade-paths [machine src-path target-leaf internal?]
  ;; → {:exited-pairs :entered-pairs :lca-len :action-refs :all-refs :epoch-bumps?}
  )

(defn- run-cascade [machine snap event cascade]
  ;; → Result with snap-after + fx (action-failure propagates)
  )

(defn- commit-snapshot [snap-after machine cascade target-leaf orig-state internal?]
  ;; → snap-final with new :state, epoch bump if needed
  )

(defn- run-spawn-reducer [machine snap-final entered-pairs parent-id event acc-fx]
  ;; → Result with snap-after-spawns + spawn-fx
  )

(defn apply-transition-once [machine snapshot event transition]
  (let [cascade (compute-cascade-paths machine ...)
        r1 (run-cascade machine snapshot event cascade)]
    (result/map-ok r1
      (fn [snap-after fx]
        (let [snap-final  (commit-snapshot ...)
              after-fx    (build-after-fx ...)
              cancel-fx   (build-after-cancel-fx ...)
              destroy-fx  (build-destroy-fx ...)
              r2          (run-spawn-reducer ...)]
          (result/map-ok r2 (fn [snap'' spawn-fx] (ok snap'' (concat fx cancel-fx destroy-fx spawn-fx after-fx)))))))))
```

Hot-path nominally unchanged (helper inlining is at the JIT's discretion).

## Estimate

~20 LoC net (the LoC stays similar; the readability gain comes from phase separation).

## Risk

Medium-high. This is THE engine fn. Test corpus is comprehensive (machine_transition_purity_test, three_arity_guards, parallel_test, tags_test, final_state_cljs_test, after_test, invoke_*) but refactoring sequence-sensitive code carries inherent risk. Land after rf2-aa2rw (Result ADT) — the failure-propagation is cleaner with the type.

## Acceptance

- Each phase fn ≤ 30 LoC.
- `apply-transition-once` body fits ≤ 40 LoC.
- All machines tests green.
- Conformance corpus passes.
- No performance regression on the perf-budget micro-bench (file separately if missing — rf2-XXXX).

## Sequencing

After rf2-aa2rw (Result ADT) lands.
notes: Landed as PR #863. apply-transition-once decomposed into compute-cascade-paths → run-cascade → commit-snapshot → run-spawn-phase. Body dropped from 139 LoC to ~25 LoC of phase composition. Eliminated the duplicate nodes-along-path walk (audit §T6 #2 side win). All 119 JVM machine tests + 1795 CLJS tests green.

title: refactor(machines): unify handle-invoke-spawn and handle-invoke-all-spawn over a shared spawn-one primitive
description:
Per findings rf2-ra1he §T7 / §A3: `handle-invoke-spawn` (transition.cljc:606-664, 59 LoC) and `handle-invoke-all-spawn` (transition.cljc:666-758, 93 LoC) are near-identical:

Both: allocate spawned-id from in-snapshot counter, materialise `:data` fn-form, run `:on-spawn` advisory callback, build a spawn-args map, emit `:rf.machine/spawn` fx.

The differences are bracket-level:
- `:invoke-all` allocates N children up-front (loop) vs single allocation
- `:invoke-all` emits one `:rf.machine/invoke-all-init` fx ahead of the per-child spawns
- per-child spawn-args has different keys (`:rf/invoke-all-id` + `:rf/invoke-all-child-id` instead of `:rf/invoke-id`)

Per Spec 005 §Spawn-and-join via :invoke-all (line 1404+): ':invoke-all' IS 'spawn-and-join sugar over N parallel :invoke's plus a join condition'. The impl should reflect the conceptual relationship.

## Proposed structure

```clojure
(defn- spawn-one
  "Single-spawn primitive used by both :invoke and :invoke-all per-child.
   Allocates spawn-id, materialises :data fn-form, runs :on-spawn, returns
   [snap' spawn-fx | :fail info]."
  [machine snap event spawn-config]
  ...)

(defn- handle-invoke-spawn [machine parent-id s acc-fx prefix n event]
  (let [config (build-invoke-config inv prefix parent-id)
        result (spawn-one machine s event config)]
    (case-result ...)))

(defn- handle-invoke-all-spawn [machine parent-id s acc-fx prefix n event]
  (let [inv-all   (:invoke-all n)
        configs   (build-invoke-all-configs inv-all prefix parent-id)
        init-fx   [:rf.machine/invoke-all-init {:join-state ...}]
        ...]
    (reduce-children spawn-one machine s event configs acc-fx)))
```

Per-child spawn-args differs are encoded in `build-invoke-config` vs `build-invoke-all-configs` — pure data assembly.

## Estimate

~60 LoC reduction. The conceptual win is bigger: a Spec 005 reader looking for 'how does :invoke-all relate to :invoke' will see the answer in code.

## Risk

Medium. The spawn / on-spawn / :data-materialise reducer in `apply-transition-once` is in the hot path. Sequencing matters — per-child :on-spawn currently sees per-child :data writes (transition.cljc:744-756 thread snap through children). Must preserve. The action-failure short-circuit (`reduced` form, transition.cljc:633-636) must propagate identically.

Tests: invoke_data_fn_form_test, invoke_all_test, machine_transition_purity_test, spawn_registry_test.

## Sequencing

Best sequenced AFTER rf2-aa2rw (Result ADT) — the action-failure propagation gets much cleaner with the Result type, and this refactor benefits.
close_reason: Closed via PR #860. spawn-one primitive extracted; both handlers now compose allocate-one + spawn-one + apply-on-spawn. Tests green: clojure -M:test (119/332), npm run test:cljs (1795/4975), test:elision pass.

title: refactor(machines): walk-path-leaf-to-root abstraction unifying 4 deepest-wins pickers
description:
Per findings rf2-ra1he §T5 / 'strongest design-taste opinion': the same `loop [i (dec (count path))] ... (recur (dec i))` walk-leaf-to-root-for-first-match shape appears at four call-sites spanning three files. The shape is the runtime's deepest-wins resolution rule (Spec 005 §Transition resolution, line 912) — implemented four times.

## Duplicated walks

1. `transition.cljc:342-387` — `pick-after-transition` (matches `:after` table containing a delay-key)
2. `transition.cljc:396-416` — `pick-transition` (matches `:on` event-id or `:*`)
3. `transition.cljc:923-943` — `pick-always-transition` (matches `:always` whose guard passes)
4. `lifecycle_fx.cljc:60-78` — `find-active-invoke-all-in-tree` (matches `:invoke-all` whose :on-child-done/:on-child-error == inner-id)

Bonus 5th: `lifecycle_fx.cljc:591-606` `find-invoke-spec-at` (root-to-leaf — inverse direction, but same primitive with a direction flag).

## Proposed surface

```clojure
(defn walk-path-leaf-to-root
  "Per Spec 005 §Transition resolution (deepest-wins). Walk path
   leaf→root through machine.:states. For each [prefix node] pair
   (deepest first), call (predicate prefix node) — return the FIRST
   non-nil result, or nil if no match. Predicate's return value is
   the caller's hit shape."
  [machine path predicate]
  ...)
```

Each picker shrinks to ~5-10 LoC.

## Wins beyond LoC

- Names the spec's 'deepest-wins' rule in code.
- Paves the way for a future `pick-trace` instrumentation hook (Causa wants 'the runtime checked these states in this order').
- Disappears the `(dec i)` off-by-one bug class.
- New pickers (e.g., per-state `:on-error` handlers, if ever added) inherit the rule for free.

## Risk

Low. Pure refactor over well-tested code paths (pick-transition is the engine's primary picker; all four are exercised by the conformance corpus and the JVM test suite).

## Acceptance

- All four pickers re-expressed via the helper.
- The helper lives in `re-frame.machines.transition` (or a tiny `re-frame.machines.path` ns if folks prefer a separate concerns home).
- Test corpus green.
close_reason: Landed via PR #854. New re-frame.machines.path-walk namespace names Spec 005's deepest-wins resolution rule once; the 4 deepest-wins pickers (pick-after-transition, pick-transition, pick-always-transition, find-active-invoke-all-in-tree) migrated to (path-walk/walk-path-leaf-to-root tree path predicate). Net delta excluding the new ns's docstring: ~-30 LoC. Tests: clojure -M:test (machines) 119/332/0/0; npm run test:cljs 1795/4975/0/0. find-invoke-spec-at intentionally left alone — it isn't a deepest-wins walk (descends to a known absolute path); rationale captured in path-walk namespace docstring.

title: P1 audit: state-machine code review — refactor opportunities for elegance/clarity/performance
description:
Mike's framing 2026-05-14 ~01:35 AUSEST: P1 — do a careful review of the state-machine code considering any refactoring that would make the code better (more elegant, more understandable, more best-practice, more efficient).

## Surfaces to review

The state-machine implementation lives across these locations:

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc` — public façade (post-rf2-5hnn split, zero emits)
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` — core transition algorithm
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx.cljc` — `:spawn`, `:destroy`, `:invoke`, `:invoke-all` fxs
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc` — `:after` wall-clock timers
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/parallel.cljc` — parallel-regions algorithm

Plus the spec:
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (~2900 lines)
- `spec/CP-5-MachineGuide.md` (deeper companion)

And tests:
- `implementation/machines/test/re_frame/machines_*_test.{cljc,cljs}` — the suite

## What the audit should produce

A findings doc at `ai/findings/machines-refactor-audit-2026-05-14.md` covering:

1. **Code-quality survey per src file** — for each of the 5 main source files, list 3-7 specific issues worth fixing:
   - Naming inconsistencies (e.g., the `reset-counters!` → `reset-timers!` rename just shipped via rf2-p8usn — what other stale names are there?)
   - Repeated patterns that could be factored to helpers
   - Multi-arity fns that could collapse
   - Comments that narrate history rather than explaining current design
   - Dead branches or v1-back-compat shims
   - Algorithm clarity (is the parallel-regions algo as clean as it could be?)
   - Variable-naming opportunities (`m` vs `machine`, `t` vs `transition`, etc — when does the short form actually hurt readability?)

2. **Architectural concerns** — anything that suggests a deeper refactor:
   - Is the public-façade / per-file split (rf2-5hnn) actually paying off, or is it ceremony?
   - Are the lifecycle-fxs idiomatically `reg-fx` or do they bend the contract?
   - Could the spec-as-data table-transition shape be simpler?
   - Is the `:invoke` vs `:invoke-all` distinction sharp enough?

3. **Performance** — any hot-path concerns:
   - Allocation patterns in `transition.cljc`'s hot loop
   - Repeated registry lookups
   - Reflection warnings (CLJ) or warn-on-infer hits (CLJS)

4. **Spec-vs-impl alignment** — does spec/005's recommended shape match what the impl actually does?

5. **Test coverage** — is the suite catching everything it should, or are there shape-of-the-thing tests that pin implementation details rather than contract?

## Output

- Findings doc with prioritised list of refactor opportunities (P0 must-fix / P1 should-fix / P2 polish)
- Each opportunity has a concrete recommended change + estimated LoC + risk note
- For each P0/P1 item, file a follow-on bead via `bd create` (priority matching the audit's assessment)
- DO NOT MAKE SOURCE CHANGES IN THIS BEAD — findings only

## Time-box

120 minutes. State-machine impl is ~2-3k LoC across 5 files; thorough review takes time. Quality of findings > quantity.

## Coordination

- READ-ONLY. No source edits.
- Disjoint from current in-flight surfaces.
- Don't fix anything; just identify.

## Pre-alpha

The state-machine code is one of re-frame2's headline features (XState-class capability, deep framework integration). It deserves masterpiece-grade review now while we can still refactor freely. Elegance/correctness/clarity over backwards-compat.

title: Examples (causa.spec) step 5: trace panel row count does not grow after dispatch — rf2-iw5ym regression
description:
On current main, examples/reagent/counter/causa.spec.cjs fails at line 153 — 'Trace panel row count did not grow after dispatch (before=0, after=0)'. Surfaced AFTER rf2-iw5ym (commit 769ba9d4) landed.

## Root cause

rf2-iw5ym moved `:rf.causa/trace-buffer` sub from thunking `(trace-bus/buffer)` (atom) to reading `(get db :trace-buffer [])`. Sub now requires the trace-buffer to be in app-db.

trace-bus/collect-trace! dispatches `:rf.causa/note-trace-event` to `:rf/causa` to mirror the buffer into app-db. But:

- The dispatch is guarded on `(frame/frame :rf/causa)` existing.
- re-frame2 doesn't auto-create frames on dispatch.
- The preload can't `(rf/reg-frame :rf/causa {})` because reg-frame requires a substrate adapter installed via rf/init!, and the preload runs at ns-load time BEFORE that.
- So in production, `:rf/causa` is NEVER registered, the dispatch is silently skipped, and `db.:trace-buffer` is always empty.

The trace panel reads via `:rf.causa/trace-feed` -> `:rf.causa/trace-buffer` sub, both of which fall through to `:rf/default` for plain-fn shell views. Sub returns [], panel renders no rows.

## Constraints

- The Causa shell currently uses plain Reagent fns for all panel views. Their `(rf/subscribe ...)` calls fall through to `:rf/default` (the framework emits `:rf.warning/plain-fn-under-non-default-frame-once` confirming this).
- Even if `:rf/causa` is registered (e.g. lazily at mount time), the plain-fn sub still reads from `:rf/default`.

## Possible fixes (need design decision)

1. **Revert iw5ym sub change**: thunk the atom again. Requires also reverting 5 tests in registry_cljs_test.cljs (sub-trace-buffer-reads-app-db, sub-trace-buffer-evicts-on-overflow-via-event, sub-trace-buffer-survives-hot-reload, sub-trace-buffer-restarts-from-clean-state, event-sync-trace-buffer-replaces-slot) + 14 helpers across panel view tests. Locally invasive — undoes most of iw5ym's surface.

2. **Register `:rf/causa` at mount time + reg-view-register shell views**: Causa shell panels become reg-view-wrapped so their subscribes carry the `:rf/causa` frame via React context. Aligns with the framework's plain-fn warning intent. Wider refactor — touches every shell panel.

3. **Make the trace-buffer sub read from a fixed-frame app-db**: `(get (frame/frame-app-db-value :rf/causa) :trace-buffer [])`. Requires `:rf/causa` registered AND a custom signal source (re-frame's reactive layer tracks the subscriber's frame, not arbitrary frames). Probably requires registering `:rf/causa` AND a sub graph hack — complex.

Same regression hits `:rf.causa/suppressed-sensitive-count` (rf2-0vxdn — same recipe); rf2-higwg patched `config/note-suppressed!` to drop the `:rf/causa` binding so the redacted-indicator works without registering the frame, but the trace-buffer path needs more design thought.

## Suggested next steps

1. Lock the architecture decision (which option above).
2. If Option 2, write a new bead for reg-view-wrapping each Causa panel.
3. If Option 3, write a new bead for the fixed-frame sub mechanism.

Source: rf2-higwg PR investigation, 2026-05-13.

title: SSR: spec the parallel-loader pattern — async data fetch fan-out during drain
description:
Per ssr-audit-20260513-1757 findings (rf2-ul137) gap #3. Spec 011's drain model is sequential: :on-create event → :fx dispatched in source order → drain to fixed point → render. The Next.js / Remix model — multiple loaders fan out in parallel, framework awaits all, then renders — has no specced equivalent. :rf.http/managed on JVM (Spec 014, java.net.http.HttpClient transport) blocks the drain thread per HTTP call.

An article-page that wants Promise.all([getArticle, getComments, getRelated]) translates to 3 sequential dispatches in re-frame2 today, multiplying latency by N.

## The primitives exist
- :invoke-all (spawn-and-join machine pattern, Spec 005 §:invoke-all + §invoke-all-join-all-completes / invoke-all-join-any-fails-cancels fixtures) does parallel-await.
- The drain settles when all spawned actors complete.
- :rf.http/managed can be invoked from spawned actors.

What's missing is the DOC that says: 'this is the canonical SSR parallel-loader pattern; here's how to spawn fetch-actors from :on-create and join their results.'

## Recommendation
File: spec/Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md (new pattern doc — same convention as Pattern-RemoteData.md / Pattern-Forms.md).

Content:
- 'The SSR drain runs to fixed point; sequential awaits inside it serialise. For parallel fetches, spawn-and-join via :invoke-all.'
- Worked example showing :rf/server-init that spawns 3 fetch actors and joins on settle.
- Cross-ref to Spec 005 §:invoke-all and Spec 014 §:rf.http/managed.
- Cross-ref from Spec 011 §80–141 (server flow).

## Effort
- 1 new Pattern doc (~200 lines).
- 1 new conformance fixture: parallel-loader-ssr.edn (3 spawned :rf.http/managed-canned-success actors join → app-db carries all three results → render).
- 1 worked example: examples/reagent/ssr-parallel-loader/.

## Surfaces touched
- spec/Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md (new file)
- spec/011-SSR.md §Server flow (cross-ref insertion)
- spec/conformance/fixtures/parallel-loader-ssr.edn (new)
- examples/reagent/ssr-parallel-loader/ (new)

## Acceptance
- Pattern doc covers the fan-out shape end-to-end.
- Fixture demonstrates 3 parallel :rf.http/managed dispatches resolving in parallel under SSR.
- Worked example shows the per-route loader idiom.
notes: PR #665 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/665. Pattern doc 'Pattern-SSR-Loaders.md' (237 lines) + index entry in spec/README.md. check_doc_slugs.py exits 0. Bead remains OPEN pending merge.

All example specs (counter-uix, login-uix, counter-helix, login-helix) pass — no observable symptom suggests latent bug.

2. Read implementation/adapters/helix/src/.../render fn — same for Spec 006 §895
3. If both confirm: close this bead with no PR + a note saying audit passed
4. If either diverges from spec: file a focused fix bead with the specific divergence

Per Spec 006 §UIx line 876 ('render wraps react-dom/client.createRoot + root.render') and §Helix line 900 (same): both adapters already use the canonical create-root path that rf2-fn5rk retrofitted into Reagent. title: SSR: implement :rf.server/request cofx — spec contract present, impl absent
description:
Per ssr-audit-20260513-1757 findings (rf2-ul137) gap #2. Spec 011 §311–323 documents the :rf.server/request cofx:

  (rf/reg-cofx :rf.server/request
    {:doc       "The active HTTP request. Server only."
     :platforms #{:server}}
    (fn [coeffects _]
      (assoc coeffects :rf.server/request *current-request*)))

re-frame.ssr never registers it. The worked example side-steps by passing 'request' as an event arg to :rf/server-init, but downstream handlers (e.g. :auth/check-session, :load-user-from-session) have no way to read URL / headers / session without that explicit arg threading. This breaks the canonical SSR auth pattern Spec 011 §687–699 describes ('Server middleware extracts the session from the request; :rf/server-init reads via cofx').

## Reproduction
(rf/reg-event-fx :load-user-from-session
  [(rf/inject-cofx :rf.server/request)]
  (fn [{:keys [rf.server/request]} _]
    ;; request is always nil — cofx unregistered
    ...))

## Recommendation
- Implement :rf.server/request as a registered cofx in re-frame.ssr OR in the host adapter (rf2-NEW-1).
- The host adapter binds *current-request* per-request before the drain runs.
- The cofx reads from that binding.
- Document the binding contract in spec.

## Dependencies
- rf2-NEW-1 (host adapter) — *current-request* binding lives in the host adapter; the cofx is the consumer surface.

## Surfaces touched
- implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc (cofx registration)
- implementation/ssr-ring/ (binding site)
- spec/011-SSR.md §311–323 (note where *current-request* gets bound)

## Acceptance
- (rf/reg-event-fx :foo [(rf/inject-cofx :rf.server/request)] handler) — handler receives :rf.server/request bound to the active request map under SSR.
- :rf.cofx/skipped-on-platform fires when invoked client-side.
notes: PR #667 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/667 — :rf.server/request cofx + per-frame request slot (set-request!/get-request/clear-request!) + :platforms #{:server} gating. 8 tests, all passing. Leaves open per dispatch protocol — Mike closes after review.
close_reason: Closed

title: SSR: ship a Ring/Pedestal host adapter — no canonical SSR boot today
description:
Per ssr-audit-20260513-1757 findings (rf2-ul137) gap #1. Spec 011 §357–363 says 'host adapter is responsible for materialising :response into the wire format' but NO host adapter ships. Users wanting SSR must hand-roll: HTTP server choice (Ring/Pedestal/Jetty/HttpKit), per-request frame-creation glue, :rf/response → Ring-response translation, cookie serialisation (RFC 6265 wire form), static-asset serving. The worked example examples/reagent/ssr/core.cljc rolls its own handle-request fn that returns a Ring-shaped map — but it's per-app. This is the gap that turns 'we have SSR' into 'we have an SSR primitive.'

## Recommendation

Ship day8/re-frame2-ssr-ring as a per-feature artefact:

- (ns re-frame.ssr.ring)
- (defn handler [opts] ...) — returns a Ring handler that per-request: make-frames, dispatches :on-create with the Ring request bound as cofx, drains, calls render-to-string, builds the Ring response from get-response + the rendered HTML + the hydration payload.
- Wraps cookie serialisation (RFC 6265) so cookie maps in :cookies become Set-Cookie: headers on the wire.
- Handles redirect short-circuit (:html absent → status+location response).
- Calls destroy-frame in a finally block.

Pedestal/HttpKit variants would follow the same shape; Ring is the v1 commit.

## Effort
- 1 spec section in 011 (host-adapter contract) OR a new spec doc (Spec-SSR-Host-Adapter.md)
- 1 new artefact dir (implementation/ssr-ring/)
- 1 example that uses the adapter end-to-end (examples/reagent/ssr-with-ring/)

## Dependencies
- rf2-NEW-2 (:rf.server/request cofx) — the host adapter is the natural site to register the cofx.
- Coordinates with rf2-0m5ea (template variant for SSR scaffolding).

## Surfaces touched (sequential — hot zone)
- spec/011-SSR.md (response contract section + host-adapter contract addition)
- implementation/ssr-ring/ (new artefact)

## Acceptance
- An app added to deps {day8/re-frame2-ssr-ring {:mvn/version ...}} and (re-frame.ssr.ring/handler {...}) gets a working Ring handler with NO per-app SSR-glue code.
- Cookies in :cookies → Set-Cookie: wire format.
- Redirect short-circuit → status+location response with no body.
- Frame destroyed in finally block (covered by leak test from rf2-NEW-7).
notes: PR #666 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/666. Ships day8/re-frame2-ssr-ring as new artefact under implementation/ssr-ring/. ssr-handler + ssr-middleware + cookie->set-cookie-header public surface. *current-request* binding site for rf2-e825b coordination. 11 deftests / 50 assertions / all green. Existing ssr suite unchanged. Hot-zone touches (implementation/deps.edn + shadow-cljs.edn) additive only. Out of scope: streaming SSR (rf2-olb64), async Ring 3-arity, reg-head (rf2-gr0n).

title: Decision: file skills/re-frame2-improver/ as a new sibling skill for framework-pattern critique
description:
Source: rf2-zf7zd investigation (ai/findings/improver-architecture-20260513-1752.md §Angle 2).

## Decision needed

Currently the skills matrix has six entries. Five are authoring/operational; one (`re-frame-pair-improver2`) is retrospective. The base `re-frame2` skill is strictly authoring with no critique surface.

Proposal: file a new `skills/re-frame2-improver/` (sibling to `re-frame2`, not a sub-mode) that retrospects on re-frame2 code Mike authored and suggests framework-pattern improvements.

## Why a sibling skill, not a sub-mode of re-frame2

Inline critique mode in `re-frame2/SKILL.md` would:
- inflate the skill past the ~250-line leaf ceiling claimed in its own SKILL.md
- blur the trigger fingerprint (re-frame2 would fire on both authoring and critique vocabulary)
- contaminate every authoring session with critique chatter
- complicate the allowed-tools surface

A sibling skill keeps both surfaces clean. Same reasoning as rf2-ncp5n's HYBRID precedent, applied inverted: prefer separation when trigger fingerprints are mutually exclusive.

## Narrow scope at launch

- **Trigger**: explicit pull only — "any improvements?", "review my re-frame2 code", "is there a better re-frame2 pattern for this?"
- **Activation precondition**: a body of re-frame2 source in conversation (read/edited `.cljs`/`.cljc`, or user-supplied snippet)
- **Output**: 7-section structured retro (Goal / Observed shape / Pattern suggestions / Higher-leverage redesigns / Bead candidates / Other / Filing offer)
- **Pattern catalogue at launch**: 6 anti-patterns (see follow-on bead from rf2-zf7zd rec #4):
  1. Manual HTTP retry loops → Managed HTTP (Spec 014)
  2. Boolean-discriminator subs for FSM states → Tags layer (Spec 005)
  3. Manual loading flags → Nine States pattern
  4. Schemaless events at HTTP boundary → Spec 010 schemas
  5. Imperative effects in event handlers → data-only fx (Spec 003)
  6. View-side state via reagent atom/useState for non-render-local concerns → app-db + reg-sub
- **Trigger rejections**: no inline interruption, no periodic check-ins, no auto-end-of-session detection

## Why P1

Adds an 8th skill to the matrix. Decision-shaped (Mike approves/rejects). High-leverage if approved: every authoring session can be retro'd for framework adoption; pre-alpha is when this is most valuable (the framework learns from how it's used).

## If approved, follow-on implementation beads

- Build the SKILL.md, spec/, references/ scaffolding (P2 implementation)
- Pre-populate the anti-pattern catalogue (rec #4 from rf2-zf7zd)
- Land alongside the shared retro-protocol leaf (rec #3 from rf2-zf7zd)

## If rejected

Mike's call to keep the matrix at 6+1 retrospect skill (pair2-retro only). No framework-pattern critique surface exists; users get framework guidance only via the (authoring-time, no-critique) `re-frame2` skill.

## Cross-refs

- ai/findings/improver-architecture-20260513-1752.md (full investigation)
- ai/findings/re-frame-pair-story-skill-investigation-2026-05-13.md (HYBRID precedent)
- skills/re-frame-pair-improver2/spec/design.md (template for the new skill's spec)
close_reason: Closed

title: fix(adapter-reagent): substrate render must use rdc/create-root before render
description:
Discovered by rf2-s2bhn (Causa Playwright spec): the Reagent adapter's `render` slot calls `(rdc/render mount-point render-tree)` directly, but React 18's `reagent.dom.client/render` expects a `Root` (from `create-root`) as the first arg — not a raw DOM element.

When Causa's `mount/open!` calls `(substrate-adapter/render [shell/shell-view] node nil)` the adapter hits `(rdc/render <div> tree)` and React throws `TypeError: root.render is not a function`. The mount silently fails — Causa's `#rf-causa-root` div lands in the DOM but the shell never renders.

Failure stack:
  TypeError: root.render is not a function
      at reagent\$dom\$client\$render
      at re_frame\$adapter\$reagent\$render
      at re_frame\$substrate\$adapter\$render
      at day8\$re_frame2_causa\$mount\$open_BANG_
      at day8\$re_frame2_causa\$mount\$toggle_BANG_

File: implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs ~line 55

Fix: create a Root from the mount-point first, render into the Root, and call .unmount() on the Root in the returned unmount fn.

    (defn- render [render-tree mount-point opts]
      (let [hydrate? (boolean (:hydrate? opts))
            root (rdc/create-root mount-point)]
        (if hydrate?
          (rdc/hydrate-root mount-point render-tree)
          (rdc/render root render-tree))
        (fn unmount [] (rdc/unmount root))))

(Plus the hydrate path also needs review — hydrate-root returns its own root.)

The rf2-s2bhn Playwright spec is shipped with `skip: 'awaiting <this-bead>'` and will go live when the adapter is fixed.

Source of discovery: rf2-s2bhn, the Causa Playwright spec running through the substrate adapter's render slot for the first time end-to-end. Aligns with the rf2-otcbz audit finding that Causa had zero browser-test coverage — the spec immediately surfaced a real bug.
close_reason: Closed

title: [spec/014] HTTP trace events MUST specify :sensitive? honoring
description:

Required:
- Specify how :sensitive? declared on the dispatching event handler propagates to :rf.http/* trace events emitted within the cascade (inheritance via :rf.trace/trigger-handler).
- Consider request-side declaration on the :rf.http/managed fx-args map ( per-call) for cases where the handler isn't sensitive but the specific HTTP call is.

title: [spec/010] Schema-validation errors MUST honour :sensitive? flag
description:
Audit rf2-ok47g §Completeness matrix found that :rf.error/schema-validation-failure trace events typically carry the failing value verbatim (Malli's default behaviour). Spec 010 and Spec 009 have zero mention of :sensitive? interaction with schema-validation errors. A registration carrying :sensitive? true with a schema that fails on user input will emit a trace event containing the raw failing value.

Required:
- Either (a) scrub the failing-value slot when :sensitive? is in scope at emit time, or (b) drop the schema-validation-failure event entirely.
- Decide the per-key fate (path-of-failure should remain visible; only the failing-value slot is sensitive).
- Cross-reference from spec/010-Schemas.md to spec/009-Instrumentation.md §Privacy.

title: [runtime] Implement :sensitive? top-level stamping per Spec 009 §Privacy
description:
Audit rf2-ok47g surfaced this as the highest-priority completeness gap. Spec 009 §Privacy (lines 1149-1268, resolved by rf2-a32kd) describes runtime stamping of :sensitive? at the top level of every trace event emitted within a registration carrying :sensitive? true on its metadata. **No such stamping logic exists in implementation/core/src/** — grep finds zero matches for :sensitive? in implementation/core/src/. Every consumer (Causa, Story, pair2 preload, 3 MCP servers) has wired against a future-shaped event; their default-drop filters are no-ops today.

Required:
- Implement :sensitive? hoisting at every trace emit point inside a handler's scope (use :rf.trace/trigger-handler to find the innermost in-scope handler, read :sensitive? from (handler-meta kind id)).
- Implement the :rf.warning/sensitive-without-redaction emission at registration time per (kind, id) pair with suppression cache reset on frame destroy (catalogued at spec/009-Instrumentation.md:870).
- Implement filter-vocab support for (rf/trace-buffer {:sensitive? bool}) per spec/009 §Filter vocabulary line 1245.
- Implement with-redacted interceptor scrub of :event/dispatched :tags :event, :event/db-changed :tags :app-db-before/:app-db-after, and :rf.error/handler-exception :tags :event.
- Tests: every emit-site that the spec calls out must be exercised.

Source: ai/findings/sensitive-elision-audit-20260513-1748.md §G1

title: [pair2-mcp] Diff-encode :epochs slice by default; full snapshots opt-in
description:
Source: rf2-jlq5j findings doc (ai/findings/wire-protocol-bigapp-20260513-1541.md), recommendation #3

THE SINGLE BIGGEST WIRE-BYTE WIN. Each `:rf/epoch-record` today carries full `:db-before` AND `:db-after` (`spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2082`). Default epoch-history depth is 50 (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:45`). So the `:epochs` slice of `snapshot` is 100x app-db in worst case — a 1MB app-db → 100MB on the wire just from this slice. `pr-str` does NOT preserve structural sharing across records, so the in-memory savings are erased on serialisation.

## Scope

`skills/re-frame-pair2/preload/re_frame_pair2/runtime.cljs:1236` (`snapshot-frame-slice :epochs`) projects each record as:

```
{:epoch-id <id>
 :event-id <id>
 :committed-at <ts>
 :trigger-event <vec>
 :db-before-hash <hash>
 :db-after-hash <hash>
 :db-delta <clojure.data/diff projection>
 ... other slots unchanged ...}
```

The existing `runtime.cljs:441 epoch-diff` helper already computes the diff in the v1 vocabulary; reuse it.

Opt-back-in via `:full-epoch-snapshots? true` arg on `snapshot` and `trace-window`. Agents that need full snapshots for time-travel restore call out explicitly.

## Scope boundary

This is a WIRE-LAYER transform at the MCP/runtime boundary. The in-memory `:rf/epoch-record` schema stays unchanged — no Spec-Schemas.md change needed. The diff projection happens in the runtime preload, before `pr-str`. Time-travel restore (which needs the full snapshot) goes via the existing `rf/restore-epoch` path, not via re-reading the snapshot wire response.

## Acceptance

- snapshot `:epochs` slice returns diff-encoded by default.
- `:full-epoch-snapshots? true` opt-in returns the full pair.
- Test: 5MB app-db, single-key change, diff-encoded payload < 1% the full-encoded payload.
- Spec/003-Tool-Catalogue (and the runtime ns docstring) document the change.
close_reason: Closed

title: [pair2-mcp] Path-based slicing for snapshot :app-db (and new get-path tool)
description:
Source: rf2-jlq5j findings doc (ai/findings/wire-protocol-bigapp-20260513-1541.md), recommendation #2

Today the snapshot tool returns full app-db via `rf/get-frame-db` (`skills/re-frame-pair2/preload/re_frame_pair2/runtime.cljs:1226`). Agents that want one key fetch everything.

## Scope

Two parts:

1. Add `:path [:user :profile]` arg to the `snapshot` tool's `:app-db` slice. Server-side `get-in` before serialising. Defaults unchanged.
2. Add a dedicated `get-path` MCP tool — small, focused primitive for targeted reads. Signature: `{:frame :stories :path [:cart :items 0]}` → `{:ok? true :value <subtree> :exists? true}`.

## Why path is the cleaner primitive

Slicing a tree by path is the operation re-frame agents already think in (subscribe vectors, `get-in`, etc.). Adding it elsewhere (subs cache reads, future causa-mcp tools) is the same pattern.

## Acceptance

- snapshot tool accepts `:path`; smoke test in test/snapshot_test.cljs covers nil (default), present path, missing path, root path.
- get-path tool exists with its own descriptor; smoke test covers same.
- spec/003-Tool-Catalogue + the runtime preload's docstring document the new path arg.
notes: PR #648 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/648 — path slicing on snapshot + new get-path tool. 84 tests / 198 assertions green; production build clean. Path vocabulary shared with causa-mcp §2. Spec updates in pair2-mcp tree; runtime preload docstring update in skills/ filed as follow-up (out of bead scope).

title: [pair2-mcp] Enforce 5K-token cap at wire boundary
description:
Source: rf2-jlq5j findings doc (ai/findings/wire-protocol-bigapp-20260513-1541.md), recommendation #1

The 5K-token cap declared normative in `tools/pair2-mcp/spec/Principles.md:127` §"Tight token budget per response" is documentation only — no code enforces it. A `snapshot` call against a real-app's 5 MB app-db produces ~1.4M tokens (290x the cap), silently corrupting the agent conversation.

## Scope

Size-check rendered `pr-str` output in `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs:57 ok-text`. On overflow:
- Return `:ok? false :reason :budget-exceeded :estimated-tokens N :hint <next-step>`
- Hints should be tool-specific: snapshot → "try `:include [:app-db]` + `:path [...]`"; trace-window → "narrow `:ms` or use `:since-id` with explicit `:limit`".
- Configurable cap with sensible default (5K tokens ≈ 17.5KB EDN).

## Failure mode being fixed

Today: silent agent-context corruption. Agent host either truncates middle of payload or wedges conversation. Answer is lost without warning.

After fix: structured error with next-step hint. Agent retries with a narrower request.

## Acceptance

- ok-text checks size pre-return.
- Unit test in `test/re_frame_pair2_mcp/` exercises both under-cap (passes through) and over-cap (returns budget-exceeded with structured data) paths.
- spec/003-Tool-Catalogue updated to document the bound on every tool.
notes: PR #641 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/641). Wire-boundary 5K-token cap enforced in tools.cljs invoke. Pluggable :strategy (today :truncate-with-marker; extensible for path-slicing rf2-tygdv, lazy summary rf2-u2029, diff encoding rf2-rl7y). Default cap 5000, per-call max-tokens arg, 0 disables. Overflow shape: {:rf.mcp/overflow {:limit :reached :token-count N :cap-tokens C :tool T :hint H}}. 17 new tests (57 total, 132 assertions, 0 fail). Spec Principles.md §Tight token budget tightened from should → must enforced; 003-Tool-Catalogue.md gained universal wire-cap section. Note: another worktree had begun uncommitted work on the original rf2-rvyzy-pair2-mcp-wire-cap branch with a per-tool-plumbed approach; this PR's centralised-at-invoke design supersedes it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Investigation: wire protocol scalability for big app-dbs (MB-scale) — MCP surface, pagination, caching, dedup
description:
Audit the wire protocol surfaces used by skills ↔ MCP servers to handle large app-db payloads (multi-MB scale). Open questions:

**Capacity**: Can the current MCP wire protocol handle a few-MB app-db without truncation, choking the conversation, or breaking the 5K-token response budget (rf2-ll0yq)? What's the failure mode today — silent truncation, error, blowup?

**Surface design**: Do MCP server tool signatures need to change for big payloads? Options:
  - **(a) Slicing**: tools accept a path/selector (e.g. EDN path, Specter-style) and return only the requested slice. The agent navigates the tree incrementally.
  - **(b) Pagination**: tools return a cursor for sequential chunks of large collections.
  - **(c) Lazy summary + on-demand drill-down**: default response is a tree summary (keys + sizes + types); agent asks for specific subtrees by id/path.
  - Mix of the above.

**Caching**: If the app-db is largely stable across consecutive tool calls, can the server cache a hash and return 'unchanged since last fetch' instead of the full payload? What's the invalidation rule (per-event? per-epoch? per-path?)? Where would this state live — per-frame, per-MCP-session, or global?

**Trace surface**: trace events also carry app-db payloads (or do they?). Same questions apply.

**Structural dedup**: Should we use an improved version of https://github.com/day8/de-dupe? That library dedupes structurally-shared data on the wire. Could collapse repeated subtrees, common keysets, common values across events in a trace window. Investigate: is de-dupe still maintained? What's its CLJS+JS reach? Is a v2 worth doing?

**Output**: Write findings to ai/findings/wire-protocol-bigapp-<timestamp>.md with:
  - Today's per-tool wire shape (concrete bytes for a worked example with a 5MB app-db)
  - Failure-mode catalogue
  - Design proposal: which combination of (slice / paginate / lazy / cache / dedup) fits which surface
  - de-dupe assessment: alive? CLJS reach? v2 scope?
  - Prioritised recommendations → bead each one

**Surfaces to read**: tools/pair2-mcp/, tools/story-mcp/, tools/causa-mcp/ (spec-only), spec/Tool-Pair.md, spec/009-Instrumentation.md (5K-token budget rule), the wire-encoding paths in each MCP server, day8/de-dupe README.
close_reason: Investigation complete. Findings at ai/findings/wire-protocol-bigapp-20260513-1541.md. 12 follow-on beads filed: rf2-rvyzy (P1 cap enforcement), rf2-tygdv (P1 path slicing), rf2-1wdzp (P1 epoch diff encoding), rf2-obpa9 (P2 de-dupe integration), rf2-u2029 (P2 lazy summary), rf2-kbqq3 (P2 pagination), rf2-ho4ve (P2 size-aware overflow), rf2-nw6sj (P2 de-dupe .cljc port), rf2-3rt1f (P2 hash-keyed cache), rf2-lwgg8 (P3 causa-mcp spec), rf2-6sddv (P3 typical-tokens hints), rf2-f3djn (P3 skill docs). day8/de-dupe is alive (April 2026), CLJS-only, no v2 needed — just .cljc port for JVM reach.

title: Decide: who owns the story-mcp consumer story (existing skills vs new re-frame-story skill)
description:
**Source**: rf2-fvy7o findings doc, finding #2 + recommendation #3.

Decision needed; not a clear implementation task.

`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools.cljc` exposes 16 MCP tools across Dev / Docs / Testing / Write. **No skill in `skills/` declares any of them in `allowed-tools`.** The agent self-healing loop (generate variant → register-variant → run-variant → read-failures → iterate) is fully specified in `tools/story-mcp/spec/` but has zero agent-side glue.

## Options

1. **Extend the existing skills.** Add `mcp__story-mcp__*` tool ids to `skills/re-frame2/SKILL.md` (for the authoring + register loop) and `skills/re-frame-pair2/SKILL.md` (for run-variant + read-failures in a live session). Plus new leaves: `skills/re-frame2/reference/tooling/story-mcp-loop.md` and `skills/re-frame-pair2/references/stories.md`.
2. **Spin a new `skills/re-frame-story/` skill.** Scope: component-development companion using story-MCP, no runtime attach required, complements `re-frame2` (authoring side) but doesn't replace it. Trigger: agent-driven Storybook MCP loop (generate → register → run → fix).

## Context

`ai/findings/re-frame-pair-story-skill-investigation-2026-05-13.md` (bead rf2-ncp5n) explicitly recommends option 1 and rejects option 2's borderline argument unless the self-healing loop becomes a dominant pattern with its own decision-flow. The findings doc's reasoning is sound; the operational confirmation in rf2-fvy7o is that **none** of the binding work has happened yet — option 1 needs to be picked up and actioned, or option 2 needs to be revisited.

## Inputs for the decision

- How dominant is the agent self-healing loop expected to be vs. ad-hoc authoring?
- Does the existing 6-skill matrix have room for a 7th without making routing harder?
- Are there workflows that exclusively need story-mcp (no `re-frame2` authoring context, no `re-frame-pair2` runtime context)?

## Next step

Mike-decision. Once locked: file the implementation beads (one per leaf to add, one per `allowed-tools` edit).

title: CI flake: counter-with-stories time-travel scrub — 'still 4'
description:
Intermittent CI failure on 'Examples (browser, headless Chromium, rf2-lyj0)' job. Reproduces on the same SHA — fails roughly 16% of the last 50 main runs (8/50). Three open PRs (#581, #603, #609) all hit it today; the PRs themselves are unrelated and red purely because of this flake.

Signature (consistent across every failed run):

    FAIL counter-with-stories: time-travel scrub did not visibly change :count (still "4")
    Error: time-travel scrub did not visibly change :count (still "4")
        at Object.run (examples/reagent/counter_with_stories/counter_with_stories.spec.cjs:866:15)

Hits §11 of counter_with_stories.spec.cjs. The scrubber click should restore the loaded variant frame (init 7 + §10 click = 8) back to count=7, but the visible count is observed as '4' and unchanged after the scrub.

Hypothesis: when the test runs §10 inc.click() after the §6 workspace + §7 clickVariant('/loaded') sequence, main.locator([data-test='inc']).first() resolves to a workspace cell's canvas (the clicked-three-times variant: init 0 + play's 3 incs = 3) rather than the loaded variant's canvas. The click bumps count 3→4 in the wrong frame. The scrubber's restore-epoch targets the active variant (loaded) whose frame is sitting at count=7, but the count cell the test reads is still showing the workspace cell's '4'.

Next steps:
- Local Playwright reproduction (npm run test:examples after shadow-cljs compile).
- Add a console probe to dump the count of [data-test='inc'] under <main> at the §10 moment.
- Either anchor §10/§11 selectors to the active variant's canvas explicitly (e.g., scope by the canvas pane's data-test once one is added), or guarantee workspace teardown finishes before clickVariant assertions proceed.

Not introduced by the three PRs surfacing it today; the same SHA passes and fails. Affects PR queue throughput — every PR sees ~16% red on this job through no fault of its own.
notes: PR #616: data-test-variant anchor on Story canvas + workspace cells; §10/§11 spec selectors scoped to active variant. Path (b) per bead. 20/20 local repeat runs pass. Root cause: shell's :selected-variant and :selected-workspace are independent slots — variant click after workspace selection leaves workspace rendered under <main>, alphabetically-first cell of :auto-grid (clicked-three-times, count=3 after :play) absorbs the §10 inc click → count=4, but right-pane slider scrubs /loaded → canvas count stays at 4. Fix anchors selectors to /loaded explicitly via data-test-variant, robust regardless of state hazard.

title: [skill] Corpus-wide SKILL.md trim pass — target sizes per skill
description:
## Skills body bloat

Every SKILL.md in the corpus exceeds Anthropic's recommended ~3-5K-byte router size by 2-4×. Total bytes loaded on activation across the six skills: 84,994 (1,031 lines). Mean SKILL.md = 14,166 B / 172 L.

Recurring offenders:

1. **Cardinal rules** with 5-line entries that re-explain a one-line rule.
2. **Workflow / Phase enumerations** that duplicate the leaf describing the same phase.
3. **Deep-dive descriptions** that paragraph-describe each leaf.
4. **Anti-patterns** that restate cardinal rules in the negative.

The actual triggers for SKILL bloat are:

- `re-frame2-implementor` (185 L, 19,518 B) — largest. Cardinal rules + Phase 1 enumeration + Phase 2 enumeration + done checklist + anti-patterns all overlap heavily with leaves. Phase 1 decisions listed twice (SKILL §Phase 1 + `reference/phase-1-decisions.md` 211 L).
- `re-frame-migration` (166 L, 15,765 B) — `MIGRATION.md` framing duplicated 5+ paragraphs; Phase 2/3/5 re-derive what each `reference/*.md` already states.
- `re-frame2` (176 L, 15,317 B) — cardinal-rules overlaps leaves; long ~80-line loading-map table.

title: [test] Run conformance corpus on CLJS — port conformance_test.clj to :node-test
description:
## Conformance corpus only runs on JVM

`implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj` is JVM-only. The CLJS counterpart (`conformance_dsl_cljs_test.cljs`) only tests the DSL `resolve-value*` micro-shape; it never loads or runs any `.edn` fixture.

All 111 fixtures are validated against ONE host. Per the conformance README's own framing — fixtures are meant to be the portable cross-host capability proof — this is a serious gap.

CLJS has materially different async semantics (the executor isn't a thread, sub-cache disposal scheduling differs, view-render trigger-handler rides via a different binding mechanism). A second-host re-frame2 port author can't trust the corpus until CLJS is the second host.

## Proposed fix

Mirror `conformance_test.clj` as `conformance_corpus_cljs_test.cljs`, target `:node-test`. Adapt the runner's reset routine for CLJS async semantics (especially the sub-cache disposal scheduling and view-render trigger-handler binding).

title: [BLOCKING] Bump CI Java from 17 to 21 — closure-compiler v20250407 needs Java 21+
description:
**Severity**: BLOCKING — every CLJS test job currently fails on `origin/main`.

**Root cause**: rf2-rlpo bumped ClojureScript to 1.12.145, which ships closure-compiler v20250407. That compiler is built for class file version 65.0 (Java 21). CI runs `java-version: '17'` everywhere (class file 61.0).

**Error**: `UnsupportedClassVersionError: com/google/javascript/jscomp/CompilerOptions has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 65.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 61.0`.

**Evidence**: PR #477 (doc-only spec/API.md edit) sees 7 CLJS jobs fail with this exact error. The failure is not caused by the PR — every CLJS PR will hit this.

**Fix scope**: Sweep `java-version: '17'` → `'21'` across:
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — 21 instances
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — 3+ instances

Total ~24 occurrences.

title: REGRESSION: browser-test plain-fn-under-non-default-frame fails post-Stage-4-E
description:
PR #250 (Stage 4-E render-to-static-markup) broke a browser test on main.

## The failure

CLJS browser-test (shadow-cljs :browser-test, headless Chromium) job fails on main with:

  FAIL in (plain-fn-under-non-default-frame) (re_frame/cross_spec_cljs_test.cljs:498:17)
  FAIL in (plain-fn-under-non-default-frame) (re_frame/cross_spec_cljs_test.cljs:512:17)

Plus warnings:
- 'You are calling ReactDOMClient.createRoot() on a container that has already been passed to createRoot() before.'
- 'The current testing environment is not configured to support act(...)'

## Likely cause

Stage 4-E added the dom.server ns + parity tests. May have:
- Disturbed the test harness's mount/unmount lifecycle (the createRoot warning suggests a root re-creation issue)
- Introduced a test that doesn't clean up properly, leaking state into plain-fn-under-non-default-frame

## Reproducer

cd implementation && npm run test:browser

The failure surfaces consistently on main as of 2026-05-11.

## Acceptance

- plain-fn-under-non-default-frame test passes
- ReactDOMClient.createRoot warning gone (or proven unrelated)
- act(...) warning gone (or proven unrelated)
- All other browser tests still pass

P1 — main CI is red.
notes:
Root cause was NOT mount-leakage from Stage 4-E parity tests; it was a load-order-dependent bug in the :adapter/current-frame and :adapter/current-component late-bind hooks. Each of the four adapter ns's (reagent, reagent-slim, uix, helix) overwrote those hooks at ns-load time. In the in-tree shadow-cljs build that loads all four, the LAST-LOADED adapter silently won — and the cross-spec test runs the bridge but the hook was reading slim's *current-component* (always nil during stock-Reagent renders). Stage 4-E shifted the load order; the underlying fragility predated it. Fix wraps each adapter's reader in a routing closure that consults (substrate-adapter/current-adapter) and runs THIS adapter's reader only when this adapter is the installed one — otherwise chains to the previously-installed reader. PR #256: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/256. Tests: 406/982/0 browser-test (was 404/980/2). 406/961/0 node-test. Elision green.
PR #256 CI: all 18 checks GREEN (run 25637297170, conclusion: success). browser-test 1m28s pass, node-test 46s pass, examples 3m19s pass, elision pass, bundle isolation pass, all 11 JVM jobs pass, lockstep pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: rf2-froe pre-existing elision regression: schemas reason strings survive in prod bundle
description:
Following rf2-froe (set-schema-validator! seam), the production-elision verifier (npm run test:elision) reports 4 failures on baseline main:

- [FAIL] re-frame.schemas/validate-app-db!: sentinel "App-db at path " expected ABSENT, was PRESENT
- [FAIL] re-frame.schemas/validate-event!: sentinel " payload failed schema " expected ABSENT, was PRESENT
- [FAIL] re-frame.schemas/validate-sub-return!: sentinel " return value failed schema " expected ABSENT, was PRESENT
- [FAIL] re-frame.schemas/validate-cofx!: sentinel " injected value failed schema " expected ABSENT, was PRESENT

These were ABSENT before rf2-froe — verified by running test:elision against the rf2-froe parent commit. The likely cause: rf2-froe restructured the validate-*! fns to gate on `(when (and interop/debug-enabled? @validator-fn) ...)` instead of the simple `(when interop/debug-enabled? ...)`. Per Spec 009 §Production builds L329: `(when (and X interop/debug-enabled?) ...)` does NOT constant-fold reliably — "Closure can't statically rule out X, and the dead branch survives into the bundle."

The fix is likely to invert the gate — outer `(when interop/debug-enabled? ...)` for DCE, inner `(when @validator-fn ...)` for the runtime check.

Discovered while implementing rf2-r2uh (boundary-validation interceptor). My change does NOT regress this — same 4 failures appear in baseline and with my changes. Filing as a separate bead per CLAUDE.md guidance: "when implementing surfaces a spec gap/inconsistency, file a bd bead".
close_reason: Fixed by rf2-qlx2 (615bc82): restore C-000.35 elision gate for validate-*! sentinels — landed on main between my discovery and PR. My rf2-r2uh branch rebased onto it; elision passes.

title: REGRESSION: rf2-froe broke production elision — 4 schema sentinels leak into prod bundle
description:
PR #237 (rf2-froe) broke C-000.35 strict elision. The CLJS production elision CI test (Spec 009 / rf2-11hn) now fails on main with 4 sentinel violations:

[FAIL] re-frame.schemas/validate-app-db!: sentinel 'App-db at path ' expected ABSENT, was PRESENT
[FAIL] re-frame.schemas/validate-event!: sentinel ' payload failed schema ' expected ABSENT, was PRESENT
[FAIL] re-frame.schemas/validate-sub-return!: sentinel ' return value failed schema ' expected ABSENT, was PRESENT
[FAIL] re-frame.schemas/validate-cofx!: sentinel ' injected value failed schema ' expected ABSENT, was PRESENT

Root cause hypothesis: the new validator-fn / explainer-fn atom-based seam in re-frame.schemas no longer presents Closure with a clear DCE-able shape for the validate-*! function bodies. The old hard-coded resolve-style pattern was either inside a goog.DEBUG branch or yielded a static call site that DCE could eliminate. The new atom-deref pattern is dynamic and Closure can't prove the body is unreachable in :advanced.

Fix path:
- Wrap the dev-time validate-*! fns' bodies in (when ^boolean js/goog.DEBUG ...) or similar elision gate so Closure can drop the entire body in prod.
- Verify the new validate-with-registered-fn path (the boundary-validation seam) does NOT take the gate — that fn intentionally runs in prod (boundary validation IS prod validation).
- Two distinct call paths needed: dev-time validate-*! (gated) + boundary validate-with-registered-fn (ungated). Already separated per rf2-froe's design but the gate apparently fell off.

Run the test locally: cd implementation && npm run test:elision

Severity: P1 — constitutional C-000.35 violation. Every push to main since PR #237 has had red CI on this step.
notes:
Fix landed in PR #240 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/240

Root cause confirmed: the combined gate predicate (and interop/debug-enabled? @validator-fn) was not a compile-time constant. The atom deref defeated Closure's reachability proof, so the four reason strings survived advanced compilation with goog.DEBUG=false.

Fix shape: restructured each of the four validate-*! entry points so interop/debug-enabled? is the OUTERMOST gate (matching the pattern in registrar.cljc, trace.cljc, router.cljc, subs.cljc, views.cljs). The @validator-fn deref now lives inside that gate.

Boundary path (validate-with-registered-fn, explain-with-registered-fn) intentionally untouched per rf2-r2uh contract.

Local verification:
- npm run test:elision: PASS — all 4 sentinels ABSENT in production, PRESENT in control.
- cd implementation/schemas && clojure -M:test: 38 tests, 136 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors.

title: Consider reimplementing re-frame-pair2 app-db/reset on top of rf/reset-frame-db!
description:
Why this suggestion exists:
`app-db/reset` is documented as a working pair-tool write op (`skills/re-frame-pair2/SKILL.md:106`, `skills/re-frame-pair2/docs/capabilities.md:86`), but its implementation appears to target the wrong API surface. In `skills/re-frame-pair2/scripts/runtime.cljs:118-138`, `app-db-reset!` logs the change and then tries to locate a frame-local `:app-db` container through `(rf/handler-meta :frame frame-id)`. The public implementation API does not expose the container that way: frame metadata is config/lifecycle data, while `rf/get-frame-db` is a value-form accessor. re-frame2 already exposes `rf/reset-frame-db!` as the canonical Tool-Pair write surface for this exact use case (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1166`).

As written, the helper can plausibly report `{:ok? true}` without actually mutating state or recording the synthetic epoch that `restore-epoch` depends on.

Suggestions to consider:
- Rebuild `app-db-reset!` on top of `rf/reset-frame-db!` instead of trying to reach a frame container through registrar metadata.
- Surface the real success/failure result from `rf/reset-frame-db!` rather than always claiming success.
- Add a runtime or fixture test that asserts `app-db/reset` both changes `app-db` and appends the expected synthetic epoch record.

title: Consider tightening multi-frame operating-frame semantics in re-frame-pair2 runtime
description:
Why this suggestion exists:
The runtime says multi-frame sessions should treat ambiguity as unsafe for writes, but the current implementation does not consistently enforce that contract. In `skills/re-frame-pair2/scripts/runtime.cljs:69`, `current-frame` falls back to `:rf/default` whenever that frame is registered, even when multiple frames exist and no frame has been selected. `pair-dispatch-sync!` then only raises `:ambiguous-frame` when frame resolution returns nil (`skills/re-frame-pair2/scripts/runtime.cljs:454-456`), so mutating ops can silently land in `:rf/default` instead of refusing.

There is a second inconsistency in the same area: `subs-sample` calls `@(rf/subscribe query-v)` with no frame threading (`skills/re-frame-pair2/scripts/runtime.cljs:194-200`). That means a prior `select-frame!` does not affect this op the way the runtime's operating-frame model suggests. The docs currently promise the opposite: `SKILL.md:76`, `docs/initial-spec.md:205`, and `docs/capabilities.md:88` all say mutating ops refuse on `:ambiguous-frame`, and the capabilities matrix marks wrong-frame routing as done.

Suggestions to consider:
- Make `current-frame` return nil when multiple frames are registered and no explicit/session frame has been chosen, so mutating ops really refuse.
- Thread the selected or explicit frame through `subs-sample` and any similar helper that currently relies on `rf/subscribe`'s default frame resolution.
- Add runtime-level tests for ambiguous multi-frame sessions and for `select-frame!` affecting read helpers.
notes: PR #190 (merged 2026-05-10): fix landed on main — current-frame returns nil under ambiguity, subs-sample threads the operating frame, 17-test multi_frame_test suite passes (bb). Bead is now effectively resolved; leaving open for Mike to close.

title: Fix UIx/Helix derived-value baseline and add regression coverage
description:
Why this issue exists:
Both non-Reagent adapters seed their derived-value watch baseline from the raw source container instead of the derived value itself. In implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:84 and implementation/adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs:88, `prev-state` starts as `(deref s)`, but the watch callback compares that baseline against `new-derived`. On the first source update, a derived computation that stays value-equal can still emit a spurious downstream notification whenever the derived value is not identical to the raw source value, for example `(odd? x)`, counts, projections, or maps.

What needs to be done:
- Seed the baseline from the current derived value rather than the raw source value in both adapters.
- Add regression coverage for the first-update/no-op case where the source changes but the derived value remains `=`.
- Prefer direct adapter-level tests under implementation/adapters/uix/test and implementation/adapters/helix/test; example-smoke coverage alone is too indirect for this behavior.

Notes:
This is easy to miss because the Reagent adapter has different internals and the UIx/Helix test trees currently provide little or no focused coverage for derived-container notification semantics.
notes: PR #192 (MERGED 2026-05-10): seeded UIx + Helix derived-value baselines from derived value, added 7 regression cases each adapter under implementation/adapters/{uix,helix}/test/re_frame/adapter/*_derived_value_baseline_cljs_test.cljs

title: Spec 009 production-elision constitutional contradiction: schema-validation-failure recovery splits dev/prod despite "all tracing eliminated in prod" claim
description:
Audit rf2-ra02 finding F-1, ranked second of top-3 most load-bearing.

Quote (audit-009 line 45): '§Default behaviour for :rf.error/schema-validation-failure says recovery is :no-recovery (dev) / :replaced-with-default (prod) (line 579). But the spec's lead claim (line 13) is "All tracing is compile-time eliminated in production builds. No exceptions." Spec-Schemas line 250 lists validate-app-db! / validate-event! / validate-cofx! / validate-sub-return! behind the same interop/debug-enabled? gate — i.e. schema validation IS dev-only. So either (a) there is no "(prod)" recovery row to discuss because validation isn't running, or (b) validation runs in prod and the §Production builds claim is overstated. This is the rf2-uuoj C-000.35 territory ("behavioural-equivalence-under-elision"). 009 has not ratified what behaviour, if any, survives the gate.'

Why load-bearing (audit-009 §3 line 72-81): :rf.error/schema-validation-failure is the only category in §Default behaviour by category that splits '(dev) / (prod)' on its recovery — every other row is single-valued. The split contradicts the spec's lead claim that production elides ALL tracing. The decision matters because Spec 010 (Schemas) builds boundary-validation policy on top of it.

Constitutional violation per audit-criterion #5: 000-Vision Goal-tier commitment ('production-elision') contradicted by the §Default behaviour table.

Resolution per audit R-L1: (a) strict elision — recovery split is fictional, remove it; (b) schemas survive elision — narrow the lead claim; (c) per-frame opt. Auditor leans (a). This is rf2-uuoj's C-000.35 held clause.
