title: Spec 002 drain-loop pseudocode :dispatch fx fails to forward envelope, contradicts cascade-propagation contract
description:
Audit rf2-8syd finding F18, ranked top-3 most load-bearing.

Quote (audit-002 line 40): '§Per-frame and per-call overrides commits to "All three override types propagate transitively through any depth of :fx [:dispatch ...] cascade … envelope-field-copying when queueing children." But the §Drain-loop pseudocode (lines 857–858) shows :dispatch fx implementation as (dispatch frame {:event ev}) — only :event and frame are forwarded. Where do :fx-overrides, :interceptor-overrides, :trace-id, :origin, :source get into the child envelope? An AI literally implementing the pseudocode produces children with NO inherited overrides — directly violating the cascade-propagation contract.'

Why load-bearing (audit-002 line 53): tests, story fixtures, and per-frame stubbing rely on cascade-propagation. The pseudocode at line 857 (:dispatch fx) builds a child envelope with only :event — no :fx-overrides, no :interceptor-overrides, no :trace-id, no :origin. An AI that implements 002's pseudocode literally produces a runtime where :fx-overrides only apply to depth-0 dispatches. The conformance corpus may catch this if there's a depth-1 fixture, but the prose claim and the pseudocode disagree, and the pseudocode is what the AI will copy.

Resolution: fix the pseudocode at line 857 to forward the full envelope (or copy the inheritable subset). Alternatively, hoist a merge-from-parent-envelope step into the pseudocode and name it. Add a fixture asserting that depth-2+ dispatches inherit :fx-overrides.
close_reason: Resolved via PR #150 — 002 drain-loop pseudocode :dispatch fx envelope-forwarding fix (commit eb70ca8).

title: Spec 002 fx-handler signature contradiction: documented binary (fn [m event]) vs drain-loop pseudocode (fx-handler frame args)
description:
Audit rf2-8syd finding F5, ranked top-3 most load-bearing.

Quote (audit-002 line 27): 'Line 540: "reg-fx's primary signature in re-frame2 is binary: (fn [m event] ...)" and line 553: "m is the same map the originating event handler received." Line 838–839 pseudocode: (let [fx-handler (lookup-fx frame fx-id)] (fx-handler frame args)) — calls with the frame record, not the handler's context map. These cannot both be the contract. The handler context map and the frame record are different shapes; an AI implementor would pick one and the conformance would diverge.'

Why load-bearing (audit-002 line 50): every fx in the runtime — the four reserved (:dispatch, :dispatch-later, :db, :raise/:spawn) and every user fx — depends on the calling convention. The §Async effects section painstakingly establishes that the binary signature is 'm, the originating handler's context map' and cites this for why (:frame m) works. The drain-loop pseudocode then passes the frame record. An AI implementor running :fx [[:dispatch [:foo]]] from the pseudocode would write (rf/dispatch event {:frame (:frame m)}) against an m that IS the frame record, which would fail. This is the kind of contradiction that breaks the whole 'AI-implementable from spec alone' goal (000-Vision Goal 2).

Resolution: pick one. Either (a) the fx-handler receives the handler context map (m) and the pseudocode should pass envelope or the assembled context, or (b) the fx-handler receives the frame record and the documented signature should say so. The documented (:frame m) reads in §Async fx (line 564) imply (a).

title: [bug] timer 7guis #4 Playwright spec fails on CI — Reset doesn't return elapsed to 0 within 2s
description:
Main branch CI has been RED since PR #50 (rf2-lyj0 examples runnable + Playwright). The Examples (browser, headless Chromium) job consistently fails with:

  FAIL timer (7guis #4): Reset did not return elapsed to 0.0 within 2s
  Error: Reset did not return elapsed to 0.0 within 2s
    at Object.run (examples/playwright/timer.spec.cjs:51:11)

Other 6 example specs (counter, flight-booker, nine-states, routing, temperature, todomvc) all PASS.

## Local-vs-CI signal

The rf2-cfig agent (PR #53) reported: 'timer 7guis spec was flaky on the first run, passed on subsequent runs' on a local Windows worktree. On Linux CI runners, it fails every run for ~4 consecutive main commits.

## Three plausible causes

1. **Real bug** — the Reset event handler doesn't actually clear :elapsed in app-db, OR the state-machine that drives ticking keeps producing :tick events that re-increment :elapsed faster than the spec can observe a 0 value.

2. **CI timing** — Linux runner is slow enough (combined with Reagent re-render / Playwright DOM-poll cadence) that the 2s assertion window expires before :elapsed is observably 0.

3. **Element-locator issue** — the Playwright spec is querying the wrong element, or querying a stale render.

Investigation order: read examples/seven_guis/src/timer/* (or wherever the timer impl lives), then examples/playwright/timer.spec.cjs:51 and the surrounding test code, then check whether the Reset event/transition actually pure-zeroes :elapsed in app-db.

## Fixes by cause

- Real bug: fix the Reset semantics. Probably a state-machine action that doesn't run, or an :elapsed slot that's reseeded by an in-flight :tick.
- CI timing: bump assertion timeout to 5s; add Playwright auto-retry on first failure of this spec; OR add a settle wait before the assertion.
- Locator issue: pin the assertion to the correct DOM element with a stable test-id.

## Why P1

- Main branch has been RED for 4 commits.
- New PRs that don't touch the timer still inherit a red main-branch CI signal at merge time.
- The 'green main' invariant is foundational; restoring it is more important than landing the next feature.

## Out of scope

- Don't disable the timer spec to make CI green. Fix it or document the flake-and-retry path properly.

Discovered from main-branch CI runs 25553697711 (and 3 prior).

title: Implement Spec 014 — :rf.http/managed (CLJS + JVM + tests)
description:
Implement Spec 014 — HTTP requests — `:rf.http/managed` and family.

The full spec is at `docs/specification/014-HTTPRequests.md`. Read it first, end to end, before starting; every behaviour has been pinned in the spec and the impl conforms exactly.

## Surface to ship

- `:rf.http/managed` — the request fx.
- `:rf.http/managed-abort` — abort by `:request-id`.
- `:rf.http/managed-canned-success` / `:rf.http/managed-canned-failure` — test stubs.
- `(rf/with-managed-request-stubs ...)` helper for test ergonomics (per Spec §Testing).

## Behaviours

- Args map per Spec §The args map (request envelope, decode, accept, retry, timeout-ms, on-success/on-failure, request-id, abort-signal).
- `:body` handling per §Body encoding (eager + thunk).
- Decode pipeline per §Decoding (schema / kw / fn / `:auto`); `:rf.warning/decode-defaulted` trace on auto-fallback.
- Schema-reflection metadata at `:rf.http/decode-schemas` queryable via `handler-meta`.
- `:accept` post-decode normalisation per §`:accept`.
- Retry + backoff per §Retry and backoff. Only final exhaustion dispatches `:on-failure`; per-attempt `:rf.http/retry-attempt` traces.
- All eight failure categories: `:rf.http/transport`, `:rf.http/cors`, `:rf.http/timeout`, `:rf.http/http-4xx`, `:rf.http/http-5xx`, `:rf.http/decode-failure`, `:rf.http/accept-failure`, `:rf.http/aborted`.
- Reply addressing per §Reply addressing — default merged-into-msg, explicit appended-payload, nil silenced.
- Frame awareness per §Frame awareness — reply lands in same frame.
- Aborts per §Aborts — `:request-id` (internal) + `:abort-signal` (external, CLJS).
- Stale-suppression via epoch carry per Pattern-StaleDetection.

## Hosts

- **CLJS:** Fetch-API-backed.
- **JVM:** `java.net.http.HttpClient`-backed. Per-row CLJS-only keys (`:abort-signal`, `:mode`, `:cache`, `:referrer`, `:integrity`) are no-ops on JVM with a one-line trace per occurrence so users see they were silently dropped.

## Production elision

`:rf.http/managed`'s runtime overhead must be code, not infra-trace pollution. Trace events (`:rf.http/retry-attempt`, `:rf.warning/decode-defaulted`, the `:rf.error/*` from failures) gate on `interop/debug-enabled?` per the existing pattern. The fx itself is dev+prod (it's user-facing).

## Tests

Substantial coverage:

- **Conformance fixtures** in `docs/specification/conformance/fixtures/`:
  - `http-managed-get-success.edn`
  - `http-managed-post-json.edn`
  - `http-managed-decode-failure.edn`
  - `http-managed-accept-failure.edn`
  - `http-managed-retry-exhaustion.edn`
  - `http-managed-retry-recover.edn`
  - `http-managed-abort-by-request-id.edn`
  - `http-managed-on-success-explicit.edn`
  - `http-managed-default-reply-addressing.edn`
  - `http-managed-frame-isolation.edn`
- **JVM smoke** in `implementation/test/re_frame/http_managed_test.clj` — lifecycle + each failure category + retry exhaustion + abort + thunk body + decode reflection metadata.
- **CLJS smoke** in `implementation/test/re_frame/http_managed_cljs_test.cljs` — Fetch-side end-to-end with `:fx-overrides` redirecting to the canned stubs.
- **Playwright integration** — add a counter-style example exercising `:rf.http/managed` against an in-process stub server, mounted via the existing `npm run test:examples` Playwright runner. Or extend an existing example (login? articles?) to use `:rf.http/managed`.
- **Elision probe extension** — extend `implementation/test/re_frame/elision_probe.cljs` and `scripts/check-elision.cjs` so the `:rf.http/managed` trace ops appear in the production-bundle absence assertion.

## Workflow

1. Confirm `C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2`. Branch `rf2-spec014-http-managed-impl` off `origin/main`. Use a private worktree (`git worktree add C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-spec014 origin/main`) to avoid contention with parallel agents.
2. Read `docs/specification/014-HTTPRequests.md` end-to-end first. Don't skip the spec.
3. Read `docs/specification/Conventions.md` §Reserved namespaces to confirm the `:rf.http/*` reservation.
4. Read existing fxs (`re-frame.fx`, `re-frame.ssr` for reg-fx examples; `re-frame.routing` for the dispatch + reply pattern; `re-frame.epoch` for trace pattern).
5. Implement in `implementation/src/re_frame/http_managed.cljc` (or split CLJS / JVM into separate files; up to you). Public surface re-exported from `re-frame.core`.
6. Implement test stubs in the same ns or a sibling (`http_managed_stubs.cljc`).
7. Author conformance fixtures.
8. Author JVM + CLJS smoke tests.
9. Add the elision-probe touches.
10. Verify: `cd implementation && clojure -M:test` (current baseline is wherever main is now after `2babfd7`); `npx shadow-cljs compile node-test && node out/node-test.js`; `npm run test:browser`; `npm run test:elision`.
11. Commit. **NO Claude attribution** (CLAUDE.md mandates this).
12. Push, open PR `feat: implement Spec 014 — :rf.http/managed (rf2-XXXX)`.
13. Report PR URL.

## If it gets too big

Acceptable to split into multiple PRs — agent's discretion:
- Phase 1: CLJS impl + JVM impl + JVM smoke + 5 fixtures.
- Phase 2: remaining 5 fixtures + CLJS smoke + Playwright integration + elision-probe extension.

If splitting, file a follow-up `bd create` for Phase 2 and ship Phase 1 first.

## Don't

- Don't deviate from the spec without filing a `bd create` for the deviation. The spec was iterated through 10 questions; deviations need explicit reason.
- Don't reach into private re-frame namespaces; use `re-frame.core` and `re-frame.late-bind`.
- Don't add HTTP/streaming / WebSocket support — Spec 014 explicitly excludes them.
- Don't ship the canned-stub fxs as production-eligible; gate them on `interop/debug-enabled?` so they elide.

Phase 1 deliverables:
- implementation/src/re_frame/http_managed.cljc — CLJS Fetch + JVM HttpClient transport, full args-map per Spec 014, retry+backoff, all 8 failure categories, abort by request-id and abort-signal, schema-driven decode, default reply addressing
- implementation/src/re_frame/fx.cljc — extended do-fx 5-arity to thread originating event into fx-handler ctx (needed for default reply addressing)
- implementation/src/re_frame/router.cljc — pass event vector through to do-fx
- implementation/src/re_frame/core.cljc — public re-exports: install-managed-request-stubs!, with-managed-request-stubs (macro + fn)
- implementation/test/re_frame/http_managed_test.clj — 13 JVM smoke tests including real in-process httpserver round-trips for: GET success, 4xx, retry exhaustion, retry recover, transport failure, abort, thunk body, with-managed-request-stubs, decode-schemas reflection metadata, timeout
- 5 conformance fixtures in docs/specification/conformance/fixtures/:
  - http-managed-default-reply-addressing.edn
  - http-managed-get-success.edn
  - http-managed-post-json.edn
  - http-managed-decode-failure.edn
  - http-managed-retry-exhaustion.edn

title: Frame-provider React context resolution returns :rf/default under Reagent 1.2 + React 18
description:
Discovered while implementing rf2-lyj0 (examples runnable in browser).

The counter example wraps :counter-buttons in a frame-provider:
  [(v/build-frame-provider :counter) :counter [counter-buttons]]

Inside :counter-buttons, (rf/subscriber) calls (current-frame) which is
supposed to read the frame from React context (the Provider's value).
At runtime under Reagent 1.2 + React 18, this resolution returns
:rf/default instead of :counter — the subscription lands on the default
frame, which has empty app-db, and the rendered span shows nothing.

Reproducer: examples/counter (after rf2-lyj0 lands) — page renders the
- and + buttons but the count span is empty. Browser inspection of
re-frame.frame/frames shows :counter has {:count 5} in app-db but
:rf/default has the [:count] subscription cached.

Likely cause (per rf2-25aq notes): the :context-type metadata on the
view wrapper is class-component-style React. With Reagent 1.2 used
against React 18, this may be silently not wiring up, so the
(.-context cmp) read in current-frame falls back to React's default
context value (an empty object), which fails the keyword? check and
defaults to :rf/default.

Fix candidates:
1. Use React's useContext hook in current-frame instead of class
   contextType. Requires the wrapper to be a function component
   that calls useContext(frame-context) at render time.
2. Wait for rf2-25aq (Reagent v2 migration); v2's hooks-flavoured
   approach replaces the class-contextType pattern.
3. Add a fallback in build-frame-provider that ALSO sets the dynamic
   var (*current-frame*) for the subtree's synchronous render.

Workaround in the meantime: examples either use the default frame, or
pass :frame explicitly via dispatch-sync / subscribe at the call site
(not via the (rf/dispatcher) / (rf/subscriber) closures which capture
current-frame at call time).
notes: Resolved by rf2-25aq (PR #73, 2026-05-09). Root cause was NOT Reagent-version-specific — :context-type (kebab-case) was ignored by Reagent under both 1.2 and 2.x; the recognized name is :contextType (camelCase, mirroring React's static-field name). Renamed in re-frame.views/reg-view* . Frame-provider context resolution now works under React 18 + Reagent 2.

title: Bug: clear-flow's :path = [:k] (single-element) leaves the key in app-db
description:
Repro:

(rf/reg-event-db :seed (fn [_ _] {:w 3 :h 4}))
(rf/reg-flow {:id :area :inputs [[:w] [:h]] :output * :path [:area]})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:seed])  ;; :area now 12 in app-db
(rf/clear-flow :area)

Expected: :area key removed from app-db (per Spec 013 §clear-flow cleanup: 'Default behaviour is dissoc-in on the flow's :path').

Actual: :area still in app-db.

Root cause: flows.cljc clear-flow has

  new-db (if (and (vector? path) (seq path))
           (update-in cur (vec (butlast path)) dissoc (last path))
           (dissoc cur path))

For path [:area], (butlast [:area]) is (), (vec ()) is []. update-in with [] does NOT call (dissoc cur :area) — Clojure's update-in with empty path falls through (assoc {} nil (apply f val args)) per its source, producing {:area 12, ... nil nil}. So the dissoc never lands.

Fix: special-case (count path) == 1 to (dissoc cur (first path)). Or use a guard: when (>= (count path) 2) update-in with butlast; when 1 dissoc directly.

Discovered by rf2-1cli flow tests (flow-toggle-via-fx and flow-recompute fixtures both expect single-element :path to clear cleanly).
notes: Fix in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/16 — single-element :path now special-cased to (dissoc cur (first path)). Smoke test added in implementation/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj.

title: Decide canonical public namespace: re-frame.core (per MIGRATION.md) vs re-frame-2.core (per impl + examples)
description:
The repo is internally inconsistent on the public namespace.

**`re-frame.core` is asserted as canonical** in:
- `docs/specification/MIGRATION.md` line 23: *"re-frame2 keeps the public API of `re-frame.core` working..."*
- MIGRATION.md line 48, 69, 70, 184, 846, 911, 927 all reference `re-frame.core` as the post-migration target.
- `docs/guide/07-from-re-frame-v1.md` line 19: *"`re-frame.core` is still the namespace. Your `(:require [re-frame.core :as rf])` lines don't change."*

**`re-frame-2.core` is asserted as canonical** by:
- `implementation/src/re_frame_2/core.cljc` (the actual ns form).
- Every example: `examples/counter/core.cljs` line 9, `examples/login/core.cljs`, etc. all `:require [re-frame-2.core :as rf]`.
- The directory layout `re_frame_2/`.

These cannot both be true. Two options:

1. **Public namespace is `re-frame.core`** (MIGRATION's view). The impl namespace gets renamed `re-frame-2.core` → `re-frame.core`; every example's `:require` is rewritten. Win: zero-change `:require` lines for v1 users (the strongest "drop-in upgrade" story). Cost: cannot have re-frame v1 and re-frame2 on the same classpath, so migration is all-or-nothing per project.

2. **Public namespace is `re-frame-2.core`** (impl's view). MIGRATION.md and ch.07 are wrong. Migration becomes one mechanical rewrite of `:require` lines per file. Win: v1 and v2 can coexist on the classpath, useful during gradual migration. Cost: every existing project's `:require` line breaks at upgrade time.

Until decided, the chapter-02 walkthrough disagrees with the example it walks through, ch.07 disagrees with every example file, and an outside reader cannot tell which document to trust.

This blocks the namespace mechanical fix in the guide. P1.
notes: Decision: spec stands. Public namespace is re-frame.core (per 000-Vision.md L413 + MIGRATION.md + ch.07). Implementation will be renamed re-frame-2.* -> re-frame.* on a branch; tests run; branch reviewed before merge. Artefact-name decision deferred to rf2-5sqd.
close_reason: Closed

title: Implementation: SSR emitter + hydration + head/meta + error projection (Spec 011)
description:
The first-pass implementation/src/re_frame_2/ssr.cljc has a STUB hiccup → HTML emitter that handles only the basics. The following Spec 011 features are NOT implemented: (a) HTML5 void-element handling (
, , ,
, etc. self-close). The current emitter treats them as which is invalid HTML5. (b) Doctype prefix option (). Currently :doctype? opt is ignored. (c) Hash-tag / class-list keyword attribute syntax (:div#id.cls). Currently bare keyword tag is supported but compound :tag#id.cls is not. (d) :rf/hydration-payload schema and the :rf/hydrate event semantics — :replace-app-db policy, :rf/version + :rf/schema-digest mismatch detection. The :rf/hydrate event handler is registered but only does `:db` replacement; no version/schema checks. Per Spec 011 §The :rf/hydrate event. (e) :rf/head model and head-mismatch detection. Per Spec 011 §Head/meta contract — reg-head, the :head route metadata, and the :rf.head/* trace events. (f) Hash-based render-tree mismatch detection (FNV-1a 32-bit over canonical EDN). Per Spec 011 §Hydration-mismatch detection. (g) :rf.server/* response-shape fx (set-status, set-cookie, redirect, error-projection). Per Spec 011 §HTTP response contract. (h) Server error projection (sanitisation at the public boundary). Per Spec 011 §Server error projection. This is a significant chunk of v1 work. The emitter pseudocode is in the spec, so rebuilding correctly is mechanical; the harder parts are the hash-mismatch detection and the head-model contract. title: Implementation: hierarchical machine states, :always microsteps, :after timers, :invoke, :spawn
description:
The first-pass implementation in implementation/src/re_frame_2/machines.cljc covers only flat FSM grammar plus the :raise reserved fx-id (machine-internal pre-commit dispatch). The following Spec 005 features are NOT implemented:

(a) Hierarchical compound states with LCA-based exit/entry cascade. Per Spec 005 §Hierarchical compound states.

(b) :always microsteps with depth-limit and self-loop detection. Per Spec 005 §Eventless :always transitions.

(c) :after delayed transitions with epoch-based stale detection. Per Spec 005 §Delayed :after transitions.

(d) :invoke declarative actor spawn-on-entry / destroy-on-exit. Per Spec 005 §Declarative :invoke.

(e) :spawn dynamic actor lifecycle and the :rf.fx/spawn-args reserved fx. Per Spec 005 §Spawning.

(f) sub-machine for reading machine snapshots reactively. Per Spec 005 §Subscribing to machines via sub-machine.

The core flat-FSM machine-transition fn passes a smoke test (traffic-light state cycle). Adding the missing pieces is mostly mechanical against the spec; the hierarchical exit/entry cascade is the trickiest part because of LCA computation.

title: Add Cross-Spec Interactions appendix for edge cases at spec boundaries
description:
Each Spec is locked, but the points where two specs meet have edge cases that no single Spec owns. An AI implementing CLJS will hit these and have no canonical answer:

- Spec 002 (Frames) meets Spec 005 (Machines): a machine instance lives in a frame; what happens to active machines when the frame is disposed? Are :after-actions run? Is :stop guaranteed to fire?
- Spec 005 (Machines) meets Spec 011 (SSR-Server): can machines run in :ssr-server preset? They probably can but with restrictions (no setTimeout-based :always; no :invoke of long async). The spec needs to say.
- Spec 012 (Routing) meets Spec 011 (SSR): routing-as-state on the server -- the route is bound by the request URL; how does the route subscription work in a request-scoped frame?
- Spec 002 (Frames) meets Spec 006 (ReactiveSubstrate): frame disposal during render -- the substrate may have a render in flight; how is teardown sequenced?
- Spec 005 (Machines) meets Spec 008 (Errors): machine action throws; what is the on-error projector receive? Does the machine state revert? Does :always still run?
- Spec 005 (Machines) meets Spec 003 (Effects): effect handler is invoked from a machine action; the effect throws; same question.

CONTENTS:

A new docs/specification/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md document:

For each interaction edge case:
1. The two (or more) specs that meet
2. The scenario in one sentence
3. The decided behaviour
4. The reason
5. A pointer to the conformance corpus fixture that pins it

Roughly 15-25 interactions. Examples to seed the list:

- Frame disposal with active machines (002 x 005) -- :stop fires in reverse-creation order; pending :after-actions cancelled; trace event emitted
- Machines in SSR (005 x 011) -- machines run; :always permitted; :invoke restricted to synchronous co-effects (no setTimeout); deadline applies to the whole dispatch
- Routing in SSR (012 x 011) -- route is bound from request; only :route reads visible; navigation effects no-op (or raise an error -- to decide)
- Frame disposal during render (002 x 006) -- substrate adapter is told to dispose; in-flight render completes (single tick) but next render is skipped
- Machine action throws (005 x 008) -- on-error fires with envelope; machine state at last commit is preserved; :always does not fire on the failed microstep; trace records the failure
- Effect throws inside machine action (005 x 003 x 008) -- machine action treated as failed; same as above; trace records both action and effect
- Hot-reload of a machine action while instance is running (005 x rf2-t070) -- next microstep uses new action; in-flight action completes with old
- Reactive substrate that does NOT support context (006 x 002) -- frame-provider degrades to per-component rebinding; documented warning
- Sub-cache hit during machine microstep (005 x rf2-76fo) -- microstep can read subs; cache hits behave as for any read; cache invalidations fire after the whole drain step settles
- Machine spawn at boot before host adapter ready (005 x 011) -- queued until adapter ready; if ssr-server preset, :invoke effects run in a synchronous scheduler

(More to be enumerated during the write.)

V1 REFERENCE:
v1 does not have these interactions because v1 does not have machines, routing as a locked surface, or frame multiplicity. Almost all of the interactions are NEW for re-frame2. A few (frame x reactive-substrate, hot-reload x sub-cache) have v1-equivalents but the contracts have shifted.

LEVERAGE FOR rf2-5pt:
This is the catch-all for the things an AI will get wrong silently. Each interaction is small, but together they are the difference between a clean implementation and one that has subtle inconsistencies that pass tests and break in production.

title: Specify hot-reload surgical-update semantics for re-registration
description:
Hot reload is mentioned across the docs (a primary developer-experience promise; one of the things re-frame v1 does well). re-frame2 inherits this but the surgical-update algorithm -- exactly what happens when an event handler, sub, fx, machine, etc. is re-registered while the app is running -- has not been written down. An AI implementing CLJS will probably implement clear-and-replace in the registry, which works for handlers but not for machines (active machine instances reference the old handler closure) or for caches (cached subs hold stale derive-fns).

CONTENTS:

A specification of the surgical-update behaviour for each registry kind:

- :event handlers -- replace registry slot; in-flight events keep the old handler (run-to-completion); next dispatch sees new
- :sub handlers -- replace registry slot; cached sub values invalidate; next deref recomputes through the new derive-fn
- :fx handlers -- replace registry slot; in-flight :fx sequences finish using the resolved (old) handler; new dispatches see new
- :cofx handlers -- replace registry slot; same in-flight rule
- :machine-actions and :machine-guards -- replace registry slot; the question: do active machine instances continue using the old action or pick up the new? Probably new on next microstep, but spec needs to say so
- Machines themselves (re-register-machine of a different definition while instances are running) -- options: stop and restart instances, vs let them run to natural termination; spec needs to choose
- :route handlers -- replace registry slot; current navigation continues; next navigation uses new
- :head handlers -- replace registry slot; SSR not affected (request-scoped frame); CSR re-renders pick up new

For each: the rule, the why, what edge cases break.

Plus a §Hot-reload contract section stating:
- Re-registration is non-destructive to in-flight work (run-to-completion)
- Cached values invalidate on relevant re-registration
- Active machine instances behave [insert chosen rule] on action/guard re-registration
- The trace bus emits a :hot-reload event so devtools can react
- During a hot reload window, dispatch is not paused -- the system stays live

V1 REFERENCE:
re-frame v1 has working hot-reload via clear-handlers and re-registration; the algorithm is mostly run-to-completion + replace registry slot + invalidate sub cache. What is NEW for re-frame2: machines (active instances + replace action/guard), the explicit run-to-completion contract, the trace event for hot reload.

LEVERAGE FOR rf2-5pt:
Hot reload is one of the affordances every CLJS dev expects. An AI given no spec for it will either skip it (silently breaking shadow-cljs reload behaviour) or implement clear-and-replace which subtly breaks machines.

FILES:
- New: docs/specification/Hot-Reload.md companion (cross-referenced from 001-Registration, 005-StateMachines, 002-Frames), OR
- New §Hot reload section in 001-Registration with cross-refs from 005 and 002

PAIRS WITH:
rf2-5pt (primary), rf2-t059 (Runtime-Architecture.md must mention hot-reload as a property of the registry component), rf2-l2ck (drain loop -- run-to-completion guarantee comes from the loop)

WHY P1: hot reload is a baseline DX promise; getting it wrong silently breaks shadow-cljs flow. Estimated effort: small focused write -- can borrow from v1.

Five contract guarantees (non-destructive to in-flight work, cached values invalidate, machine instances pick up actions on next microstep, trace event emitted, dispatch not paused). Per-kind rules table for all 13 registry kinds (event, sub, fx, cofx, machine-action, machine-guard, machine-def, view, frame, app-schema, route, head, error-projector) listing what re-registration replaces, in-flight behaviour, cache disposal, trace event. §Re-registration of a different function — collision warning section keeping v1 last-write-wins behaviour but adding :rf.warning/registration-collision detection. §How registrations interact with active machine instances clarifying the three reference paths (machine def, machine-scoped actions, globally-registered actions) and which trigger re-spawn vs apply on next microstep. §Hot-reload trace surface with stable :registry/handler-replaced shape including :reason and per-kind extras (:active-instances, :disposed-slots). §Edge cases (mid-cascade re-registration, frame :on-create not re-firing, destroyed-then-re-registered frame, prod-build hot-reload). v1 source named explicitly as the implementation reference. Cross-refs added: 002 §Re-registration — surgical update points to 001 for non-frame kinds; Runtime-Architecture.md updated to reference the now-locked section.

title: Document sub-cache contract: invalidation algorithm and lifecycle
description:
The sub-cache is referenced across 002 (frames hold a cache), 005 (subs see machine state), 006 (substrate reactions wrap cache values), 010 (schemas mention :rf/sub-cache shape) but no single place specifies the invalidation algorithm, the reference-counting / lifetime rules, or what happens on app-db change. v1 has a working sub-cache implementation in re-frame.subs; re-frame2 needs to surface the algorithm explicitly so non-CLJS implementors and the CLJS one-shotter can build it without reverse-engineering.

CONTENTS:

Specifically: a §Sub-cache section (probably in 002 or as a standalone Sub-Cache.md companion) covering:

1. Cache shape -- per-frame map keyed by [query-vector] storing {:value v :reaction r :ref-count n :inputs-fingerprint f}
2. Lookup -- (subscribe q) returns existing cache slot if present; otherwise computes, stores, returns
3. Invalidation algorithm:
   - On app-db change, traverse cache; for each entry whose computed value depends on changed paths, recompute lazily on next deref
   - Reagent does this naturally via reactions; for non-reactive substrates (or test substrate), pseudocode the equivalent
4. Reference counting and disposal:
   - Subs registered as :reg-sub-by-path are eagerly cached
   - Subs with no live readers can be disposed (per substrate); the cache must release the entry
5. Layer-1 vs Layer-2 vs Layer-3 sub semantics (v1 framing):
   - Layer-1: direct reactions on app-db
   - Layer-2: reactions over Layer-1 subs
   - Layer-3: dynamic / parameterised
   - Re-frame2 keeps the layer concept but the spec needs to say so explicitly
6. Lifetime contract: when a frame is disposed, all cached subs are disposed; no leaks

V1 REFERENCE:
re-frame.subs has the working algorithm. The sub-cache invalidation is mostly v1s algorithm. The new thing for re-frame2: per-frame cache (v1 has a single global cache); the layer-1/2/3 distinction documented in spec rather than implicit; the disposal-on-frame-dispose contract.

The pseudocode does not need to be a full implementation; it needs to be specific enough that a non-CLJS implementor can write the equivalent in their host. For CLJS, "uses Reagent reactions per Spec 006 §Reference adapter" is enough; the algorithm matters more for non-CLJS hosts.

LEVERAGE FOR rf2-5pt:
Without this, an AI implementing CLJS will probably wire Reagent reactions and call it a day -- which works on the happy path but misses the per-frame disposal and ref-counting contract. With it, the disposal-correctness is explicit.

FILES:
- 002-Frames.md: new §Sub-cache section, OR
- New: docs/specification/Sub-Cache.md companion (cross-referenced from 002 and 006)

PAIRS WITH:
rf2-5pt (primary), rf2-t059 (Runtime-Architecture.md mentions sub-cache as a component -- this is the contract for that component), rf2-i3q9 (Reagent adapter pseudocode shows the CLJS realisation -- this bead specifies the contract the realisation satisfies)

WHY P1: gates correct implementation of frame disposal (a Goal-2 surface) and substrate-portability. Estimated effort: small focused write; can lean heavily on v1 source.

title: Add drain-loop pseudocode to 002-Frames
description:
Spec 005-StateMachines defines four Levels of run-to-completion semantics (1: synchronous handlers; 2: machine microsteps via :always; 3: subscribed views recomputing inside the same drain step; 4: external/async work yielding back to the loop). The semantics are described in prose. An AI implementing CLJS has to translate four prose-described levels into a working drain loop -- which is a non-trivial leap. This bead adds explicit drain-loop pseudocode in 002 (or a new Drain-Loop appendix) that shows the actual loop structure: dequeue, process envelope, run handler, apply effects (including :raise re-enqueue), settle machines via :always, fire subscribers, repeat until queue empty.

CONTENTS:

A pseudocode block of roughly 60-100 lines showing:
- The outer drain loop (dispatched until empty)
- Per-event: pull envelope, run interceptor chain, invoke handler, collect effects map
- :fx interpretation in source order, with do-fx reentrancy rules
- :raise effect: enqueue at front (vs :dispatch enqueue at back)
- Machine settling: between events (or between :raise items?), call run-always-actions on every active machine until quiescent
- Sub-cache invalidation: triggered by app-db replace; subscribers fire after drain step settles
- Trace bus: when each phase emits trace events
- Error trapping: where on-error projector is called

Plus an inline numbered list mapping each line back to the four Levels in 005.

Plus the small set of edge cases:
- :raise inside a machine action that itself runs in :always
- An event dispatched from a render (re-entrant dispatch -- queued, not synchronous)
- Effects that call back into dispatch (-fx returning :dispatch -- normal queue path)
- Frame disposal mid-drain (event is in flight; what happens?)

V1 REFERENCE:
re-frame v1 has a working router and event-loop; the drain loop in re-frame.router.cljc is the reference. What is NEW for re-frame2 and warrants explicit pseudocode:
- :raise (front-of-queue dispatch) is a new effect not in v1 baseline
- Machine integration (:always microsteps interleaved with drain) is new
- The four Levels framing in 005 is new framing of v1 mechanics
- The sub-cache settling order between drain events vs after the entire batch -- this needs to be explicit
- Run-to-completion guarantees in the presence of :raise and machine microsteps need explicit prose

LEVERAGE FOR rf2-5pt:
The drain loop is the single most subtle piece of runtime to get right. An AI given prose Levels will probably implement something that works for the happy path but breaks on machine settling or :raise ordering. Pseudocode collapses the design space.

FILES:
- 002-Frames.md: new §Drain loop (pseudocode) section, OR
- New: docs/specification/Drain-Loop.md companion (cross-referenced from 002 and 005)

Decision on file location can happen in the implementation; new section in 002 is the simpler default.

PAIRS WITH:
rf2-5pt (primary motivation), rf2-t059 (Runtime-Architecture.md -- the diagram-level companion to this pseudocode-level), rf2-vf8m (other-host implementors need this too)

WHY P1: gates one-shot implementation. The most error-prone runtime piece. Estimated effort: medium focused write; reading v1 router source helps.
close_reason: Added §Drain-loop pseudocode subsection inside 002 §Run-to-completion dispatch (drain semantics), placed after §:fx ordering and atomicity guarantees and before §Per-frame and per-call overrides. Roughly 130 lines of pseudocode in three blocks: (1) outer drain (Level 4) with next-tick scheduling and depth-limit guard; (2) per-event drain showing interceptor chain → :db → sub-cache invalidate → :fx walk with error trapping; (3) machine event handler showing the Level-3 cascade — raise queue drain, :always microstep loop, single snapshot commit. Plus a do-fx skeleton for the four reserved fx-ids the runtime owns. Plus an Interaction map cross-referencing every component the drain touches (registrar, substrate adapter, sub-cache, trace bus, error contract, machine cascade) and five edge cases (:raise inside :always, re-entrant render dispatch, :dispatch-to-self vs :raise, frame disposal mid-drain, async fx semantics). v1 router named explicitly as the implementation reference.

title: Add Reagent reference-adapter pseudocode to 006-ReactiveSubstrate
description:
006-ReactiveSubstrate defines the adapter contract abstractly (make-state-container, subscribe-container, make-derived-value, render, render-to-string, register-context-provider, dispose-adapter). The contract is right but the bridge from contract to a working Reagent implementation is left for the AI to invent. The CLJS reference adapter -- Reagent on top of React -- has well-known patterns (r/atom for state container, r/track! for subscription, r/reaction for derived value, r/render for mount); this bead adds a §Reference adapter pseudocode appendix that shows how each contract function maps to a Reagent primitive.

CONTENTS:

For each adapter contract function, ~10-15 lines of Clojure-flavoured pseudocode showing the Reagent realisation. Roughly:

- make-state-container -> wraps a clojure.core/atom or reagent.core/atom; returns a value the runtime treats opaquely.
- read-container -> deref.
- replace-container! -> reset! (with the structural-sharing PDS guarantee).
- subscribe-container -> r/track! over a reaction; returns an unsubscribe fn.
- make-derived-value -> r/reaction; the body is the derive-fn.
- render -> reagent.dom.client/create-root + render; returns an unmount-fn.
- render-to-string -> reagent.dom.server/render-to-string (JVM-runnable).
- register-context-provider -> a thin wrapper using react-context that the frame-provider uses.
- dispose-adapter! -> dispose all reactions, unsubscribe all listeners, dissoc the registry slot.

Plus key implementation notes:
- How to wire Reagent ratoms to the framers app-db so subs see updates.
- How sub-cache integrates with r/reaction lifecycle (track!/dispose!).
- How frame-provider uses React context (and how plain-fn-under-non-default-frame warning fires).
- How the JVM-side adapter (plain-atom) differs.

V1 REFERENCE:
re-frame v1 has working Reagent integration in re-frame.interop and re-frame.subs. An AI implementing CLJS can lean on v1 source for the patterns. What is NEW for re-frame2 and worth pseudocoding: the adapter-contract boundary itself (substrate decoupling work in 006); the disposal lifecycle (re-frame v1 does not have explicit adapter disposal); the rule that adapter-internal state must be derivable from frame value (Goal 2 / rf2-edi resolved).

The pseudocode does not need to be a full impl -- just enough that the AI knows which Reagent primitives bridge to which contract functions and what the wiring looks like.

LEVERAGE FOR rf2-5pt:
Without this, the AI has to know Reagent well enough to invent the bridging. With it, the AI can produce the adapter from pseudocode and a Reagent dependency.

FILES:
- 006-ReactiveSubstrate.md: new §Reference adapter (pseudocode) appendix
- Possibly 002-Frames.md: cross-reference from the View ergonomics section

PAIRS WITH:
rf2-5pt (one-shot bar -- primary motivation), rf2-edi (closed; revertibility audit -- documents the adapter-internal state rule), rf2-vf8m (multi-impl -- a JS impl will write its own adapter; the spec needs to show what the contract realisation looks like for one host).

WHY P1: gates one-shot CLJS implementation; without the bridge the contract floats. Estimated effort: small focused write -- ~100 lines of pseudocode + a few notes.

Plus three cross-cutting subsections: §Sub-cache wiring (how reg-sub registrations realise as Reagent reactions, with v1-source-as-reference annotation, hot-reload and frame-teardown behaviour spelled out); §Frame-provider via React context (the provider component, plain-fn-under-non-default-frame warning detection, cross-ref to 002 for the read-side); §Plain-atom adapter (JVM, SSR, headless) (how it differs — no caching, render throws, no context provider, trivially revertibility-compliant). title: Add Runtime-Architecture.md — birds-eye view that ties the runtime components together
description:
No single doc currently shows the runtime as a coherent whole. The runtime is described piecewise across 002 (frames), 005 (machines), 006 (substrate), 009 (instrumentation), 010 (schemas). An AI implementing CLJS has to assemble the picture from fragments. A one-page Runtime-Architecture.md companion doc gives the missing birds-eye view.

CONTENTS:

A single page describing runtime components and relationships.

Components:
- The registry (per-kind: :event, :sub, :fx, :cofx, :machine-action, :machine-guard, :route, :head, :error-projector)
- The router (event queue per frame; FIFO; drain loop)
- The drain loop (the four Levels in 005, how it processes one event end-to-end)
- The frame container (one atom per frame holding app-db plus runtime state)
- The sub-cache (per-frame cache of computed sub values; invalidated by app-db changes)
- The trace bus (per-process trace event stream; listeners batched at debounce window)
- The fx interpreter (do-fx walks :fx vector in source order)
- The interop layer (re-frame.interop -- clock primitives, native scheduling, host-clock now-ms)

For each component: inputs and outputs, key invariants, how other components see it, one-line cross-reference to the canonical Spec.

Plus a single diagram (ASCII art works) showing the data flow:
dispatch -> envelope -> router -> drain -> handler -> effects -> :db write -> sub-cache invalidate -> view re-render.

V1 REFERENCE:
re-frame v1 has a working runtime; an AI implementing CLJS can read v1 source for component implementation. What is NEW for re-frame2 and worth documenting explicitly: frames as a layer, machines integration into the dispatch pipeline, the trace surface as a first-class component, the substrate adapter boundary. v1 does not need a runtime-architecture doc because the code IS the doc; for re-frame2 (especially non-CLJS implementors per rf2-vf8m), the doc has to exist.

LEVERAGE FOR rf2-5pt:
Probably the highest-leverage missing artefact. Without it, an AI implementing has to reverse-engineer the runtime from contracts and prose. With it, the AI has the architecture diagram in front of them.

title: First-class HTTP response contract for SSR — close the response-correctness gap
description:
The current 011-SSR.md spec has :rf.server/set-status but doesn't treat the full HTTP response as a first-class output. Modern SSR frameworks (Next.js, React Router, Astro, Nuxt, SvelteKit) all expose status / headers / cookies / redirect as explicit response shapes that handlers can populate during SSR.

Without this, re-frame2 SSR is 'HTML + state' but not 'full HTTP response' — incomplete for production use cases that need correct 404/401/302/500 behavior, cache-control, Set-Cookie, redirects, etc.

## Concrete benefit

- Correct HTTP status codes for SSR pages (404, 401, 302, 500).
- Cache-control and other response headers.
- Set-Cookie support.
- Redirects as part of render/load control flow.
- Portable adapter boundary across server hosts (Express, Ring, Fastify, etc.).

## Fit with re-frame2

- It's data, not magic — fits the data-over-magic ethos.
- Response policy stays enumerable and testable.
- Matches the per-request frame model — each request frame owns its response shape.
- Avoids pushing server behavior into host-specific glue code.
- Respects the event/fx architecture: response is just another explicit output of the request frame.

## Mechanism

A response accumulator owned by the request frame:

  {:rf/response
   {:status   200
    :headers  {"content-type" "text/html; charset=utf-8"}
    :cookies  []
    :redirect nil}}

Standard server-only fx:

- :rf.server/set-status      — set the response status code
- :rf.server/set-header       — replace a header (case-insensitive)
- :rf.server/append-header    — append (e.g., Set-Cookie can have multiple)
- :rf.server/set-cookie       — structured cookie map (name, value, max-age, secure, etc.)
- :rf.server/delete-cookie    — clear a named cookie
- :rf.server/redirect         — set status + Location; truncates HTML render

The request handler returns a structured result:

  {:html     "<!doctype html>..."
   :payload  hydration-payload
   :response response-map}

The host adapter consumes :response to build the actual HTTP response.

## Open design calls

1. **Redirect precedence over normal HTML render.** If a handler emits :rf.server/redirect mid-render, does the HTML get truncated and only the redirect goes out? Lean: yes — redirects take precedence over rendering, and the runtime emits no HTML body when :redirect is set.

2. **Multiple status setters.** If two handlers in the drain both emit :rf.server/set-status, last-write-wins or first-write-wins or warn? Lean: last-write-wins (standard re-frame semantics for :db) but emit a :rf.warning/multiple-status-set trace.

3. **Header replacement vs append.** :rf.server/set-header replaces; :rf.server/append-header adds another instance. Document both explicitly. Deduplication is left to the host adapter.

4. **Cookie shape.** Structured maps ("good") vs raw header strings ("escape hatch")? Lean: structured maps as canonical with a known shape; the host adapter serialises to wire format. Avoids cookie-attribute quoting bugs.

5. **Status defaults.** Implicit default 200 when no handler sets a status; explicit Content-Type header default; what content-type for error pages?

## Files to update when actioning

- 011-SSR.md: new §HTTP response contract; document the :rf/response slot; document the six standard fx; document the request-handler return shape; document the open-call resolutions.
- Spec-Schemas.md: add :rf/response schema; add :rf.server/cookie schema; six fx-args schemas.
- API.md: add the six :rf.server/* fx rows; add the :rf/response sub.
- conformance/fixtures/: minimum 3 fixtures: ssr-redirect.edn (handler emits redirect; verify :status 302 and :location header), ssr-set-status.edn (handler emits 404; verify :status 404), ssr-cookie.edn (handler sets a cookie; verify :set-cookie header in response).
- 009-Instrumentation.md: new :rf.warning/multiple-status-set warning category.

## Why P1 (not P2)

This is correctness for the AI-implementability goal (rf2-5pt). A JS or Python implementor of re-frame2 shouldn't have to invent the response contract; the spec defines it. Without it, conformance is 'renders HTML' but not 'serves HTTP correctly' — a real production gap.

## Pairs with

- rf2-5pt (AI can one-shot the implementation) — closes a major gap in the SSR contract.
- rf2-vf8m (multi-impl org) — re-frame-cljs and re-frame-js need the same response contract for cross-impl conformance.
- 011 existing :rf.server/set-status — extends, doesn't replace.

Status: open. Design largely locked; five open calls flagged for resolution at action time. Estimated effort: medium focused agent pass.
close_reason: Specced HTTP response contract for SSR: :rf/response accumulator, six :rf.server/* fx, request-result shape, locked redirect/multi-status/header/cookie/default behaviours; schemas, API rows, three conformance fixtures, multiple-status-set warning.

title: Navigation epoch — suppress stale async results from superseded routes
description:
When a route is loading and the user navigates away before the load completes, the old loads result can land after the user has moved on, clobbering newer state. This is a real bug class that React Router and TanStack Router both explicitly handle. The current 012-Routing.md spec doesnt address it.

This is the SAME PATTERN as the epoch-based stale-detection just locked for `:after` (rf2-f6g5, closed). The runtime increments a counter on state-change; async events carry the counter at scheduling time; on receipt, the runtime checks current vs carried; mismatch → ignored. The pattern travels naturally from `:after` to navigation.

## Concrete benefit

- Closes a real correctness bug: older loads cant overwrite newer state.
- No new cancellation primitive needed — staleness detection is enough for the user-visible bug.
- Hosts that DO support abortable fetches can also abort superseded work — but suppression alone fixes the visible problem.

## Mechanism

When a route becomes active, the runtime allocates a navigation token (epoch). Each `:on-match` dispatch receives the token in coeffects:

```clojure
{:route/id :route/article
 :params   {:id "123"}
 :query    {}
 :transition :loading
 :nav-token "nav-42"}
```

Async completions must either:
1. Carry the token in their follow-up event, or
2. Use framework-provided fx wrappers that attach it automatically.

If the carried token no longer matches the current route token, the result is ignored (and emits a `:route.nav-token/stale-suppressed` trace event for debugging — same pattern as `:machine.timer/stale-after` in `:after`).

Hosts that support abortable fetches MAY also abort in-flight work for superseded tokens. Conformance only requires suppression of stale commits.

## Implementation sketch

- `:rf/url-changed` event allocates a new `:nav-token` (gensym or counter).
- Route slice in app-db gains `:nav-token`:
  ```clojure
  {:id :route/article
   :params {:id "123"}
   :query  {}
   :transition :loading
   :nav-token "nav-42"}
  ```
- `:on-match` events receive the token in coeffects (`(:nav-token (:cofx ctx))`).
- A new fx wrapper `:rf.route/with-nav-token` automatically threads the token into the dispatched continuation event:
  ```clojure
  {:fx [[:rf.route/with-nav-token
         {:do [:dispatch [:my-handler ...]]
          :nav-token current-token}]]}
  ```
- On the receiving handler, framework-provided cofx checks the carried token against the current route token; mismatch raises `:rf.route/nav-token-stale` (silent — emits trace, no transition).

## Files to update when actioning

- 012-Routing.md: new §"Navigation tokens — stale-result suppression"; document the epoch allocation, token-in-cofx, the fx wrapper, the trace event.
- Spec-Schemas.md: extend `:rf/route-slice` with `:nav-token`; add the wrapper fx schema.
- conformance/fixtures/: new fixture `route-stale-nav-token-suppression.edn` — load route A; navigate to route B before A finishes; A finishes; verify the late result is suppressed; verify the trace shows `:route.nav-token/stale-suppressed`.
- 009-Instrumentation.md: add the new trace event type.

## Why P1

Correctness, not polish. This is a real bug class users hit constantly in production. Re-frame2 should ship with this story locked.

## Pairs with

- rf2-f6g5 (closed; `:after` epoch-based stale detection) — same idiom; this bead applies it to navigation.
- See also the cross-cutting "async stale-detection pattern" bead for the meta-pattern across `:after`, navigation, and future async features.
- rf2-5pt (AI can one-shot) — without this, the conformance bar for "route loading" is broken.

Status: open. Design locked; ready to action. Estimated effort: medium focused agent pass.

title: Deterministic route ranking — close URL-match correctness gap
description:
The current 012-Routing.md spec defines the path grammar (path syntax, params, rest segments) but does NOT specify a full ranking rule for when multiple registered routes could match the same URL. This is a correctness gap that directly blocks the AI-one-shot goal (rf2-5pt) — two implementations of `match-url` can both be "reasonable" and still disagree on which route wins for an ambiguous URL.

Mature routers solve this by ranking specificity:
- TanStack Router sorts by route-pattern specificity at registration.
- Vue Router supports expressive matching and therefore needs deterministic resolution.

## Concrete benefit

- Strengthens the pure `match-url` contract — same URL, same registrations, same match across implementations.
- Improves cross-host conformance — a CLJS impl and a JS impl produce identical results on the conformance corpus.
- Helps AI generation — route conflicts become predictable instead of relying on registration-order folklore.
- Catches developer mistakes — registering routes that shadow each other can be detected at registration time.

## Locked ranking algorithm (proposed)

When multiple registered routes match the same URL, rank by:

1. **More static segments beat fewer static segments.** `/users/me` beats `/users/:id`.
2. **Among equally-static-counted matches, longer paths beat shorter.** `/users/:id/edit` beats `/users/:id`.
3. **Named params beat rest params.** `/files/:name` beats `/files/*rest`.
4. **Rest params beat catch-all/not-found routes.** `/files/*rest` beats `/*`.
5. **Exact routes beat routes that rely on optional groups.** `/about` beats `/{:base}?/about`.
6. **Registration order is the final tiebreak only if every structural score is equal.** Discouraged — a warning at registration time when two routes have equal scores.

## Implementation

- `match-url` MUST use this ranking. Spec the algorithm in pseudocode in 012.
- The conformance corpus gets ambiguous-path fixtures: registrations with overlapping patterns; verify the same URL matches the same route across implementations.
- Tooling can warn at registration when routes have equal scores or when one shadows another.

## Files to update when actioning

- 012-Routing.md: new §"Route ranking algorithm" with the 6-rule cascade; pseudocode; warning category for shadow detection.
- Spec-Schemas.md: optionally add `:rf/route-rank` schema if the rank is exposed via tooling.
- conformance/fixtures/: new fixture `route-ranking-precedence.edn` with an ambiguous-pattern set; verify deterministic match.
- API.md: add new `:rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score` warning category.

## Why P1

This is correctness, not polish. Without the ranking lock, two implementations cannot be expected to agree, which defeats the point of cross-impl conformance. The fix is small (a defined algorithm); the win is large (deterministic cross-host behaviour).

## Pairs with

- rf2-5pt (AI can one-shot the implementation) — the conformance corpus is the verification engine; route ranking is one of the determinism requirements.
- rf2-vf8m (multi-impl org) — when re-frame-cljs and re-frame-js both ship, ranking is what keeps them in sync.

Status: open. Design locked; ready to action. Estimated effort: small focused agent pass.

title: Hierarchical compound states — substantive design work (drain-rule extensions, transition resolution across levels)
description:
Spawned from rf2-g1h. The capability matrix in 005 claims hierarchical compound states for v1, but the substantive design work is not landed in this pass. Required:

1. Drain-rule extensions for cascading entry/exit along the path (entering :a.b.c fires :a/entry then :b/entry then :c/entry; leaving fires :c/exit then :b/exit then :a/exit). Extends Level 2 of the four-level drain.
2. Deep state-id resolution semantics — :state field as either a flat keyword (current) or a vector / dotted-keyword path (post-extension). Snapshot shape extension.
3. Transition resolution across compound levels — bubbling: a transition for an event in a child state, if not handled, looks up at the parent. Precedence rules.
4. Schema additions in Spec-Schemas.md for nested :states.
5. Conformance fixtures: hierarchical-entry-exit, hierarchical-deep-target, hierarchical-transition-resolution.

Pairs with rf2-g1h (capability matrix) which claimed the capability without landing the substantive work.

title: Documentation voice: human is marketing/philosophy, AI is dry/precise
description:
Per Mike's directive on the two-track docs (rf2-doc-split):

HUMAN VERSION — marketing-oriented:
- Explains the philosophy and the reasons behind design choices
- Communicates the benefits (why this pattern, what it gives you)
- Includes enough technical detail to be useful, but not exhaustive
- Inherits re-frame's existing voice — opinionated, conversational, sometimes philosophical
- Read by humans evaluating, adopting, or building with re-frame2

AI VERSION — dry and precise:
- No narrative, no rationale, no marketing
- Just contracts, signatures, shapes, semantics, fixtures, prompts
- Optimised for AI consumption: read-and-act
- Aligns with the existing Construction-Prompts / Spec-Schemas / MIGRATION / conformance artefacts which are already in this register

The two are not redundant — they cover the same design but at different abstraction levels and for different consumers. A human reads the human track to understand WHY; an AI reads the AI track to know WHAT and HOW PRECISELY.
close_reason: Voice direction captured in memory rf2-doc-voice and now demonstrated across 8 chapters in docs/guide/. Three voice registers used: argumentative/philosophical (01, 08, with Perlis/Dijkstra epigraphs); code-led narrative (02, 03, 04, 05, 06); migration narrative (07). Voice inherits re-frame's existing tone — opinionated, conversational, sometimes rhetorical. The AI track (docs/specification/) remains in the dry/precise register it was already in, so the contrast is clear.

title: [epic] xray frame-singleton: parameterize the shell frame + capture-not-hardcode the frame in callbacks (enable N isolated instances)
description:
ROOT CAUSE (live pair-session RCA 2026-05-29, Mike). The {:frame :rf/xray} envelope strewn across Xray view code is the visible symptom of a SINGLETON-FRAME LOCK. re-frame2 resolves a dispatch/subscribe target frame from AMBIENT context (dynamic var *current-frame* -> React context -> :rf/default), which only exists DURING synchronous render. Xray panels ARE reg-views wrapped in [rf/frame-provider {:frame :rf/xray}] (shell.cljs:2354), so render-time subscribes resolve to the frame via React context with NO explicit opt. The explicit {:frame :rf/xray} appears only where the context tier is NOT in scope: (1) a component rendered outside its own provider (shell-view own subs, shell.cljs:2274); (2) raw DOM listeners (resizable_table.cljs:326-329, window pointer-move); (3) affordance click handlers using global rf/dispatch (copy/zoom/popup). In all three the frame must be supplied explicitly — and the code supplies the LITERAL :rf/xray, plus the shell hardcodes its provider frame-id, plus reg-frame :rf/xray and register-xray-handlers! assume the one frame. That literal is a singleton assumption baked throughout.
WHY IT MATTERS (latent correctness bug, not just a smell): Xray can be multi-instance. The panel gallery (Story for Xray) mounts multiple Xray instances on one page. Evidence in tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/panel_views.cljs: the PER-PANEL variants ([app-db-diff/Panel] etc.) mount bare and resolve their frame from Story per-variant frame-provider via React context (docstring 10-12, 110-112) -> correctly ISOLATED (two variants show two states). The FULL-SHELL variants (chrome-shell -> shell/shell-view) re-wrap in hardcoded [frame-provider {:frame :rf/xray}], so per the docstring (38-42) the shell reads land on :rf/xray REGARDLESS of the outer variant frame; lines 201-202 confirm Story workspaces mount multiple chrome cells side-by-side -> they ALL COLLIDE on the one :rf/xray frame (cannot show distinct states; driving one drives all). The gallery surrenders to the singleton (seeds :rf/xray directly) and only patches the modal-overlap symptom (rf2-om6fa :modal-positioning :absolute). So multi-instance is broken for the shell and already-correct for the panels — same repo, both patterns side by side.
LINEAGE: the recurring frame-leak bug class (rf2-7sdja popup, rf2-y59tb triangle toggle, rf2-kcaiz zoom — all CLOSED point-fixes that each added a {:frame :rf/xray} pin) and the open rf2-zl4rs (zoom dispatch) / rf2-aesni (coord-chip dispatch) are symptoms of this one root cause. Supersedes the earlier consolidate-{:frame :rf/xray} framing.
design: FIX = capture, do not hardcode (the framework-native pattern the per-panel gallery variants already prove). 1) Parameterize the shell frame: shell-view takes a frame-id (default :rf/xray for the production singleton) and wraps in [frame-provider {:frame that-id}]; ensure-xray-frame!/reg-frame and register-xray-handlers! become frame-id-parameterized — handlers register GLOBALLY once (re-frame2 registry is not per-frame), so only the frame-id for app-db isolation needs threading. 2) Out-of-render dispatches capture the surrounding frame at render time via the reg-view-injected (dispatcher) / frame-bound-fn (closes over the instance frame), threaded to affordances (copy/zoom/popup/coord-chip) and raw window listeners — NOT global rf/dispatch, NOT a literal. The expand-triangle on-toggle already does this (uses the threaded captured dispatch-fn); make every affordance match it. 3) REJECTED: a single xray-dispatch helper that bakes in :rf/xray (option-A from the RCA discussion) — it ENTRENCHES the singleton and makes multi-instance permanently impossible. 4) Add a guard (clj-kondo hook or test) flagging a bare {:frame :rf/xray} literal or a global rf/dispatch inside an :on-* handler under tools/xray, so the singleton/leak cannot regress. TEMPLATE: panel_gallery/panel_views.cljs per-panel mounts (context-resolved, isolated) are the reference; chrome-shell (hardcoded :rf/xray) is the anti-pattern to retire.
acceptance_criteria: Two full Xray shell instances on one page (e.g. two panel-gallery chrome-shell cells / a Story workspace) maintain INDEPENDENT state — distinct focused epoch, tab, theme; driving one does not move the other. No hardcoded :rf/xray literal remains in the panels/affordances except the single production default frame-id passed once to shell-view. Every out-of-render dispatch (callbacks, raw window listeners, components outside their provider) resolves to the surrounding instance frame via a captured dispatcher, not a literal. A clj-kondo/test guard rejects new bare {:frame :rf/xray} literals + global rf/dispatch in :on-* handlers under tools/xray. The closed frame-leak point-fixes (rf2-7sdja/y59tb/kcaiz) and the open rf2-zl4rs/aesni dispatch concerns are covered structurally (verify + cross-close/annotate). tools/xray/spec/* + relevant /spec frame-capture guidance (Spec 002/004/006) updated. Likely splits into shell-parameterization, affordance-capture, and guard sub-tasks.
notes: CORE MERGED via PR #2403 (sub-beads lnluk/r0o63/tzy0b all closed): shell-view frame-id parameterized (default :rf/xray), captured-dispatcher threaded through affordances + raw listeners, JVM frame_singleton_guard_test added, two_instance_isolation_cljs_test PASSES (two shells on one page = independent state). Handlers stay process-global; only frame-id threads. rf2-7sdja/y59tb/kcaiz structurally covered. REMAINING (EPIC stays OPEN): ~35 unmigrated panel {:frame :rf/xray} literals on the guard's pending-migration allowlist — behaviour-preserved (default to production :rf/xray via shared helper), so NOT a live bug; they only lack multi-instance readiness. Folded into rf2-nesy9 scope (mayor rec: defer to the sweep; awaiting Mike confirm). EPIC CLOSES when the allowlist is empty (multi-instance complete for ALL panels).
close_reason: EPIC complete. The rf2-nesy9 sweep burned the frame_singleton_guard pending-migration allowlist down to EMPTY (35 -> 0): every Xray panel / modal / static surface now resolves its out-of-render dispatches to the surrounding instance frame (reg-view-injected dispatch / threaded dispatch-fn / render-time current-frame for plain-call helpers / handler-entry current-frame for async continuations). The ONLY :rf/xray references left are the named defaults/default-frame-id Var used by the production-singleton infra seams (note-suppressed!, share-URL on-load restore, per-feature hydrate!) which have no surrounding render/event frame. Two full Xray shells on one page maintain INDEPENDENT state (two_instance_isolation_cljs_test + multi_frame_isolation_e2e PASS). The JVM source-text guard rejects any new bare {:frame :rf/xray} literal / global rf/dispatch in :on-* handlers + an allowlist-honesty test keeps the allowlist empty. Closed frame-leak point-fixes (rf2-7sdja/y59tb/kcaiz) covered structurally. PR #2406. Specs 008+017 updated.

title: xray/edn-inspector: collapse to a single value + optional-before renderer (remove full/diff modes, full-with-diff? flag, plain :diff lens)
description: Mike decision, live pair session 2026-05-29 (explicit): the edn-inspector should have ONE rendering path, not three modes. Inputs: value (ALWAYS) + before (OPTIONAL). before present -> full tree WITH inline diff annotations (the current full+diff / mode-3). before absent -> render value plainly, no annotations (the no-diff case: there is no before/after pair, just a value to show). "full" is no longer a mode — it is the single renderer with no pre-image; "diff" (the plain per-leaf lens) goes away. Extends rf2-vv3m6 (which retired the toggle UI but left the mode machinery). REMOVE: (1) the full-with-diff? flag (15 uses across views/edn_inspector.cljs, panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs, panels/machine_inspector.cljs, panels/epoch/view.cljs) — it only existed to distinguish the plain :diff lens (mode-2) from full+diff (mode-3); with one path it is always-on, so delete it; (2) the plain :diff lens (mode-2 — per-leaf-focused, suppresses the structural rail/chip chrome); (3) the browse-vs-diff branch in app_db_diff_state.cljs (the (= h/no-diff before) split into two ei/edn-inspector calls) — collapse to one call that passes :before only when present. KEEP the (contains? opts :before) check, but reframe the mental model from "diff mode?" to "is there a before to annotate against?".
design: Single-renderer contract: value required, before optional; annotation conditional on before presence; one auto-collapse/expand heuristic; the mode-3 rail/chip becomes the only chrome. LIKELY SUBSUMES / must check + close: rf2-xuyac (bespoke diff-paths walker still serves the :diff lens on 2/4 surfaces — removing the lens makes the Editscript engine the sole diff source) and rf2-5j7ch (:diff lens wholesale-root-replacement bug — moot if the lens is gone). REFRAMES rf2-6cm03 (spec/021 §9.1.5 silent on :full-with-diff? opt contract — with the flag removed, the spec should document the single value+optional-before renderer contract instead). Sequence BEFORE the zoom rework (rf2-zl4rs): zoom-active? logic simplifies once there is a single render path.
acceptance_criteria: edn-inspector exposes ONE rendering path (value + optional before). full-with-diff? flag removed from the codebase. plain :diff lens code paths removed. app_db_diff_state renders via a single ei/edn-inspector call (before passed only when present). A value with no before renders plainly (no annotations, no rail/chip); a value with a before renders annotated. rf2-xuyac / rf2-5j7ch checked and closed if mooted; rf2-6cm03 updated to the single-renderer contract. tools/xray/spec/* updated for the new contract. Tests: existing :diff-lens / full-with-diff? tests removed or migrated; add a no-before value-only render test + a with-before annotated render test.
close_reason: Collapsed edn-inspector to single value+optional-before renderer; removed full-with-diff? flag (14→0 uses) + plain :diff lens (mode-2) + browse-vs-diff branch in app_db_diff_state. PR #2402. Gates: tools/xray clojure -M:test 965/3804 0-fail; CLJS node 4824/15802 0-fail; xray-feature-gate 14 scenarios 0-fail; fast-pr PASS. Preserved #2401 :added?/first-run. Rewrote spec/021 §10.0.12.

title: xray/app-db: zoom glyph renders in diff mode but is inert (affordance should stay off when :before present)
description: In the App-DB panel the per-container zoom-in glyph (the lucide circle / zoom affordance from rf2-h71e0) renders but clicking it does nothing whenever the panel is showing a diff — i.e. a focused epoch with changes, :before present. This is NOT rf2-kcaiz (CLOSED, PR #2190): that frame-leak is fixed and the click now correctly dispatches :rf.xray.edn-inspector/zoom-to with an explicit {:frame :rf/xray} envelope. Root cause: the App-DB DIFF branch passes :zoomable? true (panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:264) and the edn-inspector widget self-suppresses zoom RESOLUTION when :before is present (diff force-expand and zoom hide-outside-subtree are conflicting intents, rf2-h71e0) — but it still RENDERS the glyph. The code comment at app_db_diff_state.cljs:260-264 states the intended UX explicitly: the affordance + breadcrumb should stay OFF until the operator returns to current-state (non-diff) browse. The affordance does NOT stay off; only resolution is suppressed, so the operator sees a clickable glyph that no-ops. Zoom still works in the current-state (no-diff) BROWSE branch (app_db_diff_state.cljs:222-242). Found via live pair session 2026-05-29 on examples/step-deck at http://localhost:8031/counter (App-DB tab, viewing the increment epoch diff).
design: Gate the zoom-button RENDER on (not diff?) in render-container (views/edn_inspector.cljs near line 1785, where zoom-button = (when (and zoomable? (not empty?)) ...)); diff? is already destructured in render-container arg map. This makes the glyph stay off in diff mode exactly as the app_db_diff_state.cljs:260-264 comment already promises, instead of rendering an inert affordance. The breadcrumb row is already gated on zoom-active? (which cannot be active in diff mode), so no change is needed there. Fixing it in the widget covers every :zoomable? + :before consumer uniformly, not just App-DB.

title: xray/epoch/subscriptions: active sub-name click-to-source glyph is inert (decorative icon, not coord-chip)
description: In the Epoch panel SUBSCRIPTIONS table, the sub-name (left) column shows a to-source / external-link glyph after the sub id, but clicking it does nothing. The sibling surfaces already do it right: the disposed-subs table (view.cljs ~3167) and the views rows (~3311, ~3380) both use (coord-chip/coord-chip (sub-coord sub-id) ...). The sub-coord helper (view.cljs ~3093, resolves (rf/handler-meta :sub sub-id) to {:file :line}) already exists and is already consumed by the disposed-subs table. Use sub-id (the keyword) for the coord lookup even when sub-vec drives the display label, so parameterized subs ([:counter/greater-than? 5]) resolve their registration coord. title: xray/diff: empty-collection leaves inside :added subtree misclassified as :same (covers [], {}, #{}, '())
description:
Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-29: inside a wholly-added subtree, empty-collection leaves (`[]`, `{}`) render `:same` (muted) instead of `:added` (green). They are the only paths in the subtree that lie to the operator — every other leaf is honestly green.

## Live evidence

step-deck testbed, epoch 2 (`[:ws/connection [:ws/noop]]`), HANDLER step `:db` section, FULL+DIFF mode. The cascade allocates `:rf/runtime` (absent before → populated after):

| Path | `data-rf-diff-op` | Should be |
|---|---|---|
| `:rf/runtime` | `added` ✓ | `:added` |
| `:rf/runtime :machines` | `children` ✓ | `:children` |
| `:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots :ws/connection :state` (`:disconnected`) | `added` ✓ | `:added` |
| `:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots :ws/connection :data :connections` (`0`) | `added` ✓ | `:added` |
| **`:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots :ws/connection :data :messages` (`[]`)** | **`same` ✗** | **`:added`** |
| **`:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots :ws/connection :rf/spawn-counter` (`{}`)** | **`same` ✗** | **`:added`** |

Two paths out of the entire :rf/runtime subtree mis-classify; both are empty-collection leaves.

## Root cause

Editscript treats the **empty-collection-vs-absence equivalence** as no-diff. Comparing before-side (the path doesn't exist because its ancestor was missing) against after-side (an empty `[]`, `{}`, `#{}`, or `'()`), the engine emits no entry in the edit script. The projection's `op-at` then falls through to `:same` because there's no explicit entry.

The equivalence is not type-specific. Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-29 follow-up: the bug fires for any empty-collection leaf inside an added subtree — empty vec, empty map, **empty set** (`#{}` — common for machine `:tags`), and empty list. The witness paths in epoch 2 happened to be vec + map, but the engine's equivalence rule covers all four.

Contextually the path IS new — its container was just allocated. The operator's mental model says "everything under `:rf/runtime` was just added, including these empty slots." The rendering should match.

## Fix shape

The projection's `op-at` walks up the path before falling through. **If any ancestor in the projection is `:added` or `:removed`, the descendant inherits that classification** when no explicit edit-script entry exists for it.

Concretely:

  - `op-at projection [:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots :ws/connection :data :messages]`:
    - Direct lookup → no entry (Editscript empty-vs-absent equivalence).
    - Walk up: `:data` no entry, `:ws/connection` no entry, `:snapshots` no entry, `:machines` `:children`, `:rf/runtime` `:added`.
    - Return `:added` (the nearest non-:same / non-:children ancestor).

  - Similar for `:rf/spawn-counter {}`: inherits `:added` from the `:rf/runtime` ancestor.

  - Symmetric for `:removed`: a wholly-removed subtree where a path had an empty-collection value before would inherit `:removed`.

The inheritance does NOT cross `:same` containers — only `:added` and `:removed` propagate. `:children` (a container along the path with mixed descendants) does NOT propagate (descendants get their own classification).

## What changes

  - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine.cljc` (or wherever `op-at` lives) — when no edit-script entry exists for a path, walk up to find the nearest `:added` / `:removed` ancestor and return that.
  - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs` — the local op-classifier fallback at L1698-1711 already covers the missing-sentinel case for direct comparison; this fix is in the engine, not the fallback.
  - `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/diff_engine_consistency_cljs_test.cljc` — fixtures pinning the inheritance across all four empty-collection types:
    - `(engine/op-at (build-projection {} {:a {:b []}}) [:a :b]) ⇒ :added`         ;; empty vec
    - `(engine/op-at (build-projection {} {:a {:b {}}}) [:a :b]) ⇒ :added`         ;; empty map
    - `(engine/op-at (build-projection {} {:a {:b #{}}}) [:a :b]) ⇒ :added`        ;; empty set
    - `(engine/op-at (build-projection {} {:a {:b '()}}) [:a :b]) ⇒ :added`        ;; empty list
    - Symmetric `:removed` for each type (before-side empty-collection, after-side absent).
    - Same paths through deeper nesting (≥3 levels deep inside the added subtree).

## Acceptance

  1. step-deck epoch 2 (`:rf/runtime` allocation): `:messages []` and `:rf/spawn-counter {}` render with `:added` (green) chrome — same as every other leaf under `:rf/runtime`. No `:same` paint in a wholly-added subtree.
  2. Symmetric for wholly-removed: an empty-collection leaf inside a `:removed` subtree paints `:removed` (red), not `:same`.
  3. Mid-tree boundary: a `:same` container's descendants do NOT inherit (only `:added` / `:removed` propagate downward).
  4. Engine unit tests pin the four cases (empty vec / empty map; added / removed; direct and deeply-nested).
  5. No regression on existing diff-engine consistency tests.

## Scope

Single-file dominant (the engine). Test additions. Single PR. Pre-alpha — no shim, no flag.

## Related — diff-classification family

This is the third bead in the FULL+DIFF "engine knows the truth but the projection doesn't surface it" family:

  - rf2-9d4j8 — `{}` → populated app-db ROOT: top-level new keys paint `:modified` / `:same` instead of `:added`. Container-root case.
  - rf2-fyd8u — Scalar subs `nil → value` in SUBSCRIPTIONS FULL+DIFF render with no `← was nil` annotation. Sub-cache leaf case.
  - **(this)** — Empty-collection leaves inside an `:added` subtree paint `:same`. Inherited-classification case.

All three are operator-honesty fixes for FULL+DIFF. Mike likes the "sea of green" for wholly-added subtrees (pair-debug 2026-05-29) precisely because it's honest; this bead removes the only paths that lie inside it.

Pair-debug 2026-05-29.
close_reason: fixed in PR #2395 — empty-collection leaves classify :added/:removed via expand-leaf-paths + collect-leaves leaf-treatment; engine-only, no op-at walk-up needed

title: xray: retire [diff][full][full+diff] toggle — FULL+DIFF becomes the single rendering
description:
Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-29: the three-mode diff toggle `[diff][full][full+diff]` retires. **FULL+DIFF becomes the only rendering** across every Xray surface that today carries the toggle.

## Why

Recent work has made FULL+DIFF a complete lens:

- **rf2-fqcdd** — auto-collapse unchanged subtrees in FULL+DIFF; operator sees only root + change-ancestors expanded, achieving the density `:diff` used to provide.
- **rf2-fyd8u** (in flight) — leaf-scalar `← was X` annotation in FULL+DIFF; same conveyance `:diff` had for atomic value changes.
- **rf2-9d4j8** (in flight) — added/removed keys paint green/red correctly; covers the cases `:diff` was clearest at.

Mike's call: "I'm feeling very pleased with FULL+DIFF... we don't need the other two views Diff and FULL, in which case we don't need the button bar because we're just using one way."

## Surfaces affected
