title: xray FX step: swap fx-row-args mini -> edn-inspector with :default-expanded-depth 1
description:
Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-29: the FX step's per-row args render via `[ei/mini args 80]`, which collapses nested maps to `{…N keys}` with no way to drill. The operator can see `:rf.nav/scroll`'s `:strategy :top` but `:from {…1 keys}` and `:to {…1 keys}` hide the actual coordinates.

Sibling drift: the HANDLER step's `:fx` section (canonical vec-of-vecs) was switched to **edn-inspector FULL** in rf2-p2zy0. The FX step (per-fx-row breakdown with status + duration) still uses **mini**. Same data, two renderings.

## Fix — option (3): edn-inspector with `:default-expanded-depth 1`

Mike-ruled 2026-05-29: swap the FX-row args rendering from `mini` to the canonical edn-inspector widget with `:default-expanded-depth 1`. Top-level keys visible by default; nested maps collapse to `▸` chevrons; click to drill.

Posture:
- For scalar fx (`[:dispatch [:foo]]`, args is a vec of 1 item) the row stays compact.
- For map fx (`:rf.nav/scroll`'s `{:strategy :from :to}`) the row shows the top-level keys; nested `:from` and `:to` show as `{…1 keys}` collapsed but clickable.
- For nested fx (`:dispatch-later {:ms 250 :dispatch [...]}`) same shape — top-level keys visible, payload chevroned.

## Single change site

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs` `fx-row-view` (~L2865):

Today (L2906-2907):
```clojure
[:span {:style fx-row-args-style}
 [ei/mini args 80]]
```

After:
```clojure
[:span {:style fx-row-args-style}
 [ei/edn-inspector args
  {:site-id [:rf.xray.epoch/fx-row-args fx-id idx]
   :card? false
   :zoomable? true
   :default-expanded-depth 1}]]
```

`:site-id` carries the fx-id so expansion state is per-row (clicking expand on one row doesn't affect siblings). `:zoomable?` enables the popup-overlay affordance so power-users can zoom into a complex fx args map.

## Coordination with rf2-p2zy0

That bead's HANDLER `:fx` section already uses edn-inspector with `:default-expanded-depth 16` (fully expanded). They serve different needs:

- **HANDLER `:fx`** — the raw `:fx` vec-of-vecs returned by the handler. Full-expand makes sense; the operator is reading what the handler INTENDED.
- **FX STEP rows** — per-fx execution with status + duration in a table. Compact-with-drill makes sense; the table is dense + the operator scans rows then drills into one.

Both reads are legitimate, both use the same widget, different `:default-expanded-depth` per call site.

## What changes

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs` `fx-row-view` (one line swap + the new `:site-id` map).
- `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view_cljs_test.cljs` `fx-step-args-route-through-mini-test` — rename + update to expect `ei-mounts` (edn-inspector mount) instead of `mini-mounts`. The test's `:rf.xray.epoch/fx-row-args` site-id assertion pins the per-row identity.
- `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §FX step — note the edn-inspector rendering + `:default-expanded-depth 1` posture, sibling to the HANDLER `:fx` section's FULL posture.

## Acceptance

Clicking expands the nested map.
2. Same epoch, a `[:dispatch [:something]]` row renders compactly (single-line, no chevron needed).
3. `zoomable?` affordance opens the edn-inspector popup overlay when the user clicks the zoom chip.
4. Existing `fx-step-args-route-through-mini-test` updated to expect edn-inspector mount (rename to `fx-step-args-route-through-edn-inspector-test`).
5. No regression on HANDLER step's `:fx` section rendering (that path is untouched).

title: re-frame2 trace: :rf.sub/run :cause-event-id attribution (option b from Mike's ruling)
description:
Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-29: re-frame2's trace surface misattributes sub-runs to the WRONG event when one event chains another via `:rf.fx/dispatch` within the same router tick. The Epoch panel shows the cascade's reactive work credited to whichever event was on the stack when the reactive flush fired — not to the event whose `:db` commit was the actual cause.

## Live evidence

Probed via re-frame2-pair on step-deck (tab Counter, navigated from start):

| Epoch | Event | sub-runs | renders | Slice change | Counter writes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **3** | `[:rf.route/navigate :testdeck/counter]` | **0** | **0** | nil → `:testdeck/counter` | none |
| **4** | `[:rf.route/handle-url-change "/counter"]` | **9** | **5** | `:testdeck/counter` (no change) | none |

Epoch 3 wrote the slice. Epoch 4 was a no-op on the slice (and didn't touch `:counter` data at all). But all 9 counter subs recomputed AND 5 views rendered — attributed to epoch 4.

Reading epoch 4's panel as an operator: "handle-url-change made all the counter subs recompute" — wrong cause. The actual cause was epoch 3's `:db` write.

## Mechanism

Two coupled batching layers compound:

1. **Reagent's reaction batching.** Two `(reset! app-db ...)` calls in the same JS tick coalesce; reactions fire once. Load-bearing for perf — fundamental to React's rendering contract.

2. **Re-frame2's router tick.** `:rf.fx/dispatch` doesn't queue a fresh tick; it appends to the current router queue. Navigate's `:fx [[:dispatch [:rf.route/handle-url-change ...]]]` chains handle-url-change into the same drain. The reactive flush fires once at the end of the queue.

When the flush fires, the trace context names "the currently-dispatching event" — whichever event is on the router's stack. Sub-runs and renders get tagged with THAT event-id, not the upstream event whose `:db` commit was their actual input change.

## Fix — option (b): better trace attribution

Mike-ruled 2026-05-29: this is an ATTRIBUTION-ONLY fix, NOT a behavioural change. The physical reactive flush stays batched at end-of-tick (preserves Reagent's batching contract + re-frame2's per-tick perf model). Only the trace metadata is corrected.

(Option (a) — flush after each event — was considered and rejected as too costly: extra microtasks per tick, broken Reagent batching, double-renders for chained events.)

### What the fix does

Each `:rf.sub/run` trace event carries a `:cause-event-id` (or similar) tag identifying the event whose `:db` commit triggered the sub's re-evaluation. The Epoch panel uses this to ATTRIBUTE the sub-run to the correct epoch even when the physical execution happens during a later event's flush.

### Mechanism (sketch)

1. Each app-db write (the cascade's commit step) records the COMMITTING event-id alongside the value: `{<db-path> <committing-event-id>}` or a single `:rf.router/last-commit-event-id` slot.

2. When a sub re-evaluates and reads a slot, the reactive machinery looks up the last-committer for that slot.

3. The sub-run trace event carries `:cause-event-id` = the committer's event-id (or, when the sub reads multiple slots that changed in the tick, the most-recent committer — typically the upstream cause).

4. The projection layer (Xray's epoch projection) groups sub-runs by `:cause-event-id` rather than the trace's `:event-id` field that names the currently-executing event.

### Edge cases to think through at fix-time

- **Sub with multi-input cascade.** An L2 sub reads two L1s that were both written in the tick (by different events). Which event gets credit? Recommend: the MOST RECENT write (last db-commit before the sub re-evaluates).
- **Sub triggered by reagent-internal recompute, not db-write.** E.g., a sub whose input is a `r/track!` external to the framework. Cause-event-id is nil; falls back to current-event behaviour.
- **First-run.** Sub being cached for the first time has no prior db state to attribute against. Treat as caused by whichever event triggered the view mount (which is itself the result of the upstream db change). Likely converges with the multi-input case.
- **Restore-epoch / time-travel.** When restoring a snapshot, the synthetic event that drives the restore is the cause. Already covered by the same mechanism.

## What changes

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` (or wherever the cascade's commit step lives) — stamp committing event-id at db-write time.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/cache.cljc` (or the sub re-eval path) — read the committer, stamp `:cause-event-id` on the `:rf.sub/run` trace event.
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` — document the new tag. `:rf.sub/run` trace event grows the optional `:cause-event-id`.
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc` — when partitioning trace events into per-epoch records, sub-runs route to the epoch whose `event-id` matches `:cause-event-id` (falling back to the trace's `event-id` when `:cause-event-id` is nil).
- `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection_cljs_test.cljc` — fixtures pinning the attribution flow.

## Acceptance

1. `:rf.sub/run` trace events carry an optional `:cause-event-id` tag (present when the framework can identify the upstream db-committing event; absent for reagent-internal or pre-mount cases).
2. Live step-deck (navigate Counter from Initialise): epoch 3 (`[:rf.route/navigate :testdeck/counter]`) panel shows the 9 sub-runs and 5 renders. Epoch 4 (`[:rf.route/handle-url-change "/counter"]`) panel shows ZERO (or only handle-url-change's own legitimate sub-runs — typically zero).
3. Same shape across other event-chain patterns: `(reg-event-fx :do-it (fn [_ _] {:fx [[:dispatch [:follow-up]]]}))` — both events have their own attributed cascades in Xray.
4. Sub-runs that DON'T have an identifiable db-commit cause (reagent-internal, first-run, etc.) fall back gracefully to the currently-executing event-id.
5. Tests at `implementation/core/test/re_frame/router_cljs_test.cljc` (or appropriate location) pin the committer-tracking mechanism.
6. Tests at `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection_cljs_test.cljc` pin the projection routing.
7. NO behavioural change: physical reactive flush still batched at end-of-tick. NO extra microtasks. NO double-renders. Perf gates (`scripts/test-perf-bundle.sh`, etc.) green.

## Scope

Hot-zone-adjacent: spec/009 update. Core implementation touch (router + subs/cache). Tools-side projection update.

Pre-alpha posture: clean additive trace tag, no shim, no flag.

## Related

- Sibling to rf2-fyd8u (SUBSCRIPTIONS leaf-scalar annotation + `:first-run?` flag) — both improve the Epoch panel's honesty about sub lifecycle. The `:cause-event-id` tag and the `:first-run?` flag are independent additions to `:rf.sub/run`.
- Discovered while explaining the navigate/handle-url-change two-event dance on step-deck. The misattribution makes route-driven cascades especially confusing.

Consumer-side projection/rendering (epoch projector, Xray Epoch panel) deferred to follow-on bead rf2-1cc03. Quality gates green: core (795 tests / 3516 assertions), schemas (192/18251), CLJS (4845/15891), elision probe, mkdocs --strict, doc-slugs + readme-links, clj-kondo clean.

title: docs(the-mayor-method): Standard gate menu by surface in dispatch-prompt-template (rf2-uhd5d follow-on)
description:
Filed from audit rf2-uhd5d (ai/findings/worker-gate-audit-2026-05-28.md).

## Why

#2338 (eguy4 phase B+C, 251 files) hit 3 sequential CI red iterations because the worker's pre-PR gate list covered only the artefact whose `src/` changed, not the downstream consumers that `:require` the modified public surface. Iter 1 red: tools/story consumers. Iter 2 red: CLJS `:node-test` (adapters/reagent test). Iter 3 red: tools/story-mcp consumer. Each iter = ~15 min CI runner cost.

#2341 (merge-route-slice helper extraction in routing/events.cljc) showed the same gap latent: the worker ran `cd implementation/routing && clojure -M:test` only; the JVM consumer artefacts (schemas / machines / flows / http / ssr / ssr-ring / epoch) were caught by CI's surface fan-out, not by worker-side gating. No CI failure this time (extraction was non-breaking by construction) — but the false-confidence cost remains.

## Scope

Edit `docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md`. Add a "Standard gate menu by surface" block under the "Canonical pre-checkin quality gates" section, between the `test-fast-pr.sh` paragraph and the "PR-body Quality gates section — mandatory" section.

Proposed table rows (the findings doc §4.1 has the full draft; refine in PR):

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/*` → impl JVM matrix + reagent-slim bundle-isolation
- `tools/<tool>/src/*` → `cd tools/<tool> && clojure -M:test` + every dependent tool (TESTING.md S11+S12+S13) + `npm run test:cljs` if the tool has CLJS tests
- `tools/{story,xray}/spec/*.md` → mkdocs --strict ONLY (rf2-f79t8 spec-md guard; do NOT run the JVM/CLJS tool probes)
- `tools/template/*` → `cd tools/template && clojure -M:test` + emitted-app smoke
- `tools/mcp-conformance/*`, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/*`, `tools/mcp-base/*`, `tools/story-mcp/*` → MCP conformance suite from `tools/mcp-conformance/`

- `spec/conformance/fixtures/*.edn` → impl JVM matrix + `npm run test:cljs`

2. The block cites rf2-uhd5d + #2338 (3-iteration sequence) + #2341 (latent helper-extraction gap) as evidence.

description:

## Scope

- #2333 feat(http): :after middleware hook + reshape reg-http-interceptor (rf2-uheqq)
- #2334 refactor(spec): :rf/runtime contract — phase A (rf2-eguy4)

- #2336 fix(xray): mixed-type :path sort comparator (rf2-n83r8)

- #2339 docs(skills): :rf/runtime shape sweep across skill bundles (rf2-a9sex)

- #2342 docs(elision-axis): consolidated :rf/elision sweep across skills + spec (rf2-g2grf)
- #2343 fix(xray): broken reserved-keys-buffer fixture + 4 cleanups (rf2-3v3k9 + 4)

- #2345 docs(skills/xray): rewrite app-db panel to sectioned-by-reserved-area (rf2-ssgdq)

Plus 4 open (also audit gates):

- #2341 refactor(routing): merge-route-slice helper + prose drift (rf2-g8tzb + t7rjp) — CLEAN after infra-rerun
- #2346 chore(adapters/reagent): post-eguy4 prose + indent cleanup (rf2-vmv5g + z9h7v)
- #2347 fix(impl/tests): post-eguy4 :rf/route residue + fixture sweep (rf2-86wce + 3)
- #2348 feat(xray/subs): FULL+DIFF leaf-scalar annotation + :first-run? trace flag (rf2-fyd8u, P2)

## The two questions

### Q1 — Pre-PR worker gate discipline

Did each worker run the right set of tests BEFORE opening the PR, given the surface(s) the diff touched? TESTING.md (478 lines, canonical matrix) defines what gates should run for which surface changes. Compare each worker's reported `Gate results` against TESTING.md's coverage prescription.

### Q2 — CI gate coverage

Did CI run the right test surfaces for each PR? `.github/workflows/tests.yml` is the authoritative workflow; the differential-detection logic (`Detect changed test surfaces`) decides which gates run. Does the surface-detection give every PR the right gate set?

## Specific signals from this session worth investigating

1. **#2338 (eguy4 251-file)** — initially failed JVM tools/story + CLJS :node-test in CI; phase-B impl wrote new paths but tools/story/examples still read old. Worker had only run the artefact-local gate. **Pattern:** cross-artefact path-shape changes need a worker-side cross-artefact gate; CI caught it but worker didn't.

2. **#2338 second iteration** — still failed routing_history_cljs_test.cljs:535 after extension. Worker hadn't run the CLJS gate (`npm run test:cljs`).

3. **#2338 third iteration** — failed tools/story-mcp tools_test.clj:1300. Worker had not gated against story-mcp.

4. **#2341 (routing helpers)** — worker reported `cd implementation/routing && clojure -M:test` (122 tests / 552 assertions / 0 failures) ONLY. The PR triggers cross-artefact CI gates that include JVM core/schemas/flows/ssr/ssr-ring (consumers of the routing public surface). CI's setup-clojure infra-flake masked the actual question: would a real downstream breakage from `merge-route-slice` extraction have been caught by the worker? **Answer: no.** Worker gating ≠ CI surface coverage. Document this.

5. **#2347 (test-residue)** — worker ran `cd implementation/{epoch,http,ssr} && clojure -M:test` (correct for scope: test-prose-only edits across 3 artefacts).

6. **#2348 (fyd8u P2 — gold standard)** — worker ran core (792 tests), xray (957 tests), cljs (4845 tests), mkdocs --strict, check_doc_slugs, check_readme_links --ci, clj-kondo on 8 changed files. **This is the comprehensive shape we want for a multi-artefact PR.** The dispatch prompt explicitly listed every gate; copy-pastable into other dispatches.

7. **#2344 (core-elision)** — worker ran core + schemas. Correct: schemas consumes the elision walker.

## Acceptance — deliverables

### Deliverable 1: per-PR audit matrix (ai/findings/<name>.md)

For each of the 16 PRs above, a row with:

| PR | Worker gates run | CI gates run | Per TESTING.md should-have-run | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|

Source for each:

- **Worker gates run** — pull from the worker's final-report 'Gate results' section (in conversation transcript or the agentid output file under `%TEMP%/claude/.../tasks/`).
- **CI gates run** — `gh pr view <N> --json statusCheckRollup`.
- **Per TESTING.md** — derive from diff scope. `gh pr view <N> --files` for files; map files → artefact → TESTING.md gate list.
- **Gap** — diff between (worker-ran ∪ CI-ran) and (TESTING.md prescribes).

### Deliverable 2: pattern findings

Group the gaps into patterns:

- 'Cross-artefact path-shape change → worker gates only own artefact' (eguy4-style)
- 'Helper extraction → worker doesn't gate consumers' (#2341 hypothetical risk)
- 'Spec-document change → worker doesn't run mkdocs --strict' (any?)
- 'Test-only edits → worker over-gates by running CLJS bundle gates' (false-positive cost)

Document each pattern with the PR(s) that exhibit it and the cost (CI failure cycles, time lost, false confidence).

### Deliverable 3: action beads for each gap

For each pattern that needs structural change, file a follow-on bead. Candidates (do not pre-file — let the audit decide):

- **dispatch-prompt-template update** — add a 'standard gate menu by surface' block that workers paste verbatim, e.g.:
  - touching impl/<feat>/src → `cd implementation/<feat> && clojure -M:test` AND any artefact that `:require`s `<feat>`'s public surface
  - touching tools/<tool>/src → `cd tools/<tool> && clojure -M:test` AND any tool that depends on it
  - touching spec/* → mkdocs --strict + check_doc_slugs + check_readme_links
  - touching impl/core/src/.../subs/* → cljs gate (uses sub system)
  - touching shared protocols → ALL artefact gates
- **CI surface-detection refinement** — if certain file changes don't trigger downstream gates that they should, fix the workflow's surface detector.
- **TESTING.md clarification** — if the matrix is ambiguous about which gates apply to which surfaces, edit it.

## Workflow

This is a Mayor-friendly audit (read-only). Suggested execution:

1. Dispatch a worker with read-only tools (Explore/general-purpose).
2. Worker reads TESTING.md + .github/workflows/tests.yml + the PR list + each worker's transcript-side report.
3. Worker writes the matrix to ai/findings/worker-gate-audit-2026-05-28.md.
4. Worker files action beads via bd create.
5. Worker reports findings count + file path + action beads filed.

## Why P2

Three eguy4 iterations + the #2341 false-positive (rerun-burning resources on infra flake when CI gates wouldn't have caught the real failure mode) show real cost. A 30-min audit + prompt-template update could prevent the next 3-iteration PR.

title: xray/subs FULL+DIFF: leaf-scalar '<- was X' annotation + :first-run? trace flag
description:
Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-28: the SUBSCRIPTIONS table's "value" column in FULL+DIFF mode silently drops the change signal for scalar subs, and the trace data is ambiguous about a sub's lifecycle state at run time.

## The bug (UX side)

Live evidence (step-deck testbed, epoch 5 `[:inc]`):

- The `:counter/last-clicked` sub recomputed `nil → 1779972561856`.
- `value-changed?` is `true` on the run-record.
- In FULL+DIFF mode the value cell renders `1779972561856` — NOTHING ELSE. No "← was nil" annotation. Zero `data-rf-diff-op` attributes in the cell. The change is invisible.

Root cause: the cell mounts `[ei/edn-inspector after {:full-with-diff? true :before <prev>}]`. The mode-3 R1-R8 grammar paints diff annotations on container CHILDREN; a SCALAR root has no children, so the projection falls through to "just show the value." The `:before` is threaded in but the renderer has no leaf-level surface for it.

For containers this works (a `{:a 1}` → `{:a 1 :b 2}` change paints `:b` as `:added` inside the AFTER tree). For scalars (`nil → 1779972561856`, `0 → 1`, `"even" → "odd"`) there's no scaffolding to paint on.

## The bug (data side)

The sub-run carries `:prev-value` as a plain value. There is NO way for a consumer to distinguish:

  - Sub was cached with prev value `nil`, recomputed to `1779972561856` (value change), from
  - Sub was freshly created this epoch (first deref by a newly-mounted view), so there was no prev cache entry at all — `nil` reported because there is no other answer.

For the SUBSCRIPTIONS table, these need different chrome:

  - **Value change** — inline `← was X` annotation. The row tells a "from / to" story.
  - **First cache entry** — `:added` (+ green) chrome. The row tells a "this sub is now alive" story; there's no `was`.

Today's row data collapses both into the same shape (a row with `:prev-value nil` and `:value <new>`), so the view layer can't pick the right chrome even if it wanted to.

## Fix scope — three coupled changes

### 1. Trace-side data

Per Spec 009: the `:rf.sub/run` trace tags need a discriminator. Candidates:

  - `:first-run?` boolean — was this the run that CREATED the cache entry?
  - `:had-prev?` boolean — was there a prior cache entry to compare against?
  - `:sub-cache-state` enum — `:created | :recomputed | :unchanged`

Recommend `:first-run?` — minimal, boolean, names what the operator cares about. The framework already knows the answer at emit-time (the cache-lookup before-run either returns a slot or not).

### 2. Projection-side flag

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc` `sub-run-rows` (or wherever the row data flows from the trace stream) lifts `:first-run?` onto each row. Consumers read it via `(:first-run? row)`.

### 3. View-side rendering

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs` `subs-value-cell`:

In FULL+DIFF mode, for a row with `(:value-changed? row)` true:

  - **`(:first-run? row)` true** → render value with `:added` chrome (+ green stripe / leading + glyph, matching the mode-3 R1 :added shape). No "was" annotation.
  - **`(:first-run? row)` false** → render value, then an inline trailing annotation `← was <prev>` (using `ei/mini` for the prev). The "← was" prose stays in muted text-tertiary; the prev value picks up syntax-token chrome from `mini`.

For containers (sub returns a map / vector / set), keep the existing mode-3 grammar — the R1-R8 rules already paint child-level annotations there. The leaf-scalar path is the new branch.

In `:diff` mode (already shows `prev → value` via `mini` pair), no change — it already conveys the change.

In `:full` mode (no diff), no change — that mode deliberately ignores prev.

## Cross-references

  - Mode-3 grammar source: rf2-n2jig.
  - The container-side FULL+DIFF auto-collapse-unchanged work (rf2-fqcdd) lives in the same renderer; this bead extends the same code path to leaf scalars.
  - Related drift: rf2-9d4j8 (`{}` → populated app-db diff misclassifies new top-level keys as :modified instead of :added) is the CONTAINER analog of this leaf bug — both are "the framework knows the diff but the rendering doesn't surface it." Fix landings can be sequenced or paired.
  - Sub lifecycle: Spec 006 `:rf.sub/create` and `:rf.sub/run` are the relevant trace events. The `:first-run?` discriminator could derive from either (the substrate knows at run-time whether the sub's cache slot was just allocated).

## Acceptance

  1. `:rf.sub/run` trace events carry a `:first-run?` tag (true on the first run after a sub's cache slot is created; false on every subsequent run).
  2. The Epoch panel's sub-run row data carries `:first-run?` through the projection.
  3. step-deck epoch 5 (`[:inc]`), SUBSCRIPTIONS row for `[:counter/last-clicked]`, FULL+DIFF mode: cell renders `1779972561856 ← was nil` (inline annotation). Same row for `[:counter/value]`: renders `1 ← was 0`. Same row for `[:counter/parity]`: renders `"odd" ← was "even"`.
  4. A row that represents a first-cache-entry run (sub created this epoch by a freshly-mounted view) renders with `:added` (+ green) chrome and NO "was" annotation.
  5. Unit tests at `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection_cljs_test.cljc` pin the `:first-run?` flow through the projection.
  6. Unit tests at `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view_cljs_test.cljs` pin the two rendering branches: leaf-scalar value-change with `:first-run? false` → "← was X" annotation; leaf-scalar value-change with `:first-run? true` → + green chrome, no "was."
  7. No regression on existing FULL+DIFF container-diff tests (the R1-R8 grammar for nested containers is untouched).

## Scope

Hot-zone-adjacent (Spec 009 update for the trace tag). Touches:

  - spec/009-Instrumentation.md — document the `:first-run?` tag on `:rf.sub/run`.
  - spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md — cross-reference (the lifecycle that produces the flag).
  - implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs/* — emit the flag.
  - tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc — lift onto row.
  - tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs — render the two branches.
  - implementation/core/test/* + tools/xray/test/* — tests for both halves.

Pre-alpha posture: clean addition, no shim.

Discovered while exploring the canonical step-deck testbed; affects every L1-scalar sub whose value changed during a cascade.
notes:
Implemented + PR #2348 opened. Three coupled changes landed:

1. Trace-side: :rf.sub/first-run? boolean flag emitted by all three memo wrappers (layer-1, layer-n-1, layer-n) in subs/memo.cljc. Sourced from input-cell ::unset sentinel (not last-result) so the discriminator is well-defined even when the first cached value is nil. Spec 009 + Spec 006 cross-references added.

2. Projection: tools/xray epoch projection.cljc lifts :rf.sub/first-run? onto each row as :first-run?, defaulting to false for legacy traces.

3. View: subs-value-cell's :full+diff branch routes scalar returns (not map/vector/set/sequential) through new leaf-scalar surface — :first-run? true paints :added chrome (diff-added-stripe/wash tokens + leading +), :first-run? false paints inline '← was <prev>' annotation with ei/mini for prev. Containers keep existing inspector mount.

Tests: +3 deftests in core trace_cascade_captured_test.clj, +1 in xray projection_cljs_test.cljc, +4 in xray view_cljs_test.cljs.

Gates: core 792/0/0, xray 957/0/0, cljs 4845/0/0, mkdocs --strict clean, doc-slugs no broken links, readme-links ci 0, kondo 0 errors on changed files.

title: app-db: collapse 10 framework root keys into single :rf/runtime container with subsystem groups
description:
Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-28: the framework's app-db state today spreads across 10 root keys — 6 contracted + 4 out-of-contract :rf.route/* drift. Reshape to a SINGLE reserved root key :rf/runtime containing three subsystem sub-containers.

This bead supersedes rf2-3ib8h (which scoped only the routing half).

## Target shape

```clojure
:rf/runtime
  {:machines {:snapshots   {<id> -> :rf/machine-snapshot}
              :system-ids  {<system-id> -> <gensym-id>}
              :spawned     {<parent-id> -> <slot>}}

   :routing  {:current             {:id :params :query :transition :error :fragment :nav-token}
              :pending-navigation  <payload-or-absent>
              :scroll-positions    {<url> [x y]}
              :scroll-positions-order [<url> ...]
              :nav-token-counter   <int>
              :pending-nav-counter <int>}

   :elision  {:declarations           {<path-vec> {:large? :hint :source}}
              :sensitive-declarations {<path-vec> {:sensitive? :hint :source}}}}
```

## Decisions locked (Mike, 2026-05-28)

1. Single root `:rf/runtime` (vs flat siblings) — the `:rf/*` namespace already announces "framework-owned" but a structural container makes the framework's footprint in user app-db one key instead of ten, supports future-additive without root churn, and lets tools dump "all framework state" with one key read.
2. Subsystem name `:routing` (not `:route`) — matches `implementation/routing/`, `spec/012-Routing.md`. The slice sub-key is `:current`.
3. Counters stay flat under `:routing` (`:nav-token-counter`, `:pending-nav-counter`) — overkill to nest two ints under `:counters`.
4. `:pending-navigation` lives under `:routing` (subsystem-internal payload) — folds the historical `:rf/pending-navigation` reserved root into the routing sub-container.
5. `:rf/system-ids` and `:rf/spawned` (today separate framework roots) collapse into `[:rf/runtime :machines]` alongside `:snapshots` — they're machine-runtime-owned per Spec 005.
6. The 4 `:rf.route/*` out-of-contract keys (scroll-positions / scroll-positions-order / nav-token-counter / pending-nav-counter) move into `[:rf/runtime :routing]` (the original rf2-3ib8h scope, absorbed here).

## What changes — spec

- spec/Conventions.md §Reserved app-db keys: the table goes from 6 rows to ONE row. `:rf/runtime` is the sole reserved root with a value-shape spec pointing at the three sub-containers.
- spec/Spec-Schemas.md: a new `:rf/runtime` schema; old `:rf/machine-snapshot` / `:rf/route` / `:rf/pending-navigation` / `:rf/elision-registry` either move under the new container or get re-rooted as nested schemas.
- spec/005-StateMachines.md §Snapshot location: snapshots live at `[:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots <id>]` (was `[:rf/machines <id>]`). Every cross-reference threads through.
- spec/012-Routing.md: every reference to `:rf/route` becomes `[:rf/runtime :routing :current]`. The scroll-positions / nav-counter prose lands in the same section.
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md §Size elision: the registry lives at `[:rf/runtime :elision :declarations]`.

## What changes — implementation

Every read / write / restore-epoch / SSR-hydrate / migration-agent check that touches the old roots:

title: http-middleware: add :after response-side hook (decided rf2-omwua option b)
description:
Mike DECIDED 2026-05-28 (rf2-omwua option b): add an :after response-side hook to the re-frame.http-middleware contract. Overrules the audit's defer-to-post-v1 recommendation.

## Contract

Each registered HTTP interceptor gains an OPTIONAL :after fn alongside its :before:

  - :before — (fn [ctx] ctx')         — request-side, existing v1 surface
  - :after  — (fn [ctx response] response') — response-side, NEW

The :after fn receives:
  - ctx      — the SAME ctx shape the :before chain produced for this request ({:request :args :frame :event}). Carrying the request ctx into :after is what enables response-time telemetry (wall-clock delta between :before and :after) and request-correlated header parsing.
  - response — the response map as returned by the transport / decode step.

Returns the (possibly-transformed) response map.

## Ordering

:after fns run in REVERSE registration order — mirror of the event-interceptor before/after contract (Spec 002 / the -> then <- onion). Interceptor A registered before B: request flows A.before → B.before → transport; response flows B.after → A.after.

## Open sub-decision for the implementer (flag to Mike before coding)

How to thread :after into the registration signature. Current v1 is positional: (reg-http-interceptor id opts? before). Candidates:

  (i)  Positional 4th arg: (reg-http-interceptor id opts? before after?). Symmetric with :before but 4-arity positional is awkward + ambiguous with the opts arity.
  (ii) :after rides the opts map: (reg-http-interceptor id {:after (fn [ctx response] ...)} before). Keeps before positional; after is a kwarg. Asymmetric (before positional, after in opts).
  (iii) Reshape to a single interceptor map: (reg-http-interceptor id {:frame ... :before (fn ...) :after (fn ...)}). Fully symmetric, matches the event-interceptor {:id :before :after} shape. Pre-alpha posture allows the reshape (no back-compat). MOST consistent with the framework's own interceptor vocabulary.

Recommend (iii) — it aligns the HTTP middleware with the event-interceptor mental model the whole framework already uses, and pre-alpha means the positional-before v1 shape can be retired cleanly. But this is a public-surface shape call — confirm with Mike.

## Where the change lands

  - implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_middleware.cljc — reg-http-interceptor signature + valid-args?; the interceptors atom slot (:rf/http-interceptor-meta) gains an :after key; the response-side threading fn (reverse-order reduce over the chain's :after fns).
  - implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_managed.cljc (or wherever the response is assembled post-transport/decode) — call the :after chain on the response before dispatching :on-success / :on-failure.
  - spec/014 §Middleware — document the :after contract + ordering + ctx threading. Retire the 'After-style interceptors are out of scope for v1; the slot :after is reserved' prose in http_middleware.cljc:22-24.
  - spec/Spec-Schemas.md — :rf/http-interceptor-meta gains :after (optional fn).
  - implementation/http/test/ — new tests: :after runs reverse-order; :after sees the request ctx; response transform threads through; :after-less interceptors skip cleanly; the four cited use cases (rate-limit header parse, response-time telemetry, Cache-Control inspection, 401 auth-refresh) each have a smoke.

## Acceptance

  1. spec/014 §Middleware documents :after (fn [ctx response] response'), reverse-order, ctx-carried-from-before.
  2. spec/Spec-Schemas :rf/http-interceptor-meta carries optional :after.
  3. reg-http-interceptor accepts the chosen :after shape (sub-decision above, confirmed with Mike).
  4. Response threads through the :after chain in reverse registration order before :on-success / :on-failure fire.
  5. :after sees the same ctx the :before produced (request-correlation works — response-time telemetry test computes a non-nil wall-clock delta).
  6. Interceptors with no :after are transparent in the response chain.
  7. Tests for all four motivating use cases from rf2-omwua.

## Scope

Hot-zone: spec/014 + spec/Spec-Schemas. http artefact src + tests. Single PR.
Pre-alpha posture: clean contract, no shim.

Spec 014 + Spec-Schemas :rf/http-interceptor-meta + Spec 009 error catalogue updated in same commit. 4 motivating tests + 4 contract tests added; 273 http JVM tests + 789 core JVM tests pass. 8 call-sites swept.

title: Rewrite docs/guide from scratch — human-tutorial in Steve Yegge voice
description:
## Mandate

Rewrite `/docs/guide` from scratch. The current guide is AI-shaped; this rewrite is for **humans** — the developer reading a tutorial.

## Requirements

### Audience + voice

- **Humans, not AIs.** Tutorial, not reference. Story-shaped, not contract-shaped.
- **Steve Yegge's blog voice** — long-form-rant-as-engineering-essay; conversational, funny, abrasive, self-aware; opinionated but analytical; technically deep without being dry; big-picture-meets-local-complaint; digressive by design; insider-ish.
  - Long-form rant as engineering essay — sprawling, digressive, but usually driving toward a sharp technical point.
  - Highly conversational — sounds like a very smart engineer talking at speed over coffee, not like formal documentation.
  - Funny, abrasive, self-aware — jokes, exaggeration, insults, confessions, and sudden humility all mixed together.
  - Opinionated but analytical — strong claims, but often backed by concrete experience and systems-level reasoning.
  - Technically deep without being dry — compilers, languages, tools, org design, architecture, and programmer psychology are made readable through stories and analogies.
  - Big-picture and structural — often starts with a local complaint and expands it into a broader theory of software, teams, platforms, or language design.
  - Digressive by design — tangents are part of the appeal; the essay often meanders before snapping into focus.
  - Insider-ish — assumes the reader is comfortable with programming culture, old internet humour, and strong technical opinions.

### Inspiration

- **re-frame v1 docs** for didactic structure and pedagogical sequencing. Cite what works, deviate where the v2 architecture changes the story.

### Tutorial best practices

- Each chapter teaches ONE thing well.
- Concepts introduced before notation. Notation reinforced by concrete example.
- Worked examples > toy snippets. Toy snippets > prose-only.
- **Runnable re-frame apps inline** — we have the capability via the SCI-based live cell. Use it liberally for 'try this' moments.

### Structure

- **Chapter naming: `NN-<name>.md` only.** Never `NNa-foo.md` or `NNb-foo.md` — straight integer ordering.
- **Chapter opening: 2-3 sentence problem/interest framing.** Not 'Welcome to this chapter on subscriptions.' Instead: *'You like to sleep at night and you want to add unit tests? This chapter teaches you the seam between event handlers and pure code.'* Or: *'This chapter is your basic foot in the door for understanding re-frame. By the end, you will understand 80% of the basics and be able to write your first program.'*
- **NO 'What's Next' section at end of pages.** The TOC carries that load; the chapter ends when the chapter's point is made.

### Rendering

- mkdocs-material to a GitHub Pages site (existing pipeline; see `mkdocs.yml`).
- Live-cell SCI runtime for runnable apps inline (existing capability; see the playground cells).

### Out of scope

- /docs/api reference. That's contract-shaped (machine-readable, terse, complete). The guide is the COMPLEMENT — story-shaped, narrative, opinionated.
- /tools/* and /spec/* docs.

## Scope estimate

This is a multi-day project. Worth filing follow-on beads for:

- (a) Outline / chapter list / pedagogical sequence (1 bead, 1-2 hours, can be a dispatch).
- (b) Voice exemplars / sample chapter (1 bead — write ONE chapter as a voice-test before committing to the full corpus).
- (c) Full corpus rewrite (N beads, one per chapter — only file these AFTER (a) and (b) settle).

## Acceptance (this bead — strategic scope)

- Outline + voice-test sample chapter complete.
- Mike approves the voice + outline before the full-corpus rewrite begins.

## Stance

Pre-alpha. Tutorial is a story; the reader is a person. The current guide reads like an LLM wrote it for an LLM. The rewrite reads like a smart engineer talking at speed over coffee — opinionated, funny, deep.

Per Mike 2026-05-28.

title: Audit: tools/mcp-conformance/ — first-principles review (elegance/simplicity/UX, pre-alpha)
description:
## Mandate

First-principles architectural review of `tools/mcp-conformance/` (MCP conformance harness — fixture-driven test of the Tool-Pair contract across pair/story/machines MCP servers).

**Pre-alpha posture — backwards compatibility is NOT a constraint.** Decisions can be altered, removed, or replaced entirely if a better shape exists.

## Questions to answer

For each load-bearing architectural decision in this surface:

1. **Is it correct?** Does it deliver the intended behaviour cleanly?
2. **Could it be altered?** Is there a different shape that better serves the goal?
3. **Could it be improved?** What polish or strengthening would help?
4. **Could it be removed?** Is it actually necessary, or has the surrounding system evolved past needing it?
5. **Could it be tweaked?** Small adjustments that punch above their weight?

## Goal lenses (priority order)

1. **Elegance** — does the code read like a single mind designed it?
2. **Simplicity** — could the same goal be delivered with fewer concepts / fewer moving parts?
3. **UX for human developers + AI pairs** — is the surface ergonomic for the people (and agents) building on it?

## Procedure

1. Enumerate the load-bearing architectural decisions in `tools/mcp-conformance/`:
   - Public API shape (functions, macros, namespaces, contracts)
   - Data shapes (what the surface returns / accepts / stores in app-db)
   - Lifecycle / order-of-operations
   - Naming conventions (re-frame2 `:rf/*` discipline + spec/Conventions.md)
   - Integration seams with framework + other surfaces
   - Spec-side coverage (does spec/* describe this surface accurately?)
2. For each: ask the 5 questions; record findings.
3. File a follow-on bead for **each actionable insight** via `bd create ... --type bug|task|feature --priority pN` then `bd dep add <new-id> <this-bead-id> --type discovered-from`. Grade: P1 regression / P2 defect / P3 polish / P4 cosmetic. Investigation/decision items: P3 task with explicit "decision needed" framing.
4. Write a findings doc in `ai/findings/<date>-tools-mcp-conformance-first-principles.md` summarising the review across the three lenses with verdicts per architectural decision (kept / altered / removed / tweaked / improved).
5. Close this bead with a one-paragraph verdict citing the filed beads (or "no actionable findings — surface is sound" if applicable).

## Stance

Pre-alpha. No back-compat shims. SOTA masterpiece via **ELEGANCE + CLARITY + CORRECTNESS + GOOD PRACTICE**. Causa/Story work has standing priority.

## Coordination

These audits can be dispatched as Shape-2 clusters of 4-6 reviews per worker (each bead is read-mostly + writes findings to bd + ai/findings/). Cluster by related-surface where possible (e.g. all 5 adapters, all 4 MCP-* tools).

title: edn-inspector: FULL+DIFF collapses unchanged subtrees
description:
Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-27: in FULL+DIFF mode, unchanged subtrees should collapse regardless of the depth-ceiling heuristic. Today, the widget force-expands containers that have a changed descendant (good — operator never has to drill to find a change) but unchanged subtrees still expand up to default-expanded-depth, so the screen fills with noise that has no diff signal.

Change: in default-expanded?, when :full-with-diff? is true, ignore the depth-based auto-expand entirely. Only two reasons to expand a container:

  1. depth = 0 (always show the root container's keys)
  2. has-changed-descendant? = true (an ancestor of a change site)

Otherwise collapse. The operator's sticky override (via resolve-expanded?) wins as always — they can manually expand any unchanged subtree to inspect context.
close_reason: Closed

title: Xray: HANDLER body — render :fx and 'other' effects via edn-inspector (FULL)
description:
Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-27: the HANDLER step body should render the handler's return-map effects as three sections:

1. ':db' — existing DIFF/FULL/FULL+DIFF toggle (already done, no change)
2. ':fx' — the canonical :fx vector-of-vectors, when present, rendered via the edn-inspector widget fully expanded
3. '-> other' — any other keys (the effects map minus :db and :fx), rendered via edn-inspector fully expanded

Replaces the previous per-fx-entry list rendering ('1 entry' / fx-entry-line per entry) which conflated the canonical :fx vector with legacy top-level fx-ids (:dispatch, :http/get, :navigate, ...) into one flat list.

The new shape mirrors how a reg-event-fx author thinks about the return map — :db is the state mutation, :fx is the canonical effects vector, and anything else is legacy/top-level effects.

title: Xray Epoch + Schemas framework: humanize Malli explain + redesign violation block (plain prose + inline schema link + humanized map)
description:
## Why

Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-27: the schema-violation sub-block's
content is technically accurate but reads as noise — too many
discrete fields (title / chip / headline / path / value / two
"open" buttons / collapsed raw explain map). The operator wants
**plain-prose explanation with an inline link to the schema +
the humanized error map below.**

## New shape (per Mike's spec)

```
⚠ Schema Violation Error                              [Aborted]

This value failed a [schema check](link to code) and can't be
committed to app-db.

<humanized explain map>
```

Per-`:where` prose templates (each with its own recovery-chip
text + inline link to the relevant schema source):

| `:where` | Recovery chip | Prose |
|---|---|---|
| `:app-db` | "Aborted" | "This value failed a [schema check] and can't be committed to app-db." |
| `:fx-args` | "Skipped" | "fx aborted because args failed the [schema check]." |
| `:sub-return` | "Returned nil" | "This sub returned nil because its value failed the [schema check]." |
| `:event` | "Rejected" | "This event was rejected because its payload failed the [schema check]." |
| `:cofx` | "Skipped" | "This handler was skipped because the coeffect failed the [schema check]." |

The `[schema check]` placeholder is the inline click-to-source
link — resolves to the schema's source-coord (per-`:where`
mechanism — see implementation below).

## What changes — framework side

### 1. Late-bind hook for humanize (`directory.cljc`)

Add a new hook entry parallel to existing
`:schemas/validate-event!` / `:schemas/explain-with-registered-fn`:

```clojure
{:key         :schemas/humanize-explain!
 :producer-ns 're-frame.schemas
 :description "Humanize the raw m/explain output into operator-readable shape.
              Per-validator adapters install their own humanizer; Malli's
              installs (malli.error/humanize ...). Absent the hook, the
              substrate ships only :explain (raw) and the consumer
              degrades gracefully."}
```

Plus matching `:schemas/malli-humanize` hook for the Malli
adapter (parallel to `:schemas/malli-validate` /
`:schemas/malli-explain`).

### 2. Schemas artefact — humanize on emit

When `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` is emitted (see
`schemas/validate.cljc`), if the late-bind humanize hook is
present, ALSO include `:explain-humanized` in the trace event's
`:tags` map alongside the existing `:explain`. Absent the hook
or absent Malli, the slot is omitted; consumers fall back to
raw `:explain`.

### 3. Malli adapter installs the humanize hook

The CLJS Malli adapter ns (`re-frame.schemas.malli`) already
installs `:schemas/malli-validate` + `:schemas/malli-explain`
late-bind hooks. Add a parallel `:schemas/malli-humanize` hook
that wraps `malli.error/humanize`. JVM consumers already have
the `requiring-resolve` fallback per the existing pattern.

## What changes — Xray side

### 4. Violation-block view (`epoch/view.cljs`)

Replace the current violation block's render with the new
shape:

- **Title bar**: ⚠ glyph + "Schema Violation Error" (mixed
  case, no uppercase transform) + recovery chip on the right
  (per-`:where` text; for `:app-db` rollback = "Aborted").
- **Prose sentence**: per-`:where` template with the inline
  `[schema check]` link rendered as a clickable affordance.
  The link dispatches `:rf.xray/open-in-editor` against the
  schema's source-coord.
- **Humanized explain**: rendered via `ei/mini` or similar
  inline renderer. Reads `:explain-humanized` from the
  violation row's data; falls back to raw `:explain` when
  the humanized payload isn't present (e.g. non-Malli
  validators that haven't installed a humanize hook).

### 5. Projection (`epoch/projection.cljc`)

`schema-violation-row` extends to capture `:explain-humanized`
from the trace event's tags alongside the existing `:explain`.
View-side reads through.

### 6. Per-`:where` schema source-coord resolution

For the inline `[schema check]` link, resolve the schema's
source-coord:

- `:app-db` → `(rf/app-schema-meta-at path)` returns
  `{:file ... :line ...}` (per existing
  `:schemas/app-schema-meta-at` hook).
- `:fx-args` → `(rf/handler-meta :fx fx-id)` for the registration
  carrying `:schema` metadata.
- `:sub-return` → `(rf/handler-meta :sub sub-id)`.
- `:event` → `(rf/handler-meta :event event-id)`.
- `:cofx` → `(rf/handler-meta :cofx cofx-id)`.

If the coord-lookup returns nil, the prose renders without the
link (graceful degrade — the text "schema check" stays as plain
text).

## What does NOT change

- The substrate's `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` op +
  existing `:where` / `:failing-id` / `:path` / `:value` /
  `:explain` tags — all stay; the new `:explain-humanized` is
  additive.
- The framework's validator extension point — Malli stays
  optional; non-Malli validators can opt in by providing their
  own `humanize` impl via `:schemas/humanize-explain!`.
- The other violation-attachment sites (FX `:db` row for app-db
  per rf2-8resu, etc.) — only the SHAPE of the block changes,
  not where it attaches.
- The collapsed raw explain map can stay as an "▸ raw" expand
  for power users debugging the validator itself; or drop
  entirely (Mike's call). The proposed shape doesn't show it;
  drop unless Mike says keep.

## Acceptance

1. `:schemas/humanize-explain!` late-bind hook declared in
   directory.cljc; Malli adapter installs it via
   `malli.error/humanize`.
2. `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` trace events carry
   `:explain-humanized` when the hook is present.
3. Xray's violation block renders the new shape: title with
   "Schema Violation Error" + recovery chip; prose sentence
   with inline `[schema check]` link; humanized explain map
   below.
4. Per-`:where` prose templates render correctly (5 boundaries:
   `:app-db`, `:fx-args`, `:sub-return`, `:event`, `:cofx`).
5. `[schema check]` link clicks open the schema's source in
   the configured editor.
6. Graceful degrade: when humanize hook is absent (non-Malli
   validator), block renders the raw `:explain` map in the
   `<humanized>` slot.
7. The `schema-violations` Story variant in panel-gallery
   demonstrates the new block.

## Coordination

- Touches: late-bind directory + schemas/validate.cljc + Malli
  adapter ns + epoch/projection.cljc + epoch/view.cljs.
- spec/021 §violation block update.
- spec/010 §post-violation rendering brief note pointing at the
  humanize contract.
- Pre-alpha posture: clean redesign of the block; no shim.
- Direct-action by mayor (workers on hold).

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27.
close_reason: Implemented directly on main by mayor (workers on hold). Framework: late-bind directory entries added for :schemas/humanize-explain! + :schemas/malli-humanize; re-frame.schemas.malli adapter publishes malli.error/humanize under both keys; validate.cljc gains emit-validation-failure! helper that auto-augments tags with :explain-humanized when the hook fires (replaces 2 direct trace/emit-error! call sites). Xray: schema-violation-row projection captures :explain-humanized from trace event tags; violation-block view rewritten to new shape per Mike spec (title 'Schema Violation Error' + recovery chip; per-:where prose with inline 'schema check' link to schema source; humanized explain map or raw fallback below); recovery chip text refined per :where ('Aborted' / 'Skipped' / 'Returned nil' / 'Rejected'); title style mixed-case (no uppercase transform). Bracket-balance verified on all 5 modified files.

title: Xray Epoch: retire SCHEMA HOT-RELOAD pipeline step — hot-reload drift surfaces via Issues panel only (supersedes rf2-xgeag Option A)
description:
## Why

Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-27: the SCHEMA HOT-RELOAD pipeline
step (Option A from rf2-xgeag, projected via `hot-reload-step`,
rendered via `render-schema-hot-reload-step`) carries content
nearly opaque to operators:

```
4
SCHEMA HOT-RELOAD
1 hot-reload drift
⚠ SCHEMA VIOLATION
logged + skipped
schema hot-reload · :rf/default
path: [:user/profile :age]
value: -3
```

Problems with this rendering:
- "hot-reload drift" assumes the operator already knows that
  schemas can be re-registered during dev + that re-registering
  may invalidate existing app-db values
- `:rf/default` is the affected FRAME (not a handler-id like
  other violation rows), but the rendering doesn't label it as
  such
- `path: [:user/profile :age]` lacks "in this frame's app-db"
  context
- `value: -3` is the current live value that fails the new
  schema — but the operator can't tell whether `-3` is the OLD
  value (frozen from before the re-register) or what
- MISSING: the old schema, the new schema, the file/line where
  the re-registration happened, when it happened — all rich
  context that wouldn't fit in a pipeline-step format

The Epoch panel's pipeline-step format is too narrow for the
rich context hot-reload drift needs. Worse, attaching a tail
step to a rolled-back cascade contradicts the rolled-back
mental model: "the entire cascade was aborted, but here's
another step?"

Hot-reload drift is conceptually **out-of-band** — a dev-time
event triggered by `reg-app-schema` re-registration, not a
runtime cascade event. The Issues panel is its natural home,
where rich explanatory chrome can carry the schema-before /
schema-after / file:line / pre-existing-value details that the
pipeline-step format can't accommodate.

## What changes

### 1. Projection (`epoch/projection.cljc`)

- DELETE `defn hot-reload-step` (line ~1417)
- DELETE the `(hot-reload-step violations)` call in the `project`
  fn's base-steps construction (line ~1728)
- Update the rf2-xgeag attachment-map comment table (line ~1284)
  to retire the `:schema-hot-reload` row
- The hot-reload-drift events themselves (`:rf.schema/violation`
  trace events) still ride in `:trace-events` and still feed the
  Issues panel via the existing trace-event consumer chain

### 2. View (`epoch/view.cljs`)

- DELETE `defn render-schema-hot-reload-step` (line ~3494)
- DELETE the `:schema-hot-reload` case in `render-step` (line
  ~3639) — without the projection emitting the step, the case
  dispatch never fires it, but keeping a dead case is noise
- Update view-side cross-references (line 998 comment)

### 3. Spec (`tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md`)

- The rf2-xgeag attachment-map references the SCHEMA HOT-RELOAD
  standalone tail step. Update to reflect that hot-reload drift
  routes to the Issues panel exclusively, NOT to the cascade
  pipeline.

### 4. Issues panel

The Issues panel already consumes `:rf.schema/violation` trace
events (drift fires on this op). The panel's existing row
rendering shows the violation. As a follow-on (NOT this bead):
the Issues panel's rendering for hot-reload drift could grow
richer chrome (schema-before / schema-after / file:line) —
filed as a sibling bead if needed.

## Acceptance

1. No `SCHEMA HOT-RELOAD` step appears in the Epoch panel
   pipeline for any cascade (rolled-back or not).
2. Hot-reload drift events continue to fire `:rf.schema/violation`
   trace events; the Issues panel continues to surface them as
   rows.
3. Projection layer no longer emits a `:schema-hot-reload` step;
   view layer no longer carries the dispatch case or render fn.
4. spec/021 attachment table updated.
5. The `schema-violations` Story variant in panel-gallery
   renders with ONE FEWER step (was 4: dispatch/handler/fx/
   schema-hot-reload; now 3: dispatch/handler/fx).
6. Bracket-balance verified across modified files.

## What does NOT change

- The framework's `:rf.schema/violation` trace event emission
  (still fires on re-registration with mismatching live value)
- The Issues panel's existing consumption of those events
- The other rf2-xgeag in-cascade attachments (`:event`, `:cofx`,
  `:fx-args`, `:sub-return`, `:app-db`) — all unchanged
- Spec 010 §Per-step recovery (hot-reload still has the same
  `:logged-and-skipped` recovery posture)

## Coordination

- Single-PR scope; touches projection + view + spec.
- Pre-alpha posture: clean retire, no shim.
- Direct-action by mayor (workers on hold).

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27.
close_reason: Implemented directly on main by mayor (workers on hold). projection.cljc: hot-reload-step defn deleted + its call site in the project fn's base-steps construction removed. view.cljs: render-schema-hot-reload-step defn deleted + the :schema-hot-reload case in render-step retired. Bonus fix folded into same commit: rollback recovery chip text changed from 'rolled back' to 'Commit to app-db aborted' + chip's text-transform changed from 'uppercase' to 'none' (mixed case more legible for the longer phrase; red/white chrome carries severity). Bracket-balance verified on all modified files.

title: Xray Epoch: :where :app-db violation moves from HANDLER to FX step's :db row (the implicit commit fx)
description:
## Why

Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-27: the `:where :app-db` violation
attachment in rf2-xgeag (HANDLER step) is conceptually wrong. The
`:db` commit is **an fx** — the framework just treats it as
implicit. The handler RETURNS effects; flows + interceptors process
them; then the effects map gets EXECUTED, with `:db` install being
the first thing to fire.

So the Epoch panel's FX step should show:

```
✓ :db
✓ :dispatch [:next-event]
✓ :http/get {...}
```

…or on rollback:

```
✗ :db          ← red cross, ROLLED BACK
  ⚠ SCHEMA VIOLATION
  app-db commit · path [:counter] · value "not-a-number" · …
✗ :dispatch    ← muted (rollback nullified the rest)
✗ :http/get    ← muted
```

This separates "what the handler returned" (HANDLER step's body)
from "what got executed" (FX step's rows). HANDLER step describes
return intent; FX step describes the actual commit + side effects.
The pink violation sub-block moves from HANDLER to the `:db` FX
row, where it semantically belongs (the commit itself failed, not
the handler's intent).

## What changes

### 1. Projection (`epoch/projection.cljc`)

The FX step's row list (`fx-rows` or equivalent) gains a `:db` row
as its FIRST entry when the handler's effects include a `:db` key.
The `:db` row carries:

- `:fx-id :db`
- `:status` — `:ok` (committed successfully) or `:rollback` (schema
  violation, app-db restored). Determined by the cascade's outcome
  + presence of `:where :app-db` schema-validation-failure trace
  events.
- `:violations` — the `:where :app-db` violations that fired during
  this commit. Currently attached to HANDLER step's `:violations`
  slot per rf2-xgeag; MOVES to the `:db` FX row.

### 2. View (`epoch/view.cljs`)

`render-fx-step` (or equivalent) renders the new `:db` row as the
first row, with:

- Status glyph: green ✓ for `:ok`, red ✗ for `:rollback`
- Row label: `:db`
- Empty value column (or `commit ok` / `rolled back` short text)
- When `:violations` is non-empty: the pink SCHEMA VIOLATION
  sub-block attaches UNDER this row (same chrome as the other
  attachment sites — title + recovery chip + headline + path +
  value + click-to-source links + collapsed explain)

`render-handler-step` (or equivalent) STOPS rendering the
`:where :app-db` violation sub-block. The HANDLER step's
`:violations` slot retains other violation kinds if any (today
only `:where :app-db` attached there per rf2-xgeag — so the
HANDLER step's violations slot may become empty in practice; the
existing pink-sub-block rendering path stays in place for any
future violation kinds that might attach there).

The downstream-mute treatment moves with the violation:
previously HANDLER showed the violation + the cascade's downstream
FX/SUBS/VIEWS muted. Now the `:db` FX row shows the violation +
the OTHER FX rows + downstream SUBS/VIEWS mute around it.

### 3. Spec (`tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md`)

The rf2-xgeag attachment table needs one row updated:

- `:where :app-db` → was HANDLER step → now FX step's `:db` row
  (the first row of FX when `:db` was in the handler's effects)

### 4. Fixture (`testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures_epoch.cljs`)

The `schema-violations-history` fixture currently demonstrates the
HANDLER-attached rendering. Verify the trace event shape still
drives the projection correctly (the trace event itself uses
`:where :app-db`; only the attachment rule moves — the trace
schema doesn't change). The fixture should now show the `:db` FX
row with the red ✗ + violation sub-block.

The fixture's promised four-violation-types is still aspirational
(only `:app-db` + hot-reload are seeded today per fixture line
491-504); that's a separate gap.

## What does NOT change

- The substrate trace event shape (`:rf.error/schema-validation-failure`
  with `:where :app-db`) — same emission point, same payload
- The framework's commit-time validation (router.cljc commit-db-effect!)
  — already validates the FLOW-AUGMENTED + INTERCEPTOR-PROCESSED
  value; this bead is purely about WHERE the violation RENDERS in
  Xray, not WHEN it fires
- Other `:where` attachments (`:event` → DISPATCH, `:cofx` → COEFFECT
  step, `:fx-args` → matching FX row, `:sub-return` → SUBSCRIPTIONS
  row, `:hot-reload` → standalone SCHEMA HOT-RELOAD tail step) —
  unchanged

## Acceptance

1. FX step renders `:db` as its FIRST row when the handler's
   effects included a `:db` key.
2. Status glyph: ✓ (green) for successful commit; ✗ (red) for
   rolled-back commit.
3. `:where :app-db` violation sub-block attaches UNDER the `:db`
   FX row (same chrome as other violation attachment sites).
4. HANDLER step no longer renders the `:where :app-db` violation
   sub-block.
5. Downstream-mute (rollback's blast radius) shows on the OTHER
   FX rows + downstream SUBS/VIEWS, not on HANDLER.
6. The `schema-violations` Story variant in panel-gallery renders
   with the new attachment visible.
7. spec/021 §X.Y attachment table updated.
8. Quality gates pass (test:cljs, test:browser).

## Coordination

- Single-PR scope; isolated to Epoch panel + spec/021.
- Pre-alpha posture: replace the old attachment cleanly; no
  back-compat shim.
- Refines rf2-xgeag's previously-shipped design.

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27. Direct-action by mayor (workers on hold).
close_reason: Implemented directly on main by mayor (workers on hold). projection.cljc: fx-rows synthesises :db row at front (status :ok or :rollback derived from :where :app-db violation + :rollback? flag); attach-violations :app-db case routes to FX step's :db row via new attach-to-fx-db-row helper; mark-rolled-back-downstream anchors on FX step (not HANDLER) so the FX step itself stays visible to display the red :db row. view.cljs: fx-row-view adds :rollback status (✗ + error-colour); render-handler-step drops the rolled-back-banner + violation-driven rolled-back? derivation. Bracket-balance verified on all three modified files.

title: Audit: edn-inspector 24hr review — design objectives met? Misses? Decisions to revisit? (Shape-3)
description:
## Goal

Shape-3 read-only audit of all edn-inspector work landed in the last ~24 hours. Verify design objectives are met; surface misses; flag decisions that may need revisiting. File actionable findings as follow-on beads.

## Recent edn-inspector work to audit (last ~24hr)

Enumerate authoritatively via `git log --since='24 hours ago' --oneline -- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/ tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/diff_mode_toggle.cljs` and adjacent panel files. Known PRs:

- **#2230** (rf2-n2jig) — three-mode diff toggle + mode-3 grammar (R1-R8) + Editscript A* engine + 22 Stories + 16 engine tests. **Foundation.** Default flipped to `:full+diff`.
- **#2231** (rf2-yqjrd) — universalise 3-mode toggle across App-DB + Machine Inspector + SUBSCRIPTIONS + Story snapshot.
- **#2234** (rf2-4p1vl + rf2-4spyl) — memoise `engine/project` (per-mount cache) + `f/display-value` WeakMap short-circuit (HIGH perf wins).
- **#2235** (rf2-7is22 + rf2-h0lv8 + rf2-ezqhb) — excise ~2400 LoC dead diff engine residue (annotated_tree + section_grouping + render).
- **#2236** (rf2-0cyjm + rf2-44xya) — adopt `reg-mode-sub+event!` helper + normalise 4-surface keyword naming to `:rf.xray.<surface>/diff-mode`.
- **#2241** (Cluster F — 6 beads) — diff-mode-toggle widget elegance: `^:private` helpers + drop `data-mode` + "View" discoverability prefix + `data-*-mode` normalisation + `data-testid` normalisation + CLJS unit tests.
- **#2244** (rf2-7cddi + rf2-rhmc5) — hoist gutter-row + R3 chip styles + collapse `engine/op-at` calls in edn_inspector.
- **#2245** (rf2-pvy2n + rf2-3tjkc + rf2-ot28z) — spec/021 §9.1.5.1 retitle + R-rule applicability + :machine-data row.
- **#2249** (rf2-9ec65 + rf2-ihjnx + rf2-mndut) — for→mapv + factor on-click handlers + hoist :diff-body styles.
- **#2251** (rf2-yaajg) — 6 grammar-edge Story variants (set-diff + boolean-toggle + vector-of-maps + nil-vs-missing + numeric-near-equal + redacted-context).

## Design objectives to verify against

(Cross-ref `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md §9.1.5` for canonical statement.)

1. **3-mode toggle is uniform** — same UX across App-DB / Machine Inspector / Epoch HANDLER :db / Epoch SUBSCRIPTIONS. Same widget, same naming, same testids.
2. **Mode-3 grammar (R1-R8)** rigour — gutter glyphs / row washes / "← changed from" suffixes / key-side decoration / container-subtree indicators all render correctly across all surfaces.
3. **Default = `:full+diff`** — operator gets the canonical mode without clicking.
4. **Editscript A* engine** — optimally-small EDN edit scripts; canonical output shape ().
5. **Stories coverage** — every R-rule + grammar-edge case has at least one Story variant exercising it.
6. **Memoisation** — byte-identical inputs short-circuit; cache lifetime sane.
7. **Style discipline** — hoisted styles + factored handlers; React reconciler diff fast-path preserved.
8. **Dead code excised** — no zombie engines / unused helpers / dead subs hanging around.
9. **Click-to-source** affordances on hyperlinks (sub/event/view ids).
10. **Universal-surface adoption** — every place that diffs EDN goes through edn_inspector + mode-3 grammar, not bespoke rendering.

## Coverage axes

1. **Met-the-bar check** — does the as-merged implementation satisfy each design objective above? If not, what's the gap?
2. **Misses** — any work that landed but doesn't quite hit the intent? (e.g., Cluster F's 4-surface normalisation: did it ACTUALLY normalise everything or are there straggler attributes that drifted?)
3. **Decisions to revisit** — any landed decision that, in hindsight, deserves rethinking? (e.g., the Machine Inspector Before/After CSS-Grid retirement — is the single-mount mode-3 actually better, or has Mike noticed a regression?)
4. **Spec drift** — does spec/021 §9.1.5.x accurately describe the as-merged behaviour? Any gaps between code + spec?
5. **Test coverage** — engine tests (16 from #2230), widget tests (Cluster F), grammar-edge Stories (rf2-yaajg's 6). Any holes?
6. **Surface consistency** — are all 4 surfaces TRULY uniform, or has one drifted (e.g., one surface using  while others use )?
7. **Performance** — does memoisation actually hold? Try to construct a render scenario where it might fail (e.g., expansion toggle, ResizeObserver, parent re-render with identical inputs).

## Shape — Shape-3 audit (read-only)

1. Worktree guard FIRST. Report WORKTREE_ROOT.
2. `bd update <this-bead> --claim`.
3. Enumerate the 24hr work; read the as-merged code for each touch site.
4. **Write findings doc FIRST** to `ai/findings/edn-inspector-24hr-review-2026-05-27.md` (gitignored; never commit; never link). Per-finding format:
   - severity (HIGH/MED/LOW/DEFER)
   - file:line citation
   - design objective referenced (axis 1-10 above)
   - description (what's the miss / drift / gap)
   - recommended fix shape
5. **File follow-on beads ONE AT A TIME** after the doc lands. `bd create` with appropriate priority. For each bead, append its ID to this audit-bead's notes.
6. **Close this bead** with verdict: severity counts + actionable-bead list + headline finding.
7. **NO PR** by default. Trivial ride-along fix may be added.

## Severity

- **HIGH (P1)** — design objective NOT met; user-visible defect or correctness gap
- **MED (P2)** — drift from objective, compounds across surfaces
- **LOW (P3)** — polish, micro-improvement
- **DEFER** — depends on future change

## Acceptance

1. Findings doc at `ai/findings/edn-inspector-24hr-review-2026-05-27.md` with per-finding citations.
2. Follow-on beads filed one-at-a-time, IDs appended.
3. Audit-bead closed with verdict.
4. NO audit-PR.

## Stance

Pre-alpha; no back-compat. We've done substantial work on edn-inspector; this is the moment to verify it actually hits the design intent before moving on.

## Goal

1. **Idiom adherence** — do examples use re-frame2 idioms naturally (frame-bound subs, declarative effects, machines where stateful, flows where derivational)? Or do they fall back to lower-level imperative patterns the framework was designed to obsolete?
2. **Naming + structure** — namespace layout (per-substrate `examples/<substrate>/<example>/src/...`)? Filenames mirror responsibility? Sub / event / fx IDs follow reserved-namespace conventions (`spec/Conventions.md` — single-root `:rf/*` scheme)?

4. **API choice** — `reg-event-db` vs `reg-event-fx` chosen for the right reason? Machines used where they belong (genuinely stateful UI)? Flows used for derived state, not as a Sub-substitute?
5. **Code style** — function granularity, threading-macro use, destructuring, doc-string presence on public registrations.
6. **Cross-substrate parity** — same example across Reagent/UIx/Helix: do they tell the same story idiomatically per substrate, or has one drifted into substrate-specific gymnastics?
7. **Test absence** — per CLAUDE.md "examples are test-free (locked 2026-05-19, rf2-8cevm)". Verify no `*.spec.cjs` snuck in.
8. **README quality** — does each example's README explain WHY this pattern, not just WHAT? Is the framing AI-readable (per the AI-first principles)?

title: Audit: three-mode diff toggle best-practice + elegance review (post-rf2-n2jig + rf2-yqjrd)
description:
## Goal

Shape-3 audit of the three-mode diff toggle implementation (rf2-n2jig foundation + rf2-yqjrd universalisation), specifically for **best practice and elegance**. File actionable findings as follow-on beads.

This is the sister bead to rf2-gwm0y (efficiency audit) — same scope, different axis.

## Gated on

- rf2-n2jig (foundation bead) must merge first
- rf2-yqjrd (universalisation bead) must merge second

This audit dispatches ONLY after both have landed.

## Coverage targets

The three-mode toggle is widely surfaced across Xray. Best-practice + elegance concerns:

1. **Naming + symmetry** — three modes (`:full / :diff / :full+diff`) named consistently across all surfaces? Toggle button labels uniform? `data-testid` shape uniform?
2. **API shape** — single canonical entry point (e.g. one shared `three-mode-toggle` component) used everywhere, or are there 4+ near-copies bespoke per panel?
3. **Spec alignment** — does every applied surface document its three-mode behaviour in the spec? spec/021 §HANDLER, §App-DB, §Machine, §SUBSCRIPTIONS, Story spec.
4. **Convention adherence** — naming follows `:rf.xray.<surface>/diff-mode` style? Re-frame events follow the documented shape? `frame-bound-fn` used appropriately (rf2-x005l) vs simple `dispatch`?
5. **Tooling-friendliness** — testid surface, `coord-chip` reuse, edn-inspector composition idiomatic per existing patterns?
6. **Discoverability** — does mode-3 (`:full+diff`) feel obvious without reading the spec? Toggle layout consistent w/ other Xray toggles (`coord-chip`, the existing 2-button toggle pattern)?
7. **Documentation** — Stories adequately exercise the grammar variants? spec/021 §9.1.6 explains the grammar with worked examples?
8. **Layering** — does the diff-rendering engine cleanly separate (a) projection (pure data) (b) rendering (hiccup) (c) interaction (dispatch)?
9. **Editscript adoption** — chosen well? Idiomatic Clojure usage? Edge cases (large diffs, deep nesting, equal subtrees) handled gracefully?

## Shape

Shape-3 audit (read-only research):
- WRITE THE FINDINGS DOC FIRST to `ai/findings/three-mode-diff-elegance-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md` (gitignored; never commit; never link)
- File follow-on beads ONE AT A TIME after the doc lands
- Close this audit-bead with verdict + cross-refs
- No PR by default; trivial 1-line fixes can ride along

## Acceptance

1. Findings doc with per-finding `file:line` citations + severity + recommended fix.
2. Follow-on beads filed one-at-a-time, IDs appended to this bead.
3. Audit-bead closed with verdict.
4. NO PR for the audit itself.

## Severity

- **HIGH** — clear violation of stance / convention
- **MED** — drift from elegance that compounds across surfaces
- **LOW** — micro-improvement
- **DEFER** — depends on future change

## Coordination with sister audit

rf2-gwm0y (efficiency) audits the SAME work but a DIFFERENT axis. Both can dispatch in parallel as Shape-3 audits — they only WRITE to gitignored ai/findings/ + file follow-on beads. No source-file conflict.

## What does NOT change

- Don't ship fixes (file beads).
- Skip efficiency concerns — that's rf2-gwm0y's domain.
close_reason:
Audit complete. Findings doc at ai/findings/three-mode-diff-elegance-audit-2026-05-27.md (local-only, gitignored).

## Verdict

Implementation substantially good — shared widget exists, all four surfaces consume it, R1-R8 grammar is well-tested, Editscript engine is sound + correctly isolated. Layering (projection/render/interaction) is clean.

Major drift: per-surface naming + helper-adoption did NOT follow the convention the shared widget itself documents. The reg-mode-sub+event! helper is dead code; the four surfaces hand-roll their sub+event pairs with four different naming patterns. Plus engine-fork residue: ~2400 lines of older structural-diff (annotated_tree + section_grouping + render) ship with zero production reads, contradicting the new engine's own "no double-engine state" claim.

## Severity counts

- HIGH (P1): 4 — H1 naming, H2 dead helper, H3 ~2400-line engine residue, H4 testid drift
- MED (P2):  5 — M1 data-attr names, M2 retired data-mode revival, M3 ^:private, M4 no widget tests, M5 discoverability label
- LOW (P3):  3 — L1 dead container-op-tag fn, L2 docstring missing slot, L3 mixed-path sort investigation

## Follow-on beads (priority order)

P1:
- rf2-44xya — Normalise per-surface diff-mode keyword naming + slot names
- rf2-0cyjm — Adopt or delete the dead-code reg-mode-sub+event! helper
- rf2-7is22 — Excise dead-engine residue (~2400 lines)

P2:

- rf2-xlmhh — Remove redundant data-mode attribute from the toggle bar

- rf2-hf6gb — Add CLJS unit tests for views/diff-mode-toggle
- rf2-fytu4 — Add discoverability label to the shared toggle widget

P3:

- rf2-ezqhb — Document missing :vector-removals slot in engine docstring
- rf2-n83r8 — Investigate flat-row :path sort for mixed-type segments (defer-eligible)

## Pairing recommendations for the mayor
