title: Xray: three-mode diff toggle + mode-3 grammar + Editscript engine + Stories (Epoch HANDLER :db application)
description:
## Why

Today Xray's Epoch panel HANDLER step `:db` sub-section carries a
two-mode `[diff][all]` toggle:

- `:all` — pure data (full app-db via the edn-inspector)
- `:diff` — pure diff (flat path-prefixed lines like
  `+ [:counter] 6`)

Mike pair-debug 2026-05-27: introduce a THIRD mode and standardise
the affordance as a universal three-button toggle:

- **`:full`** — pure data (renamed from `:all` for clarity)
- **`:diff`** — pure diff
- **`:full+diff`** (mode-3) — full data rendered as a tree WITH
  inline diff annotations: gutter glyphs, row washes, "← changed
  from" suffixes on modified leaves, key-side decoration on
  added/removed keys, container-subtree change indicators

This bead is the **foundation** — substrate + first application
in the Epoch panel. Sibling bead (file separately) universalises
the affordance across App-DB / Machine Inspector / Subscriptions
/ Story snapshot surfaces.

## Design source

**FULL DESIGN AT**:
`ai/findings/diff-mode-3-key-and-triangle-grammar-2026-05-27.md`
(local-only; mayor checkout). Worker MUST read end-to-end before
starting. Sections most load-bearing:

- §3 design variants (E is the picked grammar)
- §5.1 normative rules R1-R8 (as revised in §7 per Mike's
  pair-debug answers)
- §7 Mike's answers (Q1 one-shot; Q2 parent-only with R5-tinted;
  Q3 collapsed-only `[N∆]` chip; Q4 default-depth 3; Q5 LCS)
- §9 Editscript engine (locked in; pre-alpha posture, no
  fallback library)
- §10 Story acceptance (22+ variants required)

The findings doc carries the rationale; this bead body is the
spec-shaped extract.

## What changes — substrate

### 1. Editscript engine adoption (wholesale replace)

Add `juji/editscript` to `tools/xray/deps.edn` (NOT
`implementation/deps.edn` — bundle isolation per
`npm run test:bundle-isolation`). Confirm CLJS imports cleanly
under `shadow-cljs watch testbeds/panel_gallery`; if it doesn't,
stop + raise with Mike.

**DELETE the entire home-grown classifier** at
`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:
533-664`:
- `diff-op` (533-547)
- `children-changed?` (552-589)
- `op->gutter-glyph` (593-600)
- `op->gutter-tone-key` (602-621)
- `op->row-wash-key` (623-633)
- `op->row-stripe-key` (636-643)
- `gutter-colour` (646-651)
- `row-wash-bg` (653-658)
- `row-stripe-colour` (660-664)
- `diff-op-container` (667-678)

Pre-alpha posture: clean delete, no shim, no transitional
dual-engine state.

Replace with a thin projection layer (`projection/diff-engine.cljc`
or similar) that:
- takes `:db-before` + `:db-after`, calls Editscript A* with
  `(editscript/diff before after {:algo :a-star})` to produce a
  flat edit script
- walks the edit script + emits `{path → op}` map for the
  renderer chrome to consume
- `op` is one of `:added / :removed / :modified / :same /
  :children / :same-shifted` (last one is new per R6)

The projection is pure data + testable in isolation; the renderer
chrome reads off it.

### 2. Three-mode toggle widget

Replace the two-button `[diff][all]` bar at `epoch/view.cljs:???`
(worker locates `db-view-mode-toggle` or equivalent) with a
three-button bar `[diff][full][full+diff]`. The new sub
`:rf.xray.epoch/db-view-mode` returns one of `:diff / :full /
:full+diff` (default: `:full+diff` — operator's most-useful
default).

The widget is generic enough to lift into a shared component for
re-use by the sibling bead (universalisation). Suggest naming:
`views/diff_mode_toggle.cljs` — single-source, consumed by
multiple panels.

### 3. Mode-3 grammar — normative rules

Per §5.1 of findings doc, as revised by Mike's answers in §7:

- **R1**: value-side `~` gutter glyph for modified scalars +
  `← changed from <prior>` italic muted suffix (unchanged
  behaviour from existing engine, ported to Editscript output)
- **R2**: key-side `+` / `−` glyph at column 1 of the key row
  when the KEY itself is `:added` / `:removed` (distinct from
  "an existing key's value changed"). Strike-through reaches
  the key text for `:removed`.
- **R3 (revised)**: container `▼` triangle stays default
  `:text-tertiary` ALWAYS when expanded. When COLLAPSED (`▶`)
  AND the subtree carries change, a `[N∆]` count chip appears
  after the closing ellipsis: `▶ :user {…} [3∆]`. Triangle
  itself never colour-swaps. No per-op breakdown in the chip
  (single count only).
- **R4**: single 2px vertical rail in the gutter through each
  change-bearing subtree, in the dominant-op hue. Rails do NOT
  nest — innermost change-bearing ancestor draws the bar.
- **R5 (revised)**: wholly-new / wholly-removed subtrees
  reclassify to `:added` / `:removed` at the parent. Descendant
  gutter GLYPHS + 2px STRIPES are suppressed; descendant row
  WASHES are RETAINED (low-opacity tint). Always parent-only —
  no size threshold.
- **R6**: vector shift-detection via Editscript's A* + Myers
  underpinnings. Shifted-but-equal rows get a `(was N)` muted
  suffix in `:text-tertiary` and NO gutter glyph; new
  classification `:same-shifted`. New elements get `+`;
  removed elements get `−` at surgical position.
- **R7**: type-change containers reclassify to `:modified`. New
  value renders in the value column; `← was <prior>` suffix
  via the `mini` renderer (falling back to "<type> with N
  keys" when `mini` overflows).
- **R8**: one-sided `:rf/redacted` renders as `:modified` with
  curated `← was redacted` / `← now redacted` suffix (no
  sentinel text leak). Two-sided redacted classifies as
  `:same` for v1 — propagating "underlying-differs" is a
  follow-on bead.

### 4. Default-expanded-depth

Mode-3 in the Epoch panel uses `default-expanded-depth = 3`
(per Q4 — between browse's 1 and diff's 2; deep enough to
surface most app-db top-level shards). Other modes keep their
existing defaults.

## Story examples — MANDATORY (per §10)

The bead ships with a comprehensive Story variant set. Mike
must be able to visually inspect every rule + scenario when
the work is complete. Minimum inventory (per §10 of findings):

**Single-rule** (13 variants): R1 modified scalar, R2 new key,
R2 removed key, R3 collapsed-with-chip, R4 rail, R5 wholly-new
subtree, R5 wholly-removed subtree, R6 vector insert, R6
vector remove, R6 vector reorder, R7 type change, R8 was-
redacted-now-visible, R8 was-visible-now-redacted.

**Combination + edge** (7 variants): all-ops cascade, mixed-ops
subtree, deeply-nested change, long-vector-one-insert (the LCS
payoff demo), empty diff, massive diff, mode-toggle three-up.

**Theme + density** (2 variants): light + dark theme rendering;
narrow panel (320px width).

22 variants minimum. Each gets a title + 1-2 line description.
Each browser-smoke-tested at least minimally (mount + assert
expected DOM chrome).

Story home: `tools/xray/stories/diff-mode-3/...` (new dir) or
folded into `testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures_diff_mode_3.cljs`
per existing convention — worker picks.

## What retires in this bead

- The home-grown diff classifier (10 named fns in
  `edn_inspector.cljs:533-664`)
- The two-button `[diff][all]` toggle (replaced by three-button
  bar)
- The `:rf.xray.epoch/db-view-mode` sub's `:diff / :all` enum
  (replaced by `:diff / :full / :full+diff`)

## What does NOT change in this bead

- Other panel surfaces (App-DB / Machine Inspector / Subs /
  Story snapshot) — sibling universalisation bead handles
- The renderer chrome (washes, stripes, glyphs) — same chrome
  rules, reading off the new Editscript-backed `{path → op}`
  projection
- The `:rf.xray.epoch/db-view-mode` event-fx (only the enum
  values flip)
- Other Epoch panel steps (DISPATCH / COEFFECT / HANDLER's
  source / FLOW / FX / SUBSCRIPTIONS / VIEWS) — untouched

## Acceptance

1. `juji/editscript` added to `tools/xray/deps.edn`; CLJS
   import verified under `shadow-cljs watch
   testbeds/panel_gallery`.
2. Home-grown classifier deleted (10 fns at
   `edn_inspector.cljs:533-664`); no shim, no transitional
   state.
3. New projection layer produces `{path → op}` from Editscript
   edit script; unit-tested in isolation against canonical
   before/after pairs.
4. Three-mode toggle widget replaces two-mode toggle; default
   mode is `:full+diff`.
5. All 8 mode-3 grammar rules (R1-R8 as revised) render
   correctly in the Epoch HANDLER `:db` section.
6. Default-expanded-depth 3 applies to mode-3 specifically.
7. 22+ Story variants ship covering every rule + scenario +
   theme/density case per §10. Each variant titled + described.
8. Spec/021 §X.Y (Epoch panel mode-3 contract) added,
   referencing the Story variants as canonical visual
   reference.
9. All quality gates pass:
   `npm run test:cljs` /
   `npm run test:browser` /
   `npm run test:bundle-isolation`.

## Coordination

- spec/021 is hot-zone per CLAUDE.md (sequential, never
  parallel). Worker checks dashboard before dispatching.
- The sibling bead (universalisation across App-DB / Machine
  Inspector / Subs / Story snapshot) BLOCKS-ON this bead. The
  shared `views/diff_mode_toggle.cljs` widget + the
  Editscript-backed projection layer must exist before sibling
  can land.
- Pre-alpha posture: ship cleanly, no flag-gated rollout, no
  fallback engine library. If Editscript hits an unexpected
  blocker, stop + raise with Mike rather than auto-switching.

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27.

title: Xray: end-user editor override in Settings popup → General tab (localStorage-backed; for mixed-editor teams)
description:
## Why

Today the Xray editor preference (`:rf.xray/editor` — `:vscode` /
`:cursor` / `:windsurf` / `:zed` / `:idea` / `{:custom ...}`) is
**configure-time only**: the host application calls
`xray-config/configure! {:rf.xray/editor :cursor}` once at boot,
and that choice is fixed for every developer who opens the panel
in their browser.

On mixed-editor teams this fails:

- A team's app boots with `:rf.xray/editor :vscode` (the default
  if no `configure!` is made)
- One developer on the team uses IntelliJ IDEA
- They have **no way to override** the choice — clicking a
  source-coord chip launches `vscode://...` and either fails
  silently or opens the wrong editor

The framework's substrate is already there:
- The config atom in `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/
  config.cljc:386` is mutable at runtime (`reset! editor ...`)
- The URI builder at `re-frame.source-coords.editor-uri` handles
  every enumerated value + the `{:custom ...}` template
- The defense-in-depth scheme allowlist (rf2-cm93v) keeps
  arbitrary URLs out

The missing piece is the **end-user-facing affordance** to flip
the value at runtime + the persistence to survive reloads.

## Where it lives

Natural home: the Settings popup's **General tab**. Per rf2-ou3pn
the popup ships with four tabs (General · Keybindings · Buffer ·
Diff) in v1. General already houses host-environment-adjacent
controls; editor preference fits cleanly.

Files to touch (worker verifies exact paths):
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/popup.cljs` —
  Settings popup orchestrator
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/settings/general/...`
  — General tab content (worker locates the right per-tab file)
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/config.cljc` — extend the
  editor read to consult the override layer

## UX shape

A new field group inside the General tab:

```
EDITOR

Click-to-source links open in:
( ) VS Code
( ) Cursor
( ) Windsurf
( ) Zed
(•) IntelliJ IDEA (or other JetBrains IDE)
( ) Custom URI template
        ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ subl://open?url=file://{path}&line={line}        │
        └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        Placeholders: {path}, {file}, {line}, {column}

[ Reset to host default ]    Host default: VS Code
```

- Radio group for the enumerated values + Custom escape hatch
- Custom field appears (or focusable) when the Custom radio is
  selected; placeholder hint inline
- Reset button restores the host's `configure!`-supplied default
- Footer line shows what the host default IS so the developer
  knows what they're overriding

Selection is **immediate** (no separate save button — same
pattern as Story's editor picker if it has one; worker checks
Story for shape parity).

## Persistence

localStorage key: `re-frame2-xray.editor` (worker confirms naming
convention against other persisted Xray preferences — Buffer's
retain-N, Diff's mode, etc. likely have an existing key shape to
mirror).

Value shape: either a keyword name (`:vscode`, `:idea`, …) or a
map `{:custom "<template>"}` — pr-str'd for stability across
reloads.

## Resolution order — host default vs user override

The config read path (currently `(config/get-editor)`) becomes a
layered resolution:

1. **User override** (localStorage) — if present, win
2. **Host default** (the `configure!`-set atom) — if user
   override absent
3. **Framework default** `:vscode` — if neither is set

Concretely the `get-editor` fn (or whatever the call site is)
checks localStorage first via a small helper, falls back to the
atom otherwise.

The override is **purely client-side** — it doesn't mutate the
host's atom, doesn't affect other browsers / tabs / users.
Reloading after clearing the localStorage entry lands the
developer back on the host's `configure!` choice.

## What if the developer is using a NON-enumerated editor?

The `{:custom ...}` escape hatch already exists in the framework
(per `config.cljc:381`). The General-tab affordance MUST surface
it — the Custom radio + the template input — so e.g. Sublime /
Emacs / Vim users can configure their own URI without editing the
host app.

The defense-in-depth allowlist (rf2-cm93v) gates which schemes
can actually launch; if the user enters a `https://...` template,
the click-time seam will reject it. The General-tab UI can
optionally validate the template at edit-time + show an inline
warning, but the click-time gate is the security boundary.

## Acceptance

1. Settings popup → General tab carries an "Editor" field group
   with the enumerated radio set + Custom escape hatch.
2. Selecting a value updates the running config immediately —
   the next click-to-source affordance uses the new URI without
   a reload.
3. Selection persists across page reloads via localStorage.
4. "Reset to host default" restores the host's `configure!`-
   supplied value (clears the override).
5. Footer / inline hint shows the host default so the developer
   knows what they're overriding.
6. Custom template input renders the placeholders inline + is
   validated against the allowlist for obvious mistakes
   (worker decides edit-time validation strictness; click-time
   gate is the security boundary).
7. `:rf.story/editor` (Story's independent editor preference)
   gets the same treatment OR a sibling bead — Mike's call.
   Lean: file separately so each tool's UX lands independently.
8. Spec/015-Configuration.md gains a new subsection §End-user
   override under §`:rf.xray/editor` describing the
   localStorage-backed override + the host-default
   relationship.
9. `docs/xray/api/config-keys.md` mirrors the spec update
   (it's the user-facing surface).
10. Tests: a unit test confirms the resolution order
   (override > host > framework); a click-flow test confirms
   a flipped radio fires the right URI.

## What does NOT change

- The framework's editor-URI builder + the scheme allowlist —
  both already handle every enumerated value
- The `:rf.xray/editor` config key + `configure!` surface — host
  default behaviour is unchanged
- The `:rf.xray/project-root` companion key — unchanged
- Story's editor preference (separate atom, separate localStorage
  if it adopts the same pattern)
- The Settings popup's other three tabs (Keybindings, Buffer,
  Diff) — untouched

## Why this matters — programmer UX

The current configure-time-only design assumes a single editor
per team. That assumption fails on:

- **Mixed-editor teams** (a JetBrains user on a VS Code default
  team — a real, common case at agencies + open-source projects)
- **Personal preference drift** (a developer moves from VS Code
  to Cursor; the team's app still defaults to vscode for the
  rest)
- **Editor experiments** (try Zed for a week; flip back if it
  doesn't stick — no app-code change needed)

Each is a friction point Xray's substrate already solves, behind
a surface the end-user doesn't have access to. The override
closes the loop.

## Coordination

Single-bead scope. Touches:
- Settings popup (Xray-internal, isolated surface)
- Editor read path (config.cljc — small fn change)
- localStorage shim (Xray already persists other prefs;
  reuse the pattern)
- spec/015-Configuration.md (hot-zone; sequential dispatch)
- docs/xray/api/config-keys.md (user-facing reference)
- Tests

No framework changes — the editor-URI builder + allowlist are
unchanged.

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27.

Settings popup → General tab picker; slot [:general :editor-override] in the existing settings map; config/get-editor resolves override > host > :vscode. Gates green: 4791 cljs tests / 124 browser tests / bundle-isolation.

title: Framework: :schema key on reg-machine — validate machine :data + new :where :machine-data boundary
description:
## Why

Today there is no first-class way to nominate a schema for a
state machine's `:data` slot. Users CAN attach validation via
the existing `reg-app-schema` against the snapshot path:

    (rf/reg-app-schema [:rf/machines :drawer/editor :data] DataSchema)

But the schema lives apart from the machine spec, the failure
surfaces as `:where :app-db` (with a path the operator has to
mentally parse as "ah, machine data"), and the loose coupling
reads as accidental rather than designed.

Worse: spec/005 already commits to the behaviour as if it
shipped. Two foundational paragraphs claim the framework
composes `:rf/machines`'s schema "automatically from the
registered machines' `:data` schemas" — but the grammar table
at spec/005:193-201 lists the legal `reg-machine` keys
(`:initial · :data · :guards · :actions · :meta · :states · :on
· :entry · :exit`) and **no `:schema` slot exists**. Aspirational
prose without a supporting surface. Sibling bead handles the
spec reconciliation; this bead adds the surface.

## What changes — surface design

Add a `:schema` key to the `reg-machine` spec, mirroring how
`:schema` rides on every other registration kind in the
framework:

    (rf/reg-machine :drawer/editor
      {:initial :idle
       :data    {:circles [] :undo [] :redo []}
       :schema  DrawerData                ;; NEW — validates :data
       :guards  {...}
       :actions {...}
       :states  {...}})

The schema validates the machine's `:data` slot. The `:state`
slot is already validated against the machine's own state-id
inventory at compile time (registration fails if a transition
targets an unknown state); the snapshot's reserved `:rf/*` slots
are framework-owned. So the schema's job is exactly the
user-domain `:data` shape.

## Validation timing

Machine `:data` is mutated at six points:

| Mutation site | When |
|---|---|
| Initial `:data` installation | At machine bootstrap |
| `:on-spawn-actions` | At spawn time |
| `:entry` actions (incl. `:initial-entry`) | When entering a state |
| `:exit` actions | When leaving a state |
| `:action` (transition action) | Between exit + entry |
| `:always` / `:after` transitions' actions | Per-region tick |

The natural validation point is the **macrostep boundary** —
after the exit → transition-action → entry sequence completes
and the runtime is about to commit the new snapshot back to
`app-db`. Single validation per macrostep regardless of how
many actions fired; the snapshot the framework would write is
the value validated.

This is the same position in the lifecycle as the existing
`:where :app-db` check; in fact machine validation is a refined
case of app-db validation (because machine snapshots LIVE in
app-db per the Single Store invariant). The new `:where` value
gives the operator richer context — they read "machine :drawer/
editor data violated DrawerData during the :submit transition's
entry" instead of "app-db commit at [:rf/machines :drawer/
editor :data :circles 3 :radius]".

### Initial-data installation

At machine bootstrap the initial `:data` map gets installed
into the snapshot. Validate it against the schema then — the
machine spec's `:data {:circles []}` could violate the
`:schema` if the user typoed (e.g. wrote `:data {:cirles []}`).
Failing fast at registration / first-bootstrap is more useful
than waiting for the first transition.

### Recovery posture

Same as `:where :app-db` — **rollback the whole cascade**.
Machine state lives in app-db; the cascade's `:db-before` /
`:db-after` capture the pre/post snapshot of EVERY machine
along with the rest of app-db. Rollback restores all of it
atomically. The framework can't surgically roll back just the
machine's macrostep without affecting other state mutations the
handler performed; full-cascade rollback is the only consistent
option.

For the Epoch panel: same blast-radius muting treatment as
`:where :app-db` rollback (FX / SUBSCRIPTIONS / VIEWS chrome
visually muted with "cascade rolled back here ↓" indicator).

## Trace event extension

Extend the existing `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` op
with a new `:where` value + extra tags:

    {:op   :rf.error/schema-validation-failure
     :tags {:where           :machine-data
            :failing-id      <machine-id>           ; e.g. :drawer/editor
            :machine-id      <machine-id>           ; alias for clarity
            :state           <fsm-keyword-or-path>  ; the state at violation
            :phase           <phase-keyword>        ; :entry/:exit/:action/...
            :action-id       <action-id-or-nil>     ; named action's id
            :path            [<in-data-path...>]    ; sub-path that failed
            :value           <failing-value-or-:rf/redacted>
            :explain         <Malli explain map>
            :rollback?       true
            :recovery        :rolled-back
            :sensitive?      <bool>}}

Reuses the existing op so the existing Issues triage, Xray
projections, schema-violation-row plumbing, and the per-step
attachment bead (rf2-xgeag) all flow through the same row
shape with one new `:where` case.

The Epoch panel's per-step attachment (rf2-xgeag) gets one new
attachment site: machine-cascade rows (per rf2-u69j7) inside
the HANDLER step. The pink SCHEMA VIOLATION sub-block attaches
to the specific guard/action/transition row that triggered the
bad write — operator sees the failure right next to the action
that produced it.

## Spec changes

### spec/005-StateMachines.md

1. **Grammar table** (spec/005:193-201) — add the `:schema`
   row:

       | `:schema` | top-level | optional — validates the
                                  machine's `:data` slot at every
                                  macrostep boundary + at
                                  bootstrap |

2. **New §Schema validation** subsection under §Transition
   table grammar — describe the validation timing (macrostep
   boundary + bootstrap), the recovery (full-cascade rollback),
   the trace emit shape, the cross-link to spec/010.
3. **Anchor the aspirational paragraphs** (spec/005:154 + 165)
   — these become factual once this bead lands. The sibling
   reconciliation bead removes their "aspirational" framing.
4. **Conformance** (spec/005:3105+) — gain a new capability
   row for `:data` schema validation. v1 CLJS reference claims
   support; other ports declare in their conformance matrix.

### spec/010-Schemas.md

- **Per-step recovery table** (spec/010:137+) — add a 7th row:

       | 7. Machine `:data` | A machine's `:data` slot after
                              a macrostep doesn't conform to
                              its registered `:schema`. | Same
                              as 4 (app-db) — full cascade
                              rollback; emit with
                              `:where :machine-data`,
                              `:failing-id` = machine-id,
                              `:state`, `:phase`, `:action-id`. |

- **Where schemas attach** — add `reg-machine`'s `:schema`
  alongside `reg-event-*` / `reg-cofx` / `reg-fx` / `reg-sub`.

### spec/Spec-Schemas.md

- `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` tags entry — add
  `:where :machine-data` to the closed set.
- Add a new schema id `:rf/machine-data-schema-violation`
  documenting the extra tags (`:machine-id`, `:state`,
  `:phase`, `:action-id`).

### spec/Conventions.md

- The `:schema` key on `reg-machine` joins the catalogue of
  registration metadata keys; cross-reference from
  Conventions's reserved-key inventory.

## Impl changes

### `implementation/machines/`

1. **Registration** — `make-machine-handler` (or wherever
   `reg-machine` translates spec → registry entry) reads
   `:schema` from the spec, validates against the spec-schemas'
   `:rf/machine-schema` schema (it must be a valid schema in
   the registered validator's language), stores it on the
   machine's handler-meta.
2. **Bootstrap path** — `:rf.machine/bootstrap` handler
   validates initial `:data` against `:schema` before the
   first snapshot install. Failure emits the trace + refuses
   to bootstrap (the machine never starts).
3. **Macrostep commit** — wherever the runtime computes the
   post-macrostep snapshot and is about to write it back to
   app-db, validate `:data` against `:schema` first. Failure
   emits + rolls back the entire cascade (via the same
   mechanism `:where :app-db` uses today).
4. **Spawn path** — `:rf.machine/spawn` validates the spawned
   actor's initial `:data` against the actor machine's
   `:schema`. Same trace shape.

### `implementation/schemas/` (or wherever validator hot-paths live)

- New validate-at-machine-boundary call site mirroring the
  existing app-db / fx-args / sub-return surfaces.
- The validator integration is the same `(validate schema
  value)` truthy?/`(explain schema value)` pair documented in
  spec/010 §validator-fn extension point. No new validator
  affordance — just a new call site.

### Tests

- `reg-machine` accepts `:schema` and the schema validates
  initial `:data`.
- A `:schema` declaring `[:map [:n pos-int?]]` rejects
  `:data {:n 0}` at bootstrap.
- A transition action that returns bad `:data` rolls back the
  cascade + emits `:where :machine-data`.
- A spawned actor's initial `:data` violating its `:schema` is
  rejected at spawn time.
- `:where :machine-data` violations carry the full payload
  (`:machine-id`, `:state`, `:phase`, `:action-id`) so the
  Xray attachment bead has all the data it needs.
- Production elision: when `debug-enabled? false`, the
  machine-data validation site is gated like every other
  schema check (per spec/010 §Production builds).

## Tooling impact (out-of-scope here; flagged for downstream)

- **Xray Epoch panel (rf2-xgeag)** — the per-step attachment
  bead consumes `:where`; the new `:machine-data` case attaches
  to the HANDLER step's machine-cascade row matching
  `:state` + `:phase` + `:action-id`. Already covered in
  rf2-xgeag's design but flagged here for cross-reference.
- **Xray Issues panel** — cross-session triage already groups
  by `:where`; new value flows through without code change.
- **Machine Inspector / Static panels** — when the spec carries
  a `:schema`, the panel can render its shape inline (similar
  to `:guards` / `:actions` rendering). Optional follow-on.

## What does NOT change

- The `:data` slot itself — its shape, mutation grammar,
  reserved `:rf/*` keys are unchanged.
- Existing machines without `:schema` continue to work — the
  key is optional; absence means "no validation" (consistent
  with every other registration kind's `:schema`).
- `(rf/reg-app-schema [:rf/machines :foo :data] ...)` continues
  to work as a path-based escape hatch. It overlaps with the
  new declarative form; users can use either. The Conventions
  guidance recommends the new form (`:schema` on
  `reg-machine`) for locality + readability.
- The Single Store invariant — machine state still lives in
  app-db at `[:rf/machines <id>]`; this just adds a refined
  validation lens.

## Acceptance

1. `reg-machine`'s spec accepts a `:schema` key per the new
   grammar.
2. Initial `:data` installation validates against `:schema` at
   bootstrap; failure prevents the machine from starting.
3. Each macrostep that mutates `:data` validates the post-step
   snapshot against `:schema`; failure emits
   `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure :where :machine-data`
   + rolls back the entire cascade.
4. Spawned actors' initial `:data` validates against the actor
   machine's `:schema`; same trace + recovery.
5. Spec changes: spec/005 grammar table + new §Schema
   validation; spec/010 per-step recovery table + Where
   schemas attach; Spec-Schemas tags update.
6. Production elision: `debug-enabled? false` short-circuits
   the validation call site.
7. Tests pass for every acceptance criterion above.
8. Existing machines without `:schema` are unaffected.

## Coordination

Spec/005 + spec/010 + Spec-Schemas are all hot-zone files
(sequential, never parallel per CLAUDE.md). Worker checks
dashboard before dispatching.

The sibling bead (spec reconciliation for spec/005:154 + 165
prose) BLOCKS-ON this bead — those paragraphs become factual
once `:schema` ships. File the reconciliation as a follow-on
PR after this lands.

Pre-alpha posture: ship cleanly, no flag-gated rollout.

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2227 — :schema on reg-machine + :where :machine-data validation boundary. Framework: post-commit walker AND-conjoined with validate-app-schema!; spawn-fx pre-install gate; new late-bind hook :machines/validate-machine-data!. Spec: 005 grammar+§Schema validation, 010 step 4a+recovery row 7, Spec-Schemas :where enum extension. Tests: 6 JVM tests in machine_schema_test.clj. Quality gates green (JVM full sweep, CLJS 4770 tests, elision 39/39, bundle-isolation, late-bind drift).

title: Xray: Epoch panel — attach schema violations to their owning pipeline step (pink SCHEMA VIOLATION sub-block + actionable insights)
description:
## Why

Today the Epoch panel renders every schema violation in the cascade
into a single trailing SCHEMA VIOLATIONS step at the bottom. The
operator reads the violation in isolation from the work it failed
on — they have to mentally jump from "violation at row 3 of the
trailing step" back up to "which HANDLER / which cofx / which fx
that was about". The data the projection already captures
(`:where`, `:failing-id`, `:path`, `:value`, `:explain`,
`:rollback?`, `:recovery`) is enough to attach each violation
directly to the pipeline step it relates to, eliminating that
mental round-trip.

Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-27.

## Attachment mapping — every `:where` value lands on its owning step

The six boundaries map cleanly onto existing pipeline steps:

| `:where` slot | Owning pipeline step | Granularity |
|---|---|---|
| `:event` | DISPATCH | one step (the dispatched event) |
| `:cofx` | COEFFECT step matching the cofx-id | per-cofx (post-restructure) |
| `:app-db` | HANDLER (under its `:db` sub-section) | one step |
| `:fx-args` | FX step, row matching `:fx-id` | per-fx row |
| `:sub-return` | SUBSCRIPTIONS step, row matching sub-id | per-sub row |
| `:hot-reload` | — (out-of-band, no cascade step owns it) | — |

Projection: `schema-violation-row` (`projection.cljc:940-962`)
already captures `:failing-id` / `:path`. The new projection pass
walks the existing violation-rows + bins them by their owning step
(matching `:failing-id` against the step's id/row-id). The
existing pooled `schema-violations-step` retires.

## Visual shape — pink sub-block inside the owning step

Each violation renders as a **distinct sub-block within its owning
step's body** — visually unmissable, programmer-actionable. Sketch:

```
[circle 3] [HANDLER badge] reg-event-fx :user/email-changed     [12.3ms]

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  ⚠  SCHEMA VIOLATION                          rolled back│
  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │
  │  app-db commit · :user/email-schema                      │
  │  path:    [:user :email]                                 │
  │  expected: :string                                       │
  │  got:      :int  (value was 42)                          │
  │                                                          │
  │  ↗ open :user/email-schema  (reg-app-schema)             │
  │  ↗ open :user/email-changed (reg-event-fx)               │
  │  ▸ full explain map                                      │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  :db  [diff] [all]
    + [:user :email] 42
    …
```

### Chrome details

- **Background**: pink wash — a soft tint (suggest `:bg-violation`
  new palette token, light pink in light theme, deep-pink-muted in
  dark). Distinct from the SUBSCRIPTIONS badge (`:magenta-pink`
  `#ec4899` — fully saturated, not used for backgrounds elsewhere)
  AND from the SCHEMA-VIOLATIONS step badge today (`:warning`
  yellow, which retires with the trailing step). Worker picks the
  exact hex but the visual goal is *immediately legible as
  alert* without being noisy enough to overpower the cascade.
- **Border**: 1px on `:border-default` or a slightly stronger pink
  edge to set the sub-block apart from its host step.
- **Padding**: matches the COEFFECT body-row alignment (no extra
  left-padding — left-aligned with the step's content column).
- **Title**: "⚠ SCHEMA VIOLATION" — uppercase, the warning-glyph
  is part of the title, not separate. Right-aligned chip on the
  same line for the rollback / recovery posture
  (`rolled back` / `fx skipped` / `returned nil` /
  `logged + skipped`).
- **Title styling**: bold + the badge taxonomy `:warning` token
  for the glyph + title color; programmer's eye lands on the
  title in <100ms.

## Programmer-actionable content — what each sub-block carries

The point of the restructure is not just "move the violation up to
where it belongs"; it's "give the programmer everything they need
to debug it without leaving the panel". Each sub-block carries:

### Common to every violation (`:where`-agnostic)

1. **Headline line**: `<where-label> · <failing-id>` (e.g.
   `app-db commit · :user/email-schema`)
2. **Path** (when present): the in-db or in-payload path that
   failed, rendered as `path: [:user :email]`
3. **Expected** + **Got** lines: human-readable decoding of
   Malli's `explain` data structure into:

       expected: :string
       got:      :int  (value was 42)

   For schemas more complex than primitive predicates, render
   the failing sub-schema (Malli's `:errors[i].schema` field
   resolved through `m/form`). For multi-error explain maps
   (a sub-schema with N errors), render the FIRST error
   prominently + a `(+ N-1 more)` chip that expands to the
   rest.
4. **Two click-to-source links**:
   - `↗ open <failing-id> (reg-…)` — opens the editor at the
     registration call site (event handler / cofx / fx / sub /
     `reg-app-schema`). Reuses the existing source-coord
     mechanism (`(rf/handler-meta <kind> id)` → `{:file :line}`
     → `[:rf.xray/open-in-editor]`).
   - `↗ open <schema-name>` — opens the editor at the
     `reg-app-schema` declaration. For inline `:schema`
     metadata on a registration the coord is the same; for
     `reg-app-schema` it's the bulk-registration call site. If
     the framework's source-coord stamping doesn't yet cover
     this slot, file a follow-on framework bead and degrade
     gracefully (text only, no link) in the meantime.
5. **▸ full explain map** — collapsed by default; expand to
   show the raw Malli `explain` data via `ei/mini` for power
   users who want the structural view. Sensitive slots already
   redacted at substrate emit-time.
6. **Recovery chip** (right-aligned in title line): the
   recovery posture (`rolled back` / `fx skipped` /
   `returned nil` / `logged + skipped`).

### Per-`:where` tailored content

#### `:event` — event payload violation
- Render the **dispatched event vector** with the failing
  position highlighted (e.g. `[:user/email-changed 42]` with
  `42` underlined in pink).
- If the schema is a tuple/cat, show the **expected positional
  shape** next to the actual: `expected: [keyword?, :string]`
  vs `got: [keyword?, :int]`.
- Pinned to: DISPATCH step. The DISPATCH step today has just
  the event vector; the violation sub-block sits beneath it.

#### `:cofx` — coeffect injection violation
- Show the cofx-id + the injected value.
- Pinned to: the COEFFECT step matching the cofx-id (post-
  restructure each cofx is its own step).
- The injected value the cofx returned gets rendered on the
  pre-existing COEFFECT body row; the violation sub-block
  sits beneath it inside the same step.

#### `:app-db` — app-db commit violation
- Show the **path** that failed + the **before** vs **after**
  values at that path so the programmer sees what the handler
  tried to write.
- If `:rollback? true`: "This commit was rolled back. App-db
  restored to its pre-cascade state. No fx fired downstream."
  + visually mute the FX / SUBSCRIPTIONS / VIEWS steps
  downstream (greyscale shift, "rolled back" overlay) so the
  programmer instantly grasps the blast radius.
- If the violation is against the **root schema** (path = []):
  the headline reads `app-db commit · root` and the failing
  sub-path inside Malli's explain is rendered prominently.
- Pinned to: the HANDLER step's `:db` sub-section.

#### `:fx-args` — fx args violation
- Show the **fx-id** + the **failing args map** with the
  failing key highlighted.
- "This fx was skipped. Other fx in the cascade still ran."
- Pinned to: the FX step's row matching the fx-id. The row
  visually expands to host the sub-block; the row's check-mark
  flips to a warning glyph.

#### `:sub-return` — sub return-value violation
- Show the **sub-id** + the **query-vector** + the returned
  value vs the schema.
- "Sub returned nil to its consumer." (default recovery)
- Pinned to: the SUBSCRIPTIONS step's row matching the sub-id.

#### `:hot-reload` — hot-reload drift
- Out-of-band — no cascade step owns it. Two options:
  - **Option A**: keep a thin standalone SCHEMA HOT-RELOAD step
    at the bottom of the cascade carrying ONLY hot-reload
    violations (renamed from SCHEMA VIOLATIONS for clarity).
  - **Option B**: pin to the panel-level header as a one-line
    banner: "1 schema hot-reload drift in this cascade".
- Suggest A — preserves the cascade-step rhythm + keeps every
  thing in the numbered timeline.

## Edge cases — think carefully

1. **Multiple violations on the same step** (e.g. 3 fx in one
   cascade each fail args validation): each gets its own
   sub-block, stacked vertically inside the step body. The step's
   header carries `⚠ 3` count chip.
2. **app-db root + path schemas failing simultaneously**: each is
   a separate violation row; both attach to HANDLER. Two sub-
   blocks stacked.
3. **Rollback case downstream visibility**: when the HANDLER
   step's app-db violation rolls back the cascade, the FX /
   SUBSCRIPTIONS / VIEWS / SCHEMA VIOLATIONS-from-rolled-fx
   steps SHOULD still render (the operator wants to see what
   would have happened) but visually muted + with a
   `cascade rolled back here ↓` indicator at the rollback point.
   That's a substantial visual change; out-of-scope here but
   worth a follow-on bead.
4. **Sub-return violations on subs not in this cascade's
   SUBSCRIPTIONS step**: a sub can recompute on a cascade that
   doesn't display it (e.g. recompute triggered indirectly via
   a flow). Edge case — attach to the SUBSCRIPTIONS step
   anyway, with an explanatory chip "indirect recompute" if the
   row wouldn't otherwise appear in the SUBSCRIPTIONS step.
   Worker decides based on real-cascade behaviour.
5. **`:explain` map absent** (some violations may emit with no
   Malli explain — e.g. ports using a different validator):
   degrade the Expected/Got rendering gracefully to just
   "value did not conform to schema `<schema-id>`" + the raw
   value display.

## What retires

- The trailing SCHEMA VIOLATIONS step + `schema-violations-step`
  projection (`projection.cljc:974-985`) + `render-schema-
  violations-step` view (`view.cljs:2880-2918`) + the orphan
  styles (`view.cljs:965-1042`). Per pre-alpha posture — delete
  cleanly, no back-compat shim.
- The `:SCHEMA-VIOLATIONS` badge in `badge.cljc` (lines 92, 106)
  — unless preserved for the standalone hot-reload step.
- The "open issues →" button on the retired step. Each per-step
  sub-block can carry its own "↗ Issues" link if useful; or the
  panel header gets a small persistent affordance.

## What does NOT change

- The substrate's two trace ops (`:rf.error/schema-validation-
  failure` + `:rf.schema/violation`) — same shape, same payload.
- The `:rf.xray/...` events the Issues panel consumes — same.
- Spec 010 (Schemas) boundary contract — the cascade-side
  presentation changes; the underlying contract is identical.
- Per-row data captured by `schema-violation-row` — same. New
  projection consumes the existing data.

## Acceptance

1. Each violation in a cascade renders as a pink sub-block
   inside its owning pipeline step (DISPATCH / COEFFECT step /
   HANDLER / FX row / SUBSCRIPTIONS row).
2. Sub-block carries: headline, path, expected/got, two
   click-to-source links, recovery chip, full-explain expand.
3. The trailing SCHEMA VIOLATIONS step is retired (or repurposed
   as SCHEMA HOT-RELOAD standalone — Mike chooses Option A or B
   above).
4. The HANDLER step's app-db rollback visibly mutes the
   downstream cascade chrome so the operator reads the blast
   radius at-a-glance.
5. spec/021 §SCHEMA-VIOLATIONS section retired; new section
   §Violation attachment contract added describing the
   per-step sub-block + the attachment mapping.
6. Spec 010 (Schemas) gains a brief "Tooling surface — Xray
   attachment" cross-reference paragraph linking to spec/021's
   new section.
7. Tests: existing schema-violations-step tests retired;
   per-`:where` attachment tests added (5 cases — one per
   non-hot-reload boundary); rollback-mute test added.
8. The panel-gallery `fixtures_epoch.cljs` gains one or two
   violation-bearing fixtures exercising the most common cases
   (`:app-db rolled back`, `:fx-args skipped`, `:sub-return
   nil`).

## Why this matters — programmer UX

Today, when an app-db violation rolls back a cascade, the
operator reads (top-to-bottom): DISPATCH, COEFFECT, HANDLER
(with diff that looks fine), FX (with `2 fired ✓`),
SUBSCRIPTIONS (with `:user/profile recomputed`), VIEWS (with
unmount/mount events), … and ONLY at the bottom of the cascade
do they discover the SCHEMA VIOLATIONS step saying "actually,
none of that happened, the cascade rolled back". Every
intermediate step they just read was a lie.

With per-step attachment + the downstream-mute treatment, they
see the cascade is rolled back the moment their eye hits the
HANDLER step. The visual story matches the runtime story.

Same logic for `:fx-args` — the FX row carrying the failure
shows the failure inline, not as a footnote 200px below.

For `:sub-return` — the sub's row shows it returned nil at the
moment the operator sees the sub in the cascade. The
trailing-step rendering forces them to cross-reference; the
inline rendering doesn't.

This is the "scannable at a glance" lens of the Epoch panel
applied to its noisiest content. Today the panel reads the
cascade well except when something failed; the restructure
makes failure render as legibly as success.

## Coordination

Touches:
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc`
  (retire `schema-violations-step`; add per-step violation
  attachment in `project`)
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`
  (sub-block render fn + per-step injection at each owning
  render-fn — `render-dispatch-step` / `render-coeffect-step`
  / `render-handler-step` / `render-fx-step` / `render-
  subscriptions-step`; retire `render-schema-violations-step`
  + orphan styles)
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/badge.cljc`
  (retire `:SCHEMA-VIOLATIONS` taxonomy unless kept for
  hot-reload standalone)
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljc`
  (new `:bg-violation` palette token)
- `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §SCHEMA-
  VIOLATIONS section
- `spec/010-Schemas.md` brief tooling cross-ref paragraph
- Tests + fixtures per above

Hot-zone: spec/021 + spec/010 are both hot-zone files
(sequential, never parallel). Worker checks dashboard before
dispatching.

Pre-alpha posture: delete the retired surfaces cleanly.

Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-27.
close_reason: PR #2226 — schema violations attach inline to their owning pipeline step as pink sub-blocks. Hot-reload drift rides standalone tail step (Option A). Rolled-back app-db violations mute downstream cascade.

title: Xray: Epoch panel — one FLOW step per flow (mirror COEFFECT per-cofx pattern)
description:
## Why

The COEFFECT step in the Epoch cascade was restructured during
pair-debug 2026-05-26 from "one step with N rows" to "N steps,
one per coeffect". The change made each injected cofx a first-
class step in the numbered cascade — the operator scans the
pipeline + counts cofx by counting steps, not by counting rows
inside a step.

The FLOW step still carries the old "one step with N rows" shape
and should be restructured the same way: **one FLOW pipeline step
per flow that fired**, mirroring the COEFFECT pattern exactly.

## What changes

### Projection — `projection.cljc`

Current shape (`projection.cljc:622-631`):

    (defn flow-step
      [events]
      (let [rows (flow-rows events)]
        (when (seq rows)
          {:step  :flow
           :badge :FLOW
           :rows  rows})))

Target shape — splat the flow-rows into individual `:flow` steps
the way `cofx-steps` is built (mirror the `let cofx-steps (mapv …)`
pattern in `project`):

    (let [flow-rows (flow-rows events)
          flow-steps (mapv (fn [{:keys [flow-id path before after
                                         duration-ms]}]
                             {:step        :flow
                              :badge       :FLOW
                              :flow-id     flow-id
                              :path        path
                              :before      before
                              :after       after
                              :duration-ms duration-ms})
                           flow-rows)]
      …)

Then in `project` (`projection.cljc:1180-1200` — the same `let`
that builds `cofx-steps` + `steps`) replace `(flow-step events)`
with the splice of `flow-steps` (positioned between HANDLER and
FX — same slot as today). The exact splice mirrors how
`cofx-steps` is spliced before HANDLER.

`flow-rows` defn (`projection.cljc:599-620`) stays as-is — the
per-row projection is correct; only the step-aggregation shape
changes. `flow-step` defn at lines 622-631 is deleted entirely
(the splicing in `project` replaces its single call site).

### View — `view.cljs`

The current `render-flow-step` at `view.cljs:2368-2383` renders
the OLD aggregate shape. Replace with a per-flow render that
mirrors `render-coeffect-step` (the COEFFECT step's view, also
restructured during pair-debug). Target:

- **Header line** (left-to-right): numbered-circle · `:FLOW`
  badge pill · flow-id (hyperlinked to the flow's registration
  source if a source-coord is available — same affordance shape
  as the COEFFECT step's `:testdeck/now` hyperlink + the HANDLER
  step's `reg-event-fx` hyperlink) · duration chip.
- **Body row** (next line, left-aligned with the badge — no extra
  left padding, matching the pair-debug feedback "for COEFFECTS,
  the line after the badge, make it left align with the badge"):
  one diff line in the COEFFECT diff format:

      + [<path>] <before> → <after>

  (or just `+ [<path>] <after>` when there's no `:before` —
  worker decides the EDN representation; can use the existing
  `flow-row-view`'s before/after rendering with the COEFFECT
  step's body layout).

The current "2 flows recomputed" verb on the header (`view.cljs:
2377-2378`) goes away — the pipeline now has N numbered FLOW
steps so the count is visually obvious.

### Hyperlink target

The COEFFECT step hyperlinks the cofx-id to the cofx-handler's
registration source. The FLOW step should hyperlink the flow-id
to the flow's registration source (`reg-flow` call site).

If `rf/handler-meta` doesn't yet have a `:flow` lookup kind,
worker checks the framework's flow-registry surface (Spec 006
§Flows) and either:
- Uses an existing meta affordance for flows (preferred), OR
- Files a follow-on framework bead to add `(rf/handler-meta
  :flow flow-id)` parity with `:event` / `:machine`. In the
  interim, render the flow-id without a hyperlink (graceful
  degradation matching the COEFFECT step's fallback when no
  coord is captured).

## Where things stay the same

- `flow-rows` projection (`projection.cljc:599-620`) — unchanged.
  The per-row projection from `:rf.flow/computed` events is
  already correct (per rf2-yhgk8 canonical-tag fix in the 12h
  audit window).
- The cascade `:step :flow` keyword — same, just one per flow
  instead of one for the cluster.
- The badge taxonomy (`badge.cljc :FLOW` entry) — unchanged.
- `numbered-circle :FLOW` + colour token (`:accent` per Spec 005)
  — unchanged.
- The `flow-row-view` body renderer can be reused or inlined —
  worker decides. The COEFFECT step inlined the body row into
  the per-step render; FLOW can do the same.
- Conditional rendering: if no `:rf.flow/computed` events fire
  in the epoch, no FLOW steps appear (just like the old
  conditional render). Empty cascade for epochs with no flows.

## What does NOT change

- The substrate's `:rf.flow/computed` trace event shape — same.
- The flow-handler API (`reg-flow`) — same.
- Spec 006 (ReactiveSubstrate) flow contract — same.
- Other pipeline steps (DISPATCH, COEFFECT, HANDLER, FX,
  SUBSCRIPTIONS, VIEWS) — unchanged.
- The HANDLER step's flow-aware bits (if any — most flow logic
  is downstream of HANDLER, so likely no impact there).

## Acceptance

1. An epoch that fires 2 flows renders TWO numbered FLOW steps
   in the cascade pipeline — operator can scan the left rail
   and count flows by counting circles.
2. An epoch that fires 0 flows renders NO FLOW steps (same
   conditional behaviour as today).
3. Each FLOW step's header carries: numbered-circle, `:FLOW`
   badge, flow-id (hyperlinked to source where available),
   duration chip — same visual rhythm as the COEFFECT step.
4. Each FLOW step's body shows the diff on a new line, left-
   aligned with the badge (NO extra left padding) — same
   alignment as the COEFFECT step's body row.
5. The aggregate "N flows recomputed" verb is gone from any
   step header — the count is visually self-evident from the
   numbered cascade.
6. Spec/021 §9.1.X (FLOW step contract) updated to document
   the per-flow shape — same way COEFFECT is documented
   per-cofx.
7. Tests: existing flow-step tests retired / rewritten for the
   per-flow shape; new test exercises a 2-flow epoch + verifies
   2 FLOW steps render.
8. The panel-gallery `fixtures_epoch.cljs` flow-variant fixture
   updated to render N flows visually distinct.

## Coordination

Single-bead scope. Touches:
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc`
  (delete `flow-step`, splice `flow-steps` in `project`)
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`
  (rewrite `render-flow-step` as per-flow render mirroring
  `render-coeffect-step`)
- `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §FLOW step
- `tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures_epoch.cljs`
  (flow variant)
- Tests under
  `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/`

Hot-zone: spec/021 is hot-zone per CLAUDE.md (sequential,
never parallel). Worker checks dashboard for in-flight
spec/021 work before dispatching.

Pre-alpha posture (no back-compat shims); delete `flow-step`
cleanly rather than gating behind a flag.

Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-27. Mirrors the COEFFECT
restructure from pair-debug 2026-05-26 — same pattern, same
visual rhythm.
close_reason: PR #2226 — one FLOW step per flow, mirror of COEFFECT per-cofx split. Projection splats flow-rows; view renders each as a first-class numbered step.

title: Xray: Epoch panel — remove 'computational timeline' subtitle + 'cascade total' top chip (partial revert of rf2-nqt3d)

## Why

title: Framework: re-word frame-bound-fn docstring — drop superseded discipline-failure rationale (post-rf2-atqkg)
description:
## Why

PR #2200 (rf2-tvu99) shipped `rf/frame-bound-fn` with a docstring at
`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:789-822` that still
teaches the OLD (superseded) bug-class story.

Specifically, lines 815-820:

    Why this is more robust than `(rf/dispatch [...] {:frame :id})`
    at the call site: the explicit-opt pattern is correct but
    discipline-dependent — every dispatch site must remember to
    thread the opt, and **the bug class (rf2-7sdja popup, rf2-kcaiz
    zoom, rf2-p56sk subs-toggle, rf2-tvu99 epoch :db toggle) keeps
    cycling because the discipline fails.**

Per rf2-atqkg (the corrected diagnosis from pair-debug 2026-05-26),
those four beads were **NOT** frame-routing discipline failures.
They were Reagent **lazy-seq deref tracking** failures — the
dispatches landed in the correct frame the entire time; the views
just didn't re-render because the sub-derefs occurred outside
Reagent's reactive scope.

The PR's commit body acknowledges the supersession. The docstring
inside the same PR contradicts it. Future readers learning
`frame-bound-fn` from the docstring will internalise the wrong
mental model + may apply `frame-bound-fn` to bugs that are actually
lazy-seq tracking issues — masking the real fix.

## Why does this matter

1. **Onboarding hazard.** The docstring is the canonical surface for
   "when should I reach for `frame-bound-fn`?" Wrong rationale →
   wrong reach reflex.
2. **Future bug triage.** When a future "click does nothing"
   symptom appears, the docstring tells operators to look for
   "discipline failure". The actual cause is more often lazy-seq
   tracking (now known + documented in spec/006).
3. **Cross-doc consistency.** spec/006 §Lazy-seq deref tracking
   landed in PR #2212 (rf2-atqkg) and pins the correct diagnosis.
   The framework docstring should not contradict the spec.

## What is still correct in the docstring

The framework affordance `frame-bound-fn` itself remains sound. It
is the right pattern for **genuine cross-async-boundary cases**:
- `setTimeout` / `setInterval` callbacks
- `Promise.then` continuations
- `requestAnimationFrame` ticks
- WebSocket / SSE event handlers
- Worker-message handlers

In those cases the dynamic var `*current-frame*` truly is lost
across the boundary, and capture-at-wrap-time is the canonical fix.
The arguments-arity, the example shape, the implementation are all
correct. Only the bug-class rationale paragraph is wrong.

## Fix shape

Re-word the rationale paragraph at lines 815-822 of
`core.cljc`. Approximate target:

    Why prefer this over `(rf/dispatch [...] {:frame :id})` at the
    call site: explicit-opt threading is correct but verbose at
    every dispatch site, and `*current-frame*` can be lost across
    genuine async boundaries — setTimeout / setInterval callbacks,
    Promise.then continuations, requestAnimationFrame ticks,
    WebSocket message handlers — where the dispatch fires AFTER
    the surrounding `with-frame` lexical scope has unwound.
    `frame-bound-fn` captures the frame at wrap time + closes over
    it, so the callback always dispatches in the wrapped frame
    regardless of how deep the async chain goes.

    See spec/006 §Lazy-seq deref tracking (Reagent adapter) for a
    different bug class — view-doesn't-update-on-click — that
    looks superficially similar to "frame lost across React onClick"
    but is actually a Reagent reactive-tracking failure. Lazy-seq
    in a `reg-view` body whose elements deref subscriptions must be
    realised with `doall` / `mapv` / `into` inside the render
    scope. Reach for `frame-bound-fn` only when you have a
    genuine async-boundary case; reach for `doall` when you have
    a reactive-tracking case. The two are not interchangeable.

Specifics:
- DROP the "(rf2-7sdja popup, rf2-kcaiz zoom, rf2-p56sk subs-toggle,
  rf2-tvu99 epoch :db toggle) keeps cycling because the discipline
  fails" sentence entirely. Those beads were misdiagnosed; citing
  them in the docstring perpetuates the wrong model.
- ADD the spec/006 cross-reference so readers landing here on a
  view-doesn't-update bug get routed to the actual fix surface.

## Acceptance

1. `core.cljc:789-822` docstring no longer cites
   rf2-7sdja / rf2-kcaiz / rf2-p56sk / rf2-tvu99 as
   "discipline failure" examples.
2. Docstring DOES explain when `frame-bound-fn` IS the right tool
   (genuine async boundaries — list the 4-5 canonical cases).
3. Docstring includes a "see also spec/006 §Lazy-seq deref
   tracking" reference for the adjacent (different) bug class.
4. No code change to the `frame-bound-fn` implementation — only
   the docstring re-words. The 7 regression tests from PR #2200
   still pass.
5. `mkdocs build --strict` still passes (no cross-ref churn).

## What does NOT change

- `frame-bound-fn` the fn — implementation, arities, semantics
- The `bound-fn` macro — wraps the same machinery
- The 7 regression tests in `core_frame_bound_fn_test.cljs` (or
  wherever they live) — they exercise the affordance, not the
  docstring
- spec/006 §Lazy-seq deref tracking — already correct

## Coordination

Single-file edit on `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc`.
Hot-zone? No — `core.cljc` is large but the docstring re-word is
non-overlapping with any in-flight bead I'm aware of. Worker should
still `git pull --rebase` before pushing.

Per audit `12h-commit-audit-2026-05-27` ⚠️ drift #1.
close_reason: Re-worded frame-bound-fn docstring + spec/002 paragraph post-rf2-atqkg supersession. CLJS + JVM gates green. PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2221

title: feat(xray/machines): machine topology omits :always and :after transitions; chart shows partial state-graph
description:
**Severity: MED** — surfaced by audit rf2-33cqr.

**Symptom.** State machines that use `:always` (eventless conditional transitions) or state-level `:after` (timer-driven transitions) render with NO edges representing those transitions. The chart shows a partial topology — e.g. `(idle) → (loaded) → (error)` with no clue that a `loading` state has an `:after 5s → :timeout` edge.

**Root cause.** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machines/topology.cljs:156-192` (`collect-edges`) walks only `(:on state-node)` per state. `:always` and `:after` slots are never inspected.

**Spec requirement.** `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §17.4 + Figma reconcile (lines 1015-1039) require the chart to surface `:after` rings ("◴ 5s → :timeout") and the events-as-nodes / Stately-paradigm shift (rf2-qo5xy + rf2-a2b55, both landed) calls for transition rendering of `:always` choices.

**Impact.** Operators reading the topology to validate a machine design see edges that don't match the actual machine spec. Doesn't crash; misleads.

**Recommended fix.**
Extend `collect-edges` (topology.cljs:156) to emit edges for:
- `(:always state-node)` — eventless transitions, target resolved like `:on` targets. Label per Stately convention ("always [guard] / action").
- `(:after state-node)` — timer-driven transitions. Delay-source per spec 005 §Value shape (`:literal | :sub | :fn`). Label per Figma: "◴ 5s → :timeout" or equivalent.

Consult `tools/xray/design-reference/xray_devtools_reference.cljs` (`machine-panel` component) for the canonical visual semantics. Cross-reference with `:rf.machine.timer/scheduled` traces if a live-activity overlay is desired in the same pass.

**Acceptance.** A machine spec containing `:always` or `:after` transitions renders with edges for both, matching the Figma reference design + the post-paradigm-shift event-as-nodes convention.

**Safe to parallel — isolated file.
close_reason: PR #2205 — topology projection emits edges for :always + :after transitions per Stately glyph convention (rf2-a2b55). 12 new tests; spec/021 §17.4.3 updated.

title: Epoch panel: machine cascade as time-ordered + code-interleaved view (rf2-9c27r redesign)
description:
## Goal

Redesign + implement how the Epoch panel renders the machine-driven
cascade for a single event. Current Cluster-B implementation
(rf2-9c27r, landed #2193) renders the handler info as 7
CATEGORIES (TRANSITION / GUARDS / LIFECYCLE / AFTER-TIMERS /
DATA-REDUCTION / SNAPSHOT-DIFF + FX folded). Mike's call: that's
roll-up; the operator needs **temporal order**.

One event dispatched to a state machine can produce a cascade of:
- Guard evaluations (pass / fail / threw)
- Transition (from-state → to-state)
- Exit actions (potentially multiple, per state being exited)
- Entry actions (potentially multiple, per state being entered)
- Always-transitions chasing
- After-timer scheduling / firing
- Data-reduction effects per action
- FX returned by individual actions

These must render **in the order they actually occurred**. Source
code for each guard / entry / exit action should be **interleaved**
inline so the operator can read what ran and what its code is at
the same vertical position. No more "scroll up to see TRANSITION,
scroll down to see LIFECYCLE actions" — the cascade IS the story.

## Stance

Elegance + correctness. Pre-alpha. No back-compat shim — replace
the current machine-handler-section rendering with the new
temporal-cascade rendering.

## Design seed (worker refines)

```
HANDLER  [reg-machine-event-handler] :ws/connect
└─ machine: :ws/connection                                      0.12ms

   1. GUARD [valid-token?] passed                                0.01ms
      (fn [{:keys [token]}] (and token (re-matches #"jwt-.*" token)))

   2. TRANSITION  [:disconnected] → [:connecting]                0.03ms

   3. EXIT action :clear-stale-data (phase :exit)                0.02ms
      (fn [data] (assoc data :stale? false))
      ↳ Δ data: :stale? true → false

   4. ENTRY action :open-socket (phase :entry)                   0.04ms
      (fn [data {:keys [url]}] (assoc data :socket (ws/open url)))
      ↳ FX :ws/open-socket {:url "wss://..."}

   5. ENTRY action :arm-heartbeat-timer (phase :after-scheduled) 0.02ms
      (fn [data] (assoc data :hb-armed? true))
      ↳ TIMER :heartbeat scheduled (after 5000ms → :hb/tick)
```

Each row carries:
- Step ordinal + step badge
- Action / guard name (hyperlink to source)
- Phase (`:exit` / `:transition` / `:entry` / `:always` /
  `:after-action` / `:initial-entry` / `:destroy-exit`)
- Duration (right-aligned, monospace)
- Interleaved source code (always visible, syntax-highlighted)
- Outcome: data-Δ slot, fx slot, timer slot — whichever the
  action emitted

The "categories" view (current Cluster-B layout) is REPLACED, not
augmented. Information is the same; structure shifts from
category-grouped to time-ordered.

## Source-of-truth for ordering

The substrate's `:rf.machine/action-ran` trace events carry
`:phase` (rf2-82a0u landed the closed-set: `:exit / :transition /
:entry / :always / :after-action / :initial-entry / :destroy-exit`).
Guards carry pass/fail/threw outcomes. Timers carry
`:scheduled / :fired / :cancelled` with `:reason`. Use these
events' INSERTION ORDER in the epoch buffer as the canonical
sequence — the substrate already emits them in cascade order.

## Spec updates

Per [[feedback-xray-specs-kept-current]], update:
- `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §9.1.6
  (or wherever the machine-handler section is documented) —
  redesign the section's contract from category-grouped to
  time-ordered cascade.
- Cross-check `tools/xray/spec/023-Trace.md` for any documented
  ordering invariant.

## Surface

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc`
  (new projection: machine cascade → ordered row list)
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`
  (replace category-grouped renderer with cascade renderer)
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/badge.cljc`
  (new badges if needed — GUARD pass / GUARD fail / TRANSITION /
  EXIT / ENTRY / AFTER / DATA-REDUCTION etc.)
- Tests under `tools/xray/test/.../panels/epoch/`
- `tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures_epoch.cljs` —
  the `machine-driven` fixture should exercise the new
  cascade view; update it.

## Acceptance

1. For a machine-driven epoch, the Epoch panel renders a
   single time-ordered cascade view replacing the prior
   7-category roll-up.
2. Each row interleaves source code (always visible) with phase
   + duration + outcome.
3. Source-coord click-to-open works on each row (reuses
   `coord-chip` from rf2-80u5a/ehd8v).
4. Empty-state: a vanilla `reg-event-db` cascade renders the
   original DISPATCH/HANDLER/etc. pipeline unchanged (this redesign
   is machine-specific).
5. Light + dark themes render correctly.
6. Spec/021 §9.1.6 updated.
7. Existing tests pass; new tests cover the cascade ordering.

## Authority

Per Mike: "Don't wait for my approval. Do what you need to do to
make it work, so we have a high quality prototype. Goal is
elegance and correctness, pre alpha."

Worker has design authority on the precise visual encoding —
pick what reads cleanly. The example layout above is a SEED, not
a contract. If the worker can find a cleaner shape, ship it.

## Coordination

This bead's surface conflicts with rf2-zlk6h (Epoch style hoist,
currently in-flight). **Sequence**: dispatch after rf2-zlk6h merges.
The hoist defines hoisted style constants this redesign should
reuse.

title: Hoist Event-detail + diff/render per-row inline styles + share coord-chip
description:
## Source

Audit findings F4 + F5 + L2 from rf2-qa75r (xray efficiency sweep, 2026-05-26).

## Symptom (F4 — Event-detail)

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/event_detail.cljs:370-2032` — 98 inline-style sites. `perf-tier-dot`, `coord-chip`, `dispatch-body`, `db-change-row` (rendered N times per APP-DB CHANGES section), `flow-row` (N per FLOWS section), `interceptor-row` (N per AFTER INTERCEPTORS section) all build inline style maps in render bodies. APP-DB CHANGES alone can render 20-50 diff triples per focused event.

## Symptom (F5 — Diff renderer)

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/hiccup_render.cljs:46` + `diff/render.cljs:26` — 72 combined sites. `gutter`, `header-button`, `breadcrumb-segments` (per-segment loop), `origin-tag-chip`, `format-path-segment` all allocate `:style` per call. A diff render with 5 sections × 30 changed paths × 3 styled spans per row = ~450 allocations.

## Symptom (L2 — coord-chip duplication)

Three near-identical `coord-chip` / `dispatch-source-label` button shapes ("open in editor" with optional external-link icon) live as private defns in `panels/epoch/view.cljs`, `panels/event_detail.cljs`, and similar buttons in `panels/routing.cljs`. The hiccup is identical except for testid + tone. A UX tweak fans out 3 ways.

## Cost

Event-detail: ~5-7 style maps × ~30 diff rows + ~3 styles × ~5 flows + ~3 styles × ~10 interceptors = ~200-250 allocations per event-panel render. Re-runs on focus change + every detail-feed sub recompute.

Diff renderer: ~450 allocations per typical App-DB-Diff render.

## Fix shape

1. **Extract `panels/shared/open_in_editor_chip.cljs`** — promote the duplicated `coord-chip` to one shared util with `(coord-chip coord {:testid :tone :icon-only?})`. Hoist its style def. Drop the three private duplicates.

2. **Event-detail row-style defs** — `db-change-row-style-base`, `flow-row-style-base`, `interceptor-row-style-base` + their per-cell child-element styles, mirroring the rf2-5venq (Trace) extraction pattern.

3. **Diff/render row-style defs** — `gutter-row-style-base`, `gutter-glyph-style-base`, `breadcrumb-segment-style-base` (per-segment colour overlay), `header-button-style-base`, `origin-tag-chip-style-base`. Same pattern in `diff/hiccup_render.cljs` for `gutter` + `key-or-index-label`.

Token reads (`(:bg-1 tokens)` etc.) resolve at ns-load — `tokens` is a static const map; spec/007-UX-IA §CSS custom-property surface.

## Why this matters

Event-detail + App-db-diff are two of the most-pivoted-into tabs (the headline "what changed" pair). Combined ~650+ allocations per panel render. Coord-chip extraction is the secondary win — drops duplicate code + makes a UX iteration on the open-in-editor affordance a one-file change.

## Acceptance

- `panels/shared/open_in_editor_chip.cljs` carries the unified coord-chip. Three private duplicates removed (`epoch/view.cljs`, `event_detail.cljs`, plus any other site that re-creates the affordance).
- Event-detail per-row style maps reduced to hoisted base + overlays (`db-change-row`, `flow-row`, `interceptor-row`).
- Diff renderer per-row style maps reduced to hoisted base + overlays (`gutter`, `breadcrumb-segments`, `header-button`, `origin-tag-chip`).
- No behavioural change. Existing event-panel + app-db-diff browser-smoke + CLJS unit tests pass.
- Combined file `grep ":style \{"` count drops from 98 + 46 + 26 = 170 to ≤100.

## Sequencing

Lands after rf2-5venq (Trace) so the row-style extraction pattern is established. Same shape; mechanical follow-up.

title: Hoist Cancellation-cascade row inline styles to ns-level defs
description:
## Source

Audit finding F2 from rf2-qa75r (xray efficiency sweep, 2026-05-26).

## Symptom

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/cancellation_cascade.cljs:116-266` — `parent-decision-row`, `teardown-row`, `abort-row` each allocate the outer flex container `:style {...}` plus 4-5 child `[:span {:style {...}}]` cells. Cascade is open by default in the Machines side-panel mount + the cross-trace right-click popover; cascade lengths up to ~100 abort entries are plausible (one parent → child teardown → N effect aborts).

The header / dialog / backdrop styles ALREADY live as hoisted helpers in this file (`backdrop-style`, `dialog-style`) — extending the pattern to row primitives is the local-convention completion.

## Cost

~5 inline styles × ~50 rows × every render = ~250 allocations per cascade-panel render. Re-renders on focus-change, on cancel-cause filter change, on collapse-toggle.

## Fix shape

Hoist to private defs at ns top:

- `row-glyph-style` (stable — colour overlay merged via small per-kind branch)
- `time-chip-style` (stable)
- `category-label-style-base` (stable; colour overlay per kind)
- `primary-cell-style` (stable across all three row types — `flex 1; overflow hidden; text-overflow ellipsis; white-space nowrap; color :text-primary`)
- `tertiary-trailing-style` (stable)
- Outer flex-row container — split into `row-style-base` (stable) + `(if clickable? cursor-pointer-overlay cursor-default-overlay)` selector

`expand-button`, `empty-state`, `header` row styles can stay if they''re mount-once; they''re not in the per-row hot path.

## Why this matters

title: Epoch panel: VIEWS step — surface unmounted views (consumes :rf.view/unmounted, already emitted)
description:
## Why

The Epoch panel's VIEWS step shows views that re-rendered this
cascade (per rf2-6djth: view-id + consumed subs + per-view
timing). It does NOT show views that were UNMOUNTED — operator
can't see "this cascade caused N views to teardown" alongside the
re-render count.

Per Mike (pair-debug 2026-05-26): "in the Epoch panel we need to
say when a view was unmounted."

The framework ALREADY emits `:rf.view/unmounted` trace events
(per the late-bind directory: emitted on view-instance teardown
via React.useEffect cleanup / Reagent reaction-dispose unmount
hook). No framework change required — only panel consumption.

## What changes

Projection (`projection.cljc`): new helper `unmounted-views-rows`
filters the epoch's `:trace-events` for `:rf.view/unmounted` and
projects each into a row:

```clj
{:view-id <kw-or-fn-name>
 :coord   <{:file ... :line ...} or nil>}
```

`views-step` either gains a new `:unmounted-rows` slot OR a new
top-level step is added (worker picks; same pattern as the
companion disposed-subs bead).

View (`view.cljs`): VIEWS step renders an "Unmounted" sub-section
listing each unmounted view. Header counter shows:
`N re-rendered; M unmounted`. Empty when no unmounts.

Per-row rendering:
- Glyph like `–` or `✗` (red/error tone) — conveys teardown
- View-id (click-to-source when coord captured — same pattern as

- Optional duration / reason if the trace event carries them

## Acceptance

- VIEWS step gains an "Unmounted" sub-section

title: Framework: emit :rf.sub/dispose trace event (sub-cache eviction)
description:
## Why

The framework currently emits sub trace events for create / run /
skip but NOT for disposal:

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `:rf.sub/create` | A sub is created + cached |
| `:rf.sub/run` | A sub recomputes |
| `:rf.sub/skip` | A sub-run skipped (cache hit) |
| **`:rf.sub/dispose`** | **MISSING** — emitted when a sub is evicted from the cache |

Subs are evicted in two cases (per Mike, pair-debug 2026-05-26):
1. **View unmounts** — every sub the view consumed loses one
   derefer; if that view was the last derefer, the sub disposes
2. **View re-renders without accessing the sub** — e.g.
   `(when X @some-sub)` where `X` flipped false; the sub's
   subscription from this view drops; if last derefer, disposes

Both modes are SAME-tick-as-cascade — disposal happens
synchronously inside the cascade-driven re-render, so disposal IS
meaningfully attributable to the epoch that drove the re-render.
A trace event emitted at the cache-eviction site would correlate
cleanly to its causing cascade.

Why this matters: the operator needs the full subs lifecycle per
cascade — created / recomputed / skipped / disposed — to debug
"why did sub X stop running?" or "did my subscribe cleanup
correctly?". Today the "disposed" half is invisible.

## What changes

Framework: emit a new trace event `:rf.sub/dispose` from the sub
cache's eviction site (`re-frame.subs.memo` — worker locates the
eviction path). Payload mirrors `:rf.sub/run`:

```clj
(trace/emit! :rf.sub :rf.sub/dispose
             {:rf.sub/id     query-id
              :rf.sub/query  query-v
              :rf.sub/reason :no-more-derefers   ; or :view-unmount-cascade
                                                  ; — worker decides the
                                                  ; closed-set vocabulary
              :frame         frame-id})
```

Reason values (closed set — worker confirms):
- `:no-more-derefers` — last subscriber dropped the sub
- `:cache-clear` — explicit reset (e.g. test fixture, hot-reload)
- (other reasons if the framework has more eviction paths)

## Acceptance

1. `:rf.sub/dispose` fires at sub-cache eviction time.
2. Payload includes the sub-id, query vector, eviction reason,
   frame.
3. Wire-budget aware — under `interop/debug-enabled? false` the
   emit is gated (consistent with the other sub trace events).
4. Test: subscribe to a sub from a test view; unmount the view;
   verify `:rf.sub/dispose` fires with `:reason :no-more-derefers`.
5. Test the conditional-access case too — a view that conditionally
   derefs a sub; flip the condition; verify dispose fires when
   the condition stops the deref.

## What does NOT change

- The sub cache mechanism / eviction logic — only adds the trace
  emit at the existing eviction site
- Existing `:rf.sub/create` / `:rf.sub/run` / `:rf.sub/skip`
  events
- Sub-runs projection / epoch-record `:sub-runs` slot

## What DOES change

- New trace event id: `:rf.sub/dispose`
- New ns-keyword tags `:rf.sub/reason` (closed-set enum)
- Possibly: new field on epoch-record `:sub-disposals` if the
  framework wants to project disposals into the epoch shape
  (vs leaving consumers to derive from `:trace-events`)
- Privacy posture: `:rf.sub/value` redaction rules apply (consistent
  with `:rf.sub/run`)

## References

- Existing sub trace emits: `re-frame.subs.memo` line 240, 253,
  304, 359, 412
- Eviction site (worker locates — likely in `memo.cljc` or
  `subs.cljc`)
- Spec 009 §Trace events — add to the canonical inventory
- Consumer (depends on this): rf2-epoch-disposed-subs (Epoch
  panel section)
- Pair-debug 2026-05-26 — Mike's clarification of when subs
  dispose
EOF
