title: Framework: dispatch :source defaults to :ui (wrong); add :frame-init + change default to :unknown + capture coord for frame-init
description:
## Why

The framework's dispatch envelope defaults `:source` to `:ui`
(`implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:158`):

    :source (:source opts :ui)

This collapses every dispatch that doesn't explicitly pass a
`:source` opt to a single value. Live evidence (pair-debug
2026-05-26, Xray Epoch panel): a `[:testdeck/initialise]` dispatch
— clearly a frame-init dispatch, NOT from any UI gesture —
renders as "from ui" in the DISPATCH step. Operator is misled
about the actual origin.

## Two-part fix

### Part 1 — Default `:source` to `:unknown`; classify origins explicitly

Change `:source` default from `:ui` to `:unknown`. UI-handler
call sites must explicitly stamp `:source :ui`; other origins
stamp their own value per the framework's documented vocabulary.

Expanded vocabulary (per router.cljc:82 + Mike's pair-debug
2026-05-26 call):

- `:ui`          — React onClick / onChange / etc. handler-driven
                   dispatch
- `:frame-init`  — dispatch supplied at frame creation time (see
                   Part 2)
- `:fx-emit`     — already stamped in fx.cljc:194 (no change)
- `:timer`       — dispatched from a setTimeout / setInterval /
                   `:dispatch-later` / `:rf.machine/after-*`
                   resolution
- `:http`        — dispatched from an http response handler
- `:repl`        — dispatched from a REPL / eval-cljs probe
- `:machine`     — dispatched from a state-machine action's `:fx`
                   (could overlap with `:fx-emit`; worker decides
                   whether they're distinct or merged)
- `:test-harness` — already stamped (test_support.cljc:403)
- `:unknown`     — DEFAULT when no source was supplied; surfaces
                   "we lost track" rather than incorrectly
                   labelling

Worker decides whether `:framework` / `:internal` deserve separate
entries vs being subsumed by `:unknown`. Pre-alpha posture: pick
the smallest closed set that distinguishes the operator-meaningful
origins; defer additions until a real ambiguity arises.

### Part 2 — Frame-init dispatch source + call-site capture

The frame-init dispatch is a special case. The event is supplied
at frame CREATION TIME (e.g. via `init-frame!` / `frame-init!` /
whichever the framework's API is) — not at dispatch time. So the
dispatch isn't invoked via the `rf/dispatch` macro at the
call-site Xray shows.

Two concerns for frame-init specifically:

1. **Source stamping**: the frame-creation code path that fires
   the init event should stamp `:source :frame-init` (or `:frame`)
   so the panel shows "from frame-init" instead of "from unknown".

2. **Call-site capture**: the operator needs to jump to the code
   that called the frame-creation API (e.g. `(rf/init-frame!
   :step-deck {:on-init [:testdeck/initialise]})`). Options:

   - (a) **Make `init-frame!` a macro** — captures the call-site
     coord at macro-expansion time, stashes it on the frame's
     metadata, replays as `:rf.trace/call-site` on the init
     dispatch. Same pattern as `rf/dispatch`'s macro form.
   - (b) **Runtime stacktrace capture** — when the init dispatch
     fires, walk the call stack to find the frame-creation site.
     Cross-platform fragile.
   - (c) **Static analysis at registration** — record the frame
     definition's source position; init dispatches inherit that
     coord.
   - (d) **Defer / leave it** — init-dispatch call sites are
     typically traceable from the frame's name (operator already
     knows where `:step-deck` is registered). Skip the coord
     capture for now; the source-label classification (`:frame-init`)
     is enough to disambiguate from `:ui`.

   Default disposition: **(a) macro form** — consistent with the
   existing `rf/dispatch` macro pattern. Worker may pick (d) as a
   first step if (a) is bigger than warranted.

## Acceptance

1. `(:source opts ...)` default changes from `:ui` to `:unknown`
   in `router.cljc:158`.
2. Every framework-side dispatch call site that previously relied
   on the default is audited. UI-handler dispatches in React
   adapters (Reagent, UIx, Helix) explicitly stamp `:source :ui`
   when constructing the dispatch envelope.
3. Frame-init dispatch (whatever API the framework uses —
   `init-frame!`, `frame-init!`, or similar) stamps
   `:source :frame-init`.
4. Worker decides on Part 2's coord-capture option (a/b/c/d) and
   documents the choice in the PR.
5. Xray Epoch panel renders accurate source labels: `[:counter/inc]`
   from UI click → "from ui"; `[:testdeck/initialise]` from frame
   creation → "from frame-init"; etc.
6. Backwards compatibility: existing tests / fixtures that assert
   the prior `:ui` default get updated to assert the new explicit
   classification.

## Pre-alpha posture

No back-compat shim. The default change is a wire-shape change
across the framework; all consumers (Xray, story-mcp, test
fixtures) update in lockstep.

## What does NOT change

- The framework's dispatch event mechanism
- The `:rf/dispatch-origin` closed-enum (separate axis from
  `:source` — keep both per Xray A.5 contract)
- Xray's source-label rendering (already supports nil → "unknown"
  per view.cljs:350 fallback)

## What DOES change

- `router.cljc:158` default
- React adapter dispatch call sites stamp `:source :ui` explicitly
- Frame-creation init-dispatch site stamps `:source :frame-init`
- Optionally: `init-frame!` (or equivalent) becomes a macro that
  captures `:rf.trace/call-site` at definition time
- Tests / fixtures asserting prior `:ui` default updated

## Coordination with current backlog

- rf2-80u5a (DISPATCH "from ui" goto-source-link) — partially
  addressed: that bead surfaces the `[open]` affordance when coord
  is captured; THIS bead ensures coord IS captured for more
  dispatch paths (specifically frame-init).
- rf2-ehd8v (HANDLER source open-link) — orthogonal but same
  family.
- rf2-cgm4f / rf2-mmlgk / rf2-93436 / etc. — Epoch panel polish;
  this bead is upstream-framework, makes the panel's
  classification accurate.

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Audit which dispatch call sites currently rely on the `:ui`
   default vs explicit stamping. Pin the count; this is the
   "blast radius" of the default change.
2. Confirm the framework's frame-creation API name + identify the
   init-dispatch code path.
3. Decide between macro (a) and defer (d) for Part 2's coord
   capture. Pre-alpha posture allows the simpler (d) initially
   with a follow-up bead for (a) if the operator value justifies
   the macro cost.
4. Confirm the React adapters (Reagent / UIx / Helix wrappers in
   the adapter ns'es) are the right place to add explicit
   `:source :ui` stamping — they wrap React event handlers, so
   stamping there centralises the change.
5. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Default source line: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:158`
- Source vocabulary doc: `router.cljc:82-85`
- Fx-emit source stamping: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:194`
- Test-harness source stamping: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_support.cljc:403`
- Xray render: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:336-385`
  (handles nil → "unknown" already)
- Trace tooling: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/tooling.cljc:427-446`
  (reads source from envelope tags)
- Pair-debug 2026-05-26 — Mike observed `[:testdeck/initialise]`
  labelled "from ui"; confirmed the default is wrong
EOF

title: Xray panel-gallery: source-link URIs don't resolve correctly at http://localhost:8765 (relative-path issue)
description:
## Symptom

The panel-gallery testbed at `http://localhost:8765` does not open
source links correctly. Source affordances (handler-source `[open]`,
`open-in-editor` chips on coords, etc.) dispatch to
`:rf.xray/open-in-editor` but the resulting URI doesn't resolve to
the right file on the operator's filesystem.

Root cause: the coord-annotation mechanism records file paths as
RELATIVE to the repo root (e.g. `tools/xray/src/day8/...`). The
panel-gallery is served out of
`tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/` (a different relative position
than the typical example apps served out of `examples/<name>/`).
The URI-building code that converts a coord into a launcher URI
(`vscode://file/<absolute>:<line>`, `idea://...`, etc.) either:

- Doesn't resolve the repo-root-relative path correctly when the
  host page is the panel-gallery
- OR builds a URI relative to the host page's URL rather than the
  filesystem repo root
- OR works for example-app hosts but breaks for the testbed host
  because of a path-prefix assumption that doesn't hold here

Mike, pair-debug 2026-05-26: "that http://localhost:8765 does not
open source links correctly, because is a relative path".

## Fix

Audit the URI-building path in `re_frame/source_coords/editor_uri.cljc`
(or wherever the open-in-editor URI is constructed) — confirm it:

1. Resolves repo-root-relative file paths to ABSOLUTE filesystem
   paths regardless of host URL
2. Uses a stable repo-root anchor (not the host page's URL or
   relative path)

Implementation options:

- (a) **Hardcode-detect repo root** at boot via a known marker
  file (e.g. `deps.edn`, `.git`, `shadow-cljs.edn`) — walk up from
  some known location and find the marker.
- (b) **Inject repo root as a build-time constant** — shadow-cljs's
  `:closure-defines` can stamp the repo-root absolute path into
  the compiled artefact. The URI builder consumes the constant
  directly.
- (c) **Read from a runtime header** — the host serves a small
  metadata endpoint with the repo root; the URI builder reads on
  boot.

Option (b) is the cleanest — build-time constant, no runtime
discovery, no dependency on the host's filesystem layout. The
shadow-cljs build for `testbeds/panel-gallery` stamps the repo
root into the artefact; the URI builder uses it; works regardless
of which dev-http port the artefact is served from.

## Acceptance

1. Clicking any source-link affordance in the panel-gallery
   testbed opens the editor at the right file:line.
2. The same affordance works in example apps (step-deck etc.) —
   no regression.
3. Verified with at least two host scenarios: panel-gallery
   (localhost:8765) AND step-deck (localhost:8031).
4. Multiple editor schemes (vscode, idea, cursor, etc.) work
   uniformly — the resolution layer is editor-agnostic.

## What does NOT change

- The coord-annotation mechanism (still records repo-root-relative
  paths)
- The user-facing affordance UI (`[open]` chip etc.)
- Existing example apps that DO work

## What DOES change

- URI-building code uses a stable repo-root anchor (per chosen
  resolution strategy) rather than relying on host-URL relativity
- Possibly: shadow-cljs build config gains a `:closure-defines`
  entry for the repo-root constant (if option b is chosen)

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce: open `http://localhost:8765`, click a `[open]` chip
   on any handler source in a rendered variant, observe what URI
   gets built + what the OS does with it.
2. Reproduce on the working case: same gesture at
   `http://localhost:8031` (step-deck) — confirm the URI built
   there IS correct + identify what differs.
3. Trace the URI-building code path. Confirm where the
   relative-vs-absolute resolution decision is made.
4. Decide between options (a) / (b) / (c) — document choice.
5. Test against at least vscode + idea schemes.
6. Test against both host scenarios.

## References

- Live observation: pair-debug 2026-05-26
- URI builder source: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords/editor_uri.cljc`
- Allowed editor schemes (per rf2-cm93v): listed in
  `allowed-editor-uri-schemes` def in the same file
- Panel-gallery testbed host: `http://localhost:8765`, served from
  `tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/`
- Example app hosts (working baseline): `http://localhost:8031`
  (step-deck), `http://localhost:8030` (two-frame-isolation)
- Related: rf2-80u5a (DISPATCH source-link missing), rf2-ehd8v
  (HANDLER source-link missing) — those add the affordances; THIS
  bead ensures they resolve correctly across host scenarios
EOF
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2199 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2199). Root cause: panel-gallery testbed never called xray-config/configure!, so :rf.xray/project-root was nil and the chip shipped bare classpath-relative paths. Fix: mirror step_deck and seed :rf.xray/project-root at testbed boot with a query-string override. Two new tests pin URI invariance to host URL. rf2-ehd8v compatible — event payload unchanged.

title: Epoch panel: HANDLER source missing file:line + [open] affordance (per design doc §Section 1)
description:
## Symptom

The Epoch panel's HANDLER step renders the source code (with
syntax-highlighting — colours match rf2-79ojx palette) but is
missing two affordances:

1. **No file:line displayed** — operator can't tell WHERE the
   handler is defined
2. **No `[open]` affordance** — operator can't click to jump to
   the handler's source in the editor

Live (pair-debug 2026-05-26) probe of the HANDLER step DOM:
- `[data-testid='rf-xray-epoch-handler-source']` element renders
  the source body with per-token-coloured spans
- Header text is `source` (lowercase)
- Zero `<button>` / open-affordance elements within the step
- No `data-rf-coord` / `data-source-coord` / `data-file` attributes

## Design-doc reference

`ai/findings/epoch-panel-handler-section-design.md` §Section 1:

    HANDLER (reg-event-db :counter/inc)
    ─────────────────────────────────────────
    SOURCE                  counter.cljs:42  [open]
      (fn [db _ev]
        (update db :value inc))

Three elements in the source label row:
1. `SOURCE` (uppercase, treated as a section label)
2. `<file>:<line>` (the file path + line number, plain text)
3. `[open]` (clickable affordance — dispatches to open in editor)

Current panel has #1's label (lowercase "source") but missing
#2 + #3.

## Fix

The framework's coord-annotation mechanism (Spec 009 §Coord-
annotation) records `:rf.source/uri` metadata on `reg-event-*`
registrations. The handler-meta projection (used elsewhere in
Xray, e.g. Static Handler panel) reads this metadata.

For each handler shown in the Epoch panel:

1. Look up the handler's `:rf.source/uri` via the registered
   handler-meta sub
2. Parse `file` + `line` from the URI
3. Render `file:line` next to the SOURCE label
4. Render `[open]` button beside file:line; click dispatches
   `:rf.xray/open-in-editor` with the parsed coord

Reuse the existing affordance pattern from the Static Handler
panel + Event panel (both have working open-in-editor chrome).
Both panels use the `open_in_editor.cljs` ns's `open-in-editor-chip`
component (or equivalent name).

Also relabel `source` → `SOURCE` (uppercase, matching design doc
+ other section labels in the panel).

## Acceptance

1. HANDLER step's source section header reads `SOURCE` (uppercase),
   with `file:line` and an `[open]` button alongside.
2. Hovering the open button shows the file path / line tooltip.
3. Clicking the open button opens the editor at the handler's
   defining file:line via `:rf.xray/open-in-editor`.
4. When coord-annotation is unavailable (e.g. production build,
   handler registered without coord), `file:line` and `[open]` are
   simply not rendered (no broken / dead-link state).
5. Affordance treatment matches the open-affordance treatment in
   the Static Handler panel + Event panel (consistent visual
   chrome across Xray).

## What does NOT change

- The source code syntax-highlighting (already correct)
- The `code-block` widget rendering the source body
- Other panels' open-affordance behaviour
- The framework's coord-annotation mechanism

## What DOES change

- HANDLER step's source-header row gains `file:line` + `[open]`
- "source" label uppercased to "SOURCE"
- `:rf.xray/open-in-editor` dispatch wired to the click

## References

- Design doc: `ai/findings/epoch-panel-handler-section-design.md`
  §Section 1
- Existing open-in-editor mechanism: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/open_in_editor.cljs`
- Existing consumers (pattern reference): Static Handler panel,
  Event panel
- Pair-debug 2026-05-26 — DOM probe: `open-affordance-count: 0`
  inside the HANDLER step
- Coordinates with:
  - rf2-80u5a (DISPATCH "from ui" goto-source-link — same thematic
    gap, different step)
  - rf2-66wis (HANDLER source code rendering, landed; this is the
    file:line + open-link companion missing from that bead)
EOF
close_reason: HANDLER source sub-header carries file:line text + clickable [open] button via shared coord-chip widget. PR #2198.

title: Epoch panel: DISPATCH event vector rendered as plain text (should use edn-inspector for syntax colouring + uniformity)
description:
## Symptom

The Epoch panel's DISPATCH step shows the event vector (e.g.
`[:counter/inc]`) as PLAIN TEXT — not via the edn-inspector. Probe
confirms: no `data-rf-mount-id`, no `data-rf-type`, no `data-rf-mini`
spans in the DISPATCH step body. The event vector renders without
syntax colouring or any inspector widget chrome.

Live (pair-debug 2026-05-26): `[:counter/inc]` shown without
per-token syntax colours — keywords don't render in the calva
purple/magenta the rest of the panel uses; brackets aren't styled;
no width-aware tree-vs-inline behaviour.

## Why this matters

Consistency: every other VALUE rendered in the Xray UI (App-DB,
Handler panel, Machine snapshots, Issues panel, Trace expanded
payloads, COEFFECT step, SUBSCRIPTIONS step, VIEWS step) routes
through `views.edn-inspector` for one-source-of-truth rendering
(per the original rf2-oqa60 phase 1 design + the rf2-h4fce rename).

The DISPATCH step's event-vector rendering bypasses this — operator
sees a different visual treatment for the SAME kind of data (a
CLJS value) than they see elsewhere. Eye has to learn two
formattings.

Beyond consistency, the inspector brings:
- Per-token syntax colouring (rf2-79ojx palette)
- Click-to-expand for nested vectors / maps
- Sticky expansion state (rf2-pvsxs)
- Width-aware inline-vs-tree (rf2-kbdk8)
- Sentinel chrome for `:rf/redacted` / `:rf.size/large-elided`
  (rf2-ndb13)
- Click-to-zoom (rf2-h71e0, after fixing rf2-kcaiz click-leak)
- Diff mode (when comparing dispatched event to a prior or
  expected shape — useful for tests, not standard for cascade view
  but the option exists)

ALL of these vanish when the event vector renders as plain text.

## Fix

Replace the DISPATCH step's event-vector render with an
edn-inspector mount:

    [ei/edn-inspector event-vec
     {:panel-id  :rf.xray/epoch-dispatch
      :site-id   [:rf.xray.epoch/dispatch epoch-id]
      :default-expanded-depth 1}]

(`:default-expanded-depth 1` so the top-level vector reveals its
children inline when short — width-aware will keep it on one line
typical of `[:counter/inc]`-style events.)

Worker locates the DISPATCH step's body render
(`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs` —
search for the dispatch step body builder) + swaps the plain-text
emit for the edn-inspector mount.

## Acceptance

1. DISPATCH step body emits the event-vector via the edn-inspector
   widget — verified live via DOM probe finding at least one
   `[data-rf-mount-id]` element OR typed scalar spans inside the
   step body.
2. Event vector renders with per-token syntax colours (keywords
   purple, numbers orange, strings green per rf2-79ojx).
3. For long event vectors (many args, complex payloads), the
   inspector's width-aware behaviour kicks in — short stays
   inline; long expands to tree.
4. Sentinels in event payloads render as their chips
   (`:rf/redacted` etc.).

## What does NOT change

- The DISPATCH step's overall position / chrome
- The event-vector source data (still from the epoch-record's
  dispatch trace event)
- The "from ui" / "from event-fx" source label (separate row;
  see rf2-80u5a for the open-source-link affordance)

## What DOES change

- Plain-text emit → edn-inspector mount in the DISPATCH step body
- Adds rendering primitives (syntax colours, expansion, zoom,
  sentinel chrome) the inspector brings for free

## References

- Source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`
  — DISPATCH step body render
- Inspector widget: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs`
- Pair-debug 2026-05-26 (Mike: "is the event shown below DISPATCH
  using the edn-inspector? I can't see colouring")
- Parent / coordinates:
  - rf2-93a7s (DISPATCH event vector — landed but as plain text;
    this is its follow-up)
  - rf2-79ojx (palette — the colour treatment the inspector would
    apply)
  - rf2-kbdk8 (width-aware inspector — useful behaviour for long
    event vectors)
EOF
close_reason: Subsumed by rf2-8w8er; resolved in PR #2198.

title: Epoch panel: DISPATCH step missing goto-source-code link on 'from ui'
description:
## Symptom

The Epoch panel's DISPATCH step shows the dispatch SOURCE label (e.g.
`from ui`) but does NOT render a goto-source-code link next to it.
For "from ui" specifically, the source location of the dispatch
call-site (the React onClick handler that called `rf/dispatch`)
should be discoverable + clickable.

Live (pair-debug 2026-05-26): DISPATCH step shows
`1 DISPATCH from ui [:counter/inc]` — the `from ui` label has no
[open-in-editor] affordance. Operator can't jump from the panel to
the code that fired the dispatch.

## Design-doc reference

The design doc doesn't explicitly call out a dispatch-source link
in §Dispatch, but the cross-cutting concern §Click-through
navigation says:

> Every clickable element opens something useful:
> - Action id → source
> - Guard id → source
> - Fx id → reg-fx source
> - State vector segments → relevant machine-spec slice
> - Snapshot path → app-db inspector
> - Aggregate-fx attribution chip → scrolls to LIFECYCLE entry

The principle extends naturally: every named source position the
operator sees → click-through to that position. The dispatch
call-site IS such a position.

## Fix

The framework's coord-annotation mechanism (Spec 009
§Coord-annotation) records `:rf.source/uri` metadata on dispatch
events. The epoch-record's dispatch trace event carries this coord
(when the framework's coord-annotation is enabled — typically dev
default).

DISPATCH step's source label should:
- Render `from <source>` as the label
- Append `[open]` chip (like the HANDLER source `[open]` affordance)
- Click → dispatch `:rf.xray/open-in-editor` with the dispatch
  coord

For "from ui" specifically, the coord points at the React onClick
handler that called `rf/dispatch`. For "from event-fx" (a handler
returning `:dispatch`), the coord points at the dispatching handler's
`:dispatch` line. Etc.

## Acceptance

1. DISPATCH step source label has an `[open]` (or similar) chip
   next to it when source coord is available.
2. Click → opens the editor at the file:line where `rf/dispatch`
   was called.
3. When coord is absent (e.g. dispatch from a context where
   coord-annotation was disabled or unavailable), chip is absent
   (not rendered as a broken / clickable-but-dead link).
4. Consistent affordance treatment across the panel — same `[open]`
   convention as HANDLER source, fx-id source, etc.

## What does NOT change

- The dispatch event itself
- The coord-annotation mechanism (framework-side)
- Other panels' open-in-editor affordances (`rf.xray/open-in-editor`
  event already exists and works)

## References

- Design doc: `ai/findings/epoch-panel-handler-section-design.md`
  §Cross-cutting concerns §Click-through navigation
- Existing open-in-editor mechanism: `:rf.xray/open-in-editor` event
- Source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`
  — DISPATCH step's render
- Pair-debug 2026-05-26 (Mike: "No 'goto source code' link from
  dispatch where it says 'from ui'")
- Coordinates with: rf2-93a7s (DISPATCH event vector — landed; this
  is the missing companion affordance)
EOF
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2197

title: Epoch panel: COEFFECT step shows cofx result as nil (should be actual injected value)
description:
## Symptom

The Epoch panel's COEFFECT step renders the cofx result as `nil`
when the cofx actually injected a value. Live (pair-debug 2026-05-26)
for `:counter/inc` cascade, COEFFECT step body shows:

    1 coeffect injected :testdeck/now nil

`:testdeck/now` is a cofx that injects the current wall-clock
timestamp into the handler's coeffects under `:testdeck/now`. The
ACTUAL value is a millisecond integer (e.g. `1779785519293`). The
panel renders `nil` — either:

- The projection isn't picking up the resolved cofx value, OR
- The rendering format is wrong (showing args / cofx-id position)
  instead of the result

Without the actual value, the COEFFECT step gives the operator only
"a cofx ran"; not WHAT it injected. For debugging "why did the
handler see this value?", the step is unactionable.

## Design-doc reference

`ai/findings/epoch-panel-handler-section-design.md` §Section 2 example:

    + [:session] {:user-id 42 …}

Shows the cofx-id AND the RESULT VALUE. The current panel skips the
result.

## Fix

Trace which projection field carries the cofx result + thread it
through to the COEFFECT step's row render. Per Spec 009 the
epoch-record's coeffect events carry the resolved value on injection
— the cofx-injection trace event payload should have a `:result` /
`:value` slot the projection consumes.

Worker:
1. Probe live — get the raw epoch-record for a `:counter/inc`
   cascade; inspect the coeffect-injection trace events; confirm the
   resolved `:testdeck/now` value IS present in the record.
2. Trace the projection path from epoch-record → the panel's row
   data; identify where the result value is dropped (or never
   carried).
3. Add it to the row data; render in the body.

## Acceptance

1. COEFFECT step body shows the cofx-id AND the resolved value via
   edn-inspector mini.
2. For `:counter/inc` → operator sees `:testdeck/now <timestamp>`
   (the actual ms-integer), not `:testdeck/now nil`.
3. For cofx that legitimately return nil (rare; usually a sentinel),
   the body shows `nil` correctly identified as the cofx's actual
   result.
4. For cofx with structured results (e.g. `:session` returning
   `{:user-id 42 :role :admin}`), the result renders via
   edn-inspector mini with width-aware behaviour (rf2-kbdk8).

## References

- Design doc: `ai/findings/epoch-panel-handler-section-design.md`
  §Section 2 example
- Spec 009 §Trace events §Coeffect injection
- Pair-debug 2026-05-26
- Coordinates with: rf2-cq0ch (COEFFECT step — skip system :db +
  format user cofx body, landed) — this is the missing piece from
  that bead's intent
EOF
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2197

title: Xray panel-gallery testbed: add gallery_edn_inspector.cljs (widget isolation coverage)
description:
## Why

The edn-inspector widget (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs`)
has no dedicated entry in the Xray panel gallery testbed
(`tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/`). It's exercised INDIRECTLY
via every panel that mounts it (App-DB, Handler, Machines, Issues,
Routing, etc.), but no isolated harness to demo it under varying
input shapes.

The widget has ~12 active beads + dozens already shipped through
this session — workers have been validating against the live
running app. An isolated `gallery_edn_inspector.cljs` would give
each bead a stable assertion surface AND let the operator scan
"how does the widget render under this kind of value?" without
needing a real cascade to produce the data.

## Fix

Add `tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/gallery_edn_inspector.cljs`
(+ `fixtures_edn_inspector.cljs`) matching the existing gallery
pattern.

Variants the gallery should cover (one per value-shape × widget-opt
combination):

### Scalar values
1. Numbers, strings, keywords (qualified + bare), booleans, nil,
   symbols, UUIDs, instants — every type the syntax palette
   distinguishes

### Containers
2. Empty map, empty vector, empty set, empty list

title: Xray Machine chart: paradigm shift to events-as-nodes per Stately graph view (custom xyflow node types + elkjs compound layout)
description:
## Why

Predecessor beads on the Machine chart (rf2-so5b0, rf2-a2b55) have
landed but the chart still uses an **edge-labelled** paradigm
(events as text on edges between state boxes) rather than the
**events-as-nodes** paradigm Stately's graph view uses (and which
Mike found dramatically more legible during pair-debug 2026-05-26).

The paradigm shift is structural — not "tune the existing chart" but
"adopt a different visual grammar for transitions". It needs its own
focused bead because the shift cascades into custom node types,
elkjs config tuning, edge-routing changes, and the chart's whole
mental model.

## Reference

- **Canonical visual target**: Stately graph view of the
  `:ws/connection` machine — screenshot at
  `C:\Users\miket\OneDrive\Desktop\2026-05-26_17-17-37.PNG` (worth
  saving to `tools/xray/design-reference/`)
- **Live URL**: https://stately.ai/registry/new — paste the xstate
  v5 JS into the Code panel; the default Editor view IS the graph
- **xstate v5 source** for the `:ws/connection` machine (used to
  generate the reference screenshot) — captured in pair-debug
  session 2026-05-26 transcript
- **Spec source** for the same machine: `examples/reagent/websocket/connection.cljs:65`

## Paradigm shifts (this bead's central thesis)

### Shift 1 — events as visual nodes, not edge labels

**Today**: each transition is an edge between two state boxes; the
event name is plain text on the line. Guards / actions / multiple
actions degrade label legibility quickly.

**Target**: each event handler becomes its own xyflow node. State A
→ event-node → (optional) state B. Internal transitions: state →
event-node, no outgoing edge. The node has room for:
- Event name (header)
- Guard chip `[guard-name]` (when present)
- Action pills `+ action-name` (when present)

Trade-off: more nodes; visually denser per unit graph area. But
labels are always legible and the action attribution is first-class.

### Shift 2 — state boxes have structured internal layout

**Today**: state name + ancestor-path "tags" row at top + outgoing
edges. No internal sections.

**Target**: state name (top) → tag pills (small, below name) →
"Entry actions" section → "Exit actions" section → "Invoke" /
"Spawn" section → outgoing transition handles (bottom). All
vertically stacked inside one bordered container; reads top-to-bottom.

### Shift 3 — hierarchy via visual nesting

**Today**: flat layout; child states are siblings of top-level
states at the same visual level. Ancestor path conveyed via tag-row
chips inside each child box (now-cleared per rf2-so5b0 but the
underlying paradigm gap remains — the chart isn't NESTING children
inside parents visually).

**Target**: parent state = bordered container; children drawn INSIDE.
Initial child marked with `↳` glyph. Active-state highlight on the
state box's border (not via duplicate text tags).

### Shift 4 — convention glyphs

- `↳` for initial state
- `⌚` for after-delay
- `∞` for always-transitions
- `+` for action-runs-here
- `[bracket]` for guards
- Filled dot for the initial-marker source node

These are graph-paradigm conventions an operator who knows xstate/
Stately reads in 30 seconds.

## Layout / algorithm landscape

| Algorithm | Purpose | Used by | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **elkjs** layered with compound | Hierarchical layered layout, supports compound nodes | Xray today | Keep; verify the compound config is enabled |
| **dagre** | Older hierarchical; weaker compound support | Many JS libs | Skip |
| **d3-force** | Force-directed simulation | Network viz | Skip (non-deterministic; ignores hierarchy) |
| **cytoscape cose-bilkent** | Compound supported | Web-based graph libs | Stick with elkjs; switching libs is bigger scope |

For state machines, **elkjs layered with hierarchy threaded as
parent-child relationships** is the right choice. Xray already uses
elkjs; if the current layout is flat, the cause is likely the
hierarchy NOT being threaded into elkjs as compound nodes — not the
layout algorithm itself.

Edge routing: xyflow defaults to bezier — fine. The visible issue
is what's BEING routed (events as edge labels vs events as nodes,
per shift #1).

## Specific implementation tasks

1. **Define custom xyflow node types**:
   - `"rf2-state"` — bordered container with name header + tag pills + entry/exit/invoke sections + Handle components for transition attachment
   - `"rf2-event"` — smaller box with event name header + guard chip + action pills + incoming Handle + (optional) outgoing Handle
   - `"rf2-initial-marker"` — small filled dot with single outgoing edge to its target

2. **Thread state hierarchy into xyflow + elkjs**:
   - Set `parentId` on child state nodes pointing at their parent state
   - elkjs config: `org.eclipse.elk.algorithm = "layered"` + compound-node-aware sub-config (`org.eclipse.elk.hierarchyHandling = "INCLUDE_CHILDREN"`)
   - Parent state nodes auto-size to fit their children + chrome

3. **Restructure transitions as event-nodes**:
   - For each spec transition `{:on {event-id {:target ... :guard ... :action ...}}}`, emit ONE event-node + ONE edge in (from source state) + (optionally) ONE edge out (to target if `:target` present)
   - Internal transitions (no `:target`) get no outgoing edge — visual "this hangs and ends"
   - External self-transitions (`:target :same-state`) get a loop edge back to source

4. **Convention glyphs as node-type variants**:
   - Initial-marker node type
   - After-delay event-node variant (clock glyph + delay-id, no event name)
   - Always event-node variant (infinity glyph, no event name)

5. **Drop ancestor-path tag row** from state boxes (may already be done by rf2-so5b0; verify).

6. **Active-state indicator** on the state box's border (border colour + weight); not via duplicate text tags.

7. **Context (`:rf.machine/data`) readout** in a corner panel of the chart (Stately puts this top-left). Operator sees current `:data` without leaving the chart.

## Acceptance

1. Open the Machine panel; the chart renders in the events-as-nodes
   paradigm. State boxes contain entry/exit/invoke sections; event
   boxes contain guard + action attribution.
2. Compound states nest visually — `:active`'s container wraps
   `:connecting`, `:authenticating`, `:connected`.
3. Initial-state markers render with the `↳` glyph + filled-dot source.
4. After-delay (`⌚`) and always (`∞`) transitions render with their
   conventional glyphs.
5. Internal transitions render as event-nodes with no outgoing edge;
   external self-transitions as loop arrows back to source.
6. Active-state border highlight on the box itself.
7. Context readout in the chart's corner shows current `:data`.
8. Visual side-by-side vs the reference screenshot — Mike's eye
   says "this reads like the Stately graph view".

## What does NOT change

- The xyflow library or elkjs library
- The state-machine semantics
- Any existing testid (where possible)
- The trace-event-driven snapshot computation

## What DOES change

- Custom xyflow node types for state + event + initial + after + always
- xyflow node hierarchy via `parentId` for compound states
- elkjs config to enable compound layout
- Edge model — events become nodes; edges connect state → event → state
- State node internal layout (sections)
- Context readout component in chart corner

## Out of scope

- Animated transitions on state changes
- Operator-editable layout (drag a node to override elkjs)
- Multi-machine views
- Recording / playback of transition sequences
- Switching away from xyflow

## Coordination with current backlog

- rf2-so5b0 (LANDED) — earlier conventions partial cleanup
- rf2-a2b55 (LANDED) — graph-view alignment follow-up
- rf2-s5kyp (auto-fit, LANDED) — re-tune `fit-view-options` after
  compound containers change node footprints
- rf2-3d987 (LANDED) — Machine panel outer chrome; orthogonal to this

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: open http://localhost:8031/counter → Machine tab.
   Probe state-node DOM via the standard testids. Compare against
   the reference screenshot.
2. Confirm xyflow version supports `parentId` + the node-types
   pattern (xyflow v12 does; verify the running version).
3. Confirm elkjs compound-layout config syntax in the running
   version.
4. Sketch the custom node components on paper / Figma BEFORE
   implementing — this is a paradigm shift, not a tweak.
5. Test with both `:ws/connection` (compound with deeply-nested
   children) and a simpler machine (no compound) to ensure the
   paradigm holds for both.
6. Test light + dark themes.
7. Test composition with rf2-s5kyp auto-fit (compound containers
   change topology footprint).
8. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Previous beads in the chain: rf2-so5b0 (landed), rf2-a2b55 (landed)
- Reference screenshot (Stately graph view, `:ws/connection`):
  `C:\Users\miket\OneDrive\Desktop\2026-05-26_17-17-37.PNG`
- Reference URL: https://stately.ai/registry/new
- xstate v5 machine source (for reproducing the reference): preserved
  in pair-debug session 2026-05-26 transcript
- Chart source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_canvas.cljs`
- xyflow v12 parent / sub-flow docs: https://reactflow.dev/learn/layouting/sub-flows
- elkjs hierarchy handling: https://eclipse.dev/elk/reference/options/org-eclipse-elk-hierarchyhandling.html
- Stately convention docs: https://stately.ai/docs/visualization
- Pair-debug 2026-05-26 — synthesis of Stately graph view vs Xray
  current paradigm
EOF

title: Epoch panel: machine handler section per design doc (gated on rf2-82a0u trace enhancements)
description:
## Symptom

The Epoch panel doesn't render the rich machine-handler detail
described in the design doc. For a cascade triggered by a
machine-driven event (e.g. `[:ws/connect ...]` triggering a state
transition with guards, exit/transition/entry actions, after-timer
arming, data reduction, snapshot diff, per-action fx) the operator
sees only the generic pipeline. Machine-specific cascade detail is
absent — and machine-driven UIs are exactly the case where the
detail matters most.

## Prerequisite

GATED on rf2-82a0u (trace enhancements for the machine handler
section). The design doc's §Trace stream identified 3 gaps that
need closing before the panel can render fully:

1. `:rf.machine/action-ran` payload gains `:phase` keyword
2. `:rf.machine.timer/scheduled` trace event (alongside existing fx)
3. `:rf.machine.timer/cancelled` standardised across cancel paths
   with `:reason`

If rf2-82a0u hasn't landed when this bead is picked up, worker
either implements those trace enhancements as part of THIS bead OR
coordinates so rf2-82a0u lands first.

## Fix

When the cascade's HANDLER is `reg-machine`, replace (or augment)
the generic HANDLER step with the machine-handler section per
design doc §Handler — machine. Seven sub-sections:

1. **TRANSITION** — `[from-state] → [to-state]`, event id, microstep
   count, machine id.
2. **GUARDS** — per-guard row: guard-id + result (`:passed` /
   `:failed` / `:threw`) + which transition.
3. **LIFECYCLE** — phase-grouped (exit / transition / entry /
   always / after-action / initial-entry / destroy-exit). Per-action
   row: action-id + outcome + per-action fx attribution.
4. **AFTER TIMERS** — armed + cancelled (with `:reason`).
5. **DATA REDUCTION** — `:data` before / after.
6. **SNAPSHOT DIFF** — full snapshot via edn-inspector diff mode.
7. **FX** — per-action attribution (which action emitted which fx).

## Acceptance

1. Machine-handled event → machine-handler section renders (in
   place of or under the generic HANDLER step).
2. All 7 sub-sections present + populated from the post-rf2-82a0u
   trace stream.
3. Per-action fx attribution works.
4. AFTER TIMERS shows armed + cancelled with reasons.
5. Non-machine event → keeps the generic HANDLER step; machine
   section absent.

## References

- Parent: rf2-sc3r1
- Design doc: ai/findings/epoch-panel-handler-section-design.md §Handler — machine
- Trace prerequisite: rf2-82a0u
- Spec 005 — state machines
- Spec 009 §Trace events

title: Epoch panel: cascading-dispatches section (link from parent to child cascades)
description:
## Symptom

When a handler returns `:dispatch` / `:dispatch-n` fx, the cascade
triggers child cascades. The Epoch panel doesn't surface them —
no link from parent cascade to its children.

## Fix

"Dispatched events" section (or fold into FX section) lists every
child dispatch. Per-row: child event vector + "jump to" affordance.
Clicking navigates the Epoch panel to the child cascade.

When child cascade aged out of the epoch buffer → "no longer in
buffer" marker.

## Acceptance

1. Cascade with dispatch fx → section lists each child dispatch.
2. Click navigates to child's Epoch view.
3. Step omits when no child dispatches.
4. Header count: `N events dispatched`.

## References

title: Epoch panel: per-step elapsed time + cascade total (with long-step warning)

event timestamps assemble into per-step durations).

## Acceptance

2. Panel header (or footer) shows cascade total.
3. Long-step warning treatment when over threshold.
4. Timing sourced from existing epoch-record projection.

title: Epoch panel: text duplication — step header content rendered again in body
description:
## Symptom

Every pipeline step renders primary content twice — once in the
step header, once in the body. Live:
- DISPATCH: `1 DISPATCH from ui from ui`
- HANDLER: `3 HANDLER reg-event-db :counter/inc reg-event-db :counter/inc`
- (and others)

## Fix

Audit each step's render. Header = short summary (label + count);
body = detail. Drop body duplication of header content (or vice
versa — worker picks; consistency matters more than which side wins).

## Acceptance

title: Epoch panel: COEFFECT step — skip system :db + format user cofx body
description:

COEFFECT step renders for cascades that only inject system `:db`
(every reg-event-db gets it automatically). Live: `:counter/inc`

2. Handler using `(rf/inject-cofx :rf/now)` → COEFFECT shows one

title: Xray edn-inspector: diff mode misses removed-from-collection items (children-of walks only AFTER)
description:
## Symptom

In edn-inspector diff mode, items present in BEFORE but absent from
AFTER are not rendered as removed — they're invisible. Operator
sees only the post-image; can't tell what was deleted.

Live (pair-debug 2026-05-26, Mike): on a Machine snapshot's AFTER
column for the `[:active :authenticating] → [:active :connected]`
transition, the `:tags` slot has `:ws/authenticating` in BEFORE
but not in AFTER. The widget's diff render of AFTER does NOT mark
`:ws/authenticating` as deleted — the operator sees the
post-transition set without any indication that a tag was removed.

## Root cause

`children-of` (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:1034`)
returns children of the supplied value (which is the AFTER side in
diff mode). It has no `before` parameter; it can't enumerate
items that exist in BEFORE but not in AFTER.

The current diff-op classification (line 530-545) handles
`:removed` only when an AFTER child has `::missing` for its value —
which fires for explicit `{:k nil}` removal, not for the more
common dissoc-style deletion that drops the key entirely.

## Fix

When rendering in diff mode, iterate over the UNION of children
from BEFORE and AFTER, not just AFTER's children. Per
collection kind:

- **Map / record** — union of `(keys before)` + `(keys after)`.
  Iteration order: AFTER's keys in their natural order, plus any
  BEFORE-only keys at the end (or interleaved at their original
  positions — worker picks; `:end` is simpler, `:interleaved` is
  closer to what stately/devtools do).
- **Vector / list / seq** — render AFTER's items at their indices
  plus any BEFORE-only items past AFTER's count, marked removed.
  When BEFORE was longer than AFTER, render the BEFORE-tail items
  with the removed treatment.
- **Set** — union of members. Removed members render with the
  removed treatment alongside surviving members (set members have
  no natural ordering; sort by `pr-str` for stable render).
- **Scalars** — unaffected (scalars don't have children).

Removed children render with the existing rf2-awqts removed
chrome — strike-through + red row wash + `-` gutter glyph — so
the operator sees `:ws/authenticating` (struck through, red
background) at the position it would occupy if it still existed.

A new helper `children-of-pair` (or a 2-arg variant of
`children-of`) takes `(before, after)` and returns the unioned
pair-list each with a `:rf.diff/op` annotation:

    [[k value-after ::missing-before :added]
     [k value-after value-before :modified-or-same]
     [k ::missing-after value-before :removed]
     ...]

The render path consumes this enriched pair-list instead of
calling `children-of` on AFTER alone.

## Acceptance

1. Machine snapshot AFTER column for the transition where `:tags`
   loses `:ws/authenticating` → the AFTER renders `:ws/authenticating`
   with the removed treatment (strike-through + red wash).
2. Same fix applies uniformly to maps (key dropped via dissoc),
   vectors (item removed from the tail or truncation), and sets
   (member removed via disj).
3. Items added in AFTER continue to render with the added treatment
   (no regression).
4. Items modified continue to render with the modified treatment +
   `← changed from X` annotation (no regression).
5. Items unchanged still render plain (or dimmed under diff mode
   per rf2-awqts).
6. Non-diff browse mode unchanged (children-of stays as-is for
   non-diff renders).

## What does NOT change

- The diff-op classification (the four ops added/modified/removed/
  same)
- The removed-row chrome (strike-through + red wash + `-` gutter)
- The browse-mode render path
- Other panels' use of children-of (worker confirms — likely none)

## What DOES change

- A new helper for diff-mode children iteration (union of before +
  after)
- The diff-mode render path consumes the new helper instead of
  `children-of` on AFTER alone
- Test coverage added for "removed-from-set", "removed-from-vector-
  tail", "dissoc'd-map-key" cases

## Out of scope

- Vector item insertion in the middle (causes index-shift; needs a
  longest-common-subsequence diff for the "right" treatment) —
  worker can defer this; index-shift on vectors is a known harder
  case. v1 can render naively (each index compared positionally)
  and flag follow-up if needed.
- Re-ordering detection (item moved within a vector — currently
  shows as modified-at-position + modified-at-new-position; a
  proper move-detection algorithm is its own bead)
- Cross-collection-kind diffing (a map became a vector, etc.) —
  treat as modified-at-parent like today

## References

- Bug repro: pair-debug session 2026-05-26 (Mike: "the diffing
  (shown on the right in After view) does not mark items deleted.
  I'm looking at :tags at the end — `:ws/authenticating` was in
  before but not in after, but the after does not mention it as
  deleted.")
- Render source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs`
  - `children-of` at line 1034
  - `diff-op` at line 533
  - render-leaf-with-diff at line ~1893
- Diff chrome bead (landed): rf2-awqts (removed-row treatment is
  already defined; this bead surfaces it for the missing case)
- Machine AFTER-block diff-mode wiring (landed): commit 701a90740
EOF
close_reason: Fixed via PR #2187 — children-of-pair walks UNION of BEFORE + AFTER; removed map keys / vector tail / set members now render with rf2-awqts removed chrome (strike-through + red wash + - gutter glyph). 9 new tests; npm run test:cljs green (4672/4672), bundle-isolation PASS.

title: feat(xray): new Epoch panel — full visual pipeline of the computational timeline for an event
description:
## Goal

A new Xray panel that turns all available trace for an epoch into a delightful, detailed, informative visual schematic of the pipeline steps. The operator sees the complete computational timeline of a single re-frame epoch — from event dispatch through view rendering — as a chronological, numbered cascade.

## Conditional rendering — important

The panel renders steps that actually fired during this epoch. Sections are conditional, not always-present:

- If there is no flow → flows step is absent
- If there are no coeffects → coeffects steps are absent
- If FX wasn't used → FX step is absent
- Handler step adapts to handler type:
  - reg-event-db
  - reg-event-fx
  - machine event handler (machines/transition-runner)

The pipeline is a faithful projection of the trace stream — each step's presence and shape derived from what's in the epoch-record + per-frame trace ring. Cf. the machines trace enhancements landed in #2155 (rf2-82a0u) which give the Handler section everything it needs.

## Reference docs

- Mike's pair-debug spec at `ai/findings/epoch-panel-handler-section-design.md` (local-only — do NOT link from committed files; treat as background context)
- This bead body carries the visual + structural spec verbatim for worker reference (below)
- Cross-refs: rf2-82a0u (#2155 machines trace), rf2-ad7zx (Xray L&F EPIC parent — this is the Trace-redesign initiative made concrete), rf2-okq7p (#2174 :header card chrome), rf2-h71e0 (#2180 zoom + breadcrumb — useful for nested expansions)

## Visual Structure

### Layout
- Container: padding 21px, overflow auto, full height
- Header text: "The computational timeline for the event" (muted text color, margin-bottom 21px)
- Pipeline: left margin 55px to accommodate numbered circles
- Vertical line: absolute positioned, 0.5px width, starts at 13px from top, positioned at -34px from left edge
- Row spacing: 13px vertical gap between entries

### Numbered Cascade Pattern
Each step has:
1. Numbered circle: 21px diameter, positioned at -44px left, color-matched to badge type
2. Badge pill: uppercase text, 10px font (devtools-micro), rounded, padding 5px horizontal, 3px vertical
3. Verb/label: monospace text (string or hiccup)
4. Duration: right-aligned, muted, monospace (e.g., 0.1ms)
5. Target: optional secondary line below badge (muted monospace)
6. Additional content: code blocks, tables, diff displays below main content

## Fibonacci Spacing System
3px, 5px, 8px, 13px, 21px, 34px, 55px, 89px

## Badge Colors

```clojure
{:DISPATCH      "#8c959f"                  ; mid grey
 :COEFFECT      "#a855f7"                  ; light purple
 :HANDLER       "var(--devtools-active)"   ; blue
 :FLOW          "var(--devtools-active)"   ; blue
 :FX            "rgb(154, 103, 0)"         ; orange/brown
 :SUBSCRIPTIONS "#ec4899"                  ; pink
 :VIEWS         "var(--devtools-success)"} ; green
```

## Row Types & Structures

### 1. DISPATCH (Step 1)
- Badge: mid grey (#8c959f)
- Verb: "from <source>" with inline hyperlink + external-link-icon for the source (e.g., "from ui ↗")
- Target line shows event vector (e.g., [:counter-inc])
- Duration right-aligned
- Optional: expandable EDN on click ({:event ... :source ...})

### 2. COEFFECT (Steps 2-3, conditional)
- Badge: light purple (#a855f7)
- Verb: hyperlink to coeffect name (e.g., :session ↗)
- Target: diff-style addition with green "+" marker. Path in muted colour, value in success green. Shape: + [:session] {:user-id 42, :token "..."}
- Conditional: only present if the handler used :rf/coeffects

### 3. HANDLER (Step 4, always present)
- Badge: var(--devtools-active) blue
- Verb: hyperlink to handler registration form (reg-event-db, reg-event-fx, or machine-event-handler)
- Code block (always visible, not collapsed): syntax-highlighted source of the handler
- DB changes section (below code):
  - :db diff header with corner-down-right-icon
  - Diff lines per changed path (~ marker, path in muted, before-value in error, → in muted, after-value in success)
  - :fx header (if reg-event-fx) with corner-down-right-icon
  - FX effects list indented 21px (each: :fx-id value)
- For machine event handlers (per #2155): use :phase + :rf.machine/action-ran payload to render lifecycle (:exit / :transition / :entry / :always / :after-action / :initial-entry / :destroy-exit), guard evaluations (:pass/:fail/:threw), after-timer activity (:scheduled / :fired / :cancelled with :reason)

### 4. FLOW (Step 5, conditional)
- Badge: var(--devtools-active) blue
- Verb: hyperlink to flow id (e.g., ::counter-parity ↗)
- DB changes (similar to handler, simpler):
  - :db diff header with corner-down-right-icon
  - Diff line for the flow's output path (~ marker, before → after)
- Conditional: only present if a flow fired this epoch

### 5. FX (Step 6, conditional)
- Badge: orange/brown (rgb(154, 103, 0))
- Verb: "side effects"
- Body: green checkmark list per fx-id (e.g., ✓ :db → app-db, ✓ :http/post {url body}, ✓ :navigate "/confirmation")
- Conditional: only present if any fx fired

### 6. SUBSCRIPTIONS (Step 7)
- Badge: pink (#ec4899)
- Table (3 columns: sub / inputs / changed):
  - Borders on all rows (including header)
  - Cell padding py-[5px] pr-[8px]
  - sub column: hyperlink to sub form + external-link-icon
  - inputs column: app-db OR multiple inputs shown in flex-col (vertical stack)
  - changed column: green ✓ + old-value-in-error → new-value-in-success, OR grey ✗ if unchanged

### 7. VIEWS (Step 8)
- Badge: var(--devtools-success) green
- Table (2 columns: views / subs):
  - views column: hyperlink to view form + external-link-icon
  - subs column: subscriptions read (multiple in flex-col vertical stack)
  - No "changed" column

## CSS Variables (already in devtools.css)

```
--devtools-body: 13px
--devtools-caption: 11px
--devtools-micro: 10px
--devtools-chrome-bg: #f5f5f5 / #1c1c1c
--devtools-border: #d1d1d1 / #373737
--devtools-text: #24292f / #e6edf3
--devtools-text-muted: #656d76 / #8b949e
--devtools-active: #0969da / #539bf5
--devtools-success: #1a7f37 / #3fb950
--devtools-error: #cf222e / #f85149
```

## Interactive Behavior

- Expandable rows: if a row carries an :edn slot, clicking the row toggles its EDN content visibility (mount via the standard edn-inspector widget with :zoomable? true so deep tree drill-down composes naturally with rf2-h71e0)
- Tables + lists are read-only displays
- All hyperlinks click to source via the existing click-to-source machinery

## Icon Requirements

- ExternalLink icon: 13px × 13px (w-[13px] h-[13px])
- CornerDownRight icon: 13px × 13px (for arrows in db-changes sections)
- Use Heroicons or existing project icon library

## Implementation Notes

- Reagent form-2 with internal expanded-rows state atom (per-row toggle): (r/atom #{}) keyed by step-index
- Pipeline rows derived from the epoch's trace events via a pure projection fn — testable in isolation
- Each step renders only if its trace events are present (conditional cascade, not always 8 steps)
- Pixel values use the Fibonacci spacing system (3/5/8/13/21/34/55/89)
- Theme tokens via existing token table; do NOT introduce new tokens
- Wire-up under `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/` (new directory) — split projection + view files

## Spec/021

Add a new §10.1 (or sibling subsection — worker decides where it fits cleanly) documenting:
- The 7-badge taxonomy
- The conditional rendering rule
- The numbered cascade visual contract
- Composition with edn-inspector :zoomable? + :header opts

## Tests

- Pure-data projection test: epoch trace → pipeline rows. Cover all conditional combinations (no-coeffects, no-flow, no-fx, machine-event-handler).
- DOM tests for each badge's visual chrome (computed colour matches badge type).
- Mount + visual smoke against a known epoch fixture.

## Pre-alpha posture

No back-compat shims. The new Epoch panel REPLACES the existing Event/Handler/etc panels as the canonical "what happened in this epoch" surface — OR co-exists initially and the older panels deprecate. Worker decides. The Figma mock is the visual authority.

title: Xray Machine chart: align node + edge labels with xstate/stately convention (drop ancestor-tag noise, nest compounds, plate edge labels)
description:
## Symptom

The Machine panel's xyflow chart labels visually mess with the chart structure — node boxes carry redundant ancestor-path information that bloats their footprint and clutters their visual centre. With 14+ edges routing around tightly-packed nodes, the result is hard to scan as a state-machine topology.

Live probe (pair-debug 2026-05-26) of node `:active.connecting`:

| Element | Text | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `rf-mv-chart-state-tags` (`data-tag-count="2"`) | `"activeconnecting"` | Two tag chips — one per ancestor path segment + the local state name |
| State name body | `"connecting"` | The state's own label |

So each compound-child node shows its full ancestor path TWICE (once as the tag row, once via the state's own name). For a deeply-nested state the tag row swells; the node footprint grows; edges route around bulkier nodes; labels start to collide with edges.

Compare with xstate / stately convention (the dominant CLJS-ecosystem mental model for state-chart visualisation):

- **Compound states render as VISUAL CONTAINERS** (boxes wrapping their nested children). Hierarchy comes from the nesting itself; no ancestor-path labels needed inside each child.
- **State name appears ONCE per state** — at the top of its box (or centered for leaf states). No path-duplication.
- **Active state indicated by border weight / colour / glow** on the state box itself — not by a separate ancestor-tag row.
- **Entry / exit actions** listed inside the state box at the bottom, smaller font + dimmed colour, prefixed `entry / actionName` / `exit / actionName`.
- **Transition labels**: `event [guard] / action` format. Label sits on the edge with a subtle background plate so it doesn't get visually buried under crossing edges.
- **Final states**: concentric circle border (or distinct visual treatment).
- **Initial state**: small dot/marker arrow pointing to the initial state.
- **History states**: `H` (shallow) / `H*` (deep) glyph in a circle.

## Specific gaps in the current chart vs xstate/stately convention

1. **Ancestor-path tag row inside child nodes** — `data-tag-count="2"` showing "active" + "connecting" on the `:active.connecting` node. Should be eliminated; the visual nesting of `:connecting` INSIDE the `:active` container would convey the same hierarchy without text duplication. Active-config marker becomes a border/background treatment on the box itself.

2. **No visual nesting of compound states** — the chart appears flat; `:active.connecting`, `:active.authenticating`, `:active.connected` are siblings at the same visual level as `:disconnected`, not visually wrapped inside an `:active` container. xyflow v12 supports `parentId` on nodes + the `<SubFlow />` pattern — adopt it for compound states.

3. **Edge label background plates** — edges labels (`ws/connect`, `ws/arm-fail / arm-failure`) have no background, so when an edge crosses another edge or a node corner the label may be obscured. Stately/xstate render edge labels with a subtle theme-aware background rectangle so they always read clearly.

4. **Entry/exit/transition actions on edges and inside states** — verify the current chart renders these per xstate convention:
   - Transition: `event [guard] / action` on the edge label
   - State entry: inside the state box bottom, `entry / actionName` (smaller, dimmer)
   - State exit: same, `exit / actionName`
   - The current edge labels DO show `ws/arm-fail / arm-failure` (event + action) which is on the right track. Need to verify guards render as `[guardName]` and entry/exit are surfaced INSIDE the state box, not as separate edges.

5. **Initial state marker** — verify the entry point to the topology is marked per convention (a small dot with an arrow into the initial state).

6. **Final/history state markers** — verify these render with their conventional glyphs if any of the machines under test use them.

## Reference

Stately editor (the canonical UX for state-chart visualisation, used by the xstate community):
- https://stately.ai/docs/state-machines (compound states as boxes containing boxes)
- https://stately.ai/docs/visualization (active state highlighting; transition label format)

Pertinent screenshots / patterns to match:
- A compound state with 3 nested children: outer box labelled with the parent name, 3 inner boxes each labelled with their local name
- An active state: border lit up in a brand colour, with the path traced from the initial state through every ancestor down to the active leaf
- Transition labels: `event [guard] / action` with a 1-2px padding + theme-matched background
- Entry/exit actions inside state boxes, bottom-anchored, smaller font

## Fixes

### Fix 1 — drop the ancestor-path tag row from child nodes

In `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_canvas.cljs` (worker locates), the `state-tags` element with `data-tag-count` should not enumerate ancestor path segments. Each state box shows its OWN name; hierarchy comes from visual nesting (see Fix 2).

Active-config indication moves to the state box's border / background:
- Inactive state: neutral border (`:border-default`)
- Active state: thicker border + accent colour (e.g. `:active-bg` / `:accent`) — same hue family the Machine canvas already uses for active edges

### Fix 2 — render compound states as visual containers (xyflow `parentId`)

Compound states use xyflow's `parentId` field on child nodes plus `extent: "parent"` so the parent renders as a containing box around its children. The xyflow `<SubFlow />` (or v12 equivalent — worker confirms the running xyflow version's API) auto-sizes the parent to wrap its children.

For the `:ws/connection` machine:
- `:disconnected` is a top-level state, no parent
- `:active` is a top-level state, RENDERS AS A CONTAINER
- `:active.connecting`, `:active.authenticating`, `:active.connected` have `parentId: ":active"` so they nest inside the `:active` container

The elkjs layout already understands the hierarchy (it must, to position siblings within their parent's bounds). Threading the parent-child relationship through xyflow's `parentId` makes the visual nesting appear automatically.

### Fix 3 — edge labels with background plates

Stately edge labels have a `background: var(--rf-xray-bg-1)` (or theme background) with 2-4px padding so they "stamp" out a clear zone around the label text. Apply the same: wrap edge labels in a span with a theme-aware background; the label remains legible even when an edge crosses behind it.

### Fix 4 — confirm transition action / guard formatting

Audit current edge label rendering. Should be `event [guard] / action`:
- `ws/connect` (event-only) — current
- `ws/arm-fail / arm-failure` (event + action) — current
- `ws/clear [some-guard]` (event + guard) — verify
- `ws/clear [guard] / action` (all three) — verify

If guards aren't rendered today, add them in brackets per xstate convention.

### Fix 5 — entry / exit actions surfaced inside state boxes

For each state with entry / exit actions:
- Inside the state box at the bottom, list the actions: `entry / actionName-1` `entry / actionName-2` `exit / actionName-3`
- Smaller font (10px vs 12px state name) and dimmer colour (`:text-tertiary`) so they read as secondary
- If the state has many actions, truncate with a `+N more` chip (popup affordance to show all)

### Fix 6 — initial state marker

The entry point to the topology gets a small dot + arrow into the initial state, per convention. Confirm whether xyflow already supports this (likely a special node type) or whether it needs custom rendering.

## Acceptance

1. No state-node renders an ancestor-path tag row. The state box shows ONLY its own name as the label.
2. Active state is indicated by border/background treatment on the state box itself (not via duplicate text labels).
3. Compound states render as visual containers wrapping their children via xyflow's `parentId` mechanism. Verified live: `:active` appears as a containing box around `:active.connecting`, `:active.authenticating`, `:active.connected`.
4. Edge labels have a subtle background plate (theme-aware) so labels remain readable when edges cross.
5. Transition label format matches xstate: `event [guard] / action`. Verified for at least one transition with a guard and at least one with an action.
6. Entry/exit actions appear inside the state box (bottom-anchored, smaller + dimmer). Verified for any state in the test machines that has entry/exit actions.
7. Initial state marker rendered per convention. Final / history state markers rendered per convention where the machines use them.
8. Auto-fit (rf2-s5kyp) still works on mount + focus-change with the new compound-state nesting.
9. The chart reads as a state-chart topology at a glance — operator can see the hierarchy + active state + transitions without parsing redundant labels.

## What does NOT change

- The xyflow library itself
- The elkjs layout algorithm
- The chart's outer chrome (Machine panel section wrapping — rf2-3d987)
- The state-machine semantics (re-frame2's machines)
- The trace-event-driven snapshot computation

## What DOES change

- `state-tags` ancestor-path enumeration removed (state name renders alone)
- Active-state indicator moves from tag row to state box border / background
- Compound-state nodes gain `parentId` linkage; xyflow renders the parent as a visual container
- Edge labels gain a background-plate treatment
- Guards render in `[brackets]` if not already
- Entry/exit actions rendered inside state boxes
- Initial state marker added per convention

## Out of scope

- Re-implementing the chart in something other than xyflow
- Animated transitions on state changes
- Operator-editable layout (drag a node to override elkjs)
- Multi-machine views (a single chart showing multiple machines side-by-side)
- Recording / playback of transition sequences

## Coordination with current backlog

- rf2-s5kyp (auto-fit) — orthogonal; both will land independently. Auto-fit's `fit-view-options` may need tuning once compound containers change node footprints.
- rf2-3d987 (Machine panel layout fixes) — already landed. This bead is INSIDE the chart, not the surrounding panel.

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Open Stately's editor (https://stately.ai/registry) — examine 2-3 published machines to internalise the visual conventions. Pin specific decisions you'll match.
2. Confirm xyflow version in use; verify v12's `parentId` + `extent: "parent"` API for compound containers.
3. Reproduce live: open http://localhost:8031/counter → Machine tab → focus `:ws/connection`. Probe a child state's DOM to see the ancestor-tag row. Probe an edge label to see the lack of background plate.
4. Audit the current node-render code in `machine_canvas.cljs` — list every label / tag / annotation source. Map each to xstate convention.
5. Decide compound-state rendering strategy: use xyflow's native `parentId` containers, OR custom-render via SVG. xyflow native is more idiomatic.
6. Test layout with the existing elkjs config — compound containers might need elkjs tuning (`elk.algorithm` for hierarchical layout).
7. Test interaction with rf2-s5kyp's auto-fit — compound containers change the topology footprint; ensure `fit-view` still produces a reasonable initial view.
8. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Live diagnosis: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Chart source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_canvas.cljs`
- xyflow v12 parentId / SubFlow docs: https://reactflow.dev/learn/layouting/sub-flows
- Stately editor (reference UX): https://stately.ai/registry
- xstate visualisation docs: https://stately.ai/docs/visualization
- Coordinates with: rf2-s5kyp (auto-fit), rf2-3d987 (Machine panel layout — landed)

reference).

The PRIOR bead body referenced Stately's Sketch text-list mode — wrong
paradigm. Sketch lays transitions out as text rows under each state;
Xray uses graph-paradigm (drawn edges between spatially-positioned
nodes). The visual conventions hold across both Stately modes; the
geometry the bead is targeting matches the GRAPH view (Editor at
stately.ai), not Sketch.

## Side-by-side comparison

| Concern | Stately graph view (target) | Xray xyflow today |
|---|---|---|
| Compound state container | Single bordered box wrapping nested children visually. Parent name at top, children layered inside with clean spacing. | Flat — child states are siblings at the same visual level as top-level states; no visual nesting. |
| State name | Once per state, at the top of the box. | Duplicated via an ancestor-path "tags" row above the state name (`[active] [connecting]` chips). |
| Tags (Spec 005 `:tags`) | Small pills BELOW the state name (e.g. `websocket.active`, `websocket.connecting`). Subtle, secondary. | Stuffed into the ancestor-path chip row above the name — conflated with hierarchy markers. |
| Entry actions | Dedicated `Entry actions` section inside the state box, each action a pill prefixed `+ action-name`. | Not surfaced inside the state box; entry actions only visible via trace, not via chart. |
| Active-state indicator | Border / background tint on the state box itself when the machine is in that state. | Done via tag-row chip (e.g. `[active]` chip lights up) — conflated with the duplicate state-name issue. |
| Edge labels | `event` label + small action pills (`+ register-request`) beside it; clean typographic hierarchy. | Label is plain text directly on the edge path; no background plate — overlaps with crossing edges. |
| Guards on transitions | Subtle text above the event (e.g. `current-socket → ws.received → receive-message`). | Inline in edge label; can be lost in dense layouts. |
| Initial state marker | Small filled dot above the initial state's box. | None — initial state implicit; no visual marker. |
| After-delay | Clock glyph + `[delay-id] → target` (e.g. ⌚ `backoff-ms → active`). | Likely none or different convention; verify. |
| Always-transitions | Infinity glyph `∞ → target` with guard prefix. | Likely none or different convention; verify. |
| Context (`:data` / `:rf.machine/data`) | Top-left corner code-style readout — actual current values shown. | Not surfaced in chart at all — operator must drill into a separate panel. |
| Visual weight | Every state box same border/background weight; consistent typography. | Mixed — some boxes carry tag chrome, edge labels, etc. — uneven scan rhythm. |
| Edge geometry | Curved paths flowing through layout; arrowheads on terminal end. | xyflow default — similar geometry; OK baseline. |

## Net effect

For the SAME machine (`:ws/connection` with 5 top-level states, 14
transitions, 1 compound state, 1 after-delay, several guards, several
entry actions), Stately's graph view consumes meaningfully less
vertical real-estate and reads as a state-chart at a glance — Xray's
chart consumes more space and reads as "state boxes with lots of
chip noise".

## Implementation priority (refines the bead's 6 fix points)

1. **Compound containers via xyflow `parentId`** — biggest visual gain; everything else stacks on top of this. P1.
2. **Drop ancestor-path tag row from child boxes** — pure subtraction; clears the way for #3. P1.
3. **Tags as pills under the state name** — small additive; depends on #2 removing the tag-row first. P2.
4. **Entry / exit actions surfaced inside state boxes** — feature parity with Stately. P2.
5. **Edge label background plates + action pills** — readability under crossing edges. P2.
6. **Initial state marker (filled dot)** + after-delay clock + always-infinity — convention markers. P3.
7. **Context readout in chart corner** — operator sees `:data` without leaving the chart. P3 (operator can also see this in the snapshot drill-in already, so lower urgency).

## References

- Reference screenshot (paradigm-matched, graph view): `C:\Users\miket\OneDrive\Desktop\2026-05-26_17-17-37.PNG`
- Reference URL: https://stately.ai/registry — paste a machine via Code panel; default view IS the graph
- Earlier Sketch screenshot (text-list mode — DIFFERENT paradigm): `C:\Users\miket\OneDrive\Desktop\2026-05-26_17-04-16.png`
- The xstate v5 JS for `:ws/connection` used to produce both screenshots — preserve in worker's PR description for reproduction

title: Xray edn-inspector: large-sentinel detection keyed off stale :rf/large (should be :rf.size/large-elided)
description:
## Symptom

The edn-inspector has a first-class chip-rendering path for "value too large to render directly" elision markers — designed to render a clean `● large · N bytes` chip in place of the inlined value. The detection predicate (`large-sentinel?`) and the render dispatch (`:sentinel-large` case) reference a STALE marker key (`:rf/large`) that the framework no longer emits.

Per Spec 015 (§Wire elision) the current sentinel shape — emitted by `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:197` — is:

    {:rf.size/large-elided
     {:path   <vec>
      :bytes  <int>
      :type   <kw>
      :reason :schema
      :hint   <s>
      :handle [:rf.elision/at <path>]}}

But the widget detects:

    (defn large-sentinel?
      "`{:rf/large {:bytes N :head s}}` size-elision sentinel."
      [v]
      (and (map? v) (= 1 (count v))
           (let [[k m] (first v)] (and (= :rf/large k) (map? m)))))

The key is wrong (`:rf/large` vs `:rf.size/large-elided`). Real framework-emitted markers fall through to ordinary map rendering — the operator sees a generic one-key map exposing the marker's internals (`:path`, `:bytes`, `:type`, `:reason`, `:hint`, `:handle`) as plain map keys instead of the intended `● large · N bytes` chip.

Not a crash risk — the LARGE value itself never crosses the wire (the framework elides BEFORE the marker reaches Xray). But the widget's existing chip affordance is dead code today, and the operator's read is muddied by raw framework-internal slot names.

## Fix

Update `large-sentinel?` and the `collection-kind`/`render-scalar` dispatch sites to detect the current shape:

    (defn large-sentinel?
      "`{:rf.size/large-elided <body>}` size-elision sentinel per Spec
      015. `<body>` carries `:path :bytes :type :reason :hint :handle`."
      [v]
      (and (map? v)
           (= 1 (count v))
           (let [[k m] (first v)]
             (and (= :rf.size/large-elided k) (map? m)))))

Sentinel chip render (current `:sentinel-large` case around line 734) updates to read the new body shape:

    :sentinel-large
    (let [{:keys [bytes type handle hint]} (val (first v))]
      [:span {:data-rf-type "rf-size-large-elided"
              :data-testid "rf-xray-edn-inspector-large"
              :title (cond-> (str "Large value elided"
                                  (when type (str " · " (name type))))
                       hint (str "\n" hint))
              :style large-chip-style}
       [:span {:style {:font-size "10px"}} "●"]
       "large"
       (when bytes
         [:span {:style {:color (:text-tertiary tokens) :margin-left "4px"}}
          (str "· " bytes " bytes")])
       ;; rf2-XXXXX — surface the structured fetch handle as a hint so
       ;; the operator can drill in via `mcp__re-frame2-pair__get-path`
       ;; using the handle's `:path`.
       (when handle
         [:span {:style {:color (:text-tertiary tokens)
                         :margin-left "8px"
                         :font-style "italic"}}
          (pr-str handle)])])

Worker decides whether to fold the handle-render in this bead or defer (see "Out of scope" below). The minimum is the detection + chip-render keyed off the right sentinel.

## Pre-alpha posture

Drop `:rf/large` entirely. No back-compat shim, no alias. If the framework ever emits the old shape, it's a framework bug — Xray's job is to render the spec-current shape only.

## Acceptance

1. `large-sentinel?` detects `{:rf.size/large-elided <body>}` (the spec-current shape).
2. `large-sentinel?` does NOT detect `{:rf/large <body>}` (the legacy shape — confirmed gone from the framework).
3. `collection-kind` classifies a framework-emitted large marker as `:sentinel-large`.
4. `render-scalar`'s `:sentinel-large` case renders the chip with bytes count + `type` (when present) instead of rendering the marker as an ordinary map.
5. Live verification: trigger a large-elided slot (e.g. by declaring a slot `:large? true` in a frame's schema and stuffing it with a large value); confirm the operator sees the chip, not a generic map.
6. `mini` (the inline one-line render) routes large sentinels to the chip too (existing branch at line 2312).
7. No regression in adjacent sentinel handling — `:rf/redacted` and `{:rf/redacted {:bytes N}}` (redacted+size) keep their existing chip treatment.

## What does NOT change

- The framework-side elision (Spec 015) — already correct
- The widget's data-render logic for non-sentinel values
- Other sentinel detection paths (`:rf/redacted`, redacted+size)
- The `collection-kind` enum (`:sentinel-large` keyword stays)
- The `:sentinel-large` chip's visual treatment (background, colour, font-size)

## What DOES change

- `large-sentinel?` predicate detects the spec-current marker key
- `:sentinel-large` chip-render reads the new body slot names (`:bytes` may stay; `:type`, `:hint`, `:handle` are new in the body)
- Tests against the legacy `:rf/large` shape (if any) are updated or removed

## Out of scope

- Surfacing the marker's `:handle` as a clickable drill-in affordance — that's a separate UX bead (operator clicks handle → MCP `get-path` fetches subtree → inspector replaces marker with fetched value)
- Adding a "size budget warning" chip for values approaching but not exceeding the elision threshold
- Per-mount opt-out (an operator says "I want to see this huge value anyway") — sensitive vs operator-opt-in is the existing `--allow-sensitive-reads` boot gate's job; size isn't quite the same dimension

## Coordination with current backlog

Orthogonal to all 9 active edn-inspector beads (rf2-7sdja, rf2-kbdk8, rf2-63ie5, rf2-awqts, rf2-4aiaq, rf2-726ol, rf2-okq7p, rf2-h4fce, rf2-h71e0) — touches the sentinel detection + chip render, not the layout / palette / interactivity surfaces those beads modify. Land independently.

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live (if a large-elided slot is reachable in the running app): inspect the marker as it renders today; confirm it falls through to generic map render, not the chip.
2. Search the rest of the Xray codebase for `:rf/large` references — they're all dead code now and should be cleaned in the same PR.
3. Search the framework codebase for any remaining `:rf/large` emit sites — if any exist, the framework should be fixed in lockstep (likely none — Spec 015 was a coordinated migration; verify).
4. Decide whether to include the `:handle` surfacing in this bead or defer.
5. Confirm tests cover the sentinel detection (`large-sentinel-detects-spec-current-shape`); add if missing.
6. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Live diagnosis: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Stale predicate: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:323`
- Stale render case: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:734`
- Stale `mini` branch: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:2312`
- Framework marker emit: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:197`
- Spec: `spec/015-*.md` §Wire elision
