title: Xray edn-inspector: zoom-into-node + breadcrumb navigation
description:
## Why

Dense app-db trees in Xray's edn-inspector force the operator to scroll past chrome AND every intermediate level just to see one deep subtree. Sticky expansion (rf2-pvsxs) only solves part of this — even when the path is fully expanded, the surrounding tree consumes screen real-estate and visual attention.

Zoom-into-node turns the inspector into a focused window onto an arbitrary subtree. Operator clicks a "zoom into" affordance on any container; that node becomes the root of the displayed tree. A breadcrumb trail at the top shows the path from the original root; clicking any segment zooms back to that level.

Anchors to known mental models — Chrome devtools' object inspector + nav, React devtools' selected-component focus, IDE nav-to-symbol + back, file browsers' breadcrumb drill-in.

## Concept

Operator's flow:

1. Start: edn-inspector renders the whole value (e.g. App-DB).
2. Operator clicks the zoom affordance on a container — e.g. `[:rf/machines :ws/connection :data]`.
3. The inspector re-renders showing ONLY that subtree as if it were the root.
4. A breadcrumb appears above the tree: `app-db › :rf/machines › :ws/connection › :data ›`.
5. Operator clicks any segment in the breadcrumbs → tree zooms back to that level.
6. Click the home label or press Esc → tree zooms back to the original root.

State is per-mount, persisted via the `:site-id` mechanism (rf2-pvsxs) so a Tab→Tab→back round-trip preserves the zoomed-in view.

## Design decisions to nail down before implementing

### 1. Zoom affordance — where + what

Candidates:
- **(a) Small icon next to the expand triangle** on every container — e.g. `🔍` or `→`. Discoverable, doesn't collide with toggle. RECOMMENDED.
- (b) Double-click the key/value — discoverable only via tooltip; collides with text selection in dense data.
- (c) Right-click → context menu "Zoom into" — accessible but hidden; bad for a first-class feature.
- (d) Alt+click — power-user discoverable only.

Worker decides; (a) is the strongest default.

Icon choice: `⊕` (already taken by popup), `→`, `↳`, `⇲`, or a custom magnifier glyph. Coordinates with rf2-7sdja which moved popup to `↗`. Worker picks; should be visually distinct from popup `↗` and the expand triangles.

### 2. Per-mount or per-panel?

Per-mount. Different inspector instances can each be zoomed to different paths. Persisted under the same `:site-id` keying as expansion state. Consumers that want zoom share-able across mounts can pass the same `:site-id` (rare).

### 3. Breadcrumb home label

When the consumer panel passed `:header` (rf2-okq7p), the header hiccup is the natural home label. Render it as the first breadcrumb segment.

When `:header` is absent, fall back to a generic label like `root` or just the panel-id (worker picks).

### 4. Breadcrumb truncation

Deep paths (6-10+ segments) can outgrow the breadcrumb row. Middle-truncate: `home › … › :ws/connection › :data ›`. Hover any truncated segment to expand it briefly, or hover the `…` to see the elided segments. Full path in tooltip on hover of the breadcrumb container.

### 5. Diff-mode interaction

When the operator zooms into a subtree that has no changes, the diff annotations vanish from view (correct — they chose focus over change-context). But the operator might want to know "you have N changes outside this view". Surface as a small badge in the breadcrumb row (`⊕ 3 outside this view`) that, when clicked, zooms out to the nearest ancestor that contains a change.

Out of scope for v1 if it slows the implementation; can be follow-up.

### 6. Keyboard navigation

- **Esc** — pop one level (zoom up one segment)
- **Alt + ←** — same as Esc (back button convention)
- **Alt + →** — zoom into the first/focused child (forward, if a child is focused)

The Esc shortcut needs to coordinate with the popup widget's Esc-closes-top behaviour (rf2-7sdja). Order: if a popup is open, Esc closes the popup; if no popup, Esc zooms up. Or scope Esc-handling to whichever surface has focus.

### 7. Leaf interaction

Click on a SCALAR leaf does NOT zoom (nothing to zoom into). Affordance only renders on containers (maps / vectors / sets / lists / records / map-entries).

### 8. Interaction with width-aware expansion (rf2-kbdk8)

When zoomed, the rendered subtree may be shorter than the available width — width-aware expansion's behaviour should not change. The subtree gets the same width budget the original mount has. No re-measurement needed.

### 9. Composes with popup (rf2-7sdja)

The popup overlay renders its own embedded edn-inspector mount. Should zoom-state propagate from the side-panel mount into the popup? Possible interpretations:
- (a) Popup starts fresh (root view); operator can zoom inside the popup independently.
- (b) Popup opens at the side-panel's currently-zoomed path.
- (c) Popup opens at the FULL root regardless (matches "give me a roomier view of the whole thing" intent).

RECOMMENDED: (c) — popup is a "see everything in a roomy modal" surface; opening at root respects that intent. Inside the popup, zoom works independently.

### 10. URL state — deferred

Encoding zoom path in the URL would let an operator share "what I was looking at". Out of scope for v1; could be a follow-up bead.

## Public API extension

The widget gains an opt-in `:zoomable?` opt:

    [ei/edn-inspector value
     {:panel-id :rf.xray/app-db
      :card?    true
      :header   [:span "app-db"]
      :site-id  [:app-db-frame :rf/default]
      :zoomable? true                ;; NEW — enables zoom affordance + breadcrumb chrome
      }]

When `:zoomable? true`, every container in the tree gets the zoom affordance (per design decision #1 above), and the breadcrumb row renders above the body when the operator has zoomed in.

When omitted (default `false`), the widget renders as today — no affordance, no breadcrumb.

## State

A new app-db slot `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/zoom` mirrors the expansion slot shape:

    {[panel-id site-or-mount-id] zoomed-path-vec}

When `zoomed-path-vec` is `nil` or `[]`, the widget renders the full value (no zoom). Otherwise it renders `(get-in value zoomed-path-vec)`.

Sub `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/zoom-path` reads the slot for a given (panel-id, site-id). Event `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/zoom-to` sets it; `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/zoom-up` pops one segment; `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/zoom-reset` clears it.

## Acceptance

1. `[ei/edn-inspector value {:zoomable? true ...}]` renders a zoom affordance on every container in the tree.
2. Clicking the affordance sets the zoom-path; the tree re-renders showing only the subtree at that path.
3. A breadcrumb row renders above the tree when zoom-path is non-empty: `home › <seg> › <seg> › ...`. Each segment is clickable; click zooms to that level. Clicking the home segment resets zoom.
4. The breadcrumb home label is the `:header` hiccup when supplied; falls back to a generic root label otherwise.
5. Esc keypress (when the inspector or its container has focus) zooms up one level. Coordinates with popup Esc-handling (popup closes first if open).
6. Per-mount zoom state. Two side-by-side mounts zoom independently.
7. Zoom state persists across panel-leave-and-return via `:site-id` keying.
8. Width-aware expansion (rf2-kbdk8) still works inside the zoomed subtree.
9. Diff mode (rf2-awqts) still works inside the zoomed subtree — diff chrome paints on the visible nodes; nodes outside the zoom view are not rendered.
10. The popup widget opens at the FULL root regardless of the side-panel's zoom state; zoom inside the popup is independent.
11. Click on a SCALAR leaf does NOT zoom (no affordance rendered for non-containers).
12. Breadcrumb truncates middle segments when the row overflows; tooltip shows the full path.
13. Light + dark themes both support the affordance + breadcrumb chrome.

## What does NOT change

- The widget's data-render logic
- The expansion-state mechanics (rf2-pvsxs)
- The diff-mode behaviour (rf2-awqts)
- The width-aware expansion (rf2-kbdk8)
- The popup widget integration (rf2-7sdja)
- The triangle / glyph rendering
- The header+body card chrome (rf2-okq7p)
- Any existing testid
- The `:expansion-key` shape (zoom is a separate concern from expansion)

## What DOES change

- `data-display`/`edn-inspector` (post-rename rf2-h4fce) accepts `:zoomable? boolean` opt
- New app-db slot + events + sub for zoom state
- New breadcrumb component (`zoom-breadcrumbs`) rendered above the body when zoomed
- Zoom affordance rendered next to expand triangle on containers when `:zoomable? true`
- Esc-handling for "zoom up" coordinated with popup's Esc-closes-top
- Theme tokens may gain a `:zoom-affordance` colour (or reuse an existing one)

## Out of scope

- URL-encoded zoom state for shareability (separate follow-up)
- "N changes outside this view" badge for diff-mode (separate follow-up)
- Zoom history (back/forward stack beyond one level) — Esc pops one, but no multi-level forward
- Multi-select / multiple zoom regions side-by-side

## Coordination with current backlog

Land AFTER:
- rf2-h4fce (rename) — uses post-rename names
- rf2-pvsxs (site-id) — depends on the persistence mechanism
- rf2-okq7p (`:header` opt) — uses the header hiccup as the breadcrumb home label
- rf2-7sdja (popup) — coordinates Esc-handling

Can land BEFORE or AFTER:
- rf2-kbdk8 (width-aware expansion) — orthogonal
- rf2-awqts (diff chrome) — orthogonal
- rf2-3d987 (Machine panel layout) — orthogonal
- rf2-63ie5 (card chrome) — already landed

## Consumer adoption

Panels that opt in to `:zoomable? true`:
- App-DB — high value; whole-tree inspection benefits hugely
- Handler panel — db-before / db-after / fx / coeffects mounts each benefit
- Machine snapshot drill-in — operator can zoom into a particular snapshot path

Skip for:
- `mini` inline renders — too small to be useful
- Trace expanded payloads — already in their own row; zoom would conflict with the trace row layout

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Walk the design decisions above; for each, confirm the recommended choice OR justify a different choice. Document in the PR description.
2. Look at existing zoom-affordance patterns in the Xray codebase (segment-inspector? machine-canvas focus?) — reuse glyph / interaction conventions where they exist.
3. Pick the affordance glyph carefully — must visually distinct from popup `↗` and expand triangles (▾ / ▸).
4. Test the breadcrumb behaviour at multiple viewport widths — 1064px (current), 800px, 600px. Middle-truncation should trigger smoothly.
5. Coordinate Esc-handling with the popup widget — verify popup-open + zoom-in stacked state behaves correctly (Esc closes popup, then second Esc zooms up).
6. Add tests for: zoom-to, zoom-up, zoom-reset, breadcrumb-render, zoom-persists-across-unmount.
7. Audit consumer panels for opt-in decisions; document the list.
8. Report findings before pushing implementation.

## References

- Live concept: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Widget source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs`
- Persistence mechanism: rf2-pvsxs (`:site-id` keying)
- Header+body chrome: rf2-okq7p (`:header` opt as breadcrumb home)
- Popup integration: rf2-7sdja (Esc coordination)
- Expansion state: existing `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/expansion` slot (zoom slot mirrors its shape)
- Consumer panels: App-DB, Handler, Machine snapshots

title: Xray Machine panel: 8 layout fixes (spacing, side-by-side, collapsible chart, hierarchy)
description: ## Why The Machine panel's focused-event-section establishes the header+body card aesthetic the operator likes (and that other beads — rf2-okq7p — replicate elsewhere). But the panel itself has 8 layout issues that compound to make it harder to read than it should be. Bundled as one bead because they're cohesive concerns about the same panel's visual layout, all touching the same render code, and consistency across them matters (fixing one without the others would look incoherent). Measured live this session (pair-debug 2026-05-26) on http://localhost:8031/counter → Machine tab → focused on `:ws/connection`. ## The 8 issues + fixes ### 1. Zero spacing between sibling sub-panels `focused-event-section`'s children (HEADER / transition-lens / event-chart / snapshot-drill-in) sit edge-to-edge — no gap, no margin. Three different concerns read as one wall of grey. **Fix:** add `gap: 8-12px` to the section's flex/grid container. OR `margin-bottom: 8-12px` to each sub-panel. Verify the gap colour reads correctly (likely panel canvas white). ### 2. Card-in-card transition is jarring snapshot-drill-in is a WHITE nested SECTION sitting inside the grey body context. Operator's eye reads grey-chart → white-card → grey-snapshot-blocks. The white card "interrupts" the body without clear purpose. **Fix two options:** - (a) Keep white but space it well from neighbours via #1's gap (the breathing room makes the white card read as intentional). - (b) Make snapshot-drill-in match the grey body (`#f5f5f5`) since it's already inside a bordered outer section — no need for a second card layer. Worker picks one and commits; document the choice. ### 3. Before/After stacked vertically, not side-by-side Two 266px-tall blocks (Before then After) stacked. Operator wants to DIFF them; vertical stacking forces scroll-scan-scroll-scan instead of side-by-side eye-jump. **Fix:** lay them out 2-column when viewport ≥ ~800px wide; fall back to stacked when narrower. CSS Grid or flexbox with `flex-wrap` + width thresholds. Each column gets its own internal header ("Before" / "After"); the grouping header (currently "Snapshot · transition · before / after") drops the "before / after" suffix since it's now visually obvious from the two columns. ### 4. Chart sub-panel dominates (1269px = 62% of panel height) The xyflow chart takes most of the panel's vertical real-estate. The snapshot drill-in is mostly off-screen — operator forgets it's there. **Fix:** make the chart collapsible. Add a ▾/▸ toggle in its header area (or attach to a sub-header above it); default-expanded; click to collapse. Frees the operator to see the snapshot pair without scrolling. State persisted via the same per-panel localStorage / app-db mechanism Xray uses for other panel collapsed-states. When collapsed, show a one-line summary (e.g. "Machine topology · 8 nodes · 12 transitions · click ▸ to expand"). ### 5. Headers run together (no weight differential) "Snapshot transition · before / after" reads as one phrase. Operator can't quickly pick out the section name vs the qualifiers. **Fix:** add weight differential — `Snapshot · transition · before / after`. Or restructure separators — replace the middle dot with a real `→` arrow where the meaning is sequential. Apply uniformly to every section header in the panel. ### 6. transition-lens block looks identical to event-chart block Both `#f5f5f5` grey body. But transition-lens is INFO metadata (target machine instance, transition source/target); event-chart is interactive content. They don't deserve co-equal visual weight. **Fix two options:** - (a) Fold transition-lens content into the outer focused-event-section HEADER ribbon as annotations. - (b) Keep as separate sub-panel but visually distinguish — smaller font, dimmer text, italic, or `#fafafa` (one shade lighter than the body) so it reads as secondary metadata. Worker picks; (a) is more aggressive (denser header) but communicates hierarchy clearly. ### 7. Nested header uses same grey shade as outer header Both `focused-event-header` and snapshot-drill-in's HEADER use `#e8e8e8`. When nested-in-bordered-section, operator's eye gets the same chrome treatment twice — hierarchy lost. **Fix:** differentiate nested headers from outer headers: - Lighter shade (`#ededed` or `#f0f0f0`) - Smaller font (e.g. 11px vs 13px for outer) - OR text-only without a ribbon background (just a label with bottom border) Worker picks; consistent rule applied to ALL nested headers across the panel. ### 8. Panel breathing room Outer focused-event-section sits at x=388 (right column start), 12px from the panel edge. Tight against the card. **Fix:** add 16-20px padding on the panel's right column so cards don't touch its edges. Verifies in resize — narrow viewports keep some padding rather than letting cards bleed to the edge. ## Composes with related beads - **rf2-okq7p** (header+body card chrome elsewhere) — this bead is about fixing the Machine panel that PROVIDES the visual reference rf2-okq7p replicates. Visual changes here propagate aesthetic expectations. - **rf2-63ie5** (inspector card chrome) — orthogonal; affects data-display mounts, not the Machine panel's chrome. ## Acceptance 1. **Spacing**: focused-event-section's children separated by visible gaps (8-12px). Same inside snapshot-drill-in. 2. **Card-in-card**: snapshot-drill-in's chrome decision (white vs grey) is consistent — verified live, no jarring transition. 3. **Before/After side-by-side**: At viewport width ≥ 800px, Before and After render in two columns. At <800px, fall back to stacked. Each column has its own header. 4. **Chart collapsible**: Click on chart's header ▾ collapses the chart to a one-line summary; ▸ to re-expand. State persisted across reloads via the standard panel collapsed-state mechanism. 5. **Header weight differential**: Every panel header has clear semantic-vs-qualifier weight distinction. Tested in both light + dark themes for legibility. 6. **transition-lens differentiated**: Either folded into outer header OR visually distinguished as metadata (worker documents choice). 7. **Nested header differentiation**: Nested headers visually differ from outer headers (lighter shade / smaller font / borderless). Hierarchy reads at a glance. 8. **Panel padding**: 16-20px breathing room around outer cards. Cards don't touch panel edges at any viewport width. ## What does NOT change - The xyflow chart implementation - The Machine state-machine semantics - The trace-event-driven snapshot computation - The focused-event selection mechanism - The data-display widget (which this panel's inspector mounts use — that's a separate concern) ## What DOES change - focused-event-section's CSS layout (gap, padding, possibly grid for Before/After) - snapshot-drill-in's chrome (white-card decision + nested header differentiation) - Chart sub-panel gains a collapsible affordance + persisted state - transition-lens repositioned or visually-secondary'd - Panel-level padding around cards - Header text formatting (weight + separator choice) ## Out of scope - Restructuring the panel into multiple tabs (e.g. "Topology" tab vs "Snapshot" tab) — that's a larger UX rethink, separate bead if anyone wants it - Changing what the snapshot blocks SHOW (this bead is layout only) - Adding new affordances beyond chart collapse (e.g. "copy snapshot", "diff against earlier epoch") ## Worker — conduct your own review before starting 1. Reproduce live: load http://localhost:8031/counter → Machine tab → focus an event (`:ws/connection` is a good test case). Probe via DOM as this bead's measurements were captured. 2. Implement in order: easy CSS fixes first (#1, #5, #7, #8 — small CSS), then larger restructures (#2, #6 — chrome decisions), then biggest (#3 side-by-side, #4 collapsible chart). This lets the bigger changes build on a cleaner base. 3. Test at multiple viewport widths — 1064px (current), 800px (Before/After threshold), 600px (mobile-ish). The 2-column → stacked fallback in #3 should trigger smoothly. 4. Light + dark themes — every shade chosen has a theme-aware token. 5. Persist chart-collapsed state via the standard mechanism (not custom localStorage). 6. Report findings before pushing, especially the choice between options for #2, #6, #7. ## References - Live measurement: pair-debug session 2026-05-26 - Panel source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector.cljs` (worker locates the focused-event-section render + sub-panel renders) - Snapshot drill-in source: same file or sibling - Visual hierarchy reference: how Mike sees this rendered today at http://localhost:8031/counter → Machine tab

title: Xray data-display: header+body card chrome (Machine-panel aesthetic) opt-in via :header hiccup
description:
## Why

Several Xray panels mount multiple top-level data-display inspectors side by side (App-DB has 3: counter-app db, machine-app db, route params; Handler has multiple slots per epoch — event vector, db-before, db-after, fx, coeffects). Today these inspectors blend together visually — operator has to read the contents to figure out which inspector is which.

The Machine panel already uses a card aesthetic the operator likes: white-bordered SECTION wrapper + darker-grey HEADER ribbon labelling the section + lighter-grey BODY containing the content. Three-shade greyscale (`#ffffff` outer / `#e8e8e8` header / `#f5f5f5` body) reads as a single design language across the tool.

Apply this aesthetic to the data-display inspector via an opt-in `:header` arg, so consumer panels that have multiple inspectors can label each one without blending.

Measured live this session (pair-debug 2026-05-26) — Machine panel `focused-event-section` structure:

| Layer | Element | Background | Padding |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outer wrapper | `<section>` | `#ffffff` white | none |
| HEADER ribbon | `<header>` | `#e8e8e8` darker grey | `10px 12px` |
| BODY | `<div>` | `#f5f5f5` light grey | `12-14px` |
| Border | `1px solid #e8e8e8` between header + body | — | — |
| Outer border | `1px solid #d1d1d1` + `4px` radius | — | — |

Header text in the Machine panel sample: `":ws/connection [:active :authenticating] → [:active :connected]"` — names what's inside.

## What changes

### Public API — opt-in `:header` hiccup arg

The widget gains a new opt:

    [dd/edn-inspector value
     {:panel-id :rf.xray/app-db
      :card?    true                                  ; from rf2-63ie5
      :header   [:span "Counter app · " [:code ":rf/default"]]}]   ; NEW

When `:header` is supplied AND `:card? true`, the widget wraps its render in the three-layer chrome:
- Outer `<section>` (white, `1px solid #d1d1d1` border, `4px` radius)
- `<header>` row at `#e8e8e8`, `10-12px` padding, holding the supplied hiccup
- Body at `#f5f5f5`, `12-14px` padding, holding the existing render

When `:header` is omitted, behaviour is unchanged from rf2-63ie5's `:card?` — single-layer card chrome only.

When `:card? false`, `:header` is ignored (no wrapper to put it in).

### Hiccup not string — composable header content

Pass hiccup so the consumer can compose:

    :header [:span
             [:strong "Counter app"]
             " · "
             [:code ":rf/default"]
             [:button {:on-click ...} "copy"]
             [:button {:on-click ...} "reset"]]

The widget treats it as opaque hiccup — no parsing, no required shape. Consumer panels supply whatever they want (label + icon + per-inspector affordances).

### Consumer panel updates — opt in per panel

Apply to panels where multiple inspectors deserve labelling:

- **App-DB** (`panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:142,146`) — pass `:header` for each of the 3 mounts. Header text per inspector: "Counter app · :rf/default" / "Machine app · :step-deck" / "Routes".
- **Handler/Event panel** — pass `:header` for each slot: "Event", "Before", "After", "FX", "Coeffects" (worker locates the mount sites).
- **Issues panel** — pass `:header` for ex-data inspector: "ex-data" (+ exception class if available).
- **Routes panel** — pass `:header` for each top-level slot (worker confirms exact slots).

Don't apply to:
- **Machines panel** — sub-panels already use the header+body pattern; nested inspector would be card-in-card.
- **Views panel** — already wrapped in own card chrome.
- **Trace panel** — expanded payload sits inside a trace row that's already chromed.

Worker audits each consumer; the rule of thumb is "if the panel has multiple top-level inspectors that benefit from labelling, apply the chrome; if the inspector is already nested in a labelled container, skip".

## Composes with existing beads

- **rf2-63ie5** (inspector card chrome) — this bead BUILDS ON it. `:card? true` is the precondition; `:header` extends what `:card?` does. Land rf2-63ie5 first.
- **rf2-awqts** (diff state to row chrome) — diff row wash sits inside the body. No collision.
- **rf2-kbdk8** (width-aware expansion) — body's available width is the card's INNER width (post-border + padding), not the panel's. Worker measures correctly.
- **rf2-pvsxs** (expansion state survives unmount) — orthogonal; site-id still keys state across remounts.
- **rf2-h4fce** (rename → edn-inspector) — `:header` opt name unaffected by rename.

## Acceptance

1. `data-display` (or `edn-inspector` post-rename) accepts a new optional `:header` opt. Value is hiccup; widget treats as opaque.
2. When `:header` AND `:card?` are both truthy, the widget renders the three-layer chrome (section → header → body) matching the Machine panel's visual treatment. Verified live via `getComputedStyle` on the resulting DOM matching the Machine panel sample values (background shades, padding, border, radius).
3. When `:header` is supplied but `:card? false`, no header renders (the precondition isn't met — bead doesn't quietly turn the header on; consumer must opt into both).
4. When `:header` is omitted, behaviour is identical to rf2-63ie5's `:card?` alone — single-layer card chrome with no header.
5. App-DB panel mounts pass `:header` per the 3 inspectors — labels read at a glance.
6. Handler panel mounts pass `:header` per slot.
7. Issues + Routes panels apply where they have multiple labelled slots (worker decides per-mount).
8. Machines + Views + Trace mounts UNCHANGED — no `:header` added to those.
9. The hiccup header composes with arbitrary children (text + code + buttons + icons) — verified by testing a composite header with a per-inspector copy button.
10. Light + dark themes both implemented — header ribbon's darker-grey shade is theme-aware (`#e8e8e8` light; equivalent dark token).

## What does NOT change

- The widget's data-render logic
- The expansion-state mechanics
- The diff-mode behaviour
- The popup widget integration
- The triangle / glyph rendering
- The `:card?` opt's semantics (this bead extends, doesn't redefine)

## What DOES change

- `data-display` accepts a new `:header` opt (hiccup)
- Theme tokens add `:header-ribbon-bg` (or equivalent — light: `#e8e8e8`; dark: equivalent darker shade)
- Theme tokens add `:body-bg` for the body layer if not already present (overlaps with existing `:bg-1`)
- Consumer panels (App-DB, Handler, Issues, Routes — per the audit) pass `:header` at appropriate mount sites
- Skill / docs updated to describe the header+body card aesthetic

## Out of scope

- Sticky header on scroll (header scrolls with body; later polish if needed)
- Header-row affordance collisions (worker keeps the API hiccup-opaque; consumers compose their own buttons; no built-in copy/reset buttons)
- Renaming the `:card?` opt
- Re-evaluating which panels deserve header chrome (worker audits; the list in this bead is the starting point but final per-panel decision is theirs)

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: load http://localhost:8031/counter → Machine tab → confirm the focused-event-section's header+body pattern. Probe the exact background colours + padding values; verify against the values in this bead (live spec; may have drifted slightly since 2026-05-26).
2. Wait for rf2-63ie5 to land. This bead's chrome builds on `:card? true`; can't ship before that.
3. Confirm the new theme token shades work in both light + dark. The Machine panel only renders in light theme today (worker verifies its dark-theme equivalents).
4. Audit each consumer panel. Pass `:header` only where the panel has multiple labelled inspectors. Don't blanket-apply.
5. Compose with rf2-awqts (diff row chrome) — the diff row wash lives inside the body, not bleeding past the section border-radius.
6. Compose with rf2-kbdk8 (width-aware expansion) — the body's available width is post-padding, post-border.
7. Test a composite header with multiple children (label + code + button) — confirm hiccup pass-through is clean.
8. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Machine panel sample probe: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Live values:
  - Outer SECTION: `background #ffffff; border 1px solid #d1d1d1; border-radius 4px`
  - HEADER: `background #e8e8e8; padding 10px 12px; border-bottom 1px solid #e8e8e8`
  - BODY: `background #f5f5f5; padding 12-14px`
- Machine panel implementation: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector.cljs` (worker locates exact section render)
- Inspector card-chrome precondition: rf2-63ie5 (in-progress — wait for landing)
- Other coordinations: rf2-awqts (diff chrome), rf2-kbdk8 (width-aware), rf2-pvsxs (site-id persistence), rf2-h4fce (rename)
- Consumer panels:
  - App-DB: `panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:142,146`
  - Handler/Event: `panels/event_detail.cljs` (worker locates mounts)
  - Issues + Routes: worker locates

title: Xray data-display: diff state moves to row chrome (gutter + wash + stripe), unblock per-token syntax palette
description:
## Symptom

In the data-display widget's diff mode, the diff gutter glyphs (~/+/-) and the value-text type colours occupy the same colour channel — and they clash hard.

Measured live this session (pair-debug 2026-05-26) on the App-DB panel:

- Diff `~` gutter: `rgb(154, 103, 0)` dark orange
- Number values (typed): `rgb(152, 104, 1)` dark orange (essentially identical)
- Boolean values (typed): `rgb(193, 132, 1)` gold (very close)

The operator looking at a row with an orange thing in it can't tell:
- Is this a number value?
- Is this a boolean value?
- Is this a "this changed" diff marker?

All three look the same. The clash also exists in light degree for `+` (added) glyphs vs string-green, and is latent for any future palette work that introduces more saturated colours.

## Why this happens

Two design concerns are sharing one channel (text colour):

1. **Type semantics** — what kind of value is this? (rf2-79ojx introduced the calva-aligned palette: keywords purple, strings green, numbers orange, booleans gold, nil grey)
2. **Diff semantics** — did this change between epochs? (gutter glyphs + colour codes for added/modified/removed)

Both compete for the same per-token colour. There's no way to assign one orange to "number" and another orange to "modified" without confusing the operator who can't tell which is which.

## Fix (Option A — chosen design, may revisit)

Move diff semantics to ROW-LEVEL CHROME, leaving per-token text colour for type semantics. Matches GitHub's diff convention: changed lines have a green/red wash, but the code inside keeps its syntax highlighting.

Three concrete changes:

### 1. Diff gutter glyph in a reserved diff-only hue

The `~/+/-` glyphs in the gutter use a colour that does NOT appear in the syntax-highlight palette. Reserve a hue (worker picks; candidates: a desaturated mid-tone, a cool-tone grey-blue, or a custom diff-specific accent). Whatever the choice, it must NOT collide with any of `:syntax-keyword`, `:syntax-string`, `:syntax-number`, `:syntax-boolean`, `:syntax-nil`. Verify by chromatic-distance check.

### 2. Subtle row-background wash

Each diff-affected row gets a light coloured wash on its background:

- Added → light green wash (e.g. `rgba(46, 160, 67, 0.12)` light theme; equivalent dark theme value)
- Modified → light amber/yellow wash (e.g. `rgba(212, 153, 34, 0.12)`)
- Removed → light red wash (e.g. `rgba(248, 81, 73, 0.12)`)

Opacity ~10-15% so the wash reads as an environmental cue, not as obscuring the text.

### 3. Optional left-border stripe (2px) on diff rows

A 2px coloured stripe on the row's left edge in the same hue family as the row wash but more saturated. Reinforces the row-level diff state without competing with per-token text colour. Worker decides if this is strictly necessary on top of #2.

## Composes with existing features

- **Per-token syntax colour** (rf2-79ojx) — UNCHANGED. Numbers stay orange, booleans stay gold, etc. The conflict goes away because diff status is now off the text-colour channel.
- **Diff value annotation** (`← changed from X`) — still renders as today; uses neutral grey for the annotation chip + sits on the now-washed row background, so it still reads.
- **Card chrome** (rf2-63ie5) — the row wash sits INSIDE the card; the card's own background remains untouched.
- **Width-aware expansion** (rf2-kbdk8) — orthogonal; an inline-rendered diff row still gets its row wash.

## Acceptance

1. The `~/+/-` gutter glyphs are rendered in a hue NOT present in the syntax-highlight palette. Verified via chromatic-distance check against each `:syntax-*` token.
2. Diff-affected rows show a subtle row-background wash (added/modified/removed in distinct, low-saturation hues).
3. Per-token text colours UNCHANGED — number values still orange, boolean still gold, etc. No regression vs rf2-79ovx.
4. Operator scanning a diff row can distinguish "what type is this value" (text colour) from "what diff state is this" (row chrome) on independent visual channels.
5. Light AND dark themes both implemented with appropriate wash + glyph colours.
6. Composes with card-chrome (rf2-63ie5) — the row wash respects the card's content area.

## What does NOT change

- The diff-data computation (which rows are added/modified/removed)
- The `← changed from X` annotation text + position
- The widget's per-token colours (rf2-79ojx remains the source of truth for syntax tokens)
- Any non-diff-mode rendering

## What DOES change

- Diff gutter glyph colour (moved off the syntax palette into a reserved diff-only hue)
- Diff rows gain row-background wash
- Optional: 2px left-border stripe on diff rows
- Theme tokens add: `:diff-gutter`, `:diff-added-wash`, `:diff-modified-wash`, `:diff-removed-wash` (or equivalent naming)

## Out of scope for this bead

- Re-evaluating the whole Option A vs B vs C decision (may revisit later — see note below)
- Adding granularity beyond add/modify/remove (e.g. "renamed key" or "moved value" — not a current diff classification)
- Animation on diff state changes

## Note — this may be revisited

Option A is the right call now, but the wider operator-experience may justify revisiting later:
- Option B (repaint diff colours to non-clashing hues) — if the row wash proves too subtle in dense panels
- Option C (drop syntax colours entirely in diff-mode rows) — if comparing values is the dominant use of diff mode and the syntax colour becomes noise

Hold these as fallbacks; don't pursue them unless Option A proves wanting in real operator use.

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: load http://localhost:8031/counter → expand `:counter` in App-DB → trigger a click on `[+ 1]` to produce a diff → confirm the `~` gutter colour vs number/boolean value colours all look orange in the side panel.
2. Pick the reserved diff-gutter hue. Test in both themes. Verify chromatic distance from every `:syntax-*` token.
3. Tune the row-wash opacity (10-15% range). Too saturated and it competes with text; too faint and operators don't see it.
4. Decide on the 2px left-border stripe. Try with + without. If the row-wash alone is sufficient, skip it (less chrome is more).
5. Test against the diff-rendered App-DB panel + the Handler panel's epoch-diff section. Both should benefit.
6. Composability check with rf2-63ie5 (card chrome) — the row wash lives INSIDE the card's content area, not bleeding past its border-radius.
7. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Live measurement of the clash: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Conflicting source: `:syntax-number` `:syntax-boolean` `:syntax-keyword` tokens in `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljc`
- Diff-mode render path: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs` (worker locates the `render-leaf-with-diff` + map-row + gutter render sites)
- Palette source of truth: rf2-79ojx (just landed; this bead leaves it untouched)
- GitHub diff convention reference: light green/red row washes with code keeping syntax colour

title: Xray data-display: map layout alignment — triangle/line/keys/brace column
description:
## Symptom

When a map is expanded in a data-display mount, the layout has three misalignment issues that make the structure hard to follow:

1. **Nested triangle is indented away from the left edge.** The expand/collapse triangle for a nested value sits to the right of where the operator's eye expects — pushed inward by the parent's indent. Operator wants triangles to read as primary, pinned to the left.

2. **Vertical guide line doesn't align with the triangle.** When the body is expanded, a thin vertical line runs down the left of the body to mark the indentation level. But the line sits offset from the triangle that opens the body — the eye sees triangle + line as TWO unrelated marks instead of one continuous tree affordance.

3. **Map keys' left edges don't align with the vertical line.** Keys inside the expanded body start further right than the line, creating a tertiary alignment column the eye has to learn.

4. **Closing `}` doesn't align with the vertical line either.** Opening brace sits offset (from rf2-1bra5 work), and the closing `}` doesn't have a clear column reference — the eye can't follow the bracket pair vertically.

## Proposed layout

    ▾ {                              ← triangle at column 0, { at triangle's right
      │                              ← vertical line at center of triangle (col X)
      │ :counter         1
      │ :async           nil
      │ :machine-ui  {…
      │ :threshold       5
      │ }                            ← closing } aligned with vertical line
    }

(ASCII; rendering uses real CSS columns, not characters.)

Rules:
- Triangle left edge at column 0 of the map's "level"
- Vertical guide line at the triangle's horizontal center
- Keys' left edges aligned with the vertical line
- Closing `}` aligned with the vertical line
- Opening `{` sits immediately right of the triangle (current behaviour, kept)

## What changes

Edit the map-body render in `views/data_display.cljs`. Current code (line 1187-1192):

    (when (and expanded? (some? body))
      [:div {:data-testid (str (testid-for panel-id mount-id path) "-body")
             :style {:padding-left "14px"
                     :margin-left  "5px"
                     :border-left  (str "1px solid " (:border-subtle tokens))}}
       body])

The `:margin-left 5px` + `:border-left 1px` + `:padding-left 14px` arrangement puts:
- The vertical line at x=5 (where margin ends)
- The body content at x=20 (margin + border + padding)

For Mike's layout (with the 22-24px triangle font from the size bead), the triangle's center is at ~11px from its left edge. So:
- Triangle stays at x=0
- Vertical line needs to be at x=11 (triangle center)
- Body content needs to be at x=11 (same as vertical line, so keys align with line)
- Closing `}` (rendered separately, currently after the body div) needs to share the same x=11 column

Roughly:

    {:padding-left "6px"           ;; small gap from line to keys
     :margin-left  "11px"          ;; line at triangle center
     :border-left  (str "1px solid " (:border-subtle tokens))}

Numbers tunable; worker eyeballs against the running app. The 11px target depends on the final triangle font-size (22 vs 24 — coordinate with the triangle-size bead).

Closing `}` — currently rendered after the body div, presumably at the level's outer column. To align with the vertical line:
- Wrap the closing `}` in its own row that has `padding-left` matching the vertical-line position
- OR move the `}` INTO the body div as its final row (worker chooses cleanest)

Worker also removes any nested-triangle indent that pushes the triangle off the left. The triangle should be the LEFTMOST element of its row, period.

## Acceptance

1. In every expanded map, the nested triangle sits flush at the left edge of its row (no padding pushing it inward).
2. The vertical guide line's horizontal position aligns with the center of the triangle that opens it. Verified via `getBoundingClientRect()` — triangle center x ≈ guide line x ± 1px.
3. Map keys' left x-coordinates align with the vertical line. Across all keys in the same map, `getBoundingClientRect().left` equals the guide line's x.
4. Closing `}` of an expanded map sits at the same x as the vertical line. Bracket pair (`{` opening to the right of triangle; `}` aligned with line) reads as a coherent column structure.
5. Works at every nesting depth — first level, second level, third+ all follow the same rule recursively.
6. Composes with rf2-card-chrome (card-style bead) — alignment doesn't break when wrapped in a card.
7. Composes with the triangle-size bead (22-24px font) — the vertical-line x position is computed against the final triangle center, not the pre-bead 14px center.

## What does NOT change

- The triangle glyph
- Key/value column alignment within a row (rf2-1bra5 already landed)
- Diff-mode gutter
- Sentinel chrome
- Expansion state mechanics
- Popup widget

## Out of scope

- Rainbow brackets / nesting-depth-coloured punctuation
- Animation on expand/collapse
- Whatever happens at the very TOP level (the inspector's outermost `{`/`}`) — that may or may not need the same treatment; worker decides whether the outermost map deserves the triangle+line+brace rule or uses different chrome since it's wrapped in the card-chrome's border

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: load http://localhost:8031/counter → App-DB → expand `:counter` to see the current misalignment. Probe via `getBoundingClientRect()` on triangle, vertical-line container, first key, closing brace. Document the current x-coordinates.
2. Compute the target x for the vertical line given the final triangle font-size (depends on coordination with the triangle-size bead).
3. Decide where the closing `}` renders today (after body div? at body's parent? where in the hiccup?). Restructure so it lands on the vertical line.
4. Test at multiple nesting depths — first nested map, second, third. Each level's alignment should follow the same rule independently.
5. Test with diff-mode rendering — gutter glyphs (~, +, -) shouldn't displace the alignment.
6. Compose with card-chrome — alignment still right when wrapped.
7. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Live probe + visual review: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Live patch applied + verified during session: `margin-left: 10px, padding-left: 6px` on body divs (approximation pending final triangle size)
- Current map-body render: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs:1187-1192`
- Coordinates with: rf2-triangle-size (this bead's vertical-line position depends on the triangle's final center)
- Coordinates with: rf2-card-chrome (this bead's layout must work inside the card chrome)

title: Xray data-display: triangle glyph 14px → 22-24px (follow-up to rf2-tzvk9)
description:
## Symptom

After rf2-tzvk9 landed, the triangle hit-box is fine (40×32px) but the GLYPH itself is still small (14px font-size). Visually the triangles don't feel substantial enough — operator's eye doesn't immediately register them as the primary expand/collapse affordance.

In `views/data_display.cljs` — the triangle render emits the glyph as a `[:span ...]` inside the `-toggle` testid span. Locate the `:font-size` style (worker confirms exact line — possibly `triangle-style` or inline at the render site). Change `14px` → `22px`.

title: Xray data-display: inspector card chrome (background + border) on top-level mounts
description:
## Symptom

Each `[dd/data-display value opts]` mount in the App-DB panel (and elsewhere) sits transparent on the panel canvas. Multiple mounts in the same panel (e.g. App-DB shows 3: counter app db, machine app db, route params) blend into one continuous block — no visual separation, no card affordance. The eye has nothing to distinguish "this is the counter app's state" from "this is the machine app's state".

The Views panel already wraps each inspector item in a chromed card. Same chrome should apply to data-display inspectors so the operator sees them as distinct cards.

Measured live this session (pair-debug 2026-05-26): the Views panel uses `background: #f5f5f5; border: 1px solid #d1d1d1; border-radius: 8px;` on its inspector cards.

## What changes

Apply the same chrome to every top-level `[dd/data-display value opts]` mount via an opt-in widget arg:

    [dd/data-display value
     {:panel-id :rf.xray/app-db
      :card?    true                  ;; NEW — opts into card chrome
      ...}]

When `:card? true`, the widget's outermost `<div>` adds:

    {:background-color   (:bg-1 tokens)             ; #f5f5f5 light / equivalent dark
     :border             (str "1px solid " (:border-default tokens))  ; #d1d1d1
     :border-radius      "8px"
     :padding            "8px 10px"
     :margin-bottom      "8px"}

When `:card? false` (default), the chrome is omitted — preserves the current behaviour for callers that don't want it (e.g. inline `mini` renders, popup contents that already have their own modal chrome).

Theme-aware: the values come from theme tokens, not literals — both light and dark themes get their card colour.

## Consumer updates

- **App-DB panel** (`panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:142,146`) — pass `:card? true` so its 3 top-level mounts become distinct cards
- **Handler panel** (`panels/event_detail.cljs` mounts) — pass `:card? true` where the panel renders multiple side-by-side mounts (worker locates)
- **Trace panel, Machines panel, Routes panel, Issues panel** — apply same treatment where multiple mounts exist; skip where the panel only renders one

Worker audits all consumer panels and applies `:card? true` where it improves visual separation.

## Acceptance

1. `data-display` accepts optional `:card? boolean` opt (default `false`).
2. When `:card? true`, the outermost `<div>` carries the card chrome (background, border, radius, padding, margin). Verified live: `getComputedStyle` matches the Views panel inspector card.
3. Consumer panels (App-DB, Handler, others as identified) pass `:card? true` at appropriate call sites.
4. Theme-aware: switch to dark theme; cards still distinct (border + background contrast tuned per token).
5. No regression in panels that don't pass `:card? true`.

## What does NOT change

- The widget's data-render logic
- The expansion-state mechanics
- The popup integration
- The diff-mode behaviour
- The triangle / glyph rendering

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: load http://localhost:8031/counter → App-DB → confirm the 3 mounts look like one continuous block today. Then check the Views panel → confirm its cards are distinct.
2. Verify the token values: `:bg-1` should be `#f5f5f5` light theme; pick the right border token (`:border-default` or `:border-subtle` — try both, eyeball which gives the right separation).
3. Audit every consumer panel — list which deserve `:card? true` and which don't. Skip mini-mounts in tables (those render inline and shouldn't card).
4. Test light + dark themes.
5. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Live measurement: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Views panel card values: `background: #f5f5f5; border: 1px solid #d1d1d1; border-radius: 8px;`
- Widget source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs`

title: Xray data-display: expansion state lost on panel-leave-and-return (mount-id-keyed isolation)
description:
## Symptom

In the Xray panel, leaving a tab (e.g. App-DB or Handler) and returning to it resets every expand/collapse decision the operator made. All nodes snap back to `default-expanded-depth`. The operator has to re-expand the same paths every time they navigate away and back.

Reproducible:
1. Open Xray → App-DB tab
2. Expand a deep path (collapse some top-level nodes, expand some nested ones)
3. Click to Handler tab
4. Click back to App-DB tab
5. All expansion choices are gone; the tree is back to default-expanded-depth

Same behaviour in the Handler panel (also a consumer of the new data-display widget) and any other panel that mounts it.

## Root cause (live diagnosis + source review, pair-debug session 2026-05-26)

The expansion-slot in app-db is keyed by `[panel-id mount-id path]`. The `mount-id` is auto-generated inside the data-display widget's form-2 outer fn — one UUID per mount instance (`gen-mount-id` at `views/data_display.cljs:1150`).

Per design rf2-sndui: *"the public API does NOT take a `:render-id` — mount-id is generated internally. Two simultaneous mounts get independent expansion state via the auto-id."*

The flow when an operator leaves and returns to a panel:

1. Operator clicks ▾/▸ a few times → reducer writes overrides at `[:app-db, <mount-id-A>, [:counter :threshold]]` etc.
2. Operator switches to Handler tab → App-DB panel unmounts → data-display instance with mount-id `A` is destroyed
3. Expansion overrides keyed by mount-id `A` remain in app-db (no cleanup) — orphaned
4. Operator switches back to App-DB tab → React mounts a fresh data-display with mount-id `B`
5. Renderer looks up overrides at `[:app-db, B, ...]` — finds none — falls back to `default-expanded-depth 2`
6. Visible state is reset; mount-id-`A` overrides now sit forever in app-db as untraceable garbage

This is the deliberate design trade-off (per-call-site isolation: two side-by-side `[data-display value]` mounts toggle independently). The cost — only visible in the panel-leave-and-return workflow — is that the same logical site loses state on every unmount.

## Fix — opt-in stable `:site-id`, additive

The data-display widget accepts an optional `:site-id` opt. When provided, used as the expansion-key's second component INSTEAD of auto-mount-id. When omitted, behaviour is unchanged (auto-mount-id, per-call-site isolation preserved for naive callers).

Public API extension (additive):

    [data-display value {:panel-id :app-db
                         :site-id  [:app-db-frame frame-id]   ;; NEW — opt
                         :default-expanded-depth 2}]

Expansion-key derivation:

    (defn expansion-key
      "Compose the per-node expansion key."
      [panel-id site-or-mount-id path]
      [panel-id site-or-mount-id (vec path)])

Inside the widget — the form-2 outer fn picks `site-id` when supplied, falls back to auto-mount-id:

    (defn data-display
      ([value] (data-display value nil))
      ([_value _opts]
       (let [auto-mount-id (gen-mount-id)]
         (fn [value opts]
           (let [{:keys [site-id ...]} opts
                 effective-id (or site-id auto-mount-id)]
             ...)))))

### Consumer updates

Every panel that currently mounts data-display with the expectation of persistent expansion state passes a stable `:site-id`. Identified call-sites this session:

- App-DB panel (`panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:142,146`) — pass `:site-id [:app-db-frame frame-id]` (per-frame stable id)
- Handler panel (`panels/event.cljs` or similar — worker locates) — three full-widget mounts + four mini-mounts; each needs a stable id derived from the cascade's epoch-id + the slot's role (event-vec / db-before-after / fx)
- Any other panel surface using data-display where operator-friendly persistence is wanted (worker audits)

Worker decides whether `mini`-variant mounts (testid `rf-xray-data-display-mini`) should ALSO get stable site-ids or whether their ephemeral nature (rendered inline within rapidly-changing tables) justifies the auto-mount-id default.

### Bonus — orphan cleanup (low priority, may defer)

After this fix lands, the expansion-slot still accumulates orphaned mount-id overrides every time a panel that doesn't pass `:site-id` is unmounted. Two options:

- Accept the leak (small entries, app-db pruning isn't critical pre-alpha)
- Add a `:rf.xray.data-display/prune-orphaned` event that walks expansion-slot keys and drops any whose mount-id isn't currently mounted — triggered on panel-mount or periodic timer

Worker can scope this in or defer to a follow-up.

## Acceptance

1. `data-display` accepts an optional `:site-id` opt in its opts map. When supplied, it's used as the expansion-key's second component; when omitted, auto-mount-id is used (existing behaviour preserved).
2. App-DB panel passes `:site-id [:app-db-frame frame-id]` at its mount sites. Expansion choices made before leaving the panel survive a Tab→Handler→Tab→App-DB round-trip — verified by manual probe and one new test.
3. Handler panel passes stable `:site-id`s at its data-display mount sites (worker decides the right derivation key — likely epoch-id + slot-role).
4. Side-by-side `[data-display value]` mounts in the SAME consumer that don't share a site-id (because the consumer doesn't bother) continue to isolate state via auto-mount-id. The per-call-site isolation property the original design protected isn't lost — it just becomes opt-out via supplying a shared site-id (rare; mostly each call-site gets its own derivation).
5. The `:default-expanded-depth` heuristic still applies on first mount before any operator clicks — `:site-id` only affects WHICH key the override is stored under, not whether overrides exist initially.
6. Click-toggle bug (rf2-y59tb) is the dependency — this bead's testing requires that toggles actually work. Either land rf2-y59tb first, or coordinate the testing protocol.

## What does NOT change

- The widget's per-render data-display logic, palette tokens, rendering pipeline
- The expansion-slot's location in app-db (`:rf.xray.data-display/expansion`)
- The `expansion-key`'s structural shape (still `[panel-id ?-id path]`; the middle slot just sources differently)
- The auto-mount-id default (preserved)
- The diff-mode behaviour
- Spec 015 sentinel handling
- The popup widget

## What DOES change

- `data-display` opts map gains `:site-id`
- Form-2 outer-fn picks site-id over auto-mount-id when supplied
- Consumer panels (App-DB, Handler, others) pass stable site-ids
- Optional: orphan-prune affordance for the expansion-slot

## Out of scope

- Click-toggle bug (rf2-y59tb) — separate bead, but this bead's testing depends on it being fixed
- Map layout (rf2-1bra5) — separate
- Palette (rf2-79ojx) — separate
- Triangle hit-box (rf2-tzvk9) — separate

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: open the App-DB panel on http://localhost:8031/counter, expand/collapse some paths, switch to Handler tab, return — confirm visible state is reset. Confirm the expansion-slot in `:rf/xray`'s app-db still contains orphaned mount-id overrides (depending on click-toggle's status — see Acceptance #6).
2. Audit every data-display call-site in `tools/xray/`. List them. Decide for each: does it deserve a stable site-id (operator-persistence-friendly) or stay on auto-mount-id (per-call-site isolation matters more)? Document the call.
3. Decide the site-id derivation pattern. Suggested: a stable vector key like `[:app-db-frame frame-id]` for App-DB or `[:handler-event epoch-id :event-vec]` for Handler's event-vector mount. Worker picks the convention.
4. Confirm the design rf2-sndui rationale doesn't get violated — per-call-site isolation MUST still work for two `[data-display value]` mounts that don't share a site-id. Test side-by-side.
5. Decide whether to ship the orphan-prune affordance now or follow up. Document the choice in the PR.
6. State which test surfaces validate persistence-across-unmount. New test(s) needed; pin them.
7. Report findings before pushing implementation.

## References

- Widget mount-id generation: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs:1150` (`gen-mount-id` inside form-2 outer fn)
- Expansion-key derivation: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs:123-126`
- Toggle reducer: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs:131-144`
- App-DB call-site: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:142,146`
- Handler panel call-sites: worker locates (3 full + 4 mini mounts identified live this session)
- Design rationale: rf2-sndui D4=a — "the public API does NOT take a :render-id — mount-id is generated internally"
- Related: rf2-y59tb (click-toggle bug, blocks testing this), rf2-1bra5 (map layout), rf2-79ojx (palette), rf2-tzvk9 (triangle hit-box)
- Live measurement: pair-debug session 2026-05-26, App-DB + Handler panels on /counter
notes: PR #2170 merged

title: Xray data-display: triangle hit-box too small (~6.6px wide; needs ≥24px)
description:
## Symptom

The expand/collapse triangles (`▾` / `▸`) in the Xray data-display widget are hard to click. They register `cursor: pointer` but the actual hit-box is hairline-thin.

Measured live this session against the App-DB panel on http://localhost:8031/counter:

- Width: **6.6px**
- Height: **16.8px** (the row's line-height)
- Font-size: 12px
- Padding: 0px

Click target area: ~110 sq px. Comfortable mouse-target minimum is ~24×24 = 576 sq px (Fitts's Law + the WCAG 2.2 AAA 44×44 touch-target guidance). The current triangle is roughly 5× smaller than the comfortable minimum.

Effect: programmers miss-click into adjacent text instead of toggling the triangle. Every expansion of a deeply-nested node is more friction than it needs to be.

## Fix

Combine both:

1. **Padding around the triangle** — grow the click target without enlarging the glyph visually. `padding: 2px 6px` on the triangle span (or whichever element carries the click handler) takes the hit-box to ~18-22px × 21px without making the glyph feel bulky in dense data.

2. **Bump triangle font-size to ~14-16px** — explicit override on the triangle span (not inherited from the body's 12px). Glyph itself becomes more visible AND the hit area grows naturally.

Combined target: ~24px × 24px clickable area. The visual weight of the triangle increases slightly but stays subordinate to the surrounding data.

If padding shifts the visual layout of map rows (the triangle sits to the left of the key; padding might push the key right), the padding should be horizontally INSIDE the existing key-column gutter so it doesn't disturb the column-alignment fix being worked on in rf2-1bra5. Worker confirms layout-impact during their own review.

## Acceptance

1. Triangle click-target measures ≥ 24px × 24px in the DOM (verifiable via `getBoundingClientRect()`).
2. The triangle glyph itself remains visually subordinate — it doesn't dominate the row.
3. Click behaviour is unchanged (event still routes to `:rf.xray.data-display/toggle-node` — though the toggle bug itself is rf2-y59tb's concern, not this bead's).
4. No regression in row height or column alignment of the rest of the map row.
5. Both expanded (▾) and collapsed (▸) triangles get the same hit-box.
6. Diff-mode rows (which have additional gutter glyphs alongside the triangle) keep their layout — the triangle's enlarged hit-box doesn't crowd the diff gutter.

## What does NOT change

- The triangle glyphs themselves (`▾` / `▸`)
- The click handler's dispatch target
- The toggle reducer logic (that's rf2-y59tb)
- The widget's data-rendering logic
- Any public API

## What DOES change

- One or two CSS properties on the triangle span in `views/data_display.cljs` — `font-size` + `padding`
- Possibly a token in `theme/tokens.cljc` if the magic numbers should live there (worker decides)

## Out of scope

- Fixing the toggle behaviour bug (frame leak + first-click logic) — that's rf2-y59tb
- Map row layout (key/value alignment, brace offset, scalar wrap) — that's rf2-1bra5
- Hover affordance / row highlight (UX polish, separate concern)

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: probe the triangle's bounding rect against http://localhost:8031/counter. Confirm width ~6.6px before the change, ≥24px after.
2. Confirm the chosen padding + font-size doesn't disturb the surrounding column alignment. If it does, the padding goes INSIDE an existing layout gutter rather than extending into adjacent columns.
3. Check the change composes with diff-mode rendering (gutter glyphs sit alongside triangle in diff mode). Probe a diff-mode row before and after.
4. Confirm both ▾ and ▸ glyphs get the change uniformly.

## References

- Widget triangle render: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs` — the click-handler emit site (line 717 region — worker locates the exact line)
- Live measurement: pair-debug session 2026-05-26, App-DB panel on /counter
- Related (NOT to be folded together — likely already in flight): rf2-1bra5 (map layout), rf2-y59tb (toggle bug), rf2-79ojx (palette)
- Mouse target guidance: WCAG 2.2 AAA 44×44 touch, ~24×24 desktop-mouse comfort minimum

title: Xray data-display: map layout — scalars wrap below key + values don't column-align
description:
## Symptom

In the Xray App-DB panel (and any other surface using `views.data-display`), expanded maps have two related layout bugs that make them hard to scan:

### Bug 1 — Some scalar values wrap to a new line below their key

When a map is expanded, some key/value pairs render inline (`:value 1` on one line) while others wrap so the value is on its own line below the key:

    :value         1                        ← inline (good)
    :last-clicked  1779742091688            ← inline (good)
    :show-parity?
      true                                  ← wrapped (bad)
    :threshold
      5                                     ← wrapped (bad)

Measured live this session against the App-DB panel on http://localhost:8031/counter:

| Row | Height | Layout |
|---|---|---|
| `:value ~1← changed from 0` | 17.79px | one line |
| `:last-clicked ~1779742091688← changed from nil` | 17.79px | one line |
| `:show-parity?  true` | **28.79px** | two lines |
| `:threshold  5` | **28.79px** | two lines |

The taller rows are the value-on-own-line cases.

Counter-intuitive: the rows that contain MORE content (diff annotation `← changed from X`) render inline; the simpler rows wrap. The render-path heuristic has things backwards — somewhere the widget is deciding "block layout" for scalars that should obviously be inline.

### Bug 2 — Values don't align in a column across rows of the same map

Even when values DO sit inline with their key, they don't column-align across rows of the same map because each row is its own `display: flex` (key span + value span sized independently):

    :value         1                ← value starts at col ~7
    :last-clicked  1779742091688    ← value starts at col ~14
    :show-parity?  true             ← value starts at col ~14
    :threshold     5                ← value starts at col ~11

A programmer scanning the values column gets a ragged left edge because the value column doesn't exist — each row floats its value right after its key.

## Why both bugs together

They're the same render-side concern — the widget's map-row layout in `views/data_display.cljs`. Fixing one without the other leaves the panel still hard to scan. Both fixable in one edit at the map-body render site.

## Fixes

### Fix 1 — short scalar values stay inline with their key

Find the render-path divergence that pushes some scalars into block layout. Worker investigation needed; likely candidates:

- A code path that wraps "expandable" values (maps / vectors / large collections) in block layout AND mistakenly catches some plain scalars too
- The `:expanded?` resolution defaulting to `true` for some leaves and rendering them as a block-formatted expanded body even when there's nothing to expand
- A diff-mode vs browse-mode branch that lays out diff-annotated rows differently (this might be why diff rows ARE inline and non-diff rows AREN'T)

Rule: plain scalars (numbers, booleans, strings, keywords, nil, symbols) MUST render inline with their key. No exceptions. Block layout reserved for collections (maps / vectors / sets / lists) and oversized scalars (strings past `:max-inline-width`).

### Fix 2 — values column-align across rows of the same map

Change the map-body container from default-block to CSS Grid:

    {:style {:display "grid"
             :grid-template-columns "max-content 1fr"
             :column-gap "8px"
             :row-gap "0"}}

Each row's key + value emit as direct grid children (not wrapped in a per-row container). CSS Grid auto-resolves `max-content` to the widest key in the map, so every value across every row aligns to the same column.

Nested maps each get their own grid (a nested map's keys align within their own scope — alignment does NOT propagate into nested children).

If the row needs additional content (gutter glyph for diff mode, expansion triangle, popup affordance), use `grid-template-columns: <gutter> <triangle> max-content 1fr` and emit all four direct grid children per row. Each map's grid template is computed at render time so non-diff maps don't waste a gutter column.

## Acceptance

1. Bug 1: every plain scalar value in every expanded map renders on the SAME LINE as its key. Measured via DOM row-height = single-line-height for every scalar row. No diff-mode vs browse-mode divergence — both modes lay out the same way.
2. Bug 2: within a single map's expanded body, all values start at the same x-coordinate. Measured via `getBoundingClientRect().left` across all value spans in the same map — they all share one x.
3. Nested-map isolation: a nested map's value-column-x is independent of its parent's value-column-x (each map computes its own value-column from its own widest key).
4. Diff-mode gutter glyphs (the `← changed from X` annotations) still render correctly — alignment fix doesn't break the diff readout.
5. Sentinel rows (`:rf/redacted`, `:rf.size/large-elided`) render inline like other scalars.
6. Visual smoke against the App-DB panel on http://localhost:8031/counter: every `[data-rf-type]` span across every expanded map is on the same line as its preceding key span; all values within one map share the same `left` x-coordinate.
7. The popup widget (`data_display_popup`) inherits the same fix — same widget code path.

## What does NOT change

- The widget's per-token colour treatment
- The expansion-state mechanics
- The diff-mode behaviour (other than fixing the inline-vs-block divergence that incidentally splits diff vs non-diff rows today)
- The mount-id keying scheme
- Any public API of the widget
- The popup widget's API (it picks up the fix automatically via the shared render code)

## What DOES change

- Map-body render in `views/data_display.cljs` switches from per-row flex containers to a single grid container per map
- The render-path divergence that block-formats some scalars is found and removed
- Rows emit key + value (+ diff-gutter + triangle if present) as direct grid children, not wrapped in a per-row div

## Out of scope

- Pretty-printing wrap behaviour for very long inline values (e.g. a 200-char string that legitimately needs wrapping). That's a separate concern; the inline-vs-block decision for short scalars is what's broken today.
- Rainbow brackets / nested-depth-coloured punctuation.
- Hover affordances / row-highlight on hover (separate UX concern).

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce both bugs live against http://localhost:8031/counter. Probe each map row's bounding rect — confirm the height differential (single-line rows ~17.79px, wrapped rows ~28.79px) and confirm the value-x divergence across rows of the same map.
2. Find the render-path branch that block-formats some scalars. Walk `views/data_display.cljs` map-rendering code; look for any conditional that switches between inline and block layout for scalar leaves. Surface the condition + WHY it's wrong (e.g. "this branch checks `(:expanded? resolved)` but should also check `(scalar? value)` first"). The diff-vs-non-diff divergence is a strong hint — diff rows go down one code path, non-diff scalars go down another. Pin the split.
3. Validate the CSS Grid template choice — confirm `max-content 1fr` behaves correctly with very long keys (which should grow the key column to the longest key in the map, not push the value off-screen). Test against a map with a deliberately-long key (e.g. `:rf.route.with.a.lot.of.namespacing/some-counter`).
4. Confirm the grid layout composes with the existing diff-mode gutter / triangle / popup-affordance render. If they're emitted as per-row container children today, they need to be emitted as additional grid columns.
5. State which test surfaces validate map layout. If none exist, the visual regression test from Acceptance #6 is new test content this bead adds.
6. Report findings before pushing implementation.

## References

title: Xray data-display: adopt CLJS-syntax-highlight palette (token-table only)
description:
## Symptom

In the Xray App-DB panel (and any other surface using the new `views.data-display` widget), the colour-coding of EDN values does not read as syntax-highlighted. A CLJS programmer looking at the panel sees mostly blue + grey + occasional red and perceives "syntax highlighting turned off", even though the widget IS dispatching each scalar type to its own token.

Measured live this session against the running step-deck testbed:

| Element class | Count | Computed colour |
|---|---|---|
| Keyword keys (`:counter`, `:value`, …) | 45 | `rgb(9, 105, 218)` blue |
| Numbers (typed) | 6 | `rgb(5, 80, 174)` darker blue |
| Keyword values (typed) | 4 | `rgb(9, 105, 218)` blue |
| Strings (typed) | 2 | `rgb(10, 48, 105)` very dark blue |
| Nil (typed) | 5 | `rgb(140, 149, 159)` grey |
| Booleans (typed) | 2 | `rgb(207, 34, 46)` red |

Three of the five scalar types are in the SAME blue hue family with only luminance varying between them. To a CLJS programmer's eye trained on syntax-highlighted code, blue-keywords + blue-numbers + blue-strings reads as monochrome.

## Why this is wrong

CLJS programmers' eyes are trained on syntax-highlighted code in their editor (Calva, Cursive, vscode-clojure, cider, etc.). When the Xray inspector uses different colour-to-type mappings than the editor, type recognition is slower because the eye has to consciously decode rather than pattern-match.

Convention across mainstream CLJS editors (they converge):

| EDN type | Convention | Widget today |
|---|---|---|
| Keywords (`:foo`) | **Purple / magenta** | Blue |
| Strings (`"…"`) | **Green** (some themes red) | Dark blue |
| Numbers (`42`) | **Orange** (some themes cyan) | Darker blue |
| Booleans / nil | **Orange / yellow** ("constants") | Booleans red, nil grey |
| Symbols / vars | Blue | n/a |
| Punctuation / brackets | Muted grey | Grey ✓ |

The widget picked GitHub Primer's `prettylights-syntax-*` palette but mapped CLJS types onto it ad-hoc. Primer's palette is designed for inline code blocks in documentation (muted-by-design, not optimised for type-distinction in a dense inspector); the semantic mapping (which Primer token represents which CLJS type) was chosen widget-side and doesn't follow CLJS-syntax-highlighting convention.

## What changes

ONLY edits to `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljc` — the `:syntax-*` token values, both light-theme and dark-theme tables. The widget already correctly dispatches each scalar type to its own syntax token (see `data-display.cljs` lines 207-234 + 407-433 — `collection-kind` + `render-scalar`); the tokens are just bound to the wrong colours.

No `views/data-display.cljs` changes. No widget-protocol changes. No App-DB panel changes. No documentation changes (other than the tokens file's own comments).

## Specific change

Adopt a recognisable CLJS palette as the base. **Recommendation: Calva default** — most-used CLJS editor; majority of re-frame2 programmers' eyes are trained on its colour conventions. Worker may justify One-Dark-Pro, Cursive default, or another widely-used CLJS theme — but state the choice + reason.

Approximate target palette (Calva default light theme; worker confirms exact values from the source palette):

    :syntax-keyword    "#a626a4"   ; magenta — keywords (most-frequent type; must pop)
    :syntax-string     "#50a14f"   ; green   — strings
    :syntax-number     "#986801"   ; orange  — numbers
    :syntax-boolean    "#c18401"   ; gold    — true/false (in the "constant" family)
    :syntax-nil        "#a0a1a7"   ; grey    — nil (deliberately muted; "absence" reads as faded)
    :syntax-symbol     "#4078f2"   ; blue    — symbols / vars (if used)
    :syntax-punctuation "#383a42"  ; near-text — brackets, commas, colons (subtle)

Dark theme — same hues, brightness-shifted for dark backgrounds (worker takes the equivalent dark variant from the source palette).

The five MUST-DISTINGUISH types (keyword / string / number / boolean / nil) MUST come from at least four different hue families. No two type tokens may sit in the same hue family with only luminance distinguishing them.

## Acceptance

1. Token values in `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljc` updated for both light and dark theme tables.
2. The five scalar-type tokens (`:syntax-keyword`, `:syntax-string`, `:syntax-number`, `:syntax-boolean`, `:syntax-nil`) span at least four hue families — verified by chromatic-distance check against the previous palette (the previous palette had 3/5 in blue).
3. Visual smoke against the App-DB panel on http://localhost:8031/counter: probe DOM and confirm keyword spans are NOT blue, number spans are NOT blue, string spans are NOT blue. Boolean and nil colours may stay close to today's if they already fit the conventional "constants" family.
4. Theme contrast meets WCAG AA against the panel background for all five token colours (both light + dark themes).
5. Worker documents the base-palette choice in a one-line comment in the tokens file: `;; syntax-* tokens derive from Calva default (or whichever) — chosen for CLJS-programmer eye-familiarity`.
6. No `views/data-display.cljs` changes required. If the worker finds widget-code changes ARE needed to land the palette change, surface — it indicates a tokens-vs-widget coupling that should itself be unwound.

## What does NOT change

- The widget code (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs`)
- The widget's per-token dispatch logic (`render-scalar`, `collection-kind`)
- The App-DB panel integration
- The expansion-state mechanics
- The popup widget
- The diff-mode behaviour
- Any spec / API surface

## What DOES change

- Five (or six, if `:syntax-symbol` is added) `:syntax-*` token values in `theme/tokens.cljc` — light + dark tables
- One comment in the tokens file documenting the palette choice

## Out of scope (file separately if you want them)

- Differentiating keyword-as-key from keyword-as-value visually (e.g. italic for keys) — separate bead, larger UX question.
- Rainbow brackets / nesting-depth-coloured punctuation — separate concern.
- Per-substrate palette variants — single palette covers all surfaces today.
- A user-selectable palette (Calva vs One-Dark vs Cursive) — separate bead if anyone wants it; ship one good default first.

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Open the tokens file and confirm the `:syntax-*` keys are the only colour bindings the widget dispatches against. If the widget is reading any inline literals or other token names, those need to land in this bead's scope too.
2. Pick the base palette (Calva default recommended). Pull the exact colour values from the upstream palette's source so the choice is grounded, not eyeballed.
3. Confirm both light and dark theme tables exist and the widget consumes the right one per active theme.
4. Test live against the App-DB panel — visit http://localhost:8031/counter, probe the DOM, confirm each scalar type renders the new colour. (`(.-color (js/getComputedStyle span))` on each `[data-rf-type="..."]` span.)
5. Check the panel still reads cleanly — high-saturation type colours against the inspector's neutral background shouldn't be visually fatiguing for a programmer scanning hundreds of values.
6. Report findings before pushing implementation.

## References

- Widget dispatch logic: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs` (lines 207-234 `collection-kind`, 407-433 `render-scalar`)
- Token table: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljc` (existing `:syntax-keyword`, `:syntax-number`, `:syntax-string`, etc. — currently bound to GitHub Primer values)
- App-DB panel integration: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:142,146`
- Calva default theme: https://github.com/BetterThanTomorrow/calva (worker pulls exact colour values from upstream)
- Live measurement: pair-debug session 2026-05-26, App-DB panel on /counter

Direction: impl → spec alignment. Public-contract surface — consumers (Claude Code, other MCP clients) need to know that after a successful discover-app, the build arg becomes optional within the same session. Otherwise the documented contract makes every tool call appear to require an explicit `:build` arg or env var.

title: docs(spec): align pair-mcp 003 trace-window + watch-epochs with rf2-fb4hn empty-result advisory (drift from #2120)
description:
PR #2120 (rf2-fb4hn) added an `:advisory` slot to trace-window + watch-epochs envelopes that fires when a query returns no matches but per-frame epoch-history holds events. The new slot names the cause and points at the right next step. Impl + tests live in tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/.../tools/{trace_window,watch_epochs}.cljs and the matching test files; spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md §trace-window (lines 627-677) and §watch-epochs (lines 679-716) do NOT mention the new shape.

Impl-side new envelope keys / reasons:

trace-window
- `:advisory {:reason :window-excludes-history :epochs-in-history N :window-ms N :hint "..."}` — when the time window (`:ms`) excludes events that DO sit in the per-frame ring. Hint points operators at `snapshot :include [:epochs]` for historical inspection.

watch-epochs
- `:advisory {:reason :no-events-since-id :history-count N :since-count 0 :hint "..."}` — when `:since-id` is at (or past) the head.
- `:advisory {:reason :pred-excludes-history :history-count N :since-count N :hint "..."}` — when events landed since the id but `:pred` filtered them all out.

Also new on both:
- `:history-count` slot in the runtime envelope (so the tool body can pick the right advisory from one nREPL round-trip).
- `:since-count` slot on watch-epochs.

Direction: impl → spec alignment. Public-contract surface — consumers reading the spec to understand why "empty results" should not be misread as "events aren't being captured". The 2026-05-25 pair-debug session referenced in the PR body specifically called out this misread cost.

Pre-alpha posture; no shim. Add an §Empty-result advisory subsection under each of trace-window and watch-epochs documenting the `:advisory` envelope key plus the reason values + hint patterns + the new `:history-count` / `:since-count` slots on the returns shape.
