title: decision(xray): eight design points to unblock data-display widget rebuild (rf2-oqa60)
description:
STOP — surfacing design questions to Mike. rf2-oqa60 is feasible end-to-end but raises 8 design points worth Mike's call before charging the rebuild.

The bead body is substantive but leaves several pivotal choices to the worker. Per the rf2-43koh / rf2-3g9nw precedent, when 3+ design points pile up, file ONE decision bead rather than guess and dispatch speculative work.

## 1. Decomposition shape — single PR vs phased rollout

Estimated LoC delta from a single PR:
- New renderer (xray/data-display/) — ~1500 LoC (type-detection × 30+ shapes, inline-preview, depth/width caps, custom-formatter protocol)
- Popup overlay component + anchor-positioning logic — ~500 LoC
- Theme tokens (new :rf-xray-token-* family, light + dark) — ~200 LoC
- Expansion store + LRU GC — ~150 LoC
- Migration of ~16 call sites — ~400 LoC
- cljs-devtools removal (delete cljs_devtools_render.cljs 647 LoC, simplify widget.cljs 596 LoC, simplify data_display/render.cljs 723 LoC keeping diff only)
- Spec 021 §10 rewrite — ~300 LoC
- Test suite (~30 unit-test files covering parity matrix + interactions + popup + accessibility) — ~2500 LoC

Total: ~5500 LoC churn in a single PR. Reviewable? Probably not cleanly.

Options:
- (A) Single PR — one umbrella merge; risk of stalling on review
- (B) Sequence of merge-ready PRs sharing the rf2-oqa60 umbrella, each with its own sub-bead — e.g.
  - PR1: Foundation — new renderer ns + theme tokens + parity matrix tests (no integration, leaves widget.cljs calling the old path)
  - PR2: Interactions — click-to-expand persistence, keyboard nav, gestures
  - PR3: Popup overlay component + tests
  - PR4: Migrate App-DB panel to the new widget (canonical first consumer)
  - PR5: Migrate Trace/Sub/Machine/Static panels to the new widget
  - PR6: Drop cljs-devtools dep + delete cljs_devtools_render.cljs + simplify widget.cljs + spec §10 rewrite
- (C) Two PRs — Foundation+Interactions+Popup in one, migration+removal in the other

Recommended: (B) — phased. Each PR self-justifying, each gate-passing, no stranded half-built widget in main. Smaller review surface, lower merge-conflict risk against parallel xray work. Files 5-6 sub-beads with `bd dep` chained to rf2-oqa60.

## 2. Mini API mismatch

Existing surface:
- (mini value) — 1-arg
- (mini value max-len) — 2-arg
- inspect-inline — separately, with sentinel routing (:rf/redacted / :rf.size/large-elided → bespoke chip chrome from theme.data-inspector)

Bead-specified surface:
- [xray.data-display/mini value] — 1-arg only

Question: Does the new `mini`
- (A) Stay 1-arg per bead body; max-len becomes a per-call-site default in inspect-inline
- (B) Keep 2-arg overload (preserve back-compat for the ~5 call sites that pass max-len)
- (C) Subsume inspect-inline (route sentinels inside mini itself)

Recommended: (B) + (C) — keep the 2-arg overload AND fold sentinel routing into mini. Drop the separate inspect-inline function. Simpler call surface; one less function name to remember.

## 3. Sentinel chrome — keep theme.data-inspector or reimplement

theme/data-inspector.cljs carries the bespoke chrome for spec-015 sentinels (:rf/redacted striped warning yellow; :rf.size/large-elided with [fetch] button). Currently widget/inspect routes sentinels to this module.

Bead says: "Spec 015 sentinels render with distinctive chrome (:rf/redacted warning-yellow striped; :rf.size/large-elided with [fetch])"

Question:
- (A) New widget calls into theme.data-inspector for sentinels (keep that module; route sentinels to it)
- (B) New widget reimplements sentinel chrome inline (delete theme.data-inspector)
- (C) Move sentinel chrome INTO the new widget ns, delete theme.data-inspector

Recommended: (C) — sentinels become first-class type classifications inside the renderer, alongside keywords/numbers/etc. Delete theme.data-inspector as part of the rebuild. Cleaner; one widget owns the whole render contract.

## 4. Expansion key — render-id rename to mount-id?

Bead specifies key is [panel-id mount-id path] (drop render-id).

Existing API:
- ~16 call sites pass {:render-id …} to browse / inspect / diff
- data-display/render-tree registers events keyed on (expansion-key panel-id render-id path)

Question:
- (A) Rename render-id → mount-id in the public API (all call sites updated, key shape preserved)
- (B) Remove :render-id/:mount-id from public API entirely — widget auto-generates internally; callers only pass :panel-id
- (C) Keep :render-id (no rename); just fix its lifecycle to be mount-stable per the bead's "lock"

Recommended: (B) — the bead body explicitly says "Caller writes [data-display {:value v :panel-id p}]; widget auto-assigns mount-id internally on first render. No caller-side instance-id management." This is the simpler call surface; matches the bead body's locked decision. Migration: drop :render-id from every call site.

## 5. Diff renderer — keep legacy engine, or rebuild diff?

The existing data_display/render.cljs (723 LoC) carries diff semantics — op->gutter-glyph, :added / :removed / :modified / :children, "← changed from <prior>" chips, gutter-row decoration. Diff is currently used by App-DB panel's diff variant via widget/diff → data-display/render-tree.

The bead is silent on diff — focuses on single-value rendering.

Question:
- (A) Diff stays on the legacy data-display/render-tree engine (keep that file, narrow it to diff only, delete the non-diff path). The new widget handles single-value browse / inspect / mini. Two engines side-by-side.
- (B) New widget subsumes diff — extend the new renderer with :before + diff annotations. Delete data_display/render.cljs entirely.
- (C) Diff is its own separate first-class widget (parallel to data-display) since its visual language is different (gutters + chips). Two distinct surfaces.

Recommended: (B) — diff is part of "first-class data display." The new widget knows about diff ops natively. The duplication of having two engines (legacy diff + new browse) is the same impedance-mismatch pattern the bead was filed to fix. Single source of truth.

But this adds significant scope to the new renderer. (A) is the pragmatic split if (B) bloats PR1. Mike picks.

## 6. Popup mount point + anchor scope

Bead specifies:

    [xray.data-display/popup
     {:value <any-cljs-value>
      :anchor <DOM-rect-or-element>
      :panel-id :rf.xray.popup/<id>
      :on-close (fn [] ...)}]

But there is NO existing value-inspection popup infrastructure in Xray. Settings popup (settings/popup.cljs) and filter edit popup (filters/edit_popup.cljs) are panel-specific.

Question:
- (A) Mount root for value popups — new top-level overlay container managed by mount.cljs; portal-style render into Xray's iframe shell. Multiple popups stack via z-index. Anchor is always an element INSIDE Xray's UI.
- (B) Anchor can be a host-page element (debugged app's DOM) — popup floats over the debugged app
- (C) Defer popup entirely to a follow-on bead — ship inspect/browse/mini in v1; popup as v2 after the main widget lands

Recommended: (A) + (C) — popup is Xray-internal only (anchor is always an Xray-DOM element). Defer popup component itself to a follow-on bead so PR1-PR6 of the main rebuild can land independently. Right-click-to-inspect and double-click-to-popup gestures land in the follow-on with the popup.

This removes ~500 LoC from the main rebuild scope and lets the popup be designed independently with its own positioning + z-index + close-gesture semantics.

## 7. Custom formatters protocol — v1 or follow-on?

Bead specifies IXrayDataDisplay protocol with render-header + render-body methods, dispatched via satisfies? before generic rendering. No internal Xray code currently EXTENDS this protocol — it's purely an extension point for consuming projects.

Question:
- (A) Ship the protocol in v1 — public extension point from day one
- (B) Defer the protocol — first build the closed renderer; add the protocol when a real consumer requests it
- (C) Ship the protocol but flag it {:internal? true} until a consumer proves the shape

Recommended: (B) — defer. The shape of the protocol (signatures, opts threading, fallthrough rules) is best designed against a concrete consumer. Pre-alpha posture; no back-compat shims; ship the closed renderer first; add the protocol when a real consumer beads in.

## 8. Popup-vs-panel storage scope

Bead specifies popup expansion state lives keyed by :panel-id :rf.xray.popup/<id>. But panel-id for the App-DB panel is e.g. :rf.xray/app-db. The namespacing convention is unclear.

Question: What's the canonical naming convention for popup panel-ids?
- (A) :rf.xray.popup/<uuid> per popup instance (auto-generated)
- (B) :rf.xray.popup/<purpose> per semantic role (e.g. :rf.xray.popup/app-db-inspect)
- (C) :rf.xray/popup-<n> numeric per-session counter

Recommended: (A) — auto-generated UUID per popup mount. Multi-popup stacking + close-and-reopen-with-same-purpose both work cleanly; no human-readable id collision; matches the bead body's auto-assigned mount-id pattern. This is bundled with item 6 (defer popup itself).

## Summary recommendations (worker proposed, awaiting Mike's call)

1. (B) — phased PR sequence; 5-6 sub-beads chained off rf2-oqa60
2. (B) + (C) — keep 2-arg mini; fold sentinel routing into mini; delete inspect-inline
3. (C) — move sentinel chrome into the new widget; delete theme.data-inspector
4. (B) — drop :render-id from public API; widget auto-assigns mount-id internally
5. (B) — new widget subsumes diff; delete data_display/render.cljs; single engine
6. (A) + (C) — popup is Xray-internal only; defer popup to follow-on bead
7. (B) — defer custom formatters protocol to follow-on; ship closed renderer in v1
8. (A) — auto-generated UUID per popup mount (bundled with #6)

## Blocking effect

rf2-oqa60 stays open; this decision bead blocks PR1 of the rebuild sequence. Once Mike rules, I'll:
- File sub-beads per the chosen decomposition shape (item 1)
- Start PR1 (Foundation: renderer + theme tokens + parity matrix tests)
notes: RULING (Mike 2026-05-25): D1=b D2=a D3=a D4=a D5=a D6=a D7=a D8=a. D1=b phased PR sequence (5-6 sub-beads chained off rf2-oqa60). D2=a 2-arg mini, fold sentinel routing in, delete inspect-inline. D3=a sentinels become first-class types in new widget, delete theme.data-inspector. D4=a drop public render-id arg (widget auto-generates mount-id). D5=a subsume diff renderer (single source of truth). D6=a popup deferred to later bead. D7=a defer custom-formatters protocol (build closed first). D8=a auto-generated UUID per popup mount.
close_reason: Mike ratified worker's slate (b a a a a a a a) — phased decomposition; rf2-oqa60 unblocked

title: feat(xray): first-class data display widget — roll-your-own CLJS-value renderer, cljs-devtools parity, theme-aware, persistent per-path expansion, multi-surface reusable
description:
## Context

Xray has a recurring need: render an arbitrary CLJS value as a navigable, expandable tree that an operator can explore. Today this surface appears in the App-DB panel, will appear in the Trace panel's per-trace-event detail, will appear in the Subscription panel's per-sub-value inspection, will appear in popup overlays (right-click "inspect this value"), and will appear in any future surface where an operator needs to drill into a CLJS data structure.

The current implementation (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget/` + `data_display/`) attempts to be that primitive, layered on top of `binaryage/cljs-devtools`. The bug history this session shows the layered approach is fragile:

- **rf2-dw8n7** (#2134) — wired click-to-expand on top of cljs-devtools' JSONML; lost per-token colors, replaced the renderer with a custom walker, regressed on multiple axes
- **rf2-oswhk** (#2136) — attempted to restore both colors AND working clicks; partially landed (path-keying for testids), but live probe shows the click→re-render pipeline still doesn't toggle the visible triangle state, and the per-token colour palette is still flat (only keywords visually distinct)

Each fix has layered on an impedance mismatch. The underlying tension is cljs-devtools being a Chrome-console formatter (JSONML, opaque surrogates, global prefs designed for Chrome's expand-on-click behaviour) repurposed as an in-page renderer with its own click semantics, theme palette, and expansion state.

## Goal — a first-class Xray data display widget

Build a reusable, generic CLJS-value-to-hiccup data display component, owned by Xray end-to-end. **Roll our own renderer; drop the cljs-devtools dependency.** Operator preference (session 2026-05-25): the impedance-mismatch cost has exceeded the reuse value; the bug class disappears with a fresh, value-shaped renderer.

The widget MUST be:

- **Themable** via Xray's CSS token system; distinct per-type colours that read well in light AND dark themes (CSS variables, no per-theme code path)
- **Click-to-expand wired correctly** — collapse/expand toggles are real, work at every depth, isolated per node, produce immediate visible response, persist across re-renders
- **Persistent operator focus** across re-renders, epoch scrubs, panel re-mounts, hot-reload — operator's "what's open right now" survives any cause of re-render
- **Multi-surface usable** — App-DB panel, Trace per-event detail, Sub value inspector, Machine snapshot drill-in, popup overlays, future panels
- **Per-call-site isolation** — two instances in the same panel get independent expansion state; one in App-DB and one in a popup don't share state
- **Information-dense** — Xray is shown alongside the app being debugged; screen space is scarce; the widget must pack maximum signal per pixel without sacrificing readability

## First-class design constraint — feature parity with cljs-devtools

The roll-your-own renderer must not be a downgrade. cljs-devtools is the established reference for CLJS data rendering; operators have built mental models around its behaviour. The new widget achieves parity OR betters cljs-devtools on every axis:

### Type detection (the easy half — already in the edge case table)

All scalar / collection / interop types cljs-devtools handles: keywords (qualified + unqualified), symbols, strings, numbers (int / float / BigInt / BigDecimal / NaN / Inf / scientific), booleans, nil, fn (with `:name` metadata surfaced), records (with type tag), atoms / volatiles / refs (with deref), transients, lazy seqs, sorted maps / sorted sets, dates, UUIDs, regex, JS objects / arrays / Promises / Dates / RegExp, multimethods, vars, multimethods.

### Distinguish `()` / `[]` / `#{}` / seq / map-entry visually

cljs-devtools uses different bracket characters; ours must too. A map-entry `[:k :v]` renders distinctly from a 2-element vector `[:k :v]` — same characters, different meaning, different colour for the brackets.

### Inline preview in collapsed-collection summary

cljs-devtools' collapsed view shows `▸ {:a 1, :b 2, …}` (preview of first few entries + ellipsis). Don't render as `▸ Map(3)` — operator wants to see what's INSIDE without expanding.

- Default: show first 3 entries inline up to `max-inline-width`
- If first 3 fit: `▸ {:a 1, :b 2, :c 3}`
- If only some fit: `▸ {:a 1, :b 2, …}`
- If none fit: `▸ {…3 keys}` (fallback)

This preserves the "scan without expanding" UX cljs-devtools enables.

### IMeta surfacing

If a value has metadata, render with a small `^{…}` chip preceding the value, clickable to inspect the metadata. cljs-devtools shows this; we must too.

### `:name` / `:doc` metadata on functions / vars

`(defn ^{:doc "..."} my-fn [...] ...)` renders as `my-fn` (the `:name`) with the `:doc` available on hover. Vars also surface `:doc`.

### Print-level / print-length caps

cljs-devtools respects `*print-level*` / `*print-length*` bounds; depth and width caps stop runaway prints. Our widget has equivalent:

- `max-depth` (default 8) — deeper levels render as `▸ {…}`
- `max-collection-items-inline` (default 5) — inline preview shows first 5; rest as `…`
- `max-collection-items-expanded` (default 100) — expanded view shows first 100; rest as `▸ …N more`

All configurable per call-site; sensible defaults match cljs-devtools' behaviour.

### Custom formatters extension point

cljs-devtools lets users implement `IDevtoolsFormat` on a type for custom rendering. Our widget provides an equivalent: a protocol `IXrayDataDisplay` with methods `(render-header [v opts])` and `(render-body [v opts])`. Users extend it for their own types; the renderer dispatches via `satisfies?` before falling through to generic rendering.

### `pr-str` round-trip parity

Hover tooltip on any value shows its full `pr-str` form. Ctrl-click copy puts `pr-str` form on clipboard. The widget never displays a value that can't be parsed back from its `pr-str`.

### Surrogate-style references for cycles (covered in edge cases)

Already in scope: `▸ <cycle to {existing-path}>` matches cljs-devtools' surrogate approach in spirit.

### Better-than-cljs-devtools features (specific to Xray)

- **Spec 015 sentinels** — `:rf/redacted` and `:rf.size/large-elided` get first-class chrome (cljs-devtools has no equivalent)
- **Per-path expansion persistence** — survives epoch scrub / panel re-mount / hot-reload (cljs-devtools' expansion lives in Chrome console only, not portable)
- **Theme-aware colour tokens** — works in dark mode without per-theme code paths (cljs-devtools' inline rgb values look poor on dark background)
- **Path-clickable navigation** — clicking a key copies the path; right-click context menu (cljs-devtools has no analogue)
- **Width-aware truncation** — respects container width; long strings/values truncated with full value on hover (cljs-devtools assumes infinite console width)

## First-class design constraint — information density

Xray's surfaces are space-constrained. The data display lives in panels that share a screen with the user's app, often in a narrow column or a popup that can't take the whole viewport. Every pixel matters. The widget's defaults must reflect that:

- **No decorative padding** — minimal gaps between rows, no extra margins around collections
- **Tight line-height** — ~1.0 in expanded mode; one line per kv pair as the default
- **Fixed-width font** for alignment of nested structure
- **Inline-where-trivial** — empty maps render as `{}`, single-scalar maps as `{:k :v}` on one line; only collections with >1 element or any non-scalar value get vertical layout
- **Width-aware truncation** — if a rendered line exceeds the container's width, truncate with `…` and surface the full value on hover
- **Compact collapsed summaries** — collapsed collection shows `▸ Map(3)` or `▸ {…3 keys}`, NOT a long string of key previews that overflows
- **No always-on chrome** — borders, backgrounds, hover affordances appear only when relevant; static state is unornamented
- **Vertical guides for nested levels** — thin 1px lines at indent boundaries to keep deep nesting scannable without explicit indent characters consuming space

## Locked design decisions

### Persistence lives in re-frame app-db, not local reagent state

Initially considered local reagent state (less plumbing, simpler). Doesn't work because of persistence requirements:

- **Panel unmount/remount** — operator switches tabs; component re-mounts; local state lost
- **Epoch scrub** — operator scrubs epoch 17→18; panel re-renders against new app-db; local state lost
- **Re-render on app-db change** — operator clicks in the debugged app; panel re-renders; local state lost
- **Hot-reload** — shadow-cljs swaps the component fn; React re-mounts; local state lost

Operator focus is its own piece of state — not the rendered value, not the panel chrome. re-frame's app-db is the right place for state that has to survive these re-render causes. Current implementation already lives there; that's the correct architectural choice.

### The expansion key — drop `render-id`

`data_display/render.cljs:222` defines the toggle event with `expansion-key panel-id render-id path`. If `render-id` is regenerated on each render (likely — fresh UUID per mount or a render counter), dispatch and read use different keys; toggle has no visible effect. **Confirmed live this session**: click handlers fire without exception, but triangle state never changes.

**Lock**: expansion key is `[panel-id mount-id path]`:

- `panel-id` — distinguishes App-DB panel state from Trace panel from popup
- `mount-id` — auto-generated stable id, captured in the widget's form-2 outer let; persists for the lifetime of the mount; distinct per simultaneously-mounted instance
- `path` — vector of keys/indices into the value

`render-id` does NOT belong in the key. Re-renders preserve mount-id; only an actual unmount-then-remount resets it.

### Multi-instance keying via auto-generated mount-id

Two instances of the widget in the same panel (side-by-side before/after diff, popup over panel) need independent expansion state. Caller writes `[data-display {:value v :panel-id p}]`; widget auto-assigns mount-id internally on first render. No caller-side instance-id management.

### Public API

```clj
;; main entry — expandable tree renderer
[xray.data-display/inspect
 {:value <any-cljs-value>           ; required
  :panel-id :rf.xray/app-db          ; required; distinguishes per-panel state
  :path-root []                      ; optional; root path prefix (for popups
                                     ;          opened on a deep sub-value)
  :default-expanded-depth 2          ; optional; how many levels open on first render
  :max-inline-width 60               ; optional; chars before forcing vertical layout
  :on-key-click (fn [path] ...)      ; optional; clicked a key (for breadcrumb nav)
  :on-value-click (fn [path v] ...)  ; optional; clicked a value (for drill-in)
  :on-copy (fn [edn-string] ...)}]   ; optional; ctrl-click / right-click "copy"

;; one-line inline rendering (hover tooltips, log lines, popups when collapsed)
[xray.data-display/mini value]

;; overlay-shaped inspector for context menus / drill-in
[xray.data-display/popup
 {:value <any-cljs-value>
  :anchor <DOM-rect-or-element>
  :panel-id :rf.xray.popup/<id>
  :on-close (fn [] ...)}]
```

## Per-token CSS classes

Closed set; theme-aware via Xray CSS tokens:

| Class | Default colour token | Cljs-devtools equivalent (for memory) |
|---|---|---|
| `.rf-token-kw` | `--rf-xray-token-kw` (magenta light / lavender dark) | `rgb(136, 19, 145)` |
| `.rf-token-kw-ns` | `--rf-xray-token-kw-ns` (kw colour, slightly muted for namespace half) | n/a |
| `.rf-token-num` | `--rf-xray-token-num` (blue) | `rgb(28, 0, 207)` |
| `.rf-token-str` | `--rf-xray-token-str` (red) | `rgb(196, 26, 22)` |
| `.rf-token-bool` | `--rf-xray-token-bool` (teal) | `rgb(0, 153, 153)` |
| `.rf-token-nil` | `--rf-xray-token-nil` (muted gray) | `rgb(128, 128, 128)` |
| `.rf-token-fn` | `--rf-xray-token-fn` (italic gray) | gray italic |
| `.rf-token-symbol` | `--rf-xray-token-symbol` (subtle teal) | n/a |
| `.rf-token-date` | `--rf-xray-token-date` (mauve) | n/a |
| `.rf-token-uuid` | `--rf-xray-token-uuid` (sepia) | n/a |
| `.rf-token-regex` | `--rf-xray-token-regex` (olive) | n/a |
| `.rf-token-redacted` | `--rf-xray-token-redacted` (striped warning yellow) | n/a |
| `.rf-token-elided` | `--rf-xray-token-elided` (italic gray with bracket) | n/a |
| `.rf-collection-delim` | `--rf-xray-text-secondary` | `{` `}` `[` `]` `(` `)` `#{` |
| `.rf-collection-toggle` | `--rf-xray-text-tertiary` | `▾` / `▸` |
| `.rf-collection-count` | `--rf-xray-text-tertiary` (italic small) | `(3 keys)` summary |
| `.rf-indent-guide` | `--rf-xray-border-subtle` (1px vertical line) | indent rail |

## Edge cases — comprehensive

### Data type edge cases

| Type | Render |
|---|---|
| `nil` | `nil` in `.rf-token-nil` |
| `true` / `false` | distinct token colour |
| Empty collections — `{}`, `[]`, `()`, `#{}` | inline, no toggle |
| Single-scalar collections — `{:k :v}`, `[1]` | inline if width permits |
| Long strings (>40 chars) | truncate `"first 30 chars…"`; full value on hover; ctrl-click copies |
| Multi-line strings (`\n` inside) | render with visible `↵` markers OR expand to code-block view on toggle |
| Strings with escape chars / tabs / unicode | render with `pr-str` semantics (escapes visible) |
| Negative numbers | same colour as positive |
| Very large numbers (>1e15) | scientific notation `1.23e15`; full value in hover |
| Floats with precision noise — `0.1+0.2 = 0.30000000000000004` | display as-is (truthful); operator can opt into rounded display via panel setting |
| `js/Number.NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity` | render as `##NaN`, `##Inf`, `##-Inf` (CLJS canonical) |
| BigInt / BigDecimal | `N` / `M` suffix preserved |
| Qualified keywords (`:my-ns/foo`) | `:my-ns` in `.rf-token-kw-ns` muted, `/foo` in `.rf-token-kw` |
| Symbols (`'foo`, `'my-ns/foo`) | distinct from keywords; `.rf-token-symbol` |
| Vars (`#'my-ns/my-fn`) | render with `#'` prefix |
| Functions (`(fn [...])`) | `fn` italic; if `:name` metadata, `(fn foo …)` |
| Multimethods | `#multi[<dispatch-fn-name>]` |
| Atoms / Volatiles / Refs | `#atom{<deref>}` — derefs cautiously; never throws on non-derefable |
| Transient collections | `#tx{…}` placeholder; never iterate |
| Lazy seqs | take + 1 to detect remainder; `(1 2 3 …)` for infinite |
| Sorted maps / sorted sets | preserve order; no sorting/normalisation |
| Records — `(defrecord MyRec [a b])` | `#user.MyRec{:a 1 :b 2}` |
| Date — `#inst "2026-05-25T..."` | `#inst "2026-05-25T17:30:00Z"`; locale-aware in tooltip |
| UUID — `#uuid "abc..."` | distinct token colour; truncate to first 8 chars on narrow widths |
| Regex — `#"..."` | distinct token colour; escape internal `"` |
| JS objects | `#object[<constructor-name>]`; if has interpretable shape, click expands to `js->clj` view |
| JS arrays | distinct from CLJS vectors; `#js[1 2 3]` |
| Promises | `#Promise[<state>]` — never await |
| React elements | `#react/element[<type>]` placeholder; NEVER recurse |
| HTML DOM elements | `#dom[<tagName>]` placeholder; NEVER recurse |
| Maps with mixed key types (keywords + strings + numbers + records) | render each key with its own token colour; alignment preserved |
| Maps with very long keys | truncate key on display; full key in hover; clicking key copies it |
| Maps with namespaced sentinel keys (`:rf.size/large-elided`, `:rf/redacted`) | special chrome per Spec 015 |

### Cycle / depth / size edge cases

- **Cycles** — visited-set walker keyed on identity (`identical?`); when a value is encountered whose identity is already on the path-stack, render `▸ <cycle to {existing-path-as-string}>`
- **Max depth** — configurable cap (default 8); deeper levels render as `▸ {…}` collapsed; clicking expands one level (re-uses the expansion mechanism)
- **Very wide maps** (>100 keys) — render only first N keys; surface `▸ {…N more keys}` at bottom; clicking expands the next slice
- **Very wide vectors** (>1000 elements) — render first N + `▸ …M more` summary at end; opt-in to "show all" via setting
- **Very large strings** (>1KB) — NEVER inline in full; show first 30 chars + `(NkB total)` summary; click expands to popup with the full value
- **Spec 015 `:rf.size/large-elided`** — render the marker chrome with `[fetch]` button that dispatches `:rf.xray.data-display/fetch-elided` for the un-elided value
- **Spec 015 `:rf/redacted`** — striped warning-yellow chrome; non-clickable (cannot reveal); on hover, tooltip explains the redaction policy

### Display edge cases (information-density driven)

- **Width measurement** — measure rendered width per row; if exceeds container, truncate that row only (other rows unaffected); display ellipsis affordance; full value on hover
- **Inline vs vertical decision** — at each collection-render, calculate "would this fit on one line within available width?" if yes, inline; if no, vertical with each element on its own row
- **Indent depth without indent chars** — use CSS `padding-left` proportional to depth + thin vertical guide lines (`.rf-indent-guide`); no `  ` whitespace consumption
- **Key alignment in maps** — when rendering map vertically, longest key sets the column for values; align values column-style for scanability
- **Comma elision** — vertical-rendered maps elide trailing commas (cleaner); inline maps keep them
- **Multi-row hover** — hovering a row highlights just that row (subtle bg), not the whole collection
- **Theme switch** — colour tokens flip via CSS variables; no React re-render needed
- **Font size respects panel density setting** — when Xray's density is "cosy" use larger font; "compact" smaller; configurable via `--rf-xray-token-font-size`

### Interaction edge cases

| Gesture | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Click triangle | toggle just that node |
| Click triangle while text-selecting | DO NOT toggle (detect mousedown→mouseup-without-movement; if movement, treat as selection start) |
| Shift-click triangle | expand entire subtree (recursive open) |
| Alt-click triangle | collapse this node AND all siblings at this level |
| Ctrl/Cmd-click value | copy the value's EDN to clipboard; flash brief "copied" affordance |
| Ctrl/Cmd-click key | copy the path to the key (e.g. `[:counter :value]`) |
| Right-click | context menu — copy value, copy path, copy as JSON, expand-all, collapse-all, "open in popup" |
| Double-click value | open the value in a popup (full-screen-ish inspector) |
| Hover row >500ms | tooltip with full (un-truncated) value if row was truncated |
| Tab navigation | focusable order: triangles → keys → values; each focusable; visible focus ring |
| Space / Enter on focused triangle | toggle (same as click) |
| Arrow keys with focus | navigate (up/down between rows; left collapses, right expands) |
| Type-ahead while focused | jump to first key matching the typed prefix |
| Drag-select multi-row | preserve native text selection; do NOT trigger toggles |

### State edge cases

- **Value shape change** (was a map, now a vector at same path) — preserve expansion state silently; paths that don't resolve in the new value have no effect; if value reverts, prior expansion re-activates
- **Empty/nil value** — render `nil` distinctly; no triangle (nothing to expand)
- **Initial render** — `default-expanded-depth` controls how many levels are open on first sight; once operator interacts, their explicit toggles override default
- **Hot-reload preserves expansion** — re-frame state survives source reload; verify the widget reads from the same slot post-reload
- **Theme switch mid-render** — CSS variable change; no React re-render needed; colours update immediately
- **Many simultaneous instances** (e.g. popup + panel + another popup all open at once) — each independent; no state collisions; closing one doesn't affect others

### Popup-specific edge cases

- **Anchor visibility** — popup positions relative to its anchor; if anchor scrolls out of view, popup follows OR closes (configurable)
- **Multiple popups** — stack with z-index; each its own independent expansion state; closing the topmost doesn't affect others
- **Popup vs panel state** — independent (`:panel-id` differs); never share
- **Close gesture** — Esc closes; click-outside closes; explicit close button
- **Expansion retention on close** — closing a popup retains its expansion state in app-db; re-opening with same `:panel-id` restores it. Operator can opt-in to "forget on close" via the popup props.
- **Popup over a popup** — third nested popup, etc., works without interference

### Accessibility edge cases

- **Triangles have `role="button"` + `aria-expanded` true/false** so screen readers announce state
- **Focus visible** at every focusable level
- **Screen reader announces** "<key> = <value-summary>, expanded" / "collapsed"
- **Keyboard-only navigation** is fully functional (no mouse-only paths)
- **Color contrast** in both themes meets WCAG AA for all token classes
- **`prefers-reduced-motion`** — disable expand/collapse animations

### Performance edge cases

- **Wide data (1000+ keys)** — virtualize rendered rows (only render visible + small overscan); state held for all paths regardless
- **Deep data (50+ levels)** — depth cap at default 8; click-to-deepen for further
- **Many cycles** — visited-set walk bounded; never infinite
- **Many expansion entries** — see "open question" below on GC
- **Fast re-renders** (operator scrubbing epochs rapidly) — render fn must be O(visible-rows), not O(value-size)

### Test edge cases

For the visual regression test suite:

- Click ONE triangle, assert exactly one DOM node changed (others unchanged)
- Click expand, then scrub epoch, assert expansion preserved
- Click expand, then close panel, reopen, assert expansion preserved
- Two simultaneous instances, click in one, assert other unchanged
- Theme switch, assert all token colours update without re-render
- Long string, assert truncation + hover-full
- Cycle in value, assert no infinite render
- Deeply nested value, assert depth-cap respected
- Value shape change at expanded path, assert no error + graceful render

## What goes away (post-implementation)

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget/cljs_devtools_render.cljs` — delete
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget/widget.cljs` — replace body; keep public fn names (`inspect`, `inspect-inline`, `browse`, `mini`) so existing call sites don't churn
- `binaryage/cljs-devtools` from `implementation/deps.edn:185` — drop the dep; nothing else in Xray uses it
- `xray-prefs` / `with-prefs*` / `with-expanded-prefs` / JSONML walker — gone
- `data_display/render.cljs` — heavily refactored; keep the toggle event/sub plumbing but simplify the key matrix per "Lock" above

After this lands, the impedance-mismatch bug class disappears. Future bugs in the widget become bugs in OUR code, debuggable in CLJS without translating JSONML edge cases.

## Open question (worker-decidable, default specified)

**Expansion-state garbage collection.** As the operator explores many epochs and many app-dbs, the expansion-state slot grows monotonically. Strategies:

- **Default: bounded LRU at 500 entries** — keep last 500 expanded paths; older evict. Simple. Operator's deep history slowly forgets itself but never grows unboundedly.
- Alt: reachability sweep on epoch boundary (drop entries whose path doesn't resolve in the current value). More work; preserves "everything reachable stays".
- Alt: never gc (accept unbounded growth; typical session has dozens of expansions, not thousands).

Worker picks based on a one-paragraph rationale in the PR; default is bounded LRU at 500.

## Acceptance

For each surface using the widget:

1. Click ▾ → that ONE node collapses to ▸; all siblings unchanged
2. Click ▸ → that ONE node re-expands; siblings unchanged
3. Scrub to different epoch → panel re-renders with new value; expansion state at common paths preserved
4. Switch tabs and return → panel re-mounts; expansion state preserved
5. Open popup of different value → independent expansion state; no interference
6. Each value type renders with its distinct theme-aware colour (per the token table above)
7. In dark theme, all colours meet WCAG AA contrast; theme switch flips colours immediately (CSS variable, no re-render)
8. Spec 015 sentinels render with distinctive chrome (`:rf/redacted` warning-yellow striped; `:rf.size/large-elided` with `[fetch]`)
9. Deeply nested values respect default-expanded-depth
10. Width-aware truncation works on every value type; full value visible on hover
11. Expansion-state slot bounded (see GC strategy)
12. All 13 interaction gestures (table above) behave per spec
13. Accessibility — keyboard-only navigation works end-to-end; screen reader announces state

Plus visual regression tests (Playwright) for each panel using the widget, covering at least the test-edge-case list above.

## References

- Bug history this round: rf2-dw8n7 (#2134), rf2-oswhk (#2136), and the still-broken click-pipeline traced live this session 2026-05-25
- Live-probe evidence from session 2026-05-25 — click handlers verified real (React `__reactProps$.onClick`); dispatch fires; visible state never changes; confirms keying-mismatch hypothesis
- Existing implementation to replace: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget/` + `data_display/render.cljs`
- Reference impl for click-handler layering (not the renderer; we're rolling our own): re-frame-10x's `src/day8/re_frame_10x/components/cljs_devtools.cljs`
- Spec 015 sentinel types: `:rf/redacted`, `:rf.size/large-elided`
- Xray theme tokens (existing): `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/theme/tokens.cljs`
- Operator preferences this session: roll-your-own renderer (drop cljs-devtools dep), info-density first-class constraint, persistence via re-frame app-db, minimal worker-decidable open questions
notes: STOP — surfaced 8 design points via decision bead rf2-sndui. Worker awaiting Mike's call on decomposition, mini API, sentinel chrome, expansion key, diff renderer, popup mount, custom-formatters protocol, popup id convention. Worktree data-display-widget-rf2-oqa60 / branch worker/data-display-widget-rf2-oqa60 stays parked.
close_reason: Phase 1 shipped in PR #2143 — first-class data-display widget core + App-DB integration; cljs-devtools dep dropped. Follow-on phases 2-7 (rf2-hhtbl, rf2-e46qs, rf2-lxvn6, rf2-q3dzw, rf2-s0x6x, rf2-0qrcr) filed and chained.

title: decision(xray): six design points to unblock trace_bus retire (rf2-43koh)
description:
6 design decisions required to unblock rf2-43koh (retire `tools/xray/src/.../trace_bus.cljc`). Surfaced from an exploratory pass at the refactor on 2026-05-25.

The refactor is FEASIBLE and the framework's per-frame rings provide a credible substrate. But six axes are operator/UX visible or shape the architecture in load-bearing ways and benefit from Mike's call before the worker rewires the 60+ files.

## D1 — Settings buffer-depth UX unit change

`day8.re-frame2-xray.config/default-settings` carries `:buffer/trace-buffer/keep` defaulting to `1000` (events). The Settings popup → Buffer tab exposes it (rf2-ttnst). Post-retire the framework's `(rf/configure :trace-buffer {:cascades-retained N})` is the only knob and the UNIT is cascades not events (default 50).

Options:
  (a) Rename the slot `:buffer/cascades-retained`, default `50`, write through to `(rf/configure :trace-buffer ...)`. Operator-facing UI label changes from "Trace events to retain" → "Cascades to retain".
  (b) Keep `:trace-buffer/keep` as the label, change its semantics to cascades, default `50`.
  (c) Compute an event-equivalent ratio (avg ~10 events/cascade) and offer both knobs.

Recommendation: (a) — clean rename, cascade-unit honesty, matches Spec 009 vocabulary.

## D2 — Frameless-events behavioural change (B3 ruling impact)

Per spec/009 §Per-frame trace rings, frameless emits (no `:rf.trace/dispatch-id` in scope) SKIP the per-frame rings (B3 ruling, rf2-g1b2m). They stream live to listeners only. Xray's separate ring captured them and `group-cascades` buckets them under `:ungrouped` (registry-time emits, REPL evals, SSR hydration, frame lifecycle outside a drain).

The opt-in `:show-ungrouped?` toggle (rf2-r9lyy / settings default OFF) renders the `:ungrouped` bucket when on.

Options:
  (a) Keep a small frameless-only secondary buffer in Xray (a 100-event ring at the listener boundary) to back the `:show-ungrouped?` UX. Defeats "drop the separate ring" simplification partially but preserves the UX.
  (b) Drop frameless events from Xray entirely. The `:show-ungrouped?` toggle becomes a no-op or is removed.
  (c) Other shape (e.g. a per-frame `:ungrouped` synthetic bucket — but frameless events have NO frame by definition).

Recommendation: (a) — the `:show-ungrouped?` UX is genuinely useful for SSR / REPL / registry-time debugging and is silent-by-default; preserving it with a 100-event ring is cheap relative to the 1000-event ring we're shedding.

## D3 — Parallel-frames E2E coalescing-contract reshape (rf2-wq6gx)

The E2E test (`tools/xray/test/.../panels_e2e/parallel_frames_e2e_cljs_test.cljs`) drives Xray's reactive trace surface via:

  (rf/dispatch-sync [:rf.xray/sync-trace-buffer (trace-bus/buffer)])

after each host dispatch. Post-retire that handler vanishes and the sync target changes from "flat event vector" to "per-frame snapshot `{frame-id -> cascade-vector}`".

Options:
  (a) Drop the explicit sync entirely in tests; rely on a new `:rf.xray/refresh-trace-rings` helper that snapshots `(rf/trace-buffer fid)` over `(rf/frame-ids)` and writes the snapshot to Xray's app-db.
  (b) The new helper IS the production reactive surface (listener-driven microtask); tests just need a synchronous `(refresh-trace-rings-sync!)` entrypoint that bypasses the microtask.

Recommendation: (b) — the production path stays microtask-coalesced; tests get a sync entrypoint. Worker designs that helper.

## D4 — Self-noise predicates re-homing target ns

Today `xray-internal-event?`, `xray-internal-event-id?`, `xray-internal-cascade?` live in `trace_bus.cljc`. Pure data; load-bearing for filtering Xray's own machinery out of the cascade list (rf2-xs8vu + rf2-g1pt8).

Options:
  (a) New file `tools/xray/src/.../self_noise.cljc` — small, single-purpose, JVM-runnable.
  (b) Fold into `tools/xray/src/.../filters/hidden.cljc` — neighbours conceptually.
  (c) Fold into `tools/xray/src/.../filters.cljs` — main filter ns.

Recommendation: (a) — cohesive, named for its job, JVM-testable as today.

## D5 — Privacy gate re-homing target ns

Today the listener body (`collect-trace!`) is in `trace_bus.cljc`. It does: self-noise drop → privacy gate (`:sensitive?` + counter bump) → ring push → mirror-sync request. Post-retire the ring push and atom-mirror disappear; what remains is the listener body + privacy + self-noise + microtask sync of framework rings into app-db.

Options:
  (a) New file `tools/xray/src/.../trace_collector.cljs` (CLJS-only; CLJC tests for the privacy gate routed through `config.cljc` which is already CLJC).
  (b) Fold into `preload.cljs` (where the listener is registered).
  (c) New file `tools/xray/src/.../collector.cljc` + a `collector_cljs.cljs` for the microtask + dispatch sides.

Recommendation: (a) — discoverable by name, parallel to `preload.cljs`.

## D6 — Spec 013 retire vs rewrite

`tools/xray/spec/013-Trace-Bus.md` (~530 lines) documents the SEPARATE-ring rationale. Post-retire the rationale is obsolete.

Options:
  (a) RETIRE: delete the file, add a redirect note in `tools/xray/spec/README.md` pointing at `spec/009-Instrumentation.md §Per-frame trace rings`. The privacy gate + self-noise + reactive mirror move under `tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md` or a new `014-Trace-Consumer.md`.
  (b) REWRITE: keep 013 as the Xray-side consumer contract — privacy gate (counter-bump for redacted indicator), self-noise (cross-cutting `:rf.xray/*` events that slip past frame-no-emit), coalesced mirror into app-db (rf2-wq6gx). The "separate ring rationale" §§ are deleted; the consumer-side contract stays.

Recommendation: (b) REWRITE — the privacy counter, self-noise predicates, and microtask reactive surface ARE Xray-specific consumer contracts; spec 013 is the right home. Title becomes `013-Trace-Consumer.md`.

## Scope of follow-on work once Mike rules

Worker estimated 1-2 days of careful CLJS work + tests + spec. UX via 100-event secondary ring at listener boundary. D3: production stays microtask-coalesced; tests get sync entrypoint helper. D4: new self_noise.cljc. D5: new trace_collector.cljs.
