title: fix(xray): rf2-dw8n7 regressed — clicks don't collapse + lost cljs-devtools per-token colors (renderer was replaced instead of wrapped)
description:
## Symptom

After rf2-dw8n7 (#2134) merged claiming "app-db panel triangles click-to-expand wired (re-frame-10x parity)", the actual rendered behaviour regressed on two axes:

1. **Click-to-collapse is BROKEN** — every collection renders fully-expanded by default. Clicking any ▾ triangle does NOTHING (text content does not change). The triangles look interactive (cursor pointer, onclick attribute present) but the click has no effect.
2. **Per-token syntax highlighting LOST** — before rf2-dw8n7, cljs-devtools' canonical color palette was applied (magenta keywords, blue numbers, red strings, teal booleans, gray nil). After rf2-dw8n7, only keywords are distinct (accent color + dotted underline as a "clickable" affordance); numbers, strings, nil, and booleans ALL render in the same `--rf-xray-text-primary` color — no per-token-type distinction.

Plus a cosmetic regression — commas between key-value pairs are gone. The collection display reads as `{:counter ▾{:value 0:last-clicked nil:show-parity? true:threshold 5}}` instead of the prior `{:counter ▾{:value 0, :last-clicked nil, :show-parity? true, :threshold 5}}`.

## Diagnosis (live eval-cljs probes, 2026-05-25)

### Click-to-collapse broken

```clj
;; Trigger a click on the first ▾ triangle and watch for content change
(let [panel (.querySelector js/document "#rf-xray-tabpanel-app-db")
      first-triangle (some #(when (#{"▾" "▼"} (.-textContent %)) %)
                           (array-seq (.querySelectorAll panel "span")))
      text-before (.-textContent panel)]
  (.click first-triangle)
  ;; ... 200ms later ...
  {:text-changed? (not= text-before (.-textContent panel))})
;; → {:text-changed? false}
```

11 ▾ triangles in the DOM, 0 ▸ (collapsed) — everything renders expanded. First triangle has `cursor: pointer`, `onclick-present: true`. Click fires (verified via .click()), but the rendered text is identical 200ms later. State isn't being toggled, OR is being toggled but the view doesn't re-render against the new state, OR the toggle re-toggles itself.

### Per-token color regression

Probed style attribute for each scalar type:

| Token | Before rf2-dw8n7 | After rf2-dw8n7 |
|---|---|---|
| `:counter` (keyword) | `color: rgb(136, 19, 145)` | `color: var(--rf-xray-accent)` + dotted underline |
| `:value` (keyword) | `color: rgb(136, 19, 145)` | `color: var(--rf-xray-accent)` + dotted underline |
| `0` (integer) | `color: rgb(28, 0, 207)` | `color: var(--rf-xray-text-primary)` |
| `5` (integer) | `color: rgb(28, 0, 207)` | `color: var(--rf-xray-text-primary)` |
| `""` (string) | `color: rgb(196, 26, 22)` | `color: var(--rf-xray-text-primary)` |
| `nil` | `color: rgb(128, 128, 128)` | `color: var(--rf-xray-text-primary)` |
| `true` (boolean) | `color: rgb(0, 153, 153)` | `color: var(--rf-xray-text-primary)` |

Keywords got a CLICKABLE affordance (accent + underline) but lost their cljs-devtools magenta. Every other scalar type collapsed to a single neutral color. The visual distinction between data types is gone.

## What the rf2-dw8n7 fix appears to have done wrong

Bead rf2-dw8n7's recommended approach was to **layer an interactive click-to-expand wrapper ON TOP of cljs-devtools' JSONML walker** — matching re-frame-10x's `simple-render-with-path-annotations` + `jsonml->hiccup-with-path-annotations` pattern. cljs-devtools keeps doing the leaf-level formatting (colors, type detection); the wrapper adds:

- Click handler on each `object` surrogate's ▸ button → dispatches `[::toggle-expansion path]`
- Expanded-paths state in app-db; sub keyed on path
- Re-render when expanded-paths changes, swapping the collapsed header for the recursively-walked body

The actual implementation appears to have **replaced** cljs-devtools' rendering entirely with a custom hand-rolled walker. The custom walker:
- Renders fully-expanded by default (no expansion state machine to toggle against)
- Uses one accent color for keywords, one text-primary color for everything else (lost cljs-devtools' per-type palette)
- Drops collection-element separators
- Attaches onclick handlers to triangles as decoration; nothing for them to toggle

The naming convention used (`▾` for "expanded") suggests the intent was right; the implementation diverged from the re-frame-10x pattern referenced in the bead body.

## Fix direction

Revert the renderer swap. Restore cljs-devtools as the leaf formatter (color palette, scalar token distinction, collection delimiters) and layer the interactive wrapper on top per re-frame-10x's pattern:

```clj
;; re-frame-10x's actual pattern (from src/day8/re_frame_10x/components/cljs_devtools.cljs)
[:span {:class    (toggle-style :bright)
        :on-click #(do (rf/dispatch [::app-db.events/toggle-expansion indexed-path])
                       (rf/dispatch [::app-db.events/expand {:id path-id :expand? false}]))}
 [:button
  (if show-body?
    [material/arrow-drop-down]   ; ▼ when expanded
    [material/arrow-right])]]    ; ▶ when collapsed
```

The walker traverses cljs-devtools' JSONML output and:
- For each "object" surrogate → replaces the ▸ with the interactive span+button above
- For each leaf → renders cljs-devtools' span + style verbatim (preserves colors)
- On click → dispatches toggle-expansion event; re-frame app-db slot tracks per-path expansion state; subscribed sub re-renders the affected node with body shown/hidden

Default expansion strategy is debatable; re-frame-10x defaults to "show one level expanded, deeper collapsed" — operator can debate that vs. always-expanded vs. always-collapsed. But that's a UX choice independent of the regression.

## Acceptance

1. Each scalar type renders with its cljs-devtools color (keyword magenta, number blue, string red, boolean teal, nil gray)
2. Triangle click TOGGLES the corresponding node — ▼ becomes ▶ AND the body collapses to a one-line header summary; clicking ▶ re-expands
3. Collection elements have visible separators (commas + spaces between key-value pairs)
4. State persists across re-renders within the same panel mount

Visual regression test that asserts each of those would catch the current state.

## Probes (paste into eval-cljs)

```clj
;; Verify click is bound but produces no change
(let [panel (.querySelector js/document "#rf-xray-tabpanel-app-db")
      first-arrow (some #(when (#{"▾" "▼" "▸" "▶"} (.-textContent %)) %)
                        (array-seq (.querySelectorAll panel "span")))
      before (.-textContent panel)]
  (.click first-arrow)
  (js/setTimeout
    #(set! (.-__probe js/window)
           {:before-snippet (subs before 0 100)
            :after-snippet  (subs (.-textContent panel) 0 100)
            :changed?       (not= before (.-textContent panel))})
    100)
  :kicked)

;; Then re-eval to read the result
(.-__probe js/window)
```

## References

- Cause: rf2-dw8n7 (#2134) — intended to wire click-to-expand; instead replaced cljs-devtools with custom walker
- Reference impl to restore: re-frame-10x's `src/day8/re_frame_10x/components/cljs_devtools.cljs` (`simple-render-with-path-annotations` + `jsonml->hiccup-with-path-annotations`)
- Xray widget source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget/widget.cljs` + `cljs_devtools_render.cljs`
- Discovery: pair-debug session 2026-05-25 — operator reported "all the trees are expanded now but the collapse triangle not working" and "Not much in the way of syntax highlighting"
close_reason: #2136 — two distinct walker bugs fixed: (1) sibling surrogates shared :path [] → identical testids → triangles toggled together (root cause of 'clicks do nothing'); (2) expanded render emitted HEADER + BODY together → grey {…} ellipsis ghost was the 'lost colors' optical illusion. Fix mirrors re-frame-10x's data-structure-with-path-annotations: positional child-index appended to :path; render-object-interactive renders BODY-when-expanded XOR HEADER-when-collapsed. cljs-devtools per-token palette preserved end-to-end. +spec/021 §10.0a acceptance contract pinned.

title: fix(trace): per-frame trace rings sized by CASCADE count (not trace-event count) — eliminates sub-skip flood evicting real events
description:
## Symptom

Step-deck app, navigate to the Machine tab in the testbed, click "connect". All events in the Xray events list IMMEDIATELY DISAPPEAR — the list shows "No events." despite the underlying machine state having transitioned successfully and the per-frame :step-deck epoch-history still containing all the events.

The user must reload to see events again, and the cycle repeats: events accumulate, one Machine-tab click wipes them.

## Diagnosis (live eval-cljs probes, 2026-05-25)

Layer-by-layer trace through Xray's events-list pipeline:

| Layer | Sub | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Source :step-deck epoch-history | (re-frame.core/epoch-history :step-deck) | 11 epochs (initialise, connection, navigate, inc, …) — REAL events captured |
| Global trace bus | (re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer) | **200 events, ALL :operation :skip :op-type :rf.sub** |
| :rf.xray/trace-buffer sub | (get db :trace-buffer) or fallback to bus | from :rf/xray → 1000 entries, all :operation :skip |
| :rf.xray/cascades sub | groups buffer via projection/group-cascades, removes xray-internal | 1 cascade (:ungrouped) — no real cascades survive grouping |
| :rf.xray/filtered-cascades sub | filters by frame + filters + mutes | 0 cascades visible |
| L2 list render (shell.cljs:1851) | (if (empty? event-cascades) "No events." …) | **"No events." branch** |

## Root cause — trace ring is sized by trace-event count, but trace events ride at WILDLY uneven rates

Re-frame2 emits `{:operation :skip :op-type :rf.sub :reason "input-value-equal"}` whenever a subscription's recompute short-circuits because its inputs didn't change. These short-circuit signals are USEFUL DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT — performance work ("which subs are actually recomputing?"), invalidation chasing ("why isn't my view updating?") both depend on them. They must keep being emitted.

But the trace bus is a **single global ring buffer sized by trace-event count** (200 deep). When the user opens the Machine tab, Xray's machine inspector subscribes to many subs (`:machine-definitions`, `:machine-scrubber-position`, `:registered-machines`, etc.). On every app-db write, re-frame's reactive chain re-fires those subs. Most short-circuit and emit a `:skip` trace.

Clicking "connect" cascades through the :ws/connection machine's transitions (entry actions, `:after` timers, parent-level fallbacks). One single cascade can produce hundreds of trace events (real `:dispatched` / `:run-start` / `:db-changed` / `:run-end` PLUS dozens to hundreds of sub `:skip` traces from Xray's inspector). The 200-deep global ring fills within a handful of microtask cycles. Real events from EARLIER cascades get evicted by FIFO before the events list reads them.

The architectural problem: the ring's UNIT of retention is the trace event, not the cascade. A single high-volume cascade can evict every other cascade's traces — including their own real events.

## The architectural mismatch

Everything else in re-frame2 is per-frame:

- **app-db** — each frame owns its own
- **epoch-history** — per-frame ring of assembled :rf/epoch-record
- **subscription computations** — each sub runs in a frame's reactive context, against that frame's app-db
- **fx / cofx routing** — frame-aware

The **trace bus is the odd one out** — single global ring sized by raw trace-event count. Tools that mount in their own frame (Xray, re-frame2-pair-mcp, story-mcp, any future inspector) emit trace events that pollute every other consumer's view. This bug is one instance; the class is broader.

## Proposed primary fix — per-frame trace, sized by CASCADE count, not trace-event count

Two structural changes that compose:

### 1. Per-frame trace rings

Each frame owns its own trace ring (configurable depth, default 50 cascades). Trace events emitted while a frame's reactive chain is running go to that frame's ring. Joins the existing per-frame model.

**Per-frame is first-class, not an edge case.** A typical session has multiple frames coexisting:

- `:rf/xray` — the inspector's own frame (heavy sub-recompute volume, mostly diagnostic)
- the **app frame** being debugged (`:step-deck` here; whatever the consumer app uses)
- in two-frame isolation testbeds, parallel-frame demos, story variants, SSR slots — N additional app/test frames simultaneously on the page

Each gets its own independent ring. Each can be sized independently via frame metadata — `:rf/xray` might want 200 cascades to support deep diagnostic walks; an app frame defaults to 50; a transient story-variant frame might want only 10. The current single-global-ring design forces them all to share, with the loudest one winning. Per-frame storage gives each one its own budget.

### 2. Ring unit is the cascade, not the individual trace event

Each ring holds the N most recent **cascades** (dispatch-id is the unit). For each retained cascade, ALL its associated trace events are retained too — every `:run-start`, `:db-changed`, `:run-end`, every sub `:skip` and `:recomputed`, every fx/cofx run. When cascade #N+1 arrives, the OLDEST cascade (and all its associated traces) is evicted as a unit.

Operationally:
- Default: 50 cascades per frame retained, with their full associated trace
- Memory predictable from the operator's perspective ("I keep the last 50 events I dispatched")
- A burst of `:skip` emits in cascade X can never evict cascade Y's data — eviction operates on the cascade boundary
- Cascade with 1000 trace events takes 1 slot; cascade with 5 trace events also takes 1 slot

### How this fixes the reported bug

- Xray's machine-tab inspector subs run in `:rf/xray` → their `:skip` traces go to `:rf/xray`'s ring → don't touch `:step-deck`'s ring at all
- `:step-deck`'s ring keeps the last 50 cascades' traces including the connect cascade and its predecessors
- Events list reads `:step-deck`'s ring → real events visible
- Sub-skip signal preserved in `:rf/xray`'s ring (and in `:step-deck`'s ring for subs that ran during step-deck cascades) — observable wherever it belongs

## Why cascade-keyed retention is the right unit

- **Matches operator mental model** — operators think "I want to see the last 50 events"; the storage matches the unit they think in
- **Predictable retention** — a chatty sub never silently evicts the cascade you care about; only NEWER cascades push out OLDER cascades
- **Naturally bounds skip noise** — sub-skip emits stay associated with their parent cascade; the burst lives or dies as a unit with the rest of that cascade's traces
- **Aligns with epoch-history** — epoch-history is already retained per-cascade (assembled `:rf/epoch-record` per dispatch). The trace ring becomes the "diagnostic detail of the same 50 epochs", consistent retention semantic
- **No per-trace-type tuning needed** — no need to special-case skip vs recompute vs fx vs anything. Eviction is cascade-driven; trace volume per cascade is incidental

## The retention contract

- **One configurable knob per frame**: `:rf.trace/cascades-retained` (default 50)
- **ALL trace events associated with retained cascades are retained** — no per-cascade trace cap, no per-trace-type cap, no other knobs
- A cascade with 5 traces and a cascade with 50,000 traces each occupy one slot
- When cascade #N+1 arrives, the OLDEST cascade (and every trace event ever emitted under it) is dropped as a unit

This is the entire retention surface. Predictable, simple, matches operator mental model ("I want to see my last 50 events with full detail"). No worst-case memory bound on a single cascade's trace volume by design — if a cascade emits 100K traces, that cascade's slot holds 100K traces. The operator's tradeoff is in the cascade-count knob, not in trace-volume bounding.

## Locked design decisions

### Cross-frame cascades — N/A by design

Frames are isolation boundaries, not communicating agents. Re-frame2 does not support one frame dispatching into another (Xray observes other frames via Tool-Pair read APIs; it does not dispatch into them). There is no cross-frame cascade routing question. Every cascade lives in exactly one frame.

### Frameless trace events → dedicated `:rf/global` ring

Rare but real (registration-time emits like `:handler-replaced` / `:registration-collision`, init/configure lifecycle, schema-validation warnings, REPL probes outside any dispatch). They go to a dedicated `:rf/global` ring, cascade-count-sized just like the per-frame rings (default 50). They have no `:dispatch-id` so each one occupies one ring slot directly. Tools that care about app behaviour ignore `:rf/global`; tools that care about registration drift / hot-reload diagnostics read it.

### In-process API — `(trace-buffer frame-id)` returns raw trace events

`re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer` becomes a per-frame fn: `(trace-buffer frame-id)` returns the raw trace-event vector for that frame in emit order. Consumers that want cascade bundles group by `:dispatch-id` themselves — same code they already write. Smallest semantic change to existing callers; pure storage swap behind a familiar shape.

Existing zero-arg `(trace-buffer)` callers are updated to `(trace-buffer :rf/default)` (or similar default) — straightforward find-and-replace; not a back-compat-preserved zero-arg form, since the storage model genuinely changed.

### Off-box streaming wire — cascade bundles by default

`re-frame2-pair-mcp`'s `trace-window` / `watch-epochs` / `subscribe` deliver complete cascade bundles per stream tick. Matches the new storage model semantically; consumers get full cascade context atomically rather than reconstructing from individual events. Bigger items per tick but the unit matches the operator's mental model ("one cascade per row").

This DIFFERS from the in-process API (which returns raw events) because the streaming consumers are off-box (LLM agents, monitoring tools) where bundle-per-tick is the better default; the in-process surface stays closer to today's shape because existing callers can group when they want and incur no surprise.

## Probes (paste into eval-cljs)

```clj
;; Reveals the ring is all skips
(let [g (re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer)
      ops (frequencies (map :operation g))]
  {:total (count g) :by-operation ops})
;; → {:total 200 :by-operation {:skip 200}}

;; Confirms real epochs ARE captured by source frame
(count (re-frame.core/epoch-history :step-deck))
;; → 11

;; The smoking gun — sub diverges between frames
(let [from-default @(re-frame.core/subscribe [:rf.xray/cascades])
      from-xray (re-frame.core/with-frame :rf/xray
                  @(re-frame.core/subscribe [:rf.xray/cascades]))]
  {:default (count from-default)   ; → 7 (sees real cascades)
   :xray    (count from-xray)})    ; → 1 (only :ungrouped — Xray's mirror is polluted)
```

## Acceptance

- User opens step-deck Machine tab, clicks "connect", sees the new event APPEAR in the events list. Repeated machine-tab actions never wipe the list.
- After 50 user actions, the events list shows the most recent 50, with full trace detail (run-start, db-changed, run-end, all sub-skips, fx) available for each.
- Sub-skip signals remain observable for performance debugging — visible in the trace surface for whichever cascade they ran in.

## What was considered + rejected

### Rejected — "Don't emit sub-skip trace events at all"

Sub short-circuiting is useful diagnostic signal (performance work, invalidation chasing). The fix must preserve the emit; per-frame + cascade-keyed retention preserves it by routing to the right frame's ring and bundling with its parent cascade.

### Rejected — "Filter `:skip` at Xray's consumer level"

Doesn't work — by the time Xray's collector reads the global ring, the real events are already evicted. Filter-at-read is too late. The fix has to happen at INGEST or at the storage-partition level.

### Rejected — "Bigger flat ring (10× the default)"

Procrastinates the architectural mismatch without fixing it. A bigger ring still gets pollulated by tool-frame traces; still has no eviction semantic that respects cascade boundaries; still requires per-tool tuning as apps grow.

## References

- Probe results: pair-debug session 2026-05-25
- :rf.xray/trace-buffer sub: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs:124
- :rf.xray/cascades sub + xray-internal filter: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/registry.cljs:331
- :rf.xray/filtered-cascades sub: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/filters.cljs:207
- L2 list render + empty branch: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:1796-1857
- cascade-has-event? / event-id-of-cascade predicates: shell.cljs:186-269
- Spec 002 — per-frame model (existing precedent: app-db, epoch-history are already per-frame)
- Spec 009 — trace bus (the surface this bead proposes to refactor)
- Adjacent: rf2-fb4hn (pre-attach event explainer) — also surfaces ring semantics; the bundle-by-cascade model proposed here would change its shape
notes:
AMENDED RULING (Mike 2026-05-25): Q2 = B3 + B4 combined. B (frameless → :rf/default+nil cluster) overturned by hot-reload memory-leak analysis. Final design: (B3) frameless trace events SKIP the ring entirely — stream live to subscribers only; never retained in any ring. Ring holds cascades exclusively. (B4) hot-reload re-emits deduplicated by shape — only CHANGED registrations emit a trace; unchanged re-emits suppressed. Trace ring becomes exclusively 'history of dispatched cascades'; the live stream filters reload-noise; the registry is the source of truth for 'what's registered right now'. Hot-reload is a non-event for the trace bus.
Follow-on beads filed 2026-05-25 (post spec-landing PR): rf2-8uwce (framework impl — per-frame ring storage, emit-site routing, B3 frameless-skip, B4 hot-reload dedup-by-shape, CLJS tests) depends on rf2-g1b2m. rf2-q03j7 (consumer adoption — Xray drops trace_bus.cljc; Xray + Story + re-frame2-pair-mcp consume per-frame rings + cascade-bundle wire + live frameless channel; may further decompose) depends on rf2-8uwce. Dependency chain: rf2-g1b2m (spec) -> rf2-8uwce (core impl) -> rf2-q03j7 (consumer adoption).
close_reason: #2135 — spec landing for per-frame trace rings + cascade-keyed retention + B3+B4 (frameless events skip ring; hot-reload dedup-by-shape). Follow-ons: rf2-8uwce (core impl) → rf2-q03j7 (consumer adoption). spec/009 rewritten, spec/002 extended, spec/Tool-Pair §Reading the per-frame trace ring, spec/Conventions :rf.trace/cascades-retained.

title: fix(xray): app-db panel ▸ expand triangles are decoration only — missing click-to-expand wiring (re-frame-10x has it, Xray skipped that layer)
description:
## Symptom

In Xray's app-db panel, the values render with cljs-devtools' typography + colors + ▸ markers — looks like an interactive tree. But clicking any ▸ triangle does NOTHING — no expand, no collapse, no toggle. The operator can only see what cljs-devtools' header-summary shows by default (a single line per leaf, collapsed collection refs as `▸ {…}`). To actually inspect deeper, the operator has to open browser DevTools console and use cljs-devtools' interactive expand there.

## Diagnosis (live eval-cljs probes, 2026-05-25)

Walked the rendered DOM:

```clj
(let [panel     (.querySelector js/document "#rf-xray-tabpanel-app-db")
      triangles (filter #(= "▸" (.-textContent %))
                        (array-seq (.querySelectorAll panel "span")))]
  ;; First triangle:
  ;;   :onclick        ""        ← no click handler
  ;;   :role           nil
  ;;   :cursor         "auto"    ← not even styled as clickable
  ;;   :inline-style   "color: var(--rf-xray-text-tertiary); margin-right: 2px;"
  )
```

6 triangles in the panel, every one pure decoration. No click handler, no pointer cursor, no role attribute.

cljs-devtools' JSONML normally encodes expand-on-click via `["object", {object: <ref>, config: ...}]` references — Chrome's DevTools console knows to re-invoke the formatter on the referenced object on click and swap the collapsed view for the expanded body. In an in-page render, that wiring has to be reimplemented. **Xray skipped that step.**

## How re-frame-10x does it

Confirmed via re-frame-10x source (`src/day8/re_frame_10x/components/cljs_devtools.cljs`):

re-frame-10x's `simple-render-with-path-annotations` uses cljs-devtools for LEAF-level formatting (colors, type detection, scalar pretty-printing). But the JSONML walker `jsonml->hiccup-with-path-annotations` then WRAPS each collection node with an interactive span+button that dispatches re-frame events on click:

```clj
[:span {:class    (toggle-style :bright)
        :on-click #(do (rf/dispatch [::app-db.events/toggle-expansion indexed-path])
                       (rf/dispatch [::app-db.events/expand {:id path-id :expand? false}]))}
 [:button
  (if show-body?
    [material/arrow-drop-down]
    [material/arrow-right])]]
```

Expanded state is tracked per-path in re-frame app-db. On toggle, the component re-renders showing either:
- The collapsed header (cljs-devtools' header summary), OR
- The expanded body (cljs-devtools' body for that node — itself a JSONML structure that recursively re-runs through `jsonml->hiccup-with-path-annotations`)

So re-frame-10x and Xray BOTH use cljs-devtools for leaf formatting; the difference is the INTERACTIVE WRAPPER LAYER that re-frame-10x adds and Xray doesn't.

## Fix

Wire click-to-expand into Xray's `views.edn-widget.cljs-devtools-render` walker. Concrete steps:

1. **Add an expanded-paths subscription/atom** — `[:rf.xray.app-db/expanded-paths]` sub returning a set of paths (vectors of keys) currently expanded. Backed by an app-db slot or a Reagent atom local to the panel.
2. **Add `toggle-expansion` event handler** — dispatched on triangle click, flips the path in the expanded-paths set.
3. **In the JSONML→hiccup walker, when an `object` surrogate is encountered**:
   - Wrap the ▸ marker in `[:span {:on-click (fn [] (rf/dispatch [::toggle-expansion path])) :style {:cursor "pointer"}} ...]`
   - Check if `path` is in the expanded-paths set; if yes, recursively render the body (call `body-api-call` on the referenced object's surrogate, walk the resulting JSONML through the same walker); if no, render the collapsed header
4. **Use ▶ vs ▼ glyphs** instead of just ▸ (to match collapsed/expanded states visually — re-frame-10x uses Material `arrow_right` / `arrow_drop_down` icons)
5. **Style for cursor + hover** — `cursor: pointer` on the triangle wrapper; hover state via existing Xray theme tokens

The wiring is straightforward — re-frame-10x's implementation is ~30 lines for the toggle layer. The cljs-devtools formatter API has the `body-api-call` already; just need to call it on demand instead of leaving the surrogate as a static ▸.

### Alternative — render fully-expanded by default

The widget already has `value->tree-hiccup` (fully-expanded mode) used in some surfaces. Could default the app-db panel to fully-expanded, dodging the click-to-expand problem. Trade-off: a large app-db renders the entire tree on every re-render — bad perf, scrollable wall of text, no progressive disclosure. The interactive expand is the durable answer.

## Mystery solved (for the bead description's context)

Operator premise was: "re-frame-10x uses different widgetry from cljs-devtools." Half-right. Both use cljs-devtools for LEAF FORMATTING. re-frame-10x adds a custom INTERACTIVE WRAPPER that Xray skipped. The visual + functional differences the operator perceives (looks "quite different", expand icons don't work) trace exactly to that missing wrapper layer.

## Acceptance

Operator opens the app-db panel, sees collapsed top-level keys, clicks a ▸ next to `:counter` (or any collection), the triangle rotates / changes to ▼, the body expands inline showing the nested map. Clicking again collapses. State persists across re-renders. No need to open browser DevTools console.

## Testing notes

A visual regression test that:
1. Loads the app-db panel
2. Asserts at least one ▸ has `cursor: pointer` and a click handler
3. Programmatically clicks it
4. Asserts the body appears (DOM mutates to show nested content)

Would have caught the current static-rendering bug.

## References

- Xray widget source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_widget/widget.cljs` + `cljs_devtools_render.cljs`
- re-frame-10x reference impl: `src/day8/re_frame_10x/components/cljs_devtools.cljs` (the `simple-render-with-path-annotations` + `jsonml->hiccup-with-path-annotations` pair) and `src/day8/re_frame_10x/panels/app_db/{events,views,subs}.cljs` (the toggle-expansion event/sub plumbing)
- Discovery: pair-debug 2026-05-25 — DOM probes confirmed ▸ triangles have no click wiring
- Note that Xray's `cljs-devtools-render` already has the `value->tree-hiccup` (fully-expanded) path — useful reference for how the body JSONML re-walks through the same machinery; the interactive version differs only in WHEN to render the body (on-demand vs always)
close_reason: #2134 — cljs-devtools renderer walker now wraps each object-surrogate ▸ triangle in [:span] with role=button + cursor + tabindex + aria-label + on-key-down (Enter/Space); click dispatches :rf.xray/data-display-toggle-node reusing the home-grown engine's sticky-expansion contract via :rf.xray/data-display-expansion slot in :rf/xray frame; glyph swaps ▸↔▾; default expansion via §10.4 depth-heuristic; cljs-devtools :max-print-level tightened to 1 so surrogates emit per nested collection; +spec/021 §10.0 updated +tests pinning wrapper shape

title: fix(machines-viz): label collision avoidance — Phase 3/A follow-on from rf2-j10sm
description:
Phase 3 (A) follow-on from rf2-j10sm (#2131): post-render label collision avoidance.

rf2-j10sm Phase 1 (padded backgrounds) + Phase 2 (multi-event collapse) fixed the dominant overlap source (multi-event self-loop clusters + chip-on-ink merging). What remains: labels that happen to lie on a routed edge path crossing a node's interior — typically a cross-hierarchy edge whose ELK-routed bend-point sequence threads between containers and parks a label on top of a populated state.

## The Phase 3 design (from rf2-j10sm bead)

A post-process pass after ELK + label placement:

1. Walk every label, check intersection with (a) every node's bounding-box, (b) every other label's bounding-box.
2. For each collision, slide the label along its edge's path until the conflict resolves.
3. Bounded retry (e.g. 8 iterations); fall back to slight overlap if no clear position found.

Pure post-process — doesn't change ELK input or the projector. The durable answer for 'labels should never cross nodes.'

## Implementation sketch

The challenge: the current MachineChart is a Reagent form-2 component (closure state with r/atom for layout). Phase 3 needs post-mount DOM measurement after xyflow paints, which requires either:

- Convert to form-3 with :component-did-mount / :component-did-update, OR
- Mount a sibling React component using useEffect that observes the canvas + walks the label DOM.

Steps the measurement pass needs:

1. Read each label's getBoundingClientRect (xyflow's EdgeLabelRenderer portal-renders these into the canvas).
2. Read each node's getBoundingClientRect.
3. Compute intersections; for each colliding label, walk its edge's path string and find a position along the path that resolves the intersection.
4. Apply a transform: translate() override to the label's wrapper div.

Edge path data needs to be threaded through to the DOM layer (currently lives only in the transition-edge render closure). One option: emit data-edge-path-d + data-label-anchor attributes for the post-pass to read.

## Debug affordances (add when impl lands)

- data-label-collisions data-attr on the chart root listing the count + ids of edges whose label intersects another node. Visual-regression tests assert this is zero.
- ?debug-chart=1 URL flag dumps all label bboxes + intersection check results to console.

## Acceptance

Loading the :ws/connection topology, EVERY edge label sits CLEAR of EVERY node body. The data-label-collisions count on the chart root reads 0 for the testdeck :ws/connection machine + every other chart in tools/xray/testbeds/.

## References

- rf2-j10sm (#2131) — Phase 1 + Phase 2 (padded backgrounds + multi-event collapse) landed; Phase 3 deferred.
- rf2-shv82 (#2129) — structural fixes (compound Handles, self-loop fan, cross-hierarchy label placement) this rests on.
- xstate/Stately Studio applies an equivalent post-process pass for the same reason.
close_reason: #2133 — Phase 3/A post-render label collision avoidance: pure .cljc geometry (AABB + SVG-path waypoint parse + arc-length sampling + greedy resolver) + Reagent form-3 sibling overlay (matches after-rings pattern) + edge-path data-attr threading + tick integration for retro-replay; +spec/API.md §Post-render label-collision avoidance +spec/001 Phase 3 landed; +28 geometry tests +2 DOM tests

title: fix(machines-viz): visual readability — edge labels overlap nodes + multi-event self-loop label clustering + cross-node label crossing (chart unusable as debug aid)
description:
## Symptom

The :ws/connection topology now has all the right edges, containment, and routing — structural xstate/Stately parity achieved after rf2-xh1lm (#2126) + rf2-shv82 (#2129). But to a human reading the chart, it still looks like a disorganised mess. Screenshot reference: `2026-05-25_13-51-59.png`. The chart is not usable as a debugging aid in its current state.

Specific visual problems (each independently fixable):

### 1. Edge labels overlap node bodies

- `authenticating` state label partially covered by the `after(250)` edge label crossing it
- `connected` state covered by `ws/clear / clear-log ?] / log-message` — multiple edge labels merge over the node
- `disconnected` has 4+ edge labels (`ws/disa…`, `ws/connect`, `lure`, `ws/clear / clear-log`) crammed against its bottom-right edge
- User can't read state names without zooming

### 2. Multi-event self-loops produce overlapping labels

`:disconnected` has 3 self-loops (`ws/arm-fail / arm-failure`, `ws/disarm-fail / disarm-failure`, `ws/clear / clear-log`). The renderer now draws 3 distinct arcs (Handles fan from rf2-shv82) but the LABELS still cluster at near-identical positions, producing garbled text like `ws/disa…lure`. Same for `:connected` (2 self-loops).

rf2-shv82's close note mentions "self-loop label fan via concentric perimeter anchors" — that lands the arcs at different points, but the labels aren't getting spread radially with them.

### 3. Edge labels cross node interiors

The cross-hierarchy `:authenticating → :failed (after(250) / record-error)` label sits INSIDE `:active` near `:authenticating`'s top — better than the previous canvas-bottom-left, but the edge ROUTE still passes through `:active`'s interior visually overlapping with `:authenticating` and `:connected`.

The `:failed → :active` edge routes from `:failed` (top) all the way DOWN the left side of the canvas to `:active`'s top-left corner. The label `ws/connect / disarm-failure` sits in the middle of this long path — far from both endpoints — but at least it's not overlapping other elements.

### 4. `:failed → :failed` self-loop label clipped

The `ws/clear / clear-log` label for `:failed`'s self-loop appears as a small `lure` fragment at top-right of `:failed`. The arc may be off-screen or the label is clipped.

## Why this matters

The chart's purpose is debugging — operators look at it to understand machine behaviour at a glance. Disorganised labels force the operator to mentally untangle the diagram before they can answer "what events does this state respond to?", which is the question the chart is supposed to answer instantly.

xstate/Stately's Studio renders the SAME machine cleanly:
- Edge labels never cross node interiors (collision-detection re-routes them)
- Multi-event labels stack vertically with adequate spacing
- Multi-self-loop labels sit at distinct anchor points along the arc, with their labels offset radially so they don't overlap each other
- Edge routing penalises paths that cross containers visually

Our renderer has the structural primitives (Handles, fan, parent-relative coords) but lacks the LAYOUT layer that resolves visual collisions.

## Fix directions

### A. Edge-label collision avoidance (post-process)

After ELK + label placement, walk every label and check for intersection with: (a) any node's bounding box, (b) any other label's bounding box. For each collision, slide the label along its edge's path until the conflict resolves. Bounded retry; fall back to slight overlap if no clear position found within N iterations.

Pure post-processing pass; doesn't change ELK input or the projector.

### B. Multi-event label merging (xstate/Stately convention)

For N edges with same `source-target` pair (different events), render as ONE edge with N stacked labels (`ws/connect` / `ws/arm-fail` / `ws/clear` as a label list, not 3 separate labels at the same point). Cleaner visually; matches what xstate does.

Requires projector to group edges by `[source target]` before handing to xyflow, and a custom edge component that renders a label list.

### C. Better self-loop label placement

Place each self-loop's label at the OUTSIDE midpoint of its arc (not at the arc's geometric centre, which clusters them all near the source node). Each loop's arc has a different orientation (top, right, bottom-left fan from rf2-shv82); the label should ride along that orientation.

### D. Padded label backgrounds (defensive)

Give every edge label an opaque (token-bg-color) background with rounded corners + 4px padding. So even when labels overlap, each remains individually readable rather than merging into garbled text. Tiny visual change; substantial readability gain.

### Recommended combination

D (padded backgrounds) — single CSS change, applies to everything, immediate readability win. Ships in 30min.

Then B (multi-event merging) — collapses the 3 self-loops on `:disconnected` into a single 3-label arc, addressing the worst cluster.

Then A (collision avoidance) — the durable answer for "labels should never cross nodes". Heavier work but the right ceiling.

C is structural to self-loops; may fall out naturally from B + rf2-shv82's existing anchor fan.

## Probes / debug

Build on rf2-a64bi's earlier suggestions:
- `data-label-collisions` data-attr on the chart root listing the count + ids of edges whose label currently intersects another node — visual-regression tests can assert this is zero
- `?debug-chart=1` URL flag dumps all label bboxes + intersection check results to console

## Acceptance

Loading the `:ws/connection` topology, the operator can read every state name without zooming, can identify the event(s) on every edge in <2 seconds, and no two labels visually overlap. Same machine renders comparably to Stately Studio's output for the same spec.

## References

- Screenshot: 2026-05-25_13-51-59.png (post-rf2-xh1lm + post-rf2-shv82, all 16 edges visible but cluttered)
- Predecessors (machine-topology epic): rf2-tt1lt closed, rf2-xrxb1 (PARITY PLAN — match xstate/Stately), rf2-ijttt (Stately/xstate IR ground-truth)
- Latest structural fixes: rf2-xh1lm (#2126 xyflow v12 parentId), rf2-shv82 (#2129 Handle-based edge routing + self-loop fan)
- Test cases for collision detection: any compound machine with 3+ self-loops on a node, OR any machine with cross-hierarchy transitions through populated container interiors
- Discovery: pair-debug 2026-05-25 — visual readability assessment after all structural fixes landed

Phase 3 (A collision avoidance) filed as rf2-r7vsr; Phase 4 (C) auto-resolved by collapse.

Phase 4 (C — better self-loop label placement) auto-resolves via Phase 2 (multi-event self-loops are now ONE arc with one label group instead of N arcs needing per-loop slotting). The chart is now usable as a debugging aid against :ws/connection.

title: fix(machines-viz): compound-endpoint topology — 4 edges silently dropped + self-loop label collisions + cross-hierarchy label placement (xstate/Stately parity gap)
description:
## Status

After rf2-xh1lm (#2126) landed, the testdeck `:ws/connection` chart now renders compound substates correctly contained inside their `:active` parent — xstate/Stately containment parity achieved.

Three remaining rendering gaps surfaced in the 2026-05-25 pair-debug session via live eval-cljs probes. They all relate to how the chart handles transitions/labels that involve compound containers (not just compound containment itself). Filed grouped because they share a root theme: the chart's xstate/Stately parity is incomplete around compound EDGES (entry/exit + multi-event collisions), even though compound CONTAINMENT is now correct.

## Symptom

Screenshot reference: `2026-05-25_12-35-47.png`. Visible problems:

1. The user cannot see HOW the machine enters or leaves `:active` — no rendered edges go to/from the compound container at all
2. Self-loop labels on `:disconnected` and `:connected` render as overlapping garbled text instead of distinct event chips
3. The cross-hierarchy `:authenticating → :failed` label sits at the canvas bottom-left, far from where the routed edge path would visually originate

## Issue 1 — 4 edges with compound endpoint silently dropped between ELK and DOM

**Hard evidence (live eval-cljs probes, 2026-05-25):**

| Layer | Edges with `:active` as endpoint | How verified |
|---|---|---|
| Parser (`chart.layout/parse-definition`) | 4 (disconnected→active, active→disconnected, active→active self-loop, failed→active) | `(re-frame.core/machine-meta :ws/connection)` + parse-definition emitted 14 edges total |
| Projector (`chart.projection/xyflow-graph`) | 4 | xyflow-graph called against the parsed input emitted 16 edges (14 + 2 initial markers) |
| ELK input (`->elk-input`) | 4 | private fn called with parsed; ELK input had 14 edges including all 4 |
| ELK output (`.layout()`) | 4 routed | live elk-instance .layout() returned 14 edges, every one with `sections-count: 1` (computed route) |
| **DOM (`.react-flow__edge`)** | **0 of 4** | `(.querySelectorAll js/document ".react-flow__edge")` returned 12 elements, none with `:active` as source or target id |

All 4 edges survive every step of the pipeline up to and including ELK's routing. They appear in the projector's `xyflow-graph` output. They are NOT in the rendered DOM. Drop happens inside xyflow's React-Flow component (or in a chart-side filter between projector and ReactFlow render).

The 4 missing edges:

- `disconnected → active` via `:ws/connect`
- `active → disconnected` via `:ws/disconnect` (parent-level transition)
- `active → active` via `:ws/send` (parent-level self-loop fallback)
- `failed → active` via `:ws/connect / disarm-failure`

Net effect: the operator can see the substates of `:active` and the transitions BETWEEN them, but cannot see how the machine ENTERS or LEAVES `:active` at all. Every parent-level transition is invisible.

### Likely root cause

xyflow v12's React-Flow internally validates edges and may silently drop any whose source or target node has children — consistent with its `parentId` mechanic treating parents as containers (not endpoints). To verify, inspect xyflow's React-Flow internal Zustand store post-render and compare edge count to the projector's emitted count.

### Fix direction

xstate/Stately's convention for this: a parent-level transition like `:active → :disconnected (ws/disconnect)` is rendered as an arrow emerging from the COMPOUND CONTAINER'S BORDER, not from any specific leaf inside it. Two implementation paths:

- **A.** Rewrite parent-level transitions into leaf-to-leaf form before reaching xyflow: `active → disconnected` becomes 3 edges, one from each of `connecting/authenticating/connected` to `disconnected`. Visually collapse them into one if their layout converges. Loses some semantic clarity (the parent-level intent isn't preserved in the data); preserves rendering correctness.
- **B.** Synthetic "border ghost" nodes at the compound's edge that act as the visible endpoints; the actual edges go leaf-to-ghost-to-other-state. Custom node type; lets the renderer paint the edge emerging from the container border the way Stately does.

xstate/Stately's renderer uses option B in concept (the "self-transition" affordance on compound borders is the same mechanism). Worth confirming by reading the Stately renderer's IR before picking.

## Issue 2 — Self-loop label collisions

`:disconnected` has 3 self-loops: `:ws/arm-fail / arm-failure`, `:ws/disarm-fail / disarm-failure`, `:ws/clear / clear-log`. The DOM confirms 3 distinct `.react-flow__edge` elements. But the labels render at the same midpoint, producing garbled text like `ws/d... ws/clear / clear-log ilure` (visible in the screenshot).

`:active.connected` has 2 self-loops (`:ws/send`, `:ws/clear`) — same issue.

xstate/Stately convention: stack multiple self-loops as concentric arcs or fan them out from different anchor points on the source node's border, with their labels offset radially. Each event-label gets its own readable slot.

The xstate/Stately reference IR doc (rf2-ijttt) likely covers this — worth checking what they do.

## Issue 3 — Cross-hierarchy edge label placement

`:authenticating → :failed (after 250 / record-error)` — this cross-hierarchy edge is correctly emitted, ELK routes it (sections-count 1), and the edge IS in the DOM. But its label (`after(250) / record-error`) is positioned at the bottom-left corner of the canvas, far from where the user perceives the edge to originate (top of the `:active` container or near `:authenticating` inside it).

Likely cause: the label-positioning logic computes the label coords from the edge's mid-section, but for a cross-hierarchy edge with ELK-routed bend points that go OUT of the container, the midpoint can land in unexpected absolute-frame coordinates.

Stately Studio places cross-hierarchy edge labels near the SOURCE-SIDE bend point (just outside the container the edge exits), not at the midpoint. That keeps the label near its visual origin.

## Probes used (paste-able into eval-cljs)

```clj
;; Parse + projector — count + list all edges
(let [def    (re-frame.core/machine-meta :ws/connection)
      parsed (day8.re-frame2-machines-viz.chart.layout/parse-definition def)
      graph  (day8.re-frame2-machines-viz.chart.projection/xyflow-graph
               parsed
               (into {} (map (fn [n] [(:id n) {:x 0 :y 0 :width 100 :height 50}])
                             (:nodes parsed)))
               {})]
  {:parsed-edges (count (:edges parsed))
   :projected-edges (count (:edges graph))
   :projected-list (vec (map (juxt :source :target) (:edges graph)))})

;; Compare to DOM
(.-length (.querySelectorAll js/document ".react-flow__edge"))
```

## Acceptance

- Every edge the parser emits appears in the DOM with its label visible and legible (no garbled overlap, no missing edges)
- Parent-level transitions (involving compound endpoints) render visibly — operator can see how the machine enters/leaves `:active`
- Self-loops on a single node fan out so their event labels are individually readable
- Cross-hierarchy edge labels render near their visual origin (source-side bend point) rather than at the routed midpoint

## Suggested debug additions (for the next iteration)

Build on rf2-a64bi's suggestions:
- `data-edge-count-projected` and `data-edge-count-rendered` data attrs on the chart root so visual-regression tests can assert "every emitted edge is rendered"
- Console group on `?debug-chart=1` listing edges emitted vs edges actually in the React-Flow nodes/edges Zustand store, flagging any drop with the source/target ids

## References

- Discovery: pair-debug 2026-05-25 with live eval-cljs probes; screenshot `2026-05-25_12-35-47.png` (post-rf2-xh1lm, compound containment working but these 3 issues remaining)
- Predecessor wins this session: rf2-4lyvh (#2118 ELK error visibility), rf2-21rkg (#2121 testbed fix), rf2-a64bi (#2124 compound styling), rf2-xh1lm (#2126 xyflow v12 parentId)
- xstate/Stately ground-truth: rf2-ijttt (closed — IR ground-truth doc); reference Stately Studio for the multi-self-loop fan + compound-border-edge rendering conventions
close_reason: #2129 — all 3 issues: invisible Handles on 4 sides of compound + region nodes (xyflow getHandleBounds requires Handles for edge routing; root cause source-confirmed); self-loop label fan via concentric perimeter anchors; cross-hierarchy label at source-side bend point. +spec/001-Topology-Parity +spec/API.md +chart_dom tests +edges tests +projection tests

comments.text: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2129 — implementation lands across chart.nodes (handles on compound + region), chart.projection (loop-index + cross-hierarchy flag), chart.edges (8-slot self-loop fan + source-bend label anchor), chart (data-edge-count-projected attr). All gates green (clj-kondo, JVM 256, CLJS node 4438, CLJS browser 122, xray-feature-gate, bundle-isolation). Spec coverage in tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md + tools/machines-viz/spec/001-Topology-Parity.md (G6/G7/G8 closed; topology parity headline now G1-G8 all closed). Awaiting review + merge.

title: feat(re-frame2-pair-mcp): eval-cljs should default ON — the gate fights the tool's primary purpose (pair-debug = REPL)
description:
## Friction

eval-cljs is gated behind --allow-eval, OFF by default. To enable it, the operator must add it to the MCP launch args in ~/.claude.json and fully restart Claude Code (a `/mcp reconnect` re-pipes to the existing process which already started without the flag — doesn't take effect).

This fights the tool's primary purpose. re-frame2-pair-mcp exists for pair-debugging a live re-frame2 app — and the fundamental REPL primitive of a pair-debug session is "evaluate this CLJS form in the browser". Gating it forces every operator to:

1. Discover the gate (only after a failing call returns :rf.error/eval-cljs-disabled)
2. Edit ~/.claude.json with a hardcoded path arg — exactly the kind of pre-config tax the rf2-umoz2 / rf2-3grub line of work was trying to eliminate
3. Fully restart Claude Code (losing session state)

For an MCP whose entire reason for existence is REPL access, this is upside-down. Operators have explicitly chosen to install + configure re-frame2-pair-mcp; they've already declared "I want REPL access to my running re-frame2 app." The gate adds friction without meaningful additional protection.

Encountered during pair-debug 2026-05-25: the eval-cljs disabled message blocked DOM inspection that would have completed a debug investigation in 2 minutes. The operator (mike) declined to add --allow-eval to ~/.claude.json on principle ("no hardcoded args in claude.json").

## Threat-model analysis

The gate's apparent rationale parallels --allow-writes (which gates dispatch / reset-frame-db / restore-epoch — operations that can corrupt app state). But:

- **--allow-writes makes sense.** A pair-tool that can dispatch events or reset app-db can mutate state in ways that confuse the operator about what their app did vs what the tool did. Per-call write-gating preserves that distinction.
- **--allow-eval does NOT parallel this.** eval-cljs can do everything dispatch/reset/restore can do — plus arbitrary other things. So if you have --allow-writes, you may as well have --allow-eval (eval can express the writes). Conversely if you DON'T have --allow-writes, having --allow-eval lets the attacker do those writes anyway via eval. The two gates aren't independent; the eval gate doesn't add a separable protection.

The real protection is: don't expose the MCP to untrusted callers. Once exposed, eval is fully unrestricted regardless of either gate.

## Options

### Option A — Invert the default (recommended)

eval-cljs ON by default. Operators who want to gate (CI runs, shared dev environments where multiple humans share an MCP process) opt OUT via --safe-mode or --no-eval. Matches the default expectation for a REPL tool.

### Option B — Remove the gate entirely

If you're running re-frame2-pair-mcp at all, you've made the trust decision. The gate adds zero defense (per threat-model analysis) and ongoing friction. Delete it.

### Option C — Runtime toggleable via a tool call

A new MCP tool `set-eval-policy` lets the operator enable eval-cljs mid-session without restarting. Default stays OFF (preserves current behaviour as a starting state) but operators can flip on a per-session basis. More machinery; doesn't eliminate the "I forgot to enable it" failure mode but does eliminate the restart-and-lose-session cost.

### Recommended: A (invert default)

Matches operator expectations; preserves an explicit escape hatch for the rare paranoid case; zero machinery beyond changing the default value of one flag.

## Migration notes

If A is chosen, the existing --allow-eval flag becomes a no-op (kept for back-compat) and --safe-mode (or --no-eval) is the new opt-out. Document in the MCP README + skill docs that eval-cljs is the default REPL surface.

If B is chosen, --allow-eval becomes a no-op and the gate logic is deleted. README updated.

If C is chosen, --allow-eval remains for the launch-time path AND a new tool surfaces for the mid-session toggle.

## Acceptance

For A: a fresh `npm install -g @day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp` + default `~/.claude.json` entry (no extra args) → eval-cljs works on first call.

## References

- Source: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/eval_cljs.cljs (the gate logic + error response)
- Adjacent gate (--allow-writes): tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/writes.cljs
- Discovery: pair-debug session 2026-05-25 — eval-cljs blocking blocked DOM inspection
- Operator-feedback memory thread: previous declines to add hardcoded args to ~/.claude.json (cite rf2-umoz2 / rf2-3grub line of work — same "no hardcoded config" stance)
notes:
2026-05-25 — operator pick: OPTION B (remove the gate entirely).

Per discussion, the gate adds zero defense (threat-model: eval can do everything the writes gate would block, so the two gates are not independent protections — once eval is enabled, writes are de-facto enabled too) and creates ongoing friction that fights the tool's primary purpose. If you've installed re-frame2-pair-mcp and configured it in ~/.claude.json, you've already declared trust in the dev surface.

Worker: delete the --allow-eval gate logic, retain the CLI flag as a no-op for back-compat (warn on use: "ignored — eval is enabled by default since rf2-a0z0h"), update README + skill docs. The --allow-writes gate stays as-is (separate decision — writes have their own use case where a read-only debug session is genuinely desirable).

title: fix(machines-viz): PR #2124 sized :active container correctly but substates STILL render outside it — render path bug below the projection
description:
## Status

PR #2124 (rf2-a64bi) landed and is verified live in source + compiled JS:
- projection.cljc:322 widened style-arm from `region?` only to `(or region? :compound?)`
- compiled `out/examples/step-deck/cljs-runtime/day8.re_frame2_machines_viz.chart.projection.js` (mtime 2026-05-25 09:19) contains the OR branch
- 4409/4409 CLJS tests pass

But the visual symptom is unchanged after `shadow-cljs` restart + browser hard-refresh:
- :active's 3 substates (connecting, authenticating, connected) still render stacked at top-right of canvas, not inside :active
- :failed mixed in with them
- :active drawn as an oversized empty dashed container at bottom-left (correctly sized now — that part of #2124 worked)
- Edge labels for connecting→authenticating and authenticating→connected float around the :active container at bottom
- No console error — ELK ran successfully

So #2124 sized the container correctly but did NOT visually move the children into it.

## Empirical verification

### Projection output (CLJ probe, parses real testbed machine post rf2-21rkg):

    id="disconnected"               path=[:disconnected]               parent-id=nil
    id="active"                     path=[:active]                     parent-id=nil      compound?=true
    id="active__connecting"         path=[:active :connecting]         parent-id="active"
    id="active__authenticating"     path=[:active :authenticating]     parent-id="active"
    id="active__connected"          path=[:active :connected]          parent-id="active"
    id="failed"                     path=[:failed]                     parent-id=nil

xyflow-graph output for :active and substates (with simulated parent-relative coords from ELK):

    id=active                  type=compound  pos={:x 200 :y 0}  style={:width 328 :height 156}  parentNode=nil   extent=nil
    id=active__connecting      type=state     pos={:x 14 :y 34}  style=nil  parentNode="active"  extent="parent"
    id=active__authenticating  type=state     pos={:x 174 :y 34} style=nil  parentNode="active"  extent="parent"
    id=active__connected       type=state     pos={:x 14 :y 90}  style=nil  parentNode="active"  extent="parent"

Substates correctly carry :parentNode "active" + :extent "parent" + parent-relative positions. :active correctly carries :style {:width :height}. The projection is structurally correct.

### Actual ELK output (Node+elkjs probe against the exact ->elk-input shape):

    root  x=0  y=0  w=282  h=487
      disconnected  x=130  y=126  w=140 h=44
      active        x=22   y=240  w=191.33  h=220
        active__connecting     x=14    y=34   w=140 h=44  (parent-relative ✓)
        active__authenticating x=14    y=98   w=140 h=44  (parent-relative ✓)
        active__connected      x=37.33 y=162  w=140 h=44  (parent-relative ✓)
      failed        x=95   y=12   w=140 h=44

ELK returns substate coords parent-relative (worker's prior empirical claim confirmed independently). So projection + ELK are both correct.

## Conclusion

The bug is in the render path BELOW the projection — either xyflow itself is not honoring `:parentNode` + `:extent "parent"` for `:type "compound"` parents (possibly only works for `:type "parallel-region"`), or there is some other React-side glue that's missing.

Without DOM access (`--allow-eval` is gated; per-tab Playwright connection fails because shadow's dev-runtime websocket only services the original tab), no further inspection is possible from the current toolchain.

## Acceptance gap

PR #2124's three new deftests asserted the PROJECTION output (style allocated, parentNode set, substate-inside-parent invariant). All passed. But the visual symptom remained. So the assertion shape doesn't match what users see — projection-correctness doesn't imply render-correctness in this stack.

## Recommended next steps (combined)

### 1. Instrumentation (so the next debug iteration has eyes)
Adopt the suggestions from rf2-a64bi's "debug improvements" section:
- `data-elk-x` / `data-elk-y` data-attrs on every rendered xyflow node (dev-only via `interop/debug-enabled?` gate) so DOM-inspection reveals ELK's coords without needing eval-cljs or running probes
- `:rf.machines-viz/layout-applied` trace event carrying `{:input-summary :positions-extent :duration-ms}` — subscribable by Xray Issues panel, makes "did the layout actually apply" visible from the trace bus
- Optionally: a `?debug-chart=1` URL flag that flips on a verbose `console.group` of the projector + ELK output + positions handed to xyflow

### 2. Visual regression test (the missing assertion shape)
A Playwright spec that loads the testdeck step-deck machine tab and asserts:
- `data-id="active"` is in the DOM
- Each substate's bounding rect intersects `:active`'s bounding rect (NOT just that the node exists at non-(0,0) coords)
- The 3 substates are ordered top-to-bottom (or LR, per direction)

This would have failed under the current state and caught the bug.

### 3. Investigation into the render path
Hypothesis to test: xyflow's parentNode mechanic may require parent `:type "group"` (xyflow's built-in container type) — neither `:type "compound"` nor `:type "parallel-region"` are xyflow built-ins, they're registered via nodeTypes. Compound node component currently has `:pointer-events "none"` + `:position "relative"`; possibly xyflow needs additional attrs (e.g. `:style {:width :height}` PLUS some specific class or marker) for it to recognize the node as a sub-flow container.

The fact that `:type "parallel-region"` works for region containers but `:type "compound"` does not (despite #2124 making the projection identical) suggests the difference is in the React component definition — the parallel-region-node component may declare itself a sub-flow container in a way compound-node does not.

Compare parallel_region_node.cljs vs compound section of nodes.cljs side-by-side — look for any sub-flow / xyflow-container declaration that exists on the former but not the latter.

## Reproducers

- CLJ projection probe: `C:/tmp/probe-projection.clj` + `C:/tmp/probe-xyflow.clj` (both ~60 lines; bb-runnable)
- Node ELK probe: `C:/tmp/probe-elk.mjs` (uses installed elkjs)

All three should be promoted to permanent fixtures under `tools/machines-viz/dev/` so any contributor can replicate without writing them again.

## References

- Previous: rf2-a64bi (#2124) — sized compound container; tests passed; visual symptom unchanged
- Predecessors: rf2-4lyvh (#2118 ELK error visibility), rf2-21rkg (#2121 testbed fix), rf2-gpa9k (G5 cross-hierarchy assert)
- xstate/Stately parity goal: rf2-tt1lt (closed epic), rf2-ijttt (Stately/xstate IR ground-truth doc)
- Discovery session: pair-debug 2026-05-25, screenshots `2026-05-25_08-02-37.png` (pre-#2124) and `2026-05-25_09-12-22.png` (post-#2124, still broken)
notes: PR #2126 opened. Root cause: xyflow v12 reads userNode.parentId exclusively; pre-v12 parentNode key is silently ignored.
