title: fix(machines-viz): compound substates render OUTSIDE :active container — INCLUDE_CHILDREN gives ELK root-frame coords, walker assumes parent-relative
description:
## Symptom

After rf2-21rkg + rf2-4lyvh landed, the testdeck :ws/connection topology renders WITHOUT an ELK error (good — ELK accepts the graph), but the result is still visually broken (different bug):

- :active's 3 substates (connecting, authenticating, connected) are stacked in the top-right of the canvas, NOT visually contained inside :active
- :failed is mixed in with the active-substate cluster
- :active itself is rendered as an empty dashed container at the bottom-left (just the "active" label + an after(250) label inside)
- Edge labels (ws/disconnect / disarm-failure, clear / clear-log) overlap each other and the boxes
- No `[machines-viz] ELK layout failed` in console — ELK ran successfully

## Diagnosis

Ran the projector outside the browser as a CLJ probe against the live spec. The projector output is CORRECT:

    ;; parsed nodes
    id="disconnected"               path=[:disconnected]               parent-id=nil
    id="active"                     path=[:active]                     parent-id=nil       compound?=true
    id="active__connecting"         path=[:active :connecting]         parent-id="active"
    id="active__authenticating"     path=[:active :authenticating]     parent-id="active"
    id="active__connected"          path=[:active :connected]          parent-id="active"
    id="failed"                     path=[:failed]                     parent-id=nil

    ;; ->elk-children produces the right hierarchical shape
    [{:id "disconnected" ...}
     {:id "active" ...
      :children [{:id "active__connecting" ...} {...} {...}]
      :layoutOptions {"elk.algorithm" "layered" "elk.padding" "[top=34,...]"}}
     {:id "failed" ...}]

So the structure ELK SEES is correct. The bug is downstream — in how ELK result is decoded back into xyflow node positions.

## Root cause hypothesis

chart.cljs:154-156 sets `elk.hierarchyHandling INCLUDE_CHILDREN` whenever the graph nests (correct for cross-hierarchy edge routing — rf2-gpa9k closed G5 with this).

But chart.cljs:228 (elk-result->positions docstring) explicitly assumes:

> elkjs reports a child x/y RELATIVE to its parent container, which is exactly what xyflow parentNode sub-flow wants — so we record each node position AS elkjs gives it, no re-basing.

That assumption holds when ELK uses its default per-level layout (separate-children). With INCLUDE_CHILDREN ELK lays out everything as one flat graph; combined with `elk.json.edgeCoords ROOT` (also set for edge bend-points, line 117), child node positions come back in ROOT coordinates, not parent-relative.

The walker records the root-frame coords. The projector hands xyflow:

    ;; chart/projection.cljc:312-314
    (and (not region?) (:parent-id n))
    (assoc :parentNode (:parent-id n)
           :extent     "parent")

xyflow :parentNode + :extent "parent" interprets :position as RELATIVE to parent. With root-frame coords passed as parent-relative, the child renders at `parent.position + childAbsolutePosition` — way off the parent bounding box. That matches the screenshot exactly: substates appear at top-right (their root-frame ELK positions, then offset by :active position), while :active itself is empty at the bottom.

## Fix directions (pick one — or combine)

### A. Re-base child positions in the walker (smallest change)

When walking ELK result, carry an accumulated parent-offset and subtract it from each child coords before recording. elk-result->positions (chart.cljs:241) takes a parent-offset arg defaulting to {:x 0 :y 0}; the recursive walk passes {:x (+ parent-offset.x child.x) :y (+ parent-offset.y child.y)} and stores {:x child.x :y child.y} as the recorded position (already parent-relative). Pure data-side; no projector / xyflow change.

### B. Use {:position {:x x :y y}} without :parentNode for compound substates

Skip the :parentNode linkage but keep positions absolute. Children will not be auto-clipped to parent bounds but will visually sit inside if positioned correctly. Loses the auto-grouping benefits xyflow gives.

### C. Restrict INCLUDE_CHILDREN to parallel machines

Only set the flag for parallel; let layered/separate-children lay out each level independently for compound. Loses cross-hierarchy edge routing through the container (the rf2-gpa9k benefit) for compound machines — but cross-hierarchy in compound is uncommon. Worth checking what xstate/Stately renderer does: they handle compound nesting beautifully without needing INCLUDE_CHILDREN, by laying out each compound level locally and routing edges around bounding boxes after-the-fact.

### Recommended: A (re-base) + add a visual-regression test

A is the smallest correct change. Preserves both rf2-gpa9k cross-hierarchy routing AND visual containment.

## Take inspiration from xstate / Stately

Stately Studio renderer (the reference xstate visualization, called out in repo dashboard rf2-tt1lt and rf2-ijttt) handles compound machines correctly: substates are visually contained in the parent rounded container, cross-hierarchy edges route around the container edge instead of crossing through. The pattern:

- Each compound parent is a subflow container; child positions are relative to parent (matching xyflow parentNode semantic)
- Layout per level; routes computed post-layout in the global frame and projected back through the container hierarchy
- The container bounding box is computed from child extent + padding, not declared up-front

If A has edge cases, a Stately-style rewrite of the layout adapter (per-level layered passes, then absolute-frame edge routing) is the durable answer.

## Suggested debug improvements (so the NEXT bug is easier)

This bug took 30 min of source-reading + a custom CLJ probe to diagnose. Cheap improvements to put in the chart render path so the next failure is one click away:

1. Console log of ELK input/output sizes + position summary when debug-enabled? true (and a ?debug-chart=1 URL param or panel toggle). Print: parsed node count, ->elk-children top-level + nested counts, elk-result root extent, per-top-level position + size summary. A 6-line dump rather than the full tree.
2. data-elk-x / data-elk-y data attrs on each rendered xyflow node carrying the raw ELK-returned position. Operator can pull them via DOM inspection without re-running the probe. Tiny overhead; dev-only via the existing debug-enabled? gate.
3. Expose the probe form the way tools/machines-viz/test/... does — a one-liner the operator can paste into a REPL to print the projector output for any machine spec. Maybe surface as day8.re-frame2-machines-viz.chart.debug/dump-projection! so devtools-inclined operators can call it.
4. Optional but high-value: a per-render trace event :rf.machines-viz/layout-applied with input-summary + output-position-extent + duration. Subscribable by Xray Issues panel for "any chart whose root-extent is suspiciously small" heuristic detection.

## Reproducer

The CLJ probe at C:/tmp/probe-projection.clj (one-shot, 60 lines) reproduces the projector output ground-truth. Run with:

    cd C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2 && bb --classpath "tools/machines-viz/src" C:/tmp/probe-projection.clj

Worth promoting to a permanent fixture under tools/machines-viz/dev/ — operators can swap in any machine spec to debug projection issues without needing a browser.

## References

- Bug source: tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart.cljs:228-266 (elk-result->positions — the no-rebase assumption)
- Trigger: chart.cljs:154-156 (INCLUDE_CHILDREN switch)
- xyflow parentNode contract: tools/machines-viz/src/.../chart/projection.cljc:312-314
- Predecessors (machine-topology parity epic): rf2-tt1lt closed, rf2-gpa9k closed (G5 cross-hierarchy assert), rf2-ijttt closed (xstate/Stately renderer ground-truth doc)
- Surfaced after: rf2-21rkg (testbed fix) + rf2-4lyvh (silent-swallow logging) both merged 2026-05-24
- Discovery session: pair-debug 2026-05-25 with CLJ projection probe
notes: PR #2124 open. Applied alt-fix (b): widened :style {:width :height} cond-> arm in projection.cljc:309-327 from 'region? only' to '(or region? (:compound? n))', mirroring the region path verbatim. Walker untouched (prior STOP probe confirmed substate coords already parent-relative). Three new regression tests in projection_cljs_test.cljc; new 'Container sizing' subsection in tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md. Gates green: clj-kondo no new warnings; npm run test:cljs 4409 tests / 14086 assertions / 0 failures (baseline 4406/14076, +3 tests / +10 assertions).
close_reason: #2124 — compound containers receive :style {:width :height} from ELK (mirror region); +3 tests +API.md spec update; closes via Path B alternate-hypothesis fix after Path A empirical STOP

title: fix(xray): Machine panel views Chart + AfterRingsOverlay are plain Reagent fns — frame-leak to :rf/default
description:
## Symptoms

Two `:rf.warning/plain-fn-under-non-default-frame-once` warnings fire on the Step-Deck testbed at xray mount:

1. \`day8.re_frame2_xray.panels.machine_canvas.Chart\` rendered under \`:rf/xray\`; subscribe/dispatch routed to \`:rf/default\`
2. \`day8.re_frame2_xray.panels.machine_after_rings.AfterRingsOverlay\` rendered under \`:rf/xray\`; subscribe/dispatch routed to \`:rf/default\`

## Diagnosis

Both views are plain \`defn\`s, not registered via \`reg-view\`. Reagent's hiccup model strips frame context across plain fn boundaries — so any subscribe/dispatch inside Chart/AfterRingsOverlay runs against \`:rf/default\` (the host app's frame, in this case Step-Deck's), not \`:rf/xray\` (where xray's own state lives).

Per \`feedback-frames-are-isolated-contexts\`: subs MUST NOT reach into other frames; cross-frame sub computation is an anti-pattern. This is a real frame-leak.

## Surface

- \`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_canvas.cljs\` — Chart fn (~line 339-341)
- \`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_after_rings.cljs\` — AfterRingsOverlay fn

## Fix

Register both via \`reg-view\` (the canonical xray pattern). Same surgery PR #2110 (rf2-uu3lp) did for the rest of xray chrome — this is residue from that sweep.

## Context

The sweep that landed #2110 covered the obvious xray chrome views; these two Machine-panel views were missed because they didn't fire warnings until the Machine panel was mounted with a non-default frame attached (i.e. when Step-Deck — which has its own machines + non-trivial app-db — is the host). The PR #2110 audit grep apparently filtered by view-fn pattern but missed these two.

## Acceptance

1. Both warnings cease on Step-Deck testbed mount
2. Machine panel still functions identically (same chart layout, same after-rings overlay)
3. No new warnings introduced
4. Audit-grep \`tools/xray/src/.../panels/\` for any remaining plain-defn views and convert them in the same PR if found

## Related

- **#2110** rf2-uu3lp — the prior xray reg-view-warning sweep that missed these two
- **feedback-frames-are-isolated-contexts** (memory) — the cross-frame sub anti-pattern this is an instance of
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2122 — Chart + AfterRingsOverlay converted to reg-view; audit-grep confirmed no further residue (other plain-fn helpers are Clojure-call helpers from inside reg-view bodies, not Reagent component boundaries). Gates green: clj-kondo 0/0 changed files, JVM 884/3129, CLJS 4406/14076, xray-feature-gate 13/13.
close_reason: #2123 — Chart + AfterRingsOverlay reg-view conversion; spec/003 unchanged (frame-routing bug)

title: fix(xray-testbed): testdeck :ws/connection — :target :failed misuses keyword form (Spec 005 §1030), use [:failed]
notes:
## Concrete fix

	ools/xray/testbeds/testdeck/machine.cljs:166:

  :authenticating
  {:tags  #{:ws/active :ws/authenticating}
   :after {AUTHENTICATING-MS
           [{:guard :handshake-ok? :target :connected}
            {:target :failed :action :record-error}]}}   ; <-- misuse

:target :failed is keyword form. Per Spec 005 §Target resolution (line 1030): ‘:target :review resolves to a sibling of the current declaring state. The runtime resolves the keyword against the declaring state's parent's :states map.’

The declaring state is :authenticating (path [:active :authenticating]); its parent's :states is :active's :states = {:connecting :authenticating :connected} — :failed is NOT there. The runtime resolves this to [:active :failed] (a non-existent state), writes that to the snapshot, and the machine ends up in an undefined active configuration.

The projector (correctly) flags this by minting ctive__failed for the edge endpoint; ELK then rejects the graph (Referenced shape does not exist: active__failed), surfacing the misuse — see rf2-o43yg.

## Fix

Change the target to vector form (Spec 005 §1029: ‘Vector targets are unambiguous and the recommended form for cross-level transitions.’):

  {:target [:failed] :action :record-error}

## Verification

After the testbed fix:
- The :ws/connection machine's 6 topology boxes lay out correctly in Xray's Machine tab
- The runtime cascade from [:active :authenticating] to [:failed] exits both :authenticating and :active, runs :record-error, then enters [:failed] — the expected behaviour
- No projector / runtime / spec change required

## Related

- rf2-o43yg (BUG, blocked) — surfaces this; will close as resolved-via-testbed-fix once this lands
- rf2-4lyvh — added the visibility for the original ELK rejection
- Spec 005 §Target resolution — vector vs keyword (line 1025-1034)

## Optional follow-up (separate bead, not blocking)

Add a registration-time validator that rejects keyword targets that don't resolve to a state in the declaring state's parent's :states map. Would turn this silent runtime bug into a :rf.error/machine-unresolved-keyword-target registration error and catch this class of misuse before it can break anything.
close_reason: #2121 — testdeck :ws/connection :target :failed → [:failed] per Spec 005 §1029; +CLJS regression test pinning every edge endpoint resolves into :nodes

title: fix(machines-viz): chart.layout/resolve-target-path doesn't handle cross-hierarchy keyword targets — minted node-id refers to non-existent path, breaks ELK
description:
## Concrete error (with rf2-4lyvh logging applied)

\`\`\`
[machines-viz] ELK layout failed:
  Error: org.eclipse.elk.graph.json.JsonImportException:
    Referenced shape does not exist: active__failed
  {:node-count 6, :edge-count 14, :region-count 0, :parallel? false,
   :direction :tb, :layout-option-ks [], :machine-id :ws/connection}
\`\`\`

ELK rejects the entire graph because one edge references a node that doesn't exist. The projector minted \`active__failed\` for the edge endpoint, but no node in the graph has that id — the actual target is \`failed\` (top-level).

## Root cause

\`tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/layout.cljc:148-153\`:

\`\`\`clj
(defn- resolve-target-path
  [source-path target]
  (cond
    (= :same-state target) (vec source-path)
    (keyword? target)      (conj (parent-path source-path) target)   ; ← bug
    (target-path? target)  (vec target)
    :else                  nil))
\`\`\`

For a keyword target, the resolver ALWAYS produces \`(parent-of source) + target\`. That works for siblings, fails for any cross-hierarchy reference.

## Repro

The \`:ws/connection\` machine in \`tools/xray/testbeds/testdeck/machine.cljs\`:

\`\`\`clj
:active
{:states
 {:authenticating
  {:after {AUTHENTICATING-MS
           [{:guard :handshake-ok? :target :connected}
            {:target :failed :action :record-error}]}}}}    ; cross-hierarchy

:failed   ; top-level sibling of :active
{:tags #{:ws/failed} ...}
\`\`\`

The \`:target :failed\` from \`:authenticating\` (path \`[:active :authenticating]\`) resolves to \`[:active :failed]\` (sibling-of-parent), but the actual \`:failed\` state lives at \`[:failed]\` (top-level).

Observed in pair-debug session 2026-05-25 — all 6 topology boxes stacked at (0,0) when viewing the \`:ws/connection\` machine in Xray's Machine tab.

## Proposed fix

Match xstate's resolution semantics: when a keyword target doesn't exist at \`(parent-of source) + target\`, walk up the ancestor chain looking for a state whose tail name matches the target keyword. The simplest version:

\`\`\`clj
(defn- resolve-target-path
  [source-path target all-node-paths]
  (cond
    (= :same-state target) (vec source-path)
    (target-path? target)  (vec target)
    (keyword? target)
    ;; Try sibling-of-parent first (existing fast path); if no such
    ;; node exists in the graph, walk ancestors looking for the
    ;; nearest path whose final segment matches target.
    (let [sibling (conj (parent-path source-path) target)]
      (if (contains? all-node-paths sibling)
        sibling
        (or (find-ancestor-with-tail source-path target all-node-paths)
            sibling)))                                       ; fall through to original behaviour (preserves current diagnostic)
    :else nil))
\`\`\`

Requires \`all-node-paths\` (a set of every state path produced by the parse walk) to be in scope when edges are collected. The walk already produces this — just thread it through.

Alternative: ditch sibling-of-parent default entirely; always do full-ancestor scan. Cheaper to reason about, but might change semantics for ambiguous cases (state named \`:foo\` at multiple depths) — needs Spec 005 confirmation.

## Why the runtime works

The cofx / machines runtime presumably resolves these targets correctly at dispatch time — otherwise the testbed's \`:authenticating → :failed\` transition would error at runtime, and the testbed is in active use. Worth grepping \`implementation/machines/src/\` for the analogous resolution fn to copy its semantics into the projector.

## Acceptance

1. The \`:ws/connection\` machine's topology renders with all 6 states properly laid out (not stacked)
2. The \`active__failed\` synthetic id is not produced
3. Other cross-hierarchy machines (if any in testbeds/examples) also render correctly
4. Add a regression test under \`tools/machines-viz/test/.../layout_*\` with a 2-level machine containing a cross-hierarchy target

## Why isn't this caught by tests / why has it been latent

Most existing test machines are flat (single-level states) or strictly hierarchical (cross-hierarchy never used). Cross-hierarchy is allowed by Spec 005 but uncommon. The \`:ws/connection\` testbed exercises it deliberately for the \`:failed\` branch — that's exactly the surface this bug breaks. A test machine that intentionally mirrors this shape would catch the regression.

## Related

- **rf2-4lyvh** (sibling) — surfaced this error by adding console.error to the silent-swallow. Without that bead's logging this wouldn't have been diagnosable. The two should land in either order; this bead is the actual fix, rf2-4lyvh is the visibility improvement.
- Possibly **rf2-gpa9k** (G5 cross-hierarchy assert) — recent epic-close; may have intended to address this surface and missed the projector path.

## References

- Source bug: \`tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart/layout.cljc:148-153\` (resolve-target-path)
- Caller: same file, \`collect-state-edges\` (lines 165+)
- Repro machine: \`tools/xray/testbeds/testdeck/machine.cljs\` (\`:ws/connection\`, the \`:authenticating → :failed\` transition)
- Spec: Spec 005 §Targets / §Hierarchical states
- Discovery: pair-debug session 2026-05-25
notes:
## Resolved-via-testbed-fix (2026-05-25)

Closed as resolved-via-testbed-fix per the rf2-21rkg worker handover. The original premise — that `chart.layout/resolve-target-path` doesn''t handle cross-hierarchy keyword targets — was overturned: the runtime + spec + projector are all correct.

Per Spec 005 §Target resolution (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:1029-1030`):

- **Vector form** — absolute path from root; the recommended form for cross-level transitions.
- **Keyword form** — relative to the declaring state''s parent''s `:states` map.

The testdeck `:ws/connection` machine misused the keyword form for a cross-hierarchy site (`:target :failed` from `[:active :authenticating]`, where `:failed` is top-level), and the projector correctly transcribed the resulting non-existent path `[:active :failed]` into the edge endpoint id `active__failed`. ELK''s rejection was the symptom of the misuse.

Cross-reference: PR #2121 (rf2-21rkg) — single-line testbed fix to use the spec-recommended vector form `:target [:failed]`, plus a regression-guard CLJS unit test pinning the projection invariants for the testdeck machine.

Optional follow-up (separate bead): a registration-time validator that rejects keyword targets which don''t resolve to a state in the declaring state''s parent''s `:states` map would catch this class of misuse at registration time rather than at chart-layout time.
close_reason: Resolved via testbed fix (rf2-21rkg / PR #2121) — testbed misused keyword form at cross-hierarchy site; spec + runtime + projector all correct.

title: feat(re-frame2-pair-mcp): refine :runtime-not-preloaded diagnostic — distinguish preload-missing from wrong-build / dead-ws / wrong-runtime-target
description:
## Problem

\`discover-app\`'s structured \`:reason :runtime-not-preloaded\` + hint "Add the preload entry to your shadow-cljs.edn..." is misleading in most failure cases.

The probe (\`re-frame2-pair-mcp.tools.probe/runtime-preloaded?\`) checks \`js/globalThis.__re_frame2_pair_runtime\` via shadow's \`cljs-eval\`. If that returns anything other than \`true\`, the MCP server returns \`:runtime-not-preloaded\` with a hint that ASSUMES the preload is missing from the build config.

In practice, the probe can return false for many other reasons:

1. **Wrong build arg** — operator passed \`build :app\` but the running build is \`examples/step-deck\`; cljs-eval routes to the wrong build (no runtime), returns blank, probe reports false → wrong hint
2. **No browser tab connected** — shadow has no runtime to route the eval to; \`cljs-eval\` returns blank, probe reports false → wrong hint
3. **Browser ws disconnected** — shadow restarted between page load and probe; the tab's ws is dead even though the bundle is loaded with the marker
4. **Stale port file** — MCP server connected to a dead nREPL; eval responses are nonsensical → wrong hint (this was rf2-umoz2's territory but can still surface in edge cases)
5. **Wrong runtime selected** — multiple browser tabs connected to the same build; shadow picks a runtime that loaded BEFORE the preload was added

In all five cases, the operator gets the same misleading "add the preload to your shadow-cljs.edn" suggestion. During pair-debug 2026-05-25 this cost ~30 min of dead-end exploration: the preload was correctly configured, browser had the marker, but the MCP was talking to a dead shadow process.

## Discovery context

This was the single largest source of confusion in the 2026-05-25 pair-debug session. The user repeatedly verified the preload was present (in shadow-cljs.edn, in the browser via \`globalThis.__re_frame2_pair_runtime\`), but the MCP kept returning \`:runtime-not-preloaded\`. The actual failure varied: stale port file at the wrong CWD, MCP server holding a dead socket, build-id mismatch. None of those were "the preload is missing".

## Proposed fix

Before returning \`:runtime-not-preloaded\`, run a small diagnostic ladder. Each step is one nREPL round-trip; total cost ~50ms — acceptable for a failure path.

1. **Check nREPL connection alive** — \`(jvm-eval conn "1")\` — does it return 1?
   - No: \`:reason :nrepl-unreachable\` with port + hint to restart shadow
2. **Check shadow has the build** — \`(shadow.cljs.devtools.api/active-builds)\` — does build-id appear?
   - No: \`:reason :build-not-running\` with the list of running builds; suggest \`--build=<running-one>\` or shadow restart
3. **Check shadow has a runtime for that build** — \`(shadow.cljs.devtools.api/repl-runtimes :build-id)\` (or equivalent)
   - Empty: \`:reason :no-runtime-connected\` with hint to open the browser tab / refresh
4. **Probe the marker** — current check
   - false: \`:reason :runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing\` with the EXISTING hint (this is the case the current hint is for)

Each step short-circuits with a distinct \`:reason\` keyword and a specifically-actionable hint. The "fix the shadow-cljs.edn" suggestion only fires when we've confirmed (a) nREPL is reachable, (b) build is running, (c) runtime is connected, (d) marker is genuinely absent.

## Acceptance

For each of the five failure modes listed under "Problem", the operator gets a structured response whose \`:reason\` keyword and \`:hint\` distinguish the case from "preload missing" and name the actual root cause + a specific remediation step.

## References

- Source: \`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/probe.cljs\` (\`runtime-preloaded?\`, \`ensure-runtime!\`, \`preload-missing-hint\`)
- Shadow API used: \`shadow.cljs.devtools.api/active-builds\`, \`shadow.cljs.devtools.api/cljs-eval\`
- Repro session: pair-debug 2026-05-25 (~30 min of dead-end debugging)
- Predecessor in this area: rf2-umoz2 (#2105), rf2-3grub (#2109) — both improved DISCOVERY; this bead improves the DIAGNOSTIC when discovery succeeds but the probe fails
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2120
close_reason: #2120 — :runtime-not-preloaded 4-way diagnostic ladder (nrepl-unreachable / build-not-running / no-runtime-connected / runtime-loaded-but-preload-missing)

title: fix(machines-viz): chart's ELK layout swallows errors silently — all nodes fall back to (0,0)
description:
## Symptom

Open the Xray Machines tab against any registered machine (repro: \`:ws/connection\` in step-deck testbed at http://localhost:8031/counter). The state topology renders with EVERY node drawn at the same coordinate — all boxes stacked on top of each other, unreadable. No error in console, no "layout failed" indicator in the panel.

Discovered during pair-debug session 2026-05-25.

## Root cause

\`tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart.cljs:283-291\`:

\`\`\`clj
(let [input (->elk-input parsed direction layout-options)
      p     (try (.layout elk-instance input)
                 (catch :default _ nil))]              ;; (A) sync error swallowed
  (if (and p (.-then p))
    (-> p
        (.then (fn [result] (done-fn (elk-result->positions result))))
        (.catch (fn [_e] (done-fn nil))))               ;; (B) async error swallowed
    (done-fn nil)))
\`\`\`

Both \`catch\` clauses discard the error entirely. When ELK throws synchronously OR rejects async, \`done-fn\` is invoked with \`nil\`.

Callback at \`chart.cljs:484-487\`:

\`\`\`clj
(compute-layout! parsed direction layout-options
                 (fn [result]
                   (when result                         ;; nil → skip
                     (reset! layout-state result))))
\`\`\`

The \`when result\` guard skips the reset. \`layout-state\` stays at its initial \`{:positions {} :edge-points {}}\`. The projector renders every node at its default origin. **Result: all boxes stacked.**

## What's masked

The actual ELK error tells us WHY the layout failed for a specific machine — typically:
- Malformed input from the \`->elk-children\` projector for a particular shape
- Cycle in a graph that ELK's algo can't handle
- Invalid layout option combination
- ELK internal assertion failure

Right now operators see only the symptom (stacked boxes) and have no way to diagnose without adding logging themselves or stepping through with DevTools.

## Fix

Minimum: add \`(js/console.error "[mv-chart] ELK layout failed:" e)\` (or similar — match the project's logger convention) before both \`catch\` swallows.

Better: tee both errors into a single \`(report-layout-error! e)\` helper that:
1. Logs to console with enough context (machine-id, direction, node count, edge count)
2. Optionally surfaces a "layout failed — see console" overlay on the chart so the operator sees something other than stacked boxes
3. Stores the last error in a debug atom so eval-cljs callers can introspect it

## Why isn't this caught by tests

Layout is async, runs in the browser via JS-interop, and the tests under \`tools/machines-viz/test/\` mostly exercise the pure projector (\`projection/xyflow-graph\`, \`layout/parse-definition\`). The async layout glue + its error path are JS-interop-heavy and harder to unit test. Worth checking whether at least the sync-throw branch can be unit-tested with a stubbed \`elk-instance\` that throws on \`.layout\`.

## Repro

1. \`cd implementation\` + \`npx shadow-cljs watch examples/step-deck\`
2. Browser → http://localhost:8031/counter
3. Open Xray panel → Machine tab → focus the \`:ws/connection\` machine
4. Observe: all 6 state boxes (disconnected/active/connecting/authenticating/connected/failed) stacked at the same coordinate
5. Open DevTools console — no error visible (this bug is exactly the silence)

## References

- Source: \`tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/chart.cljs:283-291\` (compute-layout!)
- Callback: \`chart.cljs:484-487\` (the when-result guard)
- Layout-state init: \`chart.cljs:451\` (\`{:positions {} :edge-points {}}\`)
- Affected machine spec: \`tools/xray/testbeds/testdeck/machine.cljs\` (\`:ws/connection\`, 6 hierarchical states)
- Discovery: pair-debug session 2026-05-25

title: fix(cofx): five reg-cofx bodies use wrong arg shape — value lost, never reaches handler
description:
## Symptom (concrete repro)

Click the `+` button in the step-deck testbed counter. The `:counter/inc` event fires, `[:counter :value]` increments, but `[:counter :last-clicked]` stays `nil` forever despite the handler explicitly doing `(assoc-in [:counter :last-clicked] now)`. The cofx trace event for `:testdeck/now` fires at the right time (between event run-start and db-changed), the cofx hash is non-zero, no error is emitted — silently broken.

Discovered during a pair-debug session 2026-05-25 by tracing the cascade for `:counter/inc` and finding `[:counter :last-clicked]` absent from the db-after diff across every inc epoch.

## Root cause

Per re-frame.cofx/reg-cofx (implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:100-160), a cofx handler is called with the **interceptor context** as its first arg and must return the **updated context**. The conventional shape is `(assoc-in ctx [:coeffects <cofx-id>] value)` — there's an idiomatic helper `re-frame.interceptor/assoc-coeffect` (re-exported as `rf/assoc-coeffect` at core.cljc:1029) that does exactly this.

Five cofx handlers in the repo instead treat the arg as the coeffects map itself and `assoc` at the top level of it. Because the arg is actually the *context* (not coeffects), the value lands at `ctx[<cofx-id>]` (top of context) instead of `ctx[:coeffects][<cofx-id>]` (where event handlers read from). The handler's destructure of `:coeffects` then can't find the key — and the value is silently lost. No error fires because the cofx returns a "valid" context map (just with the value in the wrong place).

The correct re-frame.cofx/reg-cofx doc example (cofx.cljc:118-120):
```clj
(rf/reg-cofx :now
  (fn [ctx]
    (assoc-in ctx [:coeffects :now] (js/Date.))))   ; ← assoc-in [:coeffects :now]
```

## All affected sites

```
tools/xray/testbeds/testdeck/counter.cljs:56    :testdeck/now
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/cofx.cljc     :story/active-modes
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/cofx.cljc     :story/active-args
examples/reagent/realworld/http.cljs:135        :realworld/now
examples/reagent/realworld/auth.cljs            :auth.session/token
```

For reference, `examples/reagent/todomvc/db.cljs` (`:todo.storage/todos`) is written correctly — it serves as a working template.

## Recommended fix

Use the idiomatic API `rf/assoc-coeffect`:

```clj
;; Broken:
(fn cofx-testdeck-now [coeffects]
  (assoc coeffects :testdeck/now (.getTime (js/Date.))))

;; Correct (idiomatic):
(fn cofx-testdeck-now [ctx]
  (rf/assoc-coeffect ctx :testdeck/now (.getTime (js/Date.))))
```

The arg-rename (`coeffects` → `ctx`) is mandatory — the name was misleading. The body switches from `assoc` to `rf/assoc-coeffect`. For the 2-arity forms in story/cofx.cljc, the same shape applies — the second arg (the `inject-cofx`-passed value) is unchanged; only the first arg's name and the assoc target change.

## Acceptance

For each fixed cofx, the next dispatch that uses it (e.g. click `+` on the step-deck counter) should make the value visible to the handler's destructure. Verifiable via Xray Event panel (Coeffects section shows the value) or pair-debug epoch diff (the path the handler writes to now updates).

## Why this isn't caught by tests

These cofxs are silently-broken: cofx returns a "valid" context, no error fires, the handler runs (just with a nil binding), and downstream effects (db-update, etc.) still happen — the *value* that depended on the cofx is just wrong/nil. Unit tests that don't assert on the *cofx-derived field's value* miss it. Worth checking whether any existing tests cover these handlers and would have caught the bug — if not, add minimum-viable test per site.

## Possible deeper concern

The fact that five sites independently arrived at the wrong shape (across testbeds, story, and two examples) suggests the cofx API's calling-convention is easy to get wrong:
- `coeffects` as the parameter name in most user examples in re-frame v1 (where it actually was just the coeffects map in older versions of the cofx API)
- The `assoc` (vs `assoc-in [:coeffects k]`) seemingly works because no compile/runtime error fires
- No structural validation flags the wrong-place injection at registration time

Worth considering whether `reg-cofx` should warn/error on a cofx fn that *demonstrably* doesn't touch `[:coeffects]` — though that's hard to detect statically. A simpler intervention: a doc-only fix that makes `reg-cofx`'s docstring more emphatic about the calling convention + the `assoc-coeffect` helper. File as separate bead if pursued.

## References

- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:100-160` — `reg-cofx` registration + doc
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:118-120` — canonical correct example
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor.cljc:72-77` — `assoc-coeffect` helper
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1029` — `rf/assoc-coeffect` re-export
- `examples/reagent/todomvc/db.cljs` — correct cofx-body shape (reference)
- Discovery session: pair-debug 2026-05-25 against http://localhost:8031/counter
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2117 — 5 sites + 6th discovered (schema-violation testbed). Tests added/strengthened across xray testdeck, story cofx, realworld auth/tags, plus the schema-violation testbed observability.
close_reason: Merged #2117. reg-cofx arg-shape bug fixed at 6 sites (5 audit-known + 1 self-masking ::bad-counter found by worker sweep). All use rf/assoc-coeffect ctx <id> v per canonical doc example, arg rename coeffects→ctx. 5 new test files pin the contract: testdeck/now, story/active-modes + active-args, realworld/now + auth.session/token, schema_violation/::bad-counter. The self-masking ::bad-counter case: validator was reading nil and rejecting nil-as-not-pos-int; with fix it correctly catches -1. Chain to #2097: #2097 fixed the panel's display of cofxs; rf2-gg4dz fixes the underlying cofx-body shape so values actually reach handlers.

title: feat(xray): Handler panel B+ visual order — HANDLER→FLOWS→APP-DB CHANGES→FX + two pre-commit snapshots when flows fired (rf2-5t9h0 = B+)
description:

Rework the xray Handler/Event panel section ordering to match the framework's operational order, and surface the two pre-commit :db snapshots when flows fire.

## Order (most events — flow-less)
1 DISPATCH
2 COEFFECTS (only when user cofx injected — existing rf2-9dk9y fix)
3 EVENT HANDLER (show returned effects map incl. pending :db at t1)

[5] AFTER INTERCEPTORS (only when one ran with a ctx-delta — existing rf2-9dk9y fix)

There's been related work in #2097 cofx). Re-use existing trace surfaces where possible; if a new emit point is needed, file as a CORE follow-on bead — do not add the emit point in this PR.

title: spec(013-flows + Managed-Effects): record atomicity asymmetry rationale — considered + rejected 'commit past fx' alternative
description:
Mike-directed 2026-05-25. The atomicity contract — pre-commit transactional, post-commit best-effort — was confirmed today AND an alternative was explicitly considered + rejected (move commit boundary past fx so the whole event is all-or-nothing). The rationale belongs in /spec proper, not just in agent memory.

THE CONTRACT (already canonical post-#2098):
- Pre-install throw (cofx / handler / interceptor :after / flow) ⇒ deferred :db install does NOT happen. app-db unchanged. NO :db-changed. NO :fx. Clean abort.
- :db install = atomic commit boundary — irreversible.
- :fx throw post-install does NOT wind app-db back. side-effects already fired are not undone.

ALTERNATIVE CONSIDERED + REJECTED (Mike 2026-05-25):
'Maybe :db shouldn't commit until all :fx have succeeded — either it worked or it didn't.' Rejected because:
1. **Most :fx are irreversible.** :http-xhrio POST, :dispatch of further events, :local-storage-set, DOM mutations, navigation. Running fx then skipping :db commit on a later throw produces world-state ≠ app-db divergence — strictly worse than today (both reflect what happened, even with one fx blown up). The 'irreversible' set IS the set that motivated putting them in :fx in the first place.
2. **Async fx breaks composition.** :http-xhrio returns immediately; success/failure arrives async. To know 'all fx succeeded' you'd have to make the event itself async — breaks dispatch-sync, breaks the event-queue composition, widens every fx's contract to declare sync-vs-async success semantics.
3. **Three principled answers exist** (classic distributed-transaction problem): (a) optimistic local commit + compensating-action sagas; (b) two-phase commit (rare; needs sync prepare/commit in external effects); (c) accept the asymmetry. re-frame chose (c) — cheap, simple, predictable. Escape valve for fx needing rollback semantics = APPLICATION-LEVEL sagas / compensating events, paired with a state-machine tracking in-flight state.

SCOPE for the spec update:
1. **Canonical home: spec/013-Flows.md §Failure semantics** (already touched by #2098/rf2-4gh88) — add a 'Why this asymmetry?' subsection capturing the rationale above. Brief — call out the irreversibility constraint + the async-fx constraint + name the three principled answers + cite that (c) is the chosen path. Reference the saga escape valve.
2. **Cross-ref from spec/Managed-Effects.md** — short note + link from the :fx contract description: 'post-install :fx throws do NOT wind app-db back. See 013 §Failure semantics for rationale and saga escape-valve guidance.'
3. **Cross-ref from spec/002-Frames.md** if it describes the event-handling pipeline.
4. **Optional, low-priority**: an examples/migration note that points to a worked saga pattern (compensating event for HTTP POST). Don't author the example here; just cross-link if one already exists in the corpus, otherwise file a follow-on bead.

HOT-ZONES: spec/013-Flows.md + spec/Managed-Effects.md are hot-zone files per CLAUDE.md. No in-flight worker on either. SAFE.

Cite this bead in the new spec text so future readers find the design-trail. Cite Mike's 2026-05-25 ruling as the timestamp.

notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2111

Captures: (1) most fx are irreversible; (2) async fx would break composition (sync dispatch contract); (3) three principled answers (sagas / 2PC / accept asymmetry); re-frame chose 3; escape valve = app-level sagas/compensating events. Cross-refs from Managed-Effects §2 + 002-Frames §fx ordering. Cross-linked existing saga example at examples/reagent/realworld/favorites.cljs (:article/toggle-favorite + :article/favorite-rollback) and the realworld README + headless test. mkdocs --strict PASS.

title: upstream(claude-code): MCP roots/list method handler not implemented (issue #3315 closed not-planned)
description:
## Why this bead

We need Claude Code to actually implement `roots/list` so MCP servers can do generic, workspace-based project discovery (the design behind rf2-3grub). Without it, the MCP protocol primitive intended for exactly this purpose times out.

## What we found (rf2-3grub investigation, 2026-05-24)

- Claude Code advertises the `roots` capability in MCP `initialize`: `{"capabilities":{"roots":{}}}`.
- When an MCP server calls the `roots/list` request, no handler responds — the request times out after 5+ seconds.
- Upstream report: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/3315
- Status: **closed as not planned**. No alternative path offered, no roadmap commitment.
- Related compliance gap: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/31893 lists roots, list_changed, progress, sampling, messages, async as outstanding MCP gaps.
- May 2026 release notes (Releasebot, official changelog) make no mention of `roots/list` implementation work.
- Companion capability `elicitation/create` (server-to-user prompts) DID land in Claude Code 2.1.76 (2026-03-14) — so the 2+ branch of the rf2-3grub design is reachable; the 0/1 branches are not, because we can never get the candidate list without `roots/list`.

## Impact on re-frame2-pair-mcp

The rf2-3grub design becomes uncodable on its primary path: every Claude Code session would hit the timeout, then degrade to the umoz2 launch-args / HTTP-probe fallback anyway. We can implement the fallback layer, but the "proper generic solution" rf2-3grub is for is not deliverable until Claude Code ships `roots/list`.

## Options

1. **Wait** for upstream. No ETA. Issue is closed "not planned".
2. **File a new upstream issue** with the re-frame2-pair use case as motivation (different angle than #3315's original report — it focused on the capability/method mismatch; ours is the concrete workspace-discovery use case). May or may not move the needle.
3. **Interim ship** rf2-7d425-style HTTP port-range probing (currently closed as superseded). Generic across multi-shadow but still shadow-specific.
4. **Status quo** — umoz2 launch args + 9630 HTTP probe stay as the zero-config path.

## Decision needed (mayor)

Pick a path; rf2-3grub is currently **blocked** on this.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED — Mike-correction 2026-05-24. Original worker (rf2-3grub) anchored on upstream anthropics/claude-code#3315 being closed 'not planned', concluding roots/list unsupported. That conclusion is STALE: (1) issue was REOPENED 2026-01-07; (2) a working test was reported on Claude Code 2.1.39 in the issue thread; (3) Mike confirmed his local Claude Code is 2.1.150 (newer than 2.1.39 working build). roots/list is in fact supported. rf2-3grub is being re-anchored and re-dispatched to proceed with the optimistic implementation path. No upstream block.

title: feat(re-frame2-pair-mcp): MCP roots-based project discovery (proper generic solution)
description:
DESCRIPTION
## Why this bead

Two prior beads explored this problem:

- **rf2-umoz2** (in-flight) — `--project-dir` / `--http-port` / `--port-file` launch args. Operator verdict: "hardcoding in disguise; not the recommended UX". These remain in the codebase as **escape hatches** but should not be advertised as the normal path.
- **rf2-7d425** (open, blocked on umoz2) — auto-discover via HTTP probe at 9630..9635 + `/api/project-info` + elicit-if-ambiguous. Operator verdict: "still shadow-specific port-range guessing; not generic".

This bead is the **proper, generic solution**: use the MCP protocol's own `roots` capability so the MCP server learns the workspace from the client (Claude Code) — zero hardcoding, zero shadow-specific port probing, generic across MCP servers and future tools.

## Steps the MCP server takes

### Session boot (lazy — happens on first tool call)

1. **Call `roots/list` on the MCP client** to get the workspace roots Claude Code has opened (e.g. `[file:///C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2]`).
2. **Walk each root** looking for `shadow-cljs.edn` files (typical locations: at the root, at `<root>/implementation/`, or any subdir for monorepos).
3. **For each `shadow-cljs.edn` found**, look at the adjacent `.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port` file. If present → that's a candidate live shadow. If absent → shadow isn't running for that project; skip.
4. **Branch on count of candidates:**
   - **0 candidates** → return `{:reason :no-running-shadow-in-workspace :roots [...] :checked-edns [...] :hint "Start shadow-cljs watch <build> in one of these projects."}`. Accurate — we looked everywhere the user has opened.
   - **1 candidate** → attach silently.
   - **2+ candidates** → MCP `elicitation/create` request with each project's path as the choice. User picks. Cache the choice for the session.
5. **Connect** to the chosen project's nREPL via `<project-home>/.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port`. Cache `(project-home, socket)` for the session.

### Per-tool-call (after session boot)

6. **Re-read the port file** at the cached `project-home/.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port` before using the socket. If the port has changed → the cached socket is stale (shadow was restarted); close it and reconnect on the new port. Transparent to the agent.
7. **Run the tool's actual work** (e.g. `cljs-eval` for the runtime probe, then the actual tool body).

### Invalidation triggers (session cache resets)

8. **nREPL socket closes unexpectedly** → next tool call re-reads the port file (cheap path: same project).
9. **Port file is missing** at cached path → shadow may have shut down. Re-run steps 1–5 (full re-discovery).
10. **Operator-initiated re-attach tool call** → explicitly clear cache and re-run steps 1–5 (switch projects mid-session).

### Fallback if Claude Code doesn't surface `roots` or `elicitation`

11. **No `roots` support** → fall through to escape-hatch launch args (`--project-dir`, `--port-file`, `--http-port`) from rf2-umoz2. Without those, return `{:reason :workspace-discovery-unsupported :hint "Pass --project-dir or upgrade the MCP client."}`. The agent surfaces the hint.
12. **No `elicitation` support, 2+ candidates** → return `{:reason :ambiguous-shadow :candidates [...] :hint "..."}`. Agent (Claude) reads the candidate list, asks the user in chat, retries the tool with `:project-dir` arg.

## Why this is the right ceiling

- **Zero hardcoded paths** anywhere — not in `~/.claude.json`, not in launch args, not in source.
- **Zero shadow-cljs-specific port guessing** — the workspace tells us where to look.
- **Generic across MCP servers** — `roots` is the official MCP pattern; any future MCP server in this repo (or anywhere) facing the same CWD-discovery problem uses the same primitive.
- **Survives shadow restarts** transparently (per-tool port-file re-read).
- **Survives multi-project workspaces** (elicitation disambiguates).
- **Survives new clones / new machines / new contributors** — nothing to copy, nothing to configure.
- **Graceful degradation** when the client doesn't support the modern protocol features (falls through to umoz2's escape hatches).

## Investigation / open questions

- **Confirm Claude Code surfaces the MCP `roots` capability** to servers (`roots/list` request). If not — file upstream + ship rf2-7d425's HTTP-probe design as interim.
- **Confirm Claude Code surfaces `elicitation/create`** as a real user prompt. If not — the 2+ branch degrades to step 12 (agent fallback) — still works, just less polished.
- **Decide the workspace walk depth limit** — bounded shallow walk vs full recursive scan. Monorepos can have shadow-cljs.edn nested deep; need to avoid scanning node_modules / .git / target.

## Relationship to prior beads

- **Depends on rf2-umoz2** — escape-hatch launch args remain as the fallback path for clients that don't support `roots`.
- **Supersedes the design of rf2-7d425** — port-range probing is no longer the primary discovery mechanism. rf2-7d425 should be closed as superseded if this bead is accepted.

## References

- MCP `roots` capability: https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io (search "roots") — client capability exposing workspace directories
- MCP `elicitation/create`: 2025-06-18 spec — server-initiated user prompts
- Memory: `re-frame2-pair-mcp-nrepl-port-config-2026-05-18` — original problem statement and `--port-file` workaround
- Live session 2026-05-24 22:20 AUSEST where this design evolved through operator-driven critique of two prior designs

NOTES
Blocked on rf2-h0xq2: Claude Code does not implement MCP roots/list (issue #3315 closed not-planned). Primary path uncodable; mayor decides Wait / re-file upstream / interim rf2-7d425 / status-quo. Investigation: ai/findings/rf2-3grub-upstream-blocker-body.md

DEPENDS ON
  → ✓ rf2-h0xq2: upstream(claude-code): MCP roots/list method handler not implemented (issue #3315 closed not-planned) ● P2
  → ✓ rf2-umoz2: feat(re-frame2-pair-mcp): per-project nREPL port discovery via --project-dir (CWD-robust, multi-shadow-safe) ● P2

## RE-ANCHOR 2026-05-24 (Mike)

Prior worker (run on this bead) blocked-claimed roots/list was unsupported in Claude Code based on a stale auto-closed upstream issue (anthropics/claude-code#3315). That conclusion is WRONG:

- Issue #3315 was REOPENED 2026-01-07.
- A working-test comment exists on Claude Code 2.1.39.
- Mike's local Claude Code is **2.1.150** (newer than the confirmed-working build).

**Re-anchor and proceed.** The optimistic implementation path is the right path. roots/list IS supported. elicitation/create IS supported (worker's investigation confirmed this part). Build the design as specified above — no upstream block.
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2109 — roots-based discovery; live-verified end-to-end; 562 tests green

Per-tool-call port-file re-read for shadow-restart transparency. Cached (project-home, conn) with port-file-vanish invalidation. Precedence cascade now: (1) --port-file (rf2-3dbwh) → (2) $SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT → (3) MCP roots/list walk (NEW PRIMARY) → (4) shadow HTTP probe at 9630 (rf2-umoz2 fallback) → (5) CWD-relative scan (legacy). 24 unit tests + live-verify harness against SDK 1.29 confirms end-to-end protocol path. Re-anchored after prior worker's stale-issue 'upstream-blocked' verdict was operator-superseded (anthropics/claude-code#3315 was reopened 2026-01-07, working test on 2.1.39; Mike's CC 2.1.150 supports roots/list). The --port-file workaround in ~/.claude.json is now redundant but still wins as explicit override.

title: feat(re-frame2-pair-mcp): zero-config attach — auto-discover running shadow(s) via HTTP probe, elicit on ambiguity
description:
## Context — supersedes / extends rf2-umoz2 rf2-umoz2 added `--project-dir` / `--http-port` to make per-project nREPL discovery work when Claude Code launches the MCP server from a CWD that isn't the project root. That's an improvement over today's silent failure, but the operator's verdict on the design review: **any launch-time path arg is hardcoding in disguise**. The MCP server should figure out which shadow to attach to at runtime, not at config time. This bead is the next layer: **zero-config auto-attach**. ## Design — discover → branch on count → elicit if ambiguous On first tool call (and any later call after the cached attach times out): ### 1. Probe candidate shadow HTTP ports Try `GET http://localhost:

/api/project-info` for `p` in a small range (default `9630..9635` — covers the second/third concurrent shadows that fell back from 9630). Collect every responding shadow's `{:http-port :project-home :project-config :version}` map. The `/api/project-info` endpoint is live on shadow 3.x — confirmed by probing the running instance during the rf2-umoz2 design review (returned transit-encoded `[:project-home "C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\implementation" :project-config "...shadow-cljs.edn" :version "3.4.10"]`). ### 2. Branch on count | Running shadows | MCP behaviour | |---|---| | **0** | Return structured error `{:ok? false :reason :no-shadow-running :hint "Start shadow-cljs watch first."}`. No prompt — the agent surfaces the hint. | | **1** | Attach silently. The 90% case is free — no prompt, no config, no env var. | | **2+** | MCP `elicitation/create` request → client renders a multi-choice prompt: "Multiple shadow-cljs servers running. Which project?" listing each `:project-home`. Operator picks; MCP caches `(project-home, nREPL-port)` for the session. | ### 3. Derive nREPL port For the picked shadow: - Read `/.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port` (re-read per tool call so shadow restarts are absorbed transparently). - Connect. ### 4. Cache + invalidate Session-scoped cache. Invalidate on: - nREPL socket close (shadow restart with a new random port — re-read the port file). - The cached shadow's HTTP probe stops responding (shadow died — re-discover). - Explicit re-attach tool call (operator command to switch shadows mid-session). ## Fallbacks for elicitation-poor clients If Claude Code's MCP client doesn't surface `elicitation/create` as a real user prompt, the 2+-shadow case degrades to: - Return structured error `{:ok? false :reason :ambiguous-shadow :candidates [{:project-home "..."} {:project-home "..."}] :hint "Multiple shadows running; re-call with `:project-dir`."}`. - Agent (Claude) reads the candidates, asks the operator in chat, retries with `:project-dir` tool arg. So elicitation is the *preferred* UX but not load-bearing — it's a polish layer over a baseline that already works. ## Escape hatches preserved For power users / atypical setups: - `--http-port ` launch arg → MCP probes only that port (skip the 9630..9635 sweep). - `--port-file ` → existing escape hatch, kept for back-compat. - `:project-dir` tool arg → per-call override for ambiguity scenarios. ## Why this is the right ceiling - **Zero pre-config in the common case.** No paths in `~/.claude.json`. No env vars. No restart-after-edit dance. - **Survives shadow restarts.** Port file re-read on every tool call. - **Survives multi-shadow workflows.** Elicitation disambiguates; agent fallback for clients that don't. - **Survives new clones / new machines.** Nothing machine-specific to copy. - **Matches the operator's mental model.** "I started shadow; the MCP just works." ## Investigation / open questions - Confirm shadow-cljs's `/api/project-info` is stable across 3.x (probed on 3.4.10; check older versions in active use). - Confirm Claude Code's MCP client surfaces `elicitation/create` per the 2025-06-18 MCP spec. If not, file a separate request upstream and ship without the elicit layer (agent-fallback only). - Decide port-range default — 9630..9635 covers most multi-shadow cases; 9630..9640 is more permissive at the cost of slower discovery. ## References - Predecessor: **rf2-umoz2** (in-flight) — `--project-dir` / `--http-port` launch args. Likely lands first; this bead builds on it (the launch args remain as escape hatches, but stop being the recommended UX). - Memory: `re-frame2-pair-mcp-nrepl-port-config-2026-05-18` — captures the original CWD problem and the `--port-file` recommendation that became rf2-umoz2. - Shadow HTTP API: `tools/.../web/api.clj` upstream — `/api/project-info` handler. - Community reference: `Bigsy/shadow-cljs-mcp` (HTTP@9630 attach, single-shadow only); `bhauman/clojure-mcp` (`:project-dir` arg required).
notes:
2026-05-24 design-refinement (operator catch): the "0 running shadows" branch in §2 of the description is incomplete.

A shadow on a non-default HTTP port (e.g. `:http :port 9700` in shadow-cljs.edn — perfectly valid config) won't be found by the 9630..9635 probe, but IS running. Returning `:no-shadow-running` would mislead.

Refined branch logic:

| Probe result | Real situation | MCP behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| 0 ports in probe range respond | Either (a) no shadow is running, OR (b) shadow is configured on a non-default HTTP port | Return `{:reason :no-shadow-in-default-range :probed-ports [9630..9635] :hint "Either start shadow-cljs watch <build>, or pass `--http-port <n>` if shadow is configured on a non-default :http :port."}`. Don't claim "no shadow running" — we don't know that. |
| 1 port responds | One shadow running (default port range) | Attach silently. |
| 2+ ports respond | Multiple shadows running | Elicit / agent-fallback as already described. |
| Operator passed `--http-port <n>` | Skip the probe sweep; probe only that port | If it responds → attach. If not → `{:reason :shadow-http-unreachable :port n}` is unambiguous and accurate. |

Net effect: the "no shadow" diagnosis is only emitted when the operator has narrowed to a specific port AND it doesn't respond. Otherwise we report "didn't find any in the default range" with the actionable hint about non-default ports.

Worker should fold this refinement into the design before implementation.
close_reason: Superseded by rf2-3grub. rf2-3grub's design (MCP roots-based project discovery) is operator-preferred over rf2-7d425's design (shadow-specific HTTP port-range probing 9630..9635). rf2-3grub's own description explicitly states 'Supersedes the design of rf2-7d425'. The HTTP-probe foundation that rf2-7d425 would have built ALREADY lives in rf2-umoz2 (merged #2105) — single-port at 9630 with /api/project-info → :project-home. rf2-3grub will use roots/list as the primary discovery mechanism and fall back to umoz2's escape hatches if the client doesn't support roots.

title: feat(re-frame2-pair-mcp): per-project nREPL port discovery via --project-dir (CWD-robust, multi-shadow-safe)
description:
## Problem

re-frame2-pair-mcp can't find shadow-cljs's nREPL port when Claude Code launches the MCP server with a CWD that isn't the repo root. The current discovery cascade is:

1. `--port-file <path>` flag
2. `$SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT` env var
3. CWD-relative scan: `target/shadow-cljs/nrepl.port`, `.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port`, `.nrepl-port`

Claude Code spawns MCP servers with its own CWD (not the project's), so (3) silently misses. Without (1) or (2) configured, `discover-app` returns `:nrepl-port-not-found`, blocking every other tool. The MCP server's own nrepl.cljs docstring acknowledges this:

> An MCP server launched as a subprocess of the agent host (Claude Code / Cursor / Copilot) frequently has a cwd that is NOT the consumer project root — in that case the scan misses silently and only the env var or `--port-file` work.

`bhauman/clojure-mcp` hit the same wall and requires explicit `:port` / `:project-dir` args.

## Design constraint — multi-shadow concurrency

**Rejected: "auto-discover via fixed HTTP port 9630"**. shadow-cljs's web UI uses 9630 by default, but only ONE process can bind to it on a machine. Devs commonly run two shadow-cljs JVMs in two repos at once; the second falls back (9631) or fails. An MCP server hitting fixed 9630 would connect to whichever shadow grabbed it first — not necessarily the project the user wants to debug. Silent wrong-target is worse than today's `:nrepl-port-not-found`.

**Conclusion**: the MCP server cannot intuit which project to target. It must be **told** at launch — per-project config is unavoidable. The goal of this bead is to make per-project config ergonomic and durable across shadow restarts.

## Proposed fix — `--project-dir` as primary, `--http-port` as escape hatch

### Primary: `--project-dir <abs-path>`

The MCP server reads `<project-dir>/shadow-cljs.edn`, finds `:http :port` and (if present) `:nrepl :port`, and:

- If `:nrepl :port` is a fixed int → connect there directly (no port-file scan needed; survives shadow restarts).
- Else read the live `<project-dir>/.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port` (re-read on each tool call, so shadow restarts that re-randomise the port are picked up automatically).

Project-relative paths are stable forever — survives shadow restarts, doesn't depend on CWD, single source of truth (`shadow-cljs.edn`).

### Escape hatch: `--http-port <n>`

User passes shadow's HTTP port explicitly (knows it because they configured it). MCP server queries `http://localhost:<n>/api/<endpoint>` for the live nREPL port. Useful when there's no shadow-cljs.edn on disk (rare) or for ad-hoc setups.

### Precedence

`--port-file` > `$SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT` > `--http-port` > `--project-dir` > CWD-scan (existing back-compat).

### Per-repo MCP entries

For two re-frame2 repos open at once, the user adds two MCP server entries (`re-frame2-pair-projectA`, `re-frame2-pair-projectB`) each with its own `--project-dir`. Standard MCP pattern across the ecosystem — no special-case logic needed.

- Decide what `<project-dir>` resolves to when `:nrepl :port` is absent from shadow-cljs.edn — fall through to the project's port file path.
- Update README + docs/setup to make `--project-dir` the recommended config.

Per-repo MCP entry in `~/.claude.json`:
```json

  "C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/out/server.js",
  "--port-file",
  "C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/.shadow-cljs/nrepl.port"
]
```

For two repos open at once, two MCP entries, each with its own `--port-file`. Works today; just verbose.

Live pair-debug session 2026-05-24 22:20 AUSEST. Browser tab had the preload loaded (confirmed via `globalThis.__re_frame2_pair_runtime` showing fresh session-id after Ctrl+F5); shadow runtime green-dot connected at http://localhost:9630/runtimes; MCP server was silently scanning a non-existent path and reporting `:runtime-not-preloaded` (misleading — the runtime IS preloaded; the MCP server just couldn't reach the right nREPL). Multi-shadow constraint surfaced when operator asked "what happens if shadow runs in two repos?".

- Community pattern (HTTP@9630): https://github.com/Bigsy/shadow-cljs-mcp — works for single-shadow case only

title: decide(xray): Event-panel visual order — keep Figma 'HANDLER → DB CHANGES → FLOWS → FX' or swap to operational 'HANDLER → FLOWS → DB CHANGES → FX'
description:
Mike-flagged in rf2-hm4gi delta audit. The Xray Event-panel currently renders sections in the Figma re-skin order (rf2-xawwb, post-#2089):

  1 DISPATCH · 2 COEFFECTS · 3 EVENT HANDLER · 4 APP-DB CHANGES · 5 FLOWS · 6 AFTER INTERCEPTORS · 7 FX

But the framework's operational order is:

  HANDLER (writes pending :db) → FLOWS (reshape pending :db) → ATOMIC COMMIT (db-changed emit) → FX

So in real time-order: FLOWS run BEFORE the diff exists (the diff is the post-commit observable). The current panel shows the resulting diff FIRST and then attributes it to flows that contributed — a 'result-then-attribution' framing.

The honest audit read: the panel's display order IS inconsistent with the framework's actual operation order. A new user learning the framework via Xray could plausibly conclude that flows fire AFTER the commit (because they're displayed after APP-DB CHANGES). The atomicity contract — load-bearing-worth-teaching ('flows are part of the same atomic write as the handler') — is OBSCURED by this visual order.

The docstring at tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/event_detail.cljs:1299-1305 acknowledges the tension with a hedge paragraph.

THREE COHERENT POSITIONS (Mike to pick):

A. Keep the Figma order (status quo). Diff-leads-attribution-follows.
   pros: diff is the user's mental anchor (what did the event DO?); flows show as attribution; matches authority Figma.
   cons: teaches a wrong framework mental model; docstring hedge is the workaround.

B. Swap to operational order: HANDLER → FLOWS → APP-DB CHANGES → FX.
   pros: visual order matches operational order; new users absorb atomicity contract for free; framework correctness foregrounded.
   cons: deviates from Figma authority.

C. Keep Figma order BUT add stronger visual signalling. e.g. an inline note BELOW the APP-DB CHANGES header: 'These are the post-flow committed changes. See FLOWS below for which flows contributed which slots.'
   pros: preserves Figma; minimises confusion.
   cons: signal is text-only; doesn't fix root mental-model gap.

Audit's read (not a decision): framework's atomicity contract is the rarest+most-load-bearing thing about this feature; sacrificing visual signal of it to match a Figma drawn BEFORE the contract was pinned (rf2-9eca7 originally placed FLOWS BEFORE DB CHANGES, then #2089 reverted to Figma order — the Figma surface predates Mike's 2026-05-24 atomicity decision) feels like an inversion of priorities. A is the safe vote; B is the correct vote.

Files involved:
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/event_detail.cljs:1345-1352 (candidates vector — section order)
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/event_detail.cljs:12-31 + 1287-1311 (docstrings)
- tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/event_detail_cljs_test.cljs:851 (test pinning current order: flows-step-sits-after-db-changes-before-fx)
- spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md §2.2 (Figma authority)

Found in delta-audit rf2-hm4gi (Shape-3); MED priority because user-facing tool that teaches the framework via its UI.
close_reason: DECIDED 2026-05-25: B+. Mike voted: 'B+ Swap + show two snapshots when flows fire (t1 post-handler + t2 post-flow); collapses cleanly when no flows (most events) → reads as B for those.' The panel will render HANDLER → FLOWS (only when fired) → APP-DB CHANGES → FX, with HANDLER showing the returned effects map (incl. t1 pending :db) and FLOWS showing the t1→t2 diff. AFTER INTERCEPTORS step also conditional on contribution. Flow-less events read as the simpler B shape. Impl bead being filed separately.

title: test(integration): routing × flows AND http × flows × cancellation atomicity coverage gaps
description:
rf2-vug0k (#2072) added 4 cross-subsystem flows integration tests but two of the compositions named in rf2-hm4gi's audit-Q5 list remain unpinned end-to-end:

COVERED (existing in implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/flows_integration_test.clj):
- machines × flows (machine-multi-microstep-macrostep-then-single-flow-eval)
- schemas × flows (flow-output-schema-failure-installs-then-rolls-back-whole-db + flow-throw-aborts-event-no-db-changed-no-partial-commit)
- SSR × flows (flow-augmented-value-renders-under-ssr-sync-drain)
- child-dispatch × flows (each-child-dispatch-gets-its-own-independent-flow-eval)

GAPS:
1. routing × flows. A (rf/dispatch [:rf.route/navigate ...]) (or a popstate-driven navigation) is a normal event that drains through the same chain — flows transform the pending :db after route-slice writes. A regression that altered the order of route-internal interceptors vs the flow transform could pass the 'flow output reads :rf/route slice' use case silently. Add a deftest that registers a flow whose :inputs overlap [:rf/route] and asserts the flow output reflects the post-navigation route.

2. http × flows × cancellation. A :rf.http/cancel (or auto-cancellation from :rf.http/managed's dedup path) emits per-request events that drain through the chain. A flow over [:rf.http/in-flight ...] should see the cancelled state atomically on a flow-augmented db install. Pin that a cancellation event's flow re-eval observes the cleared :in-flight slot in the SAME install (not the next event).

Both deftests can live in implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/flows_integration_test.clj (same classpath rationale — ssr/deps.edn already pulls routing + http where needed). ~60 LoC each.

Found in delta-audit rf2-hm4gi (Shape-3); MED severity — these compositions were audited SOUND by rf2-ytqzi but the audit acknowledged the lack of permanent regression tests, and rf2-vug0k closed four of six with these two remaining.

Gates: ssr 236/815 PASS, http 265/1404 PASS, npm test:cljs PASS, clj-kondo + splint clean.

title: fix(re-frame2-pair): eval-cljs returns misleading {:ok? true :value nil} when target build has no live runtime — fail loud
description:
REPRO (this session): ran skills/re-frame2-pair/scripts/eval-cljs.sh against the live step-deck testbed WITHOUT setting SHADOW_CLJS_BUILD_ID. The shim defaults the build to 'app' (per ops.clj), but the running shadow-cljs watch is build 'examples/step-deck'. Every read returned {:ok? true :value nil} — including (count ...), which can NEVER return nil. discover-app worked (it was passed --build=examples/step-deck) but standalone eval-cljs silently evaluated against a non-running/wrong build and reported SUCCESS with a nil value. Cost ~30min of dead-end debugging because :ok? true is indistinguishable from a genuine nil.

ROOT CAUSE: the eval path does not verify a live re-frame2-pair runtime exists for the resolved build before eval'ing, and treats 'no value' as :ok? true :value nil instead of an error.

FIX: preflight the runtime sentinel before eval. ops.clj ALREADY has a runtime-loaded? probe (js/globalThis.__re_frame2_pair_runtime). Wire it into the eval op: if the sentinel is absent for the resolved build, return {:ok? false :reason :no-runtime-for-build :build <id> :running-builds [...] :hint "pass --build=<running-build> or set SHADOW_CLJS_BUILD_ID; the default 'app' build is not running"} — NEVER :ok? true :value nil for a runtime-absent eval. Bonus: enumerate the running shadow-cljs build ids in the error so the operator immediately sees the right --build. Apply the SAME guard to the MCP server's eval-cljs tool (tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/) since the bash shim is deprecated in favour of it — both must fail loud. Add a test for the runtime-absent path. Isolated surface (ops.clj + the MCP eval tool); no redesign coupling.
notes: SCOPE: NOT testbed-specific — general footgun. The testbed exposed it only because its build id is 'examples/step-deck' (!= the default 'app'). ANY re-frame2 app whose build id isn't 'app', or any build missing the runtime preload, triggers the same silent {:ok? true :value nil}. ENHANCEMENT (general, fold into the fix): eval-cljs should AUTO-DETECT the running shadow-cljs build instead of blindly defaulting to 'app' — discover-app already detects it. If exactly one build is running, use it; if multiple, error listing them. Combined with the fail-loud runtime-sentinel preflight, this removes the footgun entirely so the operator never has to know/set --build. Both the bash shim (ops.clj) and the MCP server eval tool should share this resolution+preflight logic.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2044 — fail-loud :no-runtime-for-build + auto-detect running build, shared across MCP (probe/eval_cljs/wire) + bash shim (ops.clj). Tests: new eval_cljs_test.cljs (9 cases) + conformance fixture + 4 shim tests. Gates: MCP 510/0, shim 11/0, conformance flag-gates+e2e GREEN, clj-kondo 0 errors.

title: Substrate: :rf.view/rendered missing :deref-subs (spec'd, absent live) — needed for Causa Views per-view reason + shared-sub detection
description:
## Summary

The `:rf.view/rendered` trace event is **spec'd to carry a `:deref-subs` list** (the set of
subscriptions a view read during that render) but **does not carry it in the live build**.
This data is required for two Causa Views-tab features.

## Spec vs live

- **Spec 009 §`:rf.view/rendered`** (rf2-9hoos): the after-render marker carries cascade
  attribution + per-view ACTION/REASON data, including **`:deref-subs`** (the per-render
  deref sink, capped at 100/cascade) and `:mount?`. The `:deref-subs` is explicitly what
  makes the re-render reason PER-VIEW.
- **Live (parallel-frames, post-`:rf.*`-migration):** `:rf.view/rendered` tag keys are only
  `[:rf.view/render-key :rf.view/id :frame :rf.view/mount?]` — **no deref-subs** (under any
  spelling). 11 rendered events sampled.

## Why it matters (blocks two Views-tab features)

Per `ai/prompt/causa-ui-figma-brief.md` (Views tab):
1. **Per-view "reactive vs parent re-render" reason.** To classify a re-render as *reactive*
   (a sub the view derefs changed) vs *parent re-render* (structural), you intersect the
   view's `:deref-subs` with the cascade's value-changed subs. Without `:deref-subs` the
   reason can't be computed per-view.
2. **Shared-subscription detection** ("which views read sub X"). The only available link is
   the sub-side `:rf.sub/reader-render-key`, which names just the **triggering** view of a
   recompute — not all readers, and not unchanged subs a view also reads. So "this sub feeds
   views A, B, C" needs the per-view `:deref-subs` lists (or sub-cache reader introspection).

## Verify first

The sampled `:rf.view/rendered` was a **mount** (`:rf.view/mount? true`). Confirm
`:deref-subs` is **genuinely absent** vs. only-emitted-on-re-renders (not mounts) before
fixing — sample a non-mount re-render (e.g. click `+` so `counter-view` re-renders without
remounting) and re-check the tags.

Also check whether the recent `:rf.*` migration (rf2-y4qpy) dropped/renamed the slot, vs it
never having been implemented — the spec'd key predates the migration.

## Fix

Emit `:deref-subs` on `:rf.view/rendered` from the substrate view wrapper (the
frame-aware-view render wrapper that already emits this op), namespaced consistently
(`:rf.view/deref-subs`), capped per spec (100/cascade with the `-cap-reached` marker). Then
wire Causa's Views/Reactive consumer to read it for the per-view reason + shared-sub edges.

## Files

- Substrate emit: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views*` (the registered-view render
  wrapper that emits `:rf.view/render` / `:rf.view/rendered`).
- Spec: `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §`:rf.view/rendered`; `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`.
- Consumer: `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/reactive_panel_subs.cljs` (+ the
  Views panel) — reads the per-view deref set.

## Acceptance

- A non-mount `:rf.view/rendered` carries `:rf.view/deref-subs` (the subs that view derefed),
  capped per spec.
- Causa's Views tab can compute per-view reactive-vs-parent reason and shared-subscription
  edges from it.
close_reason: PR #1982. STEP-1 verification: :rf.view/deref-subs was NOT missing — fully implemented in #1941 (rf2-9hoos), carried through the :rf.* migration (#1973), spec'd in 009, and already consumed by Causa for the per-view reactive-vs-parent reason. The bead's empty sample was a mount of a sub-less view (absent by spec). Capture mechanism (per-render *view-deref-sink* + subscribe-side push) exists in full. The one genuine outstanding feature — shared-subscription detection ('which views read sub X') — is added in #1982 as a pure consumer (sub-readers projection + 'read by' column on the L1/L2 sub tables). Gates: node-test 4127 tests/12604 assertions 0 failures; causa-feature-gate 13 scenarios 0 failures.

title: Findings: Replicant vs Reagent comparison (rendering substrate angle)
description: Compare Replicant (https://replicant.fun/learn/) against Reagent as CLJS rendering layers, framed for re-frame2's substrate-adapter model (Reagent/UIx/Helix are all React-based; Replicant is non-React, data-driven, no virtual-DOM-via-React). Cover: programming model (hiccup/data-driven vs reactive atoms+ratoms), rendering mechanism (Replicant's own diff vs React reconciler), lifecycle/effects, event handling (data-driven vs fns), perf characteristics, server-rendering, ecosystem maturity, and — most importantly — what a re-frame2 Replicant adapter would look like vs the existing Reagent adapter (what the substrate contract would need, where it fits/clashes). Output: ai/findings/2026-05-23-replicant-vs-reagent.md (local-only).
close_reason: Findings doc written: ai/findings/2026-05-23-replicant-vs-reagent.md. Verdict: Replicant adapter feasible but not a drop-in; crux is reactivity (top-down whole-frame vs per-view). Spike-bead recommendation surfaced to Mike (decision).

title: Promote bare :rf.event operation to :rf.event/run-start + :rf.event/run-end (uniform :rf.<family>/<op> + fix 009 line-171 ref)
description: Naming-quality finding (audit rf2-og6lp). The cascade run-start/run-end markers are emitted with the BARE family keyword as the operation: (trace/emit! :rf.event :rf.event {... :rf.trace/phase :run-start}) at router.cljc:893 and :run-end at router.cljc:825. This is the ONLY operation in the whole :rf.* vocabulary that is a bare :rf.<family> keyword rather than :rf.<family>/<op> — every other op is :rf.event/dispatched, :rf.sub/run, :rf.fx/do-fx, :rf.view/render, etc. Spec 009 §':op-type versus :operation' promises :operation is 'typically a namespaced keyword like :rf.event/dispatched'; the bare form forces consumers to branch (and (= op :rf.event) (= phase :run-start)) instead of (= operation :rf.event/run-start). INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY: 009 line 363 documents the bare emit, but 009 line 171 (the :rf.view/cause-event-id tag row) refers to ':rf.event/run-start event-id' — an operation that is NEVER emitted (grep-confirmed: zero :rf.event/run-start|run-end in impl), so a tool author reading that row hunts for a non-existent op. FIX: emit :rf.event/run-start and :rf.event/run-end as real operations (keep or drop :rf.trace/phase as desired). Bounded change: 2 emit sites (router.cljc) + phase-branching consumers + 009 docs (lines 363, 471, 490 'bare :rf.event op' notes; line 171 ref becomes correct as-written) + any fixtures. Payoff: removes the only bare-operation special case, makes :operation uniformly :rf.<family>/<op>, fixes the line-171 spec/impl mismatch. Findings doc: ai/findings/2026-05-23-keyword-naming-quality-audit.md (local-only).
close_reason: Promoted bare :rf.event op to real :rf.event/run-start + :rf.event/run-end operations (op-type stays :rf.event). Kept :rf.trace/phase (still load-bearing for :rf.event/db-changed :rollback). Fixed Spec 009 line-171 mismatch. Migrated all consumers (projection domino-bucket, epoch capture/state/listeners, pair runtime, 63 conformance fixtures, Causa/Story/pair-mcp tests, spec 009/013 docs). All gates green. PR #1981.
