title: Causa Add-filter dialog: strip to Only-include/Filter-out by event-id — remove the Match-scope section (event-args/source-coord/tags) + its plumbing
description:
## Problem

Causa's "Add filter" dialog (`filters/edit_popup.cljs`, `popup-view` ~257-384) shows more
than it should. It has:
- **Mode** — in/out radios. KEEP (these are "Only include" / "Filter out").
- **Pattern** — the event-id pattern input. KEEP.
- **Match scope** — 4 checkboxes: `event-id` (always-on), `event-args`, `source-coord`,
  `tags`. The last three are **non-functional** — the matcher only honours `:event-id`
  and the popup itself labels them "(pre-alpha: stored, not yet matched)". This is
  speculative future-widening scaffolding shipped in the UI.

Realistically the only filter is **filter out / only include, by event-id**. Everything to
do with args / source-coord / tags should be removed.

## Desired

The dialog reduces to exactly:
- **Mode**: two clear options — "Only include" (`:in`) and "Filter out" (`:out`). (Ensure
  `mode-radio` labels read as words, not terse "in"/"out", if they don't already.)
- **Pattern**: the event-id matcher input (keyword · glob `:foo/*` · namespace · substring).
- Footer: Cancel / Add (Apply) / Delete-when-editing.

No "Match scope" section. Event-id is the implicit, only scope.

## Remove (no shims — pre-alpha; don't ship non-functional UI)
- The **Match scope** section in `popup-view` (edit_popup.cljs ~344-357).
- `scope-checkbox` fn (~224-255) and its `rf-causa-edit-popup-scope-*` testids.
- The `:rf.causa/edit-popup-toggle-scope` event.
- Scope-widening data scaffolding in `pill->draft` (~194-199) and `draft->pill`
  (~169-189): drop the `:scope` plumbing — pills are implicitly event-id; don't store or
  read `:scope`. (Confirm `matcher.cljc` / `typed_predicates.cljc` don't rely on `:scope`;
  they already only match event-id.)
- Update the ns docstring + ASCII diagram (the "Match scope" box, ~14/24-30).

## Note
The dialog already only creates **event-id-pattern** pills — there is no machine /
http-correlation / fx KIND selector in this dialog (those typed-predicate kinds arrive via
other paths). So this change is purely removing the scope checkboxes + their plumbing, not
a kind-selector removal.

## Tests
Update/remove edit-popup tests asserting the scope checkboxes / `edit-popup-toggle-scope`.
Keep mode + pattern + apply/cancel/delete coverage.

## Coordination
Light overlap with rf2-4vp5j (ribbons redesign) — that relocates the add-pill TRIGGER into
the events ribbon but doesn't restructure this dialog's body. Different files
(edit_popup.cljs vs shell.cljs/pills.cljs), so largely independent; just avoid both
editing edit_popup.cljs at once.

## Acceptance
Open "Add filter" → only Mode (Only include / Filter out) + Pattern + footer. No args /
source-coord / tags / scope options anywhere.

Pill shape now {:pattern}. Updated spec 018/020. Gates green: test:cljs 0 failures, causa-feature-gate 13/13.

title: Causa nav buttons: properly disable ◀/▶/⏭ at boundaries (visual inert + disable ⏭ at head), not just a not-allowed cursor
description:
## Problem

Causa's L2 nav buttons (`◀ ▶ ⏭`, `ribbon-nav-cluster`, shell.cljs:444-498) don't *look*
disabled at the boundaries even though clicks are blocked. Two issues:

1. **Weak disabled visual (◀ and ▶).** Both already set the native `:disabled`
   attribute (`:disabled (boolean at-tail?)` on `◀`, `(boolean at-head?)` on `▶`), so
   clicks ARE blocked. But the only disabled signal is `cursor: not-allowed` (the
   "red-circle") plus a faint `:text-tertiary` colour — the border and background are
   unchanged, so the button still reads as clickable. Give it a proper disabled
   appearance (dim background + dim border + reduced opacity + no hover affordance) so
   the inert state is visually obvious, not just a cursor change.
   - `◀` (prev/backwards) → disabled on the FIRST event (`at-tail?`).
   - `▶` (next/play-forward) → disabled on the LAST event (`at-head?`).

2. **`⏭` (fast-forward) is never disabled — should be disabled on the last event.** The
   component currently documents `⏭` as "never disabled; pressing it always snaps focus to
   head + resumes LIVE" (no `:disabled`, no `at-head?` check). On the last event there is
   nothing to fast-forward to, so it should be disabled (functionally + the same proper
   visual) like `▶`.
   - NUANCE to resolve: `⏭` also *resumes LIVE*. If the user is at head but PAUSED,
     `⏭` is not a pure no-op. Decide: disable `⏭` only when `at-head?` AND already live
     (so a paused-at-head user can still resume), or disable whenever `at-head?`. Lean
     "at-head? AND live" so resume stays reachable; confirm with Mike if unsure.

## Desired
All three buttons are *properly* disabled at their boundary — visually inert (greyed,
no hover, no pointer affordance) AND non-interactive — rather than looking active with a
not-allowed cursor.

## Files

  `btn-style` / `dim` styles (462-475) and the three `:button`s; the `at-head?`/`at-tail?`
  flags arrive as props (computed at shell.cljs ~718-722 / passed at ~1473). Add an
  `at-head?` gate to `⏭` (`rf-causa-nav-head`).
- Keep `aria-disabled` in sync with `:disabled` for all three.

## Coordination
Overlaps with **rf2-4vp5j** (top-ribbons redesign), which MOVES `ribbon-nav-cluster` from
the chrome ribbon into the new events ribbon. Same component + file → sequence, don't
parallel. Cleanest: fold this fix into rf2-4vp5j (the nav cluster is being relocated
there anyway), or land this first and have rf2-4vp5j carry it along.

## Acceptance
- On the first event: `◀` is visibly disabled (inert styling) and unclickable.
- On the last event: `▶` and `⏭` are visibly disabled and unclickable.
- Disabled styling is unmistakable (not just a not-allowed cursor).

title: Causa spec drift: reconcile tools/causa/spec with implementation after this session's changes (epoch-per-event, trace rework, filter/persistence, tool-frame gate, machines, ribbons redesign, :rf.* migration)
description:
## Problem

The Causa spec (`tools/causa/spec/`, 22 docs) has drifted from the implementation after
this session's wave of changes. Per the project's prime directive â€” *the spec is the
artefact; the code is downstream* â€” this drift is significant: the normative Causa spec no
longer matches what Causa does, and several docs describe panels/filters/trace semantics
that have been reworked or removed. This bead tracks the reconciliation; it likely warrants
promotion to an epic with per-doc / per-driver children when scheduled.

## Drift drivers â†’ affected spec docs

| Change (bead / PR) | What changed | Stale spec docs |

| Machines parity (epic rf2-nrrtb: #1953/#1957/54s5a) | xstate/Stately-level topology rendering + on-chart simulation | 003-Machine-Inspector |
| Ribbons redesign + frame-as-view-scope + mode dropdown + X-fix (rf2-4vp5j / rf2-fq491) | chrome ribbon (Frame + Dynamic/Static dropdowns, âš™/âœ•) + events ribbon; frame is a VIEW SCOPE not a filter; mode-pill â†’ dropdown; âœ• actually closes | 007-UX-IA, 018-Event-Spine, 021 (Â§3 frame dropdown, Â§4 event list, ribbon) |

## Notable specifics to fix

title: Causa: fix the ✕ close button (close-shell sets a flag but never hides the shell)
description:
The Causa shell `✕` close button does nothing.

## Root cause
The button (`shell.cljs:662-667`, `rf-causa-icon-close`) dispatches `:rf.causa/close-shell`
correctly. But the handler (`registry.cljs:420-425`) only does `(assoc db :close-requested?
true)` — a reactive flag whose comment claims "mount.cljs reads the slot to drive the
CSS-only hide", yet **nothing consumes it**. So clicking `✕` sets a flag and nothing hides.

`mount.cljs` already has the real hide mechanism: `hide-shell` (~535), the `display:none`
set (~215), and the visibility toggle (~546). The event is simply not wired to it.

## Fix
Wire `:rf.causa/close-shell` to actually hide the shell — e.g. make it a `reg-event-fx`
that fires a `:rf.causa/hide-shell` effect calling `mount/hide-shell`, OR have `mount.cljs`
observe `:close-requested?` and hide when true. Keep the reactive flag so tests can assert
the round-trip. Verify the `Ctrl+Shift+C` keybinding path closes too.

## Scope / independence
Touches `registry.cljs` + `mount.cljs` only (the `shell.cljs` button itself needs no
change). **Independent of the ribbons redesign and the rf2-swclw gate** — it does not touch
`frame_switcher.cljs`, `filters*`, or the shell ribbon layout — so it can land immediately.

## Files
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/registry.cljs:420-425` (`:rf.causa/close-shell`)
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/mount.cljs` (~215 display:none, ~535 hide-shell, ~546 toggle)
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/shell.cljs:662-667` (the button — likely unchanged)

## Tests
Causa unit test asserting the close round-trip actually drives the hide (not just the flag);
keep/extend the existing `:close-requested?` assertion.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1968: :rf.causa/close-shell was a reg-event-db that only set the :close-requested? flag with nothing consuming it. Now a reg-event-fx that sets the flag AND fires :rf.causa.fx/hide-shell (registered in mount.cljs via install-fx!), which calls mount/close! — the real CSS-only hide. Re-opens via the existing open! mechanism. 2 new CLJS unit tests prove the round-trip. Gates green: test:cljs 0 fail, causa-feature-gate 13/13.

title: Causa typed pills (:machine/:http/:fx) causal-parent matching under epoch-per-event
description:
Parent: rf2-jvghz (defect #2). Design question.

Under epoch-per-event, a :machine typed IN-pill (filters/typed_predicates.cljc) matches only the machine's OWN epoch/cascade, not the parent event that spawned the machine transition. Same shape applies to :http-correlation and :fx typed pills: each matches the cascade carrying its tag, but loses the causal-parent relationship now that each event is its own epoch.

Design how typed pills relate cascades to their causal parents under epoch-per-event so 'filter to this machine' shows the spawning event's cascade too (not just the machine's bare epoch). Touches typed/cascade-matches-* predicates and the cascade projection's parent linkage. Defect #2 of rf2-jvghz — separate from the indicator (defect #1, landed).

title: Causa L2 filters: decide persist-vs-reset of filter pills/frame-pin across reload (design, Mike)
description:
Parent: rf2-jvghz (defect, persist question). Design decision for Mike.

Currently Causa persists the IN/OUT filter pills (localStorage key re-frame2.causa.filters.v1), the frame pin (re-frame2.causa.frame-switcher.v1), and the mute set (causa.spine.muted-event-ids) across reload. After the epoch-per-event merges this surfaced as a confusing 'tool looks broken on reload' symptom: persisted filters silently suppressed L2 rows. rf2-jvghz defect #1 landed a prominent 'N events hidden by filters' indicator + one-click Clear so the suppression is now VISIBLE, but it did NOT change WHETHER filters persist.

Decide: should filter pills / frame-pin / mutes persist across reload at all, or reset to unfiltered on each fresh session (first-session honesty)? Options: keep-all-persist (current, now with the indicator); reset-frame-pin-only; reset-all; per-surface policy. Mike's call.
notes: DECISION (Mike, 2026-05-22 — go): RESET transient filters to unfiltered on every page load — the event IN/OUT pills (filters/persistence.cljs), muted-event-ids (mount.cljs:451 hydrate), and frame-pin (frame_switcher.cljs). PERSIST only durable view prefs (density/layout). Rationale: an inspector's prime directive is to show the truth; a fresh load must never silently carry a stale filter (the trap that fooled even the author). The #1962 hidden-count indicator stays as the in-session safety net. QUEUED: dispatch after rf2-2qaqh merges (shared mount.cljs surface — sequence to avoid conflict).
close_reason: Landed in PR #1967: reset transient filters (IN/OUT pills + muted-event-ids + frame pin) to unfiltered on every page load via a single ::reset-transient-filters first-mount hook that clears the stale localStorage slots; durable Dynamic/Static mode still restores. title: Causa self-instrumentation saturates the shared raw trace buffer (:rf/causa-frame events evict all app events)
description:
Observed (parallel-frames, live): the raw re-frame.trace.tooling/trace-buffer was 100% :rf/causa-frame events (200/200; :n-app 0) — Causa's own UI :sub/run + :view/render trace emissions had evicted EVERY application event from the shared ring. Causa keeps its own cascade accumulator (so its L2 cascades survive), but ANY other consumer reading the raw buffer sees only Causa noise — re-frame2-pair's raw-buffer reads during this session returned zero app events for exactly this reason. Also a heap-churn concern.

EXPECTED: the inspector tool's own reactivity should not flood the buffer it inspects. Causa already filters :rf/causa from CASCADES; it should also be excluded from trace EMISSION (tool frames produce no trace), or trace should be per-frame / the tool frame should run with trace disabled.

FIX DIRECTION (decide): (a) gate trace emission off for tool frames (:rf/causa) entirely — cleanest; (b) per-frame trace ring; (c) raise the cap. Prefer (a).

ALSO CHECK: observed buffer length was 200 while Causa settings reported :buffer {:trace-buffer/keep 1000}. Possible separate cap/config discrepancy worth a glance.

Files: re-frame.trace emit gating (implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/*), Causa frame setup (tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/mount.cljs), interop/debug-enabled? gating.

Tool frames (:rf/causa) emit no trace via canonical trace/frame-trace-disabled? predicate populated by reg-frame; emit!/emit-error! short-circuit on the :frame tag inside the debug-enabled? gate (DCE-safe). Causa marks :rf/causa in mount/ensure-causa-frame!. title: Spec: reconcile 002 Run-to-completion rule 3 (rollback) to per-event epoch boundary
description:
Follow-up flagged by rf2-nj6p7 (PR #1952). Under the now-implemented per-event epoch model, there is NO whole-drain rollback: each settled event is independently atomic + durable. On drain-depth-exceeded, already-settled :ok epochs (and their db writes) are KEPT; the remaining queue is discarded; the halting event (which never ran) gets a single trailing :halted-depth marker with :db-before = :db-after = the durable last-settled db, and the error trace carries :rollback? false.

This SUPERSEDES spec/002-Frames.md §Run-to-completion Rule 3 prose ('restore app-db to its pre-drain snapshot' / 'epoch history records nothing for the failed drain'), which was written for the per-DRAIN model and left stale by PR #1948 (the epoch-per-event spec change explicitly deferred this to the impl bead). The conformance fixture (spec/conformance/fixtures/drain-depth-limit.edn) was already updated by nj6p7 to the per-event behavior; this bead brings the NORMATIVE PROSE in 002 into line with it.

FIX: update spec/002-Frames.md Rule 3 (and any sibling rollback/halt language) to the per-event semantics above; cross-check §depth-rollback note (~L794) and the halt/abort path. Keep consistent with the :halted-depth epoch record (rf2-v0jwt) + the merged epoch-per-event wording (002 §Drain versus event). Verify against the updated drain-depth-limit.edn fixture. Hot-zone (002) — sequential. mkdocs build --strict. DEPENDS ON rf2-nj6p7 (reflect merged behavior). Mike reviews PR.

description:

title: bug(causa): machine topology (xyflow) renders unstyled — React Flow base CSS (@xyflow/react/dist/style.css) is not loaded
description:
The Machines panel's state-chart topology is meant to look like Stately/xstate (sized state nodes, transition arrows, laid out, with the per-event annotation overlay). - The xyflow ReactFlow component DOES mount: 54 .react-flow els, 4 state nodes, 15 edges, 1 Controls, a .react-flow__viewport with a real pan/zoom transform, fit-view ran, nodes at distinct (x,y).
- BUT: document.styleSheets has ZERO rules whose selector matches react-flow/xyflow; .react-flow__node computed width = 603px (no sizing); svg <marker> count = 0 (no arrowhead defs). => React Flow's base stylesheet is absent, so nodes have no absolute-positioning/sizing (stack at full width), edges have no arrowhead markers, Controls are bare.

BUNDLE ISOLATION: @xyflow/react is a Causa-only devDependency; the CSS injection must stay dev-only and not leak into production bundles (same posture as the rest of Causa).

OUT OF SCOPE: the per-event annotation overlay (transition FROM/TO, actions, guards) already works once a transition event is focused (verified: :title/flow :loading->:loaded with action record-reply-success annotated). This bead is purely the chart styling.

title: Impl: machine-internal events front-of-queue insertion (router)
description:
Implement machine front-of-queue per the spec (rf2-l038q; decision rf2-7ml7m=(b)). See ai/findings/2026-05-22-epoch-per-event-and-machine-queue.md Theme B. DEPENDS ON rf2-l038q (spec first) AND rf2-nj6p7 (both touch implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc — sequence to avoid conflict).

CHANGE:
- Router enqueue path: insert machine-INTERNAL continuation events at the FRONT of the per-frame FIFO queue (head), so the machine drains its macrostep to quiescence before the next EXTERNAL event. External events (user/UI/non-machine effects) keep going to the BACK.
- MARKING MECHANISM (the impl decision the spec deferred): determine how a dispatch is tagged machine-internal. Likely: a dispatch issued during machine action/entry/exit/transition processing carries a marker (e.g. via handler-scope / an :rf.machine/internal? envelope flag set by the machine fx path) — pick the cleanest seam in machines.cljc / core_machines.cljc + router build-envelope. Document the chosen seam.
- :raise stays unchanged (in-memory intra-macrostep). This is only for machine-originated events that go through the router queue.
- Preserve: drain-to-fixed-point, microtask scheduling, epoch-per-event (each leap-frogged event still its own epoch). Front-insert changes ORDER only.

GATES: core JVM, npm run test:cljs, npm run test:elision (absent in prod). Tests: (1) a machine entry-action :fx dispatch leap-frogs ahead of a pending external event; (2) an external event targeting a machine stays FIFO; (3) macrostep reaches quiescence before next external event; (4) no regression to epoch-per-event granularity. Worker worktree guard mandatory. Mike reviews PR.

title: Spec: event-loop model + machine front-of-queue (002 drain/scheduling + 005 internal-event priority)
description:
DECISION rf2-7ml7m resolved (b): machine-internal events leap-frog to the front of the queue; NO flush-dom. Spec it. See ai/findings/2026-05-22-epoch-per-event-and-machine-queue.md Theme B.

PART 1 — spec/002-Frames.md: make the event-loop/scheduling model EXPLICIT (currently implicit):
- Drain runs to FIXED POINT (all synchronously-cascaded events in one go), scheduled between drains via goog.async.nextTick (a MICROTASK, via interop/next-tick) — NOT setTimeout/rAF.
- Background-throttle property: because the drain is microtask-scheduled, the EVENT loop is NOT throttled in a backgrounded/CPU-throttled tab; only RENDER stalls (render = the adapter's :adapter/after-render hook, rAF-ish, decoupled from the drain). State this as a deliberate property.
- NO :flush-dom: re-frame2 has no queue-pause-for-render state (v1's :flush-dom). Post-render needs are served by after-render EFFECTS, not by pausing the queue. State this explicitly (v1 had flush-dom; re-frame2 deliberately does not).

PART 2 — spec/005-StateMachines.md: ADD machine front-of-queue (this REVERSES the current ~L813-816 'no reordering, no priority lanes, no front-of-queue' — update that section):
- Machine-INTERNAL continuation events (dispatched FROM a machine's action/entry/exit/transition processing) are inserted at the FRONT of the queue, so the machine completes its macrostep to quiescence BEFORE the next EXTERNAL event. SCXML-aligned.
- :raise remains the in-memory, intra-macrostep, pre-commit mechanism (unchanged) — front-of-queue is the additional lever for machine-originated events that DO go through the router queue (e.g. action :fx [[:dispatch ...]], inter-machine dispatches).
- DEFINE THE CUT precisely: an event leap-frogs iff it is a machine-originated continuation (dispatched during machine action/transition processing); events from user/UI/non-machine effects stay FIFO even if they TARGET a machine. (The marking mechanism is an impl concern — the impl bead owns it — but the spec must state the observable rule.)
- Keep consistent with epoch-per-event (just-merged #1948/#1949): each leap-frogged event is still its own epoch/cascade; ordering changes, not granularity.

Hot-zone (002, 005) — one worker, both docs, sequential. mkdocs build --strict. Mike reviews PR. Impl follows (separate bead, deps this + rf2-nj6p7 since both touch router.cljc).

title: DECISION: should machine-associated dispatches go to the front of the event queue? (contradicts current Spec 005)
description:
DECISION BEAD — needs Mike's call before any impl (see ai/findings/2026-05-22-epoch-per-event-and-machine-queue.md Theme B). Do NOT implement until resolved.

QUESTION (Mike): if a dispatch is associated with a state machine, should it be placed at the FRONT of the event queue (process to quiescence before the next external event), SCXML-macrostep style?

THE TENSION (found via Explore map): Spec 005 (~L813-816) currently states the OPPOSITE — 'Dispatched events go to the back... No reordering, no priority lanes, no front-of-queue insertion.' And macrostep atomicity is ALREADY achieved via :raise (intra-machine, in-memory, pre-commit), NOT via queue priority. So front-of-queue would REVERSE a deliberate spec decision.

Narrowed question: :raise already covers INTRA-machine atomicity. The only gap is INTER-machine :fx :rf/dispatch / machine entry-action dispatches that currently go FIFO to the back. Do those need to complete before unrelated external events?

OPTIONS:
(a) KEEP current (no priority lanes; :raise is the macrostep mechanism; FIFO elsewhere). Mayor lean if :raise covers the real cases — predictable, no spec reversal. Closes with a spec clarification that :raise is THE macrostep mechanism and FIFO is intentional.
(b) ADD front-of-queue for machine-INTERNAL events (SCXML quiescence-before-next-external). Precedent: SCXML/xstate. Spawns: spec/005 + event-queue spec change, router impl (priority insert), Causa macrostep grouping. Must define the internal-vs-external cut crisply (machine-RAISED internal events jump; external events targeting a machine stay FIFO).

DELIVERABLE: Mike picks (a) or (b). Then I file the follow-on spec/impl/tools beads (option b) or the clarifying spec bead (option a). Orthogonal to epoch-per-event (rf2-u6jsj/nj6p7) — queue ORDER doesn't change the per-event epoch granularity.
notes: RESOLVED 2026-05-22: Mike chose (b) — machine-internal events leap-frog to front-of-queue; NO flush-dom. Rationale recorded in findings doc. Spec = rf2-l038q (002 event-loop model + 005 front-of-queue), impl = rf2-j20a7 (router, dep l038q + nj6p7). Closing this decision bead; work tracked in those two.
close_reason: Decided (b) front-of-queue, no flush-dom; spawned rf2-l038q (spec) + rf2-j20a7 (impl)

title: Spec: epoch-per-event invariant — one :rf/epoch-record per dequeued event (all origins)
description:
Define the epoch-per-event invariant normatively (Mike-directed; see ai/findings/2026-05-22-epoch-per-event-and-machine-queue.md Theme A).

INVARIANT: one :rf/epoch-record per DEQUEUED event — irrespective of origin: UI dispatch, :fx :rf/dispatch, or the frame-creation initial event. Each event = its own epoch = its own 6-domino cascade = its own trace.

MACROSTEP-PRESERVATION CONSTRAINT: :raise sub-events and :always microsteps are NOT separate events — they are in-memory microsteps within a single machine macrostep (Spec 005 §raise / §macrostep). They MUST remain inside the triggering event's epoch. Only separate dequeued events (incl :fx :rf/dispatch) get their own epoch. So epoch boundary = per top-level dequeue; raises ride the triggering event's epoch.

CURRENT GAP: spec/impl currently bind an epoch to a drain-settle (a drain processes all queued events together), so :fx-dispatched children fold into the parent's epoch (root cause of rf2-48nsi).

EDIT (hot-zone, sequential — do 002 then 009):
- spec/002-Frames.md — the run-to-completion/drain-loop section: state that each dequeued event runs its full 6-domino cascade and gets its own epoch; clarify drain vs event boundary.
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md — the epoch / :dispatch-id / :parent-dispatch-id correlation section (~L51-68): bind epoch to event, not drain; document that :raise/:always stay within the triggering event's epoch.

Keep consistent with the existing macrostep wording in spec/005 (do not contradict it — raises are intra-macrostep). This is the spec head of the epoch-per-event chain (A1); impl (A2) + Causa (rf2-48nsi re-scoped) depend on it. Mike reviews the PR.

title: bug(causa): Trace tab "X / Y in view" denominator is the unscoped global buffer, not the focused cascade/epoch (reads as '113 in this epoch')
description:
The Trace tab is meant to be a per-cascade lens (rf2-ycoct), but its 'X / Y in view' header shows a denominator (Y) that escapes the cascade scope, so it looks like the focused epoch has ~113 trace items when it has 8.

DIAGNOSED LIVE via re-frame2-pair:
- :rf.causa/trace-feed :counts = {:total 113, :rendered 8, :cascade-dispatch-id 5}.
- The 8 RENDERED rows are correctly cascade-scoped — all from :below (the focused cascade, dispatch-id 5). Scoping of the displayed rows works.
- The 113 :total is the WHOLE trace-bus buffer, computed BEFORE the cascade scope. Its composition: by-frame {nil 52, :rf/default 7, :above 27, :below 27}; by-dispatch-id {nil 85, 2->6, 3->8, 4->6, 5->8}. So it spans every recent cascade AND multiple frames.
- The focused epoch itself (epoch 2, :below) has 25 raw trace-events; the cascade window (dispatch-id 5) projects to 8 rows.
- NOTE: Causa's own :rf/causa self-trace is correctly excluded from the buffer (0 of the 113) — this is NOT a self-pollution bug.

ROOT CAUSE: panels/trace.cljs :rf.causa/trace-feed (~857) -> h/project-feed-from-state computes :rendered AFTER the cascade-scope (:cascade-dispatch-id from focus) but :total from the full feed-state (the whole trace-bus buffer). So the denominator leaks the unscoped, cross-frame, multi-cascade total.

FIX: make the denominator reflect the cascade scope (the system invariant per rf2-ycoct), and at minimum the focused frame (frames are isolated contexts — the 113 wrongly mixes :above/:rf/default/nil into a :below-focused view). i.e. 'X / Y in view' should be: Y = events in the focused cascade's window (before user chip filters), X = after chip filters. Update project-feed-from-state (trace_helpers.cljc) so :total is the cascade/frame-scoped count, and check the epoch-indicator ('epoch #N · X ops', trace.cljs ~230) tells the same story. Add/adjust the helper test to pin the scoped-total semantics.
notes:
REFINEMENT (Mike, live): the dispatch-id cascade-scope is wrong on BOTH ends, not just the denominator.

Observed: a counter-inc shows only 4 Trace rows (event/dispatched, event x2, event/db-changed) — the SYNCHRONOUS event-side. But the cascade's epoch (epoch 16, :below) holds 12 trace-events: by-dispatch-id {427 -> 4, nil -> 8}. The nil-dispatch 8 are the cascade's ASYNC reactive effects — :sub/run x5, :view/render x1, :rf.view/rendered x1, :frame/created x1 — i.e. the subs that recomputed and the views that re-rendered. They fire post-cascade (reaction/commit time) with nil dispatch-id, so the panel's :cascade-dispatch-id filter EXCLUDES them.

So scoping by dispatch-id:
  - RENDERED rows are too FEW — drops the cascade's whole reactive half (subs/renders), showing an incomplete domino trail.
  - TOTAL/denominator is too BIG — counts the unscoped buffer (boot noise + all cascades + all frames).

CORRECT FIX: scope the Trace panel by the focused EPOCH's :trace-events (the per-frame settling epoch — epoch 16 here = the full 12), NOT by dispatch-id. The epoch already folds both the synchronous event-side (dispatch-id N) AND the async reactive events (nil dispatch-id) for that cascade. That makes rendered = the complete domino trail and the denominator = the epoch's own total (before user chip filters). This supersedes the earlier 'just scope the denominator to dispatch-id' note — dispatch-id is the wrong key; the epoch is the right one. (Same cascade-vs-epoch seam as rf2-48nsi.)

Files: panels/trace.cljs (:rf.causa/trace-feed / :rf.causa/trace-feed-state — read the focused epoch record's :trace-events instead of the trace-bus buffer + dispatch-id filter), trace_helpers.cljc (project-feed-from-state).

notes:

OBSERVED OUTPUT:
- (+ 1 2 3) => 6
- defn+println+nested coll => *out* "computing..." captured + => {:squares (1 4 9 16), :set #{:a :b}, :nested {:k [1 2]}}
- (this-var-does-not-exist 1 2) => "ERROR: Unable to resolve symbol: this-var-does-not-exist" (rendered, no crash; cell still evals after)

RESOLVED VERSIONS: @nextjournal/clojure-mode 0.3.3 · @nextjournal/lezer-clojure 1.0.0 (transitive) · scittle 0.8.31 (CDN classic-script global) · @codemirror/state 6.6.0 · @codemirror/view 6.43.0 · @codemirror/commands 6.10.3 · @codemirror/language 6.12.3 (transitive) · @codemirror/autocomplete 6.20.2 (transitive) · esbuild 0.28.0 · playwright 1.60.0.

RECIPE:
- Scittle is a CLASSIC <script>, NOT an ES module. Load <script src=cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/scittle@0.8.31/dist/scittle.js>; installs window.scittle global; read window.scittle.core.eval_string at eval time. Do NOT import it.
- CM6 + clojure-mode ARE ES modules; bundle with esbuild --format=iife. clojure-mode exports default_extensions (array) + complete_keymap (array = paredit+builtin keybindings).
- Eval keymap MUST be Prec.highest(keymap.of([{key:"Mod-Enter", preventDefault:true, run}])). Without Prec.highest the keypress is swallowed before the handler runs (this was the bug that made the cell render nothing).
- eval_string returns the actual CLJS value (numbers as JS numbers) and THROWS a real JS Error (.message) on eval failure.
- Eval wrapper that captures *out* + result as a JS array:
    (clj->js
      (let [r# (atom nil)
            o# (with-out-str (reset! r# (do <USER-SRC>)))]
        [o# (pr-str (deref r#))]))
  Read out[0]=printed, out[1]=pr-str'd result.

GOTCHAS for Phase 1:
1. No JVM classes in SCI: java.io.StringWriter does NOT resolve. Use (with-out-str ...) to capture printed output.
2. A CLJS vector returned to JS is a PersistentVector OBJECT, not a JS array — out[0]/out[1] return internal fields (garbage). Wrap return in (clj->js ...) to get a real JS Array (clj->js and into-array both work). This + #1 were the two real bugs found.
3. with-out-str captures only explicit prints, not the body's return value — stash return in (atom) inside the with-out-str body, pr-str it after.
4. Scittle logs eval errors to console.error AND throws. The throw is what you catch/render; the console.error noise is expected, NOT a real page error — don't fail tests on it.
5. pr-str of maps/sets renders cleanly: {:a 1, :b [1 2], :c #{:x :y}}. For big structures Phase 1 may load scittle.pprint.js (ships in dist) for multi-line pretty output.
6. esbuild local-binary gotcha: use node_modules/.bin/esbuild (or npm run build). A bare `npx esbuild` pulls a fresh global esbuild that can't resolve locally-installed @codemirror/* deps.
7. complete_keymap does NOT bind Mod-Enter for eval (it's paredit+builtin only). The eval keybinding lives in the separate @nextjournal/clojure-mode/extensions/eval-region module which we do NOT import — so there's no Mod-Enter conflict; we supply our own eval keymap. (Phase 1 could import eval_region for at-cursor/top-level eval granularity if desired.)

BUNDLE SIZE: CM6+clojure-mode unminified IIFE ~866 KB; --minify shrinks substantially. Scittle core ~876 KB raw / 183 KB gzip (loaded separately from CDN). Matches findings doc estimates.

title: audit(pair-mcp): port-file discovery is cwd-relative — add --port-file launch flag
description: nrepl.cljs:49-67 (port-file-candidates / read-port-from-fs). The MCP server runs as a subprocess of the agent host (Claude Code/Cursor/Copilot) whose cwd is frequently NOT the consumer project root; in that case all three file fallbacks miss silently and only SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT works. README documents the 4-step precedence but does not flag that steps 2-4 are cwd-dependent. Fix: (a) add a --port-file <path> launch flag in server.cljs/parse-launch-flags that takes absolute precedence over env+file scan (cwd-independent escape hatch); (b) optionally resolve candidates relative to a project-root anchor env var falling back to cwd; (c) document the cwd-relative constraint in README. title: audit(ssr): streaming writer thread is non-daemon despite docs/tests calling it a daemon thread
description: ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/streaming.clj:262-274 constructs the per-request streaming writer via (Thread. ^Runnable fn ^String name) + .start with NO (.setDaemon true) call. Yet streaming.clj ns docstring (line 212 'runs on a daemon thread'), stream-handler docstring, and BOTH test ns docstrings + the daemon-thread-name-prefix vars (streaming_robustness_test.clj, concurrency_stress_test.clj:163) assert it is a daemon thread (contract #3: 'the daemon thread MUST terminate'). It is a user (non-daemon) thread. Consequence: the JVM-shutdown protection a daemon thread implies does NOT exist — a writer blocked on .write to the bounded 16KiB PipedOutputStream of a slow-loris client is a live non-daemon thread that can keep the JVM from exiting at shutdown. Normal+disconnect operation terminates via the writer's finally (tests prove this under load), so leak-detector tests pass; the doc/code mismatch is the bug. Fix (masterpiece-bar): add (.setDaemon true) before .start, e.g. (doto (Thread. ^Runnable writer-thread ^String name) (.setDaemon true) (.start)). Alternatively, if non-daemon is intentional for graceful-shutdown flush, correct the word 'daemon' across the ns + stream-handler + 2 test docstrings and rename daemon-thread-name-prefix -> writer-thread-name-prefix. See ai/findings/ssr-bestpractice-2026-05-21.md Finding 1.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1908

title: audit(routing): :int query coercion asymmetric across JVM/CLJS — hydration-mismatch hazard
description: routing.cljc:276-283 (coerce-by-type-form, :int branch). Long/parseLong (JVM) and js/parseInt (CLJS) disagree on non-strict input: for ?page=12abc JVM throws -> caught -> returns string "12abc"; CLJS js/parseInt returns number 12. Same route (:query [:map [:page :int]]) + same URL yields DIFFERENT :rf/route :query slices server- vs client-side (string vs number) -> Spec 011 hydration-mismatch class + violates Spec 012 'same handler both sides' + Spec 000 Goal 2 cross-host conformance. Malformed :int also silently string-passthroughs on JVM only, defeating the coercion contract on one host. Fix: make :int strict + identical on both hosts — parse via shared strict regex (#"^-?\d+$") before convert, returning v unchanged on no-match on BOTH hosts (removes the try/catch). Add conformance fixture asserting ?n=12abc gives identical output JVM+CLJS. Found in routing best-practice audit; see ai/findings/routing-bestpractice-2026-05-21.md.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1905

title: research(docs): evaluate Maria (mhuebert/maria) vs Klipse for the docs/cljs live-CLJS surface
description: Mike-question 2026-05-21: could github.com/mhuebert/maria power the docs/cljs side (live 'read ClojureScript' cells) instead of Klipse? Evaluate: current Klipse setup (docs/cljs/index.md + docs/klipse/klipse-bootstrap.js — the instant-safe ~7MB vendored self-bootstrapping client-side eval from PR #1875) vs Maria's architecture (the maria.cloud editor + underlying libs). Eval model (client-side self-hosted CLJS? can cells require reagent/re-frame2?), bundle size/perf, instant-nav compatibility, editor/UX quality, maintenance/activity, licence, migration effort. Output: ai/findings doc + recommendation (switch / stay-Klipse / hybrid). No code changes.
close_reason: VERDICT: Stay on Klipse — Maria not viable. CRUX: Maria (maria.cloud, mhuebert/maria) is a standalone hosted notebook APP, not an embeddable inline-cell library — no npm/CDN distributable, no iframe/widget/embed API, zero examples of it embedded in 3rd-party docs. editor2 is a full SPA (Firebase auth, ProseMirror single-doc, bidi routing, Radix UI, Clerk, Emmy), eval=SCI interpreter (sci 0.8.41), CodeMirror 6, EPL-2.0; third-party libs 'require a PR to this repo' so cells can't dynamically require reagent/re-frame2. Last commit 2024-02 (quiet). It does not beat Klipse on the deciding axes: embeddability(fails), client-side-only-widget(none), deps-in-cells(no), perf-as-widget(heavier), instant-nav(n/a). Klipse already solved guarded single-page load + sub-path safety + navigation.instant re-mount (PR #1875/rf2-zr5r5) — a switch would discard that. Migration effort to adopt Maria-as-is = very high / build-it-yourself (fork editor + author non-existent embed layer). Better future option if 7.4MB/dormancy bites: a SCI+nextjournal-clojure-mode CM6 mini-cell (borrow Maria's building blocks, not Maria) — separate larger initiative, not warranted now (all cells are plain core CLJS). Findings: ai/findings/2026-05-21-maria-vs-klipse-docs-cljs.md (gitignored, read-only research, no PR).

title: review(machines): missing registration-time :rf.error/machine-compound-state-missing-initial validation
description:
Spec 005 §Initial-state cascading (005-StateMachines.md:930): a compound state (declares :states) without :initial is a registration error — emits :rf.error/machine-compound-state-missing-initial at registration time and fails registration.

validation.cljc does not check this. At runtime initial-cascade (transition.cljc:250-258) stops descending when :initial is nil and returns the path pointing at the compound node itself — yielding a snapshot whose :state is a NON-leaf path. Downstream leaf-assuming code then misbehaves silently instead of the author getting the named registration error.

Fix: in lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc, for every state node with a non-empty :states map, require a keyword :initial; throw :rf.error/machine-compound-state-missing-initial with :tags {:state <kw>} otherwise. (Parallel-region region bodies already require :initial via validate-parallel!; this is the non-parallel compound-node case.)
Files: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1851

title: review(machines): missing registration-time :rf.error/machine-always-self-loop validation
description:
Spec 005 §Self-loop forbidden at registration (005-StateMachines.md:1290-1301) and §Drain semantics gotchas (:889) REQUIRE make-machine-handler to reject at registration any :always entry whose :target resolves to the declaring state itself with the SAME :guard reference (or no guard), surfacing :rf.error/machine-always-self-loop with :tags {:state <kw> :machine-id <id>}. A self-targeting :always with a DIFFERENT guard is permitted.

validation.cljc has no such check. A same-state same-guard :always self-loop is accepted at registration and only caught at RUNTIME after 16 wasted microsteps via :rf.error/machine-always-depth-exceeded + rollback — wrong error, late, firing-path-only.

Fix: add validate-always-self-loop! to lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc walking each state's :always entries; resolve keyword/vector :target against the declaring state and reject same-state+same-guard (or no-guard).
Files: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/validation.cljc.

In the live handler path the runtime machine spec carries :rf/parent-id (stamped by registration.cljc/prepare-machine-ctx) and deliberately NOT :id (Spec 005:187 — spec map MUST NOT carry :id). So both error traces ship :machine-id nil in production.

Guard/action traces + run-action correctly use (or (:rf/parent-id machine) (:id machine)) (transition.cljc:142, :473). Only these two depth-limit emits regressed.

Spec 005 §Drain semantics (005-StateMachines.md:807) and §Bounded depth (:1278) pin :tags {:machine-id <id> ...} on these errors. Existing depth test (machines_always_cljs_test) asserts the trace exists but not its :machine-id, so it passes.

title: review(ssr): streaming build-final-payload ignores :rf2/runtime-version (rf2-asmj1 S8 un-fixed on stream path)

The audit note rf2-asmj1 S8 (implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/payload.clj:44-51) states the prior inline (or version 1) silently disagreed with the client-side hook and defeated the version-mismatch check on hosts that did not pass :version explicitly. Same bug remains on the streaming path: streamed responses ship :rf/version 1 regardless of the registered hook, so :rf.ssr/version-mismatch detection silently fails for streaming SSR on any host registering the hook without an explicit :version. streaming.cljc is in the ssr artefact and cannot :require ssr-ring resolve-version; lift the resolution to a shared site (e.g. re-frame.ssr.payload-policy or a new shared helper).

title: review(core): path interceptor :after throws on empty stack when its :before was short-circuited
description:
When an interceptor EARLIER in the chain throws in :before, execute-chain short-circuits all downstream :before stages (including path's) but STILL runs every :after in reverse (Spec 002 §rule 2). path's :after does:

  (let [stack (:rf/path-stack ctx [])   ; absent -> []  (before never pushed)
        original-db (peek stack)         ; nil
        new-stack (pop stack)            ; (pop []) THROWS
        ...] ...)

(pop []) throws (IllegalStateException JVM / equivalent CLJS). The throw is caught by interceptor/invoke-after and recorded into :rf/interceptor-errors, so the drain does not abort — but it produces a SPURIOUS second error and path teardown is broken whenever path sits downstream of a :before-throwing interceptor.

The sibling unwrap interceptor is written defensively for exactly this case: (if-let [original (:rf/unwrap-stash ctx)] ... ctx) returns ctx unchanged when its :before never ran. path should mirror that guard (only pop/splice when :rf/path-stack is non-empty).

Files: implementation/core/src/re_frame/std_interceptors.cljc:44-63 (path :after); contrast :98-104 (unwrap :after). Interaction: interceptor.cljc:119-176.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1849

title: review(core): event-vector schema validation failure bypasses interceptor :after pass
description:
The two pre-handler schema-validation failures use asymmetric mechanisms:

- Cofx failure (Spec 010 step 2): maybe-validate-cofx! sets :rf/skip-handler? true; the interceptor chain STILL executes end-to-end, the handler-wrapper :before skips the handler, and every :after stage runs (teardown preserved). Correct. (cofx.cljc:95-97)
- Event-vector failure (Spec 010 step 1): run-chain is called with event-ok? false and returns initial-ctx unchanged WITHOUT executing the chain — no :before AND no :after runs. (router.cljc:691-707, validate-event! :244-276)

Spec 002 §Interceptor chain execution rule 2 (lines 835-837) is unconditional: the :after pass ALWAYS runs in full "regardless of whether a :before or handler throw occurred" so cleanup-on-:after interceptors (debug pp/snapshot, Story snapshot capturer) fire even after a :before failure. The event-vector path silently skips :after.

Because the :before stages also never ran in this path, no resource was allocated, so the practical leak is narrow — but the contract is unconditional and the two validation paths should be symmetric. Cleaner shape: set :rf/skip-handler? on event-vector validation failure (same as cofx) and let the chain run so :after fires, rather than skipping run-chain wholesale.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1855

title: review(adapters): test-react mount! lexicographic gensym sort returns stale mount after 10 mounts
description: test-react's mount-record-from-unmount-fn (implementation/adapters/test-react/src/re_frame/adapter/test_react.cljc:247-272) sorts active mounts via (sort-by (comp str :id) ...) then takes last, with the stated intent to 'pick the max-id mount'. But :id is (gensym "test-react-mount-") and the sort is LEXICOGRAPHIC on the gensym string, not numeric: "test-react-mount-10" < "test-react-mount-9" lexicographically. After a process mints >=10 mounts, mount! can return a STALE MountedComponent whose lifecycle-log / render-tree belong to the wrong mount, silently corrupting any test holding >9 mounts in one run. The docstring's 'max-id mount' intent does not match the code. Minimal fix: sort numerically on the gensym suffix (parse the integer tail) instead of lexicographically; proper fix widens the substrate render return shape so mount! does not need the side-channel hack at all (already flagged 'minimal-skeleton hack' in the docstring). Spec ref: n/a (test adapter); the contract is internal correctness of the test driver.

title: review(routing): /*rest mis-ranked equal to catch-all /* (rule-4 classifier too broad)
description: Spec 012 §Route ranking rule 4 (012-Routing.md:167) + pseudocode (is-catch-all? (= pattern '/*'), :181) define catch-all as the UNNAMED root splat /* only; a named root splat /*rest is a rest-param and MUST out-rank /*. The impl parse-pattern (match.cljc:264-278) computes catch-all? (and (= 1 total) (= 1 splat) (zero? static) (zero? named) (zero? optional)) which is true for /*rest just as for /*. Both get rule-4 score 0 and identical structural rank [0 1 -1 0 0], tying at rule 6 (registration order) instead of /*rest strictly beating /*. Small blast radius (two root splats together is rare; route-shadowed-by-equal-score warns) but a cross-host conformance divergence — route-ranking-precedence.edn would pin /*rest > /*. Fix: align catch-all? with spec — only the unnamed root splat (no capture name) is catch-all. File: implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/match.cljc:264-278. Spec: spec/012-Routing.md:167,:181-189.

title: review(schemas): digest map-key ordering — spec says (compare a b), impl uses (compare (pr-str a) (pr-str b))
description: Spec 010 §Digest algorithm step 1 (010-Schemas.md:403) says schema-props map keys are sorted by (compare a b) after coercing to a comparable representation. The impl (re-frame.schemas.validator/canonicalise-schema-form + compare-by-pr-str, validator.cljc:77-103) sorts by (compare (pr-str a) (pr-str b)). The spec body contradicts its own parity-fixture rationale (test/.../digest_parity_fixtures.cljc:157-160 documents the pr-str variant). Harmless for the CLJS reference (keyword keys; both orders agree, digests cross-runtime stable). Exposure is cross-PORT: a TS/Rust port implementing the literal (compare a b) produces a different digest for heterogeneous/numeric props keys (e.g. 2 vs 10: numeric compare 2<10, pr-str compare '10'<'2'), breaking the SSR cross-host digest handshake. Fix: pin Spec 010 step-1 wording to (compare (pr-str a) (pr-str b)) (the impl's actual tested contract) so all ports compute identical bytes. description:

## 2. Add example use / snippets per member WHERE IT HELPS
For each API member · if a short usage snippet makes it clearer · add a fenced clojure example under Description. Judgement:
- Macros like reg-event-db · reg-sub · reg-view → YES · canonical call
- Trivial accessor / predicate → skip if signature is self-explanatory
- Complex multi-arity / opts-map fns → YES · common shape

## 3. Link to real example use in /examples

- reg-event-db → link to examples/reagent/counter (or wherever it is first used cleanly)

- **In the wild**: [counter example](../../examples/reagent/counter/) · or the github-pages link if docs link out

title: fix(causa): route collections through cljs-devtools in the EDN widget — matches re-frame-10x (rf2-gycfj gap)
description:
Mike-observation + clarification (2026-05-21): cljs-devtools is NOT used in the App-DB panel. ## Mike-direction (clarified · SIMPLER than a hybrid diff)
- **Diff views** → KEEP the home-grown technique (it owns the before/after diff vocabulary · cljs-devtools has none)
- **Non-diff views** → use cljs-devtools for EVERYTHING including collections. App-db panel + Trace panel + Event :db/:fx/coeffects show CURRENT state · there is NO diff needed there. Those should render the whole collection through cljs-devtools (the 10x look).

So the split is by MODE, cleanly:
- browse/current-state mode → cljs-devtools (collections + scalars · whole value)
- diff mode → home-grown render-tree (unchanged)

## The fix
1. browse mode in widget.cljs: route collections through cljs-devtools too (not just scalars). The JSONML walker in cljs_devtools_render.cljs already handles container tags · extend if nesting needs it.
2. diff mode: leave as home-grown · NO change.
3. Confirm App-DB panel current-state view + Trace + Event :db/:fx call browse (not diff) so they pick up cljs-devtools. If App-DB panel ONLY has a diff view · add/confirm a current-state browse view that uses cljs-devtools.

## Acceptance
- App-DB panel current state → cljs-devtools look (type-coloured · expandable nested map)
- Trace panel payloads → cljs-devtools
- Event :db / :fx / coeffects → cljs-devtools
- Diff views (cascade before/after) → unchanged home-grown
- bundle-isolation green

title: feat(causa): wire zprint + highlight.js into EDN widget code-block (replace stand-in tokeniser)
description:
Mike-direction (rf2-n4ad0 verbatim): "Handler code formatted via zprint at runtime + highlight.js for clojure-mode token colours (~40KB total · much lighter than CodeMirror)".

## Current state

`tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/views/edn_widget/widget.cljs:130-272` ships a ~140-line bundled tokenizer + per-token colour switch. Functional for short handler bodies, but it is a hand-rolled Clojure lexer — `let` `loop` etc. coloured as builtins via a 25-symbol whitelist; multi-line strings, namespaced symbols, reader macros, character literals fall back to `:symbol`. The `:lang` slot is honoured only for `:clojure`; other languages render as mono text.

The bundle comment at `widget.cljs:181-184` and `widget.cljs:232` self-deprecates: "A heavier highlight.js integration could land via a follow-on bead". This bead IS that follow-on.

zprint is a separate concern: it would re-format multi-line handler source to a canonical width / indent before highlighting. Currently the substrate captures source verbatim via `:rf.handler/source` meta (`event_detail.cljs:630-639`) and the highlighter renders as-is — a poorly-formatted source registration shows up poorly-formatted.

## Scope

- Add `zprint-cljs` + `highlight.js` (or an embeddable Clojure-mode subset) to `tools/causa/deps.edn` (CLJS-side) or via npm if highlight.js comes in via JS interop.
- Replace the inline `tokenize-clojure` + `highlight-clojure-token` + `classify-token` machinery in `widget.cljs/code-block` with a thin highlight.js wrapper.
- Pre-format the source via zprint inside `code-block` before tokenising.
- Bundle-isolation: zprint + highlight.js MUST stay dev-only (Causa already gates the whole bundle on `interop/debug-enabled?` — confirm DCE on production build).
- Preserve the widget's public API surface (`{:source :lang :testid}` props).
- Preserve theme-token colour mapping (no hex literals in styles).

## Acceptance

- Event panel handler-source slot renders the registered handler form with canonical zprint formatting + highlight.js token colours (keywords violet · strings green · numbers cyan · builtins violet).
- Bundle-isolation gate stays green — neither dep ships in the production bundle.
- Perf-budget gate green — no production regression.
- CLJS unit tests pin the rendered hiccup shape (NO new Playwright).

title: audit+fix: error message quality pass — every (ex-info ...) audited for actionability, user-facing vocabulary, debug context
description:
Mike-direction (2026-05-21 v1-polish sweep): every (throw (ex-info ...)) site in the codebase should be audited against three criteria. Errors are the user-facing surface that matters most for trust and debuggability; pre-1.0 is the moment to tighten them.

## The three criteria

### 1. Is the message actionable?
Does it tell the user WHAT TO DO to fix it · not just what went wrong?
- BAD: "Invalid spec" (action unclear)
- GOOD: "Invalid spec at <path> — expected a map with :event key · saw <value>. Fix the call site at <source-coord> to supply :event."

### 2. Does it name the user-facing concept (not impl-detail)?
- BAD: "late-bind directory lookup miss for :schemas/validate-app-schema!" (impl-detail · user has no model of late-bind directory)
- GOOD: "Schema validation requires `re-frame.schemas` to be on the classpath · add `[day8/re-frame2-schemas]` to deps · or call without :schema."

### 3. Does it include enough context to debug?
- The relevant identifier (event-id · sub-id · machine-id · path · …)
- The relevant value (truncated if huge · privacy-aware if marked :sensitive)
- A reference to the spec section or doc page when applicable

## Approach

### Phase 1 — Audit (read-only)
Worker:
1. `grep -rn "ex-info\|throw" implementation/ tools/` enumerates the surface
2. For each site, classify: PASS · MARGINAL · FAIL against the three criteria
3. Write findings to `ai/findings/2026-05-21-error-message-quality-audit.md` with per-site verdict
4. Identify load-bearing patterns: which errors should follow a common shape?
5. Propose a common error-shape (data keys · `:rf.error/<id>` convention · message structure)

### Phase 2 — Fix
After Mike reviews the audit + locks the common shape:
- Worker file sub-beads for each cluster of FAIL/MARGINAL errors
- Each sub-bead fixes a coherent set (e.g. all schema-validation errors · all machine-transition errors · all HTTP errors)

## Surface (audit phase)
- READ: implementation/* + tools/* (every (ex-info ...) call site)
- READ: spec/* (already-named error ids that errors should reference)
- WRITE: ai/findings/2026-05-21-error-message-quality-audit.md

## Common shape candidates (worker proposes)
The Spec already uses `:rf.error/<id>` keys for some errors. Likely common shape:
```
(ex-info "Human-readable message · what + how to fix"
         {:rf.error/id <namespaced-keyword>
          :rf.error/source-coord {:file ... :line ...}
          ;; surface-specific keys below
          :event-id ...
          :path ...
          :spec-doc "spec/010-Schemas.md#section-anchor"})
```

## Posture
Pre-alpha · v1-readiness polish · errors are the user-trust surface · masterpiece bar

## Gates (audit phase)

## Hard cap
Phase 1: 180m. Phase 2 sub-beads filed by worker for mayor to dispatch separately.

title: audit(spec): /spec completeness vs /implementation — could a TS/JS team independently implement re-frame2 from /spec alone?
description:
Mike-direction (2026-05-21): /spec is the load-bearing artefact for re-frame2 - /implementation is the CLJS reference per the project posture. Verify that /spec is sufficient for an independent team (e.g. building re-frame2 in TS/JS) to roll their own implementation from scratch. Identify what /implementation reveals as load-bearing that /spec does not capture.

## Phase 1 — audit (deliverable is a findings doc)

The audit answers two questions:

### (1) Sufficiency
Could an independent team reading ONLY /spec build a re-frame2-compatible runtime? For each spec section, evaluate:
- Does it state the CONTRACT precisely enough that two independent implementations would behave identically?
- Are the data shapes, event ordering rules, lifecycle invariants, error semantics all there?
- Are corner cases enumerated (or named-but-unspecified, which is worse)?
- Are the cross-spec compositions explicit (e.g. how does a frame-scoped sub interact with a flow whose input is a sub from another frame)?

### (2) Implementation-leaked load-bearing detail
For each major /implementation surface, check if /spec captures everything an alternative impl would need:
- The trace-bus emit timing (when exactly does each :rf.trace/* event fire?)
- The cascade-engine ordering (subs run, then renders, then effects, then ... ?)
- The interceptor chain semantics (re-entry, exception propagation, :before/:after composition)
- The frame lifecycle (mount, unmount, hot-reload reconciliation, frame teardown order)
- Machine actor lifecycle (spawn, raise, transition, microstep semantics)
- HTTP managed lifecycle (request, response, retry, abort, decode, stub)
- SSR hydration mark-and-sweep
- Schema validation seams (when does validate-app-schema! fire?)
- Privacy elision composition order (sensitive-mark → walker → wire → ...)
- Routing :rf.route/* event ordering
- Late-bind directory contract (every late-bind hook name + producer ns + consumer surface)

For EACH leak found: is it deliberate (impl-detail, not contract) or an oversight (should be in /spec)?

## Phase 1 deliverable
ai/findings/2026-05-21-spec-completeness-audit.md with:
- Per-section sufficiency rating
- Per-leak classification (deliberate impl-detail vs spec gap)
- Concrete list of additions /spec needs to be Phase-2 actionable

## Phase 2 — file sub-beads
For EACH oversight identified in the audit, file a new sub-bead with the specific spec addition needed. Each sub-bead is dispatchable independently. The audit itself does NOT touch /spec - just identifies gaps.

## Surface (audit phase)
- READ: /spec/* and tools/causa/spec/* and tools/story/spec/* and tools/machines-viz/spec/*
- READ: /implementation/* (every artefact: core, schemas, machines, flows, routing, http, ssr, ssr-ring, epoch + all adapters)
- WRITE: ai/findings/2026-05-21-spec-completeness-audit.md

NO PRODUCTION CODE in Phase 1.

## Posture
Pre-alpha · spec is the contract · /implementation is one valid reading of that contract · the audit measures the contracts completeness for second-implementation parity

## Gates (audit phase)
- None (no code change)
- mkdocs build --strict if findings doc has anchors

## Hard cap
- Phase 1 (this bead): 180m. This is research + careful writing.
- Phase 2 (per-gap fix beads): filed by the Phase 1 worker · dispatched separately by mayor

## Scope (STRICT)

INCLUDE: ONLY /docs/guide/
EXCLUDE: /docs/causa/, /docs/story/, /docs/migration/, /docs/api/ (or whatever the API docs path is), /docs/cljs/ — leave those alone.

## Current state

The /docs/guide/ tree has 20+ files with inconsistent numbering:
- 02-app-db.md, 03-your-first-app.md, 04-events-state-cycle.md, 04a-schemas.md ←  "04a" pattern · BAD
- 05-coeffects.md, 06-views-and-frames.md, 06a-frames.md ← "06a" again
- 07-interceptors.md, 08-forms.md, 09-state-machines.md, 10-doing-http-requests.md

- 17-routing.md, 17a-routing-reference.md ← "17a"
- 18-from-re-frame-v1.md ← migration · OUT OF SCOPE for this refresh but stays in guide
- 19-adapters.md, 20-where-next.md
- 22-trace-to-datadog.md ← gap at 21
- 23a-privacy-secrets.md, 23b-large-blobs.md ← "23a/23b"
- 24-configuration-and-safety/ (sub-folder with index + 8 chapters)

## Mike-locked structural changes

1. **Renumber so all chapters are sequential integers** — drop "04a" / "06a" / "17a" / "23a/23b" — these become 05, 07, 18, 24, 25 (or wherever they slot). Fill gaps too (gap at 15, gap at 21).
2. **Short chapter names so LHS navigation does not wrap.** Currently "the-dynamic-model" / "doing-http-requests" / "from-re-frame-v1" / "configuration-and-safety" are too long. Target: ≤ 22 characters in the slug component.
3. **mkdocs.yml nav re-wire** to match new file names.

## Voice — Steve Yegge (per rf2-0pvm3 successful template)

- Long-form paragraphs that wander productively
- Self-aware asides + jokes about programming tropes
- Strong opinions backed by reasoning
- Anecdotes from the trenches that make a point
- Dry wit (not slapstick)
- Builds intuition first, syntax second
- First-person plural (we), conversational

## Tutorial best practices per chapter

- Clear "what youll build" / "what youll learn" at the top

- Complete code blocks (full ns require + surrounding fn · no divination fragments)
- "You should now see Y" confirmation moments after each change

## Screenshot placeholders

title: docs(story): capture 10 annotated screenshots for Yegge tutorial via Playwright (rf2-0pvm3 follow-on)
description:
Mike-direction (2026-05-21): the Story tutorial refresh (rf2-0pvm3 / PR #1799) left 10 `📸 Screenshot needed` placeholders because the agent could not drive a browser. Now: dispatch a Playwright-driving agent to actually capture them.

## Approach

Use Playwright (already used for story_browser_scenarios.cjs etc) to:
1. Start shadow-cljs watch on tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories
2. Drive a browser to each scenario the placeholders describe
3. Inject HTML/SVG overlay elements via page.evaluate for arrows + numbered callouts BEFORE the screenshot — that way the saved PNG is annotated, not raw
4. Save to /docs/images/story/<chapter>-<topic>.png

## Locate placeholders

Read each chapter file under docs/story/ and grep for the placeholder marker pattern:

```
> 📸 **Screenshot needed**: <description>
>
> Save as: `/docs/images/story/<chapter>-<topic>.png`
```

Each placeholder names:
- The page/scenario to capture
- The numbered callouts (which elements + what they say)
- The save-path

Implement each one:
- Navigate to the variant URL
- Inject overlay SVG: arrows pointing at the named element selectors + numbered callout boxes
- screenshot()
- Save at the placeholder save-path
- Replace the markdown admonition with the actual image embed: `![alt](path)`

## Style for overlays

- Red arrows (similar to Skitch defaults)
- Numbered callout boxes (yellow bg · black text · numbered 1 2 3...)
- Subtle drop-shadow so they pop on light + dark themes

Keep it consistent across all 10 screenshots so the visual language is uniform.

## Surface

- docs/story/index.md + 01-first-story.md → 07-multi-substrate.md (replace placeholders with image embeds)
- docs/images/story/*.png (new files · 10 of them)
- A new helper script under examples/scripts/ or tools/story/scripts/ for the capture-and-annotate flow (re-usable for future tutorial expansions)

## Posture

Pre-alpha · docs work · Playwright USE is acceptable here even though we generally prefer CLJS unit tests · because the ENTIRE PURPOSE is browser-driven visual capture (the screenshots themselves are the deliverable)

## Gates

- All 10 PNGs created + image embed lines in markdown resolve
- mkdocs build --strict (every link + image ref resolves)
- Visual sanity check (worker can pop up `start` or analogous viewer to confirm screenshots non-empty + annotations visible)

title: feat(machines-viz): migrate MachineChart from ELK+SVG to xyflow — Mike override of 2026-05-19 lock
description:

- Loss of substrate-agnostic hiccup contract — chart becomes React-component-shaped

- Loss of aesthetic coherence — xyflow has its own visual conventions

- Spec re-litigation: spec/000-Vision.md §Decision trace §Interactive renderer

title: fix(story): "open" chip does not work — port Causa open-in-editor impl + document custom-editor config
description:
Mike-direction (2026-05-21): Story open-in-editor chip does not work with vscode. Causa version DOES work. Both supposedly use the same underlying library `re-frame.source-coords.editor-uri`. Find the divergence and fix.

## Investigation hints

- Both impls exist:
  - `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/open_in_editor.cljs`
  - `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/open_in_editor.cljs`
- The Causa file says (verbatim line 4): `Mirrors re-frame.story.ui.open-in-editor — same chip shape, reads...`
- So Causa was DERIVED from Story, then evolved (likely fixing something).

Compare:
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/config.cljc:243` — `editor` atom default `:vscode`
- `tools/causa/src/.../config.cljc:308` — same editor keys catalogue
- `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/open_in_editor.cljs` (entire file · find the chip → click → URI navigation path)
- `tools/causa/src/.../open_in_editor.cljs` (entire file · find what differs)
- `re-frame/source_coords/editor_uri.cljc` (the underlying URI builder · same for both)

Likely candidates for the divergence:
- Story does not set `:rf.story/project-root` so the URI is built with a relative path · vscode does not resolve it
- Source-coord map shape differs (some chips passing classpath-relative path; vscode needs absolute file URL)
- Click handler differs (Story may not actually navigate; Causa may)
- Allowlist gate / sanitisation differs

## Fix path

Port the Causa implementation into Story · keep the public chip API identical. Or: identify the SINGLE divergence and patch Story to match Causa.

## Custom editor configuration

Mike question: "what happens if the programmer is using a different editor — how do they configure?"

Both Story + Causa already support:
- `:vscode` (default)
- `:cursor`
- `:idea`
- Custom template: `{:custom "<uri-template>"}` where the template carries `{:file}` / `{:line}` / `{:column}` placeholders

But this is NOT DISCOVERABLE. Add to scope:
- `docs/story/` — document "Open in editor" config (likely the new Yegge-voice tutorial chapter)
- `docs/causa/` — same for Causa
- README / contributing — point at the config key

The config call shape (per existing impl):
```
(story/configure! {:rf.story/editor :cursor})
(causa-config/configure! {:rf.causa/editor :idea})
(story/configure! {:rf.story/editor {:custom "myeditor://{file}:{line}"}})
```

## Surface
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/open_in_editor.cljs (likely entire file rewrite to match Causa)
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/config.cljc (verify defaults)
- docs/story/01-first-story.md or wherever the open chip first appears in the Yegge tutorial — add a callout for the editor config
- docs/causa/* — symmetric callout

## Posture
Pre-alpha · NO back-compat shims · port + document

## Gates
- npm run test:cljs (Story open-in-editor unit test if exists)
- clojure -M:test from tools/story
- mkdocs build --strict
- Manual smoke: with vscode installed, click an open chip · verify file opens at the right line

title: audit(machines-viz): review tech-stack choice for MachineChart — Stately Studio bar · tech-first then styling
description:

## Question to answer (Phase 1 · audit · NO CODE YET)

Is our current rendering stack (ELK layout + custom SVG render in tools/machines-viz/) the RIGHT CHOICE to hit the Stately Studio quality bar (tools/machines-viz/spec/000-Vision.md §Quality bar)?

Candidates to evaluate:
- **Current**: ELK layout (`tools/machines-viz/src/.../chart/elk_layout.cljs`) + custom SVG (`chart/svg.cljc`)
- **xyflow / react-flow** (used by Stately Studio open-source) — Reagent wrapper or interop layer needed
- **elkjs + d3-graphviz** — alternative renderer over same layout
- **mermaid** — markdown-syntax state-charts · widely adopted · loses interactive granularity
- **dagre-d3** — older but interactive
- **Cytoscape.js** — full graph editor underlying
- **Custom Reagent + SVG** (rewrite from scratch) — least friction but most maintenance

For EACH candidate evaluate:
- Interactivity (clickable nodes/edges/guards/actions live response · keyboard nav · hover affordance)
- Layout robustness (nested compound states · parallel regions · multi-source edges · edge-crossing tolerance at app-scale)
- Visual ergonomics (typography · spacing · color hierarchy · motion · density)
- Bundle cost (dev-only is fine but smaller is better)
- Interop story with Reagent + framework view tagging (data-rf-view-id)
- Long-term maintenance (active upstream? Clojure community familiarity?)

`ai/findings/2026-05-21-machines-viz-tech-stack-audit.md` (gitignored):
- Per-candidate evaluation matrix

DO NOT WRITE PRODUCTION CODE in Phase 1. The findings doc IS Phase 1.

## Phase 2 — only after Mike picks (filed as separate bead)

Adopt the chosen stack. Polish to Stately Studio quality bar.

## Quality bar (spec/000-Vision.md verbatim)

> Good interactive, integrated visualisation, robust to complexity, beautiful, highly ergonomic. The comparator is Stately Studio. Machines-Viz v1.0 MUST match Stately Studio on interactivity, layout robustness, visual ergonomics.

Browse-all reg-schema + late-bind validators. Columns: id · kind (frame/sub/event/cofx/fx) · :spec ref · :enforce policy.

title: docs(story): refresh /docs/story tutorial with annotated screenshots — Storybook-inspired structure + Steve Yegge voice
description:
Refresh the Story tutorial at /docs/story/ (index.md + 01-first-story.md through 07-multi-substrate.md) to bring it to modern user-tutorial standards.

## Inspiration

**Structure**: Borrow from Storybook's user documentation organisation — task-oriented progression, narrative arc from 'first story' to advanced multi-substrate work, copy-pasteable code with full context, deliberate scaffolding. Storybook's tutorials nail the 'follow-along' shape.

**Don't constantly reference Storybook though.** A few comparison callouts where genuinely useful, but the docs are about Story (re-frame2's own tool) — not a comparison piece. The reader landed here because they're building re-frame2, not because they were Googling Storybook alternatives.

## Voice — Steve Yegge

Mike wants the docs FUN to read for a human. Steve Yegge's style:
- Long-form paragraphs that wander productively
- Self-aware asides + jokes about programming tropes
- Strong opinions backed by reasoning
- Stories from the trenches (anecdotes that make a point)
- Dry wit, not slapstick
- Doesn't pull punches when criticising patterns
- Builds intuition first, syntax second

## Annotated screenshots

Put images under /docs/images/story/ (already exists). Each chapter should have 2-5 annotated screenshots: arrows, callout boxes, color-highlighted regions pointing at the affordance under discussion. Capture from the live Story testbed at tools/story/testbeds/counter_with_stories/ (or panel_gallery if Causa-side surfaces are involved).

Capture workflow:
1. shadow-cljs watch on a testbed
2. Browser to localhost:<port>
3. Use a screen-annotation tool (Excalidraw, Skitch, Cleanshot) to add arrows + numbered callouts
4. Save under /docs/images/story/<chapter>-<topic>.png
5. Reference in the markdown with alt text + a one-line caption

## Tutorial-best-practice checklist

- [ ] Clear 'what you'll build' at the top of each chapter
- [ ] 'You should have X working before you start' prereq line
- [ ] Code blocks are COMPLETE (include the ns require + the surrounding fn) — not snippets that need divination
- [ ] After each code change: 'You should now see Y in your browser' — confirmation moments
- [ ] Mistakes section: 'If you see error Z, you probably did A — fix is B'
- [ ] 'Next chapter teases X' at the bottom
- [ ] All inter-chapter links resolve (anchor + filename)
- [ ] Voice stays consistent — first-person plural ('we'), conversational, occasionally funny

## Existing structure to refresh

- index.md — landing page · the elevator pitch + navigation map
- 01-first-story.md — 'Hello, Variant'
- 02-mode-tabs.md — the chrome (test / docs / source / args)
- 03-recorder-codegen.md — capture-and-replay
- 04-workspaces.md — multiple variants composed
- 05-snapshot-identity.md — hot-reload safety
- 06-time-travel.md — replay history
- 07-multi-substrate.md — Reagent / UIx / Helix across one tutorial

Keep these chapter boundaries unless a refactor lands cleaner shape. Consider splitting into Part 1 (Story basics) + Part 2 (Story in anger).

## Posture

Pre-alpha. The docs surface evolves with the API; the Yegge voice survives major API churn (it's about HOW we write, not WHAT we describe). Annotated screenshots will need re-capture as Story chrome iterates.

## Gates

- mkdocs build --strict (every link resolves)
- spell-check (manual or ci-spell)
- Visual review of each screenshot — annotations point at the right thing
- Read-aloud test for the prose: does it sound like a human wrote it with personality?

title: fix(story): play-runner :dispatch-sync of :rf.assert/* event must bridge handler-recorded failure into step-result (failing-play CI gate fix)
description:
The Story play-script runner classifies step success/failure from step-result :passed? — but :dispatch-sync of a :rf.assert/* event records its outcome on app-db's :rf.story/assertions, not into the runner's step stream. Result: a play-script consisting of [[:dispatch-sync [:rf.assert/path-equals [:count] 999]]] structurally CANNOT fail at the play-runner level even when the handler records :passed? false.

This is why story.counter-diagnostics/failing-play has been showing CI MISS (expected=fail actual=pass) since the audit-rename push completed — the test fixture has been broken all along, masked by admin-merges through structurally-irrelevant reasoning.

Fix: extend exec-dispatch! + exec-dispatch-sync! in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/play/runner_events.cljc to (a) snapshot the assertion-record count before dispatch, (b) post-dispatch check for new records with :passed? false, (c) convert the first such record into a step-fail (instead of step-skip).

Gates: npm run test:cljs · clojure -M:test tools/story.

title: spec(machines): unify machine-callback signatures to single context-map arg (audit-of-audits #7)
description:

Single context-map argument across ALL machine callbacks. Every callback receives a context map with keys present only when meaningful.

| Slot | Old signature | New |
|---|---|---|
| :guard | (fn [data event]) | (fn [{:keys [data event]}]) |
| :action | (fn [data event]) | (fn [{:keys [data event]}]) |
| :entry | (fn [data event]) | (fn [{:keys [data event]}]) |
| :exit | (fn [data event]) | (fn [{:keys [data event]}]) |
| :on-spawn | (fn [data id]) | (fn [{:keys [data id]}]) |
| :on-done | (fn [data result]) | (fn [{:keys [data result]}]) |
| :after | (fn [snapshot]) | (fn [{:keys [snapshot]}]) |
| :spawn :data | (fn [snapshot event]) | (fn [{:keys [snapshot event]}]) |

## Why

- Future slot additions don't expand the arity-permutation matrix
- Destructuring at call site makes the meaningful keys explicit

notes:
Mike-LOCKED 2026-05-20 audit-of-audits #7 final design:

## INPUT: uniform context-map across ALL machine callbacks
(fn [{:keys [data event id result snapshot]}])  ; only meaningful keys present per slot type

## OUTPUT: three shapes — narrow by purpose
- :guard                                        → boolean
- :action / :entry / :exit / :on-done / :spawn :data → new :data value (NOT snapshot · prevents accidental logical-state change)
- :on-spawn / :after                            → nil (ignored · advisory)

## Why data-only return on state-mutating
Logical state (:loading/:loaded/:error) is reserved for declarative transition apparatus (:on / :always / :after). Actions can ONLY update working memory (:data bag). Returning ONLY :data structurally prevents callbacks from nudging the machine into a state the spec didn't declare. Matches xstate's assign invariant.

## Snapshot-level escape hatch
If a callback NEEDS to touch :errors / :status / :data + something else from inside · use explicit fx: (dispatch [:rf.machine/update-snapshot {:errors ... :status ...}]). NOT buried in callback return shape.

## Action shape
Worker rewrites all machine-callback signatures + return-handling in implementation/machines + all consumer callbacks. Mechanical · wide blast radius · pre-alpha license to do the clean break.

title: substrate(trace): :rf/dispatch-origin tag on :event/dispatched
description:
Per Causa design doc (#1720, spec/021 §12 substrate gaps) + super-prompt A.5: every epoch has a dispatch origin (user / router / websocket / http / ssr / fx-emit / timer / test-harness / tool / internal). Causa's L2 epoch timeline tags each row with this origin.

The substrate must capture WHERE a dispatch came from. Today the `rf/dispatch` macro stamps `:rf.trace/call-site` (file:line). Extend to also stamp `:rf/dispatch-origin` as a closed-enum value per the A.5 taxonomy.

**Where origins are inferable**:
- `:user` — synthesised from UI handlers; default origin from `rf/dispatch` macro (call-site is a UI namespace?)
- `:router` — re-frame.routing module dispatches → tag at the routing emit-site
- `:fx-emit` — fx handlers dispatching follow-ons → tag at fx-emit site
- `:http` — HTTP managed-request settling → tag at managed-handler success/failure
- `:ssr` — :rf/hydrate dispatch → tag at hydrate boot site
- `:timer` — operator self-tags? or detect setTimeout/setInterval callers?
- `:test-harness` — `rf/dispatch-sync` from clojure.test body → tag at dispatch-sync if a fixture is active
- `:tool` — Causa/Pair-MCP dispatches → tag at tool emit site
- `:internal` — re-frame.core internal dispatches (e.g. :rf.route.internal/settle) → tag at emit site

**Implementation**:
- Closed-enum schema for `:rf/dispatch-origin`
- Default origin via call-site heuristic OR explicit `(rf/dispatch event :origin :foo)` opts
- Spec 009 catalogue row for the new tag

**Acceptance**:
- `:event/dispatched` trace ops carry `:rf/dispatch-origin` field
- All 10 origin categories are populated by appropriate emit sites
- Causa L2 timeline can render the per-row origin tag

title: substrate(trace): :rf.view/rendered trace op + per-substrate adapter instrumentation
description:
Per Causa design doc (#1720, spec/021 §12 substrate gaps): the Reactive panel's cascade attribution needs view-render observation that's NOT substrate-specific introspection.

Add a new trace op `:rf.view/rendered` emitted by each substrate adapter (Reagent / UIx / Helix) when a view re-renders. Carries:
- `:frame` — which frame
- `:view-id` — view identifier (per Spec 006 substrate contract; e.g. component fn name)
- `:cause-event-id` — which event's reactive cascade caused this re-render (the focused epoch id)
- `:cause-subs` — sub ids whose value changes triggered this view's re-render (the sub-chain attribution)

**Per-substrate work**:
- Reagent adapter: hook into ratom watch chain at render time
- UIx adapter: hook into hook-firing
- Helix adapter: hook into render counts

**Pre-alpha posture**: emit always-on per DEBUG gate (no production cost); bounded to 100 views per epoch with "+N more" indicator at capture site.

**Acceptance**:
- All 3 adapters emit the op
- Causa Reactive panel can read it for cascade attribution
- Bundle-isolation gate confirms NOT in production bundles
- Per-adapter testbed smoke verifies emission

Cascade attribution sourced from re-frame.epoch.capture/cascade-cause walk over the in-flight buffer, published as :epoch/cascade-cause late-bind hook. title: test-helpers(rf2-7icrs): add subscribe-once primitive — required for SSR Playwright→CLJS migration
description:
