Current rf2-7icrs (multi-frame CLJS e2e helpers) provides frame-creation, event-dispatch, and view-assertion primitives. What's missing: a synchronous static-HTML check that reads the rendered output ONCE without registering an ongoing subscription. Standard `subscribe` returns a reactive ratom; for SSR's pre-hydration assertion you want the value at a point in time, then discard.

**Direction**: add `(test-helpers/subscribe-once frame query)` returning the current value of the sub *without* keeping a live subscription. Implementation likely: register sub, deref, immediately dispose. Must work in both JVM (SSR pre-hydration) and CLJS (client-side post-hydration) contexts since the SSR migration runs in both.

**Acceptance**:
- New `subscribe-once` exported from `re-frame.test-helpers` (or wherever rf2-7icrs helpers live)
- Works for JVM SSR-side renders and CLJS client-side
- One test asserting the no-leak property (sub doesn't stay registered after the call)
- Doc note in spec/008-Testing.md (or wherever rf2-7icrs surface is described)

**Prereq for**: 3 SSR migration beads (Wave 3 of rf2-tglku) — ssr_basic / ssr_hydration_mismatch / ssr_multi_frame Playwright → CLJS unit tests.

**Pre-alpha posture**: clean new primitive, no shims.

title: Migrate substantive Playwright assertions to CLJS unit tests + adapter testbed smokes
description:

   - **(B) Substrate mounting / hooks behaviour** — assertion is about substrate adapter API (r/atom subscription, UIx hooks, Helix hooks) — movable to the 3 adapter testbed smokes (extend smoke fixtures)
   - **(C) Visual chrome / CSS / layout / real-browser API** — assertion requires actual DOM rendering, focus management, keyboard events with browser semantics, or browser-only APIs (URL, localStorage, IndexedDB) — STAYS Playwright

2. **Migration phase** — implement (A) and (B) migrations spec-by-spec
   - Each migration is its own bead; can parallel-dispatch when surfaces are disjoint
   - Pre-alpha posture: delete the old Playwright assertion when its replacement lands; no dual-coverage

3. **Reshape phase** — after migrations, the residual Playwright gate scope is much smaller
   - Drop it from per-PR REQUIRED gating; move to nightly + release-only
   - Keep a screenshot-baseline check for chrome regression (Playwright again but ~10s scope, runs per PR on chrome-touching diffs only)

**Sister bead**: rf2-k9ekz (path-filter tightening for the gate as-is) is a different layer — gate the existing Playwright run smartly. This epic migrates the assertions OUT so the gate can shrink or disappear.

**Open question for Mike**: should the audit + migration plan be done as a single big bundle, or as per-testbed beads dispatched gradually? Recommend: audit as one worker (produces a manifest doc), then dispatch per-spec migration beads.

Acceptance:
- Manifest doc lists every current Playwright assertion classified A/B/C
- All (A) and (B) assertions migrated to CLJS unit tests / adapter smokes
- Playwright residual = (C)-only
- Decision recorded on whether to drop per-PR Playwright gating once migrated

title: pair-mcp: simplify raw-state polarity — collapse force-redact?/force-elision? to single intention-naming predicate or effective-* fn
description:
Discovered from rf2-c8ohr (re-frame2-pair-mcp wire-surface audit, Finding #2 — major; folds in Finding #11 nit).

tools/raw_state.cljs:53-81. Boot-gate atom allow-raw-state? (default false). Two consumer predicates force-redact? and force-elision? are defined identically as (not @allow-raw-state?) — same body, two names (Finding #11 — 1:1 aliases).

Per-tool call sites currently chain three negations to answer 'did the operator opt in?':
  incl?    (if (raw-state/force-redact?) false (args/parse-bool-arg raw-args :include-sensitive))
  elision? (or (args/parse-bool-arg raw-args :elision) (raw-state/force-elision?))

The predicate name 'force-redact?' asserts an ACTION but the truthy value means 'operator hasn't opted in'. Triple-negation tax on every reader following the privacy posture.

Action options (Mike's call):
  (a) Collapse to single predicate gate-closed? (matches truth value — true when gate closed and per-call args dropped), OR
  (b) Replace with effective-include-sensitive / effective-elision fns that take the raw-arg value and return the post-gate value (one inversion-free call per site).

Option (b) is preferred — fewer reader hops, intention-naming. Folds in Finding #11 (the 1:1 alias).

Call sites to update: tools/snapshot.cljs:26-44, tools/get_path.cljs:32-49, tools/trace_window.cljs:28-32, tools/watch_epochs.cljs:33-37, tools/subscribe.cljs:447-466.

title: pair-mcp: discipline :reason keyword vocabulary across bare / :rf.error/* / :rf.mcp/* dialects
description:
Discovered from rf2-c8ohr (re-frame2-pair-mcp wire-surface audit, Finding #1 — major).

Failures on :ok? false responses tag :reason under three dialects:
- ~32 bare reasons (:invalid-kind, :missing-path, :not-an-event-vector, etc.)
- 3 :rf.error/* reasons (:rf.error/eval-cljs-disabled, :rf.error/concurrent-stream-limit, :rf.error/stream-abuse-detected)
- 1 :rf.mcp/* reason (:rf.mcp/cursor-stale)

Real but undocumented rule: :rf.error/* = operator-gated denial bypassing the tool body; bare = per-call validation; :rf.mcp/* otherwise reserved for wire-replacement substitution markers. :rf.mcp/cursor-stale is the lone outlier crossing the substitution-marker namespace into the :reason slot.

Action: (a) document the rule explicitly in spec/Conventions.md or spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md (one paragraph), AND (b) migrate :rf.mcp/cursor-stale -> :rf.error/cursor-stale so :rf.mcp/* stays exclusively for substitution markers. Optionally consider promoting :runtime-not-preloaded -> :rf.error/runtime-not-preloaded (server-gate denial shape).

Hot-zones: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md, spec/Conventions.md, tools/cursor.cljs:110-123. No back-compat shim (pre-alpha posture).

Evidence: tools/eval_cljs.cljs:42-49, tools/resource_controls.cljs:198-212, tools/subscribe.cljs:378, tools/cursor.cljs:110-123.

title: fix(spec): at-boundary should reject :spec-less handler at registration (rf2-ycqtv finding #8)
description:
rf2-ycqtv audit Finding #8 (minor escalating to major impact). Current behaviour: at-boundary interceptor attached to a handler with no :spec emits :rf.warning/boundary-without-spec once per handler-id in production builds only. Dev path is no-op (no warning fires).

A developer who attaches at-boundary intending to enforce shape validation, but forgets the :spec metadata, doesn't learn until production deploy. The inversion of the dev/prod axis on at-boundary semantics (Finding #2) means dev gives no signal.

Three options:
(a) emit :rf.warning/boundary-without-spec ALSO in dev so developer sees warning immediately;
(b) make registration-time error — registrar rejects (rf/reg-event-fx :foo [at-boundary] handler-fn) when the metadata-map has no :spec; emits :rf.error/boundary-handler-missing-spec;
(c) leave as-is and rely on API.md docstring.

Option (b) is the strongest move — the boundary interceptor is structurally meaningless without a :spec to validate against.

Couples to rf2-todvi (Finding #2) — if at-boundary is renamed, this rejection logic moves with the rename.

Owner: 010-Schemas.md + implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc + implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc (registrar). Inputs: ai/findings/2026-05-20-schemas-api-review.md §Finding 8.

Isolated surface for option (b) — additive validation at reg-event-* time.
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1691 — registrar now hard-rejects schema-less at-boundary registrations with :rf.error/at-boundary-missing-schema. Replaces dispatch-time :rf.warning/boundary-without-spec with uniform dev+prod registration-time error. Gates green (core JVM, schemas JVM, CLJS node, browser, browser-schemas-boundary-prod, mkdocs --strict).

title: decide(spec): tear-down verb axis discipline — clear/destroy/reset/dispose/un- (rf2-k6xyr #1)
description:
From rf2-k6xyr Finding #1 [major]: 5 verbs (clear-, destroy-, reset-, dispose-, un-) used for what is structurally one operation (release a registered or cached thing). The 4-bucket bang rule (Conventions L295-357) pins the bang axis but the verb-choice axis is unspecified.

Examples of the mess: clear-event (registrar), clear-sub-cache! (process), destroy-frame! (lifecycle), dispose-adapter! (lifecycle), unsubscribe (registry decrement).

Mike decision needed:
(a) add a verb-choice axis section to Conventions documenting which verb attaches to which mechanism, or
(b) collapse to two verbs (e.g. clear- for in-process; destroy- for lifecycle boundaries) with explicit deprecation of outliers.

Once decided, follow-on worker renames + updates Conventions + API.md.
notes:
Mayor 2026-05-20: don't wait for Mike. Picking option (b) — collapse to TWO verbs: clear- for in-process registrar+cache+buffer; destroy- for lifecycle boundaries (frames, adapters). Deprecate dispose-, reset-, un-prefix.

Migration skill MUST update: every rename here is a v1→v2 surface change. Worker must update skills/re-frame-migration/ + migration/ + docs/skills/re-frame-migration.md to capture old-name → new-name mappings.

Renames to action:
- dispose-adapter! → destroy-adapter!
- reset-frame! → destroy-frame!+make-frame (or keep but document as the singular compound)
- unsubscribe → clear-sub (consider — collides nothing; or keep un- as the only registry-decrement verb)

Status: convert to type=task once Mike confirms; for now type=decision per default. NOT DISPATCHED YET.
close_reason: Closed

title: fix(causa): the 3 new feature-matrix scenarios from #1608 fail under Playwright harness
description:
## Symptom

PR #1608 (Causa spec+matrix currency landing) shipped 3 new Playwright scenarios that pass `npm run test:cljs` but FAIL under `EXAMPLES_FILTER=causa-feature-matrix npm run test:examples`:

1. `event-lifecycle status colour — cross-site consistency` (rf2-b8pui) — 'Could not dispatch ::initialise for settled-success cascade'
2. `static Routes — browse list, Simulate-URL hermetic preview, → Runtime jump` (rf2-wj46n) — 'Could not opt into Static mode / inject routes override'
3. `static Machines — topology render, browse-list JUMP-to-Runtime, cascade-greyed` (rf2-1laqx) — 'locator.waitFor: Timeout 5000ms exceeded'

## Root cause hypothesis

The worker who shipped these used the test-only `:rf.causa/set-registered-routes-override-for-test` seam + Static-mode opt-in via `configure!`. Those work in CLJS Node tests but NOT under the Playwright harness path — the matrix harness invokes scenarios externally; the testbed needs to be configured for Static mode AND have the override seam available at the right ID resolution timing.

Likely fixes:
- The 3 scenarios may need a dedicated staged-build entry with Static mode pre-configured at testbed initialisation, rather than runtime via `configure!`
- OR the test seam needs a wire-up path that survives the harness's setup sequence
- OR the scenarios need to be authored as multi-frame e2e CLJS Node tests (rf2-7icrs pattern) instead of Playwright

## Acceptance

- All 3 scenarios pass under `EXAMPLES_FILTER=causa-feature-matrix npm run test:examples` locally
- 5x consecutive local runs pass
- CI Story/Causa gate green

## Action plan

The fastest path is to **strip the 3 scenarios from #1608's diff** and re-add them in a follow-on PR with a working harness setup. PR #1608's spec content (5 doc edits + matrix-row updates) is valuable and independent — should land clean.

This bead = follow-on PR scope. Either:
(a) Author them as multi-frame e2e CLJS Node tests (rf2-7icrs pattern — faster, no Playwright friction)
(b) Wire up the testbed setup correctly under the matrix harness

Recommend (a) — Mike's posture this session has been moving Playwright work to CLJS Node tests.

## Cite

PR #1608 CI run https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/actions/runs/26106218160
Source bead chain: rf2-b8pui, rf2-wj46n, rf2-1laqx

title: fix(story): causa-available? predicate false-negative under node-test (find-ns-obj walk)

description:
Mike directive 2026-05-19/20: make the view-assertion test pattern (dispatch → view-fn → walk hiccup → assert content) as easy as possible for app developers, not just internal tool builders.

## Why this exists
Current state:
- docs/guide/13-testing.md §End-to-end through a frame shows dispatch + app-db state assertion
- DOES NOT show how to assert the view actually surfaces the new state
- App-db can be correct AND view broken (rf2-70tkv panel-frozen class shows this exactly)
- find-by-testid / text-content / extract-handler helpers exist as ad-hoc utilities inside tools/causa/test/ — not framework-shipped

## Scope (one PR, ~150-200 LoC)

### Part 1 — Promote helpers to framework
Create implementation/core/src/re_frame/test_helpers.cljc (or .cljs if React/Reagent-specific only) shipping:
- find-by-testid [hiccup-tree test-id] — walk hiccup looking for [_ {:data-testid "..."} ...]
- find-all-by-testid [hiccup-tree test-id]
- text-content [hiccup-node] — recursively join string leaves
- extract-handler [hiccup-node event-key] — pull :on-click / :on-change etc. from attrs
- invoke-handler [hiccup-node event-key & args] — find-and-invoke
Maybe also a small data-testid helper for view-side authoring.

Existing usage in tools/causa/test/.../helpers/* shows the canonical shape. Lift + generalize, drop the Causa-specifics.

title: redesign(testbed/parallel-frames): drop the continuous clock-tick dispatch chain — annoying + low value
description:
Mike feedback 2026-05-19 watching live testbed: the recursive ::clock-tick dispatch (CLOCK-TICK-MS interval, two frames out of phase) pollutes the event spine with infrastructure noise and adds little teaching value. Per the testbed posture (feedback_testbeds_are_test_surfaces: 'no teaching layers, no anti-pattern demos'), the clock-tick mechanism should be redesigned.

## Current shape
tools/causa/testbeds/parallel_frames/core.cljs:
- ::clock-start dispatches ::clock-tick via :dispatch-later
- ::clock-tick recursively dispatches another ::clock-tick
- Two frames (frame-a, frame-b) each run their own chain with slight phase drift
- Goal: demonstrate parallel-frame timing divergence via clock-tick count divergence

## Problems
- Constant spine pollution (recursive dispatches forever)
- Forces L2 list re-renders for relative-time refresh (caught separately as rf2-0s2at)
- Drowns out actual interesting events in the spine
- Teaching value is low — parallel-frame isolation can be demonstrated with on-demand events

## Redesign options (worker chooses; document the call)
- **(a) Remove clock-tick entirely** — replace with user-triggered 'Tick Frame A' / 'Tick Frame B' buttons. Demonstrates parallel-frame isolation on demand. Spine shows ticks ONLY when the user clicks. Simplest, cleanest.
- **(b) Replace recursive dispatch with direct app-db update** —  calls a non-dispatched mutation. The clock advances but the spine doesn't see it. Demonstrates 'parallel frames have independent state' without spine noise. Slight tension with 'everything goes through dispatch'.
- **(c) Keep dispatch but slow rate dramatically (e.g. 30s)** + tag as :rf.causa/infrastructure? — preserves the clock-drift demo but the spine isn't drowning. Depends on Causa-side filter (rf2-ikuwt) for the tag to be respected.

Worker recommendation: **(a) on-demand ticks** — matches testbed posture, no Causa-side dependency, demo still meaningful.

## Files
- tools/causa/testbeds/parallel_frames/core.cljs (events + view)
- tools/causa/testbeds/parallel_frames/index.html (maybe)
- tools/causa/testbeds/parallel_frames/spec.cjs (update if it asserts clock-tick count)
- tools/causa/testbeds/parallel_frames/README.md if any

## Source

## Companion
- rf2-0s2at (relative-time refresh) — independent
- rf2-ikuwt (event-id mute filter) — independent, possibly no longer urgent if this lands

title: fix(causa): relative-time refresh on new-event-arrival (not per-second) — kill the L2 list flicker
description:
Mike feedback 2026-05-19 watching parallel-frames testbed at localhost:8030: the L2 event list flickers because Causa refreshes relative timestamps (e.g. '3s ago') every second, causing the whole list to re-render. Combined with the parallel-frames testbed's clock-tick chain (CLOCK-TICK-MS dispatched recursively), the flicker is constant.

## Design (Mike's call)
Refresh relative timestamps **only when a new event arrives in the spine**. Each new event re-establishes 'now', so all older entries get their relative-time delta recomputed. Between events, displays stay frozen — that's acceptable; relative-time is meaningful between events, not between seconds.

## Approach
- Identify the existing 'now' tick / interval that drives per-second relative-time refresh in the L2 event-row view (tools/causa/src/.../shell.cljs event-row, or wherever).
- Remove the per-second tick.
- Add a derived 'time-anchor' sub that flips on every event-arrival in :rf.causa/spine. Each event row computes its relative time vs the anchor at render-time only.
- Verify: open parallel-frames testbed; flicker should be gone; relative times for older events update lazily as new events arrive.

## Out of scope
- Filtering testbed clock-tick events out of the spine (separate bead: that's about event-id filtering / muting, not relative-time refresh)
- Per-row reactivity optimization (separate concern)

## Hot zone
tools/causa/src/.../shell.cljs (L2 event-row + maybe header now-display)

## Source
Mike's directive watching the parallel-frames testbed live. Cmd-Shift-M / Cmd-K independently confirmed working.

title: audit: testing posture + coverage across /tools — file actionable beads per finding
description:
Mike directive 2026-05-19. Audit the testing posture + coverage across the /tools tree. File severity-tagged follow-on beads for every actionable insight.

## Scope (READ-ONLY)
Audit every tool tree under /tools:
- tools/causa/ — Causa (Runtime + Static surfaces; feature_matrix; testbeds; CLJS + JVM tests)
- tools/story/ — Story (Reagent class-3 mount, RHS embed, sidebar, toolbar, testbeds; JVM + CLJS tests; existing per-testbed spec.cjs files)
- tools/machines-viz/ — newly extracted (PR #1570); has chart tests + theme tokens tests; lightly covered
- tools/mcp-base/ — MCP shared
- tools/mcp-conformance/ — gate tests (NAMING, TOKEN-BUDGETS, end-to-end)
- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/ — pair MCP + the new probe-mcp-path tests
- tools/story-mcp/ — story MCP
- tools/template/ — template tool

## Evaluation lens

**Posture (pre-alpha masterpiece + 3-adapter-smoke policy):**
- Examples policy: examples/ is TEST-FREE; exactly 3 adapter smokes total (Reagent/UIx/Helix), all OUTSIDE examples/. See feedback memory smoke-tests-on-examples-low-value + rf2-8cevm cull bead. The /tools audit should LINE UP with this — find any per-example-equivalent tests in /tools that aren't pulling weight.
- Contract coverage > example coverage. Substrate contract tests, the Causa feature-matrix gate, bundle-isolation, perf-budget, mcp-conformance NAMING/TOKEN-BUDGETS — these are the high-signal gates.
- Pre-alpha masterpiece bar: tests must catch real regressions, not just exist for completeness. Per-line/per-branch coverage is not the goal.

**Three diagnostic axes per tool:**
1. **Redundant coverage** — same regression caught by multiple tests; redundant ones are CI tax
2. **Genuine gap** — a contract / invariant / surface with no test that should have one
3. **Misshapen test** — flaky, slow, brittle, or coupled to implementation details that should test contract not internals

## Method (similar to rf2-9puyf / rf2-qfufu spec audits)

1. For each tool tree, inventory the test layout: directories, frameworks (clojure :test, shadow-cljs :node-test, Playwright .spec.cjs, .cjs), runner scripts, CI workflow gates.
2. Walk each test file → classify as load-bearing-contract / nice-to-have / redundant / brittle.
3. Map current coverage to the Critical Path catalogue (Mike's 'real bugs land in (a) substrate primitives, (b) Causa lens behaviour, (c) bundle/perf invariants').
4. Cross-reference against the existing posture: would removing test X meaningfully reduce confidence? If no, X is a cull candidate.

## Output

### Required deliverables
1. **ai/findings/2026-05-19-tools-testing-audit.md** (gitignored): per-tool inventory + 3-axis classification table + posture verdict.
2. **Follow-on beads — MANDATORY** for every actionable finding:
   - CULL beads (rf2-8cevm-style: 'delete these specs') for redundant coverage
   - GAP beads ('add contract test for X') for genuine gaps where coverage matters
   - REWRITE beads ('replace brittle X with contract Y') for misshapen tests
   - Severity: P1 (load-bearing) / P2 (important) / P3 (polish)
   - Each bead names the file, the current shape, the proposed shape, and why
   - Use --design flag for the design call

Audit verdict alone is NOT enough — Mike's directive: every actionable insight becomes its own bead.

## Out of scope
- Editing test files
- /implementation tree (separate concern; covered by triple-audit earlier this session)
- examples/ tree (already covered by rf2-8cevm cull bead)
- Beads under audit are tested-by-virtue-of-being-meta — don't recurse

title: feat(story): identity-bearing loading skeleton during four-phase loader lifecycle — rf2-38pb9 follow-on
description:
## From rf2-38pb9 audit

Per tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md, variants go through a four-phase loader lifecycle (mount → loaders → drain → render). Currently the intermediate loading UI is implementation-defined per shell — no spec lock. For variants with heavy :loaders this means a blank canvas for visible time.

Storybook ships generic skeleton rows in the sidebar tree. Story's audience would appreciate an *identity-bearing* loading skeleton on the canvas — an amber-shimmer pulse that reads as 'workshop loading'.

## Acceptance criteria

- Spec the canvas loading state in tools/story/spec/003-Render-Shell.md §Loading state
- Skeleton shows when variant is in :loaders or :drain phase and no render has happened yet
- Visual: amber-shimmer pulse on a slate ground (matches theme/colors.cljc tokens)
- Reduced-motion fallback: static amber inset edge, no shimmer
- Default :loaders-complete-when applies (no spec change to lifecycle)
- Skeleton hides immediately on first render
- Playwright test: a variant with a slow :loaders shows the skeleton during the loader phase
- data-test selector: story-canvas-loading-skeleton

## Severity
MED — Story's voice extends into a gap currently undefined.

## References
- ai/findings/2026-05-19-storybook-design-lessons.md §Empty / loading / error states
- tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md §Four-phase lifecycle
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/theme/colors.cljc — accent-amber-soft / accent-amber
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/theme/motion.cljc — shimmer easing curve (add if absent)

## Hot-zone
None. tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/canvas.cljs is the impl surface.

## Out of scope
- Skeleton for the sidebar tree (registry is sync; no loading state)
- Per-variant custom skeleton (lock to canonical workshop skeleton for v1)

- **Sidebar search** = 'I know the component family — narrow the tree to its branches'

- Search input at top of sidebar, above the tree

- Empty-state row for no matches
- 'Escape' clears search

title: feat(story): distinctive icon vocabulary for sidebar rows — rf2-38pb9 follow-on
description:
## From rf2-38pb9 audit

Story sidebar today uses text-only rows with tag badges (rf2-nwiwr). Storybook's audience expects per-row glyphs (story / variant / workspace / docs-leaf / test-leaf) — glyph + text scans noticeably faster than text alone.

**Important — REJECT Storybook's icon set.** Pick a distinctive set with editorial bias matching Story's IBM Plex / amber-accent voice. Candidates:
- Phosphor Icons (variable weight; characterful)
- Tabler (rounded; refined)
- Custom workshop / atelier glyphs

NOT Lucide (AI-slop floor), NOT Heroicons (Tailwind default), NOT Material Icons.

## Acceptance criteria

- Five canonical row-kind icons: story (parent), variant (leaf), workspace, docs-only-variant, test-only-variant
- Selected vocabulary documented in tools/story/spec/014-Chrome-Features.md §Sidebar
- Icon stroke / weight matches Plex's editorial weight (medium / regular pair)
- Inline SVG (no font/CDN dep — Story self-hosts everything)
- Icons honour text colour (currentColor) so they pick up theme tokens

title: fix(machines): :after sub-vec subscription leak when resolved delay is non-positive (rf2-fva6c follow-on)
description:
**MED** — resource leak found by audit rf2-fva6c.

`re-frame.machines.timer/schedule-after-timer!` (implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc:231-309) leaks a subscription ref-count when the delay-key is a subscription vector AND the resolved value is not a positive number.

Path:
1. `resolve-delay-ms` calls `(subs/subscribe frame-id delay-key)` for the vector form (line 135) — bumps the sub-cache ref-count.
2. Caller branches in `schedule-after-timer!` (line 254-262): if resolved-ms is nil / non-number / non-positive, emits `:rf.warning/no-clock-configured` and returns nil — WITHOUT ever calling `cancel-after-timer-entry!` (no entry was stored) and WITHOUT `subs/unsubscribe` on the reaction.
3. The watcher add-watch is also skipped (lines 282-300) so no add-watch path runs.
4. The reaction holds a sub-cache slot ref alive until grace-period evicts — except no future cancellation path will unsubscribe (no entry exists in `after-timers`).

Net: every time the sub's delay resolves to nil/0/negative on first attempt, the per-(parent, delay-key) sub-cache entry's ref-count bumps without a paired decrement. Repeated sub-changed re-resolutions to bad values stack the leak.

Spec citation:
- Spec 006 §Reference counting and disposal — subscribe MUST be paired with unsubscribe to avoid cache-slot accumulation.
- Spec 005 §Delayed :after transitions — `:rf.warning/no-clock-configured` is the documented recovery for a bad resolved delay.

Recommendation: in the bad-delay branch (cond clause line 253-262), unsubscribe the reaction before the early return — or restructure `resolve-delay-ms` to return the reaction only on success and call `subs/unsubscribe` internally on the bad-value path. Either way: every `subscribe` call must have a paired `unsubscribe` on every exit path.

**Acceptance**:
- Test fixture: register a machine with `:after` delay-key = subscription vector that resolves to 0 / nil / negative; assert the sub-cache ref-count returns to zero after the `:rf.warning/no-clock-configured` trace fires.
- The other early-exit paths (server? true, after-watch-failed) are also audited for the same shape.

Parent: rf2-fva6c audit.
close_reason: PR #1557 merged. schedule-after-timer! pairs subs/unsubscribe in bad-delay branch.

Coordinate via separate findings docs; Search issues across title and ID (excludes closed issues by default).

ID-like queries (e.g., "bd-123", "hq-319") use fast exact/prefix matching.
Text queries search titles. Use --desc-contains for description search.
Use --status all to include closed issues.

Examples:
  bd search "authentication bug"
  bd search "login" --status open
  bd search "database" --label backend --limit 10
  bd search --query "performance" --assignee alice
  bd search "bd-5q" # Search by partial ID (fast prefix match)
  bd search "security" --priority-min 0 --priority-max 2
  bd search "bug" --created-after 2025-01-01
  bd search "refactor" --status all  # Include closed issues
  bd search "bug" --sort priority
  bd search "task" --sort created --reverse
  bd search "api" --desc-contains "endpoint"
  bd search "cleanup" --no-assignee --no-labels

Usage:
  bd search [query] [flags]

Flags:
  -a, --assignee string              Filter by assignee
      --closed-after string          Filter issues closed after date (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339)
      --closed-before string         Filter issues closed before date (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339)
      --created-after string         Filter issues created after date (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339)
      --created-before string        Filter issues created before date (YYYY-MM-DD or RFC3339)
      --desc-contains string         Filter by description substring (case-insensitive)
      --empty-description            Filter issues with empty or missing description
      --external-contains string     Filter by external ref substring (case-insensitive)
      --has-metadata-key string      Filter issues that have this metadata key set
  -h, --help                         help for search
  -l, --label strings                Filter by labels (AND: must have ALL)
      --label-any strings            Filter by labels (OR: must have AT LEAST ONE)
  -n, --limit int                    Limit results (default: 50) (default 50)
      --long                         Show detailed multi-line output for each issue
      --metadata-field stringArray   Filter by metadata field (key=value, repeatable)
      --no-assignee                  Filter issues with no assignee
      --no-labels                    Filter issues with no labels
      --notes-contains string        Filter by notes substring (case-insensitive)
      --priority-max string          Filter by maximum priority (inclusive, 0-4 or P0-P4)
      --priority-min string          Filter by minimum priority (inclusive, 0-4 or P0-P4)
      --query string                 Search query (alternative to positional argument)

title: design: Story distinctive backgrounds + depth (replace flat solids)
description:
Story chrome uses solid hex backgrounds with zero box-shadow declarations on any surface. Toolbar / sidebar / canvas / right-panel all share #252526 ground; no depth hierarchy. The canvas frame (the actual focal region — the work-under-development) is visually identical to every inspector panel.

Per the frontend-design rubric: 'Create atmosphere and depth rather than defaulting to solid colors. Apply creative forms like gradient meshes, noise textures, layered transparencies, dramatic shadows, decorative borders.'

See ai/findings/2026-05-19-story-design-causa-integration.md §Part A pillar 5.

1. Layered surface system — base canvas / inspector panels / floating overlays at visibly distinct elevations (shadow + ground colour).
2. Canvas frame (the focal workshop region) carries a distinctive accent edge or shadow so the user's eye snaps to it.
3. Consider a subtle grain / noise overlay on dark grounds (~2-3% noise) to cut eyestrain.

title: design: Story motion + transitions (currently zero)
description:
Story chrome has ZERO motion. No transitions, no micro-interactions, no entrance choreography. Hover states snap; help overlay opens with no fade; shell mount throws every region onto the page in one synchronous render.

Per the frontend-design rubric: 'Use animations for effects and micro-interactions. Focus on high-impact moments: one well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals (animation-delay) creates more delight than scattered micro-interactions.'

See ai/findings/2026-05-19-story-design-causa-integration.md §Part A pillar 3.
acceptance_criteria:
1. New ns re-frame.story.theme.motion with timing + easing tokens (e.g. :micro-tap 80ms ease-out, :panel-slide 220ms cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1), :overlay-fade 180ms).
2. Hover transitions on every clickable chrome element (sidebar rows, chips, tabs, toolbar buttons).
3. Staggered entrance choreography on shell mount (toolbar → sidebar → main → right-panel reveal sequence).
4. Focus-ring animation on :focus-visible.
5. Help overlay + recorder dialogs fade in/out via the overlay-fade token.
6. Use Web Animations API or CSS transitions — no extra deps required.

- Sort options: Name asc (default), States desc, Live desc.
- Empty state: 'No machines registered. reg-machine to add the first.'
- Selection persists to localStorage `causa.static.machines.selected-id` (per host).
- Per-row `→ Runtime` chip — JUMPS to Runtime Machines tab with this machine pre-selected (Q6 worker lean a).

### Definition detail header (L4-right top)
- Title: `<machine-id> · <source-coord> ↗ · <N> states · <M> live (→ Runtime)`.

### 4-mode sub-strip (per findings §3.2 + Mode-S findings §2.1)
- Pill row `[Topology][Sim][Instances][Cascade]` immediately below header.
- Mnemonics: `t` / `s` / `i` / `c` (fire when focus in right-pane per findings Q12 lean).
- Default: Topology.
- Selected sub-mode persists to localStorage `causa.static.machines.sub-mode.<machine-id>`.

### Topology mode renderer (Static default, per findings §3.3)

- NO live-state highlight in Static (Topology in Static is static-read).
- Source-coord chips on state nodes when source-coord lifted from `reg-machine` (degrades gracefully if missing).
- Definition-stale indicator post hot-reload (per findings §3.3 last table row).
- Click state → metadata rail (incoming/outgoing edges, source-coord chip, J = jump to source).
- Auto-pan to active state: N/A (no active state in Static Topology).
- 'Open chart in popout' affordance available.

### Instances mode (per findings Q6 — JUMP)
- Clicking the pill SWITCHES to Runtime + opens Runtime Machines tab + selects this machine + picks Mode B or C per consolidated-design §0ter.3 auto-detect (Mode B for 2-8 instances, Mode C for ≥8).

- The Static surface stays static.

title: spec(009+005+Spec-Schemas): document :rf.machine/guard-evaluated + :rf.machine/action-ran traces (rf2-2nwfd follow-on)
description:
**Origin:** audit rf2-d1kdf (2026-05-19 /implementation vs /spec alignment review).

## Drift
rf2-2nwfd #1469 added two new trace events emitted from `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc`:

- **`:rf.machine/guard-evaluated`** `{:guard-id <kw-or-fn> :input {:data <data> :event <event>} :outcome :pass | :fail}` — emitted from the unified `evaluate-guard` helper at the three guard call sites (pick-transition, pick-after-transition, pick-always-transition). Only user-declared guards emit; synthesised always-true skipped; first-fail short-circuit preserved.
- **`:rf.machine/action-ran`** `{:action-id <kw-or-fn> :input {:data :event} :outcome <return> | :ok | :rf.error/action-threw :exception <Throwable>}` — emitted from `run-action`. Success-with-nil-return becomes `:ok`; throwing actions emit one trace with `:rf.error/action-threw` + the Throwable before propagating the failure Result.

Both traces flow through `trace/emit!` so `*handler-scope*` auto-stamps `:dispatch-id` under `:tags` — Causa's `:rf.causa/machine-transitions-for-focused-event` sub groups them with the originating event without explicit threading.

The substrate change is intentional and tested (`implementation/machines/test/re_frame/guard_action_traces_test.clj`, 221 lines — 7 named scenarios).

## Spec silence (three places)

1. **`spec/009-Instrumentation.md` line 390** — enumerates `machines/transition.cljc` trace surface. The list reads `:rf.machine/event-received`, `:rf.machine/transition`, `:rf.machine.microstep/transition`, `:rf.machine/snapshot-updated`, `:rf.machine.lifecycle/created`, `:rf.machine/system-id-bound`, `:rf.machine/system-id-released`, `:rf.machine.timer/*` + machine-error categories. The new pair is missing.

2. **`spec/005-StateMachines.md`** — §Trace events does not mention `:rf.machine/guard-evaluated` or `:rf.machine/action-ran`. Guards / actions are user-facing first-class concepts; the trace surface is part of the user-discoverable contract.

title: feat(causa): reshape Routes lens — flat list + search + Simulate-URL (drop decorative tree)
description:
From ai/findings/2026-05-19-routing-inheritance-audit.md (verdict B, 2026-05-19 15:36 AUSEST).

## Why
Causa's current Routes lens (tools/causa/src/.../panels/routing.cljs + routing_helpers.cljc) renders routes as a tree indented by URL-path-segment depth. The audit found:

- Routes are FLAT in the spec (012-Routing.md) and in re-frame.routing impl
- :parent is a render-side data convention with ZERO runtime inheritance (:on-match / :can-leave / :on-error / :tags / :params / scroll — every meta key resolves from active route only)
- Causa's tree groups routes by URL-prefix similarity, NOT by :parent — so it MISLEADS more than informs
- The match-resolver is structural (6-rule rank on URL pattern), not hierarchical

## What to ship
Replace project-route-tree + indented row rendering with:
1. Flat list sorted by :path (lexicographic) — same data, no indentation
2. Per-row chips: route-id, :path, :doc + small icons for routes carrying :on-match / :can-leave / :tags / :parent
3. Click-to-expand inline meta map on chip
4. Substring search box across route-id + :path + :doc
5. **Simulate-URL input** — paste URL, show 6-rule rank tuple per candidate (from :rf.route/rank) and the winner; this is the load-bearing interactive surface
6. For routes with :parent: compact inline '↑ parent → :route/X' annotation; hover/click expands :rf.route/chain
7. Delete project-route-tree depth-from-path-segments logic

title: feat(causa): surface Flows in Event Detail panel — peer section between Effects + Returned-value
description:
**Source:** ai/findings/2026-05-19-causa-machine-inspector-mode-s.md §13 + §11 Comment 8 (Mike, 2026-05-19 ~15:00 AUSEST).

## Gap
Flows (`reg-flow` derived computations that fire automatically AFTER event handlers complete) are INVISIBLE in Causa's Runtime lens today. Step 4 of the cascade (handler effects fire → app-db writes → FLOWS FIRE → subs invalidate → views re-render) is invisible to the user. Users see app-db change but cannot attribute the change to the flow that caused it; views re-render but cannot trace back to the originating flow.

## What to ship
Cascade-step Flows section in the Event Detail panel, rendered as a PEER section between Effects and Returned-value (NOT folded into Effects — flows have a distinct lifecycle: 'what the framework did automatically' vs 'what the handler said to do').

Proposed structure (per findings §13):

```
EVENT     [event-id]    :cart/add-item
COEFFECTS :db (read), :now, :random, …
EFFECTS   (handler-returned, fired in declared order)
          :db        → 1 path written: [:cart :items]
          :dispatch  → [:analytics/track-add]
FLOWS     (auto-fired after effects, cascade order)
          ▸ :cart-total              wrote [:cart :total] 47.50 → 52.50
                                     read  [:cart :items]
          ▸ :tax-due                 wrote [:tax :due] 4.75 → 5.25
                                     read  [:cart :total]
          ▸ :grand-total-display     wrote [:checkout :grand-total]
                                     read  [:cart :total] [:tax :due]
RETURNED VALUE  (handler return)
```

## Per-flow row payload
- Flow id (jump-to-source via standard chip)
- Inputs (read paths from `:inputs` slot of reg-flow)
- Outputs (write paths from `:output` slot)
- Before/after values (same formatting as App-db diff slices)
- Subtle 'via' markers or indent when one flow's output triggers another (cascade order)

## NOT in scope
- A separate top-level tab. The 6-tab Runtime bar stays; flows are cascade detail inside Event Detail.
- Cross-cutting App-db path tagging or Views attribution — those are sibling beads (bead 2, bead 3).
- Static-side Flows sub-tab — that is bead 8.

## Dependencies
- May depend on bead 4 (flow trace events): if re-frame2's flow mechanism doesn't emit trace events, the framework needs to add them first.

## Citations
- Comment 8 (Mike, 2026-05-19 ~15:00 AUSEST) in §11 of Mode S findings.
- §13 of Mode S findings (post-iteration design).

## Parent
None (new design surface, downstream of Causa runtime work).

Helpers (flows-fired, flows-skipped, flows-with-chain-marks) live in panels.event_detail and are pure data → data. Ready for rf2-s8r6c consumer.

title: fix(causa): section-grouping count-rendered-nodes overstates :same subtree cost, shatters legitimate clusters
description:
Discovered by rf2-ogkh0 corpus sweep (53 real diff pairs, 1325 runs). Findings doc: ai/findings/2026-05-19-causa-section-grouping-heuristics.md §5.1.

## Bug
`count-rendered-nodes` (in tools/causa/src/.../section_grouping.cljc) walks the entire subtree counting :same siblings verbatim. But the renderer collapses each :same subtree to a single chip. The split-overfilled rule uses this inflated count to decide when to split a cluster, so it misfires on legitimately coalesced clusters with many :same siblings.

## Repro
`pg/large-multi-tier` corpus entry: 50 new `:catalog/sku-new-*` keys merged into a 200-key map. Defeats EVERY (depth, context) combination in the swept space (depth ≤ 5, context ≤ 100). Re-run with extended sweep up to context=250 still fails. Tuning alone doesn't fix this.

## Fix proposal (~10 LoC per worker)
Charge each `:same` child as 1 in `count-rendered-nodes` instead of recursing into the subtree.

## Surface
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/section_grouping.cljc — count-rendered-nodes fn
- tools/causa/test/.../section_grouping_test.cljc — add regression test covering the pg/large-multi-tier shape

## Acceptance
- Regression test pins the bug
- pg/large-multi-tier corpus entry from rf2-ogkh0's findings renders as one cluster (not shattered)
- rf2-ogkh0's recommended defaults (depth=2, context=40) work correctly post-fix on the full 53-pair corpus

## Parent
rf2-ogkh0 (closed; recommended-defaults rollout gates on this fix landing first OR explicitly accepting the pg/large-multi-tier shatter as a known limitation).

title: fix(causa): keybinding listener should respect :launch.keybinding/enabled? at runtime, not just preload (rf2-q7who.1 follow-on)
description:
Surfaced by rf2-q7who.1 worker on PR #1500.

CURRENT BEHAVIOR (rf2-4eyik PR #1497):
- causa-config.cljc defines :launch.keybinding/enabled? (default true)
- causa/keybinding.cljs/attach! is called at PRELOAD time
- attach! reads the slot once at attach time
- If preload runs before any consumer sets the slot to false, the listener is attached and stays attached

CONSEQUENCE FOR STORY (rf2-q7who.1 PR #1500):
- Story's causa-preset bridges :launch.keybinding/enabled? false via story/causa-preset/ensure-causa-mounted!
- BUT ensure-causa-mounted! fires at MOUNT time (later than preload)
- Causa's preload has already attached the listener with the default-true reading
- Story's bridge sets the slot to false too late — listener stays attached → Ctrl+K still swallowed
- PR #1500 ships the declaration at the right surface (contract is correctly expressed) but doesn't actually disable the listener at runtime

FIX SHAPES:
(a) attach! becomes REACTIVE — subscribes to the slot value and detaches/reattaches as it flips. Most architecturally honest; the slot becomes a live config knob.
(b) Causa exposes a public detach! fn — Story calls it from ensure-causa-mounted! after setting the slot. Simpler; the slot remains attach-time-only but the caller has an escape hatch.
(c) Restructure: defer keybinding/attach! until first user interaction OR first config read instead of preload. Lazier; sidesteps the timing issue.

Recommendation: (b) — minimal change; the slot's contract stays attach-time-only; Story (or any other embedder) can opt out by calling detach! after setting the flag. (a) is also fine if we want the slot to be a runtime knob in general.

Acceptance:
- Story-mounted Causa: Ctrl+K reaches Story's command palette at runtime, not just intent-declared
- Standalone Causa: unchanged (preload attaches; nothing calls detach!)
- Test exercises the runtime path: mount Causa in a Story-like host that bridges the slot to false, dispatch Ctrl+K, assert Story's handler fires (not Causa's)

Parent: rf2-q7who.1 (PR #1500 awaiting CI green). Companion / follow-on. Could ship in a separate small Causa-side PR after #1500 merges, OR be added to the rf2-q7who.1 PR before merge (depends on Mike's preference for sequencing).

title: feat(causa+story): clean multi-frame testbed — one app in :above + :below frames, isolated, exercises Causa's full feature surface (machines, HTTP, Issues, etc.)
description:
Replaces the shop testbed anti-pattern (rf2-yhxk3) that violates frame isolation by routing data across frames. Per Mike (2026-05-19): 'subs should never get to other frames. Frames are isolated contexts.' Architectural rule: feedback_frames_are_isolated_contexts memory.

## Shape

ONE app, mounted in TWO frames on ONE page.

Frame ids: :above and :below.

Both frames mount the same app code. Each is a fully isolated reactive context. There is NO cross-frame sub computation; NO routing data between frames; NO 'route data home' pattern. The app runs independently in each frame.

## Goal

Test bed must accomplish two things at once:
1. **Test Causa's frame-switching** — the developer can use Causa to switch between observing :above and :below independently. The picker, the focus controls, the L2/L3/L4 panels must all correctly scope to the active frame.
2. **Exercise Causa's full feature surface** — the app must use enough features that switching frames in Causa reveals interesting differences:
   - Machines (state machines firing inside each frame)
   - HTTP (correlation IDs, in-flight/settled/error states)
   - Issues (intentional + edge-case scenarios)
   - Sub recomputation patterns (mounted/re-rendered/unmounted)
   - Cascades + events
   - App-db evolution

The two frames running the SAME app at the SAME time on the SAME page means: Causa shows two parallel reactive contexts that diverge as the user interacts with each independently. That's the demo's punchline.

## Anti-patterns to avoid

- DO NOT put one frame's data into another frame's app-db
- DO NOT use any cross-frame sub mechanism
- DO NOT have one frame's events affect another frame's state
- DO NOT share dispatch buses across frames

Each frame is its own world.

## Surface

- Likely: tools/causa/testbeds/<new-name>/ (e.g. multi-frame-isolation, or simpler — pick a memorable name in keeping with the existing testbed naming patterns)
- Source: probably ~200-400 LoC for the app + a small driver that mounts it twice
- Documentation: a README explaining the demo's point (frame isolation + Causa's frame-switching affordance) and what to try in Causa to see the isolation
- Spec docs: cross-link from spec/006-Reactive-Substrate.md (or wherever frames are normatively documented) to this testbed as the canonical multi-frame demo

## Companion decision

The existing shop testbed (rf2-yhxk3 / PR #1479) is the anti-pattern. After this clean testbed lands, the shop testbed should likely be removed (or marked anti-pattern with a prominent doc note). That's a separate decision — file as follow-on once this clean testbed exists and Mike's seen it live.

Priority P2 — testbeds are infrastructure for Causa development quality. Without a clean exemplar, the anti-pattern persists.
notes: ADDITIONAL CONSTRAINT (mayor 2026-05-19, from Mike): testbeds are TEST surfaces, not tutorial surfaces. The replacement must contain NO deliberate bugs (no ':cart/subtotal-WRONG'-style intentional brokenness), NO teaching layers ('LAYER 5' comments), NO anti-pattern demonstrations. Exercise features cleanly in a working configuration. The exercise IS observing two isolated frames diverge as the user interacts with each — not 'fix this bug.' Memory note: feedback_testbeds_are_test_surfaces.md.

No cross-frame subs. No deliberate bugs. Slow mock-fetch (~600ms) is legitimate Issues source. 831 LoC across 7 files. All gates green. Shop testbed deletion follow-on filed as rf2-ljmm1.

title: bug(causa+story): investigate vscode:// URI not opening files even with absolute paths
description:
Per Mike's heads-up (2026-05-18 20:18 AUSEST): previously reported in Story context — even when full absolute path was supplied, vscode:// URI did NOT load the file.

This is distinct from rf2-6jyf6 (relative→absolute path fix). The DEEPER question: does the vscode:// URI mechanism actually work from the Causa/Story DOM at all?

Investigation surface:
- tools/causa/src/.../open_in_editor.cljs — current URI construction + dispatch mechanism (window.location.assign per rf2-muvs8 #1433)
- tools/story/src/.../ui/* — Story's open-in-editor (if separate)
- Browser console logs when 'open' chip is clicked: does any URI fire? Does Windows intercept it? Does vscode register the URI scheme?

Possible causes:
(a) URI scheme not registered properly on the user's system (vscode setup issue, not framework bug)
(b) Wrong URI shape — should be vscode://file/<abspath>:<line>:<col> but actually emitting something else
(c) window.location.assign() launches the URI but VSCode silently rejects it (e.g. malformed encoding, wrong column number, file doesn't exist)
(d) Windows defender / browser security intercepting the cross-protocol launch
(e) Should be using a different mechanism: open-in-editor-protocol-handler, or a small native helper, or vscode-insiders:// for insiders builds

Recommend: small audit worker to verify in browser console + try alternative URI shapes + report what actually works. Could be a documentation issue (require vscode://file/ prefix explicitly + show troubleshooting).

Coupled to rf2-6jyf6 — that bead's fix assumes URI-loading works once path is absolute. This bead questions that assumption.

title: bug(causa): Event lens 'open' chip — relative path fails to open in VSCode
description:
Per Mike's live-testbed observation (2026-05-18 20:13 AUSEST, shop @ :8767, post-#1490 Event lens 7-section order):

This is distinct from rf2-muvs8 (#1433 fixed the .assign() vs window.location.href bug on Windows). That's a different layer.

Two candidate fixes:

(a) Substrate change: capture absolute paths at registration time
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords/* — record absolute path (or repo-root + relative) when reg-event-* / reg-sub / reg-fx fires
- Substrate has access to the absolute path via *ns* + classpath; resolves at reg-time

(b) Causa-side fix: resolve relative → absolute at open-time
- tools/causa/src/.../open_in_editor.cljs — prepend a configured project root before dispatching :rf.editor/open
- Project root could come from a Causa configure! option, or detected at preload-time

(c) Hybrid: substrate captures relative; Causa configure! takes project-root; open-in-editor combines them

Recommend (c) — substrate stays minimal (no abs-path baggage in registry meta), Causa's open-in-editor takes a configurable root, app-author sets it once at preload.

Affects ALL source-coord chips:
- Event lens Dispatch SITE chip
- Event lens Handler chip  
- Event lens Interceptors chip

- Possibly others

Investigation surface:

notes:
CROSS-PLATFORM REQUIREMENT (Mike 2026-05-18 20:25): fix must work on Windows + Linux + macOS.

Cross-platform URI construction rules:

WINDOWS (Mike's test results):
- Working: vscode://file/C:/Users/miket/.../file.cljs:LINE  OR  vscode://file/c:/Users/...
- BROKEN: vscode://file//c/Users/...
- Detect+normalise: paths shaped //<letter>/... or /<letter>/... → <letter>:/...
- Native Windows backslashes (C:\Users\miket\foo.cljs): replace \ with /
- Drive-letter case (C: vs c:) doesn't matter — don't bother normalising

LINUX (absolute path /home/user/...):
- Expected working: vscode://file/home/user/foo.cljs:LINE  (single slash; leading / of path concatenates with file/)
- Or possibly: vscode://file//home/user/foo.cljs:LINE  (double slash; needs verification)
- Detection: starts with / but NOT followed by single-letter+/ (which would be Windows-shape POSIX)
- Pass through; URI = vscode://file<absolute-path-with-leading-slash>:LINE

MACOS (absolute path /Users/user/...):
- Same shape as Linux: vscode://file/Users/user/foo.cljs:LINE
- Same detection + pass-through rule

DETECTION FUNCTION (Clojure sketch):
(defn ->vscode-uri [path line col]
  (let [norm (cond
               ;; Windows POSIX-via-git-bash (//c/...): strip // + add :/
               (re-matches #'^//[A-Za-z]/.*' path)
               (clojure.string/replace path #'^//([A-Za-z])/' ':/')
               
               ;; Windows single-slash POSIX (/c/...): same shape
               (re-matches #'^/[A-Za-z]/.*' path)
               (clojure.string/replace path #'^/([A-Za-z])/' ':/')
               
               ;; Windows native (C:\...): replace backslashes with forward slashes
               (re-matches #'^[A-Za-z]:[\/]+.*' path)
               (-> path (clojure.string/replace '\' '/'))
               
               ;; POSIX absolute (/home/..., /Users/...): pass through
               :else
               path)
        ;; Windows shape needs leading slash for URI: vscode://file/C:/...
        prefixed (if (re-matches #'^[A-Za-z]:/.*' norm)
                   (str '/' norm)
                   norm)]
    (str 'vscode://file' prefixed ':' line)))

PLATFORM DETECTION (if needed):
- Use window.navigator.platform OR window.navigator.userAgentData.platform
- 'Win32' or 'Win64' → Windows path rules
- 'Linux' or 'MacIntel' → POSIX pass-through
- Could also auto-detect via path-shape patterns above (no platform-detection needed; pattern-based normalisation handles all cases)

The auto-detection pattern-based approach is preferred — works regardless of what userAgent reports.

TESTS:
- Windows-via-git-bash path //c/Users/miket/foo.cljs → vscode://file/c:/Users/miket/foo.cljs:1
- Windows native C:\Users\miket\foo.cljs → vscode://file/C:/Users/miket/foo.cljs:1
- Linux /home/user/foo.cljs → vscode://file/home/user/foo.cljs:1
- macOS /Users/user/foo.cljs → vscode://file/Users/user/foo.cljs:1

If the in-flight worker has already shipped a Windows-only fix, file a follow-on for Linux+macOS coverage. Worker should ideally see this update during their PR composition phase.

title: design(causa): Causa-as-Story-RHS embedding-contract gaps (Ctrl+K + <nav> + getByText collisions)
description:
rf2-drprn investigation revealed three real collision points when Causa is preloaded into the existing :examples/counter-with-stories build (where Story tests already exist):

1. Keyboard collision: Causa keybinding.cljs attaches a global keydown listener with capture=true that calls stopPropagation() - Ctrl+K opens Causa's command palette. Story's own Ctrl+K command palette never fires because Causa swallows the event. Surfaces as Story command-palette browser tests timing out at .click() because Causa's overlay intercepts.

2. <nav> role ambiguity: Causa's L3 tab bar is a <nav data-testid='rf-causa-tab-bar'>. Story's sidebar is also <nav>. Playwright's getByRole('navigation') becomes strict-mode-ambiguous; every Story test using that role lookup fails.

3. Aside text-content overlap: Causa is mounted inside Story's <aside role='complementary'>. Tests using getByRole('complementary').getByText('Schema') match Causa's frame-picker <option value=':story.counter-matrix/schema-invalid'> (hidden) and time out on .first()'s visibility wait.

Workaround taken in rf2-drprn: created a dedicated under-featured testbed (tools/story/testbeds/causa_rhs_smoke/) that has no Ctrl+K palette, no Schema panel, no mode-tab chrome - so the 4 Causa-as-RHS regression scenarios run cleanly. The broader counter-with-stories testbed deliberately does NOT preload Causa for the same reason.

Real fix shape - three independent threads, all Causa-side:
A. Keybinding suppression: causa-config.cljc adds :launch/keybinding/enabled? false toggle; when false, keybinding.cljs/attach! short-circuits. The Story shell would set this in its causa_preset call.
B. <nav> role: re-tag Causa's tab bar as role='tablist' (more accurate ARIA) or non-landmark <div>. The :nav element is wrong: tabs aren't site navigation.
C. Frame picker option text: scope the frame-picker text content so it can't collide with host-app assertions, or move the selector behind an explicit data-testid the host can rely on (already there) - the collision is purely a Story-side test-quality issue if A + B are fixed.

The contract that says 'Causa embeds cleanly into [data-rf-causa-host]' (rf2-q9kv5 + rf2-om6fa) holds visually but breaks for host-app keyboard + accessibility-role surfaces. Three threads should be filed separately so they can ship independently.
close_reason: Decision-resolved: 3 threads (A+B+C) split into child beads. A (rf2-4eyik keybinding toggle) + B (rf2-lvf8t tab-bar ARIA) shipped via PR #1497 (squash 6ff422f0). C (rf2-7cqak frame-picker text scope) deferred per parent body — reassess after A+B fix the structural causes (likely auto-resolves to Story-side test-quality). Follow-on rf2-q7who.1 filed by worker for Story-side wire-up of :launch.keybinding/enabled? false.

title: feat(causa): focus-navigation primitive — L2 row gutter sets focus set; [◀][▶] step within it
description:
Per design captured through Mike's interactive refinement (2026-05-18). NOT a filter — full L2 list stays visible; in-focus rows highlighted, out-of-focus dimmed; nav buttons skip out-of-focus to next/prev in-focus row.

## Lens model

| Row state | Visual |
|---|---|
| Out of focus | Dimmed (40% opacity) |
| In focus | Full opacity + open marker ⦿ in left gutter |
| Pivot (anchor) | Filled marker ⦿ in gutter |

## Gesture model

The left gutter (~6-10px) is the FOCUS surface. The row body is the SELECTION surface. Distinct gestures.

| Gesture | Effect |
|---|---|
| Click out-of-focus row's GUTTER | Becomes new pivot; focus rebuilds around its dimension |
| Click out-of-focus row's BODY (outside gutter) | Selects; focus CLEARED |
| Click pivot's GUTTER again | Toggles focus OFF |
| Click in-focus row's BODY | Selects within subset; focus stays |
| Esc key | Clears focus |
| Ribbon chip ✕ | Clears focus |

## Navigation

When focus is SET: [◀] [▶] skip past out-of-focus rows, land on next/previous in-focus row.
When focus is OFF: [◀] [▶] behave exactly as today (one row at a time, full stream).
Boundary behaviour: greys out OR shows soft '← back to all events' hint at first/last in-focus row.

## Default dimensions (implicit from gutter-clicked row)

| Clicked row property | Focus dimension |
|---|---|
| Event-id (e.g. :cart/add-item) | All rows with same event-id |
| Triggered a machine transition | All events involving that machine instance |
| Triggered an HTTP fx | All events in that HTTP correlation chain |
| Has source-coord X | All events dispatched from X |

The dimension is implicit-from-context. Right-click on gutter (future enhancement; defer) could let user override the default dimension.

## Ribbon chip

When focus is active: small chip in ribbon area shows '🎯 <pivot-id> ✕'. Click ✕ also clears focus. Provides at-a-glance 'I'm focused' status.

## Cross-panel triggers (rf2-si9o5 cross-link)

Same focus mechanism lights up from other panels:
- Click machine in Machines panel → focus = events involving that machine
- Click managed-fx row → focus = events in that fx's correlation chain
- Click slice in App-db panel → focus = events that mutated that slice (future)

The focus set is stored centrally (spine); panels are sources that set it.

## Surface to touch

- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/spine.cljs — add :rf.causa/focus-set slot + reducer (predicate or set of dispatch-ids). New events: :rf.causa/set-focus :rf.causa/clear-focus :rf.causa/step-focus-next :rf.causa/step-focus-prev
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/[L2 row component] — gutter UI (clickable strip) + dim CSS via :class style binding
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/shell.cljs — ribbon chip + Esc keybind handler
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/focus_helpers.cljc — pure dimension-picker + predicate-builder helpers
- Updated nav-button event handlers — read focus set when picking prev/next
- Tests: tools/causa/test/day8/re_frame2_causa/{spine, focus_helpers}_test.cljc covering all 4 dimensions + edge cases

## In-flight collision avoidance

Other workers + open PRs touch:
- tools/causa/src/.../panels/event_detail.cljs (rf2-zh2qc Event lens panel — different file)
- tools/causa/src/.../panels/routing.cljs + shell.cljs (rf2-nrbs9 Routing tab — shell.cljs same file, different sections)
- tools/causa/testbeds/shop/ (PR #1479 — testbeds tree, disjoint from src/)
- tools/story/ (PR #1478 — disjoint)

shell.cljs is the most likely conflict point. Both rf2-nrbs9 (adds :routing tab to nav) and this bead (adds ribbon chip + Esc handler) touch shell. Different sections; should merge cleanly. If the Routing tab PR lands first, rebase this against it.

## Acceptance

- Spine carries :rf.causa/focus-set; 4 events wire it (set/clear/step-next/step-prev)
- L2 rows render gutter affordance; gutter-click sets focus; body-click clears focus
- Dim CSS applied to out-of-focus rows
- Esc key + ribbon chip ✕ both clear focus
- Nav buttons skip out-of-focus rows when focus set; greyed at boundary
- Default dimension correctly inferred per row type (event-id / machine / HTTP / source-coord)
- Tests cover all 4 dimensions + each unfocus path

## Posture
Pre-alpha; no compat shim. Estimated ~250 LoC across spine + shell + L2 row + helpers + tests.

CSS variable --rf-causa-row-dim-opacity (host-tunable). Cross-panel triggers wire through single :rf.causa/set-focus event.

title: feat(causa): Routing tab (7th tab) — lens on focused event per Mike's design

title: feat(substrate): Event lens substrate gaps — dispatch-site + effects-returned on traces + interceptor default tag
description:
Per ai/findings/2026-05-18-event-lens-design.md Q3 + §10 + Mike's 2026-05-18 16:30 decision (one bead).

Three small DCE-gated substrate changes that unblock the Event lens redesign:

## Change 1: Hoist :rf.trace/call-site onto :event/dispatched (success path)

File: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc (emit-dispatched-trace! around line 1238) + implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc (build-event hoist).

Today: dispatch-site coord is captured into the dispatch envelope by the dispatch/dispatch-sync macros (core_call_site_macros.cljc; rf2-ts1a) but only hoisted onto traces on ERROR path (trace.cljc:227 — call-site bound only when error?).

Change: hoist :call-site (or :rf.trace/call-site) to the success-path emit. The Event lens Section 2 (Dispatch site) reads it directly off :event/dispatched.

## Change 2: Stamp handler return shape onto :event/do-fx

File: implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc (around the :event/do-fx emit at L592).

Today: the handler's full return map (the {:db <next> :fx [...] :dispatch ...}) is NOT traced — it lives in the interceptor context's :effects slot, visible during the cascade, never stamped on a trace.

Change: stamp the :fx vector + :db-present? marker (not the full :db value — that's huge; the App-db diff trace already carries the slice changes). 2-3 keys on the emit. The Event lens Section 5 (Effects returned) reads this.

## Change 3: :rf/default? tag on framework-auto-wrapped interceptors

File: implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc (wrap-event-handler around L178; the auto-wrappers for :rf/db-handler / :rf/fx-handler / :rf/ctx-handler).

Today: Causa-side would need an allowlist of {:rf/db-handler :rf/fx-handler :rf/ctx-handler} to filter framework defaults from the Interceptors section.

Change: assoc :rf/default? true on the auto-wrapped interceptor maps. Self-describing; allowlist disappears.

## Constraints

- All three DCE-gated via interop/debug-enabled? (consistent with other instrumentation)
- No prod cost when debug is off
- Tests: per-change unit assertion that the new key/tag rides on the trace shape in dev

## Acceptance

- :event/dispatched success-path trace carries :call-site
- :event/do-fx trace carries :fx + :db-present? markers
- Framework-auto-wrapped interceptors carry :rf/default? true on their interceptor maps

title: design(causa): :ungrouped pseudo-cascade events have no L2 surface — :rf.ssr/* + registry-time + REPL events can't be focused via UI
description:
Surfaced by rf2-u6dhp fix-up worker (PR #1458):

L2 event list filters out :ungrouped pseudo-cascade rows (per rf2-639lc). That means events emitted outside any dispatch — :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch from verify-hydration!, registry-time emits, REPL evals, frame lifecycle events — have NO surface in Causa's user UI. Issues raised by these events are invisible to focus-scoping.

## Two options
- **(A)** Show :ungrouped in L2 as a special row ('untraced events' or similar); user clicks → focus the :ungrouped bucket; downstream panels scope to it
- **(B)** Leave L2 clean (current behavior); add a 'Show untraced' affordance in chrome (toolbar chip / settings toggle) that surfaces :ungrouped when the user opts in

(A) is simpler but adds noise. (B) is cleaner default + opt-in for SSR/REPL workflows.

## Acceptance
- Users with SSR / REPL / registry-time-emit workflows can focus the :ungrouped bucket
- Default L2 stays clean (no :ungrouped row visible)
close_reason: Mike 2026-05-19: (B) Opt-in chip in chrome. Default L2 stays clean; toolbar chip / Settings toggle surfaces :ungrouped when user opts in. Aligns with silent-by-default. Filing follow-on impl bead.
