title: fix(causa): Trace tab frame-filter chip is now redundant — cascade-scoping (rf2-ycoct #1459) makes it meaningless
description:
Mike: 'Trace allows you to filter on a frame but that makes no sense given you have to select both a frame and an event to even be seeing anything in the trace panel.'

Per rf2-ycoct #1459, Trace is now cascade-scoped — you focus on an event in L2; Trace shows that event's cascade. The event implies its frame. So a frame-filter chip is doubly redundant: (1) you'd have to focus an event first to see anything, and (2) the event has only one frame anyway.

## Fix
- Remove the frame-filter chip from Trace tab's chip strip
- Remove its sub + dispatch handler if dead
- Other chips (severity, prefix, since-ms) stay — they're orthogonal to focus

## Surface
- tools/causa/src/.../panels/trace.cljs (chip strip)
- registry.cljs (drop the sub/event if dead)

## Acceptance
- Trace tab chip strip no longer has frame-filter
- Other chips preserved
- Cascade-scoping (rf2-ycoct #1459) intact
close_reason: Shipped via PR #1464 — Trace tab frame-filter chip dropped post-cascade-scope (rf2-ycoct #1459 made it redundant). Rebase resolved via UNION on 4 trace files; all gates green including causa-feature-gate (13/13 scenarios pass).

title: design(causa): focus-navigation set — L2 row gutter click sets a focus set; [◀][▶] step within it (not a filter — full list still shown)
description:
Per Mike (2026-05-18):

> 'In the events list at the top, we want a compact display of selectable events. THEN in the same row, perhaps on the left there is a column which if clicked immediately focuses on events with the same event-id. Then as you click forwards and backwards through events, you would move forward and backwards to the next event of the same name. Thus allowing you to easily move forward and back through the machine's execution.'

> 'Thinking about this some more, this is NOT a filter thing, it is a FOCUS thing. Certain events are now in focus, they are the ones being stepped through.'

## The mental model — focus, not filter

| Concept | Filter | Focus-navigation |
|---|---|---|
| L2 list shape | Removes non-matching events | Full list still visible |
| Visual signal | Hidden rows | Highlighted (in-focus) rows + dimmed (out-of-focus) rows |
| [◀] [▶] nav | Steps through visible items | Steps through IN-FOCUS items |
| Click out-of-focus row | Selects it (no focus change) | Selects it + ALSO becomes the focus 'pivot' |

This is much cleaner than filtering. The full event stream stays visible (you see context: 'before my :cart/add-item there were these other events'); the nav buttons just step through the subset you've focused on.

## The L2 row gutter — focus affordance

Each L2 row gains a left gutter (~6-10px wide). Clicking it sets a focus set based on a sensible dimension:

| Row property | Dimension when gutter clicked |
|---|---|
| Same event-id (e.g. :cart/add-item) | All events with event-id = :cart/add-item |
| Triggered a machine transition | All events that triggered THIS machine instance |
| Triggered an HTTP fx | All events in this HTTP correlation chain |
| Has source-coord X | All events dispatched from X |

The dimension is implicit-from-context — clicking gutter on a :cart/add-item row defaults to event-id focus; clicking gutter on a machine-triggering row defaults to machine focus (perhaps with a quick-select on hover to pick the dimension).

## Visual + interaction
- Out-of-focus rows: dimmed (e.g. 40% opacity)
- In-focus rows: full opacity + small ⦿ marker in the gutter
- The 'pivot' (the row that established the focus): the marker is filled
- Click any out-of-focus row: it becomes the new pivot + the focus set rebuilds around its dimension
- Click the gutter on the pivot again: clears focus (back to all-events nav)

## Implementation notes
- Independent of the auto-filter substrate (rf2-ak4ms / rf2-drcyb). Filter hides; focus highlights + scopes nav.
- Implementation: store  predicate +  in the spine. Nav buttons consult the set; row rendering reads the set + applies dim/highlight.
- For the gutter click: a tiny default-dimension picker (event-id is the obvious default) + a right-click quick-menu for other dimensions.
- Surface integration: clicking a machine in Machines panel → focus set = events involving that machine; clicking a managed-fx row → focus set = events in that fx's correlation chain. Same mechanism, different sources.

## Cross-links
- rf2-si9o5 (Machines lens with pinned-machine-instance) — REFINE: the 'pin' is a focus set, not a filter
- rf2-drcyb (surface-aware filters) — DIFFERENT primitive; complementary
- rf2-htik0 (L2 vector rendering, shipped) — adds row foundation
- rf2-639lc (default-focus + L2 fixes, shipped) — adds L2 foundation

## Acceptance
- L2 row left gutter is clickable (default: event-id focus)
- Setting focus dims out-of-focus rows + highlights in-focus rows
- [◀] [▶] step through in-focus rows only
- Right-click gutter → choose dimension (event-id, machine-instance, http-corr, source-coord, …)
- Clear focus by clicking pivot's gutter again
close_reason: Design captured; implementation filed as rf2-a1z3b with full scope (gutter/body distinction, 4 default dimensions, Esc/gutter-toggle/body-click unfocus, ribbon chip, cross-panel triggers per rf2-si9o5). rf2-a1z3b dispatched 2026-05-18 17:25 AUSEST.

title: design(causa): surface-aware filters — generalize auto-filter beyond keyword matching (machine instance, HTTP correlation, fx kind, …)
description:
Per Mike's thinking out loud:

> 'I guess we have filters on events already but I wonder how to make that more machine specific. Maybe more HTTP specific. Other?'

## The opportunity
Today's auto-filter (rf2-ak4ms #1404) is keyword-pattern-based — match on event-id text. Powerful but narrow. Mike wants surface-aware filters:
- Filter by machine instance (events involving this machine)
- Filter by HTTP correlation-id (events linked to this request/response pair)
- Filter by fx kind (events that triggered :rf.fx/http vs :rf.fx/ws vs :rf.fx/dispatch)
- Filter by causal ancestry (events that descended from THIS event)
- Filter by source-coord (events dispatched from this file/line)
- Filter by interceptor presence (events that hit this non-standard interceptor)

## Mechanism
Auto-filter pills today are typed [event-id] patterns. Generalize to typed [predicate] pills where predicate is:
- {:kind :event-id-pattern :pattern '...'} (today's default)
- {:kind :machine :id :auth/session} (events involving this machine)
- {:kind :http-correlation :id 'abc-123'} (events linked to this HTTP exchange)
- {:kind :fx :id :rf.fx/http} (events that triggered this fx)
- {:kind :descendant-of :event-pos N} (causal ancestry)
- {:kind :source-coord :file 'foo.cljs' :line 42}

Pill rendering: each typed pill renders distinctly (icon + label per kind).

## UI
- Right-click on a machine row in Machines panel → 'Filter to this machine'
- Right-click on a managed-fx row → 'Filter to events that triggered this fx'
- Right-click on a Causality popover node → 'Filter to descendants of this event'

## Acceptance
- The auto-filter system accepts typed predicates
- UI affordances per surface (right-click in Machines / Managed-fx / Causality) to add filters
- Multiple filters AND together (e.g. 'this machine' + 'in last 5 minutes')

## Cross-links
- rf2-ak4ms — auto-filter substrate (#1404)
- rf2-a9cke — Machines tab fix (uses machine-instance filter)
- (Future) HTTP-correlation requires substrate stamping of correlation-id (some surfaces already have it per #1422 managed-fx)
close_reason: Mike decision 2026-05-19: ship narrowly — 3 kinds (:machine + :http-correlation + :fx). Drops :descendant-of (Causality moot). Defers :source-coord + :interceptor. Pre-alpha posture: ~300 LoC v1 work. Filing follow-on impl bead.

title: design(causa): Machines panel as a true event-driven lens — focus + machine-instance filter + step through machine's logical moves
description:
Per Mike's canonical Machines design (2026-05-18 morning):

When an event is selected, the Machines panel shows:

1. **If event unrelated to a machine** → nothing (silent by default).

2. **If event triggered a machine transition**:
   - The machine's **topology** (state chart)
   - **Current state** highlighted (where the transition starts)
   - **New state** highlighted (where the transition lands)
   - The **transition edge** between them (the one that's happening)
   - Any **guards** that ran — with their input values + evaluation result (passed/failed)
   - Any **actions** that ran — with their input data + side-effect

That's the canonical lens-on-focused-event for Machines.

## The prerequisite work
'We just have to come up with a nice stable way to draw machines.' The chart-drawing primitive needs:
- Reliable layout (ELK with layered fallback — shipped in rf2-m7co9 #1410)
- Compact + scannable (font fix in flight — rf2-isgqu + rf2-gz7vi)
- Highlight semantics: current-state outline, new-state outline + arrow, transition-edge bold, guards/actions inline on the edge or as a side-rail
- Stable across re-renders (no jitter as cascade unfolds)

## Pinned-machine mode (also Mike's idea — see rf2-si9o5 original body)
- Pin a machine instance → L2 list filters to events for THAT machine
- [<] / [>] step through that machine's events
- Each step shows the topology with the right transition highlighted
- 'Clear pin' returns to all-events view

## Cross-links
- rf2-a9cke — Machines tab focus invariant fix (audit follow-on)
- rf2-ak3ty — spine epoch-id prereq (foundation; in flight)
- rf2-isgqu + rf2-gz7vi — chart font/density (in flight)
- rf2-m7co9 — ELK layout (shipped #1410)
- rf2-drcyb — surface-aware filters (machine-instance is one)

## Acceptance
- Event focused: Machines panel renders per the rules above (silent if unrelated; topology + transition if related)
- Pin machine: L2 filters; nav buttons step through; topology updates per step
- Chart draws reliably + compactly
close_reason: Mike decision 2026-05-19: yes, proceed. Subsumed by rf2-1asvh §0ter.3 Machines tab findings (just landed; ai/findings/2026-05-17-causa-consolidated-design.md). Machines panel as true event-driven lens (focus + machine-instance filter + step through machine's logical moves) is one of the proposals in §0ter.3 with open questions for Mike. No separate dispatch; consolidated with kxt18 under the findings doc.

title: Spine prereq: focus-cascade-reducer must compute :epoch-id from cascades (spec/018 §Spine events) (rf2-omdal follow-on)
description:
Audited as part of rf2-omdal (audit doc: ai/findings/2026-05-18-tab-focus-invariant-audit.md).

## Status
SPEC/IMPLEMENTATION GAP — root cause for the Views tab bug AND a latent App-db bug.

## Spec
tools/causa/spec/018-Event-Spine.md L544 — :rf.causa/focus-cascade event MUST 'Set :dispatch-id <id>, **compute :epoch-id from cascades**, flip :mode → :retro'. The spec is explicit. The spine sub's shape (:rf.causa/focus → {:dispatch-id :epoch-id :frame :mode :head? :previewing?}) includes :epoch-id as a first-class slot.

## Implementation gap
tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/spine.cljs:126-142 focus-cascade-reducer writes :dispatch-id / :mode / :previewing? / :frame. **Never :epoch-id.** It also writes legacy :selected-dispatch-id / :selected-dispatch slots, but NOT :selected-epoch-id.

So clicking an L2 row leaves (:epoch-id focus) nil AND leaves :selected-epoch-id untouched.

## Downstream consequences
- **Views tab** (rf2-... follow-on, separate bead) — falls back to head cascade because find-cascade-index cannot match focus's :dispatch-id (opaque router counter) against epoch record's :event-id (keyword) / :epoch-id (per-frame counter).
- **App-db tab** — reads :rf.causa/selected-epoch-id; that slot is not updated by L2-list clicks. App-db DOES pivot when user picks an epoch in Time-Travel panel (which dispatches :rf.causa/select-epoch) but NOT when user clicks L2.
- **views-sub-diff-subs.cljs** — caches by :epoch-id from current epoch record, which is broken by the same chain.

## Why this is a prereq, not a co-fix
No projection currently links cascade :dispatch-id ↔ epoch :epoch-id:
- group-cascades (implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace/projection.cljc:200-239) groups by trace bus :dispatch-id. No :epoch-id slot.
- build-record (implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc:168-220) writes :epoch-id from state/next-epoch-id. No :dispatch-id slot.

The link is genuinely missing — has to be built before the spine can fill :epoch-id.

## Fix options (Mike's call)
**Option A — Index sub (less invasive).** Add :rf.causa/dispatch-id->epoch-id composing :rf.causa/cascades + :rf.causa/epoch-history. Walk both, match by frame + first-trace-id, build {dispatch-id epoch-id} map. Then focus-cascade-reducer reads it (would need access via a separate reactive path — events can't deref subs cleanly, so either compute the join lazily in the focus sub itself, or maintain the index in app-db and write through it).

**Option B — Primary-key fix (cleaner, more invasive).** Extend build-record in assembly.cljc to record the cascade's root :dispatch-id directly on the epoch record. Adds a :dispatch-id slot to the :rf/epoch-record schema in Spec-Schemas.md. Lookup becomes a direct (filter #(= focus-dispatch (:dispatch-id %)) history).

Option B is the cleaner answer for a pre-alpha codebase: the missing link is structurally a primary key, not a derived join. The schema change is small and the runtime already has the dispatch-id available at epoch-record assembly time (it's in the trace events that build-record consumes).

## After this lands
- Update spine.cljs focus-cascade-reducer to compute + write :epoch-id (and :selected-epoch-id for legacy consumers).
- Unblocks Views fix (one-line change in find-cascade-index).
- Unblocks App-db pivoting from L2 list clicks.
- Should also unblock the right-direction shim for views-sub-diff cache.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #1453 (merged 2026-05-18). Spine focus-cascade-reducer now computes :epoch-id per spec/018. Unblocks Views focus + fixes App-db pivot. Legacy :select-dispatch-id shim writes the new slot too.

title: Issues tab: doesn't honour focused-event invariant — global feed, no focus dep (rf2-omdal follow-on)
description:
Audited as part of rf2-omdal (audit doc: ai/findings/2026-05-18-tab-focus-invariant-audit.md).

## Status
DOESN'T HONOUR. No :rf.causa/focus dependency. Issues feed is global across the whole buffer.

## Evidence
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/issues_ribbon.cljs:426-430 — :rf.causa/issues-ribbon composite chains :<- [:rf.causa/trace-buffer] (full) + :<- [:rf.causa/issues-filters]. No focus.
- issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc:280-295 apply-filters — filters by :severities, :prefixes, :since-ms only. No dispatch-id or cascade-window filter.

## Test reading
Focusing event A (which raised a warning) vs event B (no issues) → identical Issues feed. Every error/warning/advisory in the buffer regardless of focus.

## Required UX call
Two options:
1. **Default cascade-scope, toggle to all issues.** Add :<- [:rf.causa/focus] + pre-filter feed to issues whose :dispatch-id matches focused :dispatch-id. Add 'cascade only · all issues' chip. Honours invariant.
2. **Highlight + count overlay.** Keep global feed but visually highlight rows whose :dispatch-id matches focused cascade, plus 'N issues this cascade' badge. Preserves global affordance.

Option 1 honours invariant. Option 2 preserves a 'what's gone wrong everywhere' workflow Mike may want. Mike's UX call.

## Files
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/issues_ribbon.cljs (composite)
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc (apply-filters)

description:
Audited as part of rf2-omdal (audit doc: ai/findings/2026-05-18-tab-focus-invariant-audit.md).

## Status
DOESN'T HONOUR. No :rf.causa/focus dependency. Transition ribbon shows ALL transitions for the picker-selected machine across the whole buffer.

## Evidence
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/machine_inspector.cljs:918-930 — :rf.causa/machine-inspector-data composite chains registered-machines, snapshots, definitions, :rf.causa/trace-buffer (full), :rf.causa/selected-machine-id, :rf.causa/target-frame. No focus dep.
- machine_inspector_helpers.cljc:236-266 project-transitions filters trace-buffer to :rf.machine/transition events for machine-id only. No dispatch-id / cascade-window filter.

Focusing event A (which triggered transition X in machine M) vs event B (which triggered transition Y in same machine M) → identical transition ribbon. Selecting a different machine via picker rebinds; selecting different event via L2 does nothing.

Machines has TWO existing axes — (a) machine picker, (b) scrubber/arc-highlight. Focus is at most a sub-selection within (b). A reasonable interpretation that honours invariant:
1. Chart's arc-highlight defaults to the state the machine was in DURING the focused event's cascade.
2. Transition ribbon retains full list but visually highlights transitions attributable to focused :dispatch-id.
3. Pivot affordance — if focused event triggered a transition in machine M, picker defaults to M.

machine_inspector_arc.cljs already has scrubber-position state — infrastructure is partially in place. Nothing reads :rf.causa/focus to drive it.

title: Views tab: doesn't honour focused-event invariant — root cause is spine never writes :epoch-id (rf2-omdal follow-on)
description:
Audited as part of rf2-omdal (audit doc: ai/findings/2026-05-18-tab-focus-invariant-audit.md).

## Status
DOESN'T HONOUR in production. Panel-gallery testbed appears to honour because fixtures equate :epoch-id == :dispatch-id, which is NOT the production id shape.

## Root cause (deepest)
Spec 018 §Spine events says the :rf.causa/focus-cascade event 'Sets :dispatch-id <id>, **computes :epoch-id from cascades**, flips :mode → :retro'. But spine.cljs:126-142 focus-cascade-reducer ONLY writes :dispatch-id / :mode / :previewing? / :frame. **Never :epoch-id.** So (:epoch-id focus) is nil for every L2-list click.

Plus: no projection links cascade :dispatch-id to epoch :epoch-id. The cascade record (group-cascades, projection.cljc:200) has no :epoch-id slot. The epoch record (build-record, assembly.cljc:168) has no :dispatch-id slot.

## Proximate cause (Views layer)
views_subs.cljs:21-39 find-cascade-index falls back to matching focus's :dispatch-id (opaque router counter) against epoch record's :event-id (keyword), :dispatch-id (slot doesn't exist), or (first :trigger-event) (also keyword). None match in production → fallback to head at line 78.

## Fix sequence
1. **Prereq (separate bead — file before this one starts):** make focus-cascade-reducer compute :epoch-id. Either (a) build a :rf.causa/dispatch-id->epoch-id index sub composing :rf.causa/cascades with :rf.causa/epoch-history, or (b) extend build-record (assembly.cljc) to record the cascade's root :dispatch-id. Option (b) is the cleaner primary-key answer.
2. **This bead:** once spine carries :epoch-id, replace find-cascade-index with direct lookup by :epoch-id. One-line change.
3. **Test:** add views_subs unit tests with production id shape (epoch-id != dispatch-id) — there are currently zero tests for views_subs.cljs.
4. **Fix the fixtures:** stop equating :epoch-id = :dispatch-id in tools/causa/testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures_views.cljs — use distinct ids so the testbed exercises the production lookup shape.

## Files
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/views_subs.cljs (find-cascade-index + composite)
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/spine.cljs (focus-cascade-reducer; spec gap)
- tools/causa/testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures_views.cljs (fix id shape)
close_reason: Shipped via PR #1455 (merged 2026-05-18). Views tab now honours focused-event invariant via :epoch-id lookup. Spine prereq rf2-ak3ty unblocked the one-liner.

title: fix(causa): Event Detail empty-state text talks about 'pick a dispatch from cascade list' — should reflect L2 event-list focus like all other panels
description:
The Event Detail panel (or similar L4 detail) shows: 'Pick a dispatch from the cascade list to see its handler, effects, subscriptions, and source coord.'

This is wrong because:
1. The interaction model is the L2 event-list (left side) picks the focused event. ALL panels reflect that focus.
2. 'Pick a dispatch from the cascade list' refers to an older / different interaction model that doesn't apply.
3. The text claims an affordance ('cascade list pick') that may not exist or works differently now.

Per Mike's invariant: every panel reflects the event chosen in the event list. Empty state should either:
- (a) Just be empty (silent by default per text audit)
- (b) Show 'No event focused. Pick one from the event list →' (or omit the arrow if the layout makes it obvious)

## Surface
- tools/causa/src/.../panels/event_detail.cljs — find this text
- Could also be in other panels — sweep for 'cascade list' / 'pick a dispatch' / similar pre-spine wording

title: feat(story+causa): element-level click-to-code — inspector mode that opens view-fn source for the clicked DOM element (React-Devtools-style)
description:
Story today ships per-variant Open-in-editor chip (tools/story/src/.../ui/open_in_editor.cljs + spec/005-SOTA-Features.md) — opens the story-spec source.

Extension: element-level click-to-code. Click any rendered DOM element on the canvas → opens the view-fn that produced it, at the exact line.

## Why
React Devtools and Vue Devtools have this; users expect it. For re-frame2 view fns are pure + composition is direct, so 'who rendered this' has an unambiguous answer. Most useful when navigating an unfamiliar component tree.

## What to build
1. Source-coord injection — macro pass that augments hiccup output. Two options:
   - (A) Wrap every element-returning fn with attribute injection. Fine-grained; cost: every element gets a data-rf-source attribute like path/to/file.cljs colon 42.
   - (B) Inject only at view-fn boundaries. Coarse; less DOM bloat. Recommended.
   Macro candidate: reg-view (across Reagent / UIx / Helix adapters).

2. Inspector mode — toolbar toggle 'Inspect' (or Alt+click default-on). When active:
   - Hover any DOM element → highlight + tooltip showing 'view-name at file:line'
   - Click → resolve to closest ancestor with data-rf-source attr + dispatch the editor-open fx with that coord
   - Cursor: crosshair while inspector mode is on
   - Esc to exit inspector mode

3. Editor URI dispatch — reuse the existing editor-uri/editor-uri builder + the allowlist scheme gate (rf2-cm93v). Same gate Story's chip already uses; same gate Causa uses.

4. Causa integration — Causa's trace tab can show a 'view-source' chip per trace entry where the call-site coord is known (extends the existing source-coord rendering Causa already does).

## Files
- New: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/element_inspector.cljs (toggle + hover overlay + click handler)
- Modify: re-frame view macros (across Reagent / UIx / Helix adapters) to inject the data-source attr
- Modify: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/toolbar.cljs (add inspector chip)
- Tests: macro injection produces correct attrs; inspector toggle; click dispatches editor URI

## Open questions
1. Adapter coverage: Reagent only first, or all three in one PR?
2. Element granularity: every hiccup element or just at view-fn boundaries (recommended)
3. Production bundle: must elide via existing dev-tools-only path (bundle isolation)
4. Should the inspector also work inside Causa's panels themselves (Causa-on-Causa dev recursion)?

## Acceptance
- Inspector toggle visible in Story toolbar
- Alt+click on rendered element opens the view-fn source in user's editor
- Macro pass covered by tests (golden hiccup → expected attrs)
- Bundle isolation: production builds elide inspector entirely
- Reuses existing editor-uri allowlist + scheme gate (rf2-cm93v)

title: design(story): deprecate Story's RHS scrubber/trace/actions inspectors in favor of embedded Causa
description:
Story's RHS panel was designed before Causa was a mature devtool. It carries three inspector panels (Scrubber, Trace, Actions) that each duplicate work Causa now does — and does better.

## The duplication

| Story RHS panel | Causa equivalent | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Scrubber (per-variant epoch nav) | Causa ribbon [◀ ▶ ⏭] + L2 event list | Duplicate |
| Trace (event-bus log) | Causa Trace tab (richer filtering, focus, cascade nav) | Duplicate |
| Actions (dispatch + fx log) | Causa Event tab cascade view + filtered Trace | Duplicate |
| Dispatch Console | (none in Causa) | Story-unique; keep |
| Controls (per-variant) | (none in Causa) | Story-unique; keep |
| Play status + viewport + backgrounds | (none in Causa) | Story-unique; keep |

## Strategic move

Delete the three duplicated panels. Mount Causa in the RHS by default (or via a single toolbar toggle). Story becomes purely: variant chrome + interaction surfaces + canvas + Causa.

## Wins
- Removes ~3 panels of duplication
- Eliminates 'RHS shows internals of the panel that IS the inspection view' recursion (the trigger for Mike's observation)
- Causa-side improvements (UC1 Sim, scrubber, machine inspector, panels we haven't built yet) automatically flow into Story
- Forces Causa-quality inspection everywhere by default
- Smaller Story chrome surface; less to maintain

## Concerns / open questions
1. Stories that showcase non-Causa apps (counter, cart) still need an inspector. Causa is now Story-aware (rf2-q9kv5 Causa preset; #1413 viewport awareness) — does it embed cleanly enough to replace the scrubber/trace/actions for those cases?
2. Causa-embedded means TWO Causa instances when showcasing a Causa-panel variant — needs the modal-scoping fix (rf2-om6fa) first
3. Performance: Causa is heavier than the three lightweight Story panels. Lazy-mount?
4. What's the toggle UX — Causa always-on by default? Toolbar button? Keybinding?
5. Migration path for users who pin Story's scrubber/trace/actions in their workflow

## Dependencies
- rf2-om6fa (modal scoping fix) should land first OR be part of this work
- Verify rf2-q9kv5 (Causa preset) handles all the embedding cases

## Acceptance
- Design proposal for the new RHS shape
- Spec proposal for Story's reduced surface
- Migration plan for users on the old shape

description:
Per ai/findings/2026-05-18-causa-ssr-machines-routes-fx-debugging.md §Feature 5 and tools/causa/spec/019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md.

## Bug class
Wall-clock time is under-served in Causa today. Machines that use :after timers (retry backoffs, debounce windows, timeout guards) have invisible countdowns — developers don't know how long until next fire, can't see throttling working, can't catch 'why didn't this fire?' until it's silent.

## Insight Causa provides
A small countdown ring rendered AROUND the state-node in the Machine Inspector chart:
- Live mode: animates from full-circle (just-armed) to empty-circle (about-to-fire)
- Retrospective mode (scrubber): shows the ring at the position it was at scrubber time
- Color: green if firing-soon, amber if mid-cycle, red if past deadline
- Hover: shows ms remaining + fire deadline timestamp
- Cancelled timer: ring fades to gray + crossed-out

## Tests
- Ring projection (pure): timer state + current time → ring fraction
- Cancellation transitions ring to :gray
- Hover handler dispatch
- Scrubber-driven ring fraction

title: feat(causa): cancellation cascade visualiser — single waterfall view of rf2-wvkn parent decision → destroy → child teardown → per-HTTP abort
description:
Per ai/findings/2026-05-18-causa-ssr-machines-routes-fx-debugging.md §Feature 2 and tools/causa/spec/019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md §Machines.M.3.

## Bug class M.3
Machine parent decides to destroy child actor → child actor teardown → every in-flight HTTP/WS effect the child started gets :rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy. Today these trace entries scatter through the Trace tab as a flurry — devs can't see the cascade as a coherent unit. Especially painful when the cancellation was unintentional (parent destroyed too early; lifecycle bug).

## Insight Causa provides
A single vertical waterfall in the Machines tab side-panel:
  PARENT DECISION
    └─ [destroy-child] dispatched at 1234ms by :auth/logout
  CHILD TEARDOWN
    └─ child:user-session destroying at 1240ms (5 in-flight fxs)
  EFFECT ABORTS (in order)
    ├─ HTTP GET /api/profile  aborted at 1242ms (:cancel-cause :actor-destroyed)
    ├─ HTTP POST /api/log     aborted at 1242ms (:cancel-cause :actor-destroyed)
    ├─ WS send :heartbeat     aborted at 1243ms (:cancel-cause :actor-destroyed)
    ├─ :after timer fire      aborted at 1243ms (:cancel-cause :actor-destroyed)
    └─ machine-invoke fetch  aborted at 1244ms (:cancel-cause :actor-destroyed)

Each row clickable → jumps to the trace entry / event.

## UI
- Side-panel section in Machines tab when focused machine had a recent destroy/teardown
- OR popover triggered by clicking a destroy-event in Trace tab
- Group by :cancel-cause root
- Show :correlation-id where available

## Tests
- Cascade projection (pure): trace → cascade record
- Multi-cascade in same epoch (rare but possible)
- Cross-link to Trace + Event
- Empty case (no in-flight when destroyed)

## Files
- tools/causa/src/.../panels/cancellation_cascade.cljs
- tools/causa/src/.../panels/cancellation_cascade_helpers.cljc
- tools/causa/test/.../panels/cancellation_cascade_*_test.cljc/cljs

title: feat(story): :play fn — post-mount interaction script (Storybook play-equivalent)
description:
Storybook has a play() function that runs after the story mounts and simulates user interactions (clicks, types, dispatches). This lets stories self-verify behavior, not just render statically.

re-frame2's Story equivalent: a :play key on story-spec that dispatches a sequence of events + makes assertions against app-db / DOM.

## Schema
{:play {:script [[:dispatch [:my/event arg1]]
                [:wait 100]
                [:dispatch [:my/other-event]]
                [:assert-db [:my-state :status] :loaded]
                [:assert-dom "[data-test=foo]" :visible]]}}

## Step types
- [:dispatch event-vec] — re-frame dispatch
- [:dispatch-sync event-vec] — sync dispatch
- [:wait ms] — wait N ms (for async)
- [:assert-db path value] — assert app-db value at path
- [:assert-dom selector :visible|:hidden|text-content] — DOM assertion
- [:click selector] — DOM click
- [:type selector text] — DOM type

## UI
- Auto-runs play() on mount (configurable per-story)
- Toolbar shows: ▶ Re-run | ⏸ Pause | Status (pass/fail/running)
- Step-by-step log in Causa Trace (each :dispatch/:assert step emits a trace entry)
- Failed assertion: red banner + click to highlight failing element

## Tests
- play schema validates
- :dispatch step fires event + updates app-db
- :assert-db pass/fail
- :assert-dom pass/fail (mock DOM in tests)
- :wait honored
- :click + :type via mock DOM events
- Failure surfaces in toolbar status
- Re-run resets app-db + replays

## Files (new)
- tools/story/src/.../play/runner.cljc (pure step executor)
- tools/story/src/.../play/runner_events.cljc (re-frame side)
- tools/story/src/.../ui/play_status.cljs (toolbar status chip + re-run button)
- tools/story/test/.../play/runner_test.cljc
- tools/story/test/.../ui/play_status_test.cljc
- tools/story/src/.../schemas.cljc — extend Story schema with :play key

title: feat(story): play step-debugger UI for test-mode pane — step/pause/rewind controls (highest-leverage Storybook-parity fix)
description:
From the Story-vs-Storybook deep-dive findings (ai/findings/2026-05-17-story-vs-storybook-deep-dive.md §8 opinion #2 + R1): the single missing piece that costs Story a 'feature parity with Storybook' claim. Highest-leverage fix in the deep-dive analysis.

## The gap
Storybook's Interactions panel ships a UI with step / pause / rewind / breakpoint controls for play() functions. When a developer authors a play sequence (a scripted interaction story), they can run it step-by-step in the panel, pause at any step, rewind to inspect, set breakpoints — making the play sequence debuggable not just executable.

Story's :test mode pane (per tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md) is good for running play sequences but lacks this step-debugger UI. The runtime substrate IS already there per tools/story/spec/004-Assertions.md (which mentions the play-stepper hook). Only the UI is missing.

## Scope (impl + docs in one PR)

### Implement
- Step/pause/rewind UI controls in Story's :test mode pane
- Current-step indicator (which assertion / which play step is active)
- Optional: breakpoint affordance (click step → set breakpoint → next run pauses there)
- Optional: step-back / replay-from-step
- Hooks into the existing 004-Assertions play-stepper runtime substrate; no runtime changes needed

### Document
- Update tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md to spec the UI surface (was implied; now explicit)
- Update tools/story/README.md to mention the step-debugger
- Update tools/story/spec/000-Vision.md if it has a key-features section

### Tests
- Per-test-mode browser smoke that drives the step controls + asserts pause/resume/rewind behaviour
- Add to tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md matrix

## Why high-leverage
Per the deep-dive: 'Everything else Storybook does, Story either does (often better) or has explicitly out-of-scoped.' The play-stepper UI is THE last visible-feature gap. Closing it lets Story credibly claim Storybook-parity for the use cases that matter.

- Runtime substrate changes (already exists)
- Other test-mode-pane improvements unrelated to play-stepper

title: docs(story): promote force-fx-stub to marketing-tier headline in Story spec — it's structurally better than MSW
description:
From the Story-vs-Storybook deep-dive findings (ai/findings/2026-05-17-story-vs-storybook-deep-dive.md §8 opinion #1): force-fx-stub is currently buried as a sub-section of 004-Assertions.md. It deserves marketing-tier headline status.

## What force-fx-stub is
Story can stub ANY registered fx in three lines of variant body:

  (reg-variant :Variant.checkout/network-failure
    {:force-fx-stub {:http/managed (constantly :rf.http/failed)}
     ...})

This stubs the HTTP fx for that variant. But because it works on ANY :reg-fx-registered effect — not just HTTP — the same primitive covers analytics fx, websocket fx, geolocation fx, storage fx, navigation fx, etc.

## Why this matters
Storybook's ecosystem needs separate addons for each:
- mock HTTP → msw-storybook-addon (2.3M weekly npm)
- mock analytics → custom decorator or msw-extended
- mock websocket → another addon
- mock storage → another addon
- mock navigation → yet another
- ...

Each addon is a single-purpose plugin the user has to find, install, and learn. Story has it as ONE PRIMITIVE in the framework: every fx has a handler, every handler can be stubbed.

## Human-friendly framing for the marketing copy
The current 004-Assertions.md sub-section is dry + technical. Story spec needs prose that says (in re-frame2's voice):

> 'Don't mock just the network. Mock anything.
>
> Storybook ships a separate addon for each thing you want to fake — HTTP via MSW, analytics via custom decorators, storage via shim libraries. Story has it in one primitive: any effect handler you registered can be stubbed in three lines.
>
> Set up a variant that fails the checkout HTTP call:
>   {:force-fx-stub {:http/managed (constantly :rf.http/failed)}}
>
> Or fails analytics. Or websocket. Or anything else you reg-fx'd.
>
> This isn't a feature competition; it's an architectural win. Storybook has to translate 'mock the network' into 'mock everything you care about' via a parade of single-purpose addons. Story has it in one decorator.'

## Scope
- Promote force-fx-stub to a top-level section in tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md (or as its own brief spec doc if warranted)
- Cross-link from 004-Assertions.md to the new home
- Update tools/story/README.md to mention it in the feature list
- Update tools/story/spec/000-Vision.md §key-features if it has one
- Tone: re-frame2 voice — opinionated, comparative, technical but human

## Source

- ai/findings/2026-05-17-story-vs-storybook-deep-dive.md §4 (gap analysis context)

title: Fix M-16: top-level (rf/dispatch-later …) calls — function-form removed, only effect-key remains (gh-1378)
description:

## Why this matters
v1 function form was common at boot/mount sites: build-ready event handlers, window.onload listeners. These are boot-critical — silent compile + runtime throw is most painful to diagnose.

## Fix
Update M-16 with sub-rule for top-level call shape. Replace (rf/dispatch ^:flush-dom [:x]) with effect-form equivalent inside an event handler, OR drop the dispatch-later semantics entirely if the latency was incidental (common case at boot).

title: design(causa): UC1 follow-up — interactive simulation of static machine definition as Machine Inspector affordance (child of rf2-bnlo4)
description:
Per Mike 2026-05-17: focused follow-up to rf2-bnlo4 findings. The design doc covered UC2 (dynamic-instance debugging) well + the strategic recommendation (collapse machines-viz into Causa) but missed UC1's INTERACTIVE SIMULATION affordance.

## The gap
§2 (Static-definition UX) in ai/findings/causa-machines-design-2026-05-17.md treats the definition view as inspection-only (browse registry + render diagram + show metadata). It does NOT cover the playground-style 'simulate this machine without a live app' affordance:

- User clicks a state in the diagram
- UI shows the events that would transition out of this state
- User picks one event
- Watches the diagram update to show the new state
- Can step through multi-event scenarios on the static definition

This is Stately-Visualizer-playground territory: explore the machine's behaviour BEFORE you commit it to code, or REVISE a definition by simulating edge cases. No app, no :data, no event bus — just topology + simulated state walks.

## Worker scope
Amend Causa's Machine Inspector design to include this affordance as a first-class Mode-B' alongside the existing Mode A (0 live instances) / B (1-3 live instances) / C (4+ live instances). Call it Mode S (simulation) or similar — name's TBD.

## Required design elements
1. **Entry surface**: how does the user enter simulate mode? Toggle? Always-on overlay? Cmd-K command 'simulate :checkout/flow'?
2. **State selection**: how does clicking a state surface available transitions?
3. **Event picker**: dropdown? Floating panel? Inline near the cursor?
4. **Transition animation**: same animation as live? Distinguishable visually (sim mode = simulated, not real)?
5. **Multi-step replay**: can the user sequence multiple events? Save a sequence as a 'test case'?
6. **Guards**: many transitions have guards depending on :data. In simulation, what does the user provide? Mock :data inputs? Skip-guards mode? Both?
7. **Side-by-side with live**: can the user see a simulated walk side-by-side with how a real instance behaved? (May be too ambitious for this round — flag if so.)
8. **Visual distinction**: simulated state highlight must be visually distinguishable from live-instance highlight (color? striped? badge?).
9. **Reset**: how does the user reset to initial state mid-simulation?
10. **Exit**: how does the user leave sim mode + return to live observation?

## Prior art to reference concretely
- **Stately Visualizer playground mode** (the strongest example): click state, see transitions, pick event, animate. THE reference benchmark.
- **XState @xstate/inspect 'simulate' affordance** (where it exists)
- **Storybook play functions** — script-driven simulation; useful inspiration but different surface
- **VS Code's debugger 'step' / 'run' / 'reset' chrome** — UX pattern for state-machine-like stepping

## Output
Amend the EXISTING findings doc ai/findings/causa-machines-design-2026-05-17.md with a new section (suggested: §2.5 'Interactive simulation of the static definition' between current §2 and §3). 1-2 pages. ASCII/Mermaid sketches as needed. Reference Stately concretely per design choice.

title: design(causa+machines): does machines-viz survive if Causa does its job? + UX for static defs + dynamic multi-instance observability
description:
Per Mike chat 2026-05-17: re-examine the relationship between Causa and machines-viz. Causa should be the front door for everything observable in a re-frame2 app. The current plan has machines-viz as a separate tool that Causa embeds — Mike's instinct: that may be over-decomposed.

## Strategic question
If Causa does its job as the observability front door, is machines-viz really necessary as a separate artefact (tools/machines-viz/)? Or does the MachineChart component just become a Causa internal? What about the Mermaid emitter (rf2-deo2i) — does it move?

## Dynamics question (the meatier one)
Current machines-viz discussion has focused on STATIC definitions (rendering the reg-machine body). But Causa's job is observing what's HAPPENING. State machines in production aren't 'the definition' — they're instance #47 of :checkout that started 12s ago, currently in :payment-validation, fired by event :submit. Multiple instances per definition. Instances appear and disappear in complicated situations (spawn/destroy lifecycles).

## UX/UI design brief
Worker should think carefully about:

1. **Browse all registered machines** — entry point. Like Chrome DevTools' Sources tab or VS Code's Explorer for machines. How does the user navigate the machine registry?
2. **Inspect one definition** — diagram view of the registered shape (states, transitions, guards, actions). The 'static' view.
3. **Inspect live instances of that definition** — multiple instances simultaneously. Each with its own current state. How to list/filter/visualize many instances? List view? Activity-monitor style? Per-instance lane view?
4. **Time-dimension** — how an event moved an instance from state A to state B. Replay. Integration with existing Causa time-travel panel.
5. **Cross-machine causality** — machine A's :final triggers machine B's :spawn. How does this show up in Causa's causality-graph panel? Does it deserve its own surface?
6. **Parent-child / invoked sub-machines** — how does the hierarchy show?
7. **Multi-instance scale** — how to handle 50+ instances of a heavily-spawned machine without UI collapse?
8. **AI-pair workflow** — when user in pair2 session says 'show me the :checkout machine', what happens in Causa? Does the AI command 'open machine :checkout in Causa' work cleanly?

## Surfaces to consider (and challenge if needed)
- Causa devtools panel — IS Causa, no embed needed
- User-app drop-in for production UI — does anyone actually want a state-machine diagram in their PRODUCTION ui? Or is this speculative scope?
- Docs cells — could be Mermaid-only? Or needs interactive?
- AI-pair chat replies — Mermaid text via emitter, doesn't need machines-viz the tool

Challenge: is the 'three renderers, multiple surfaces' framing right, or is it premature decomposition?

## Reference reading (must)
- spec/005-StateMachines.md — instance vs definition semantics
- spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md — how machines integrate with the substrate
- tools/causa/spec/000-Vision.md, 007-UX-IA.md — what Causa already commits to
- tools/causa/spec/017-Test-Coverage-Matrix.md — what panels exist
- tools/machines-viz/spec/000-Vision.md + DESIGN-RATIONALE.md (Lock #1)
- tools/causa/src/* — actual Causa shell / panel registry / Cmd-K palette (just shipped per PR #1369)

## Prior-art reference
- XState's @xstate/inspect — runtime actor inspection
- Stately Studio's instance/actor view
- Erlang Observer (thousands-of-process scale)
- Chrome DevTools Performance / Memory tabs (multi-instance browsing)
- AWS X-Ray service map (causal flow visualization)
- VS Code Explorer (browse-many-things UX)

## Output (findings doc)
Write to ai/findings/causa-machines-design-2026-05-17.md (gitignored, do not commit). Sections:

1. **Strategic recommendation**: machines-viz survives as separate tool? Or fold into Causa? Or hybrid (Causa owns the UI; machines-viz becomes a thin lib for the rendering primitive)? Argue both sides; recommend one with rationale.
2. **Static-definition UX**: browse + inspect one definition. Wireframe-quality sketches in prose / ASCII / Mermaid where possible.
3. **Dynamic-instance UX**: list/filter/visualize live instances. Multi-instance scale. Per-instance state highlighting + history.
4. **Time-dimension UX**: integration with Causa time-travel. Replay event → state movement.
5. **Integration with existing Causa panels**: causality-graph, time-travel, event-detail. Where machines show up; where they don't.
6. **AI-pair workflow**: how pair2's 'show me this machine' resolves through Causa.
7. **Bead implications**: which beads (rf2-omsnb, rf2-OMSNB-child rendering-stack, etc.) need re-scoping if recommendation is to collapse machines-viz.

## NOT in scope
- Writing any code.
- Filing rebaselining beads. Mike decides after reading findings.
- Mockups in actual image format — ASCII/Mermaid/prose is fine.

- Worktree: C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2-worktrees\causa-machines-design (mayor will create)
- assert-worker-worktree.ps1 first
- Read-only. No source edits. No PR. No bead close.
- Mayor handles all post-findings decisions.

## Source
- Mike chat 2026-05-17: 'If Casua does its job, is machine-viz really necessary?' + 'What about seeing how events are moving an instance of a state machine from one state to another. For every state machine definition, there could be multiple instances (and they might appear and be destroyed in complicated situations).'
notes: CLARIFICATION 2026-05-17 (Mike): two first-class use cases, equally weighted. UC1 = static artifact exploration (Stately-Visualizer-style playground): browse registry, inspect definition, INTERACTIVELY SIMULATE the definition — click a state, pick an event from available transitions, watch the diagram move; no live app needed. UC2 = dynamic debugging (XState @xstate/inspect-style): observe live instances; each instance has an arc — sequence of events that moved it through states over time; where born / how transitioned / where now / spawned-by-what / dies-when. Multiple instances of same definition simultaneously, each with own arc. Bar: beautiful + ergonomic + robust to complexity. title: spec(machines-viz): lock rendering stack — ELK.js layout + hand-rolled SVG + Mermaid for static (child of rf2-omsnb)
description:
Per Mike's research-conversation 2026-05-17: lock the v1.0 MachineChart rendering stack so the eventual impl worker has a concrete decision-trail instead of a blank slate.

## Decision

**Layout engine: ELK.js**
- Reasoning: Eclipse Layout Kernel ported to JS; clear leader for hierarchical/compound graphs — handles nested states, parallel regions, multi-source edges with bundling. Used by Stately Studio (their production stack), VS Code's mermaid-state-machine preview, Eclipse-derived tools. Active maintenance; mature algorithms (ELK Layered = Sugiyama, plus stress/force variants).
- Bundle: ~600KB
- License: EPL-2.0 — needs 5-min compatibility check before committing (re-frame2 is MIT). EPL-2.0 is compatible with MIT use but worth a deliberate sign-off.

**Rendering surface: hand-rolled SVG**
- Reasoning: full visual control matches the 'beautiful + integrated' bar. Avoids React Flow's opinionated aesthetic (rounded corners, default edge style, 'looks like React Flow'). Active-state highlighting is just a CSS class swap on rendered SVG nodes. DOM-debugability + a11y for free.
- Cost: ~couple weeks of polish to match React-Flow's out-of-the-box ergonomics. Pays off in distinctive aesthetic.

**Static-surface renderer: Mermaid (already shipped)**
- The existing tools/machines-viz/src/day8/re_frame2_machines_viz/mermaid.cljc (per rf2-deo2i) keeps its role: text-to-SVG via stateDiagram-v2 DSL for static surfaces — docs blocks, README, AI-pair chat replies (when AI says 'show me this machine' and the user isn't in a running-app session). Don't extend Mermaid into interactive territory — live active-state highlighting would require re-rendering the whole SVG.

## Three renderers, one shared model

| Renderer | Layout | Output | Surface | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mermaid | dagre (Mermaid internal) | static SVG via DSL | docs, chat, README | shipped (mermaid.cljc) |
| ELK + SVG (MachineChart) | ELK.js | interactive SVG | Causa panel + user-app drop-in + docs cells | v1.0 commitment |
| ELK + SVG (same component) | ELK.js | interactive SVG | standalone web tool | v1.1 if Lock #1 reversed |

All three consume the same reg-machine body — one model, three surfaces.

## Decisions traced to XState/Stately prior art

| Decision | Stately/XState | re-frame2 | Why diverge (if at all) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Layout engine | ELK (Studio); Dagre (legacy Visualizer) | ELK | Same. They got it right; Dagre stalled. |
| Rendering library | React Flow (Studio); custom SVG (legacy) | Hand-rolled SVG | Visual control; React Flow aesthetic doesn't match our bar |
| Static renderer | None (Studio replaces static export) | Mermaid (existing) | We already shipped it; valuable for docs + AI chat |
| License chain | Closed proprietary on top of MIT/BSD libs | MIT throughout (need EPL-2.0 sign-off for ELK) | Open-source posture |

## Alternatives rejected (with reasons)

- **Graphviz-WASM (hpcc-js-wasm)**: excellent quality but ~1.5MB. Devtool needs to feel responsive; not worth the bundle.
- **Dagre / dagre-d3**: smaller (~100KB) but weak on nesting; maintenance stalled. Stately migrated AWAY from this; we shouldn't migrate to it.
- **Cytoscape.js**: full graph lib; canvas-first; ~350KB; more opinion than we want.
- **D3-hierarchy + custom routing**: end up reinventing ELK badly.
- **React Flow alone**: opinionated aesthetic; doesn't meet our 'beautiful' bar without significant override work.
- **JointJS / GoJS**: commercial; wrong fit for OSS posture.

## Scope of this bead (pure spec amendment, child of rf2-omsnb)

- Add a §Rendering Stack section to tools/machines-viz/spec/000-Vision.md (or to the rf2-omsnb-amended Vision doc)
- Capture the table above + the XState-decision-trace rationale
- Add an EPL-2.0 compatibility check task (mayor or Mike: confirm OK before MachineChart impl bead is dispatched)
- Cross-link to spec/Conventions.md (bundle-isolation rules — devtool nss must not leak to production)
- mkdocs --strict clean

## NOT in scope
- Implementation of MachineChart. That's a separate v1.0 bead, dispatched AFTER this spec lands.
- Reversing Lock #1.
- Any UI design beyond the rendering-stack decision (typography, color, transitions, etc. — those are MachineChart impl-time).

## Parent
rf2-omsnb — spec(machines-viz): amend Vision with quality bar + xstate-decision trace for v1.0 MachineChart

Renderer: hand-rolled SVG (deliberately diverges from Stately Studio's React Flow choice; rationale: aesthetic coherence with Causa, distinctive look, full visual control; weeks of polish accepted vs days-to-MVP). Static surface: Mermaid (already shipped, stays). 'Go with Stately decisions' = trust their architecture picks (ELK, EDN, traceability) but renderer divergence stays per bead rationale. title: Add MIGRATION rule for day8.re-frame/http-fx → re-frame2 managed HTTP (gh-1374)
description:

There is no rule covering the actual transition from day8.re-frame/http-fx's :http-xhrio fx (v1 standard for HTTP-from-events) to re-frame2's managed HTTP.

Add an O-rule (next available: O-17, since O-16 is async-flow-fx). 'Convert day8.re-frame/http-fx :http-xhrio fx to re-frame2 managed HTTP'. Coverage:
- :http-xhrio request map → [:rf.http/managed {…}] fx entries

description:

title: Add MIGRATION rule for day8.re-frame/async-flow-fx → reg-machine (gh-1368)
description:
Per gh-1368 (Mike, 2026-05-17): spec/MIGRATION.md has no rule for migrating projects that depend on the v1 add-on lib day8.re-frame/async-flow-fx (latest 0.4.0). The related core surface (on-changes interceptor) is covered by M-21, but the separate add-on lib that provides the :async-flow fx for boot/init/wizard orchestration is not.

## Why this matters
async-flow-fx is reasonably common in real-world v1 codebases for multi-step boot orchestration (auth → config-fetch → reference-data-load → ready). State machines (day8/re-frame2-machines, M-28) are the natural v2 successor. Without an explicit rule, migration agents either hand-wave the conversion or leave the lib in place via :exclusions — both technical debt.

## Proposal (verbatim from gh-1368)
Add an O-rule (opt-in modernisation) — call it something like O-N: 'Convert day8.re-frame/async-flow-fx flows to reg-machine'. Document the canonical shape of the conversion:
- How async-flow's :rules (:when, :dispatch, :halt?, :halt-fns?) map onto machine :states / :on / :final constructs
- Where HTTP-completion events thread into machine input
- The :first-dispatch → initial-state mapping
- Recommended handling of :id and the multi-event :when predicates

If the rule body is large enough it doesn't fit MIGRATION.md's per-rule conventions, ship as a separate doc that MIGRATION.md cross-links (similar to how Causa-replaces-10x lives outside the M-rule list).

Type B rule (semantic rewrite, ask first) — agent surfaces every flow and gets operator approval per call site.

## Hot zone
spec/MIGRATION.md is hot-zone (sequential never parallel per CLAUDE.md). Worker must verify no other in-flight worker is touching MIGRATION.md before starting.

title: fix(causa): Event-detail 'Clear' button is misnamed + misplaced — it's a back/return-to-list affordance
description:
Reported by Mike 2026-05-17 00:08 AUSEST via testbed UX session.

tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/event_detail.cljs:346-356

The Event-detail panel renders a 'Clear' button in the Cascade header row. The action dispatches :rf.causa/clear-selected-dispatch-id which DESELECTS the current dispatch — effectively returning the panel to the event-list state.

## Two problems

### 1. Misnamed

'Clear' implies clearing/erasing DATA (the cascade itself, the trace buffer, the selection). It actually means 'deselect this event and go back to the list'. Better labels:
- '← Back'
- '← Events'
- '← All events'
- 'Back to list'

The '←' affordance is the well-known web-app pattern for navigation-back.

### 2. Misplaced

Currently right-aligned in the Cascade header row (via justify-content: space-between). Back affordances by web convention sit:
- TOP-LEFT (matches reading order, browser back button position)
- Often as an icon-arrow with optional text

A right-aligned label-only 'Clear' next to the section heading reads as a section-action ('clear the cascade'), reinforcing the wrong mental model.

## Fix shape

1. Rename button label to '← Events' (or 'Back')
2. Move to top-left of the panel (before / above the 'Cascade' h2 or in the header alongside the panel h1)
3. Optionally style as text-only with leading arrow rather than bordered button — back affordances are usually visually lighter than primary actions
4. Update :data-testid if the test surface needs to reflect the semantic ('rf-causa-event-detail-back' vs 'rf-causa-event-detail-clear') — coordinate with any scenarios that probe this

Same panel-UX-polish wave as:
- rf2-pcitk (typography density + sidebar width + long-keyword handling)
- panel-cascade-label-clarity (raw {:phase :run-end} leaking into UI)
- rf2-q8154 (app-db panel white-on-white)

When dispatched as a unified Causa-UX-polish cluster: this is a small panel-by-panel pass.

- Button label communicates 'back' not 'clear'
- Position matches the back-navigation convention (top-left, lighter visual weight)

- Visual review: action is recognisable as 'return to event list' without thinking

title: design(causa): tighten typography density + narrow LHS panel selector — info-dense surface, long Clojure keywords
description:
Reported by Mike 2026-05-16 23:55 AUSEST via testbed UX session.

Causa is an information-dense surface (inspect-time dev tool). Current typography is too LARGE for that role, costing screen real estate on every panel.

Three concrete issues observed:

1. **Font size too large overall** — Causa panels show app-db slices, trace events, machine state trees, etc. Each cell often holds a fully-qualified Clojure keyword (e.g. :rf.causa/sync-trace-buffer, :rf.epoch/snapshotted). Larger type = more wrapping + fewer rows visible. Dense dev tools (Chrome DevTools, Sentry, Datadog logs) use 11-13px not 14-16px.

2. **LHS panel selector (sidebar) too wide** — currently ~192px (per shell.cljs L213). Wider than needed for short panel names. Trim to ~140-160px and let panel canvas reclaim the space.

3. **Long-keyword overflow handling** — When keywords are unavoidably long (e.g. :rf.causa/issues-feed-projection), they currently wrap or truncate inelegantly. Consider:
   - Smaller base font (auto-mitigates wrapping)
   - Explicit truncation with hover-to-expand for narrow cells
   - Right-align so the namespace tail (most informative) stays visible while the leading 'rf.' clips

## Scope

Audit and tighten across all ~15 Causa panels:
- Base font: 14px → 12-13px (or use a CSS variable for easy tuning)
- Mono font for keyword cells: ~11-12px
- Line-height: tighten from default to ~1.35
- LHS sidebar: width: 192px → 140-160px
- Long-keyword cells: ellipsis + hover-to-expand OR right-align truncation
- Panel headers + tabs: scale down to match

## Acceptance

- Browser-side visual comparison: dense panels (trace, app-db diff, causality graph) show MORE rows in the same vertical space
- LHS sidebar is visibly narrower; panel canvas wider
- Long Clojure keywords don't wrap aggressively or feel awkward
- The shell still renders comfortably (not cramped — info density != claustrophobia)

## Out of scope (separate bead candidates)

- Theme system / dark mode toggle
- Font family change (keep current; only size + density)
- Specific panel layout redesigns

- tools/causa/src/.../shell.cljs (L213 sidebar width, L394+ shell typography)
- tools/causa/src/.../panels/*.cljs (per-panel cell sizing)

This is design-y feedback but the implementation is mechanical: change CSS values + cross-panel sweep. Audit-first cluster shape (read every panel, propose values, then apply) likely best.

title: Decide :rf.http/managed abort-vs-decode-failure precedence
description:
Per rf2-vpplo audit (2026-05-16). When a managed HTTP request is aborted (via :rf.http/managed-abort or the actor-destroy hook) AT THE SAME TIME a malformed response is mid-decode, which classification wins?

Spec 014 §Failure taxonomy enumerates the failure categories (:rf.http/aborted, :rf.http/aborted-on-actor-destroy, :rf.http/decode-failed, :rf.http/transport, ...) but does NOT specify precedence when both abort and decode-failure apply at the same moment in the transport lifecycle.

Possibilities:
(a) **abort wins** — the abort intent supersedes any in-flight decode. Matches AbortController / SIGTERM convention; cleaner semantics for cancellation-as-intent (the user said 'stop'; surfacing decode-failure post-abort is noise).
(b) **whichever fires first** — race-determined; depends on host transport. Today this is most likely the actual behaviour by accident.
(c) **decode wins** — you got SOME response, surface its error. Less common in the canceller-design literature.

Today's impl is most likely (b). The canned-stub transport (re-frame.http-test-support) dispatches the reply synchronously without an abort window, so the race cannot be reliably reproduced in tests. On real JVM HttpClient and browser Fetch the race window exists but is host-dependent.

Codifying (a) would require a deterministic transport seam — possibly a 'pause decode until abort window closes' shim, or an explicit ordering rule in finalise-failure! / finalise-success!. The seam touches http_transport.cljc + maybe http_handlers.cljc.

Bead filed from audit-bead rf2-vpplo. See ai/findings/rf2-vpplo-audit-2026-05-16.md (local-only).
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1335 — abort-always-wins seam: :aborted? cell on handle, sampled in finalise-* after winning the once-only CAS; 3 deterministic regression tests + spec/014 normative paragraph. Gates: http JVM 190/0, CLJS 2344/0, fast-PR pass, full JVM sweep pass.

title: Decide :rf.machine/destroy fx on already-finished (auto-destroyed) actor
description:
Per rf2-6txsp audit (2026-05-16). When a state-machine actor enters its :final? state, finalize-machine runs the synchronous auto-destroy cascade (unregister handler, dissoc snapshot, clear system-id reverse-index, emit :rf.machine/destroyed with :reason :rf.machine/finished).

Open question: what happens if an explicit [:rf.machine/destroy <actor-id>] fx was queued (or dispatched separately) BEFORE the auto-destroy cascade ran but PROCESSED AFTER? destroy-single-actor! short-circuits on (when actor-id ...) but does NOT explicitly check whether the actor is still registered before doing the exit-cascade run. Possibilities:

(a) The explicit destroy is a silent no-op: the snapshot is gone, exit-cascade/run-child-exit! finds nothing to do, the unregister! is idempotent. EFFECTIVELY no-op today by accident.
(b) The explicit destroy double-fires :rf.machine/destroyed with :reason :explicit — both reasons appear in the trace stream, confusing tools that key on :reason.
(c) The explicit destroy should be an explicit idempotency guard with a typed trace (:rf.warning/destroy-of-finished-actor or :rf.info/destroy-idempotent-noop).

Spec 005 §Final states (D6) is explicit about the auto-destroy + reason discrimination but silent on this race. Spec 005 §Spawning is silent on idempotent destroy.

The current implementation is most likely (a) but the contract is not documented. A test pinning either (a) or (c) would be a real invariant; option (b) is a regression.

title: Decide :on-destroy handler throw semantics (frame teardown)
description:
Per rf2-gh1mj audit (2026-05-16). The frame teardown sequence calls fire-on-destroy-event! as step 1, which dispatch-sync's the user's :on-destroy event handler. Currently fire-on-destroy-event! does NOT wrap the dispatch-sync in try/catch — if the :on-destroy handler throws, the exception propagates up through destroy-frame! and ABORTS the rest of the teardown sequence (no machine cascade, no sub-cache disposal, no late-bound hooks, no dissoc-from-registry, no registrar unregister). The frame is left half-destroyed: lifecycle/destroyed? is still false, sub-cache reactions still hold references, machine actors still registered, and frame still appears in (rf/frame-ids).

Compare to safe-call-hook! (frame.cljc:341-347) which is the protective wrapper used for every late-bound cleanup hook downstream of fire-on-destroy-event!. Those hooks swallow throws so one bad hook can't block teardown.

Possible resolutions:
(a) Wrap fire-on-destroy-event! in try/catch like safe-call-hook! — consistent with the rest of the teardown step list; quiet failure mode.
(b) Catch + emit :rf.error/on-destroy-handler-exception trace, then continue teardown — observable failure, frame still fully destroyed.
(c) Keep current behaviour — escalation forces user to fix their handler; explicit failure beats silent half-state.

Audit also flags a sibling decision: :on-destroy re-entrancy (handler calls destroy-frame! on the same frame from inside :on-destroy). Currently undefined — recursive destroy would re-enter fire-on-destroy-event! then early-return at (when-let [f (frame id)] ...) on the second pass since the recursive call hits a still-non-destroyed frame and would loop infinitely OR be re-entrant-safe depending on impl details. Worth pinning.

Spec 002 §Destroy currently says 'Fires :on-destroy events before teardown if specified' but is silent on throw semantics. Resolution should land in spec/002-Frames.md alongside the other teardown contract details.

Bead filed from audit-bead rf2-gh1mj. See ai/findings/rf2-gh1mj-audit-2026-05-16.md (local-only).
notes:
DECISION Mike 2026-05-17 00:18 AUSEST: (b) Catch + emit :rf.error/on-destroy-handler-exception trace, then continue teardown. Frame must be fully destroyed regardless of user :on-destroy throw; observable via trace event so user knows their handler has a bug. Per pre-alpha masterpiece bar — correctness + observability both win.

ALSO pin the sibling decision flagged by rf2-gh1mj audit: :on-destroy re-entrancy. Recommend mirror semantics: re-entrant call to destroy-frame! during :on-destroy MUST be a no-op (return falsey/idempotent) since the outer destroy is already in flight.

Resolution lands in spec/002-Frames.md §Destroy + implementation in implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc fire-on-destroy-event!. Single PR, ~30 LoC change + 2 regression tests.

New trace event :rf.error/on-destroy-handler-exception (frame/event/exception/exception-message/where tags). destroying-frames atom for re-entrancy guard. spec/002 §Destroy 2 normative paragraphs. 4 regression tests. Late-bind hooks for trace listener install (bundle-isolation-safe). Frames now fully destroyed regardless of user handler throw.

title: perf+spec(core): elide :source-coord capture in production builds (~3-8 KB win + Mike-decision on error-surface impact)
description:
Per Mike's 2026-05-17 'we don't need source code coordinates in production builds — is that easy to get rid of?'.

## Today

Per Spec 001 §Source-coordinate capture, every `reg-*` macro stamps `:source-coord {:file ... :line ... :column ...}` into the registration metadata. CLJS preserves Var metadata in `:advanced`, so the coords ship to production.

rf2-53tcf bundle-size audit verdict was KEEP (bytes-per-reg is small) — but Mike's call: at typical app sizes (~100-200 reg-* calls) that's ~3-8 KB raw / ~1-3 KB gzipped. Modest but real.

## Fix shape (recommended A)

Macro-time conditional: the reg-* macros read the build profile (shadow-cljs's `*compiler*` env or a build-define) and OMIT the `:source-coord` metadata when the target is `:advanced + goog.DEBUG=false`.

Mechanics:
- ~7 macros in implementation/core/src/.../core_reg_macros.cljc, core_reg_view_macro.cljc, core_call_site_macros.cljc
- Each macro currently emits `(reg-X* id handler {:source-coord ~coord ...})`
- New: `(reg-X* id handler ~(if production-build? (dissoc opts :source-coord) opts))`
- Detection helper in a shared macro-side ns: `production-build?` reads `*compiler*`'s build-define for `goog.DEBUG`

## Mike-decision required (in this bead OR file as side-decision bead)

**Production error surfaces use :source-coord**. Spec API.md §Error-emit + Spec 009 §Tags include `:source-coords` in production-survivable error tags. If we strip in prod:
- Sentry-style error reports lose source-line info
- The recovery-message can't say 'failed at login.cljs:42'

Mike's choice:
- **(a)** Strip coords from EVERYTHING in production (errors lose source-line; biggest win)
- **(b)** Strip coords from reg-meta but KEEP them in error-tag emit paths (smaller win; production errors stay useful)
- **(c)** Make it configurable: `(rf/configure :production {:source-coords :strip|:keep})` default keep

Mayor recommendation: **(b)** — production errors are load-bearing for prod observability; reg-meta is dev tooling only (Causa Open-in-editor needs them but Causa is preload-style dev-only). Best of both.

## Acceptance

- Production bundle (`:advanced + goog.DEBUG=false`) ships without `:source-coord` in reg-meta
- Per Mike's (a/b/c) decision: errors retain or strip accordingly
- Test counter app's bundle drops by ~3 KB raw (verify via shadow-cljs report mode)
- Dev/test builds unchanged (Causa Open-in-editor still works)
- Spec 001 §Source-coordinate capture annotated with the production-elision contract

## Cross-refs

- rf2-53tcf (bundle-size audit findings — said KEEP, but Mike's call overrides)
- rf2-zfy1e + rf2-5m5n2 (Open-in-editor consumers — dev-only, unaffected by prod-strip)
- Spec 001 §Source-coordinate capture — needs amendment
- Spec API.md §Error-emit — Mike-decision interaction
close_reason: Merged in #1295 — source-coord prod elision (Mike 'b'): dual-channel (Policy A strip from reg-meta, Policy B retain in error-emit). Realworld -2.7 KB raw / -1.2 KB gzipped. Spec 001 amended.

- All 8 per-feature JVM tests (schemas / machines / routing / flows / http / ssr / ssr-ring / epoch) — NONE relevant to Story-UI changes

title: fix(noise): silence 8 shadow-cljs warnings across 3 files (CI signal hygiene)
description:

title: docs(guide): tutorial-quality docs for :sensitive? + large-blob elision (humans audience)
description:
Per Mike's request 2026-05-17: update docs around `:sensitive?` handlers and large-blob elision for human readers (tutorial style — NOT AI-shaped spec prose).

## Audience

Human developers building re-frame2 apps. They want to know:
1. Why does this exist? (problem definition)
2. When should I reach for it? (decision tree)
3. How do I use it correctly? (concrete example with full code)
4. What can go wrong? (common pitfalls)

NOT a normative spec — that lives in spec/Security.md + spec/API.md.

## Writing discipline

- **Define the problem solved** — before showing the API, explain what goes wrong without it (password in trace, credit-card in app-db snapshot, etc.)
- **Good pacing** — short paragraphs, examples interspersed with explanation, not 200-line code dumps
- **Progressive disclosure** — start with the minimal case (mark one handler as :sensitive); layer up to advanced (custom redact-fn + large-blob policy + Tool-Pair interaction)
- **Positive voice** — "Mark handlers that touch secrets as :sensitive — re-frame2 redacts them everywhere they flow" (not "if you don't do this, your secrets will leak")
- **Carefully-chosen examples**:
  - Avoid: faceless `:auth/login {:password "xxx"}` (cliché)
  - Prefer: relatable real-world shapes — payment form submission, OAuth token refresh, API-key configuration, PII fields (DOB, SSN equivalent)
  - Show BEFORE-and-AFTER trace output so the reader sees the redaction in action

## Surface to update

Probably needs new docs pages under `docs/guide/` (which is human-facing per the project layout). Candidates:
- `docs/guide/<chapter>/sensitive-handlers.md` (new)
- `docs/guide/<chapter>/large-blob-elision.md` (new)
- OR combined: `docs/guide/<chapter>/privacy-and-elision.md` (new — tells the story end-to-end)

Likely chapter: 24-configuration-and-safety (where rf2-wp70d.4 just added the framework-config reference). Possibly its own chapter if the topic deserves more space.

## Cross-refs (already-shipped surface to LINK to, not duplicate)

- spec/Security.md §Privacy / secret handling (normative)
- spec/API.md §Event-emit / §Error-emit (handler-meta :sensitive? semantics)
- spec/Tool-Pair.md §Time-travel §Redaction hook (just landed via rf2-wp70d.1)
- tools/pair2-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md §Universal app-installed :redact-fn (just landed via rf2-wp70d.4)
- tools/causa/spec/002-Time-Travel.md (just landed via rf2-wp70d.4)

## Existing implementation surface (covered, not duplicated)

- rf2-wxe9t conformance fixture (handler-meta :sensitive? error-emit redaction)
- rf2-mrsck epoch :rf.epoch/sensitive? rollup
- rf2-wp70d :redact-fn at build-record time

## Acceptance

- Human reader can go from zero knowledge to correctly marking sensitive handlers in <10 minutes
- Tutorial works through 2-3 concrete examples (login / payment / config)
- Cross-links to normative spec for the contract details
- Passes `mkdocs build --strict`
- Verifies any code snippets actually run (don't ship broken examples)

title: perf(subs): move sub-topology + sub-cache-snapshot to a tooling sibling ns for prod DCE (~0.8 KB)
description:
Per ai/findings/implementation-bundle-size-2026-05-17.md §Part 4 P2 (rf2-53tcf audit).

`core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:830-896` carries two tool-facing query fns:

- `sub-topology` — pure-data query over the registrar; returns sub-id → input chain shape. JVM + CLJS. Public re-export via `re-frame.core`.
- `sub-cache-snapshot` — dev-gated read of a frame's sub-cache as a Tool-Pair-friendly shape. CLJS-only, gated on `interop/debug-enabled?` but the entry-point Var survives DCE.

Both are consumed only by Causa / pair2-mcp / re-frame-10x; no production app reads them. They currently survive DCE in `examples/counter` because they are public Vars re-exported by `re-frame.core`. Estimated cost in counter: ~0.8 KB raw / ~0.25 KB gzipped of subs.cljc's 7.5 KB total.

## Proposal

Move both into `re-frame.subs.tooling` (or merge into the proposed `re-frame.trace.tooling` ns from rf2-qwm0a — symmetry win if both land together). `re-frame.core` re-exports route through the late-bind seam so a no-tooling production build DCEs them wholesale.

## Acceptance

- Production counter bundle drops ~0.8 KB raw / ~0.25 KB gzipped
- The two fns still resolve via `re-frame.core/sub-topology` / `rf/sub-cache-snapshot` (no consumer-side change)
- Tool-Pair test suites still pass (causa, pair2-mcp, story-mcp)
- A new bundle-isolation sentinel pins the contract

## Risk

LOW. Pure relocation. Neither fn sits on the hot subscribe path. The drift-test pattern (`late_bind_drift_test`) provides precedent for the late-bind seam tooling moves.

## Refs

- ai/findings/implementation-bundle-size-2026-05-17.md
- rf2-qwm0a (sibling tooling-split for trace; could land combined)
- rf2-53tcf (parent audit)
notes: Cluster review 2026-05-17: pair with sibling — both extract dev-tooling Vars from production-survivable namespaces into sibling tooling namespaces in implementation/core/src/re_frame/. Recommend ONE worker, 2 commits, single review pass. Shared pattern; rf2-53tcf worker explicitly noted 'could merge'. Sibling: rf2-qwm0a (trace.cljc) + rf2-bmzq0 (subs.cljc).
