Bundle delta: 0B counter (DCE already covered) / +545B realworld for keyword interns. Real win: bundle-isolation contract + architecture clarity. Fix-up commit 39f74517 routed 4 missed pair2 preload call sites.

title: perf(core): split re-frame.trace public-tooling buffer surface to a sibling ns for prod DCE (~1.5 KB)
description:
Per ai/findings/implementation-bundle-size-2026-05-17.md §Part 4 P1 (rf2-53tcf audit).

The 458-LoC `re-frame.trace` (core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc) carries the public dev-tooling API alongside the runtime emit path:

- `trace-buffer` / `clear-trace-buffer!` / `configure-trace-buffer!` / `configure`
- `register-trace-cb!` / `remove-trace-cb!` / `clear-trace-cbs!`
- the buffer-state atom + the filter-predicate body inside `trace-buffer`

In production counter (`examples/counter` :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false) the buffer machinery survives DCE (~1.5 KB optimised contribution within trace.cljc's 4.1 KB total) because the Vars are re-exported via `re-frame.core` and counted as reachable from the public surface. Tool-Pair (causa / pair2-mcp / re-frame-pair / re-frame-10x) need them; counter-only production apps do not.

## Proposal

Move the buffer + listener-registry tooling surface into a sibling `re-frame.trace.tooling` (or `re-frame.trace.buffer`) ns. `re-frame.trace/emit!` and `emit-error!` stay where they are (always loaded; cheap). The sibling ns lives on the same artefact (`core`) so consumers `(require '[re-frame.trace.tooling])` explicitly when they need the buffer API; the re-frame.core re-exports route through the late-bind seam so a no-tooling production build DCEs the body wholesale.

## Acceptance

- Production counter bundle drops ~1.5 KB raw / ~0.4-0.5 KB gzipped
- Existing trace-related elision tests still pass (`rf.registry/handler-replaced`, etc.)
- Tool-Pair consumers (causa, story-mcp, pair2-mcp) still resolve trace-buffer via `re-frame.core/...` (no consumer-side change)
- A new bundle-isolation sentinel added to `scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs` pins the contract: the no-tooling counter bundle MUST NOT carry the `trace-buffer` filter-predicate's distinctive keyword fragments

## Risk

LOW. Pure relocation. The trace.cljc emit path is the hot fast path; tooling surface is cold. Code review must confirm no internal trace.cljc callsite reaches into the tooling Vars.

## Refs

- ai/findings/implementation-bundle-size-2026-05-17.md
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md (the trace contract)
- rf2-53tcf (parent audit)
notes: Cluster review 2026-05-17: pair with sibling — both extract dev-tooling Vars from production-survivable namespaces into sibling tooling namespaces in implementation/core/src/re_frame/. Recommend ONE worker, 2 commits, single review pass. Shared pattern; rf2-53tcf worker explicitly noted 'could merge'. Sibling: rf2-qwm0a (trace.cljc) + rf2-bmzq0 (subs.cljc).
close_reason: Merged in #1305 — perf-tooling sibling-ns extraction (re-frame.trace.tooling + re-frame.subs.tooling) + pair2-mcp fix-up. Bundle delta: 0B counter (DCE already covered) / +545B realworld for keyword interns. Real win: bundle-isolation contract + architecture clarity. Fix-up commit 39f74517 routed 4 missed pair2 preload call sites.

title: fix(test): de-flake resubscribe-mid-grace-cancels-parent-and-preserves-inputs (sub_cache_deferred_grace_test.clj:405)
description:
Test `resubscribe-mid-grace-cancels-parent-and-preserves-inputs` at `implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_cache_deferred_grace_test.clj:405` has been intermittently failing on `(identical? r1 r2)` for the entire 2026-05-16 / 17 session. Affected 5+ unrelated PRs (rf2-yudol Causa mount / rf2-8xzoe.2 causa-mcp server / rf2-8xzoe.3 causa-mcp nrepl / rf2-bo3se Causa hero walks / rf2-jcjul adapter dispose). Reruns sometimes pass, sometimes fail.

Root cause likely: timing-sensitive sub-cache grace-period test that races against a deferred dispose timer. The `identical?` check assumes the same reaction object survives across the grace window — but under JVM scheduler variation (especially CI), a new instance may be created.

## Likely fix shape

Use a deterministic gate instead of timing assumption: poll for the reaction's identity over a bounded window, or arrange the test to make the grace-period boundary deterministic.

## Scope

- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/sub_cache_deferred_grace_test.clj:405` (the failing test)
- Possibly the test fixtures that set up grace-period timing

## Acceptance

- 100x local pass rate (Windows + Linux)
- Test passes on next 5 PRs in a row without rerun

## Why P2

Blocks the merge pipeline. Force-merging through with --admin works (per pre-alpha; the test failure isn't gating on the PR's actual change), but creates friction. P2 to fix soon.

## Cross-refs

- rf2-ka3n6 (audit: replace fixed async sleeps with deterministic gates) — deferred earlier, this is one specific case of that
- Affected PRs: #1257, #1263, #1271, #1279, #1282, #1285 (likely more)
notes: PR #1299 — long grace + back-to-back unsubscribe/subscribe; 100x local pass (50 normal + 50 under 6-job CPU contention); same fix pattern applied to mid-grace-window-resubscribe-stress; production code unchanged
close_reason: Merged in #1299 — de-flake via Option B (deterministic gate, grace=60000ms for identity assertion + split timer-cancel check to sibling test). 100/100 local + full suites green. ENDS session-long --admin force-merge friction.

title: perf(causa): trace-feed projection — incremental update or per-frame debounce instead of full re-walk per push
description:
tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:239-344 project-feed is already single-pass per recompute (rf2-7mwc8 optimisation), but is recomputed fully on every note-trace-event dispatch.

Under burst at 60Hz against a 1000-entry buffer that's ~60k row-touches/sec on the main thread just for chip-counts / distincts — before any actual rendering.

Options:
(a) Incremental update on note-trace-event: handler computes delta (new event adds to distinct/counts; evicted oldest subtracts). Maintain :rf.causa/trace-feed-state in app-db.
(b) Debounce: collapse multiple pushes in a single animation frame via r/track! + js/setTimeout 16. Trades latency (≤16ms) for amortised cost.

Couples naturally with F1 (rf2-z4fza, trace row-key) — schedule together.

Discovered: ai/findings/causa-story-ui-stress-audit-2026-05-17.md F11
Parent: rf2-yb5xx
acceptance_criteria: Trace-feed sub recompute cost under burst (e.g. 1000-event buffer at 60Hz) drops from O(buffer * axes) per push to either O(1) (incremental) or O(buffer * axes) per debounced frame. Benchmark: perf-budget test that asserts under N pushes/sec the main-thread time spent in trace-feed projection stays under a budget.
close_reason: Merged in #1315 — causa-trace-helpers cluster. rf2-44vzy perf: incremental projection ~48x faster (push+filter) / ~206x faster (push-only) vs OLD 4.136ms full re-walk. rf2-vu0mp UX: orphan filter chips rendered with dashed-border affordance + click-to-drop on no-matches state. 25 new helper tests, all gates green.

title: fix(story): controls repeater/tuple rows must key on stable per-entry id, not positional index
description:
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/controls.cljs:466-477 (repeater-widget) + L489-497 (tuple-widget) key entries positionally:

  (for [[i entry-value] (map-indexed vector entries) ...]
    ^{:key i} ...)

Deleting a middle entry shifts everything up. Values render correctly (driven by new entries[i]) but React reuses original DOM nodes — an input with focus / selection at position i+1 now displays position i's value with the SAME focus state.

Same focus-leak class as rf2-kgn0c fixed in workspace.cljc.

For :repeater :set (vector-coerce at L414 uses sort-by str) any edit reshuffles ordering — positional keys hold all DOM nodes in original positions while values shuffle around them.

Discovered: ai/findings/causa-story-ui-stress-audit-2026-05-17.md F10
Parent: rf2-yb5xx
Related: rf2-kgn0c
acceptance_criteria: repeater-widget and tuple-widget rows derive their React key from a stable per-entry id (e.g. an incrementing counter held on the cell-override, or a content-hash). Mid-list delete preserves focus / cursor position on the SURVIVING rows; the focused input visually moves to its new position with the user's edit intact. Regression: focus row [2] of a 4-row repeater, type some text, click delete on row [1] — the typed text remains in row that was [2] (now [1]).
notes: PR #1286 — 4th and final rf2-kgn0c-class sibling. Monotonic row-ids in shell-state at [:rf.story/repeater-row-ids [variant-id path]]; sync via 3 pure transitions (ensure/append/remove). Repeater: r:<monotonic-id>; Tuple: t:<i> (positional legit since fixed arity). 9 JVM + 6 CLJS tests. Discipline cluster COMPLETE.
close_reason: Closed

title: fix(causa): teardown! must drain inline-mounts and reset :rf/causa app-db
description:
tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/mount.cljs:324-338 teardown! resets mount-state, auto-open-state, diagnostic-state but:

1. Does NOT iterate @inline-mounts to call each panel's unmount fn. Inline panels mounted via mount-inline-panel! (line 402) leak after teardown — the React render tree persists, holding references and continuing to subscribe to the still-registered :rf/causa frame.

2. Does NOT unregister :rf/causa or clear its app-db. Subsequent test runs / re-opens inherit prior :trace-buffer / :suppressed-counters state — non-deterministic test isolation.

Discovered: ai/findings/causa-story-ui-stress-audit-2026-05-17.md F9
Parent: rf2-yb5xx
acceptance_criteria: teardown! iterates @inline-mounts calling each :unmount fn, then resets the map to {}. teardown! resets :rf/causa app-db to {} (or unreg-frame if framework exposes one). Test that runs open! → mount-inline-panel! → teardown! has no React-rendered nodes left in DOM and :rf/causa's :trace-buffer/:suppressed-counters are empty.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by rf2-yudol PR #1279 (in queue) — its teardown! drains inline-mounts as part of clearing all 3 singletons.

title: fix(causa): popout window — wire onunload cleanup to release popout-state
description:
tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/mount.cljs:373-400 popout! stores {:ok? true :window win :node node :unmount unmount} in popout-state but never observes the window's close event.

After the user closes the popout:
- popout-state references a dead window.
- popout! called again returns the stale state instead of opening a new window.
- The stored unmount fn is never called against the closed window's document; Reagent's render tree leaks (and may throw if invoked post-close).

Discovered: ai/findings/causa-story-ui-stress-audit-2026-05-17.md F8
Parent: rf2-yb5xx
acceptance_criteria: popout! installs window.addEventListener('beforeunload', cleanup) on the opened popout. cleanup invokes the stored unmount and clears popout-state. Calling popout! again after the user closes the window opens a fresh popout (not a stale state map referencing a closed window). Idempotent.
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by rf2-yudol PR #1279 (in queue) — its register-popout-unload-cleanup! wires pagehide+unload listeners on the popout window.

title: fix(story): qr-svg-string crashes the share popover on overlong URLs
description:
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/qr.cljs:61-76. qrcode-generator at type-number 0 + ECC 'M' supports ~4296 alphanumeric chars at most. A share URL with a large :cell-overrides map (long strings, nested EDN) can exceed this. qr-svg-string doesn't try/catch; the error propagates into Reagent render and the popover crashes.

Consumer: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/share.cljs:180 splices the result via :dangerouslySetInnerHTML — an uncaught throw blanks the popover and the copy-link button is unreachable.

Discovered: ai/findings/causa-story-ui-stress-audit-2026-05-17.md F7
Parent: rf2-yb5xx
acceptance_criteria: qr-svg-string returns a value (or nil) for any input; never throws into the render path. When URL exceeds the QR capacity at the chosen ECC level, the popover renders a degraded panel ('URL too long for QR — copy link instead') and keeps the copy-link affordance live. Regression with a pathological cell-override of ~10KB EDN.

title: ux(causa): trace panel orphan filter — active value disappears from chip rows after buffer rotation
description:
tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/trace_helpers.cljc:214-224 distinct-values is computed over the CURRENT buffer only. When the buffer rotates and the selected filter value's last instance ages out, :trace-filters still carries the selection but the chip-row no longer shows that value.

User sees :no-matches empty state with no chip highlighted and no obvious clue what's being filtered (only 'Clear filters' affordance).

Fix options:
- Union the active filter value into distinct list so chip always renders highlit.
- Or add an 'Active filters' strip in the :no-matches empty state showing each axis=value pair.

Discovered: ai/findings/causa-story-ui-stress-audit-2026-05-17.md F6
Parent: rf2-yb5xx
acceptance_criteria: Active filter value remains visible (highlit) in the chip row even when no buffered event currently carries that value. Empty-state :no-matches surfaces the active filter so the user always knows what's narrowing the view.
close_reason: Merged in #1315 — causa-trace-helpers cluster. rf2-44vzy perf: incremental projection ~48x faster (push+filter) / ~206x faster (push-only) vs OLD 4.136ms full re-walk. rf2-vu0mp UX: orphan filter chips rendered with dashed-border affordance + click-to-drop on no-matches state. 25 new helper tests, all gates green.

title: fix(story): test-pane scrubber must guard against in-flight re-run + key expanded on assertion identity
description:
tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/state.cljs:92-117 select-step! calls epoch/restore-epoch on the variant frame with no guard on :running?.

Race:
1. User clicks Re-run → begin-run! flips :running? true; reset-variant promise in flight.
2. User clicks a scrubber tick from the prior (visible) results.
3. select-step! calls restore-epoch against the frame currently being reset.
4. store-result! resolves and writes NEW :epoch-ids slice — prior :selected-step now indexes a different epoch.
5. Subsequent ticks may target nonexistent epoch ids → silent no-op.

Also: :expanded set in tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode/view.cljs:317-320 keys by positional index i. Re-run that reorders assertions (e.g. a play step inserts) opens the wrong row.

Discovered: ai/findings/causa-story-ui-stress-audit-2026-05-17.md F5
Parent: rf2-yb5xx
acceptance_criteria: select-step! no-ops when slot is :running? true (or queues until run resolves). :expanded set keyed by stable assertion identity (e.g. assertion :label or :id), not row index — so a re-run that reorders or inserts assertions does not open the wrong row.

title: decide(causa): pick Panel vs *-view (008-Embedding-Contract vs API.md drift)
description:
Per causa-mount-strategy-audit (rf2-a6tvr) finding Q2-3.

## The drift

`tools/causa/spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md` (the embedding contract for Story / external React hosts) describes embeddable panels as a public `Panel` component:

```clojure
[causa-event/Panel
 {:frame    (:frame variant-data)
  :compact? true
  :height   320}]
```

`tools/causa/spec/API.md` (lines 82-101) admits that the actual symbols are `*-view` (lower-kebab):

> Each panel exports its `*-view` component for embedding (per `008-Embedding-Contract.md`). The embedding contract names the public symbol `Panel`; the present impl exports under `*-view`. **Promoting to a capital-`Panel` alias is the open decision tracked under the embedding-facade bead** — the canonical symbol list as of today is:
>
> `day8.re-frame2-causa.panels.event-detail/event-detail-view`
> ... (16 view symbols)

Story (the primary embed consumer) does not exist yet, so the drift hasn't bitten yet — but pre-alpha posture says: pick now, don't carry the alias.

## Decision needed (Mike)

- **(A) Rename to `Panel` everywhere.** Update all sixteen `*-view` exports to `Panel` aliases (or rewrites). Touches `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/` + tests + 008 stays unchanged + API.md drops the open-decision note.
- **(B) Update 008 to spec `*-view`.** Keep the existing lower-kebab convention; 008's prose, examples, JS-export snippet (`{EventDetailPanel}`) all need rewriting to match.
- **(C) Hybrid — public alias `Panel` plus internal `*-view`.** Adds an alias layer; mildly inconsistent with the pre-alpha 'no shims' posture.

Recommended (Claude): **(A)** — the embedding-contract spec is the consumer-facing surface; the imp should follow. Renaming sixteen exports + updating 008's JS-side camelCase rules is mechanical.

## Cross-refs

title: decide(causa): keep or delete dock!/undock!/mount-inline-panel! debug modes
description:
Per causa-mount-strategy-audit (rf2-a6tvr) findings Q1-3, Q1-5, Q2-2.

## The choice

`tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/mount.cljs` exports four launch-mode entry points beyond the spec'd inline / overlay / popout trio:

| Fn | Lines | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `dock!` / `undock!` | 296-316 | Hardcoded 40% body-padding-right; unspec'd in 011-Launch-Modes.md. |
| `mount-inline-panel!` / `unmount-inline-panel!` | 402-430 | Imperative inline-panel mount; overlaps with 008-Embedding-Contract.md's declarative `Panel` component path. |

All four are exported on `window.day8.re_frame2_causa.*` (preload.cljs:164-176).

### Why dock! is suspect

The 40% body-padding model is **exactly the dock model the rf2-eehov true-inline design replaced** as the default. Keeping it as a 'debug option' violates the pre-alpha posture (no back-compat shims). The popout covers the 'I want Causa on a second monitor' use case more cleanly; the inline-host covers the 'I want Causa beside the app' case.

### Why mount-inline-panel! is suspect

`008-Embedding-Contract.md` describes Story-side embedding via a public `Panel` component with props-only interface — declarative, isolation handled by the spec'd frame-provider wrapper. `mount-inline-panel!` is an imperative escape hatch that bypasses the frame-provider (the wrap is inside `shell-view`, not at the panel level today). Two paths to the same outcome means the embedding contract is muddy.

## Decision needed (Mike)

For each of `dock!`/`undock!` and `mount-inline-panel!`/`unmount-inline-panel!`:
- **(A) Delete.** Drop from mount.cljs, preload.cljs exports, core.cljs facade, tests. Update spec/API.md to reflect the cleanup.
- **(B) Spec + harden.** Add a normative contract to spec 011 (dock width configurable; embed-mode isolation rules) and align with 008-Embedding-Contract.md.

Recommended (Claude): **delete both** under pre-alpha posture. The popout + inline-host cover the dock use case; the declarative `Panel` component (when 008 is wired against the actual codebase) covers the embedded-panel use case.

title: decide(causa): scope and shape of a new causa skill (and maybe causa-implementor)
description:
Per causa-mount-strategy-audit (rf2-a6tvr) finding Q3-1.

## Gap

`skills/` enumerates re-frame2, re-frame2-setup, re-frame2-implementor, re-frame2-improver, re-frame-migration, re-frame-pair2, re-frame-pair-retro2. **No `causa` skill exists.**

Causa is the structural successor to re-frame-10x with sixteen panels + a planned MCP server. The 0-skill posture is inconsistent with the rest of the tooling triad (`re-frame-pair2` has its own skill; Story implies a future Story skill). An AI agent advising a user on "open Causa and find X" has no canonical reference.

## Decision needed (Mike)

1. **Scope of a `causa` user skill** — does it cover (a) just the launch-mode + panel-tour decision tree, or (b) the full workflow catalogue ("find the wrong sub", "scrub to the bad epoch", "redaction indicator means…")?
2. **Sibling `causa-implementor` skill?** — parallel to `re-frame2-implementor`, for working on Causa itself (panel-facade/leaf split, mount lifecycle, frame-provider isolation rules).
3. **Authoring sequencing** — wait for the doc fixes (rf2-ap3d1, rf2-yudol, the Panel-vs-*-view decision) to land first so the skill cites the canonical surface?

## Recommended shape (Claude's read)

- A read-only `causa` skill, mirroring `re-frame-pair2` in structure (SKILL.md + spec/ + references/).
- Covers: launch-mode decision tree (from spec 011 §Default summary), the 16 panels' purpose, the canonical workflows (find-wrong-sub, scrub-bad-epoch, click-to-source), and the launch hotkey grammar (Ctrl+Shift+C / Ctrl+Shift+/).
- Defer the implementor skill until Causa's surface stabilises post-alpha.

## Cross-refs

title: Audit: harden conformance runner and template rare failure modes
description:
Slice: tools/mcp-conformance process/filesystem safety plus tools/template emitted conformance assets.

Audit findings:
- mcp-conformance already has thoughtful safety handling around stale nREPL port files, workspace escape checks, symlink realpath checks, and degraded live-test skips.
- Rare gaps remain on Windows and in process cleanup: junction/reparse-point escapes, directories deleted between realpath and spawn, child processes that ignore timeout, stale port files that cannot be removed, and template-generated tests that silently skip too much.
- These are low-frequency but high-confusion failures. When they hit, they look like flaky infrastructure rather than product bugs unless the conformance runner reports them explicitly.

References to inspect first:
- tools/mcp-conformance/lib/exec-safety.cjs
- tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-live-pair2-overflow-hermetic.cjs
- tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/test-all.cjs

- Tests simulate deleted workspace/leaf paths between resolution and execution and assert structured failure.
- Timeout tests prove the whole child process tree is cleaned up and stale port files do not affect the next run.
- Template-emitted conformance tests distinguish unsupported, skipped, degraded, and failed states in machine-readable output.

title: audit(causa): review mount strategy — design quality + documentation + skill discoverability
description:
Audit the current Causa mount strategy end-to-end. Three orthogonal questions:

## 1. Is it good (design)?

Read the current strategy in:
- tools/causa/src/.../host/ and tools/causa/src/.../layout/ (mount + host code)
- tools/causa/spec/011-Launch-Modes.md (incl. the CSS custom-property contract from rf2-um813)
- tools/causa/spec/008-Embedding.md (or wherever embedding contract lives)
- The 4 launch modes: inline / pop-out / docking / body-padding (verify against spec)

Evaluate:
- Are the launch modes well-bounded? Is the boundary contract clean?
- Does the default (true-inline per rf2-eehov) cover the common case?
- Are there gaps where authors hit walls (e.g. need a 5th mode)?
- Is the mount lifecycle clean? Does it tear down cleanly on host re-init?
- Pre-alpha posture: any back-compat shims to clean up?

## 2. Is it documented correctly?

Check coverage across:
- tools/causa/spec/* (normative — primary owner)
- docs/causa/* (user-facing guide)
- spec/Tool-Pair.md (cross-spec interaction with Tool-Pair contract)
- tools/causa/README.md (entry-point summary)

Evaluate:
- Is the spec normative + complete? Resolved-decisions captured per SA-4?
- Does the docs/causa/ guide match the spec?
- Are the CSS custom-property contracts (rf2-um813 :--rf-causa-inline-width) cross-linked?
- Are gotchas / failure modes documented?

## 3. Is it known to the right skills?

Check:
- skills/re-frame2/* — does it mention Causa mount?
- skills/re-frame-migration/* — does migration call out mount strategy for upgrading apps?
- skills/causa/* (if exists) or skills/causa-implementor/* — primary owner skill
- Any skill that consumes Causa (skill references via mcp / pair2-mcp / story integration)

Evaluate:
- Do relevant skills know about the mount strategy?
- Are example invocations / configure snippets present?
- Is the launch-mode decision tree captured in skill prompts?

## Process

Shape-3 audit (read-only). Produce findings doc at ai/findings/causa-mount-strategy-audit-2026-05-17.md (local-only, gitignored). File follow-on beads ONE AT A TIME post-findings for each actionable gap.

## Cross-refs

- rf2-um813 (Causa inline resize CSS contract — landed)
- rf2-eehov (default left inline side panel launch mode — landed)
- rf2-jhgw8 (tooling audit — broader scope, mentions tools/causa lightly)
- rf2-xshc1 (Causa canonical usage audit — different focus, tightens API use not mount)
- rf2-6e2ph (Story audit — sibling shape; Story has different mount strategy worth contrasting)
notes:
## Verdict

Audit complete. Findings doc: `ai/findings/causa-mount-strategy-audit-2026-05-17.md` (local-only).

### Q1 — Design quality

**Mostly good.** True-inline default (rf2-eehov + rf2-um813) is well-grounded. The default covers the 95% case cleanly; popout covers second-monitor cleanly. Issues are concentrated in:
- **2 H lifecycle bugs**: `teardown!` leaks `popout-state` + `inline-mounts`; popout has no unload cleanup (rf2-yudol).
- **2 M unspec'd modes**: `dock!` (body-padding 40% — exactly what true-inline replaced) and `mount-inline-panel!` (shadows the 008-Embedding-Contract Panel path) are exported but not in spec 011 (rf2-sbfb7 decision needed).
- **3 M-L cosmetics**: DOM-id collision risk, dual mode-attribute axis, vapour Ctrl+Shift+P / Ctrl+K keybindings (rf2-27zh2, rf2-h3ekl, rf2-zkfiz).

### Q2 — Documentation

**Partially correct.** Spec 011 itself is strong post-rf2-um813/rf2-eehov/rf2-1barg. Drift is concentrated outside 011:
- **1 H drift**: `tools/causa/spec/API.md` §Preload-style enablement still describes pre-rf2-eehov posture ("floating pill", "closed by default", mounts to body) — rf2-ap3d1.
- **1 H install snippets**: docs/causa/, README, skills/re-frame2-setup all show `flex: 0 0 420px` (bare pixel) — the rf2-um813 `var(--rf-causa-inline-width, 420px)` contract is invisible to consumers reading the install path (rf2-n2tij).
- **1 M decision**: Panel vs `*-view` symbol name (008 vs API.md) — rf2-sf38d.
- **1 M cross-link**: spec/Tool-Pair.md does not reference Causa's mount strategy — rf2-8p161.
- **1 L status block**: README claims "In design. Implementation begins after spec ratifies" — wrong; 16 panels + tests + 8 testbeds exist (rf2-w1ufa).

### Q3 — Skill discoverability

**Partially.** Largest gap: no Causa-specific skill exists.
- **2 H gaps**: no `causa` skill (rf2-jw6lc decision needed); `re-frame-migration` does not mention Causa as the 10x successor (rf2-sv0rj).
- **2 M gaps**: `re-frame2` skill covers Causa only as a trace consumer (no `tooling/causa.md`); `re-frame-pair2` mentions Causa once in passing (rf2-hoqhw).

## Follow-on beads filed (11 total)

**P1 (immediate dispatch candidates):**
- rf2-yudol — fix(causa): teardown! tears popout-state + inline-mounts; popout registers unload cleanup
- rf2-ap3d1 — docs(causa): API.md §Preload-style enablement matches preload.cljs post-rf2-eehov

**P3 (cleanup / sequenced after others):**

- rf2-hoqhw — skills(re-frame2 + re-frame-pair2): tooling/causa.md reference + cross-skill mount-strategy mentions

## Recommended dispatch order

First wave (parallelisable, disjoint surfaces): rf2-yudol (mount.cljs) || rf2-ap3d1 (API.md) || rf2-sv0rj (migration skill).
Decision beads hold for Mike: rf2-sbfb7, rf2-sf38d, rf2-jw6lc. The rest sequence behind these.

4. Install snippets show bare pixel; rf2-um813 contract is the CSS variable.

title: audit(spec-links): add link integrity checks and remove placeholders
description:
Scope: Markdown links, anchors, and bead-reference links across `/spec`.

Audit findings:
- The corpus relies heavily on deep local anchors. A preliminary link scan reported many anchor mismatches; some are likely slug-algorithm false positives, but several high-confidence issues are real, especially placeholder links of the form `[rf2-...](#)` and bare `(#)` references.
- Placeholder bead links appear in core docs such as Conventions, Tool-Pair, MIGRATION, ReactiveSubstrate, SSR, HTTP, Schemas, and Cross-Spec-Interactions. A placeholder link is worse than plain text for an agent: it looks navigable but loses the issue lookup path.
- Many anchor links point to headings with punctuation, backticks, slashes, symbols, or em dashes. Without a CI-grade checker that matches GitHub's slug algorithm, link drift is hard to distinguish from checker noise.

Actionable work:
- Add a Markdown link/anchor checker that uses GitHub-compatible slug generation and runs over `/spec` in CI or preflight.
- First fix high-confidence failures: missing files, empty `#` links, and `[rf2-id](#)` placeholders. Use plain bead ids, `bd show` references, or real URLs instead of fake anchors.
- Then triage generated anchor mismatches and update headings/links to stable forms where needed.
acceptance_criteria: /spec has an automated Markdown link checker; placeholder and empty links are removed or replaced; remaining deep anchors pass the checker or are explicitly ignored with rationale.

title: audit(spec-companions): refresh migration prompts patterns and AI audit
description:
Scope: `spec/MIGRATION.md`, `spec/Construction-Prompts.md`, `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md`, `spec/AI-Audit.md`, and `spec/Pattern-*.md`.

Audit findings:
- These companion artefacts are high-value because they turn the spec into operational instructions for agents and implementors.
- `AI-Audit.md` states that some numbered specs are graded only indirectly until a later audit pass. Given the current corpus now includes 013 Flows and 014 HTTP in substantial form, that coverage policy should be refreshed.
- `Construction-Prompts.md` is long and mostly example-driven. That is useful, but its generated-code shapes should be checked against the current API/projection status, especially event vector map-payload guidance, canonical fx ids, and optional artefact boundaries.
- `MIGRATION.md` is intentionally large and historical. It should remain mechanically actionable: each migration rule should name type A/B classification, replacement shape, test or grep strategy, and current shipped status. Historical bead links that are just `(#)` do not help an agent execute the rule.
- Pattern docs should stay thin and point to canonical owners; they should not introduce fresh normative obligations that bypass the numbered spec or schema/conformance path.

Actionable work:
- Refresh AI-Audit coverage so every numbered spec either has a current scoring table or a specific reason and bead for indirect grading.
- Add lightweight consistency checks for Construction-Prompts examples against API.md/Conventions/Spec-Schemas.
- Audit MIGRATION rule entries for mechanical completeness and replace dead placeholder bead links with useful references or plain bead ids.
- For each Pattern doc, verify that normative claims point back to an owner spec and that examples use current canonical names.

title: audit(spec-security-toolpair): make trust-boundary contracts executable

- For each row, name owner doc, security default, opt-in escape hatch, implementation hook/helper, conformance/test coverage, and downstream tool consumers.
- Convert forward-looking security/tool obligations into concrete beads or explicit third-party contract notes.

title: audit(spec-conformance): align fixture corpus docs and lint rules
description:
Scope: `spec/conformance/README.md` and `spec/conformance/fixtures/*.edn`.

Audit findings:
- The fixture corpus is substantial: 124 EDN fixtures, all with `:fixture/spec-version "1.0"`.
- The README fixture table is no longer complete. A filename scan found 46 fixture files not mentioned by filename in `conformance/README.md`, including many HTTP, routing, schema, flow, actor, and spawn/system-id fixtures.
- The documented naming convention says the filename mirrors `:fixture/id` with `/` rewritten as `-`, but 61 fixtures do not match that exact rule. Example: `after-hierarchy.edn` has id `:machine/after-hierarchy`, which the written rule would name `machine-after-hierarchy.edn`. The implementation may be intentionally using shorter filenames, but the README and corpus disagree.
- The corpus uses 42 capability tags. That tag vocabulary should be generated or centrally registered so typo/claim drift can be caught before harness runtime.
- The README says each fixture is a single file of `<200` lines. Current fixtures satisfy that, but a numeric line limit should be advisory at most; fixture cohesion and one-interaction focus are the real rule.

Actionable work:
- Decide and document the actual filename/id convention, then add a lint check for it.
- Generate the README fixture table and capability tag catalogue from the EDN corpus instead of maintaining it by hand.
- Replace the `<200 lines` statement with a cohesion-focused fixture guideline, or explicitly mark it as a soft review smell.
- Verify the reference harness fails unknown capability tags as documented.
acceptance_criteria: The conformance README is generated or checked against the 124-fixture corpus; filename/id rules and capability tags are linted; fixture size guidance is cohesion-based rather than an arbitrary hard limit.

title: audit(spec-schemas): make shape catalogue traceable
description:

- Move normative behavioural rules out of schema comments when they belong in an owning spec, leaving the schema entry as the shape projection plus cross-reference.

description:

- Mixed audiences appear in the same documents: implementor obligations, spec-author obligations, CLJS-reference choices, and companion/tool obligations. The docs often explain the audience well, but the individual RFC terms do not always carry an explicit addressee.

- Decide the corpus rule: either reserve capitalized RFC terms for id'd obligations, or allow prose-level RFC terms but require a nearby stable clause id / owner / audience tag.

- Convert high-impact un-id'd obligations first: Tool-Pair direct-read privacy, Security behavioural MUSTs, SSR host-adapter obligations, trace/error catalogue obligations, and machine/runtime invariants.

title: audit(spec-index): reconcile ownership status and v1 roadmap
description:
Scope: `spec/README.md`, `spec/Ownership.md`, `spec/000-Vision.md`, `spec/Runtime-Architecture.md`, and `spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md`.

Audit findings:
- The ownership model is strong: `README.md` and `Ownership.md` explicitly distinguish normative specs, companion docs, projections, and external canonical homes.
- Status language has drift. Core docs such as `000-Vision.md`, `001-Registration.md`, and `004-Views.md` still say `Status: Drafting` while also describing v1-required surfaces. `000-Vision.md` still contains roadmap text saying state machines are post-v1/foundation-only, while the corpus now has `005-StateMachines.md`, a full conformance fixture set, and implementation artefacts.
- `Cross-Spec-Interactions.md` has a dated current-state note from 2026-05-09 and still lists many interactions as provisional/future targets. That may be accurate, but it needs a refresh pass against the now-expanded fixture corpus and open beads.
- The single-source rule is good, but the current docs rely on readers noticing projection/non-canonical notes. A lightweight machine-readable owner/status index would make drift much easier to catch.

Actionable work:
- Normalize every top-level spec header to a small status vocabulary: `v1-required`, `optional capability`, `post-v1`, `reference`, `projection`, `pattern`, `migration`, etc.
- Refresh `000-Vision.md` and `Cross-Spec-Interactions.md` so roadmap claims match the current implementation/conformance state.
- Add a status/owner lint check or generated index from `Ownership.md` so every contract surface has exactly one owner and every projection names that owner.

title: audit(comments-naming): favor invariants and canonical vocabulary
description:

- Naming is generally strong and intentional: `implementation/README.md` establishes `adapters` as canonical terminology, and MCP conformance has a naming guide. Preserve that approach.
- Comment quality is uneven. Useful invariant comments sit beside stale size/provenance comments, old stage markers, and bead-history notes that now obscure the current contract.
- Public API naming can be confusing where similar concepts are exposed at different levels: `handler-ids` vs `registrations`, Story `ids`, projected epoch helpers, and adapter/artefact/internal helper names need docs that explain when each is canonical.
- Review guidance should prefer comments that explain invariants, authority boundaries, privacy/egress behavior, and non-obvious concurrency semantics. It should avoid comments that merely record implementation history, line-count budgets, or previous refactor stages.

- Sweep comments touched by the audit for stale line-count, stage-history, and obsolete-size claims.
- Add a short vocabulary/naming note or API-doc section for commonly confused public concepts.
- Keep bead IDs and historical provenance in specs/notes where useful, but avoid making hot code comments depend on old workflow context.

title: audit(causa): tighten canonical re-frame2 usage and stale comments
description:
Scope: `tools/causa` production code, tests, and docs where it consumes re-frame2 APIs.

Audit findings:
- Causa mostly uses the canonical frame-bound API correctly: global callbacks and preload/mount code re-enter through `rf/with-frame :rf/causa` or explicit `{:frame :rf/causa}` options, and devtools-only direct reads use framework introspection deliberately.
- Some panel read paths use `rf/registrations` where the code appears to need only ids. Prefer `rf/handler-ids` for id-only enumeration, and keep `rf/registrations` for metadata/source-coordinate reads. Candidate panels include routes, effects, and flows.
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/time_travel.cljs` dispatches `[:rf.causa/pin-current target-eid label]`. For multi-value payloads, prefer a single map payload so event schema, naming, and future extension stay stable.
- `tools/causa/test/day8/re_frame2_causa/registry_cljs_test.cljs` has a stale docstring claiming `registry.cljs` is 1818 LoC and the central registrar. The current registry is a smaller orchestrator, so the comment misleads reviewers.
- Existing `rf2-711z4` already captures the Causa-specific rule that panels should split only on logical seams, not by size. This bead should focus on canonical API use, payload shape, and stale comments.

Actionable work:
- Audit Causa panel introspection paths and switch id-only readers to `handler-ids`.
- Convert multi-position Causa event payloads to map payloads where more than one value is carried.

title: audit(testing): replace fixed async sleeps with deterministic gates
description:
Scope: async tests and browser testbeds under both `implementation` and `tools`.

Audit findings:
- Fixed sleeps are common in places that should wait on observable state: browser testbeds use `page.waitForTimeout` or `setTimeout` waits in Causa and Story, while Clojure tests use `Thread/sleep` in core subscription-cache tests, HTTP managed-request tests, SSR-ring tests, and router-drain tests.
- Some sleeps are legitimate because the behavior under test is a grace period, backoff, timer, or debounce. Those should be named as timer-semantics tests rather than mixed with incidental async settling.
- The current pattern makes failures slower and more timing-sensitive than necessary, especially on CI and Windows.

Actionable work:
- Introduce shared deterministic wait helpers: bounded `eventually`/poll helpers for JVM/CLJS tests and Playwright helpers based on selectors, DOM text, trace-drain hooks, or `waitForFunction`.
- Replace incidental fixed waits in Causa/Story testbeds and implementation async tests with those helpers.
- Leave real timer-contract sleeps in place only when they assert the timer behavior itself, and annotate that intent locally.
acceptance_criteria: Incidental sleeps in implementation/tools tests are replaced by deterministic wait helpers; remaining sleeps are explicitly tied to timer semantics; relevant focused gates pass locally.

title: audit(implementation): partition namespaces by cohesion, not line count
description:
Scope: implementation namespaces under `implementation/**`, with emphasis on namespace cohesion and loose coupling rather than arbitrary file-size targets.

Audit findings:
- The codebase still contains comments that describe a `250-LoC` or similar leaf-size ceiling, including `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc`, `core_call_site_macros.cljc`, `core_reg_view_macro.cljc`, and `core_reg_macros.cljc`. The current policy should be cohesion-driven; line count can prompt inspection but must not be acceptance criteria.
- Several implementation namespaces are intentionally large but also carry separable responsibilities: `re-frame.routing` combines route parsing, matching, caches, URL/nav effects, scroll restoration, link view, and standard subscriptions; `re-frame.epoch` combines capture, projection, restore, reset, and privacy; `re-frame.router`, `re-frame.subs`, and machines transition/lifecycle files are other high-coupling review candidates.
- Existing thin-facade examples such as HTTP/SSR splits are the right direction, but comments should explain the responsibility boundary and invariants, not celebrate line-count reduction.

Actionable work:
- Replace line-ceiling comments with cohesion/coupling guidance.
- For high-coupling implementation namespaces, preserve the public facade while moving cohesive internal responsibilities behind narrower internal namespaces.
- Add focused tests around any facade-preserving split so the public API and late-bind behavior remain stable.
acceptance_criteria: Implementation namespace guidance no longer encodes numeric line limits; any proposed split names the responsibilities being separated, preserves public facades, and has focused regression coverage.
notes: Cluster: implementation hygiene (2 beads from 2026-05-17 audit-the-audit pass). Both sweep implementation/** — rf2-ytazg targets stale comments + naming clarity, rf2-lmd5t targets namespace cohesion + size-ceiling-comment removal. Recommend pairing: rf2-ytazg's stale-comment sweep includes the 250-LoC ceiling comments rf2-lmd5t also targets. One agent, one PR.

title: fix(adapters): cross-adapter sub-cache walk parity in dispose-adapter!
description:
Per ai/findings/framework-quality-audit-2026-05-17.md §A3 [MED]:

Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle (rf2-9fdkb) lists four MUSTs; obligation 1 is 'Cancel all in-flight reactive subscriptions — walk every live frame's per-frame sub-cache and dispose each cached Reaction.'

Drift:
- Reagent adapter (`implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:110-151`) walks `frame/frames` × `:sub-cache`, clears pending-dispose timers, disposes reactions. CORRECT.

Risk: headless test bundles switching adapters between cases without component-unmount disposal leak per-frame cache entries closed over stale reactions.

Action: lift the cache-walk into `spine/dispose-frame-sub-caches!`; call from all three adapter dispose paths.
notes: PR #1271 — new spine helper dispose-frame-sub-caches! wired into make-dispose-adapter!. title: test(epoch): projected-record idempotent under :redact-fn (rf2-wp70d child)
description:
Smoke-test the composition of build-time redaction + off-box projection. See ai/findings/epoch-redaction-hook-design-2026-05-17.md §Bead 3 for the matrix.

## Dependencies

**Sequential — waits for rf2-wp70d.2 (impl) to merge.** Tests cite the runtime behaviour landed there.

## Scope

`implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_redact_fn_projection_test.clj` (new file).

Coverage matrix:

- The four payload slots (`:db-before`, `:db-after`, `:trigger-event`, `:trace-events`) under various redact-fn outputs.
- Redact-fn replaces a whole slot with `:rf/redacted` (scalar sentinel) — `elide-wire-value` must pass through scalars unchanged at the projection pass.
- Redact-fn returns a partially-redacted map (e.g. `:db-after` with one path replaced by sentinel) — projection further redacts schema-declared sensitive paths against the SAME map, no double-walk corruption.
- Composition with the `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` rollup: the rollup reflects RAW signals (computed pre-redaction), so a record with all sensitive paths sentinel'd still carries the correct rollup.
- `projected-record` against a nil-slot record (halted-destroy path) — projection still works.
- `projected-history` over a mixed ring (some records redacted, some not — though in practice the redact-fn is stateless so all records receive the same treatment, the test pins the iteration shape).

## Hot-zone

No — new test file in a single artefact tree.

## Why this is separate from the impl bead

The impl bead pins the runtime contract; this bead pins the composition contract between the new build-time hook and the existing rf2-mrsck off-box egress projection. Splitting keeps each PR's diff small and reviewable; the impl bead's tests cover the direct surface, this bead covers cross-surface composition.

title: feat(epoch): app-supplied :redact-fn at build-record time (rf2-wp70d child)
description:
Implement the in-process redaction hook documented in rf2-wp70d.1. See ai/findings/epoch-redaction-hook-design-2026-05-17.md for the full design + code sketch.

## Dependencies

**Sequential — must wait for rf2-wp70d.1 (spec edits) to merge.** Hot-zone collisions on Tool-Pair.md / Security.md otherwise.

## Scope

`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc`:

- Add `:redact-fn` slot to the `default config` (default `nil`).
- Extend `configure!` validation: accept `fn?` or `nil`; drop other shapes (mirror the `non-neg-int?` pattern for the numeric slots).
- Add `maybe-redact` helper with try/catch + warning emit (`:rf.warning/epoch-redact-fn-exception` with `:frame` + `:ex-msg` tags).
- Thread `maybe-redact` BETWEEN `build-record` and `record!` / `notify-listeners!` in:
  - `settle!` (both arities)
  - `perform-reset-frame-db!` (the synthetic-record commit path)
  - `on-frame-destroyed!`'s `:halted-destroy` partial-record commit path
- Add `:rf.warning/epoch-redact-fn-exception` to the warning catalogue (and the conformance test pin if one exists).

## Critical invariants (test these)

1. `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` rollup is computed from RAW signals BEFORE the redact-fn runs. (Otherwise rollup lies about redacted records.)
2. `maybe-redact` is failure-isolated: a throwing redact-fn warns AND falls back to the raw record (no broken drain).
3. The redacted record is what lands in the ring AND what listeners receive — never the raw form, ever (when `:redact-fn` is set).
4. `projected-record` / `projected-history` are unchanged. The two-pass composition (build-time redact + off-box projection) is idempotent under `:rf/redacted` sentinels.
5. Production builds elide via the existing `interop/debug-enabled?` gate — NO new gate, NO new compile-time constant.

## Tests (this bead's branch)

`implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_redact_fn_test.clj` (new file):
- `configure!` validates: `fn?` and `nil` accepted, other shapes silently dropped.
- Redact-fn runs once per drain-settle; ring AND listener record both reflect the redacted shape.
- `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` rollup reflects RAW signals — redact-fn can erase the leaves without affecting the rollup.
- Failure isolation: throwing redact-fn emits the warning AND raw record lands in ring.
- Interaction with `:trace-events-keep`: a redact-fn that elides `:trace-events` survives the keep-window elision (idempotent dissoc).
- Interaction with `reset-frame-db!`'s synthetic record.
- Interaction with `:halted-destroy` partial record (rf2-v0jwt path).

## Hot-zone

No. Single-artefact (`implementation/epoch/src/` + `implementation/epoch/test/`).

Parent: rf2-wp70d. Sequenced after rf2-wp70d.1.
notes: PR #1273 — epoch redact-fn impl complete. maybe-redact threaded at all 3 sites (settle! both arities + perform-reset-frame-db! + on-frame-destroyed! halted-destroy). All 5 invariants pinned: rollup-from-raw-before-redact / ring-and-listener-same-shape (3 listeners) / throw-warns-and-falls-back / runs-before-trace-events-keep-cap / projected-record-idempotent. +19 deftests. Production-elision 31/31 absent (new :rf.warning/epoch-redact-fn-exception sentinel verified). Also threaded :redact-fn nil into 4 sibling test fixtures. Composition with projected-record: no surprises.

title: spec(security): document :redact-fn slot on :epoch-history configure (rf2-wp70d child)
description:
Sequential prerequisite for the rf2-wp70d redaction-hook impl beads. See ai/findings/epoch-redaction-hook-design-2026-05-17.md (local-only) for the full design.

## Scope

Document the new `:redact-fn` slot on `(rf/configure :epoch-history {...})` across the four owning specs:

- **spec/Tool-Pair.md §Time-travel** — one-paragraph addition to the bounded-history / configure prose. Document `:redact-fn` shape (`fn?` or `nil`), build-time placement (between `build-record` and `record!`/`notify-listeners!`), failure isolation (`:rf.warning/epoch-redact-fn-exception` + fallback to raw), and the `restore-epoch` caveat (a redacted `:db-after` will be the new app-db on restore).
- **spec/Security.md §Epoch privacy posture** — add a fifth bullet ("App-supplied redact-fn (build-time)") to the pattern-level MUSTs. Position: between the existing "Trace retention bounds the in-process surface" and "Sensitive rollup at the record level" bullets.
- **spec/Spec-Schemas.md §`:rf/epoch-record`** — one sentence noting slot values may be `:rf/redacted` (or arbitrary app-chosen shapes) when the app installed a redact-fn.
- **spec/API.md §configure / Tool-Pair config-knob row** — extend the v1 keys catalogue for `:epoch-history`.

## Key contract pins to document

- Build-time placement (NOT listener-fan-out time): one pass per record; ring + listeners see the same redacted shape.
- `:rf.epoch/sensitive?` rollup runs **before** the redact-fn (rollup reflects raw signals; redact-fn may erase the leaves the rollup keyed on).
- Failure isolation: throwing redact-fn warns and falls back to raw (no broken drain).
- `restore-epoch` against a redacted `:db-after` rewinds app-db to the redacted shape — apps that need restore fidelity should leave `:db-before`/`:db-after` alone in their redact-fn and target only `:trace-events` / `:trigger-event`.
- Composition with `projected-record`: idempotent under `:rf/redacted` sentinels.
- Production-elision: shares the existing `interop/debug-enabled?` gate — no new gate.

## Why this is a separate bead

Hot-zone files (Tool-Pair.md, Security.md, Spec-Schemas.md, API.md). MUST land FIRST so the impl bead (rf2-wp70d Bead 2) can cite the spec without forward-ref. Sequential dependency.

## Owning spec edits

Spec sections owned by this bead. Impl bead has no spec edits.

title: ci(docs): narrow docs.yml paths filter — tools/**/*.md is not staged into docs site
description:
The .github/workflows/docs.yml pull_request paths filter includes:

    paths:
      - 'docs/**'
      - 'spec/**'
      - 'skills/**/*.md'
      - 'tools/**/*.md'    ← this one
      - 'mkdocs.yml'
      - 'mkdocs_hooks.py'
      - 'TESTING.md'
      - …

But `tools/**` is NOT staged into the MkDocs docs site:

- `mkdocs_hooks.py:31` — '# - tools/      (tool source + per-tool spec; not staged into docs/)'
- `mkdocs_hooks.py:147` — '# tools/ tree (per-tool source + per-tool spec/; not staged into docs/).'
- Per-tool spec links are rewritten in mkdocs_hooks.py from `../tools/...` to GitHub blob URLs precisely BECAUSE those files don't exist in the staged docs tree.

So a PR that only edits `tools/<tool>/spec/*.md` triggers a full MkDocs build that has nothing to do with the changed files. Wastes ~3 min of CI per PR; pure noise on the changed-surface signal.

## Observed instance

PR #1262 (rf2-zfy1e Story open-in-editor) touched `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md`. MkDocs build ran successfully but the change has zero effect on the docs site.

## Same applies to skills/**/*.md?

`skills/**/*.md` is in the same filter. Check if skills/ is staged into the docs site — if not, narrow that too.

## Fix

Remove (or narrow) the `tools/**/*.md` line in docs.yml's paths filter. If specific per-tool .md files DO get rewritten/included in the docs build for some structural reason, narrow to those specific paths.

## Cross-ref

- Pattern matches rf2-mvugr lesson: 'new artefact = classifier rule + workflow gate co-requirement' codified in TESTING.md §Changed-surface classifier (just landed via rf2-sk6js).
- This is the inverse: an OVER-BROAD filter, not a missing one. Audit the docs.yml paths against actual MkDocs staging behaviour.
notes: PR #1265 — single-file +7/-4 in .github/workflows/docs.yml. Removed both tools/**/*.md AND skills/**/*.md from paths filter (both confirmed over-broad: skill internals at SKILL.md/references/tests/ are also NOT staged — only hand-authored docs/skills/X.md summaries render). Local mkdocs build: 4.66s → 3.92s, link-validator self-test 7/7 pass.
close_reason: Merged via PR #1265

title: bug(causa): Open-in-editor needs project-root config (mirror of rf2-zfy1e)
description:

The shared helper `re-frame.source-coords.editor-uri/editor-uri` now
accepts an optional 3-arg form with `{:project-root <string>}` that
prefixes the classpath-relative source-coord :file slot with the
on-disk root before the URI ships. Story plumbs this via

Causa's surface (`day8.re-frame2-causa.open-in-editor/resolve-uri` and
the `:rf.editor/open` reg-fx) still calls the 2-arg form, so clicking

hit the same "Path does not exist" failure rf2-zfy1e fixed for Story.

Fix surface:

  `project-root` atom + getter/setter + `:project-root` key on
  `configure!`.
- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/open_in_editor.cljs` — update
  `resolve-uri` to pass `{:project-root (config/get-project-root)}`
  through.
- Mirror Story's test matrix in `tools/causa/test/`.

Trivial follow-on now that the shared helper accepts the opt.

Divergence from Story: registry_cljs_test.cljs fixture also resets project-root (Causa has shared CLJS runtime across registry + open_in_editor tests; leak surfaced in CI). 543 Causa JVM + 2173 impl CLJS, all green.

title: bug(story): Open-in-editor button constructs incomplete path (missing project root prefix)
description:
When a user clicks the Story shell's 'Open' button on a variant in the panel-gallery testbed (Phase 1a/1b on main, PR #1242 + #1254), VS Code (the configured editor at re-frame.story.config/editor default :vscode) opens with an error dialog:

> Path does not exist
> The path \panel_gallery\event_detail_stories.cljs:115:3 does not exist on this computer

Observed by Mike 2026-05-16 while exploring the live panel-gallery dev server (http://127.0.0.1:8766/#/stories).

## Diagnosis (initial)

The path Story is handing to VS Code is the BARE filename-with-leading-backslash + line:col, e.g. `\panel_gallery\event_detail_stories.cljs:115:3`. The actual file lives at:

  C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\tools\causa\testbeds\panel_gallery\event_detail_stories.cljs

So Story is dropping (or never had) the project-root prefix. The 'last 2 path segments' shape suggests the source-coords capture is keeping only the leaf+parent, not the full project-relative path.

## Surface to investigate

- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/open_in_editor.cljs — where the vscode:// URL is constructed
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/config.cljc — editor preference + URL template
- The source-coords capture path (likely shared with re-frame core's :source-coords mechanism per Spec 001 §Source-coordinate capture) — where the file path metadata is set when reg-* fires

Either (a) the source-coords are being captured as a relative path and the editor URL builder doesn't have a project-root to prepend, or (b) the source-coords ARE absolute but the URL builder is stripping prefix.

## Fix direction

Most likely needs:
- A project-root configuration (atom in config.cljc — e.g. `re-frame.story.config/project-root`) defaulting to nil (no prepend)
- A worker-side discovery (read `shadow-cljs.edn` :source-paths) or runtime info from the build (shadow-cljs sets cljs.core/*ns-name* etc but file paths…)
- OR: the source-coords mechanism in core/registrar should always capture absolute paths; UI shells just consume.

Per pre-alpha posture: pick the most elegant. Worth a brief audit before fixing.

## Acceptance

- Click 'Open' on any variant in the panel-gallery testbed → VS Code opens the file at the correct line:col, no error dialog.
- Works for variants in BOTH `tools/causa/testbeds/panel_gallery/event_detail_stories.cljs` and `tools/<other>/testbeds/<other-testbed>/` (different artefact roots).

## Cross-refs

- Exemplar surface: tools/causa/testbeds/panel_gallery/event_detail_stories.cljs:115:3 (Phase 1a variant)
- Story open-in-editor module: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/open_in_editor.cljs
- Source-coords capture: spec/001-Registration.md §Source-coordinate capture (referenced by rf2-45kaz registrar warnings BUG)
notes: PR #1262 — (A) approach: source-coords stamped by reg-* are classpath-relative per Spec 001; editor URI handlers need absolute. Shared helper re-frame.source-coords.editor-uri/editor-uri grows optional :project-root opt. Story exposes via (story/configure!). Conservative composition: blank/nil root → v1 verbatim, absolute paths pass through, separators normalised. 45 JVM editor-uri tests (10 new) + 1 story-runtime + 5 CLJS chip tests + 1 CLJS editor-uri smoke. Filed follow-on rf2-5m5n2 for Causa to adopt same 3-arg form.
close_reason: Merged via PR #1262

title: ci(classifier): add spec/conformance/fixtures/* rule → implementation_jvm + cljs_browser + cljs_prod
description:
MED severity finding from ai/findings/ci-test-routing-audit-2026-05-16.md. The .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh classifier has no rule for spec/conformance/fixtures/*.edn. Fixtures are consumed by:
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj (JVM core job, always-on)
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_corpus_cljs_test.cljs (cljs job, always-on)
- Per-artefact _conformance_test.clj files in implementation/flows/, implementation/ssr/, implementation/machines/, implementation/schemas/, implementation/routing/ — each gated behind implementation_jvm='true'.

A fixture-only PR (no impl change, no test change) would run the corpus runners in core but would SKIP every per-artefact _conformance_test.clj. So a new fixture targeting flows would only be exercised by the corpus runner in core, not by flows_conformance_test.clj.

PRs affected this batch: #1246 (sensitive-handler-exception-redaction.edn), #1248 (routing-malformed-url-fail-closed.edn + routing-query-keyword-discipline.edn), #1249 (flow-eval-exception.edn + flow-frame-destroy-teardown.edn). All rescued by concurrent impl changes — the gap is latent.

Surgical fix (one block) in .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh — mirrors the per-feature rule at line 103:

      spec/conformance/fixtures/*)
        implementation_jvm=true
        cljs_browser=true
        cljs_prod=true
        ;;
notes: PR #1257 — 4-bead CI classifier completeness cluster. rf2-4zqn7: TESTING.md spec-impl-pair convention doc (35 lines). rf2-7vsfm: testbeds/* → cljs_browser + examples_browser classifier rule. rf2-qmiiz: spec/conformance/fixtures/* → implementation_jvm + cljs_browser + cljs_prod classifier rule. rf2-mvugr (P1): added implementation/ssr-ring/* to classifier alternation + new jvm-ssr-ring workflow job modelled on jvm-ssr + scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh entry. Local JVM sweep PASS across all 13 artefacts incl. new ssr-ring (58 tests / 299 assertions / 0F).
close_reason: Merged

title: investigate(causa): rf2-f89ce direction — re-scope vs promote-rows vs ease criteria
description:
Per Mike's call 2026-05-16 (decision #3 of remaining-questions): investigate before deciding. Source: ai/findings/causa-testing-work-review-2026-05-16.md Q1.

## Problem

rf2-f89ce (Causa feature/load coverage matrix) absorbed ~3K lines of new test code recently. All 21 matrix rows are still marked `partial`. Three possible explanations:

1. The matrix's `complete` criteria are reasonable; the work doesn't actually meet them. → re-scope rf2-f89ce to add the missing pieces.
2. The matrix's `complete` criteria are reasonable; the work DOES meet them but row promotion is bookkeeping that hasn't happened. → promote rows + close rf2-f89ce.
3. The matrix's `complete` criteria are too strict. → ease them via spec edit, then re-evaluate row status.

## Required action

This is a read-only audit. Worker decides which case applies and reports back with:

1. The matrix's `complete` definition (cite source file:line — likely in tools/causa/spec/ or similar).
2. For each of the 21 rows: does the recently-shipped work meet the `complete` criteria? Verdict per row.
3. Summary: which case (1/2/3) applies, and the recommended action.
4. If case 2 (promote rows): the worker MAY do the bookkeeping in this same PR.
5. If case 1 or 3: file follow-on bead(s) with the concrete next step + close rf2-f89ce as superseded if appropriate.

## Acceptance

- One findings doc at ai/findings/rf2-f89ce-investigation-2026-05-16.md (local-only).
- Concrete recommendation per case (1/2/3) with row-by-row evidence.
- If case 2: rows promoted + rf2-f89ce closed.
- If case 1/3: follow-on bead(s) filed.

## Cross-refs

- Findings: ai/findings/causa-testing-work-review-2026-05-16.md (Q1)
- Parent: rf2-f89ce

title: spec(story): formalise the Story-Causa coexistence convention (host init events MUST preserve Story frame runtime slots)
description:
Per Mike's call 2026-05-16 (decision #5 of Story-on-Causa decision queue): formalise as documented contract. Source: ai/findings/causa-testing-work-review-2026-05-16.md Q3.

## Background

The cart-total slice (commit c2accadf) surfaced a real coexistence bug: :cart/initialise was replacing the whole app-db, wiping Story's frame runtime slots. The fix preserved the slots correctly, but the rule isn't written anywhere — the next Causa host app could trip the same wire.

## What to write

A short normative section in tools/story/spec/ (Story is the imposing party — its frame slots are what need preserving). ~10 lines. Suggested location: a new §"Coexistence with hosting framework state" in 002-Runtime.md or wherever frame-runtime semantics already live; pick the natural home.

Content:
- Story installs runtime slots (variant-id, watch-mode hash cache, layout state, etc.) into the host frame's app-db at known reserved keys (enumerate or cite the convention).
- Host apps' init events MUST preserve those keys when seeding/resetting app-db.
- Recommended pattern: instead of `(assoc {} :my-app-key ...)`, use `(merge db {:my-app-key ...})` — or use a Story-aware seed helper if one exists.
- Cross-ref the cart-total fix as the originating evidence.

## Acceptance

- One short normative paragraph + idiomatic example landed in tools/story/spec/.
- The cart-total exemplar's commit (c2accadf) is referenced as the originating bug.
- mkdocs build clean.

## Cross-refs

- Findings: ai/findings/causa-testing-work-review-2026-05-16.md (Q3)
- Findings: ai/findings/story-on-causa-feasibility-2026-05-16.md (gallery v2 will rely on this convention)
- Originating fix: commit c2accadf
close_reason: Landed via PR #1236 — Story-Causa coexistence convention formalised in tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md (51 lines, no mkdocs warning regression). Cross-refs commit c2accadf as the originating bug.

Replace the current top-level `npm run test:bundle-comparison` shape with an adapter-owned Reagent Slim bundle isolation gate.

The current script is valuable, but it is in the wrong conceptual bucket. It uses `examples/counter-slim-and-fast` and a global-ish `bundle-comparison` name, while the actual invariant belongs to `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim`: advanced slim builds must not pull stock Reagent implementation sentinels, and the slim SSR path must not pull `react-dom/server`.

Preserve the invariant unless a separate design decision explicitly retires Reagent Slim bundle purity as a product goal. Remove the human-example coupling and do not keep this as a general PR CI gate.
acceptance_criteria:
- Reagent Slim has an adapter-owned bundle-isolation command with a clear name, for example `test:reagent-slim:bundle-isolation`.
- The replacement preserves the current S3-008 stock-Reagent-absence check and S3-005 `react-dom/server`-absence check, including a non-vacuous positive/control check.
- The fixture is adapter-owned or testbed-owned, not presented as a human-facing example.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` no longer runs the old `test:bundle-comparison` as a global PR gate; any CI wiring is changed-surface/nightly/release appropriate.
- Documentation references in the Reagent Slim IMPL-SPEC, quiet-tests docs, examples docs, and skills/examples map are updated or removed.
- Passing output remains quiet; failures remain actionable and name the violated contract and reproduction command.
notes: Decision source: 2026-05-15 testing-tiering review. Mike agreed `npm run test:bundle-comparison` is no longer needed in its current form. The mayor recommendation was: kill the current shape, keep the invariant unless Reagent Slim bundle purity is explicitly retired.
close_reason: Merged PR #1210 (09bed974): tiered PR CI, changed-surface gates, rigorous/nightly workflows, testing policy docs, and Reagent Slim bundle-isolation rehome landed.

title: impl(pair2-mcp): emit :data slot in notifications/progress per Pair2ProgressNotificationParams
description:
Surfaced by rf2-4gr88 PR #1194 testing.

The conformance gate's Malli schema Pair2ProgressNotificationParams requires `params.data` (map with `dropped-events` + `dropped-bytes` + optional `overflow-reason`). The actual pair2-mcp server emits `notifications/progress` frames WITHOUT `:data` — gate fails on `params.data MUST be map; got undefined`.

Either:
1. **Server emits :data** — pair2-mcp's progress emit code should populate the custom data shape. Find the emit site in pair2-mcp source and add the `:data` map with the required slots.
2. **Schema relaxes :data** — make `:data` optional in the wire-vocab Malli schema. But this loses the conformance signal; the slot exists in the schema for a reason.

Pre-alpha pick: option 1 (server emits, conformance gate validates the actual contract).

Once this lands, re-enable the live-subscribe gate in `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-live-pair2-overflow-hermetic.cjs` (currently commented out).

## Cross-refs
- rf2-4gr88 PR #1194 (harness fix; onprogress wiring works)
- rf2-zb5z6 (original conformance gate)
- rf2-i3ffz (mcp-conformance audit parent)
close_reason: Resolved by moving Pair2 progress extension data to SDK-preserved params._meta.data, updating the server/schema/tests/docs, and passing the hermetic live subscribe conformance gate.

title: test(reagent): pin dispose-adapter! MUST(2)/(3)/(4) + dispose-ordering invariant
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-afm8m (`ai/findings/reagent-slice-audit-2026-05-15.md` finding M2+L2).

## Problem

The Reagent adapter's `dispose-adapter!` body (`reagent.cljs:110-151`) implements all four MUSTs from Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle, but only MUST(1) — the per-frame sub-cache walk — has explicit pin coverage (`dispose_adapter_sub_cache_walk_cljs_test.cljs`, rf2-a47kq).

MUST(2) (active-roots drain — rf2-9fdkb), MUST(3) (hiccup-emitter clear), and MUST(4) (post-dispose throw shape — rf2-6wxys) are unpinned at the adapter's user-facing surface.

UIx has them all pinned in `adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_dispose_adapter_cljs_test.cljs` (99 lines, three deftests, rf2-8llol). Reagent should match.

## Fix

New file `adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/dispose_adapter_must_2_3_4_cljs_test.cljs` (or extend `dispose_adapter_sub_cache_walk_cljs_test.cljs`):

1. `dispose-clears-hiccup-emitter-cell` — install emitter via `set-hiccup-emitter!`, dispose, assert next `render-to-string` raises `:rf.error/no-hiccup-emitter-bound` (MUST(3)).
2. `dispose-is-idempotent-with-no-tracked-roots` — drive `(:dispose-adapter! adapter)` twice, assert both return nil. Optional: mock `active-roots` cell to verify drain happens (MUST(2)).
3. `post-dispose-delegation-calls-throw-adapter-disposed` — exercise `:rf.error/adapter-disposed` shape via `substrate-adapter/dispose-adapter!` → `make-state-container` (MUST(4)).
4. `dispose-ordering-pin` (covers L2): install adapter, set up frame with one cached reaction, dispose, observe the reaction was actually disposed (proves `interop/dispose!` was still routed correctly because the install slot hadn't been cleared yet).

Mirror UIx shape; reuse the `reset-lifecycle-state-for-tests!` cold-start fixture.

## Acceptance

- All four MUSTs from Spec 006 §Adapter disposal lifecycle pinned for the Reagent adapter at the user-facing surface.
- Dispose-ordering invariant (substrate-adapter clears install slot AFTER calling adapter's `:dispose-adapter!`) is asserted.
- New tests pass cold-start.
close_reason: Cleanup 2026-05-15: completed by main commit a2ff9f3a (test(adapters): pin reagent dispose-adapter MUSTs(2)/(3)/(4) + ordering invariant).

title: fix(causa): dead :rf.causa/restore-epoch-failed handler + parallel storage tension
description: Per audit rf2-imynx §1b + §4a. tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/time_travel.cljs:686-698 registers an event-db handler that nothing dispatches. The restore-epoch-fx-fn writes failures into the restore-epoch-last-result atom and dispatches :rf.causa/bump-restore-epoch-tick + :rf.causa/clear-selected-epoch — but never :rf.causa/restore-epoch-failed. The handler also writes to :last-restore-failure in app-db, parallel to the atom-backed :rf.causa/last-restore-failure sub — two storage paths for the same concept, only one wired. Pick one mechanism: atom-backed-with-tick OR app-db-via-event. Today there are both, only one wired. If atom-route is the design, delete the dead handler. If app-db-route is preferred, dispatch the event from fx-fn and drop the atom. Either way unify storage.
close_reason: Fixed Causa time-travel registration/failure dispatch bugs and graph layout cache regression; added CLJS regressions.

title: fix(reagent): swap set-fn! → chain-fn! for :reagent/set-hiccup-emitter! (parity with UIx/Helix)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-afm8m ( finding M1+L1).

## Problem

`implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:182` and `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:122` both use `late-bind/set-fn!` for the `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!` hook:

```clojure
(late-bind/set-fn! :reagent/set-hiccup-emitter! set-hiccup-emitter!)
```

UIx (`uix.cljs:188`) and Helix (`helix.cljs:198`) use `chain-fn!`:

```clojure
(late-bind/chain-fn! :reagent/set-hiccup-emitter! set-hiccup-emitter!)
```

`set-fn!` overwrites whatever was at the hook key; `chain-fn!` composes (every contributor's installer fires when SSR resolves the head of the chain — see `late-bind.cljc:44-65`).

## Impact

In a multi-adapter test bundle, ns-load order matters. If Reagent loads LAST after UIx/Helix, Reagent's `set-fn!` clobbers the chain — UIx + Helix emitter slots silently never wire when `(require '[re-frame.ssr])` resolves the hook. The current bundle ordering accidentally hides this; a future ns-load reshuffle could flip it.

The UIx audit (rf2-f4exv) already noted this as a Reagent-side observation; same for the Helix audit (rf2-1xcfz).

## Fix

1. `reagent.cljs:182`: `set-fn!` → `chain-fn!`
2. `reagent_slim.cljs:122`: `set-fn!` → `chain-fn!`
3. New deftest in `adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/late_bind_hooks_cljs_test.cljs` (or new file) that exercises chained installation order across adapters and pins that the chained-install fan-out reaches every adapter. Models on the UIx publication test pattern (`uix_late_bind_publication_cljs_test.cljs`).

## Acceptance

- All four adapter ns's (Reagent, reagent-slim, UIx, Helix) consistently use `chain-fn!` for `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!`.
- New deftest pins multi-adapter chained-install fan-out under all load orders.
- Existing tests still pass (`adapter_render_to_string_cljs_test.cljs` still pins post-`(require 're-frame.ssr)` happy path).

title: fix(causa): causality-graph cache returns nil layout on cache-hit-after-filter
description: Per audit rf2-imynx §1d. tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/causality_graph.cljs:401-413. The cache stores :layout (when-not filterable? layout) — meaning if filterable? is true at write time, the cached layout slot is nil. On the NEXT call where cache-hits AND filterable? is false, the destructured layout is nil, the cond hits the (and cache-hit? (not filterable?)) branch (TRUE), and returns nil as the layout. The view then reads :layout nil and the SVG renders with no positions — visible as a stack of overlaid nodes at origin. Reproducer: select an epoch (filter active) → topology change writes nil layout → unselect epoch → next render hits cache, returns nil layout. Fix: always cache the unfiltered layout; recompute filtered layout on demand. OR invalidate the cache when filterable? was true at write time so the next read forces a miss.

title: impl(registrar): emit :rf.warning/missing-doc + :rf.warning/registration-collision per Spec 001
description:
Audit rf2-m84iv findings F1 + F2 (medium). Per ai/findings/spec-impl-alignment-sweep-2026-05-15.md.

## Gap

Spec 001-Registration normatively requires two warnings the impl does not emit:

### F1: :rf.warning/missing-doc

spec/001-Registration.md §:doc is dev-warned when absent (lines 285-299) — five obligations:
1. Emit on every reg-* call whose final metadata-map carries no :doc (or :doc is nil/empty)
2. Suppress per (kind, id) within a runtime process
3. Production elision via re-frame.interop/debug-enabled?
4. Every kind in scope (event/sub/fx/cofx/view/frame/route/app-schema/head/error-projector/flow)
5. Trace envelope: :operation :rf.warning/missing-doc, :tags {:kind <k> :id <id> :source-coords ...}

Impl: grep ':rf.warning/missing-doc' implementation/ → zero matches.

### F2: :rf.warning/registration-collision

spec/001-Registration.md §Re-registration of a different function — collision warning (line 220-223) — the runtime can be configured to warn at registration time when an id is reassigned to a different fn (compare source-coord pair from §Source-coordinate capture).

Impl: grep ':rf.warning/registration-collision' implementation/ → zero matches. Today registrar.cljc DOES compute :different-fn? and tag :rf.registry/handler-replaced with it (good), but no separate collision warning.

## Why now

AI-first surface: documented handlers are the difference between a navigable registry and an opaque one. Without missing-doc, an undocumented :event slot is silent.

## Approach

Ship both warnings together — same elision discipline (:advanced + goog.DEBUG=false constant-folds them out), same trace surface, same one-shot suppression cache pattern as the existing :rf.warning/plain-fn-under-non-default-frame-once and :rf.warning/boundary-without-spec.

Hook point: registrar.cljc/register! sits AFTER the kind-validation but BEFORE the slot write. Add a small (when interop/debug-enabled? ...) gate that:
- emits :rf.warning/missing-doc if metadata's :doc is nil/empty AND (kind, id) not in seen-set
- emits :rf.warning/registration-collision if previous slot exists AND :different-fn? AND source-coord pair differs AND (kind, id) not in seen-set

Tests: add a per-warning test in core/test/re_frame/ (one for each warning, exercising the per-process suppression cache and the elision-probe assertion that Closure constant-folds the call site under :advanced).

## Severity

Medium — these are dev-only warnings; missing them doesn't break production. But the AI-first surface depends on them firing in dev.

## Hot-zone

registrar.cljc is not on the hot-zone list. Safe to dispatch.

## Bead

audit rf2-m84iv
notes: PR #1251 — both warnings shipped. F1 missing-doc: macro-path gate via (:ns metadata); suppression via defonce atom keyed [kind id]; clear-all! resets. F2 collision: emitted alongside preserved :rf.registry/handler-replaced trace when handler-fns differ; same suppression. Both inside outer interop/debug-enabled? gate. Production elision: 30/30 absent in :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false. +12 tests / +24 assertions. No spec drift.
close_reason: Merged via PR #1251

title: perf(core): late-bind get-fn sticky cache for production hooks
description:
HIGH severity from perf-sweep audit rf2-fzrav (ai/findings/perf-sweep-2026-05-15.md §H3).

implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind.cljc get-fn (lines 37-42) is an atom deref + map lookup. Every dispatch reads multiple late-bind keys per event:
- :schemas/validate-event!
- :schemas/validate-app-db!
- :flows/run-flows!
- :epoch/settle!
- :epoch/capture-event
- :event-emit/dispatch-on-event
- :router/dispatch! (fx :dispatch / :dispatch-later)

For a 100-event cascade this is ~600+ derefs of the same atom, bounded by GC barriers (JVM) / V8 IC busting (CLJS).

Pattern already used by re-frame.registrar (line 104, emit!-cache): memoise the resolution. Generalise:

Implementation sketch:
- (def-sticky-hook ^:private capture-event-cache :epoch/capture-event)
- expands to a defonce atom seeded nil + a fn (get-cached) that does:
    (or @cache (when-let [f (get-fn key)] (reset! cache f) f))
- Invalidation: chain-fn! and dev-mode set-fn! should null out the cache atom.
  - Add an :invalidate hook into late-bind/set-fn! that iterates a registry of sticky-cache atoms keyed by hook-key.

Subtle:
- Production registers each hook once at boot then never again — cache hits 100%.
- Dev hot-reload of an artefact re-registers; cache miss on next call — same as today's behaviour.
- The atom-deref churn matters more on V8 than JVM (V8 inline caches go megamorphic on the @hooks site if many keys are read in quick succession).

Files (read-only audit pass):
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind.cljc
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc (call sites)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc (existing pattern at line 104)

Hot-zone: late-bind.cljc — NOT in the hot-zone list; safe. The router.cljc edits would just call get-fn-cached instead of get-fn at sticky-hook sites.

Pre-alpha; recommend benchmarking first to confirm headroom is worth the cache mechanism.

title: perf(ssr): streaming/walk pre-scans every DOM subtree for suspense boundaries
description:
HIGH severity from perf-sweep audit rf2-fzrav (ai/findings/perf-sweep-2026-05-15.md §H2).

implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc walk (line 289) calls (some-suspense-boundary? el) on every DOM-tag descent. The predicate is itself recursive (lines 179-187: full subtree scan). For a shell with N DOM nodes and K boundaries deep in the tree, this is O(N * tree-depth) pre-scan cost. The fast path it gates (emit-element) is already optimal.

Options:
- (a) Compute a boundary-id set ONCE at render-shell entry, threaded through walk as part of acc. Each descent does an identity / membership check.
- (b) Just always recurse — cost is one keyword check per node either way; the fast path 'short-circuit to emit-element' saves a fn-call boundary but not much else when emit-element is itself a tight tree-walk.
- (c) Cache (per-walk) the boundary-status of subtrees we've already pre-scanned to amortise.

Recommend option (b) — simplest. The pre-scan was an optimisation that may itself cost more than it saves.

Hot-zone: NO. Isolated to ssr/ streaming.cljc. Safe to parallel.

Pre-alpha.
