title: [examples-split] Build 11 shared framework-behavior testbed surfaces in top-level testbeds/
description:
**Action**: Build the 11 shared framework-behavior testbed surfaces in new top-level `testbeds/` directory. These are framework-behavior fixtures consumed by multiple tools (Causa, Story, pair2-mcp, causa-mcp).

**Parent decision**: rf2-XXX [umbrella]. Structure: top-level `testbeds/<surface-name>/` — first-class siblings of `examples/`, `tools/`, `implementation/`.

**Tier 1 surfaces (load-bearing for Causa + Story; build first)**:

1. **`testbeds/deliberate-throw/`** — buttons that throw on `:on-click` dispatch; multi-flavour:
   - synchronous throw in handler
   - throw inside fx
   - throw inside flow `:output`
   - throw inside machine action

2. **`testbeds/schema-violation/`** — buttons that dispatch events failing the registered `:rf/app-schema`:
   - app-db slice failure at known path
   - event-vector spec failure
   - cofx spec failure
   - fx-args spec failure

3. **`testbeds/http-toggle/`** — single button with toggleable outcome:
   - 200 success
   - 4xx client error
   - 5xx server error
   - timeout
   - abort
   - network-error
   - decode-failure
   - CORS

**Tier 2 (state-machine + frame surfaces)**:

4. **`testbeds/multi-frame/`** — 3+ frames with cross-frame dispatch + per-frame app-db
5. **`testbeds/deep-machine/`** — hierarchical machine with parallel regions, `:after`, `:always`, `:invoke`, `:invoke-all`; 5+ levels deep
6. **`testbeds/long-flow-w-failure/`** — flow taking seconds to complete; configurable failure injection mid-flow

**Tier 3 (devtools edge cases)**:

7. **`testbeds/drain-depth-trigger/`** — handler that recursively dispatches itself; configurable depth ceiling
8. **`testbeds/non-trivial-app-db/`** — app-db with ~5-level nesting, ~50 paths, for diffing visualisation
9. **`testbeds/sensitive-dispatcher/`** — handler-meta-marked `:sensitive?` events; verify redaction in trace + recorder + MCP wire
10. **`testbeds/large-dispatcher/`** — events with payloads above the elision threshold; verify `:rf.size/large-elided` marker

**Tier 4 (a11y)**:

11. **`testbeds/known-bad-a11y/`** — a Story variant with deliberate a11y violation; verify a11y panel surfaces it (cross-references rf2-qgms1's investigation: must scope to variant root, NOT Story chrome)

**Per surface**:
- Own subdirectory under `testbeds/<surface-name>/`
- Each surface has its own `deps.edn` / `shadow-cljs.edn` boot
- README explains the surface + which test scenarios from the 53-scenario list it supports (cross-ref the in-flight Section B numbering)
- Single-substrate apps (Reagent canonical); a few may need substrate variants if testing cross-substrate behaviour

**Acceptance**:
- All 11 surfaces exist + are runnable via `clojure -M:dev` or similar
- Each surface README cites the test scenarios it supports
- Surfaces are written for testing CLARITY (deliberately error, deliberately leak, deliberately blow budgets) — NOT for tutorial value
- No content from surfaces leaks into tutorial examples
- `npm run test:examples` glob discovers any specs.cjs in testbeds/

**Sequencing**: best as multiple PRs (one per tier, or one per Tier 1 surface). Tier 1 alone unlocks ~half the 53-scenario test list.

**Cross-tool consumption**: Story will reference `testbeds/deliberate-throw/` to verify recorder captures errors; Causa will reference the same for trace-panel verification; pair2-mcp tests via MCP wire. The surfaces don't know about consumers; consumers test against them externally via Playwright.
notes: Tier 1 (deliberate-throw + schema-violation + http-toggle) shipped on PR #1082 (feat/rf2-testbeds-tier1, 2026-05-14). Each surface lives at top-level testbeds/<snake_case>/ with core.cljs + index.html + README.md; per-surface shadow-cljs build entries land under :testbeds/<kebab-case> in implementation/shadow-cljs.edn following the :examples/* shape (incl. Causa dev preload). All three release-build clean, no impl bleed (test:cljs + test:bundle-isolation green). Orchestrator wiring (broadening serve-and-run-examples-tests.cjs glob to testbeds/) is deferred to rf2-p8f2s mechanical step 1. Tier 2-4 surfaces (multi_frame, deep_machine, long_flow_w_failure, drain_depth_trigger, non_trivial_app_db, sensitive_dispatcher, large_dispatcher, known_bad_a11y) remain open under this bead.
close_reason: Landed via PR (rf2-20w5i #1099 story QR+axe; rf2-epiao #1098 machines-viz-mcp privacy; rf2-kzcim #1100 testbeds Tier 3+4 final, all 11 surfaces shipped)

title: [EPIC] Split examples/ into tutorial vs testbeds (Mike decided YES + colocation)
description:

- **Tool-specific testbeds**: `tools/<tool>/testbeds/<scenario>/` — colocated with the owning tool, parallels existing `tools/<tool>/spec/` + `tools/<tool>/test/` pattern.

**Source design**: `ai/findings/examples-split-design-and-test-suite-2026-05-14.md` (local). Section A laid out the case; Section B enumerated 53 browser-test scenarios + 11 shared testbed surfaces.

- `examples/reagent/counter_with_stories/counter_with_stories.spec.cjs` is 1310 lines (33× canonical counter spec) — labelled tutorial but functionally a Story feature-matrix testbed

1. **Migration mechanical step 1** — separate bead. Move tool-side specs to `tools/<tool>/testbeds/`; extract `counter-with-stories` to `tools/story/testbeds/`; de-pollute `examples/reagent/counter/core.cljs` (restore canonical reg-event-fx).
2. **Build 11 shared testbed surfaces** — separate bead. Top-level `testbeds/` directory; surfaces enumerated in findings Section B (deliberate-throw, schema-violation, http-toggle, multi-frame, deep-machine, long-flow-w-failure, drain-depth-trigger, non-trivial-app-db, sensitive-dispatcher, large-dispatcher, known-bad-a11y).
3. **Write 53 browser-test scenarios** — separate bead. 26 Causa-side + 18 Story-side + 6 cross-cutting; ~18 migrate from existing specs after step 1; ~35 new ground.

**Test discovery**: extend `npm run test:examples` glob to `{examples,tools/**,testbeds}/**/spec.cjs` — single command discovers everything; spec path tells reader what's being exercised.

**Spec impact** (verify cross-refs after migration):
- `spec/011-SSR.md`, `spec/Pattern-Boot.md` — reference example paths
- `skills/re-frame2-setup`, `skills/re-frame-pair2` — cite example paths
- `tools/causa/spec/`, `tools/story/spec/` — verification paths

**Sequencing**:
1. Mechanical migration first (low risk, cleans the surface)
2. Tier 1 shared testbeds (deliberate-throw + schema-violation + http-toggle — unlock ~half the scenario list)
3. Fill test suite incrementally as shared surfaces land
4. Tier 2-4 surfaces as needed

**Tracking**: this umbrella stays open until all sub-beads close.
notes: Decision added 2026-05-15: adapter smoke tests are product-internal compatibility gates and should live with the owning adapter, not in human-facing examples. examples/ should become tutorial/showcase-only; adapter canaries belong under implementation/adapters/<adapter>/ or adapter-owned testbed paths, tool testbeds under tools/<tool>/testbeds, shared framework fixtures under top-level testbeds/. title: [EPIC] Stand up causa-mcp — implement the wire pipeline, tools, and server (greenfield, per spec/000-Vision + 004-Wire-Pipeline)
description:
**Greenfield state (as of 2026-05-14)**: `tools/causa-mcp/` carries only `README.md` + `spec/` (000-Vision, 004-Wire-Pipeline, DESIGN-RATIONALE, Principles, findings). No `src/`, no `deps.edn`, no `package.json`, no `shadow-cljs.edn`, no tests. The full pre-impl scaffold is in place; this epic stands up the implementation.

**Reference impl**: `tools/pair2-mcp/` is the verbatim port target. Where shapes match (subscribe pipeline, eval-cljs gate, runtime injection, lifecycle/reconnect, bencode pin), port don't reinvent. Where causa-mcp's catalogue diverges (eighteen tools vs nine; origin tag `:causa-mcp` vs `:pair`; runtime ns `re-frame2-causa-mcp.runtime` vs `re-frame-pair2.runtime`), wire the difference but keep the shape.

**Decided contracts the impl MUST honour**:

1. **Per-drain-batch progress notifications** (rf2-h95hl) — `subscribe` emits one drain-batch per `notifications/progress`, not one event per notification. Port pair2-mcp/subscribe shape verbatim: server polls runtime's drain at `poll-ms` (default `100`) and emits a progress notification per non-empty batch carrying an `:events` vector plus per-tick dedup table. Pinned at `tools/causa-mcp/spec/004-Wire-Pipeline.md §Streaming over batch` (PR #1076). MUST-inventory row 20 captures the test contract.

2. **Direct-read MUST runs `elide-wire-value`** (rf2-b2hip / rf2-czv3p) — every direct-read tool (`get-app-db`, `get-app-db-diff`, `get-machine-state`, sub-cache reads, direct epoch slices) routes returned values through `rf/elide-wire-value` with **both** `:include-sensitive?` AND `:include-large?` defaulting `false` before egress. Pinned at `tools/causa-mcp/spec/004-Wire-Pipeline.md §Privacy` + `spec/Tool-Pair.md §Direct-read privacy posture`. MUST-inventory row 19.

3. **`eval-cljs` gated behind `--allow-eval` flag, default OFF** (rf2-zyoj2 / rf2-cxx5s — same pattern landed in pair2-mcp at PR #1075). The CLI accepts `--allow-eval`; without it the `eval-cljs` tool is not registered. Port the gate verbatim from pair2-mcp; surface in `discover-app` health summary.

**Pointer at pair2-mcp**: port the following verbatim where possible —
- `subscribe.cljs` (drain pipeline, poll-ms cadence, dedup table per-tick, queue caps, overflow markers)
- `tools.cljs` `eval-cljs` gate + `--allow-eval` flag wiring
- `wire-pipeline` shape (six mechanisms: token cap, path slicing, cursor pagination, lazy summary, structural dedup, size elision)
- `runtime.cljs` injection pattern (re-namespaced to `re-frame2-causa-mcp.runtime`)
- `discover-app` / `tail-build` session-probe shape
- privacy filter (`:sensitive?` default-drop + `:include-sensitive?` opt-in)
- lifecycle/reconnect (runtime re-injection on browser reload)
- bencode pinning (`bencode@2.0.x`)

**Scope (substantial, multi-PR; cleanly decomposable)**:

- **Build substrate** — `tools/causa-mcp/deps.edn`, `package.json`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, `src/day8/re_frame2_causa_mcp/`, `test/`, npm coord locked at Lock #6.

title: spec(causa-mcp): pin eval-cljs async-escape boundary semantics for origin tagging
description:
Sec-audit follow-on (rf2-rjnu8 / M2). Findings doc at ai/findings/sec-audit-causa-mcp-2026-05-14.md.

## Gap

`tools/causa-mcp/spec/Principles.md` L106-114 and `DESIGN-RATIONALE.md` Lock #4 say `:origin :causa-mcp` is set at the boundary of `eval-cljs` via the `current-origin` dynamic var, and side-effects inherit the tag "for the dynamic extent of the eval call." The spec doesn't acknowledge the asynchronous-escape failure mode:

A form like `(js/setTimeout #(dispatch [...]) 100)`, `(go (>! chan ...))`, a Promise callback, or an event listener registered inside the eval fires its dispatch OUTSIDE the dynamic extent of `current-origin`'s binding. Result: an agent's `eval-cljs` call can author dispatches the trace bus doesn't tag `:origin :causa-mcp`, breaking the load-bearing audit-trail differentiator the spec names in DESIGN-RATIONALE Lock #4.

This is the default behaviour of any asynchronous CLJS form — not malicious.

## Fix

1. Add §"Boundary semantics of `eval-cljs` origin tagging" subsection to `Principles.md` naming the dynamic-extent limitation and asynchronous-escape risk explicitly.
2. Pin the mitigation contract for the impl pass. Three options:
   - (a) Reject async forms before eval (impractical).
   - (b) Accept that async dispatches from `eval-cljs` land tagged `:app` (or `:rf/unknown`); document the limitation as a known incompleteness.
   - (c) Patch the async substrate (setTimeout / go-loop / Promise resolution) to capture and replay the dynamic var.
3. Update MUST-inventory row I1 to reflect the picked mitigation — currently says "every-mutation-tagged-by-default" which papers over the gap.

Verified that pair2-mcp currently ships option (b) by default (no setTimeout wrapper in `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs`); causa-mcp can inherit that picked posture or choose differently.

## Scope

Pure spec-doc edit + MUST-inventory update; no code (slice is greenfield).
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1067 — §'Boundary semantics of eval-cljs origin tagging' subsection added to Principles.md. Picked posture: option (b) — synchronous-extent only; async dispatches documented as known-incomplete coverage. Mirrors pair2-mcp precedent. MUST-inventory row I6 pins the binding contract for the impl pass.

title: spec(causa-mcp): split eval-cljs authority class from named-mutation tools; spec --read-only launch flag
description:
Sec-audit follow-on (rf2-rjnu8 / H2). Findings doc at ai/findings/sec-audit-causa-mcp-2026-05-14.md.

## Gap

`tools/causa-mcp/spec/Principles.md` L233-254 treats `dispatch`, `reset-frame-db`, `restore-epoch`, and `eval-cljs` as peers under a single consent model: "the user enabling the MCP server is the user delegating their in-panel rights to the agent." Two gaps under the pre-alpha pragmatic stance:

(a) **`eval-cljs` is a stronger authority class** than the three named mutation tools. The three mirror in-panel right-click affordances the human user could trigger; `eval-cljs` executes arbitrary CLJS in the runtime, exceeding the panel's authority surface. Treating it as a peer collapses two distinct authority levels into one.

(b) **No spec-supported `--read-only` launch flag exists.** A developer who wants causa-mcp's read-mostly catalogue (14 tools) and not the mutation band (4 tools) has no way to ask for that subset. Pre-alpha is the right window to spec the gate even if default is "enabled".

## Fix

1. Add a §Threat model + authority levels subsection to `Principles.md` documenting the consent model explicitly — what enabling the server delegates, what it doesn't, trust boundary at MCP stdio.
2. Name two authority classes in `Principles.md`: panel-mirror mutations (`dispatch` / `reset-frame-db` / `restore-epoch`) vs arbitrary-eval (`eval-cljs`). Pin the contract that `eval-cljs` requires a launch-time opt-in flag (`:enable-eval-cljs?`, default-`true` for parity, documented as the gate operators may flip off).
3. Spec the `--read-only` / `:enable-mutation? false` launch flag as a Principles section, default-`true` for current behaviour. Read-only mode disables all four mutation-class tools; the other fourteen work unchanged.

## Cross-ref

Cross-references **rf2-czv3p** (P1, open) which names "authority model for mutation tools versus arbitrary `eval-cljs`" as an action item. This bead is the spec-side implementation of that decision once it lands.

## Scope

Pure spec-doc edits; no code involved (slice is greenfield).
notes: Impl audit trail: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1073 lands the authority-class split (eval-cljs --allow-eval gate, named-mutation no-extra-gate) as decided by rf2-czv3p. Bead remains closed-as-decided.
close_reason: DECIDED via rf2-czv3p (Mike, 2026-05-14): Split eval-cljs from named-mutation tools. Named-mutation tools (dispatch, restore-epoch, reset-frame-db) require NO extra gate beyond MCP enablement — invoking causa-mcp = explicit consent. eval-cljs is qualitatively different (arbitrary code execution) — gated with --read-only launch flag default OFF; published causa-mcp ships with eval-cljs DISABLED; user opts in explicitly via --allow-eval (or similar) at server launch. Low-friction default-safe posture.

`tools/causa-mcp/spec/004-Wire-Pipeline.md` L53-57 says payload redaction on direct-read tools (`get-app-db`, `get-app-db-diff`, `get-machine-state`) is "the `with-redacted` interceptor's job, not the forwarder's". That contradicts `spec/Tool-Pair.md` L569-571 normative MUST which requires direct-read tools to route through `rf/elide-wire-value` with `:include-sensitive? false` and `:include-large? false` defaults. A future impl pass authored against the L53-57 wording ships those tools without the egress walker; the trace-stamp + `with-redacted` together do NOT protect the live value a direct read returns.

The same file's §Size elision section (L292-321) correctly lists those tools as walker consumers — so the spec already internally knows the walker must run. The §Privacy section just under-specifies.

## Fix

1. Rewrite L53-57 Scope bullet to disambiguate the `:sensitive?`-trace-stamp scope vs the direct-read elision scope. Direct-read tools ride the walker contract pinned at `spec/Tool-Pair.md:561-583`; `with-redacted` is the writing-handler interceptor that shapes the trace's `:db-before` / `:db-after` only.
2. Add cross-reference from L53-57 to L292-321 in this file and L569-571 in `spec/Tool-Pair.md`.
3. Update `findings/MUST-inventory.md` to add a Causa-MCP-private row pinning direct-read tools must default `:include-sensitive? false` (row #15 currently pins `:include-large?` only; the `:include-sensitive?` direct-read default is upstream MUST per `spec/Tool-Pair.md:569` and not mirrored locally).

## Cross-ref

Cross-references **rf2-czv3p** (P1, open) — Mike's queued decision bead names this exact reconciliation as one of its two action items. Land after that decision lands, or treat rf2-czv3p as input for the wording.

## Scope

Pure spec-doc edits; no code involved (slice is greenfield).

title: Close Story testing holes beyond the current counter-with-stories smoke
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done:

The current Story example smoke at `examples/reagent/counter_with_stories/counter_with_stories.spec.cjs` is materially stronger than the current Causa smoke and covers a large portion of the interactive Story shell. It exercises the live app, Story shell mount, variant navigation, mode tabs, docs mode, test mode, tag filters, workspaces, args editing, toolbar, trace, actions, time-travel, scrubber cross-reference, a11y, layout-debug, save-layout, custom panel render, and route back to the live app.

That said, important Story spec areas remain unproven by the current smoke and need explicit test coverage so the feature's health is not overstated.

Current holes in testing:
- `tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md`: macro-time validation and source-coordinate stamping are not covered by the browser smoke.
- `tools/story/spec/002-Runtime.md`: direct runtime API semantics such as `watch-variant`, `destroy-variant!`, lower-level lifecycle edges, and teardown behaviour are only partially covered.
- `tools/story/spec/006-MCP-Surface.md`: the Story MCP boundary is not covered here.
- `tools/story/spec/013-Static-Build.md`: static-build behaviour is not covered by the example smoke.
- Parts of `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md` remain unproven in this example path, especially QR share, multi-substrate side-by-side, and Causa epoch embed behaviour.
- The current browser smoke proves many UI surfaces exist and basically work, but it does not yet establish a clear coverage map from spec sections to browser/integration tests.

Proposed direction:
- Turn the current gap list into an explicit Story test matrix keyed by spec section.
- Add the missing coverage at the right layer: browser smoke where user-facing shell behaviour matters, CLJS integration/unit tests where runtime semantics and authoring contracts matter, and build-level tests where static export / bundle shape matter.
- Prefer filling the most user-visible and regression-prone gaps first: static build, mount/teardown semantics, and any Story MCP contract that is expected to be stable.

Acceptance:
- There is a documented Story coverage matrix mapping major spec sections to concrete tests.
- At least the currently unproven high-signal areas above have explicit follow-up tests or intentionally documented exclusions.
- Future Story status summaries can point to concrete coverage rather than a coarse qualitative judgment.

title: Clean up Story browser warnings in counter-with-stories smoke
description:
Why this issue exists and what needs to be done:

The focused Playwright run for `examples/reagent/counter_with_stories/counter_with_stories.spec.cjs` passed end to end, but the browser console still emitted framework-level warnings that indicate the Story/live-app handoff and Story trace styling are not fully clean.

Observed uncleanness from the browser run:

- React warning: `You are calling ReactDOMClient.createRoot() on a container that has already been passed to createRoot() before. Instead, call root.render() on the existing root instead if you want to update it.` Likely source: the `#/` <-> `#/stories` route handoff in `examples/reagent/counter_with_stories/core.cljs`, where the live app and Story shell both mount against `#app` and manage separate roots.

Why it matters:
- The example currently passes, but the warnings indicate non-clean mount/update semantics and noisy dev-mode ergonomics.
- These warnings make the Story feature look less production-ready and can hide real regressions during browser-driven debugging.

Proposed direction:
- Normalise the trace-row selected styling so React is not reconciling `padding` and `paddingLeft` on the same element across renders.
- Audit the app/story root ownership model for `#app` and ensure the route transition reuses or fully tears down roots without triggering the duplicate-`createRoot` warning.

Acceptance:
- Re-running the focused `counter-with-stories` browser smoke no longer emits the two warnings above.
- The fix preserves the current passing end-to-end behaviour.

title: [infra] Tests should be silent on success — quiet stdout, surface only failures
description:
**Rule**: Test suites SHOULD be silent on success. Only failures should emit output. Agents reading test output burn context proportional to verbosity — a green 1900-test run today produces hundreds-to-thousands of lines, when the actionable signal is the final 3-line summary.

## The current shape

A typical `npm run test:cljs` green run emits:
- `Testing <namespace>` line per test namespace (~120 namespaces × 1 line = ~120 lines just for banners)
- Per-deftest `Testing <fn-name>` (if reporter shows them — varies by tool)
- Stray `println` traces inside test bodies — some tests print debug state during setup or assertion construction
- Runtime trace emissions that fire DURING test dispatches — `:rf.warning/*`, `:rf.error/*`, schema-validation, sometimes routed to stdout in dev test contexts
- Final summary: `Ran N tests containing M assertions. K failures, L errors.`

For an agent running `cd implementation && npm run test:cljs`, the green-path output displaces ~2-5K tokens of context per run. With 5+ test-running gates per agent PR (cljs + per-artefact JVM + examples + elision + bundle-isolation + perf-bundle), green runs burn 10-25K tokens per agent run on noise.

## Goal

Green run = `Ran N tests containing M assertions. 0 failures, 0 errors.` (3 lines) — nothing else.
Red run = the green shape, prefixed only by the FAILING `Testing X` lines + the failure assertions + the failure stack.

## Scope (audit + sweep)

1. **`Testing <ns>` namespace banners** — suppress on success. Most CLJS test runners (cljs.test, shadow-cljs `:node-test`, etc.) emit these by default. Either:
   - Use a custom report multi-method that suppresses `:begin-test-ns` / `:end-test-ns` on the success path
   - Use a quieter reporter from `clojure.test/with-test-out` shims
2. **`Testing <var>` per-deftest banners** — same multi-method approach for `:begin-test-var` / `:end-test-var`
3. **Stray `println` in test bodies** — grep `implementation/**/test/**/*` + `tools/**/test/**/*` for `println` / `prn` / `pprint` calls. Most should be deleted; the few that are essential for diagnostics should be guarded under `(when-not (zero? *failure-count*) ...)` shape.
4. **Runtime trace emissions during dispatch** — re-frame2's runtime emits `:rf.warning/*` and informational traces during test dispatches. Verify these route to `*test-out*` only when there's a related failure, OR suppress them entirely under a test-time gate.
5. **Per-artefact test runners** — each artefact's `clojure -M:test` invocation. Confirm `:test-runners` or alias config supports the quieter shape.
6. **CI workflow logs** — `.github/workflows/*.yml` should benefit from the quieter output (less log volume = faster log loading + easier triage).

## Test-the-test

A regression test (clever): run a known-green suite, capture stdout, assert `<= 5` non-blank lines on success. Prevents future "let's just add a println" creep.

## Why P2

This is dev-experience + agent-productivity infrastructure. Not a correctness bug, but it directly multiplies the throughput of every agent that runs tests — which is every code-landing agent.

## Related

- CLAUDE.md project guidance: "Default to writing no comments... Don't explain WHAT the code does" — same minimalism principle applied to test output.
- Tests already exist for asserting test SHAPES (conformance corpus, perf budgets); this proposal extends the discipline to test STDOUT.
notes:
Shipped via PR #1079 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1079.

Tests now silent on success across implementation/* (10 artefacts incl. 4 adapters), tools/* (7 artefacts), examples/scripts/* (Playwright runner + orchestrator), and scripts/* (2 Python check scripts).

New implementation/test-quiet/ artefact provides the shared clojure.test/cljs.test report overrides + a self-test pin asserting ≤5 non-blank lines on a known-green sub-suite.

Concrete reductions: core 219→3 lines, schemas 41→3, causa 51→3. npm run test:cljs emits zero Testing banners + zero runtime warnings on the cljs.test reporter side.

Follow-on rf2-ls3wn tracks shadow-cljs :infer-warning blocks that remain in the test-build compile output (separate concern).

title: Investigate why Causa time-travel stays empty on the counter example
description:

2. Open Causa.

- `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/time_travel.cljs`

title: feat(security): epoch redaction/scrubbing hook for app-db snapshots + raw traces
description:
Follow-on from rf2-0la4f security audit (closed in PR #1049).

The audit recommended a redaction/scrubbing hook before epoch persistence and listener fan-out so apps can strip secrets from `db-before` / `db-after` / `:trace-events` even when the JVM debug gate is left at its default `true` reading. PR #1049 addressed the deeper concern (the JVM prod gate inerts epoch surfaces in SSR) but did NOT add the in-process redaction hook.

## Why this is its own bead

Design-shaped, not mechanical:
- New public API surface (`(rf/configure :epoch-history {:redact-fn ...})` shape TBD).
- Retention policy semantics — does redaction run at `build-record` time (cheap, fewer slots retained) or at listener fan-out (every listener sees the original)?
- Composition with `:trace-events-keep` cap (rf2-iegsz).
- Tool-Pair interaction — does pair2/causa-MCP see the redacted form? They probably should.

## Recommended starting shape

```clojure
(rf/configure :epoch-history
  {:depth 50
   :redact-fn (fn [record]
                (-> record
                    (update :db-before scrub-secrets)
                    (update :db-after  scrub-secrets)
                    (assoc  :trace-events :rf/redacted)))})
```

The fn runs at `build-record` exit (before ring-buffer landing AND before listener fan-out), so neither path sees the raw form.

Spec impact: `spec/Tool-Pair.md` (epoch-record shape), possibly `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (privacy-locus consolidation).

## Files to touch

- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc` — `configure!` accepts `:redact-fn`; `build-record` runs it.
- `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_redaction_test.clj` — new test file.
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` — document the hook.
notes: Research returned: ai/findings/epoch-redaction-hook-design-2026-05-17.md (local-only). Recommended API: (rf/configure :epoch-history {:redact-fn ...}). Build-record timing. Whole-record fn. Failure-isolated via try/catch with :rf.warning/epoch-redact-fn-exception. 5 child beads filed (rf2-wp70d.1 through .5) with dependency chain: spec → impl → tests/docs in parallel → prod-elision. Parent stays open until all 5 close.
close_reason: All 5 children closed (rf2-wp70d.1/.2/.3/.4/.5 — spec doc + build-record impl + idempotence test + tools docs + prod-elision test). Per parent's own contract ('Parent stays open until all 5 close'), satisfied. The :redact-fn surface ships at build-record time with try/catch warn-once isolation. Verified by bd show child status 2026-05-17.

title: audit(security): skills/re-frame-migration
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

This slice is a Claude Code migration skill for moving a re-frame v1.x project to re-frame2. Its attack surface is the instruction set itself: it authorizes repo reads/writes, dependency edits, compile/test/smoke execution, and live upstream lookups that can influence code changes.

## Findings

- High: The skill tells the agent to execute project code during compile/test/smoke phases without a trust gate or operator confirmation. `reference/kickoff-prompt.md:23,27` explicitly says to run compile, tests, and smoke tests; `SKILL.md:67` repeats that verification loop; `reference/sequencing.md:131-136` assumes clean compile/test cycles as part of normal operation. On an untrusted or newly cloned repo, this is arbitrary code execution via the build/test toolchain.
- Medium: The skill allows mutable remote content to drive migration behavior at runtime. `reference/kickoff-prompt.md:21` tells the agent to clone/load `MIGRATION.md` from GitHub if needed, and `reference/setup.md:104-112` chooses the target version from live GitHub files/releases. That expands the trust boundary beyond the local repo and makes dependency rewrites depend on unpinned upstream state.

## Recommended changes

- Add an explicit trust boundary rule: do not run compile, test, smoke-test, or browser-launch commands unless the operator confirms the repo is trusted. Default to printing the exact commands for the author to run.
- Require a local, pinned migration source. Prefer the checked-in `spec/MIGRATION.md`; if a remote fetch is unavoidable, require a commit SHA or release tag and record it in the migration report.
- Require an author-approved target version instead of auto-selecting the latest GitHub state. At minimum, treat remote version discovery as advisory and stop for confirmation before editing dependency files.
- Reconcile the conflicting guidance about who runs verification so the skill does not accidentally execute project code while other docs say the author runs tests.

## Spec or policy impact

- Operator review: whether this skill is allowed to execute build/test/smoke commands against third-party or otherwise untrusted repositories.
- Policy review: `spec/authoring-prompt.md:71` asks the agent not to disclose AI authorship in commits/PR text, which affects provenance and auditability.

## Commands checked

- `bd prime`
- `rg --files skills/re-frame-migration`
- `git status --short -- skills/re-frame-migration ...`
- `Get-Content -Raw` / line-numbered `Get-Content` on slice files
- `rg -n` keyword searches across `skills/re-frame-migration`

## Files checked

- `skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/README.md`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/package.json`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/reference/kickoff-prompt.md`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/reference/setup.md`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/reference/sequencing.md`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/reference/breaking-changes.md`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/reference/auto-call-site-rewrites.md`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/reference/auto-cross-cutting.md`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/reference/guided-handlers-state.md`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/reference/guided-interceptors-subs.md`
- `skills/re-frame-migration/reference/error-events.md`

title: audit(security): skills/re-frame-pair-retro2
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`skills/re-frame-pair-retro2` is a documentation-only meta-skill that retrospects on a `re-frame-pair2` session and optionally drafts or files improvement work. Its security surface is prompt/config driven rather than code driven:

- `SKILL.md` frontmatter grants tool access, including `Bash(bd *)`, `Edit`, `Write`, and `mcp__re-frame-pair2__discover-app`.
- The skill consumes session transcripts and recap text, which may contain secrets, internal URLs, paths, or malicious shell metacharacters.
- The reference docs include bead-filing command examples and a recommendation to probe a live runtime during retrospectives.

## Findings

- High: Over-broad mutation permissions for a read-mostly retrospective skill. [`skills/re-frame-pair-retro2/SKILL.md:30`](C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\skills\re-frame-pair-retro2\SKILL.md) grants `Bash(bd *)`, `Edit`, and `Write`, while the same skill says it should default to diagnosis, not contribution, and must not file work without explicit approval ([`SKILL.md:55`](C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\skills\re-frame-pair-retro2\SKILL.md), [`SKILL.md:107`](C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\skills\re-frame-pair-retro2\SKILL.md)). Because the shared retro protocol also permits `Edit` for mechanical rewrites ([`skills/shared/retro-protocol.md:36`](C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\skills\shared\retro-protocol.md)), prompt injection or model error could mutate user code or issue state during what users expect to be a retrospective.
- High: The filing template encourages unsafe shell interpolation of transcript-derived content. [`skills/re-frame-pair-retro2/references/issue-template.md:64`](C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\skills\re-frame-pair-retro2\references\issue-template.md) shows `bd create --title "<title>" --body "<body>"`, while the skill’s primary input is the raw conversation/session transcript ([`spec/inputs.md:7`](C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\skills\re-frame-pair-retro2\spec\inputs.md)). If an agent copies untrusted session text into those shell placeholders, quotes, command substitution, or newline payloads can break the command or execute unintended shell content.
- Medium: The slice mixes a transcript-only contract with live runtime probing. The spec says the improver works on the in-conversation transcript and not the live app state ([`spec/inputs.md:9`](C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\skills\re-frame-pair-retro2\spec\inputs.md), [`spec/inputs.md:76`](C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\skills\re-frame-pair-retro2\spec\inputs.md), [`spec/design.md:162`](C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\skills\re-frame-pair-retro2\spec\design.md)), but `known-frictions.md` recommends running `mcp__re-frame-pair2__discover-app` at the start of a retrospective ([`references/known-frictions.md:142`](C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2\skills\re-frame-pair-retro2\references\known-frictions.md)). That creates unnecessary runtime access and metadata disclosure in recap-only/offline retrospectives.

## Recommended changes

- Remove `Edit` and `Write` from this skill’s default tool grant. If filing is needed, gate it behind an explicit user-approved mode and expose only the minimum `bd` commands required.
- Replace `Bash(bd *)` with a narrower allowance or procedural rule such as read-only `bd` commands by default, with `bd create` enabled only after an explicit approval step.
- Rewrite the bead-filing examples to avoid shell interpolation of raw text. Use a temp file, stdin, or another escaping-safe mechanism, and state plainly that transcript/user text must never be embedded directly into a shell command string.
- Change the `discover-app` guidance so it is opt-in and only used when the retrospective is explicitly tied to an in-conversation live session where runtime access is already expected.
- Remove maintainer-specific local paths from filing examples and replace them with placeholders; this aligns the docs with the slice’s own “redact unnecessary local paths” rule.

description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface
This slice is a Claude skill plus reference documentation for guiding an engineer through building a new `re-frame2` implementation in another host language or substrate. It has no executable runtime code, no dependencies, and no install scripts. The real attack surface is the workflow guidance itself: it tells an agent to read a user-supplied `re-frame2` spec checkout, write code into a target repo, and create `bd` items when it decides the spec is incomplete.

## Findings
1. Medium: cross-repo `bd create` writes are encouraged without an explicit approval gate.
   Evidence: `skills/re-frame2-implementor/reference/kickoff-prompt.md:30-34`, `skills/re-frame2-implementor/reference/cardinal-rules.md:9,33`, `skills/re-frame2-implementor/reference/conformance.md:59,96,126`.
   Risk: a fresh session running in a third-party port repo is told to create beads in the upstream `re-frame2` repo based on model judgment alone. That is an uncontrolled external-write path and can leak private port details or create tracker spam.
2. Low: the trusted spec input is mutable and not pinned before use.
   Evidence: `skills/re-frame2-implementor/reference/kickoff-prompt.md:22`, `skills/re-frame2-implementor/spec/inputs.md:26`.
   Risk: the skill treats a locally cloned `re-frame2` checkout and published spec URLs as the contract, but does not require verifying origin or pinning a commit before implementation begins. A stale or malicious checkout can steer generated code or conformance behavior.

No actionable code-level vulnerabilities were found in this slice.

## Recommended changes
- Change the default from "file a bead" to "draft bead text and ask for approval." If external filing remains allowed, limit the payload to public spec-gap evidence and avoid copying private port details.
- Require a pinned `re-frame2` commit or tag at kickoff, verify the checkout origin before reading it, and record that hash in `DECISIONS.md` before Phase 1 starts.

title: audit(security): skills/re-frame2-setup
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

This slice defines a Claude Code setup skill for scaffolding a greenfield re-frame2 ClojureScript app. The main attack surface is agent behavior rather than app runtime code: auto-matched skill instructions, shell-capable `allowed-tools`, installation into `~/.claude/skills` or project `.claude/skills`, package-manager/network activity during setup, and optional nREPL-based live inspection.

## Findings

1. **High: overly broad shell permissions in the skill frontmatter.** `skills/re-frame2-setup/SKILL.md:20-24` grants `Bash(clojure *)`, `Bash(npm *)`, `Bash(npx *)`, and `Bash(shadow-cljs *)`. The documented workflow only needs a narrow subset of commands, but these wildcards allow arbitrary subcommands and, in the case of `npx`, arbitrary package execution. That expands the skill from "project setup" into a general code-execution surface if prompts or repo content steer it off the happy path.
2. **Medium: setup guidance pulls latest npm packages from the public registry by default.** `skills/re-frame2-setup/reference/deps-versions.md:74-91` recommends `<latest-2.x>`, `<latest-18.x>`, `npm view ... version`, then `npm install`. That makes generated projects non-reproducible and increases exposure to newly published malicious or broken packages. The repo's own pinned versions are presented only as a fallback rather than the default trusted baseline.
3. **Medium: install instructions treat mutable repo content as executable skill code without a trust warning.** `skills/re-frame2-setup/README.md:75-98` tells users to `git clone` the repo and symlink or copy the skill into `~/.claude/skills` or a project `.claude/skills` directory. Those instructions effectively promote repo content to executable agent instructions with shell access, but they do not tell users to pin a tag/commit or review the skill before installation. The global symlink variant also tracks a mutable working tree.
4. **Low/Medium: nREPL guidance omits a dev-only / localhost-only warning for a code-execution interface.** `skills/re-frame2-setup/reference/shadow-cljs.md:95-99` and `skills/re-frame2-setup/reference/first-counter.md:128-131` describe attaching `re-frame-pair2` over nREPL, including port discovery, but do not state that nREPL should remain local/dev-only and must not be exposed on shared or public interfaces.

## Recommended changes

- Scope `allowed-tools` to the exact subcommands the skill actually needs. In particular, remove blanket `npx *` and `npm *`; prefer tightly scoped patterns such as version lookup, install, and the specific `shadow-cljs` watch command.
- Change the default dependency guidance to use repo-vetted pinned versions first. Treat "latest from npm" as an explicit opt-in path, and consider shipping or generating a lockfile-backed baseline.
- Update the installation docs to require pinning a release tag or commit and reviewing the skill before copying or symlinking it into Claude skill directories. Prefer copying from a pinned checkout over symlinking a mutable working tree.
- Add a short security note anywhere nREPL is mentioned: dev-only, localhost-only, and never expose it outside a trusted workstation or network.

## Spec or policy impact

- No framework `/spec` changes identified.
- Operator/policy review: define least-privilege standards for published skills so `allowed-tools` are subcommand-scoped rather than blanket `npm *` / `npx *`.
- Operator/policy review: define provenance requirements for installing or vendoring skills under `~/.claude/skills` and project `.claude/skills`.
- Operator/policy review: define standard warning text for docs that advertise nREPL or similar live code-execution attachment points.

description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface
`skills/re-frame2-improver` is a critique-mode skill for existing re-frame2 code. It ingests repo `.cljs` / `.cljc` files and user-supplied snippets, classifies them against anti-pattern leaves, cross-links to canonical docs/specs, and can propose or apply inline `Edit`s. The slice is prompt-only, so the main security surface is agent behavior: how untrusted source text is handled, when writes are allowed, and whether the catalogue catches trust-boundary validation gaps.

## Findings
1. High: no prompt-injection boundary for reviewed code or snippets.
   Evidence: `skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md:5-12,48,65,72-79` requires the agent to read user-supplied snippets and repo source, but never says those inputs are untrusted or that embedded instructions/comments must be ignored. The normative shared protocol it loads is also silent on that point (`skills/shared/retro-protocol.md:15-34`).
   Impact: a hostile comment, string literal, or pasted snippet can bias the audit, suppress real findings, or steer the agent toward broader reads or writes.
2. Medium: critique-mode write permission is overly permissive and internally inconsistent.
   Evidence: the slice grants `Edit` in frontmatter (`skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md:23-27`) and repeatedly allows inline fixes when the agent is "confident" (`skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md:32,57,76`), while only later adding "don't apply `Edit` ... for any finding the user hasn't agreed to" (`skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md:100`). The shared protocol still says mechanical rewrites may use `Edit` when confident (`skills/shared/retro-protocol.md:36-38`).
   Impact: during a review-style invocation, an over-eager model or injected snippet can turn analysis into code modification without a clean explicit-consent gate.
3. Medium: boundary-schema detection can miss production validation gaps.
   Evidence: `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md:9-12` flags missing `:spec`, missing `reg-app-schema`, or some missing `validate-at-boundary` cases, but line 20 states both schema mechanisms are dev-elided in production unless `validate-at-boundary` is attached. The canonical fix then softens this to handlers that "must validate in production builds" (`skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md:20,24`), so a boundary handler with `:spec` and `reg-app-schema` but no production interceptor can still pass review.
   Impact: the skill can miss untrusted HTTP / WebSocket / query-string / `postMessage` paths that bypass runtime validation in production.

## Recommended changes
- Add a locked "untrusted evidence" rule to `skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md` and `skills/shared/retro-protocol.md`: treat reviewed code, comments, snippets, traces, and linked docs as data, not instructions; ignore in-band attempts to change tool use, approvals, or scope unless the user explicitly confirms.
- Make critique mode read-only by default. Either remove `Edit` from this skill's normal path, or require an explicit post-findings confirmation before any `Edit`. The shared retro protocol and this skill should say the same thing.
- Tighten `references/schemaless-events.md` so any handler crossing an untrusted boundary is flagged unless production validation is present (`validate-at-boundary` or an equivalent always-on gate), even when `:spec` and `reg-app-schema` already exist.
- Add a regression example for each of the above: injected instructions inside a reviewed snippet are ignored, review mode does not edit without confirmation, and a boundary handler lacking production validation is reported.

## Spec or policy impact
- `/spec`: update `skills/shared/retro-protocol.md` as the canonical retro-protocol home called out by `spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md:34-41`, then mirror the hardening in `skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md`.
- Operator/policy review: decide whether review-mode skills are allowed to apply any `Edit` without an explicit confirmation step.

# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`skills/re-frame2` is an authoring-only skill pack: prompts, canonical snippets, and tooling guidance that steer an AI toward writing re-frame2 application code. The slice does not execute app logic itself; the security surface is indirect but real because its "canonical" examples shape how generated apps handle credentials, untrusted input, tracing, snapshots, stories, and MCP tooling output.

## Findings

1. High: `skills/re-frame2/patterns/websocket.md:34-35,49-51,73-75,107` stores a raw `auth-token` in machine `:data` and passes it back into the socket actor on reconnect. Because machine data lives in framework state, this pattern encourages long-lived credential retention in places that other tooling can inspect or serialize (snapshots, story fixtures, pair tooling, debug traces). The same leaf explicitly warns not to store the JS `WebSocket` object in app state, but it does not apply the same discipline to bearer credentials.
2. Medium: `skills/re-frame2/patterns/forms.md:32-60,76-79` uses the general-purpose form slice for a login flow, keeps `:password` inside `:draft`, posts the whole `draft`, and compares `draft` with `submitted` for `:dirty?`, but never points the reader at the privacy rules in `skills/re-frame2/reference/cross-cutting/privacy-and-elision.md:5,16-26,98-110`. For auth forms, that recipe steers generated code toward retaining secrets in app state longer than necessary and makes accidental persistence, tracing, or fixture capture more likely.
3. Medium: `skills/re-frame2/reference/tooling/story-recorder.md:15-17,35-39,67,79` says the recorder captures raw `:event/dispatched` vectors and turns them into pasteable `:play` snippets, filtering only by op-type, frame, and Story-specific event ids. There is no sensitive-event filter and no warning against recording secret-bearing flows. Recording login, 2FA, token refresh, or similar interactions can therefore write secrets into story source or MCP tool output.

## Recommended changes

- Rewrite the WebSocket canonical recipe so credentials do not live in machine `:data`. Prefer an opaque credential reference, a client-only cofx lookup at actor spawn, or host-side actor state. If a refresh event still carries a secret, show it with `:sensitive?` and `rf/with-redacted`.
- Add an explicit "auth / secret-bearing form" note to `patterns/forms.md`: do not persist password/TOTP drafts, clear secret fields after submit, avoid copying them into `:submitted`, and mark submit handlers with the privacy/redaction pattern from `privacy-and-elision.md`.
- Add recorder/MCP guidance and ideally enforcement: do not serialize `:sensitive?` events into `:play`; either hard-fail or redact before `gen-play-snippet` / `record-as-variant` returns data.
- Align the WebSocket leaf with `skills/re-frame2/reference/fundamentals/schemas.md:5,42-45`: inbound `:ws/received` payloads should be schema-validated at the boundary before `:route-message` dispatches or mutates app state.

## Spec or policy impact

- Operator/policy review: decide whether Story recorder / story-mcp are allowed to capture and return secret-bearing events at all, or must refuse/redact them unconditionally.
- `/spec` review only if the repo keeps the skill's canonical WebSocket/auth-form recipes in lockstep with normative pattern docs outside this slice.

title: audit(security): skills/re-frame-pair2
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`skills/re-frame-pair2` is a live-runtime debugging skill for re-frame2 apps. Its attack surface is intentionally powerful: it can attach to a local shadow-cljs nREPL, eval arbitrary CLJS in the browser runtime, dispatch events, inspect full `app-db` / trace / epoch state, time-travel with `restore-epoch`, synthesize DOM clicks, and expose a streaming subscription surface through the preload runtime plus legacy shell shims.

## Findings

- High: The default privacy guarantee is broader than the implementation. `SKILL.md:175` says sensitive data does not cross the LLM boundary by default, but runtime filtering only suppresses raw trace events with top-level `:sensitive? true` (`preload/re_frame_pair2/runtime.cljs:596-623`, `774-788`). Unfiltered epoch records still stream (`790-801`), `dispatch-and-collect` returns full epochs (`1394-1405`), and `snapshot-state` returns verbatim `:app-db`, `:epochs`, and `:traces` slices (`1434-1492`). The slice's own docs conflict: `references/vocabulary.md:75-81` admits epoch records are not dropped, while `references/wire-size-budget.md:80` and `references/streaming-subscriptions.md:138-140` imply broader/per-call privacy control. Result: operators can reasonably think the default is safe while ordinary epoch/snapshot flows still expose secrets or PII to the LLM.
- Medium: Streaming subscriptions have per-sub queue caps but no global cap, lease, or idle expiry. Every `subscribe!` allocates a fresh entry in the global `subscriptions` atom (`preload/re_frame_pair2/runtime.cljs:548-560`, `803-856`), defaults to 500 events / ~5 MB per subscription (`550-560`, `811-851`), and persists until explicit `unsubscribe!` (`859-866`). `drain-subscription!` clears queued events but does not retire stale subscriptions (`868-892`). A buggy or hostile client can open many subscriptions and force browser-memory exhaustion.
- Medium: `app-db-reset!` emits full pre- and post-reset app-db values through `tap>` (`preload/re_frame_pair2/runtime.cljs:149-182`), and the docs present that as a safety guardrail (`docs/capabilities.md:86`). Any active tap consumer receives the full state, which can duplicate secrets or PII outside pair2's privacy controls.

No other actionable security issues stood out in the reviewed slice. The legacy shell shims are thin wrappers around `bb ops.clj`; I did not find separate credential handling or obvious shell-injection bugs there.

## Recommended changes

- Align the privacy model immediately. Either narrow the docs to "raw trace subscriptions only" or enforce default suppression/redaction for every epoch/app-db-carrying surface (`:epoch` subscriptions, `dispatch-and-collect`, `snapshot-state`, related MCP tools).
- Pick one privacy override model and document it precisely. The current slice mixes session-global `configure-privacy!` semantics with docs that describe per-call `include-sensitive?`.
- Add runtime-side resource controls for subscriptions: cap active subscription count, add idle TTL or lease renewal, and enforce a process-wide byte ceiling before accepting new subscriptions.
- Change `app-db-reset!` to tap metadata or a diff summary by default. Put full before/after payload tapping behind explicit opt-in.

## Spec or policy impact

- `/spec` review if pair2 is supposed to guarantee default privacy for epoch/app-db surfaces, not just raw trace subscriptions.
- Operator/policy review for whether session-global `configure-privacy!` is acceptable and whether full-state `tap>` emission is allowed in the default dev posture.

description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`tools/template` is a build-time `clj-new` template that accepts `:name` and `:substrate`, then emits a runnable re-frame2 starter app. The main trust boundaries are:

- template inputs handled in `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2.clj`
- emitted browser shell in `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/shared/index.html`
- emitted build/deploy defaults in `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/{reagent,uix,helix}/shadow-cljs.edn` and `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/shared/README.md`

## Findings

- Low: the generated app ships with no browser hardening baseline. `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/shared/index.html:1`-`:11` emits a bare host page with no CSP or similar controls, and `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/shared/README.md:62`-`:63` tells users to serve `resources/public/` from any static host without any security-header guidance. Because the scaffold uses only same-origin JS/CSS and no inline script/style, a strict default policy is feasible here. As shipped, apps deployed unchanged have no browser-enforced mitigation layer if a later DOM XSS or asset-injection bug is introduced, and no default anti-clickjacking posture.

- No other actionable issues found in this slice. Spot checks showed `:substrate` is allowlisted in `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2.clj:52`-`:72`, renderer substitutions are escaped, and I did not reproduce a write-outside-target path traversal from `:name`.

## Recommended changes

- Add a baseline CSP for generated apps. Preferred: document server-side headers in the generated README. Acceptable fallback: emit a `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" ...>` in `shared/index.html`.
- Start with a strict default policy compatible with the current scaffold, e.g. `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`.
- Add a short “Production hardening” section to the generated README covering release-only deploys plus `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and `Referrer-Policy`.
- If embedded deployments or third-party asset/CDN origins are intended, make that an explicit template/spec choice instead of leaving each consumer to weaken the policy ad hoc.

## Spec or policy impact

- `/spec`: update `tools/template/spec/002-Generated-Shape.md` to define the generated host-page hardening baseline and deployment guidance.
- Operator/policy review: decide whether the scaffold should default to `frame-ancestors 'none'` and self-only assets, or whether embedding / external origins are first-class and need explicit allowances.

title: audit(security): skills/shared
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface
`skills/shared/retro-protocol.md` is the canonical workflow leaf for retro-style skills. It tells agents how to ingest evidence from session transcripts, code snippets, stack traces, and user recaps; classify findings; cite evidence; optionally edit code; and optionally draft/file beads. Because both consuming skills and the spec inventory treat this file as normative (`skills/re-frame-pair-retro2/SKILL.md:78,125`, `skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md:79,107`, `spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md:32-40`), any weakness here propagates across multiple agent workflows.

## Findings
1. High: no explicit prompt-injection boundary for untrusted evidence.
   Evidence: `skills/shared/retro-protocol.md:15-34` tells the agent to read transcripts, code, snippets, and error traces, then classify and cross-link them, but never says to treat those sources as untrusted data or to ignore embedded instructions. The same leaf also permits `Edit` in some cases (`skills/shared/retro-protocol.md:36-40`).
   Impact: a malicious code comment, pasted trace, or transcript line can steer findings, suppress real issues, or bias the agent toward unauthorized edits/bead drafts.
2. Medium: redaction is required only for bead filing, not for normal findings output.
   Evidence: Step 4 requires concrete evidence citation (`skills/shared/retro-protocol.md:29`), while Step 6 limits redaction to "Before filing" (`skills/shared/retro-protocol.md:39-40`).
   Impact: routine retro/improver output can echo tokens, internal URLs, local paths, or sensitive payload fragments from traces/transcripts even when nothing is filed externally.

## Recommended changes
- Add a normative "untrusted evidence" rule near Step 1 or the Evidence discipline section: treat code, comments, stack traces, transcripts, and referenced docs as data, not instructions; ignore in-band attempts to change tool use, approvals, or routing unless the user explicitly confirms.
- Extend redaction from filing-only to all surfaced evidence. Findings, bead drafts, and quoted snippets should mask secrets, tokens, internal URLs, and unnecessary local paths with stable placeholders.
- Tighten write behavior after hardening: either require explicit user approval for any `Edit` from retro-style skills, or at minimum require confirmation when an edit suggestion is derived from user-supplied/transcript evidence rather than canonical repo idioms.
- Add a small regression check for each consumer showing that injected instructions inside reviewed code/transcripts are ignored and that sensitive strings are redacted in findings.

## Spec or policy impact
- `/spec`: update the canonical retro-protocol leaf because `spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md` treats it as the shared home for this workflow shape.
- Operator/policy review: decide whether critique-mode `Edit` without explicit confirmation remains acceptable once prompt-injection handling is formalized.

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`
- `rg --files skills/shared`
- `Get-ChildItem -Force skills/shared`
- `Get-Content -Raw skills/shared/retro-protocol.md`
- `rg -n "retro-protocol|skills/shared|retro protocol" -S .`
- `rg -n "redact secrets|tokens|internal URLs|local paths|untrusted|prompt injection|treat .* as data|do not follow instructions" skills spec -S`

- `Get-Content skills/re-frame-pair-retro2/SKILL.md | Select-Object -First 180`
- `Get-Content skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md | Select-Object -First 160`
- `Get-Content spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md | Select-Object -First 120`

## Files checked

- `skills/re-frame-pair-retro2/SKILL.md`
- `skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md`
- `spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md`

title: audit(security): tools/story-mcp
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`tools/story-mcp` is a JVM stdio JSON-RPC/MCP server that exposes Story read tools plus a gated write surface (`register-variant`, `unregister-variant`, `record-as-variant` write-back). The attack surface is any local agent/process that can launch the server and send `tools/call` requests; the highest-risk inputs in this slice are `:include-sensitive?`, `:body`, `:timeout-ms`, `:duration-ms`, and raw JSON frame size.

## Findings

- High: sensitive-read redaction is fully caller-bypassable. The public schemas expose `:include-sensitive?`, `include-sensitive?` accepts it from any request, and `elide-app-db` / `scrub-assertions` return raw values unchanged when that flag is true. There is no separate boot-time/operator gate for sensitive reads, so any connected MCP client can opt out of redaction and exfiltrate raw `app-db` data or assertion records. References: `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/schemas.cljc:24-43`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/helpers.cljc:95-102`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/helpers.cljc:182-220`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc:94-100`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:43-46`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:120-127`.
- Medium: `register-variant` parses untrusted EDN with bare `clojure.edn/read-string`. The write path accepts a string body and feeds it directly to `edn/read-string` with no reader allowlist, payload-size bound, or depth bound. Immediate impact is parser/resource exhaustion; if classpath data readers are ever introduced, tagged literals widen the risk surface further. References: `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/write.cljc:41-53`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/write.cljc:71-98`.
- Medium: a single client can trivially monopolize the server process. The main loop is synchronous, `record-as-variant` blocks the request thread with caller-controlled `Thread/sleep`, `run-variant` accepts caller-controlled `:timeout-ms`, and inbound frames are read with unbounded `BufferedReader.readLine`. One client can hold the only worker for a long time or force large allocations before tool logic even runs. References: `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:171-203`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:26-34`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:118-146`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:27-37`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:147-148`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/protocol.cljc:135-148`.

## Recommended changes

- Add a server-side `allow-sensitive-reads?` gate, default `false`, and require both that gate and per-call `:include-sensitive? true` before returning raw values. If the gate is off, omit `:include-sensitive?` from `tools/list` for those tools.
- Harden `register-variant` input parsing. Best option: accept structured object bodies only. If EDN strings must stay, parse with an explicit reader policy (`:readers {}` plus a rejecting `:default`) and enforce a small payload-size/depth limit before parse.
- Add resource bounds at the protocol and tool layers: maximum JSON frame length, capped `:timeout-ms`, capped `:duration-ms`, and cancellation/timeout handling for long-running tool calls so one request cannot block the whole stdio loop indefinitely.

## Spec or policy impact

- `/spec` review needed: decide whether `:include-sensitive?` is meant to be an unrestricted per-call escape hatch or an operator-controlled capability. Current behavior makes redaction advisory, not enforced.
- Operator/policy review needed: define whether raw secret-bearing Story state is allowed to cross into AI-agent MCP sessions by default, especially for shared dev hosts and CI-like environments.
- If EDN-string `:body` support is removed or tightened at the API contract level, update `tools/story-mcp/spec/API.md` and `tools/story-mcp/spec/002-Tool-Registry.md`.

## Commands checked

- `bd prime`
- `Get-ChildItem -Force tools\story-mcp`
- `rg --files tools/story-mcp`
- `rg -n "include-sensitive?|elide-app-db|scrub-assertions|with-include-sensitive" tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp`
- `rg -n "edn/read-string|duration-ms|timeout-ms|Thread/sleep|deref-blocking" tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp`
- `rg -n "readLine|parse-json|ex-data" tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp`
- `clojure -M:test`
- `node test\stdio-roundtrip.js`

## Files checked

- `tools/story-mcp/README.md`
- `tools/story-mcp/deps.edn`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/protocol.cljc`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/config.cljc`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cap.cljc`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/helpers.cljc`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc`

Symmetric with --allow-eval (rf2-zyoj2). MCP client cannot bypass without explicit operator opt-in. Follow-on impl bead will cover all 3 findings: HIGH gate + MEDIUM EDN reader policy + MEDIUM DoS bounds.

title: audit(security): tools/story
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`tools/story` is a dev-only component/story playground. Its attack surface is mostly browser-side:

- URL generation and sharing for live variant state, including `:active-modes` and `:cell-overrides`.
- Runtime DOM/script injection for optional tooling (`share` QR rendering, `a11y` scanning).
- Local browser persistence (`localStorage`) for UI state.
- Clipboard writes and editor handoff links.
- Trace/recorder/test helpers that intentionally handle app event data.

## Findings

- High: QR sharing sends full variant state to a third-party service. `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/share.cljc:5-8`, `:14-18`, `:24-28`, `:65-96`, `:122-140` encode `:cell-overrides` directly into the share URL, and `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/share.cljs:124-130` loads a QR image from `https://api.qrserver.com/...&data=<share-url>`. Any override value the user typed into controls is sent off-box to that service and will also land in its logs, intermediary logs, and browser network history. This bypasses Story’s sensitive-trace protections entirely.
- Medium: The a11y panel executes third-party JavaScript from a public CDN without a local trust boundary. `tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/a11y.cljs:26-29` documents CDN loading, and `:80-113` injects `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/axe-core@4.10.0/axe.min.js` as a `<script>` at runtime. That gives remotely hosted code full DOM access to the Story page, creates a supply-chain dependency for a security-sensitive devtool, and will fail under strict CSP/offline environments.

No other actionable security issues stood out in the reviewed storage, clipboard, recorder, or open-in-editor paths.

## Recommended changes

- Replace remote QR generation with a local QR encoder or a self-hosted asset. If remote QR must stay, gate it behind explicit opt-in, show a warning that the full share URL leaves the machine, and consider suppressing QR when overrides are present.
- Treat share URLs with overrides as potentially sensitive data. At minimum, document that overrides are serialized verbatim; preferably add a redaction/allowlist layer for fields that should never be shared.
- Bundle or vendor `axe-core` with the tool, or load it from a project-controlled origin. If a remote fallback remains, require an explicit config flag and add `integrity`/`crossorigin` plus CSP documentation.

## Spec or policy impact

- `/spec`: `tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md` currently presents QR share and the a11y panel as default Stage 6 features without documenting third-party network egress. The spec should either require local/self-hosted implementations or explicitly describe the privacy/CSP tradeoff.
- Operator/policy review: decide whether Story is allowed to contact third-party services from developer sessions (`api.qrserver.com`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`). If yes, publish an allowlist/CSP requirement; if no, these paths should be removed or redirected to first-party assets.

title: audit(security): tools/pair2-mcp
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`tools/pair2-mcp` is a local MCP server that exposes a live re-frame runtime over stdio, backed by a persistent localhost nREPL socket. Its attack surface is concentrated in:

- arbitrary CLJS execution via `eval-cljs`
- event-triggered state mutation via `dispatch`
- direct reads of `app-db`, `sub-cache`, `machines`, traces, and epochs via `snapshot` / `get-path`
- long-lived streaming subscriptions via `subscribe`

This is a high-trust tool by design, but the slice still needs to keep its structured tools narrower than raw eval and to enforce the documented privacy posture on direct-read surfaces.

## Findings

- High: `dispatch` is a hidden arbitrary-eval path, not a constrained event-dispatch surface. `dispatch-tool` takes user-controlled `event` text and injects it with `rt-raw` directly into the generated form, so a caller can supply arbitrary CLJS instead of an EDN event vector. That defeats the documented boundary between `dispatch` and `eval-cljs`, and any future policy that disables or audits `eval-cljs` would still be bypassable through `dispatch`. Evidence: [tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/dispatch.cljs](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/dispatch.cljs) lines 26-33, [tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs) lines 46-59.

- High: direct-read privacy is incomplete and currently drifts from the canonical Tool-Pair contract. `snapshot` only runs `re-frame.core/elide-wire-value` over `:app-db`; `:sub-cache` is never elided/redacted, and the helper used for direct reads only threads `:rf.size/include-large?`, not `:rf.size/include-sensitive?`. The slice’s own descriptor text also says `app-db / sub-cache / machines` pass through unchanged. That conflicts with the Tool-Pair requirement that direct-read `sub-cache` and `get-path` surfaces use the wire walker with off-box defaults and honor `include-sensitive?`. Evidence: [tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/snapshot.cljs](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/snapshot.cljs) lines 37-64, [tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/elision.cljs](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/elision.cljs) lines 38-47, [tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/descriptors_data.cljs) lines 159-173, [spec/Tool-Pair.md](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/spec/Tool-Pair.md) lines 561-575.

## Recommended changes

- Parse `dispatch.event` as EDN and require a vector shape before building the runtime call. Do not splice caller text with `rt-raw`; reject unreadable or non-vector input with a structured error.

- Apply `re-frame.core/elide-wire-value` to `snapshot`’s `:sub-cache` values before egress, not just `:app-db`.

- Thread `include-sensitive?` into the direct-read elision path for `snapshot` and `get-path` so the default is suppress and the documented opt-in actually works for direct reads.

- Update `pair2-mcp` docs/tests to match the intended privacy contract. Today the descriptors and tests reinforce the weaker behavior.

## Spec or policy impact

- `/spec`: reconcile `tools/pair2-mcp` with `spec/Tool-Pair.md` direct-read privacy requirements for `sub-cache`, `get-path`, and `include-sensitive?`.

- Operator/policy review: decide whether `dispatch` is intentionally allowed to be equivalent to arbitrary code execution. If yes, document it explicitly as such; if no, narrow it to EDN event vectors only.

title: audit(security): tools/mcp-conformance
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`tools/mcp-conformance` is a test-only MCP conformance harness. It spawns local MCP servers over stdio, launches `clojure`, `node`, `npx shadow-cljs`, Playwright/Chromium, opens loopback HTTP and nREPL connections, and in the hermetic path may auto-run `npm install` inside `skills/re-frame-pair2/tests/fixture/`.

The main trust boundaries are:

- Executable resolution for spawned commands on developer/CI hosts.
- Filesystem writes during hermetic cleanup (`nrepl.port` deletion).
- Loading repo-controlled fixture code and dependencies during the hermetic run.

## Findings

- Medium: Windows command-hijack risk from bare executable names in repo-controlled working directories.
  `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-live-pair2-overflow-hermetic.cjs:311-318` and `:386-392` invoke `npm.cmd` / `npx.cmd` with `shell: true` and `cwd` set to the fixture directory. `tools/mcp-conformance/test/end-to-end-story.js:34,69-73` invokes bare `clojure` with `cwd` set inside the repo. On Windows, this allows repo-local executables or batch files with those names to be preferred over the intended toolchain, which turns a crafted checkout into host-side code execution when the harness runs.

- Low: Stale-port cleanup is not symlink-safe.
  `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-live-pair2-overflow-hermetic.cjs:367-370` unlinks candidate port files without verifying that the resolved path stays under `FIXTURE_DIR`. If a candidate parent directory is symlinked, the cleanup step can delete a file outside the fixture tree before the harness does any other validation.

- No current dependency advisories were reported for this package by `npm audit --omit=dev --package-lock-only` at audit time.

## Recommended changes

- Resolve trusted absolute paths for `npm`, `npx`, and `clojure`, then run them with `shell: false`. On Windows, explicitly reject executables that resolve inside the workspace.
- For the hermetic runner, consider failing closed when fixture dependencies are missing instead of auto-running `npm install`, or move that install step into CI setup where policy is explicit.
- Before deleting stale port files, use `lstat`/`realpath` and reject any candidate whose resolved parent escapes `FIXTURE_DIR` or traverses a symlinked directory.

## Spec or policy impact

- Operator/policy review: decide whether a test invocation is allowed to perform nested networked dependency installation automatically (`npm install` inside the fixture) or whether that must be prepared out-of-band by CI/bootstrap steps.

## Commands checked

- `bd prime`
- `rg --files tools/mcp-conformance`
- `rg -n "spawn|spawnSync|exec|eval|http|get\\(|net\\.connect|process\\.env|shell:|unlinkSync|writeFile|resolvePlaywright|require\\.resolve|page\\.goto|waitForFunction|new Context|StdioClientTransport|allow-writes|127\\.0\\.0\\.1|localhost|SHADOW_CLJS_NREPL_PORT|STORY_MCP_CMD" tools/mcp-conformance`

title: audit(security): tools/mcp-base
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface
`tools/mcp-base` is the shared CLJC boundary library for the MCP triplet. It normalizes agent-supplied args, strips sensitive trace data, counts size-elision markers, diff-encodes epoch payloads, and applies the cross-server overflow cap before data crosses into the agent surface. The main attack surface is untrusted MCP call input plus large or malformed outbound payloads that rely on this slice for redaction and budgeting.

## Findings
1. High: `parse-keyword` interns arbitrary agent strings into JVM keywords, which enables unbounded memory growth on long-lived Clojure servers. `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/args.cljc:84` calls `keyword` on raw input, and `parse-mode` repeats the pattern for rejected mode strings at `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/args.cljc:125`. Story-MCP feeds user-controlled `:variant-id`, `:substrate`, `:active-modes`, and similar ids through this helper (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/helpers.cljc:125`, `:149`, `:167`). Repeated unique values can permanently grow the keyword table and eventually DoS the JVM.
2. Medium: the shared cap is not a hard response bound. `token-estimate` uses `(quot (count s) 4)` (`tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/overflow.cljc:30`), which can materially undercount CJK, emoji, code, base64, and other high-token-density text. Separately, `sum-text-tokens` only budgets `:content` text slots (`tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cap.cljc`), not sibling payload slots. Story-MCP also duplicates payloads into `:structuredContent` (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/helpers.cljc:68`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cap.cljc:56`), so a response can exceed the intended 5k budget while still passing the base check.
3. Low: the default-sensitive filter is fail-open on malformed truthy stamps. `sensitive-event?` only drops the literal boolean `true` (`tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/sensitive.cljc:34`), and the test suite explicitly pins `"true"` and `:yes` as pass-through (`tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/sensitive_test.clj:23`). If any upstream serialization or instrumentation bug changes `:sensitive?` away from boolean `true`, sensitive events will cross the MCP boundary instead of being suppressed.

No other actionable security issues were identified in this slice.

## Recommended changes
- Stop interning raw MCP strings. For finite option sets like `mode`, normalize strings and compare against an allowlist before creating keywords. For registry-backed ids, keep strings until lookup or convert only from a bounded known set.
- Tighten response budgeting so it measures the full serialized result, not only `:content` text. At minimum, include `:structuredContent` in the budget and add a conservative secondary byte cap. Add tests with CJK/emoji/base64-heavy payloads.
- Fail closed on malformed `:sensitive?` values at the egress boundary, or drop-plus-log any non-boolean truthy-ish stamp so contract drift cannot silently leak data.

## Spec or policy impact
- `/spec` review is likely needed for any cap change that alters the documented `token-estimate = (quot (count s) 4)` rule or broadens what counts toward the 5k budget.
- Operator/privacy review is likely needed if the project changes the current posture that malformed non-boolean `:sensitive?` values pass through instead of being suppressed.
- Keyword-interning hardening can likely be done as an implementation-only change if external arg semantics stay the same.

## Commands checked
- `rg --files tools/mcp-base`
- `Get-Content tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/*.cljc`
- `Get-Content tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/*_test.clj`
- `Get-Content tools/mcp-base/deps.edn`
- `Get-Content tools/mcp-base/spec/README.md`
- `rg -n "parse-keyword|parse-mode|sensitive-event?|strip-sensitive|apply-cap|token-estimate|structuredContent" ...`
- `clojure -M:test` in `tools/mcp-base` (`89` tests, `0` failures)

## Files checked
- `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/{args,cap,diff_encode,elision,overflow,sensitive,vocab}.cljc`
- `tools/mcp-base/test/re_frame/mcp_base/{args,cap,diff_encode,elision,overflow,sensitive,vocab}_test.clj`
- `tools/mcp-base/deps.edn`
- `tools/mcp-base/spec/README.md`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/helpers.cljc`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cap.cljc`
- `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/cap.cljs`
