title: audit(security): tools/machines-viz-mcp
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

This slice is currently spec-only: [`tools/machines-viz-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md`](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/machines-viz-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md). It defines a planned Node/CLJS MCP server that bridges an AI host to the running app over stdio JSON-RPC plus nREPL. The planned attack surface is:

- machine enumeration and transition-table reads
- direct reads of `[:rf/machines <id>]` snapshots
- share-URL generation for a machine plus snapshot
- SVG/PNG export for a machine plus snapshot
- future streaming of `:rf.machine/*` trace events

Because this is an off-box MCP surface, the main security concern is data egress to the agent host / LLM boundary, not in-process mutation.

## Findings

1. **Missing normative privacy and elision rules for the MCP boundary.**  
   [`tools/machines-viz-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:156-172`](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/machines-viz-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:156) defines fetch, export, share, and streaming tools, but the slice does not pin the privacy and size-budget rules that sibling MCP specs already treat as MUST-level. In particular, this slice does not currently require default suppression of `:sensitive?` trace events, `elide-wire-value` on tree-shaped reads, or the cross-MCP control/indicator slots `:include-sensitive?`, `:include-large?`, `:dropped-sensitive`, and `:elided-large`. That leaves room for a conforming implementation to ship raw machine snapshots or raw `:rf.machine/*` events over MCP.

2. **Share/export path inherits a policy contradiction that can expose arbitrary snapshot data.**  
   This slice explicitly plans to wrap the canonical share-url encoder unchanged ([`tools/machines-viz-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:159-163`](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/machines-viz-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md:159)). Upstream, the share payload schema still allows `[:snapshot [:data :any]]` ([`tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:254-258`](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:254)), while the upstream policy says shares must exclude user-input/session data ([`tools/machines-viz/spec/Principles.md:105-125`](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/machines-viz/spec/Principles.md:105)). As written, the MCP wrapper would turn that ambiguity into a one-call off-box exfil path for whatever a machine stores in `:data` unless the policy is tightened first.

No executable code exists in this slice yet, so I did not find implementation-level bugs beyond these pre-implementation spec gaps.

## Recommended changes

- Add a `machines-viz-mcp` wire/privacy spec before implementation, mirroring the cross-MCP contract already used by `pair2-mcp` and `causa-mcp`: default-drop `:sensitive?` events, run `re-frame.core/elide-wire-value` on tree-shaped reads, define `:include-sensitive?` / `:include-large?`, and require `:dropped-sensitive` / `:elided-large` in tool results and streaming ticks.
- Treat `fetch snapshot`, `export`, and `share-url` as tree-shaped egress surfaces, not as harmless helpers. They should inherit the same redaction/elision defaults as other direct-read MCP tools.
- Resolve the share-payload policy contradiction before the MCP tool lands. The cleanest options are: omit `:snapshot :data` from shares entirely, allow only a redacted/summary form, or make inclusion an explicit opt-in with a clear sensitive-data warning and matching tests.
- Add conformance tests once implementation exists: sensitive-event suppression, large-value elision, and a regression test proving the share/export tool cannot leak disallowed snapshot fields by default.

## Spec or policy impact

- `/spec`: add a privacy/wire-pipeline contract for `tools/machines-viz-mcp/` equivalent to the existing MCP servers' security posture.
- `/spec` or operator/policy review: reconcile `tools/machines-viz` share semantics for snapshot `:data` versus the stated “no user-input/session data in shares” rule before exposing that encoder over MCP.

## Commands checked

- `rg --files tools/machines-viz-mcp`
- `Get-Content -Raw tools\machines-viz-mcp\spec\000-Vision.md`

title: audit(security): tools/machines-viz
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

This slice is currently spec-only; there is no implementation code under `tools/machines-viz` yet. The security-relevant surfaces defined here are the share-URL encoder/decoder, the read-only viewer that parses `location.hash`, clipboard export helpers, and the decision to include machine snapshots and source-coordinate metadata in shared artifacts.

## Findings

1. High: the share schema allows arbitrary machine snapshot data to leave the app, even though the surrounding prose says shares contain no user data or runtime data.
   Evidence: `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:254-258` allows `[:snapshot ... [:data :any]]`; `tools/machines-viz/spec/Principles.md:105-128` forbids user-input data in shares; `tools/machines-viz/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:300-305` says the share URL "does not leak run-time data"; `tools/causa/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md:230-234` says shares contain "no ... user data".
   Impact: a normal "Copy machine as -> Share URL" flow can exfiltrate tokens, form contents, request payloads, or other sensitive machine `:data` through URLs, clipboard history, chat logs, PRs, and docs.

2. Medium: the share payload includes source-coordinate metadata that can expose local filesystem paths and internal repo layout, and the viewer does not need it.
   Evidence: `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:259-260` includes `:source-coords`; `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:355-360` allows `:file` and explicitly says it may be absolute; `spec/005-StateMachines.md:681-699` shows the machine coord index carrying per-element `:file` / `:line` / `:column`; `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:156-176` defines the viewer as read-only with callbacks disabled.
   Impact: shared URLs can leak usernames, workstation paths, monorepo structure, and internal file names to external recipients with no clear viewer-side benefit.

3. Medium: the nested allowlist for `:source-coords` is effectively unconstrained, so the "only allowed fields survive" rule can be bypassed inside an already-allowed key.
   Evidence: `tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md:259-273` says unknown top-level fields are dropped, but `:source-coords` is typed as `[:map-of :any :any]`.
   Impact: crafted share URLs can carry arbitrary nested data under `:source-coords`, weakening privacy review and making future enforcement easy to misread as stronger than it is.

## Recommended changes

- Narrow the share snapshot contract to `:state` only by default, or to an explicit redacted/allowlisted subset. Do not allow raw `:data :any` in v1 share URLs.
- If snapshot data must be shareable, require an explicit opt-in flag plus a redaction hook aligned with the project's existing sensitive-data posture.
- Remove `:source-coords` from share URLs entirely for the read-only viewer, or strip `:file` and other host-local details before encoding. Treat full source coords as an operator-controlled opt-in, not a default.
- Replace `[:source-coords [:map-of :any :any]]` with a concrete schema for the actual coord index shape, and reject unknown nested keys.
- Add spec-level limits for the future viewer implementation: maximum fragment bytes, maximum decoded topology size, and fail-closed behavior before parsing/rendering oversized payloads.

## Spec or policy impact

- `/spec`: required. The share payload schema and the prose in `tools/machines-viz` and `tools/causa` currently disagree on what data may leave the app.
- Operator/policy review: required if the project wants any share surface to include runtime snapshot data or local source-path data by default.

## Commands checked

- `rg --files tools/machines-viz`
- `Get-ChildItem -Force tools/machines-viz`
- `Get-Content` on `tools/machines-viz/README.md` and `tools/machines-viz/spec/*.md`
- Targeted `rg -n` searches across the slice and cited upstream specs for `share-URL`, `snapshot`, `source-coords`, `:data :any`, privacy claims, and source-coordinate shape

- `tools/machines-viz/README.md`

- `tools/machines-viz/spec/Principles.md`

- `tools/causa/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md`
- `spec/001-Registration.md`

title: audit(security): tools/causa-mcp
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`tools/causa-mcp` is a spec-only slice for an agent-facing MCP server that will expose Causa/re-frame2 runtime state over stdio JSON-RPC via a persistent nREPL bridge into the browser runtime. The planned surface is high authority: read access to traces, app-db, machine state, epoch history, and subscription state; write access via `dispatch`, `restore-epoch`, `reset-frame-db`; and arbitrary runtime execution via `eval-cljs`.

The main attack surface is local agent/tool access crossing the MCP boundary into runtime data and control. The two security-critical classes are:

- Sensitive data egress from traces, app-db, epoch snapshots, and other tree-typed reads.
- State mutation or arbitrary code execution initiated by an attached agent or by prompt-injected tool use.

## Findings

1. High: mutation and arbitrary eval are effectively pre-authorized for any connected agent, which conflicts with Causa's own "mutate by confirmation" posture. `tools/causa/spec/Principles.md:12-16` says pokes, dispatches, and rewinds require a user-confirmed action, but `tools/causa-mcp/spec/Principles.md:243-252` reduces that to "enabling the MCP server delegates in-panel rights" and `tools/causa/spec/010-MCP-Server.md:164-168,208-220` explicitly ships unrestricted `dispatch` and arbitrary `eval-cljs`. That gives a prompt-injected or mistaken agent immediate write/exec authority; `:origin` tagging helps audit after the fact but does not prevent misuse.

2. Medium: the direct-read privacy contract is internally inconsistent, which creates a real chance of shipping raw sensitive state over MCP. `tools/causa-mcp/spec/004-Wire-Pipeline.md:53-57` says state reads like `get-app-db`, `get-app-db-diff`, and `get-machine-state` rely on `with-redacted`, but `spec/Tool-Pair.md:563-575` says direct reads must go through `rf/elide-wire-value` with sensitive-data opt-ins off by default because `with-redacted` only shapes traces. The same local file later says tree-typed tools do run through the walker (`tools/causa-mcp/spec/004-Wire-Pipeline.md:292-321`). That ambiguity is enough to produce a vulnerable implementation or incomplete tests around raw app-db/epoch/db-diff egress.

## Recommended changes

- Make the server read-only by default. Require explicit, separate capabilities for `dispatch`/`restore-epoch`/`reset-frame-db` and for `eval-cljs`, with the latter treated as a stronger authority class than panel-equivalent mutations.
- Define an operator-visible approval model for write/eval tools instead of treating server enablement as blanket consent. A launch flag or host-mediated approval gate is the minimum; per-call approval for high-risk tools is better.
- Reconcile `tools/causa-mcp/spec/004-Wire-Pipeline.md` with `spec/Tool-Pair.md` so every direct-read/tree-typed tool is explicitly required to pass through `rf/elide-wire-value` with `include-sensitive? false` and `include-large? false` by default.
- Add MUST-inventory coverage for direct-read privacy on `get-app-db`, `get-app-db-diff`, `get-machine-state`, and epoch payloads so the future implementation cannot accidentally inherit the weaker reading.

## Spec or policy impact

- `/spec`: define the authority model for mutation tools versus `eval-cljs` in `tools/causa-mcp/spec/Principles.md` and the future `003-Tool-Catalogue.md`.
- `/spec`: reconcile the direct-read privacy wording in `tools/causa-mcp/spec/004-Wire-Pipeline.md` with `spec/Tool-Pair.md`'s direct-read elision contract.
- Operator/policy review: decide whether raw sensitive-data opt-ins and arbitrary `eval-cljs` should be available at all by default, or only behind separate launch-time/host approval gates.

## Commands checked

- `bd prime`
- `Get-ChildItem -Force tools\causa-mcp`
- `rg --files tools/causa-mcp`
- `Get-Content -Raw` on the slice spec files
- `rg -n "Tool catalogue|eval-cljs|include-sensitive|confirm|confirmation|mutate|sensitive|origin|subscribe|dispatch|restore-epoch|reset-frame-db"` across the slice and upstream contracts
- `Get-Content ... | Select-Object ...` for line-numbered citation checks

## Files checked

- `tools/causa-mcp/README.md`
- `tools/causa-mcp/spec/README.md`
- `tools/causa-mcp/spec/000-Vision.md`
- `tools/causa-mcp/spec/004-Wire-Pipeline.md`
- `tools/causa-mcp/spec/Principles.md`
- `tools/causa-mcp/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md`
- `tools/causa-mcp/spec/findings/MUST-inventory.md`
- `tools/causa/spec/010-MCP-Server.md` (context)
- `tools/causa/spec/Principles.md` (context)
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` (context)
- `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` (context)

Both HIGH findings cross-reference open decision bead rf2-czv3p (P1) which already names them in its action items. Highest-impact finding: H1 — 004-Wire-Pipeline.md L53-57 says direct-read tools rely on with-redacted, contradicting spec/Tool-Pair.md L569-571 which requires the elide-wire-value walker — wording commits future impl to ship raw sensitive values over the MCP wire.

title: audit(security): tools/causa
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`tools/causa` is a dev-only in-browser diagnostics shell for re-frame2. In the reviewed slice it registers global `:rf.causa/*` events/subs/fx, collects trace data, exposes time-travel/debugger UI, provides clipboard export, and includes a read-only AI co-pilot rail plus an "open in editor" helper.

Primary attack surface in this slice:

- Browser-local privileged actions: `window.location` handoff, clipboard writes, global keybinding.
- Globally registered re-frame events/effects callable by any code running in the page.
- Planned direct-to-provider browser LLM integration in the co-pilot rail.

## Findings

- High: `:rf.causa/copilot-chip-clicked` is an arbitrary dispatch gadget, which breaks the co-pilot's read-only contract. In [tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/ai_co_pilot.cljs](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/ai_co_pilot.cljs:586) the handler trusts caller-supplied `:target` and emits `[:dispatch [target value]]` with no allowlist or namespace check. The intended safe targets are defined in [tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/ai_co_pilot_helpers.cljc](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/ai_co_pilot_helpers.cljc:173), but the handler does not enforce them. That means any page code able to dispatch `:rf.causa/copilot-chip-clicked` can trigger arbitrary re-frame events, including host-app events, which contradicts the read-only model in [tools/causa/spec/009-AI-CoPilot.md](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/causa/spec/009-AI-CoPilot.md:171).

- Medium: the open-in-editor path accepts unsanitized custom URIs and raw file strings. The shared builder in [implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords/editor_uri.cljc](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords/editor_uri.cljc:159) substitutes `{:custom ...}` templates verbatim and explicitly does no URL encoding for paths or query values; the Causa helper in [tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/open_in_editor.cljs](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/open_in_editor.cljs:38) then assigns the result to `window.location`. This is not fully wired into the main shell yet because panels currently dispatch the stub `:rf.causa/open-in-editor` event, but once the helper is used by live panels or host code it will permit arbitrary scheme launch/navigation and query injection via raw `:file` content.

- No other actionable security issues were identified in the reviewed slice files.

## Recommended changes

- For co-pilot chip clicks, ignore caller-supplied `:target`. Accept only `:chip-key` plus `:value`, resolve the target server-side from the fixed `chip-targets` map, and reject anything outside an explicit allowlist. Also bind the follow-on dispatch to `:rf/causa` so it cannot escape into the host frame.

- For open-in-editor, treat `:custom` as an operator-only allowlisted feature. Reject `javascript:`, `data:`, `http:`, and `https:` schemes, validate the final URI scheme against a safe set, and encode query components for handlers like `idea://open?...`. If arbitrary templates are not required, remove `{:custom ...}` from the supported contract.

- Add regression tests that prove `:rf.causa/copilot-chip-clicked` cannot dispatch arbitrary targets and that open-in-editor rejects unsafe/custom schemes.

## Spec or policy impact

- No `/spec` change is required for the co-pilot dispatch issue; the implementation should be tightened to match the existing read-only spec.
- Operator/policy review is needed for `{:custom ...}` editor templates: either remove them from the supported surface or define an explicit safe-scheme policy.

## Commands checked

- `rg --files tools/causa`
- `rg -n "<security-relevant patterns>" tools/causa/src tools/causa/test tools/causa/spec`

- `rg -n "editor-uri|open-button-title|has-source?|uri-template" implementation/core/src implementation/core/test`

title: audit(security): implementation/ssr-ring
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`implementation/ssr-ring` is the Ring host adapter for SSR. It creates a per-request frame, exposes the Ring request via `:rf.server/request`, renders HTML, serializes the hydration payload, and materializes SSR response state into Ring `:status`, `:headers`, `:body`, `Set-Cookie`, and redirect output.

Primary trust boundaries in this slice:

- Request-derived data can flow into server event handlers through `:rf.server/request`.
- Server state can flow back to the client through the hydration payload.
- HTML shell options can inject content into `<head>`, `<body>`, and script tags.
- SSR response headers/cookies/redirects are turned into wire-visible HTTP output.

## Findings

1. Medium: hydration defaults to shipping the entire `app-db`, which makes accidental server-side data exposure the default behavior.

Files:
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:198`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:113`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/payload.clj:60`

Details:
- `ssr-handler` documents `:payload-keys` as optional and explicitly says the default is to ship the whole `app-db`.
- `build-full-response` always passes the frame `app-db` into `build-payload`.
- `build-payload` falls back to `app-db` unchanged when `:payload-keys` is absent.
- The response accumulator leak was already fixed by moving it out of `app-db`, but ordinary application secrets, tokens, per-request auth/session material, internal flags, or server-only derived data can still be exposed if app code stores them in `app-db` during SSR.

2. Medium: `default-html-shell` interpolates `:app-element-id` and `:script-src` into HTML attributes without escaping or validation.

Files:
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj:73`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj:92`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj:106`

Details:
- Most HTML emission in this stack goes through shared escaping helpers, but these two options are concatenated directly into `id="..."` and `src="..."`.
- If a deployment sources either value from operator/admin/tenant configuration instead of a code constant, quote injection can break attribute context and produce script or DOM injection.
- `:body-end` is documented as raw HTML, but these two fields are not documented as raw escape hatches and look safer than they are.

No other actionable issues were found in this slice during this pass. Existing protections cover payload `</script>` escaping, cookie attribute CR/LF/NUL rejection, generic 500 body sanitization, request-slot teardown, and the upstream SSR header/redirect value validation path.

## Recommended changes

- Change hydration payload policy to explicit allowlisting by default. Options:
- Require `:payload-keys` for production handlers.
- Add a deny-by-default mode and make callers opt into full-db shipping explicitly.
- At minimum, emit a loud server-side warning whenever SSR ships the full `app-db`.
- Escape `:app-element-id` and `:script-src` through the existing HTML attribute serializer instead of concatenating raw strings.
- Add regression tests that prove quotes in `:app-element-id` / `:script-src` cannot break attribute context.
- Document raw trust surfaces clearly. At minimum, treat `:html-shell`, explicit `:head`, and `:body-end` as config-only inputs and do not source them from user-controlled content.

## Spec or policy impact

- `/spec` review required if the default hydration behavior changes from "ship whole `app-db`" to explicit allowlisting or deny-by-default, because the current public contract documents whole-db shipping as the default.
- Operator/policy review recommended for any deployment that currently sources shell options from mutable admin or tenant configuration, especially `:script-src`, `:app-element-id`, `:head`, or `:body-end`.

## Commands checked

- `bd prime`
- `rg --files implementation/ssr-ring`
- `rg -n "redirect|Location|set-header|append-header|body-end|script-src|read-string|eval|sh |Process|exec|shell|request slot|clear-request|trace|escape-script-body-string|attr-string" implementation/ssr-ring`
- `rg -n "TODO|FIXME|XXX|HACK|unsafe|security|xss|csrf|csp|nonce|origin|host|proto|scheme|forwarded|remote-addr|edn/read-string|payload-script-id" implementation/ssr-ring`
- `clojure -M:test` in `implementation/ssr-ring` -> 29 tests, 146 assertions, 0 failures

## Files checked

- `implementation/ssr-ring/deps.edn`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/payload.clj`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/headers.clj`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/cookie.clj`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj`
- `implementation/ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj`
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc`
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc`
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/emit.cljc`
close_reason: Audit rollup confirms both findings (full-app-db default; unescaped :app-element-id/:script-src) are tracked under rf2-briq0 (P1 OPEN spec-review) as policy/trust-model decisions. Under Mike's pragmatic stance (Security.md: trust the explicit invoker; shell options are caller-controlled config), no new follow-on beads needed. Recent landings strengthen the slice: PR #1118 (Security.md split), PR #1093 (SSR validators), PR #1121 (streaming), rf2-7ksyr (payload < escape), rf2-2n5gg (CSP allowlist). Findings doc: ai/findings/ssr-ring-security-audit-2026-05-15.md. Tests: 40/191 (was 29/146).

title: audit(security): implementation/schemas
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface
- Owns schema registration, schema digesting, and validation helpers for `app-db`, event payloads, coeffects, effect args, and subscription returns.
- Emits `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` traces, including `:sensitive?`-based redaction decisions.
- Exposes the schemas-side seam used by production `validate-at-boundary`, so fail-open behavior here affects trust-boundary handlers too.
- Main attacker-controlled inputs are event payloads, subscription query vectors, cofx/fx args, and any app boot/config path that disables validator hookup.

## Findings
- High: validation fails open when the Malli adapter or any custom validator is not loaded. `default-malli-validate` returns `true` if `:schemas/malli-validate` is absent, and `run-validator` also returns `true` when the validator atom is `nil` (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:55-66`, `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validator.cljc:253-261`; boundary seam at `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:492-502`). Impact: schemas can be present while both dev-time checks and production boundary validation silently accept untrusted input.
- Medium: sensitive subscription validation traces leak raw `:query-v`. The generic redactor only scrubs `:value`, `:received`, and `:explain`, but `validate-sub-return!` includes unredacted `:query-v` in failure tags (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:91-101`, `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc:377-397`). Impact: caller-supplied tokens, emails, IDs, or similar secrets can still be emitted when the subscription is marked `:sensitive?`.
- Medium: opaque/non-EDN schema forms disable schema-driven `:sensitive?` and `:large?` extraction. The walker intentionally skips any non-vector schema form, and tests pin that behavior (`implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc:25-35`, `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc:184-186`, `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_walker_operators_test.clj:113-124`). Impact: compiled Malli schemas, registry refs, or other opaque schema values may still validate, but their nested sensitivity annotations are invisible to the redaction/elision layer, so failure traces can leak values the schema author expected to be protected.
- No additional actionable issues were found in `storage.cljc`, `digest.cljc`, or the declaration-feeder code.

## Recommended changes
- Add a strict mode or at least a one-time warning when schemas are registered but no live validator hook is available. Boundary-marked handlers are the highest-priority place to fail closed or warn loudly.
- Redact `:query-v` on sensitive sub-return failures and add regression coverage beside `implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_sensitive_test.clj`.
- Either reject opaque schema forms for built-in sensitivity/elision features, or emit a one-time registration warning that `:sensitive?` and `:large?` extraction will not work for that schema value.

## Spec or policy impact
- `/spec` or operator review: decide whether the current soft-pass/no-validator contract is acceptable for production boundary validation, or whether boundary-validated handlers must warn or fail when validator hookup is missing.
- `/spec`: classify `:query-v` as payload-bearing for sensitive sub validation traces and require redaction.
- `/spec`: decide whether non-EDN/opaque schema forms are supported for the built-in `:sensitive?` and `:large?` features. If not, registration-time rejection or warning should be part of the contract.

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`
- `git status --short`
- `rg --files implementation/schemas`
- `rg -n "read-string|slurp|spit|eval|resolve|requiring-resolve|Class/forName|System/getenv|System/getProperty|java\\.io|clojure\\.java\\.io|MD5|SHA-|MessageDigest|println|prn|print|js/|localStorage|sessionStorage|swap!|reset!|atom|postMessage|fetch|ajax|http|File|digest|sensitive|elide|mask|redact" implementation/schemas/src implementation/schemas/test`
- `rg -n ":query-v|query-v" implementation/schemas`
- `Get-Content` review of the source and test files listed below
- Read-only cross-check of `implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc` to confirm boundary-seam ownership

title: audit(security): implementation/http
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface
- `implementation/http` provides the managed outbound HTTP surface for both CLJS (`fetch`) and JVM (`java.net.http.HttpClient`): request helpers, retries, aborts, decoding, middleware/interceptors, trace emission, privacy redaction, and a machine wrapper.
- The main attack surface is any user-influenced request data (`:url`, `:params`, `:headers`, `:body`, `:abort-signal`), middleware that mutates requests, JVM/SSR use of outbound HTTP, and every trace event emitted around request setup and failure handling.

## Findings
- High: privacy redaction is bypassed on multiple warning/error trace paths, so secret-bearing URLs can leak into traces. `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_middleware.cljc:136-145` emits `:rf.error/http-interceptor-failed` with raw `:url`; `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:156-159` emits `:rf.warning/http-header-invalid` with raw `:url`; `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:220-232` emits `:rf.http/cljs-only-key-ignored-on-jvm` with raw `:url`. None of these paths call the privacy composers in `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_privacy.cljc:216-268`, so denylisted query params are not redacted and denylist-only requests are not stamped `:sensitive?`.
- Medium: the CLJS timeout safety default is silently disabled whenever a caller supplies `:abort-signal`. `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_handlers.cljc:40-53` defaults absent `:timeout-ms` to `30000`, but `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:70-89,455,500-502` only arms the timeout when `internal-controller` exists, and `internal-controller` is created only when `abort-signal` is absent. A custom `AbortSignal` therefore bypasses both explicit and default timeouts.
- Low: JVM builds keep the canned stub fx IDs registered even though the docs describe them as test-only. `implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj:105` hardcodes `debug-enabled?` to `true`; `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_managed.cljc:151-164` gates `:rf.http/managed-canned-success` and `:rf.http/managed-canned-failure` only on that flag; `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_test.clj:588-602` explicitly asserts that these stub fx IDs remain registered on JVM, including “the only value on JVM in production use”.
- No other actionable issues were confirmed in this slice from the code and tests reviewed.

## Recommended changes
- Route every HTTP-side trace site that carries request context through `re-frame.http-privacy/prepare-emit-tags` or `prepare-emit-failure` before calling `trace/emit!` or `trace/emit-error!`. Minimum fix points are `http_middleware/run-interceptor-chain!`, `http_transport/jvm-build-request`, and `http_transport/emit-cljs-only-skipped!`.
- In CLJS, decouple timeout enforcement from ownership of the abort controller. The timeout path should still fire when `:abort-signal` is supplied, either by composing signals or by always owning an internal timeout controller.
- Decide whether canned stub fx IDs should ever exist on JVM outside tests. If not, replace the current gate with an explicit test/dev opt-in and update the corresponding JVM assertions.
- Add regression coverage for the missing cases: interceptor-failure URL redaction, JVM warning-path URL redaction, and CLJS `:abort-signal` plus timeout interaction.

## Spec or policy impact
- `/spec` or operator/policy review is needed for JVM canned-stub registration. Current code/tests intentionally keep `:rf.http/managed-canned-*` registered on JVM, which conflicts with the stated “do not ship canned stubs as production-eligible” intent.

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`
- `rg --files implementation/http`
- `rg -n "trace/emit!|trace/emit-error!|abort-signal|timeout-ms|managed-canned|http-interceptor-failed" implementation/http/src implementation/http/test`

title: audit(security): implementation/flows
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface
`implementation/flows` implements frame-scoped derived-state "flows": callers can register `:id`/`:inputs`/`:output`/`:path` flow maps via `rf/reg-flow`, `rf/clear-flow`, or `:rf.fx/reg-flow`; the runtime re-evaluates them after each `:db` commit and writes results back into app-db. The main attack surface is runtime registration/clearing, post-drain execution of arbitrary flow functions, per-frame state retained in the `flows` and `last-inputs` atoms, and trace/error emission from `:rf.flow/*`.

## Findings
- High: frame teardown does not clean up flow state. `destroy-frame!` has cleanup hooks for SSR, machines, privacy, and epoch state, but flows never register an `on-frame-destroyed` hook, so `flows` and `last-inputs` retain entries for destroyed frames. References: `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:28-48`, `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:158-203`, `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:239-328`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:456-521`. I verified this with a `clojure -M -e` reproducer: after `rf/destroy-frame`, the destroyed frame's flow registry entry and cached `last-inputs` row were still present. Impact: unbounded memory growth for request-scoped/ephemeral frames, retained sensitive input snapshots outside app-db teardown, and stale flow definitions surviving into a reused frame id.
- Medium: flow evaluation failures bypass the always-on error channel. A throwing flow emits `:rf.flow/failed` and rethrows inside `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:153-180`; `router/run-flows!` catches that and only calls `trace/emit-error!` at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:374-384`. Unlike handler exceptions, this path never calls `error-emit/dispatch-on-error!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:265-340`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:90-122`). In CLJS production builds, the trace surface is compiled out, so flow failures can become effectively silent to `:on-error` policy handlers and off-box error listeners while leaving stale/missing derived state behind.

## Recommended changes
- Add a flows teardown hook for `destroy-frame!` that removes `flows[frame-id]`, removes that frame from every `last-inputs[flow-id]`, and unregisters `:flow` registrar entries whose last owning frame was destroyed.
- Add regression tests for `destroy-frame!` cleanup, frame-id reuse, and SSR-style repeated frame churn.
- Route `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` through the always-on error substrate as well as the dev trace path, so `:on-error` policies and `register-error-emit-listener!` observers see flow failures in production.
- Decide explicitly whether a failed flow should keep its prior output or clear/fail-closed that path; whichever behavior is intended should be enforced and tested.

## Spec or policy impact
- `/spec`: Spec 002/013 should explicitly require cleanup of flow registry state and dirty-check caches on frame destroy.
- `/spec` or operator/policy review: Spec 009/013 should define whether `:rf.error/flow-eval-exception` must hit the always-on error channel in production, and whether flow failure preserves or clears prior derived output.

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`

title: audit(security): implementation/machines
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

`implementation/machines` implements the state-machine runtime: machine registration, transition execution, declarative `:invoke` / `:invoke-all` spawning, `:after` timers, destroy/finalize flows, and machine query helpers. The main attack surface is untrusted event payloads reaching machine handlers, synthetic child/timer events, actor-id and system-id allocation, and the split between per-frame machine state in `app-db` and globally registered event handlers.

## Findings

1. High: `:invoke-all` accepts forged child-completion events. In `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc:224-267`, `intercept-invoke-all-event` trusts `child-id` from the inbound event and adds it directly to `:done` / `:failed`. `join-condition-met?` in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc:79-98` then resolves purely from set counts versus the spec child count. There is no check that the reported `child-id` exists in the runtime-tracked `(:children join-state)`. Any code path that can dispatch `[parent-id [on-child-done <bogus-id>]]` or `[parent-id [on-child-error <bogus-id> ...]]` can resolve joins early, fire parent success/failure transitions, and cancel legitimate siblings.

2. High: spawned actors still use the global event registrar while their snapshots live per-frame. `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:12-16` explicitly notes that the spec's frame-local handler registry is not built yet; `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:314-317` registers handlers globally; actor ids are deterministic and reused across frames in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:170-186` and `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:47-59`; and destroy paths globally unregister by event id in `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:72,145`. In concurrent frames or SSR, one frame can overwrite another frame's spawned handler or destroy it, breaking frame isolation and potentially routing events through the wrong machine definition.

No other actionable security issues were identified in the rest of this slice on this pass.

## Recommended changes

1. In `intercept-invoke-all-event`, reject unknown `child-id` values before mutating join state or evaluating resolution. Emit a trace/error for unexpected completions, and add regression tests for forged `:on-child-done` / `:on-child-error` ids and repeated bogus completions.

2. Finish the spec-intended frame-local handler registry for spawned actors, or otherwise frame-qualify spawned actor ids and unregister by `(frame-id, actor-id)` instead of a single global `:event` id. Add multi-frame tests covering same actor id in two frames, destroy in one frame not affecting the other, and divergent inline spawned definitions across frames.

## Spec or policy impact

None

title: audit(security): implementation/routing
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface
- Implements route registration, URL parse/build, history updates, scroll restoration, navigation guards, and the `:route/link` view for `implementation/routing`.
- Main untrusted inputs are request/browser URLs flowing through `match-url`, `:rf/url-changed`, `:rf.route/handle-url-change`, `:rf/url-requested`, and route-link `:query` / `:fragment` props.
- On CLJS this slice also calls `history.pushState`, `history.replaceState`, `document.getElementById`, and emits anchor `href` values.

## Findings
- Medium: untrusted query material is interned as Clojure keywords before validation, which enables memory-growth DoS on JVM/SSR and long-lived clients. `match-url` keywordizes every query key at `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:418-420`, and `coerce-by-type-form` turns `:keyword` query values into keywords at `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:317-329`. Verified with `routing/match-url "/search?x=abc&tab=reports"` returning `{:query {:x "abc" :tab :reports}}`, so undeclared keys and arbitrary keyword-typed values are interned from user-controlled URLs.
- Medium: malformed percent-encoding throws instead of failing closed, so a hostile URL can abort routing and potentially break client navigation or crash SSR request handling. `url-decode` directly calls `URLDecoder/decode` / `decodeURIComponent` at `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:39-44`, and callers in `match-against` and `match-url` do not catch decode failures (`implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:291-292`, `417-420`). Verified with `routing/match-url "/search?x=%"` throwing `java.lang.IllegalArgumentException`.
- No other actionable security issues stood out in this slice from source review.

## Recommended changes
- Parse raw query keys as strings first, and only convert to keywords for a bounded declared set derived from the route's schema/defaults. Unknown keys should stay strings, be dropped, or fail validation before any interning.
- Remove generic `(keyword v)` coercion for `:keyword` query values. Convert only after the value matches an allowed enum/whitelist, or keep it as a string and let the validator decide.
- Wrap percent-decoding in a safe helper that catches decode exceptions and turns them into a route miss or structured validation failure instead of throwing through `match-url`.
- Add regression tests for malformed `%` inputs and for repeated unique query-key/value spray against the CLJ path.

## Spec or policy impact
- `/spec` review needed: whether `match-url` must keep returning keywordized query keys/values, or whether unknown query keys may remain strings / be dropped / be rejected.
- `/spec` review needed: define the contract for malformed percent-encoding (`nil` no-match vs `:validation-failed?` vs structured error).

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`
- `rg --files implementation/routing`
- `rg -n "..." implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc implementation/routing/test/re_frame`

title: perf(causa): implement real per-epoch diff cache for :rf.causa/selected-epoch-diff
description:
`tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/panels/app_db_diff.cljs:539-554` claims in comments that "the diff is computed lazily on panel mount and the result cached per :epoch-id" — but the actual `:rf.causa/selected-epoch-diff` sub just calls `h/diff-paths` directly inside the composite. The reagent-sub identity caching only applies when underlying tuple is identical?-equal; with a fresh `history` vector each frame, every recompute re-runs the diff over the host app-db.

On apps with large app-db this is the most likely user-visible Causa slowdown.

Fix: add a real epoch-id-keyed cache, bounded to the retained epoch-history depth. Either `clojure.core.cache` LRU or a manual `{epoch-id triples}` atom bounded by depth. Update the comment to match (or remove if implementation doesn't match the comment intent).

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-causa-2026-05-14.md finding 2.
Audit-bead: rf2-7tnsv.
close_reason: Fixed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1056 — :rf.causa/selected-epoch-diff now wraps a private (atom {}) keyed on :epoch-id. On miss: compute, store, prune to live history's :epoch-id set; on hit: identical?-equal return. Bounded by epoch-history depth without LRU surface. Comment rewritten to match reality. Tests pin: identical?-equal cache hit, age-out eviction, cross-selection roundtrip.

title: audit(security): implementation/core
description:
# Slice Security Audit
## Current purpose / attack surface
`implementation/core` is the runtime kernel: global registrar, frame/router dispatch loop, fx/cofx execution, privacy/redaction, trace/event/error emission, and source-coordinate tooling. The main security surfaces are public listener registration (`register-trace-cb!`, `register-event-emit-listener!`, `register-error-emit-listener!`), per-frame `:on-error` callbacks, handler metadata (`:sensitive?`, source coords), and dev-tool helpers that turn captured file paths into emitted trace data or editor URIs.

## Findings
- High: sensitive handler exceptions can leak raw event payloads to always-on error observers. `router/emit-handler-exception!` forwards the original `event` to `error-emit/dispatch-on-error!` unless `with-redacted` populated `:rf/redacted-event` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:298-337`). The always-on error substrate then ships that event to `register-error-emit-listener!` listeners and frame `:on-error` policies, but only runs size/path elision; it does not honor handler-level `:sensitive?` the way `event-emit` does (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:90-122`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:437-503`, contrast `implementation/core/src/re_frame/event_emit.cljc:82-95`). Result: `^{:sensitive? true}` without `with-redacted` is warning-only, not enforcement, so a thrown auth/payment/PII event can leave the process unredacted.
- Medium: JVM/headless deployments keep dev trace surfaces enabled by default. `re-frame.interop` hardcodes `debug-enabled?` to `true` on the JVM (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj:105`). That keeps `trace/emit!`, the default 200-entry `trace-buffer`, registry trace emits, and public trace listener APIs live in SSR/headless production (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:173-199`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/trace.cljc:428-477`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:562-566`). Those events include payloads, exceptions, and source-coord metadata. There is no built-in prod-off switch equivalent to CLJS `goog.DEBUG=false`.

## Recommended changes
- Make the always-on error path enforce privacy, not just warn about it. Minimum fix: if handler meta is `:sensitive? true`, either drop error-emit records entirely or force `:event` through a handler-level redaction policy before `dispatch-on-error!`. Add coverage for "sensitive handler throws without with-redacted".
- Add a real JVM production gate for trace/registry diagnostics. Environment/config based is fine, but it should disable trace emission and buffer retention by default in SSR/headless production, with an explicit opt-in for local debugging.

## Spec or policy impact
- `/spec` or privacy-policy review: decide whether `:sensitive? true` must be an enforcing guarantee on the always-on error path, rather than a warning-only convention unless `with-redacted` is also present.
- `/spec` or operator-policy review: decide whether JVM/SSR should keep the current "always dev" behavior, or gain an explicit production gate for trace/buffer/source-coord diagnostics.

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`
- `rg --files implementation/core`
- `rg -n "eval|read-string|slurp|spit|shell|exec|js/eval|innerHTML|dangerouslySetInnerHTML|fetch|http|editor-uri|privacy"` `implementation/core/src`
- `rg -n ":on-error|error|trace|privacy|source-coord|with-redacted|sensitive"` `implementation/core/src`
- `Get-Content` on the key source and test files listed below

title: audit(security): implementation root/tooling
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface

This slice is the top-level build and test coordinator for `implementation/`.

- The root files (`package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`) define the combined CLJS/JVM build, pinned Node tooling, and npm entrypoints.
- `implementation/scripts` is the active tooling surface. It spawns `shadow-cljs`, `http-server`, and Playwright; serves compiled assets on `127.0.0.1`; and writes generated files such as patched `index.html`, `manifest.json`, and `.rf-harness-token`.
- The main trust inputs are environment variables: `BROWSER_TEST_ROOT`, `BROWSER_TEST_PORT`, `BROWSER_TEST_URL`, `BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, `STORY_BUILD_TARGET`, `STORY_BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR`, and `STORY_BUILD_INDEX_HTML`.
- `npm audit --package-lock-only --json` reported no currently-known advisories for the pinned lockfile.

## Findings

1. Medium: `implementation/scripts/check-story-static.cjs:29,59-81,183-209` uses a fixed localhost port and treats any HTTP responder on `127.0.0.1:8040` as "ready", then drives Playwright against it.

   The script does not verify server ownership, unlike `implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-browser-tests.cjs:71-91,214-235`. A local port squatter or stale listener can win the race and serve foreign content to the headless browser. The later `serverDown` check reduces the window but does not remove the core TOCTOU problem, because readiness is still defined as "someone answered on 8040" rather than "the child process we launched is serving `OUT_DIR`".

2. Medium: env-controlled path overrides are used as write targets without boundary checks.

   - `implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-browser-tests.cjs:40-67,95-106` resolves `BROWSER_TEST_ROOT` and then may rewrite `${ROOT}/index.html` and create/delete `${ROOT}/.rf-harness-token`.
   - `implementation/scripts/story-build.cjs:49-58,63-65,88-97,113-114` accepts `STORY_BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR` and `STORY_BUILD_INDEX_HTML`, then blindly writes `${OUTPUT_DIR}/index.html` and `${OUTPUT_DIR}/manifest.json`.

   In normal local use these env vars are probably trusted, but in CI, wrappers, or downstream reuse with inherited environment state this becomes an arbitrary file-write primitive outside the repo/worktree.

## Recommended changes

- Rework `check-story-static.cjs` to reuse the hardened ownership model from `serve-and-run-browser-tests.cjs`: free-port selection, child-exit detection during readiness, and a per-run token fetched over HTTP before Playwright starts.
- Constrain writable path overrides to approved roots.
  For `BROWSER_TEST_ROOT`, require a path under `implementation/out`.
  For `STORY_BUILD_OUTPUT_DIR`, require a path under `implementation/out` unless an explicit opt-in flag allows out-of-tree publishing.
  For `STORY_BUILD_INDEX_HTML`, require a repo-relative source path unless explicit opt-in is set.
- Replace Windows `npx` launches that rely on `shell: true` with `process.execPath` plus resolved package bin paths where possible. That removes shell parsing around env-derived values such as `STORY_BUILD_TARGET` and `BROWSER_TEST_ROOT`.
- If out-of-tree overrides are intentionally supported for downstream consumers, document them as trusted-only inputs and avoid inheriting them implicitly from ambient CI environment.

## Spec or policy impact

- Operator review: decide whether `BROWSER_TEST_ROOT` and `STORY_BUILD_*` are meant to be trusted internal overrides only, or a supported public surface for downstream consumers. The code hardening is straightforward either way, but the allowed-path policy should be explicit.

## Commands checked

- `bd prime`
- `rg --files implementation`
- `Get-ChildItem implementation -File | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName`
- `Get-ChildItem implementation\scripts -File | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName`

Windows npx/shell:true narrowing documented as defensive option but deferred — npx.cmd shell wrapping is structurally required on Windows.

title: audit(security): implementation/adapters
description:
# Slice Security Audit
## Current purpose / attack surface
`implementation/adapters` provides the Reagent, UIx, Helix, and `reagent-slim` substrate adapters. The main security-sensitive surfaces in this slice are mount/hydrate entrypoints, raw React interop (`:r>` / `:>`), prop-map translation, and `reagent-slim`'s custom static-markup serializer used for HTML export / SSR seed generation.

## Findings
1. High: `reagent-slim`'s static-markup serializer emits arbitrary DOM props as literal HTML attributes instead of stripping React event props. In [implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs:192), `emit-attr` only skips `:key`, `:ref`, and `:dangerouslySetInnerHTML`; everything else is lowercased by `attr-name` ([135](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs:135)) and stringified by `attr-value-string` ([182](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs:182)). That means inputs like `{:on-click "alert(1)"}` would serialize to `onclick="alert(1)"`, and function-valued props can leak into HTML as strings. The parity suite currently exercises class/id/data/aria/boolean/void/raw-HTML cases but not event-prop stripping ([implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/dom/parity_cljs_test.cljs](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/test/reagent2/dom/parity_cljs_test.cljs:106)). This widens the XSS surface for static export / SSR output and diverges from React server rendering.
2. Medium: `reagent-slim` builds props objects and caches with plain JS objects plus unfiltered `aset` on user-controlled keys, which leaves `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` key paths open. The relevant writes are in [implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:95), [134](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:134), [210](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:210), [242](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:242), [255](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:255), [319](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:319), and [499](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:499). A malicious prop key can mutate the prototype of the per-element props object or shared caches instead of becoming a normal own property, which can inject inherited props such as `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` or event handlers and cause unstable renderer behavior.

## Recommended changes
- In `reagent2.dom.server`, stop serializing React event props and other non-HTML props. At minimum, drop `on*` names and function-valued props; better, align with a narrow allowlist/denylist based on React DOM server behavior. Add parity tests for `:on-click`, `:onClick`, function-valued props, and reserved React props.
- In `reagent2.impl.template`, build caches and props objects with a null prototype (for example `js/Object.create nil`) or explicitly reject reserved keys such as `__proto__`, `prototype`, and `constructor` before `aset`. Add tests covering reserved keys on DOM props, fragment props, and nested prop maps.
- Document `:dangerouslySetInnerHTML` / `:r>` as trusted-input-only escape hatches in the slim adapter docs while fixing the code paths above.

## Spec or policy impact
None. Both fixes align with the existing React-parity intent and should not require `/spec` or operator/policy review.

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`
- `Get-ChildItem -Recurse -File implementation/adapters | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName`
- `rg -n --hidden --glob '!**/.cpcache/**' ... implementation/adapters`
- `Get-Content` on the adapter source, `reagent-slim` support code, and targeted test files
- Line-numbered `Get-Content ... | ForEach-Object { '{0,4}: {1}' -f $i, $_; $i++ }` for evidence capture

## Files checked
- `implementation/adapters/README.md`
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs`
- `implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs`
- `implementation/adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs`
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/README.md`
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md`
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs`
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/core.cljs`
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom.cljs`
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/client.cljs`
- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/server.cljs`

HIGH: render-to-static-markup strips event-handler props (on*) and fn-valued props at emit-attr (matches react-dom/server). MEDIUM: cached-prop-name returns reserved keys verbatim without caching; kv-conv drops __proto__/constructor/prototype before aset on the props object that flows into React.createElement. Regression tests pin both contracts.

title: audit(security): implementation/epoch
description:
# Slice Security Audit

## Current purpose / attack surface
- `implementation/epoch` implements dev/pair-tool epoch history: per-frame state snapshots, raw trace capture, listener fan-out, time-travel restore, and out-of-band `app-db` replacement.
- The exposed security-relevant surfaces are `epoch-history`, `register-epoch-cb!`, `restore-epoch`, `reset-frame-db!`, and the late-bind hooks they publish.
- The slice stores full `db-before` / `db-after` values and raw `:trace-events`, so any secrets present in `app-db` or event payloads can be retained and replayed.

## Findings
- `Medium`: The slice's "dev-only" read/write surfaces are effectively always enabled on JVM. `restore-epoch`, `reset-frame-db!`, `settle!`, `capture-event!`, and destroy cleanup all rely on `interop/debug-enabled?` in [implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc), but on JVM that flag is hardcoded `true` in [core/src/re_frame/interop.clj](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj:105). If `day8/re-frame2-epoch` is present in a server/SSR/JVM process, arbitrary in-process code keeps access to history reads and state rewrite APIs in production.
- `Medium`: Epoch records persist and broadcast full application state without redaction. `build-record` stores verbatim `:db-before`, `:db-after`, and `:trace-events` in [implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:571), default config keeps a 50-record ring and retains raw trace vectors unless `:trace-events-keep` is set in [implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:59), and listeners receive the full record in [implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc](C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:201). This increases exposure of tokens, PII, and other sensitive state in heap memory, crash dumps, logs built from listeners, and any tool/plugin callback registered in-process.

## Recommended changes
- Add a JVM runtime guard separate from `goog.DEBUG`, defaulting the epoch artefact off outside tests/dev. The safest seam is to refuse late-bind registration and reject `restore-epoch` / `reset-frame-db!` unless an explicit opt-in flag is set.
- Add a redaction/scrubbing hook before persistence and listener fan-out so apps can strip secrets from `db-before`, `db-after`, and `:trace-events`.
- Tighten retention defaults for sensitive environments: at minimum document `:trace-events-keep 0`, and consider a config mode that omits raw traces or full DB snapshots entirely.

## Spec or policy impact
- `/spec`: clarify whether "dev-only" is a CLJS-only guarantee or must also be enforceable for JVM/SSR consumers.
- Operator/policy review: define whether unredacted `app-db` snapshots and raw event payloads are acceptable in epoch history, and what retention/redaction defaults are required.

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`
- `Get-ChildItem -Force -Name`
- `rg --files`
- `Get-Content -Raw src\re_frame\epoch.cljc`
- `Get-Content -Raw test\re_frame\epoch_test.clj`
- `Get-Content -Raw deps.edn`
- `rg -n "defn|defonce|late-bind/set-fn!" src\re_frame\epoch.cljc`
- Line-range `Get-Content` checks against `src\re_frame\epoch.cljc`, `core\src\re_frame\interop.clj`, `core\src\re_frame\core_epoch.cljc`, and `core\src\re_frame\spec.cljc`
- `clojure -M:test`

## Files checked
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc`
- `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj`
- `implementation/epoch/deps.edn`
- `core/src/re_frame/interop.clj`
- `core/src/re_frame/core_epoch.cljc`
- `core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc`

Redaction/scrubbing hook for db-before/db-after/:trace-events deferred to a follow-on bead.

title: [spec] Define security posture in /spec — Security.md or distributed?
description:

title: audit(performance): tools/story-mcp
description:
# Slice Performance Audit

## Current purpose / runtime profile
- `tools/story-mcp` is a JVM stdio JSON-RPC server that exposes Story read/test/write tools to MCP hosts; it is not part of the browser bundle.
- The request path is synchronous: `server/run-loop!` -> `dispatch` -> `cap/invoke-tool` -> tool handler -> JSON write (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:171`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cap.cljc:66`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/protocol.cljc:150`).
- The expensive work is not protocol framing. It is Story-runtime execution plus post-processing in `preview-variant`, `run-variant`, `record-as-variant`, and registry reads like `list-stories`.
- Current repo scale looks modest from source counts: about 26 `reg-story`, 44 `reg-variant`, and 12 `reg-mode` call sites, so most issues are “likely next pain” rather than immediate breakage.

## Likely hot paths
- `preview-variant` and `run-variant` both call `story/run-variant`, then walk/scrub/serialize the result (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc:63`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:16`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/helpers.cljc:182`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:559`).
- `list-stories` filters the story registry and then calls `story/variants-of` for every returned story (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/docs.cljc:12`); `variants-of` is itself an O(N variants) scan (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/registrar.cljc:340`).
- `record-as-variant` blocks on `Thread/sleep` inside the request thread, then emits both captured events and a generated snippet (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:26`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:68`).
- The wire-boundary cap runs after handler work, so any large response already paid the full cost of elision, EDN rendering, and JSON rendering before overflow replacement can happen (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cap.cljc:66`, `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cap.cljc:149`).

## Dev vs prod considerations
- Dev is the real hot environment here: agents tend to probe `list-stories`, `preview-variant`, `run-variant`, and `read-failures` repeatedly while the Story runtime is live.
- “Prod” here is automation/CI or a long-lived JVM MCP host, not a shipped UI bundle. The slice is isolated from production CLJS bundles by design (`tools/story-mcp/README.md`, `tools/story-mcp/deps.edn`).
- The write surface is gated off by default, so `register-variant`, `unregister-variant`, and `record-as-variant` write-back cost normally only matters in explicit dev sessions.
- `run-a11y` is usually cheap in JVM-standalone mode because it only reads the CLJS violations atom when co-hosted; otherwise it returns an empty/note payload (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/testing.cljc:71`).

## Findings
- `High`: most structured tools duplicate large payloads into both `:content` text and `:structuredContent` via `h/text-result` (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/helpers.cljc:68`), but the cap only counts `:text` slots (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cap.cljc:60`, `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/cap.cljc:149`). That means `preview-variant`, `run-variant`, `list-stories`, `get-story`, `get-variant`, `read-failures`, and `record-as-variant` can do roughly 2x wire serialization/allocation work while the cap underestimates the real response size.
- `Medium`: `list-stories` does a per-story `variants-of` lookup (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/docs.cljc:12`), and `variants-of` is documented as an O(N variants) scan (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/registrar.cljc:340`). Today’s scale is small, but this is the registry query agents are most likely to spam, so the shape is avoidably O(stories * variants). The tool also does not call this out locally; if the implementation stays as-is, add a short hot-path comment.
- `Low`: `record-as-variant` monopolizes the single stdio request loop for the full `:duration-ms` window because it sleeps inside the handler (`tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:26`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:121`, `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc:171`). That is acceptable for short recordings, but large durations will stall unrelated MCP calls.

## Recommended changes
- Make cap accounting reflect actual wire cost. Lowest-risk fix: teach the story-mcp `ResultIO`/cap path to include serialized `:structuredContent` size, not just `:content[*].text`, before deciding whether to overflow.
- Keep the current tool contracts, but avoid unnecessary duplication where possible. If a tool already ships full `structuredContent`, the text slot should be justified as agent-readable value, not a second full-fidelity copy by default.
- Rewrite `list-stories` to build story -> variants in one pass from the variant registry, or add a small Story-side helper that does the same. That preserves behavior and turns the query into O(stories + variants).
- Leave `run-variant` and `preview-variant` synchronous unless profiling says otherwise. Their cost is mostly real Story work plus required redaction; extra concurrency would add complexity fast.
- Keep `record-as-variant` simple, but document or guard against very large `:duration-ms` values. A warning/error for obviously abusive durations is cheaper than making the server concurrent.

## Spec impact
None

## Commands checked
- `git status --short`
- `rg --files tools/story-mcp`
- `Get-ChildItem -Recurse tools/story-mcp/src`
- `rg -n "<hot-path symbols/patterns>" tools/story-mcp/src`
- `Get-Content -Raw` on slice source/spec files and the downstream Story / mcp-base / elision files used by this slice
- `rg -n "\(reg-story\b|\(reg-variant\b|\(reg-mode\b"` across repo paths to gauge current registry scale

## Files checked
- `tools/story-mcp/README.md`
- `tools/story-mcp/deps.edn`
- `tools/story-mcp/spec/API.md`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/config.cljc`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/protocol.cljc`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/server.cljc`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cap.cljc`
- `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/dev.cljc`

title: audit(performance): tools/template
description:
# Slice Performance Audit

## Current purpose / runtime profile
- `tools/template` is a build-time `clj-new` template. `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2.clj` runs once per scaffold and is never on a generated app's runtime classpath.
- The only slice code that can reach app dev/prod runtime is the emitted scaffold under `src/clj/new/re_frame2/{reagent,uix,helix,shared}`. In practice, the live path is limited to `core.cljs` init and `views.cljs` render functions.
- The heaviest recurring work in this slice today is dev/CI, not production: JVM tests generate temp apps, parse emitted CLJS, and optionally spawn `clojure -P`. One local `clojure -M:test` run took about `10.4s`.

## Likely hot paths
- Dev only: `shadow-cljs` `:after-load` re-runs `{{namespace}}.core/init`, which re-initializes re-frame2, dispatches `:counter/initialise`, and re-renders the root (`reagent/core.cljs:20-30`; same shape in UIx/Helix).
- Dev and prod in generated apps: `views.cljs` render functions and hook/subscription calls (`reagent/views.cljs:15-18`, `uix/views.cljs:11-16`, `helix/views.cljs:12-17`).
- Dev/CI only: `template_emission_test.clj` repeatedly reads and regex-scans framework source during the static surface audit.
- Dev/CI only: `re_frame2_test.clj` repeats `clojure --help` and `clojure -P` per substrate.

## Dev vs prod considerations
- The template generator itself has no production runtime impact; only emitted files matter after scaffolding.
- The `init` re-run/reset behavior is intentionally dev-biased. It is the right tradeoff for hot reload and not a prod concern because release builds call `init` once.
- The render-path code in the generated counter is intentionally minimal. That is fine for the starter app, but it is example code users may copy into real hot paths.
- The two test hotspots matter only for local iteration and CI wall-clock time.

## Findings
- No meaningful production hotspot was found in `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2.clj`; the generator does small, bounded file I/O and string rendering once per scaffold.
- `tools/template/test/clj/new/template_emission_test.clj:204-227,280-324` is doing repeated `slurp` plus regex work for the same framework files inside the per-symbol audit loop. That cost will grow with more emitted files, more substrates, or more `re-frame.*` references.
- `tools/template/test/clj/new/re_frame2_test.clj:65-86,126-204` is likely the biggest current test-time cost: the suite probes the CLI repeatedly and runs `clojure -P` once per substrate. The observed test run was about `10.4s` and included three expected skip paths from `clojure -P`.
- `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/{reagent,uix,helix}/views.cljs` is on the live render path, but the files do not explicitly say that the inline event handlers and per-render dispatch acquisition are starter-template simplicity, not a pattern to cargo-cult into heavier views. A short comment should be added if these templates remain the canonical example.

## Recommended changes
- Memoize `defined-symbols` in `template_emission_test.clj` and reuse cached namespace-to-file lookups. This is low complexity and the best dev/CI payoff in the slice.
- Probe `clojure` CLI availability once per JVM and run at most one deps-resolution smoke check per suite, or gate `clojure -P` behind an opt-in env var for slower CI/release lanes.
- Keep the generated `core.cljs` and `views.cljs` simple; do not add memoization or handler-hoisting noise to a counter template unless the emitted example becomes materially more complex.
- Add one short comment in each generated `views.cljs` noting that this is render-path code kept intentionally minimal for the starter app, and that heavier list/grid views should revisit allocation and subscription shape.

## Spec impact
None

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`
- `rg --files tools/template`
- `git status --short`
- `Get-Content -Raw ...` on generator, emitted scaffold, tests, and spec files in `tools/template`
- Line-numbered `Get-Content` passes on `src/clj/new/re_frame2.clj`, generated `core.cljs` and `views.cljs`, and both JVM test namespaces
- `clojure -M:test` in `tools/template` (`0` failures/errors; about `10.4s`; expected `clojure -P` skip messages)

## Files checked
- `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2.clj`
- `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/shared/events.cljs`
- `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/shared/subs.cljs`
- `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/shared/events_test.cljs`
- `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/shared/README.md`
- `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/reagent/core.cljs`, `views.cljs`, `deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`
- `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/uix/core.cljs`, `views.cljs`, `deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`
- `tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/helix/core.cljs`, `views.cljs`, `deps.edn`, `shadow-cljs.edn`
- `tools/template/test/clj/new/re_frame2_test.clj`
- `tools/template/test/clj/new/template_emission_test.clj`
- `tools/template/README.md`
- `tools/template/spec/API.md`
- `tools/template/spec/001-Substrate-Variants.md`
- `tools/template/spec/002-Generated-Shape.md`

title: audit(performance): tools/pair2-mcp
description:
# Slice Performance Audit
## Current purpose / runtime profile
- `tools/pair2-mcp` is a Node/CLJS MCP server over stdio that keeps one persistent nREPL socket open and turns pair2 runtime operations into MCP tools.
- It is dev-first infrastructure. The dominant runtime costs are nREPL round-trips, EDN decode/encode, and post-eval tree transforms on `snapshot`, `trace-window`, `watch-epochs`, `get-path`, and `subscribe`.
- The highest-value optimization posture is low fixed latency for many small interactive calls, not raw bulk throughput.

## Likely hot paths
- `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/probe.cljs`: `ensure-runtime!` probes the runtime before non-streaming calls.
- `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/snapshot.cljs` plus `tools/wire_pipeline.cljs` and `tools/snapshot_pipeline.cljs`: large read path with multiple whole-structure passes.
- `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/summary.cljs`: summary generation on rich slices.
- `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/trace_window.cljs`, `tools/watch_epochs.cljs`, and `tools/dedup.cljs`: diff-encode plus dedup on every epoch page.
- `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/subscribe.cljs` and `tools/subscribe_emit.cljs`: 100ms poll loop, per-tick filtering/dedup, and progress serialization.
- `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/nrepl.cljs`: `decode-all-frames` and `send-op!` are the transport hot path under frequent calls or streaming.
- `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/cache.cljs` and `tools/precheck.cljs`: hot only when `cache true` is in use.

## Dev vs prod considerations
- This slice is mostly a dev/staging tool because it depends on shadow-cljs nREPL and the preloaded pair2 runtime.
- The important stress case is still prod-sized state in a dev-like session. `snapshot`, `get-path`, cache precheck, and cap enforcement can all hit very large values.
- `discover-app` already flags `:debug-disabled` in production builds, so trace/epoch surfaces matter less there than app-db reads and fixed per-call overhead.
- `subscribe` polling is primarily a dev ergonomics cost: background eval traffic and local processing while a stream is open.

## Findings
- `tree-summary` is the clearest avoidable hot-path cost. In `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/summary.cljs`, the docstring says summary is "one pass" and "no deep walk", but `:bytes` is computed with `count (pr-str v)` for maps, vectors, sets, and seqs. That means the default summary path still deeply serializes the full value before returning only a marker.
- Every non-streaming tool currently pays an extra probe round-trip. `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/probe.cljs` runs `runtime-preloaded?` before the real eval, so narrow reads and health checks effectively become two nREPL evals on the common path.
- The `snapshot` path is intentionally multi-pass, not accidentally quadratic. `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/wire_pipeline.cljs` runs scrub -> slice -> diff -> dedup -> elision-count -> summary. That is real CPU/allocation work on large payloads, but it is also well-factored and well-commented; I would not fuse it without timings.
- Structural dedup looks justified for the target shapes. `npm test` reports about `1.40x-1.45x` compression on raw trace bursts, `10.80x` on high-share replays, and `89.5%` reduction on the shared-`db-before` epoch fixture. This is not complexity that should be removed casually.
- `subscribe` is a steady-state hot path by design. The poll loop in `src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/subscribe.cljs` does one drain eval per tick plus local strip/count/dedup/serialize work. That is acceptable for interactive dev, but it will dominate cost during long-running sessions more than any single one-shot tool.
- Most real hot paths are already commented. The notable exception is not missing commentary but misleading commentary: `tree-summary` currently describes a cheaper algorithm than it actually runs.

## Recommended changes
- Cache a successful runtime probe per live socket/runtime generation. Invalidate on socket close and on failed evals. This should cut the fixed latency on the common read path without changing the wire contract.
- Make `:rf.mcp/summary`'s `:bytes` field a cheap hint instead of paying full `pr-str` cost on large values. The field is already documented as `~B`, so approximate post-shrink cost is enough for planning. Also fix the `tree-summary` comment to match the actual algorithm.
- Add lightweight timing around `ensure-runtime!`, `snapshot` pipeline stages, `trace-window`/`watch-epochs` transforms, and `subscribe` drain ticks. The slice already has good tests; it lacks cheap runtime evidence for where CPU is really going.
- Keep diff-encode plus dedup as the default. Only add small fast paths if profiling shows lots of tiny pages or tiny subscribe ticks where dedup cost outweighs the win.
- If cache-enabled large-frame sessions become common, move precheck from `hash(snapshot)` to a runtime-maintained digest updated at mutation time. That is a worthwhile next optimization, but only behind real usage.

## Spec impact
None.

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`
- `rg --files tools/pair2-mcp`
- `Get-ChildItem -Force tools/pair2-mcp | Format-Table -AutoSize`
- `rg -n "^\\(ns|^\\(defn|^\\(def " tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/...`
- `rg -n "rf\\.mcp/summary|:bytes|Lazy summary|tree-summary" tools/pair2-mcp/spec tools/pair2-mcp/README.md tools/pair2-mcp/test`
- `npm test`

## Files checked
