title: audit(performance): implementation root/tooling
description:
# Slice Performance Audit

## Current purpose / runtime profile

This slice is build and test orchestration, not application request-path runtime. The real cost surface is dev/CI: root `shadow-cljs` compiles/releases, the aggregate `deps.edn :test` classpath, and the Node harnesses that serve browser tests or inspect built bundles.

There is effectively no direct prod hot path here beyond producing or validating prod bundles. The important prod-facing risk in this slice is incorrect or noisy bundle validation.

## Likely hot paths

- `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:25` is the dominant dev hot path. The root coordinator pulls 39 `:source-paths` across artefacts, tests, tools, and examples into one build graph.
- `implementation/deps.edn:55` is the JVM-side equivalent. The top-level `:test` alias adds 17 extra paths and is intentionally broad.
- `implementation/scripts/check-bundle-isolation.cjs:220`, `check-elision.cjs:231`, `check-perf-bundle.cjs:62`, and `check-schemas-bundle.cjs:68` all do full bundle-tree reads or gzip passes. These are CI/dev-only hot paths, but they are the main script-level cost centers in this slice.
- `implementation/scripts/serve-and-run-browser-tests.cjs:214`, `run-browser-tests.cjs:47`, and `check-story-static.cjs:76` use polling loops. They matter less than compile/startup time, but they are the recurring browser-harness path.

## Dev vs prod considerations

- Dev cost is dominated by broad classpaths and repeated `shadow-cljs` work. `package.json:16-27` wires many scripts to separate `compile` or `release` invocations.
- Prod relevance is mostly validation: the scripts assert elision, bundle isolation, and bundle-size envelopes for advanced builds defined in `shadow-cljs.edn:153-260`, `:282-335`, and `:535-541`.
- No root file here looks like a user-facing runtime bottleneck. The risk is slower iteration and false-positive audit failures.

## Findings

- `implementation/scripts/check-counter-slim-and-fast.cjs:119-136` already documents a real local-dev trap: stale `cljs-runtime/` files can survive `shadow-cljs release` and poison recursive scans. The sibling scripts `check-bundle-isolation.cjs:220-240`, `check-elision.cjs:231-250`, `check-perf-bundle.cjs:62-77`, and `check-schemas-bundle.cjs:68-84` still recurse through the full output tree. That is both unnecessary I/O and a likely correctness problem for local runs.
- The root coordinator is intentionally heavy. `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:25` centralizes 39 source paths so every root build pays for every artefact/test/example/tool tree. That is the main dev hot path for this slice.
- The broad test classpath in `implementation/deps.edn:55-79` is fine as a convenience surface, but it should stay a convenience surface. Using it as the default fast-iteration path will always be slower than per-artefact runs.
- Some traversal hot paths are under-commented. `check-counter-slim-and-fast.cjs` explains why it filters to top-level release files; the other bundle walkers do not. If they remain hot-path code, they should carry the same rationale.

## Recommended changes

- Normalize the bundle readers so release-based checks inspect only the shipped release artefact, not recursive leftovers. Best option: share one helper used by `check-bundle-isolation`, `check-elision`, `check-perf-bundle`, and `check-schemas-bundle`.
- Do not keep expanding the root `shadow-cljs.edn` fast path. If more probes or examples are added, prefer a narrower task-specific build/config for the common edit-test loop instead of growing the monolithic coordinator further.
- Keep the aggregate `deps.edn :test` alias for ad hoc REPL coverage, but keep per-artefact test entrypoints as the expected performance path.
- Leave the browser polling loops alone unless timings show they matter. They are secondary compared with compile/release breadth.

## Spec impact

None

## Commands checked

- `bd prime`
- `Get-ChildItem -Force implementation`

title: fix(http): pure-clojure JSON reader bounds-check absent on backslash-uXXXX escape
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P2.6.

## Surface

implementation/http/src/re_frame/util_json.cljc:61-65

## Evidence

`(subs s (+ p 2) (+ p 6))` for a `\u` escape near end-of-string throws `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

## Exploit sketch

Upstream returns `"x\u"`. SIOOBE caught and classified as decode-failure. Not directly exploitable, but small-payload high-rate malformed responses burn stack frames and produce noisy traces.

## Recommendation

Bounds-check before `subs`. Throw `:rf.error/malformed-json :reason :truncated-unicode-escape` with a clean error payload.

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P2.6.
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1042 — bounds-check + hex-validation in util_json.cljc json-read* surface :rf.error/malformed-json with :reason :truncated-unicode-escape / :invalid-unicode-escape

title: fix(ssr): hiccup attribute key not escaped — XSS via attacker-controlled keys
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P2.5 (and §P3.1 attribute-key parity).

## Surface

implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:48-59 (`attr-string`)

Also: implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj:55-78 (`:html-attrs` / `:body-attrs` flow same helper).

## Evidence

`attr-string` does `(str (name k) "=\"" (escape-attr v) "\"")` — values are escaped, **attribute names are not**.

## Exploit sketch

Rare but real — any app that builds attribute maps from app-db data and stores attacker-controlled keys becomes vulnerable. E.g. `(into {} (for [[k v] (:custom-attrs row)] [k v]))`. Attacker chooses a key like `(keyword "onclick=alert(1) data-x")` → renders `… onclick=alert(1) data-x="…"` and executes script.

## Recommendation

Validate attribute keys against HTML5 grammar `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_:-]*`. Throw `:rf.error/ssr-invalid-attribute-name` on violation. The "developer-literal only" assumption is fragile.

Fixing in `attr-string` covers both element attrs and the `:html-attrs` / `:body-attrs` shell flow (§P3.1).

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P2.5 + §P3.1.
close_reason: Fixed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1043 (batched ssr security sweep — 5 P1 + 2 P2 + 1 structure)

title: fix(http): unbounded request read on JVM when :timeout-ms omitted
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P2.3.

## Surface

implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:131-146 (request builder) + 126-129 (timeout wiring)

## Evidence

10-second **connect** timeout is enforced, but no per-request **read** timeout unless `:timeout-ms` is supplied by the caller. The `CompletableFuture` never completes on a slow-loris response.

## Exploit sketch

JVM app fetches a partner JSON endpoint without `:timeout-ms`. Partner is compromised; stalls the body forever. Connection pool fills with hung futures → DoS.

## Recommendation

Either:
- Require `:timeout-ms` (throw `:rf.error/http-request-missing-timeout` on JVM if absent), OR
- Apply a generous default (60s, configurable per-frame).

Lean toward the default — fewer surprises for typical apps.

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P2.3.
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1042 — 30000 ms default codified in Spec 014; opt-out semantic (:timeout-ms nil / 0) documented; regression tests pin the boundary at normalise-args + jvm-build-request

title: fix(http): JVM http transport silently drops headers with invalid values
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P2.2.

## Surface

implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:131-146 (`jvm-build-request`)

## Evidence

`(try (.header b (str k) (str v)) (catch Throwable _ nil))` silently swallows HttpClient's header validation throw. Header doesn't reach the wire, no error surfaces.

## Exploit sketch

Not directly exploitable — but security-relevant middleware that depends on `Authorization` being attached cannot detect that its header was stripped because the value contained a stray `\r`. Silent failure of security headers is the canonical "swallowed error" anti-pattern.

## Recommendation

Surface dropped header as `:rf.warning/http-header-invalid` trace event (or `:rf.error/http-header-invalid` depending on policy). Don't swallow.

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P2.2.
close_reason: Fixed in PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1042 — jvm-build-request catch now emits :rf.warning/http-header-invalid with URL + header name + JDK cause message (value omitted as it may carry secrets)

title: fix(ssr-ring): default-on-error leaks exception messages in production
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P2.1.

## Surface

implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/handler_defaults.clj:12-26 (`default-on-error`)

## Evidence

Response body is `(str "SSR error: " (or (.getMessage t) ...))` on any escaping `Throwable`. `.getMessage` carries internal paths, SQL fragments, file names.

## Exploit sketch

Attacker triggers any unhandled JVM exception. Response body returns e.g. `SSR error: Connection refused: jdbc:postgresql://internal-db.svc.cluster.local:5432/auth` — internal topology disclosed.

## Recommendation

Default-on-error should return a generic `"Internal error"` body (match the projector's `fallback-public-error`). Apps wanting dev-mode detail override via `:on-error`.

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P2.1.

title: audit(ns-structure): pair2-mcp — subscribe-emit.cljs is single-consumer helper, recommend re-merge
description:
The audit found one borderline split in pair2-mcp: `tools/subscribe-emit.cljs` (88 L) is consumed by ONLY `tools/subscribe.cljs` (229 L). The split was justified by the leaf-size ceiling but the boundary is artificial — `subscribe-emit` is tightly coupled to the streaming-loop state shape and has no independent consumers or test surface.

## Findings

- `tools/subscribe.cljs` — 229 L. The MCP `subscribe` tool body.
- `tools/subscribe-emit.cljs` — 88 L (3 fns: `progress-payload`, `final-summary`, `emit-progress-tick!`).
  - Only `:require` consumer: `subscribe.cljs`.
  - No direct test consumers (the conformance test `with_indicators_test.cljs` line 152 names `subscribe-emit-site-routes-through-with-indicators` but reaches through `subscribe-tool`, not into `emit` directly).

The split's docstring says: 'Split out of `tools/subscribe.cljs` (rf2-vrbwx) so the streaming-loop body stays under the leaf-size ceiling.' Combined LoC: 317 — over 250 L guideline but well within Mike's brief framing ('namespaces should be as long as they need to be if logically coherent and related').

## Contrast with `snapshot-pipeline.cljs` (NOT a re-merge candidate)

Superficially similar shape, but `tools/snapshot-pipeline.cljs` (164 L) has properties that justify its split:

1. **Multi-consumer:** consumed by `wire-pipeline.cljs` (the dispatcher) across THREE payload kinds, not just one tool.
2. **Independent tests:** 4 separate test files reach into its public fns:
   - `dedup_test.cljs` — `dedup-epochs-in-snapshot`
   - `diff_encode_epochs_test.cljs` — `diff-encode-epochs-in-snapshot`
   - `lazy_summary_test.cljs` — `resolve-slice-mode`, `summarise-other-slices-in-snapshot`
   - `path_slicing_test.cljs` — `slice-app-db-in-snapshot`
3. **Reusable seam:** the pure transforms are parameterised across multiple wire kinds.

`subscribe-emit` has none of those.

## Recommendation

**Re-merge `subscribe-emit.cljs` → `subscribe.cljs`.** Result: one 317-L file under one "streaming subscribe tool" concept. Reading the streaming-loop body top-down stays linear instead of bouncing between two files when state-shape (per rf2-w5etd) changes. Imports drop by one per consumer site. Tests don't need touching — they don't reach `subscribe-emit` directly.

The 250 L ceiling is a guideline; 317 L for one coherent MCP tool is well within the brief's framing.

## NOT in scope

Other pair2-mcp/tools/* leaves stand up to scrutiny — the per-tool layout (`eval_cljs.cljs` 21 L, `dispatch.cljs` 38 L, `unsubscribe.cljs` 24 L, etc.) is justified by the MCP `tools/list` catalogue mapping. Each tool ns IS one MCP-listed tool. The `descriptors-knobs` / `descriptors-data` / `descriptors` triangle is structurally required to break a circular require with `registry`.

## Sequencing notes

Isolated to `pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/`. Touches:
- `tools/subscribe.cljs` (absorb the 3 fns, drop the `:require`)
- `tools/subscribe-emit.cljs` (delete)
- `tools.cljs` docstring (one line listing the leaves)

No public API change — tests reach `subscribe-tool` only.

Parent rf2-zkca8: leaf-size discipline acknowledged that 'going over for cohesion is fine if the ns reads as one idea' — this is the canonical case.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1055. subscribe-emit.cljs folded back into subscribe.cljs (~315 L). Single-consumer helper; no independent test surface.

title: audit(ns-structure): machines — re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx is a façade-of-a-façade
description:
The audit found one structurally awkward shape in the machines artefact: `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.cljc` (93 L) is a façade that ONLY re-exports from its sub-leaves into the outer façade. The outer façade then re-exports the same names again. The intermediate hop adds no semantic value.

## Current shape

```
re-frame.machines              (240 L façade — public artefact surface)
  └── re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx           (93 L sub-façade)
        ├── 5 def re-exports from sub-leaves
        ├── 3 query fns (machines, machine-meta, machine-by-system-id)
        └── re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx.{registration,spawn,destroy,join,
                                            finalize,validation,teardown}
```

The flow: `re-frame.machines/reg-machine* → lifecycle-fx/reg-machine* → registration/reg-machine*`. Same name, two hops, two file opens.

## Findings

- `machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx.cljc` — 93 L. Contents:
  - 5 `def` re-exports (`create-machine-handler`, `reg-machine*`, `spawn-fx`, `invoke-all-init-fx`, `destroy-machine-fx`).
  - 3 query fns owned: `machines`, `machine-meta`, `machine-by-system-id` (per Spec 005 §Querying machines).
- Consumers of `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx`:
  - `re-frame.machines` (outer façade) — the only `:require` consumer.
  - `re-frame.machines.transition` — docstring references only, no `:require`.

The 3 query fns belong on the public artefact surface per Spec 005 §Querying machines; they're already re-exported from `re-frame.machines/{machines,machine-meta,machine-by-system-id}`.

## Recommendation

**Dissolve `re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx`:**

1. Move the 3 query fns (`machines`, `machine-meta`, `machine-by-system-id`) verbatim into `re-frame.machines.cljc`. The outer façade currently 240 L; adds ~30 L → ~270 L, marginally over guideline but defensibly one concept ("machines artefact public surface").
2. Replace the outer façade's 5 `def` re-exports through `lifecycle-fx` with direct reach to the sub-leaves:
   - `reg-machine*` ← `lifecycle-fx.registration`
   - `create-machine-handler` ← `lifecycle-fx.registration`
   - `spawn-fx` ← `lifecycle-fx.spawn`
   - `invoke-all-init-fx` ← `lifecycle-fx.spawn`
   - `destroy-machine-fx` ← `lifecycle-fx.destroy`
3. Update the 2 docstring references in `machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` (lines 17 + 810) to point at `re-frame.machines` or the concrete sub-leaves.
4. Delete `machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx.cljc`.

The 7 leaves under `machines/lifecycle_fx/` (registration, spawn, destroy, join, finalize, validation, teardown) stand — they're cohesive concerns each owning a Spec 005 surface.

## Alternative (lighter touch)

If 270 L on `re-frame.machines` reads as too much, leave `lifecycle_fx.cljc` in place but drop its 5 re-export defs (let the outer façade reach down to the lower siblings directly). The 3 query fns stay in a thin ~50-L `lifecycle-fx` ns. Less elegant but preserves directory shape.

## Sequencing notes

Isolated to machines artefact. Touches:
- `machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc` (re-export edits)
- `machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx.cljc` (delete or trim)
- `machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc` (2 docstring lines)

Tests should not need touching — the outer façade's public surface is unchanged.

Parent rf2-zkca8: this is symmetric cleanup to the leaf-size ceiling — a façade-of-a-façade is the opposite over-correction.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1045. re-frame.machines.lifecycle-fx dissolved (façade-of-a-façade): 3 query fns moved verbatim into re-frame.machines; 5 def re-exports replaced with direct reach to sub-leaves; file deleted. Docstring refs updated in transition.cljc, exit_cascade.cljc, trigger-handler test, Spec 009 emit-site table.

title: audit(ns-structure): ssr-ring — 9-leaf split has 2 single-consumer trivia worth folding back
description:
Audit run 2026-05-14 found ssr-ring's 9-way source split (per rf2-pjsrc) is the most over-eager wave from the recent leaf-size discipline sweep. Two of the nine leaves are single-consumer fragments that hurt more than they help. The test mirror is a single 842-L `ring_test.clj` — if the source concerns were genuinely disjoint, the tests would have followed the split. They didn't, because the concerns are sequential pipeline stages.

## Findings

- `ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/response.clj` — **28 L, 1 fn** (`ssr-response->ring-response`). Only consumers: `ring.clj` (façade) + `pipeline.clj`.
- `ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/handler_defaults.clj` — **45 L, 2 fns + 1 map** (`default-on-error`, `handler-defaults`, `validate-handler-opts!`). Only consumer: `ring.clj`.
- `ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj` — 114 L. Consumes `response`, `headers`, `lifecycle`, `payload`.
- `ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj` — 247 L façade.
- `ssr-ring/test/re_frame/ssr/ring_test.clj` — **842 L monolith** (no split mirroring).

## Recommendations

1. **Merge `response.clj` → `pipeline.clj`.** The single fn `ssr-response->ring-response` is called twice — once from `ring.clj`'s redirect short-circuit, once from `pipeline.clj`'s `build-full-response`. It belongs with the pipeline stages that surround it. Result: `pipeline.clj` grows from 114 → ~140 L, still well under ceiling. One fewer require + one fewer file open per consumer.

2. **Merge `handler-defaults.clj` → `ring.clj`.** The 45 L is one default-opts map (`handler-defaults`) + a default-error fn + a 13-L validator that `ring.clj` calls inline at handler construction. Result: `ring.clj` grows from 247 → ~292 L, marginally over the 250 L guideline but defensibly one concept ("handler constructor"). Consistent with the Spec 011 §HTTP response contract reading top-down.

3. **Leave the rest alone** — `cookie.clj` (102 L, RFC 6265 serialiser), `headers.clj` (65 L), `lifecycle.clj` (102 L), `payload.clj` (67 L), `pipeline.clj` (114 L), `shell.clj` (78 L) each cover a distinct Spec 011 concern with at least one cross-leaf consumer.

Net: leaves go 9 → 7. No public-API change (every external caller reaches `re-frame.ssr.ring/<name>` through the façade — internal merges are invisible).

## Sequencing notes

Isolated artefact, no blockers. Dispatchable to a background agent.
Touches: `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/{response,handler_defaults,pipeline,ring}.clj` and the one test file's `:require` block.

Parent rf2-zkca8 carried the leaf-size discipline; this is the symmetric cleanup pass.

title: audit(ssr): implementation/ssr test coverage + robustness
description:
# SSR Slice Audit

## Current status

- `implementation/ssr` is in strong shape on the JVM side. `clojure -M:test` passed with 82 tests, 267 assertions, 0 failures, and 0 errors.
- Slice-local CLJS coverage exists for SSR hash parity. `shadow-cljs compile node-test` plus `node out/node-test.js` passed; that broader node-test run included `re-frame.ssr.hash-parity-cljs-test` and finished green with 1816 tests, 5040 assertions, 0 failures, and 0 errors.
- The slice has good breadth across conformance, end-to-end SSR lifecycle, head/meta, request cofx, teardown hygiene, late-bind absence, and JVM↔CLJS parity checks.

## What is well covered

- The SSR conformance gate is meaningful, not ceremonial. `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_conformance_test.clj` runs all ten `ssr-*.edn` fixtures and they all passed: render-to-string, hydrate, hydration mismatch, head emits, head hydration, cookie, redirect, set-status, known error mapping, and error sanitisation.
- `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_end_to_end_test.clj` gives strong lifecycle coverage: request bootstrap, server render, payload build, client hydrate, mismatch detection, response status/header/cookie behavior, redirect short-circuit, default/custom error projectors, bad-projector fallback, head hash mismatch, and install/default-response helpers.
- Head/meta coverage is strong. `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_head_test.clj` exercises `reg-head`, `render-head`, `active-head`, default fallback, snapshot isolation/cleanup, canonical HTML ordering, escaping, JSON-LD emission, and missing-head failure.
- Request-slot and teardown hygiene are well covered. `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_request_cofx_test.clj` and `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_teardown_load_test.clj` cover cofx registration, server/client platform behavior, multi-frame isolation, explicit override injection, repeated cleanup of request/response/error side channels, and leak resistance under a 2000-request load test.
- Cross-runtime parity and split-artefact seams are pinned well. `hash_parity_test.clj`, `ssr_hash_test.clj`, `source_coord_parity_test.clj`, `ssr_source_coord_test.clj`, `late_bind_missing_test.clj`, and `test/re_frame/ssr/hash_parity_cljs_test.cljs` cover JVM↔CLJS hash parity, source-coord formatting parity, nil-pruning invariants, and the documented missing-artefact errors on the `re-frame.core` re-exports.

## Robustness risks / coverage gaps

- The positive `:rf.ssr/compatibility-check-skipped` path is not actually pinned. `implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_compatibility_checks_test.clj` only drives the explicit `{:expected ... :actual ...}` form, so the scalar lookup path and missing-hook behavior in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc` are still untested.
- Redirect precedence is only partially covered. Current tests prove redirect short-circuiting and multi-redirect last-write-wins, but there is no slice-local test for `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/error_listener.cljc` preserving an existing redirect status when an error is buffered later in the same request.
- Redirect normalization accepts `:location`, `:url`, or `:to`, but the suite only exercises `:location`. That leaves a small public-API regression window in `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc`.
- The public `ssr/adapter` surface is only covered indirectly through the shared test fixture. There is no direct assertion on the adapter contract itself, especially the deliberate `:render` failure path for headless SSR.

## Actionable insights

- Add scalar-form compatibility tests for `:rf.ssr/check-version` and `:rf.ssr/check-schema-digest`, including a missing-hook case that must emit `:rf.ssr/compatibility-check-skipped`.
- Add one redirect-plus-error test that seeds a redirect, buffers an error, then reads the response and asserts projector drain does not overwrite the redirect status.
- Add one small redirect-alias test covering `{:url ...}` and `{:to ...}` normalization to `:location`.
- Add one direct `ssr/adapter` smoke test that proves `:render-to-string` is installed and `:render` throws `:rf.error/render-on-headless-adapter`.

  - result: 82 tests, 267 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors

title: audit(flows): implementation/flows test coverage + robustness
description:
# Flows Slice Audit
## Current status
- `implementation/flows` test alias passed cleanly: `37` tests, `138` assertions, `0` failures, `0` errors.
- The slice-local conformance gate ran all six `flow-*.edn` fixtures and passed all six.
- I found one concrete `clear-flow` robustness defect by direct runtime repro, plus one slice-local coverage gap worth tightening.

## What is well covered
- Registration and validation are covered well: required keys, malformed `:inputs`/`:path`, cycle detection, cycle-path shape, and replacement-that-would-introduce-a-cycle.
- Runtime behavior is covered well: recompute on input change, skip on `=`-equal rewrites, topo ordering, hot-reload recompute, `:rf.fx/reg-flow` / `:rf.fx/clear-flow`, and late-bind missing-artefact errors.
- Trace coverage is strong: `:rf.flow/registered`, `:rf.flow/computed`, `:rf.flow/skip`, `:rf.flow/cleared`, and `:rf.flow/failed` all have direct assertions, and the slice-local conformance runner checks the flow fixtures end to end.

## Robustness risks / coverage gaps
- `clear-flow`'s nested-path branch in `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:178-185` is not robust when the output path was never materialized. Repro: register a flow with `:path [:step-2 :result]`, clear it before any drain, and app-db becomes `{:step-2 nil}`. Current slice tests only clear nested paths after the flow has already written its output (`implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:71-112`, `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj:566-595`), so this case is not covered.
- The same branch throws on non-map intermediates. Repro: app-db `{:step-2 1 :foo 3 :bar 4}`, flow path `[:step-2 :result]`, then `clear-flow` throws `ClassCastException`. There is no slice-local regression for this.
- Explicit frame scoping is only covered outside the slice. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/smoke_test.clj:180-229` does verify same-id-across-frames behavior, but `implementation/flows`' own test alias does not pin `{:frame ...}` registration/clear semantics.

## Actionable insights
- Harden `clear-flow` at `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:178-185` with a safe nested dissoc helper. It should leave app-db unchanged when the output path was never materialized, avoid creating `nil` parents, and treat non-map intermediates as a no-op instead of throwing.
- Add two slice-local regressions in `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj`: one for clearing a nested-path flow before its first compute, and one for clearing when the parent path currently holds a scalar.
- Add one minimal slice-local frame-scoping test for `{:frame ...}` registration/clear behavior. The contract already has cross-artefact coverage in core, but the flows artefact should not rely on another slice's smoke test for its own gate.

## Commands checked
- `bd prime`
- `rg --files implementation/flows .claude`
- `rg -n "flows|implementation/flows" -S .`
- `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/flows`

title: audit(ssr-ring): implementation/ssr-ring test coverage + robustness
description:
# SSR-Ring Slice Audit

## Current status

- `implementation/ssr-ring` has a focused JVM test suite and it currently passes: `clojure -M:test` ran 19 tests, 80 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors.
- Coverage is strongest at the public adapter level: request lifecycle, render flow, redirects, cookies, payload privacy, request cofx wiring, title sourcing, and the main regression fixes are all exercised end to end.
- Confidence drops on a few slice-local helper and failure seams. Most remaining risk is not “core flow is untested”; it is “defensive branches and output-hardening paths are lightly pinned or currently flawed.”

## What is well covered

- End-to-end `ssr-handler` happy-path rendering is covered for status, HTML body, content type, payload script presence, and render-hash emission.
- Per-request lifecycle is covered for frame create/destroy, request-slot cleanup, and request-slot isolation across sequential requests.
- Redirect short-circuiting is covered, including empty-body behavior and `Location` header materialisation.
- Cookie materialisation is covered for common attributes and multi-cookie `Set-Cookie` emission.
- Error handling is covered for render-time failure with both the default `:on-error` and a custom override.
- The `rf2-6t36h` regression is well pinned: fn-form `:root-view` is asserted to run exactly once, and the wire hash is asserted to match the payload hash.
- Payload privacy is covered well for the `rf2-jbcmt` boundary: response accumulator data stays out of hydration payloads while still reaching response headers.
- Route/head title behavior is covered well for “head supplies title”, “default head”, and “head with no title”.
- Middleware fall-through is covered for a custom `:match?` predicate.

## Robustness risks / coverage gaps

- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj` injects `payload-edn` raw into `<script id="__rf_payload" type="application/edn">...</script>`. There is no escaping or regression test for payload strings containing `</script>` or similar parser-breaking content. If user-controlled data reaches `app-db`, this is a real XSS / broken-markup risk, not just a missing test.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/headers.clj` documents `ensure-content-type` as case-insensitive, but it only checks `"content-type"` and `"Content-Type"`. A mixed-case existing header such as `"CONTENT-TYPE"` or `"CoNtEnT-TyPe"` would currently duplicate the header instead of preserving it. The suite does not cover that case.
- The suite covers render-time failure, but not setup-time failure in `setup-request-frame!` (`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj`). There is no direct proof that an exception during `:on-create` / `reg-frame` cleanup leaves no leaked frame or request slot and still routes through `:on-error`.
- Invalid-option defensive paths are untested: missing required opts at handler construction, invalid `:root-view` shape, invalid `:on-create` shape, cookie `:expires` validation, and payload version/schema-digest wiring.
- `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj` says `resolve-head-html` degrades to `""` while “the trace surface still carries the throw,” but the implementation just catches and returns `""` with no trace emission. There is no test covering a broken head function, so this is currently either silent-loss observability or stale documentation.

## Actionable insights

- Highest priority: harden `default-html-shell` so hydration payloads cannot break out of the `__rf_payload` script tag. Then add a regression test with payload content containing `</script>` and `<script>`.
- Fix `ensure-content-type` to normalize header names case-insensitively before checking for an existing content type, and add one test using a mixed-case preexisting header.
- Add one setup-failure test where `:on-create` throws. Assert all three outcomes: caller gets the `:on-error` response, the frame registry does not retain the per-request frame, and `ssr/get-request` returns `nil` for the captured frame id.
- Decide the intended contract for head-resolution failures. If silent fallback is intended, tighten the docstring and add a test. If observability is intended, emit a trace from `resolve-head-html` and add a test for that trace.
- Add small helper-level tests for `resolve-version` / `:schema-digest`, invalid `:root-view`, invalid `:on-create`, and cookie `:expires`. Those are cheap tests and would pin the remaining defensive logic without much harness work.

title: audit(http): implementation/http test coverage + robustness
description:
# HTTP Slice Audit

## Current status

- `implementation/http` is well covered on the JVM side. `clojure -M:test` passed with 136 tests, 385 assertions, 0 failures, and 0 errors.
- The slice has strong coverage for the managed HTTP happy path and major failure paths on JVM, plus good coverage for privacy, interceptor behavior, actor-destroy cancellation, machine-wrapper behavior, helper shapes, and the late-bind missing-artefact seam.
- Confidence is materially lower for slice-local CLJS transport behavior. The CLJS tests in this slice are mostly smoke/regression checks for helper shape, interceptor registry behavior, and wrapper registration, not direct transport-path tests.

## What is well covered

- Transport classification on JVM is exercised for `:rf.http/http-4xx`, `:rf.http/http-5xx`, `:rf.http/transport`, `:rf.http/timeout`, `:rf.http/aborted`, and the "status before decode" rule. See `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_test.clj`.
- Retry and abort behavior are covered for retry exhaustion, retry recovery, request-id abort, supersede suppression of `:on-failure`, supersede trace emission, and non-superseded abort reply behavior. See `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_test.clj`.
- Actor-destroy cancellation is covered well, including single-child cancellation, multiple in-flight requests under one actor, sibling isolation, direct non-actor dispatch not being cancellable via actor-destroy, and `:after`-driven cancellation. See `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_actor_destroy_cancellation_test.clj`.
- Machine-wrapper behavior is covered on JVM for success, failure, parent-driven cancellation, `:after` composition, and coexistence of the wrapper machine with the ordinary fx surface. CLJS smoke coverage also exists for wrapper registration and spawn-time wiring. See `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_machine_test.clj` and `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_machine_cljs_test.cljs`.
- Privacy/redaction coverage is strong on the failure/trace side: header denylist, query-param denylist, app-extended denylist, effective `:sensitive?` calculation, request/failure redaction helpers, and end-to-end trace stamping/redaction against a real JVM server. See `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_privacy_test.clj` and `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_privacy_integration_test.clj`.
- Interceptor behavior is well covered on JVM for transform-to-wire, ordering, frame scoping, throwing interceptors, single clear, bulk clear, replacement-in-place, and registry isolation. CLJS smoke tests cover registry semantics and late-bind publication. See `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_test.clj` and `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_cljs_test.cljs`.
- Call-site helper coverage is strong for pure shape on both CLJ and CLJS, plus canned-fx integration on JVM. See `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_test.clj`, `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_cljs_test.cljs`, and `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_helpers_integration_test.clj`.
- The missing-artefact late-bind contract is pinned for the stub-helper re-exports. See `implementation/http/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj`.

## Robustness risks / coverage gaps

- The `:accept` pipeline is barely pinned end-to-end. Current slice tests only prove helper pass-through of `:accept` and unit redaction of `:rf.http/accept-failure` detail. There is no slice-local test that exercises:
  - a custom `:accept` returning `{:failure ...}` and landing in `finalise-success!`
  - a malformed `:accept` return shape
  - an `:accept` function that throws
- Several decode branches remain weakly covered:
  - no Malli decode success path
  - no Malli schema-validation-failure path
  - no slice-local assertion on `:rf.warning/decode-defaulted`
  - no direct test of `re-frame.util-json` JVM fallback behavior when Cheshire is unavailable
- Retry coverage is good at the main behavior level but light on edge branches:
  - no proof that `:rf.http/aborted` is never retried even if included in `:retry :on`
  - no test of `:rf.http/retry-attempt` trace payloads, including final `:next-backoff-ms nil`
  - no test that thunk request bodies are re-realised on every retry attempt rather than only once
- Reader-conditional CLJS transport branches are not pinned inside this slice:
  - no slice-local tests for `cljs-fetch`
  - no slice-local tests for `classify-cljs-error` timeout vs abort vs transport
  - no slice-local tests for external `:abort-signal` vs internally created `AbortController`
  - no slice-local tests for CLJS timeout race behavior
- A few JVM defensive branches are also untested:
  - `check-cljs-only-keys!` warning emission on JVM
  - `handle-response!` fallback branch for non-2xx/non-4xx/non-5xx statuses such as 1xx/3xx
  - interceptor `:before` returning a non-map ctx, which is a different failure mode from throwing

## Actionable insights

- Highest-value next additions are end-to-end `:accept` tests. They close the largest behavioral gap with the least new harness work because the JVM managed-request test server already exists.
- Add one schema-decode success test and one schema-validation-failure test against `decode-response-body` or the managed JVM path. That would pin the Malli branch instead of only the thrown-decoder branch.
- Add one retry trace test and one "aborted is not retried" test. Those directly defend the control-flow promises implemented in `maybe-retry!`.
- Add one JVM test for `check-cljs-only-keys!` trace emission and one middleware test where a valid interceptor returns a non-map. Both are cheap and target real defensive branches.
- If slice-local CLJS confidence matters, add one dedicated CLJS transport test file under `implementation/http/test` that stubs `js/fetch` and drives timeout, abort, and transport-classification behavior. Right now those branches are not locally pinned.

## Commands checked

- `bd prime`
- `rg --files implementation/http`
- `git status --short`
- `rg -n "transport|classif|accept|decode|retry|abort|cancel|privacy|redact|clj|cljs|reader|json|late-bind" implementation/http/src implementation/http/test`
- `Get-Content implementation/http/deps.edn`
- `rg -n "deftest|testing|is " implementation/http/test`
- `rg -n "^\\(deftest|classif|decode|accept|retry|abort|timeout|supersede|cljs-only|privacy|redact|abort-signal|fetch|transport|machine|actor|destroy|request-id" implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_cljs_test.cljs implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_interceptors_cljs_test.cljs implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_privacy_integration_test.clj implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_helpers_integration_test.clj implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_actor_destroy_cancellation_test.clj implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_machine_test.clj implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_machine_cljs_test.cljs`

- `rg -n "retry-attempt|decode-defaulted|cljs-only-key-ignored-on-jvm|aborted-on-actor-destroy|http-interceptor-failed|accept-failure" implementation/http/test/re_frame`
- `rg -n "json-stringify|json-parse|params->query|merge-params|encode-body|compute-backoff-ms|realise-body|build-reply-event|resolve-origin-event" implementation/http/test/re_frame`
- `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/http`
  - result: 136 tests, 385 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors

close_reason: Audit complete. All findings are test-coverage gaps (no embedded correctness bugs), catalogued in bead description. Findings remain discoverable for any future http test-coverage batch. Specific gap clusters: :accept pipeline, Malli decode branches, retry edge cases, CLJS transport reader-conditionals, JVM defensive branches. title: audit(routing): implementation/routing test coverage + robustness
description:
1. Current status
- JVM slice tests pass: 28 tests, 110 assertions, 0 failures.
- The slice has decent smoke coverage for navigation flow, pending-nav continue/cancel, stale-nav suppression, scroll metadata/fx, route-link SSR/CLJS behavior, and late-bind missing-artefact errors.
- The main weakness is not obvious breakage but fragile behavior in route ranking and URL parsing that is only lightly or indirectly pinned.

2. What is well covered
- End-to-end navigation writes to `:rf/route`, including `:rf.route/navigate`, `:rf/url-requested`, `:rf/url-changed`, and `:rf.route/handle-url-change` happy paths.
- Pending-navigation protocol is covered for block, cancel, and continue.
- Nav-token stale-result suppression is covered for old-token suppressed / current-token accepted.
- Scroll metadata and emitted `:rf.nav/scroll` args are covered, plus pure scroll-position helpers and storage shape.
- Route-link coverage is good across JVM SSR href synthesis and CLJS click interception/modifier-key behavior.
- Late-bind failure contracts for missing routing artefact are pinned.

3. Robustness risks / coverage gaps
- No slice-local tests pin the route ranking algorithm directly (`compute-rank` / registration-order tie-break / equal-score warning). This is the most fragile unpinned area.
- Query parsing/coercion is only partially pinned: there are tests for repeated keys and empty values, but not for `:query-defaults`, schema coercion of `:int` / `:keyword` / `:boolean`, query key order preservation, or malformed percent-encoding.
- Fragment handling is only indirectly covered via scroll args; there is no test that fragment-only `:rf/url-changed` updates `:fragment` without re-firing `:on-match` or allocating a new nav-token.
- Multi-frame risks are mostly asserted at the pure-helper level only. There are no slice-local tests proving frame-isolated nav-token counters, pending-nav counters, or `:can-leave` / `route-link` dispatch landing in the intended frame.
- `:rf.route/continue` ignores the supplied pending-nav id and resumes whatever is in `:rf/pending-navigation`; current tests do not pin or challenge that behavior.
- `:rf.route/navigate` catches route-url failures and falls back to `/`; there is no test pinning that fallback or its consequences for bad route ids / missing params.
- Framework-shipped route subs (`:rf/route`, `:rf.route/id`, `:rf.route/params`, `:rf.route/query`, `:rf.route/transition`, `:rf.route/error`) are registered but untested in this slice.

4. Actionable insights
- Add direct ranking tests for overlapping static/named/splat/optional/catch-all routes, plus registration-order tie-breaks and `:rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score` emission.
- Add focused `match-url` / `route-url` tests for query coercion/defaults, key-order round trips, optional-group emission/elision, splat precedence, and malformed URL input.
- Add an event-level fragment-only navigation test that proves no `:on-match` dispatch and no nav-token bump.
- Add multi-frame tests that exercise separate frame dbs through real events, especially for nav-token allocation, pending-nav ids, and `:can-leave` resolution.
- Decide whether `:rf.route/continue` should validate its `_pn-id`; if yes, add tests before tightening behavior, and if no, document the intentional ignore.

5. What I actually checked
- Files read: `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc`, `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/routing_test.clj`, `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_test.clj`, `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/route_link_cljs_test.cljs`, `implementation/routing/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj`, `implementation/routing/deps.edn`.
- Commands run: `bd prime`, `git status --short`, `rg --files implementation/routing`, targeted `rg -n` searches over source/tests, and `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/routing`.
close_reason: Audit complete. Findings text catalogued in bead description (routing ranking + query-coercion test gaps). No embedded correctness bugs in current findings. Specific gap clusters listed for follow-on bead-filing. Same pattern as rf2-dvnop, rf2-76a52 closures.

title: audit(machines): implementation/machines test coverage + robustness
description:
1. Current status
- Slice looks healthy overall. I reviewed the implementation and ran a focused JVM test set plus the machines Mode B conformance runner.
- Result: `72 tests / 231 assertions` passed, and the machines conformance runner reported `36/36` runnable fixtures passing.
- Coverage is strong around final-state teardown, single `:invoke`, core `:invoke-all` join modes, timer epoch handling, and snapshot/tag/parallel shape.

2. What is well covered
- Finalization / teardown: `test/re_frame/final_state_cljs_test.cljc` pins `:final?`, `:on-done`, `:output-key`, synchronous auto-destroy/unregister, `:rf.machine/destroyed` reason tagging, singleton symmetry, and `:system-id` release ordering.
- Single `:invoke`: `test/re_frame/spawn_registry_test.clj`, `test/re_frame/invoke_data_fn_form_test.clj`, `test/re_frame/initial_entry_test.clj`, and the CLJS invoke tests cover runtime spawn-slot tracking, cleanup on exit, keyword-destroy back-compat, `:data` fn-form materialisation, and bootstrap/entry behavior.
- `:invoke-all`: `test/re_frame/invoke_all_test.clj`, `test/re_frame/machine_transition_purity_test.clj`, and the conformance runner cover `:all`, `:any`, `{:n N}`, `{:fn pred}`, validation failures, and deterministic counter allocation.
- Timers / `:after`: `test/re_frame/after_test.clj`, `test/re_frame/timer_frame_scope_test.clj`, CLJS `machines_cljs_test.cljs`, and conformance cover literal/fn/sub delay smoke, stale detection, guard suppression, invoke-bearing `:after`, frame-scoped timer tables, and frame/reset teardown.
- Snapshot compatibility: `test/re_frame/tags_test.clj`, `test/re_frame/parallel_test.clj`, and conformance round-trips cover `:tags` union/elision, parallel `:state` map shape, `pr-str`/`read-string` round-trip, and storage at `[:rf/machines <id>]`.

3. Robustness risks / coverage gaps
- Dynamic sub-driven `:after` re-resolution is not directly pinned. `src/re_frame/machines/timer.cljc` implements `on-sub-changed!`, `:rf.machine.timer/cancelled-on-resolution`, and watcher-based rescheduling, but I did not find a test that changes the subscribed delay value and proves cancel/reschedule/cleanup behavior.
- Finalization recovery branches are under-tested. `src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/finalize.cljc` explicitly handles thrown `:on-done` callbacks and missing parent snapshots, but the tests exercise only the happy path / optional `:on-done` path.
- Unresolved `:invoke-all` exit teardown is not directly pinned. Source supports tracked destroy via `{:rf/invoke-all true}` for leaving an `:invoke-all` state before join resolution, while existing tests focus on resolution-time cancellation.
- Join-edge behavior is thin around post-resolution late completions and `:cancel-on-decision? false`. `src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/join.cljc` has dedicated logic for both branches, but I did not find tests that would catch double-dispatch / over-cancel regressions there.

4. Actionable insights
- Add one test that changes a subscription-backed delay while the state stays active, then assert `:cancelled-on-resolution`, a fresh scheduled delay, and watcher/timer cleanup on state exit or frame destroy.
- Add final-state tests for `:on-done` throwing and for child completion after the parent snapshot is already gone; assert error trace + child teardown still happen.
- Add an `:invoke-all` parent-exit test that leaves the invoke-all state before resolution and asserts all children plus the join-state slot are torn down.
- Add join-edge tests for late completion after resolution and `:cancel-on-decision? false`.

5. What I actually checked

- Commands run:
  - `bd prime`
  - `rg --files implementation/machines`

title: audit(schemas): implementation/schemas test coverage + robustness
description:

The slice-local JVM suite passed cleanly: 133 tests / 383 assertions / 0 failures, including the schemas conformance runner with all 5 schema fixtures passing. App-db schema frame scoping, digest stability, printer swapping, late-bind missing-artefact defaults, and JVM digest parity are also directly tested.

I also did not find a test that locks the documented stale-schema declaration behaviour after a schema stops claiming a previously populated `:large?` or `:sensitive?` path. Add a declaration-lifecycle test that proves whether stale schema-derived elision/sensitive entries intentionally persist after schema flag removal or path removal. title: audit(adapters): implementation/adapters test coverage + robustness
description:

- `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim` has the deepest substrate-internal lifecycle coverage, but the actual `re-frame.adapter.reagent-slim` wiring is much thinner than the classic Reagent adapter.
- JVM coverage is effectively absent for `reagent`, `uix`, and `helix`; `reagent-slim` has a small JVM-only macro/classification suite.

The slice strongly tests `reagent2` internals, but `re-frame.adapter.reagent-slim` itself mostly has structural/current-component checks; `reagent_slim_cljs_test.cljs` explicitly punts on the true `render-to-string` failure path and real render-path assertions.

- For reagent-slim, add a small set of re-frame integration ports (runtime/routing/provider/render parity) so the adapter wiring is tested above the `reagent2` substrate layer, not just the substrate internals.

title: audit(epoch): implementation/epoch test coverage + robustness
description:
## Current status
- `implementation/epoch` has a substantial dedicated JVM test namespace and the slice-local test run is currently green: `clojure -M:test` passed with 62 tests / 244 assertions.
- The source reads as intentionally defensive around restore/reset preconditions, trace-leak prevention, and destroyed-frame listener silencing.

## What is well covered
- Ring-buffer basics are well pinned: one-record-per-settle, multi-event cascade collapsing, per-frame isolation, FIFO eviction at configured depth, depth-0 no-recording, and partial-drain discard.
- Restore coverage is strong: happy path, unknown frame, unknown epoch, schema mismatch, missing route/machine handler, non-machine event disambiguation, version mismatch, during-drain rejection, and downstream effects on subs/flows/routes/frame isolation.
- Reset coverage is strong: container replacement, synthetic undo epoch, trace emission, listener fanout, unknown frame, during-drain rejection, schema mismatch, no-schema permissiveness, subscription updates, missing-artefact behavior, and no trace leakage into the next cascade.
- Listener lifecycle coverage is also strong: fire-per-settle, same-key replacement, removal, exception isolation, destroyed-frame silencing, one-shot silencing, re-arm after re-registration, and direct `on-frame-destroyed!` / `clear-frame-history!` seams.

## Robustness risks / coverage gaps
- `configure!` documents `:depth` as a non-negative integer, but it accepts and stores any value. That means `nil` or non-numeric values can survive configuration and later explode when `record!` calls `pos?` on the stored depth, instead of failing fast at the config boundary.
- Slice-local coverage does not actually pin prod/dev gating. The namespace is `cljc`, but this artefact only has JVM tests here; there is no slice-local test proving `interop/debug-enabled?` false-path behavior or Closure dead-code-elision in production builds.
- There is no test that combines ring-buffer eviction with restore, e.g. proving an evicted epoch deterministically fails as `:rf.epoch/restore-unknown-epoch` after truncation.
- The docs say depth `0` disables recording while assembled records can still reach listeners, but there is no explicit test for that listener-with-depth-0 behavior.
- Rejected restore/reset paths are checked for app-db stability and trace emission, but the tests do not explicitly pin that those failures also avoid listener fanout and avoid mutating epoch history.

## Actionable insights
- Validate or sanitize `:depth` in `configure!`, then add explicit tests for `nil`, non-numeric, and negative depth inputs.
- Add one slice-local gate test strategy for `interop/debug-enabled?` false behavior, or cover it in a CLJS/advanced-build path if that is the only meaningful place to prove production elision.
- Add a restore-after-eviction test and a depth-0-listener test to close the most obvious ring-buffer semantics gaps.
- Add explicit assertions that rejected restore/reset attempts do not append history and do not notify epoch listeners.

## What I actually checked
- Files read: `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc`, `implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj`, `implementation/epoch/deps.edn`.
- Commands run: `bd prime`, `bd search "audit(epoch): implementation/epoch test coverage + robustness"`, `rg --files implementation/epoch`, targeted `rg -n` searches across the slice, `git status --short`, `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/epoch`, and a small `clojure -M -e` check confirming `pos?` throws on `nil` / non-numeric values.

title: spec(flows): reconcile multi-frame flows with the public registrar query model
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: spec weakness.
Spec 013 allows the same flow id to exist independently on multiple frames, but the public registrar query model is still effectively `id -> metadata`.
Implementation: per-frame runtime flow definitions are stored correctly, but the public `:flow` registrar entry is last-registration-wins across frames.

Preserve: the per-frame runtime registry and the current cleanup rule that only unregisters when the last frame releases the id.

Options:
1. Add a frame-aware flow query surface, e.g. `flow-meta` / `flows` by frame.
2. Change `:flow` registrar storage to a frame-indexed metadata shape.
3. Narrow the spec to forbid same flow ids across frames if public query must stay `id -> metadata`.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1007 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1007) — refactor(flows) round-2 polish batch.

title: fix(adapters): differentiate disposed-adapter from never-installed state
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: post-dispose adapter calls must distinguish `adapter disposed` from `no adapter installed`.
Implementation: `dispose-adapter!` resets the install slot to `nil`, so subsequent calls raise `:rf.error/no-adapter-installed` and lose that distinction.

Preserve: clearing the install slot so a fresh adapter can be reinstalled.

Options:
1. Introduce a disposed sentinel distinct from `nil`.
2. Retain last-disposed state until the next successful install and throw `:rf.error/adapter-disposed`.
3. If the simpler behavior is intentional, weaken the spec explicitly.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1041 — adapters shared batch cluster

title: fix(schemas): prune stale schema-derived elision declarations on re-registration
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: current schema-derived elision declarations are authoritative after re-registration.
Implementation: schema-walk feeding only overwrites paths still present in the new schema, so stale `:source :schema` `:large?` / `:sensitive?` entries persist after the flag is removed.

Preserve: declared entries still override schema entries, and schema-source hints already refresh cleanly on hot reload.

Options:
1. Recompute the schema-derived map and replace only the `:source :schema` subset wholesale.
2. Prune orphaned schema-source paths before merging new declarations.
3. Keep `:source :declared` untouched while deleting only schema-derived keys no longer claimed.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1006

title: fix(core): align rf/handlers predicate contract with metadata-only spec
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: `rf/handlers` filter predicate is applied to each metadata map.
Implementation: registrar calls the predicate as `(pred-fn id meta)`, so a unary predicate written to spec arity-fails, while code written to current behavior is not portable.

Preserve: id-aware filtering is still useful.

Options:
1. Change the implementation to unary metadata.
2. Support both 1-arg and 2-arg predicates, with unary as canonical.
3. Add a separate id-aware query surface if the richer filter is still wanted.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1009 — handlers predicate now metadata-only (unary) per spec; test updated.

title: fix(core): emit :rf.registry/handler-replaced on every re-registration
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: Spec 001 / Spec 009 require `:rf.registry/handler-replaced` on every re-registration.
Implementation: registrar only emits when `:handler-fn` identity changes, so kinds like `:frame` never emit the required event on re-registration.

Preserve: current `:different-fn?` distinction as data for tooling.

Options:
1. Always emit on slot replacement.
2. Keep `:different-fn?` in tags so tooling can suppress idempotent reload noise.
3. If needed, add a second advisory event for true fn-identity changes.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #1009 — :rf.registry/handler-replaced now fires on every re-registration; :different-fn? preserved in tags.

title: spec(machines): normalize invoke-all join-state shape in Spec 005
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: spec weakness.
Spec: Spec 005 alternates between two incompatible `:invoke-all` join-state shapes: direct map at `[:rf/spawned <parent> <invoke-id>]` vs nested `:join` state below that slot.
Implementation and tests currently use the direct-slot map.

Why it matters:
- This is a real portability/conformance problem for non-reference implementations.
- Useful current behavior to preserve: runtime-owned bookkeeping under `:rf/spawned`, map-vs-keyword disambiguation, and lazy cleanup on exit.

Options:
1. Bless the direct-slot map and rewrite all `:join` path references in Spec 005.
2. Bless nested `:join` and update implementation/tests to match.
3. If read-tolerance is desired, specify one canonical write shape and one permissive read shape explicitly.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1045. DECISION (pre-alpha): bless direct-map shape — Spec 005 rewritten to match the implementation + tests (already direct-map); nested :join references dropped. Map-vs-keyword disambiguation at the destroy site handles single-invoke vs invoke-all split. Also corrected stale :rf.warning/* -> :rf.error/* spellings of machine-state-not-in-definition and machine-snapshot-version-mismatch.

title: fix(machines): add snapshot compatibility checks at handler entry
description:
Confirmed by the spec-vs-implementation audit.

Class: implementation drift.
Spec: Spec 005 snapshot compatibility and warning behavior.
Implementation: machine handler entry only distinguishes bootstrap vs existing snapshot; it does not verify that the snapshot state still exists in the current definition or that snapshot version matches `:meta :rf/snapshot-version`.

Why it matters:
- Re-registration / restore can keep driving incompatible snapshots without the spec's warning and fallback behavior.
- Useful current behavior to preserve: snapshot-as-value restore with no init replay, and unchanged behavior for already-compatible snapshots.

Options:
1. Add a pre-step reconcile helper in `create-machine-handler`.
2. Reset missing states to the new `:initial` and emit `:rf.warning/machine-state-not-in-definition`.
3. Compare snapshot/definition versions and emit `:rf.warning/machine-snapshot-version-mismatch` before stepping.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1045. DECISION (pre-alpha): combined Options 1+2+3 — single pre-step reconciler inside prepare-machine-ctx. Version check first, then state-resolves-in-definition. Reset replaces snapshot with fresh initial + :rf/bootstrap-pending? true so :entry fires same handler call. Parallel-region machines: every region's path must resolve. Independent from rf2-ujhzw. Test file added: snapshot_compat_test.clj.

title: Causa shell: reg-view-wrap panels for immediate reactive trace-buffer updates
description:
Follow-on from rf2-e9s81 (which reverted rf2-iw5ym's app-db mirror because :rf/causa cannot be registered at preload time and chain-resolving to :rf/default polluted the host app-db / consumed drain-depth headroom).

Current state: :rf.causa/trace-buffer is a layer-1 sub thunking trace-bus/buffer (the process-global atom). Visible trace-panel update lag is bounded by the host's next dispatch, which is fine for trace-rate UI cadence on every shipped example but NOT the architecturally clean shape — the framework's plain-fn warning fires for every Causa panel (subscribe / dispatch route to :rf/default instead of the surrounding :rf/causa frame).

## What to do

Two paths land the architecturally-correct shape:

1. **reg-view-wrap shell panels + lazy-register :rf/causa at mount.** Convert every Causa panel view to reg-view so subscribes carry the :rf/causa frame via React context. Requires :rf/causa to be a real frame — lazy-register from mount.cljs after rf/init! has installed the substrate adapter (the preload runs too early; mount fires on the Ctrl+Shift+C keypress, well after init!). With :rf/causa registered + panels routing subs through React context, the trace-buffer sub re-fires on Causa-side app-db changes; combine with rf2-iw5ym-style :rf.causa/note-trace-event dispatches and panels re-render IMMEDIATELY on every push.

2. **Fixed-frame sub mechanism.** Introduce a sub signal source that lets a sub read from an arbitrary frame's app-db independent of the subscriber's frame. Heavy framework surface change; defer unless path 1 turns out to have other gaps.

## Surface

Path 1 touches at least:
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/shell.cljs (top_strip, sidebar, canvas, bottom_rail)
- tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/mount.cljs (lazy reg-frame after init!)
- 11 panel view files (event-detail, time-travel, app-db-diff, causality-graph, trace, machines, flows, routes, performance, issues, schemas, hydration, mcp-server, copilot — pick the 11 surfaced by the plain-fn warnings)

Estimated >15 files, 200-400 LoC.

## Notes

This is the masterpiece-grade fix the e9s81 escalation called out; the revert is the minimum-viable spike that gets the regression test green. Tackle this when the framework's reg-view + React-context tier is stable enough to absorb the migration.
close_reason: Resolved by PR #1064 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1064. Wired Causa shell + 16 panels through reg-view; lazy-registered :rf/causa from mount.cljs/open!; restored iw5ym-style mirror dispatch from collect-trace! so :rf.causa/trace-buffer sub re-fires on standard app-db-write reactive path. 22 files, +532/-164 LoC. Tests: 518 JVM + 1923 CLJS green; perf-bundle PASS.

title: refactor(adapters): switch make-derived-value prev-state atom to volatile (Helix + UIx)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-w0u2w. **Findings doc:** `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-helix-2026-05-14.md` §P-2.

## Problem

`make-derived-value` in both `adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs:96` and `adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:92` creates a `prev-state` atom (line 96) that is only ever read once and written once inside the watch callback (lines 100-105):

```clojure
(let [prev-state (atom (recompute))]
  ...
  (add-watch s k
    (fn [_ _ _ _]
      (let [new-derived (recompute)
            prev-derived @prev-state]
        (reset! prev-state new-derived)
        (notify prev-derived new-derived)))))
```

No reader outside the watch callback sees `prev-state`. The atom's CAS / lock cost is wasted; a volatile suffices.

## Recommendation

Switch `prev-state` to `(volatile! ...)` with `vreset!` / `@` — same single-thread semantics, no CAS. Apply in both Helix and UIx. Fold under the rf2-3vwbx helpers extraction if that lands first (the shared helper would just use a volatile from the start).

## Severity

P2 — micro-perf.

## Coordination

If rf2-3vwbx merges first, this change folds into the helpers extraction.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1041 — adapters shared batch cluster

title: refactor(adapters): drop dead #js {} in inject-source-coord-attr + cover existing-attr passthrough (Helix + UIx)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-w0u2w. **Findings doc:** `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-helix-2026-05-14.md` §T-4.

## Problem

`inject-source-coord-attr` in both `adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs:378-400` and `adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:372-394` does:

```clojure
(let [props        (.-props out)
      existing     (when props (aget props "data-rf2-source-coord"))
      merged-props (if existing
                     #js {}
                     #js {"data-rf2-source-coord" coord-attr})]
  (if existing
    out
    (React/cloneElement out merged-props)))
```

In the `existing` branch, `merged-props` is computed as `#js {}` and then discarded (the outer `(if existing out ...)` returns the original element). Dead JS-object allocation per existing-attr wrap-view call.

Additionally: no test asserts that a user-supplied `data-rf2-source-coord` survives a wrap-view pass.

## Recommendation

Hoist the `existing` short-circuit above the let:

```clojure
(let [props (.-props out)
      existing (when props (aget props "data-rf2-source-coord"))]
  (if existing
    out
    (React/cloneElement out #js {"data-rf2-source-coord" coord-attr})))
```

Add a regression test in both Helix and UIx parity test files asserting the user-attr-passthrough path.

## Severity

P2 — dead allocation + test gap.
notes: Test added in commit 77ca04df. The "drop dead #js {}" part of the bead was already addressed by the rf2-3vwbx spine refactor — per-adapter copies of inject-source-coord-attr were collapsed into one spine fn whose existing-attr branch returns `out` directly without computing a dead merged-props.

title: refactor(adapters): namespace adapter :kind values (:rf.adapter/helix etc) to avoid third-party collisions
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-w0u2w. **Findings doc:** `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-helix-2026-05-14.md` §S-4.

## Problem

Each adapter's `:kind` value is an unqualified keyword:
- `adapters/reagent`: `:reagent` (line 121)
- `adapters/reagent-slim`: `:reagent-slim` (line 173)
- `adapters/uix`: `:uix` (line 434)
- `adapters/helix`: `:helix` (line 441)

`:kind` is the discriminator for `substrate-adapter/current-adapter` routing. In a reserved-namespaces world (`spec/Conventions.md` declares `:rf/*` as the reserved root for re-frame keys), unqualified keywords expose a silent-collision footgun: a third-party building a custom adapter and naming `:kind :helix` collides with ours and the routing predicate matches the wrong adapter.

## Recommendation

Namespace the values: `:rf.adapter/reagent`, `:rf.adapter/reagent-slim`, `:rf.adapter/uix`, `:rf.adapter/helix`. Update the routing predicate in `substrate-adapter/route-hook!` to key off the namespaced form. Update the docs / spec references. Pre-alpha — back-compat not a concern.

## Severity

P2 — bug-magnet; the collision is unlikely but silent.

title: test(helix): cover frame-provider :children branches (sequential / single / nil)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-w0u2w. **Findings doc:** `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-helix-2026-05-14.md` §T-3.

## Problem

`frame-provider` (`adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs:209-212`) has three branches none of which are tested:

```clojure
[{:keys [frame children]}]
(let [frame-kw (or frame :rf/default)]
  (apply adapter-context/provider-element frame-kw
         (if (sequential? children) children [children])))
```

- `children` sequential → splat directly
- `children` non-sequential → wrap-in-vec then splat
- `frame` nil → fall through to `:rf/default`

The nil-fallback matters because rf2-sixo's rationale was "tooling-generated trees that elide the prop" — a regression here is precisely the "tooling broke" failure mode.

## Recommendation

Add three tests asserting each branch resolves correctly (use `React/createElement` directly + assert on the React-element shape produced, or render-into-jsdom and read the rendered tree). Same shape in `adapters/uix/test/` for parity.

## Severity

P2 — covers two defensive branches + the nil-fallback that exists to absorb tooling drift.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1046 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1046. Added implementation/adapters/helix/test/re_frame/adapter/helix_frame_provider_children_cljs_test.cljs with four deftests covering: (1) sequential :children splat, (2) single non-sequential :children wrap-in-vec then splat, (3) nil :frame falls through to :rf/default, (4) missing :frame key falls through to :rf/default. title: refactor(adapters): hoist source-coord wrap-view's debug-enabled? gate to return user-fn unchanged in prod (Helix + UIx)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-w0u2w. **Findings doc:** `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-adapter-helix-2026-05-14.md` §CQ-4.

## Problem

`wrap-view` in both `adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs:414-421` and `adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:407-414` gates the source-coord injection in two places:

```clojure
[id metadata user-fn]
(let [coord-attr (when interop/debug-enabled?
                   (format-source-coord id metadata))]
  (fn wrapped-user-fn [& args]
    (let [out (apply user-fn args)]
      (if interop/debug-enabled?
        (inject-source-coord-attr id coord-attr out)
        out))))
```

The outer `when` AND inner `if` both gate on the same constant. Under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false the elision-prod-test confirms DCE works — but the shape is fragile: a future closure-compiler that doesn't fold the outer binding will leave the `let` allocating a `nil` and wrapping every registered view in a passthrough closure.

## Recommendation

Hoist the gate to the entire fn body; return `user-fn` unchanged in production:

```clojure
[id metadata user-fn]
(if interop/debug-enabled?
  (let [coord-attr (format-source-coord id metadata)]
    (fn wrapped-user-fn [& args]
      (let [out (apply user-fn args)]
        (inject-source-coord-attr id coord-attr out))))
  user-fn))
```

Net effect: production builds skip the wrapper closure allocation entirely per registered view. Same change in both adapters.

## Severity

P2 — micro-perf + robustness against compiler-version drift.
notes: Already addressed by the rf2-3vwbx spine refactor (PR #1015). The shared  in  already has the hoisted shape this bead recommends — returns  unchanged under , so production builds skip the wrapper closure entirely. Helix and UIx adapters now read  from the spine via ; no per-adapter copies remain. Closing as duplicate-of-spine-refactor work.

Drop `[helix.core :as helix]` from the ns require form. ~-1 LoC.

title: investigate(uix): measure Reagent's reach into UIx-only bundles; explore lighter :adapter/ratom hook
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-0fgm8 (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/uix`, 2026-05-14).

## Problem

The UIx adapter routes `:adapter/ratom` to `reagent.core/r/atom` (uix.cljs lines 473–474) and `:adapter/make-reaction` / `:adapter/add-on-dispose!` / `:adapter/dispose!` / `:adapter/reactive?` to `reagent.ratom/*`. The rf2-3yij promise (uix.cljs lines 7–8): "apps targeting Reagent depend on day8/re-frame2-reagent instead; apps targeting UIx depend on day8/re-frame2-uix instead." — but every UIx app's bundle still drags `reagent.core` + `reagent.ratom` transitively because `day8/re-frame2` core lists `reagent/reagent 2.0.1` as a runtime dep (`implementation/core/deps.edn` line 41) and uix.cljs explicitly `:require`s both `reagent.core` and `reagent.ratom`.

This is a known consequence of "views.cljs is Reagent-coupled" (Spec 006 §CLJS reference scope), but the rf2-3yij separation promise is not fully delivered.

## Recommendation

1. **Measure** how much Reagent code is actually reachable from a UIx-only bundle (`npm run test:perf-bundle` baseline vs a hypothetical UIx-only build that swaps out the `:adapter/ratom` hook).
2. **Decide** whether the `:adapter/ratom` hook can hand out something lighter — e.g. a plain `atom` shape sufficient for the sub-cache's internal use — and whether `:adapter/make-reaction` can be replaced by the IDeref+IWatchable wrapper UIx already uses for `make-derived-value`.
3. **If the swap is feasible**, file a follow-on bead for the actual refactor.

## Severity

P2 — bundle-isolation finding; the rf2-3yij separation promise. Pre-alpha rule makes it worth measuring.

## Audit context

Same finding applies to Helix; the investigation should cover both.
notes:
## Measurement (2026-05-15)

UIx counter (examples/counter-uix release bundle): 358,878 chars raw / 101,798 B gzipped.
Reagent counter (examples/counter): 373,296 chars / 105,124 B gzipped.

Reagent.* in the UIx-only bundle (shadow build-report, :optimized column):
- reagent/ratom.cljs           6.4 KB  (1.79 %)
- reagent/impl/batching.cljs   1.7 KB  (0.47 %)
- reagent/impl/template.cljs   493 B   (0.14 %)
- reagent/core.cljs            391 B   (0.11 %)
- reagent/impl/util.cljs        44 B   (0.01 %)
- TOTAL                        ~9.0 KB optimized (~2.5 %)
- gzipped: ~2-3 KB

## Why reagent.* survives DCE in UIx bundles

Two pulls:
1. core/substrate/spine.cljs:36 requires reagent.ratom for the IDisposable protocol; spine.cljs:149 reifies ratom/IDisposable in make-derived-value. Any UIx/Helix consumer drags reagent.ratom through this require.
2. UIx adapter late-bind impls route :adapter/add-on-dispose!, :adapter/dispose!, :adapter/ratom, :adapter/ratom?, :adapter/make-reaction, :adapter/reactive? to reagent.{core,ratom} Vars (uix.cljs:160-175).

But: core production code calls only interop/add-on-dispose! (sub-cache slot teardown, subs.cljc:403) and interop/dispose! (frame.cljc:382, subs.cljc:580/724/752). interop/ratom, /make-reaction, /reactive? have ZERO production call sites in core — only late-bind directory + tests reference them.

## Verdict: (B) Lighter :adapter/ratom — implementable; refactor lever is on the spine's IDisposable choice, not on :adapter/ratom itself.

Replacing reagent.ratom/IDisposable in substrate/spine.cljs with a re-frame-owned disposable protocol drops both reagent.ratom.cljs (6.4 KB) and reagent.impl.batching.cljs (1.7 KB, only pulled via reagent.ratom internals). Estimated saving: 8-9 KB optimized / 2-3 KB gzipped per UIx-only and Helix-only bundle. Scope ~30 LoC + new tiny protocol ns + Reagent adapter shim to accept either shape.

## Follow-on

Filed rf2-jicu2 — refactor(core): replace reagent.ratom/IDisposable in spine with re-frame-owned disposable protocol. P2. Includes scope, tests, hot-zone note (spine.cljs is shared across UIx+Helix+reagent-slim, sequential).

## Cross-cutting

Helix-only bundles carry the same ~9 KB tail (spine require is the shared cause). Same fix recovers both.

## Findings doc

ai/findings/uix-bundle-measurement-2026-05-15.md (local-only, in rf2-ykqee-work worktree). Full breakdown of: measurement methodology, every interop/* call site grep, the protocol-swap design, and the recommended bundle-isolation assertion script.

## Out-of-band note

Perf-bundle baseline (npm run test:perf-bundle) PASS — 0 sentinels off-counter, 12 sentinels on-counter. No incidental issues surfaced.
close_reason: Verdict (B) — lighter :adapter/ratom feasible. Reagent.* contributes ~9 KB optimized / ~2-3 KB gzipped to UIx-only bundles, dominated by reagent.ratom.cljs (6.4 KB) pulled via core/substrate/spine.cljs's ratom/IDisposable reify. Findings doc ai/findings/uix-bundle-measurement-2026-05-15.md (worktree-local). Follow-on rf2-jicu2 filed for the protocol-swap refactor (saves bytes in both UIx-only and Helix-only bundles).

title: refactor(uix): make format-source-coord public (or lift to shared helpers) for test pinning

title: refactor(uix): publish set-hiccup-emitter! through late-bind hook (parity with Reagent's :reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-0fgm8 (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/uix`, 2026-05-14).

## Problem

The Reagent adapter publishes its emitter via:
```clojure
(late-bind/set-fn! :reagent/set-hiccup-emitter! set-hiccup-emitter!)
```
(`implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs` line 141)

The UIx adapter (`implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs` lines 151–156) exports `set-hiccup-emitter!` as a public fn but does NOT register it through the late-bind hook table.

Effect: an SSR consumer that does `(require '[re-frame.ssr])` and expects the emitter to auto-wire will succeed under Reagent but fail under UIx — the UIx user has to call `(uix-adapter/set-hiccup-emitter! ...)` directly.

Same gap likely exists in Helix.

## Recommendation

1. **First verify** by reading `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc` (or wherever SSR's ns-load hook resolution lives) which hook keys it consumes. If it consumes `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!` literally, decide whether the hook key should be:
   - per-adapter (`:reagent/...`, `:uix/...`, `:helix/...`) and SSR tries each in turn, or
   - adapter-agnostic (`:adapter/set-hiccup-emitter!`) and the routed hook lands on the currently installed adapter.

2. Then publish the chosen hook from the UIx + Helix adapters and document the contract in the adapter ns docstring (matching Reagent's lines 16–20 explanation).

## Severity

P2 — late-bind contract divergence. Affects SSR-from-UIx users (small population pre-alpha, but the divergence is masterpiece-grade-worthy).
close_reason: Landed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1051

title: refactor(uix): extract chain-fn! helper for chained late-bind hooks (:adapter/clear-warn-once-caches!)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-0fgm8 (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/uix`, 2026-05-14).

## Problem

The chained `:adapter/clear-warn-once-caches!` registration block at uix.cljs lines 502–507 (and helix.cljs lines 510–515, and likely `re-frame.views` for the per-views cache) uses an inline get-prev-and-wrap pattern:

```clojure
(let [previous (late-bind/get-fn :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches!)]
  (late-bind/set-fn! :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches!
    (fn uix-adapter-clear-warn-once-caches! []
      (clear-warned-non-dom-roots!)
      (when previous (previous))
      nil)))
```

This is the same idiom as `substrate-adapter/route-hook!` but for chain-style hooks (every chained contributor runs; not adapter-routed). Each new contributor copies the get-prev-and-wrap dance.

## Recommendation

Add `(late-bind/chain-fn! hook-key step-fn)` that does the get-prev-and-wrap dance internally, mirroring `substrate-adapter/route-hook!`. Adapters then call:

```clojure
(late-bind/chain-fn! :adapter/clear-warn-once-caches!
  uix-adapter-clear-warn-once-caches!)
```

Single-line idiom; consistent with the route-hook! shape.

## Estimate

~5 LoC removed from each adapter that uses the chain idiom (~3 adapters = ~15 LoC) plus a clearer surface.

## Severity

P2 — duplication-of-idiom rather than duplication-of-code. Pre-alpha rule makes it worth doing alongside the rf2-3vwbx / rf2-gsh49 cluster.
close_reason: Landed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1051
