title: test(reagent-slim): add warn-once-keyword-prop! test coverage
description:
Per audit rf2-bgnin (T-2).

reagent2.impl.template/warn-once-keyword-prop! (implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:184-200) has zero test coverage. The dev-only one-shot warning for non-HTML keyword props on non-HTML attr names is silent if it regresses.

Spec'd in IMPL-SPEC §7.2 D2: 'keywords stringify only for HTML-attribute prop names; other named values pass through unchanged.' The warning is part of the contract — under goog.DEBUG, console.warn fires exactly once per (k, v-name) pair.

Coverage needed (in template_cljs_test.cljs):
1. Render [:> SomeFn {:value :foo}] — warn fires once for [:value :foo].
2. Render twice with same [:value :foo] — warn does NOT fire a second time.
3. Render with [:value :bar] (same k, different v) — warn fires (different cache key).
4. Production-elision check: under goog.DEBUG=false, no warn call. (Likely covered by the bundle-isolation tests already; if not, add to perf-bundle suite.)

Mock console.warn via with-redefs or set! a counter.

Net LoC: +20-30 test code.
close_reason: 4 tests added for warn-once-keyword-prop! contract: fires once per (k,v-name) pair; HTML-attr paths silent; cache discriminates on v-name.

title: refactor(reagent-slim): expand-seq fold key-warning into single pass
description:
Per audit rf2-bgnin (P-2).

implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:416-433: expand-seq walks the input seq s twice.

First pass: (into-array (map as-element s)) realises the lazy seq.
Second pass (DEBUG-only): (loop [items s] (when-let [el (first items)] ...)) walks s again for :key-missing warnings.

Production is unaffected (the warn loop is goog.DEBUG-gated). But:
- Two passes mean the lazy seq s is referenced twice; can't be GC'd until after the second loop. On a very large children seq this matters.
- The DEBUG path has 2x the iteration cost it needs.

Fix: fold the warn-check into the conversion pass:
  (let [arr #js []]
    (loop [items s]
      (when-let [el (first items)]
        (when ^boolean js/goog.DEBUG
          (when (and (vector? el) (not (get-react-key el)))
            (warn-once-no-key el)))
        (.push arr (as-element el))
        (recur (rest items))))
    arr)

Net LoC: -5 to ±0.
close_reason: expand-seq folds key-warning into single pass. Production DCE'd; DEBUG path 2× → 1× iteration.

title: refactor(reagent-slim): replace reduce-kv with loop in make-element multi-child path
description:
Per audit rf2-bgnin (P-1).

In implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:407-414, the multi-child path of make-element uses reduce-kv with a (when (>= k first-child) ...) predicate over the full argv:

  (let [args (reduce-kv (fn [^js a k v]
                          (when (>= k first-child)
                            (.push a (as-element v)))
                          a)
                        #js [component js-props]
                        argv)]
    (.apply (.-createElement react) nil args))

For [:div {} a b c] (n=5, first-child=2), this iterates k=0..4 and tests the predicate at every step. A (loop [i first-child] ...) skips the first N tests.

Negligible at small fan-out; real at large children counts (1000-row tables, dynamic lists).

Fix:
  (let [args #js [component js-props]
        n    (count argv)]
    (loop [i first-child]
      (when (< i n)
        (.push args (as-element (nth argv i nil)))
        (recur (inc i))))
    (.apply (.-createElement react) nil args))

Net LoC: ±0. Hot-path improvement at fan-out > ~50.
close_reason: make-element multi-child path now loops from first-child instead of reduce-kv over full argv. Hot-path improvement at fan-out.

title: refactor(reagent-slim): as-element-fn unregistered → throw under goog.DEBUG (not silent pass-through)
description:
Per audit rf2-bgnin (A-4).

In implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:85-93, ->react-element silently passes hiccup through unchanged if no as-element fn is registered:

  (defn- ->react-element [hiccup]
    (if-let [f @as-element-fn]
      (f hiccup)
      hiccup))

Comment claims 'before the fn is registered ... raw hiccup falls through unchanged, matching the pre-fix shape.' But that pre-fix shape is the bug rf2-08t0 fixed (raw CLJS vector reaches React, 'Objects are not valid as a React child').

The fall-through is only reachable in a hand-rolled test bundle that requires component without template. Production path makes it impossible (dom/client.cljs requires template, which registers the fn).

Fix: in goog.DEBUG, throw :rf.error/as-element-fn-unregistered with a clear message. In production builds (goog.DEBUG=false), keep the silent pass-through for forward compat OR throw too (preferred: honest failure is the slim adapter's discipline).

Tests (rf2-bgnin T-3): add a test exercising 'load component without template, build a class, render → throws-or-warns' to lock in the design choice.

Net LoC: +3-5.
close_reason: as-element-fn unregistered now throws :rf.error/as-element-fn-unregistered. Honest fail-fast over the silent pass-through that was rf2-08t0's bug shape. Test: rf2-n9nlk.

title: refactor(reagent-slim): factor shared hiccup-shape detection helper (has-props/first-child)
description:

Five places re-derive the same shape question. A shared helper:

(or a destructuring-friendly tuple) would consolidate. Probably lives in reagent2.impl.template (server.cljs already :requires template for parse-tag).

title: refactor(reagent-slim): hoist single in-tree void-tags set (template+server dedup)
description:
Per audit rf2-bgnin (CQ-6).

The HTML5 14-void-tag list lives in two in-tree representations:

- reagent2.dom.server/void-tags (server.cljs:99-102) — a #{} set
- reagent2.impl.template/void-tag? (template.cljs:375-382) — a (case ...) over the same 14 literals

(Also re-frame.ssr/void-elements but that's a different artefact, excluded per bundle isolation.)

Fix: hoist a single void-tags set into one impl ns (probably template.cljs since it's loaded earlier in the dep graph). Make server.cljs :require [template :refer [void-tags]] or call (template/void-tag? tag-str). Pick whichever shape — set check or fn — is cleaner at the call sites.

Net LoC: ~-10.

title: refactor(reagent-slim): trim provenance narration density in component.cljs
description:
Per audit rf2-bgnin (CQ-4).

implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs is 666 LoC and carries ~17 rf2-XXXX / 'Stage 4-D' / 'per IMPL-SPEC §N' / 'stock Reagent's reagent.impl.component' cross-references inside ns docstrings AND inside fn-internal comment blocks.

The make-render-method docstring (lines 487-496) is ~50 LoC and ~80% provenance ('stock Reagent does X, the rewrite does Y because Z, per IMPL-SPEC §4.4'); the function's job (build the React render method) gets ~20%.

Net LoC: -60 to -100 across the file (narration deletion; no behaviour change). Subjective.

title: refactor(mcp-conformance): drop dead 'fixtures' extra-path from wire-vocab/deps.edn
description:
**Source:** refactor-audit r2 of \`tools/mcp-conformance\` (rf2-azk9c), finding **F-DEAD-1**.

## The dead path

\`tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/deps.edn:37\`:

\`\`\`clojure
:aliases
 {:test {:extra-paths [\"test\" \"fixtures\"]
         ...

Alternative: surface fixtures as EDN files under a new \`fixtures/\` directory. More work, and the inline form is currently the right shape (fixtures live next to their schemas; the test file is small enough). Recommend the trivial fix.

P2 — purely cosmetic dead-code removal. No observable effect today; the path is silently ignored. Worth fixing for the same reason any dead-code is worth fixing — the artefact reads as pre-alpha-masterpiece and a dead extra-path slot is a minor smell.

2 min.

One-line change in \`wire-vocab/deps.edn\`. Trivial.

title: refactor(mcp-conformance): use negative-lookahead regex for inline-emit anti-pin substring matches
description:
**Source:** refactor-audit r2 of \`tools/mcp-conformance\` (rf2-azk9c), finding **F-NEARMISS-1**.

## The bug

\`indicator_field_test.clj:367-383\`:

\`\`\`clojure
(deftest no-inline-indicator-slot-emit-outside-the-helper
  (let [slot-literals [\":dropped-sensitive\" \":elided-large\"]
        srcs          (pair2-mcp-source-files)]
    ...
    (doseq [rel srcs slot slot-literals ...]
      ...
      (is (not (str/includes? src slot)) ...))))
\`\`\`

Raw \`str/includes?\` would false-positive any future legitimate extension like \`:dropped-sensitive-warning\` or \`:elided-large-summary\` (e.g. a tool that wraps the count in a typed wrapper).

## Fix

Use the existing elegant pattern from \`slot_name_test.clj:266-275\`:

\`\`\`clojure
(defn- variant-regex [s]
  (re-pattern (str (java.util.regex.Pattern/quote s)
                   \"(?![\\w\\-?/!*+'<>=])\")))
\`\`\`

Replace \`(str/includes? src slot)\` with \`(re-find (variant-regex slot) src)\`. Existing test fixtures pass.

## Severity

P2 — defensive; today there's no near-miss extension, so this is future-proofing. The pattern is already in the artefact (rf2-zvv65); this just propagates it.

## Time estimate

10 min.

## Coordination

Touches \`indicator_field_test.clj\` only. Isolated, parallel-safe.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1063 (refactor+perf(mcp-infra): batched cluster — 7 follow-on beads). https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1063

title: refactor(mcp-conformance): extract Node-side watchdog + SDK-client teardown helper
description:
**Source:** refactor-audit r2 of \`tools/mcp-conformance\` (rf2-azk9c), finding **F-DEDUP-2**.

## The duplication

\`end-to-end-pair2.js\`, \`end-to-end-story.js\`, \`live-pair2-overflow.js\` all repeat:

- watchdog setTimeout + clearTimeout pair
- main().then(0).catch(1)
- SDK \`Client\` + \`StdioClientTransport\` construction
- \`transport.stderr?.on('data', ...)\` piping
- \`try { ... } catch (err) { try { client.close(); } ... throw err; }\` teardown

~40 LoC × 3 files of pure ceremony.

Locations:
- \`end-to-end-pair2.js:62-77, 236-262\`
- \`end-to-end-story.js:67-80, 205-234\`
- \`live-pair2-overflow.js:303-323, 460-487\`

## Fix

Create \`tools/mcp-conformance/test/_runner.js\` exposing:

\`\`\`js
async function runWithWatchdog({ watchdogMs, transportSpec, clientName }, body) {
  // Construct transport + Client, pipe stderr, install watchdog,
  // call body(client, transport), tear down on success or error,
  // exit with appropriate code.
}
\`\`\`

Each test body shrinks to the workflow steps. Adding a fourth Node test (causa-mcp impl) becomes ~30 LoC instead of ~110.

## Severity

P2 — not a correctness issue, but the three-script split is the surface a fourth Node test will land on (causa-mcp impl, eventually a third pair2 variant, etc.). Same posture as F-DEDUP-1's reasoning.

## Time estimate

30-45 min.

## Coordination

Touches all three test/\*.js files + adds test/\_runner.js. Isolated, parallel-safe with non-overlapping mcp-conformance beads.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1063 (refactor+perf(mcp-infra): batched cluster — 7 follow-on beads). https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1063

title: refactor(epoch): consider :trace-events elision policy for older records per Spec-Schemas
description:
Per refactor-audit r2 (rf2-lwn4t): Spec-Schemas.md:2224 says `:trace-events` is optional because for long histories the per-epoch trace can be large — 'implementations may choose to drop traces from older epochs'. But the current impl never elides; every record in the ring buffer carries the full `:trace-events` vector forever.

For a ring depth of 50 with cascades averaging 20 traces each, that's 1000 trace events held in memory per frame indefinitely. The structured projections (`:sub-runs`/`:renders`/`:effects`) are cheap by comparison.

Proposed knob: `(rf/configure :epoch-history {:depth 50 :trace-events-keep 5})` — keep raw traces for only the most recent N records; older records keep structured projections but drop `:trace-events`.

Defer until someone complains; the ring depth (50) caps the worst case. Findings doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-epoch-2026-05-14.md` §F3.1.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #1003 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1003) — batched-by-surface r2 epoch polish cluster (rf2-lwn4t follow-ons).

title: refactor(epoch): test gap — capture-buffer cross-contamination from out-of-drain trace emits
description:

Test plan:
1. Drive a cascade on `:frame/a` — lands record 1.
2. `(rf/reset-frame-db! :frame/a ...)` — emits `:rf.epoch/db-replaced` out-of-drain.
3. Drive a second cascade `(rf/dispatch-sync [:foo] {:frame :frame/a})`.
4. Assert the second record's `:trace-events` does NOT contain `:rf.epoch/db-replaced`.
5. Assert `:trigger-event` is `[:foo]` (not `[:rf.epoch/db-replaced]`).

title: test(reagent): exercise :rf.warning/write-after-destroy nil-container path at reagent integration tier
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-z3oab.

## Problem

The `re-frame.substrate.adapter/replace-container!` defense-in-depth nil-guard (rf2-ft2b) emits `:rf.warning/write-after-destroy` when a write reaches a destroyed frame's nil container. The guard is core-side, but the reagent-adapter integration path (router commit, flows recompute, epoch restore, SSR write) is where the original bug was reported.

No CLJS test exercises this path under the Reagent adapter. The contract guarantee — \"no NPE on a background thread; structured warning emitted\" — is unpinned at the reagent integration tier.

## Recommendation

Add a test under `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/` that:

1. Installs the Reagent adapter, creates a frame.
2. Destroys the frame (calls into the destroy path).
3. Triggers a router commit / scheduled drain against the destroyed frame.
4. Asserts that the `:rf.warning/write-after-destroy` trace was emitted with `:recovery :no-recovery`.
5. Asserts that no exception was thrown on any thread.

Coverage gap is P2; the original bug (rf2-ft2b) was high-impact, so an integration-tier pin is worth the effort.

## Severity

P2 — coverage gap for a known-historical-pain integration shape.
close_reason: Closed by PR #1048 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1048). New CLJS test ns write_after_destroy_cljs_test.cljs pins :rf.warning/write-after-destroy emission under the Reagent adapter — two scenarios (direct nil-container + live-destroy then captured-container-write).

title: refactor(reagent): drop (boolean (:hydrate? opts)) defensive coercion across React-shaped adapters
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-z3oab.

## Problem

All four React-shaped adapters wrap `(:hydrate? opts)` in `(boolean ...)`:

- `adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:70`
- `adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:121`
- `adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:141`
- `adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs:144`

Spec 006 §`render` types `:hydrate?` as a boolean. Truthy non-bool values (e.g. `\"yes\"`) are undefined-behaviour per the spec. The `(boolean ...)` coercion is a small per-render tax defending against a non-conforming input that the spec does not promise to accept.

## Recommendation

Drop the `boolean` call; `(if (:hydrate? opts) ... ...)` is the idiomatic CLJS branch on a truthy value.

LoC: -1 per adapter (4 total).

## Severity

P2 — cosmetic / micro-perf; aligns with pre-alpha rule of dropping defensive bridges.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1058: (boolean (:hydrate? opts)) defensive coercion dropped from spine (covers UIx + Helix), Reagent, and reagent-slim render fns. Spec 006 §render types :hydrate? as a boolean.

title: refactor(mcp-base): parameterise scrub-snapshot with explicit strip-fn (lets pair2-mcp delete its scrub-snapshot-sensitive)
description:
## What

In `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/sensitive.cljc`, take `scrub-snapshot` (lines 63-92) and admit an explicit `:strip-fn` option. Today the function hard-codes `strip-sensitive` as the predicate; pair2-mcp can't reuse the helper because it wants a union predicate (`sensitive-event? OR sensitive-epoch?`).

Sketch:

```clojure
(defn scrub-snapshot
  ([snapshot include?] (scrub-snapshot snapshot include? strip-sensitive))
  ([snapshot include? strip-fn]
   ;; uses strip-fn instead of strip-sensitive
   ...))
```

Then `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/sensitive.cljs` can delete `scrub-snapshot-sensitive` (lines 77-101) and call the base helper directly with its own strip-fn.

## Why

`scrub-snapshot-sensitive` in pair2-mcp is a ~17-line near-duplicate of `scrub-snapshot` in the base — same shape, different strip-fn closure. Parameterising the base lets pair2-mcp delete the duplicate. Also fixes a quiet bug: pair2-mcp's version uses `atom` where base uses `volatile!` — single-threaded scrub doesn't need an atom (lens-3 perf nit F12).

Caught by round-2 audit (rf2-n4q62, F10).

## Estimated impact

- base: +3 LoC (extra arity + opt).
- pair2-mcp: -17 LoC (delete `scrub-snapshot-sensitive`; thread strip-fn through).

## Source

rf2-n4q62 round-2 audit, finding F10.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #1001 (refactor(mcp-base): round-2 polish cluster). Commit 5add3854: scrub-snapshot grows three-arity form; pair2-mcp scrub-snapshot-sensitive collapses to one-line delegate (atom regression fixed).

title: refactor(mcp-base): parse-mode should strip leading ':' (consistency with parse-keyword)
description:
## What

In `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/args.cljc` `parse-mode` (lines 123-137), recognise `":diff"` AND `"diff"` as the keyword `:diff`. Today `parse-mode ":diff" :diff #{:diff :full}` returns `:diff` via the default fallback — masquerading as success.

Add a guard / route the string arm through `parse-keyword`:

```clojure
(string? raw) (let [kw (parse-keyword raw)]
                (if (contains? recognised kw) kw default))
```

(While here: F3 — `(keyword raw)` is computed twice in the same cond. Let-bind it.)

## Why

`parse-keyword` strips leading `:` (lines 105-121). `parse-mode` does not. Inconsistency within the same namespace — an agent that's learned `:include-sensitive? ":diff"` works when the value is routed through `parse-keyword` but silently default-falls-back when routed through `parse-mode`.

Caught by round-2 audit (rf2-n4q62, findings F2 + F3).

## Tests

Add to `args_test.clj`:
```clojure
(deftest parse-mode-strips-leading-colon
  (is (= :diff (args/parse-mode ":diff" :full #{:diff :full})))
  (is (= :full (args/parse-mode ":full" :diff #{:diff :full}))))
```

This test will FAIL before the fix lands — that's the regression-pin.

## Estimated impact

-3 LoC body, +5 LoC test.

## Source

rf2-n4q62 round-2 audit, findings F2 + F3.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #1001 (refactor(mcp-base): round-2 polish cluster). Commit d318de6d: parse-mode routes string arm through parse-keyword; F2/F3 fixed + regression pin (F16) added.

title: refactor(causa-mcp): collapse Principles/Vision overlap (origin-tagging, MCP-not-IDE, tool-consumes-framework)
description:

Three section pairs across Principles.md and 000-Vision.md cover substantially overlapping content:

1. **Origin tagging**: Principles.md §"Origin tagging is the convention, not a suggestion" (53 lines, lines 102-134) + 000-Vision.md §"Every MCP-driven mutation leaves a visible footprint" (25 lines, lines 233-257). Same point, two homes.

Tolerable in a spec scaffold where Principles is tie-breaker and Vision is the "why" — but the reader absorbs 47% more text than the unique content warrants. Pattern fix: keep one canonical home per pair (Principles for tie-breakers, Vision for "why"), collapse the other side to a cite.

Suggested:
- §Origin tagging stays in Principles (it's a tie-breaker — "opt-out, not opt-in"); Vision §Every MCP-driven mutation collapses to a 4-line cite + the differentiator table.
- §MCP-not-IDE stays in Principles; Vision §Why a server folds to a single sentence cite.

title: test(causa): add holistic sub-registration smoke test
description:
## Context

Filed from round-2 audit rf2-imynx (P2-9, lens 5 test coverage).

## Problem

`register-causa-handlers!` is implicitly tested via per-panel composite tests, but no test asserts the full sub-graph wires up after one call. If a panel migration (rf2-d4xda) drops a sub registration silently, the per-panel test still passes (the sub is defined; the test isn't checking REGISTRATION-via-orchestrator).

## Fix

Add one smoke test to `registry_cljs_test.cljs`:

```clj
(deftest registers-every-canonical-rf-causa-sub
  (registry/reset-for-test!)
  (registry/register-causa-handlers!)
  (let [expected #{:rf.causa/trace-buffer
                   :rf.causa/selected-panel
                   :rf.causa/event-detail
                   :rf.causa/time-travel
                   :rf.causa/causality-graph-data
                   :rf.causa/app-db-diff
                   :rf.causa/subscriptions-data
                   :rf.causa/effects-data
                   :rf.causa/flows-data
                   :rf.causa/routes-data
                   :rf.causa/machine-inspector-data
                   :rf.causa/schema-violation-timeline
                   :rf.causa/hydration-debugger-data
                   :rf.causa/issues-ribbon
                   :rf.causa/trace-feed
                   :rf.causa/performance-data
                   :rf.causa/mcp-server
                   :rf.causa/copilot-conversation
                   :rf.causa/copilot-open?}]
    (doseq [q-v expected]
      (is (some? (rf/subscribe [q-v]))
          (str q-v " must be registered after register-causa-handlers!")))))
```

## Why it matters

When rf2-d4xda lands the install! migration, this test catches any panel's `install!` being silently dropped from the orchestrator. The expected-set itself becomes a documented contract.

## Impact

~50 LoC of test code; high signal-to-noise.

title: fix(causa): land core.cljs facade promised by spec/API.md + README.md (or update spec)
description:
## Context

Filed from round-2 audit rf2-imynx (P2-7, lens 4 spec-vs-impl).

## Problem

Spec drift between `spec/API.md` + `README.md` and the impl:

  - `spec/API.md:46` documents `(causa/init! opts)`, `(causa/open!)`, `(causa/close!)`, `(causa/toggle!)`, `(causa/popout!)`, `(causa/active-frame)`, `(causa/active-panel)`, etc. from `day8.re-frame2-causa.core`
  - `README.md:148` says `├── core.cljs    ; init!, panel mount, settings`
  - Glob: `tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/core*` → no file

Actual mount surface lives in `mount.cljs` (`open!`, `close!`, `toggle!`, `teardown!`), called only from `keybinding.cljs`. Config surface lives in `config.cljc`. There's no programmatic entry point covering the API.md contract.

## Fix — pick one

(a) **Add `core.cljs` as the spec promises.** Re-export from mount.cljs + config.cljc; add stubs for `active-frame` / `set-active-frame!` / `active-panel` / `set-active-panel!` (these are partly implemented via the registry's `:rf.causa/selected-panel` sub — wire them up). Add `popout!` (the Ctrl+Shift+P shortcut from the README) once that's beaded.

(b) **Update the spec.** Move the API.md entries that reference `day8.re-frame2-causa.core` to point at `day8.re-frame2-causa.mount` + `day8.re-frame2-causa.config` as the canonical surfaces. Remove or defer the entries that have no impl yet (`popout!`, `load-theme`, etc.).

The spec is the artefact (CLAUDE.md), so **(a) is preferred** unless the spec is intentionally aspirational. Decision needs Mike's call.
close_reason: DECIDED (Mike, 2026-05-14): Option (a) — add core.cljs facade as the spec promises. Spec is the artefact; alignment goes from spec toward impl. Three rationales: (1) mirrors framework's own pattern (re-frame.core canonical entry, parallel idiom for tooling); (2) one canonical import is correct ergonomics — programmer calls causa/init!, causa/toggle!, causa/active-frame without knowing internal ns layout (low-friction stance); (3) API stability separates contract from implementation — internal refactors can split mount.cljs etc. without breaking consumers. Follow-on impl: create tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/core.cljs that re-exports init!/open!/close!/toggle! from mount, config knobs from config.cljc, and wires active-frame/set-active-frame!/active-panel/set-active-panel! against the existing :rf.causa/selected-panel registry sub. popout! stays in the spec as TBD with a future-impl marker (depends on Ctrl+Shift+P shortcut wiring). load-theme similarly TBD.

description:
compute-rank (routing.cljc:163-181) returns a 5-vec [static total (- splat) catch-all? (- optional)]; reg-route (:201) conj's (- idx) to make a 6-vec. The rule-6 shadow check (:212) does (vec (drop-last other-rank)) which assumes 6 elements. The default in match-url (:378) is [0 0 0 0 0 0] (6-element).

Fragile: adding any new rank dimension silently breaks the (drop-last) shadow check. The docstring describes a 5+idx tuple but the function returns 5; reg-route adds idx externally; match-url defaults to 6.

Fix one of:
  - compute-rank accepts idx and returns the canonical 6-tuple directly
  - Maintain shadow-check tuple structurally separate from match tuple (e.g. as a separate :rf.route/shape derived value)

title: refactor(routing): can-leave? returns wrong polarity when :subs/subscribe-value late-bind is unset (lets nav through)
description:
routing.cljc:667-670 can-leave?:

  (if-let [sub-id (:can-leave route-meta)]
    (when-let [subscribe-value (late-bind/get-fn :subs/subscribe-value)]
      (boolean (subscribe-value frame [sub-id])))
    true)

If :subs/subscribe-value late-bind is unset, when-let returns nil. The caller (routing.cljc:677-678) inverts via (not ok?) — (not nil) = true — meaning the not-ok branch runs.

Wait: re-read. The when-let returns nil which means ok? = nil, then (not ok?) is true → blocks. Actually that's OK: a missing :subs/subscribe-value should block, not let through.

The real bug: when :can-leave is declared but the sub itself doesn't return a boolean, (boolean (subscribe-value ...)) silently coerces. Should also distinguish 'sub missing' from 'sub returns false'.

Lower-priority correctness item — trace a warning when :can-leave declared but sub returns nil or :subs/subscribe-value hook is missing.

title: refactor(causa): factor ctrl-shift-key? predicate in keybinding.cljs
description:
## Context

Filed from round-2 audit rf2-imynx (P2-9 / P3-2).

## Problem

`keybinding.cljs:35-53` (`causa-toggle-key?`) and `:55-74` (`copilot-toggle-key?`) are near-identical 9-line predicates differing only in the key code being matched.

```clj
(defn- causa-toggle-key? [event]
  (let [^js e event
        k         (.-key e)
        code      (.-code e)
        ctrl?     (.-ctrlKey e)
        shift?    (.-shiftKey e)
        meta?     (.-metaKey e)
        alt?      (.-altKey e)]
    (and ctrl? shift? (not meta?) (not alt?)
         (or (= "C" k) (= "c" k) (= "KeyC" code)))))
```

## Fix

Factor:

```clj
(defn- ctrl-shift-key? [event match?]
  (let [^js e event]
    (and (.-ctrlKey e) (.-shiftKey e)
         (not (.-metaKey e)) (not (.-altKey e))
         (match? (.-key e) (.-code e)))))

(def causa-toggle-match?
  (fn [k code] (or (= "C" k) (= "c" k) (= "KeyC" code))))

(def copilot-toggle-match?
  (fn [k code] (or (= "/" k) (= "?" k) (= "Slash" code))))
```

## Impact

~20 LoC removed; future key-bindings (the spec promises `Ctrl+K` for command palette etc.) drop in cleanly.

title: perf(routing): match-url's with-defaults reduce + coerce-query-value's schema scan are O(N) on hot path
description:
Two micro-perf wins in match-url's query handling:

  1. with-defaults (routing.cljc:371-375): when defaults is empty (most routes don't declare :query-defaults), still runs reduce-kv and materialises an (array-map). Add a short-circuit:
     (cond
       (and (nil? coerced) (empty? defaults)) nil
       (empty? defaults)                       coerced
       :else                                   (reduce-kv ...))

  2. coerce-query-value (routing.cljc:300-328) walks (rest schema) to find each query key's type-form — O(N*M) where N = declared keys, M = actual query values. Compile the schema to a flat {:key type-form} map at reg-route time (alongside :rf.route/compiled); coerce in O(M).

Both fire on every URL-driven navigation.

title: refactor(routing): fuse pattern-shape + compile-pattern into a single pass; lift inner-names-by-group to compile time
description:
Two coupled pattern-walking refactors:

  1. reg-route currently walks the pattern TWICE: compute-rank → pattern-shape (walk 1), then compile-pattern (walk 2). Both walk char-by-char with the same segment-end calls. Fuse into (parse-pattern pattern) returning {:rank ... :regex ... :names ... :inner-names-by-group ...} in one pass. One-time cost reduction at registration; eliminates the double pattern-logic correctness risk.

  2. route-url's emit-group calls collect-param-names-in-group to scan each {...}? group for inner param names — that scan duplicates work the same compile pass could capture. Move :inner-names-by-group into compile-pattern's output (a small map by group index); route-url looks it up.

Both are ~30-50 LoC refactor, registration-time one-time saving, but the bigger value is dropping the duplicated walking logic (CQ2 / segment-end-no-? exists only because of the two-walk split).

title: refactor(routing): implement :url-bound? frame metadata + :rf.error/duplicate-url-binding
description:
Spec 012 §Multi-frame routing: 'Only one frame can own the URL at a time' — re-registering a :url-bound? true frame emits :rf.error/duplicate-url-binding. Routing impl never reads :url-bound?, so non-default frames will happily fire :rf.nav/push-url today, racing with the default frame for the URL.

Implementation: hook reg-frame to check :url-bound? — only one frame may have it true at a time. The :rf.nav/push-url / :rf.nav/replace-url fxs (routing.cljc:858-872) should consult the frame and no-op if the frame isn't url-bound (or trace a warning).

Coordinate with core/frame.cljc :url-bound? handling — needs read access via frame metadata.

title: refactor(routing): implement :query-retain semantics in :rf.route/navigate

Spec 012 §Reserved route-metadata keys and §Query strings document :query-retain (set of keys carried across navigations). title: refactor(ssr): cluster — destroy-time trace symmetry + cofx-canonical surface + shell payload-id contract
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-cegm7 (`ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-ssr-2026-05-14.md`) — P2 cluster of three coupled polish items.

## CQ-2: destroy-time trace symmetry on head-cleanup hook

`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/request.cljc:130-135` silently swallows ALL Throwable from the `:ssr/head-on-frame-destroyed` hook:

```clojure
(when-let [head-cleanup! (late-bind/get-fn :ssr/head-on-frame-destroyed)]
  (try (head-cleanup! frame-id)
       (catch #?(:clj Throwable :cljs :default) _ nil)))
```

Round-1's R6 fix tightened `destroy-frame-quietly!` at `ssr-ring/ring.clj:411-420` to emit a `:rf.ssr/destroy-frame-failed` warning trace on catch. Symmetric inconsistency here — a head-cleanup throw vanishes silently when the surrounding pattern is now 'trace-on-catch.'

Fix: mirror the trace-on-catch pattern in `on-frame-destroyed!`. Emit a structured `:rf.ssr.head/cleanup-failed` warning trace (or extend the existing key with a `:hook` discriminator).

## A2 / A3: Ring adapter — drop the positional-arg :on-create conj path

`ssr-ring/ring.clj:454-468` (`on-create-with-request`) conj's the Ring request map onto the caller's `:on-create` event vector — a fallback for handlers that don't `(inject-cofx :rf.server/request)`. Round-1's rf2-afxhv shipped the `:rf.server/request` cofx as the documented spec contract; the conj path is the back-compat for handlers that pre-date the cofx.

Pre-alpha rule (CLAUDE.md): no back-compat. Pick one canonical surface — the cofx — and drop the positional-arg conj. The conj has subtle pitfalls: a handler expecting `[:rf/server-init]` (1-vector) gets `[:rf/server-init {ring-request...}]` after conj and may forget to destructure.

Fix: drop `on-create-with-request`, pass the caller's `:on-create` verbatim. The cofx is the spec-documented read path. `ssr-ring/ring.clj:462-468` `nil?` arm becomes dead with this change (A3).

Affects `examples/` worked examples that follow the conj shape — sweep and update those to use the cofx.

## CQ-3 / TC-1: published contract for the hydration-payload script id

`ssr-ring/ring.clj:329` emits `<script id="__rf_payload" type="application/edn">...</script>`; the client-side bootstrap (per `spec/Construction-Prompts.md:996`) reads `document.getElementById("__rf_payload")`. The linkage is convention-by-string, not a published contract — a user who customises `:html-shell` with a different id silently breaks the bootstrap.

Fix options:
  (a) Add `spec/Conventions.md §Hydration payload script id` pinning the literal `__rf_payload`.
  (b) Introduce a `rf2/payload-script-id` constant (`def` in a shared ns; e.g. `re-frame.ssr.constants` or extend an existing one) that both shell-emit and client-read import.

Recommend (b) — the string lives in one place; the shell and client both reference the same var. Tooling that searches for the id pattern (e.g. 10x's payload inspector) reads the constant.

Test: a fixture asserting that the default shell emits the script tag with the canonical id; a docs cross-reference confirming the client convention.

## Coordination

All three are localised to either `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/` or `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj` plus minor spec / convention edits. Sequence after rf2-pjsrc (split ring.clj) and rf2-h2ujj (default-html-shell honours :html-attrs) if those are active — same hot-zone file.

Linked from rf2-cegm7. Estimated: ~25 LoC across three sub-items + tests + Conventions update.

title: fix(machines): timer resolve-delay-ms silently catches fn-form throws (TM5 carryover)

     [v nil])

title: refactor(schemas+spec): redact-tags should know :fx-args canonically — drops validate-fx! extra-redact lambda
description:
Source: rf2-whepe round-2 audit, 2026-05-14 09:40 AUSEST.

`schemas/validate.cljc:368` passes a 1-line lambda to `run-validation` to scrub the `:fx-args` slot in the failure tags:

```clojure
(fn [tags] (assoc tags :fx-args redacted-sentinel))
```

This is the ONLY use of the `extra-redact` parameter on `run-validation`. The other three meta-bearing surfaces (validate-event! / validate-cofx! / validate-sub-return!) pass nil.

The asymmetry exists because Spec 010 §`:sensitive?` line 293-294 lists `:value`, `:received`, `:explain` as the canonical redacted slots; `:fx-args` isn't listed. So the lambda is doing what the spec doesn't say to do.

Options:
  1. Add `:fx-args` to Spec 010 §`:sensitive?` redacted-slots list; `redact-tags` (`validate.cljc:103-113`) gains a cond-> clause for it; the extra-redact parameter on `run-validation` goes away entirely.
  2. Keep the extra-redact escape hatch as-is, document it as 'future-proofing for per-surface extra redaction targets.'

(1) is the cleaner shape — and the canonical-list claim is exactly what specs are for. `:fx-args` is a doubled-id slot semantically equivalent to `:received` for the fx surface; the spec should bless it explicitly.

Net: spec edit + ~-15 LoC (drops the parameter from `run-validation`'s signature, drops the lambda from validate-fx!, adds one cond-> clause to redact-tags).
close_reason: Closed via PR #1054 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1054). redact-tags now handles :fx-args canonically; extra-redact escape hatch dropped from run-validation; Spec 010 §:sensitive? lists :fx-args in canonical redacted slots.

title: refactor(schemas): change run-validation sensitive?-fn contract from fn to boolean — drops sensitive-by-meta? adapter
description:
Source: rf2-whepe round-2 audit, 2026-05-14 09:40 AUSEST.

`schemas/validate.cljc:81-101` has three sensitivity predicates:

```clojure
(defn- meta-sensitive? [m] (true? (:sensitive? m)))
(defn- sensitive-by-meta? [m _schema] (meta-sensitive? m))                          ;; 2-line adapter that discards _schema
(defn- sensitive-by-meta-or-schema? [m schema] (or (meta-sensitive? m) (walker/schema-has-sensitive? schema)))
```

`sensitive-by-meta?` is a 2-line adapter that drops `_schema` — used only by `validate-event!` because event vectors aren't schema-walked. It exists because `run-validation`'s contract requires `sensitive?-fn` to take `[meta schema]`.

Recommend: change `run-validation`'s contract — `sensitive?` becomes a boolean computed at the wrapper, not a fn. Pushes the decision up one frame, deletes the adapter, makes each call site read clearer:

```clojure
;; before
(run-validation handler-meta event sensitive-by-meta? ...)

;; after
(run-validation handler-meta event (meta-sensitive? handler-meta) ...)
```

For the sub-return / cofx / fx call sites, the boolean is `(or (meta-sensitive? m) (walker/schema-has-sensitive? schema))` — same line that's inside the helper, just inlined at the call.

Net: -10 LoC. Clarity. `run-validation`'s parameter list reads as data flowing through, not predicate-as-fn.

title: perf(machines): pre-build prefixes in walk-path-leaf-to-root
description:
Round-2 audit finding · rf2-2ukxv · P-r2-3.

path_walk.cljc:96-103 — walk-path-leaf-to-root builds (vec (take (inc i) path)) on every step. For a path of depth D, the walk builds D prefixes via take + vec; each is a fresh vector allocation.

Per macrostep:
- flat machine (D=1): one allocation.
- deeply hierarchical (D=5): 5 sub-vectors per picker call.
- 4 pickers per macrostep (pick-transition, pick-after-transition, pick-always-transition, find-active-invoke-all-in-tree) — so up to 20 prefix vectors per macrostep on a D=5 machine.

Fix: pre-build prefixes once at the top of the walk:

   (let [prefixes (mapv #(vec (take (inc %) path)) (range (count path)))]
     (loop [i ...] ...))

Or use subvec consistently (zero-copy slice).

Risk: low. Tiny perf win + clarifies the prefix-shape invariant.

```
::call* (let [[_ qsym args] form]
          (str "(" (if (symbol? qsym) (str qsym) (str qsym))
```

Both arms return `(str qsym)`. Either drop the `if` or fix the intent (likely `(name qsym)` for symbol-vs-string distinction). Today no caller uses a string-shaped qsym; `'hash` is the only consumer.

Bonus follow-ons (group in this bead): EF2 (reject bare-string args at `emit-arg` for safety), EF3 (recurse into collections of IR nodes), TC3 (`::call*` string-qsym test if branches diverge).

Est: -3 LoC + ~15 LoC for defensive fixes + ~10 LoC tests. Risk: low.

title: refactor(story): extract styles map from large UI files to honour 250-LoC leaf ceiling (controls / shell / view / schema_validation)
description:
## Context

From round-2 refactor audit rf2-cgqam (see `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-tools-story-2026-05-14.md` A1 / A3).

## State of the tree

The round-1 wave shipped the leaf-size ceiling (rf2-zkca8: <=250L / <=16KB). Most pure-data `.cljc` modules now honour it. **Five CLJS UI surfaces remain above the line:**

| File | LoC | Concerns |
|---|---|---|
| `controls.cljs` | 693 | styles (~95) + 8 widget renderers + dispatch + components |
| `shell.cljs` | 575 | hot-reload poll + watch-mode poll + listener wiring + shell |
| `view.cljs` (test_mode) | 563 | styles (~150) + 8 section renderers + test-view |
| `schema_validation.cljc` | 575 | pure (~270) + styles + render helpers + panel |
| `sidebar.cljs` | 561 | styles + pure helpers + components + chrome test widget |

## Repeatable pattern — extract styles

The test_mode split (rf2-8n2fz, just shipped) proved out the three-namespace pattern: pure / state / view. The styles block alone is a natural extraction:

```clojure
;; controls/styles.cljs  -- pure data, no Reagent
(def styles {:wrap {...} :row {...} ...})

;; controls.cljs
(:require [re-frame.story.ui.controls.styles :refer [styles]])
```

This is a pure rearrange -- styles ARE a leaf (no dependencies). Each extraction sheds 100-150 LoC and leaves the call-site references intact (`(:wrap styles)` etc.).

## Recommended scope (in priority order)

1. **`controls.cljs` -> `controls/styles.cljs`** (95 LoC out). Combined with the round-1 widget-vocabulary expansion this leaves the eight per-widget render fns (render-text/textarea/number/boolean/select/radio/date/color) as candidates for a further `controls/widgets.cljs` extraction (-120 LoC); but the styles split alone gets controls under 600.

2. **`view.cljs` -> `test_mode/view/styles.cljs`** (150 LoC out). The biggest single styles block in the tree. Leaves view.cljs at ~410 LoC.

3. **`shell.cljs` -> `shell/hot-reload-poll.cljs` + `shell/listener-state.cljs`** (200 LoC out across two extractions). The poll surface (`compute-fingerprint-snapshot`, `detect-and-tick!`, `watch-mode-tick!`, `poll-tick!`, `start-hot-reload-poll!`, `stop-hot-reload-poll!`) is one concern. The listener wiring (`listened-variants` atom + `ensure-listeners-for-variant!` + `teardown-listeners-for-variant!` + `ensure-variant-frame!`) is another. Leaves shell.cljs at ~370 LoC.

4. **`schema_validation.cljc` -> `schema_validation/pure.cljc`** (270 LoC out). The pure helpers (`schema-validation-event?` / `project-failure` / `project-failures` / `map-schema?` / `map-entries` / `args-violations` / `format-explain`) are already grouped under reader conditionals. Splitting them into a pure namespace mirrors the test_mode/pure.cljc precedent.

5. **`sidebar.cljs` -> `sidebar/styles.cljs` + `sidebar/test_widget.cljs`** (200 LoC out). The chrome test widget (`run-opts-for-variant` / `run-one-test!` / `run-all-tests!` / `watch-rerun!` / `test-widget`) is one cohesive concern at the foot of the sidebar -- and `run-one-test!` / `watch-rerun!` are already callable from `shell.cljs`, so a sibling ns is the natural home. Leaves sidebar.cljs at ~360 LoC.

## Notes

- Pre-alpha; no back-compat concerns. Pure rearranges; existing tests pass.
- Aligned with the round-1 leaf-size ceiling (rf2-zkca8).
- Each extraction can ship as a separate small PR; they're independent (different files).
- Bead parent: rf2-cgqam.

## Sequencing

Hot-zone-safe (sidebar.cljs / shell.cljs / controls.cljs / view.cljs are isolated leaves, no spec changes). Can dispatch in parallel as four sibling beads if Mike prefers, or do them sequentially in one PR each.

title: test(flows): pin clear-flow :frame opt routing + multi-frame registrar-slot retention
description:
From audit rf2-0b2eh §TC-2.

## Problem

`flows_test.clj` exercises `clear-flow` against the default frame only. The `:frame` opt path is documented in `registry.cljc:166`:

```clj
(clear-flow id {:frame :left})
```

— but no test runs it. Untested branches:

1. **Frame opt routing.** `(clear-flow :foo {:frame :left})` must remove the flow from frame `:left`'s slot only; sibling frame `:right`'s identically-named flow stays intact.

2. **'Last frame holding id' registrar-slot retention** (`registry.cljc:192-194`). When the same flow id is registered against two frames, clearing it from one frame must NOT unregister the registrar slot — the other frame still needs it for hot-reload tracking. Clearing from the second frame should then unregister.

3. **app-db dissoc-in is frame-local.** Clearing on frame `:left` must dissoc `:left`'s app-db only; `:right`'s app-db is untouched.

Spec 013 §Frame-scoping (line 91-105) calls out all three properties — currently unverified.

## Estimate

~30 LoC for a new deftest `clear-flow-routes-via-frame-opt` covering the three branches. Needs the test to register two frames via `reg-frame`, register the same flow id against each with different `:output` fns, then drive a clear on one frame and verify the three invariants.

Pre-alpha.

Source: audit rf2-0b2eh §TC-2.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1014 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1014. New clear-flow-routes-via-frame-opt deftest pins all three properties from audit §TC-2: frame opt routing, multi-frame registrar-slot retention, and frame-local app-db dissoc.

title: refactor(flows): consolidate reg-flow / clear-flow vs reg-flow-fx! / clear-flow-fx! late-bind hooks
description:
From audit rf2-0b2eh §ARCH-3.

## Problem

`re-frame.flows` publishes FOUR late-bind hooks for what is essentially two operations:

- `:flows/reg-flow` — public-API path
- `:flows/reg-flow-fx!` — fx-handler path
- `:flows/clear-flow` — public-API path
- `:flows/clear-flow-fx!` — fx-handler path

The fx-side delegates (`flows.cljc:80-86`) are one-line pass-throughs to the API-side `reg-flow` / `clear-flow`. The only reason they exist as distinct hooks is that the fx-side caller (`fx.cljc`'s `call-frame-scoped-hook!`) supplies `{:frame frame-id}` as a second arg, while the API-side caller (`core_flows.cljc` `defwrapper`) supplies user-supplied opts. Today these shapes are identical so both routes coincidentally work either way.

## Options

(a) **Consolidate to two hooks.** Unify the API-side and fx-side signatures to `(flow opts)` / `(id opts)` where opts always carries `{:frame ...}` (defaulting to `(current-frame)`). Drop `reg-flow-fx!` / `clear-flow-fx!` as separate hooks; both call sites resolve `:flows/reg-flow` / `:flows/clear-flow`.

(b) **Document the asymmetry.** Add a comment to `flows.cljc`'s hook-publication block explaining why four hooks rather than two.

## Files

- implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc:80-86, :192-198 — drop or document.
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:60-65 — drop two directory entries if option (a).
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:166-172 — point at the consolidated hook if option (a).
- implementation/flows/test/re_frame/late_bind_missing_test.clj — coverage adjusts if option (a).

## Estimate

~30 LoC if consolidating; doc-only if not. Defer to Mike — late-bind seam decisions belong in Spec 002.

Pre-alpha; no back-compat concern.

title: refactor(flows): conformance test should consume topo/depends-on? + lift faster prefix? to production
description:
Cluster from audit rf2-0b2eh (findings ARCH-2 + PERF-1).

## Problem

Two duplications around the prefix-overlap dependency rule:

### A. `prefix?` perf

`topo.cljc:25-27`:
```clj
(defn- prefix? [a b]
  (and (>= (count b) (count a))
       (= a (vec (take (count a) b)))))
```

`(vec (take n b))` allocates a fresh vector every call. The cheaper form is `(subvec b 0 n)` — O(1), allocates only a thin view. Inputs are always Clojure vectors by the time they reach topo (`valid-path?` enforces `vector?`), so `subvec` is safe.

Called O(n²·k) times per `topo-sort` invocation. Topo-sort runs every drain AND every `reg-flow`. Negligible at v1 flow counts but free win.

### B. Code duplication

`flows_conformance_test.clj:368-383` inlines a local `prefix?` (using `subvec` already!) + an `overlap?` helper to build the dep-graph for the `:flow-graph-topology` assertion channel. The flows artefact already exports `re-frame.flows.topo/depends-on?` (line 29-38) doing the same job.

If the dependency rule ever evolves, the conformance gate will silently disagree with the runtime.

## Work

1. Replace `topo.cljc`'s `prefix?` body with the `subvec` form.
2. In `flows_conformance_test.clj` `flow-graph-deps`: drop the local `prefix?` / `overlap?` helpers; call `(topo/depends-on? this-flow other-flow)` directly. Note the argument order: `depends-on?` takes `(b-flow a-flow)` — verify the inversion is correct (we want 'this-flow depends on other-flow').

## Files

- implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/topo.cljc:25-27 — 1-line perf change.
- implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_conformance_test.clj:368-383 — drop ~15 lines of duplication; `:require` `re-frame.flows.topo`.

## Estimate

~1 LoC production change, ~15 LoC test simplification.

Pre-alpha; no back-compat concern.

Source: audit rf2-0b2eh §ARCH-2 / PERF-1.

title: test(http): :rf.http/managed-abort on nonexistent request-id is silent no-op
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 5.3.

\`managed-abort-handler\` at \`http_managed.cljc:218-224\` silently no-ops when the id isn't in the registry. The behaviour is correct (idempotent abort) but not asserted. A regression that throws here would only surface as a flake.

title: test(http): redact-url edge cases — fragment, malformed, empty value
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 5.2.

\`http_privacy.cljc:307-312\` (\`redact-url\`) wraps \`redact-url-query-string\` which handles fragments (\`#…\`) per \`split-query-on-fragment\`. Tests at \`http_privacy_test.clj\` don't exercise:

- \`?param=val#frag\` with denylisted \`param\` (fragment preservation)
- \`#frag-only\` (no query string)
- malformed query (\`?\` with no \`=\`)
- empty value (\`?api_key=\`)

These edge cases are hand-written parser territory — exactly where coverage matters most.

**Fix:** add ~5 unit tests covering fragment + malformed + empty-value + denylist + sensitive-all edge cases. ~30 LoC test code.
close_reason: Added 8 new redact-url edge-case tests: fragment-only URLs, empty query-string, denylisted+fragment, empty-value-denylisted, sensitive-true+fragment, fragment with =/&, plus redact-url wrapper pinning. 61 privacy tests pass.

title: refactor(http): wire malli-decode through Spec 010 schemas decode pipeline
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 4.2.

Spec 014 §Schema reflection (line 188-208) and §Cross-references (line 1132) refer to \`Spec 010 §Schemas\` for \"Malli decode integration; \`:decode <schema>\` runs through \`010\`'s decode pipeline.\"

\`malli-decode\` at \`http_encoding.cljc:110-140\` \`requiring-resolve\`s \`malli.core/decode\` directly — not via any Spec 010 surface. The schemas artefact exposes decode helpers; this one bypasses them.

Either:
- **Spec drift** (claims integration that isn't there) — relax spec wording.
- **Impl shortcut** (claim correct but unwired) — switch http to call into \`re-frame.schemas/decode-with-schema\` or whichever canonical helper exists.

**Investigate first**: does \`implementation/schemas\` already expose a JSON-transformer-aware decode helper that http should be calling? If yes, switch. If no, file a downstream bead for the integration.
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: refactor(http): prepare-emit-tags walks :url twice (denylist-hit + redact)
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 3.4.

\`http_privacy.cljc:466-474\`:

\`\`\`clojure
(let [denylist-hit? (or (query-denylist-hit? (:url tags))
                        (query-denylist-hit? (get-in tags [:failure :url])))
      stamp?        (or (true? sensitive?) denylist-hit?)]
  (-> tags
      (redact-request-tags (true? sensitive?))      ;; walks :url AGAIN
      ...))
\`\`\`

\`query-denylist-hit?\` (line 429-445) parses the URL's query string. Then \`redact-request-tags\` calls \`update :url redact-url sensitive?\` (\`redact-url-query-string\`) which parses the query string **again**. Two passes per emit.

**Fix:** fuse. \`redact-url-query-string\` already returns \`[redacted-url any-redacted?]\` — use the existing return shape in \`prepare-emit-tags\` rather than computing the hit separately. Same fix for \`prepare-emit-failure\`. ~15 LoC.

Fires per retry-attempt emit on a sensitive surface; worth the touch.
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: refactor(http): split http-encoding — too many concerns under one roof
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 2.3.

\`http-encoding.cljc\` mixes 6 concerns (per its own docstring): URL/query encoding, body encoding, decode pipeline, \`:accept\` normalisation, failure-map / reply addressing, backoff. Hint the seam is too wide.

The URL/query bit (\`url-encode\`, \`params->query\`, \`merge-params\`) is naturally paired with \`http-privacy\`'s URL-redaction (split-on-query, redact-query-param). Lift both into a **\`http-url\`** sibling that owns URL handling end-to-end.

Better split: \`http-encoding\` → \`http-body\` (encode-body + realise-body + run-accept) and \`http-decode\` (decode-response-body + sniff-decoder + malli-decode + maybe-emit-decode-defaulted!). The two are unrelated to each other and to \`compute-backoff-ms\`.

**Minimum fix:** factor \`http-url\` out. \`merge-params\` is the only \`http-encoding\` fn called from \`http-transport\`; the body / decode / accept fns all sit elsewhere in the call graph. ~50 LoC moves.

Cross-references finding 2.2 (http-privacy is 489 LoC — splitting URL out of privacy shrinks both files toward the 250-line leaf-size ceiling per rf2-zkca8).
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: refactor(http): extract handlers out of http-managed.cljc façade
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 2.1.

\`http_managed.cljc\`'s docstring (lines 50-82) claims \"thin public façade\", but the file still holds two non-trivial handlers (~80 LoC): \`normalise-args\`, \`managed-handler\`, \`managed-abort-handler\`. These hold the only call to \`middleware/run-interceptor-chain!\` and the only call to \`transport/check-cljs-only-keys!\`.

Every other concern has its sibling (encoding, registry, middleware, transport, machine-wrapper, privacy). The handlers are the conspicuous absence.

**Fix:** extract into \`re-frame.http-handlers\`. \`http-managed.cljc\` becomes pure re-exports + \`fx/reg-fx\` calls + late-bind publishing. ~120 LoC moves.

**Counter-argument:** the handlers are the public-fx entry point; the registration site lives at the façade. Reasonable to keep them next to \`(fx/reg-fx :rf.http/managed ...)\`. Mike decides — defer if symmetry-vs-locality is open.
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: refactor(http): dedupe dispatch-reply pattern across transport + machine-wrapper
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 1.6.

\`http_machine_wrapper.cljc:62-71\` (\`canned-success-handler\`) and \`:73-88\` (\`canned-failure-handler\`) each manually:
- compose \`build-reply-event\`
- check \`late-bind/get-fn :router/dispatch!\`
- \`dispatch!\` with frame-cond plumbing

That's a near-verbatim copy of \`http_transport.cljc:222-234\` (\`dispatch-reply!\`). Same shape, three places.

**Fix:** lift a shared \`dispatch-reply-via-late-bind!\` helper into \`http-encoding\` (already the home of \`build-reply-event\`) or a new \`http-dispatch\` sibling. Call from \`http-transport/dispatch-reply!\` and both canned-stub handlers. ~10 LoC saved + one truth point for \"how does http dispatch its reply\".
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: refactor(http): pin clear-in-flight! ownership — triple-cleared on abort
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Top finding #3.

Cleanup is over-eager. The abort path:

1. \`managed-abort-handler\` (\`http_managed.cljc:220\`) — \`clear-in-flight!\` (1-arg).
2. Invokes \`(:abort-fn handle)\`.
3. abort-fn closure (\`http_transport.cljc:434\`) calls \`finalise-failure!\`.
4. \`finalise-failure!\` calls \`clear-in-flight!\` again (\`http_transport.cljc:266\`).

The actor-destroy path is worse:

1. \`abort-on-actor-destroy\` (\`http_registry.cljc:186-201\`) — \`swap! actor-in-flight dissoc\` + per-handle \`swap! in-flight dissoc rid\`.
2. Invokes \`:abort-fn :actor-destroyed\`.
3. abort-fn → \`finalise-failure!\` → \`clear-in-flight!\`.

Three layers. The redundancy is masked by tolerance of already-gone state, but doubles \`swap!\` traffic per abort.

**Fix:** pick one site of truth. Pull \`clear-in-flight!\` OUT of \`finalise-failure!\` into call sites that don't pre-clear (retry-exhaustion + natural-completion paths); OR leave it in \`finalise-failure!\` and remove eager clears in \`managed-abort-handler\` + \`abort-on-actor-destroy\`. Either way, **document the ownership contract** in docstrings. ~10 LoC + a docstring.

Note: the retry-side \`clear-in-flight!\` at \`http_transport.cljc:317\` IS necessary (no \`finalise-failure!\` call in that branch); preserve it.
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: refactor(http): compute-actor-id derefs app-db on every managed request
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Top finding #2.

\`http_registry.cljc:235-249\` (\`compute-actor-id\`) calls \`(frame/frame-app-db-value frame-id)\` — a full \`@(:db frame)\` deref — and walks \`[:rf/spawned <parent> <invoke-id>]\` looking for the originating event-id, on **every** \`:rf.http/managed\` invocation. Apps that don't use state machines pay the deref + the \`some\` walk for every HTTP request. Hot path for search-as-you-type, infinite scroll.

**Fix progression** (pick one):

1. **Cheap (~5 LoC):** early-out \`(when (seq (:rf/spawned db)) ...)\` guard in \`spawned-actor-id?\` — still derefs but bails before the walk.
2. **Cheaper:** \`(defonce spawn-registry-empty? (atom true))\` flip-flop maintained by spawn-fx — http hot path is a single-atom deref.
3. **Cheapest, structural:** invert ownership — spawn-fx maintains a sibling \`spawned-actor-ids\` atom keyed by actor address. \`compute-actor-id\` becomes \`(when (contains? @spawned-actor-ids event-id) event-id)\` — O(1), no \`app-db\` involvement.

Recommend (1) immediately + file separate bead for (3) if Mike wants the reverse-index restructure.
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: test(mcp-conformance): story-mcp tripwire for :rf.mcp/overflow trips on docstring references
description:
The conformance test `wire_vocab_test.clj/story-mcp-still-emits-zero-cross-mcp-markers` (rf2-j2z7o) fails because `tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools.cljc` contains two docstring/comment references to `:rf.mcp/overflow`:

- line 946: \"\`{:rf.mcp/overflow {...}}\` marker emitted via\"
- line 1047: \"replaced with a structured \`{:rf.mcp/overflow ...}\` marker. Per\"

These are documentation references — story-mcp emits the marker via `re-frame.mcp-base.overflow/overflow-payload` (per mcp-base), not via an inline literal. The tripwire was authored to catch \"story-mcp now emits this marker\" but the current shape (story-mcp re-uses mcp-base's overflow machinery) means the marker IS conceptually emitted by story-mcp — just not via an inline literal in story-mcp's own source.

## Fix options

1. **Add story-mcp to the marker's `:servers` set** for `:rf.mcp/overflow` and add a fixture. This is the spirit of the tripwire — story-mcp DOES emit overflow via mcp-base, so the contract pins it. This is also what the tripwire's failure message recommends.
2. **Whitelist docstring-only matches** in the tripwire — distinguish comment-string occurrences from real code emissions. More fragile.

Option 1 is the right shape; needs:
- Update `canonical-markers` `:rf.mcp/overflow` `:servers` to `#{:pair2-mcp :causa-mcp :story-mcp}`.
- Add a story-mcp fixture under `:fixtures` (the marker shape is the canonical mcp-base form — pair2-mcp's fixture is already a fair representation).
- Extend `server-source-files` `:story-mcp` to include the source files mentioning the marker.

Discovered while landing rf2-6m8tq (#866). Out of scope for that PR — the failure pre-dates the bead and the fix needs its own thought.
close_reason: PR #913 — strip comments and string literals (including docstrings) before the story-mcp absence-check in wire_vocab_test.clj. story-mcp's tools.cljc still mentions :rf.mcp/overflow and :rf.size/large-elided in docstrings (it routes through mcp-base.overflow/overflow-payload), but those are documentation, not inline emissions. New  state-machine helper lets the tripwire ignore them. Other source-text pins (literal-appears, near-miss-variants) keep their full-text view — typos in docstrings are still drift. Pre-fix: 4 failures/2 errors. Post-fix: 2 failures/2 errors (pre-existing, unrelated to this bead).

title: test(story-mcp): coverage gaps — instructions-spec parity, boot-precedence, recursive-catch, recorder flakes
description:
Per audit rf2-1sdzn (findings doc: ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-story-mcp-2026-05-14.md, S5 / TE2 / TE4 / TE5 / TE6).

Test-coverage gaps surfaced by the audit:

title: refactor(causa-mcp): pin day8/de-dupe compression factor with a benchmark before catalogue-entry contract enforces typical-token hints
description:
## Goal

Causa-MCP spec's Principles.md:399 cites `day8/de-dupe` "typically compresses trace bursts 3-5× without semantic loss" as a quantitative claim. No in-repo benchmark binds the number. At impl-pass time the per-tool typical-token hints will inherit the imprecision.

## Finding (from audit rf2-m9yoi)

The 3-5× compression factor is approximate-vibes today. When `003-Tool-Catalogue.md` lands, the catalogue-entry-contract requires each tool to declare its typical-token hint (per Principles.md:293-299). Hints that reference the de-dupe ratio (every trace-bus-shaped tool) inherit whatever number the spec asserts.

## Proposed action

When Causa-MCP impl lands (or earlier — could land standalone), add a small benchmark:
- New artefact at `tools/causa-mcp/bench/` or extend existing `tools/perf/`
- Fixture trace bursts at typical app scale (100/1k/10k events, varying structural depth)
- Measure de-dupe ratio per fixture
- Pin the typical-token hint to the measured number

The 3-5× claim survives or is refined. Either outcome is better than today's vibes-number-in-spec.

## Risk

Low; new artefact, no impact on existing surfaces.

## Linked
- Parent audit: rf2-m9yoi
- Findings: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-causa-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §P2-perf
notes: Closed by PR #945 — corpus-based benchmark at tools/pair2-mcp/test/re_frame_pair2_mcp/dedup_benchmark_test.cljs measured day8/de-dupe across three call-site regimes. Replaces 3-5× vibes-quote in causa-mcp/spec/004-Wire-Pipeline.md §5 with: raw trace bursts ~1.4× (28-31% reduction), high-share replays ~10× (~90% reduction), epoch slices 5-10× (already pinned for rf2-obpa9). Catalogue-entry contract can now cite regime-appropriate typical-token hints.

As mechanisms #2-#6 land more catalogue-binding contract, the section grows. pair2-mcp keeps wire-pipeline guidance in `Principles.md` and is paying the retrofit cost (rf2-rvyzy + 10 siblings in flight) — partly because the section's gravity exceeds the doc's natural boundary.

- §Privacy / default-drop section (currently Principles.md:202-247) — same concern domain

- Tool consumes the framework; doesn't extend it
- Origin tagging is the convention
- EDN canonical
- MCP not IDE plugin
- Single persistent nREPL socket
- Stage-marker-independent
- Degraded boot

- Closed-set + escape valve

The catalogue-entry contract (binding `003-Tool-Catalogue.md` to declare which mechanisms apply per tool) lives in `Principles.md` today. title: refactor(core): consolidate privacy + sensitive? + redaction into re-frame.privacy ns
description:
Audit finding A6 / SP from rf2-spr6q.

Privacy / sensitivity / redaction interact across THREE namespaces with no single point of contact:

1. privacy.cljc:50 defines redacted-sentinel = :rf/redacted.
2. elision.cljc:430 defines redacted-sentinel = :rf/redacted (DUPLICATE).
3. The :sensitive? flag is read from meta in three different ways:
   - trace/sensitive?-from-meta (trace.cljc:245-253)
   - event_emit/dispatch-on-event! (event_emit.cljc:210)
   - error_emit lookups error-event :tags :sensitive? (different path)
4. The public sensitive? predicate lives in trace.cljc:255-267 (not in privacy.cljc).

Proposed:
- Consolidate into re-frame.privacy ns (already exists).
- Move the sentinel + sensitive?-from-meta helper + the public sensitive? reader there.
- Trace stays as the emission site; privacy as the policy site.
- elision.cljc:430 sentinel becomes a re-export of privacy/redacted-sentinel.

Net: + ~ 30 LoC in privacy.cljc, -10 elsewhere, net +20 but much clearer policy locus. The conceptual win — 'where does the privacy policy live?' — answers cleanly to one namespace.

Time-box: ~ 2 hr. Risk: medium — touch points span trace, elision, event_emit, error_emit, privacy. Existing privacy + elision tests must still pass.

Surface: implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc, trace.cljc, elision.cljc, event_emit.cljc, error_emit.cljc.
close_reason: PR #938 — consolidated redacted-sentinel + sensitive?-from-meta + sensitive? into re-frame.privacy. elision sentinel re-exports privacy; router + event_emit + core + tool consumers migrated. npm run test:cljs (1818/5054 PASS) + core JVM (456/2439 PASS) + bundle-isolation PASS. title: test(pair2-mcp): conformance corpus runner + JS/CLJS test-layering README
description:
Two test-coverage gaps surfaced by rf2-7hie3 audit.

## TE3 — Conformance corpus runner

The test corpus is a unit suite, not a contract suite. There's no "for each tool, given this MCP call, expect this wire shape" corpus. The sibling machines audit (rf2-ra1he) noted the same for the framework: `spec/conformance/` fixtures aren't run from the artefact's CI.

**Recommend** a conformance ns that drives every tool through `invoke` against a stub `conn` and asserts against recorded wire-shape EDN.

## TE4 — JS vs CLJS test-layering documentation

Live nREPL tests via `test/live-nrepl.js` exist; the CLJS test corpus has no equivalent — it can't exercise the full nREPL path. The JS side covers shape; the CLJS side covers logic. The boundary is invisible.

**Recommend** `tools/pair2-mcp/test/README.md` documenting:
- What the CLJS test corpus covers (unit + pipeline logic)
- What the JS harness covers (stdio + nREPL round-trip)
- When to add a test on each side

## Why

P2 — together these would lock in current behaviour as contract and make the test-layering visible to contributors.

Surface: new files under `tools/pair2-mcp/test/`; possibly `tools/mcp-conformance/`.

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §TE3 / TE4.

title: perf(pair2-mcp): micro-benchmarks for wire-pipeline allocations, count-elided walk, dedup pass
description:
Three performance suspicions surfaced by rf2-7hie3 audit. None proven; each is a measurement task.

## Items

1. **Wire-pipeline intermediate allocations** (tools.cljs:1654-1665 in `snapshot-tool`). 5 reduce-kv passes over the per-frame map — for `:frames :all` against 3 frames, ~15 frame-map allocations to process the same 3 frames five times. ~1500 intermediate maps/sec at 100 events/sec. Likely below GC noise; worth measuring.

2. **`count-elided-markers` full-payload walk** at every emit-site. Three of the five sites (trace-window, watch-epochs, subscribe) currently can never elide (the comment says so). For them, the walk is pure waste. Skip when the eval form didn't run elision.

3. **dedup pass on 50-record epoch payloads** (`de-dupe.core/de-dupe-eq`). Equality-based; structural equality per shared subtree. Dominant cost is the per-record `:db-before` shared 50x. Likely fine; worth measuring if pagination ever pushes responses above 100 records.

## Why

P2 — none is hot today, but the file is on the hot path of every read-tool. Measurement bead so the conclusion is data-driven, not vibes-driven.

## Suggested setup

Add bench-pair2-mcp ns under `tools/perf`. Compare allocation profiles against representative payloads.

Surface: new perf-bench file; tools.cljs / vocab.cljc unchanged unless results justify.

See `ai/findings/refactor-audit-tools-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md` §P1 / P2 / P3.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1055. wire_pipeline_benchmark_test pins three suspicions. Dedup dominates snapshot pipeline (~266ms / 50-epoch); count-elided walk ~14ms; allocation churn well within budget.

title: refactor(schemas): add bundle-cost CI gate per Spec 010 §Bundle cost
description:
Spec 010 §Bundle cost (lines 567-606) catalogues exact KB measurements:

- Baseline (no schemas, no Malli): 91.7 KB
- [re-frame.schemas] required, no Malli: 97.2 KB (+5.6 KB)
- [re-frame.schemas] + [malli.core], no validation: 120.8 KB (+29.1 KB)
- Typical app: 121.5 KB (+29.8 KB)
- Heavy: 156.1 KB (+64.5 KB)

There's no CI gate verifying these stay in band. A regression that drags a transitive 50 KB into the schemas-required bundle would land silently.

Recommend: add a bundle-isolation test (similar pattern to npm run test:perf-bundle, npm run test:bundle-isolation) asserting the schemas-required-but-Malli-unused bundle is ≤ 100 KB gzipped (per the spec's 97.2 figure + margin).

Variants worth gating:
- schemas-no-malli ≤ 100 KB
- schemas+malli ≤ 125 KB
- schemas+malli+typical-app ≤ 130 KB

Falls in same family as bundle-isolation work; mostly tooling.

title: refactor(flows): perf polish — prefix? zero-alloc, complexity comment, last-inputs index shape
description:
Per audit rf2-o3hok findings Q2/Q3/Q10/PF5. Performance polish cluster:

- **Q3 — `prefix?` zero-alloc**: today `(= a (vec (take (count a) b)))` allocates a fresh vec per call. Element-compare `loop`/`recur` is zero-alloc. (~-2 LoC, clearer; flows.cljc:50-52)
- **Q2 — Complexity-bound comment on `topo-sort`**: O(N² × max-inputs × max-path-length) for graph build. Tiny at v1 target counts but worth a marginal note. Just a comment.
- **Q10/PF5 — Restructure `last-inputs` index** (flows.cljc:228-237): today `invalidate-flow-on-replace!` walks ALL `last-inputs` entries (O(N), N = total entries across frames). Re-shape `last-inputs` as `flow-id → {frame-id → inputs}`; invalidation becomes O(1) `(dissoc last-inputs flow-id)`. Wins compound during dev with many hot reloads.

Total: small but-real wins. Land as one PR.

title: bookish aesthetic mockups: produce HTML design variants for Mike to review
description:
Mike's direction 2026-05-14 ~02:35 AUSEST (appended to ai/findings/bookish-aesthetic-for-guide-2026-05-14.md):

1. As close to Nystrom's gameprogrammingpatterns.com as possible.
2. LHS index/TOC tree of material visible on every page.
3. Remove per-page "What's on this page" right-rail.
4. Remove (or minimise) top + bottom navigation bars — LHS tree replaces them.
5. Wider main content column on desktops (Nystrom's ~600px feels too tight; try 800-900px).
6. Inline-aside style (Tufte sidenotes off the table since LHS occupies left margin).

## What ships

Several self-contained HTML mockups in `ai/findings/bookish-mockups/` for Mike to review side-by-side. Each:
- Single .html file (inline CSS, no external deps beyond Google Fonts).
- Uses the SAME sample re-frame2 chapter content (pick ch.05-coeffects or ch.10-http; use the existing markdown converted to HTML; ~600-1200 words).
- Includes:
  - LHS persistent TOC tree (sketched with 8-12 chapter entries, mark the current chapter active)
  - Wider main column (test 700/800/900px variants)
  - Nystrom-style inline asides (offset box, slight indent, icon optional)
  - At least one Klipse cell mockup (just a styled code block for visual; doesn't need to work)
  - Sample code block + headings + lists + a blockquote

## Mockup variants to produce (≥5, ideally 8-10)

Vary deliberately on these axes:
- Body typeface: Cardo · EB Garamond · Lora · ET Book (self-hosted via CDN OK)
- Palette: cream (#fbf6e8-ish) · paper-white (#fbfaf6-ish) · darker-cream
- Column width: 700px · 800px · 900px
- LHS tree style: compact-monospace · serif-and-spacious · sans-serif-tight
- Aside style: Nystrom block-quote-with-vertical-rule · indented-italic · light-grey-background-box

Don't produce every cartesian combo — produce 8-10 SELECTED combinations that span the design space meaningfully. Each .html file should have a `<title>` describing its choices ("Cardo + cream + 800px + serif-tree + Nystrom-aside") so Mike can identify them at a glance.

Plus a parent `index.html` linking to all the variants with one-line descriptions, so Mike can open one tab and browse the lot.

## Coordination
- TOUCH ONLY `ai/findings/bookish-mockups/`. Brand new directory. Nothing to conflict with.

## Pre-alpha
This is design-research — throwaway HTML. Don't worry about polish or production-readiness. Focus on aesthetic variation so Mike can pick.

## Time-box
75 min — design-taste is the rate-limiter, not LoC. Quality of variation matters more than quantity.

## Wrap-up
- Set of `.html` files in `ai/findings/bookish-mockups/`.
- `index.html` linking all of them.
- Brief one-paragraph note in the bookish-aesthetic findings doc noting the mockups landed.
- `bd update <bead> --notes "Mockups at ai/findings/bookish-mockups/index.html; <N> variants"` → close.

Use good design taste. Cite Nystrom; cite Tufte CSS; cite mkdocs-material screenshots — but the output is original variants, not direct copies. Think of yourself as a design-taste consultant Mike's hired for an afternoon.

Source: Mike, 2026-05-14 ~02:35 AUSEST.
notes: Mockups: ai/findings/bookish-mockups/index.html; 9 variants across 5 axes (typeface · palette · width · TOC-style · aside-style); strongest candidates IMO #01 (Cardo+cream+800+serif-tree+Nystrom-aside — 'Nystrom widened', closest to brief) and #09 (Merriweather+Nystrom-stone-palette+900+sans-tight — strict-fidelity homage); #04 (EB Garamond 900 italic) the wildcard if you want overtly literary.

title: Klipse cells not loading on live ch.00 — diagnose + fix + live-test the deploy
description:
Mike's report 2026-05-14 ~02:25 AUSEST: "The Klipse part is not working" on live deployed ch.00. Need to TEST the live deploy and fix the root cause.

## Symptom
Live page https://day8.github.io/re-frame2/guide/00-clojurescript-for-non-clojurians/ — Klipse cells are not evaluating in the browser.

## Verify first via WebFetch
1. Fetch https://day8.github.io/re-frame2/guide/00-clojurescript-for-non-clojurians/ via WebFetch — confirm the page loads.
2. Look for the `<script src="../../klipse/klipse_plugin.min.js">` tag (currently in `docs/guide/00-clojurescript-for-non-clojurians.md` near the bottom). Verify the URL resolves to a 200 response by independent fetch.
3. Check whether the fenced code blocks emit `<code class="language-klipse">` after mkdocs's pymdownx custom_fences treatment.

## Likely root causes (test each)
1. **Path resolution**: from `/guide/00-clojurescript-for-non-clojurians/` (mkdocs serves docs/*.md as directories), `../../klipse/klipse_plugin.min.js` resolves to `/klipse/...`. If mkdocs serves it differently (e.g., as `/guide/00-clojurescript-for-non-clojurians.html`), the relative path is wrong.
2. **Fence class emission**: mkdocs.yml has a `pymdownx.superfences` `custom_fences` entry mapping `klipse` to `language-klipse`. If the config is wrong, the class doesn't get emitted.
3. **klipse_plugin.min.js 404**: the vendored file at `docs/klipse/klipse_plugin.min.js` may not be copied into the built site (mkdocs by default includes everything under `docs_dir` — verify).
4. **CSP / cross-origin issues**: GitHub Pages might block the inline `<script>` or the relative-path script load.
5. **Klipse internal failure**: klipse_plugin.min.js loads but errors at runtime.

## Fix
Once root cause identified, apply the targeted fix. Likely candidates:
- Switch to absolute path `/re-frame2/klipse/...` (note: GitHub Pages serves under /re-frame2/ for day8.github.io/re-frame2)
- Or use the `site_url`/`docs_url` mkdocs templating to make path-resolution build-time
- Or add the klipse path to mkdocs.yml `extra_javascript` (which mkdocs path-rewrites correctly)
- Or fix the `custom_fences` config

## Test the fix
After the fix is in:
1. Locally: `cd <repo> && mkdocs build --strict` should succeed.
2. Push to a test branch, watch deploy succeed.
3. WebFetch the live URL again — confirm the script tag is present, its href resolves, and a sample Klipse cell loads.

## Scope guard
NO new content edits to ch.00 — that's separate (rf2-i85w9 for redo with faithful porting). This bead is the Klipse wiring fix only.

## Coordination
- TOUCH docs/guide/00-clojurescript-for-non-clojurians.md (the script tag region) and possibly mkdocs.yml. Disjoint from in-flight surfaces.

## Pre-alpha
Klipse is the marketing feature. If it doesn't work, ch.00 doesn't deliver on its promise. Fix at root.

## Time-box
45 min — debugging + fix + live verification.
