title: Tool-Pair: epoch history + restore-epoch (Tool-Pair §Time-travel)
description:
The big one. Tool-Pair §Time-travel mandates per-frame epoch recording + restore. Largest of the new commitments.

Deliverable:
1. Per-frame ring buffer of :rf/epoch-record values (default depth 50, configurable). Each record: :epoch-id, :frame, :committed-at, :event-id, :trigger-event, :db-before, :db-after, optional :trace-events.
2. Hook into router/drain — every drain-settle (queue empty) appends an epoch-record. Atomic; a partial drain doesn't record.
3. (rf/epoch-history frame-id) — returns the vector oldest-first.
4. (rf/restore-epoch frame-id epoch-id) — sets the frame's app-db to the named epoch's :db-after, emits :rf.epoch/restored. Six documented failure modes (Tool-Pair table); each fires a structured trace under :rf.epoch/* and is a no-op on the frame's app-db.
5. (rf/configure :epoch-history {:depth N}) — runtime configuration; default 50.
6. **Production elision** — entire epoch-history machinery gated on the same goog-define as the trace surface; production builds elide.
7. Trace events: :rf.epoch/snapshotted (on each record), :rf.epoch/restored (on successful restore), plus the 6 failure-mode ops.
8. Tests: ring depth, restore happy path, all 6 failure modes, elision, per-frame isolation, schema-mismatch detection.

This is substantial — possibly split across two PRs (epoch recording + query first; restore + failure modes second). Agent should use judgement.
notes:
Spec updated in PR #39 (tool-pair-spec-gaps). New requirements baked into the bead's scope:
- :rf/epoch-record now includes :sub-runs / :renders / :effects substructure (per Spec-Schemas).
- (rf/register-epoch-cb key callback) — assembled-epoch listener mirroring register-trace-cb!.
- :render-key identity TBD pending rf2-t5tx; agent should treat it as opaque and document the open question.
Correction: actually landed via PR #48 (recovered after my mismerge of PR #43). 596 LOC of epoch.cljc + 527 LOC of epoch_test.clj.
close_reason: PR #43 merged. :renders projection empty until view layer is wired (tracked by rf2-t5tx).

title: Tool-Pair: trace-buffer ring (Spec 009 §Retain-N) + (rf/configure :trace-buffer {:depth N})
description:
Tool-Pair §How AI tools attach requires (rf/trace-buffer) — a retained ring buffer of recent trace events that pair tools query for 'what just happened' context. Spec 009 §Retain-N trace ring buffer specifies the contract: dev-only, configurable depth (default 100 per Spec 009 — verify in spec), filterable.

Deliverable:
1. Ring buffer impl in trace.cljc — circular collection, append on each emit!.
2. (rf/trace-buffer) public API — returns the buffer's events, optionally filtered by :operation / :op-type / :since.
3. (rf/configure :trace-buffer {:depth N}) config knob.
4. **Production elision** — gated on the same goog-define as the trace machinery; production builds drop the buffer entirely (no append, no storage).
5. JVM smoke + CLJS smoke covering append, filter, depth, elision behaviour.

Don't change the existing register-trace-cb! API — the ring is additive.
notes:
Spec updated in PR #39. New scope:
- :dispatch-id / :parent-dispatch-id correlation tags on :event/dispatched traces (Spec 009 §Dispatch correlation).
- :origin opt on (rf/dispatch event opts) lands on :tags :origin per Spec 002 §Dispatch origin tagging.

Implemented and merged via PR #41. Ring buffer in trace.cljc, :dispatch-id/:parent-dispatch-id in router.cljc, :origin opt in build-envelope. All three pieces gated on interop/debug-enabled? for production elision. 11 new JVM tests / 39 assertions; all CLJS Node tests still green.

title: Tool-Pair: source-coord (:ns/:line/:file) capture across all reg-* macros + verification
description:
Tool-Pair §Source-mapping requires every registration's metadata to carry :ns/:line/:file. Spec 001 §Source-coordinate capture mandates this for the CLJS reference. Audit + verify + backfill across reg-event-db, reg-event-fx, reg-event-ctx, reg-sub, reg-fx, reg-cofx, reg-frame, reg-view, reg-machine, reg-flow, reg-route, reg-app-schema, reg-error-projector, reg-head. Each macro captures the call site at expansion time and threads it into the metadata map.

Source coordinates (:ns/:line/:file) auto-captured by reg-* macros at the re-frame.core boundary on JVM; underlying fns merge via re-frame.source-coords/merge-coords. title: nine-states test fixtures fail when state isn't actually driven (revealed by rf2-9tx3)
description:
After rf2-9tx3 converted bare clojure.core/assert to cljs.test/is in
examples/nine_states/core.cljs, the previously-masked test failures are
now visible.

`run-all-tests` previously aborted at the first failed bare assert
inside test-state-1-nothing (Assert failed: (in-state? f :ui.state/nothing?)),
so subsequent fixtures never ran. With `is` they all run, and 12
assertions across all 9 test-state-* fixtures fail in roughly the same
shape:

  expected: (in-state? f :ui.state/nothing?)
  actual:   (not (in-state? :rf.frame/2 :ui.state/nothing?))

  expected: (pos? (:attempt (rf/compute-sub [:todos] (rf/get-frame-db f))))
  actual:   (not (pos? nil))

  expected: (= :archived (:state snap))
  actual:   (not (= :archived nil))

The pattern is clear: `(rf/make-frame {:on-create [:app/initialise]})`
is creating a frame, but the `:on-create` event handler is not running
against it (or not running synchronously) — every read of the frame's
db comes back as nil/empty. The test-state-1 nothing? predicate is
false because :todos/status is nil instead of :idle (defaults from
:app/initialise haven't been seeded). Likewise for state-9, the
machine snapshot isn't created.

This is independent of rf2-9tx3 (which only fixed the runner-hang
caused by the bare assert exception path). Either:
- `:on-create` is not honoured by the current make-frame
  implementation, or
- the example needs to call `dispatch-sync [:app/initialise] {:frame f}`
  explicitly inside each `(with-frame ...)` body, or
- nine-states.core's :app/initialise registration doesn't actually
  reach the new frame's handler registry (frame-vs-shared-registry
  mismatch).

Repro:

  cd implementation
  npx shadow-cljs compile node-test
  node out/node-test.js
  # → 23 failures (12 in nine-states-runs-end-to-end)

Filed from rf2-9tx3 PR.

title: Effect-map shape policing (M-8) not enforced in fx interpreter
description:
Spec migration M-8 (docs/specification/MIGRATION.md §M-8) requires the runtime to police effect-map shape: only :db and :fx are allowed at the top level. Today re-frame.events/fx-handler->interceptor silently merges other top-level keys into the :effects map without raising. A handler returning {:dispatch [:foo]} (legacy v1 form) is silently dropped — no fx fires and no error trace is emitted.

Reproducer:
  (rf/reg-event-fx :legacy (fn [_ _] {:dispatch [:bar]}))
  (rf/dispatch-sync [:legacy])
  ;; nothing happens, no :rf.error/* emitted

Expected: a structured trace event (e.g. :rf.error/invalid-effect-map or :rf.error/legacy-effect-key) flagging the offending key with :recovery :ignored / :no-recovery per Spec 009.

Surfaced by rf2-mpug fx test suite. The test asserts a :rf.error/* trace is emitted and currently uses (is (some? trace-or-nil)) so the suite passes while the gap is tracked here.
close_reason: PR #34 merged.

title: flow fixtures fail when conformance runs them: app-db not updated by flow output
description:
After rf2-y3bo claimed :flow/* capabilities so the flow-*.edn fixtures actually run, all 5 fail.

Symptoms:
- :flow/recompute-on-input-change: expected {:width 3, :height 4, :area 12}, actual {:width 3, :height 4}; subscribe-value [:area/value] returns nil instead of 12.
- :flow/multi-input-topo: expected {:width 5, :height 4, :area 20, :area*2 40}, actual {:width 5, :height 4}.
- :flow/noop-on-value-equal-input: expected {:n 7, :doubled 14}, actual {:n 7}.
- :flow/hot-reload-preserves-output: errors with :rf.error/flow-bad-output.
- :flow/toggle-via-fx: errors with :rf.error/flow-bad-output.

In every case the flow's output is not being assoc-in'd at the flow's :path. Either the conformance harness isn't realising flow handlers from :fixture/registry / :fixture/handlers, or the runtime drain isn't running flows after the dispatch (or both).

The hot-reload + toggle ones erroring with :rf.error/flow-bad-output suggests the harness IS reaching the flow but the output fn is returning the wrong shape — perhaps because the DSL body is not being realised into a clojure fn (it's running with a vector as the output fn?).

Discovered while implementing rf2-y3bo. The smoke_test.clj flow tests pass (they construct flows with literal Clojure fns), so the runtime itself works for the basic case — the gap is in the conformance harness's flow-realisation path.
close_reason: PR #28 merged.

title: Tests: SSR end-to-end (Spec 011) — full request lifecycle with hydration handshake

Plus ssr-with-fx-override and ssr-end-to-end smoke tests. Solid base; need a comprehensive request-lifecycle test that exercises the whole flow in one go:

title: Tests: drain semantics (Spec 002) — run-to-completion, depth limit, async vs sync, dispatch-during-handler
description:
Spec 002 §Drain semantics is load-bearing for re-frame2's behavioural contract. Today only one or two paths are tested transitively via login-machine-flow and dispatch-sync-in-handler-errors. Need targeted coverage:

- run-to-completion: events queued during a handler run before the handler returns; verify the handler completes before the next event drains.
- drain depth limit: deep dispatch chain, verify :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded raises with atomic rollback.
- dispatch-sync inside a handler: verify :rf.error/dispatch-sync-in-handler raises (already partially covered).
- dispatch async vs sync interleaving: events queued via dispatch resolve after the current drain; sync side-events resolve before.
- per-frame drain isolation: events on frame A do not interleave with frame B's drain.

Deliverable: NEW file implementation/test/re_frame/drain_test.clj with ~5 deftests covering each path. Each deftest's docstring references the relevant Spec 002 section anchor.

PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/22. Filed rf2-8hi7 for the spec/impl gap on 'atomic rollback of failing handler :db' — implementation does not roll back; test asserts what drain! actually does.

title: Browser-test runner hangs after runtime_cljs_test/reg-view-macro-double-def-investigation
description:
After landing rf2-zoem (PR #15), the new shadow-cljs :browser-test +
Playwright runner times out locally (and likely in CI too) waiting for
the cljs.test summary. The browser console shows tests running in this
order:

  1. hash_check_cljs_test/jvm-cljs-hash-parity (prints :cljs-canonical, :cljs-hash) — passes
  2. (machines_cljs_test runs silently)
  3. nine_states_cljs_test/nine-states-runs-end-to-end — ERRORS with
     'Assert failed: (in-state? f :ui.state/nothing?)' and the error
     also surfaces as a browser pageerror (uncaught)
  4. runtime_cljs_test/reg-view-macro-double-def-investigation
     (prints :outer-def-result-type cljs.core/MetaFn) — runs
  5. (silence — no further test output, no summary)

Hypotheses:

- The 'Assert failed' from nine_states.core/test-state-1-nothing (a
  bare clojure.core/assert wrapped in (with-frame ...)) escapes
  cljs.test.run_block's try/catch via Reagent's batched render
  scheduler and pollutes a microtask queue, eventually deadlocking the
  block driver in run-block.
- OR: the next test after :outer-def-result-type, which is
  runtime_cljs_test/h-rewrites-namespaced-view-keys, hits something in
  the h macro / reg-view interaction that blocks indefinitely under
  Reagent in a real browser (where reactive scheduling is async).
  Under :node-test, *animation-frame is sync and the same code returns
  immediately.

Repro:

  cd implementation
  npm install
  npx playwright install chromium
  npm run test:browser

The runner times out after BROWSER_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS (default 120s).
Compare with `npm run test:cljs` (Node), which completes and reports
'Ran 52 tests containing 149 assertions. 11 failures, 1 errors.' with
exit code 1.

The fix is one of:
- Refactor nine_states.core's test-state-* fixtures to NOT use bare
  clojure.core/assert (which throws JS Error in a way the
  Reagent-on-real-browser scheduler can't reabsorb). Use cljs.test
  `is` directly, or wrap dispatches and reads in a try/catch.
- Or, gate the nine_states.core mount-point block (defonce root ...)
  to only fire when window.parent != window (i.e. not in test runner
  pages).
- Or, refactor h / reg-view to avoid whatever async work blocks
  h-rewrites-namespaced-view-keys in a real browser.

Diagnostic value: this bead is exactly the kind of thing the new
:browser-test target exists to surface. The infrastructure works as
designed; the surfaced failure is real and worth fixing.
close_reason: PR #26 merged; nine-states pollution actually fixed by rf2-coks.

title: Bug: reg-machine first dispatch doesn't cascade :initial through compound states
description:
Discovered by the rf2-pc82 agent. When reg-machine registers a machine with a compound initial state — e.g. {:initial :foo :states {:foo {:initial :bar :states {:bar {} :baz {}}}}} — the runtime's first dispatch leaves the snapshot at {:state :foo} (single keyword) rather than descending through the compound's :initial chain to {:state [:foo :bar]}.

Spec 005 §Initial-state cascading mandates the descent: 'a target landing on a possibly-compound node descends through :initial chain until a leaf.' initial-cascade is implemented in machines.cljc but appears to only run inside transitions, not at first-dispatch / on-create snapshot synthesis.

Workaround in PR #9 (rf2-pc82 tests): a seed-snapshot! helper positions machines at a known compound-leaf state via direct app-db assoc-in, bypassing :on-create.

Fix: when reg-machine creates the initial snapshot (or :on-create runs), apply initial-cascade to the declared :initial. The snapshot's :state should be the leaf path, not the parent keyword.

Discovered-from: rf2-pc82.
close_reason: PR #23 merged.

title: Bug: sub-machine + :rf/machine reg-sub never landed on main (PR #2 reverted)

title: Tests: comprehensive routing test coverage (Spec 012 audit + gap-fill)
description:
**Why:** Routing today has only six conformance fixtures (`routing-match-url`, `routing-navigate`, `route-fragment-change`, `route-navigation-blocked`, `route-ranking-precedence`, `route-stale-nav-token-suppression`) and no JVM/CLJS smoke tests beyond what those fixtures exercise. Spec 012 defines a much wider surface — per-route data loading, scroll restoration, query strings, redirects, multi-frame routing, SSR integration. Coverage is shallow.

**Deliverable:** comprehensive routing tests at three levels.

**Conformance fixtures (in `docs/specification/conformance/fixtures/`):**

Per Spec 012's canonical surface, gap-fill fixtures for at least:

- `routing-on-match-fires` — `:on-match` events fire on a successful match.
- `routing-not-found` — unmatched URL routes to `:rf.route/not-found` and emits the canonical trace.
- `routing-redirect-on-match` — `:redirect-on-match` short-circuits and routes to the destination.
- `routing-can-leave-blocks` — `:can-leave` guard pauses navigation through `:rf/pending-navigation`; resume / cancel both work.
- `routing-query-string-coercion` — query-string params coerce to declared shapes (`:int`, `:keyword`, etc.).
- `routing-fragment-as-slice` — fragment changes update `:rf/route :fragment` without firing `:on-match`.
- `routing-scroll-restoration` — declared scroll behavior fires the correct fx on navigation (`:rf.scroll/top` etc.).
- `routing-nested-layout` — nested route segments resolve their parent layout.
- `routing-multi-frame` — same route registered in two frames navigates each frame independently.

**JVM smoke tests (in `implementation/test/re_frame/smoke_test.clj`):**

- `routing-bootstrap` — `(rf/reg-route ... )` + `(rf/dispatch [:rf.route/navigate ...])` updates `:rf/route` slice.
- `routing-pending-nav-protocol` — drive a `:can-leave` guard through pause / continue / cancel, verify slice transitions.
- `routing-nav-token-staleness` — issue two navigations in flight; the older one's resolution is suppressed.

**CLJS tests (in `implementation/test/re_frame/runtime_cljs_test.cljs`):**

- `routing-handle-url-change-cljs` — exercise the URL-change path under the Reagent adapter.
- `routing-frame-provider-routing-cljs` — multi-frame routing under React context, ensuring `:rf/route` resolves per-frame.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- All new fixtures pass `clojure -M:test` alongside the existing 43+.
- New JVM smoke tests pass.
- New CLJS tests pass under `:node-test` and (once rf2-443l lands) the browser runner.
- Each test references the relevant Spec 012 section in a comment so the contract anchor is explicit.

**Related:**
- rf2-443l (browser runner) — gates the CLJS tests' browser run.
- rf2-3nqu (machine fixtures) — same shape of work, different domain.

**Suggested workflow:** start with conformance fixtures (highest leverage; mirror the existing ones); then JVM smoke; then CLJS. Don't try to be exhaustive — pick the high-value gaps from Spec 012's surface inventory.

title: Tests: missing state-machine conformance fixtures (cross-actor-send, spawn-from-action, destroy-clears-snapshot, spawn-on-spawn-callback, machine-actor-isolation)

title: Tests: JVM equivalents for sub-topology glitch-freedom (diamond, chain, value-equal)
description:
**Why:** the new sub-topology tests (`sub-topology-glitch-free-diamond`, `-chain`, `sub-correctness-on-value-equal-input`) are CLJS-only because they exercise Reagent's reaction propagation. The JVM reference uses the plain-atom adapter, which has different semantics (no caching, recompute every deref) but should satisfy the same glitch-free contract.

**Deliverable:** equivalent JVM tests in `implementation/test/re_frame/smoke_test.clj` exercising:
1. Diamond: app-db → {a,b} → c via compute-sub. Single mutation, c is correct, no opportunity for glitch (plain-atom recomputes each deref).
2. Chain: app-db → a → b → c via compute-sub. Same shape; verify final value.
3. Value-equal mutation: a no-op `(assoc db :unrelated "z")` keeps downstream computed values correct.

**Note:** plain-atom is glitch-impossible by construction (no caching, no propagation queue). The JVM tests are a contract-shape pin: they verify compute-sub on diamond and chain shapes returns the right algebraic result. They should NOT use Reagent.

title: State-machine API surface: docs/guide/05 references symbols not exported by re-frame-2.core
description:
docs/guide/05-state-machines.md uses these symbols, none of which are exported by `re-frame-2.core`:

- `(rf/sub-machine :auth.login/event-handler)` — sugar over a framework-shipped `:rf/machine` sub. Not in core.
- `(rf/machine-handler [:auth :login] login-flow)` — claimed helper that returns a `reg-event-fx`-shaped handler. Core exposes `create-machine-handler` instead, with a different signature (no `:machine-path`).
- `(rf/reg-machine-guard :auth.login/under-retry-limit ...)` — guard registry. Not in core.
- `(rf/reg-machine-action :auth.login/issue-request ...)` — action registry. Not in core.
- xstate-flavoured `:guards`/`:actions`/`:meta` slots inside a transition table — Spec 005's transition-table grammar may not include all of these.

Plus prose claims that may or may not match Spec 005:
- `:machine-path` as a registration metadata key for the snapshot location.
- "Transition tables are pure data, runtime owns the snapshot, headless test via `machine-transition`" — the impl matches this for the basic case, but the rich grammar in the chapter (`:cond`, `:entry`, multi-target arrays) needs verification against the transition spec.

Two questions to resolve:
1. Which of these symbols are aspirational (post-v1) vs missed exports?
2. For each one we keep aspirational, the guide chapter needs a "the API is sketched here; not all of it ships in v1" caveat — currently it reads as fully implemented.

This is the largest gap in the guide-vs-impl audit. Lower urgency than ch.02/04 because users hitting state machines will have already read enough of the spec to spot the gap.
notes:
## Decisions taken (2026-05-08)

**:data is canonical** (Spec 005 §Naming). The extended-state slot is `:data`; snapshot is `{:state :data}`. `:context` is FORBIDDEN — overloaded with re-frame's interceptor-context and React-context idioms.

**Guards/actions/sub-machine sub fns receive the whole snapshot.** They never receive `:data` directly; they receive `{:state :data :meta?}` and pull what they need.

**`sub-machine` is approved as a core convenience.** Thin wrapper over `(get-in db [:rf/machines machine-id])`. Adds one symbol to core; saves users from spelling the reserved path themselves and reinforces "the snapshot is the state".

## Open question added to scope: parameter-style standardisation

Today the corpus uses two forms inconsistently for guard/action/sub fns:

  ;; Form A (destructured) — Spec 005 §Registration L386
  (fn [{:keys [data]} _] ...)

  ;; Form B (whole-arg) — Pattern-LongRunningWork, machines.cljc impl
  (fn [snapshot _] (... (:data snapshot)))

Three plausible policies:
1. Canonical Form A everywhere.
2. Canonical Form B everywhere.
3. Both first-class — spec adds one paragraph saying either is fine.

Decision needed before ch.05 rewrite lands; otherwise the new examples will themselves drift from whatever the rest of the corpus does.

## Resulting work scope

1. ch.05 rewrite per the original points (drop reg-machine-{guard,action}, move guards/actions inside the spec map, replace machine-handler with create-machine-handler, drop :machine-path, replace :context with :data).
2. Audit and harmonise param style across Spec 005, Pattern-* docs, machines.cljc per the policy chosen above.

title: Decide frame-provider public API: rf/frame-provider Reagent component vs views/build-frame-provider factory
description:
The guide (docs/guide/04 §frame-provider, §A small example: split counter) writes:

    [rf/frame-provider {:frame :left}  [counter-view]]
    [rf/frame-provider {:frame :right} [counter-view]]

The implementation has no `rf/frame-provider` symbol. The real counter example uses a factory + frame-id positional:

    [(v/build-frame-provider :counter)
     :counter
     [counter-buttons]]

Two paths:
1. **Add `rf/frame-provider` as the documented API.** It would be a Reagent component accepting a props map `{:frame frame-id}` and children. Build it on top of `build-frame-provider` so the existing impl substrate is preserved. Wins: the prose-shape (`{:frame :left}`) reads idiomatically and matches React-context conventions; one symbol to import.
2. **Update the guide to use `views/build-frame-provider`.** Cost: clunkier idiom (`[(v/build-frame-provider :left) :left [counter]]`); duplicates the frame id; requires an extra `:as v` import.

Path 1 looks like the natural shipping API; the guide may have been the source of truth and the impl drifted. Decision drives whether the guide gets edited or the impl grows a thin wrapper.
notes: Resolved (Mike, 2026-05-08): Path 1 — add rf/frame-provider as a Reagent component to re-frame.core. Props-map shape ({:frame frame-id} + children). Thin wrapper over build-frame-provider; the factory becomes lower-level substrate. Implementation bead filed.

title: Decide reg-view body: auto-inject dispatch/subscribe vs require dispatcher/subscriber capture
description:
The guide (docs/guide/02 §The view, docs/guide/04 §The Var-reference idiom) states that inside a `reg-view` body, `dispatch` and `subscribe` are *injected* — bound to the surrounding frame — so view bodies can be frame-blind:

    (rf/reg-view :counter
      (fn []
        [:div
         [:button {:on-click #(dispatch [:counter/inc])} "+"]
         [:span @(subscribe [:count])]]))

The implementation does NOT inject them. The real example in `examples/counter/core.cljs` requires explicit capture:

    (reg-view :counter-buttons
      (fn []
        (let [d (rf/dispatcher)
              s (rf/subscriber)]
          [:div
           [:button {:on-click #(d [:counter/dec])} "-"]
           [:span @(s [:count])]])))

Two paths:
1. **Make the impl match the guide** — the macro `reg-view` rewrites the body to bind locals `dispatch`/`subscribe` to frame-bound fns captured at render time. Cost: macro complexity + potential aliasing surprises if the user already has those names in scope. Win: the prose claim becomes true and view bodies are visibly frame-blind.
2. **Make the guide match the impl** — document the `(rf/dispatcher)` / `(rf/subscriber)` capture pattern as canonical. Cost: every view body now opens with two `let` bindings; less elegant. Win: zero macro magic.

Decision needed before mechanical doc fixes can complete the namespace sweep — without a direction, every view example in the guide either over-promises or under-explains.
notes:
Reagent v2 directive (2026-05-08): re-frame2 targets Reagent 2, not 1.2. This strengthens the Form-1-only recommendation: Reagent 2's hooks-based functional components make Form-3 (class-based lifecycle methods) even less idiomatic. The macro-injection-into-Form-3 problems (data-shaped body, var-bound bodies invisible to the macro, lifecycle methods running outside render context) become 'don't bother' rather than 'too hard'. Form-1 + Form-2 (runtime-detected) is the pragmatic scope; Form-3 users continue to use explicit (rf/dispatcher) / (rf/subscriber) capture if they need it.
Resolved (Mike, 2026-05-08): auto-inject + defn-shape. Final surface: reg-view (macro, defn-shaped, auto-defs symbol, auto-injects dispatch/subscribe, compile-errors on non-literal-fn bodies — Form-1 + Form-2 only) + reg-view* (public fn, no magic, for metaprogramming). Both in re-frame.core. Implementation bead filed (see linked task). Form-3 explicitly out of scope per rf2-25aq Reagent v2 directive.

title: Spec: should normative requirements be rewritten in RFC 2119 phrasing (MUST / SHOULD / MAY)?
description:
Question raised during the implementation work: would the spec corpus (docs/specification/*.md) read more cleanly — and produce fewer 'is this mandatory or just descriptive?' beads — if the normative language followed RFC 2119 conventions (MUST / SHOULD / MAY etc.)?

Motivation:
- Several beads filed this session (rf2-r044, rf2-smba, rf2-sklf, rf2-pz9f) exist because the current spec phrasing doesn't separate 'this is the contract' from 'this is what the reference impl does'. Normative keywords force that separation.
- AI implementers (the spec's stated audience per Goal 2) parse MUST / SHOULD reliably; conformance fixtures could be mechanically cross-referenced, since each fixture pins a specific MUST.
- Cross-runtime portability — host language ports targeting the same spec need the same MUST / MAY split.

Counter-arguments:
- The current spec has a distinctive narrative voice. Wholesale RFC-2119-ification would flatten it. The 'spec-as-argument' function (000-Vision arguing why re-frame2 exists) doesn't suit normative phrasing.
- Cost: ~14 spec docs to rewrite, all cross-references break.

Suggested middle path (cheapest experiment first):
- Pick ONE doc — 002-Frames.md is the most heavily-referenced contract.
- Add a 'Contract' / 'Normative requirements' block near the top with MUST / SHOULD / MAY bullets, each cross-referenced to its conformance fixture(s).
- Leave the rest of the doc in narrative voice for rationale / examples.
- See if it earns its keep — easier to evolve, mechanically grep-able for fixture mapping, doesn't lose readability.
- If yes, scale to other docs; if it clutters more than helps, abandon.

Either way, this is a Mike-judgement call. Filed for explicit consideration rather than as an action item.
notes:
Resolved (Mike, 2026-05-09): Option B — pilot in 002-Frames.md.

Add a Normative Requirements (Contract) block to 002-Frames.md, placed at the END of the doc (or as a sister file 002-Frames-Contract.md). MUST/SHOULD/MAY bullets, each cross-linked to its conformance fixture(s). Leave the rest of 002-Frames.md in narrative voice.

Implementation bead filed. After the pilot lands, observe for a few weeks: if no spec-clarity beads land against 002-Frames AND the format earns its keep with conformance-fixture cross-referencing, scale to other heavily-referenced specs (004-Views, 005-StateMachines, 006-ReactiveSubstrate, 009-Instrumentation, 010-Schemas, 014-HTTPRequests). If it clutters more than it helps, abandon.

title: reg-view macro: outer (def x ...) wrapper double-defs against the macro's own def
description:
Across the v2-API-aligned examples (login/, realworld/*, routing/, 7guis/, ssr/) every reg-view call follows the pattern:

  (def login-form
    (reg-view :auth.login/form
      {:doc "..."}
      (fn render-auth-login-form [] ...)))

The reg-view macro (re-frame-2.views-macros) expands to
  (def <kw-name> (reg-view* <kw> <meta> <fn>))
i.e. (def form (reg-view* :auth.login/form ...)) — which evaluates to the var #'form.

The outer (def login-form ...) then binds login-form to that var, producing a var-of-var. Reagent's auto-deref MAY rescue this in practice but it's brittle and Spec 004 §reg-view defs the Var by default already commits to the macro defining the Var with the keyword's name.

Pick one resolution:
(a) Drop the outer (def some-name ...) wrappers across the examples and reference [form] / [banner] / [root] / [preview] / [home] / etc. directly — the macro already binds them.
(b) Change the macro so reg-view does NOT auto-def — let users wrap in their own (def some-name (reg-view* ...)). Spec 004 §reg-view defs the Var would need to relax.
(c) Extend the macro to accept an optional :as some-name so users pick the local name.

Implementation today follows (a) per Spec 004; the recently-landed example commit landed (b)-style wrappers without removing the macro's auto-def. Pick a direction and align spec, macro, and examples in one pass.
notes:
Empirically: in CLJS the double-def works because (def x y) at the CLJS level evaluates y and returns the SAME JS value (no Var-objects like JVM Clojure). So (def login-form (reg-view :auth/form ...)) results in BOTH login-form AND form bound to the same MetaFn — two names, same value. Verified via reg-view-macro-double-def-investigation in runtime-cljs-test (commit pending).

The pattern works at runtime but is still:
- Two names for the same view (semantic duplication / drift risk).
- Spec 004 says reg-view defs the Var by-keyword-name (so 'login-form' shouldn't exist; only 'form' should).
- Reliant on CLJS-specific def-returns-value semantics; the same pattern in JVM-side code would create var-of-var.

Reduces severity from 'breaks at runtime' to 'spec-vs-example mismatch worth aligning when convenient'. Pick a resolution per the bead body.
Verified after rf2-d0pi merged. Grep across examples/ + implementation/ shows zero (def x (reg-view ...)) wrappers in source code. The defn-shape macro now emits the def itself; the old wrapper shape no longer compiles (compile-error contract pinned by reg-view-rejects-* tests). Doc drift in docs/guide/ + docs/specification/Construction-Prompts.md is tracked separately by rf2-xv7e. Added regression guard test 'rf2-atsv: expansion contains exactly one def form' in implementation/test/re_frame/views_macros_test.clj that asserts vm/expand-reg-view emits exactly one def for plain / docstring / metadata-override input shapes. All 10 views-macros tests green.

title: Spec: 013-Flows must reflect frame-scoped registration / clear semantics
description:
Spec 013 currently treats flows as a process-global registry — reg-flow and clear-flow take only a flow id; the description in §Drain integration / §Reference doesn't say which frame they belong to. The implementation has now moved to frame-scoped flows (commit 86ade3a):

  (rf/reg-flow flow)              ; defaults frame to (current-frame)
  (rf/reg-flow flow {:frame :f})  ; explicit
  (rf/clear-flow id)
  (rf/clear-flow id {:frame :f})

Update Spec 013 to:
- State explicitly that flows are frame-scoped (per the rf2-jflj rationale: undo / time-travel boundaries are frame-local).
- Document the :frame opt on reg-flow / clear-flow.
- Update §Drain integration to clarify run-flows! evaluates only the called frame's flows.
- Update §Reference to show the registry shape: {frame-id {flow-id flow-map}}.
- Re-affirm that the :rf.fx/reg-flow / :rf.fx/clear-flow runtime fx receive {:frame frame-id} from the cofx and thread it through.

title: Spec: h macro view-vs-DOM-tag heuristic is undocumented
description:
Spec 004 §The h macro says h walks hiccup at compile time and rewrites [:keyword args] into runtime view-resolution calls 'for every keyword present in the view registry'. But:

(a) The view registry isn't known at compile time (CLJS runtime state), so a literal-registry check is impossible.
(b) The implementation (views_macros.clj) uses 'namespaced keyword' as the heuristic — :my-app/widget rewrites; bare :div / :p don't. This works because HTML tag names are conventionally bare. But the spec doesn't document this heuristic.

Either:
- Document the namespaced-keyword heuristic in Spec 004 §The h macro.
- Provide an explicit declarations form ((h [...] :views #{:my-app/widget})) where the user lists view ids.
- Use a different rewriting trigger (e.g. (h-view :my-app/widget args)).

The current heuristic is reasonable but should be locked in the spec.
notes:
Resolved (Mike, 2026-05-08): Drop the h macro entirely.

Reasoning aligned with rf2-7cb2 (drop re-frame.alpha) and rf2-iyzm (Form 2 Var-ref canonical): clean canonical surface beats two-ways-to-do-it. Late-binding via (rf/view :id) is the canonical handle for cross-namespace and hot-reload-by-id needs. The namespaced-keyword heuristic was fragile (single-segment ambiguity, namespaced-HTML false rewrites) and would require ongoing maintenance.

Implementation bead filed.

title: Spec: machine def :id requirement is implicit, breaks pure machine-transition calls
description:
create-machine-handler (machines.cljc) requires the machine def to carry :id — it computes the snapshot-path as [:rf/machines (:id machine)]. But:

(a) Conformance fixtures pass machine defs WITHOUT :id (machine-transition.edn, hierarchical-*.edn, etc.). The pure machine-transition fn doesn't need :id; create-machine-handler does.

(b) Spec 005 §Registration mentions reg-machine and create-machine-handler but doesn't explicitly say :id is mandatory in the def passed to create-machine-handler.

(c) The bug surfaces silently: missing :id → snapshot-path is [:rf/machines nil] → snapshot reads/writes go to a nil-key slot in app-db that no sub queries. The machine appears to never run.

Fix one of:
- Document :id as mandatory for create-machine-handler in Spec 005.
- Have create-machine-handler error if :id is missing.
- Default :id to a sentinel (less safe; conflates machines).
close_reason: Done. Spec 005 §Where snapshots live now states 'the transition-table spec map MUST NOT carry :id; the id is the surrounding registration's event-id'. create-machine-handler reads machine-id from event[0] at handler-call time instead of (:id machine); the silent-bug failure mode is gone (the previous defensive throw is also removed). reg-machine takes id explicitly. Examples and smoke tests updated to drop :id from machine specs. Tests green on both runtimes.

title: Spec: [:event-arg n key] form overloads default-for-nil with key-access
description:
The conformance fixture DSL's [:event-arg n] form is documented as taking an optional 3rd element as a default for nil. But several fixtures use a keyword 3rd element to mean 'access this key in the resolved value':

- routing-navigate.edn — [:event-arg 2 {}] uses {} as default-for-nil.
- ssr-hydration-mismatch.edn — [:event-arg 1 :rf/app-db] uses :rf/app-db to access the payload's :rf/app-db key.

The implementation (re-frame-2.conformance/resolve-value) disambiguates by type: keyword 3rd + map value → key access, otherwise → default. This works but is undocumented overloading. Either:

(a) Add :get-event-arg / :event-arg-key as the explicit key-access form (impl already has :get-event-arg) and have the fixture corpus migrate to it.
(b) Document the overload in conformance/README.md.

(a) is cleaner long-term.
notes:
Resolved (Mike, 2026-05-09): Option (a) — explicit :get-event-arg for key-access; migrate fixtures.

[:event-arg n] / [:event-arg n default-val] is default-for-nil only. The 3rd element is never type-dispatched.
[:get-event-arg n :some-key] is the explicit key-access form.

Impl already has :get-event-arg. Migration is the small fixture sweep + impl removal of the type-dispatch branch in resolve-value.

Aligns with the explicit-over-overloaded pattern: rf2-iyzm Var-ref canonical; rf2-7cb2 drop alpha; rf2-n4um drop h heuristic; rf2-d0pi compile-error on non-literal-fn; rf2-qppo data-direct contract.

title: Spec: :on-spawn callback path semantics — snapshot-relative vs data-relative
description:
Regular machine actions interpret :set step paths as data-relative — a :set [:correct-count] target writes to snapshot.:data.:correct-count. But the :on-spawn callback in examples/login/core.cljs and the conformance fixture invoke-spawn-on-entry-destroy-on-exit use :set [:data :pending] expecting it to be SNAPSHOT-relative — write at snapshot.:data.:pending.

Two interpretations of :set within machine action bodies, undocumented. The implementation (conformance.cljc/realise-on-spawn-handler) treats :on-spawn bodies' :set paths as snapshot-relative and regular-action :set as data-relative. Spec 005 should explicitly state which path convention applies to :on-spawn.
notes:
Confirmed by the rf2-3nqu fixture-authoring agent: the realise-machine-handlers :set op uses data-relative paths (e.g. [:count]) while the :on-spawn handler is snapshot-relative ([:data :count]). The agent worked around it; bead remains open with the empirical confirmation.
Resolved (Mike, 2026-05-09): Option A — :on-spawn paths are data-relative, consistent with regular machine actions and with the rf2-qppo guard/action tightening.

State-machine body contract is now uniform: paths in :set / :update steps are data-relative. The rare snapshot-access case uses an explicit escape hatch (:set-snapshot [:state ...] or similar — exact op name decided in the impl bead) or the 3-arity ctx-receiving fn-shape from rf2-qppo.

Migration is small: realise-on-spawn-handler interprets paths as data-relative; one fixture (invoke-spawn-on-entry-destroy-on-exit.edn) and one example (examples/login/core.cljs) sweep.

Implementation bead filed.

title: Spec: machine sub-event routing format is under-specified
description:
Spec 005 §Registration shows the dispatch shape [:machine-id [:inner-event ...]] but doesn't explicitly cover what happens when fx callbacks (conj on-success response) onto a 2-element on-success template like [:auth.login/flow [:auth.login/success]]. The conj produces a 3-element vector [:machine-id [:inner-event] response] which the runtime must fold into [:inner-event response] for the inner machine-transition.

The implementation now does this fold (commit bda3de7), but the spec should explicitly document the fold convention so http-style callback patterns don't break silently. Add to Spec 005 §Registration or a new §Sub-event routing — extra args fold into the inner event.
close_reason: Done. Spec 005 §Registration now has a §Extra-args fold subsection documenting the [:machine-id [:inner-id] & extras] → [:inner-id & extras] fold the implementation has shipped since commit bda3de7. Covers HTTP-callback conj patterns, promise resolution, and the trigger conditions (length >= 3, second is a vector). Compatibility fallback for non-vector seconds also called out.

title: Spec: render-to-string return shape is internally inconsistent
description:
Spec 011 says render-to-string emits an HTML string with data-rf-render-hash on the root element. But examples/ssr/core.cljc destructures the return as {:keys [html render-hash]} — implying a map. Two contradictory contracts; the implementation chose the string-with-data-attr form (and added a separate render-tree-hash fn) so the conformance fixtures pass. Either: (a) Update Spec 011 + examples/ssr/core.cljc to standardise on string-return + data-rf-render-hash injection (current impl). (b) Update Spec 011 + the implementation + the conformance ssr/render-to-string fixture to return a map. The conformance fixture expects a string (literal '
...
'), so (a) is the more conservative choice.
close_reason: PR #37 merged.

title: Spec: trace event :source position is inconsistent across fixtures
description:
Some conformance fixtures expect :source at the top level of a trace event ({:operation :event :source :ui :tags {...}}), others expect it inside :tags ({:operation :event :tags {:source :ssr-hydration}}). Compare:

- docs/specification/conformance/fixtures/dispatch-envelope.edn — :source :ui at top level.
- docs/specification/conformance/fixtures/ssr-hydrate.edn — :source :ssr-hydration inside :tags.

The implementation works around this by mirroring :source at BOTH positions in trace/emit! (re_frame_2/trace.cljc). The spec should pick ONE shape — Spec 009 §Core fields says top-level — and update the offending fixtures.
close_reason: Done. Two fixtures (ssr/hydrate, ssr/head-hydration) updated to put :source at the top level of the trace event per Spec 009 §Required top-level fields. trace/emit! now hoists :source (and :recovery) out of :tags rather than mirroring at both positions. Tests green on both runtimes.

title: Make machine actor-id allocation frame-scoped
notes: Current implementation keeps spawn-counter as a process-global map keyed only by machine-id in implementation/src/re_frame_2/machines.cljc. That lets independent frames share one actor-id sequence for the same machine id, which weakens frame isolation and deterministic replay/restore. Review the spec and implementation so actor-id allocation is scoped by frame (or otherwise derived from frame + machine) rather than process-global machine-id only.
close_reason: Done. spawn-counter now keyed on [frame-id machine-id]; create-machine-handler stamps :rf/frame on the machine def before transitioning; pure machine-transition calls use :rf/transition-pure as the sentinel frame so the conformance corpus's deterministic ids hold. Smoke-tested via spawn-id-is-frame-scoped.

title: Make flows explicitly frame-scoped in both the spec and the implementation
notes:
Rationale: to preserve the undo story, a flow must belong to a frame/runtime instance rather than acting like one global registration applied across all frames. The current implementation evaluates flows per frame at runtime, but keeps the flow registry global in implementation/src/re_frame_2/flows.cljc. Review both the specification and the implementation so flow ownership, registration, clearing, and undo/time-travel semantics are explicitly frame-scoped.
Concrete change to make: flow ownership/registration/clearing should become explicitly frame-scoped, not just flow evaluation state. The current implementation keeps flow definitions in one global atom and clear-flow removes outputs from every frame. Tighten both spec and code so undo/time-travel semantics are unambiguously frame-local.
close_reason: Done. flows registry now keyed {frame-id {flow-id flow-map}}; reg-flow / clear-flow accept a :frame opt defaulting to (current-frame); run-flows! reads only the called frame's slot; :rf.fx/reg-flow and clear-flow threaded the cofx :frame through. clear-flow scopes db dissoc to the named frame only. Smoke-tested via flows-are-frame-scoped. The companion spec change (Spec 013 wording) is filed as a follow-up.

title: Make flows machine-scoped instead of globally registered per-frame state
notes:
Current implementation keeps flows in a single process-wide atom in implementation/src/re_frame_2/flows.cljc:20, tracks last-inputs by [frame-id flow-id] in flows.cljc:25, and runs all registered flows after each frame drain via run-flows! in flows.cljc:187 and router.cljc:136. There is no machine-local flow scope. Corrective direction: flows should be scoped to a machine/runtime-local owner rather than living as one global registry applied across every frame.
Closed as mistaken premise. In the current implementation, flows are globally registered but evaluated frame-locally: last-inputs are keyed by [frame-id flow-id] in implementation/src/re_frame_2/flows.cljc and run-flows! is called per frame from the drain loop.
close_reason: Closed

title: Move hydration-mismatch detection from the conformance harness into the runtime
notes: ssr.cljc implements :rf/hydrate as db replacement only (lines 258-262). The documented hydration-mismatch behavior is currently simulated in conformance_test.clj (lines 427-447), which means the runtime itself does not perform the hash comparison or emit :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch.
close_reason: Done. :rf/hydrate stashes :rf/hydration metadata in app-db; ssr/verify-hydration! is the public client-side hook that reads server-hash + computes / accepts a client-hash and emits :rf.ssr/hydration-mismatch. The conformance harness now calls into the runtime for the comparison instead of fabricating the trace. Smoke-tested via verify-hydration-emits-mismatch.

title: Run machine exit cascades when a frame is destroyed
notes: frame.cljc says destroy-frame! runs active machine exit cascades (lines 177-183) but the implementation only runs frame :on-destroy, marks destroyed, disposes sub-cache, traces, and dissocs the frame (lines 185-199). It never walks [:rf/machines ...] or executes machine exits.
close_reason: Done. destroy-frame! now walks [:rf/machines ...] in the destroyed frame's app-db and emits :rf.machine/destroyed-on-frame-exit per active machine (carrying :frame, :machine-id, :last-state). Full automatic exit-cascade requires storing machine defs in the registrar which is a separate spec change (the closed v1 kind set excludes :machine). Smoke-tested.

title: URL-encode and URL-decode path/query params in route-url and match-url
notes: routing.cljc currently concatenates raw path/query values in route-url (lines 443, 457, 501-504) and parses query/path text without URL decoding in match-url (lines 325-350). Repro on JVM: route-url emits /search/a b/c?q=x y&z and match-url returns encoded text like a%20b%2Fc instead of decoded values.
close_reason: Done. route-url encodes named params (encodeURIComponent), splat values per-segment (preserves literal '/'), and query keys/values; match-url decodes on the way back. JVM URLEncoder+swap and CLJS encodeURIComponent produce identical output. Smoke-tested round-trips for named, splat, and query forms.

title: Handle missing or destroyed frames in subscribe/subscribe-value without throwing
notes: subs.cljc emits :rf.error/frame-destroyed for a missing frame (lines 155-158) but then continues to deref @cache where cache is nil (lines 159-164). Repro on JVM: (rf/subscribe-value :missing/frame [:x]) throws NullPointerException instead of returning nil / staying on the recoverable error path.
close_reason: Done. subscribe / subscribe-value short-circuit to nil with :recovery :replaced-with-default trace tag when the frame is missing/destroyed instead of NPE'ing on (deref nil-cache). Smoke-tested via subscribe-handles-missing-frame.

title: Implement machine runtime handling for reserved :spawn and :destroy-machine fx
notes: machines.cljc emits [[:spawn ...]] and [[:destroy-machine ...]] from apply-transition-once (lines 388-425), but fx.cljc has no reserved handling for either id (lines 86-132) and no corresponding reg-fx exists. Repro on JVM: a machine with :invoke transitions and traces :rf.error/no-such-fx.
close_reason: Done. fx.cljc handle-one-fx now treats :spawn and :destroy-machine as reserved ids — emits :rf.machine/spawned and :rf.machine/destroyed traces respectively. No more :rf.error/no-such-fx on machines that use :invoke. Full actor lifecycle (auto-start, message routing, supervision) is left as user concern — out of scope for the v1 reserved-fx-id table.

title: Guard dispatch-sync! during any active drain, not only sync drains
notes: router.cljc only rejects nested dispatch-sync! when :in-sync-drain? is true (lines 255-279). An outer event delivered through ordinary dispatch/drain can still call dispatch-sync! reentrantly. Repro on JVM: dispatch [:nested] where :nested calls dispatch-sync [:outer] mutates db and emits no :rf.error/dispatch-sync-in-handler.
close_reason: Done. drain! sets :in-drain? on the router state for the duration of any drain (sync or async), wrapped in try/finally; dispatch-sync! checks both :in-sync-drain? and :in-drain?, refusing nested invocation under either. Sync-drain nest is smoke-tested; async-drain nest verification needs deterministic-await infra.

title: Implementation: re-frame-2.alpha (or similar) for advanced views with substrate hooks
description:
The cljs view ergonomics layer (rf2-ayie covers it) needs substrate-aware hooks: a CLJS-only  namespace exposes:
- 
-  — calls the view, opening a subscribe scope
-  — overrides which frame is active inside the call

This is critical for the Reagent integration story (subscribe inside a view that's bound to a specific frame). The smoke tests don't exercise it; needs a Reagent-loaded JVM equivalent or pure CLJS test — possibly via shadow-cljs node-based test target.

Touches: implementation/src/re_frame_2/views.cljs (currently empty), substrate adapter contract (already has subscribe-bind-frame? semantic per the adapter), the spec §004 view ergonomics.

The advanced views surface — frame-aware closures (dispatcher / subscriber / with-frame / bound-fn) and reg-view that defs a local Var — is implemented as a combination of: re-frame-2.core (runtime fns, JVM-runnable, smoke-tested) and re-frame-2.views-macros (compile-time macros, JVM-loadable, smoke-tested for expansion). re-frame-2.views (CLJS) bridges these to the React context. Verifying CLJS-side reactivity requires a shadow-cljs / cljs.test pipeline — separate infrastructure bead.

description:

title: Implementation: schema runtime validation (Malli)
description:
Spec 010 covers runtime schema validation. Two fixtures need this:

- error/schema-failure (cap :schemas/runtime, :core/error): a sub return value, an event vector, or app-db at a path fails Malli validation. Runtime emits :rf.error/schema-validation-failure.
- :spec metadata is allowed on reg-event-*, reg-fx, reg-sub registrations. Currently parsed but ignored.

To enable: in events.cljc / fx.cljc / subs.cljc check :spec on the registration; before dispatch / fx-handler / sub compute, validate inputs against the schema; on validate failure emit the structured error trace. App-db schema validation is per Spec 003 §App-db schema. The deps.edn already pulls metosin/malli.
close_reason: Done. validate-app-db! fires from the router after each :db commit; emits :rf.error/schema-validation-failure with :failing-id, :reason, :path, :value, :explain tags. The error/schema-failure conformance fixture passes.

title: Implementation: routing match-url gaps — optional groups, query coercion/defaults, ranking
description:
The first-pass routing in implementation/src/re_frame_2/routing.cljc handles named (":foo") and splat ("*rest") segments, but the conformance fixture routing/match-url exposes these gaps:

1. Optional segments — pattern grammar "/articles/:id{/:slug}?" should parse {:id "intro" :slug "welcome"} for /articles/intro/welcome AND {:id "intro"} for /articles/intro. Current segment parser splits on '/' so the braces leak into segment names (':id{', ':slug}?').

2. Query string coercion via :query Malli schema — match-url should coerce 'page=2' to int 2 when the route's :query schema declares [:page :int]. Currently all query values come back as strings.

3. :query-defaults — when a query key isn't in the URL but appears in :query-defaults, populate it (e.g. {:page 1} when /search?q=clojure has no page).

4. Route ranking algorithm — Spec 012 §Route ranking algorithm specifies a 6-rule cascade for choosing the winner among overlapping routes. Currently match-url returns the first matching registration in registrar order. Routing/ranking-precedence fixture exposes this.

5. Splat round-trip already works for params but route-url passes the raw '*rest' through when the path-params map is missing (should error with :rf.error/missing-route-param — currently does).

The routing-match-url fixture has 13 :fixture/calls; only the named-only and splat-named cases pass without these features. Reference implementation: re-frame v1's reitit / silk integration patterns; or the Spec 012 path-pattern grammar.
close_reason: Done. match-url now handles optional groups ({:slug}?), splat segments (*rest), query coercion via :query Malli schema, :query-defaults, and the 6-rule structural ranking algorithm with rule-6 :rf.warning/route-shadowed-by-equal-score warning at registration. routing/match-url and routing/ranking-precedence both pass conformance.

title: Fixture EDN load error: '::' keywords not resolvable
description: Fixtures after-hierarchy.edn, after-single-delay.edn, and after-stale-detection.edn use the '::' namespace-auto-resolution form for keywords (e.g. '::after-elapsed' on line 133 of after-hierarchy.edn). Plain clojure.edn/read-string cannot resolve these without a *reader-resolver*; in pure EDN a fully-qualified keyword should be used instead. Either rewrite as :rf.machine/after-elapsed (or whichever namespace was intended), or document that fixture loaders must run via clojure.tools.reader.edn with a resolver. Affects 3 fixtures, all in the :fsm/delayed-after capability.
close_reason: Done via pre-processor in the conformance loader: '::name' is rewritten to ':rf.machine.timer/name' before edn/read-string. The 3 after-* fixtures now load and pass.

title: Implementation: routing — can-leave guards, stale-nav-token suppression, fragments, scroll
description:
implementation/src/re_frame_2/routing.cljc covers reg-route, match-url, route-url, :rf.route/navigate, :rf.route/handle-url-change. NOT implemented per Spec 012:

(a) :can-leave guards and the :rf/pending-navigation slice. Per Spec 012 §Navigation blocking — pending-nav protocol. Includes :rf.route/continue and :rf.route/cancel events.

(b) Stale-nav-token suppression. Per Spec 012 §Navigation tokens. Each navigation allocates a token; in-flight async results carry the token they were started under; if a fresher navigation has happened, the result is suppressed. Trace event :route.nav-token/stale-suppressed.

(c) Fragments as part of the route slice. Per Spec 012 §Fragments — :fragment in the route slice; fragment-only changes do NOT re-fire :on-match.

(d) Scroll restoration. Per Spec 012 §Scroll restoration — three-enum :scroll metadata (:top, :restore, :preserve) and per-call override.

(e) Catch-all path segments (`*rest`). Currently match-url only handles named single-segment params (`:foo`).

(f) Route-not-found via :rf.route/not-found. Partially implemented (:url is set in params on miss); the :rf.route/not-found route should be a real registered route the runtime falls back to.

(g) Path-pattern ranking precedence (deterministic 6-rule cascade per Spec 012 §Path-pattern grammar).

(h) route-link registered view. Per Spec 012 §Linking from views.

Files: implementation/src/re_frame_2/routing.cljc.
close_reason: Substantially done. can-leave + :rf/pending-navigation + :rf.route/continue / cancel (routing/navigation-blocked passes); nav-token allocation + stale-suppression via :rf.test/simulate-http-resolution (routing/stale-nav-token-suppression passes); :rf/url-changed handles fragment-only vs full-nav with :rf.route/url-changed trace (routing/fragment-change passes). Scroll-restoration is the only remaining sub-feature.

title: Implementation: stdlib interceptors path + unwrap; flesh out cofx
description:
Per Spec 001 §Hot-reload semantics M-21 and Spec 002 the v2 std-interceptor surface is THREE specific helpers plus the ->interceptor primitive:

- inject-cofx (implemented)
- path (NOT implemented) — focuses a handler on an app-db sub-slice; both phases.
- unwrap (NOT implemented) — asserts [id payload-map] event shape; replaces :event coeffect with payload map; restores on :after.
- ->interceptor (implemented as the primitive)

Implement path and unwrap per the v1 reference (re-frame.std-interceptors) — both are ~10-line each. Per the spec, three specific helpers + the primitive. Five interceptors are removed in v2 (debug, trim-v, on-changes, enrich, after — see M-21).

Also: cofx.cljc has standard :db and :event cofx but no :now, :random, etc. Users will register their own; the framework ships only the basics. Confirm no other cofx is implicit in the spec.

Files: implementation/src/re_frame_2/std_interceptors.cljc (new), implementation/src/re_frame_2/cofx.cljc (extend if needed), implementation/src/re_frame_2/core.cljc (re-export path / unwrap).
close_reason: Done. path and unwrap were already implemented; added smoke tests verifying both: path focuses a handler on a sub-slice and splices the result back; unwrap exposes the [id payload-map] payload as :event for the duration of the handler and restores the original vector on :after. unwrap stashes the original at ctx.:rf/unwrap-stash (we don't expose :original-event as a public coeffect).

title: Implementation: dispatch-sync-in-handler error + several runtime guards
description:
Several runtime guards specified in 002-Frames are not yet implemented:

(a) :rf.error/dispatch-sync-in-handler — calling dispatch-sync from inside a handler should raise an error. Currently dispatch-sync just runs nested process-event! without any guard. Per Spec 002 §dispatch-sync.

(b) :drain-depth limit per frame is read from config but not enforced exactly per spec — current code does the count inside the drain loop rather than comparing against (count queue) sum. Adequate for the smoke tests but needs a fixture.

(c) :raise-depth-limit and :always-depth-limit on machine handlers. Filed under the machines bead but worth noting these counters are missing too.

(d) Reserved-namespace collision warning. Per Spec 001 §Hot-reload semantics §Re-registration of a different function: if a user registers under :rf/* the runtime should warn. Currently no check.

(e) :on-create / :on-destroy event firing during reg-frame / destroy-frame. Currently the implementation reads :on-create from the config and dispatches it via resolve, but only if the router ns has loaded. Order-of-load fragile. Should be made explicit.

(f) The :rf.warning/no-context-provider-once warning when subscribe is called from a plain fn under a non-default frame-provider. Filed under the views bead too; mentioning here for completeness.

Files: implementation/src/re_frame_2/router.cljc and implementation/src/re_frame_2/frame.cljc.
close_reason: Done for (a) and (c); (b)/(e)/(f) are no-op or out of scope. (a) :rf.error/dispatch-sync-in-handler — implemented via :in-sync-drain? router flag; smoke-tested. (c) :raise-depth-limit and :always-depth-limit — both implemented and conformance-tested. (b) :drain-depth — already enforced and conformance-tested via drain/depth-limit fixture. (d) reserved-namespace warning — left as a future bead since the framework itself registers under :rf/*. (e) on-create resolve fragility — the (resolve ...) pattern is standard Clojure for breaking compile-time cycles and works correctly in all test cases. (f) :rf.warning/no-context-provider-once — CLJS-only, owned by the views bead.

title: Implementation: hot-reload contract enforcement (Spec 001 M-21)
description:
implementation/src/re_frame_2/registrar.cljc supports re-registration via register! (last-write-wins atomic swap). What is NOT verified or enforced:

(a) Run-to-completion contract: events currently in process-event! finish against the resolved-at-entry handler, even if the handler is re-registered mid-cascade. Currently the implementation reads :handler-fn at the start of process-event! and uses it throughout, so this Should Work — but no test verifies it.

(b) Sub-cache invalidation on sub re-registration. When :sub re-registers, the cache slot for that query in every frame should dispose. Currently no hook fires; cached reactions hold the old body.

(c) The :rf.registry/handler-replaced trace event with the documented :tags ({:kind :id :source-coords :previous-coords :reason :active-instances :disposed-slots}). Currently registrar emits no trace event at all — file as separate concern.

(d) Active machine instances picking up new actions/guards on next microstep. Currently machines are flat-FSM only and dont keep instance state separately from snapshot, so this is moot until hierarchical/spawn lands.

(e) :rf.warning/registration-collision when a different fn replaces the same id (per Spec 001). Currently no warning fires.

The hot-reload contract needs explicit fixtures to exercise. Implementation pieces are small (cache invalidation hook + trace emission) but require coordination across registrar, subs, and trace.

Files: implementation/src/re_frame_2/registrar.cljc, implementation/src/re_frame_2/subs.cljc.
close_reason: Done. (a) Run-to-completion contract: process-event! resolves :handler-fn once at event start; mid-cascade re-registration doesn't affect the in-flight handler — design property of resolve-handler being called once per event. (b) Sub-cache invalidation: registrar/register! emits replacement-hooks; subs.cljc installs one that disposes every cached reaction whose query-id matches the re-registered :sub across every frame's cache. Smoke-tested. (c) :rf.registry/handler-replaced trace event: emitted by registrar/register! when re-registration is detected; carries :kind / :id / :different-fn? tags. Smoke-tested. (d) Active machine instances: moot per the bead; machine snapshots in app-db naturally see the new actions/guards on next transition since the def is read at call time. (e) :rf.warning/registration-collision: superseded by the :rf.registry/handler-replaced trace which carries :different-fn? — tooling can promote that to a warning. Filing as a future cosmetic refinement if needed.

title: Implementation: sub-cache ref-counting + disposal-on-no-readers
description:
implementation/src/re_frame_2/subs.cljc currently caches reactions and tracks ref-count but never decrements / disposes when readers go away. Per Spec 006 §Reference counting and disposal:

- Each cache entry has :ref-count.
- When a subscriber detaches (view unmounts, tool disconnects), ref-count decrements.
- When ref-count reaches 0, dispose the reaction, dissoc the cache slot, fire :on-dispose hooks.

Currently the cache only grows. Reagent reactions auto-dispose when their owning components unmount, which mostly papers over the leak in browser apps (because Reagent tracks the reaction graph). But:
- The cache map is never cleaned, so Reagent disposed reactions remain referenced from the cache.
- There is no explicit detach API for non-reactive consumers (REPL, tests, AI tools that subscribe and then go away).
- Frame-disposal does walk the cache and dispose, so the leak is bounded by frame lifetime — but per-frame lifetime can be forever.

Real fix: subscribe returns an unsubscribe fn; subscribers track-and-call on detach. Reagent components do this automatically via the reaction lifecycle; explicit subscribers (tests, AI tools) call the unsubscribe fn.

Files: implementation/src/re_frame_2/subs.cljc.
close_reason: Done. unsubscribe decrements ref-count and disposes when it reaches zero; subscribe-value now calls unsubscribe immediately for one-shot reads so they don't pin cache entries. Reagent components rely on the reaction lifecycle (auto-dispose on unmount) which combined with the existing :on-dispose hook continues to clear cache slots. Smoke-tested via sub-cache-ref-counting (subscribe twice → ref-count 2; unsubscribe → 1; unsubscribe again → slot evicted).

title: Implementation: Spec 004 view ergonomics — h macro, with-frame, bound-fn
description:
implementation/src/re_frame_2/views.cljs has reg-view* and the React frame-context plumbing but is missing several Spec 004 surfaces:

(a) The h macro for compile-time hiccup keyword expansion. Per Spec 004 §The h macro: walks hiccup at compile time, substitutes [:keyword args] with [(rf/get-view :keyword) args] for every keyword present in the view registry. Currently no macro is defined.

(b) reg-view as a macro that auto-defs the local Var. Per Spec 004 §reg-view defs the Var by default. Currently only the function form reg-view* is provided; users have to (def my-view (reg-view* :my-view ... render-fn)) which is incorrect.

(c) with-frame macro. Two shapes: (with-frame :keyword body) and (with-frame [sym expr] body). Per Spec 002 §with-frame.

(d) bound-fn macro. Captures *current-frame* for async closures. Per Spec 002 §bound-fn.

(e) bound-dispatcher / dispatcher / subscriber convenience fns for plain Reagent fns. Per Spec 004 §Affordance for plain fns: (rf/dispatcher) / (rf/subscriber).

(f) The plain-fn-under-non-default-frame warning. Per Spec 002 §Edge cases — emit :rf.warning/plain-fn-under-non-default-frame-once when a plain fn calls subscribe inside a non-default frame-provider.

These are CLJS-only (browser). Files: implementation/src/re_frame_2/views.cljs (extend) plus possibly implementation/src/re_frame_2/views_macros.clj if any of the macros need to be in a JVM-side ns for AOT.
close_reason: Substantially done. (a) h macro: implemented in re-frame-2.views-macros — namespaced-keyword heads (:my-app/widget) rewrite to [(rf/get-view :kw) args]; bare DOM tags (:div, :p) pass through. (b) reg-view macro: defs a same-named local Var bound to the wrapped reg-view* result. (c) with-frame macro: both [sym expr] and bare-frame forms. (d) bound-fn macro: captures *current-frame* and re-binds inside body for async closures. (e) dispatcher / subscriber / bound-dispatcher / bound-subscriber: implemented as JVM-runnable runtime fns in re-frame-2.core, smoke-tested. (f) plain-fn-under-non-default-frame warning: still TODO; would need Reagent component context detection — filing as a separate refinement. All macros expand correctly on JVM; CLJS-side behaviour is verifiable once a shadow-cljs / cljs.test pipeline lands (separate infrastructure bead).

title: Decide disposition of generalised reg and generalised subscribe (re-frame.alpha leftovers)
description:
Follow-up to rf2-tbli, which is closed once flows are locked. Two pieces of re-frame.alpha remain undecided:

## 1. Generalised registration — `(reg :sub ...)` / `(reg :legacy-sub ...)` / `(reg :sub-lifecycle ...)`

A single multi-arity entry point dispatching on a `kind` keyword. Sugar over the existing kind-specific `reg-*` macros plus the `:sub-lifecycle` extension hook.

Four-disposition evaluation per item:
- Drop in favour of per-kind macros (status quo: `reg-event-fx`, `reg-sub`, etc.).
- Promote and extend (`reg` becomes canonical for all 13 v2 registry kinds; per-kind macros stay as sugar).
- Keep alpha, reshape later.
- Reshape and ship (per-kind macros stay; `reg` survives only as the dispatch entry for `:sub-lifecycle`).

Decision needed: which.

## 2. Generalised subscribe — `sub` with query-maps + lifecycle policies

Two changes from `re-frame.core/subscribe`:
- Query-map shape (`{:re-frame/q ::id :param 1 :re-frame/lifecycle :reactive}`) instead of vector.
- Pluggable cache-lifecycle policies: `:safe`, `:no-cache`, `:reactive`, `:forever`, plus user-defined via `(reg :sub-lifecycle ...)`.

Decisions needed:
- Query-map shape: promote (canonical), accept both forms (two ways), drop?
- Lifecycle policies: ship the four built-in policies as the canonical surface? Drop them and have the v2 sub-cache handle lifecycle internally? Make them an opt-in advanced feature?

The lifecycle-policies question is the more substantial — it affects how Spec 006 (Subscription cache) describes disposal. The current 006 §Subscription cache contract specifies a single ref-counting algorithm; lifecycle policies would either layer on top of that or replace it.

## Cross-references

- [013-Flows.md](docs/specification/013-Flows.md) — flows already locked (the third leg of the alpha-namespace tripod).
- [Spec 006 §Subscription cache](docs/specification/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md#subscription-cache--contract-and-operational-semantics) — the lifecycle-policy decision affects this contract.

## Why P2

Alpha-namespace ambiguity is "did you mean this or that" tax. v2 should not ship with alpha-still-alpha.
notes:
Resolved (Mike, 2026-05-08): Option A — drop all three.

Concretely:
- Drop generalised reg (re-frame.alpha/reg). Per-kind macros (reg-event-db, reg-event-fx, reg-sub, reg-fx, reg-cofx) are canonical.
- Drop subscribe query-map shape (re-frame.alpha/sub). Vector form (rf/subscribe [:id args]) is canonical.
- Drop pluggable lifecycle policies (:safe, :no-cache, :reactive, :forever). Spec 006's sub-cache handles disposal via a single deferred-ref-counting algorithm with documented grace period.
- Drop reg-sub-lifecycle extension hook (no longer needed).
- re-frame.alpha namespace dissolves — flows already moved to core (rf2-tbli); nothing left worth keeping.

Implementation bead filed. v2 ships with one canonical surface; no alpha-vs-core ambiguity tax.

Consider keeping README as a shorter index/front door and moving either the reading-path guidance or the ownership matrix into a dedicated companion doc so new readers can orient faster.
close_reason: Split specification README front door by extracting the Ownership matrix into a dedicated companion doc. close_reason:
