title: xray: shorten inline diff annotation from '<- changed from X' to '<- was X'
description:
Per Mike pair-debug 2026-05-29: the inline diff annotation Xray paints to the right of a `:modified` leaf today reads `← changed from X` — verbose. Shorten to `← was X`.

Example today: `3 ← changed from 2`
Example after: `3 ← was 2`

## Where the runtime string lives

Single emission site in the framework:

  - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs:756` — `(str "← changed from " (try (pr-str before) ...))`.

## What changes

1. Runtime string at `edn_inspector.cljs:756` — replace `"← changed from "` with `"← was "`.
2. Mode-3 grammar spec text — any `← changed from <prior>` references in docstrings/comments/prose update to `← was <prior>` so future-readers don't see drift between the prose contract and the runtime emission. Hits at minimum:
   - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/edn_inspector.cljs` — ns docstring (L25), opt-doc (L77), style docstring (L742), inline comments at L751, L1074, L1462, L1934, L2209, L2216.
   - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs` — ns docstring + view docstrings (L61, L67, L259, L277, L530).
   - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_helpers.cljc` — fn docstrings (L383, L448).
   - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_subs.cljs` — sub docstring (L303).
   - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch_panel.cljs` — ns commentary (L204).
   - `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs` — fn docstring (L3045).
   - `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §4.3 §10 — wherever the inline-annotation contract is documented.
3. Tests that pin the annotation string — replace expected string literals.

## Acceptance

1. Live Xray (any panel rendering FULL+DIFF or :diff): a `:modified` leaf renders `<after> ← was <before>` (mixed case, no "changed from").
2. `git grep -nE "← changed from"` across `tools/xray/src` returns zero matches.
3. Any tests pinning the annotation string updated to expect `← was`.
4. spec/021 §inline-annotation contract reads `← was <prior>`.

## Scope

Single-file dominant (edn_inspector.cljs). Documentation/spec sweep cosmetic. Single PR. Pre-alpha — no shim.

## Related

- Sibling to rf2-fyd8u (leaf-scalar SUBSCRIPTIONS annotation in FULL+DIFF) — that bead surfaces the annotation pattern in a new place; this bead shortens the string everywhere it appears. Land rf2-fyd8u's renderer using `← was X` directly.
- Sibling to rf2-9d4j8 (container empty→populated diff misclassification) — different bug class but same Mode-3 grammar surface; coordinate string-literal touches if both land in adjacent PRs.

Pair-debug 2026-05-29.

title: naming(core): rename frame/get-frame-db (container) to disambiguate from core/get-frame-db (value)
description:
Follow-on from rf2-i3kj2 (naming audit of implementation/core).

**Problem.** Two same-named fns with semantically different return types:

- `re-frame.frame/get-frame-db` (frame.cljc:191) returns the **container** (substrate-managed reactive cell holding `:app-db`).
- `re-frame.core/get-frame-db` (core.cljc:1062) returns the **value** (deref'd plain map).

Public callers (apps, MCP tools) reading `rf/get-frame-db` get the value; internal code reading `frame/get-frame-db` gets the container. A grep cannot tell them apart by name; you must read the source to know which you are holding.

**Proposal.** Rename `re-frame.frame/get-frame-db` to make the container axis part of the name. Candidate names:

- `re-frame.frame/app-db-container` (preferred — symmetric with the value-side `re-frame.frame/frame-app-db-value` which already exists)
- `re-frame.frame/frame-app-db-container` (verbose but unambiguous)

Public `re-frame.core/get-frame-db` (value) stays as-is — that is the consumer contract per spec/API.md.

**Touch scope.** Internal callers of `frame/get-frame-db`:

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc (subscribe layer-1 input-signal source — hot path)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc (registry walks)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/marks.cljc (registry walks)
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc (docstring reference only)
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_test.clj (test direct call)
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/adapter/react_shared_suite.cljs (test direct call)

~6 src/test files; single grep-and-replace + ns-test sweep.

**Gates.** `cd implementation/core && clojure -M:test` (792+ tests) + `cd implementation/schemas && clojure -M:test` (consumes the elision walker that uses this name) + clj-kondo + `npm run test:cljs`.

**Reference.** Finding F1 in `ai/findings/naming-audit-implementation-core.md`. Posture: pre-alpha masterpiece — rename outright; no back-compat alias.
notes: Renamed re-frame.frame/get-frame-db → re-frame.frame/app-db-container. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2380. Scope was 25 files (broader than bead's ~6 estimate: cross-artefact consumers in epoch/flows/machines/ssr/schemas + tools/story-mcp/xray + examples + spec/006 prose). All gates pass: core 792 tests, schemas 192 tests, npm test:cljs 4845 tests, clj-kondo 0 new errors.

title: audit(naming): review naming best-practice across skills/re-frame2-xray
description:
Naming-best-practice audit for the **`skills/re-frame2-xray`** slice. Mike-filed 2026-05-29 ~00:18 AUSEST as one of 33 distinct surfaces.

### Surface character — skills bundle

This is a Claude Code skill bundle, NOT a CLJS artefact. The naming surface is:

- The bundle's directory name and any sub-references in `SKILL.md`
- Section headings within `SKILL.md` + `references/*.md`
- Filenames under `references/` (e.g. `cross-cutting/privacy-and-elision.md`)
- Anchor slugs (`<a id="...">`) that other docs / beads point to
- For skills that ship preload code (e.g. `re-frame2-pair/preload/`) — apply the CLJS naming criteria below to that subtree

Focus on operator-facing clarity: when an operator runs `/re-frame2-xray` (etc.), does every label, reference, and filename communicate its role unambiguously? Are there inconsistencies vs sibling skills?

## Scope — questions to answer

For the `skills/re-frame2-xray` slice ONLY:

1. **Namespaces** — are they well named? Do filenames match? Are sibling namespaces consistent in shape?
2. **Function names** — public surface + private helpers. Are verbs/nouns appropriate? Predicates end `?`, side-effects end `!`?
3. **File names** — match namespace? Are there orphan / stale / vague filenames?
4. **Let-bindings + threading + parameters** — descriptive? Or stub-names (`x`, `tmp`, `m`, `e`) that hide a real semantic role?
5. **Test names** — `deftest` + `testing` strings narrate the assertion?
6. **Cross-slice consistency** — same concept named the same way across this slice? Flag the renames needed if not.
7. **Domain vocabulary** — does the slice's naming match the spec's vocabulary? Or has drift accumulated?

## Posture

Pre-alpha masterpiece — rename outright where it improves clarity. NO back-compat shims. Mike's CLAUDE.md guidance: ELEGANCE + CLARITY + CORRECTNESS + GOOD PRACTICE are the primary lenses.

## Deliverables

1. **Inline renames** — small renames that don't touch the public surface (private helpers, internal let-bindings, internal namespaces) can be applied as part of this bead's PR.
2. **Follow-on beads** — larger renames touching public surface (anything a downstream artefact / consumer / skill / example `:require`s or references by name) get follow-on beads. These will need a cross-artefact rewire and Mike-approval at the surface level before dispatch.
3. **Findings doc** at `ai/findings/naming-audit-skills-re-frame2-xray.md` listing: every named entity reviewed, the verdict (KEEP / RENAME-INLINE / RENAME-NEEDS-FOLLOWUP), and the reasoning. Local-only / gitignored.

## Worker dispatch shape

Read-only audit + small inline renames. Shape-1 (or Shape-2 if multiple commits within the slice). Worktree under `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/naming-audit-<bead-id>`.

Quality gates depend on slice kind — for CLJS artefacts: `cd skills/re-frame2-xray && clojure -M:test` + clj-kondo + `npm run test:cljs` if the slice has cljs/cljc files affecting the cljs build. For skills/examples: prose-only, mkdocs --strict + check_doc_slugs + check_readme_links if any cross-references move.

## Reference

This bead is one of a 33-bead audit wave covering every distinct surface under implementation/, tools/, examples/, skills/. Sibling beads file the same audit shape for adjacent surfaces; cross-reference them in the findings doc if a rename naturally spans a sibling boundary.

title: docs(the-mayor-method): enforce canonical '## Quality gates' heading in PR-body section (rf2-uhd5d follow-on)
description:
Filed from audit rf2-uhd5d (ai/findings/worker-gate-audit-2026-05-28.md §3.3 + §4.2).

## Why

5 of 16 PRs in the 2026-05-28 audit window used variant headings for the PR-body gate-results section:

- #2333: `## Gates`
- #2337: `## Gates run`
- #2343: `## Gates`
- #2345: `## Gates`
- #2346: `## Gates`

The dispatch-prompt-template explicitly names `## Quality gates` as the canonical heading (lines 192-221), but the variant headings drift in. This breaks any future automated PR-body scan (e.g. `gh pr view <n> --json body --jq '...'` looking for the section), and the audit work above had to fall back to a tolerant grep across 4 variants.

2 PRs (#2334, #2335) omitted the gate section entirely. Both were spec-only / docs-only with no impl gates required — arguably acceptable for "no gates needed" cases, but the template policy says "every editing dispatch's PR body MUST include a ## Quality gates section."

## Scope

Edit `docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` "## PR-body Quality gates section — mandatory" block. Tighten the language:

1. "Use the verbatim heading `## Quality gates` — not `## Gates`, not `## Gates run`, not `## Tests run`."
2. For spec-only / docs-only PRs where no impl gates apply, the section is still mandatory but is permitted to be a one-line `no impl gates required (spec-only diff)` placeholder + the docs gates (mkdocs --strict + slugs + readme-links).
3. Add a one-line note: "A canonical heading is a contract — it enables automated audits (e.g. rf2-uhd5d) and avoids the maintenance cost of tolerant greps."

## Acceptance

1. The `## PR-body Quality gates section — mandatory` block lands the verbatim-heading instruction.
2. The spec-only / docs-only exception is documented as `## Quality gates` + one-line "no impl gates required" + docs gates list.
3. mkdocs build --strict + check_doc_slugs --verbose + check_readme_links --ci all pass on the edit.

## Notes

Shape-1 single-file edit. Can be bundled with rf2-gyqpj (the gate-menu block) into one PR — both are dispatch-prompt-template edits, same file.

Pre-alpha posture: prescriptive ("MUST use exact heading"), not advisory.
notes: Resolved by PR #2349 (commit a51d6adb1): tightened the '## PR-body Quality gates section — mandatory' block with verbatim-heading instruction + spec-only/docs-only exception + canonical-heading-as-contract rationale. Bundled Shape-2 with rf2-gyqpj. 3 docs gates green (mkdocs --strict + check_doc_slugs + check_readme_links --ci).

description:

title: investigate: :rf/hydration app-db root unaccounted for in Conventions reserved-app-db-keys table
description:
Audit rf2-32j96 (impl/ssr surface) surfaced a pre-existing inconsistency NOT introduced by eguy4: the hydrate handler writes `(assoc db :rf/hydration metadata)` at the app-db root (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc` L74), and `verify-hydration!` reads `[:rf/hydration :server-hash]` (L267). Spec 011 §The :rf/hydrate event (L304) calls this "a runtime-managed app-db path" that user code SHOULD NOT write.

But the Conventions.md "Reserved app-db keys" table (L148-176) enumerates EXACTLY ONE reserved root: `:rf/runtime`. `:rf/hydration` is missing from the table. The table text says: "Exactly one key at the root of every frame's app-db is reserved."

So either:
1. `:rf/hydration` should have been folded into `:rf/runtime` (e.g. `[:rf/runtime :ssr :hydration]`) as part of the eguy4 restructure — completeness gap.
2. `:rf/hydration` is intentionally outside `:rf/runtime` because the slot has a different lifecycle (it's seeded by the server-emitted payload, not by a runtime subsystem) — but then Conventions and/or the spec needs to acknowledge it as a SECOND reserved root.
3. The slot is genuinely user-shaped (the spec says "SHOULD NOT write" not "MUST NOT") and the "exactly one" framing in Conventions is the actual contract — in which case `:rf/hydration` is just an app-db-key the framework uses by convention, not a reserved root.

## Recommended

Mike-decision bead. The pre-alpha clean-break ethos suggests option (1) — fold into `[:rf/runtime :ssr :hydration]` so the reserved-root invariant remains "exactly one." But option (2) is consistent with how some other framework state lives outside app-db (response-slots, request-slots, head-snapshots — side-channel atoms, not app-db keys). The hydration metadata is SMALL and PER-FRAME and SHOULD travel with the frame on revert, so it has the property that motivated `:rf/runtime` in the first place.

## Severity

P3 — pre-existing, not regressed by eguy4. Worth a decision before someone files a Type-B-migration false-positive on user code touching `:rf/hydration`.

## Sites referenced

- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hydrate.cljc` L73-74 (write), L267 (read)
- `spec/011-SSR.md` L304 (the prose calling it a "runtime-managed app-db path")
- `spec/Conventions.md` L148-176 (the table that omits it)
close_reason: VERDICT: PRE-EXISTING DRIFT (predates eguy4). hydrate.cljc:74 (write) + L267 (read) wrote/read :rf/hydration at app-db ROOT; Conventions reserved-keys table had :rf/runtime as the sole reserved root. Per Mike-blessed pre-alpha posture: FOLDED to [:rf/runtime :ssr :hydration] in PR #2388. Spec 011 §304 prose + Conventions catalogue + Spec-Schemas Runtime schema all updated. New :ssr sub-container row added (HydrationMetadata schema). 5 SSR tests + core smoke + conformance-test comments rewired. Before/after grep: 25 hits → 1 (historical narrative line in Spec-Schemas.md). No back-compat alias.

title: test(ssr): sample-app-db fixtures still seed flat :rf/route — update to :rf/runtime shape for realism
description:
Audit rf2-32j96 (impl/ssr surface) — two test fixtures still seed a top-level `:rf/route` key in their sample-app-db value. The tests pass because the assertions don't probe the routing slice, but a real app-db post-eguy4 wouldn't carry this shape — the fixtures drift from production reality.

## Sites

`implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy_cljs_test.cljc` L24-29:
```
(def sample-app-db
  {:public/articles  [:a :b :c]
   :public/user-id   "u-42"
   :server-only/auth "SECRET_TOKEN"
   :server-only/flag true
   :rf/route         {:id :route/home}})
```
The fixture is used by payload-policy select-keys tests — the `:rf/route` key never appears in any allowlist, so functionally it's just a "non-public key" stand-in. Update to `:rf/runtime {:routing {:current {:id :route/home}}}` to match real-world app-db shape.

`implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_end_to_end_test.clj` L797-798:
```
payload {:rf/version 1
         :rf/app-db  {:rf/route {:id :route/article :params {:id "123"}}}
         :rf/render-hash "head-hash-server-A"}
```
The `:rf/app-db` payload field carries the AUTHORITATIVE app-db value the client adopts at hydrate; a server emitting this today would write `{:rf/runtime {:routing {:current {...}}}}`. The test only asserts on `:server-hash` — the route slice is unused — but the fixture's shape is wrong.

Note: the WIRE payload key `:rf/route` (Spec-Schemas:1982) is intentionally preserved by eguy4 as a wire-protocol convenience field; this is NOT that key — this is the app-db value INSIDE `:rf/app-db`.

## Fix shape

Rewrite both fixtures to use `[:rf/runtime :routing :current]` shape. No assertion changes needed (the tests don't probe the route slice in either case).

## Severity

P3 — cosmetic / realism. Doesn't affect green CI; future readers cargo-culting from these fixtures will get a wrong picture of app-db shape.

title: machines: consider :rf/runtime :machines path-helpers to compress 80+ literal-path call sites
description:
## Surface

implementation/machines/src/* (12 files, 99 literal-path call sites)

## Finding

After eguy4, the machines surface carries:

- ~47 occurrences of `[:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots <id>]` (longest spelling: 5 elements)
- ~35 occurrences of `[:rf/runtime :machines :spawned <parent-id> <invoke-id>]` (6 elements)
- ~9 occurrences of `[:rf/runtime :machines :system-ids <sid>]`

Plus matching docstring mentions (total `:rf/runtime` references in machines: 192 src + 192 test ≈ 384).

The teardown projection (`teardown.cljc`, 60 LOC) is the densest cluster — **10 `[:rf/runtime :machines ...]` literal-path uses in a single function** with three sibling slots being mutated (`:snapshots`, `:system-ids`, `:spawned`). E.g.:

```clojure
new-db (cond-> db
         actor-id     (update-in [:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots]
                                 dissoc actor-id)
         released-sid (update-in [:rf/runtime :machines :system-ids]
                                 dissoc released-sid)
         track?       (update-in [:rf/runtime :machines :spawned parent-id]
                                 dissoc invoke-id))
```

The eguy4 rewrite was mechanical (s/[:rf/machines/[:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots/g, etc.). Two organic micro-patterns ALREADY exist:
- `registration.cljc:265` binds `path [:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots machine-id]` locally.
- `finalize.cljc:185` binds `parent-path [:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots parent-id]` locally.

## Fix shape

Add a small `re-frame.machines.paths` (or inline in `re-frame.machines`) helper namespace:

```clojure
(defn snapshot-path
  ([machine-id]      [:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots machine-id])
  ([machine-id k]    [:rf/runtime :machines :snapshots machine-id k])
  ([machine-id k k2] ... ))

(defn system-id-path
  ([]   [:rf/runtime :machines :system-ids])
  ([sid] [:rf/runtime :machines :system-ids sid]))

(defn spawned-path
  ([]                       [:rf/runtime :machines :spawned])
  ([parent-id]              [:rf/runtime :machines :spawned parent-id])
  ([parent-id invoke-id]    [:rf/runtime :machines :spawned parent-id invoke-id]))
```

Lets the teardown projection read as:

```clojure
(cond-> db
  actor-id     (update-in (system-id-path released-sid) ...))
  ;; etc — paths now self-documenting
```

## Severity

P3. The surface is correct, readable, and the eguy4 rewrite kept docstring + impl in lockstep. A helper would shrink LOC modestly (~80 sites × ~8 chars saved each), reduce diff cost on future path migrations (eguy4-style restructures), and surface dialect 'this is the machines snapshot' vs reading a runtime-path-shaped vector. Not load-bearing — Option A in rf2-owvvr is the higher-priority cleanup.

## Discovered from

rf2-rd3fj (this audit). The pattern was visible during the eguy4 mechanical rewrite (#2338 changed every site in lockstep) but the rewrite was kept minimal — a helper would have been net-new code under a tighter scope.
close_reason: PR #2400 — added re-frame.machines.paths leaf ns (snapshot-path/system-id-path/spawned-path); routed 23 executable call-sites across 12 src files. Pure readability refactor, app-db shape identical. Gates: machines 298/980 0F0E, cljs 4820/15792 0F0E, fast-pr PASS.

title: spawn.cljc:58 — hand-emitted-spawn fallback allocator writes to app-db root :rf/spawn-counter (eguy4 residue or spec drift)
description:
## Surface

implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc

## Finding

`allocate-actor-id-in-db` (line 49-61) writes/reads the spawned-id counter at app-db ROOT `[:rf/spawn-counter <machine-id>]`:

```clojure
(defn- allocate-actor-id-in-db
  [db machine-id]
  (let [db' (update-in db [:rf/spawn-counter machine-id] (fnil inc 0))
        n   (get-in db' [:rf/spawn-counter machine-id])]
    ...))
```

This is the **only** `[:rf/spawn-counter ...]` write/read at app-db root anywhere in the codebase (`git grep 'db \[:rf/spawn-counter' -- implementation/` returns just this site).

## Why this is a finding

The eguy4 restructure (rf2-9x5u3 / PR #2338) collapsed 10 framework root keys into the single `:rf/runtime` container. `spec/Conventions.md` §Reserved app-db keys (lines 152-175) now lists `:rf/runtime` as the **sole** reserved app-db root.

But `spec/005-StateMachines.md` lines 1958-1961 still document a TWO-TIER counter split:
- Declarative spawn → inside parent snapshot at `[:rf/spawn-counter <id-prefix>]` (snapshot-internal — fine, listed at spec/Conventions.md:184 as 'snapshot root').
- **Hand-emitted `:rf.machine/spawn` fx → at frame-app-db root `[:rf/spawn-counter <id-prefix>]`** ← this is an UNMIGRATED app-db root key per the new contract.

## Fix shape

Two options Mike picks between:

**Option A (preferred — honour eguy4 contract):** migrate the hand-emitted fallback counter under the new container:
- `spawn.cljc:58-59` rewrites the path to `[:rf/runtime :machines :spawn-counter <machine-id>]` (a new sibling under `:rf/runtime :machines` alongside `:snapshots`, `:system-ids`, `:spawned`).
- `spec/Conventions.md` reserved-keys table grows a `:rf/runtime :machines :spawn-counter` row.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` :rf/runtime schema grows the slot.
- `spec/005-StateMachines.md` two-tier table at line 1958-1961 updates the second row's path.
- Any conformance fixture that pins the post-spawn db (hand-emitted spawn shape) updates.

**Option B (acknowledge the exception):** keep the implementation path but document `:rf/spawn-counter` as a SECOND reserved app-db root. Conventions table grows back to two rows. Loses the eguy4 'single-root' invariant.

## Severity

P3. Pre-alpha clean-break posture (CLAUDE.md) favours Option A. The 'one row' invariant is load-bearing — tools (Xray App-DB panel, re-frame2-pair-mcp snapshot reader) and the migration agent all key off it.

## Discovered from

title: core/marks: collapse read-transform-write triplet into swap-elision-slot! helper
description:
After rf2-9x5u3 (eguy4 phase B), `implementation/core/src/re_frame/marks.cljc` now repeats the same shape FIVE times: `(swap-app-db! frame-id (fn [db] (let [reg (get-in db [:rf/runtime :elision]) ... new-reg ...] (write-elision-slot db new-reg))))`. Call sites:

  - `write-marks!` (lines 222-237)
  - `add-marks` (lines 267-277)
  - `set-marks` (lines 307-321)
  - `clear-app-db-marks!` (lines 329-337)
  - (and the same shape inline in `elision.cljc/swap-registry!` lines 71-94)

Each call follows: read reg, compute new-reg from reg, write-elision-slot. The skeleton is identical; only the reg→new-reg transform differs.

Fix shape: introduce `(defn- swap-elision-slot! [frame-id f] ...)` that wraps `swap-app-db!` + the read + `write-elision-slot` step, taking a single `(fn [reg] new-reg)` transform. Each call site collapses to `(swap-elision-slot! frame-id (fn [reg] ...))`.

Best paired with rf2-x8p3v (extract shared write-elision-slot first, then layer the swap-elision-slot! helper on top — solves both layers of duplication in one PR if both fixes are landed together).

title: http: refresh 3 stale assertion-message strings in routing_http_composed_corners_test post :rf/runtime rewire
description:
## Context

Audit of implementation/http for the rf2-eguy4 :rf/runtime restructure (rf2-3q04j) found three assertion-message strings that still reference the old shape verbally:

- implementation/http/test/re_frame/routing_http_composed_corners_test.clj:234 — `":rf/pending-navigation slot is cleared post-cancel"`
- implementation/http/test/re_frame/routing_http_composed_corners_test.clj:246 — `"post-cancel: :rf/route slice still on the active editor route"`
- implementation/http/test/re_frame/routing_http_composed_corners_test.clj:309 — `"post-continue: :rf/route slice is on the continued target"`

These are pure prose (not load-bearing — the actual `get-in` paths next to them are correctly on `[:rf/runtime :routing :pending-navigation]` / `[:rf/runtime :routing :current :id]`). But the eguy4 disambiguation rule preserves `:rf/route` only as a sub-id / wire-protocol field, NOT as a logical-slot label. Reading these assertion failures in CI could mislead an operator into looking for a top-level `:rf/route` key that no longer exists.

## Fix shape

Rewrite the three message strings to refer to the slots by their new logical names — e.g.:

  - `"pending-navigation slot is cleared post-cancel"` (or `"[:rf/runtime :routing :pending-navigation] slot ..."`)
  - `"post-cancel: current route slice still on the active editor route"`
  - `"post-continue: current route slice is on the continued target"`

## Scope

P3, single-file, no semantic change. ~3 string edits. No tests, no spec, no gates beyond `clojure -M:test` in implementation/http/.

rf2-3q04j (http audit for the :rf/runtime restructure).

title: tools/machines-viz: MachineChart 38+ props — consider :overlays slot pattern (decision)
description:
DECISION NEEDED. MachineChart's prop surface in tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md is wide — 38+ props. The trend: each new overlay (after-rings, spawn-all-join, cancellation-cascade, fired-edge highlight, parallel regions) brought 3-5 new props (the spec data, a tick, callback wiring).

A future overlay would add another 3-5 props to an already-wide signature. Worth considering whether MachineChart should expose **slot props** for overlays:

  [viz/MachineChart
    {:machine-id :auth
     :definition def
     :current-state state
     :overlays [{:id :after-rings
                 :specs after-ring-specs
                 :tick now-ms
                 :on-hover #(...)
                 :on-leave #(...)}
                {:id :spawn-all-join
                 :spec spawn-all-spec
                 :on-child-click #(...)
                 ...}]}]

Hosts compose overlays through the slot instead of growing the trunk signature. Existing presentation-side overlay namespaces (chart.overlays.after-rings, chart.overlays.spawn-all-join, chart.overlays.cancellation-cascade) already carry the per-overlay rendering — only the wiring needs lifting.

Decision needed before action — the existing API is correct and the prop-soup might be acceptable for a charting library where each prop is genuinely independent.

Discovered in Tools-MCP first-principles audit. See ai/findings/2026-05-28-tools-mcp-cluster-first-principles.md §F-MV-1.
notes: Adopted the :overlays slot for MachineChart per Mike's ruling. Collapsed the 7 flat host-fed overlay-wiring props (after-rings / spawn-all-join / cancellation-cascade + the two shared ticks) into a single :overlays vector of {:id ...} descriptor maps; per-descriptor :tick unifies the old :after-ring-tick + :overlay-tick (one host-owned rAF clock, Lock #8). Renderers unchanged — wiring lifted via render-overlay dispatch on :id; unknown :id ignored with dev-only warn. :fired-edge-ids + structural props stayed on trunk. Spec API.md updated in lockstep (new :overlays descriptor multispec). No host call-sites needed migration (flat props had no live consumer). Gates green: test:cljs 4836/15853 0F0E, test:browser 126/357 0F0E, clj-kondo clean. PR #2330.

title: Decision: HTTP privacy surface — consolidate http-privacy / http-privacy-headers / http-url denylists?
description:
## Decision needed

The HTTP privacy surface is split across three siblings with overlapping mental models:

- `re-frame.http-privacy` — orchestrating composers (`request-sensitive?`, `prepare-emit-failure`, `prepare-emit-tags`).
- `re-frame.http-privacy-headers` — header denylist (`declare-sensitive-header!`, `clear-sensitive-headers!`, `default-header-denylist`).

title: decision: broaden test-react adapter adoption OR demote from canonical adapter set (rf2-tfmse cluster)
description:
**Decision needed.**

The test-react adapter (`implementation/adapters/test-react/`, rf2-gqyqv) was filed as a placeholder skeleton — a pure-CLJC React class-3 lifecycle simulator that catches React-lifecycle-driven bugs (rf2-4l7t2 class) at JVM-unit-test speed.

**Current state (2026-05-28 audit, rf2-tfmse):**
- Adapter ships the 9-fn contract.
- Test surface: `test_react_test.cljc` — 5 demo scenarios (happy-path lifecycle, sync-unmount throw, dispose drain, mount! identity, render-to-string survives dispose). All demonstration cases — none ported from a real production bug.
- No production-class lifecycle bug has been caught by it yet.
- bd rf2-gqyqv flags it as P4 placeholder; that label is currently honest.

**Three options:**

1. **Broaden adoption.** Port one or two known lifecycle bugs (e.g. the rf2-4l7t2 manifestation, or any sub-cache ref-count bug that fired during a render) into test-react cases as living regressions. This earns the adapter's keep — every future lifecycle bug class becomes a JVM-unit-test fixture instead of a browser smoke.
2. **Demote.** Remove test-react from the canonical adapter set; keep the lifecycle-simulator code as an example or documentation artefact only. Removes adapter-contract maintenance burden.
3. **Keep as-is.** Status quo: pays the adapter-shape cost (LOC, contract conformance, dispose semantics) without earning the catch-bugs-cheaply payoff. **This is the worst of both options.**

**Recommendation:** Option 1 — port 2-3 known lifecycle bugs in a follow-on bead, then revisit in 3 months. If still under-used after that, demote.

**Audit lens:** P3 because it's a decision about scope/maturity, not a defect. No code change without the decision.

**Found via** rf2-tfmse cluster (adapters first-principles audit, 2026-05-28). See `ai/findings/2026-05-28-adapters-first-principles.md` (gitignored, worktree-local).
notes: Mike ruled Option 1 (broaden). PR #2332 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2332): added render bodies + recursive child mounting (mount-child!), global render-depth guard, and ported 3 real lifecycle bug classes as living regressions — organic rf2-4l7t2 sync-unmount-during-render (no fabricated in-flight state), unbalanced subscribe/dispose (orphaned root), double-render. README rewritten in lockstep. Gates: clojure -M:test 12 tests/37 assertions 0 fail; clj-kondo clean. No follow-on split — recursive child mounting landed in-PR. Revisit in ~3 months; demote if still idle.

title: Audit: examples/helix/process_monitor_helix/ — code comments review (best-practice for AI + human readers)
description:
## Mandate

Audit the code comments in `examples/helix/process_monitor_helix/` for best-practice quality.

## Audience

**Future AIs and humans reading the code — both readers AND understanders.**
Comments should serve the LLM scanning a file as much as the human studying it.

## Questions to answer

For each comment / docstring / TODO / FIXME / inline note:

1. **Necessary?** Is this comment serving a purpose, or could the code be made self-documenting?
2. **True?** Does the comment still match the code, or has the code drifted past it (stale comments are worse than no comments)?
3. **Intent vs behaviour?** Does the comment explain *why* (the design intent, the constraint that forced the shape), or merely *what* (which the code already shows)?
4. **AI-ergonomic?** Would an LLM reading this file in isolation grasp the surrounding context from the comments + docstrings, or does it require off-file context?
5. **Citation / cross-ref?** Where a decision references spec/* or a non-obvious convention, is there a pointer? (`Per Spec 006 §...`, `Convention: ...`).
6. **TODO/FIXME hygiene?** Are TODOs annotated with context (bead-id, date, condition)? Or are they bare reminders that have aged?
7. **Voice match?** Does the comment match the surrounding voice + tone? (Terse where surrounding is terse; expansive where surrounding is expansive.)

## Anti-patterns to flag

- **Restating the obvious.** `;; increment the counter` above `(inc x)`.
- **Stale claims.** Comment says "returns nil" but fn now throws.
- **Decorative-only.** ASCII boxes / banners without semantic content.
- **Bead-ref residue.** `(rf2-XXXXX)` left over from an in-PR justification that no longer earns its keep in the canonical record.
- **Apologetic comments.** `;; hack — should refactor` without context. Better: file a bead + reference it.
- **Magic-number comments.** Should be named constants, not commented integers.
- **Drift-prone comments.** Specific line numbers, exact counts that the code can move past.

## Best-practice traits to preserve

- **Why-not-what** docstrings on public fns.
- **Cross-refs to spec/*** for non-obvious contract details.
- **Block headers** that name a section's purpose (`;; --- Lifecycle ---`).
- **Inline notes** explaining surprising decisions (`;; deliberately not deduped — caller relies on order`).
- **Sensible TODOs** annotated with bead-ids and rough timing.

## Procedure

1. **Read** every `.cljc / .cljs / .clj / .cjs / .md` (where applicable) file in `examples/helix/process_monitor_helix/`.
2. **Skim comments + docstrings**: ~10-30 per file typically.
3. **Apply the 7 questions + anti-pattern checklist** to each.
4. **File a follow-on bead per actionable insight**:
   - `bd create "<scope>(<surface>): <one-line>" --priority p3|p4 --type chore|bug --description "<finding with file:line + before/after>"`
   - `bd dep add <new-id> <this-bead-id> --type discovered-from`
   - Default priority P4 (cosmetic); use P3 if the comment is actively misleading (anti-pattern: stale-claim).
   - **Group small fixes** into a single bead when they're the same kind of fix across many files (e.g. "drop ~15 bead-refs from comments in `examples/helix/process_monitor_helix//src/*`").
5. **Write findings** to `ai/findings/2026-05-28-examples-helix-process_monitor_helix-comments.md` (gitignored). Per-file or per-pattern summary. Cite line numbers + before/after where useful.
6. **Close this bead** with a 1-paragraph verdict: comment-quality grade (A / B / C / D) + filed findings.

## Stance

Pre-alpha. SOTA masterpiece via **ELEGANCE + CLARITY + CORRECTNESS + GOOD PRACTICE**. Code comments are part of the artefact — they get the same masterpiece bar as the code.

## Coordination

These audits can be dispatched as Shape-2 clusters of 4-6 surfaces per worker. All are read-only on source + write only `.beads/issues.jsonl` + `ai/findings/*.md`. Zero collision with source-edit workers.
close_reason: Audit complete. Grade A- — comment-quality is strong across 245 lines of core.cljs + README + index.html. The ns docstring positions the example in the design-led trio explicitly (naming Reagent Notebook + UIx Atlas dashboard by shape). One marginally-misleading word noted ('Pick a random process for the synthetic log line' at line 75 — the code is deterministic mod-arithmetic, not random; sub-P4, included in the banner-style finding rather than its own bead). One P4 hygiene finding filed (banner-style consistency — rf2-uq6ix, joint with uix dashboard). Full audit: ai/findings/2026-05-28-examples-r3-uix-helix-scripts-comments.md (local-only).

title: Epoch DISPATCH body — event vector renders via str, not edn-inspector (bead 93a7s acceptance gap)
description:
**Severity: P3 polish** — surfaced by review rf2-uzcpg.

**Symptom.** The DISPATCH step's body renders the dispatched event vector by calling `projection/event-display`, which is just `(str event-vec)` — a one-line monospace block (see `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:1829-1834` and `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs` (`dispatch-body`)). The bead body for rf2-93a7s explicitly stated 'Render the dispatch event vector in the DISPATCH step body via edn-inspector browse mode (consistent with App-DB / Handler panels). Width-aware (rf2-kbdk8) handles inline vs tree.' — i.e. mount the canonical `edn-inspector` widget, not a custom monospace block.

**Operator impact.** Simple event vectors like `[:counter/inc]` render fine, but a verbose event vector (e.g. a machine event with a large map payload) wraps as flat text rather than drilling through edn-inspector's width-aware tree / inline-fit logic. The DISPATCH body is the one body slot in the Epoch cascade that diverges from the canonical edn-inspector mount convention; sibling slots (COEFFECT values via `edn/inspect-inline`, HANDLER `:db` via the full edn-inspector, SUBSCRIPTIONS values via `edn/mini` / the 3-mode toggle, FX args, etc.) all route through edn-inspector.

**Recommended fix.** Replace the `proj/event-display` body call site in `dispatch-body` with an `edn-inspector` mount (the same shape COEFFECT uses — small payloads inline, large ones drillable). The boxed monospace chrome can be preserved or dropped depending on aesthetic alignment with sibling step bodies.

**Acceptance.** DISPATCH step body mounts edn-inspector for the event vector; width-aware rules (rf2-kbdk8) drive inline-vs-tree rendering; a verbose payload no longer wraps as flat text.

**Discovered from rf2-93a7s review.**
close_reason: Already fixed in PR #2198 (commit 3af051b1a — rf2-8w8er subsumes rf2-nszcv); dispatch-body at view.cljs:1365 mounts edn-inspector. Bead was filed against stale state. No code change in #2285; verified no call-sites of proj/event-display remain in epoch/view.cljs.

title: examples/realworld: drop redundant :conduit.routing/pending-navigation sub — framework provides :rf/pending-navigation
description:
Discovered during review rf2-7goum of rf2-fgkte (PR #2239). The realworld example registers `:conduit.routing/pending-navigation` as a sub that simply reads `(:rf/pending-navigation db)`:

```
examples/reagent/realworld/routing.cljs:138
(rf/reg-sub :conduit.routing/pending-navigation
  (fn [db _] (:rf/pending-navigation db)))
```

But the routing framework already registers `:rf/pending-navigation` for exactly that slot at `implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc:2205`:

```
(subs/reg-sub :rf/pending-navigation
  {:doc "Subscribe to the `:rf/pending-navigation` slot ..."}
  (fn [db _] (:rf/pending-navigation db)))
```

The example's sub is a duplicate read of the same slot under a renamed id. Two subs cache the same value. The cleaner option is to drop the example's local reg-sub and subscribe directly to the framework-provided `:rf/pending-navigation`. The original rf2-fgkte fix correctly broke the name collision by renaming — this follow-up removes the duplication entirely.

## Files to touch
- examples/reagent/realworld/routing.cljs:138-139 — delete the reg-sub
- examples/reagent/realworld/core.cljs:150 — change subscribe to `:rf/pending-navigation`

## Scope
Pure example cleanup. No framework / spec change. Tests should keep passing (the framework sub returns the same value).

title: Epoch panel: DISPOSED sub-section is missing click-to-source affordance for the reg-sub
description:
rf2-wpfjo's bead acceptance #4 required: 'Click on a disposed-sub row opens the editor at the `reg-sub` source if coord captured.' The merged PR (#2214 — landed as part of the rf2-gmw1i + rf2-wpfjo + rf2-tzmmf cluster) does NOT add a click-to-source affordance to the disposed-subs-table.

Current code (tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:3083-3089):

     (cond
       (vector? query) [ei/mini query 40]
       (some? sub-id)  [ei/mini sub-id 40]
       :else           [:span ... "<anonymous sub>"])]

Compare with the sibling unmounted-views-table (same PR, same cluster) which DOES carry click-to-source:

Where `sub-coord` would resolve `(rf/handler-meta :sub sub-id)` → `{:file :line}` per the registrar shape — same affordance the regular subscriptions-table already uses for its rows.

This is an inconsistency between unmounted-views (got it right) and disposed-subs (missed it) — bead-acceptance shortfall, not a major UX failure but the disposed-row is unactionable until the operator clicks elsewhere to find the registration.

title: Epoch panel: SUBSCRIPTIONS per-row schema violations render below the table, not inline with the row
description:
rf2-xgeag's bead acceptance #1 requires schema violations to attach inline to their owning row for FX **and SUBSCRIPTIONS**. The PR (#2226) correctly inlines FX-row violations via `fx-row-with-violations` (renders row + its :violations block as one unit), but SUBSCRIPTIONS rows do NOT get the same treatment — `render-subscriptions-step` first renders the full subscriptions-table + disposed-subs-table, then renders per-row violations as a foot-of-step block via a separate `(for [row per-row-vio] (violation-blocks ...))`.

The contradiction is explicit in the code comment at view.cljs:3174-3177:
    ;; rf2-xgeag — `:sub-return` boundary violations. Per-row
    ;; attachments are rendered below their matching sub row;
    ;; step-level violations (indirect recomputes that don't
    ;; surface a row) ride at the foot.
which claims 'below their matching sub row' but the code emits them after the entire table.

Secondary issue: the `for` form at view.cljs:3178-3181 returns a lazy seq of `violation-blocks` outputs without per-iteration keys. The outer hiccup may produce React key warnings when N>1 sub-return violations attach to different rows in the same cascade.

Fix shape (parallel to FX): introduce `subs-row-with-violations` that renders one row + its :violations sub-block inline, and use it via the table's per-row render. Resizable-table doesn't support inline sub-row content easily — alternative is to drop violations out of the resizable-table cell and into a per-row wrapper.

Discovered during review rf2-h6aih (Causa-Epoch cluster B).
close_reason: Fixed in #2285 — SUBSCRIPTIONS per-row violations now attach INLINE via resizable-table's :row-extras slot (parity with FX step's fx-row-with-violations). Step-level violations still ride at the foot. Tests: subscriptions-row-violations-attach-inline-test + subscriptions-step-level-violations-still-at-foot-test.

title: Framework: native React DevTools inspector panel for re-frame2 (à la Redux DevTools / Apollo / MobX)
description:
## Why

React DevTools has an extension API for libraries to register a
**custom inspector panel** for their components. Apollo Client,
MobX, Redux DevTools all use it — each gets a native presence in
DevTools' Components inspector alongside the standard Props /
State / Hooks panels.

re-frame2 could do the same. The substrate has rich data that no
generic React DevTools view can surface:

- The view's registered id (post-quick-wins bead, this is the
  React displayName — but the inspector panel can show MORE)
- Subs the view currently consumes + their LIVE values from the
  sub cache
- The frame the view is running in
- Last render epoch + duration (from the trace stream)
- Schema violations attached to the view or its parent handler
- Click-to-source jumping straight to the `reg-view` definition

This would make re-frame2 a first-class React DevTools citizen
the way Redux is — operators investigating a re-frame2 app
via DevTools see substrate context inline, not just generic
React props.

Blocks-on / sibling: P2 quick-wins bead (displayName + JSX
source-coord props + Context labelling). The native inspector
builds on top of those.

## What changes — high level

A custom inspector panel registered with the React DevTools
backend API. The panel renders inside DevTools' Components
inspector right pane (alongside Props / State / Hooks), titled
"re-frame2".

For a selected reg-view'd component, the panel shows:

### Source surface
- Registered view-id (keyword)
- Source coord (file:line)
- "Open in editor" link → reuses Story's `open-in-editor` launcher

### Reactive surface
- Subs the view consumed during last render (read from sub
  cache; rf2-mrnur's dispose trace tells us the active
  derefer-set)
- Live values for each sub (via `edn-inspector/mini` for
  one-line rendering, expand-to-full inline)
- Visual indicator if any sub's value changed since last render

### Cascade surface
- Last render epoch-id + wall-clock duration
- "Show in Xray Trace" link → dispatches into the host's
  `:rf/xray` frame to focus that epoch
- Render-count since page load

### Frame surface
- Frame-id this view is in (`:rf/default` / `:rf/xray` / custom)
- Frame's preset / fx-overrides / etc. (from `rf/frame-meta`)

### Schema surface
- Any `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` events attached to
  the view's owning handler in the recent trace buffer
- Recovery posture (rolled-back / fx-skipped / etc.)

## Technical considerations

### React DevTools backend API

React DevTools is open-source; the API for libraries to
register inspector panels is in the `react-devtools-shared`
package (`reactDevtoolsAgent.addInspectorPanel(...)` or
similar — worker confirms exact API surface). Apollo's
implementation is a reference. The API is dev-only — there's
no production cost.

### Bundle isolation

The DevTools inspector code MUST live in a build path that
elides under `interop/debug-enabled? false`. The pattern
matches Xray's bundle-isolation contract (per
`npm run test:bundle-isolation`). Code lives in
`implementation/core/devtools/` or a sibling
`implementation/devtools/` artefact; nothing in production
paths `:requires` it.

### Cross-frame considerations

A view rendered under `:rf/xray` shows different data than the
same view under `:rf/default`. The inspector panel reads the
view's actual current frame (already known to the framework)
and surfaces frame-scoped data. Same view-id under two frames
shows two different sub-value sets.

### Hot-reload + identity

The inspector panel should survive `:after-load` hot-reloads of
the user's app. If the React DevTools backend tracks component
identity by displayName + position, the panel rebinds cleanly.
Worker confirms the API's reload semantics.

### Integration with existing Xray

The inspector panel's "Show in Xray Trace" link assumes the host
app has Xray installed. When Xray isn't present:
- Either degrade gracefully (link greyed out with tooltip "Xray
  not installed in this app")
- Or surface ALL the data inline in the DevTools panel without
  cross-linking

Lean: graceful degradation. The DevTools panel works
standalone; Xray is an optional cross-link surface.

## Possible scope additions (bundled or follow-on)

These naturally fold into the inspector panel work:

- **View args as named React props** (item 3 from pair-debug's
  bullet list): pretty-print CLJS view args instead of opaque
  varargs blobs. Reuses the inspector's edn rendering.
- **React Profiler integration** (item 6): tag `:rf.view/render`
  trace events with React's render-id so the operator can
  cross-reference Xray's per-cascade trace with React's profiler
  timeline.
- **Hot-reload identity preservation** (item 8): verify reg-view'd
  components preserve identity across `:after-load`. If they
  don't, fix or document.

Worker decides whether to fold into this bead or file as P4
follow-ons.

## What does NOT change

- The framework's runtime contracts — additive panel only
- Production builds — entire panel elides
- React DevTools itself — uses its existing extension API
- Xray's own surfaces — they remain the canonical heavy-data
  view; the DevTools inspector is the lighter Components-tab-
  embedded surface

## Acceptance

1. Loading a re-frame2 app with React DevTools installed shows a
   "re-frame2" subpanel in the Components inspector right pane
   when a reg-view'd component is selected.
2. Subpanel renders the source / reactive / cascade / frame /
   schema surfaces enumerated above.
3. Live values update as the underlying state mutates.
4. "Open in editor" + "Show in Xray Trace" links function (the
   latter degrades gracefully when Xray isn't installed).
5. Production builds elide the entire panel; bundle-isolation
   gate passes.
6. Worked example in `examples/<...>` demonstrates the inspector
   panel + documents the React DevTools setup required to see
   it.

## Coordination

- New code under `implementation/core/devtools/` (or a sibling
  artefact). Hot-zone consideration if it lives under core.
- Possibly spec/006 §Source-coord annotation + a new
  spec/DevTools-Integration.md normative doc.
- Pre-alpha posture: lock in to React DevTools backend API as
  the integration shape; no fallback for non-React-DevTools
  inspectors.

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27.

## Blocks-on

P2 quick-wins bead (displayName + JSX source-coord props +
Context labelling). The native inspector layers on top of those
foundations.
notes: DEFERRED (Mike, 2026-05-28): post-alpha. Native React DevTools inspector panel is a feature epic; not pre-alpha-critical and Xray already covers live inspection (app-db, trace stream, epoch scrub). Revisit after alpha.

title: Investigate flat-row :path sort behaviour for mixed-type path segments in diff/engine.cljc
description:
Per audit rf2-gpuv3 finding **L3** (defer-eligible).

## Problem

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine.cljc:508,672` both sort flat-row maps by their `:path` vector:

```clojure
(sort-by :path flat-rows)
```

Clojure's default vector comparator compares element-by-element. For paths mixing keyword and integer segments (a common case: `[:rf/machines :flow 3]`) this throws `ClassCastException` at the comparison.

The engine's wrapping `try/catch` at line 169 short-circuits ONLY if the underlying Editscript call throws. When Editscript returns valid edits, `sort-by :path` runs unguarded and the mixed-type compare bubbles up to the consumer.

May not be exercised in the current test suite (the R6 vector tests use homogeneous integer paths). Real app-dbs with mixed `:rf/machines` map + vector indices would hit it.

## Investigation

1. Construct a fixture with a mixed-type path that produces flat-rows containing mixed-type `:path` vectors (e.g. before `{:flow {:phases [:a :b]}}` vs after `{:flow {:phases [:a :b :c]}}` — yields flat-row `:path` of `[:flow :phases 2]` (keywords + integer)).
2. Run `engine/project` on it; observe whether `sort-by :path` succeeds or throws.
3. If throws — pick a comparator strategy:
   - Sort by `pr-str` of the path (stable lexicographic, may not match operator intuition)
   - Custom comparator that orders by path length first then by per-segment `pr-str`
4. Add a regression test once the fix is in.

## Defer-eligible

If no current Story / production trace surfaces the issue and an investigation finds the case is already short-circuited elsewhere, this is DEFER. File a follow-on the next time a flat-rows panel sees a CCE in the wild.

## Files

- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine.cljc:490-509,660-672`
- New test in `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine_cljs_test.cljc` if a real repro lands.

## Acceptance

1. Investigation outcome documented (file as finding or as a follow-on bead with the right shape).
2. If a real fix lands, regression test added.
notes: Fixed via PR #2336 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2336). Investigation finding: the engine's PUBLIC surface does not currently reach the CCE failure mode — R7 type-change reclassification short-circuits per-leaf descent before mixed-type siblings can surface in flat-rows. The fix is a defensive hardening: introduce a private compare-path comparator (length first, then per-segment pr-str) at both sort sites in tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/diff/engine.cljc. Pinned by three regression tests in engine_cljs_test.cljc (n83r8-*). 956/3764 JVM tests green; clj-kondo 0 errors / 0 new warnings.

title: spec/005: reconcile aspirational machine-schema prose after :schema-on-reg-machine lands
description:
## Why

spec/005-StateMachines.md carries two foundational paragraphs
that commit to a runtime behaviour the framework can't actually
deliver until the sibling bead (`:schema` key on `reg-machine`)
ships. They read as factual prose but describe an aspirational
feature.

spec/005:154 (under §Where snapshots live):

> The runtime composes `:rf/machines`'s schema automatically
> from the registered machines' `:data` schemas —
> `(rf/app-schema-at [:rf/machines])` returns
> `[:map-of :keyword :rf/machine-snapshot]`, and per-machine
> entries refine `:rf/machine-snapshot` against the registered
> machine's declared `:data` shape.

spec/005:165 (under §What the Single Store gives us for free):

> **Schema validation.** `(rf/reg-app-schema [:rf/machines]
> ...)` validates the whole machine map; per-machine `:data`
> schemas refine it (per §Where snapshots live).

Both reference "the registered machine's declared `:data`
shape" — but the registration grammar (spec/005:193-201)
declares no `:schema` slot. There is no way for a user to
*supply* the `:data` shape the runtime is supposedly composing
schemas from. The prose describes a phantom feature.

The implementation matches: grep across
`implementation/machines/` finds no `:data-schema` /
`:machine.*:schema` reference on the registration path. The
only `:schema` references are user-data in `:meta` slots
(`:meta {:schema-version 7}` — unrelated, user-domain).

## What this bead does

Reconcile the spec prose with the surface once the sibling
bead lands (the `:schema` key on `reg-machine`):

1. **Anchor the prose** — both paragraphs become factual once
   `:schema` ships. Edit them to reference the new surface:
   - spec/005:154 — "registered machines' `:data` schemas"
     becomes "the `:schema` slot on each registered machine
     (per §Schema validation)".
   - spec/005:165 — same anchor; add a cross-reference to
     the new §Schema validation subsection.
2. **Cross-link spec/010** — both paragraphs gain a "see
   spec/010-Schemas §Per-step recovery row 7" link so readers
   following from the Single Store narrative land on the
   recovery semantics.
3. **Verify no other aspirational schema prose** — sweep
   spec/005 for any other reference to machine-side schema
   validation; ensure every mention points to the new
   `:schema` slot.

## Why split from the sibling bead

The sibling bead is the substantive feature (spec change +
grammar table + new validation site in `implementation/
machines/` + new trace `:where` value + tests). Folding the
prose reconciliation into it would muddy the PR; folding the
prose reconciliation BEFORE it lands would create a window
where the spec contradicts itself (the prose says the feature
ships; the grammar table still has no `:schema`).

The clean shape: sibling bead lands first → grammar table +
implementation + trace emit + new §Schema validation
subsection all ship together → this bead lands after, doing
just the cross-reference + prose-anchoring sweep so the
foundational paragraphs cite the new section by name.

## Acceptance

1. spec/005:154 prose references the `:schema` slot on
   `reg-machine` (new surface from sibling bead).
2. spec/005:165 prose references the new §Schema validation
   subsection.
3. Cross-references to spec/010 §Per-step recovery added at
   both sites.
4. No other phantom schema-validation prose remains in
   spec/005.
5. `mkdocs build --strict` passes (all cross-refs resolve).

## What does NOT change

- The semantics described in the two paragraphs — those were
  always the intent. We're matching the prose to the surface,
  not changing what the runtime does.
- spec/010 (the sibling bead handles spec/010 changes).
- Any other spec file (sweep is bounded to spec/005).

## Coordination

Spec/005 is hot-zone (sequential, never parallel per
CLAUDE.md). Worker checks dashboard before dispatching.

**BLOCKS-ON the sibling bead** (the `:schema`-on-reg-machine
feature). Cannot land until the new §Schema validation
subsection + the `:schema` grammar row exist for these
paragraphs to anchor against.

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27.
close_reason: PR #2229 — spec/005 prose at lines 154 + 165 rewritten to describe the shipped :schema-on-reg-machine surface (rf2-jbbp7 / #2227) as fact, with cross-refs to the new §Schema validation subsection and Spec 010 §Per-step recovery row 7. Also de-aspirational-ised the §Schema validation closing cross-ref. Gates: python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py exit 0; python -m mkdocs build --strict exit 0.

title: Xray: Epoch machine-cascade surfaces source for inline-fn :entry/:exit + transition :guard + transition + timer rows
description:
## Why

The Epoch panel's machine-cascade view (rf2-u69j7, PR #2203) renders
ALWAYS-VISIBLE source code interleaved with each cascade row — but
only for **named guards + named actions** referenced via keyword.
Four classes of cascade rows currently show behaviour without
source:

1. Inline-fn `:entry` / `:exit` actions on state nodes
2. Inline-fn `:guard` slots on transitions
3. Transition rows themselves (the `{:from} → {:to}` step)
4. Timer rows (`:rf.machine.timer/cancelled`)

The macro DOES stamp source-coords for cases 1-3 already (per
rf2-8bp3 — CLJS-only because JVM reader meta doesn't ride on map /
vector literals; the cascade is a CLJS surface, so this is fine).
The data is there; the projection + view layer just don't reach
for it.

## Where the gap lives — pin the file/line

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:1381-1392`
— `cascade-row-source-key`:

    (case kind
      :action (when action-id [:actions action-id])
      :guard  (when guard-id  [:guards guard-id])
      nil)   ;; :transition + :timer + inline cases fall here

That single dispatch is the entire surface deciding which rows get
the source-link + always-visible source-form rendering.
`view.cljs:680-705` (`cascade-row-coord` + `cascade-row-source-form`)
both feed off this key.

## Why this matters

The cascade is the "what just happened in this machine" lens. When
the operator sees row N with phase `:entry`, action verb "(inline
fn)" — no source link, no body — they have to mentally chase the
machine spec elsewhere to find the code that ran. For named actions
the cascade closes that loop in-tool. For inline fns + transitions
+ timers, the loop reopens.

The Spec 005 §`:guards`/`:actions` doc actively encourages naming
compound logic (e.g. lines 311-319 of `spec/005-StateMachines.md`:
"even better — declare a named compound in the machine's `:guards`
map — the name carries semantic content visualisers and AIs read").
So the inline-fn case is somewhat discouraged. But idiomatic v2
state machines still use inline fns for one-liners, and transitions
+ timers carry no choice — they are always "inline" in the spec.

## What changes

Extend `cascade-row-source-key` (or replace with a richer dispatch)
so each row kind/phase resolves to the spec-path tuple under which
the macro stamped its coord. Then extend
`cascade-row-source-form`'s `get-in` lookup to use the same key,
so the always-visible source body renders for these rows too.

### A — inline-fn `:entry` / `:exit`

The row arrives with `:phase :entry` (or `:exit`, `:initial-entry`,
`:destroy-exit`) and either:
- `:action-id <keyword>` → named action, current code path works
- `:action-id nil` (or a synthetic id) → inline fn

For inline-fn entries, the macro stamps the coord at
`[:states <state-id> :entry]` / `[:states <state-id> :exit]`. The
cascade row needs to carry `:state-id` (which it already does —
verify in `projection.cljc :311-...` `action-cascade-row`) so
the source-key dispatch can return `[:states state-id :entry]` /
`[:states state-id :exit]` when `:action-id` is nil.

The `cascade-row-source-form` `get-in` against the spec resolves
to the inline fn literal at that path.

### B — inline-fn `:guard` on a transition

The row arrives with `:kind :guard`, `:guard-id nil` (because
there is no named guard — the form is the guard) and an event-id
+ state-id pair. The macro stamps the coord at
`[:states <state-id> :on <event-id> :guard]`.

For inline guards, source-key returns
`[:states state-id :on event-id :guard]` so coord + form lookup
both work. Note: the transition can carry a vector of
target-options (each its own map with `:guard`), so the path may
need to include the option index (e.g. `[:states ... :on ... 0
:guard]`). Worker confirms against rf2-8bp3 stamping rules.

### C — transition rows (`{:from} → {:to}` step)

The row arrives with `:kind :transition`, an event-id, and from
/ to state ids. The transition map literal in the spec has its
own coord at `[:states <from-state-id> :on <event-id>]` (or
similar — worker confirms exact path; transitions can be vector-
of-options).

For transitions, source-key returns
`[:states from-state-id :on event-id]` so the operator clicks
through to the transition map literal in the spec.

The source-FORM render is more nuanced — the transition map is
`{:target :foo :guard ... :action ...}`, which is data, not a
fn body. The cascade could:
- Render the transition map verbatim (4-5 lines of EDN), OR
- Render only the source-coord chip (click-through, no inline
  body), OR
- Render only `:action` portion's fn-body if `:action` is inline

Mike's call. The minimum-viable shape is the coord chip; the
delight shape is the inline EDN. Suggest starting with the chip
and elevating only if the EDN is short.

### D — timer rows

The row arrives with `:kind :timer`, a state-id, and a closed-set
reason (`:on-exit / :on-destroy / :on-resolution / :on-supersede /
…`). Timers come from `:after` slots, which sit per-state under
`[:states <state-id> :after <delay-ms>]` or
`[:states <state-id> :after <delay-ms> :target]`.

The macro doesn't yet stamp coords for `:after` (Spec 005 §Source-
coord stamping only enumerates `:guards / :actions / :on-spawn-
actions` + state-tree paths — `:after` is a *map key* not an *fn
form*, so JVM/CLJS reader meta limitations cap what's reachable).

For timers, two paths:
- **D1 (cheap)** — surface the state-id's own coord
  (`[:states <state-id>]`) so click-through lands on the state
  node carrying the `:after` slot. Operator orients from there.
- **D2 (rich)** — extend the macro stamping to walk `:after`
  slots + stamp coords at `[:states <state-id> :after <delay-ms>]`.
  Requires a small framework change (`reg-machine` macro). Worth
  it if timer cascades are common; deferrable if rare.

Suggest D1 first; D2 can follow as its own bead if Mike judges
the timer-row use-case load-bearing.

## Acceptance

1. `cascade-row-source-key` dispatches on all four row classes:
   inline-fn `:entry`/`:exit`, inline-fn `:guard`, `:transition`,
   `:timer`.
2. Every cascade row in a CLJS-built machine spec renders the
   click-to-source affordance — verify in panel-gallery's
   `fixtures_epoch.cljs` machine-driven fixture (which already
   exercises every row kind per rf2-u69j7).
3. Inline-fn `:entry`/`:exit` and inline-fn transition `:guard`
   rows render the always-visible source-form body the same way
   named actions/guards do (`view.cljs:1019-...` cascade-row-view
   surface).
4. Transition rows render the source-coord chip (always); the
   source-form body is optional — operator + worker decide based
   on EDN size + readability.
5. Timer rows render at minimum the parent state's source-coord
   chip (D1); the richer per-`:after` coord (D2) is a follow-on
   if worth it.
6. spec/021 §9.1.10.1 (the rf2-u69j7 cascade contract) updated to
   say "every cascade row carries source visibility" instead of
   the current "guards + named actions".
7. New projection tests: each new source-key path resolves
   correctly; old paths unchanged.
8. View test: a fixture with one transition + one inline `:entry`
   renders the source chips/bodies the same way the named
   action fixture does.

## What does NOT change

- The `reg-machine` macro's stamping pass (already stamps the
  paths we need for cases A/B/C; case D's macro extension is
  deferrable)
- `:rf.machine/source-coords` index shape — same map, just more
  paths populated
- The `:rf.machine/*` trace events — no payload change
- spec/005-StateMachines.md §Source-coord stamping (rf2-8bp3)
  contract — already documents the index; just more cascade
  surfaces consume it
- Named guard/action source rendering — already works

## Coordination

Single-bead scope. Touches:
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc`
  (`cascade-row-source-key` + maybe row-builder fns if
  `:state-id` isn't already on the row)
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs`
  (`cascade-row-coord` + `cascade-row-source-form` get-in path)
- `tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md` §9.1.10.1
- New tests under
  `tools/xray/test/.../panels/epoch/projection_cljs_test.cljc`
  + `view_cljs_test.cljs`

Hot-zone? No — Xray internal surface, single PR scope. Parallel-
safe with non-Xray work.

Per pair-debug 2026-05-27. Follow-on to rf2-u69j7.
close_reason: PR #2224 — Epoch machine-cascade source surfacing for inline-fn :entry/:exit/:guard/:action + transition + timer rows. Source-key dispatch extended; rows enriched with state/event correlation; view-side body renders for :transition rows; timer rows surface verb-chip only (D1). Spec §9.1.5 updated. Tests: 10 projection + 4 view = 14 new tests.

title: Add Reagent substrate-level :rf.sub/dispose tests (view-unmount + conditional-deref) — rf2-mrnur acceptance #4+#5
description:
## Why

rf2-mrnur (`:rf.sub/dispose` trace event, PR #2204) shipped with
JVM-side cache-eviction tests but did NOT cover the substrate-level
view-unmount / conditional-deref round-trip explicitly called for
in the bead's acceptance.

The bead's acceptance criteria #4 + #5 read (verbatim):

    4. Test: subscribe to a sub from a test view; unmount the view;
       verify `:rf.sub/dispose` fires with `:reason :no-more-derefers`.
    5. Test the conditional-access case too — a view that conditionally
       derefs a sub; flip the condition; verify dispose fires when
       the condition stops the deref.

PR #2204 shipped `sub_dispose_trace_test.clj` (JVM, cache-level —
exercises the eviction code path directly + tags reasons correctly).
That coverage is good and arguably stronger for the framework
contract, but it does NOT exercise the **Reagent-side derefer-count
machinery** that drives disposal in real apps:

- Component mounts → subscribes → 1 derefer
- Component unmounts → derefer drops to 0 → cache evicts → trace emit
- Component re-renders without derefing (conditional `when` flips
  false) → derefer drops → cache evicts → trace emit

The cache-level tests pin "if eviction is called with reason X, the
trace fires with reason X". The view-level tests would pin "real
mount/unmount + conditional-deref flows DO trigger eviction the way
operators rely on for cascade-attributed disposal".

## Why does this matter

Today the gap means:
- If a future change to Reagent integration (e.g. derefer-count
  bookkeeping in the cache, hooks-substrate behaviour) regresses
  the view-unmount → dispose path, no test fires.
- The Epoch panel's disposed-subs section (rf2-wpfjo, also landed
  in this 12h window via PR #2214) depends on this exact round-trip
  working — view unmounts in the focused cascade, dispose trace
  fires, projection surfaces it.

So the rf2-wpfjo Epoch surface is **load-bearing on the untested
half** of rf2-mrnur. A regression in derefer-count bookkeeping
would silently break the disposed-subs section with no CI signal.

## Fix shape

Add substrate-level tests covering the two cases from rf2-mrnur
acceptance #4 + #5. Probable test home:

`implementation/adapters/reagent/test/.../sub_dispose_view_test.cljs`

(or wherever Reagent adapter integration tests live — worker locates
the canonical home; mirror the existing `:rf.sub/run` view-level
test surface if there is one).

### Test 1 — view unmount → dispose

    (deftest sub-dispose-on-view-unmount
      ;; Mount a view that derefs sub :foo.
      ;; Capture trace events for :rf.sub.
      ;; Unmount the view.
      ;; Assert: :rf.sub/dispose fires with :reason :no-more-derefers,
      ;;         payload includes the sub-id + query-vector + frame.

### Test 2 — conditional deref → dispose on condition flip

    (deftest sub-dispose-on-conditional-deref-flip
      ;; Mount a view: (when @cond @sub-foo).
      ;; Initially `cond` = true → sub-foo is referenced.
      ;; Flip `cond` to false → re-render → sub-foo no longer derefed.
      ;; Assert: :rf.sub/dispose fires for sub-foo with
      ;;         :reason :no-more-derefers.

Both tests should also cover the multi-derefer case as negative
control:
- Two views deref same sub; unmount one → NO dispose.
- Unmount the second → dispose fires.

## Acceptance

1. Two new tests pass in the Reagent adapter test suite:
   - view-unmount → dispose
   - conditional-deref flip → dispose
2. Multi-derefer negative control: dispose does NOT fire while ≥1
   derefer remains.
3. Tests run as part of `npm run test:cljs` (or `test:browser` if
   Reagent integration requires DOM).
4. Tests use the public trace-subscription API, not internal cache
   inspection — to prove the contract from the operator's
   perspective.
5. The existing JVM `sub_dispose_trace_test.clj` is NOT replaced
   — both layers (cache + substrate) get coverage. The JVM tests
   pin the framework contract; the new view tests pin the
   substrate integration.

## What does NOT change

- The framework emit logic — already correct + tested
- `:rf.sub/dispose` schema, reasons enum, payload shape
- Existing cache-level JVM tests
- Epoch panel rf2-wpfjo disposed-subs section — gains a CI safety
  net but no code change

## Coordination

Test-only addition under `implementation/adapters/reagent/test/`.
Parallel-safe per CLAUDE.md (test-only dirs are isolated surfaces).
No hot-zone concerns.

UIx + Helix adapters: optional follow-on if the same view-unmount
contract applies (worker confirms — likely yes for UIx via hooks,
deferred for Helix if its derefer-count integration is incomplete).

Per audit `12h-commit-audit-2026-05-27` ⚠️ drift #2.
close_reason: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2222 — Reagent-substrate sub_dispose_view_cljs_test.cljs: view-unmount cascade emit, conditional-deref flip emit, multi-derefer negative control. 3 tests / 29 assertions green. Quality gates: test:cljs 4841/4841, test:browser 124/124, test:elision 38/38 absent.

title: chore(xray): unify panel-gallery + projection-test fixtures against the canonical trace/emit! shape (kill the fixture-co-bug pattern)
description:
**Severity: LOW** (process / test-quality issue) — surfaced by audit rf2-33cqr LOW-2.

**Detail.** Multiple fixtures across the xray test+gallery surfaces use DIFFERENT (and in many cases WRONG) tag-names + op-names compared to what the substrate's `trace/emit!` actually stamps:

- `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection_cljs_test.cljc:81-86` — uses `:rf.flow/recomputed` (wrong; substrate emits `:rf.flow/computed`).
- `tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures_epoch.cljs:118-126` — same drift.
- `tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures_trace.cljs:328-339` — uses canonical `:rf.flow/computed` (correct). Internal inconsistency across fixtures.

This is the **root cause** of why rf2-yhgk8 / rf2-slnce / rf2-ipaza / rf2-w2r4p went undetected — the projection tests + the gallery used the SAME wrong names as the reader code, so the wrong reader "passed" all tests + looked right in the gallery, but real-substrate cascades produced nothing.

**Recommended structural fix.**

1. Extract a single canonical trace-event-builder helper, sharable across:
   - Substrate test-helpers (already roughly canonical — `implementation/.../test/.../*_test.{clj,cljc}`).
   - Panel-gallery fixtures (`tools/xray/testbeds/panel_gallery/fixtures_*.cljs`).
   - Projection unit tests (`tools/xray/test/.../projection_*_test.cljc`).

2. Better: extend at least one projection test to drive a REAL `trace/emit!` invocation against the substrate (an end-to-end test that fires a flow / fx / cofx via the actual cascade machinery and asserts the projection result), so a substrate-side rename can never silently desync from the panel-gallery synth fixtures.

**Dependency.** Should land AFTER (or in the same PR as) rf2-yhgk8 / rf2-slnce / rf2-ipaza / rf2-w2r4p — fix the readers first, then sweep the fixtures.

**Acceptance.** No fixture across xray uses a tag-name or op-name that diverges from substrate emit-site reality. A grep for fixtures-vs-substrate names returns zero discrepancies.

**Sequential after the four HIGH reader-fix beads land; safe to parallel with rf2-509pq + rf2-ezqpm.

title: chore(xray): drop dead :event top-level fallback in dispatch-row + project; documents intent against future drift
description:
**Severity: MED** (defensive-coding clarity gap) — surfaced by audit rf2-33cqr.

**Detail.** `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:96` reads:

```clojure
(or (common/tag-of ev :rf.event/v)
    (common/tag-of ev :event)
    (:event ev)            ; ← dead arm
    fallback-event)
```

The `(:event ev)` arm reads a TOP-LEVEL key off the trace event. Trace events never carry `:event` at top level — the substrate stamps `:rf.event/v` under `:tags` per spec 009. The fallback is legacy and dead. Same shape duplicated at projection.cljc:883-889 inside `project`'s `fallback` / `event-id` resolution.

**Impact.** Today: none (the canonical-tag read at `:rf.event/v` matches first). Future: invites drift — reads as "this slot might be at top level", which is wrong. Newcomers may add similar top-level fallbacks elsewhere, propagating the misleading pattern.

**Recommended fix.**
- projection.cljc:96 — drop the `(:event ev)` arm.
- projection.cljc:883-889 — drop the same arm in the `fallback` and `event-id` resolutions.
- Document in the projection ns docstring (or a code comment near the reads) that trace events carry the event-vector under `[:tags :rf.event/v]` per spec 009 §canonical per-frame routing key.

**Acceptance.** No `(:event ev)` top-level reads in projection.cljc; the file's intent reads cleanly as "the canonical tag with fixture-compat fallbacks for legacy tag-names only".

**Safe to parallel — single file, isolated edit.
close_reason: Landed in PR #2210 (cluster: epoch-projection-tag-drift).

title: DEFERRED: document tool frame-envelope convention in spec/Conventions or spec/002-Frames (post-rf2-tvu99)
description:
The recurring frame-envelope class (rf2-7sdja, rf2-kcaiz, rf2-p56sk,
and others) is the same pattern: tool surfaces forgetting to tag
dispatches with their tool frame, so events route to `:rf/default`
and silently no-op or read the wrong app-db.

`rf2-tvu99` is in flight and may land a structural fix that
supersedes per-call-site envelope tagging. Spec edit should wait
until that lands so the doc reflects the final pattern.

After rf2-tvu99 lands, decide which spec gets the convention text:

- `spec/Conventions.md` — the dispatch envelope convention (`{:frame
  <tool-id>}`) as part of the reserved-namespace guidance for
  canonical devtools.
- `spec/002-Frames.md` — the substrate-side contract (tools call
  cross-frame dispatch through the same machinery as user code, but
  must opt in via the envelope).

## Why DEFER

Editing the spec now would either:
1. Codify a pattern rf2-tvu99 might retire (the per-call-site `{:frame
   :rf/xray}` discipline), OR
2. Document the structural fix before it lands.

Either way is wrong-shaped.

## Acceptance (once rf2-tvu99 lands)

- Convention or framework spec documents the tool-frame envelope
  contract.
- Cross-reference rf2-7sdja, rf2-kcaiz, rf2-p56sk, rf2-tvu99 as the
  reference-case beads.
- spec compiles via `mkdocs build --strict`.

Per rf2-tawqp audit `ai/findings/xray-spec-drift-audit-2026-05-26.md`
DEFER1.

## Blocked by

`rf2-tvu99` (in flight).
close_reason: Convention documented in spec/Conventions.md (new section 'Tool dispatch frame-envelope convention'). Distinguishes the two cases (sync dispatch from a tool view → bare dispatch envelope; async boundary → frame-bound-fn) and explicitly notes that rf2-atqkg lazy-seq deref tracking is a DIFFERENT bug class with a different cure. Cross-refs rf2-tvu99 / rf2-x005l / rf2-atqkg / rf2-nmusx. PR #2225 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2225 — mkdocs --strict clean, 4756/4756 CLJS tests pass.
