title: Trace.Panel — replace linear focused-cascade scan with layer-3 sub
description:
## Source

Audit finding F7 from rf2-qa75r (xray efficiency sweep, 2026-05-26).

## Symptom

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/trace.cljs:631-638`:

```clojure
(let [{:keys [envelope outcome bands empty-kind] :as _data}
      @(rf/subscribe [:rf.xray/trace-feed])
      cascades        @(rf/subscribe [:rf.xray/cascades])
      focus           @(rf/subscribe [:rf.xray/focus])
      focused-id      (:dispatch-id focus)
      focused-cascade (when focused-id
                        (some #(when (= focused-id (:dispatch-id %)) %)
                              cascades))
      ...]
  ...)
```

Trace.Panel subscribes to the full `:rf.xray/cascades` vector + linearly scans it via `some` to find the focused cascade. Re-runs on every focus change or cascades push. For N=500+ cascades (the spine retention default may be higher under bench), the scan walks the list.

## Cost

O(N) scan per Panel render. Memoisation defeats: the result is identity-stable only when the focused-cascade record itself is identical-by-reference — but the `some`+`when` construction allocates a fresh path each time. The Panel re-renders any time `cascades` reference changes (every dispatch in the host).

## Fix shape

Register a layer-3 composite sub:

```clojure
(rf/reg-sub :rf.xray.trace/focused-cascade
  :<- [:rf.xray/cascades]
  :<- [:rf.xray/focus]
  (fn [[cs focus] _]
    (let [focused-id (:dispatch-id focus)]
      (when focused-id
        (some #(when (= focused-id (:dispatch-id %)) %) cs)))))
```

Panel reads `:rf.xray.trace/focused-cascade` directly. Memo kicks in when the input vec + focus map are identity-stable. Render body shrinks. The `cascades` + `focus` subs are still needed for unrelated uses elsewhere; that''s fine — re-frame de-dupes the underlying signals.

## Why this matters

Trace.Panel is the most-pivoted-into panel; render-body computation that runs on every cascade push is a small constant added to every dispatch. MED priority because the scan is fast in practice (vector traversal of ~500 entries is microseconds) but it''s the kind of pattern that compounds — a future second panel doing the same `some` would push the cumulative cost up.

The fix also follows spec/Conventions.md §reg-sub layer-3 idiom — composite subs over signal subs, no scanning in render bodies.

## Acceptance

- `:rf.xray.trace/focused-cascade` registered in `panels.trace/install!`.
- `Panel` body uses `@(rf/subscribe [:rf.xray.trace/focused-cascade])` instead of the inline scan.
- No behavioural change. Trace browser-smoke + CLJS unit tests pass.
- The same `cascade-status-bar` call site continues to work (the sub returns the cascade record verbatim).
close_reason: Layer-3 composite sub :rf.xray.trace/focused-cascade replaces inline scan in Trace panel render body. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2215

title: Machine inspector — pass records into focused-event-view + hoist section styles
description:
## Source

Audit finding F6 from rf2-qa75r (xray efficiency sweep, 2026-05-26).

## Symptom

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_inspector.cljs:872-1029` — Two sub-graph inefficiencies plus ~56 inline-style sites.

1. **Duplicate subscribe** — `Panel` (line 980-981) derefs `:rf.xray/machine-inspector-data` + `:rf.xray/machine-transitions-for-focused-event`. `focused-event-view` (line 872-873, called from Panel''s `else` branch) derefs `:rf.xray/machine-transitions-for-focused-event` AGAIN. Same Reaction handle is constructed twice per Panel render.

2. **Sub-cascade in focused-event-section** — `focused-event-section` derefs `:rf.xray.machine-canvas/chart-collapsed-for` + the inner `:rf.xray.machine-canvas/view-mode-for`. These are fine in isolation (different signals; both stable per machine-id), but they sit inside a `focused-event-section` called from `focused-event-view`. The chain is OK but visible to future eyes as a cascading-sub trail.

3. **Inline styles** — Panel''s outer section style, header style, focused-event-host wrapper style, and the per-section header / list-view chrome inside `focused-event-section` are all inline literals.

## Cost

The duplicate subscribe is a constant-factor inefficiency — one extra Reaction handle per Panel render. Sub-graph is memoised so the result map is identical; just a small wasted construction step.

Inline styles: ~10-15 layout/header-style maps per Panel render. Lower than the per-row panels (F1-F4) because machine_inspector renders one focused-event-section per cascade, not N rows.

## Fix shape

1. Refactor `focused-event-view` to accept `records` as an arg from `Panel`. Drop its private subscribe. Panel''s `let` already has `records` in scope.

2. Hoist `Panel`-level + `focused-event-section`-level layout/header styles to ns-top defs (`machine-inspector-section-style`, `machine-inspector-header-style`, `focused-event-section-style-base`, `focused-event-section-header-style`).

3. Leave the `:rf.xray.machine-canvas/chart-collapsed-for` + `view-mode-for` subs in place — they''re per-machine signals; pulling them to Panel-level would require lifting machine-id resolution upward, which is more refactoring than reward.

## Why this matters

MED priority — machine_inspector is event-driven (renders one section when the focused event triggered a machine transition; BLANK otherwise). Less hot than Trace/Cascade/Event-detail but the duplicate-subscribe is the kind of thing that drifts further if not fixed early.

## Acceptance

- `focused-event-view` takes `records` as an arg; no internal subscribe to `:rf.xray/machine-transitions-for-focused-event`.
- Panel + focused-event-section layout styles hoisted to defs.
- No behavioural change. Machine-inspector browser-smoke + CLJS unit tests pass.
close_reason: PR #2216 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2216) — focused-event-view now accepts records as an arg from Panel (drops duplicate sub-deref); 6 section-level layout/header styles hoisted to ns-top defs. Site count 56 to 50. Gates: test:cljs 4814/15662 green, test:browser 124/353 green, test:bundle-isolation green.

title: Epoch panel: COEFFECT + SUBSCRIPTIONS pills share magenta — original mock had them distinct
description:
## Symptom

The Epoch panel's COEFFECT and SUBSCRIPTIONS pill badges render in
ALMOST the same colour. Live (pair-debug 2026-05-26) DOM probe:

| Pill | Background |
|---|---|
| DISPATCH | `rgb(140, 149, 159)` grey |
| **COEFFECT** | `rgb(177, 70, 194)` magenta |
| HANDLER | `rgb(9, 105, 218)` blue |
| **SUBSCRIPTIONS** | `rgb(177, 70, 194)` magenta ← IDENTICAL to COEFFECT |
| VIEWS | `rgb(26, 127, 55)` green |

Five pipeline steps; only four unique pill colours. The operator
can't visually distinguish COEFFECT from SUBSCRIPTIONS at a glance.

Per Mike, pair-debug 2026-05-26: "the original mock was different."

## Root cause

`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/badge.cljc`
deliberately maps both badges to the same `:magenta` token:

    :COEFFECT          :magenta
    ...
    :SUBSCRIPTIONS     :magenta

A comment at line 62-63 calls this "intentionally pull magenta-
family tokens" — but it contradicts (or was unaware of) the
original mock which used distinct colours.

## Fix

Reassign one of the two badges to a distinct token. The five pills
need five visually-distinct colours.

Worker picks one of the two:

- **Keep COEFFECT magenta; move SUBSCRIPTIONS** — to a different
  hue family. Candidates: `:orange` / `:yellow` / `:info` (cool
  blue distinct from HANDLER's blue) / a new theme token.
- **Keep SUBSCRIPTIONS magenta; move COEFFECT** — to a different
  hue family. Same candidates.

Default disposition: **move SUBSCRIPTIONS to `:orange`** (warm tone
distinct from the cool blue/green family; reads as "reactive trail"
distinct from COEFFECT's "input" identity). Worker may choose
otherwise based on visual cohesion testing.

Recover the ORIGINAL MOCK's colour assignment if recoverable —
worker checks the design references (potentially in
`tools/xray/design-reference/`).

Update the comment at badge.cljc:62-63 to reflect the new
assignment + WHY (visual distinguishability) rather than the
prior "intentionally same magenta" framing which the mock didn't
support.

## Acceptance

1. Five pipeline pill badges render in FIVE visually-distinct
   colours.
2. COEFFECT and SUBSCRIPTIONS no longer share a background colour.
3. Light + dark themes both render the new colour assignment
   correctly (via existing theme tokens).
4. Operator can distinguish all five steps at a glance from the
   pill colour alone (no reading of label text required).

## What does NOT change

- The pill chrome (rounded shape, 10px font, uppercase, white
  text)
- DISPATCH / HANDLER / VIEWS colours (unchanged)
- Pipeline step ordering
- Pipeline step semantics

## What DOES change

- `badge.cljc`'s `:COEFFECT` OR `:SUBSCRIPTIONS` token mapping
  reassigned to a non-magenta token
- The comment at lines 62-71 updated to reflect the new mapping

## References

- Pair-debug 2026-05-26 — Mike: "Coeffect pill and SUBSCRIPTIONS
  pill have almost the same colour. But original mock was
  different"
- Source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/badge.cljc`
- Reference assets directory: `tools/xray/design-reference/` —
  worker checks for the original mock
- Coordinates with: rf2-79ojx (CLJS palette — landed; this bead
  doesn't change the syntax palette, just the pipeline-pill
  semantic-colour mapping)
EOF
notes:
## Update — exact mock colours confirmed (pair-debug 2026-05-26)

Mike confirmed the original mock's exact colours:

- **COEFFECT: `rgb(168, 85, 247)` = `#a855f7`** — violet
- **SUBSCRIPTIONS: `rgb(236, 72, 153)` = `#ec4899`** — pink

These two hex values are ALREADY documented in `badge.cljc:33,40,45`
as the original mock's intent — the implementer chose to collapse
both onto the existing `:magenta` token to avoid adding a new
palette token (comment at lines 62-68):

> "the project's palette doesn't carry a separate pink hue and
> adding to it for this single use site would erode the palette's
> single-source-of-truth posture (per spec/022). The view
> differentiates them with their text label rather than a hue
> split."

Mike's call (pair-debug 2026-05-26) overrides that decision: the
visual distinction at a glance MATTERS more than palette
minimalism. Restore the mock's distinct hues.

## Updated fix (replaces the prior default disposition)

Add a new `:magenta-pink` theme token (or `:pink`) to the palette
holding `#ec4899` (and the dark-theme equivalent — worker picks
hue-matched dark variant or uses the same hex if it reads OK in
dark). Wire `:SUBSCRIPTIONS` to the new token.

COEFFECT continues to pull `:magenta`. Worker confirms the existing
`:magenta` token resolves to `#a855f7` (the COEFFECT mock value);
if it resolves to a different magenta shade, update the token to
match the mock OR add a `:violet` token for COEFFECT specifically.

Updated `badge.cljc` mapping:

    :COEFFECT          :magenta        ; #a855f7 violet
    :SUBSCRIPTIONS     :magenta-pink   ; #ec4899 pink (NEW token)

Update the comment block at badge.cljc:62-68 to reflect the new
mapping + WHY (visual distinguishability + mock restoration). Cite
this bead.

## Coordination with the palette single-source-of-truth posture

Adding `:magenta-pink` (one new token) doesn't erode the palette's
posture so long as:
- The token is justified by a real visual-distinction need (this
  bead documents it)
- It's used consistently across panels (no one-off; if some other
  panel needs pink in the future, this token serves it)

## Acceptance (refines the prior list)

1. New `:magenta-pink` (or `:pink`) theme token defined in light +
   dark theme palettes
2. Light theme: `:magenta-pink` resolves to `#ec4899` (or visually
   equivalent)
3. Dark theme: `:magenta-pink` resolves to a tonally appropriate
   pink (worker picks)
4. `:SUBSCRIPTIONS` badge maps to the new token
5. `:COEFFECT` badge maps to `:magenta` (confirmed `#a855f7` or
   updated to match)
6. Live verification: DOM probe shows COEFFECT bg `rgb(168, 85, 247)`
   and SUBSCRIPTIONS bg `rgb(236, 72, 153)` (or theme-equivalent
   in dark mode)
7. badge.cljc comment block updated to reflect the new mapping +
   the bead reference + the design rationale (mock restoration)
close_reason: Pipe pill colour split fixed — COEFFECT keeps :magenta (re-tuned to violet #a855f7); SUBSCRIPTIONS routes to new :magenta-pink (#ec4899). PR #2198.

title: Epoch panel: VIEWS hover treatment ('pink stripe') removed/regressed
description:
## Symptom

The Epoch panel's VIEWS step previously rendered a pink/stripe
mouseover affordance on the view name row — a visual cue that the
row was hoverable / interactive. That treatment has GONE — hovering
the view name shows no chrome.

Live (pair-debug 2026-05-26): hovering the `:testdeck.panel/counter-tab`
row in the VIEWS step body produces no hover treatment. Mike:
"The mouse over view name pink/stripe thing has gone".

Either:
- The hover treatment was REMOVED in a recent commit (regression)
- The hover treatment is conditioned on a flag / state that's
  currently off
- The CSS class / hover selector was renamed and the new selector

2. Treatment is theme-aware (light + dark).

title: Xray Machine panel: auto-fit chart viewport on mount + focused-machine change
description:
## Symptom

Every time the Machine panel renders the xyflow topology chart for a machine, the operator has to click the "zoom to fit" button manually to see the whole chart. Default zoom/pan after mount typically shows only a fragment of the topology — operator can't see the full state graph until they intervene.

This happens on:
- Initial mount of the panel
- Switching focus to a different machine
- Any re-render that resets the chart's viewport

Cumulative friction adds up across a debugging session — every focus switch costs one click + a moment of "where am I in this chart?" disorientation.

## Fix

Auto-fit the viewport when the chart renders for a new machine (or on initial mount).

xyflow's React Flow component exposes a `fitView` prop AND a `fitViewOptions` map. The widget already has a "zoom to fit" affordance (somewhere in `machine_canvas.cljs` — worker locates), which calls into xyflow's `fitView()` method. The fix is to wire that same call into the chart's lifecycle:

- On initial chart mount → call `fitView` once
- On focused-machine change → call `fitView` again after the new nodes/edges are committed

Implementation pattern (xyflow standard):

    [:> ReactFlow
     {:nodes              nodes
      :edges              edges
      :fit-view           true               ;; auto-fit on mount
      :fit-view-options   {:padding 0.2
                           :duration 0       ;; instant; no animation churn
                           :max-zoom 1.5}
      :on-init            on-init-callback   ;; can also call fitView()
                                              ;; here on re-init
      ...}]

For focused-machine changes (when the same React Flow component instance receives new nodes/edges), use a `useEffect`-equivalent in Reagent to call `fitView()` on the imperative API when the focused-machine-id changes.

## Don't disrupt the operator after they've manually zoomed

Once the operator pans/zooms, auto-fit shouldn't snap them back. Track "operator-has-interacted?" state:

- Reset to `false` on focused-machine change (new machine = new viewport)
- Set to `true` on first `on-move-end` / `on-zoom-end` / `on-pan-end` event from xyflow
- Auto-fit fires only when `operator-has-interacted? == false`

This makes auto-fit a "smart default that yields to the operator" rather than a constant disruption.

Alternative simpler version (if the interaction-tracking adds complexity): auto-fit only on FOCUSED-MACHINE CHANGE, not on every render. Operator's manual zoom persists within a focus session; switching machines resets.

Worker picks; the simpler version may be enough.

## Acceptance

1. Opening the Machine panel for the first time → chart auto-fits to viewport without operator clicking anything.
2. Focusing a different machine via the focused-machine selector → chart auto-fits to the new machine's topology.
3. Operator pans / zooms manually → their view persists across re-renders within the same focused machine (auto-fit doesn't snap them back). [optional — depends on which implementation route worker picks]
4. The existing manual "zoom to fit" button still works (operator can re-fit at any time).
5. Auto-fit's padding leaves visual room around the topology (≥ ~10-20% padding so nodes don't touch the chart edges).
6. No animation flicker on auto-fit (`duration: 0` or near-instant; the chart appears already-fitted, not zooming in from elsewhere).
7. Works for both small topologies (2-3 nodes) and large ones (10+ nodes) — auto-fit's max-zoom prevents tiny topologies from rendering at absurd zoom levels.

## What does NOT change

- The "zoom to fit" button (kept; operator can re-trigger any time)
- The xyflow chart's node/edge layout (elkjs)
- The chart's visual treatment (node colours, edge routing)
- The panel's outer chrome (rf2-3d987 layout already landed)

## What DOES change

- Chart's React Flow mount adds `fit-view` + `fit-view-options`
- May add `on-init` callback to trigger fit on re-init
- May add focused-machine-change effect to re-fit
- May add operator-interacted? state if implementing the smart-yield variant

## Out of scope

- Tracking per-machine fit-state (so re-focusing returns to the operator's last manual zoom) — likely more complexity than benefit; auto-fit on focus-change is fine
- Animated zoom transitions — keep instant; animation is operator-friendly only when they triggered the change
- "Zoom to selected node" affordance — separate feature

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: open Machine panel on http://localhost:8031/counter; confirm the chart doesn't auto-fit (operator must click).
2. Locate the existing "zoom to fit" button + its handler — likely calls xyflow's `fitView()` via the imperative API.
3. Check xyflow's `fit-view` + `fit-view-options` prop semantics (xyflow v12+ — worker confirms the running version).
4. Decide between the smart-yield variant (track operator interaction) and the simpler focus-change-only variant.
5. Test with multiple machines focus-switching back and forth — confirm fit happens on every switch.
6. Test with the panel's collapsible-chart affordance (rf2-3d987 issue #4) — collapsing then re-expanding shouldn't trigger an unwanted re-fit if the operator had manually zoomed within that session.
7. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Live observation: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Chart source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_canvas.cljs` (worker locates the React Flow mount + the existing zoom-to-fit handler)
- xyflow `fit-view` prop docs: https://reactflow.dev/api-reference/react-flow#fit-view
- Coordinates with: rf2-3d987 (Machine panel layout fixes — already landed)

title: Xray App-DB panel: remove hairline dividers between inspector cards (redundant with card chrome)
description:
## Symptom

In the App-DB panel, the inspector cards (each top-level mount + each reserved-area section) are visually separated by hairline divider lines drawn between adjacent sections. Now that each card carries its own chrome — `1px solid <border-default>` border, `4px` border-radius, `bg-1` background, header ribbon (rf2-63ie5 + rf2-okq7p) — the inter-card divider is redundant and visually noisy.

Operator sees: card-border + space + divider + space + card-border. The divider competes with the card borders for the eye's attention; the cards already self-separate via their chrome.

## Root cause

`section-shell` in `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs` renders a `border-top` divider on every section after the first:

    [:section {:data-testid testid
               :style       (cond-> {:padding "12px 12px 4px"}
                              (not first?)
                              (assoc :border-top
                                     (str "1px solid " (:border-subtle tokens))))}
     ...]

The divider was the inter-section separator when sections rendered FLAT (no per-section card chrome — the pre-rf2-63ie5 design). Post-rf2-63ie5 / rf2-okq7p, every section's body carries its own card border + radius; the section-shell's divider became double-chrome.

## Fix

Drop the `border-top` divider entirely. Each card's own border + the existing inter-card vertical gap (the `margin-bottom: 8px` the inspector card chrome adds) is enough visual separation.

Alternatively, if any section ISN'T wrapped in card chrome (the empty-state sections still use `empty-body` rather than an inspector, so they have no card border), the divider might still serve those. Two options:

- (a) **Drop the divider unconditionally.** Empty-state sections become slightly less visually distinct, but they're rare and labelled with their H3 — readable without a divider.
- (b) **Drop the divider only when the body is card-chromed.** `section-shell` gains a `:body-has-card?` opt (or detects from the body shape); when true, no divider. Empty-state sections still get the divider.

Worker picks; (a) is simpler and probably the right call (empty sections are infrequent; the H3 already labels them).

## Acceptance

1. App-DB panel: no hairline divider lines between adjacent cards. Verified live via DOM probe — no `border-top` on `<section>` elements inside `#rf-xray-tabpanel-app-db`.
2. Cards still read as visually distinct via their own card chrome (border + radius + background + bottom margin).
3. Empty-state sections (when present) still read cleanly — operator can tell them apart from neighbouring sections via the H3 label + vertical spacing.
4. Other panels that use `section-shell` (if any) audited — worker confirms the divider removal doesn't regress any other surface. If `section-shell` is App-DB-local (`defn-`), this is App-DB only.

## What does NOT change

- The card chrome itself (rf2-63ie5 + rf2-okq7p)
- The header+body card aesthetic
- The reserved-area section iteration / ordering
- Empty-state body rendering
- The H3 labels for empty-state sections
- Any testid

## What DOES change

- `section-shell` either drops the `border-top` conditional unconditionally OR gains a `:body-has-card?` flag and conditionally renders the divider
- Each caller of `section-shell` may need to pass the new flag (option b) — App-DB's `top-section`, `instance-section`, `instances-area`, `singleton-area`

## Coordination with current backlog

- rf2-63ie5 (inspector card chrome) — LANDED. This bead removes the redundant divider the chrome made obsolete.
- rf2-okq7p (header+body chrome) — LANDED. Same redundancy.

Land independently of the other open beads.

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Reproduce live: open App-DB panel on http://localhost:8031/counter; confirm the hairline divider between cards is visible.
2. Search for other consumers of `section-shell` — if any panels outside `app_db_diff_state` use it, confirm the divider removal doesn't regress them.
3. Pick (a) vs (b). (a) is simpler; (b) preserves divider for empty-state sections. Document the choice.
4. Test in both light + dark themes.

## References

- Live observation: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- `section-shell` source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_state.cljs:71`
- Card chrome: rf2-63ie5 (landed)
- Header+body chrome: rf2-okq7p (landed)

The fixture stamps `:rf.event/coeffects` on the `:rf.fx/do-fx` trace (line 455):

```clojure
{:id (+ id-base 3) :op-type :rf.fx :operation :rf.fx/do-fx
 :tags (assoc tag :rf.event/fx [[:db nil]]
                  :rf.event/db-present? true
                  :rf.event/coeffects {:now "2026-05-18T19:00:00Z"
                                       :local-storage {...}})}
```

But per rf2-9dk9y (2026-05 — `e4c1fbfd3 fix(xray): Handler panel — cofxs reach COEFFECTS, AFTER INTERCEPTORS shows ctx delta`) the substrate stamp moved OFF `:rf.fx/do-fx` and ONTO `:rf.event/run-end`, because do-fx never fires for handlers that return only `:db` and no `:fx`. The impl (`event-detail/user-coeffects`, line 535) reads from the cascade's `:handler` slot (= run-end trace).

Result: the gallery's `:story.xray.event/lens-with-coeffects` variant silently renders no COEFFECTS section — the absence-by-omission path triggers — defeating the variant's documented purpose ("Event lens with the §3 COEFFECTS section populated by two user-injected coeffects").

The fixture's own docstring still references the stale stamp location:

> "Stamps two user-injected coeffects (`:now` + `:local-storage`) onto
>  the `:rf.fx/do-fx` trace's `:tags :coeffects` slot"

## Cross-references

- The CLJS test helper `cascade-evs` in `event_detail_cljs_test.cljs` lines 102-106 already stamps on `:rf.event/run-end` correctly — gold standard for fixture shape.
- The impl's source comments (event_detail.cljs lines 60-65 — "Change 4 (rf2-9dk9y, supersedes rf2-jhhqt) :rf.event/run-end traces carry :rf.event/coeffects") confirm the contract.

## Fix

Move the `:rf.event/coeffects` slot off the `:rf.fx/do-fx` trace (id-base+3) onto the `:rf.event/run-end` trace (id-base+2). Update the fn docstring to match. Consider mirroring `cascade-evs`'s shape more directly so future contract changes land in one place.

Suggested patch (event_lens_with-coeffects-buffer):

```clojure
{:id (+ id-base 2) :op-type :rf.event :operation :rf.event/run-end
 :tags (assoc tag :rf.trace/phase :run-end :duration-ms 7
                  :rf.event/coeffects {:now "2026-05-18T19:00:00Z"
                                       :local-storage {...}})}
{:id (+ id-base 3) :op-type :rf.fx :operation :rf.fx/do-fx
 :tags (assoc tag :rf.event/fx [[:db nil]]
                  :rf.event/db-present? true)}
```

## Impact / urgency

LOW. Gallery-only. No production impact, no test impact (the test seed uses the correct stamp location independently). Just one variant in the story gallery that silently fails to demonstrate its feature. Worth a one-line fix to keep the gallery true.

## Acceptance

- Gallery variant `:story.xray.event/lens-with-coeffects` renders the COEFFECTS section with `:now` + `:local-storage` rows.
- Fixture docstring updated to reference `:rf.event/run-end` (rf2-9dk9y).

title: feat(xray): COEFFECTS row shape — two-line <id ↗> \\n + [<id>] <value> per spec/021 §2.2 + design-reference
description:
Audit rf2-ge2oe finding (outcome: impl drift).

## Current shape (event_detail.cljs `coeffect-row`, lines 540-568)

Single-line per coeffect:

```
:now ↗   "2026-05-18T19:00:00Z"
```

i.e. `<id-with-chip>   <value-via-edn-inspect>` on one row.

## Design / spec shape

**spec/021 §2.2 dense-case mockup** (lines 295-300):

```
②  COEFFECTS
 │    :now ↗
 │      + [:now]      #inst "2026-05-23T12:30:05.123Z"
 │    :session ↗
 │      + [:session]  {:user-id 42, :token "..."}
```

**design-reference `xray_devtools_reference.cljs` §2 COEFFECTS** (lines 429-449):

Two-line shape per coeffect:
- Line 1: `<id> [external-link]` (link styling, accent color)
- Line 2: `+ [<id>] <value>` — `+` glyph in `--devtools-success` green; `[<id>]` in `--devtools-text-muted`; value in `--devtools-success` green

Indentation: line 2 sits 21px (or one step) right of line 1.

## Drift

The current impl collapses the two lines into one, drops the `+` glyph, and drops the `[<id>]` repetition. The single-line is more compact but loses three signal-carrying pieces of the design idiom:

1. The `+` glyph that links COEFFECTS visually to APP-DB CHANGES (`+ [path] value`). The two sections share an "added to ctx" reading; the glyph teaches it.
2. The `[<id>]` path-form repetition that mirrors the diff line shape used in APP-DB CHANGES, AFTER INTERCEPTORS ctx-delta, and FLOWS write-paths.
3. The visual breathing room of the two-line layout (id on its own line, value indented under it), which scales gracefully to multi-line / nested values where the current single-line crams the value next to the id.

## Impact / urgency

LOW. The current rendering is FUNCTIONAL — all conditional branches work (has-coeffects / no-coeffects / qualified-keyword / empty-map / nil-handler) and tests pass. The drift is purely visual: the section reads as a flat KV table instead of the diff-idiom block the spec calls for. Decided to file as a bug rather than spec-update because:

- The spec mockup + design-reference agree (two-line, `+ [path]` shape)
- The two-line shape carries information the single-line doesn't
- Pre-alpha posture: align the impl with the design rather than retrofit the spec to match a simpler impl

## Notes

- The two-line shape needs a `[<id-as-vector>]` rendering — `:now` → `[:now]`. That's a trivial `(pr-str [id])` or `(str "[" (pr-str id) "]")`. The design pre-encodes the id in vector brackets to signal "path under ctx where this value lives".
- The chip (click-to-source) belongs on the id-row (line 1), as in the current impl. Position unchanged.
- Tests would need to assert on a second per-coeffect element (e.g. `rf-xray-event-detail-coeffect-add-row-<suffix>`).
- Sibling sections (APP-DB CHANGES, AFTER INTERCEPTORS ctx-delta) already use the `+/~/-` glyph + `[path] value` idiom via `op->glyph` / `ctx-delta-row`. Reusing those primitives (or at least their style tokens — `:green` for `+`, `:text-tertiary` for `[<path>]`) keeps the visual rhythm consistent.

## Acceptance

- COEFFECTS section renders id+chip on line 1 and `+ [<id>] <value>` on line 2 per design-reference + spec/021 §2.2 lines 295-300.
- All existing test coverage continues to pass (id-row testids unchanged).
- Add tests asserting the second per-row line presence + correct testid suffix.

## Out of scope

- The `:rf.event/coeffects` stamp location (already correctly stamped on `:rf.event/run-end` per rf2-9dk9y).
- The empty-state behaviour (already correct — absence by omission).

title: Xray data-display → edn-inspector rename (coordinated)
description:
## Why

The widget at `views/data_display.cljs` is currently named `data-display`. Better name: `edn-inspector`.

Rationale (discussed pair-debug 2026-05-26):

- **"Inspector"** is the dominant ecosystem-wide name for this widget class (Chrome devtools "object inspector", cljs-devtools, vscode debug "variables" panel). CLJS programmers recognise it immediately as "the thing that shows you a value with click-to-expand". Anchors to a known mental model.
- **"EDN"** signals the data format — the widget knows about keywords, namespaced keywords, sets, records, sentinels. Not a generic JSON viewer.
- **"Display"** (current) is passive — connotes a non-interactive readout. The widget is interactive (expand/collapse, popup, diff mode, sticky state).

Alternatives weighed and rejected:
- `edn-viewer` — "viewer" reads passive
- `inspector` (no prefix) — collides with React/DOM "inspectors"; loses CLJS specificity
- `value-inspector` — generic, loses CLJS specificity

Decision: `edn-inspector`.

## Scope

Coordinated rename across:

### Namespace rename
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs` → `views/edn_inspector.cljs`
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display_popup.cljs` → `views/edn_inspector_popup.cljs`
- `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display_protocol.cljs` → `views/edn_inspector_protocol.cljs`
- Namespace declarations updated accordingly: `day8.re-frame2-xray.views.edn-inspector` etc.

### Public symbols
- `data-display` → `edn-inspector` (the widget fn)
- `data-display-diff` → `edn-inspector-diff` (diff convenience)
- `mini` → unchanged (already a generic name)
- `popup-affordance-button` → unchanged (internal)
- `IXrayDataDisplay` protocol → `IXrayEdnInspector`

### Event ids (re-frame event keywords)
- `:rf.xray.data-display/toggle-node` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/toggle-node`
- `:rf.xray.data-display/set-node` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/set-node`
- `:rf.xray.data-display/reset-expansion` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/reset-expansion`
- `:rf.xray.data-display-popup/open` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector-popup/open`
- `:rf.xray.data-display-popup/close` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector-popup/close`
- `:rf.xray.data-display-popup/close-top` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector-popup/close-top`
- `:rf.xray.data-display-popup/close-all` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector-popup/close-all`

### Sub ids
- `:rf.xray.data-display/expansion` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector/expansion`
- `:rf.xray.data-display-popup/stack` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector-popup/stack`
- `:rf.xray.data-display-popup/entries` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector-popup/entries`
- `:rf.xray.data-display-popup/open?` → `:rf.xray.edn-inspector-popup/open?`

### App-db slot keys
- `:rf.xray.data-display/expansion` slot — renamed (operator's localStorage / persisted state cleared at upgrade time; pre-alpha, no migration needed)
- Same for the popup stack / entries slots

### Testid prefixes
- `rf-xray-data-display-` → `rf-xray-edn-inspector-`
- `rf-xray-data-display-popup-*` → `rf-xray-edn-inspector-popup-*`
- All `-toggle`, `-body`, `-affordance` suffix variants follow

### Consumer panels
Every panel that requires or calls the widget — App-DB, Handler, Trace, Machines, Routes, Issues, Views, Static panels, etc. — updates:
- the `:require` alias (likely `[... :as dd]` → `[... :as ei]`)
- the call-site `[dd/data-display ...]` → `[ei/edn-inspector ...]`
- any dispatched events / subscriptions on the renamed ids

### Tests
Every test file referencing `data-display` updates — by ns, by symbol, by event id, by testid.

### Docs / comments
Comments inside source files referencing `data-display` update for consistency.

## Pre-alpha posture

No back-compat shim, no alias namespace, no event-id alias map. Clean cut. The old names disappear entirely; everything moves to the new name in one coordinated PR.

`/spec/` references (if any) update in the same PR.

## Acceptance

1. All renames per the scope above. No `data-display` string remaining in `tools/xray/`, `implementation/`, `tools/`, `examples/`, `spec/`. Verified via grep across the corpus.
2. `bd remember` history / closed-bead references stay as-is (those are historical artefacts; renaming them retroactively muddles the audit trail).
3. Test suite green after rename.
4. Every panel still renders correctly — visual smoke check.
5. Popup still works (depends on rf2-popup-fix bead being done first OR concurrently; coordinate).
6. Expansion state persistence still works (rf2-pvsxs's slot keys are renamed; the app-db slot at the new name starts empty; that's fine pre-alpha).

## What does NOT change

- The widget's behaviour
- Public API shapes (only names change)
- Theme tokens
- Spec 015 sentinel handling
- The form-2 mount pattern
- The reg-view registration mechanism

## What DOES change

- Every file in the scope above is touched
- The widget's namespace path
- Public symbols, event ids, sub ids, app-db slot keys, testids
- Consumer panel call-sites
- Tests

## Out of scope

- Re-organising the widget's internal structure
- Behaviour changes (those land in their own beads — card chrome, alignment, triangle size, popup fix)
- Changing what gets exported / hidden
- Adding new features

## Worker — conduct your own review before starting

1. Grep the corpus for every occurrence of `data-display`, `data_display`, `dataDisplay`. Categorise by file type (source / test / spec / docs). Pin the count.
2. Decide rename strategy — single PR with mechanical sed-style replacement, or two-phase (introduce the new name, sweep call sites, retire the old). Pre-alpha posture favours single PR.
3. Identify any external consumers that might reference the names (the npm package surface, MCP tools, the re-frame2-pair skill, the re-frame2-xray skill, plugin packages). List them.
4. Verify the rename doesn't collide with anything else named `edn-inspector` already in the codebase.
5. Coordinate with the other 4 active beads (card-chrome, popup-fix, triangle-size, alignment) — likely lands either before or after them; landing concurrently means massive merge conflict. Worker picks order.
6. Report findings before pushing.

## References

- Naming discussion: pair-debug session 2026-05-26
- Current widget: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display.cljs`
- Current popup: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display_popup.cljs`
- Current protocol: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display_protocol.cljs`
- Mental-model anchor: feedback memory `feedback_skill_anchor_to_known_mental_models`

title: docs(audit-tooling): calibrate ai/link-sweep-v2.py to MkDocs slug rules (not GitHub)
description:
Discovered by #2158 worker (rf2-69nh9) — only 3 of 5 anchor links the rf2-oavap README sweep flagged in migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md were genuine defects. The other 2 were already correct under the project's actual slug gate.

## Root cause

The audit script at `ai/link-sweep-v2.py` was calibrated for **GitHub-rendered** Markdown slug rules. This repo publishes via **MkDocs** using `pymdownx.slugs.slugify`. Two differences matter:

1. **Placeholder text in `<...>`**: GitHub keeps the literal token (e.g., `<name>` survives as 'name' in the slug). MkDocs strips both the brackets AND the text between them. So `### M-38. CLJS namespace rename — re-frame.substrate.<name> -> re-frame.adapter.<name>` slugifies differently:
   - GitHub slug: `m-38-cljs-namespace-rename--re-framesubstratename--re-frameadaptername`
   - MkDocs slug: `m-38-cljs-namespace-rename--re-framesubstrate--re-frameadapter`
2. **Duplicate-header disambiguation**: GitHub uses `-N` (hyphen). MkDocs uses `_N` (underscore). So two `### Errors` headings produce `#errors` + `#errors-1` on GitHub vs `#errors` + `#errors_1` on MkDocs.

## Fix

Either:
- (a) **Use the project's own gate as the source of truth.** `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` embeds `pymdownx.slugs.slugify` — the audit script should call this directly OR import the same slugifier, not roll its own.
- (b) **Document the slug-rule assumption explicitly.** If the audit script must stay self-contained, add a top-of-file comment + a CLI flag `--slugifier {github,mkdocs}` (default mkdocs since that's the project's renderer).

(a) is the elegant answer — reuse the existing slugifier so the audit and the gate agree by construction.

## Scope

- `ai/link-sweep-v2.py` (the audit script) — local-only, gitignored. If the script gets promoted from `ai/` to `scripts/` per the rf2-oavap close note, this calibration must land first.
- No spec/impl change. No tests required beyond the gate it would replace.

## Out of scope

- Re-running the rf2-oavap sweep — only do this if Mike wants a second pass. The 5 derived beads already filed cover the genuine defects (verified by checking against the actual gate).

Discovered by: rf2-69nh9 PR #2158 worker.

title: audit: sweep all READMEs for stale/broken links
description:
**Scope:** Every `README.md` in the repo (88 files; excludes `node_modules/`, `.shadow-cljs/`, generated `site/`). Check every link in every README and identify any that:

1. Point to a moved/renamed file (e.g., post-#2138 `tools/playground/` → `docs/tools/playground/`; post-#2145 `spec/013-Trace-Bus.md` → `013-Trace-Consumer.md`; the data-display widget rename in tools/xray/).
2. Point to a deleted file (e.g., `data_display/render.cljs` deleted in #2151; `theme/data_inspector.cljs` deleted in #2151; `trace_bus.cljc` deleted in #2145).
3. Point to a broken external URL (HTTP 404 / domain expired) — best-effort; rely on `curl -sIL` rather than perfect coverage.
4. Anchor-fragment (`#section`) that no longer exists in the linked file.

## Method

```bash
# Inventory
find . -name 'README.md' -not -path './node_modules/*' -not -path './site/*' -not -path './.shadow-cljs/*'

# Per file: extract markdown links
# Internal: validate via Test-Path / stat against the resolved target
# External: curl -sIL --max-time 5 — flag non-2xx/3xx
# Anchors: grep ^# headers in target file; slugify; compare
```

Slug check tooling already exists at `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` — runs over mkdocs `docs/` and `spec/` for the published doc set, but does NOT cover READMEs (only tracked-in-nav markdown). This bead specifically extends coverage to **every README**.

## Deliverables

- **One bead per stale link cluster.** Group by README file (one README → one bead unless its issues are unrelated). Title shape: `docs(README): fix broken/stale links in <path>/README.md`. Priority P3 unless the link is on a high-traffic README (repo-root, `tools/README.md`, `implementation/README.md`) — those get P2.
- **Summary in this bead's notes.** Total READMEs scanned, links found, links broken, beads filed.

## Out of scope

- Links inside `docs/` (already covered by `check_doc_slugs.py` + mkdocs --strict).
- Links inside committed spec docs other than their README.
- Fix the links here — that's the derived beads' job; this bead just inventories.
- ai/findings/ READMEs (gitignored tree).

## Why now

The last 24h burst included 4 known file-move/delete operations (#2138 playground relocate; #2145 trace_bus retire; #2151 data-display legacy delete; pair-mcp dedup.cljs additions). Each is a potential README-link-rot vector. Plus the project's overall reorganisation pace (Mayor Method has produced ~150 PRs in the past month) means stale link debt has accumulated.

Discovered from Mike directive 2026-05-25.

title: design(xray): default IXrayDataDisplay formatters for common CLJS types (rf2-0qrcr follow-on)
description:
Phase 7 of rf2-oqa60 (#2148) shipped the IXrayDataDisplay protocol with a worked Money deftype example in spec/021 §10.0.6. The protocol is dispatchable but ZERO built-in default implementations ship.

Question for Mike: should the framework provide opinionated defaults for common types that benefit from custom formatting?

Candidates:
- **uuid?** — currently renders as the full 36-char string; could compact to '…last8' on collapse, full on expand
- **inst?** (Date / js/Date) — currently renders as ISO string; could format as relative-time ('3 min ago') with hover-for-ISO, or just a friendlier format
- **uri?** / java.net.URL — render as a clickable link in the widget chrome
- **bigint?** / **ratio?** — currently render as raw repr; could format with thousands separators
- **byte arrays / blobs** — show byte count + first few bytes rather than the raw seq

Trade-off: each default formatter is a small piece of opinionated UI baked into the widget. Mike's stance applies — if defaults serve elegance/clarity for common cases, ship them; if they bloat the widget for marginal gain, skip. Pre-alpha posture (no back-compat) means we can add and remove freely.

Three valid resolutions:
- (a) Ship a curated default set (uuid + inst + uri are the strong cases)
- (b) Ship empty defaults; let downstream apps register their own via IXrayDataDisplay
- (c) Ship only inst (the most clearly broken raw repr) and defer the rest

Surface for Mike's pick during a quiet moment. Not blocking anything.

References:
- rf2-0qrcr #2148 (phase 7 IXrayDataDisplay protocol landing)
- spec/021 §10.0.6 (protocol contract + Money example)
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/views/data_display_protocol.cljs
notes: PR #2168 merged (uuid+inst shipped; uri deferred — domain types use the IXrayDataDisplay seam)

title: fix(spec/Tool-Pair): trace-buffer signature drift — line 382 still shows old opts-only form; spec/009 + impl have frame-id-required form
description:
## Spec drift

Worker on rf2-8uwce (#2139) spotted: spec/Tool-Pair.md:382 still describes `(rf/trace-buffer opts)` as a registry-wide opts-only form. Spec/009 (load-bearing for trace surface) and the core impl in #2139 have the new `(rf/trace-buffer frame-id)` / `(rf/trace-buffer frame-id opts)` shape (frame-id required, cascade bundles by default, `:flat` opt-in).

## Fix

Update spec/Tool-Pair.md:382 (and any other site that references the old signature in that doc) to match the spec/009 + impl shape:

`(rf/trace-buffer frame-id)` — returns cascade bundles for frame-id  
`(rf/trace-buffer frame-id {:flat true})` — returns raw trace events for frame-id  
`(rf/clear-trace-buffer! frame-id)` — clears the named frame's ring  

The frame-id is required (no registry-wide form). Cross-frame consumers iterate frame-ids + merge by `:dispatch-id`.

## Hot-zone

spec/Tool-Pair.md is hot-zone (sequential, single worker). No other worker is on it right now.

## Acceptance

- spec/Tool-Pair.md describes the new signature only
- mkdocs build --strict clean
- python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py --verbose clean
- No drift between spec/Tool-Pair, spec/009, and the impl

## Related

- **#2139** (rf2-8uwce) — core impl that surfaced the drift
- **#2135** (rf2-g1b2m) — spec/009 landing of the new signature
- Worker's PR body for #2139 documented the gap deliberately (didn't patch mid-PR to keep scope tight)

Other 5 trace-buffer hits in the file already aligned with new signature.

title: chore(playground): relocate tools/playground → docs/tools/playground — boundary matches actual audience (docs build pipeline)
description:
## Why

`tools/playground/` produces artefacts (playground.js, playground.css, playground-rf2.js) that ONLY ship into `docs/cljs/` and are consumed exclusively by mkdocs. It's docs build infrastructure, not a first-class tool that other consumers use. The current location under `tools/` implies parity with `tools/xray/`, `tools/story/`, `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/`, `tools/machines-viz/` — but those are dev-time inspectors / framework instrumentation that operate against running re-frame2 apps. Playground operates against markdown pages. Different audience, different lifecycle.

Moving it under `docs/` aligns directory scope with audience scope.

Inventory of current consumers (verified via `git grep`, excluding the beads DB):

- `docs/cljs/index.md` — 87 plain `cljs` cells (Scittle-eval)
- `docs/guide/interactive-counter.md` — 5 `cljs-rf2` cells (live re-frame2 components)
- `docs/guide/interactive-tutorials.md` — references playground in prose
- Built outputs land in `docs/cljs/` (already)

Total surface served: 2 docs pages + 92 cells. Pure docs concern.

## Where

Recommended destination: `docs/tools/playground/` (mirrors the operator's mental model from session 2026-05-25). Alternative: `docs/playground/` (simpler, no new `docs/tools/` subdir). Worker picks.

## What changes

File relocation under git's rename detection (preserves history):

- `tools/playground/{src,sci,scripts,test,README.md,package.json,package-lock.json}` → `docs/tools/playground/...`

References to update (`git grep -l "tools/playground"` minus beads DB):

- `.gitattributes` — line-ending / merge-strategy rules
- `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` — CI changed-surface attribution
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` — CI build job that runs `npm run build` against playground
- `TESTING.md` — testing matrix documentation
- `docs/guide/interactive-tutorials.md` — prose reference
- `mkdocs.yml` — mkdocs config
- Internal cross-references within the moved tree (`sci/scripts/copy-bundle.mjs`, `sci/shadow-cljs.edn`, `scripts/copy-css.mjs`, `src/playground.mjs`, `test/smoke.test.mjs`) — relative paths likely fine but verify

Build outputs already in `docs/cljs/` — no change there; the move is source-side only.

## What does NOT change

- Build commands (`npm --prefix <path> run build`) — only the path changes
- Output artefacts (`docs/cljs/playground.js` + `playground.css` + `playground-rf2.js`)
- The cells in `docs/cljs/index.md` and `docs/guide/interactive-counter.md` — they reference the OUTPUT via mkdocs, not the source
- Public API surface (the `cljs` and `cljs-rf2` fence kinds and their semantics)

## Acceptance

1. `git log --follow docs/tools/playground/README.md` shows the file's history from before the move (rename preserved)
2. `npm --prefix docs/tools/playground run build` succeeds; outputs land in `docs/cljs/` unchanged
3. mkdocs build is clean; cells in `docs/cljs/index.md` and `docs/guide/interactive-counter.md` render and execute identically
4. CI workflow (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) passes on the renamed path
5. `git grep -l "tools/playground"` returns zero hits outside `.beads/issues.jsonl` (historical bead text — never rewritten)

## Risks / things to look out for

- **Symlinks / hardlinks** — if any consumer references via absolute path or symlink, will break silently. Inventory above suggests no such case but worth a final `git grep` after the move.
- **CI cache keys** — `.github/workflows/test.yml` may key npm cache on the old path; new path will cache-miss on first run, fine after.
- **Operator muscle memory** — anyone with the old path memorized needs to update. Cheap to absorb.

## References

- Session that surfaced this: pair-debug 2026-05-25 — operator inspected `tools/playground/`, noted it serves only docs (2 pages, 92 cells), suggested move
- Existing precedent: `tools/causa/` was already removed (different reason — rename residue) but established that `tools/` is for runtime/dev-tier code, not docs-build infrastructure
- Related: `docs/scripts/` already exists for docs-side scripting; `docs/tools/` would be a sibling category

title: feat(scripts): mayor checkout pre-commit hook refuses commits touching worker-tracked surfaces (worker boundary defence-in-depth)
description:
## Discovery context

Surfaced during rf2-oswhk (#2136) post-mortem (worker acb252dc, 2026-05-25): an initial commit attempt via PowerShell landed on the mayor checkout's local main because PowerShell's `cwd` defaults to the project's implementation directory rather than tracking a `cd` from another tool call. Worker noticed + recovered (reset mayor back to origin/main; re-committed via Bash in the worker). The bogus commit only carried a bd `--claim` flip — no source/test/spec damage — but it COULD have carried real worker-tracked source changes.

## Gap

`scripts/assert-worker-worktree.ps1` catches EDIT attempts (worker scripts gate edits on `WORKTREE_ROOT`). It does NOT catch COMMIT attempts. A worker that bypasses the edit guard via a separate code path (PowerShell cwd leak, Bash `pwd` shifting between tool calls, etc.) can write a commit into the mayor checkout's main branch.

## Proposed fix

Install a pre-commit hook on the mayor checkout (`C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2/.git/hooks/pre-commit`) that refuses commits whose source diff touches worker-tracked surfaces. The hook would:

1. Detect mayor checkout via path comparison (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel == C:\Users\miket\code\re-frame2`)
2. Inspect the staged diff (`git diff --cached --name-only`)
3. Allow files in mayor-permitted zones (`.beads/issues.jsonl` for closures, `ai/` for dashboard, no others)
4. Refuse any commit touching `implementation/`, `tools/`, `spec/`, `docs/`, `examples/`, `skills/`, `scripts/`, `migration/` — these are worker-tracked surfaces
5. Print clear error: "This is the mayor checkout. Commits touching <files> must originate from a worker worktree."

## Install

Extend `scripts/install-git-hooks.ps1` + `scripts/install-git-hooks.sh` to install the pre-commit hook alongside the existing post-merge hook (rf2-6jj3r, #2113).

## Acceptance

- Attempting to commit a source-file change in the mayor checkout fails with the descriptive error
- bd-closure commits in the mayor still work (`.beads/issues.jsonl` is in the permitted zone)
- ai/dashboard.md writes are local-only (never committed; if attempted, hook refuses but with a softer 'this is local-only, did you mean to gitignore-respect?' message)
- Worker worktrees are unaffected (hook only activates when toplevel == mayor checkout path)

## Related

- **Discovery**: rf2-oswhk (#2136) worker acb252dc near-mishap, 2026-05-25
- **rf2-6jj3r (#2113)** — existing post-merge stale-binary hook pattern + installer
- `scripts/assert-worker-worktree.ps1` — the edit-time guard this complements
- [[feedback-mayor-orchestrate-no-code]] memory — the discipline this enforces in tooling
notes: PR #2137 open. Hook + library + tests + README + installer extensions + docs note all landed. 10/10 smoke tests pass.
close_reason: #2137 — POSIX-sh pre-commit hook + testable library (10/10 smoke pass) + cross-platform installers (.sh + .ps1) + marker file at <git-common-dir>/mayor-marker (workers' per-worktree git-dirs leave marker absent → hook no-ops; verified end-to-end); allow-list policy (only .beads/issues.jsonl + root MEMORY.md permitted); per-hook marker pairs for idempotent install. Closes the worker-near-mishap gap from rf2-oswhk #2136.

title: fix(machines-viz): chart doesn't auto-fit to content on initial mount — fitView runs on empty layout-state, never re-fires when positions arrive
description:
## Symptom

Every time the operator enters a Machine tab (or hot-reloads, or navigates back), the topology renders at an arbitrary zoom/pan — usually too small to see, or off-screen. The operator must manually click the "fit to size" control to scale the chart to fit. Repro: load http://localhost:8031/machine in step-deck — chart appears off-screen / tiny; user clicks fit-to-size to make it readable.

Discovered in pair-debug 2026-05-25 — recurring friction every time the chart re-mounts.

## Root cause

`chart.cljs:746` already passes `:fitView true` + `:fitViewOptions #js {:padding 0.1}` to <ReactFlow>. So xyflow IS asked to auto-fit. The fit fires once on initial mount — BUT mount happens BEFORE ELK's async `compute-layout!` resolves.

The component's `layout-state` atom starts at `{:positions {} :edge-points {}}` (chart.cljs:451). xyflow renders every node at its default `:position {:x 0 :y 0}` because `(get positions (:id n) {:x 0 :y 0})` falls through. xyflow then runs fitView on a set of nodes all clustered at (0,0) → fits to a degenerate point near the origin.

When ELK's promise resolves (a few hundred ms later), `(reset! layout-state result)` populates real positions, the nodes move to their ELK-computed coords — but xyflow's already used its one-shot fitView. The viewport never re-fits, leaving the new chart content positioned outside the visible viewport.

## Fix

Call `fitView()` programmatically after the FIRST positions arrive (and ideally after any subsequent layout recompute that significantly changes the chart extent).

Two implementation paths:

### A. Hook fitView into the layout-state's async settle

In `chart.cljs`'s MachineChart, after `(reset! layout-state result)` succeeds, get a reference to the xyflow instance (via React-Flow's `useReactFlow` hook — Reagent-side wrap) and call `(.fitView instance #js {:padding 0.1})`. Single explicit call right after the data arrives.

### B. Track "fit needed" state + auto-fit on next render

Add a small atom `(r/atom :pending-fit)`. On mount → `:pending-fit`. After `layout-state` first becomes non-empty → flip to `:fit-now`. On the render where `:fit-now`, call the xyflow instance's `.fitView()` and flip to `:fitted`. Survives multiple re-renders during the same machine-id view.

A is simpler; B is more defensive against multi-render or layout re-trigger cases.

## Edge cases to handle

- Multiple compute-layout! cycles (e.g. user toggles direction, or hot-reload triggers a re-layout) — should re-fit on each significant extent change, not only the first
- Operator has manually zoomed/panned — DO NOT re-fit on every layout re-compute (would clobber user's view). Re-fit only on first arrival or on explicit user request (the fit button stays as the manual escape hatch)
- Inspector mode / Xray's machine inspector may have specific viewport requirements — verify the fix plays nicely with the chart's host (machine_canvas / machine_inspector / topology_view)

## Acceptance

Loading a Machine tab → the chart appears at the correct zoom/pan with the topology fully visible inside the canvas, no operator action required. Tested with: `:ws/connection` (compound), any flat machine, and at least one parallel machine.

## References

- Bug source: `chart.cljs:746` (fitView declared) + `chart.cljs:451` (empty layout-state on mount) + `chart.cljs:484` (compute-layout! async settle)
- xyflow v12 API: `useReactFlow().fitView({padding, includeHiddenNodes})` — programmatic re-fit
- Predecessors: rf2-xh1lm (#2126 xyflow v12 parentId), rf2-shv82 (#2129 Handle-based edge routing) — both addressed structural correctness; this is operator-ergonomics
- Discovery: pair-debug 2026-05-25 — recurring friction on every Machine-tab entry
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2132 (auto-fit chart on initial layout settle, Path A onInit-stash). Gates: cljs 4446/0, browser 122/0, kondo clean. PR mergeable; awaiting CI / review.
close_reason: #2132 — Path A via :onInit capture + fit-state atom (key-gated to fire once per layout-cycle) + rAF-deferred fitView; symmetric :onInit branch handles cached-settle race; layout-error skips fit (banner paints); test seam invoke-fit-view! mirrors invoke-elk-layout! (rf2-4lyvh); +spec/API.md +auto_fit_view tests

title: feat(re-frame2-pair-mcp): eval-cljs :await true — server awaits Promise-returning forms before serializing, eliminates the js/window mailbox dance
description:
## Friction

eval-cljs captures the synchronous return value of the form and pr-str's it. When the form returns a JS Promise (any async work — `.layout()`, `fetch`, `async` fns, anything chained with `.then`), the synchronous return IS the Promise object. pr-str produces `"#object[Promise [object Promise]]"` — a string saying "I'm a Promise" with no access to the eventually-resolved value.

Hit this in pair-debug 2026-05-25 while probing ELK's actual layout output. I wanted:

    (-> (.layout instance elk-input)
        (.then (fn [result] (extract-edges result))))

The `(-> ...)` evaluates to a Promise with `.then` chained. eval-cljs grabs that Promise, pr-strs it, returns the string. The `.then` callback eventually fires in the browser, but eval-cljs already returned — the result is lost.

## Workaround required today — JS-window mailbox

Two round-trips:

    ;; Call 1 — kick off, stash on a global, return a sentinel
    (set! (.-__elkProbe__ js/window) "pending")
    (-> (.layout instance elk-input)
        (.then (fn [result]
                 (set! (.-__elkProbe__ js/window) (transform result))
                 :resolved)))
    "kicked off"

    ;; Call 2 — read the mailbox
    (let [r (.-__elkProbe__ js/window)]
      (if (string? r) {:status r} {:status :resolved :data r}))

Plus polling if the work is slow (re-query Call 2 every N ms until status changes). Pollutes `js/window` with debug globals. Easy to forget the initial "pending" sentinel, making timeout-vs-still-running ambiguous.

## Proposed fix — `:await true` arg

Opt-in (not default) await-aware mode on eval-cljs:

    {:form "(-> (.layout instance input) (.then transform))"
     :await true
     :timeout-ms 5000}

Server-side behaviour when `:await true`:

1. Evaluate the form; capture the synchronous return value
2. If the return value is a thenable (any object with `.then`), await it (with the configured timeout)
3. pr-str and return the resolved value as `:value`
4. On rejection, return `{:ok? false :reason :rf.error/eval-cljs-rejected :rejection <pr-str of rejection>}`
5. On timeout, return `{:ok? false :reason :rf.error/eval-cljs-timeout :timeout-ms n}`
6. If the return value is NOT thenable, behave exactly as today (return the value directly)

Default `:await false` preserves current semantics — callers who DO want the Promise object back unchanged still get it.

## Why opt-in (not always-on)

- Backward compatibility: existing callers that pass-through Promises get the same string-ified shape
- Some forms intentionally return Promise objects (handing them off to other code); awaiting would change semantics
- Timeout policy is caller-controlled rather than implicit

## Acceptance

This single-call form succeeds end-to-end:

    {:form "(-> (js/Promise.resolve {:hello \"world\"}) (.then identity))"
     :await true}
    → {:ok? true :value {:hello "world"}}

And a rejecting form surfaces structured:

    {:form "(js/Promise.reject (ex-info \"nope\" {}))"
     :await true}
    → {:ok? false :reason :rf.error/eval-cljs-rejected :rejection "..."}

And a hung form respects timeout:

    {:form "(js/Promise. (fn [_ _]))"  ;; never resolves
     :await true :timeout-ms 500}
    → {:ok? false :reason :rf.error/eval-cljs-timeout :timeout-ms 500}

## Why this is worth shipping

Async work is unavoidable in browser-side probing — DOM operations (waiting for layout), IndexedDB queries, fetch calls, elkjs / d3 layouts, any third-party JS library that returns Promises. Without `:await`, every such probe needs the two-call mailbox dance and the operator-side polling that goes with it. With `:await`, the probe is a single call.

Bonus: subsequent rf2-fb4hn-style observability features (pre-attach event explainers, etc.) can themselves use Promise-based browser-side helpers without the mailbox tax.

## References

- Source: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/eval_cljs.cljs
- Cited friction: pair-debug 2026-05-25 — ELK probe needed two round-trips + a `js/window.__elkProbe__` global to capture an async result the form already had in hand

title: fix(xray): AfterRingsOverlay reg-view root is non-DOM (component fn) — wrap body in :div so Spec 006 source-coord annotation can stamp
description:
## Symptom

After #2123 (rf2-m4xz1) converted \`AfterRingsOverlay\` from a plain Reagent fn to \`rf/reg-view\`, a new console warning fires:

\`[re-frame] reg-view :day8.re-frame2-xray.panels.machine-after-rings/AfterRingsOverlay — root element is #object[day8$re_frame2_machines_viz$chart$overlays$after_rings$AfterRingsOverlay]; data-rf2-source-coord skipped (Spec 006 §Source-coord annotation: pair tools fall back to :rf/id for non-DOM roots).\`

## Diagnosis

The xray view at \`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/machine_after_rings.cljs\` is a thin wrapper that renders the machines-viz overlay:

    (rf/reg-view AfterRingsOverlay
      [& _opts]
      [machines-viz.chart.overlays.after-rings/AfterRingsOverlay ...])

The root is another component function, not a hiccup vector with a DOM element. Per Spec 006 §Source-coord annotation: the source-coord stamping system requires a DOM hiccup root to attach \`data-rf2-source-coord\`. With a component-fn root, it falls back to \`:rf/id\` (functional, but loses the source-coord click-to-source link) and warns once.

## Fix

Wrap the body in a \`:div\` (or other DOM element) so the reg-view's root is a DOM hiccup vector:

    (rf/reg-view AfterRingsOverlay
      [& _opts]
      [:div.xray-after-rings-overlay  ;; or similar — match neighbouring class conventions
       [machines-viz.chart.overlays.after-rings/AfterRingsOverlay ...]])

## Audit

Grep \`tools/xray/src/.../panels/\` for any other \`reg-view\` whose body is \`[some-fn ...]\` rather than \`[:dom-element ...]\` — apply the same wrap-in-:div fix in the same PR.

## Spec note

Per [[feedback-xray-specs-kept-current]]: \`tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md\` likely needs a note that overlay views must have a DOM root for source-coord annotation, OR \`spec/006\` already says this and the xray spec just needs to point at it. Worker decides.

## Related

- **#2123** (rf2-m4xz1) — the conversion that exposed this
- **Spec 006** §Source-coord annotation — the contract for \`data-rf2-source-coord\`
notes: PR #2125 open. Worker pushed branch worker/after-rings-dom-root-rf2-fkpuv with the fix + audit + spec touch + tests. All gates green.

title: feat(re-frame2-pair-mcp): tail-build response should carry initial + final probe values for diagnosis
description:
## Friction

\`tail-build\` polls a probe form until its return value changes. Current response shapes:

- Success: \`{:ok? true :t <ms> :soft? false}\`
- Timeout: \`{:ok? false :reason :timed-out :note "Probe did not change within wait-ms. Likely a compile error."}\`

Neither shape carries the probe values themselves. On timeout, the operator can't tell:

- Whether the probe ran at all (form had a typo, threw, etc.)
- What value the probe returned (stayed the same? returned nil?)
- Whether the cljs-eval routed to the right runtime

Pair-debug session 2026-05-25 hit this: I passed \`probe: "(let [m (re-frame.core/handler-meta :cofx :testdeck/now)] (:handler-fn-hash m))"\` to wait for a recompile. The probe timed out. The hint said "Likely a compile error" but the compile was fine — my probe form was the problem. With no probe-value information returned, I had to fall back to calling \`handler-meta\` manually to confirm the recompile landed.

## Proposed fix

Include probe values in the response on both success and timeout paths:

\`\`\`edn
;; success
{:ok? true :t <ms> :soft? false
 :probe-values {:initial <v0> :final <v1>}}

;; timeout
{:ok? false :reason :timed-out
 :probe-values {:initial <v0> :final <v-last>}
 :note "Probe value did not change within wait-ms. Possible causes: (a) compile error in shadow, (b) probe form returns the same value as before, (c) probe form errored — check the values."}
\`\`\`

If the probe consistently throws, expose that too:

\`\`\`edn
{:ok? false :reason :probe-errored
 :probe-error <stringified ex>
 :note "Probe form raised an exception every iteration."}
\`\`\`

## Acceptance

On timeout, the response carries enough information for the operator to distinguish "compile didn't happen", "compile happened but the probe values are equal", and "probe form is broken".

## References

- Source: \`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/tail_build.cljs\` (\`tail-build-tool\`)
- Repro: pair-debug session 2026-05-25 — tail-build with probe form timed out, no diagnostic value
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2120
close_reason: #2120 — tail-build envelope :probe-values {:initial :final} on success+timeout; :probe-errored disambiguator

title: feat(re-frame2-pair-mcp): trace-window / watch-epochs should surface 'pre-attach events invisible' explainer when epoch-count > 0 but matches = 0
description:
## Friction

\`discover-app\`'s \`:epoch-counts\` field reads from each frame's per-frame \`epoch-history\` ring (Spec 002 §Frame) — every assembled \`:rf/epoch-record\` for that frame since the ring last rolled. \`trace-window\` and \`watch-epochs\` read from the SHARED trace ring (Spec 009) — only events captured by the \`:re-frame2-pair\` listener that was registered when the MCP attached.

These two stores can wildly diverge. During pair-debug session 2026-05-25:

- \`discover-app\` → \`:epoch-counts {:step-deck 9}\`
- \`trace-window\` (any window) → 0 epochs
- \`watch-epochs\` (no since-id) → 0 epochs

The user clicked \`+\` repeatedly; the per-frame count climbed; the trace ring stayed empty. Spent several minutes confirming we weren't looking at a listener-routing bug before realising "the listener registered AFTER the page already had 7 events". Standard pre-attach invisibility.

## Proposed fix

When \`trace-window\` / \`watch-epochs\` would return an empty matches vector AND the requested frame's per-frame epoch-history has a non-zero count, include an advisory in the result:

\`\`\`edn
{:ok? true
 :matches []
 :count 0
 :advisory {:reason :listener-pre-attach
            :frame :step-deck
            :epochs-in-history 9
            :listener-attached-at-ms 1779632780123
            :hint "9 epochs exist in :step-deck's per-frame history but none were captured by the live trace listener (registered at <timestamp>). To see live events, dispatch one now. To inspect historical epochs, use `snapshot :include [:epochs]`."}}
\`\`\`

The advisory only fires when the divergence is real (history non-zero, matches zero). No additional cost when the live stream genuinely has matches.

## Acceptance

In the empty-window + non-empty-history case, the response carries an \`:advisory\` that names the pre-attach invisibility, the count in history, and the alternative path (snapshot) to inspect them.

## Related

A complete fix would also document this in the skill's references (\`references/ops.md\` §Trace vs Epoch). The current docs imply trace-window covers "events in the last N ms" without noting the listener-registration cutoff.

## References

- Source: \`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/trace_window.cljs\`, \`watch_epochs.cljs\`
- Per-frame epoch-history: Spec 002 §Frame
- Trace ring: Spec 009 §Listener
- Discovery: pair-debug session 2026-05-25
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2120
close_reason: #2120 — trace-window + watch-epochs :advisory slot when matches=0 / history non-empty

title: fix(re-frame2-pair-mcp): handler-meta returns :ok? false :reason :unexpected-shape with actual handler data baked into :value as EDN string
description:
## Symptom

Calling \`handler-meta\` for a registered event / cofx / sub returns:

\`\`\`edn
{:ok? false
 :reason :unexpected-shape
 :kind :event
 :id "inc"
 :value "{:ns testdeck.counter, :file \"testdeck/counter.cljs\", ..., :handler-fn-hash 1140207590, ...}"}
\`\`\`

The handler's actual registration metadata IS present — just embedded as an EDN string inside the \`:value\` field of what reports itself as an error. The agent has to detect the inconsistency, parse the EDN out of the error response, and proceed. Pair-debug session 2026-05-25 hit this on every \`handler-meta\` call (8+ times across different kinds).

## Why this is wrong

Two valid responses; this is neither:

1. **Success** — \`{:ok? true :kind :event :id :counter/inc :ns testdeck.counter :file "..." :line 82 ...}\` — the structured data the descriptor schema documents
2. **Honest error** — \`{:ok? false :reason <something> :hint "..."}\` — when the lookup genuinely failed

What we're getting is "structured error wrapping the successful payload as a string" — the worst of both. Consumers can't reliably destructure on \`:ok?\` because the success case is hiding inside an error.

## Probable cause

Looking at \`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs\`: the tool likely fetches the metadata via \`(rf/handler-meta kind id)\`, expects a specific shape, and falls into a fallback path for "unexpected shape" while still including the raw value for forensic purposes. The result of that fallback is structured as an error even though the underlying data is fine.

## Fix

If the underlying \`(rf/handler-meta kind id)\` returns a map, return it as the success payload (or destructure into the documented descriptor shape). Only return \`:reason :unexpected-shape\` for the rare case where the runtime fn returned something genuinely unparseable (not a map, not a vector — i.e. an actual shape error).

Worth also confirming the SHAPE the MCP descriptor documents matches what \`rf/handler-meta\` actually returns; if the descriptor was written expecting a different shape (e.g. flat keys vs nested), the descriptor should be updated rather than the tool body adding a fallback.

## Acceptance

\`handler-meta\` for a registered handler returns \`:ok? true\` with the metadata as top-level keys. Only genuinely missing / unparseable cases return \`:ok? false\`.

## References

- Source: \`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs\`
- Underlying runtime fn: \`re-frame.core/handler-meta\`
- Repro: pair-debug session 2026-05-25 — every \`handler-meta\` call for \`:counter/inc\`, \`:testdeck/now\`, etc. returned the wrapped-success-as-error shape
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2120
close_reason: #2120 — handler-meta now returns :ok? true with real top-level keys (registrar-describe dissoc :handler-fn + EDN re-parse)

title: feat(re-frame2-pair-mcp): cache discover-app's resolved build-id session-wide
description:
## Friction

Every tool call after \`discover-app\` still needs an explicit \`build\` arg. discover-app already resolved which shadow build is running (and reports it in the result), but subsequent calls default to build \`:app\` (the env-var fallback). When the operator forgets the arg, the tool silently targets the wrong build and returns \`:runtime-not-preloaded\` — looking like a fresh discovery failure rather than a "you forgot the build arg" hint.

Repro from pair-debug session 2026-05-25: after a successful discover-app against \`examples/step-deck\`, calling \`trace-window\` without the build arg returned \`:runtime-not-preloaded\` (because trace-window defaulted to \`:app\`, which doesn't exist). The fix was to remember to add \`build: "examples/step-deck"\` to every single tool call.

## Proposed fix

When discover-app resolves a single running build (or the operator picks one via elicitation), cache that build-id on the conn-atom (alongside the existing \`:probed-builds\` cache from rf2-sjpx0). Subsequent tool calls without an explicit \`build\` arg default to the cached build-id instead of the env-var fallback.

Invalidation: cache resets on nREPL reconnect (same trigger as \`:probed-builds\`). If the operator explicitly passes a build, the explicit value wins (no surprise).

## Acceptance

After a successful \`discover-app\` against one running build, every subsequent tool call works without passing \`build\` — and routes to the same build that discover-app resolved.

## References

- Pair-debug session 2026-05-25 against http://localhost:8031/counter
- Adjacent existing cache: \`re-frame2-pair-mcp.tools.probe/runtime-preloaded?\` (rf2-sjpx0)
- The wire-arg helper: \`re-frame2-pair-mcp.tools.wire/arg-build\`
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2116
close_reason: Merged #2116. discover-app's resolved build-id cached session-wide on conn-atom (:resolved-build-id slot alongside existing :probed-builds). Reset triggers mirror :probed-builds lifecycle: make-conn → nil; connect! → cleared on every (re)connect; close! → cleared. Write triggers: discover-app success + :ok? true warning branches (ambiguous-frame, no-source-coord-annotation). Precondition failures do NOT cache. Explicit-wins: an explicit :build arg always beats the cache. 11 deftests cover precedence + explicit-arg override + lifecycle. Binary rebuilt courtesy. README updated with Per-call build-id resolution subsection.

title: feat(core): capture t1 pending :db snapshot on a CORE trace so Xray Handler panel can render the t1 effects-map value + t1->t2 flow reshape diff
description:
Follow-on from rf2-ynnre (Xray Handler panel B+ visual order).

The rf2-ynnre PR landed the operational section order + a t1 returned-effects sub-block under EVENT HANDLER, but the block only shows `:db` slot PRESENCE (not the pending value) because the framework currently does not stamp the pending `:db` onto any trace.

This bead: add the t1-pending-`:db` snapshot to a CORE trace so the Handler panel can show:
  (a) the pending :db value itself in the t1 returned-effects sub-block (or a richer diff against `:db-before`)
  (b) the t1 to t2 reshape diff under FLOWS (per-flow `:before`/`:result` already cover the per-flow case but a single t1->t2 unified view needs both endpoints)

Design considerations:
- Memory cost: the full :db can be huge. The current `:rf.fx/do-fx` :tags carry `:rf.event/db-present?` (boolean) + `:rf.event/fx` (the vector) deliberately to keep wire+memory cost down. A direct :db stamp would balloon. Options:
  (1) Stamp a structural diff against the pre-event :db (path-set + per-path before/after) — memory cost rides with diff size, not db size.
  (2) Stamp the full pending :db only when DEBUG is enabled AND a config opt-in toggles it on.
  (3) Reuse :rf.event/db-changed's pipeline: emit a `:rf.event/db-pending` trace right before flows fire, with the same slice-centric diff projection.
- Where to emit: either at the run-end emit (router.cljc:962) or at a dedicated pre-flow emit-point. The handler-cascade phases live in `commit-and-flow!` — between handler completion and flow-transform :after, the pending :db is fully observable.
- Trace-id stability + ordering: the new trace would sit between `:rf.event/run-end` and `:rf.flow/computed` records in stream order; consumers (Xray, Story, off-box monitors) need a stable :op-type + :operation.

Gate: spec/009 §Trace events catalogue gets a new entry; spec/013 §Failure semantics may want a note that t1 capture rides the dev-only path (no production cost).

Files likely:
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc (the emit point)
- spec/009-Instrumentation.md (catalogue addition)
- tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/event_detail.cljs (panel-side: surface the t1 value in handler-returned-effects-block + render the t1->t2 reshape inline under FLOWS)
- corresponding tests
notes:
RULING (Mike 2026-05-25): store the full :db value returned by the handler (t1), the same way :fx is stored — no diff, no gating, no DEBUG conditional. PDS makes the cost trivial (references not copies). If flows later transform :db, store that post-flow value too (t2). Both values stamped on trace records as full values. Xray Handler panel computes t1→t2 reshape from the two stored values rather than the framework stamping a pre-computed diff. Supersedes the three design options (1/2/3) in the original description; aligns with how :fx is already handled.
PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2128
