title: chore(re-frame2-pair-mcp): warn or auto-rebuild stale binary after pull when MCP source changed
description:
## The gap

`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/out/server.js` is the binary an MCP host (Claude Code, Cursor, …) actually executes. Per `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/.gitignore`, `out/` is **intentionally not committed** — standard JS-project convention (build artifacts are treated like `node_modules/`, each environment rebuilds locally).

The unintended consequence: pulling source changes silently invalidates the local binary, with no notification. Symptoms in the wild:

- Operator pulls `main`, which includes a fixed MCP server in `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/...`.
- Operator opens Claude Code; the MCP server child process is still running the **pre-pull** binary.
- Tool calls fail with stale-binary symptoms (e.g. `:nrepl-port-not-found` in the case that surfaced this gap — fix was merged in #2105 + #2109, but `out/server.js` mtime predated both).
- Operator has no way to know the binary is stale unless they happen to read the file mtime.

Discovered in pair-debug session 2026-05-25 while retrying re-frame2-pair after rf2-umoz2 and rf2-3grub merged — the binary on disk was from 2026-05-24 23:33, well before either merge.

## Options (lightest → heaviest)

| Approach | Pro | Con |
|---|---|---|
| **A.** Git `post-merge` hook prints a warning when `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/` changed in the pulled commits — "MCP source changed; run `npm --prefix tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp run build` and bounce the MCP server" | Cheap; user keeps control of when to build | Still requires manual rebuild step |
| **B.** Same post-merge hook, but auto-runs the build instead of just warning | Zero user action | Slow on every pull where MCP changed (shadow-cljs cold-start JVM tax); silent failure if shadow not installed |
| **C.** MCP server itself includes a "binary outdated" check on `discover-app` (compare mtime of `out/server.js` against the latest commit touching `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/` in the local repo) and warns in the result | Catches the staleness where the operator sees it (in the tool result) | Complexity inside MCP; requires the MCP process to know its install path & be inside a git repo; doesn't apply to released npm builds |
| **D.** Document in the MCP server README + setup-skill and leave on operators | Simplest | Most error-prone (the current state) |

**Recommended: A.** It's the lightest layer, doesn't surprise anyone, and matches existing dev-workflow ergonomics elsewhere in the repo (the post-checkout / pre-push beads hooks already in `.beads/hooks/`).

## Acceptance

After `git pull` brings down a commit that touches `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/`, the operator sees a clear stderr message identifying the stale binary and naming the exact command to refresh it. No silent failure mode.

Bonus (optional): same hook also runs for `tools/story-mcp/src/` if/when story-mcp ever ships a JS-bundled binary the same way — currently story-mcp is JVM-in-process so doesn't have this problem, but the hook should be parameterised, not hardcoded to the pair-mcp path.

## References

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/.gitignore` — `out/` excluded intentionally
- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/package.json` — `npm run build` = `shadow-cljs compile server`
- `.beads/hooks/` — pattern for existing repo-managed git hooks
- Predecessor incidents: pair-debug session 2026-05-25 (this discovery); also implicit in the rf2-umoz2 close note: *"…no longer needed after rebuilding the MCP binary."*
- Related: rf2-umoz2 (#2105), rf2-3grub (#2109) — both merged, but their fixes were inert until rebuild
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2113 — Approach A (post-merge warning hook). 34/34 tests pass. Live-verified positive (HEAD~10) + negative (HEAD~1) cases.
close_reason: Merged #2113. POSIX-sh post-merge git hook + testable detection lib + bash & PowerShell installers (idempotent, block-aware — coexists with bd hooks install in same git/hooks/post-merge file). Warns on MCP src/shadow-cljs.edn/deps.edn/package.json changes; lists changed files + rebuild command + bounce hint. Cross-platform (POSIX-sh, no bashisms; verified under Git Bash on Windows). 34/34 tests passing (unit + smoke). Live-verified: positive case fires (HEAD~10 covering rf2-umoz2 + rf2-3grub MCP src), negative case silent (HEAD~1 docs-only). Docs updated: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md + tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/test/README.md + skills/re-frame2-pair/references/mcp-transport.md.

title: fix(xray): clean up reg-view warnings in console — non-DOM roots on 3 shell views + plain-fn frame leak in ribbon-theme-toggle
description:
## Symptom

Loading http://localhost:8031/counter (or any step-deck testbed page) emits four `[re-frame] warn-once` messages in the browser console. All four originate from Xray's own UI (`day8.re-frame2-xray.shell.*`), not from the testbed app. Captured during pair-debug session 2026-05-24 ~22:20 AUSEST.

## The four warnings

### 1. `shell-view` — non-DOM root (`frame_provider`)
```
[re-frame] reg-view :day8.re-frame2-xray.shell/shell-view —
root element is #object[re_frame$views$provider$frame_provider];
data-rf2-source-coord skipped
(Spec 006 §Source-coord annotation: pair tools fall back to :rf/id for non-DOM roots).
```
Root returns the `frame_provider` React component (wraps children in a frame context), not a DOM element. Stack: `mount.cljs:265 → spine.cljs:1485 → reagent_root → reagent8 → comp → shell-view`.

### 2. `surface-composer` — non-DOM root (`MetaFn`)
Same warning shape; root element is `cljs.core.MetaFn` (a function with metadata returning another view — indirection layer).

### 3. `dynamic-chrome` — non-DOM root (React Fragment `:<>`)
Same warning shape; root element is the React Fragment sentinel `:<>`.

### 4. `ribbon-theme-toggle` — plain-fn under non-default frame
```
[re-frame] :rf.warning/plain-fn-under-non-default-frame-once —
day8.re_frame2_xray.shell.ribbon_theme_toggle rendered under :rf/xray;
subscribe/dispatch routed to :rf/default. Plain Reagent fns do not pick
up the surrounding frame; their dispatch/subscribe targets :rf/default.
To capture the surrounding frame, register the view via reg-view.
```
`ribbon-theme-toggle` is a plain Reagent fn rendered inside Xray's `:rf/xray` frame. Per Spec 002, plain fns don't participate in frame-aware dispatch/subscribe routing — its dispatches/subs land in `:rf/default` (the host app's frame). If it dispatches a `:xray/set-theme` event, that event lands in the wrong frame.

## Why each is a real issue

**1–3:** Per Spec 006, the source-coord annotation system is meant to attach `data-rf2-source-coord` to every registered view's root so pair tools (re-frame2-pair, Xray itself) can map DOM clicks back to source. When the root is not a DOM element, click-to-source silently degrades for those views. The user can't right-click `shell-view`, `surface-composer`, or `dynamic-chrome` in Xray and jump to source.

**4:** Frame leak. The `ribbon-theme-toggle`'s dispatch/subscribe routes to `:rf/default` instead of `:rf/xray`. Either:
- (a) Intentional — the theme is meant to be global / app-level state (in which case the warning is cosmetic and should be suppressed at the call-site with a comment explaining why), OR
- (b) A bug — the theme toggle is meant to live inside `:rf/xray` and is leaking into the host app's frame.

Worth a sanity check before fixing.

## Proposed fixes

### For #1–3 (non-DOM roots)
Wrap each of `shell-view`, `surface-composer`, `dynamic-chrome` in a thin DOM element (e.g. `[:div.xray-shell-root ...]`) so the source-coord attribute has somewhere to land. Or, if that adds undesired DOM noise, use the documented `:rf/id`-fallback path explicitly so the warn-once stays silent (per Spec 006, the `:rf/id` registration is the supported alternative).

### For #4 (plain-fn frame leak)
Two paths:
- If theme is intentionally app-global → suppress the warning at the call-site (`{:warn-on-plain-fn? false}` or similar), document why
- If theme should live in `:rf/xray` → convert `ribbon-theme-toggle` to a `reg-view` registration

Confirm intent before picking.

## Acceptance

Loading http://localhost:8031/counter (or any step-deck page) emits **zero** `warn-once` messages from `day8.re-frame2-xray.shell.*` in the console.

## References

- Source: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs` (the four affected views/fns)
- Mount path: `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/mount.cljs:265` (mount_shell_into_BANG_)
- Spec contracts: Spec 002 (frames + plain-fn routing), Spec 006 (source-coord annotation)
- Related (closed) prior incident: `rf2-0d35` — plain-fn-under-non-default-frame regression in browser tests
- Related: rf2-00li, rf2-gsh49 (source-coord wiring across adapters)
- Discovered: pair-debug session 2026-05-24 ~22:20 AUSEST while attempting to attach to step-deck testbed

Both render inside :rf/xray as plain Reagent fns; their dispatch/subscribe leak to :rf/default. Worker should fold these into the same fix-pass as ribbon-theme-toggle — convert to reg-view or suppress the warning at the call-site if intentional (decide per-view).

title: docs(cofx): foreground the inline-interceptor escape hatch alongside reg-cofx/inject-cofx
description:
Mike-directed 2026-05-24 — design decision recorded: KEEP reg-cofx/inject-cofx as the canonical path (it earns its weight for the 5-10% of cofxs that get test-stubbed, hot-rebound at the REPL, or are enumerated by tooling like Xray's cofx list). But for the ~90% of cofxs that are define-once-use-locally-never-stubbed, the registry indirection is ceremony without delivering its hot-rebind / tooling-enumeration benefit. The framework ALREADY supports inline interceptor maps as an escape hatch ( is legal in any interceptor vector today), but the docs / guide / skill don't foreground this — they push everyone through reg-cofx/inject-cofx.
SCOPE: documentation work. NO refactor. Add inline-interceptor escape-hatch coverage where coeffects are taught:
1. skills/re-frame2/ (the authoring skill) — wherever coeffects are introduced, add a 'when reg-cofx is overkill' paragraph + worked example.
2. docs/guide/ — find the cofx section in the guide; same addition.
3. spec/ — if cofxs are described normatively (likely spec/Coeffects.md or spec/API.md), add a brief 'inline interceptors are also legal' note. Don't bury the registry path; complement it.
WHEN TO USE WHICH (the rubric to teach):
- Use reg-cofx + inject-cofx when: (a) you might want to mock/stub the cofx in tests by id, (b) you want hot-rebind at the REPL (re-registering takes effect on the next dispatch with no event-handler re-registration), (c) you want devtools (Xray) to enumerate it, (d) it's parameterised by id (e.g. localStorage-by-key).
- Inline  when: define-once-use-locally, never stubbed, the cofx is trivial. Reading-cost win, ceremony-cost lose.
WORKED EXAMPLE to include (small): an event handler that wants a current-millis cofx for one event only — show both forms, explain the trade.
Cite this bead in the prose so future maintainers can find the rationale (no link to ai/findings/* per the no-link rule).
Gates: mkdocs --strict (load-bearing), no code changes.

title: test(epoch): pin flow-throw epoch shape (db-before == db-after, :outcome :ok, :rf.error/flow-eval-exception in :trace-events)
description:
After the flows-after-handler atomicity work (rf2-u0zz5/#2065 + rf2-vug0k/#2072), one downstream-observability invariant remains unpinned at the epoch-record level.

Today:
- implementation/core/test/re_frame/event_emit_test.cljc :: listener-marks-flow-throw-as-non-ok-outcome pins :outcome :flow-error on the always-on event-emit record.
- implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/flows_integration_test.clj :: flow-throw-aborts-event-no-db-changed-no-partial-commit pins the trace stream + app-db invariants.

Gap:
- implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj has no flow-throw coverage. settle-event-epoch! (router.cljc:1175) does NOT receive the outcome — it just gets (frame-id db-before db-after) — so a flow-throw event commits an epoch with :outcome :ok and :db-after == :db-before (since flow-throw skipped the install). This is the existing intentional design (per epoch/assembly.cljc:264-275 docstring: "the reference runtime commits one of three: :ok / :halted-depth / :halted-destroy") — but it is NOT pinned by any test.

The implied contract — "a flow-throw event is observable in the epoch as (:db-before == :db-after) with a :rf.error/flow-eval-exception event in :trace-events" — could quietly regress (e.g. if someone later widened settle to surface non-ok outcomes and accidentally rolled :flow-error into one of the halted-* enums).

Work: add an epoch-test deftest asserting the flow-throw epoch shape:
- :db-before == :db-after (no install happened)
- :outcome :ok (current intentional behaviour — flow-throw rides :trace-events, not the outcome slot)
- :trace-events contains a :rf.error/flow-eval-exception entry

~30 LoC; lives in implementation/epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_test.clj. Optional contrast: a clean flow eval epoch where :db-before != :db-after (the flow-augmented value landed).

Found in delta-audit rf2-hm4gi (Shape-3); LOW severity (regression-guard for an existing-correct behaviour).
notes: PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/2096
close_reason: Merged #2096. 2 deftests in epoch_test.clj pinning flow-throw epoch shape: :db-before==:db-after, :outcome :ok, :trace-events contains :rf.error/flow-eval-exception. title: fix(xray/test): restore semantic intent of "namespace prefix collision guard" fixture (Causa->Xray rename leftover)
description:
**Source.** Audit rf2-26pwy (Causa→Xray operational/semantic rename audit) found one
fixture whose semantic intent was broken by the rename.

**File.** `tools/xray/test/day8/re_frame2_xray/trace_bus_self_noise_cljs_test.cljc:228-234`

**Bug.** The `namespace prefix collision guard` test-block under
`xray-internal-event-id?-keyword-namespace` is documented as:

```
;; A keyword whose namespace STARTS with `rf.xray` but is not
;; exactly `rf.xray` (e.g. `:rf.causal/x`, `:rf.causal-link/y`)
;; must NOT match. The contract is namespace equality, not
;; prefix matching.
(is (false? (trace-bus/xray-internal-event-id? :rf.causal/x)))
(is (false? (trace-bus/xray-internal-event-id? :rf.causal-link/y)))
```

`:rf.causal/x` does NOT start with `rf.xray` — it starts with `rf.causal`. The
fixture passes only because any non-`rf.xray` namespace returns false from the
implementation (`(= "rf.xray" (namespace event-id))`). The named failure mode —
"a similarly-prefixed but non-equal namespace must not false-positive" — is no
longer being guarded against.

**Origin.** Fixture originated in `4e813ddd5 (rf2-g1pt8)` when the predicate was
`causa-internal-event-id?` checking for `rf.causa` equality. There `:rf.causal/x`
+ `:rf.causal-link/y` genuinely did start with `rf.causa` so the fixture was
correct. The rename commit `731188b1f (rf2-3pdp9)` updated the predicate string
to `"rf.xray"` but left the fixture keyword values intact (presumably to avoid
re-introducing the "causa" string into the renamed file). Result: the test now
passes trivially, not by satisfying its docstring contract.

**Fix shape.** Replace the fixture values with keywords whose namespace **actually
starts with `rf.xray`** but isn't equal to it — e.g. `:rf.xray-test/x` and
`:rf.xray-foo/y`. Update the surrounding comment. One-line test change, no
production-code change.

**Why low severity.** The implementation is already correct (equality, not
prefix). The test does not regress in green-status. The bead is correctness-of-
test-intent, not behaviour.

**Suggested branch.** `worker/fix-xray-prefix-collision-fixture-<id>` off
`origin/main`. Isolated-surface change (single test file).

**Refs.** rf2-26pwy (this audit), rf2-imxfn (pure-string check that found
clean), rf2-3pdp9 (the rename commit), rf2-g1pt8 (original fixture authorship).

title: remediate: implementation/adapters/reagent (correctness + completeness + clarity findings)
description:
Consolidated remediation for implementation/adapters/reagent from the 3-lens sweep. Verdict: correct + complete + clean — a thin, faithful shim over make-ratom-spine; all 9 Spec 006 fns conform; no completeness gaps. All findings low-severity. Docs: ai/findings/review/{correctness,completeness,clarity}--implementation-adapters-reagent.md

CORRECTNESS
- [P3] :rf.error/derived-container-replaced is specified (Spec 006:163) but implemented nowhere in the stack.
- [P3] SSR hiccup-emitter wiring is load-order fragile; the adapter docstring overstates "load-order-independent".
- [P3] render slot's active-root tracking is bypassed by the browser smoke testbed (mounts via raw rdc/*).

COMPLETENESS
- (none — complete against the contract.)

CLARITY / MINIMALISM
- [P2] Late-bind hook block is duplicated verbatim across the two ratom adapters (reagent + reagent-slim) — factor it the way the spine surfaces are. (See also the uix/helix twin finding — consider one React-adapter-assembly factoring across all adapters.)
- [P3] :substrate-name "Reagent" is dead config (never read by make-ratom-spine).
- [P3] register-context-provider private fn is more verbose than the equivalent UIx wiring.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #2011 — extracted React-adapter assembly into spine (make-react-adapter + make-ratom-adapter, bundle-isolated via injected hook-ops); reconciled eager/lazy (spine make-derived-value now lazy, matching Reagent/plain-atom, per Spec 006); fixed reagent-slim Reaction._run error-state clobber; deleted dead realise-sub-handler; collapsed do-fx arity ladder; inlined fx-runs-on-platform?; dropped reagent :substrate-name dead config; inlined register-context-provider; reagent-slim set-hiccup-emitter! docstring + parse-tag docstring/test; synced helix use-current-frame docstring; added hydrate render-branch test for the React-hook spine (UIx+Helix). Deferred P3 :rf.error/derived-container-replaced (unimplemented across stack — needs its own bead). All gates green.

title: bug(causa): Trace tab shows contradictory "no epoch focused · N ops" on fresh load — LIVE head-tracks to an epoch-less :rf/init cascade
description:
On a fresh page load (before any user interaction) the Trace tab's epoch-indicator reads 'no epoch focused · N ops' — contradictory, since N ops ARE scoped to a focused cascade.

ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed live via re-frame2-pair): LIVE head-tracking lands the focus on the head cascade, which on fresh load is the framework-internal [:title/flow [:rf/init]] machine-init cascade. That cascade IS traced (it appears in :rf.causa/cascades and has trace ops), but it produces NO :rf/epoch-record — e.g. :below's only captured epoch is [:parallel-frames.core/initialise] (epoch 2); there is no epoch for the :rf/init cascade. So compose-focus (spine.cljs, rf2-70tkv) cannot derive :epoch-id from the focused cascade -> :epoch-id nil -> the epoch-indicator (panels/trace.cljs ~237: (if (some? epoch-id) (str "epoch #" epoch-id) "no epoch focused")) renders 'no epoch focused' while the cascade-scoped ops still render.

EVIDENCE:
- Before any click: focus = {:frame :below, :dispatch-id 5, :epoch-id nil, :head? true}; the dispatch-id-5 cascade = [:title/flow [:rf/init]] (:below); :below epochs = [epoch 2 :initialise] ONLY (no epoch for dispatch-id 5).
- After clicking + once: focus = {:dispatch-id 622, :epoch-id 27}; :below epochs = [2 (:initialise), 27 (:counter-inc)]; indicator resolves to 'epoch #27'.

So it is TRANSIENT — self-clears on the first user action that produces a real epoch. But it is the INITIAL state every user sees when opening the Trace tab.

FIX OPTIONS:
- Skip epoch-less cascades when resolving the focusable head (focusable-head-id / compose-focus) so the focus never lands on a cascade with no :rf/epoch-record; and/or
- Filter framework-internal :rf/init (and similar non-user) cascades out of the focusable cascade list — Causa probably should not surface a machine's :rf/init as a head cascade; and/or
- Graceful-degrade the epoch-indicator: when a cascade with ops is focused but has no epoch, show the cascade/event (e.g. '[:title/flow [:rf/init]] · N ops') instead of the contradictory 'no epoch focused'; and/or
- Substrate: capture an :rf/epoch-record for machine-init cascades so the mapping is complete.

Files: spine.cljs (compose-focus / focusable-head-id / cascades sub), panels/trace.cljs (epoch-indicator ~230-246). Distinct from rf2-r6d6u (the denominator) though same Trace header.
notes: RE-SCOPED 2026-05-22 (Mike's epoch-per-event invariant): root cause is the substrate epoch-per-DRAIN boundary, fixed by rf2-u6jsj (spec) + rf2-nj6p7 (impl). Once each event mints its own epoch, every focusable cascade has an :epoch-id and 'no epoch focused' disappears. This bead now = the CAUSA/TOOLS side: after nj6p7 lands, verify/adjust spine.cljs compose-focus + epoch-id-for-cascade + registry.cljs :rf.causa/cascades so per-event epoch resolves, and confirm the fresh-load Trace indicator no longer reads 'no epoch focused'. The original Causa-only fix-options (skip epoch-less cascades / capture init epoch) are STALE — there is no epoch-less cascade once nj6p7 lands. Depends on rf2-nj6p7. Shares trace.cljs surface with rf2-r6d6u — sequence the two Causa edits.
close_reason: Superseded: o6yqq removes the 'no epoch focused · N ops' epoch-indicator widget entirely (display bug gone); the underlying child-dispatch-id epoch resolution is covered by nj6p7 (substrate per-event epochs) + td380 (scope Trace rows by focused epoch). No remaining standalone work.

title: bug(instrumentation): mount-render burst spuriously attributes to the first post-mount cascade — Views tab shows an extra view on the first interaction (rf2-qs6dl follow-up)
description:
Follow-up to rf2-qs6dl/#1935. A view's MOUNT render is double-attributed: once correctly to the initialise epoch, and once spuriously to the FIRST post-mount cascade. So the Views/Reactive panel shows an extra view in 'views re-rendered' on the user's first interaction after a page (re)load, then self-corrects.

DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION (parallel-frames testbed, :below frame, single tab, via re-frame2-pair):
  refresh page
  epoch 2  initialise   RENDERED [frame-panel counter-view title-view]   <- correct (all mount)
  1st '+' click         RENDERED [counter-view TITLE-VIEW]              <- title-view spurious; its subs are unchanged (changed? false)
  2nd '+' click         RENDERED [counter-view]                          <- clean thereafter

The extra title-view is title-view's mount render committing late and attaching to 'the most-recently-settled epoch', which by commit time is the first counter-inc rather than initialise. #1935's post-settle back-fill handles the steady state correctly but mis-files the mount burst.

NOT a reactivity bug: on a counter-inc only counter-view should re-render, and from the 2nd click onward it does. Subs are correct throughout (counter changed? true; title subs changed? false; L2 ::counter-parity cascades on counter / skips on title). Confirmed clean by closing rf2-wi900 (the earlier 'sub lag' was multi-tab/hot-reload chaos, not real).

FIX DIRECTION: in the epoch-capture back-fill (epoch/capture.cljc, the rf2-qs6dl path), attribute a late-arriving MOUNT render to the mount/initialise epoch (the cascade that actually caused the view's first render) rather than the most-recently-settled epoch — or de-dup a render already attributed to its mount epoch so it isn't also filed against the next cascade.

IMPACT: cosmetic, first-interaction-after-load only, self-correcting. Low severity but a genuine correctness nit in freshly-merged render attribution.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1939

title: audit(pair-mcp): send-op! writes to socket without nil-guard — connect→write race surfaces native error + leaks pending entry
description: nrepl.cljs:280-283 (inside send-op!). After connect! resolves, send-op! reads (:socket @conn-atom) and calls (.write sock ...). connect!'s idempotent fast path guarantees a live socket at resolve time, but the socket close/error handlers (attach-handlers! lines 174-180) can fire between connect! resolving and the .write executing — flipping :closed? true, and close! nils :socket. If the socket is nil at that instant, (.write nil ...) throws a native 'Cannot read properties of null (reading write)' synchronously in the Promise executor: the op rejects but with an opaque message instead of the structured :closed?/reconnect signal the rest of the ns uses. The just-registered id is also left in :pending (no dissoc on this throw path) — a small leak until next close!. Fix: re-check liveness immediately before the write — (if-let [sock (:socket @conn-atom)] (.write sock (bencode/encode op)) (do (swap! conn-atom update :pending dissoc id) (js/clearTimeout timer) (reject (js/Error. "nREPL socket dropped before write — retry to reconnect")))). Rare today (single in-flight op, sequential dispatch) hence P3, but it is the one unguarded boundary in an otherwise carefully-guarded transport.

title: audit(machines): single-map :always escapes guard/action ref validation
description: validation.cljc:460 (validate-machine!). The grammar admits :always as a vector OR a single transition map (Spec 005 Eventless :always; runtime pick-always-transition at transition.cljc:1234 normalizes both, and the self-loop validator normalizes via the in-file always-entries helper at validation.cljc:314). But the guard/action ref-resolution loop iterates (:always state-node) WITHOUT normalizing: (doseq [t (:always state-node)] (check-guard! (:guard t) s) (check-action! (:action t) s)). For a single-map :always like {:guard :missing :target :x}, doseq iterates its MapEntries ([:guard :missing] [:target :x]), so (:guard t)/(:action t) return nil and both checks no-op. A dangling guard/action ref in single-map :always slips past registration and only surfaces at runtime (late, on the firing path) instead of fail-fast at registration. Vector form is validated correctly; only single-map affected. No test covers :always ref validation in either form (existing unresolved-guard/-action tests only exercise :on). Fix: reuse the existing in-file normalizer -> (doseq [t (always-entries state-node)] ...). Add regression test: single-map :always with dangling :guard/:action must throw :rf.error/machine-unresolved-guard/-action at registration. P3/MED.

title: machines: :raise-depth-limit bounds breadth only, not transitive self-chaining depth
description: Discovered while fixing rf2-r26e2 (PR #1853). The machine :raise drain's depth-limit bounds only BREADTH — raise siblings drained from one queue. A self-chaining single-raise (a state whose :raise re-targets a path that raises again) recurses on the JVM call stack via nested machine-transition-single calls, each starting a FRESH drain-raises depth counter. So transitive self-chaining depth is NOT bounded: instead of a clean :rf.error/machine-raise-depth-exceeded, a runaway self-chain blows the JVM stack (StackOverflowError). Fix: thread a transitive depth counter across nested machine-transition-single recursion (not just within a single drain-raises queue) so self-chaining raises hit the same depth-limit guard. File: implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc (drain-raises + machine-transition-single recursion). Add a self-chaining-raise test asserting the clean error fires (not a stack overflow). Narrow trigger (requires a self-chaining raise loop), hence P3, but it's a robustness gap — the engine should fail cleanly, not crash the host stack.

title: review(http): interceptor-failure trace :cause not redacted when request sensitive
description: On a :before throw, re-frame.http-middleware/run-interceptor-chain! (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_middleware.cljc:185-211) emits :rf.error/http-interceptor-failed through privacy/prepare-emit-failure, which redacts :url/:headers/:body/:body-text/:decoded/:detail but NOT :cause. :cause is the interceptor's thrown message ((:reason (ex-data t)) or (.getMessage t)), interceptor-author-controlled and could echo a secret the interceptor was handling (e.g. a token-validation message embedding the token). For a sensitive request the cause rides the trace surface un-redacted. Add :cause to the sensitive redaction set in prepare-emit-failure, or scrub at the interceptor emit site.

title: review(http): CLJS :decode :blob/:array-buffer/:form-data returns body-text string, not binary
description: Spec 014 Decoding (Explicit content type, lines 164-170) lists :blob (binary blob), :array-buffer, :form-data as distinct decode shapes. On CLJS the transport always reads the Fetch response via (.text resp) (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:125), so decode-response-body resolves :blob/:array-buffer/:form-data to the body-TEXT string (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_decode.cljc:179-186) rather than a Blob/ArrayBuffer/FormData. A caller asking :decode :blob for an image gets a lossy UTF-8 string. :auto never resolves to :array-buffer/:form-data (sniffer only emits :json/:text/:blob) so this only bites explicit binary decode. Resolution: either implement true binary read on CLJS (response .blob()/.arrayBuffer()/.formData(), which means not pre-reading .text) or narrow the CLJS-reference decode modes in Spec 014.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1850

title: review(http): build-reply-event silently default-merges on non-vector non-nil explicit :on-success/:on-failure
description: re-frame.http-encoding/build-reply-event (implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_encoding.cljc:176-196) treats explicit :on-success/:on-failure as an event vector only when (vector? value). A supplied non-nil non-vector value is supplied? true but not vector?, so it falls into the :else default-merge branch and dispatches back to the originating event-id, silently ignoring the caller's explicit target. Spec 014 types :on-success as 'event vector or nil'; a malformed value should surface a structured error rather than silently re-route. Low-likelihood footgun; consider a validation throw or at least a warning trace.

title: review(core): event-emit :outcome reports :ok for schema-rollback + flow-throw dispatches
description:
The always-on event-emit record's :outcome is computed purely from the interceptor-chain exception: (if error :error :ok), where `error` is only the chain's :rf/interceptor-error. A dispatch whose :db effect is ROLLED BACK by a post-commit app-db schema failure (Spec 010 row 4) or whose flow :output THREW (Spec 013 §Failure semantics rule 3) does NOT set `error` — those are detected and handled inside commit-and-flow! and never flow back to the trailer. So a dispatch that failed validation/flows reports :outcome :ok to off-box observability shippers (Datadog/Sentry/Honeycomb).

Spec 009 §Event-emit listener §Record shape only ties :error to "handler exception", so this is defensible per the letter — hence SPEC-GAP, not BUG. But it is misleading for production observability: a dispatch that rolled back its entire :db write surfaces as a clean :ok event.

Decision: either (a) widen :outcome :error to cover rollback + flow-throw, or (b) the spec explicitly pins those outcomes as :ok for the event-emit record (error riding the error-emit substrate only). Needs Mike's call on observability semantics.

Files: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:746-826 (emit-cascade-trailers! / run-handler-cascade!), :709-744 (commit-and-flow! returns only the chain error); event_emit.cljc:84-96.

title: review(core): layer-2+ sub input ref-counts never decrement on plain-atom (JVM/SSR) adapter
description:
compute-and-cache! registers the symmetric input-release (unsubscribe each :<- input when the parent reaction disposes) via interop/add-on-dispose!. On the plain-atom adapter (JVM/SSR/headless) the :adapter/add-on-dispose! and :adapter/dispose! hooks are NOT published (only Reagent/reagent-slim/UIx/Helix publish them), so:

- interop/add-on-dispose! is a silent no-op -> the input-release callback is never registered.
- interop/dispose! (called by dispose-entry-now! and grace teardown) is a silent no-op.

Consequence: on JVM, when a layer-2+ sub's cache slot is disposed (every subscribe-once unsubscribes with {:grace 0}), the parent slot is removed but its inputs' ref-counts are never decremented. Over a frame's lifetime input-sub ref-counts on JVM accumulate monotonically and never reach 1->0, pinning forever until destroy-frame! / clear-sub-cache! resets the cache. Violates Spec 006 §Reference counting and disposal invariant ("ref-count reflects live refs").

Low severity: SSR tears the per-request frame down after each render, bounding the leak. But a long-lived JVM frame that repeatedly subscribe-once-es deep chains grows its sub-cache without bound.

Files: implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:277-292; interop.cljs:62-72; substrate/plain_atom.cljc:31-38 (make-derived-value reifies no IDisposable).

(test_react.cljc:200-214) drains active-mounts but never disposes per-frame sub-caches (can't — CLJC, spine is CLJS), diverging from the Spec 006 MUST 1 the other four adapters honour. title: ci(lint): triage Splint baseline and flip the Splint job to fail-loud
description:
Follow-on to rf2-60nez. Splint stays report-only in the CI gate because the Splint config-loader has a Windows-specific bug — it builds the default-config resource path with backslashes (`io/file 'noahtheduke' 'splint' 'config' 'default.edn'`) and `io/resource` rejects backslash-separated keys, so the linter exits with `Cannot open <nil> as a Reader.` on every dev machine. That means we can't slice the warning baseline locally.

This bead lives behind the dev-machine workaround OR a CI-run-driven triage:

## Strategy A (preferred — CI-driven)

1. From a CI run's log, slice the Splint warning baseline by rule. Per rf2-60nez's notes the headline rules are:
   - `lint/prefer-method-values` (503) — `(.method obj)` → `(Class/method obj)` (Clojure 1.12 method-values; mechanical).
   - `style/eq-zero` (240) — `(= 0 x)` → `(zero? x)` (mechanical).
   - `lint/identical-branches` (135) — likely real bugs (then = else clauses).
   - `style/prefer-clj-string` (112) — `(.toLowerCase s)` → `(clojure.string/lower-case s)` (mechanical).
2. Apply `--autocorrect` where Splint marks the rule `:safe true` (most of the mechanical ones).
3. Investigate `identical-branches` cases individually — those are real.
4. Either fix-forward or exclude per-rule via `.splint.edn` (`{lint/foo {:enabled false}}` or per-path `:excludes`).

## Strategy B (Windows workaround)

Patch Splint upstream — the one-liner is in `noahtheduke/splint/config.clj:47`:

```clj
(def default-config-file
  (io/resource (str (io/file 'noahtheduke' 'splint' 'config' 'default.edn'))))
```

Replace `(str (io/file …))` with `(clojure.string/join '/' [...])` and submit a PR; once the next Splint release ships the dev-machine workflow works again.

## Tightening the gate

Once warnings + errors hit zero (or are baselined via `.splint.edn` exclusions):

- `.github/workflows/lint.yml` — remove `continue-on-error: true` from the `splint` job + the trailing `|| true` on the `Run Splint` step.
- The clj-kondo job is already fail-loud after rf2-60nez; this bead's scope is only Splint.

## Surface

- `.splint.edn` (per-rule disables / exclusions)
- `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (tighten the Splint job)
- Source-wide edits for the mechanical rules
- Optional: upstream Splint PR for the Windows config-loader

title: decide(tooling): clj-kondo status — keep config + add CI gate, replace with modern tool, or drop entirely
description:
The .clj-kondo/config.edn (4KB, line-by-line analyzed) is configured for editor-integration awareness (Calva/CIDER/Cursive) but NO CI gate runs clj-kondo (zero references in .github/* or scripts/*). It's vestigial-as-CI-gate but live-as-editor-config.

## Question for Mike
Three options:

**(a) Keep .clj-kondo + add CI gate.** Run clj-kondo --lint on PR + nightly. Catches unresolved-symbol drift, unused-namespace cruft, redefined-var bugs early. The config already exists; CI integration is ~10 lines of YAML. Cost: another gate to babysit; some linter false positives on re-frame2's macro-heavy code.

**(b) Replace with a modern tool.** Splint (Clojurists Together-funded, 2024+) is pure Clojure, faster, cleaner false-positive profile. Or clojure-lsp (which embeds clj-kondo and adds rename + def-jump). Cost: migration friction; editor team needs to retool.

**(c) Drop /.clj-kondo entirely.** Pre-alpha posture: linting deferred until v1.0 stabilises (when API names stop churning). Editor users either install clj-kondo with global defaults or use a different lint integration. Cost: lose all editor lint-feedback today.

## Surface
- .clj-kondo/config.edn
- .github/workflows/* (if adding CI gate)
- editor-setup docs (skills/re-frame2 README + docs/contrib if any)

## Posture
Pre-alpha. The question is whether linting is high-leverage now (pre-1.0 churn era) or premature optimisation. Mayor's lean: (a) — the config is already there + a CI gate would catch unresolved-symbol regressions like the recent rf2-f4h6a chrome_fullscreen typo.
notes: DECISION (Mike, 2026-05-21): Keep kondo + add CI gate. Add Splint ALONGSIDE kondo (different rule sets, complementary). Implementation: (1) GitHub Actions YAML job 'lint' running clj-kondo --lint . on PR + nightly; (2) Add Splint to project deps + CI job 'splint-lint'; (3) Both jobs report independently; (4) Document the dual-linter posture in CONTRIBUTING / docs/contrib.

title: substrate(trace): :rf.sub/skipped + :rf.flow/skipped + :rf.cascade/captured aggregate
description:
Per Causa design doc (#1720, spec/021 §12 substrate gaps): the reactive cascade DAG requires capturing the "not recomputed" branches — operator needs to see "considered, no recompute" entries in the cascade, dimmed.

**New trace ops to add**:
- `:rf.sub/skipped` — emitted when a sub's input db-path is unchanged → no recompute. Tags: `:frame :sub-id :reason :input-paths-unchanged`
- `:rf.flow/skipped` — same for flows (input-paths-unchanged → no recompute). Tags: `:frame :flow-id :input-paths-unchanged`
- `:rf.cascade/captured` — focused-event-only aggregator: per-epoch record of the full cascade DAG (db-paths → subs recomputed/skipped → views rendered). Stored in the epoch buffer for inspection later.

**Why focused-event-only**: capturing for EVERY epoch is too expensive. Only the operator's focused epoch + a small back-buffer (say last 5 epochs) captures full cascade detail. Other epochs in the buffer keep just summary info (counts, no per-sub attribution).

**Pre-alpha posture**: no shim; clean new trace ops + DEBUG-gated capture.

**Acceptance**:
- New trace ops emitted by re-frame.subs and re-frame.flows
- `:rf.cascade/captured` records full DAG for the focused epoch
- Bounded: cap at 50 subs / 100 views per epoch (per panel design)
- Causa Reactive panel reads the captured DAG for the focused epoch
close_reason: Landed in #1729 admin-merge (same inherited mkdocs failure; diff is in implementation/{core,flows,epoch} + spec/009)

title: Story feature-parity with Storybook — build /docs/Story tutorial mirroring Storybook React tutorials + identify gaps
description:
Mike directive 2026-05-20 — defer until most existing Story P2 work lands.

**Goal**: Story should achieve feature parity with Storybook. Use the construction of a /docs/Story tutorial set (mirroring https://storybook.js.org/docs/get-started/why-storybook React-tutorial tracks; ignore Vue/Svelte/etc sections) as a forcing function to discover gaps.

**Process**:

1. **Attempt to build the tutorial set** at /docs/Story — emulating the Storybook React tutorial structure, but leveraging re-frame2's strengths (immutable app-db, frames isolation, decorator-as-data, parallel-frames, machines, etc.) and idioms (no JSX, Reagent hiccup, EDN data shapes). Don't copy Storybook's surface — translate the *learning goals* into re-frame2-native shapes.

2. **As you attempt each tutorial section**, identify gaps:
   - **Capability gaps** — Story doesn't provide a feature Storybook does. File as P2/P3 feat bead with reproduction (the tutorial section that couldn't be written cleanly).
   - **Polish gaps** — Storybook is visually more polished. Use the **frontend design Skill** (or equivalent UI/UX review) to specify what's missing: animation timing, hover states, focus rings, typography hierarchy, spacing rhythm, dark-mode contrast, microcopy. File as P3 polish beads.
   - **DX gaps** — e2e tooling experience is rough. Story has Playwright-driven recording (rf2-l6jev work), but is the dev loop tight? Hot reload? Vite-equivalent fast feedback? File as P2/P3 DX beads.
   - **Insight gaps** — what does Storybook do conceptually that Story hasn't framed? Decorators as global/story/variant overlays already covered; what about: \"Args\" (typed prop tables with controls auto-derivation — rf2-b87h2 covered this), \"Play functions\" (rf2-wfizd open), Visual regression testing (Chromatic), Composition (linking multiple stories), Test runner ergonomics, Add-ons system, MDX-style documentation pages, Theming presets.

3. **Output**:
   - **Tutorial set** at /docs/Story (the docs are themselves a deliverable — they become Story's onboarding path)
   - **Manifest doc** at ai/findings/YYYY-MM-DD-story-vs-storybook-gap-audit.md (gitignored draft, then committed as tools/story/spec/Feature-Parity-Audit.md once stable)
   - **Per-gap beads** filed: capability/polish/DX/insight (use the frontend design Skill for polish reviews)

**Sequencing**:

- Phase A — Audit pass with the frontend design Skill (read-only; produce gap manifest)
- Phase B — Operator review of manifest (Mike decides which gaps to action; some may be deliberate divergence)
- Phase C — Per-bead implementations (parallel-dispatchable across distinct gaps)
- Phase D — Tutorial set written end-to-end (gates on most P2 gaps landing)

**Deferral condition**: defer this epic until the following Story P2 beads close:
- rf2-p1ai7 (Story modal ARIA)
- rf2-u01y5 (Story controls panel accessible names)
- rf2-wfizd (decision: :play vs :play-script — likely answered by Storybook tutorial parity)
- rf2-c2770 (Template :include-story? scaffolding)

**Why defer**: doing the parity audit now means the audit's gap list is polluted by gaps that are already in-flight or queued. Better to clear the ready Story backlog first, then audit against \"what's actually missing\".

Reference: Storybook React tutorial — https://storybook.js.org/docs/get-started/why-storybook
Frontend design Skill — TBD (review what's available; rf2-4w88j HCM/axe-core may be related).

Acceptance:
- /docs/Story tutorial set exists, structured as a learning ladder from \"hello world\" through advanced patterns
- Feature-Parity-Audit.md catalogues every Storybook capability + Story's coverage status (matches / divergent-by-design / gap)
- All gap beads filed and dispositioned (action / defer / reject) by Mike
close_reason: Substantially-done. Tutorial scope delivered by rf2-0pvm3 / PR #1799 (Yegge-voice refresh of /docs/story/ · 8 chapters · tutorial best-practices applied). The remaining 'Storybook gap audit' premise was explicitly de-scoped during rf2-0pvm3 (bead body: 'Dont constantly reference Storybook'); if useful later, file as its own scoped bead.

- If `:play-script` is the live-shell winner (DOM-steps + :assert-dom are the killer features), promote it to canonical in 001-Authoring.md §reg-variant and document it in API.md alongside `:play`.
- If `:play` is canonical, mark `:play-script` as v2-experimental in the testbed README so tutorial authors know to avoid it.

title: docs(story): document :fx-override last-wins asymmetry in 001-Authoring.md (F-7, rf2-l6jev)
description:
Decorator composition order:
- `:hiccup` — story decorators outermost, variant decorators innermost; LIFO walk (last decorator wraps first)
- `:frame-setup` — declared order (story then variant)
- `:fx-override` — declared order; collisions on `:fx-id` resolve LAST-WINS

The last-wins rule for `:fx-override` is the right call (the inner-most decorator is closest to the variant's intent) but it's not symmetric with the other kinds. A reader who learnt 'outermost wraps innermost' for `:hiccup` will be surprised by `:fx-override`'s 'innermost overrides outermost' inversion.

Tutorial impact (rf2-l6jev, F-7): Chapter 7 (decorators) has to explain the asymmetry. Doc gap, not a feature gap.

Direction: document the rule explicitly in tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md §reg-decorator — name the asymmetry so readers don't trip on it. One paragraph + a comparison table.

title: pair-mcp: rename :short-circuit? step predicate to :skip-when? in wire-boundary-pipeline
description:
Discovered from rf2-c8ohr (re-frame2-pair-mcp wire-surface audit, Finding #6 — minor).

tools/boundary_step.cljs:55-61 and the apply-cache-step / apply-cap-step predicates in tools.cljs:147-177. The :short-circuit? predicate runs BEFORE its step; a truthy result skips THIS step but the pipeline continues to the next step.

A reader who sees :short-circuit? expects halt-the-chain semantics; the actual semantics are 'this step is opt-out for this context'. The name is a false friend.

Action: rename :short-circuit? -> :skip-when? across the wire-boundary-pipeline step shape. Update the boundary-step ns docstring + the four step defs in tools.cljs. Pre-alpha posture: no back-compat shim, hard rename. Small surface, ~5-10 line refactor.

Evidence: tools/boundary_step.cljs:55-61,88-95; tools.cljs:159-177.
close_reason: Closed

title: pair-mcp: unify elision-opts-edn polarity between :include-large? and :include-sensitive?
description:
Discovered from rf2-c8ohr (re-frame2-pair-mcp wire-surface audit, Finding #5 — minor).

tools/elision.cljs:79-82. The walker's :include-large? opt is computed as (not enabled?) (so when MCP arg elision=true, the walker emits markers). :include-sensitive? is computed as (boolean include-sensitive?) — no flip. Two sibling walker opts, opposite parsing rules.

The polarity-flip is semantically correct (MCP arg 'elision' = apply the walker; walker opt :include-large? = pass large slots through). But sibling-opt asymmetry reads as accretion.

Direction options:
  (a) Rename MCP arg 'elision' -> 'elide' (matches walker emit-side action: elide true => emit markers, aligning with :include-sensitive? true => pass-through), OR
  (b) Rename walker opt :include-large? -> :elide-large? (aligns with include-sensitive?'s pass-through polarity).

Both have downstream impact (wire docs + sibling story-mcp). Pick one polarity and unify the pair. Mike's call on direction; impl scope is small.
close_reason: Closed

title: pair-mcp: decide whether wire-pipeline and snapshot-pipeline consolidate or document the split
description:
Discovered from rf2-c8ohr (re-frame2-pair-mcp wire-surface audit, Finding #3 — major).

tools/wire_pipeline.cljs (per-tool post-eval shrink, dispatching on :kind :epoch-vector | :snapshot-map | :scalar-value) and tools/snapshot_pipeline.cljs (snapshot-specific path-slicing, summarisation, diff-encode/dedup of :epochs slices) overlap conceptually.

The snapshot tool body invokes wp/run-wire-pipeline with :kind :snapshot-map, which inside calls into the snapshot-pipeline functions. wire-pipeline = orchestrator; snapshot-pipeline = dispatchee — but both are full namespaces with their own docstrings; a reader following :kind :snapshot-map walks across two files.

Direction options:
  (a) Merge snapshot-pipeline into wire-pipeline (one file owns all post-eval shrink, :kind-dispatched per-kind transforms). Cost: reintroduces leaf-size pressure.
  (b) Document the split rationale at wire-pipeline ns docstring ('snapshot-specific transforms are factored to snapshot-pipeline because the path-slicing + slice-mode resolution is more elaborate than other kinds need'). Lighter touch.

Decision-flavored: this is a structural call for Mike before any code moves. Evidence: tools/snapshot.cljs:106-146, tools/snapshot_pipeline.cljs:28-164.
close_reason: Decided: (b) document the split. Mayor + Mike's 'don't block on me' directive · 2026-05-20. snapshot-pipeline's specialised path-slicing stays factored out; wire-pipeline gets ns-docstring explanation. Implementation filed as follow-on.

title: audit-followon(mcp-conformance): document JSON-RPC error-code union in NAMING.md / vocab.cljc (rf2-li7dw F5)
description:
Audit rf2-li7dw F5: JSON-RPC error-code contract under-documented.

`tools/mcp-conformance/test/_runner.cjs` (`assertJsonRpcErrorCodes`, L204–238) accepts either `-32602 InvalidParams` OR `-32603 InternalError` for malformed `tools/call` (missing :name). Per the in-code comment: JSON-RPC §5.1 reads -32602; SDK actually emits -32603; accepting the union prevents an SDK tightening from breaking the gate.

The pragmatism is correct. The documentation gap is that the union lives in **only** that comment. `NAMING.md` §Error-vocabulary alignment (L163–177) catalogues the `:rf.error/*` / `:rf.epoch/*` / `:<server>.error/*` keyword namespaces but says nothing about the JSON-RPC code layer. `mcp-base/vocab.cljc` (referenced as canonical home of every code constant) is the right anchor but agents/contributors reading the cross-MCP docs see no answer.

Direction: add a §"JSON-RPC error codes" subsection under `NAMING.md` §Error-vocabulary documenting the cross-MCP contract:
- `-32601 MethodNotFound` — canonical for unknown JSON-RPC method
- `-32602 InvalidParams` / `-32603 InternalError` — both conformant for malformed-params today; a Lock entry in `vocab.cljc` records the choice
- the conformance gate accepts the union to absorb SDK behaviour drift

title: audit-followon(mcp-conformance): NAMING.md violates its own single-source-of-truth tool-count rule (rf2-li7dw F4)

  ### Story-mcp (19 tools)

The doc's own §"Single source of truth for tool counts" (L122–161) says: "Every other doc that needs to cite the count links to the catalogue rather than repeating the integer."

(a) Tighten — replace the integer in each heading with a `[see catalogue]` link; audit table loses an annotated count column but the doc stops self-violating.
(b) Formalise — add an explicit exception to §"Single source of truth" saying "audit snapshot tables MAY carry an integer count, pinned to last-audit-pass".

title: fix(schemas): walker should emit :rf.warning/schema-walker-opaque for non-vector schema forms (rf2-ycqtv finding #12)
description:
rf2-ycqtv audit Finding #12 (nit). The Malli schema walker (re-frame.schemas.walker) handles only vector-form Malli EDN — compiled m/schema values and registry refs are treated as opaque leaves. Per-slot :sensitive? / :large? flags inside an opaque value are SILENTLY skipped. The walker's docstring at walker.cljc:37-69 documents this discoverability caveat but no warning fires — a user that registers (rf/reg-app-schema [:user] :my/user-schema) and puts :sensitive? per-slot flags inside the registry-ref schema gets no redaction on validation-failure traces, and no signal that the flags were ignored.

Direction: emit a one-shot :rf.warning/schema-walker-opaque at reg-app-schema registration time when the registered schema is not a vector form. Symmetric with :rf.warning/schema-validator-unavailable warn-once-per-process pattern. Cost: one boot-time predicate per reg-app-schema call.

The two workable shapes (vector form, or registration-meta :sensitive? fallback) stay documented; the warn-once is the discoverability nudge.

Owner: implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc (registration-time check); requires new entry in Spec 010 § and Spec 009 §Error event catalogue. Inputs: ai/findings/2026-05-20-schemas-api-review.md §Finding 12.

Owner: spec/API.md §Registration. Inputs: ai/findings/2026-05-20-schemas-api-review.md §Finding 6.

title: feat(re-frame2): test-helpers — handle Reagent class-3 components + convention re :data-testid vs :data-test
description:
## Source

Per rf2-piucm worker report (PR #1611): the just-shipped framework-level `re-frame.test-helpers` (from rf2-irp6j PR #1605) doesn't handle Reagent class-3 components gracefully — it crashes on `r/create-class` instances. Also keys on `:data-testid` while Story uses `:data-test`.

## Two coupled gaps

### Gap 1: Reagent class-3 handling

`expand-tree` in test-helpers.cljc walks function components but crashes on `r/create-class` instances. Real-world re-frame2 apps + tools (Story, Causa) mix function components and class-3 components freely.

**Fix**: `expand-tree` should detect class-3 and expand via the appropriate render path (typically `(.render impl)` or by accessing the `:reagent-render` slot of the class config).

### Gap 2: :data-testid vs :data-test convention

re-frame.test-helpers/find-by-testid keys on `:data-testid` (React convention). Story uses `:data-test` (legacy convention from pre-rename). Causa uses `data-rf-causa-*` (own prefix).

**Options**:
- (a) Test-helpers accepts both `:data-test` and `:data-testid`; documented as 'either convention works'
- (b) Test-helpers accepts a configurable attribute key; `find-by-attr [tree attr val]` as a generalisation, with `find-by-testid` as a thin wrapper
- (c) Sweep Story to migrate `:data-test` → `:data-testid`. Larger surface, breaks compatibility.

Recommend (b) — most flexible, no migration cost.

## Acceptance

- expand-tree handles class-3 components without crashing
- find-by-attr generalisation present + find-by-testid stays as the common-case wrapper
- Story's existing `:data-test` selectors work via find-by-attr
- Tests added covering both gaps

## Cite

PR #1611 (rf2-piucm) worker report — Helpers section.
PR #1605 (rf2-irp6j) — original test-helpers shipping.
close_reason: Closed

title: spec(causa): DESIGN-RATIONALE — Lock #17: Visual language REJECT patterns (no commodity fonts / addons / pixels-as-first-class)
description: rf2-vtd5z audit (Causa-JS-devtools lessons) produced normative REJECT patterns that drove this session's design polish: 'no commodity fonts' (Fraunces display face for chrome surfaces, not system-ui); 'no addon-per-concern' (one density knob via one CSS var, not size-axes-per-feature); 'no pixels-as-first-class' (every type/spacing/motion value is a token, never a magic number). These are direction-setting REJECT decisions that drove rf2-5kfxe (design polish), rf2-n8i2c (--rf-causa-font-size calc-anchor), and rf2-ybjkx (Cmd-K palette as single nav primitive rather than addon-per-tab). Currently no lock points to them. See ai/findings/2026-05-19-causa-spec-currency-audit.md §L5.
design: Add Lock #17 — Visual language locks (REJECT patterns). Locked 2026-05-19 (Mike) per rf2-vtd5z audit. Question: what does Causa's visual identity reject? Pick (three REJECTs as one lock): (1) no commodity fonts — Fraunces display face for L1 ribbon + mode pill + chord callouts, Inter for UI sans, JetBrains Mono for data; NOT system-ui as the chrome face. (2) no addon-per-concern growth — one density knob = one CSS var = --rf-causa-font-size, not three different size axes per addon; the Cmd-K palette is the cross-tab nav primitive, NOT per-tab burger menus. (3) no pixels-as-first-class — every type / spacing / motion value is a token (e.g. type-scale resolved via calc anchor; spacing on the 4px grid; motion via the three duration tiers in Principles.md). Magic numbers are reviewable as bugs. Why: Causa's UX is dev-tool-class; the audit found peer tools (TanStack Query Devtools, Vue DevTools, Vite DevTools) that drifted to commodity fonts + addon-soup + magic-number sprawl, and the lock prevents that path. Cross-reference: ai/findings/2026-05-19-causa-js-devtools-lessons.md (the audit doc). Date locked: 2026-05-19.

title: docs(story): record Storybook anti-patterns Story explicitly rejects — rf2-38pb9 follow-on
description:
## From rf2-38pb9 audit

The audit surfaced eight Storybook patterns Story should explicitly NOT adopt. Story's DESIGN-RATIONALE already records four of these (CSF Factories, first-party visual regression, component-co-located fixtures, MCP server in-process). The audit found four more worth recording so future workers don't drift back.

## Anti-patterns to record in tools/story/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md §Rejected

1. **Brand pink / hot accent on cold grey chrome** — Storybook's #FF4785 on #333 is a Material-floor combo; amber-on-warm-slate is Story's signature.
2. **Inter / Nunito Sans / system-ui as default font** — the IBM Plex pick is identity-bearing. PRs proposing 'platform consistency' fonts should be challenged.
3. **Addon-per-concern architecture** — Storybook fragments theme + viewport + locale + a11y + actions + measure + outline + highlight into separate addons. Story uses reg-mode :axis + reg-story-panel + force-fx-stub to collapse the surface. Question every 'let's add an addon for X' against existing registries.
4. **Throw-on-first-failure for assertions** — Storybook throws on first failed assertion; Story records into :assertions and continues (DESIGN-RATIONALE §record-not-throw). Future test-mode work should not drift back.

(Items 1-2 are NEW additions; items 3-4 reinforce existing rationale with explicit Storybook-comparison framing.)

## Acceptance criteria

- DESIGN-RATIONALE.md §Rejected section gains a 'Storybook commodity patterns' subsection listing each of the four, each with: pattern name, what Storybook does, why Story rejects, what Story does instead
- Cross-reference back to ai/findings/2026-05-19-storybook-design-lessons.md (gitignored; cite the audit bead rf2-38pb9 instead)
- One paragraph at the section head explaining that 'Storybook is the popular comparator; copying its choices would erase Story's identity'

## Severity
LOW — documentation polish. The anti-patterns are observed in practice; the doc capture is defensive future-worker guidance.

## Hot-zone
DESIGN-RATIONALE.md is in tools/story/spec/. Not on the global hot-zone list but is touched by other Story workers — coordinate with Phase 2 cluster (rf2-p0wur + rf2-v58dm + rf2-v1ach) before editing.

## Out of scope
- Editing the existing four §Rejected entries (just add the new subsection)

title: enh(scripts): extend rf2-flzdp drift gate to cover Bash(...) entries (rf2-l3jq1 follow-on)
description:
Per the skill-creator audit (rf2-l3jq1), the existing skill↔MCP drift gate (`scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py`, rf2-flzdp) only checks `mcp__<prefix>__*` entries — it cannot catch Bash-prefix gaps like the one filed under rf2-scpaa (re-frame-migration missing `Bash(gh issue *)` despite cardinal rule 7 instructing the agent to file GitHub issues).

**Evidence:**
- `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py:204-210` — the `STRICT_NAME_RE` regex extracts `{:name '...'}` from MCP-server-source-cljs/cljc files; there is no corresponding extraction for Bash allow-list checks.
- `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py:300` — `prefix_marker = f'mcp__{host_prefix}__'` filters only MCP entries from the skill's `allowed-tools` block; Bash entries are dropped.
- Cross-skill body inspection (grep `gh issue`, `shadow-cljs`, etc.) shows SKILL.md bodies referencing CLI commands; agents will trip the permission gate when allow-lists don't match.

**Effect:** silent skill↔body drift on Bash surfaces. Audit found one concrete instance (re-frame-migration); other instances may exist or be introduced going forward.

**Recommendation:** extend the drift gate with a second class of cross-check:

1. Parse `Bash(...)` entries from each skill's `allowed-tools` frontmatter — collect into a normalised set (e.g. `gh-issue-create`, `shadow-cljs-compile`).
2. Lex the SKILL.md body for references to those binaries / commands (rg patterns: `gh issue create`, `shadow-cljs compile`, `npm install`, `clojure -M:test`).
3. Report MISSING-IN-ALLOWLIST when the body references a command the allow-list doesn't permit.
4. Optional reverse: MISSING-IN-BODY (allow-list permits a command not referenced anywhere — pure cleanup signal).

A simpler v0 — just maintain a hand-curated MAPPING table of (skill, expected-bash-prefix) per the Published-skill `allowed-tools` baseline in `skills/README.md`. That's enough to catch the four or five common-command surfaces (`gh issue *`, `gh pr *`, `npm *`, `shadow-cljs *`, `clojure -Stree*`).

**Acceptance:**
- `scripts/check_skill_mcp_drift.py` (or a sibling script) catches the rf2-scpaa case before it lands.
- CI gate either folded into the existing rf2-flzdp workflow step or run as a sibling step in `.github/workflows/test.yml` on skill-path-changes only.
- Baseline support analogous to the MCP gate's `_BASELINE` so the gate can land before all existing gaps are closed.

title: docs(mcp-base): document the handler-arity divergence between pair-mcp (3-arity) and story-mcp (1-arity) (rf2-h1izl follow-on C7)
description:
Per audit rf2-h1izl Finding C7 (LOW).

## Problem

The two MCP servers use DIFFERENT registry-handler arities:

- tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/registry.cljs:41-45,89-103 — every handler is (fn [conn args extra]).
- tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/registry.cljc:14 — every handler is (fn [args] result-map-or-error).

Reason: pair-mcp uses conn for the nREPL session (browser runtime) and extra for streaming subscribe callbacks (real surface). Story-mcp is JVM-side single-process, neither slot has meaning.

Impact: cross-MCP-aware tooling (mcp-base) cannot abstract the handler invocation shape; each server dispatcher is a distinct implementation. Adds friction for a future fourth MCP author who consults both as examples (and immediately for the causa-mcp impl per C1 / rf2-hvl1g).

## Recommendation

Two-phase approach:

### Phase 1 (this bead) — document the divergence

- Add tools/mcp-base/spec/handler-arity.md (new file): explains the two shapes, why they diverge (pair-mcp nREPL conn + streaming extra; story-mcp pure-data), and acknowledges this as a deliberate gap pending crystallisation across three servers.
- Reference from each server registry ns docstring.
- File a follow-on bead Phase 2 for the unification once causa-mcp lands (C1) and crystallises a third instance.

### Phase 2 (future, separate bead — not part of THIS work)

- Factor an explicit ExecutionContext type into mcp-base (likely a record / map with optional :conn / :progress-callback / :request-meta slots).
- Refit both servers to (fn [ctx args]) handler shape.
- Causa-mcp adopts the unified shape from day one.

## Hot-zone

Phase 1 is doc-only: new file tools/mcp-base/spec/handler-arity.md + two registry-ns docstring tweaks. Safe to land standalone.

## Acceptance

- tools/mcp-base/spec/handler-arity.md exists and reads cleanly.
- pair-mcp + story-mcp registry ns docstrings reference the new doc.
- Phase 2 unification bead filed for post-C1 (causa-mcp) execution.

title: fix(scripts+template): strengthen worker worktree boundary detection
description:
rf2-zszmu audit worker wrote findings to mayor checkout instead of its worktree (worker's report cited ). The worktree-boundary block in dispatch-prompt-template.md is supposed to prevent this; it didn't.

## Hypothesis
The worker correctly invoked the guard script + got the right WORKTREE_ROOT. But path-resolution during file Write leaked because the worker used a repo-relative path that resolved against the session root (mayor checkout) instead of the worker's git root.

## Method
- scripts/assert-worker-worktree.ps1 currently prints WORKTREE_ROOT on success. Extend to print a 'CANARY' file path under WORKTREE_ROOT/ai/findings/.canary that worker should write to FIRST. Mayor post-dispatch can verify the canary landed in the worker worktree, not the mayor checkout.
- Alternatively: add a mayor-side post-dispatch check that runs  and warns if NEW files appear there (since findings should be gitignored and ONLY created by workers in their own worktrees, the mayor checkout's ai/findings/ should stay empty).

## Acceptance
- A worker that 'accidentally' writes to mayor checkout's ai/findings/ is caught BEFORE submitting its report
- The dispatch-prompt-template.md gains a 'canary' protocol or 'verify-after-first-write' step

## Source
Session observation 2026-05-19: rf2-zszmu worker leaked the findings doc into the mayor checkout. We managed (the file is gitignored so no harm), but the boundary failed silently.

title: fix(docs): repair link rot blocking mkdocs --strict
description:
mkdocs build --strict aborts on broken cross-doc links. Two distinct categories:

## Category A — skills/ file links into repo spec/ tree (~12 warnings)
skills/re-frame2-implementor.md uses '../spec/001-Registration.md', '../spec/002-Frames.md', '../spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md', '../spec/004-Views.md', '../spec/009-Instrumentation.md', '../spec/000-Vision.md', '../spec/Implementor-Checklist.md', '../spec/conformance/README.md' etc.

Root cause: skills/ is built INTO the mkdocs site (so mkdocs treats relative ../spec/ links as broken because repo spec/ is not in docs/ nav). 

Fix options:
- (a) Exclude skills/ from mkdocs build entirely (skills are AI-targeted source, not user docs)
- (b) Rewrite ../spec/ links to absolute GitHub URLs (e.g. https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/blob/main/spec/001-Registration.md)
- (c) Mirror or symlink spec/ into docs/spec/ so the links resolve

Recommend (a) — cleanest, matches intent. mkdocs.yml exclude pattern + verify gh-pages doesn't lose anything.

## Category B — missing anchor in existing doc (~1 warning)
guide/24-configuration-and-safety/01-framework-config.md links to '../../spec/Security.md#epoch-privacy-posture--raw-in-process-records-vs-projected-egress' but that anchor is missing from spec/Security.md.

Fix: either re-add the heading, OR remove the anchor portion of the link to land on the top of Security.md.

## Acceptance
- mkdocs build --strict exits 0 (currently aborts with 6+ warnings on main)
- gh-pages deploy not affected
- No accidental loss of user-discoverable docs
notes: PR #1540. Root-cause fix (not Cat A or Cat B from the bead). mkdocs_hooks.py gains on_pre_build that auto-stages spec/ + migration/ into docs_dir. The bead's symptoms (skills/ warnings, Security.md anchor) were all consequences of unstaged spec/ + migration/, not actual link rot — after staging both, every warning resolves. Before: Aborted with 72 warnings (clean checkout); after: 0 warnings. tools/causa/spec/018-Event-Spine.md was a separate slug-check failure already fixed upstream in PR #1536.
close_reason: PR #1540 merged 2026-05-19. Root-cause fix: mkdocs_hooks.py on_pre_build auto-stages spec/+migration/ into docs_dir. CI had it via .github/workflows/docs.yml; local builds didn't. Resolves --strict warnings (72→0) without skills/ exclusion or anchor restoration.

title: feat(flows): add :before slot to :rf.flow/computed payload (rf2-oz0m7 polish)
description:
**Source:** ai/findings/2026-05-19-flow-trace-events-audit.md (rf2-oz0m7 audit).

## What

Add a :before slot to the :rf.flow/computed trace event's :tags, carrying the pre-write value at the flow's :path. Currently :rf.flow/computed carries :result (the new value) but not the before value — Causa's Event Detail panel (rf2-lo37i) and the App-db diff origin-tagging (rf2-s8r6c) currently recover the before-value from the cascade's :db-before snapshot, which works but means the flow trace stream is not fully self-contained.

## Why this is polish, not required

The three rf2-oz0m7 sibling beads (rf2-lo37i / rf2-s8r6c / rf2-tv8t1) can all ship today using the existing emit sites — :flow-id, input paths, output path, after-value, cascade position via :dispatch-id are all present. The before-value is recoverable from the epoch record's :db-before slot which Causa already holds. This bead adds optional self-contained-ness to the flow trace stream.

## Concrete change

In implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows.cljc, evaluate-flow!'s success branch (around line 136):

```clojure
(let [new-output (apply (:output flow) new-inputs)
      old-output (get-in db (:path flow))          ;; NEW
      new-db     (assoc-in db (:path flow) new-output)]
  ;; ...
  (trace/emit! :flow :rf.flow/computed
               {:flow-id      flow-id
                :input-values ...
                :result       (elision/elide-wire-value new-output ...)
                :before       (elision/elide-wire-value old-output ...)  ;; NEW
                :path         (:path flow)
                :frame        frame-id}))
```

Under the existing interop/debug-enabled? gate so prod is unaffected. Elided through elision/elide-wire-value matching the :result slot for size/sensitive handling.

## Spec updates

- spec/009-Instrumentation.md §Flow trace events: add :before to the :rf.flow/computed row's :tags payload column.
- spec/013-Flows.md §Flow tracing summary table: align with the 009 entry.

## Tests

- Add a flows_trace_test case asserting :before is present on :rf.flow/computed and equals the pre-write value at :path.
- Add a case asserting the first-evaluation :before is nil (last-inputs was uninitialised so the path was unwritten before).

## Citations

- Parent: rf2-oz0m7 (audit verdict: PARTIAL — this is the one soft gap).
- Audit doc: ai/findings/2026-05-19-flow-trace-events-audit.md (see §Gap analysis + §Recommendation).

title: docs(spec): author guidance for ex-data + exception messages under path-level :sensitive? (rf2-4ku9l follow-on)
description:
Mike decision 2026-05-19 (closure of rf2-4ku9l under path-level model in spec/015): add author guidance for the residual exception-path leak surface. 

The path-level :sensitive? model in spec/015-Data-Classification.md redacts at 5 observation surfaces (trace bus emit, Causa, MCP, AI/LLM context, third-party log sinks). It does NOT walk exception messages or ex-data automatically. The author must ensure they don't stuff sensitive-path values into exception strings or ex-data maps.

## Scope (doc-only, ~10-15 line edits)

### spec/Security.md §Privacy / secret handling
Add paragraph:

> ### Author guidance for exceptions under path-level :sensitive?
> 
> The framework's path-level :sensitive? declarations (spec/015) redact at 5 observation surfaces — trace bus, Causa, MCP, AI/LLM context, third-party log sinks. The framework does NOT walk exception messages or ex-data automatically to redact values that originated from sensitive paths.
>
> Author responsibility: when throwing inside a handler that reads sensitive-path values, do not include those values in:
> - The exception message string (e.g. avoid (str (get-in db [:user :password])))
> - The ex-data map (e.g. avoid {:event event-vector :password (get-in db [:user :password])})
>
> Common-case safety: if a handler reads a sensitive path, computes derived state, writes to app-db, and a downstream trace event captures the new app-db, redaction WILL happen at emit-time. The exception path is the gap.

### spec/015-Data-Classification.md §Author guidance (or new section)
Cross-link to the Security.md paragraph + add example:

> When a sensitive-handler throws:
>
> Clojure 1.12.4
user=>

title: fix(examples): EXAMPLES_FILTER narrows build but not spec runner on Windows
description:
Discovered by rf2-dbiut worker (2026-05-19, PR #1514 worker report):

> EXAMPLES_FILTER behaviour: the build narrows correctly (only causa-rhs-smoke compiled) but the inner spec runner still scans all 20 spec files. The 18 unrelated '404 / build artifact missing' failures are a runner-harness quirk on Windows, NOT regressions — only the filtered build was compiled.

## Symptom
`EXAMPLES_FILTER=causa-rhs-smoke npm run test:examples` (or equivalent shadow-cljs filter) compiles only one build but the playwright/spec runner attempts to load all 20 spec files. Specs whose builds weren't compiled fail with '404 / build artifact missing'. The intended scoped run becomes noisy.

## Repro
1. `cd implementation`
2. `EXAMPLES_FILTER=causa-rhs-smoke npm run test:examples` (or however the Windows path is — set env var via PowerShell `$env:EXAMPLES_FILTER='causa-rhs-smoke'; npm run test:examples`)
3. Observe: only causa-rhs-smoke build compiles, but 18+ specs fail with missing-artifact errors

## Expected
The runner should ALSO filter the spec list to specs matching the filter expression, not just the compile step.

## Surface
Likely `examples/scripts/run-examples-tests.cjs` or `examples/scripts/serve-and-run-examples-tests.cjs` — wherever the playwright spec list is enumerated. The filter logic is in one place (the build narrowing) but missing from the spec-runner enumeration.

## Acceptance
- EXAMPLES_FILTER=foo narrows BOTH build AND spec discovery to specs matching foo
- Specs for non-matched builds are SKIPPED (not run + fail)
- Works on Windows + Unix

## Memo (re saved memory orchestrator-filter-substring-trap-2026-05-18)
The path-separator substring trap is still load-bearing — this fix preserves that behaviour (specs filtered by path-substring match) but extends it to the spec discovery step too.

## Parent
rf2-dbiut (closed). Discovered while running per-spec smoke.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #1520. EXAMPLES_FILTER now narrows BOTH build AND spec runner. Specs for non-matched builds SKIPPED. Path-substring trap preserved per saved memory orchestrator-filter-substring-trap-2026-05-18.

title: feat(epoch): annotate egress projection with redacted-paths-modified count (rf2-bz1cl follow-on)
description:
Causa's redacted-paths-modified chip (rf2-bz1cl) currently derives a heuristic count from raw epoch records: paths where both :db-before and :db-after carry :rf/redacted AND the parent subtree's pointer differs. The heuristic is a tight upper bound (every counted path is in a mutated subtree) but it CAN over-state when a sibling slot changed and the redacted slot was incidentally untouched.

Enhancement: thread an accurate counter through the egress contract / epoch record assembly. Compute, at the moment the :redact-fn would substitute the sentinel (or, equivalently, before egress projection), the SET of paths whose underlying value actually differed between db-before/db-after. title: bug(causa): Views panel header shows :cart-frame cascade 35 while body says 'No event focused'

title: feat(substrate): cross-frame sub computation — first-class affordance for multi-frame data routing
description:
Per PR #1479 (rf2-yhxk3 shop testbed) worker observation. Subs are per-frame (Spec 006); when consolidating a single-frame demo to multi-frame, you either route data to the consuming frame's app-db (loses semantic colocation) or hand-roll cross-frame projection. The shop testbed had to put :checkout/snapshot, :checkout/tax-rate, :checkout/shipping on cart-frame's app-db because :cart/subtotal-WRONG (deliberately-wrong sub for the 3pm tutorial) needs to read them from the cart-panel's frame-provider scope.

Proposal: a first-class 'cross-frame sub' affordance. Options:
(a) :rf.subs/cross-frame metadata — sub declares it needs values from another frame; substrate handles the cross-frame deref
(b) :rf.subs/projection helper — given a frame-id + path, returns a deref-able value scoped to that frame
(c) accept as-is; document the 'route data home' pattern

Discovered from PR #1479 rf2-yhxk3. Doc'd inline in tools/causa/testbeds/shop/core.cljs LAYER 5 comments + README frames table.
close_reason: REJECTED — frames are isolated reactive contexts by design. Subs MUST NOT reach into other frames. Cross-frame sub computation in any shape (metadata, projection helper, documented 'route data home' pattern) is an anti-pattern. The shop testbed (rf2-yhxk3) that surfaced this is itself an anti-pattern and needs rebuilding. Architectural rule saved in feedback memory: frames-are-isolated-contexts. Replacement testbed bead will be filed separately (one app mounted in :above + :below frames, each isolated, exercises Causa's frame-switching + full feature surface).

title: feat(causa): hydration debugger sub-attribution panel
description:
Follow-on to rf2-1mcax (Phase 4 of rf2-abts7, structural-diff epic).

Phase 4 shipped the bisector + Phase-3 hiccup engine adoption for per-pane rendering. Sub-attribution was deferred: the runtime does not yet emit a per-side sub-runs trace event during SSR (server-side vs client-side), so the panel cannot surface 'subscription :user/locale returned nil on server vs :en-US on client' yet.

## Scope
- Substrate change: re-frame2 SSR pipeline emits :rf.ssr/sub-run trace events tagged with :side {:server | :client} during hydration
- hydration_debugger panel surfaces a 'sub-attribution' section under each mismatch detail:
  - Match server-side sub-runs vs client-side sub-runs by [sub-id query-v]
  - For each diverging sub: surface the structural diff of the return value (re-use Phase 1 sections-per-cluster renderer)
  - For each sub whose return is the divergent value at the mismatched node, surface the app-db slice each side observed

## Acceptance
- New :rf.ssr/sub-run trace event in Spec 011
- Substrate emits one per sub-run during server render + client first render
- Causa surfaces a 'Sub attribution' section in the hydration debugger drilldown
- Tests cover the per-side projection + matching

## Why this is deferred
Phase 4's bisector + per-pane hiccup-render lands without sub-attribution because the SSR side of the substrate does not yet emit per-sub-run traces during hydration. The bisector + diff annotation answers WHERE/WHAT diverges; sub-attribution answers WHY. WHY needs new runtime emissions.

title: fix(story): :play-script :pred symbol resolution under advanced CLJS (rf2-8i2a9 follow-on)
description:
Follow-on from rf2-8i2a9 PR #1411.

The :pred form of :assert-db ([:assert-db path :pred fn-sym]) resolves the symbol differently per target:

- JVM: requiring-resolve — works for any namespace-qualified symbol on the classpath.
- CLJS: best-effort goog.global walk on munged dotted names — only finds fns that are :^export'd or reachable from window.<ns>.<name>.

Under advanced compilation, ns names get mangled by closure; the goog.global walk won't find author-defined predicates unless they're explicitly exported.

## Scope
- Build a Story predicates registry (a small reg-pred surface) so authors register their predicates by keyword id ([:assert-db path :pred :my-app/positive?]).
- Update runner-events to look up via the registry instead of resolving symbols.
- Keep the symbol form as a JVM-only escape hatch (or deprecate it).
- Migrate the existing single test that uses 'clojure.core/pos?'.

## Coordination
- The framework registrar already hosts ALL re-frame kinds (event, sub, fx, cofx, …); a sibling Story kind :predicate would be the natural home.
- :loaders-complete-when uses a similar pattern — coordinate so both consume the same registry.

## Done when
- reg-predicate or equivalent ships; advanced-CLJS-compiled stories can use :pred resolution; tests gate green.
close_reason: Shipped via PR #1457 (merged 2026-05-18). :play-script :pred accepts fn-direct OR symbol; fn-direct works under advanced CLJS without ^:export tagging.
