title: design(causa): consider shipping built-in resize handle (auto-injected or opt-in via configure!) (pitch8 field feedback)
description:
From pitch8.com.au mayor session 2026-05-17 (real-world v1→v2 migration), item 6 (low-confidence ask).

## The proposal
Every Causa consumer will want a resize handle. Shipping it in Causa means projects don't reinvent + diverge. Two delivery modes:
- (a) Auto-injected: Causa detects [data-rf-causa-host] and mounts a resize handle next to it
- (b) Opt-in: (causa-config/configure! {:layout/resizable? true}) opts in to the built-in handle

## Tradeoffs
- PRO: Consistency across Causa consumers; one canonical drag UX; no reinvention; less project boilerplate
- CON: More Causa surface area; weighs against re-frame2's 'minimal default' stance; projects with custom layout chrome may want to opt-out anyway
- Pitch8 mayor noted: 'Not strongly held; doc fix (item 5) covers most of the value' — so this is OPTIONAL

## Mike's design call
Two paths:
- (A) Doc-only path (item 5 from sibling bead) is sufficient. Decline this work. The canonical pattern in the recipe doc covers 95% of value at 5% of cost.
- (B) Ship the built-in handle. Requires design exploration: which mode (auto-injected vs opt-in), how to handle projects that want their own handle, a11y, pointer events, mobile/touch, persistence.

Recommend (A) for now — sibling bead's doc cluster will likely close the gap. Re-visit only if MULTIPLE consumer projects reinvent diverging handles after the doc lands.

## NOT gated on #1373
Different surface (tools/causa/src/). But low-priority pending Mike's design call.

- pitch8.com.au mayor session output, pasted by Mike 2026-05-17 (item 6)

title: decide(epoch): projected-record idempotence under :large? markers
description:
Source: rf2-xrlyi MCP-egress conformance test (epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj) discovered that `projected-record` is NOT idempotent under repeated application when the record carries a `:large?`-declared slot. On the second projection pass, `elide-wire-value` re-walks the previous pass's marker map (which itself sits at the same `:large?`-declared path) and substitutes a NEW marker — whose :bytes reflects the printed length of the previous marker. The :sensitive? substitution IS idempotent (the :rf/redacted scalar sentinel is not re-matchable by the walker).

## Why the asymmetry

`:rf/redacted` is a scalar keyword — the walker has no larger structure to descend into when it encounters one at a sensitive-declared path. The :rf.size/large-elided marker is a map carrying `:path` / `:bytes` / `:digest` / `:handle`; the walker sees a map at the still-:large?-declared path and treats it as a new value to substitute.

## Decision needed (Mike)

1. **Don't fix — document only.** A forwarder pipeline that double-projects is a bug (waste). Document the asymmetry in Spec Security.md §Epoch privacy posture and move on. The rf2-xrlyi test pins the sensitive-irreversibility guarantee (which is the security-load-bearing one); large-marker drift is a recordkeeping wobble, not a leak.

2. **Make `elide-wire-value` marker-aware.** Teach the walker to pass markers through unchanged: if `(elision/marker? v)` at a :large?-declared path, return `v` rather than re-marking. Pros: full idempotence; downstream forwarders compose safely. Cons: an edge case in the walker; potential drift between fresh and re-projected marker bytes (the FIRST pass's :bytes reflects the original payload; cheaper for clients to compare).

3. **Make `projected-record` short-circuit on already-projected records.** Add a record-level flag (e.g. `:rf.epoch/projected?` true) that short-circuits the entire wire-elision walk. Pros: cheap; explicit contract. Cons: another bookkeeping slot; doesn't help direct-read consumers that hand a marker to elide-wire-value outside the projected-record path.

## Ref

- rf2-pk8ur sibling (rf2-kp835 Phase-3 follow-on cluster)
- rf2-xrlyi MCP egress conformance test (`forwarder-projected-record-is-sensitive-idempotent` documents the asymmetry inline)
- Spec Security.md §Epoch privacy posture (line 104) — projection is the off-box egress contract
close_reason: Decision (Mike 2026-05-17): Option 2 — marker-aware walker. Walker now passes through existing :rf.size/large-elided markers at :large?-declared paths, making projected-record uniformly idempotent across both :sensitive? and :large? substitutions. Pre-alpha masterpiece bar: fix at root, no shim. PR #1362. Conformance pinned by forwarder-projected-record-is-large-idempotent in epoch_mcp_egress_conformance_test.clj; focused walker unit tests in core/elision_test.clj; Security.md off-box-egress bullet updated.

title: test(causa): flaky 'Expected at least one trace op-type filter chip' in rigorous spec.cjs §6
description:
The rigorous testbed's section 6 (trace panel: row growth, filter activation, filter clearing) intermittently fails at line 375 with:

    Expected at least one trace op-type filter chip.

Failure rate observed during Tier-2 cluster work (rf2-5aw5v.9..14, 10x repeat runs against a freshly-served counter bundle): ~1 in 10. Confirmed pre-existing — reproduced with the Tier-2 spec sections (12–16) stashed out.

Section 6 calls `clearTraceBuffer(page)` then `waitForCondition` for a settled below-cap state, then expects `[data-testid^="rf-causa-trace-axis-chip-op-type-"]` to have >= 1. The intermittent failure suggests the trace panel's filter chip row hasn't rendered any chip yet — likely a race between the buffer clear (which drops all events) and a render cascade re-populating the buffer with at least one event whose op-type makes it past the panel's chip-row filter.

Repro: from `implementation/`:

    cd implementation
    npx shadow-cljs compile examples/counter
    mkdir -p out/examples/counter && cp ../examples/reagent/counter/index.html out/examples/counter/
    node scripts/run-rigorous-only.cjs   # rerun ~10 times; ~1 in 10 fails

Suggested fix: extend the `waitForCondition` post-clear to also require `(>= chipCount 1)` before the assertion. The chip row's render path depends on the panel's projection sub firing at least once after the post-clear buffer repopulates; the wait-loop should pause until the chip-row has a deterministic floor.

File: tools/causa/testbeds/rigorous/spec.cjs §6 around line 373–376.

P3 because the failure mode is transient and re-runs cleanly; it does not block any feature path.
close_reason: Fixed by worker/rf2-lml33-flake-fix — replaced synchronous opTypeChips.count() + throw with waitForCondition >= 1. Verified 30/30 consecutive runs of the rigorous spec PASS (10× streak then 20× streak).

title: fix(scripts): check_doc_slugs.py LINK_RE matches inside inline-code spans
description:
Discovered by the rf2-0hert + spec-corpus audit fix-up worker (PR #1320 fix-up).

scripts/check_doc_slugs.py uses _LINK_RE to extract markdown links from spec docs + reject broken targets. The _strip_fences helper handles fenced (triple-backtick) code blocks but NOT inline code spans (single backticks).

Result: any doc using backticked link-syntax PLACEHOLDERS like `[NNN-DocName](NNN-DocName.md)` trips the link checker because the regex extracts the link pattern from inside the inline-code span — even though it's deliberately a placeholder, not a real link.

Concrete example that hit this: spec/Spec-Schemas.md L58 used backticked placeholder examples in a metadata table; fix swapped to concrete real-doc refs (002-Frames, Ownership.md). That works but is a workaround — the underlying script bug is latent.

## Fix shape

Extend _strip_fences (or add _strip_inline_code) to remove inline-code spans before _LINK_RE runs.

## Acceptance

- check_doc_slugs.py ignores link-syntax inside backticked inline code
- Add regression test with a doc fixture that uses both backticked placeholder links AND real links
- Existing real-link checking still works
notes: PR #1332 opened. Fix adds _strip_inline_code (CommonMark §6.1 inline code span semantics) applied inside _extract_links just before _LINK_RE runs. _slug_index unchanged (heading-line inline code must feed slugifier verbatim). Two regression fixtures wired in: inline_code_placeholder_ignored (0 broken — covers single/double-backtick, mixed line, multi-placeholder, real link still validates) and inline_code_negative_control (1 broken — proves no over-masking on same-line real broken link).
close_reason: Merged in #1332 — check_doc_slugs.py LINK_RE inline-code-span fix. _INLINE_CODE_RE + _strip_inline_code (CommonMark §6.1 compliant); length-preserving space mask preserves slug indices. 2 new fixtures pin positive (placeholders ignored) + negative (real broken link outside backticks still caught) cases. Self-test 7→9 pass.

title: story: thin re-frame.story facade toward cohesive internal modules
description: rf2-6e2ph audit observed re-frame.story.cljc (886 LoC) is a high-coupling public facade covering: (1) the seven reg-* macros + their *-fn programmatic surface, (2) registrar query helpers (registrations / handler-meta / ids / variants-of / variants-with-tags / tags-by-axis), (3) canonical-vocabulary boot (install-canonical-vocabulary! + canonical-installers), (4) configure! + clear-all!/clear-kind!/unregister! fixture surface, (5) run-variant / reset-variant / watch-variant / snapshot-identity / destroy-variant / variant-frames lifecycle surface, (6) assertions-passing? / read-assertions / execute-play! assertion + play surface, (7) layout-debug-* + variant-share-url / register-substrate! / registered-substrates SOTA surface, (8) static-mode? + stage probe, (9) mount-shell! / unmount-shell! / active-shell, (10) recorder start/stop/recording?/recorder-state/clear/gen-play-snippet. The public ns is appropriate as a facade; the goal is to keep every public symbol stable while moving the *implementation weight* behind cohesive internal namespaces. Candidate seams (some already exist as siblings): re-frame.story.query (re-exports registrar query fns), re-frame.story.canonical (canonical-installers + install-canonical-vocabulary! + the late-bind shim wiring), re-frame.story.lifecycle (run/reset/watch/destroy/lifecycle-state delegators). Facade then becomes a re-export shell. Discovered during rf2-6e2ph audit (2026-05-16). Acceptance: every existing public symbol resolves under the same name; per-internal-ns tests grow.
design:
# rf2-l8eso — Seam proposal for thinning `re-frame.story` facade

- **Bead**: rf2-l8eso (P3, phase-1 propose; sibling of rf2-6e2ph audit cluster)
- **Surface**: `tools/story/src/re_frame/story.cljc` (886 LoC)
- **Date**: 2026-05-17 00:32 AUSEST
- **Posture**: READ-ONLY proposal. NO source/test edits. Story is Causa/Story priority axis → conservative seams only.
- **Hard constraint**: every public `re-frame.story/*` symbol must resolve under the exact same name post-cut (acceptance text of rf2-l8eso).

---

## 1. What `story.cljc` actually contains (886 LoC inventory)

By line range and weight, the facade is doing five distinct jobs. Counts include docstrings (which carry most of the LoC; this is doc-heavy code).

| Job | Lines | LoC | Public surface | Internal weight present here? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. ns declaration + cljs `:require-macros`** | 1–73 | ~73 | — | sets up macro self-refer |
| **B. The seven `reg-*` macros** | 75–275 | ~200 | `reg-story`/`reg-variant`/`reg-workspace`/`reg-mode`/`reg-story-panel`/`reg-decorator`/`reg-tag` | thin: each macro just calls `macros/expand-reg-story` or `macros/gen-reg-call` |
| **C. Registry query API** | 277–396 | ~120 | `registrations`/`handler-meta`/`ids`/`registered?`/`all-kinds-with-counts`/`variants-of`/`variants-by-story`/`variants-with-tags`/`list-tags`/`list-modes`/`tags-by-axis`/`tags-without-axis`/`tags-default-excluded`/`canonical-tags`/`canonical-axes`/`canonical-status-values`/`canonical-role-values`/`tag->axis-index` | thin: every fn is a 1-line delegation to `registrar/*` or `schemas/*` |
| **D. Programmatic `reg-*` surface** | 398–412 | ~15 | `reg-story*`/`reg-variant*`/`reg-workspace*`/`reg-mode*`/`reg-story-panel*`/`reg-decorator*`/`reg-tag*` | thin: seven `def` re-exports |
| **E. Canonical-vocabulary boot** | 414–462 | ~50 | `install-canonical-vocabulary!` | **fat**: `install-late-bind-shims!` (private wiring) + `canonical-installers` ordered vector (12+ installer fns referenced) live here |
| **F. configure! + clear / unregister** | 464–527 | ~65 | `configure!`/`clear-all!`/`clear-kind!`/`unregister!` | mostly delegation; `configure!` body does 4 conditional dispatches to `config/set-*!` |
| **G. Stage-3 lifecycle surface** | 529–631 | ~105 | `variant->edn`/`workspace->edn`/`run-variant`/`reset-variant`/`watch-variant`/`snapshot-identity`/`destroy-variant!`/`variant-frames`/`variant-frame?`/`lifecycle-state` | thin: every fn delegates to `runtime/*`, `frames/*`, or `loaders/*` |
| **H. Stage-5 assertions+play** | 633–688 | ~55 | `assertions-passing?`/`read-assertions`/`canonical-assertion-ids`/`execute-play!`/`force-fx-stub-id` | thin: all delegation |
| **I. Stage-6 SOTA surface** | 690–747 | ~58 | `layout-debug-measure-id`/`layout-debug-outline-id`/`layout-debug-pseudo-id`/`variant-share-url`/`register-substrate!`/`registered-substrates` | thin: all delegation |
| **J. Helpers (args/decorators)** | 749–764 | ~16 | `resolve-args`/`resolve-decorators` | thin |
| **K. static-mode? + stage probe** | 766–786 | ~21 | `static-mode?`/`stage` | thin |
| **L. Stage-4 UI shell mount** | 788–829 | ~42 | `mount-shell!`/`unmount-shell!`/`active-shell` (CLJS-only) | thin |
| **M. Recorder surface** | 831–886 | ~56 | `start-recording!`/`stop-recording!`/`recording?`/`recorder-state`/`clear-recording!`/`gen-play-snippet` | thin |

### Key observation

**The facade is already 95% one-line delegation.** Counted by *executable* code (strip docstrings), the facade is closer to ~150 LoC of code wrapped in ~700 LoC of docstrings. The only non-trivial body is:

- **E.** `install-late-bind-shims!` (10 LoC) + the `canonical-installers` ordered vector with its CLJS reader-conditional tail.
- **F.** `configure!`'s 4-way `when/contains?` dispatch (8 LoC).
- **B.** The seven `defmacro` forms (each ~3 LoC of body, ~25 LoC of docstring).

Everything else is `(defn foo [x] (other-ns/foo x))`.

### Coupling: how widely is the public surface used?

`grep` across the repo shows 87 call-sites of `story/<query-or-tag-fn>` across 14 files (production code, tests, testbeds, story-mcp, causa). Public-symbol stability is genuinely load-bearing — every cut must preserve names.

---

## 2. Seam proposals

Per Mike's "small wins beat ambitious refactor" directive on the Causa/Story priority axis, I propose **two** seams worth doing now (S1, S2) and **one** worth filing for later (S3-deferred). The doc-bloat observation (S4) is mentioned but explicitly NOT a seam.

### S1 — `re-frame.story.canonical` (extract boot block)

**Scope**: Move the canonical-vocabulary install machinery out of `story.cljc` into a new `re-frame.story.canonical` namespace.

**What moves**:
- `install-late-bind-shims!` (currently private at lines 416–425)
- `canonical-installers` vector (currently private at lines 427–444)
- `install-canonical-vocabulary!` body (lines 446–462) — only the body; the public def stays in `story.cljc` as `(defn install-canonical-vocabulary! [] (canonical/install!))` so the user-facing call-site doesn't change.

**What stays**: The public `re-frame.story/install-canonical-vocabulary!` symbol.

**Why this seam**:
1. **Highest cohesion gain.** This is the only block in `story.cljc` that imports >10 internal nses for orchestration (rather than 1:1 delegation). Currently the facade transitively requires `assertions`, `fx-stubs`, `play`, `late-bind`, `frames`, `runtime`, `loaders`, `save-variant`, `layout-debug`, `ui-cofx`, `ui-multi-substrate`, `ui-panels` *just so canonical-installers can reference them*. Moving this out lets future query-only consumers of the facade (e.g. story-mcp's read paths) require a thinner ns surface.
2. **Most surgical.** All three forms (`install-late-bind-shims!`, `canonical-installers`, `install-canonical-vocabulary!`) are co-located, internally cohesive, and have no other call-sites in `story.cljc`.
3. **Public surface preserved.** Only one public symbol affected (`install-canonical-vocabulary!`) and it's preserved by a 1-line forwarder.
4. **Net LoC saving on facade**: ~50 LoC out, ~3 LoC back (the forwarder + a new `:require [re-frame.story.canonical :as canonical]` line).
5. **Independent testability**: a new `re-frame.story.canonical` test can verify installer order + idempotency without booting the whole facade.

**Risk**: low. The new ns transitively requires the same heavy chain (decorators, runtime, …) the facade does today — no DAG change. The only concern is that `install-canonical-vocabulary!` is called once at boot and re-running it must remain idempotent; this is already the case (each installer is documented idempotent).

**Estimated cut size**: ~80 LoC moved, new file ~100 LoC, facade shrinks 886 → ~840.

---

### S2 — `re-frame.story.query` (extract registry query API)

**Scope**: Move the registry query API (job **C** above, lines 277–396) into a new `re-frame.story.query` namespace and re-export its public symbols from the facade via `def`/`potemkin-style` aliases (or explicit per-symbol delegating defs — see "Implementation note" below).

**What moves**:
- Body of 18 query fns/defs: `registrations`, `handler-meta`, `ids`, `registered?`, `all-kinds-with-counts`, `variants-of`, `variants-by-story`, `variants-with-tags`, `list-tags`, `list-modes`, `tags-by-axis`, `tags-without-axis`, `tags-default-excluded`, `canonical-tags`, `canonical-axes`, `canonical-status-values`, `canonical-role-values`, `tag->axis-index`.

**What stays**: Every `re-frame.story/<query-fn>` symbol — facade re-exports each via `(def registrations query/registrations)` (or by `defn` wrappers if docstring discipline is preferred — see implementation note).

**Why this seam**:
1. **Largest LoC win** (~120 LoC of the facade is this block).
2. **High cohesion**: every member of this block reads from the registrar side-table; none mutate; none depend on lifecycle/runtime/play state. The block is a pure read-API and deserves its own ns.
3. **Enables future read-only consumers**. Story-MCP's introspection tools (heavily-used "hot path" per the `variants-by-story` docstring) could in principle require `re-frame.story.query` directly without loading the canonical-installers chain. That's a follow-up, not part of S2, but S2 unlocks it.
4. **Public surface preserved**: 18 facade symbols stay where they are via `def` aliases (or thin `defn` wrappers).

**Risk**: low-medium. Slightly larger than S1; touches 18 symbols. The CLJS macro self-refer at the top of `story.cljc` (lines 70–73) does NOT need to change — only `defn`s/`def`s move, not macros.

**Implementation note** (for phase-2 worker, not for me): two approaches to the re-export:
- **(a) `def` aliases**: `(def registrations query/registrations)`. Loses docstrings on the facade ns (they only live on `query`); IDE goto-def jumps through one hop. Most compact.
- **(b) `defn` wrappers**: `(defn registrations [kind] (query/registrations kind))`. Preserves docstrings on both nses; IDE goto-def stops at facade. Verbose but matches the current pattern in `story.cljc`.
  Recommend **(b)** for parity with how Stage-3 lifecycle (job G) is written today, and because docstrings on the facade are the spec's user-facing surface.

**Estimated cut size**: ~120 LoC of bodies moved out; ~60 LoC of thin re-exports (option b) or ~25 LoC (option a) added back; facade shrinks 886 → ~780–820 depending on (a)/(b).

---

### S3 (deferred) — `re-frame.story.lifecycle` (extract Stage-3/5/6 delegators)

**Scope**: Group jobs G (Stage-3 lifecycle), H (Stage-5 assertions+play), I (Stage-6 SOTA non-shell), and J (args/decorators helpers) into a `re-frame.story.lifecycle` namespace.

**Why deferred**:
1. The bead description suggests this as a candidate seam, but each of these symbols is already a single-line delegation to its owning module (`runtime/*`, `frames/*`, `loaders/*`, `assertions/*`, `play/*`, `share/*`, `layout-debug/*`, `args/*`, `decorators/*`). Moving them into a *grouping* namespace adds an extra hop without consolidating any orchestration logic. They are *already* cohesive at the destination module level — the only "noise" is that they're listed together in the facade.
2. **Risk of churn vs Causa/Story priority**: rf2-6e2ph audit cluster is actively touching nearby surface; rf2-von3 (Stage 3) and rf2-h8et (Stage 5) are landing recent commits. Bunching delegators behind a lifecycle ns now risks a future merge-conflict and gives the user no observable benefit (every symbol still resolves at `re-frame.story/...`).
3. **Defer until**: S1 and S2 land, audit cluster fully merges, and there's a concrete consumer asking for a `re-frame.story.lifecycle` surface (e.g. an MCP runtime adapter).

**Recommendation**: file as a follow-up bead `rf2-story-lifecycle-seam-phase3` blocked on S1+S2 merges + Causa/Story audit cluster settling. Do NOT pursue in this proposal cycle.

---

### S4 (NOT a seam, just noted)

The facade is ~80% docstring text by line count. Docstrings are appropriate here (public-surface contracts) and the spec-treats-code-as-documentation posture means these docstrings ARE the per-symbol spec. **Do not** strip or compress them. Move them with their fns.

---

## 3. Recommended cut order

| Order | Seam | Why first | Approx facade LoC after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **S1 `re-frame.story.canonical`** | Smallest scope, biggest cohesion win, only 1 public symbol touched. Lowest risk of merge conflict with the Causa/Story audit cluster. Builds confidence for S2. | 886 → ~840 |
| 2 | **S2 `re-frame.story.query`** | Larger but mechanical. After S1 lands, the facade's transitive require chain is already thinner, so the new query ns can be authored with its minimal `[registrar :as r] [schemas :as s]` requires from the start. | ~840 → ~780 (with defn wrappers) |
| 3 | *deferred — file separate bead* | — | — |

Each seam = one PR. Between PRs: wait for green CI + Mike review. Do NOT chain.

---

## 4. Public-surface preservation checklist (for the phase-2 worker)

The phase-2 worker MUST verify, for each cut PR:

1. `grep -r "re-frame\.story/" <repo>` produces the same set of symbols pre- and post-cut.
2. Every public symbol listed in §1 columns "Public surface" still has a `(def …)` or `(defn …)` form in `re-frame.story` (not just in the child ns).
3. `tools/story/test/re_frame/story_test.clj` and `story_cljs_test.cljs` pass without modification (these test the *public facade*, which is what we're preserving).
4. `story-mcp` tests (`tools/story-mcp/test/re_frame/story_mcp/tools_test.clj`) pass — they consume `re-frame.story/list-stories` & co.
5. Causa testbeds (`tools/causa/testbeds/cart_total/stories_cljs_test.cljs`) pass — they consume `re-frame.story/run-variant` & co.

---

## 5. Constraints honoured

- READ-ONLY: no `src/` or `test/` edits in this branch.
- Conservative posture: 2 active seams + 1 explicitly deferred; ambitious facade-decomposition refactors rejected.
- Public surface preserved: every symbol named in §1 stays at `re-frame.story/<name>`.
- Causa/Story priority axis: seam ordering minimises overlap with concurrent audit-cluster work.

## 6. References

- Bead: `bd show rf2-l8eso`
- Audit context: rf2-6e2ph (implementation-audit-cluster sibling that flagged the 886 LoC; partial overlap on the docstring stage-history removal — not in `origin/main` yet)
- Spec: `tools/story/spec/001-Authoring.md` §3.1 (reg-* macros), §3.2 (runtime), §3.5 (assertions), §5.4 (canonical-vocabulary)
- Conventions: `spec/Conventions.md` §reserved-namespaces (`re-frame.story.*` is the reserved sub-tree this proposal stays within)

Per the audit: preserve the public facade while moving cohesive internal responsibilities behind narrower internal namespaces with focused regression coverage. notes:
Phase-1 (rf2-0ytl4) findings doc written (local-only, ai/findings/rf2-0ytl4-router-subs-seam-proposal-2026-05-17.md).

Router (1558 LoC): 5 candidate seams analysed.
  - R-A router.envelope (~210 LoC): build-envelope + apply-overrides + sentinels + dynvar — RISK 4/5, defer (hot-path on every dispatch; *fx-overrides* dynvar is public ABI via with-fx-overrides macro).
  - R-B router.diagnostics (~90 LoC): fallthrough warning + cross-frame warning + handle-no-handler! — RISK 1/5, TAKE (all dev-only, all gated on interop/debug-enabled?, zero hot-path cost).
  - R-C router.cascade (~430 LoC): the per-event handler cascade — RISK 5/5, REJECT (perf surgery on per-dispatch path; in-file rf2-mccjv phase decomposition already delivers readability).
  - R-D router.drain (~330 LoC): FIFO queue + drain loop + rf2-ynk7 lock mgmt — RISK 3/5, defer (per-event take-event! crosses ns boundary; microbenchmark first).
  - R-E router.entry: rejected on public-surface grounds (dispatch! / dispatch-sync! are the public ABI via :router/dispatch! late-bind).

Subs (883 LoC, already split with subs.tooling per rf2-bmzq0): 5 candidate seams analysed.
  - S-A subs.cache (~310 LoC, ~250 after carving out cache-key): Spec 006 cache + ref-counting + grace-period + dispose + invalidate-on-replace — RISK 3/5, TAKE (cache-key stays on facade to preserve inlining on per-subscribe hit path; Spec 006 already names this seam in its pseudocode at line 627).

  - S-C subs.registration (~95 LoC): reg-sub + clear-sub + parse-reg-sub-args — RISK 1/5, defer (cold but public-surface re-export burden; small payoff).
  - S-D subs.compute (~55 LoC): the pure compute-sub Spec 008 testing form — RISK 1/5, defer (re-export burden, tiny benefit).
  - S-E subs.invalidate (~35 LoC): registrar-replacement hook — fold into S-A.

Phase-2 recommendation: take S-A + S-B + R-B together. Total ~540 LoC moved into 3 internal nss; facade total drops 2441 → ~1900 LoC. Defer R-A + R-D pending microbenchmarks; reject R-C (perf surgery) and R-E (public ABI). Cut order: S-B → S-A → R-B.

- rows = 16 surface groups
- columns = 13 classifier outputs
- mark intersections with checkmark

- + caption explaining the trigger semantics

## Acceptance

- TESTING.md mermaid diagrams replaced with matrix tables
- All information from the diagrams preserved (16 surfaces, 13 outputs, blast triggers highlighted)

title: docs(conventions): codify React-key discipline for re-frame2 UIs (4 siblings landed)
description:
The rf2-kgn0c discipline class produced 4 sibling fixes this session:

- rf2-kgn0c (PR #1259) — workspace cells use `v:<variant-id>`
- rf2-z4fza (PR #1281) — Causa trace ribbon uses `t:<trace-id>`
- rf2-c56hr (PR #1283) — workspace cell re-init uses full run-key tuple
- rf2-c8kfy (PR #1286) — controls repeater uses `r:<monotonic-id>`; tuple uses `t:<i>` (positional legit because fixed-arity)

Codify the discipline so future contributors don't re-create the class.

## Scope

Add a section to Conventions doc (likely `spec/Conventions.md` or a tool-side equivalent at `tools/story/spec/` / `tools/causa/spec/`):

- **React keys MUST be stable per-row identity, NOT positional, when the row collection can be mutated mid-list** (mount-unmount semantics depend on this).
- Recommended namespacing for re-frame2 UIs:
  - `v:<variant-id>` for variant cells
  - `t:<trace-id>` for trace rows (or fixed-arity tuples — see below)
  - `r:<row-id>` for mutable repeater rows
  - Bare positional `<i>` only acceptable when arity is fixed (e.g. tuple types)
- When the cell uses `r/with-let` for one-time init: the init AND any re-init triggers must be keyed on ALL relevant inputs (full run-key tuple), not just hot-reload-tick.

## Acceptance

- Conventions doc has the discipline written
- Cross-link to the 4 fixing PRs as reference cases
- Mention rf2-yb5xx audit (the one that surfaced the discipline gap)

title: chore(causa): mount cleanups — id collisions, mode attr dedup, conventions doc, mount-state :mode parity
description:
Per causa-mount-strategy-audit (rf2-a6tvr) findings Q1-4, Q1-8, Q1-9, Q1-10, Q2-8.

## Cluster of small cleanups

All cosmetic / low-risk; clustering to avoid mount.cljs hot-zone churn.

### Q1-4 — DOM-id collision risk

`mount.cljs:111` (overlay) and `mount.cljs:154` (inline) both set `id = "rf-causa-root"`. Singleton mount-state precludes coexistence today, but the invariant is fragile. Either (a) distinct ids (`rf-causa-root-inline`, `rf-causa-root-overlay`), or (b) enforce singleton at create-fn level. **Defer until rf2-sbfb7 resolves dock!/overlay disposition.**

### Q1-8 — `mount-state :mode` slot inconsistency

The atom-shape comment (mount.cljs:61) lists `<:inline|:overlay|:docked>` but the popout never writes mount-state. shell-view's `case mode` (shell.cljs:400-416) covers `:inline`, `:popout`, default. `:docked` falls through to the default-overlay styling. Tidy after rf2-sbfb7.

### Q1-9 — `set-mode-attrs!` writes both `data-rf-causa-mode` and `data-mode` — duplicate axis

`mount.cljs:175-180`. Tests / CSS can hit either. Pick one (the spec-published `data-rf-causa-mode`) and drop `data-mode`, or document why both exist. Currently shell.cljs:388 also writes `data-mode` in the shell hiccup.

### Q1-10 — `teardown!` does not detach the keybinding

Acceptable for production (defonce preserves the listener), but tests calling `teardown!` then re-running mount tests may see stale `toggle!` calls. Audit tests; either thread `keybinding/detach!` through `teardown!` or document the test-fixture obligation.

### Q2-8 — Mount conventions absent from `tools/causa/spec/Conventions.md`

The artefact-local Conventions doc covers panel-facade/leaf only. Add a §Mount conventions section: singleton mount-state, defonce-across-reload, data-attribute scheme (after Q1-9 resolves).

## Sequencing

Wait for rf2-sbfb7 (dock!/inline-panel-mount decision) and rf2-yudol (teardown lifecycle) to land first — those touch the same lines and resolve some of the underlying questions (e.g. Q1-4 is moot if dock! goes away).

title: perf(schemas): memoise extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema + default-edn-print
description:
Per ai/findings/framework-quality-audit-2026-05-17.md §S2 + §S4 [both LOW]:

(1) `schema-sensitive-at?` (walker.cljc:242-282) extracts the whole `{path decl}` sensitive map per call. Two consecutive failures on the same schema re-walk it. Failure-branch only, but memoising by schema identity (`(memoize extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema)`) is free since schemas are immutable values.

(2) `default-edn-print` (validator.cljc:105-123) re-canonicalises every call. The digest pipeline (digest.cljc:69-79) calls `run-printer` once per registered schema per digest call. Memoising by schema identity for the digest hot path is "free" — schemas are immutable values.

Both are tiny perf wins (memoise wrapper).
close_reason: PR #1353: memoised extract-sensitive-paths-from-schema (walker) + default-edn-print (validator) by schema-value identity. Pure-over-immutable so cache is bounded by registered-schema cardinality. npm test:cljs + schemas/core JVM all green.

title: cleanup(core): registrar warn-once cache + dispatch-counter comment + sticky hooks polish
description:
Per ai/findings/framework-quality-audit-2026-05-17.md §C4, §C5, §C7 [all LOW]:

Three LOW-severity cleanups bundled (each <5 line):

(1) `dispatch-counter` (router.cljc:49-52) comment claims "the counter increments harmlessly" under production — but the call site at line 91 already gates on `interop/debug-enabled?` so the counter does NOT increment in CLJS prod. Either fix the comment or delete it (redundant).

(2) `clear-kind!` (registrar.cljc:327) does NOT partial-clear the per-process warn-once caches for `:rf.warning/missing-doc` / `:rf.warning/registration-collision`; only `clear-all!` (line 340) does. Test fixtures targeting a single kind keep stale suppression. Decide: partial-clear (filter by kind) OR document the asymmetry.

(3) `views.cljs:158` calls `(late-bind/get-fn :adapter/wrap-view)` per reg-view — should be `get-fn-cached` per the sticky-hook convention (rf2-f72pd) since `:adapter/wrap-view` is published once at ns-load and never withdrawn.

All three are doc / single-keyword changes.
close_reason: PR #1353: (1) router.cljc dispatch-counter comment corrected (no harmless increment under production — the call site already DCEs). (2) registrar.cljc clear-kind! now drops matching slots from missing-doc-warned + collision-warned warn-once caches so per-kind fixtures start clean. (3) views.cljs apply-adapter-wrap-view uses late-bind/get-fn-cached per sticky-hook convention (rf2-f72pd) since :adapter/wrap-view is published once at adapter ns-load and route-hook! invalidates the cache on hot-reload.

title: doc(subs): compute-sub N^2 risk + plain-fn-warning gating asymmetry
description:
Per ai/findings/framework-quality-audit-2026-05-17.md §C2 [MED] + §C3 [LOW]:

(1) compute-sub (subs.cljc:518-555) recurses through :<- chains with full recomputation at every node — N^2 work for deep chains. Test/SSR/story consumers may walk deep trees expecting "fast pure compute". Doc the cost; optional memoised wrapper.

(2) `subscribe`'s 1-arity path (subs.cljc:446-487) runs the plain-fn-under-non-default-frame-once warn-check; the 2-arity form skips it. May be intentional (explicit frame = opt-out) but docstring doesn't say. Spec 006 §Plain-fn warning (rf2-d3k3) should clarify.

Doc/spec follow-on; no code change required other than docstrings.
close_reason: PR #1353: doc-only. (1) compute-sub now documents the N^2 cost on deep :<- chains and the reactive-subscribe immunity contrast. (2) subscribe docstring + Spec 006 §Plain-fn-under-non-default-frame warning now explicitly document the arity-gated check: 1-arity runs detection, 2-arity skips by design (explicit frame-id IS the opt-out).

title: decision(adapters): :adapter/after-render under UIx / Helix — publish or doc-only
description:
Per ai/findings/framework-quality-audit-2026-05-17.md §A4 [MED]:

`re-frame.interop/after-render` (interop.cljs:31-36) is the documented seam for scheduling work after the next render. Only Reagent and reagent-slim publish the `:adapter/after-render` hook; UIx and Helix do not.

Calls from a UIx- or Helix-only app fall through to nil — silent no-op.

Adapter docstrings (helix.cljs:154-161) justify NOT publishing the other reactive hooks because UIx/Helix have no reactive atom — but `after-render` is a React-lifecycle question (Reagent's `r/after-render` is a thin wrapper around React commit), not a reactive-atom one.

Decision needed:
(A) Publish a `React.useLayoutEffect`-backed `after-render` from the spine.
(B) Explicitly document `interop/after-render` as Reagent-only and rename or restrict the seam.

Today's silent no-op is the worst of both.
close_reason: DECISION 2026-05-19 (Mike): PUBLISH (A) — useLayoutEffect wrapper for UIx + Helix. Closes silent no-op. Impl bead filed today.

title: policy(spec): document spec-impl-pair convention OR add classifier rule for spec/*.md
description:
LOW-MED watch-item from ai/findings/ci-test-routing-audit-2026-05-16.md (M3). The .github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh classifier has no rule for top-level spec/*.md files. A spec-only PR (e.g. a normative-only refinement to spec/011-SSR.md with no impl change) would run NO surface-conditional jobs — only the always-on jvm-core, cljs, js-harness-self-tests, verify-version-lockstep, verify-skill-mcp-drift, and the MkDocs build (from a separate workflow).

Current safety net is convention: every spec change in this 16-PR batch was paired with an impl change that fired the broad classifier rules. But this is policy-by-convention, not by classifier.

PRs that touched spec/*.md this batch (all rescued by paired impl changes): #1241 (spec/Security.md), #1243 (spec/011-SSR.md), #1244 (spec/014-HTTPRequests.md + spec/Conventions.md + spec/MIGRATION.md), #1248 (spec/012-Routing.md), #1249 (spec/002-Frames.md + spec/013-Flows.md + spec/API.md).

Why no proposed classifier change: adding 'spec/* → fire everything' would be a sledgehammer; spec is the normative artefact and not every spec edit needs the full impl test matrix. The right intervention is either:
(a) A pre-push hook that flags spec-only PRs and asks for confirmation, OR
(b) A CI 'spec-impl-pair' check that warns (not blocks) on spec-only PRs, OR
(c) Per-spec-file rules (spec/011-SSR.md → fire jvm-ssr-ring + jvm-ssr; spec/013-Flows.md → fire jvm-flows; etc.) — surgical but high maintenance.

Defer until someone actually files a spec-only PR — first-incident triggers the decision.
notes: PR #1257 — 4-bead CI classifier completeness cluster. rf2-4zqn7: TESTING.md spec-impl-pair convention doc (35 lines). rf2-7vsfm: testbeds/* → cljs_browser + examples_browser classifier rule. rf2-qmiiz: spec/conformance/fixtures/* → implementation_jvm + cljs_browser + cljs_prod classifier rule. rf2-mvugr (P1): added implementation/ssr-ring/* to classifier alternation + new jvm-ssr-ring workflow job modelled on jvm-ssr + scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh entry. Local JVM sweep PASS across all 13 artefacts incl. new ssr-ring (58 tests / 299 assertions / 0F).
close_reason: Merged

title: fix(story-or-causa): workspace-switch surfaces stale subscribe→nil derefs in app-db-diff/subscriptions variants
description:
Observed in rf2-5nvk2 Phase 1b smoke run: clicking from one `:variants-grid` workspace to another within the same browser session triggers "No protocol method IDeref.-deref defined for type null" pageerrors in variants that subscribe to subs whose composite chain reads through `:rf.causa/target-frame-db` (-> `(rf/get-frame-db :rf/default)`). Each workspace renders correctly on a fresh page; the error is workspace-switch-induced.

Repro: load #/stories, click Workspace.causa.event-detail/all (12/12 OK), then click Workspace.causa.app-db-diff/all → ~22 pageerrors at app_db_diff_view's `@(rf/subscribe [:rf.causa/app-db-diff])` deref. The phase-1b smoke now uses a fresh page per workspace to side-step this, but the underlying issue is real.

Hypothesis: Reagent retains the prior workspace's variant cells' subscribe-reactions across the workspace swap; when the new workspace renders, a stale reaction continues to deref against a frame that's been torn down or never existed in the new variants' frame-id space.

Owner surface: tools/story (workspace teardown / cell-overrides reset). May be related to existing :grace 0 unsubscribe behaviour; needs investigation before Phase 2.

Not a blocker for rf2-5nvk2 — the gallery works correctly in actual use (each panel viewed on its own); the smoke gate has been adapted accordingly.
notes: PR #1259 — Strategy A (React-key keying). Root cause: positional cell keys (str 'v-' i) made React reuse cells across workspace switches; cell's r/with-let initializer never re-ran with new variant id, so subscribe against unallocated frame returned nil → @nil threw. Fix: cells key on v:<variant-id>, workspace root <section> keys on workspace id. New tests: 3 CLJS unit tests + new Playwright scenario walking 5 workspace selections + new _workspace_switch_smoke.cjs walking all 3 Phase 1b gallery workspaces in ONE session (56 variant roots, 0 pageerrors). Fresh-page-per-workspace mitigation from PR #1254 is no longer required.
close_reason: Merged

title: refactor(reagent): dispose-adapter! Step 1 should call subs/clear-sub-cache! (DRY)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-afm8m (`ai/findings/reagent-slice-audit-2026-05-15.md` finding M3).

## Problem

`adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:136-145` inlines the body of `re-frame.subs/clear-sub-cache!` inside an outer per-frame `doseq`:

```clojure
(doseq [[_ frame-record] @frame/frames]
  (when-let [cache (:sub-cache frame-record)]
    (doseq [[_k entry] @cache]
      (when-let [h (:pending-dispose entry)]
        (try (interop/clear-timeout! h) (catch :default _ nil)))
      (when-let [r (:reaction entry)]
        (try (interop/dispose! r) (catch :default _ nil))))
    (reset! cache {})))
```

This is byte-for-byte the body of `subs/clear-sub-cache!` (`subs.cljc:744-754`) — except wrapped in a per-frame loop.

## Risk (low — hygiene only)

Two sites for the same teardown algorithm means a future fix to one (e.g. additional cache-entry slots like `:on-dispose` callbacks; a switch to `try-finally` for ordering) won't reach the other. Not a bug today.

## Fix

Replace Step 1 of the dispose body with:

```clojure
(doseq [[fid _] @frame/frames]
  (subs/clear-sub-cache! fid))
```

Add `[re-frame.subs :as subs]` to the `(:require ...)`. Verify no circular require — `subs.cljc` does not require `re-frame.adapter.reagent`, so safe.

## Acceptance

- `adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs` calls `subs/clear-sub-cache!` per frame from `dispose-adapter!`.
- `dispose_adapter_sub_cache_walk_cljs_test.cljs` continues to pass (the test asserts observable behaviour, not the inlined body shape).
close_reason: Cleanup 2026-05-15: completed by main commit 9cfe4e1b; Reagent dispose-adapter now delegates to subs/clear-sub-cache! for the sub-cache teardown step.

title: perf(elision): walk container branches use (range)+mapv with eager path conj per child
description:
MED severity from perf-sweep audit rf2-fzrav (ai/findings/perf-sweep-2026-05-15.md §M3).

implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc walk (lines 598-615) — vector / seq / set container branches:

(vector? v)
(mapv (fn [idx vv] (walk vv (conj path idx) ctx))
      (range) v)

(range) creates an infinite lazy seq; mapv consumes until v ends. Two per-child allocations: the path conj (always) and the cons cell from (range). For a wide vec slice (large :items collections), this fires on every wire-emit walk.

Alternative — hand-rolled reduce with explicit index, deferring path conj until something actually needs it (only when the registry lookup at this path could hit):

(vector? v)
(let [n (count v)]
  (loop [i 0 acc (transient [])]
    (if (< i n)
      (recur (inc i)
             (conj! acc (walk (nth v i) (conj path i) ctx)))
      (persistent! acc))))

The path-conj is still eager because every recursive call needs path... unless we add a path-lazy optimisation where the registry-of-frame check is the only reader and we know it's nil → skip the conj. That's harder.

Simpler: drop the (range) cons-cell allocation by switching to an indexed loop. Worth a benchmark before doing it.

Same pattern for seq? branch (lines 609-615).

Set branch (line 607) just does (map ... v) with no index — already optimal.

Files (read-only audit pass):
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc

Hot-zone: NO. Isolated to elision.cljc. Safe to parallel.

Pre-alpha. Confirm with a bench before changing — the (range)+mapv pattern is idiomatic and JIT-friendly; the win may be smaller than expected.

title: perf(adapters): Reagent make-derived-value lazy map deref + apply on every recompute
description:
MED severity from perf-sweep audit rf2-fzrav (ai/findings/perf-sweep-2026-05-15.md §M2).

implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:35-37 make-derived-value:

(defn- make-derived-value [source-containers compute-fn]
  (ratom/make-reaction
    (fn [] (apply compute-fn (map deref source-containers)))))

(apply compute-fn (map deref ...)) — lazy seq + apply. For each reaction recompute (every sub recompute, N times per dispatch) this creates a lazy seq with one cons per source.

Subs typically chain off 1 input (layer-2 single :<-) or 0 (layer-1 reads db). Specialise:

(defn- make-derived-value [source-containers compute-fn]
  (let [n (count source-containers)]
    (ratom/make-reaction
      (case n
        0 (fn [] (compute-fn))
        1 (let [s (first source-containers)]
            (fn [] (compute-fn @s)))
        2 (let [s0 (nth source-containers 0)
                s1 (nth source-containers 1)]
            (fn [] (compute-fn @s0 @s1)))
        (fn [] (apply compute-fn (mapv deref source-containers)))))))

The 0/1/2 cases cover >95% of sub registrations and replace the lazy-map-apply path with direct calls.

Mirror the same change in:
- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/...
- implementation/adapters/uix/...
- implementation/adapters/helix/...

(Wherever make-derived-value lives per-adapter. Check first.)

Files (read-only audit pass):
- implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs
- (plus reagent-slim / uix / helix variants)

Hot-zone: NO. Per-adapter source. Safe to parallel.

Pre-alpha.

title: perf(epoch): fuse the three projection walks of the events buffer into one reducer
description:
MED severity from perf-sweep audit rf2-fzrav (ai/findings/perf-sweep-2026-05-15.md §M1).

implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc build-record (line 666) calls project-sub-runs, project-renders, project-effects (lines 513-601) — each is an independent transducer walk over the same events vector. For a 100-event cascade buffer this is 3 * 100 = 300 walks vs 100 in a fused reducer.

The pattern is already used in find-trigger-event (line 610, single reduce accumulating two slots, per rf2-txrq9). Lift the same pattern to the three projectors:

(defn- project-all [events]
  (reduce
    (fn [{:keys [sub-runs renders effects] :as acc} ev]
      (let [op (:operation ev)
            t  (:tags ev)]
        (cond
          (= :sub/run op)
          (update acc :sub-runs conj {:sub-id (:sub-id t) :query-v (:query-v t) :recomputed? true})

          (= :view/render op)
          (update acc :renders conj {:render-key (or (:render-key t) [:rf.view/anonymous nil])
                                     :triggered-by (:triggered-by t)
                                     :elapsed-ms (:elapsed-ms t)})

          (or (= :rf.fx/handled op)
              (= :rf.fx/skipped-on-platform op)
              (= :rf.error/fx-handler-exception op)
              (= :rf.error/no-such-fx op))
          (update acc :effects conj <project-effect-entry>)

          :else acc)))
    {:sub-runs [] :renders [] :effects []}
    events))

Then build-record destructures the three slots.

Fires once per cascade settle (= once per user-dispatched event under steady state).

Files (read-only audit pass):
- implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc

Hot-zone: NO. Isolated to epoch artefact. Safe to parallel.

Pre-alpha.

title: prod-elision: add runtime tests for routing / http / flows trace-emit DCE
description:
Per audit rf2-toib5 §G7 (DEFER). Production-elision RUNTIME testing today covers: core (event-emit, on-error, trace-listener, source-coord), schemas (boundary prod), adapters (source-coord-dom).

The runtime prod tests (event_emit_elision_prod_test, on_error_elision_prod_test, etc.) exercise the BEHAVIOUR elides under goog.DEBUG=false — they instantiate the bundle, dispatch, assert no trace/error/listener side-effects.

The complementary string-grep check (check-elision.cjs / DEV_ONLY_SENTINELS) catches sentinel-string survival in the bundle blob — that covers the 'is it DCE'd?' axis for many surfaces (including epoch, schemas, trace, registrar). Routing / http / flows trace-emit sentinels ARE in DEV_ONLY_SENTINELS but no RUNTIME prod-elision test confirms the trace-emit calls themselves don't fire.

Surfaces lacking the runtime prod-elision test:

- routing — :rf.route/* trace events under goog.DEBUG=false should not fire (the (.pushState ...) host call IS unconditional; the surrounding trace/emit-error! IS gated).
- http — :rf.http/managed trace events (request-start, response-received, error) should DCE.
- flows — :rf.flow/computed, :rf.flow/skip, :rf.flow/registered, :rf.flow/failed trace emits should DCE.

This is DEFER because:
(a) check-elision.cjs catches the string-side regression for these.
(b) The behavioural test for trace-emit DCE is a duplication of the elision contract's sentinel test in slightly different shape.
(c) Cost: 3 new cljs prod-elision test files + serve-and-run-prod-elision-tests.cjs wiring.

Track here so if a future regression slips through the sentinel grep (e.g. via dynamic string construction), we have the bead to escalate.

Reference: ai/findings/test-coverage-sweep-2026-05-15.md §G7.

Verdict: DEFER — covered by string-grep complement; behavioural runtime check is symmetry not load-bearing.

title: fix(http): JVM response headers comma-join breaks multi-valued cookies — pin shape vs vector-on-multi
description:
Found by audit bead rf2-wui5v.

## Issue

`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:283-285`:

```clojure
(defn- jvm-headers->map [^java.net.http.HttpHeaders hh]
  (into {}
        (for [[k vs] (.map hh)]
          [(str/lower-case k) (str/join "," vs)])))
```

Multi-valued response headers are comma-joined to a single string. Spec 014
§Request envelope says headers map is `string → string (or string → vector
of strings for multi-valued)`. Asymmetric outcome:

- JVM: `Set-Cookie: a=1\nSet-Cookie: b=2` → `"a=1,b=2"`
- CLJS Fetch: `Headers.forEach` callback gives one value per name (browser
  pre-joins, also comma-separated)

Cookies are the canonical breakage: `Set-Cookie` values legally contain commas
(e.g. `Expires=Wed, 21 Oct 2026 ...`), so the comma-join produces unparseable
cookies. Apps reading `Set-Cookie` from a response's `:headers` slot get
malformed data.

## Two ways to fix

**Option a — preserve vector for multi-valued (matches the spec's "or" branch)**:

```clojure
(into {}
      (for [[k vs] (.map hh)]
        [(str/lower-case k)
         (if (= 1 (count vs)) (first vs) (vec vs))]))
```

Downstream consumers handle both shapes; the CLJS path needs symmetric
treatment (it currently produces strings from `Headers.forEach`).

**Option b — special-case Set-Cookie to vector, leave the rest string-only**:

Pragmatic; preserves the simpler string-only mental model for 99% of headers.

## Decision needed

Mike's call — option a respects the spec wording but ripples through every
consumer reading response headers; option b is conservative.

## Surface

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:270-285` (`jvm-headers->map`)
- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:43-47` (`fetch-headers->map` for symmetry)

## Discovered through

Audit bead rf2-wui5v (http slice).
close_reason: Closed via PR #1354 (worker hit content-filter on 4th bead rf2-8l0lz; first 3 completed cleanly with passing gates).

title: test(http): pin :rf/http-interceptor-meta source-coords actually flow into stored slot
description:
Found by audit bead rf2-wui5v.

## Issue

rf2-gsl5v (PR #1165) promoted `rf/reg-http-interceptor` to a `defreg-macro`
form so source-coords (`:ns`/`:line`/`:column`/`:file`) capture at the call
site and flow into the per-frame interceptor side-table. Spec-Schemas now
documents `:rf/http-interceptor-meta` as `[:merge RegistrationMetadata ...]`.

No test currently asserts that an interceptor registered via
`rf/reg-http-interceptor` ACTUALLY carries those coords in its stored slot —
the `@http-managed/interceptors` map should expose them on each chain entry.

Other reg-* surfaces have analogous tests (see
`implementation/core/test/re_frame/source_coords_test.clj`).

## What to pin

```clojure
(deftest reg-http-interceptor-captures-source-coords
  (rf/reg-http-interceptor
    {:id     :auth
     :before (fn [c] c)})
  (let [chain (get @http-managed/interceptors :rf/default)
        slot  (first (filter #(= :auth (:id %)) chain))]
    (is (= 're-frame.http-source-coords-test (:ns slot)))
    (is (pos-int? (:line slot)))
    (is (pos-int? (:column slot)))
    (is (some? (:file slot)))))
```

Plus a test that user-supplied `:doc` / `:tags` / `:spec` / `:sensitive?`
flow through into the slot (they sit alongside the auto-captured coords).

Plus a regression test that user-supplied `:ns` / `:line` overrides the
auto-captured values per the source-coords contract.

## Surface

- New: `implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_source_coords_test.clj`

title: perf(http): redact-url-query-string still does two walks for changed? — fold into single pass
description:
Found by audit bead rf2-wui5v.

## Issue

`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_url.cljc:186-191`:

```clojure
(let [pairs    (str/split query #"&")
      redacted (mapv (fn [p] (redact-query-param p (true? sensitive?)))
                     pairs)
      changed? (boolean (some true? (map not= pairs redacted)))
      rebuilt  (str base "?" (str/join "&" redacted) (or fragment ""))]
  [rebuilt changed?])
```

The mapv walks N pairs producing redacted forms; then `(map not= pairs redacted)`
walks both again producing a lazy seq of N booleans for the `some true?` test.
Per rf2-02vzz the redact + denylist-hit were supposed to be fused into ONE walk
— currently it's effectively still two.

## Suggested fix

Carry a transient boolean flag through the redactor and report it alongside
the redacted output. `redact-query-param` can return `[redacted-pair changed?]`
or signal via a thread-local volatile so the outer `mapv` retains its shape.

Alternative: replace `(some true? (map not= pairs redacted))` with `(not= pairs redacted)`
— still O(N) under the hood (vector equality) but no intermediate lazy seq allocation.

## Why this matters

The redactor runs once per trace emit that carries `:url`. Trace surface elides
in production (per `interop/debug-enabled?` gates at call sites), so this is
NOT a production hot path. BUT during dev / pair-shaped tooling sessions the
trace surface is permanently on; every `:rf.http/*` emit pays the double-walk.

## Surface

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_url.cljc:160-192` `redact-url-query-string`

title: fix(http): classify-jvm-error string-match fallback can misclassify errors as timeout/abort
description:
Found by audit bead rf2-wui5v.

## Issue

`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:317-323`:

```clojure
(or (instance? java.net.http.HttpTimeoutException cause)
    (and msg (str/includes? (str/lower-case msg) "timed out")))
;; ...
(or (instance? java.util.concurrent.CancellationException cause)
    (and msg (str/includes? (str/lower-case msg) "abort")))
```

The instance checks should be sufficient. The `str/includes?` fallbacks are
fragile substring matches — a server error message that happens to contain
"timed out" or "abort" in its body / exception message (e.g. a downstream
service's own error wrapper) would misclassify as `:rf.http/timeout` /
`:rf.http/aborted`, polluting the failure taxonomy.

## Suggested fix

Narrow to instance-checks only:

```clojure
(instance? java.net.http.HttpTimeoutException cause)
{:kind :rf.http/timeout ...}

(instance? java.util.concurrent.CancellationException cause)
{:kind :rf.http/aborted ...}
```

Confirm JDK reliably surfaces these instance types for all timeout/cancel paths;
drop the substring fallback. (The original substring fallback was defensive but
the JDK contract is now well-understood.)

## Surface

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport.cljc:312-326` `classify-jvm-error`

title: test(flows): pin :rf.error/flow-cycle-extract-invariant defence throw in extract-cycle-path
description:
**Impl:** `flows/topo.cljc:88-94` raises `:rf.error/flow-cycle-extract-invariant` if Kahn's stuck-set yields a dead end during cycle-path extraction:

```clojure
(when (nil? next-dep)
  (throw (ex-info ":rf.error/flow-cycle-extract-invariant"
                  {:reason   ":rf.error/flow-cycle-extract-invariant"
                   :node     node
                   :stack    stack
                   :seen     seen
                   :remaining remaining
                   :recovery :no-recovery})))
```

The branch is unreachable by design — by Kahn's algorithm every stuck node has at least one stuck dep — but the throw is load-bearing defence: a closing-repeat vector built from a dead end would lie to tools (Causa, the flow panel) about the offending chain.

**Fix shape:** A unit test against the private `extract-cycle-path` (via internal alias) or via a constructed graph that violates the invariant (artificially). Pin the throw + ex-data shape so a future refactor cannot silently break the defence.

```clojure
(deftest extract-cycle-path-invariant-throws-on-dead-end
  ;; Construct a stuck-set whose graph entries don't point into the stuck-set
  ;; — the dead-end case the invariant guards against.
  (let [graph     {:a #{:b} :b #{}}    ; :b has no deps, can't be stuck
        remaining #{:a :b}]
    (is (thrown? Throwable
                 (#'re-frame.flows.topo/extract-cycle-path graph remaining)))))
```

title: perf(flows): clear-flow skip replace-container! when dissoc-in-safe was a no-op
description:
**Impl:** `flows/registry.cljc:265-270`. `dissoc-in-safe` returns `cur` unchanged when the parent is missing or non-map (per audit rf2-q25os Repro 1 / Repro 2). `clear-flow` then calls `replace-container! container cur` anyway — triggers reactive sub-cache invalidation for a no-op write.

```clojure
(let [cur    (adapter/read-container container)
      new-db (cond
               (not (vector? path))   (dissoc cur path)
               (empty? path)          cur
               (= 1 (count path))     (dissoc cur (first path))
               :else                  (dissoc-in-safe cur path))]
  (adapter/replace-container! container new-db))    ;; fires even when new-db = cur
```

**Impact:** Cheap-but-needless invalidation. Most subs will short-circuit on `=`-equal compute, so the user-visible cost is one extra walk of the sub graph. Not a correctness problem; cleanliness only.

**Fix shape:**

```clojure
(when-not (identical? new-db cur)
  (adapter/replace-container! container new-db))
```

(`identical?` is the right check — `dissoc-in-safe` returns `cur` literally when no change is made; `identical?` is O(1) where `=` is O(n).)

title: fix(flows): reset-flows! should also reset last-inputs (test-fixture footgun)
description:
**Impl:** `flows/registry.cljc:397-405`. `reset-flows!` resets only the `flows` atom. The flow-test fixtures in `flows_test.clj`, `flows_destroy_frame_teardown_test.clj`, and `flows_trace_test.clj` ALL reset `flows/flows` AND `flows/last-inputs` because they must — `reset-flows!` alone leaves stale dirty-check state that silently no-ops the next re-registration's first evaluation when inputs happen to be `=`-equal to a leftover.

**Impact:** Footgun for test fixtures or pair2/causa harnesses calling `reset-flows!` standalone. The docstring claim "Test-only" is accurate but the function name suggests it resets all flow state.

**Fix shape (option A — extend behaviour):** Have `reset-flows!` reset both atoms:

```clojure
(defn reset-flows!
  []
  (reset! flows {})
  (reset! last-inputs {})
  nil)
```

**Fix shape (option B — rename / split):** Rename current `reset-flows!` → `reset-flow-registry!` and add `reset-flow-state!` that resets both. Migrate test fixtures.

Option A is the smaller change and matches how callers actually use these.

**Regression test:** Use `reset-flows!` standalone; register a flow with same inputs as a prior test; assert the new flow re-evaluates on its first drain (not skipped by leftover `last-inputs`).

title: fix(flows): :rf.error/flow-cycle ex-info uses non-standard ex-data shape
description:
**Impl:** `flows/topo.cljc:171-173`:

```clojure
(throw (ex-info ":rf.error/flow-cycle"
                {:cycle (extract-cycle-path ...)}))
```

Every other flow ex-info uses the standard shape built via `flow-error` helper (`registry.cljc:95-108`):

```clojure
{:error    <kw>
 :where    'rf/reg-flow
 :recovery :no-recovery
 :reason   "..."
 :flow     ...}
```

Tools (Causa, 10x, late-bind-missing wrappers) read these fields uniformly across error surfaces. Flow-cycle is the outlier — its ex-data lacks `:error`, `:where`, `:recovery`, `:reason`.

**Impact:** Tools doing uniform error-data unpacking miss `:error` / `:where` / `:recovery` / `:reason` on flow-cycle. The ex-info's `(ex-message ...)` is `:rf.error/flow-cycle` (string-as-message) and `(ex-data ...)` is `{:cycle [...]}` only.

**Fix shape:** Build the cycle ex-info with the standard shape:

```clojure
(throw (ex-info ":rf.error/flow-cycle"
                {:error    :rf.error/flow-cycle
                 :where    'rf/reg-flow
                 :recovery :no-recovery
                 :reason   "Cyclic flow dependency — A.path overlaps B.inputs and B.path overlaps A.inputs."
                 :cycle    (extract-cycle-path graph (set (keys remaining)))}))
```

`topo.cljc` is the pure-data module — it has no `:requires`, so cannot use `flow-error`. Either inline the shape (as above) or move the helper up to `topo.cljc` or extract a shared `flows/errors.cljc`.

**Regression test:** Assert `(ex-data ex)` keys = `#{:error :where :recovery :reason :cycle}` after registering a cyclic pair.

**Impl:** `flows.cljc:262-275` publishes 6 late-bind hooks at namespace-load time:
- `:flows/reg-flow`
- `:flows/clear-flow`

title: decision(flows): :rf.flow/registered double-emits with :rf.registry/handler-replaced on re-registration
description:
**Impl:** `flows/registry.cljc:189-202` — `reg-flow` calls `registrar/register!` (which emits `:rf.registry/handler-replaced` on re-registration per Spec 001 §Hot-reload trace surface) AND then directly emits `:rf.flow/registered` (per Spec 013 §Flow tracing).

Both fire for the same re-registration. Tools subscribed to BOTH op-types (most do — 10x flow panel reads `:flow`; epoch buffer reads everything) count one re-registration twice in their hot-reload event ledger. Per-frame "reload count" metrics are inflated 2x for flows.

**Impact:** Tooling-only. Hot-reload metrics off by 2x for flows; per-flow vs cross-kind double-counting in long dev sessions.

**Fix shape:** Either gate `:rf.flow/registered` to first-time-only (read the `:was` slot from `registrar/register!`'s return), or accept the redundancy as a tool-side normalisation problem. The first is the smaller change:

```clojure
(let [{:keys [was]} (registrar/register! :flow flow-id ...)]
  ...
  (when (nil? was)
    (trace/emit! :flow :rf.flow/registered {...})))
```

(But this changes the trace contract — `:rf.flow/registered` then fires only on first-time, with `:rf.registry/handler-replaced` carrying the hot-reload signal. Spec 009 doesn't currently distinguish.)

**Recommendation:** P3 — note in the audit; defer pending Mike's call on whether the per-flow trace should fire on every registration or first-time-only. (Mirrors a question for machines.)

description:

**F-HYG-1 / F-COUPLE-3** — normalise `.cjs` vs `.js` extensions across the artefact. `_runner.js` emits `module.exports` from a `.js` file; `exec-safety.cjs` is explicit CJS; the orchestrator is `.cjs`. `package.json` has no `"type": "module"`, so all `.js` is CJS by default — but the mix reads as "I switched conventions mid-artefact". **F-HYG-2** — centralise SKIP pattern in `_runner.js` as `runWithWatchdog.skip(reason)`. `end-to-end-causa.js` and `live-pair2-overflow.js` both duplicate the SKIP-marker prose today. ~5 LoC saved.

**F-PERF-2** — tighten `POLL_MS` from 500 → 100 in hermetic orchestrator. Trivial cumulative latency win.

**F-PERF-3** — `strip-comments-and-strings` memo cache holds ~50KB on cold JVM; revisit only if test set grows past ~100 files. Annotate; don't act today.

**F-COUPLE-1** — document asymmetry between `resolveTrustedExe` (story-mcp, needs PATH walk for system-wide `clojure`) and `process.execPath` (pair2-mcp, always-safe-by-construction) in `lib/exec-safety.cjs` preamble.

~80 LoC across the cluster.

P3 — polish; quality-of-life. Land as one PR or split per-finding at the actioner's discretion.

description:

**F18**: `apply-cap-byte-cap-trips-when-only-secondary-fires` test
(cap_test.clj:198-223) argues at length that the secondary char cap is
'mathematically impossible' to trip in isolation under the current
`(quot c 4)` rule, then asserts only that
`byte-cap-multiplier = 8` and that `sum-text-chars` reads the same
content as `sum-text-tokens`. The deftest name promises behaviour the
body doesn't deliver. Either:

    the docstring novella; OR

(b) Add a ResultIO that under-reports tokens (override sum-text-tokens
    via protocol method) and exercise the secondary cap in isolation.

out the actual gate. Pick (a) unless the gate is load-bearing.

**F19**: `re-frame.mcp-base.sensitive`'s malformed-counter (an
AtomicLong / atom) has no public reset and no test exercises its
value. The fail-closed posture's observability is a real feature for
operators; without tests the counter is just a side-effect with no
guarantee of behaviour. Either:

(a) Make `malformed-count` public and add tests for the increment.

(b) Add a reset! fn for test isolation.

title: refactor(mcp-base): retire parse-keyword after fresh-id callsite migration (rf2-u64jt F5)
description:
Per rf2-u64jt audit F5 (ai/findings/mcp-base-slice-audit-2026-05-15.md).

`re-frame.mcp-base.args/parse-keyword` carries a v1-bridge docstring
note: 'Eventually a follow-on bead retires this in favour of
`safe-keyword` everywhere.' Pre-alpha; we can do the retirement now.

Two remaining consumer callsites (per ripgrep):

  - tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/write.cljc:204 —
    variant id; comment says 'intern via parse-keyword' deliberately,
    bounded by registry.
  - tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/recorder.cljc:193 —
    same pattern, paired with an explicit `safe-keyword` first-pass.

Both sites already use `safe-keyword` as the primary lookup with
`parse-keyword` as a fallback for fresh-id creation. The
fresh-id-creation pattern is genuine (registering a NEW variant id
that doesn't exist yet). Three options:

(a) Add a third primitive `fresh-keyword` to args that documents the
    fresh-id-by-policy posture (e.g. bounded-prefix check).

(b) Retire `parse-keyword` and have callers inline `keyword` with a
    comment + the bounded-prefix check.

(c) Keep `parse-keyword` but rename to `unsafe-keyword` so the threat
    model is on the surface.

(a) is the masterpiece bar — adds a positive primitive instead of a
warning-laden one. (b) is the YAGNI option.

title: perf(mcp-base): thread accumulator through collect-patches recursion (rf2-u64jt F12)
description:
Per rf2-u64jt audit F12 (ai/findings/mcp-base-slice-audit-2026-05-15.md).

`re-frame.mcp-base.diff-encode/collect-map-patches` (diff_encode.cljc:160-199)
recurses via `(into acc (collect-patches av bv p))` for sub-map values.
Each recursion allocates an intermediate patches vector that's then
into-ed back into the parent accumulator. For deep app-db diffs (5-10
levels of nesting on the typical re-frame app) this is one extra
allocation per recursion site.

Two refactor options:

(a) Pass the accumulator through: `(collect-patches a b path acc)` —
    `collect-map-patches` then `(reduce-kv ... acc b)` and recursion
    threads the same acc.

(b) Use a transient vector across the whole collect-patches call,
    persisted only at the public boundary.

(a) is the cleaner surface (the new signature is honest). Benchmark on
a representative app-db diff before merging; if the saving is sub-10%
on a deep diff, leave the simpler form in place. The win is mostly
allocation pressure on the GC, not throughput.

title: test(mcp-base): pin apply-patches contract on malformed input (rf2-u64jt F17)
description:
Per rf2-u64jt audit F17 (ai/findings/mcp-base-slice-audit-2026-05-15.md).

`re-frame.mcp-base.diff-encode/apply-patches` silently no-ops on
malformed patches. A patch like `[[:a]]` (missing op) destructures to
`op nil`, falls through the cond to `:else acc`, and the corrupted
patch is dropped without a peep.

Two acceptable resolutions:

(a) Document the contract — silent passthrough on unknown op — and pin
    it with a test (`(is (= base (apply-patches base [[[:a]]])))`).

(b) Validate on entry via `patches-schema` and throw `:rf.error/bad-diff-patches`
    (mirrors the encoder boundary).

(a) is the cheap fix; (b) is the masterpiece bar. The decode boundary
already trusts the encoder's pinned grammar — and `decode-db-after`
calls `apply-patches` directly with the encoder's emission. A third-
party caller (causa-mcp's wire decoder) crossing the boundary with a
malformed patch SHOULD see the error. **Pick (b).**

`diff_encode_test.clj`. Pre-alpha.

title: refactor(epoch): replace positional [:fail kw tags] with destructure or map shape
description:
## Finding

Parent audit: rf2-3391t (round-3 epoch audit). See `ai/findings/epoch-slice-audit-2026-05-15.md` §F4.

**Severity:** LOW — readability / masterpiece-bar hygiene.

## Impl citation

`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:1077-1080` (restore-epoch) and `epoch.cljc:1178-1181` (reset-frame-db!):

```clojure
(case (first result)
  :ok   (perform-restore! frame-id (second result))
  :fail (do (emit-precondition-failure! (second result) (nth result 2))
            false))
```

The `(nth result 2)` reads as positional access into a tagged tuple — a code smell. The pattern repeats in both dispatch sites.

## Fix options

**Option A — destructure at call site:**

```clojure
(let [[outcome kw tags] result]
  (case outcome
    :ok   (perform-restore! frame-id kw)  ;; here kw is actually the epoch
    :fail (do (emit-precondition-failure! kw tags) false)))
```

But this conflates the `:ok` second-slot (the resolved epoch record) with the `:fail` second-slot (the trace op keyword). Slightly awkward.

**Option B — map result shape:**

```clojure
(let [{:keys [outcome epoch op tags]} result]
  (case outcome
    :ok   (perform-restore! frame-id epoch)
    :fail (do (emit-precondition-failure! op tags) false)))
```

Update precondition helpers to return `{:outcome :ok :epoch <epoch>}` or `{:outcome :fail :op <kw> :tags <map>}`. Clearer.

**Option C — leave as is** but pull the `:fail` branch into a small helper:

```clojure
(defn- emit-fail! [[_ kw tags]]
  (emit-precondition-failure! kw tags)
  false)
```

Lowest-churn. The positional nth at the dispatch site disappears.

Option B reads best for masterpiece-bar; option C is the smallest diff. Author's choice.

title: [spec+impl] reg-http-interceptor bypasses :rf/registration-metadata — no :doc / source-coords / spec schema
description:
## Source
rf2-bc0k6 audit finding G5 (MEDIUM severity).

## Gap
`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_middleware.cljc` L46-89 `reg-http-interceptor` accepts `{:frame :id :before}` and stores ONLY `{:id :before}` in a frame-keyed atom (`interceptors`). It bypasses the registrar entirely. No `:doc`, no source-coords, no `:tags`, no `:spec`.

Spec-Schemas catalogues 10 per-kind metadata shapes after rf2-kxs6j (`:rf/event-handler-meta`, `:rf/sub-meta`, ..., `:rf/error-projector-meta`) plus `:rf/route-metadata`. There is NO `:rf/http-interceptor-meta`.

Spec 014 §Middleware doesn't describe registration metadata at all — only the chain semantics.

## Effect
- Spec 001 intro promises 'every reg-* accepts' registration-metadata. `reg-http-interceptor` is an undocumented exception.
- pair2-mcp's `handler-meta` tool can't introspect interceptors at all (no registrar slot).
- A future Causa HTTP-middleware panel can't show 'this interceptor lives at line 42 of foo.cljs.'
- Story / docs tools can't surface 'this interceptor does X' via a `:doc` slot.

## Fix
Twofold:

1. **Spec.** Add `:rf/http-interceptor-meta` to Spec-Schemas, composing with `:rf/registration-metadata`. Cross-reference Spec 014.

2. **Impl.** Have `reg-http-interceptor` capture source-coords (via the same mechanism as other reg-* — call-site-macros or merge-coords). Store the registration-metadata alongside `:before`. Either:
   - Add a dedicated `(http-interceptor-meta frame id)` query that returns the metadata, OR
   - Fold the frame-keyed interceptor side-table into the registrar under `:http-interceptor` kind (would expand the closed v1 kind set — needs SA-3 review).

Probably option 1 (separate query) — keeping the registrar's closed v1 set stable. Cross-cutting with rf2-44zpf (pair2-mcp kind enum extension) — both could land together as 'pair2 introspection covers HTTP middleware too.'

## Why pre-alpha
SA-3 says every contract surface has a schema in Spec-Schemas. Interceptors are a contract surface. Currently they aren't covered.

title: [tools] pair2-mcp handler-meta response never gets :rf.source/uri decoration (pipeline + shape mismatch)
description:
## Source
rf2-bc0k6 audit finding G4 (MEDIUM severity).

## Bug
`tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/handler_meta.cljs` L13-16 claims: 'The wire-pipeline (post-rf2-cibp8) decorates every :source-coord map with an :rf.source/uri string — so the AI host renders an immediate jump-to-editor link off the handler-meta response.'

Reality — TWO compounding problems:

1. **Pipeline never runs.** `handler_meta.cljs` L191-202 returns `(wire/ok-text {:ok? true ...})` directly. It does NOT call `wp/run-wire-pipeline` (compare snapshot.cljs L119, trace_window.cljs L91, etc.).

2. **Even if it did, the shape wouldn't match.** The source-uri walker (`tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/source_uri.cljs` L57-66 `coord-map?`) looks for a map with a `:source-coord` slot whose VALUE is a map carrying `:file`. But registration metadata stores `:ns`/`:line`/`:file`/`:column` FLAT at the top level (see rf2-bc0k6-G3 / new bead on Spec-Schemas wording).

## Effect
The promised 'one-click jump-to-definition affordance for every event/sub/fx the agent inspects' (source_uri.cljs L18-20) DOES NOT FIRE for handler-meta. It does fire on trace events / snapshot / watch-epochs (which DO nest source-coord as a sub-map per TraceEvent — Spec-Schemas L429-433). So the walker is not dead-on-arrival, but its handler-meta consumption is.

## Fix options
- (a) Route handler-meta through wire-pipeline AND nest the four flat keys under `:source-coord` before piping.
- (b) Extend source-uri's walker to also probe for the FLAT `:ns/:line/:file/:column` shape and decorate the parent map with `:rf.source/uri`. Simpler.
- (c) Have handler-meta produce both shapes (flat keys for backward compat + a `:source-coord` sub-map of the same four keys) and pipe through wire-pipeline.

Mike's call. Probably (b) for minimum disruption.

## Bundle with
- rf2-4h8ny (Spec-Schemas wording fix) — the right text depends on which shape we standardise on
- Fix `handler_meta.cljs` L13-16 docstring as part of this bead
notes: Landed in PR #1165 (cluster: registration-metadata fallout)
close_reason: Landed via PR #1165 registration-metadata fallout cluster

title: [spec] Spec-Schemas :rf/source-coord-meta wording says 'sub-map' but impl emits flat keys
description:
## Source
rf2-bc0k6 audit finding G3 (MEDIUM severity, doc-only).

## Drift
`spec/Spec-Schemas.md` describes `:rf/source-coord-meta` as 'Returned (as a sub-map of :rf/registration-metadata) from (rf/handler-meta kind id)' (L342) and 'read its source-coord sub-map' (L375). The implementation does NOT produce a sub-map.

Impl reality (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc` L43-52): `merge-coords` MERGES `{:ns :line :file :column}` FLAT into user-meta. Verified by `implementation/core/test/re_frame/source_coords_test.clj` L51-59 which asserts `(:ns meta)` / `(:line meta)` / `(:file meta)` — flat reads.

Other spec docs CORRECT:
- `spec/Tool-Pair.md` L452: ':ns/:line/:column/:file keys on (handler-meta ...) return'
- `spec/API.md` L336: 'View registrations include source-coord keys (:ns / :line / :column / :file)'

So Spec-Schemas is the outlier.

## Note on trace events
`:source-coord` IS a sub-map on trace events — see Spec-Schemas L429-433 TraceEvent's `:rf.trace/trigger-handler` `:source-coord` shape. The Schema shape itself (the 4-key map definition L344-350) is correct; only the WORDING around it ('sub-map of registration-metadata') is wrong.

## Fix
Doc-only. Rewrite Spec-Schemas L342 + L375 to say:
- 'The registration-metadata map carries flat `:ns` / `:line` / `:file` / `:column` keys at the top level, conforming to `:rf/source-coord-meta`'s shape. Trace events nest these same four keys under `:source-coord` (per TraceEvent's `:rf.trace/trigger-handler` slot).'

Also consider correcting pair2-mcp's `handler_meta.cljs` L13 doc-string ('carrying :source-coord (file/line/column/ns)') — same drift, downstream of this. Bundle with rf2-bc0k6-G4 fix.
