title: design(ssr): unify validator-failure render path (tag-name vs CRLF) — fixed body or projected page?
description:
Surfaced by rf2-to8pm PR #1159 e2e tests.

## The asymmetry

Two SSR JVM validator paths reach the wire differently:

1. **tag-name validator** (e.g. \`(keyword \"has space\")\`) — throws *inside* \`render-to-string\` → outer \`try/catch\` in \`ssr-handler\` routes to \`:on-error\` → wire = **500 + fixed \"Internal error\" body** (rf2-kzvwq path).
2. **CRLF cookie/header validators** (\`:rf.server/set-cookie\` / \`:rf.server/set-header\` with CRLF) — throw mid-drain via \`:rf.error/cookie-invalid-value\` / \`:rf.error/header-invalid-value\` → SSR error projector buffers + projects → **500 status**, but render still proceeds and body content still emits.

Both produce a 500. Both fail-fast before the bad bytes hit the wire (assertion confirms no CRLF in any wire header value). But the **body contract differs**:
- Path 1: fixed canonical error string
- Path 2: whatever the projector renders (could be the error page, could be the original view minus the rejected cookie/header)

## Why it matters

\`Spec/011 §Server error projection\` lets you render an error page — so path 2 is by-spec. Path 1's fixed string is the bare-minimum fallback when render itself blows up. These are two different recovery layers, both legitimate.

But the inconsistency is observable from the client. A monitor that expects 500-bodies to be 'Internal error' on the tag-name failure mode will see a richer body on the CRLF mode. That's not necessarily wrong, but it's not principled.

## Options

- **(A)** Leave as-is and document the layering in Spec/011 (render-time failures = fixed body; drain-time failures = projector). My recommendation if we want minimal API change.
- **(B)** Route tag-name failures through the projector too — render fails → projector renders an error page → uniform body contract. Requires moving the tag-name try/catch one layer up.
- **(C)** Route CRLF failures through the fixed-body fallback — uniform but loses the projector's value for header-level failures.

Pre-alpha posture: pick whichever yields the most elegant invariant. My instinct is (B) — projector becomes the single render-side failure surface — but Mike's call.

## Cross-refs

- rf2-to8pm — e2e tests that surfaced this (PR #1159).
- rf2-kzvwq — fixed-body fallback origin.
- Spec/011 §Server error projection — the projector layer.
close_reason: DECISION 2026-05-19 (Mike): (B) PROJECTOR AS SINGLE RENDER-SIDE FAILURE SURFACE. Tag-name failures route through projector; uniform 500 body contract. Impl bead filed today.

title: [test] Conformance fixtures for http-interceptors (reg / clear / before pipeline)
description:
Split out from rf2-f082b — HTTP-interceptor conformance fixtures need new runtime plumbing the bead didn't carry.

## Problem

`reg-http-interceptor` / `clear-http-interceptor` are direct fn-call APIs, not fx that the conformance DSL can drive. The existing http-managed-*.edn fixtures use `:rf.http/managed` as an fx via `:fx-overrides`, but there is no `:rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor` runtime fx — so a portable EDN fixture has no way to register / clear an interceptor.

## Proposed scope

Add a `:rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor` (and `:rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor`) runtime fx wrapper around `re-frame.http-middleware/reg-http-interceptor` (and `clear-http-interceptor`) so the conformance DSL can drive them via the existing `:fx` op. Then add fixtures:

- `http-interceptor-before-transforms.edn` — register a `:before` interceptor; observe `:rf.http.interceptor/registered` trace and that the interceptor body modifies the outbound request shape (via a captured side-channel app-db slot the interceptor writes to).
- `http-interceptor-clear.edn` — register then clear; observe `:rf.http.interceptor/cleared` trace and that a subsequent canned-success request runs without the interceptor's effect.

## Source

rf2-f082b sweep — http-interceptors carve-out.
notes: PR #1162 https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1162 — implementation complete; awaiting merge.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1162 — :rf.fx/reg-http-interceptor + :rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor fx wrappers in implementation/http/; 2 EDN conformance fixtures in spec/conformance/fixtures/; harness contract fix (registry-without-handler no longer noops framework reg); canned stubs now walk request-side interceptor chain (correctness fix surfaced by the work)

title: [JVM core test flake] re-frame.substrate.plain-atom derived-value identity check fails intermittently
description:
Surfaced on PR #1142 CI (docs-only change; JVM core test failed unrelated to diff). Failure: '(not (identical? #object[re_frame.substrate.plain_atom$make_derived_value$reify__3930 ...] #object[re_frame.substrate.plain_atom$make_derived_value$reify__3930 ...]))' with both reified objects holding {:status :ready, :val 5}.

Likely identity check on a derived-value reify that should be returning the same instance but isn't. Possibly the make-derived-value cache key drift, or a non-deterministic reagent-shaped state churn.

Suggested investigation:
1. Locate the failing test in implementation/core/test/re_frame/substrate/plain_atom_test.cljc
2. Reproduce locally (may need multiple runs to surface)
3. Either fix the identity-preservation logic OR weaken the assertion to value-equality

Priority P3 — intermittent; doesn't block functional correctness. Should be tracked.
close_reason: Duplicate of rf2-e8e74 (PR #1299 merged 2026-05-16). Root cause: sub_cache_deferred_grace_test.clj's grace=200ms + Thread/sleep 80ms left ~120ms margin against JVM ScheduledExecutorService — deferred-dispose timer could fire before second subscribe arrived, evicting the slot. PR #1299 commit 99a0222d replaced grace=60000ms + back-to-back unsubscribe/subscribe (CAS-based, wall-clock-independent). Worker rf2-jzudg-v2 verified 30/30 stable under heavy scheduler pressure. No new code needed. Closed 2026-05-17 04:50 AUSEST.

title: doc(schemas/walker): clarify non-vector schema-form skip + suggest opt-in warn
description:
Security audit follow-up (rf2-kojc4 F3; ai/findings/schemas-security-audit-2026-05-15.md).

## Action

`walker.cljc:25-35` documents that non-vector schema forms (compiled Malli, registry refs) are leaves to the walker — their internal `:sensitive?` / `:large?` annotations are invisible. The contract is correct but discoverability is poor; users can mark a registry-ref'd schema with per-slot `:sensitive?` and the walker silently doesn't honour it.

## Direction options (pick one)

(a) Doc-only update: enrich the docstring at `walker.cljc:25-35` to be more explicit + add an inline example showing how registration-meta (`{:sensitive? true}` on `reg-event-*`) gets you the coarse honour even when per-slot doesn't apply. Cheap.

(b) Warn at registration time: if `reg-app-schema` receives a non-vector schema value, emit a one-time `:rf.warning/schema-walker-non-vector-form` per (schema-id, form-shape) hint that per-slot `:sensitive?` / `:large?` won't apply. Defence-in-clarity.

Bead opens with default position (a). Mike picks direction at dispatch time.

## Cross-refs

- rf2-kojc4 (parent audit bead).
- `schemas_walker_operators_test.clj:113-124` — current behaviour pin.
close_reason: PR #1353: docstring at walker.cljc now explicitly documents the silent-skip for non-vector schema forms, recommends two workable shapes (vector form or registration-level meta for coarse honour), and includes a side-by-side vector-form vs registry-ref example.

title: feat(schemas): one-time warn when reg-app-schema runs but validator hook unbound
description:
Security audit follow-up (rf2-kojc4 F1; ai/findings/schemas-security-audit-2026-05-15.md).

## Action

Schemas default to soft-pass when no validator is registered (`validator.cljc:55-66, 253-261`). This is intentional per Spec/010 §Recommended soft-pass — but boundary-validated handlers can silently accept untrusted input when the Malli adapter ns isn't loaded.

Emit a one-time process-lifecycle warning when `reg-app-schema` / `reg-app-schemas` is invoked AND `:schemas/malli-validate` late-bind hook is unbound AND `validator-fn` is still the framework default.

## Concrete steps

1. `storage.cljc` (or `schemas.cljc`) — on `reg-app-schema` / `reg-app-schemas`, check validator availability and emit `:rf.warning/schema-validator-unavailable` once per process via a dedup atom.
2. Skip emit when an explicit non-default validator is registered (apps that opted out of Malli).
3. Skip emit on tear-down / re-registration after the first warning has fired.
4. Tests: warn fires once; warn doesn't fire after `set-schema-validator!` is called with a non-default fn; warn doesn't fire on second `reg-app-schema` call.

## Acceptance

- New trace event documented under Spec/009 §Warning catalogue (or refer to Conventions reserved-prefix `:rf.warning/*`).
- One-time-per-process dedup; tests pin behaviour.
- Schemas test suite stays green.

## Cross-refs

- rf2-kojc4 (parent audit bead).
- Spec/010 §Recommended soft-pass.
- Security.md §Production gates.
close_reason: PR #1353: :rf.warning/schema-validator-unavailable emitted once per process from reg-app-schema/s when :schemas/malli-validate is unbound AND validator-fn is still the default. Suppressed when Malli adapter loaded OR explicit non-default validator installed. Production elides via interop/debug-enabled?. 8 new tests; Spec 009 catalogue + schemas.cljc emit-source list updated.

title: fix(core): drop stale :app-db-before / :app-db-after refs from privacy.cljc docstrings
description:
DOC DRIFT — cheap fix.

`implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc:30-32` (ns docstring) and lines 156-160 (`with-redacted` docstring) reference `:event/db-changed` `:tags :app-db-before` / `:app-db-after` slots as something `with-redacted` scrubs. The runtime's actual `:event/db-changed` emit (`router.cljc:426, 439`) carries `{:event-id :event :frame :phase?}` only — NO `:app-db-*` tags.

Spec/009 line 130 mentions `:app-db-before` / `:app-db-after` aspirationally in the `:tags` 'existing examples' row but does not require them on `:event/db-changed`. Spec/009 line 1225's normative MUST only requires `:event` to be scrubbed under `with-redacted`.

FIX: edit the two docstring references in `privacy.cljc` to drop the `:app-db-before` / `:app-db-after` claims. The `:rf.trace/trigger-handler` and `:rf.error/handler-exception` references in the same docstring ARE accurate (those events do copy the event vector and consult `:rf/redacted-event`).

FILES: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/privacy.cljc:30-32, 156-160`.

title: test(skills-shared): regression checks for retro-protocol hardening (prompt-injection + redaction)
description:
Follow-on from the rf2-g6auh audit verification (see ai/findings/skills-shared-audit-verification-2026-05-15.md, finding 4).

# Goal
Add a small regression suite that asserts the two normative protections in skills/shared/retro-protocol.md actually hold across consumer skills (re-frame2-improver, re-frame-pair-retro2):

1. Injected instructions inside reviewed code / transcripts / docstrings are ignored.
2. Sensitive strings (tokens, internal URLs, home-dir paths, PII) are redacted in findings output, not just bead/issue bodies.

# Scope
- Fixture-based prompts that embed injection-carrier evidence and assert the agent's response doesn't follow them.
- Fixture-based prompts seeded with redaction-target strings (API tokens, /Users/<name>/, internal hostnames, emails) and assert the agent masks with stable <REDACTED-*-N> placeholders.
- Run against both consuming skills.

# Out of scope
- Hardening the protocol itself — already complete (PR #1116, PR #1127).
- New attacker classes beyond those enumerated at retro-protocol.md:17-22.

# Acceptance
- New test artefact (or extension to an existing one) that runs each scenario.
- Wired into a workflow gate so future protocol drift gets caught.

# References
- skills/shared/retro-protocol.md (audit target)
- ai/findings/skills-shared-audit-verification-2026-05-15.md (verification doc)
- rf2-g6auh (original audit)
- PR #1116 (rf2-k4a2u — protocol hardening)
- PR #1127 (rf2-wy48o + rf2-k99pt — improver adoption)

title: harden(skills/re-frame2-improver): schemaless-events catalogue — production-validation gap (downstream of rf2-wy48o finding 3)
description:
Follow-on to rf2-wy48o (security audit, finding 3).

## Audit excerpt (rf2-wy48o)

> Boundary-schema detection can miss production validation gaps.
> Evidence: `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md:9-12` flags missing `:spec`, missing `reg-app-schema`, or some missing `validate-at-boundary` cases, but line 20 states both schema mechanisms are dev-elided in production unless `validate-at-boundary` is attached. The canonical fix then softens this to handlers that "must validate in production builds" (`schemaless-events.md:20,24`), so a boundary handler with `:spec` and `reg-app-schema` but no production interceptor can still pass review.
> Impact: the skill can miss untrusted HTTP / WebSocket / query-string / postMessage paths that bypass runtime validation in production.

## Scope

- Tighten `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md` so any handler crossing an untrusted boundary (HTTP / WebSocket / query-string / postMessage / `localStorage` rehydration) is flagged unless production validation is present (`validate-at-boundary` or an equivalent always-on gate), **even when `:spec` and `reg-app-schema` are already attached**.
- Update the detection-rule wording so dev-elided mechanisms no longer satisfy the catalogue rule on their own.
- Add a regression example (boundary handler with `:spec` + `reg-app-schema` but no production interceptor) that the rule flags.

## Acceptance

- The catalogue leaf flags a boundary handler that has dev-only validation.
- `mkdocs build --strict` warning count unchanged.

## Boundaries

- Surface: `skills/re-frame2-improver/references/schemaless-events.md` only (and possibly a minor cross-link tweak in the improver SKILL.md).
- Do NOT touch the shared `retro-protocol.md` — that leaf is catalogue-agnostic.

## Cross-refs

- rf2-wy48o — parent security audit (this bead carries finding 3)
- rf2-k4a2u — sibling fix on retro-protocol (closed audit findings 1 + part of 2)
- rf2-yt7ea — sibling fix on improver SKILL.md Edit-gate alignment (remainder of audit finding 2)

title: align(skills/re-frame2-improver): surface evidence-shaped vs canonical-idiom Edit gate distinction (downstream of rf2-k4a2u)
description:
Follow-on to rf2-k4a2u. The shared protocol now distinguishes:

- **Evidence-shaped Edit** — content/motivation derived from user-supplied evidence (snippet, transcript, stack trace, recap, in-source comments). Requires explicit user approval, even when mechanical.
- **Canonical-idiom Edit** — content derived from canonical repo idioms (spec/, skills/re-frame2/patterns/). Remains unrestricted; the location came from evidence but the rewrite came from the spec.

`skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md` currently says:

- Line 76 (Workflow step 5): *"Grounded mechanical rewrites can use Edit when the agent is confident."*
- Line 100 (Anti-patterns): *"Mechanical rewrites with a clear canonical idiom only."*

Both statements are *consistent* with the shared protocol (canonical-idiom edits remain unrestricted), but neither surfaces the new evidence-shaped vs canonical-idiom distinction. A reviewer reading only `re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md` would still apply the old "confident → Edit" rule.

## Scope

- One-paragraph addition or line-edit in `skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md` §Workflow step 5 and/or §Anti-patterns making the distinction visible at the consuming-skill layer.
- Cross-link to `../shared/retro-protocol.md#the-seven-step-protocol` (Edit-gate sub-bullets).
- Possibly extend `re-frame2-improver/references/README.md` to flag that anti-pattern rewrites must be canonical-idiom shaped, not evidence-shaped.

## Acceptance

- A reader of `skills/re-frame2-improver/SKILL.md` alone understands the evidence-shaped Edit gate.
- `mkdocs build --strict` warning count unchanged.

## Boundaries

- Surface: `skills/re-frame2-improver/` only.
- Do NOT mirror the prose at retro-protocol depth — the shared protocol is the normative source; the consuming skill cross-links.
- Pre-alpha: no back-compat shim.

## Cross-refs

- rf2-k4a2u — parent (this fix landed)
- rf2-bscrl — original decision (yes-all)
- rf2-wy48o — security audit; this bead partially addresses finding 2.

title: test(ssr): JVM-side end-to-end validator coverage (tag-name + header/cookie CRLF)
description:
Follow-on from rf2-ik4io.

The SSR browser-testbed surfaces (rf2-ik4io) cover the hydration
round-trip from the *client* end. The recently-landed JVM-side
safety primitives — tag-name validator (rf2-z7gor) and
header-name + cookie-field CRLF validators — fail-fast on the
JVM render path, before any HTML bytes go on the wire. The
client never sees the broken HTML, which is the *point* of
fail-fast, but this also means there's no client-side surface
where these validators can be exercised.

These validators have strong JVM-only coverage in
implementation/ssr/test/ (the conformance + end-to-end + emit
tests). What's missing is the *integrated* round-trip: spin up
a real JVM SSR host, hit it with HTTP, observe that bad
tag-name keywords / CRLF-bearing cookie values produce a
structured error response (e.g. a 5xx with the error payload
projected via the error-projector surface), and that no
malformed HTML reaches the client.

Approach options:

  A. Add a JVM-integration test in implementation/ssr-ring/test/
     that starts a real Ring host, dispatches a known-bad
     handler, asserts on the response shape.

  B. Add a Playwright fetch() probe in a new
     testbeds/ssr_validator_*/ surface that hits a JVM
     endpoint (requires a running JVM SSR host).

  C. Stay JVM-only — the validator's contract (":rf.error/*"
     thrown ex-info) is fully observable from clojure.test.
     Document the boundary in spec/011-SSR.md so consumers
     know where to look.

Recommend C unless cross-language porters need an
integration-shaped regression net. The JVM contract is the
load-bearing one; browser testbeds are scoped to the client-
visible behaviour by design.

Cross-references:
  - rf2-ik4io (parent: SSR browser integration tests)
  - rf2-z7gor (tag-name validator)
  - PR #1113 (the rf2-ik4io PR; out-of-scope note here)
  - spec/011-SSR.md \xa7HTTP response contract (the
    affected fxs' validators)

title: codify canonical event-vector shape [event-id <optional-map>] — best-practice doc only (no enforcement)
description:
Mike confirmed (during rf2-jvzxh walkthrough): the canonical re-frame2 event-vector shape is **[event-id]** or **[event-id <map>]** (map optional). Variadic args ([:ev x y z]) are NOT canonical.

## Current state

PR #1092 (rf2-vflrg) tightened pair2-mcp dispatch from raw text-splice to EDN-parse + `(vector? parsed)` check. But the vector? check is too permissive — it accepts ANY vector shape including variadic.

## Two surfaces to address

### 1. Codify the canonical shape

If not already documented, add to:
- spec/Conventions.md (likely) — event-vector shape MUST line
- spec/002-Frames.md §Dispatch envelope — describe canonical [event-id <map>] shape
- spec/API.md — dispatch/dispatch-sync signatures + canonical shape

Check first if it's already documented — grep spec/ for 'event-id' or '[event-id' or canonical event shape language. If already there, just cross-ref.

### 2. Tighten validators in:
- tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/dispatch.cljs — replace `(not (vector? parsed))` with strict shape check:
  - 1-element vector with keyword 1st elem → OK
  - 2-element vector with keyword 1st + map 2nd → OK
  - Anything else → :reason :non-canonical-event-shape (structured error with hint pointing at canonical form)
- Likely also: re-frame.core/dispatch + dispatch-sync internal validation? Check current behavior — does the framework itself accept variadic events? If yes, that's a wider drift.

## Why this matters

- Pre-alpha masterpiece: canonical shape needs ONE shape, not 'mostly canonical except this edge case'
- AI implementers reading the spec deserve unambiguous contract
- Variadic events make migration tooling harder (re-frame v1 was variadic)

## Boundaries

- Pre-alpha: no back-compat for variadic — fail-fast at the boundary
- If grep reveals variadic event vectors in worked examples or testbeds, file as separate cleanup bead (one for each surface family)

## Cross-refs

- rf2-jvzxh (CLOSED with #1092 + Mike's confirm) — surfaced this gap
- PR #1092 — the validator that's too loose
- Memory rf2-pattern-thesis (language-agnostic pattern — canonical shapes are load-bearing)

## Priority

P2 — quality-tightening; not blocking shipping. Could become P1 if downstream tooling (migration, story-mcp dispatch, causa-mcp) inherits the looseness.
notes: PR #1117 opened: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1117 — codified canonical event-vector shape [event-id <optional-map>] in spec/Conventions.md (new section), spec/API.md (dispatch/subscribe annotation), implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc (dispatch+dispatch-sync docstrings), implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc (dispatch! docstring). Doc-only, no validator changes. CLJS tests pass 2014/0, link validator clean.

title: [testbeds/http_toggle] canned-failure stub bypasses :rf.http/<kind> trace emit
description:
**Action**: The http_toggle testbed README claims each canned-failure click emits an ordered `:rf.http/dispatched` / `:rf.http/<kind>` trace stream. But the framework's canned-failure-handler (`re-frame.http-machine-wrapper/canned-failure-handler`) skips `finalise-failure!` — only `finalise-failure!` calls `(trace/emit-error! (:kind failure) redacted)`. So canned-failure clicks fire NO `:operation :rf.http/<kind>` trace events at all.

The only Spec 014 trace events the canned-failure stub produces are the generic ones from the fx walker (`:event/dispatched`, `:rf.fx/handled` with `:fx-id :rf.http/managed-canned-failure`). The `:operation :rf.http/<kind>` (category-attributed) emit only happens on the live failure path.

**Discovered**: while landing rf2-fe84r cross-cutting scenario #2 (HTTP failure cascade with category attribution). The scenario passes by asserting on the fx-id + the DOM mirror (category survives the reply round-trip), not on the README's documented `:rf.http/<kind>` trace.

**Fix decision**: either
1. Make `canned-failure-handler` call `(trace/emit-error! kind ...)` to match the live path's contract, or
2. Update the testbed README to match the actual behavior — the `:rf.http/<kind>` traces only fire on the LIVE failure path.

Option 1 makes the testbed match its docs and lets the cross-cutting scenario assert directly on the trace bus's `:rf.http/<kind>` operation rather than the fx-handled proxy.
notes: PR #1134 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1134

title: [testbeds/drain_depth_trigger] error-emit listener never fires for :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded
description:
**Action**: The drain_depth_trigger testbed (rf2-kzcim) registers an `install-halt-listener!` via `rf/register-error-emit-listener!` that's supposed to flip the `:halted?` mirror to true after a drain-depth-exceeded halt. But the framework only emits `:rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded` via `trace/emit-error!` — NOT through `error-emit/dispatch-on-error!` (which is what `register-error-emit-listener!` subscribes to). The listener's callback is never invoked; the mirror stays "false" forever.

Source: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` lines 743-766 — the depth-exceeded path calls `(trace/emit-error! :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded ...)` only. Compare with `emit-handler-exception!` (lines 285-360) which uses BOTH `error-emit/dispatch-on-error!` (always-on) AND `trace/emit-error!` (dev-only).

**Discovered**: while landing rf2-fe84r cross-cutting scenario #6 (drain-depth rollback). The scenario passes without asserting on the `:halted?` mirror — the framework-side observables (`:depth-reached` rolling back to 0, the `:halted-depth` epoch record landing in `rf/epoch-history`) cover the contract. The testbed's halt-listener is unused.

**Fix decision**: either
1. Make the framework dispatch `:rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded` through the always-on error-emit substrate (matching the handler-exception pattern), or
2. Remove the `install-halt-listener!` / `:halted?` mirror from the testbed since it's unused.

Option 1 is the canonical fix (matches the Spec 009 §What IS available in production contract — drain-depth IS a production-observable failure). Option 2 is cosmetic.
notes: PR #1134 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1134 (option b — drop unused mirror)

title: review(docs): assess Causa + Story tutorials against best-practice criteria once rf2-6e53j lands
description:
## Why this exists

Follow-on to **rf2-6e53j** (lift CLJS/Story/Causa to top ribbon + write Playwright-screenshot tutorials for Causa + Story). Once the Causa + Story tutorials land, review them against **best practices for positive human-facing tutorials** and produce concrete improvement recommendations.

## Scope

Read both tutorials end-to-end after rf2-6e53j lands. Assess against best-practice criteria:

### Tutorial quality dimensions

1. **Voice + tone** — Friendly, walking-through-it; never condescending; never reference-manual-shaped. Should pull the reader through, not page-by-page reference. Inherits re-frame's existing voice (see `docs/guide/on-dynamics.md` style).

2. **Sequencing** — Strong opening (hook + payoff promise within first paragraph). Each section builds on the previous. Each step has a clear "now I can do X" payoff. End with a "where to go next" pointer (NOT just stops).

3. **Annotated screenshots** — Used at every conceptual transition (not just decorative). Annotations are crisp + necessary (no overload). Captions reinforce what the reader's eye should latch onto.

4. **Concrete examples** — Real fragments of code / state / output, not hand-waved "imagine your app does this." Reader can copy-paste + verify.

5. **Friction removal** — Every "but what if I want to X" moment answered inline, not deferred to reference. Common mistakes called out at the point they'd happen.

6. **Length pacing** — Multi-page if needed (per Mike's clarification). Each page covers one cohesive theme. No page should feel like padding.

7. **Cross-substrate consistency** — Causa + Story tutorials should feel like sibling artefacts (same chrome, same patterns, same voice).

### Specific risks to check

- **Lecture mode**: tutorial reads as "here are all the panels" instead of "let me show you how to debug a real session." Likely failure mode for devtool docs.
- **Screenshot decay**: screenshots out of sync with current UI. The Playwright pipeline (rf2-6e53j step D) should re-generate on docs commits — verify CI catches drift.
- **Sterile examples**: every example uses `counter` because that's what the testbeds provide. Push for at least one more substantial walkthrough (e.g., an HTTP cascade or a state-machine).
- **Buried hero features**: rf2-g5q8d (click-to-source) and Story Test Codegen are USP-level — they should be early in the tutorials, not buried.

### Reference material

- **`docs/guide/on-dynamics.md`** — the canonical re-frame voice exemplar
- **Storybook 9's docs** — for Story tutorial comparison
- **Redux DevTools docs** — for Causa tutorial comparison (similar shape; opportunity to be cleaner)
- **`ai/findings/bookish-aesthetic-for-guide-2026-05-14.md`** — for aesthetic direction

## Output

**Findings doc**: `ai/findings/tutorials-review-causa-story-YYYY-MM-DD.md` (date when actioned).

Structure:
- One section per tutorial (Causa, Story)
- Per-section: per-dimension verdict (✅ / ⚠️ / ❌) with concrete evidence
- Specific recommendations: rewrite passages / replace screenshots / split or merge pages / add cross-refs
- Optional: file follow-on improvement beads per ⚠️ + ❌

## Acceptance

- Findings doc lands
- Specific actionable recommendations filed as follow-on beads (or rolled directly into a tutorial-polish PR if scope is small)
- Mike eyeballs the findings + decides which to action

## Dependencies

- Blocks on **rf2-6e53j** — tutorials must exist first

## Boundaries

- **Review-only.** Do NOT edit tutorials in this bead. Recommendations only.
- Findings doc lives in `ai/findings/` (gitignored).

## Priority

P3 — quality polish on docs that don't exist yet. Should be done within a week of rf2-6e53j landing while context is fresh.

## Cross-references

- rf2-6e53j (parent)
- rf2-tmr1s (guide-coverage audit — informs what NOT to duplicate)
- Storybook 9 + Histoire + Ladle docs (Story comparison)
- `ai/findings/bookish-aesthetic-for-guide-2026-05-14.md` (aesthetic context)
notes: Review complete 2026-05-15 02:55 AUSEST. Findings doc at `ai/findings/tutorials-review-causa-story-2026-05-15.md`. Verdict: solidly good, not yet masterpiece bar. Three patterns: lecture-mode drift (Causa chs 7-10, Story ch 5), counter-monoculture across both, USP execution under-delivers on hero-chapter screenshots. Filed 6 follow-on beads: rf2-we013 (P2, annotate screenshots), rf2-0sg12 (P2, non-counter examples cart-total+login-form), rf2-tadee (P3, Causa voice rescue chs 7-10), rf2-hhwcm (P3, reposition Causa ch 6), rf2-2yvwh (P3, deepen Story ch 5), rf2-duat7 (P3, 8 missing screenshots + bookkeeping). Closing as REVIEWED-with-follow-ons.

Filed 6 follow-on beads: rf2-we013 (P2 annotate screenshots), rf2-0sg12 (P2 non-counter examples), rf2-tadee (P3 Causa voice rescue chs 7-10), rf2-hhwcm (P3 reposition Causa ch 6), rf2-2yvwh (P3 deepen Story ch 5), rf2-duat7 (P3 8 missing screenshots + bookkeeping).

title: [infra] shadow-cljs :infer-warning blocks in test build mask quiet-reporter signal
description:
Following rf2-try1x (PR #1079), the cljs.test reporter is silent-on-success but `npm run test:cljs` still emits ~32 shadow-cljs :infer-warning blocks (~16 lines each ≈ 500 lines). Baseline measurement: green run = 521 lines, but the actual cljs.test stdout is 3 lines; the rest is compile-time warnings.

Path forward: either (a) fix the inference warnings in the offending test bodies (e.g. `implementation/core/test/re_frame/substrate/spine_dispose_cljs_test.cljs:111` — call site lacks type hint on (.-unmount root)), or (b) tighten shadow-cljs build config to suppress :infer-warning in the :node-test build.

Repro: `cd implementation && npm run test:cljs 2>&1 | wc -l` — currently 521 lines on a green run (expected ≈ 5 once warnings cleared).
notes: PR #1103 open: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1103. Approach B (single-line config). Root cause: shadow-cljs :infer-externs :auto root-binds *cljs-warnings* :infer-warning=true AFTER merging user :warnings overrides, so :warnings {:infer-warning false} has no effect; fix is :infer-externs false on :node-test. Green-run: 524 → 154 lines (23 infer-warning blocks eliminated, 9 real analyser warnings retained). test:cljs PASS, test:bundle-isolation PASS.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1103 — :infer-externs false on :node-test target; green-run 524→154 lines

title: [impl rf2-zfm8v] Ship :rf.server/safe-redirect fx with URL validation + scheme/allowlist gating
description:
**Action**: Implement rf2-zfm8v decision (Option A — ship `safe-redirect-fx`, decided Mike 2026-05-14).

**Files**:
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc` — add `:rf.server/safe-redirect` fx alongside the existing `redirect-fx`

**API shape**:
```clojure
{:fx [[:rf.server/safe-redirect
       {:location next-url
        ;; one of:
        :allow ["myapp.com" "myapp.dev"]   ;; allowlist of hostnames
        :relative-only? true}]]}
```

**Validation logic** (in order):
1. Parse the URL. If unparseable → error trace `:rf.error/safe-redirect-invalid-url`, abort (do not set Location header).
2. Reject `javascript:` / `data:` / `vbscript:` schemes (consistent with rf2-vwcsq's custom-editor scheme rejection) → `:rf.error/safe-redirect-scheme-rejected`.
3. If `:relative-only? true` and the URL has a host → reject with `:rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed`.
4. If `:allow [...]` provided, check hostname against the allowlist → reject with `:rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed` if not in allowlist.
5. On pass: set Location header to the validated URL.

**`redirect-fx` docstring cross-ref**: add one-liner — "For caller-trusted location strings (e.g. `?next=` URL params), use `:rf.server/safe-redirect` instead. See Spec Security.md §Open-redirect."

**Tests**:
- `implementation/ssr/test/...` — pin each reject path (unparseable, scheme reject, relative-only violation, allowlist violation)
- Pin the happy path (relative URL passes; allowlist hostname passes)

**Spec updates**:
- `spec/Conventions.md` — register the 3 new error keywords (`:rf.error/safe-redirect-invalid-url`, `:rf.error/safe-redirect-scheme-rejected`, `:rf.error/safe-redirect-host-disallowed`)
- The Security.md catalogue entry happens automatically when rf2-edfhh's Security.md draft lands

**Quality gates**:
- `cd implementation/ssr && clojure -M:test`
- `cd implementation && npm run test:cljs`
- `python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py`
- `mkdocs build --strict`

**Solo justified**: decision-resolved, single fx + tests, ~80-150 LoC.

**NO AI attribution**.

title: Story mode-tabs strip emits React borderBottom/border reconcile warning
description:
Pre-existing React style-reconcile warning, observed while fixing rf2-fq1yg's two bead-named warnings.

  Warning: ... a style property during rerender ... Removing borderBottom border

Source: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/mode_tabs.cljs. The :tab style carries shorthand `:border "none"` plus longhand `:border-right`; when a chip activates, the merged :tab-active style adds longhand `:border-bottom`. React reconciles between renders that mix shorthand + longhand and warns.

NOT in scope for rf2-fq1yg (that bead names two specific warnings; this is the third).

Acceptance: rerunning counter-with-stories browser smoke emits zero React style-reconcile warnings.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #1071 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1071. Converted :tab style's shorthand :border "none" to all-longhand sides; :tab-active's :border-bottom now reconciles cleanly. Pattern matches rf2-fq1yg trace.cljs fix.

title: [examples] Strip rf2-XXX bead-id references from examples/ source comments (impl/tools keep them)
description:
**Rule**: `examples/` is the human-facing read-it-to-learn surface. Source comments in `examples/` MUST NOT contain `rf2-XXXXX` bead-id references — they're noise to a learner who isn't tracking the project's internal task graph.

**In contrast**: `implementation/` and `tools/` source comments MAY keep bead-id references when the WHY needs the historical anchor (e.g. `;; rf2-3vwbx: substrate-spine extraction`). Those audiences include framework contributors who use the IDs to navigate context.

## Scope

Sweep all `examples/**/*.cljs` + `*.cljc` + `*.clj` for inline `rf2-[a-z0-9]+` patterns in comments + docstrings. Remove the bead-id token (and any surrounding "per", "from", or "rf2-" parenthetical scaffolding) while preserving the underlying WHY explanation.

## Method

1. `grep -rn "rf2-[a-z0-9]" examples/` to inventory occurrences.
2. For each: rewrite the comment to keep the WHY without the bead-id reference. If the comment was JUST the bead-id (no WHY), delete the comment entirely — the well-named identifier should explain the WHAT.
3. Verify `cd implementation && npm run test:examples` still passes (no test should depend on the comment text).

## Why now

The recent comments-sweep work (rf2-0a1yz umbrella) targeted `implementation/` + `tools/` — explicitly excluded `examples/` because the rule there is different. This bead captures the examples-side rule explicitly so the next sweep agent doesn't accidentally extend bead-id references INTO examples while doing other work.

## Related

- **rf2-0a1yz** umbrella — comments-sweep for `implementation/` + `tools/` (currently in flight via comments-sweep-v2)
- Per CLAUDE.md project guidance: "Don't explain WHAT the code does, since well-named identifiers already do that. Don't reference the current task, fix, or callers..." — examples should follow this strictly.
close_reason: Fixed via PR #1071 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1071. 49 occurrences swept from 26 cljs/cljc files under examples/. Each comment rewritten to preserve WHY without bead-id; pure-bead-id comments deleted. examples/, cljs/, story test gates all green.

title: [guide] Re-render five infographics with 'frame's app-db' label (lockstep with rf2-0w7h/ih7h/npu4)
description:
**Follow-on from the docs(guide) restructure cluster (PR landed 2026-05-14, AUSEST).**

The five v1 infographics ported in that cluster all embed the label **app-db** graphically in the PNG. Under re-frame2 the load-bearing relabelling is: each frame carries its own app-db, so the diagrams should read **the frame's app-db** instead.

The cluster shipped the images verbatim with caption-paragraphs underneath flagging the relabelling. This is a deliberate ship-now-fix-later trade — the prose port and structural changes were the high-value bit, and the caption-paragraphs are visually loud enough that no reader will be misled. But the diagrams themselves should be re-rendered for the masterpiece-target.

**Images to re-render** (all under `docs/images/guide/`):

| File | Where it appears | Relabel |
|---|---|---|
| `6dominoes.png` | `docs/guide/README.md` Overview + `docs/guide/04-events-state-cycle.md` §Walking one event | central `app-db` → `frame's app-db` |
| `event-dispatch.png` | `docs/guide/04-events-state-cycle.md` §Domino 1 | central `app-db` → `frame's app-db` |
| `handling-one-event.png` | `docs/guide/04-events-state-cycle.md` end-of-dominoes recap | central `app-db` → `frame's app-db` |
| `subscriptions.png` | `docs/guide/06-views-and-frames.md` §The Signal Graph | bottom-of-stack `app-db` → `frame's app-db` |
| `interceptors.png` | `docs/guide/07-interceptors.md` §The sandwich | no `app-db` label; nothing to relabel — re-rendering is a nice-to-have for visual consistency only |

**Source PNGs** were sourced from `github.com/day8/re-frame` master and ep-002-reframe-instances branches; under MIT and same authorship line. Re-rendering can be done by:

1. Reproducing the diagram in a vector tool (drawio / figma / excalidraw) and exporting to PNG at the same dimensions.

When the re-renders land, remove the caption-paragraph 'the central app-db is *the frame's* app-db' clarifications from the five chapters; the diagrams will speak for themselves.

**Coordination**: Pure docs/images/ + docs/guide/ surface. No code touch. Safe to dispatch as its own one-bead PR after the restructure cluster merges.

**Source bead cluster**: rf2-0w7h, rf2-ih7h, rf2-npu4 (the three relabelling beads, each ported the image verbatim and deferred the actual relabel to this follow-on).

title: perf(story): incremental watch-mode hash recompute (registrar-driven, not blind 500ms full scan)

title: perf(pair2-mcp): cache runtime-preloaded? probe per socket/build generation
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md finding 2. tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/probe.cljs:30-60 — every non-streaming tool calls ensure-runtime!, which runs a bencode round-trip evaluating (some? globalThis.__re_frame_pair2_runtime) before the real eval. Doubles fixed-cost latency on cheap-read paths. Once the runtime is loaded for a socket generation, it can't unload mid-session without socket teardown. Fix: cache the probe result keyed on (conn build-id) or a socket-open generation counter; invalidate on socket close and on any failed eval. Probe at most once per socket lifetime per build.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1055. Probe cache on conn-atom; positive results short-circuit; resets on (re)connect / close.

title: perf(pair2-mcp): make tree-summary :bytes a cheap approximation (drop deep pr-str)
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-pair2-mcp-2026-05-14.md finding 1 (bug-shaped). tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/summary.cljs:12,30,52,58,62,66 — tree-summary's docstring describes summary as 'cheap, no deep walk' but every branch computes :bytes via (count (pr-str v)), deeply serialising the value just to discard it. The field is already documented as approximate (~B). Affects snapshot, trace-window, watch-epochs, get-path, subscribe paths when the cap fires summary markers. Fix: replace with cheap heuristics (maps -> 16 * count, vectors/sets/seqs -> 8 * count), update header comment + docstring to match. Alternative: drop :bytes from summary markers entirely.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1055 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1055. Tree-summary :bytes now entry-count × constant. Eliminates the 54MB pr-str allocation per summary call.

title: perf(story-mcp): validate :duration-ms ceiling on record-as-variant to prevent server stall

The MCP server's request loop is single-threaded (server.cljc:171), so unrelated calls stall for the duration. Fix: validate :duration-ms at the call site — emit a structured error for values above some sane ceiling (say 30000ms). Document the cap in the tool schema.

title: perf(story-mcp): single-pass list-stories index instead of O(stories × variants)

Fix: add a Story-side helper that returns {story-id [variant-ids ...]} in one pass over the variant registry, call it once inside tool-list-stories. Or maintain a lazy inverse-index on the Story side, refreshed on registry mutation. Add HOT PATH comment at tool-list-stories.

title: perf(story-mcp): cap accounting must include :structuredContent size (or dedup text/structured)
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-story-mcp-2026-05-14.md finding 1. tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/cap.cljc:55-64 (content-texts) returns only :content text strings, while tools/story-mcp/src/re_frame/story_mcp/tools/helpers.cljc:68-77 (text-result) writes the same payload into BOTH :content[*].text AND :structuredContent. Cap underestimates wire by ~50% on every structured tool: preview-variant, run-variant, list-stories, get-story, get-variant, read-failures, record-as-variant. Fix: extend cap accounting in the ResultIO reify to count :structuredContent JSON-encoded size as well; OR drop the :text slot when :structuredContent is present (spec/2025-06-18 tools guidance permits this), keeping :text only when it carries a genuinely different human-readable summary.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1050. cap.cljc's result-io reify now extends content-texts to include the :structuredContent slot (serialised via h/pr-edn); sum-text-tokens transduces both slots under one budget. Tests: cap-counts-structured-content-size + cap-trips-on-structured-content-alone.

title: perf(ssr-ring): collapse double header-map build in ensure-content-type / response materialisation
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-implementation-ssr-ring-2026-05-14.md finding 2. implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/headers.clj:27-56 (ensure-content-type builds a Ring header map to check for content-type), and implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/response.clj:10 (ssr-response->ring-response rebuilds the header map for the actual response). Two header-map materialisations per request. Fix: collapse content-type defaulting into response materialisation, or replace ensure-content-type's full-map build with a case-insensitive scan over header pairs. Small impact; cheap to fix.
close_reason: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1052 — batched ssr stack cluster (7 follow-on beads). Streaming walker + threaded hash + single-pass header build + CSP-host warning. 4-pass → 1-pass for the SSR hash pipeline.

title: perf(ssr-ring): eliminate duplicate render-tree-hash pass on default HTML request path
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-implementation-ssr-ring-2026-05-14.md finding 1. implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/pipeline.clj:107-112 — line 109 calls ssr/render-to-string with :emit-hash? (which itself calls hash/render-tree-hash internally per implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:245-247), then line 112 calls ssr/render-tree-hash again on the same hiccup to feed :rf/render-hash into the payload. Two full canonicalisation/hash passes per request. Fix: introduce an internal SSR helper that returns {:html ... :hash ...} from a single emit pass, OR have render-to-string return the hash alongside HTML when :emit-hash? is true, then reuse that single hash for both the DOM attribute and :rf/render-hash. Composes with rf2 perf(ssr) combined walker bead.
close_reason: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1052 — batched ssr stack cluster (7 follow-on beads). Streaming walker + threaded hash + single-pass header build + CSP-host warning. 4-pass → 1-pass for the SSR hash pipeline.

title: perf(ssr): combined render+hash walker (eliminate second tree pass when :emit-hash? true)
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-implementation-ssr-2026-05-14.md finding 2. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:225-250 — render-to-string with :emit-hash? true does two full-tree walks: line 246 computes hash/render-tree-hash, then line 247 emits HTML via emit-element. Strictly multiplicative on the cost in rf2 perf(ssr) single-pass walker. Fix: introduce a combined walker that emits HTML AND feeds the FNV-1a state in one pass; OR thread a pre-computed hash through render-to-string when callers already have it. The latter composes with the SSR-ring duplicate-hash bead — coordinate.
close_reason: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1052 — batched ssr stack cluster (7 follow-on beads). Streaming walker + threaded hash + single-pass header build + CSP-host warning. 4-pass → 1-pass for the SSR hash pipeline.

title: perf(ssr): single-pass render-tree-hash (collapse canonical-edn + fnv-1a-32 into a streaming walker)
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-implementation-ssr-2026-05-14.md finding 1. implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/hash.cljc — render-tree-hash currently builds a full canonical EDN string via pr-str-like emission, then walks that string a second time in fnv-1a-32. Extra whole-tree allocation plus a re-walk per request when :emit-hash? is true (and again on the client during verify-hydration!). Bench (200-row tree, 500 renders) showed ~14% overhead. Fix: replace canonical-edn -> bytes -> fnv-1a-32 with a single streaming walker that feeds bytes/chars directly into the FNV-1a state without materialising the string. Identical output, half the allocations, one pass. Pin against existing test corpus.
close_reason: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1052 — batched ssr stack cluster (7 follow-on beads). Streaming walker + threaded hash + single-pass header build + CSP-host warning. 4-pass → 1-pass for the SSR hash pipeline.

title: perf(http): warn-once when JVM JSON fallback is active (or make Cheshire mandatory)
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-implementation-http-2026-05-14.md finding 2. implementation/http/src/re_frame/util_json.cljc:34-175 — when Cheshire is absent on the JVM classpath, the slice silently falls back to a pure-Clojure JSON parser/writer for successful JSON responses AND JSON request bodies. The fallback is allocation-heavy compared to Cheshire/native; no warning is emitted, so apps may run on the slow path indefinitely. Fix: either (a) make Cheshire a hard JVM dep for this slice, or (b) emit a one-shot warning when the fallback is exercised so the operator notices. Add a 'slow path' comment at the fallback branch.
close_reason: fixed in PR #1053 — Cheshire is now a hard JVM dep; fallback reader and requiring-resolve delays deleted (~165 LoC); util_json shrinks 310→115

title: perf(http): cache or short-circuit merged denylists in sensitive-header? / sensitive-query-param?
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-implementation-http-2026-05-14.md finding 1. implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_privacy_headers.cljc:80-86 (sensitive-header?) and implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_url.cljc:95-102 (sensitive-query-param?) — both predicates call (set/union default-denylist @extra-*) on every invocation; redact-headers calls the predicate once per header. N headers = N set/unions per request. Always-on on JVM (interop.clj sets debug-enabled? true). Fix: cache the merged set in a delay-style atom invalidated on mutation, or simply use (or (contains? default-* k) (contains? @extra-* k)) — no allocation per check.
close_reason: fixed in PR #1053 — denylist predicates short-circuit via two contains? checks; no set/union per call

title: perf(adapters): stable structural-equality deps key for use-subscribe
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-implementation-adapters-2026-05-14.md finding 1. implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:524-573 — use-subscribe-2 uses #js [frame-kw query-v] as deps for useMemo/useCallback/useEffect. Fresh CLJS query-v per render forces cache-hit subs/subscribe + watch add/remove churn per render. Fix: derive a stable structural-equality key (hash or memoised = ref via useRef + previous-value compare) and use that as the JS deps element. The unsubscribe-pairing already in place (line 564-568) is correct and stays.
notes: PR #1108 open: useRef + = stable structural-equality deps key. Both frame-kw and query-v compile to new instances per render; fix combines them in a single useRef tuple. Regression test asserts 1 subscribe at mount, 0 churn across 5 re-renders, 1 unsubscribe at unmount. All quality gates pass.
close_reason: Landed via PR (rf2-mwft2 #1108 use-subscribe-2 stable deps; rf2-5br2q #1109 sensitive-filter test fail-closed contract)

title: perf(core): router/apply-overrides fast path for no-override common case
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-implementation-core-2026-05-14.md finding 2. implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:220-232 (apply-overrides) and :448-459 (prepare-handler-ctx) — every dispatch builds fresh override maps and interceptor vectors even when there are no per-frame/per-call overrides (the dominant prod path). Fix: short-circuit when both override maps are empty AND extra-interceptors is empty — reuse the handler's own interceptor vector, return shared empty maps. Validate by running the router tests. Add a HOT PATH comment at prepare-handler-ctx.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1068 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1068) — router/apply-overrides + prepare-handler-ctx override-free fast path.

title: perf(core): hoist elision registry/opts out of walk recursion
description: Per ai/findings/perf-audit-implementation-core-2026-05-14.md finding 1. implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:454-557 — walk re-reads (registry-of frame-id) and re-destructures opts on every recursive node. The registry is constant for the duration of one elide-wire-value call. Hot in prod when event-emit/error-emit listeners are installed. Fix: hoist reg + opts-derived locals into the top arity of elide-wire-value and thread them positionally through walk. Behaviour-preserving. Add a HOT PATH comment at walk's entry point.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1068 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1068) — elision/walk: registry + opts hoisted out of recursion via ctx struct.

title: perf(template): comment emitted views.cljs as starter-template, not render-path pattern
description:
`tools/template/src/clj/new/re_frame2/{reagent,uix,helix}/views.cljs` is the live render path of scaffolded apps. Inline event handlers and per-render dispatch acquisition are fine for a counter — but users will copy the pattern into list/grid views where allocation churn and subscription shape matter.

Fix: add a short comment in each generated `views.cljs` noting that this is starter-template render-path code kept intentionally minimal, and that heavier list/grid views should revisit allocation and subscription shape. Comment lives in the emitted file (user sees it post-scaffold) — preventative footgun guard.

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-template-2026-05-14.md finding 3.
Audit-bead: rf2-z7bzu.
notes: Resolved via PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1061 (commit f54e6e5a). Added preventative footgun-guard comment to each substrate's views.cljs ns docstring (Reagent / UIx / Helix) calling out inline-handler and collection-subscription scale-up hazards.
close_reason: Closed

title: perf(template): gate per-substrate clojure -P deps-resolve behind opt-in env var
description:
`tools/template/test/clj/new/re_frame2_test.clj:65-86,126-204` probes `clojure` CLI availability per substrate and runs `clojure -P` deps-resolution smoke per substrate. Dominates local-test wall-time (~10.4s observed).

Fix: probe `clojure` availability once per JVM. Either:
(a) gate the per-substrate `clojure -P` runs behind `RF2_TEMPLATE_DEPS_RESOLVE=1` (default off for local fast loop; on for CI/release lanes), or
(b) run one substrate's `clojure -P` per suite as a representative smoke; leave the others emit-only.

(a) preserves CI coverage; (b) is simpler and faster. Pick one.

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-template-2026-05-14.md finding 2.
Audit-bead: rf2-z7bzu.
notes: Resolved via PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1061 (commit e54d0a7a). Picked option (a): gate per-substrate clojure -P behind RF2_TEMPLATE_DEPS_RESOLVE=1 (default off for local; CI sets it via .github/workflows/test.yml). Also probe clojure --help once per JVM via delay. Local wall-time 9.3s -> 2.8s.
close_reason: Closed

title: perf(template): memoize defined-symbols in template_emission_test
description:
`tools/template/test/clj/new/template_emission_test.clj:204-227` (`defined-symbols`) re-slurps each framework `.cljc`/`.cljs` source file from disk and re-runs the regex inside the per-symbol audit loop. Cost grows with #emitted-files × #substrates × #`re-frame.*` references.

Fix: memoize `defined-symbols` by file path (or by path+mtime if hot-reload during test is a concern; the JVM-only test surface suggests path is enough). One slurp+regex per framework source file per test JVM.

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-template-2026-05-14.md finding 1.
Audit-bead: rf2-z7bzu.
notes: Resolved via PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1061 (commit 42e3f67f). Hoisted def-pattern to top-level def (one Pattern compile per JVM); split scan-defined-symbols / defined-symbols; memoise by absolute path.
close_reason: Closed

title: perf(causa): fix inaccurate hot-path comments in feed builders and app-db diff
description:
Several comments in `tools/causa` describe behaviour the code does not exhibit:

- `trace_helpers.cljc:238-240` claims "one pass" but `feed-state` (`:263-288`) calls `project-rows` twice (raw + filtered) plus axis/count loops
- `issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc:313-315` same pattern (`:339-360`)
- `mcp_server_helpers.cljc:310-312` same pattern (`:336-354`)
- `panels/app_db_diff.cljs:539-544` claims a per-:epoch-id cache that does not exist in the implementation (`:545-554`)

Fix: update comments to match reality, OR implement the claimed shape (the diff-cache one is covered by the separate diff-cache bead; the feed-builder ones are open-ended single-pass collapses that may not pay off after row caps land).

For this bead: at minimum, fix the comments so the code reads truthfully. Pairs naturally with the row-cap + diff-cache beads.

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-causa-2026-05-14.md finding 4.
Audit-bead: rf2-7tnsv.
close_reason: Fixed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1056 — rewrote project-feed docstrings in trace_helpers, issues_ribbon_helpers, mcp_server_helpers to describe the multi-pass shape the code actually exhibits (project + apply-filters + axis loops) and to point at the deferred single-pass-collapse follow-on. The app_db_diff.cljs comment is fixed in lockstep by the companion rf2-qvaa0 commit.

title: perf(causa): split hydration sidebar presence from full mismatch-detail composite
description:
`tools/causa/src/day8/re_frame2_causa/shell.cljs:184-188` subscribes to `:rf.causa/hydration-debugger-data` only to read `:has-mismatch?`. That composite (`panels/hydration_debugger.cljs:468-504`) builds mismatch summary, resolves selection, computes `mismatch-detail`, and computes `source-coord-for-mismatch` — every shell render, regardless of whether the panel is open.

Fix: split into:
- `:rf.causa/hydration-has-mismatch?` — cheap boolean (just `(boolean (seq summary))`) for the sidebar
- `:rf.causa/hydration-debugger-data` — full composite used only by the open panel

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-causa-2026-05-14.md finding 3.
Audit-bead: rf2-7tnsv.
close_reason: Fixed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1056 — added cheap :rf.causa/hydration-has-mismatch? sub (boolean over the same projection) and rewired shell.cljs's sidebar to read it. Full :rf.causa/hydration-debugger-data composite unchanged so the panel view's contract holds. Tests pin: presence sub registered, false on empty buffer, true on mismatch land, frame-awareness honoured, agreement with full composite.

title: perf(machines-viz): pin layout/runtime separation as load-bearing invariant in spec/impl
description:
Highest-risk future regression for `tools/machines-viz` is coupling live snapshot/trace updates to full graph recompute. Once that coupling lands it is hard to remove without rewriting the rendering pipeline.

When implementation lands:
- keep topology/layout state strictly separate from runtime highlight state
- transitions/microsteps/timer updates must change attrs/classes only — never re-lay-out
- add a comment at the layout-invalidation boundary marking it load-bearing
- one chart-level visibility-gated animation clock for `:after` rings — never per-node timers

Spec (`tools/machines-viz/spec/API.md`, `DESIGN-RATIONALE.md`) already says this; the bead exists to surface the invariant to whoever implements.

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-machines-viz-2026-05-14.md findings 1+2.
Audit-bead: rf2-j3iwt.
close_reason: Landed via PR (rf2-grpgc #1101 causa rigorous unskip; rf2-t1yvw #1102 machines-viz perf invariant — Locks 8/9/11 normative)

title: perf(mcp-base): elide validate-patches? in pair2-mcp release bundle
description:
`diff_encode.cljc` ships a goog-define-elidable `validate-patches?` flag, but pair2-mcp builds `:simple` (not `:advanced`) so the goog-define is not DCE'd in the shipped bundle. Every epoch diff therefore pays a full Malli validation tree-walk on top of the diff walk.

Options:
(a) set `:closure-defines {re-frame.mcp-base.diff-encode/validate-patches? false}` in pair2-mcp release shadow-cljs config (and story-mcp/causa-mcp where applicable); keep dev/test validating.
(b) wrap `validate-patches!` body in a `goog.DEBUG` check so validation cost only lands in dev/test regardless of consumer build config.

Option (b) is cheaper to ship safely; option (a) is more explicit. Pick one.

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-mcp-base-2026-05-14.md finding 2.
Audit-bead: rf2-vrjkc.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1063 (refactor+perf(mcp-infra): batched cluster — 7 follow-on beads). https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1063

title: perf(mcp-base): fast-path strip-sensitive when no events drop
description:
`strip-sensitive` (`tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/sensitive.cljc:46-61`) always allocates a fresh vector via `filterv` even when nothing is dropped. The docstring promises "identical-vector return + zero drop count" on the common path; the implementation does not deliver that.

Fix: scan first via `some` for any sensitive event; return `[events 0]` unchanged when none found. Fall through to allocating `filterv` only when ≥1 match. Extra single pass on the rare dropped case; zero extra cost on the common case; identical-vector identity preserved.

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-mcp-base-2026-05-14.md finding 1.
Audit-bead: rf2-vrjkc.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1063 (refactor+perf(mcp-infra): batched cluster — 7 follow-on beads). https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1063

title: perf(scripts): shared release-bundle reader for check-* scripts
description:
`check-bundle-isolation.cjs`, `check-elision.cjs`, `check-perf-bundle.cjs`, `check-schemas-bundle.cjs` each do recursive `readAllJs(dir)` walks over the full output tree, including stale dev-build `cljs-runtime/` artefacts. `check-counter-slim-and-fast.cjs:119-136` already documents the trap and filters to top-level release files; the four sibling scripts do not.

Fix: factor a shared helper (e.g. `scripts/lib/read-release-bundle.cjs`) that reads only the top-level release artefact files (or filters out `cljs-runtime/`). Route all four bundle scanners through it.

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-implementation-root-2026-05-14.md finding 1.
Audit-bead: rf2-wzvul.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1068 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1068) — scripts/lib/read-release-bundle.cjs shared by 4 check-* scanners.

title: perf(epoch): add hot-path comments to buffer-event! and append-record
description:
Hot-path comment thinness. `capture-event!`, `find-trigger-event`, `record-observation!` are well-commented re hot-path posture; `buffer-event!` (`epoch.cljc:353`) and `append-record` / `elide-older-trace-events` (`:123-147`) are not.

Fix: add 2-3 line comment above each explaining call frequency and current complexity. Pairs naturally with the O(1) eviction fix.

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-epoch-2026-05-14.md finding 4.
Audit-bead: rf2-tqr4z.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1068 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1068) — hot-path comments on append-record / elide-just-crossed-trace-events / buffer-event!.

title: perf(epoch): O(1) append eviction for :trace-events-keep
description:
Currently `elide-older-trace-events` (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:123-147`) rewrites the full retained history on every append via `map-indexed` + `dissoc` when `:trace-events-keep` is set. Only the record that just crossed the keep-boundary actually needs its `:trace-events` dropped.

Fix: after `subvec` to cap depth, if `count > keep` and the record at index `(- n keep 1)` still has `:trace-events`, `update` it to `dissoc :trace-events`. O(1) per append.

Cite: ai/findings/perf-audit-epoch-2026-05-14.md finding 1.
Audit-bead: rf2-tqr4z.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1068 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1068) — perf(epoch): O(1) trace-events eviction.

title: [guide] Rewrite Overview — drop chapter guide, restate features/benefits from repo README
description:
**Action**: Rewrite the guide's "Overview" section (currently the chapter-listing intro in `docs/guide/README.md`) so it does NOT carry the chapter guide. Replace the chapter guide with feature-listing content adapted from the repo-root `README.md`.

**Rules for the new Overview**:
- Do **not** re-explain the novelty / "why" / argument side of things.
- Lead with: **re-frame applications are a virtual machine.** That's the opening sentence.
- Follow with nice, clear, positive statements describing what this reference implementation will give the reader — the **features** and the **benefits**.
- Tone: **not** evangelical. Just clear positive statements of what's in the box.

**Why** (orientation, not to be written into the chapter): The current Overview reads like an argument for the framework. Mike wants it to read like a description of what they're getting — closer to a product feature-page than a manifesto. Argument lives in ch.01 (which rf2-db6pf may remove) and in the "Voice" section further down.

**Source material**: repo-root `README.md` carries the feature inventory. Pull the feature/benefit statements; drop the novelty-pitch lines.

**Open**: where does the chapter guide go? Probably moves below the Overview into its own clearly-labelled section, OR readers find chapters via mkdocs nav and the chapter-guide table just gets a heading like "Reading order". Decide during impl.

**Touches**: `docs/guide/README.md` only (probably).
close_reason: Landed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1057 (docs-guide restructure cluster — Overview rewrite + ch.23 split + ch.01 removal + 6 image ports + ch.00 faithful re-port). Follow-on rf2-izqiz filed for 'frame's app-db' diagram re-renders.

title: [guide] Remove ch.01 'Why re-frame2' chapter
description:
**Action**: Remove `docs/guide/01-why-re-frame2.md` ("Why re-frame2") from the guide entirely.

**Why**: Mike's call. The "why" argument doesn't carry its weight as ch.01 of the linear core path — readers either don't need convincing (they're already here) or won't be convinced by a chapter that has to argue against frameworks they haven't met yet. The guide should open with the framework itself, not a defence of it.

**Touches**:
- Delete `docs/guide/01-why-re-frame2.md`
- `docs/guide/README.md`: remove the row from the Core-path table; remove the "If you're skeptical, [01]... is where the argument lives" sentence; remove the "If you're impatient, read [01]..." sentence; bump remaining chapters' framing if needed.
- `mkdocs.yml`: remove the nav entry (if listed).
- Grep for inbound links `01-why-re-frame2` and remove / re-target.
- Renumber? Probably not — keep current numbering and just leave a gap, OR shift 02→01 (decide during impl; ripple is small).

**Open**: Renumber-or-leave-gap is the only real question. Default: leave the gap to avoid rippling cross-refs through the rest of the chapters.
close_reason: Landed in https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1057 (docs-guide restructure cluster — Overview rewrite + ch.23 split + ch.01 removal + 6 image ports + ch.00 faithful re-port). Follow-on rf2-izqiz filed for 'frame's app-db' diagram re-renders.

title: [guide] Split ch.23 into Secrets + Large Blobs; group with ch.22 under 'Useful patterns' heading
description:
**Proposal**: Split `docs/guide/23-privacy-and-elision.md` into two dedicated chapters and group them with ch.22 "Production observability" under a new "Useful patterns" heading in the guide nav.

**Why**: Privacy elision (`:sensitive?`) and large-blob elision (`:large?`) are two distinct concerns sharing one chapter today. Splitting yields:
- **Secrets** (`:sensitive?` → drop) — credentials / tokens / PII.
- **Large blobs** (`:large?` → elide-with-fetch) — 5MB payloads, file uploads, big collections.

They share the same elision walker (`rf/elide-wire-value`) but have different motivations, different writer-side ergonomics, and different reader-side recovery semantics. One chapter conflates the story.

**Grouping**: ch.22 (Production observability), Secrets, Large blobs are all "useful patterns" — concrete real-world recipes that aren't core to the mental model. Put them under a heading in `docs/guide/README.md` (and `mkdocs.yml` nav) so readers find them as a cluster.

**Open questions**:
- Chapter numbers — keep 22 / renumber 23a / 23b? (Renumbering ripples through cross-refs.)
- Heading name — "Useful patterns"? "Production patterns"? "Recipes"?
- Should the new heading live above or below the existing optional-deep-dives table?

**Touches**: `docs/guide/23-privacy-and-elision.md` (split), `docs/guide/README.md` (nav restructure + heading), `mkdocs.yml` (nav), cross-refs from chapters that point to ch.23 today.

title: fix(ssr-ring): default-html-shell :body-end CSP-host warning (dev mode)
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P3.4.

## Surface

implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/shell.clj:43-49 (`default-html-shell` — docstring acknowledges the raw injection)

## Evidence

`:body-end` content is injected raw into the HTML shell. The docstring acknowledges this is intentional (escape hatch for analytics, third-party scripts, etc.). No contract change requested.

## Recommendation

No code change to the contract. Add a **dev-mode runtime warning** when `:body-end` contains `<script src="...">` whose host is not in the configured CSP `:script-src` allowlist (if one is configured).

Cheap defence-in-depth without breaking the escape-hatch use case.

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P3.4.

title: decision(pair2-mcp): document + gate eval surface against production builds
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P3.3 (and audit Q1 — Mike decision).

## Surface

- tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/nrepl.cljs
- tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/eval_cljs.cljs
- tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools/dispatch.cljs:29 (uses `rt-raw` to splice agent-supplied event string into eval form verbatim)

## Evidence

The pair2-mcp eval surface accepts arbitrary CLJS / Clojure source from the MCP client; pipes to shadow's `cljs-eval`. nREPL socket binds 127.0.0.1 (good local-only default).

## Threat model

An MCP client under prompt injection could `(slurp "~/.ssh/id_rsa")` over `jvm-eval` and exfiltrate via the response. This is the intended capability of an agent-paired REPL surface — but worth flagging.

## Mike decision (audit Q1)

Three positions:

**A — Document and accept.** pair2-mcp is dev-loop only (laptop, paired with shadow). No production exposure. Document the unsafe-eval surface in tools/pair2-mcp/README.md and Principles.md. Add a `:rf.pair2/allowed-builds #{:dev}` gate that hard-refuses to start in `:advanced` builds.

**B — Sandbox the eval.** Allow-list forms (`prevent slurp/spit/shell/io`). High effort, breaks the agent pair-programming use case.

**C — Document + gate + add CI guard.** Document AS A; add the `:dev`-only gate; add a CI assertion that pair2-mcp doesn't compile into any `:advanced` build (matches existing bundle-isolation contract).

Lean C — cheap defence-in-depth alongside the by-design choice.

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P3.3.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1075 — eval-cljs gated with --allow-eval launch-flag opt-in, default OFF; structured error :rf.error/eval-cljs-disabled when off. Per rf2-czv3p cascade (same posture as causa-mcp's split per rf2-zyoj2). https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1075

title: decision(ssr): redirect-fx open-redirect mitigation — framework or app concern
description:
From security audit 2026-05-14 §P3.2 (and audit Q2 — Mike decision).

## Surface

implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/response.cljc:213-243 (`redirect-fx`)

## Evidence

`:rf.server/redirect` accepts arbitrary `:location` strings with no allowlist or relative-only check. By framework design (caller-trusted), but no doc-string nudge for the canonical mitigation.

## Exploit sketch

App has a post-login redirect that reads `?next=` from the request and dispatches `[:rf.server/redirect {:location next-param}]`. Attacker sends a phishing URL with `?next=https://evil.example.com/login`. The framework happily redirects to the attacker's site after auth.

## Mike decision (audit Q2)

Three positions:

**A — Framework concern, ship `(ssr/safe-redirect-fx allowlist-pred)`** alongside `redirect-fx`. Apps wanting safety wrap their dispatches. Pro: discoverable, opt-in by API. Con: adds a public surface.

**B — Doc-string warning + recipe in guide ch.11** — leave `redirect-fx` as caller-trusted; document the open-redirect risk and a canonical safe-redirect pattern. Pro: minimal surface. Con: easy to ignore.

**C — Both** — ship `safe-redirect-fx` AND warn in docs. Belt + braces.

Lean A or C (depending on appetite for public surface).

Audit doc: ai/findings/security-audit-2026-05-14.md §P3.2.
close_reason: DECIDED (Mike, 2026-05-14): Option (A) — ship ssr/safe-redirect-fx alongside redirect-fx. Programmer chooses; first-class safe primitive available; existing redirect-fx still works for legit caller-trusted forwarders. AND: the safe-redirect surface (plus framework config knobs more broadly) needs guide documentation — Mike noted this raises a wider gap, the guide currently has no dedicated chapter for framework-level config + security primitives. Follow-on impl will (1) ship the safe-redirect-fx primitive in implementation/ssr/, (2) catalogue entry in spec/Security.md (in flight via rf2-edfhh draft), (3) NEW guide chapter / pattern doc covering framework config knobs + safety helpers — filed as separate bead.

title: decision(ssr-ring): resolve-head-html silent fallback vs trace-emit on broken head fn
description:
Split from rf2-dvnop audit.

`implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring/lifecycle.clj` says `resolve-head-html` degrades to `""` while "the trace surface still carries the throw," but the implementation just catches and returns `""` with no trace emission.

The docstring and the impl disagree. **Mike's call**:

## Option A — silent fallback (impl matches the simpler shape)

Tighten the docstring: "Returns empty string on broken head fn. No trace emitted; debug via direct head-fn testing."

## Option B — observability (matches the existing docstring promise)

Emit `:rf.error/ssr-head-resolution-failed` trace from `resolve-head-html` before returning `""`. Adds a regression test.

## Recommendation

**Option B**. The docstring captures the intent; the impl drifted. Trace surface is cheap to emit; observability matters for production SSR debugging.

Sourced from: rf2-dvnop §Robustness risks.
close_reason: DECIDED (Mike, 2026-05-14): Option (B) — emit :rf.error/ssr-head-resolution-failed trace from resolve-head-html before returning ''. Spec is the artefact; the docstring already captured the intent (trace surface carries the throw); the impl drifted. Three converging reasons: (1) docstring + impl alignment goes from spec toward impl; (2) no programmer friction added — trace only fires when something IS broken, and when broken the dev NEEDS the signal (matches pragmatic stance: gate accidents not theoretical attacks; secure by default without friction); (3) production SSR observability matters — broken :head fn produces visually-broken page with zero diagnostic under (A); under (B) the always-on error-emit substrate (rf2-vnjfg / rf2-bacs4) carries the trace to user's observability stack. Implementation is ~3 lines: try/catch wrapping the head-fn call, emit-error with :exception + :recovery :no-recovery, then return ''.

title: test(helix): parity test for :rf.error/frame-context-corrupted under Helix adapter
description:

title: test(uix): exercise frame-provider :children single-vs-sequential coercion + nil :frame fallback
description:

## Problem

`frame-provider` (uix.cljs lines 183–207) carries two branches that no test pins:

title: perf(uix): replace gensym in use-subscribe add-watch key with hash-based keyword
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-0fgm8 (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/uix`, 2026-05-14).

## Problem

`use-subscribe`'s `subscribe-fn` (uix.cljs line 266–272) builds a fresh `gensym` per re-render where the `reaction` reference changes:

```clojure
(fn [on-change]
  (let [k (gensym "rf-uix-use-sub-")]
    (when reaction (add-watch reaction k ...))
    ...))
```

`gensym` is a process-wide CLJS counter. A render-heavy app (lots of `use-subscribe` calls; lots of subs changing) churns it. Same shape in Helix.

## Recommendation

Use a hash-of-reaction-identity-based key:

```clojure
(let [k (keyword "rf-uix-use-sub" (str (hash reaction)))]
  ...)
```

— or just keyword the reaction's gensym'd CLJS name once and reuse. Either skips the process-wide counter step.

Probably negligible in practice; flagging because pre-alpha + masterpiece-grade.

## Severity

P3 — micro-perf; cross-adapter.

## Coordination

This should roll up under the rf2-gsh49 / rf2-3vwbx extraction once those land — the `subscribe-fn` will live in shared helpers.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1058: hash-of-reaction-identity keyword replaces per-call gensym in spine's use-subscribe; prefix-to-keyword-namespace conversion lifted out of the inner closure (computed once in make-react-spine).

title: perf(uix): tighten make-derived-value notify-loop allocations (run! over vals)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-0fgm8 (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/uix`, 2026-05-14).

## Problem

`make-derived-value`'s `notify` path (uix.cljs lines 79–81):

```clojure
notify (fn [prev nu]
         (when (not= prev nu)
           (doseq [[_ w] @watchers] (w prev nu))))
```

allocates a map-entry seq per source-change notification (the `@watchers` map's `doseq` boxes each entry). Net: 1 deref + 1 seq alloc per source change. Identical shape in Helix.

## Recommendation

Swap to:

```clojure
notify (fn [prev nu]
         (when (not= prev nu)
           (run! (fn [w] (w prev nu)) (vals @watchers))))
```

— or use `reduce-kv` to avoid the `(vals ...)` intermediate. The change is mechanical; semantic-preserving; one allocation removed per notification.

Probably negligible in practice (notifications fire on source change, not on every render), but pre-alpha rule: masterpiece-grade.

## Severity

P3 — micro-perf; cross-adapter.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1058: make-derived-value notify swapped to run! over vals (was doseq over map-entries). One map-entry seq allocation removed per source-change notification.

title: docs(uix): clarify use-current-frame vs :adapter/current-frame hook docstring divergence
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-0fgm8 (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/uix`, 2026-05-14).

## Problem

`use-current-frame` (uix.cljs lines 172–181) and the routed `:adapter/current-frame` hook (uix.cljs lines 470–472) both ultimately interrogate the React context, but they're NOT strict aliases:

- `use-current-frame` goes through `uix/use-context` — React-context tier only.
- `:adapter/current-frame` is routed to `adapter-context/function-component-current-frame` — the full resolution chain (dynamic-var → React-context → `:rf/default`).

A reader who sees both surfaces in the file could reasonably confuse them. Same shape in Helix.

## Recommendation

Add one line to each fn's docstring naming the resolution chain shape explicitly:

- `use-current-frame`: "React-context tier only. For the full resolution chain (dynamic-var → React-context → :rf/default) use `(rf/current-frame)`."
- The `:adapter/current-frame` hook comment block: already mostly explains this; reinforce that `use-current-frame` is a narrower surface.

## Severity

P3 — docstring; one-line edit per adapter.

title: refactor(uix): drop dead (or x nil) wrapping in flush-views! act-resolution (cross-adapter)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-0fgm8 (round-2 audit of `implementation/adapters/uix`, 2026-05-14).

## Problem

`flush-views!` (uix.cljs lines 283–298) contains:

```clojure
(when-let [act (or (.-act React)
                   ;; React 18 moved act into react-dom/test-utils;
                   ;; if not on React directly, swallow gracefully.
                   nil)]
  (act f))
```

The `(or (.-act React) nil)` is a no-op (`x` if truthy, else `nil`); the swallowing is via the outer `when-let`. The dead `nil` branch reads like the author meant to add a fallback resolution path (`react-dom/test-utils`) but never wired it.

Same dead branch in helix.cljs.

## Recommendation

Either:
- **Drop the dead `(or ... nil)` wrapping**: `(when-let [act (.-act React)] (act f))` — cosmetic.
- **Or actually wire the fallback**: `(or (.-act React) (.-act test-utils))` and add the test-utils `:require`.

Pick the drop-it option unless someone confirms React 18 + UIx ships React with no `.-act` on the React object (in which case the actual fallback matters).

## Severity

P3 — cosmetic; cross-adapter.
close_reason: Already resolved by rf2-3vwbx (substrate-spine cluster). flush-views! act-resolution now goes through resolve-act-fn in re-frame.substrate.spine — a proper chain (React.act → react-dom/test-utils.act via try/catch), not a dead (or x nil). No dead branch remained at PR #1058 dispatch time.
