title: refactor(mcp-conformance): doc clarification — five top-level markers, one embedded fetch-handle tag
description:
**Source:** refactor-audit r2 of \`tools/mcp-conformance\` (rf2-azk9c), finding **F-DOC-2**.

## The drift

\`wire-vocab/README.md:12-19\` lists SIX wire markers:

\`\`\`
:rf.mcp/overflow       — token-budget overflow marker
:rf.mcp/summary        — tree-summary lazy-mode marker
:rf.mcp/dedup-table    — structural-dedup wrapper
:rf.mcp/diff-from      — diff-encoded :db-after marker
:rf.size/large-elided  — size-elision wire marker
:rf.elision/at         — size-elision fetch-handle tag
\`\`\`

But \`wire_vocab_test.clj/canonical-markers\` (line 348+) has FIVE entries. \`:rf.elision/at\` is embedded inside \`ElisionMarkerBody\` as \`:handle [:tuple [:= :rf.elision/at] [:vector :any]]\` — it's a fetch-handle TAG, not a standalone top-level wire marker.

The docstring in \`wire_vocab_test.clj:25-26\` shows the same six-item list.

## Fix

Update \`wire-vocab/README.md\` and the \`wire_vocab_test.clj\` ns docstring to say:

> Five top-level cross-MCP wire markers, plus the \`:rf.elision/at\` fetch-handle tag (embedded inside the \`:rf.size/large-elided\` body's \`:handle\` slot — not a standalone marker).

Or: enumerate the six but explicitly mark \`:rf.elision/at\` as 'embedded; pinned via the elision-marker body's handle schema'.

## Severity

P3 — pedantic documentation precision; the code is correct.

## Time estimate

5 min.

title: refactor(epoch): on-frame-destroyed! does not drop in-flight capture-buffer (destroy-mid-drain race)
description:
Per refactor-audit r2 (rf2-lwn4t): `on-frame-destroyed!` (`epoch.cljc:199-222`) drops `histories[frame-id]` (line 222) but does NOT drop `capture-buffers[frame-id]`. If a drain is mid-flight (events captured for that frame, cascade not yet settled), and the frame gets destroyed (e.g. hot-reload, deliberate destroy), the next drain that registers a same-keyed frame may harvest a stale partial buffer.

The router's `discard-buffer!` call (`router.cljc:659`) handles the cascade-abort path. But a destroy-during-drain might race past it depending on call order. Worth pinning a test:

1. Register `:frame/a`.
2. Inside a handler running on `:frame/a` — emit some traces via `(trace/emit! ...)` with `:frame :frame/a`.
3. From the handler, call `(rf/destroy-frame :frame/a)` (synthetic — drain still in flight).
4. Re-register `:frame/a`, drive a cascade.
5. Assert the new record's `:trace-events` does NOT carry the pre-destroy events.

May surface a real race; may already be safe by virtue of run-to-completion. Either way the test pins the contract.

Findings doc: `ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-epoch-2026-05-14.md` §F5.3.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #1003 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1003) — batched-by-surface r2 epoch polish cluster (rf2-lwn4t follow-ons).

title: refactor(epoch): test gap — multi-listener same-frame observation + re-register dissocs observed-frames
description:
Per refactor-audit r2 (rf2-lwn4t): test gap. `notify-listeners!` is correct under inspection but no test pins:

1. Two listeners both observe the same frame on the same drain (verify both entries in `observed-frames-by-cb`).
2. Re-registering a listener under the same id resets BOTH the listener entry AND the `observed-frames-by-cb` entry (`epoch.cljc:152` — the `(swap! observed-frames-by-cb dissoc id)` is non-obvious).

The existing `listener-same-key-replaces` test (`epoch_test.clj:214`) covers the listener side but doesn't probe the observed-frames side — so a future regression that drops the dissoc would not be caught.

title: test(reagent): pin late-bind hook list published at adapter ns-load time
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-z3oab.

## Problem

`re-frame.adapter.reagent` publishes 9 late-bind hooks at ns-load time:

- `:reagent/set-hiccup-emitter!`
- `:adapter/current-frame`
- `:adapter/current-component`
- `:adapter/ratom`
- `:adapter/ratom?`
- `:adapter/make-reaction`
- `:adapter/add-on-dispose!`
- `:adapter/dispose!`
- `:adapter/reactive?`
- `:adapter/after-render`

(Counted at `adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:141-187`.)

No test pins this list. A future refactor that silently drops a hook (or adds one without documenting it) goes unobserved until a downstream consumer breaks.

## Recommendation

Add a CLJS test that, after `(require 're-frame.adapter.reagent)`, enumerates the late-bind directory and asserts the set of hooks the reagent adapter contributes (cross-referenced against `re-frame.late-bind/directory.cljc` if there's a per-hook source tag).

Same pin applies to reagent-slim (~9 hooks), uix (~9 hooks + `:adapter/wrap-view` + `:adapter/clear-warn-once-caches!`), helix (~10 hooks). File once here; the test pattern lifts to each adapter.

## Severity

P3 — guardrail; no current regression, but the adapter contract is closed-set per Spec 006 and the late-bind set is a documented stability surface.
close_reason: Closed by PR #1048 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1048). New CLJS test ns late_bind_hooks_cljs_test.cljs pins the closed set of 10 hooks the Reagent adapter publishes at ns-load time + asserts directory consistency.

title: refactor(reagent): drop wrong ^js hint on IReactiveAtom satisfies? predicate (cross-adapter)
description:
**Parent audit:** rf2-z3oab.

## Problem

All four React-shaped adapters carry the same predicate:

```clojure
(fn ratom?-impl [x] (satisfies? ratom/IReactiveAtom ^js x))
```

at:
- `adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:174-176`
- `adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:222-223`
- `adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:475-477`
- `adapters/helix/src/re_frame/adapter/helix.cljs:483-485`

`IReactiveAtom` is a CLJS protocol; `^js` is the externs-inference hint for raw JS objects. A protocol-`satisfies?` check on a `^js`-hinted CLJS value either silently disagrees with the analyser or contributes nothing. Likely copy-paste from one inception.

## Recommendation

Drop the `^js` hint. If `:advanced` builds need an externs-inference hint elsewhere, that belongs at a different call site.

## Severity

P3 — cosmetic; no observable behavioural impact. Lands in the cross-adapter dedup refactor (rf2-3vwbx) for free if that one merges first.
close_reason: Landed via PR #1058: ^js hint dropped from IReactiveAtom satisfies? predicate across all four React-shaped adapters (reagent, reagent-slim, uix, helix).

title: refactor(mcp-base): perf nits — collect-map-patches set allocation, count-elided-markers redundant map? check
description:
## What

Two low-impact perf / clarity nits in `tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/diff_encode.cljc` and `vocab.cljc`:

1. **`collect-map-patches` builds an intermediate `#{}`** (F11). `(into #{} (concat (keys a) (keys b)))` allocates the full key-union before reducing. For the typical app-db diff case where `a` and `b` share most keys, two passes (or a merge-with-sentinel approach) avoid the intermediate. Estimate: +3 / -1.

2. **`count-elided-markers` double-tests `map?`** (F13). The two arms

```clojure
(and (map? v) (contains? v large-elided-key))  1
(map? v)                                       (reduce-kv ...)
```

collapse to one outer `(map? v)`:

```clojure
(map? v) (if (contains? v large-elided-key) 1 (reduce-kv ...))
```

Same LoC, one fewer test.

## Why

Round-2 audit (rf2-n4q62, findings F11 + F13). Neither load-bearing; group as a single cleanup bead.

## Source

rf2-n4q62 round-2 audit, findings F11 + F13.

title: refactor(mcp-base): collapse parse-positive-int + parse-non-negative-int via shared helper
description:
## What

`tools/mcp-base/src/re_frame/mcp_base/args.cljc` ships two functions (lines 39-95) that differ only in their floor clamp: `parse-positive-int` clamps to `(max 1 ...)`, `parse-non-negative-int` clamps to `(max 0 ...)`. The three input arms (int / number / string + try/catch) are 100% repeated.

Factor a shared helper:

```clojure
(defn- parse-int* [raw default floor]
  (cond
    (nil? raw)     default
    (integer? raw) (max floor (long raw))
    (number? raw)  (max floor (long raw))
    (string? raw)  #?(:clj (try (max floor (Long/parseLong (str/trim raw)))
                                (catch NumberFormatException _ default))
                      :cljs ...)
    :else default))

(defn parse-positive-int     [raw default] (parse-int* raw default 1))
(defn parse-non-negative-int [raw default] (parse-int* raw default 0))
```

## Why

~24 LoC of duplication. Pure refactor — cross-platform CLJC carries the reader-conditional only once.

Caught by round-2 audit (rf2-n4q62, F4).

## Estimated impact

-10 LoC net.

## Source

rf2-n4q62 round-2 audit, finding F4.

title: refactor(causa-mcp): replace 5 [Text](#) placeholder links with backticks or real targets
description:
Parent audit: rf2-c33xi. Source: ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-tools-causa-mcp-2026-05-14.md §CQ1.

Five occurrences of `[Text](#)` placeholder links — render as clickable but point at the page itself:

- 004-Wire-Pipeline.md line 23: `[`001-Wire-Protocol.md`](#)`
- 004-Wire-Pipeline.md line 24: `[`002-nREPL-Transport.md`](#)`

- 004-Wire-Pipeline.md line 229: `[`003-Tool-Catalogue.md`](#)`
- DESIGN-RATIONALE.md line 682: `[`003-Tool-Catalogue.md`](#)`

The intent is forward-reference to files that don't exist yet, but `[Text](#)` is a lint-invisible footgun: link-checkers silently pass (the anchor resolves to the page). mkdocs strict can't catch it.

1. Backticks-only: ``003-Tool-Catalogue.md`` — when the link adds no value.
2. Real target: `[Text](./003-Tool-Catalogue.md)` — mkdocs strict will flag the missing target until impl lands, which is the right signal.

Pick option 2 for the cites that are actual forward-references (so mkdocs strict shouts when impl lands and the file exists but the anchor doesn't); option 1 for the dressier 'will-land-with-impl' references in the file header.

Trivial mechanical fix. Filed P3.

title: polish(ssr): P3 cosmetic cluster — façade re-exports, dead arms, magic defaults, spec asymmetries
description:
Per round-2 audit rf2-cegm7 (`ai/findings/refactor-audit-r2-ssr-2026-05-14.md`) — P3 polish bundle. Low priority; bundle for one PR.

## CQ-1: ssr.cljc façade — 26 (def x target/x) lines could compress

`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:90-132` has 26 explicit re-export defs. A tiny `(re-export <ns> name1 name2 ...)` macro would collapse the block to ~10 lines. Trade-off: macros hide def shape; explicit defs are debuggable. Accept today; revisit if drift accumulates.

## CQ-4 / S4: default-html-shell :lang "en" magic + 0-arity active-head hardcodes :rf/default

`ssr-ring/ring.clj:319` defaults `:lang "en"`; ties to rf2-h2ujj (if :html-attrs :lang is honoured, the magic default becomes a fallback).
`head/registry.cljc:203` `(active-head)` resolves to `(active-head :rf/default)`. Used by dev tools; SSR pipeline always passes explicit frame-id. Either drop the 0-arity or make the default frame-id lookup-via-late-bind. Defer pending dev-tool needs.

## S2: Spec 011 §829 prose lag

`spec/011-SSR.md:829` (Resolved decisions summary) says 'two re-frame.ssr defonce side-channel atoms'; should be **three** after rf2-jbcmt (response-slots, request-slots, pending-error-traces). Line 784's table is correct; line 829 lags. One-line edit.

## S5: hydration-mismatch :failing-id discriminator clarification

`spec/011-SSR.md:544` documents head-vs-body discrimination via `:failing-id :rf.ssr/head-mismatch` vs `:failing-id :rf/hydrate`. In v1 the body-hash covers both head and body, so the runtime always emits `:failing-id :rf/hydrate` (per `hydrate.cljc:215`). The spec's wording is aspirational for the post-v1 head-only-hash channel. Clarify §544 with 'in v1 always :failing-id :rf/hydrate; the discriminator is reserved for the post-v1 head-only-hash channel.'

## A1: error_listener/apply-error-projection! dual semantics

The unified 1-arity (drain-and-project-last) and 2-arity (project-given-trace) is Round-1's Q12 win. The dual semantics is documented but not named. Consider explicit named entry points: `(drain-and-project-buffered! frame-id)` + `(project-trace! frame-id trace-event)`, with `apply-error-projection!` as either deprecated or the drain entry. Minor.

## A5: head/emit.cljc emission-order asymmetry

`emission-order` data var omits `:title` because title is a singleton (different signature). A future maintainer adding `<base>` (another singleton) would naturally extend the vector. Add a comment on `emission-order` flagging the singleton-vs-collection asymmetry. ~2 LoC comment.

## P2 / P3 perfs (defer)

  - `resolve-version` late-bind lookup per request — cache once at `ssr-handler` construction. Tiny.
  - `emit-element` registry lookup per element — measure first, cache later if needed.
  - `default-html-shell` string concat allocation — measure first; StringBuilder if profiled.

## CQ-6: route-head-id two-stage lookup

`head/registry.cljc:175-188` walks `(:id route)` → registry lookup → `:head` field. If `:rf/route` carried `:head` directly (denormalised at navigate-time), this is one slot read. Per-render cost is small; defer.

## Coordination

All P3 items; bundle in one PR. No hot-zone conflicts. Linked from rf2-cegm7.

Estimated: -30 LoC + a few small comments + 2 spec edits.

title: refactor(schemas): drop coerce-opts dead nil? branch + ::unset sentinel polish
description:
Source: rf2-whepe round-2 audit, 2026-05-14 09:40 AUSEST. Carried from round-1 Q3 / Q4.

Two micro-polish cleanups that survived round-1:

1. **`storage.cljc:39-50` coerce-opts dead nil? branch.** All callers (`app-schema-at`, `app-schema-meta-at`, `app-schemas`, `app-schemas-digest`) have zero-arities that explicitly pass `{}`. The `(nil? opts-or-frame-id) {}` branch is unreachable. Drop the branch (or rename the fn `opts-or-frame-id->opts` to make intent legible).

2. **`validator.cljc:187-201` ::unset sentinel.** `set-schema-validator!`'s map arity uses `{validate ::unset explain ::unset print ::unset}` to detect 'key not supplied'. The idiomatic shape is `(contains? m :validate)`:

   ```clojure
   (when (contains? m :validate) (reset! validator-fn (:validate m)))
   (when (contains? m :explain)  (reset! explainer-fn (:explain m)))
   (when (contains? m :print)    (reset! printer-fn   (:print m)))
   ```

   Reads cleaner; no namespaced sentinel; `nil` as a legitimate value (disable validation) is unambiguous.

Net: -6 LoC total. Trivial. Worth doing as a single bead because both touch validator/storage atom-management surface.

title: test(flows): pin _hot-reload-hook defonce-idempotency on namespace reload
description:
From audit rf2-0b2eh §TC-3.

The hot-reload `last-inputs` invalidation hook (`registry.cljc:213-222`) installs once via `defonce ^:private _hot-reload-hook`. No test verifies that `(require 're-frame.flows.registry :reload)` doesn't double-install.

If the defonce protection ever regressed (`defonce` -> `def`, or someone refactors the body), every replacement would invalidate `last-inputs` twice — harmless functionally but a silent bookkeeping bug.

## Action

Add a deftest:
1. Capture `(count @re-frame.registrar/replacement-hooks)` before reload.
2. `(require 're-frame.flows.registry :reload)`.
3. Assert count unchanged.

## Estimate

~10 LoC. Pre-alpha.

title: refactor(flows): clear-flow last-frame check is O(F·N) — review for many-frame topologies
description:
From audit rf2-0b2eh §PERF-3.

`registry.cljc:192-194`:

```clj
(when (every? (fn [[_ frame-flows]] (not (contains? frame-flows id)))
              @flows)
  (registrar/unregister! :flow id))
```

For each `clear-flow` call, scans every frame's flow-map. Fine for typical 1-2-frame apps. Becomes O(F·N) where F = frame count.

Not urgent — `clear-flow` isn't a hot path — but worth tracking if many-frame topologies show up in profiling. Alternative: maintain a reverse index `{flow-id #{frame-id ...}}` updated by `reg-flow` / `clear-flow`, lookup is O(1).

## Estimate

Profile-driven. ~15 LoC if the reverse index lands; 0 if we skip. Pre-alpha.

Source: audit rf2-0b2eh §PERF-3.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1007 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1007) — refactor(flows) round-2 polish batch.

title: test(http): clear-then-reg http-interceptor position contract
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 5.5.

\`http_middleware.cljc:89-107\` (\`clear-http-interceptor\`) clears by id without preserving order: \`(vec (remove ...))\`. \`reg-http-interceptor\` (lines 74-83) replaces an existing slot **in place** — preserves the position. But after a \`clear\` followed by a fresh \`reg\`, the new entry appends to the end — losing the prior position.

Spec 014 §Chain order line 516 covers replace-in-place but not the clear+re-register sequence. Tests don't pin the post-clear-position behaviour.

**Fix:** decide the contract (does clear-then-reg restore prior position, or land at the end?) and add a test. Document on the spec side too. ~10 LoC test + spec clarification.
close_reason: Decision: clear-then-reg lands at the end (slot's prior position is forgotten on clear). Documented in Spec 014 §Chain order and http_middleware reg-http-interceptor docstring. Two tests pin the contract.

title: refactor(flows): elevate extract-cycle-path's 'dead end' branch to an assertion
description:
From audit rf2-0b2eh §CQ-4.

`topo.cljc:67-73` returns `(conj stack start)` if no stuck dep is found from the current DFS node — a defensive branch. The comment honestly admits 'shouldn't happen because every stuck node has at least one stuck dep'. If it ever fired, the returned vector would be malformed (no closing repeat on the right node).

Two options:

(a) **Remove the branch.** Let the impossible case throw a meaningful internal error. Reduces dead code.

(b) **Promote to assertion.** Replace with `(throw (ex-info ':rf.error/flow-cycle-extract-invariant ...))` so the impossible state surfaces clearly rather than being silently consumed.

Recommendation: (b) — the topo-state-corruption case is rare enough to warrant a fail-loud signal rather than dead code.

## Estimate

~5 LoC. Pre-alpha.

Source: audit rf2-0b2eh §CQ-4.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1007 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1007) — refactor(flows) round-2 polish batch.

title: test(http): canned-stub fxs elide in prod (CLJS goog.DEBUG=false)
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 5.4.

\`http_managed.cljc:243-249\` gates the canned-stub fx registrations on \`interop/debug-enabled?\`. On CLJS+advanced+\`goog.DEBUG=false\` the body DCEs (Closure compiler removes fx-id keywords, docstring, handler refs). On JVM \`debug-enabled?\` is \`true\` so the gate always fires.

The elision is **load-bearing for prod-bundle isolation** — the canned stubs must not ride to production.

**Fix:** add a bundle-isolation or production-elision test that asserts \`:rf.http/managed-canned-success\` is NOT registered when \`debug-enabled?\` is false. Likely fits in \`implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_test.clj\` with a binding rebind, or extends the existing \`test:perf-bundle\` / \`test:bundle-isolation\` workflows. ~20 LoC.
close_reason: Added JVM-side gate-behaviour test using alter-var-root on debug-enabled? + ns reload. Asserts canned-stub fxs absent when gate is false; production fxs always present. Companion test pins methodology (gate-true case registers the stubs). Complements the existing CLJS bundle-grep elision check.

title: docs(spec): document :bad-entries / :bad-elements ex-data keys in Spec 009 flow error contract
description:
From audit rf2-0b2eh §SVI-2.

`registry.cljc:82, 92, 110` adds two ex-data keys to `reg-flow`'s validation errors:

- `:bad-entries` — vector of malformed input entries (for `:rf.error/flow-bad-inputs`).
- `:bad-elements` — vector of malformed path elements (for `:rf.error/flow-bad-path`).

Spec 009 §Error contract (lines 996-998) documents the ex-data shape as `:flow`, `:reason` only. These extra keys are undocumented spec drift.

Recommendation: **document them** — they help callers fix flow maps without a stack-trace dig, so they're carrying their weight. Add `:bad-entries` / `:bad-elements` as optional ex-data fields in the relevant rows of Spec 009's error contract table.

## Estimate

~2 LoC spec edit. Pre-alpha.

Source: audit rf2-0b2eh §SVI-2.
close_reason: Spec 009 error-contract table now documents :bad-entries (on :rf.error/flow-bad-inputs) and :bad-elements (on :rf.error/flow-bad-path) per audit rf2-0b2eh §SVI-2. PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/994. Both marked optional (?-suffixed) — they're absent on the outer shape-rejection paths (:inputs / :path not a vector, or :path empty) per implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:82,92,110.

title: refactor(http): resolve jitter ±25% vs ±12.5% discrepancy
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 4.3.

\`http_encoding.cljc:297-308\`:

\`\`\`clojure
jittered (if jitter
           (let [j (* capped 0.25)
                 offset (* j (- 0.5 (rand)))]
             (max 0 (+ capped offset)))
           capped)
\`\`\`

\`(- 0.5 (rand))\` is in [-0.5, +0.5]; multiplied by \`j (= 0.25 × capped)\` gives offset in [-0.125 × capped, +0.125 × capped]. So total jitter is **±12.5%**, not ±25%.

Spec 014 §Retry and backoff line 250 says \"\`:jitter true\` → Add random ±25% jitter to each delay.\"

**Fix options:**

1. Spec change — \"±25% half-width = ±12.5% effective spread\" matches industry convention (most jitter libs).
2. Impl change — \`(* j (- 1.0 (* 2 (rand))))\` for true ±25% spread.

Pick one direction. ~1 LoC code OR 1-line spec edit.
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: refactor(flows): topo-sort fast-paths for 0- and 1-flow registries
description:
From audit rf2-0b2eh §PERF-2.

`topo.cljc:107-116` unconditionally builds the full O(n²) dep-graph at the top, before checking trivial cases. For the common case of 0- or 1-flow registries, this is wasted allocation.

`topo-sort` runs on every drain AND every `reg-flow` call. Trivial fast-paths:

```clj
(defn topo-sort [flow-map]
  (let [ids (vec (keys flow-map))]
    (case (count ids)
      0 []
      1 ids
      ;; ... existing body
      )))
```

## Estimate

~5 LoC. Pre-alpha. Defer until perf measurement (or other PERF beads) hit the area.

Source: audit rf2-0b2eh §PERF-2.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1007 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1007) — refactor(flows) round-2 polish batch.

title: refactor(flows): collapse redundant 'every? vector?' clause in validate-flow
description:
From audit rf2-0b2eh §CQ-2.

`registry.cljc:82-86` checks:

```clj
(not (every? vector? (:inputs flow)))
```

The subsequent clause (line 88-92):

```clj
(not (every? valid-path? (:inputs flow)))
```

already requires `(vector? x)` via `valid-path?` (line 71). The first check is strictly subsumed.

The argument for keeping it: distinct error reason text ('entries must each be a vector' vs. 'must each be a non-empty vector of scalar keys') aids diagnosis. The argument against: two ex-data shapes for one logical malformation; redundant cond arms.

## Action

Defer to whoever next touches `validate-flow` — collapse the two arms into one, OR leave for diagnostic precision. Document the choice in a comment.

## Estimate

~5 LoC. Pre-alpha.

Source: audit rf2-0b2eh §CQ-2.
close_reason: Landed in PR #1007 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1007) — refactor(flows) round-2 polish batch.

title: refactor(http): split http-privacy.cljc (489 LoC; over leaf-size ceiling)
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 2.2.

\`http_privacy.cljc\` is 489 LoC — largest of the http siblings. Single big-bag of concerns: header denylist, query-param denylist, redaction walker, sensitivity-resolver, trace-event composition (\`prepare-emit-tags\`, \`prepare-emit-failure\`).

Per the leaf-size ceiling codified in rf2-zkca8 (commit 09f53791 \"docs(skills): codify leaf-size ceiling — ≤250L / ≤16KB\"), this surface is over budget by ~95%.

**Fix:** split. Options:

1. Three siblings: \`http-privacy-headers\`, \`http-privacy-url\`, \`http-privacy-stamp\`.
2. Pull URL-redaction (split-on-query, split-on-fragment, redact-query-param, redact-url, redact-url-query-string) into a \`http-url\` sibling — composes with bead rf2-5ijhk (http-encoding split, moving \`url-encode\` / \`params->query\` / \`merge-params\` over too). Privacy then shrinks to header + stamp surface.

Option 2 is cleaner — one URL home for the whole http artefact.
close_reason:
Split http-privacy.cljc (489 LoC) into three siblings:

- http-privacy-headers.cljc (105 LoC, leaf) — header denylist + redact-headers
- http-url.cljc (210 LoC, leaf) — query-param denylist + URL query-string redaction (redact-url, redact-url-query-string, query-denylist-hit?). Future home of url-encode / params->query / merge-params when rf2-5ijhk lands.
- http-privacy.cljc (234 LoC, orchestrator) — sensitivity resolver + trace-event composers (request-sensitive?, prepare-emit-tags, prepare-emit-failure)

Namespace shape: 3 siblings (Option 1 from bead, with Option-2 url home).

Before/after LoC: 489 -> 234+210+105 (total 549; +60 LoC docstrings + leaf-local redacted-sentinel).

Consumers updated directly (no re-export indirection in http-privacy): http_managed (header re-exports -> privacy-headers), http (facade re-exports split), tests (split aliases). http_transport / http_encoding / http_registry unchanged.

Gates green: JVM (136/385), cljs (1816/5040), bundle-isolation.

PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/998

title: refactor(http): trim narration comments in http-managed late-bind block
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 1.7.

\`http_managed.cljc:270-293\` — block of \`late-bind/set-fn!\` calls each followed by a comment explaining which bead motivated the hook. Comments duplicate the docstring on the impl side and are histories (\"rf2-wvkn — :invoke cancellation cascade\") rather than reasons.

**Fix:** one block-header comment (\"see http-managed/* docstrings for the contracts; bead refs are in the docstrings\"), drop per-line narration. Saves visual noise, doesn't lose information. ~15 LoC removed.

title: refactor(http): drop maybe-emit-decode-defaulted! dead inner gate
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 1.3.

\`http_encoding.cljc:173\` — \`decode-response-body\` calls \`maybe-emit-decode-defaulted!\` only when \`(or (= :auto decoder) (and (not decode-supplied?) (= decode :auto)))\`. Then the callee re-checks \`(not decode-supplied?)\` internally (line 152).

Two filtering layers; the inner gate is redundant given the outer caller already enforces the condition.

**Fix:** inline the \`(when interop/debug-enabled? (trace/emit! ...))\` body into \`decode-response-body\` and delete \`maybe-emit-decode-defaulted!\`. Saves one indirection. ~15 LoC.
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: refactor(http): malli-decode CLJ/CLJS deref asymmetry — wrap once
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 1.5.

\`http_encoding.cljc:127-137\`:

\`\`\`clojure
decoded (cond
          (and decode transformer)
          #?(:clj  ((deref decode) schema value ((deref transformer)))
             :cljs (decode schema value (transformer)))
          ...)
\`\`\`

JVM branch needs \`(deref decode)\` because \`requiring-resolve\` returns a var; CLJS branch uses \`resolve\` which returns the value directly. The asymmetry creates four \`#?(:clj ... :cljs ...)\` blocks in this one fn.

**Fix:** wrap once at the top of the fn — \`(let [decode-fn #?(:clj @decode-var :cljs decode-var)] ...)\` — so call sites are platform-uniform. Or single reader-conditional helper returning \`{:decode <fn> :transformer <fn> :validate <fn>}\`. Halves the noise. ~20 LoC.

Composes with P3 \"memoise requiring-resolve\" bead — fix them together.
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: refactor(http): memoise requiring-resolve for malli + cheshire
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Finding 1.4.

\`http_encoding.cljc:115-126\` — three sequential \`try (requiring-resolve ...) (catch ...)\` blocks for \`malli.core/decode\`, \`malli.transform/json-transformer\`, \`malli.core/validate\`. Each is wrapped in the same shape. Plus a second pass of deref-when-CLJ.

\`util_json.cljc:151,164\` — same pattern for Cheshire.

The Malli/Cheshire vars don't change at runtime; resolving once per JVM is enough.

**Fix:** \`(defonce malli-decode-fn (delay (try (requiring-resolve 'malli.core/decode) (catch Throwable _ nil))))\` etc., consult at call time. Cleans up visual noise + saves three try/resolve cycles per decode. ~30 LoC.
close_reason: Shipped in batched PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1010 (round-2 http polish cluster, 12 beads).

title: refactor(http): inline tiny helpers — failure-map, realise-body, default-accept-fn
description:
**Audit source:** rf2-jklja (round-2 http audit). Findings 1.1, 1.2, 3.3.

Three thin one-liners that don't pay their helper cost:

1. **\`failure-map\`** (\`http_encoding.cljc:234-238\`) is \`(assoc tags :kind kind)\`. 11 call sites in \`http_transport\` — readers must trace into the helper to confirm it's just \`assoc\`. Inline OR document as future-proofed for additional canonical slots.

2. **\`realise-body\`** (\`http_encoding.cljc:60-64\`) is \`(if (fn? body) (body) body)\`. **Single call site** at \`http_transport.cljc:416\`. Pure helper extraction pays its weight when shared; this one isn't.

3. **\`default-accept-fn\`** (\`http_encoding.cljc:213-223\`) allocates a closure per response that closes over \`status\`. \`run-accept\` calls \`(or accept-fn-or-nil (default-accept-fn ctx))\` — fresh closure per request even when user didn't supply \`:accept\`. Inline into \`run-accept\`. ~10 LoC saved + one closure-alloc per response.

Total: ~25 LoC cleanup, 11 call-site touches.
close_reason: Inlined failure-map and realise-body into call sites; default-accept-fn already done. 11 call sites simplified. 0 regressions across 148 http tests / 416 assertions.

title: refactor(pair2-mcp): rename coord to re-frame2 shape at v1.0-major-bump
description:
## Goal

Eliminate the coord-shape divergence between pair2-mcp (`@day8/re-frame-pair2-mcp`) and the rest of the MCP triplet (causa-mcp's `@day8/re-frame2-causa-mcp`, story-mcp's `day8/re-frame2-story-mcp`).

## Context

Per rf2-l7skx (now resolved), causa-mcp's Lock #6 was amended to pin the divergence: pair2-mcp's coord pre-dates re-frame2's rename; the bare `re-frame` framework + tool-name-`pair2` shape was locked-in by published artefacts before `re-frame2` existed. New MCP artefacts (causa-mcp, story-mcp) use the `re-frame2-<tool>-mcp` shape. The Lock explicitly defers the permanent fix to a v1.0-major-bump.

## Scope

When v1.0 ships:
- Rename `@day8/re-frame-pair2-mcp` → `@day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp` (or whatever the chosen shape is — decide at scope time).
- Maven coord `day8/re-frame-pair2-mcp` → `day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp`.
- Update `tools/pair2-mcp/README.md`, `tools/pair2-mcp/deps.edn`, `tools/pair2-mcp/package.json`, `skills/re-frame-pair2/scripts/*.sh`, `tools/pair2-mcp/spec/*.md`, related docs.
- Publish deprecation alias for the old coord (per published-artefact migration practice).
- Amend pair2-mcp's DESIGN-RATIONALE with the rename Lock.

## Out of scope (now)

- Doing the rename today. Published artefacts make this a deliberate major-bump migration concern; the spec-side divergence is documented at causa-mcp Lock #6's Why subsection and that's the right level for pre-impl.

## Linked

- rf2-l7skx (the reconcile that pinned the divergence)
- rf2-m9yoi (the audit that surfaced the silence)
close_reason: Already shipped via rf2-e2ufx (PR #1504, merged 2026-05-18). The rename re-frame-pair2 -> re-frame2-pair landed across skill + MCP + npm + namespaces + docs + CI + bead memory. Current state: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/ (dir), @day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp (npm), day8/re-frame2-pair-mcp (maven coord in deps.edn), skills/re-frame2-pair/ (skill). Verified grep across the repo (excluding .beads/): 0 live references to old shape; only .beads/issues.jsonl carries historical citations (per rf2-e2ufx scope note 'NOT historical citations in close-reasons'). No pair-mcp DESIGN-RATIONALE Lock to amend — the v1.0-deferral text was in causa-mcp's Lock #6 (already amended by rf2-l7skx). No PR needed; closing as superseded.

title: spec(009): refactor §What IS available in production to 'six surfaces' with event-emit and error-emit as sibling items
description:
Round-2 alignment audit (rf2-qi9v0) follow-up. Findings doc: ai/findings/spec-impl-alignment-audit-2026-05-14-evening.md.

2. Update the lead sentence to 'Six surfaces survive elision...' or rephrase to 'Six substrates' if 5 logical bullets feels more natural.

close_reason: Landed in PR #1039 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/1039). spec/009 §What IS available in production refactored: error-emit listener promoted to its own numbered item #3, lead sentence updated to 'Six surfaces', subsequent items renumbered (Performance API #4, SSR error-projector #5, native browser #6). title: spec(Conventions): document :rf.causa/* status — framework-reserved alongside :rf.epoch/* or carve-out (decision required)
description:
Round-2 alignment audit (rf2-qi9v0) follow-up. Findings doc: ai/findings/spec-impl-alignment-audit-2026-05-14-evening.md.

## Drift
Causa registers hundreds of :rf.causa/* events, subs, fxs across tools/causa/src/ (598 mentions in 30 files).

Conventions.md line 8: 'Every framework runtime id... lives under :rf/* or one of its sub-namespaces.' Conventions.md §The single-root reserved set table has no :rf.causa/* row.

Per Conventions line 65-72 §Library-owned prefixes, only :story.<...> and :Workspace.<...> are documented as library-owned — and those are OUTSIDE the :rf.* root. Causa is the first library to register under :rf.<X>/* without being framework-reserved.

This may be intentional (Causa is canonical-by-Tool-Pair and framework-distance-zero, like the epoch ns) — but the Conventions table does not say so, and the §Library-owned table says library prefixes are OUTSIDE the framework root.

The INF-2 round-2 informational. DECISION REQUIRED.

## Decision needed
A or B:
- A. :rf.causa/* is framework-reserved (alongside :rf.epoch/* per the Tool-Pair contract). Add a row to Conventions.md §The single-root reserved set.
- B. :rf.causa/* is a Tool-Pair-consumer carve-out — document the carve-out explicitly (mirror of the rf2-qk5s8 :route.nav-token/* documentation that landed for the same shape).

Story has :story.<...> and :Workspace.<...> as :rf.*-OUTSIDE library-owned. Causa registering :rf.causa/* INSIDE :rf.* is a different pattern that needs an explicit policy decision.

## Why P3
Pre-alpha; non-blocking; will compose more cleanly post-decision.
close_reason: DECIDED (Mike, 2026-05-14): Option (A) — framework-reserved. :rf.causa/* joins :rf.epoch/* as canonical framework-distance-zero namespaces in spec/Conventions.md §The single-root reserved set. Rationale: (1) Causa IS framework-distance-zero per spec/Tool-Pair.md (canonical devtools); (2) registers keys in framework-tooling-domain (panel state, registry watches, trace-buffer mirror) — distinct from Story's :story.* which lives in user-author-domain (user-assigned variant keys); (3) future-proofs the framework family (machines-viz, etc. follow the same pattern). Follow-on impl: small spec edit to spec/Conventions.md — add row to §The single-root reserved set + clarifying sentence to §Library-owned prefixes distinguishing canonical devtools (under :rf.*) from third-party libraries (outside :rf.*).

title: docs(guide/22): fix :time <inst> → :time <millis> and adapter (.getTime time) → time (rf2-rirbq lockstep)

title: docs(guide/05): add note that coeffects MUST be synchronous (cannot be async operations)
description:
Mike's framing 2026-05-14 ~01:30 AUSEST: add a note to the end of docs/guide/05-coeffects.md that coeffects can't be an async operation.

## Why this matters
- Coeffects run inside the 6-step pipeline before the handler. The handler expects all coeffects materialised when it runs.
- An async coeffect (returning a Promise / channel / callback) would either block the cascade (defeating async-ness) or run the handler against an unrealised value (broken).
- The right pattern for async data acquisition: dispatch an event from the user's interaction, fetch via :rf.http/managed (managed external effect), and dispatch a follow-on event with the result. NOT a coeffect.
- This is a common mental-model mistake for developers from sync-coeffect frameworks like Redux-saga or imperative architectures.

## What ships

A short note at the end of docs/guide/05-coeffects.md — under a heading like '### A note on async' or 'When NOT to use a coeffect'. ~10-20 lines covering:
1. The MUST: coeffects are synchronous — they run inside the cascade preparation step, before the handler.
2. The why (one paragraph): the handler expects all cofx values materialised when it runs; an unresolved promise/channel/callback would either block the cascade or run the handler with a placeholder.
3. The correct pattern for async data: dispatch event → effects (managed-HTTP / WS / etc) → follow-on event. Cross-link to ch.10 (HTTP) and Pattern-AsyncEffect.
4. One short worked example showing the wrong shape (async coeffect — DON'T DO THIS) vs the right shape (event + managed effect).

## Coordination
- TOUCH ONLY docs/guide/05-coeffects.md. Disjoint from in-flight surfaces.
- Don't expand into broader ch.05 rewrite; this is one closing note.

## Pre-alpha
Doc-only addition. Should not block other work.

## Time-box estimate
20 minutes.

Source: Mike, 2026-05-14 01:30 AUSEST.

title: Guide sweep: remove spec/ cross-references — guide is for humans, spec is for AIs
description:
The docs/guide/ tree is the human-facing artefact. The spec/ tree is the normative, AI-targeted contract. Currently many guide chapters cross-link to spec/ docs as 'further reading' — which leaks the AI-oriented surface into the human reader's path and breaks the audience-separation principle.

## Examples of the drift (just from recent landings)

- docs/guide/22-trace-to-datadog.md (my recent rewrite) cross-links to spec/Managed-Effects.md, spec/009-Instrumentation.md, etc.
- docs/guide/23-privacy-and-elision.md cross-links to spec/Conventions.md, spec/009, spec/Spec-Schemas.md.
- docs/guide/11-server-side.md (recently refreshed) cross-links to spec/011, spec/Pattern-Forms.md, etc.
- docs/guide/04a-schemas.md, ch.15 (devtools), and most other chapters likely follow the same pattern from the original v1 doc conventions.

## What the sweep should do

For each docs/guide/*.md:
1. Find every link to ../../spec/foo (or relative variants)
2. Decide per-link:
   - **Most cases**: remove the cross-link entirely. The guide should be self-contained.
   - **Rare case**: replace with a guide-to-guide cross-link (e.g., 'see ch.15 for devtools') if the same information is covered guide-side.
3. NEVER recommend the human reader 'read spec/X' as further-reading.
4. Allowed exception: a single section at the END of each chapter titled 'For AI tooling and porters' that explicitly notes 'this chapter is human-facing; the normative spec lives at spec/'. Maybe one such block per chapter, not interspersed.

## Effort estimate

~20-25 guide chapters. Each chapter likely has 3-10 spec-link replacements. ~150-250 link edits + per-link decision. Several hours of focused work. Should not be done piecemeal — needs one consistent pass with one mental model.

## Why low priority

The current cross-links don't break anything; they just leak the AI surface into the human path. This is a polish item; landing it now would conflict with every concurrent guide-touching agent. Better to land after the privacy/elision simplification (rf2-j40u7) and the SSR-streaming arc (rf2-olb64) when the guide is more stable.

## Coordination
- File as **P3** to keep priority clear.
- Should land in ONE PR, not split — readers need consistency.
- Don't block any other work; this is a finishing touch.

Source: Mike, 2026-05-14 01:20 AUSEST — 'create a low priority bead which will run later to do a sweet over the guide and remove references to the spec. This is a human facing document. The spec is for AIs'.

The broader per-guide-chapter cross-link sweep remains open — that's the real scope of this bead. URLs at /spec/... still resolve (spec/ staging still happens in docs.yml), so guide cross-links continue to work until they get swept.

title: Findings: explore bookish 'gameprogrammingpatterns.com' aesthetic for docs/guide (Tufte CSS via mkdocs?)
description:
Mike was struck by the look of https://gameprogrammingpatterns.com/component.html — serif body, narrow column, marginalia/sidenotes, restrained palette, bookish typography. The doc explicitly asks: can re-frame2's guide adopt this aesthetic?

## The reference
- Site: https://gameprogrammingpatterns.com/
- Source: https://github.com/munificent/game-programming-patterns (Bob Nystrom)
- Stack: custom Python build script (script/format.py) + Markdown + hand-rolled HTML/CSS + underscore.js templating. No JS frameworks. Cardo serif body + Source Sans Pro asides + Source Code Pro monospace.

## The aesthetic components
1. Serif body font (Cardo / EB Garamond / Lora)
2. Narrow text column (~600px) + generous side margins
3. Marginalia / sidenotes in a sans-serif aside font, for tangents + illustrations
4. Restrained palette (cream/off-white, dark grey text, one accent colour)
5. Bookish asides as offset boxes
6. "Code that plays" inline panels — small, focused, in-context

## The question
Can mkdocs-material be coaxed into this look, or is a different platform needed? Specifically:
- mkdocs-material has palette/font config; harder thing is the MARGINALIA (single-column content area). 
- Tufte CSS (https://github.com/edwardtufte/tufte-css) is the canonical drop-in for marginalia / sidenotes / books-on-the-web typography.
- mkdocs-tufte exists but maintenance state unclear (community plugin).
- Alternative: custom mkdocs theme extending Material with sidenote support.
- Alternative: switch platforms entirely (e.g., 11ty + Tufte CSS, or write something like Bob did).

## Deliverable: findings doc
A findings doc at ai/findings/bookish-aesthetic-for-guide-2026-05-14.md surveying:
1. **mkdocs-material customisation depth**: how far can extra_css + theme overrides go before the cost-benefit flips?
2. **Tufte CSS-on-mkdocs**: status of mkdocs-tufte plugin + any maintained alternatives + community recipes
3. **Replatform**: 11ty / Astro / mdBook / custom Python (Bob's path) — cost to migrate, what we'd lose (search, build integration, plugins)
4. **Klipse compatibility** — rf2-zyetf just landed Klipse in mkdocs-material; whichever path is picked must keep interactive CLJS cells working. (Tufte CSS is layout-only, should compose; replatform would mean re-integrating Klipse.)
5. **Effort estimate** for each path (S/M/L/XL)
6. **Recommendation** with rationale

## Scope guard
NO implementation. Pure research. Findings doc + maybe 1-2 follow-on beads for the chosen path.

## Pre-alpha
This is aesthetic + reading-experience — orthogonal to the framework's correctness/elegance. But re-frame2 markets itself as a masterpiece-grade architectural pattern; the docs aesthetic should match that level of care.

Source: Mike, 2026-05-14 ~00:25 AUSEST — 'file a research bead'.
notes: Findings: ai/findings/bookish-aesthetic-for-guide-2026-05-14.md; recommendation: stay on mkdocs-material, ship Path A (cosmetic-only serif/cream/narrow-column via extra_css; S effort, zero Klipse risk). Follow-ons: rf2-z7qax (Path A impl, decision-pending), rf2-plg71 (Path B sidenote layer, deferred until Path A judged insufficient). Replatform options (11ty Eleventufte / Astro / mdBook / custom Python) all cost L-XL and would force Klipse re-integration; no maintained mkdocs-tufte plugin exists; squidfunk explicitly not adding native sidenotes (mkdocs-material#4688). 80% of Nystrom's bookish gestalt is typographic, not marginalia-driven.

title: Causa preload cb-dispatch loop: principled fix + cleanup of trace/clear-trace-cbs! workaround
description:
Follow-on to rf2-nk01x's cheap fix. rf2-nk01x landed Option A: trace-bus/self-emitted? short-circuits Causa's own bookkeeping self-emits (note-sensitive-suppressed, note-trace-event, clear-trace-buffer, reset-suppressed-counters, sync-trace-buffer) in collect-trace! before any counter bump or buffer push.

This bead covers two follow-ons:

## A) Principled fix: framework-level :no-trace event meta

The cheap fix lives ENTIRELY in the consumer (trace-bus.cljc) — every framework-published trace consumer (Story, pair2-mcp, story-mcp, causa-mcp) that dispatches an event from its own trace-cb has the same loop risk. A framework-level hook would let any consumer declare 'this event MUST NOT emit a trace event' and the runtime would skip emit-dispatched-trace! + the handler-scope emits.

Shape sketch:

    (rf/reg-event-db :rf.causa/note-sensitive-suppressed
      {:rf.trace/no-emit? true}
      (fn [db [_ frame-id]] ...))

Or as a dispatch-time opt:

    (rf/dispatch [:rf.causa/note-sensitive-suppressed frame-id] {:no-trace? true})

The Spec 009 trace-emit gates check the flag and short-circuit. Pure framework concern; the cheap fix becomes obsolete once this lands.

## B) Cleanup of trace/clear-trace-cbs! workaround in elision_demo test

examples/reagent/counter_with_stories/elision_demo_cljs_test.cljs line 49 calls (trace/clear-trace-cbs!) in its before! fixture as a workaround for the loop (per rf2-vw0to's investigation). Post-rf2-nk01x the Causa cb no longer infinite-loops; the workaround can be removed and the listener-count tests run with Causa's cb live (matches production wiring).

Verify by deleting the clear-trace-cbs! line and asserting npm run test:cljs still passes.

Pre-alpha. Source: rf2-nk01x dispatch-PR, 2026-05-14.

title: :large? on [:maybe [:string {:large? true}]] schema is silently dropped by walker
description:
rf2-vw0to follow-on. schema-properties in the elision walker reads only top-level Malli props on a reg-app-schema slot.

When the slot is declared as [:maybe [:string {:large? true :hint ...}]], the :large? prop is nested INSIDE the [:maybe …] wrapper, so schema-properties (which reads top-level) sees no :large? and emits no elision declaration. The slot is treated as non-large.

This is an ergonomic sharp edge: writing [:maybe schema-with-large-flag] is the idiomatic Malli shape for 'optional but typed', and the user's intuition is that the inner :large? should propagate.

## Two paths

A) Fix the walker to recursively descend wrappers (and :and, :or, :enum) when extracting elision properties. Most elegant.
B) Document the limitation in spec/010 + ch.04a + add a check_doc_slugs-like linter that flags [:maybe [:string {:large? ...}]] as a defect.

A is the right answer for masterpiece-grade; B is a band-aid.

Pre-alpha. Source: rf2-vw0to agent finding, 2026-05-13 ~23:50 AUSEST.

title: [pair2-mcp] server-side hash precheck for cache (skip nREPL round-trip on cache-hit)
description:
Follow-on from rf2-3rt1f.

The rf2-3rt1f cache saves wire bytes but still pays the nREPL round-trip on every call: tool runs server-side, result is computed, then hashed client-side, then either emitted or replaced with a :rf.mcp/cache-hit marker.

A full optimisation would precompute a stable hash on the runtime side (e.g. (hash app-db) — or per-frame, or per-slice — at the point of state-mutation, exposed via a cheap accessor). The MCP server's first call to a tool would:

1. Ask runtime for the current hash via a single bencode round-trip.
2. If hash matches the LRU entry for (tool, args), short-circuit with the :rf.mcp/cache-hit marker. No body fetch.
3. Else proceed with the full tool eval and replace the cached hash with the new one.

That collapses the cost of the byte-identical second-inspect from 'full snapshot eval + transform pipeline' to 'one bencode round-trip with a number'.

The wire-protocol vocabulary stays the same — :rf.mcp/cache-hit is the contract. Only the implementation shifts from 'compute result then compare' to 'compare then maybe compute result'.

## Subtleties

- The runtime hash needs to be cheap to read. (hash app-db) on every dispatch is too expensive; better to cache it at the point of mutation (next-db wrap).
- Per-frame: each frame's app-db hash separately, since the snapshot/get-path tools key by frame.
- Path-sliced reads (rf2-tygdv) need their own sub-hash — cache per (frame-id, path-vec, db-hash).
- The probe op needs to live in re-frame-pair2.runtime — e.g. (re-frame-pair2.runtime/app-db-hash frame-id) returning the cached value.

## Acceptance

- Runtime exposes a stable per-frame app-db-hash accessor.
- pair2-mcp's apply-cache short-circuits with the marker when the prepass hash matches, without running the tool eval form.
- Latency observation: a same-state snapshot/get-path call is one bencode round-trip; the dispatch path skips snapshot-state + transform pipeline.
- Tests: probe hash matches before/after no-op; mismatches after dispatch; benchmarks confirm short-circuit.

title: day8/de-dupe: tools.build pom emitter ignores :mvn/scope — provided-scope semantics lost vs lein
description:
rf2-ucbuz follow-on. After the lein→tools.build swap, the published pom now lists org.clojure/clojure and org.clojure/clojurescript as ORDINARY (non-provided) dependencies. Previously (project.clj) they carried :scope "provided", meaning consumers wouldn't transitively pull a specific Clojure/CLJS version.

Root cause: clojure.tools.build.tasks.write-pom/to-dep only handles :exclusions / :optional, NOT :mvn/scope. Even adding :mvn/scope "provided" to deps.edn won't affect the emitted pom — the emitter silently drops it.

For a CLJC library this is a minor semantic change (consumers usually have Clojure/CLJS already, and version resolution picks the higher), but worth tracking. Options:
1. Accept — lib is small, consumers have these anyway.
2. Post-process the emitted pom.xml in build.clj to inject <scope>provided</scope> on the Clojure deps before jar.
3. Wait for upstream tools.build to honor :mvn/scope (raise an issue at https://github.com/clojure/tools.build).

Recommend option 2 (cheap, explicit). Implement in build.clj's jar fn between write-pom and copy-dir: parse + modify pom.xml on disk.

Source: rf2-ucbuz agent's final report, 2026-05-13 ~20:48 AUSEST.

title: [story] :play step-through scrubber on :test pane (10x epoch wiring)
description:
## SB9 parity (rf2-v05qb)

Storybook 9's debug panel lets you step through the play sequence interactively — click a step in the timeline and the canvas re-renders at that step. Story's :test pane today shows the assertion record + source-coord per failure (tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md §'Per-test rows') but no step-by-step scrubber.

The runtime data is all there: each event in :play is a dispatch, the trace bus emits each, and re-frame-10x already does this for the host app via its epoch buffer. Story has the 10x epoch panel registered as :rf.story/10x-epoch (per tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md §'10x epoch panel embed').

## Proposed shape

Wire the 10x epoch buffer to the :play step indices when the user is viewing the :test pane:

1. On :test-pane mount, the variant's frame's epoch buffer becomes the data source.
2. Each event in :play maps to one epoch (the trace bus already emits :event/dispatched per dispatch).
3. The :test pane shows a thin timeline strip above the per-row table: one tick per :play event, with status colouring (pass = the row's assertions passed; fail = at least one assertion failed at that step).
4. Click a tick → 10x's load-epoch event re-positions the variant's app-db at that step; the canvas re-renders against it.

## Where this lives

- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/test_mode.cljs (timeline strip)
- tools/causa or day8/re-frame2-causa (10x epoch integration — depends on Causa's load-epoch surface staying stable; per tools/story/spec/005-SOTA-Features.md §'10x epoch panel embed')
- tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md (new §'Step-through scrubber')

## Depends on

- :rf.story/10x-epoch panel registration (shipped per spec/005)
- Causa's load-epoch / next-epoch / previous-epoch surface (per tools/causa/)

title: [story] Watch-mode auto-re-run :test on variant content change
description:
## SB9 parity follow-up (rf2-v05qb)

Storybook 9's Vitest addon ships a watch-mode toggle (eye icon) that re-runs only the changed stories on file save. Story's :test pane explicitly defers this (tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md §'Out of scope at v1') because the runtime does not yet expose a stable signal for 'this variant's :play sequence changed since the last run' — the hot-reload signal fires on registration changes generally but doesn't differentiate :play / :events drift from docstring drift.

## Proposed shape

Two changes:

1. **Registrar refinement.** `re-frame.registrar/handlers` emits a stable :rf/content-fingerprint per registration (already shipped via snapshot-identity for variants per spec/007 §Variant snapshot identity). Watch mode subscribes to fingerprint deltas and triggers re-run only when the variant's serialised body (events + play + decorators) actually changes.
2. **Watch-mode toggle.** An eye-icon button on the chrome-level test widget (depends on rf2-q0irb landing first) toggles auto-re-run. When on: a variant whose fingerprint changed re-runs in the background; its sidebar status dot transitions through 'running' to the new pass/fail.

## Where this lives

- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/state.cljc (watch-mode flag + fingerprint subscription)
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/sidebar.cljs (eye-icon toggle on the widget)
- tools/story/spec/009-Test-Mode.md (move watch-mode out of 'Out of scope at v1')

## Depends on

- rf2-q0irb (chrome-level test widget — watch-mode is the toggle on the widget; without the widget there's no host for the affordance)
- snapshot-identity already shipped per spec/007 §Variant snapshot identity, so the fingerprint primitive is in place.

title: [story] reg-tag: add :axis + :default-filter slots (status/role/team facets)
description:
## SB9 parity (rf2-v05qb)

Storybook 9 explicitly names status / role / team / feature as the four canonical tag axes; `.storybook/main.ts` declares tags with `defaultFilterSelection: 'include' | 'exclude'`. Story's seven canonical tags are flat (no axis), and every tag starts unfiltered (no default-exclude pattern), so :internal / :experimental show up alongside :dev in the sidebar until manually toggled off.

## Proposed shape

Extend reg-tag body shape:

```clojure
(rf/reg-tag :alpha
  {:doc "Pre-release status."
   :axis :status                      ;; new — toolbar grouping hint
   :default-filter :exclude})          ;; new — pre-applied to the sidebar filter

(rf/reg-tag :auth-team
  {:axis :team})
```

The sidebar tag-filter row groups by :axis (mirroring 010-Toolbar.md §Optional grouping for reg-mode) and renders each axis as a collapsible facet group. Tags with :default-filter :exclude pre-exclude their variants from the dev sidebar at boot.

title: spec/011 SSR: pin :rf.server/request storage substrate (defonce side-channel atom, MUST NOT ride app-db)
description:
Drift sweep observation from rf2-2d1f3 audit:

The :rf.server/request impl (rf2-e825b, implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc) uses a per-frame defonce side-channel atom keyed by frame-id (mirrors pending-error-traces). The docstring explicitly justifies this:

  '... not in app-db so the request never rides the hydration payload to the client.'

This is load-bearing — putting the request in app-db would leak Host/Cookie/Authorization headers to the client via the hydration payload. The spec (011-SSR.md §Server-only reg-cofx for request context, around line 316) defines the cofx contract but is silent on the storage substrate.

Recommendation: option (a) — too easy to get wrong in a fresh port. The privacy risk is concrete (auth headers leaking client-side).

title: Worktree hygiene cron: skip 'permission-denied' worktrees instead of nuking their git pointers
description:
From rf2-fn5rk PR #671's process note: my hygiene-sweep cron destroyed rf2-fn5rk's worktree mid-flight. The git pointer was removed even though the filesystem dir was permission-denied (Windows file lock from the running agent). The agent's process kept going, lost its worktree-tracking, and had to recreate as agent-rf2-fn5rk-redo and reapply 4 edits.

Self-healed cleanly, but it shouldn't have happened.

Fix the hygiene-sweep loop prompt to:
1. Check if 'git worktree remove -f -f <path>' returns a permission-denied error
2. If yes: SKIP that worktree (its agent process is still running)
3. Don't proceed with the git pointer removal — leave it intact so the agent's process doesn't see its tracking disappear

Current loop wording (in cron 93fea78b at :23 hourly):
'for each worktree under .claude/worktrees/agent-*, check whether its branch has any commits unique to it via git log <branch> --not origin/main. If empty: the work has landed; run git worktree remove -f -f <path>. Skip any worktree whose branch carries unique commits — those are mid-flight or unpushed work.'

title: spec/009 §Size elision: add DESIGN-RATIONALE paragraph for why markers stay separate (sensitive vs large)
description:
Follow-on from rf2-vbk6j (kept rf2-hmmx7's separate-markers lock-in). The unified-marker intuition is structurally beautiful — a future agent will likely re-ask 'why aren't these the same?'. Add a single explainer paragraph in spec/009 §Size elision composition (or a parallel DESIGN-RATIONALE Lock in the appropriate spec doc) capturing the three reasons:

1. Path-leak risk is STRUCTURALLY WORSE with unified marker — hoisting :path to its own field advertises 'this slot is worth redacting' (stronger breadcrumb than today's per-key :rf/redacted sentinel)
2. Handle is REDUNDANT for sensitive — when :include-sensitive? true, value is inline (no marker); when false, event vanishes (nothing to fetch from). No useful in-between state.
3. Defense-in-depth would be LOST — today: trace stream is read-only metadata (one boundary) + get-path auth-gates retrieval (second boundary). A handle-bearing sensitive marker collapses these into one policy decision.

Plus: the size axis genuinely NEEDS the handle (5MB value can't ride the wire even when wanted); sensitive has no size pressure (a redacted string fits inline). The handle's value is asymmetric, not symmetric.

title: SSR: register :rf.ssr/check-version + :rf.ssr/check-schema-digest fxs — spec dispatches them, no handler
description:
Per ssr-audit-20260513-1757 findings (rf2-ul137) gap #12. Spec 011 §272–276 names two fxs the :rf/hydrate handler dispatches:

- :rf.ssr/check-version — compares the payload's :rf/version against the runtime's; mismatch emits :rf.ssr/version-mismatch trace.
- :rf.ssr/check-schema-digest — when payload includes a digest, hashes the client's registered app-schema set and compares to the server's digest; mismatch emits :rf.ssr/schema-digest-mismatch.

NEITHER is registered in re-frame.ssr.

The reference :rf/hydrate handler at ssr.cljc:462 doesn't dispatch them either (it only stashes server-hash + version in app-db).

The worked example's hand-rolled :rf/hydrate (examples/reagent/ssr/core.cljc:112) dispatches both of them:

  {:db app-db
   :fx (cond-> [[:rf.ssr/check-version version]]
         schema-digest (conj [:rf.ssr/check-schema-digest schema-digest]))}

These dispatches will silently surface :rf.error/no-such-handler traces at hydration time.

## Recommendation
Three options:

A) **Land both fxs** in re-frame.ssr. They're cheap:
   - :rf.ssr/check-version: compare payload version against (resolve 'rf2-version) or equivalent; emit warning trace on mismatch.
   - :rf.ssr/check-schema-digest: hash (rf/handlers :schema) ids; emit warning trace on mismatch.
   AND wire them into the reference :rf/hydrate handler so the example's pattern works out-of-the-box.

B) **Drop them from spec**. The :rf/version slot is already stashed in [:rf/hydration :version]; the schema-digest case is rare. Apps can register their own check handlers if they care.

C) **Mark as deferred** with a banner like reg-head's.

Recommendation: A (implement). Schema-digest mismatches are a real production concern when deploy-drift puts mismatched schemas on server vs client.

## Surfaces touched
- implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc (register both fxs; update :rf/hydrate to dispatch them).
- spec/011-SSR.md §272–276 (no spec change if going with A).

## Acceptance
- (rf/reg-fx :rf.ssr/check-version ...) and :rf.ssr/check-schema-digest are registered with :platforms #{:client}.
- Reference :rf/hydrate handler dispatches both when payload carries the keys.
- Mismatch traces fire as documented.

## Severity rationale (P3)
Not blocking — :rf.error/no-such-handler is recoverable; default projector maps it to 404 server-side but client-side it's just a trace. But it's a clear spec/impl drift; should resolve.

title: Meta: file a cross-cutting designs inventory (wire elision + retro protocol + token budgets + naming + origin)
description:
Source: rf2-zf7zd investigation (ai/findings/improver-architecture-20260513-1752.md §The unified-improver-surface proposal §Resonance).

## The cross-cutting-design pattern

Multiple session-13 investigations converged on cross-cutting design surfaces — patterns that span multiple artefacts and that each artefact would otherwise re-derive locally. Examples emerged independently:

1. **Wire elision** (rf2-vnmt6 large-path elision + rf2-ok47g sensitive-audit elision) — unified elision surface for "don't put X on wire"
2. **Retro protocol** (rf2-dhe9v from this bead) — unified retro surface for "critique a body of work"
3. **Token-budget posture** (rf2-ll0yq umbrella) — unified budget surface for "cap MCP response size"
4. **Cross-MCP naming conventions** (rf2-fvy7o finding #5) — unified naming surface for "tool name → behaviour mapping"
5. **Origin tagging** (pair2-mcp + story-mcp + causa-mcp + causa overlay) — unified origin surface for "where did this event come from?"

## The meta-pattern

Pre-alpha is the time when cross-cutting designs emerge. The codebase is small enough that one pattern reused in 3 places is visible to a single investigator. Once the codebase grows, each instance evolves independently and the shared pattern is lost.

Filing a cross-cutting designs inventory NOW captures the shape before the divergence happens.

## Proposed deliverable

A new spec or docs artefact enumerating each cross-cutting design surface:

- Location candidates: `spec/CrossCutting.md`, `docs/development/cross-cutting-designs.md`, or extend `spec/Conventions.md` with a §Cross-cutting designs section
- Per entry: name, the pattern, the consumers (skills/MCP servers/tool artefacts that implement it), the canonical specification location, the open evolution direction

## Process

Future investigations check the inventory before designing a new local implementation of a cross-cutting concern. When a new cross-cutting concern is identified, file a bead to add it to the inventory.

## Why P3

Meta-bead; quality-of-design improvement, not a blocking feature. Mike-decision on whether to spawn an inventory artefact now or defer until v0.1.

title: Populate re-frame2-improver anti-pattern catalogue with 6 launch patterns
description:
Source: rf2-zf7zd investigation (ai/findings/improver-architecture-20260513-1752.md §Angle 2 §Pattern catalogue).

Depends on: rf2-sqw80 (skill must exist before catalogue is populated).

## Six launch anti-patterns

| # | Anti-pattern | Symptom in code | Canonical re-frame2 idiom | Detect-from |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Manual HTTP retry loops | cljs-http calls inside reg-event-fx with manual retry counters or setTimeout retries | Managed HTTP (Spec 014 / Pattern-RemoteData) | Repeated setTimeout + counter + same URL across 2+ events |
| 2 | Boolean discriminator subs for FSM states | reg-sub :screen/loading?, :screen/error?, :screen/empty?, :screen/loaded? all on same key | Tags query layer (Spec 005 §Tags + :rf/in-tag sub) | 3+ boolean subs on same path; FSM-shaped key set |
| 3 | Manual loading flags | (assoc db :foo/loading? true) + (dissoc ... :foo/loading?) | Nine States pattern (patterns/nine-states.md) | :*/loading? keys + manual flip events |
| 4 | Schemaless events at HTTP boundary | reg-event-fx :api/loaded with no :rf/event-schema and no reg-app-schema for the destination path | Spec 010 schemas | New event whose :effects include :http and whose :db writes to a previously-unschemed path |
| 5 | Imperative effects | (.setItem js/localStorage ...) in event handler body | Data-only fx via reg-fx (Spec 003 fundamentals) | Direct DOM/JS API calls inside reg-event-db/fx body |
| 6 | View-side state via React hooks for non-render-local state | reagent/atom inside view body for app-wide-visible state; useState for non-render-local concerns | Move to app-db + reg-sub | Reagent atom declared at component top + read by sibling component |

## Leaf shape per pattern

Option A — one leaf per pattern (~50-80 lines each, 6 leaves total):
- `patterns/manual-retry-loop.md`
- `patterns/boolean-discriminator-subs.md`
- `patterns/manual-loading-flags.md`
- `patterns/schemaless-boundary.md`
- `patterns/imperative-effects.md`
- `patterns/view-side-state.md`

Each leaf carries: detection signal / symptom shape / canonical idiom / migration recipe / cross-link to skills/re-frame2/patterns/<canonical>.md.

Option B — condensed: one `references/anti-patterns.md` (~250-300 lines) with all six in a table-and-detail layout.

Option B is preferred for launch (single file, easier to grow incrementally); refactor to Option A once the catalogue grows past 10 patterns.

## Cross-link policy

Each pattern entry must cross-link to the canonical pattern leaf it suggests adopting:

- Pattern #1 → skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md
- Pattern #2 → skills/re-frame2/reference/state-machines/tags.md
- Pattern #3 → skills/re-frame2/patterns/nine-states.md
- Pattern #4 → skills/re-frame2/reference/fundamentals/schemas.md
- Pattern #5 → skills/re-frame2/reference/fundamentals/fx.md
- Pattern #6 → skills/re-frame2/reference/fundamentals/subs.md

## Growth procedure

When a new anti-pattern surfaces across 3+ retro sessions, add it to the catalogue. Mirrors how `re-frame-pair-improver2/references/known-frictions.md` grows organically.

## Out of scope at launch (defer to later beads)

- Anti-pattern #7: view renders only happy state (no clauses for loading/error/empty)
- Anti-pattern #8: effect handlers writing to a foreign frame's app-db (Spec 002 frame isolation violation)
- Plus: anti-patterns involving stories, routing, decorators, state-machine misuse

## Cross-refs

- ai/findings/improver-architecture-20260513-1752.md §Angle 2
- skills/re-frame-pair-improver2/references/known-frictions.md (template for catalogue shape)
- spec/Pattern-RemoteData.md / spec/005-StateMachines.md / spec/010-Schemas.md / spec/014-HTTPRequests.md (canonical idiom sources)

title: [Tool-Pair] Document direct-read privacy posture for sub-cache and get-path
description:
Audit rf2-ok47g §Composition tests + §G9 found that direct-read surfaces (sub-cache via rf/sub-cache, app-db via get-path) bypass :sensitive? entirely. :sensitive? is a trace-event flag; direct reads against app-db return the live value. with-redacted only scrubs the trace emit, not the live db.

This is architecturally correct (the trust boundary is the trace surface plus MCP egress) but creates a privacy hole that needs documentation. pair2-mcp's scrub-snapshot-sensitive explicitly passes sub-cache through unchanged with the comment 'redaction of those payloads is the with-redacted interceptor job, not the forwarder job'.

Required:
- Add a §Direct-read privacy posture subsection to spec/Tool-Pair.md (or DESIGN-RATIONALE in pair2-mcp / causa-mcp).
- Document: apps that need path-level privacy use with-redacted on the writing handler, OR do not put sensitive values in app-db at all, OR use a future path-level privacy mechanism (G11).
- Note get-path bypasses :sensitive? by design.

title: pair2-mcp DESIGN-RATIONALE: add Lock entry for wire-cap design (egress-centralised + pluggable strategy + truncate-with-marker)
description:
Follow-on from rf2-rvyzy (PR #641). The cap enforcement landed in pair2-mcp's Principles.md (MUST-level), but the comparative analysis — WHY this design — wasn't captured in tools/pair2-mcp/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md.

Follow the rf2-lwgg8 pattern (PR #642 added Lock #9 to causa-mcp's DESIGN-RATIONALE.md). For pair2-mcp's DESIGN-RATIONALE.md, add a Lock entry that captures:

**Decision**: enforce token cap at the invoke/egress boundary (centralised), not per-tool.
**Options considered**:
- (a) Per-tool: each tool function knows its cap. Rejected: cap-logic scattered across many functions, hard to compose new strategies.
- (b) Egress-centralised + pluggable strategy (CHOSEN): wrapper at invoke boundary, :strategy keyword lets future beads (path slicing, lazy summary, diff encoding) plug in without rebuilding the wrapper.
- (c) Caller-side: agent enforces its own budget. Rejected: agent context already corrupted by then.
**Overflow shape decision**: truncate + {:rf.mcp/overflow {...}} marker, NOT silent truncation or refuse-with-error.
**Token rule**: (quot (count s) 4) on serialised string; sum across multi-part :content slots.

Source: rf2-rvyzy PR #641 'Key design decisions'; investigation context in ai/findings/wire-protocol-bigapp-20260513-1541.md.

When this lands, the findings doc loses one more reason to exist — once all 12 wire beads have their corresponding spec + rationale entries, the findings doc can be deleted.

title: [causa-mcp] Bake cap + slicing + pagination + lazy-summary into spec before implementation

## Scope

When the causa-mcp `001-Wire-Protocol`, `002-nREPL-Transport`, `003-Tool-Catalogue` specs land (currently the spec folder has 000-Vision, Principles, DESIGN-RATIONALE, README), each tool entry MUST carry:

- `typical-tokens` hint (e.g. ~1.2k, ~3k under :sample).
- Cap-reached behaviour (truncate-with-cursor / `:budget-exceeded`).
- Slicing surface where applicable (path-based for any app-db read).
- Pagination surface for unbounded lists (cursor + default :limit fitting the cap).
- Lazy-summary mode for rich payloads (default :sample, opt-in :full).

Mirror the pair2-mcp Principles §"Tight token budget per response" verbatim.

## When

Before causa-mcp `tools.cljs` (or equivalent) lands.

## Acceptance

- causa-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue (when authored) lists all tools with token hints and cap behaviour.
- causa-mcp/spec/001-Wire-Protocol (when authored) declares the same 5K cap as pair2-mcp.
- No tool in causa-mcp ships without these slots.

title: re-frame-pair-improver2: allow discover-app for live tool-catalogue introspection
description:
**Source**: rf2-fvy7o findings doc, finding #7 + recommendation #6.

The improver skill is retrospective: it analyses a just-finished pair2 session for friction. Its `allowed-tools` correctly excludes the live-runtime tools (it doesn't operate on the runtime). Lower-priority because the canonical lists are in `re-frame-pair2/references/ops.md` which the improver can `Read`. The improvement is small — surfaces the live build's id to the retrospective. File and revisit if a retrospective session shows the improver guessing wrong about tool availability.

Option B (lighter): Keep the policing but generalise the message — don't enumerate v1 keys; just say "only `:db` and `:fx` are allowed at the top level".

title: [hygiene] Repo P3 polish batch (.editorconfig + .clj-kondo/ + .gitignore + COC/CONTRIBUTING/SECURITY + version-pin)
description:
## Repo hygiene quick wins

Batch of P3 polish items from the repo-best-practice sweep:

### 1. Repo-root `.editorconfig` (missing)

Minimal — `indent_style = space`, `indent_size = 2` for `.clj{,c,s}`, `end_of_line = lf`, `insert_final_newline = true`, `trim_trailing_whitespace = true`. Reduces friction for external contributors.

### 2. Repo-root `.clj-kondo/config.edn` (empty `{}`)

Activates project-aware analysis in Calva/Cursive/CIDER for any contributor. The template ALREADY ships this pattern for generated apps; the repo itself should follow suit. Add `/.clj-kondo/.cache/` and `/.clj-kondo/.cache-version` to `.gitignore`.

### 3. Repo-root orphan `package-lock.json`

Empty lockfile, no corresponding `package.json`. Delete locally (it's not in the repo); add an explicit `/package-lock.json` to `.gitignore` if a future stray npm invocation at the repo root is likely.

### 4. Explicit `.gitignore` entries for `examples/.edge-cdp/` and `.claude/worktrees/`

Both are currently ignored by git without an explicit rule (working but accidental). Adding them documents intent.

### 5. CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md

Pre-alpha-public-publish OSS hygiene. None block release; all are easy adds before the first Clojars publish.

### 6. tools/pair2-mcp/package.json shadow-cljs version pin

`^3.4.10` (caret) vs `implementation/package.json` exact `3.4.10`. Align to one policy (pre-1.0, exact pin is the safer convention).

### 7. release.yml DAG comment block doesn't mention tools/* deploys

Once tools/causa, tools/story, tools/template, tools/story-mcp join the release pipeline (presumably as separate leaves), the comment block at the top of `release.yml` (lines 4-17) will need to grow.

title: [api] destroy-frame / reset-frame public re-export strips bang — document or align
description:
## Convention asymmetry

`core.cljc:471-472`:
```clojure
(def reset-frame     frame/reset-frame!)
(def destroy-frame   frame/destroy-frame!)
```

Internal names have bangs (they mutate the frames table). Public re-export drops the bang. By the convention (registrar-shaped registrations are not bang-shaped), this is defensible — but the internal/public split is a footgun for contributors reading core.cljc cold.

## Proposed fix

Either:
- Add a comment block at line 470 explaining the strip.
- Or align internal: `frame/reset-frame!` → `frame/reset-frame`, `frame/destroy-frame!` → `frame/destroy-frame`. The latter is cleaner — by the documented convention, frames-as-registrar-entries don't carry bangs anywhere. DECISION needed.

close_reason: Closed

title: [api] Move or rename clear-subscription-cache! (outlier in clearing block)
description:
## API elegance — outlier in clearing block

`core.cljc:727-732`:
```clojure
(def clear-event events/clear-event)
(def clear-sub   subs/clear-sub)
(def clear-fx    fx/clear-fx)
(def clear-subscription-cache! subs/clear-subscription-cache!)
```

First three are bang-less ("registry clear"); fourth is bang-suffixed ("runtime cache clear").

## Proposed fix

Either:
- Move `clear-subscription-cache!` out of this section into the "runtime introspection / cache" cluster (`core.cljc:1219+`).
- Or rename to `clear-sub-cache!` for terseness (matches `sub-cache` reader two lines away).

Sites: `core.cljc:727-732`, `spec/API.md` L55.

title: [api] Clarify validate-at-boundary is an interceptor val, not a fn
description:
## API elegance — value, looks like fn

`core.cljc:1270`: `(def validate-at-boundary spec/validate-at-boundary)`.

API.md L358 documents this as the only "interceptor val" in the public surface. Every other `re-frame.core` export with the same shape (lower-case symbol, no suffix) is a fn or a macro. Users will reach for `(rf/validate-at-boundary ...)` and get an `ArityException`.

## Proposed fix

Either:
- Add `^{:rf/interceptor-val true}` meta + clarifying docstring ("pre-built interceptor value; use it in a `reg-event-*`'s interceptor vector — do not call it as a fn").
- Or rename to `boundary-validator` (noun-shaped).

Sites: `core.cljc:1270`, `spec/API.md` L358.

title: [api] Rename subscribe-value → subscribe-once OR read-sub (naming convention drift)
description:
## API elegance — naming convention drift

`core.cljc:760`: `(def subscribe-value subs/subscribe-value)`.

API.md L69 distinguishes `subscribe` (returns reaction) and `subscribe-value` (one-shot read, no caching). The naming convention elsewhere in re-frame for "one-shot" is NOT `-value` (cf. `dispatch` / `dispatch-sync` — qualifier names the INVOCATION MODE, not the RETURN SHAPE).

## Proposed fix

Consider `subscribe-once` or `read-sub`. The current `-value` suffix leads readers to think `subscribe` returns "not a value" (it returns a reaction; colloquially also a "value"). DECISION needed.

Sites: `core.cljc:760`, `subs.cljc` impl, `spec/API.md` L69.

title: [api] Rename view → view-fn OR sharpen docstring (fn returns a fn)
description:
## API elegance — fn that returns a fn

`(rf/view :my-view)` returns a function, not a hiccup tree. From the name "view", the natural reading is "a view" (something renderable). Sibling `reg-view` / `reg-view*` already implies "register-view".

## Proposed fix

Either:
- **(a)** Rename `view` → `view-fn`. Closes the trio (`reg-view` register / `reg-view*` register-fn / `view-fn` lookup-fn). Sites: `core.cljc:444`, `spec/API.md` L86, Spec 004 references.
- **(b)** Sharpen the docstring (3-line fix): "returns the render-fn for use in hiccup as `[(rf/view :id) args...]`".

Use in hiccup as [(rf/view :id) args...]...'. Option (a) rename to view-fn is a public-API rename — left to a separate decision.

title: [api] Rename emit-trace! → emit-trace-event! (name asymmetry)
description:
## API elegance — name asymmetry

`core.cljc:1276`: `(def emit-trace! trace/emit!)`.

Internal name is `trace/emit!` — one word. Public name `emit-trace!` puts "trace" as awkward noun-adjective. Pair with siblings `trace-buffer` / `clear-trace-buffer!` (both compound with `trace` as noun) and the asymmetry sharpens.

## Proposed fix

Either:
- Rename public to `emit-trace-event!` (most accurate).
- Or move internal `re-frame.trace/emit!` → `re-frame.trace/emit-trace-event!` and re-export under same name.

Sites: `core.cljc:1276`, `spec/API.md` L372, any direct callers (story panels likely).

title: [api] Rename has-tag? → machine-has-tag? OR cut entirely
description:
## API elegance — too-bare name

`core.cljc:1180`:
```clojure
(def has-tag? rf-machines/has-tag?)
```

Reading `(rf/has-tag? machine-id tag)`, "tag" is one of the most overloaded words in software. re-frame already has `:tags` on routes, machine state nodes, trace events, stories.

## Proposed fix

Sibling machine surfaces all carry `machine-` prefix (`machine-meta`, `machine-by-system-id`, `machine-transition`, `machine->xstate-json`). Rename to `machine-has-tag?` for consistency.

Alternative: cut entirely (per API.md L611 it's pure sugar over `(subscribe [:rf/machine-has-tag? machine-id tag])`).

DECISION needed.

title: [api] Cut handler-ids OR document partition with handlers
description:
## Surface bloat

`handler-ids` is `(-> (handlers kind) keys set)` per registrar.cljc:191-194 — five chars of inlining. User code that wants ids almost certainly wants the meta-map too.

## Proposed fix

Either:
- Cut `handler-ids` from public surface; inline.
- Or document the partition explicitly: "use `handlers` when you want metadata; use `handler-ids` when you only need to enumerate."
