title: [api] Cut or rename registry-summary (one-liner over handlers)
description:
## Surface bloat

`(registry-summary)` is a one-liner over `handlers`: `(into {} (map (juxt key (comp count val))) @kind->id->metadata)`. Six characters of inlining over the full meta map.

## Proposed fix

Either:
- Cut `registry-summary` from the public surface; inline at the ~3 dev-tooling call sites that use it.
- Or rename to `handler-counts` so the return shape is in the name.

Hold-open if `:strategy = preserve dev-tooling helpers`.

title: [api] Rename handlers → registrations (misleading name; returns map not seq)
description:
## API elegance — misleading name

`(handlers kind)` returns a MAP `{:my/event {<meta>}, :other/event {<meta>}, ...}` keyed by id — not a sequence of handlers. The plural-noun `handlers` shape is misleading; a reader expects a seq of handler fns.

Pre-alpha rename window is open. The registrar internally uses `registrar/register!` for the operation; `registrations` is the more accurate name.

## Proposed fix

Rename `handlers` → `registrations`. Sites:
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc`
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:1184` — the def re-export
- `spec/API.md` L328 — row
- ~12 internal call sites (mostly story / causa)

title: [examples/managed-http-counter] assert :loading transition — cancel sub-test currently vacuous against fastpath stubs
description:
Per ai/findings/examples-playwright-audit-2026-05-13.md §Per-spec (managed_http_counter).

examples/reagent/managed_http_counter/managed_http_counter.spec.cjs lines 72-77:

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Start long' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' }).click();
  await expectTextEquals(status, 'idle');

If the canned-stub for 'Start long' resolves synchronously (fastpath) before the Cancel dispatch, the status lands at :idle naturally and the Cancel sub-test passes vacuously — without exercising :rf.http/managed-abort.

## Action

Assert the status transitions through an intermediate :loading (or whatever the example surfaces) BEFORE the Cancel click. Either:

- (a) Slow the 'Start long' stub enough that the :loading state is observable, OR
- (b) Use `expectTextContains` to verify status reads :loading immediately after Start-long, then proceed with Cancel + idle assertion.

Bead context: rf2-lxd3 already changed reply behaviour on supersede; this spec needs to align with the current contract.
close_reason: PRs #527-#531 merged

title: [examples/websocket] expose reconnect-attempts counter — RECONNECTING window currently invisible to spec
description:
Per ai/findings/examples-playwright-audit-2026-05-13.md §Per-spec (websocket).

examples/reagent/websocket/websocket.spec.cjs asserts that after a Drop click the status returns to CONNECTED, but it does NOT verify the intermediate RECONNECTING phase actually rendered. The spec comment acknowledges: "Either we catch the brief RECONNECTING window, or the cascade resolved already and we're already back to CONNECTED. Both are valid evidence the reconnect machinery worked" — but it isn't, because if the reconnect path were silently bypassed the spec would still pass.

## Action

1. Add a `data-testid="ws-reconnect-attempts"` counter to the websocket view that reads from the :ws/connection machine's :retries slot.
2. Update the spec to assert it advances after Drop (`>= 1` after a click that previously read 0).

This makes the reconnect machinery a load-bearing assertion, not a vacuous fallback.
close_reason: PRs #527-#531 merged

title: [examples/flight-booker] pin seeded date — spec asserts hardcoded 2026-05-06 baseline
description:
Per ai/findings/examples-playwright-audit-2026-05-13.md §Per-spec (flight_booker).

examples/reagent/7Guis/flight_booker/flight_booker.spec.cjs line 31:

  await expectInputValue(start, '2026-05-06', 10000);

The seeded start-date drifts with calendar "today" — once the system clock passes 2026-05-06 the example's :flight/initialise computes a different default and this assertion fails.

## Action

- The artefact-not-on-Clojars path is gracefully skipped.

Coverage gap: the test does NOT actually RUN the emitted events_test.cljs against the generated app — it only verifies the file exists and shadow-cljs.edn is wired. A regression where:

- The test file emits with a stale ns require (e.g. references a renamed re-frame ns),
- The events_test fixture pattern is incompatible with the substrate adapter (e.g. UIx vs Reagent's reset story),
- The :node-test build fails to compile due to missing optional dep,

ships green from the static-shape assertions.

Extend tools/template/test/clj/new/re_frame2_test.clj OR add a sibling test that — best-effort, gated on shadow-cljs being available on the host — does ONE OF:

(a) Runs  on the generated app and asserts exit 0 + the events_test deftest passes. Gated similarly to the existing  skip pattern.

(b) Statically parses the emitted events_test.cljs and asserts it requires re-frame.core (the bang-rename + views-macros cut would surface if the template's test file still imports the renamed surface — currently it's emitted from the template's own scaffold but no test guards drift between scaffold + framework).

(b) is cheaper and catches the most likely regression. (a) is fuller fidelity but slow + brittle until alpha publish.

title: [test-add] sub-cache disposal: layer-2+ disposal under deferred grace-period + hot-reload race
description:
Per ai/findings/test-currency-audit-2026-05-13.md.

rf2-f3rd #501 added layer-2+ input ref-count decrement on disposal (sub_cache_test.clj covers it). The new tests use grace-period-ms 0 (sync dispose path) for assertion clarity.

Coverage gap: the deferred-dispose path (grace > 0) interacting with the new cascade is NOT directly asserted. Specifically:

1. **Layer-2 disposal cascade under non-zero grace**: parent and inputs may all enter their grace-period windows simultaneously; cancellation semantics across the chain are nontrivial. Pre-fix this path could have been wrong without any test catching it because grace=0 short-circuited the cancellation logic.

2. **Hot-reload during pending layer-2 cascade**: reg-sub re-registration on an input mid-cascade-dispose. The hot_reload_test covers single-sub re-reg, sub_cache_test covers single-sub grace cancellation, but the COMBINATION (cascade-pending-dispose + re-reg-mid-cascade) is not covered.

3. **Disposal symmetry with on-create**: layer-2 sub's on-create incrs N input ref-counts; disposal MUST decr exactly N. Test asserts the matched-pair invariant directly (e.g. via a recording wrapper around subscribe/unsubscribe) rather than the indirect cache-state-after-dispose assertion the current tests use.

## Scope

Add 2-3 deftests to sub_cache_test.clj (or a new sub_cache_grace_test.clj) covering 1-3 above. JVM-only is sufficient — the substrate work is platform-agnostic.

title: [docs] Conventions: document the configure / set-! / per-frame-metadata partition
description:
Per API elegance audit (rf2-6abd1) Gap 1 + Mike walkthrough decision 2026-05-13: B = document the three-bucket partition, NOT pool everything under (configure).

## Current state (three orthogonal config surfaces)

1. (rf/configure {:foo bar}) — keyword-keyed fn for global runtime knobs.
2. (rf/set-schema-validator! ...) / (rf/set-schema-explainer! ...) / (rf/install-adapter! ...) — dedicated set-! fns for adapter-pluggable hooks.
3. :fx-overrides + similar per-frame metadata keys passed via with-frame opts or (reg-frame) — per-frame override metadata.

Today these are scattered; the user-facing 'where do I configure X?' question has three different answers with no documented rule.

## Decision

Document the partition in spec/Conventions.md (alongside the §Naming bang rule that rf2-wmgp8 just shipped). Three buckets with a one-line rule each:

- **configure** = process-level runtime knobs that apply globally (e.g. debug-mode, performance-instrumentation enabled).
- **set-! fns** = adapter-pluggable hooks where the consumer needs a strong reference to a specific implementation (schema validator, schema explainer, adapter).
- **per-frame metadata** = overrides scoped to a single frame's lifetime, expressed in the frame's :overrides map at creation/with-frame time (e.g. :fx-overrides for test-side fx stubs).

## Action

Edit spec/Conventions.md — add new section '## Configuration surfaces: configure vs set-! vs per-frame metadata' near the §Naming bang rule. Enumerate the three buckets with one example each, and the decision tree for slotting a new config option.

## Cross-refs

- ai/findings/api-elegance-review-2026-05-13.md (audit Gap 1)
- spec/Conventions.md §Naming (the analogous rule that rf2-wmgp8 just shipped)
- Cross-link from API.md §Configure row to this section.

title: Conventions doc: when a surface carries a bang (listener registrations) vs not (registrar / dispatch)
description:
Audit (rf2-6abd1) surfaces a naming asymmetry that's principled but undocumented:

- register-trace-cb! / remove-trace-cb! / clear-trace-cbs! / register-epoch-cb! (post rf2-1pqc) — bang.
- reg-event-db / reg-event-fx / reg-sub / reg-fx / reg-cofx / reg-frame / reg-flow / reg-route — no bang.
- dispatch / dispatch-sync / subscribe / unsubscribe — no bang.
- install-adapter! / dispose-adapter! / init-platform (ghost) — bang.
- set-schema-validator! / set-schema-explainer! / clear-subscription-cache! — bang.
- clear-event / clear-sub / clear-fx / clear-flow / reset-frame / destroy-frame — no bang.

The rule (audit's reverse-engineering):

1. **Registry-shaped registrations** (the registrar IS the side-effect abstraction): no bang. reg-* / clear-*.
2. **Listener registrations** (caller hands a fn to a global hook): bang. register-*-cb!.
3. **Adapter / platform installation** (process-level state mutation outside the registrar): bang. install-adapter!, set-schema-validator!.
4. **Dispatch and subscribe** (frame-relative side-effects but the side-effect is the 'normal mode of operation'): no bang. Same as 'IO is the program' — bang would be noise.

## Action

Add §Naming subsection to spec/Conventions.md documenting this rule. Surfaces the audit catalogued in the table above as the canonical examples. Future-additions slot into one of the four buckets.

From ai/findings/api-elegance-review-2026-05-13.md (rf2-6abd1).

title: Drop (rf/init!) no-arg arity — let language-level ArityException replace runtime ex-info
description:
Per rf2-agql there is no default-adapter registry: (rf/init!) with no args raises :rf.error/no-adapter-specified at runtime via ex-info. Pre-alpha: consider dropping the no-arg arity from the fn defn entirely, so the call fails at compile time (CLJS) / load time (CLJ) with a language-level ArityException.

## Argument for cutting the arity

- ArityException is more discoverable than a runtime ex-info — it fires earlier, the stack trace points directly at the user's call, IDEs flag it.
- The no-arg-form error message (core.cljc:847-851) is excellent but only fires if the user runs the code. ArityException prevents the call from ever being valid.

## Argument for keeping the arity (current state)

- The ex-info message is detailed: 'rf/init! requires an explicit adapter spec map. Require the adapter ns and pass its adapter var: (require ...) (rf/init! reagent/adapter). Per rf2-agql the default-adapter registry was removed; there is no implicit default.'
- ArityException would just say 'wrong number of args (0) passed to: re-frame.core/init!' — less educational.

## Resolution

Mike-blocked. Either:

title: Collapse dispatcher/subscriber and bound-dispatcher/bound-subscriber to one pair
description:
re-frame.core exports two name-pairs that do the same thing:

- (rf/dispatcher) / (rf/subscriber) — return a frame-bound dispatch/subscribe fn.
- (rf/bound-dispatcher) / (rf/bound-subscriber) — same. Literally (defn bound-dispatcher [] (dispatcher)). See core.cljc:613-623.

Per spec/API.md:
- L80-82: dispatcher / subscriber rowed under §View ergonomics with prose 'called during render → frame-bound dispatch fn'.
- L80 also rows bound-dispatcher with prose '(bound-dispatcher m) → (fn [event] ...)' — but the impl is the no-arg shape, NOT a 1-arity-m shape.

The duplication is a docs artefact. Pre-alpha: pick one pair.

## Options

(a) Keep dispatcher / subscriber, cut bound-dispatcher / bound-subscriber. Argument: shorter names; the 'bound-' prefix is redundant because the only fn that returns these is one that captures the current frame.

(b) Keep bound-dispatcher / bound-subscriber, cut dispatcher / subscriber. Argument: 'bound-' communicates the async-safety property (you can call this from a callback after the dynamic var has unwound) — the canonical Spec 002 §bound-fn / bound-dispatcher language.

(c) Keep both as canonical for different idioms — (dispatcher) for inside-render, (bound-dispatcher) for capture-and-pass-to-async-cb. Argument: matches Reagent practice.

## API.md row mismatch

L80 documents bound-dispatcher signature as (bound-dispatcher m) → (fn ...), but the impl is no-arg. Independent of which option chosen, the row needs correction.

Mike-blocked: this is a naming decision. From ai/findings/api-elegance-review-2026-05-13.md (rf2-6abd1).
notes: Decision 2026-05-13: cut bound-dispatcher + bound-subscriber; keep dispatcher + subscriber. Reasoning: shorter; the verb-form names already imply capture semantics; aliases are pure. Cross-ref ai/findings/api-elegance-review-2026-05-13.md B6. Hold dispatch until rf2-1pqc (in-flight bang rename, also touches core.cljc + API.md) lands to avoid 3-way merge conflict on shared surface.

title: Decide: event-vector Clojure metadata as opt-channel — implement or strip
description:
Spec/002-Frames.md L359 says: "Clojure metadata on the event vector is accepted as a backwards-compat shim — see MIGRATION.md."

Grep across `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc` and `core.cljc` (the dispatch path) shows no `(meta event)` read — no implementation of the metadata channel exists. The promise dangles.

## Two outcomes

**Outcome A — Implement.**
Add a `(meta event)`-aware path in `router/dispatch!` that merges any vector-attached metadata into the dispatch envelope's opts map (the two-arg `(dispatch event opts)` form). Warn-once per call site that the metadata channel is a back-compat shim and the two-arg form is canonical.

**Outcome B — Strip the promise.**
The two-arg `(dispatch event opts)` form is the canonical mechanism per Spec 002 §The two-arg dispatch form. M-16 already deprecates `^:flush-dom` event-vector metadata — the only documented event-meta channel. Outside of that one case (covered by M-16's `:dispatch-later {:ms 0}` rewrite), there is no documented use for event-vector metadata in v2.

Outcome B is preferred — fewer dispatch paths, no shadow-channel for envelope opts, simpler runtime contract.

## Task

Decide; if Outcome B, edit spec/002-Frames.md L359 to remove the sentence and add a one-line footnote: "Event-vector metadata is not an opt-channel in v2; use the two-arg `(dispatch event opts)` form." If Outcome A, file an impl bead.

## Reference

- `ai/findings/back-compat-deprecation-audit-2026-05-13.md` §Per-surface table row 5
- Spec/002-Frames.md L331-359 (two-arg `dispatch` form)
- MIGRATION §M-16 (`^:flush-dom` removal — the one event-meta case v2 explicitly handles)
close_reason: actioned in PR #499 (batched back-compat audit cleanup); merged

title: Spec-clarify: :http in example fx is user-supplied, not framework-supplied
description:
`:http` is used as an example fx-id in many spec files but reads as if framework-shipped — because of brand association with re-frame's historical `:http-xhrio` libs and the un-namespaced form. The framework actually ships `:rf.http/managed` (Spec 014). `events.cljc` L69-79 *rejects* `:http` as a top-level effect-map key (per migration M-8).

## Affected files

- `spec/002-Frames.md` — L41, L101, L610-626, L748, L1075-1085
- `spec/007-Stories.md` — L86, L160, L263, L277, L363, L386
- `spec/008-Testing.md` — L22, L152-167

## Options

**Option A — One-line clarifying note at first-use sites.**
Append at the first occurrence in each file: "`:http` here is a placeholder for a user-supplied fx; the framework ships `:rf.http/managed` (see [014-HTTPRequests](014-HTTPRequests.md))."

**Option B — Rename example fx-ids to `:my-app/http` (or `:user-http`) everywhere.**
Removes the ambiguity entirely. The example domain becomes clearly user-namespaced.

Option B is preferred — examples should not use framework-adjacent un-namespaced keywords when a v2 canonical exists under a `:rf.http/*` namespace.

## Discipline

This is a doc-only spec edit. No impl changes. No bead chains.

## Reference

- `ai/findings/back-compat-deprecation-audit-2026-05-13.md` §Per-surface table row 10
- Spec/014-HTTPRequests.md (canonical `:rf.http/managed` surface)

title: layout-debug toggle clicks don't update the rendered checkbox
description:

title: Fix reg-view macro to return primary id (matches reg-* contract)
description:
The `reg-view` macro currently returns the auto-defed Var (its expansion ends with `(def sym (re-frame.core/view id))`, and `def` returns the Var, not the body value). Every other `reg-*` returns its primary id per Conventions §`reg-*` return-value convention. The deviation breaks the uniform pattern that lets call-site code thread the registration id without a separate literal.

Fix: change the macro's expansion to return the id (the auto-derived `(keyword (str *ns*) (str sym))` or the `:rf/id` override). One shape is wrapping the `do` so the final expression is `id`, e.g.

```
(do
  (binding [...] (reg-view* id ...))
  (def sym (re-frame.core/view id))
  id)
```

The Var auto-def is a side effect and remains intact; only the macro's terminal value changes.

Scope: implementation/core/src/re_frame/views_macros.clj `expand-reg-view`. Update or add a unit test asserting `(macroexpand-1 '(reg-view foo [x] body))` returns id at the call site, and an integration test asserting `(rf/reg-view foo [x] :body)` evaluates to `:my.ns/foo` (or the explicit `:rf/id` override).

`reg-view*` (the plain fn) already returns id — no change needed there.

Source: rf2-4far (spec PR pinning the uniform reg-* return-value contract).

title: [adapter-docs] Document the imperative escape hatch per adapter (Form-3 / use-effect)
description:
Each CLJS adapter exposes a different imperative-escape-hatch shape for cases where a view genuinely needs to own a piece of host DOM lifecycle (animation listeners, third-party library mount, ref-based scroll, etc.). The shape exists in each adapter but isn't documented in a discoverable place.

**Edits — one subsection per adapter README/IMPL-SPEC:**

| Adapter | File | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| Reagent | implementation/adapters/reagent/README.md (create if missing) | Form-3 via reg-view* + reagent.core/create-class. Capture (rf/dispatcher) in render closure for frame-aware async dispatch. Cleanup in :component-will-unmount. |
| Reagent-slim | implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md (already exists; add 'animations / listeners' worked example) | Same shape; 7-key cap; :component-did-mount attach + :component-will-unmount cleanup is canonical. |
| UIx | implementation/adapters/uix/README.md (create if missing) | uix.core/use-effect with deps + cleanup return. Capture (rf/dispatcher) in let above use-effect. |
| Helix | implementation/adapters/helix/README.md (create if missing) | helix.hooks/use-effect with deps + cleanup return. Capture (rf/dispatcher) in let above use-effect. |

Each subsection should include:
- a worked example wrapping an animationend listener (or similar — the canonical animation case)
- the cleanup-fn mandate (without it the listener leaks across re-mounts and hot-reloads)
- the dispatcher-capture pattern (dispatcher captured during render; lifecycle hook fires after commit but closure is established)
- cross-reference to Spec 002 line 373 (the silent fall-back-to-:rf/default rule) and rf2-i5n9 for the broader outer/inner pattern

**Findings:** ai/findings/animation-pattern-audit-2026-05-12.md §1.2 + §5 row 7.

**Discipline:** these are adapter-local docs (close to the code), not spec-tier. Keep each adapter section short — one page maximum. The full spec-side discipline is in 004-Views and Pattern-AsyncEffect; adapter docs just show the per-substrate spelling.

title: Forms page (05a/09): evaluate colocated handlers for HTTP + flows for error-state consolidation
description:
Design-review for `docs/guide/05a-forms.md` (post-rf2-aqys: `docs/guide/09-forms.md`).

Two questions:

## Q1 — Should colocated handlers be used for the HTTP work?

The Forms page demonstrates form submission. Currently the HTTP submission uses standalone `reg-event-fx` handlers (likely registered at namespace top level, separate from the view that dispatches them).

**Question**: would **colocated** handlers — handlers registered inline with the view (or alongside it in the same namespace, near the dispatch site) — read more cleanly for the Forms pattern? The submission handler is specific to that form; lifting it to a top-level registration adds distance between where it's defined and where it's used.

Evaluate:
- Does re-frame2's surface support colocated registration cleanly? (`reg-view` + `reg-event-fx` in the same form?)
- What's the trade-off between "registration lives near use" and "registration lives at namespace boundary"?
- Does the existing Forms page implicitly recommend one shape via its example? Should it explicitly pick a side?

## Q2 — Could flows be used to automatically consolidate error state?

The Forms page's `Pattern-Forms` shape carries error state in `:errors` (per-field) + `:submit-error` (transport-level). Currently these are written by handlers (validation handler writes `:errors`; HTTP failure handler writes `:submit-error`) and read by per-field-error subs.

**Question**: could a **flow** (Spec 013) declaratively consolidate these? A flow could observe both `:errors` and `:submit-error` paths and produce a single `:all-errors` derived slot, eliminating the per-field-error sub's need to OR across multiple sources.

Evaluate:
- Is this a good fit for flows, or does it stretch them? Flows are declarative derivations; per-field errors are a derivation, but the question is whether the derivation justifies the flow machinery.
- Would it simplify or complicate the Pattern-Forms idiom?
- What's the runtime cost of a flow for this case vs the current sub-based approach?
- Does the answer change for `:form-region` machines (which already use machine `:data`)?

## Output

A `bd` note appended to this bead with the recommendation per question:
- Q1: Should the Forms page recommend / show colocated handlers? Y/N + rationale.
- Q2: Should the Forms page recommend / show a flow for error consolidation? Y/N + rationale.

If the answer to either is yes, **file a follow-up bead** scoping the actual page edits. Don't edit the page in this bead — this is design-review only.

## Discipline

- Read-only review.
- Output: notes appended via `bd update --notes` OR a recommendation file in `ai/findings/forms-page-design-review-<date>.md` (local-only).
- **Do NOT commit** `ai/`, `findings/`.
- No PR for this bead — the deliverable is the recommendation.

## Cross-references

- `spec/Pattern-Forms.md` — the canonical Pattern-Forms shape.
- `spec/013-Flows.md` — flows spec.
- `examples/reagent/realworld/auth.cljs` — runnable Pattern-Forms example.
- `examples/reagent/realworld/settings.cljs` — runnable `:form-region` machine variant.

## Status note

Held by rf2-aqys (chapter renumber in flight). After the renumber, the target file becomes `docs/guide/09-forms.md`.
notes:
@
Design review complete. Findings doc: ai/findings/forms-page-design-review-2026-05-12.md (local-only, gitignored).

TERMINOLOGY NOTE first: "co-located handler" already means something specific in chapter 10 / Spec 014 — one event id handles BOTH request and reply via the :rf/reply sentinel. Pattern-Forms current shape (three sibling handlers, explicit :on-success / :on-failure) is chapter 10s documented escape hatch. The bead Q1 reads "colocated" in the namespace-organisation sense, which is a different concept. Both senses considered below.

== Q1 — Colocated handlers for HTTP work in the Forms page ==

RECOMMENDATION: NO. Keep the three-handler shape (:submit, :submit-success, :submit-error). Optionally add a §Variations paragraph naming chapter-10s co-located-reply shape as an alternative for very small forms with convergent paths.

Sub-question A (ns-local registration — handlers live near the view): already present in the chapter and in auth.cljs / settings.cljs. No change.

Sub-question B (chapter-10 §co-located reply — collapse the three submit handlers into one via :rf/reply):
1. The seven-event lifecycle is the conventions teachable spine; collapsing breaks it.
2. :submit-success and :submit-error paths DIVERGE non-trivially (snapshot vs cond-> over structured-vs-transport) — exactly the case chapter 10 names as a reason to opt out of co-located default.
3. Three handlers map 1:1 onto three state transitions; the §"round-trip walk-through" leans on that mapping.
4. The :form-region machine variant (settings.cljs) routes via three sibling events broadcasting three machine transitions — it cannot consolidate the same way. Pages adopting handler-side consolidation for the slice variant would teach two shapes; net pedagogical loss.

== Q2 — Flows for error-state consolidation ==

RECOMMENDATION: NO. A flow watching :errors and :submit-error to produce an :all-errors slot fails three of Spec 013s four §When-to-use-a-flow gates:

- value is part of app-state, not view input — NO, only views consume it
- other handlers / machines / schemas need to read it as plain app-db — NO
- value should survive SSR / time-travel / serialisation — IRRELEVANT (form runtime errors arent SSR-hydrated)
- derivation is stable enough to register — yes, but isolated

Spec 013 is explicit: "The derived value is consumed only by views → use a subscription (lighter, sub-cache native, no app-db write)." This is exactly that case.

Additional reasons:
- A flow doesnt eliminate the gating sub (the touched-OR-submit-attempted rule still has to run somewhere). It would be an intermediate cache, not a replacement.
- The existing :field-error sub already merges three sources (:errors, :touched, :submit-attempted?); adding :submit-error is a one-line addition to its signal vector — no flow needed.
- :errors and :submit-error are DELIBERATELY separate per Pattern-Forms §":submit-error vs :errors" (renderable validation vs opaque transport failure, rendered through different view code paths). A consolidated :all-errors flattens a distinction the pattern works to maintain.

Answer doesnt change for the :form-region machine variant — same analysis applies. The machine variant tilts MORE against the flow because the :data map is already the consolidation boundary; a flow that re-projected pieces of :data into another app-db slot would split the locality the machine pattern relies on.

== Follow-up beads ==

None filed. Both recommendations are NO.

Optional candidate (not filed by default — flag for Mikes decision):
- Forms page §Variations: name the chapter-10 co-located-reply shape as an alternative for very small forms where success and failure converge into the same slice writes. One-paragraph addition. Low priority.
@
close_reason: Design review complete. Q1 (colocated handlers): NO — current 3-handler shape is right per Spec 014 co-located-reply opt-out conditions. Q2 (flows for error consolidation): NO — fails 3/4 of Spec 013's 'when to use a flow' gates; view-only derived state belongs in subs. Optional flagged: §Variations note in 09-forms.md naming ch.10's :rf/reply pattern for small convergent forms (not filed as bead — Mike's call if to surface). Findings doc: ai/findings/forms-page-design-review-2026-05-12.md (local-only).

title: JVM flake: async-dispatch-resolves-after-current-drain timing race (drain_test.clj:317)
description:
Sister flake to the one rf2-iosc stabilised (`destroy-frame-discards-pending-events`). Different test, same family.

## Symptom

`async-dispatch-resolves-after-current-drain` in `implementation/core/test/re_frame/drain_test.clj:317` fails intermittently on JVM CI. Captured on PR #354 (rf2-fgvi, docs-only — zero impl changes, so the failure cannot be code-caused):

```
FAIL in (async-dispatch-resolves-after-current-drain) (drain_test.clj:317)
  expected: (= :ok (deref done 2000 :timeout))
    actual: (not (= :ok :timeout))

FAIL in (async-dispatch-resolves-after-current-drain) (drain_test.clj:319)
  expected: (true? (:outside? (rf/get-frame-db :rf/default)))
    actual: (not (true? nil))

FAIL in (async-dispatch-resolves-after-current-drain) (drain_test.clj:322)
  expected: (some #{:outside-async} (clojure.core/deref order))
    actual: (not (some #{:outside-async} [:sync-only :sync-only]))
```

The test waits 2000ms for an async dispatch to complete. Under CI load, the 2s budget sometimes runs out before the async resolves.

## Likely fix shape

Same approach as rf2-iosc — `with-redefs [interop/next-tick ...]` to make the async path deterministic in this test. Or, alternatively, bump the timeout (less principled — papers over the race).

Look at how rf2-iosc fixed `destroy-frame-discards-pending-events` and apply the same pattern.

Admin-merge affected docs-only PRs (no real code risk) and re-run on CI when the test is touched.

description:
Follow-up to **rf2-3nn8** (handler source-coord on error traces).

rf2-3nn8 attaches the **registration site** of the triggering handler to error events — i.e. for `:rf.error/no-such-cofx` fired inside `(reg-event-fx :user/save ...)`, the trace gets the line where `:user/save` was registered. That's free because registrations already carry source-coord.

This bead adds the **call site**: the specific line *inside* the handler body where the failing call lives — e.g. the `(inject-cofx :foo)` line, the `(subscribe [:bad-sub])` line, the `(dispatch [:missing-event])` line. With both pieces, tooling can render two clickable links per error: "handler defined at X:142" and "failed call at X:147".

## Why P3

- Registration-site coord (rf2-3nn8) is the bigger immediate win — that lands first.
- Call-site coord is precision — diminishing returns for the cost.
- Cost is real: every callable surface that can emit an error (`inject-cofx`, `subscribe`, `dispatch`, `dispatch-sync`, `re-frame.core/->fx`, etc.) needs a macro form that captures `(meta &form)` at the call site.

## Scope

- Decide which call surfaces get macro-form variants vs stay function-only.
- For each macro form, capture `(meta &form)` and bind it to a dynamic var or pass via an internal arg so the runtime can pull it on error.
- Add `:rf.trace/call-site` to the error event shape (sibling of `:rf.trace/trigger-handler`).
- Decide elision behaviour — same as trigger-handler (kept in production) or different.

## Open questions for spec walkthrough later

1. Macro form on existing fn surfaces, or new `dispatch!` / `subscribe!` variants?
2. Single key `:rf.trace/call-site {:ns :file :line :column}` or nest call-site coord under trigger-handler?
3. Elision: same as rf2-3nn8 (production), or dev-only?

## Cross-references

- **rf2-3nn8** (P2) — registration-site coord on error events. Land first. This bead is the precision follow-up.
- spec/Spec-Schemas.md will need the new key added once the questions above are locked.
notes: Decisions 2026-05-13: Q1=C (existing-name macro + dispatch* fn variant per established convention), Q2=A (flat :rf.trace/call-site key), Q3=B (dev-only elision). Pre-alpha green-light. Hold dispatch until queue capacity opens.

title: rf2-hoiu spec: re-frame.core.X collides with goog.provide; use re-frame.core-X
description:
Implementing rf2-hoiu (clarity refactor: split optional-artefact wrappers out of re-frame.core) revealed a hard CLJS constraint: goog.provide for re-frame.core unconditionally overwrites the parent object, wiping out any previously-loaded re-frame.core.X namespace.

Reproduction:
  goog.provide('re_frame.core.machines'); // re_frame.core.machines.reg_machine = fn
  goog.provide('re_frame.core');           // re_frame.core = {} -- WIPES the nested ns

So having both 're-frame.core' and 're-frame.core.flows' as cljs namespaces is structurally impossible in the goog.provide model. (Empirically verified in this branch: re_frame.core.machines.reg_machine was defined, then immediately undefined after re_frame.core loaded.)

The bead's spec said Q6 'flat re-frame.core.X (not .impl.X)' -- intent was clearly to avoid deep .impl. paths. The next-cleanest flat form that ACTUALLY WORKS on CLJS: 're-frame.core-X' (dash, not dot). Other valid options: 're-frame.api.X', 're-frame.optional.X', 're-frame.X-api'. Single-hyphen 're-frame.core-flows' preserves Q6's flatness intent and the user-facing 'rf' alias still resolves rf/reg-flow via re-export.

Decision applied in PR (clarity-core-cleanup branch): rename re-frame.core.{flows,machines,routing,schemas,ssr,epoch,http} -> re-frame.core-{flows,machines,routing,schemas,ssr,epoch,http}. Public surface unchanged (rf/reg-flow etc. still resolve via def-aliases in re-frame.core).

References: clojurescript.org/about/differences (lists goog.provide as the canonical reason cljs cannot have a.b and a.b.c both as namespaces); rf2-hoiu bead.
close_reason: Closed

**Scope (quoted from audit B-IMP-9):**

title: [guide] Teach the subscription Signal Graph — four layers, Layer 2 extractors, propagation pruning
description:
Re-frame2's ch.02 introduces `reg-sub` and shows chaining with `:<-`. Neither chapter teaches the **Signal Graph**: the ground-truth → extractors → materialised-view → leaves structure. V1's `subscriptions.md` is the canonical introduction.

**Scope (quoted from audit B-IMP-5):**

Re-frame2's ch.02 introduces `reg-sub` and ch.02 shows chaining with `:<-`. Neither chapter (nor any other) teaches the **Signal Graph**: the ground-truth → extractors → materialised-view → leaves structure that governs *why* you write extractor subs as small as possible, *why* `:<-` exists at all, and *why* tooling like `sub-topology` (ch.11) makes sense. title: Guide ch.02 'The Frame' section: add reassurance note that frames aren't normally globals
description:
In docs/guide/02-your-first-app.md, the "The Frame" section walks through the canonical counter example which defines a frame as a top-level def. A new reader might worry "wait, is this a global? Is re-frame2 telling me to define globals?"

Add a quick clarifying note at the bottom of "The Frame" section. Something like:

> Note: In a real app, frames are rarely defined as top-level globals. They're typically either:
> - **Unit-test specific** — created inside `(with-frame [f (rf/create-frame :test/X)] ...)` and destroyed when the test exits, OR
> - **Attached to a view** — created once when a parent view mounts, then accessed by all child views via `current-frame` (the dynamic binding pattern, see ch.04 / Pattern-MultiFrame for the canonical shape)
>
> The top-level def in this example is a minimal-mount shortcut — fine for the counter, but you wouldn't ship app code that way.

title: [a11y] Story shell: landmark wrapping + scrollable-region keyboard access — fix axe-core violations from the shell
description:
Discovered by Mike 2026-05-12 alongside the counter-side a11y bead. Axe-core's run from the A11Y panel inside the Story playground showed violations that are the Story shell's responsibility (not the rendered variant's).

1. **All page content should be contained by landmarks** — the Story shell renders into a generic <div>. Wrap the top-level layout in a <main> and possibly <nav> (sidebar) / <aside> (right panel) so screen readers can navigate by landmark.

title: Guide ch.05: :record-error action signature shown differently from runnable example
description:
Chapter 05 §Guards and actions shows `:record-error` as:
  (fn [data [_ err]]
    {:data (-> data (update :attempts inc) (assoc :error (or (:message err) "Login failed.")))})

The runnable companion at examples/reagent/state_machine_walkthrough/core.cljc:73-76 has:
  (fn [data [_ {:keys [failure]}]]
    {:data (-> data (update :attempts inc) (assoc :error (or (:message failure) "Login failed.")))})

The difference is the destructure key: the inner event vector folded by the managed-HTTP extras-fold is shaped `[<event-id> {:kind :failure :failure m}]` per Spec 014, so the action sees a map under the :failure key — not a raw err. The guide oversimplifies; readers who copy the snippet will see `(:message err)` always return nil and the fallback string always render. Either (a) match the runnable example's destructure, or (b) add a one-line note that this is a simplified shape and link the runnable. The chapter §Dispatching to a machine §'extras-fold' DOES describe the {:kind :success :value v} / {:kind :failure :failure m} envelope, so updating the snippet to match is consistent with the chapter's own explanation.

title: http-managed supersede! fires :on-failure reply on the prior request
description:
## Problem

`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_managed.cljc:155-167` — `supersede!`:

```clojure
(defn- supersede! [request-id]
  (when-let [prev (lookup-in-flight request-id)]
    (clear-in-flight! request-id)
    (try
      ((:abort-fn prev) :request-id-superseded)
      (catch ... _ nil))))
```

The `:abort-fn` was constructed by `run-attempt-cljs!` / `run-attempt-jvm!` capturing the original ctx. On invocation it calls `finalise-failure!`, which fires `dispatch-reply!` against the captured `:origin-event` / `:explicit-on-failure` — i.e. the PRIOR request's reply target.

If the prior request's `:on-failure` was a real event vector, that event fires with `{:kind :failure :failure {:kind :rf.http/aborted :reason :request-id-superseded ...}}` even though the user's intent was "the new request replaces the old one." Two replies arrive at the original target: first the abort, then the success/failure of the new request. Invites race bugs in debounce-search patterns.

## Spec status

Per Spec 014 §`:request-id` (internal): "a fresh request with the same `:request-id` supersedes the previous one." The contract is silent on whether the prior request fires its reply.

## Fix — Mike-decision flagged

Two options:

1. **Suppress the reply on superseded aborts.** In `finalise-failure!` (cljs + jvm variants), skip `dispatch-reply!` when failure kind is `:rf.http/aborted` AND `:reason = :request-id-superseded`. Matches the debounce-search mental model.

2. **Document the dual-reply behaviour.** Update Spec 014 §`:request-id` to call out that supersede fires a failure reply on the prior request; users handle the abort-replay explicitly.

Option 1 is more user-friendly; option 2 is more conservative. Mike's call.

## Scope

Internal to `re-frame.http-managed`. Spec touch: Spec 014 §`:request-id` (internal). Test coverage: at least one supersede-flow test should assert the chosen behavior.

Found by 2026-05-12 correctness review: ai/findings/correctness-review-2026-05-12.md §P3-3.
notes:
PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/500 (merged 2026-05-12). Fix landed as decision A (suppress :on-failure reply on superseded aborts). Bead was not formally closed at merge time; closing retroactively. Implementation lives in:
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport_cljs.cljc:152-158 (CLJS finalise-failure!)
- implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_transport_jvm.cljc:171-177 (JVM finalise-failure!)
Tests in implementation/http/test/re_frame/http_managed_test.clj:574-743 (3 deftests cover: supersede MUST NOT fire :on-failure; supersede still emits :rf.http/aborted trace event with :reason :request-id-superseded; non-supersede abort STILL fires :on-failure as regression guard).
close_reason: Closed

title: subs layer-2+ inputs leak ref-count on Reagent auto-dispose
description:
## Problem

`implementation/core/src/re_frame/subs.cljc:166-284` — `compute-and-cache!` for a layer-2+ sub recursively calls `subscribe` on each `:<-` input (line 199-201). Each `subscribe` increments the input sub's ref-count via `compute-and-cache!`-on-miss (`:ref-count 1`) or via the hit-path inc.

When the parent reaction is later disposed by Reagent (because its sole watcher — a view — unmounted), the parent's `add-on-dispose!` callback (line 278-283) dissocs the parent's cache slot. But it does NOT call `unsubscribe` on the input subs whose ref-counts it incremented during construction.

## Impact (mostly observability, mild correctness)

- Inspector reading `(rf/sub-cache)` between hot reloads sees lingering high `:ref-count` integers that don't reflect actual subscribers.
- Tests that subscribe imperatively (incrementing ref-count) and then have the Reagent reaction disposed externally (`(interop/dispose! r)`) find the cache slot disappeared without the integer decrementing.
- Hypothetical leak: if the parent reaction were ever reconstructed (hot-reload, `clear-subscription-cache!` followed by new subscribe) AND the input subs' cache slots were still present with elevated ref-counts, those slots would never be disposed even after all subscribers detached. `invalidate-sub-on-replace!` (line 497-522) doesn't reset ref-counts on subs that weren't themselves re-registered.

## Fix — Mike-decision flagged

Two options:

1. **Tighten the contract.** Document that `:ref-count` is dev-introspection-only when Reagent autodispose is in play. Production apps shouldn't read it. Touch the Spec 006 doc and the `subs.cljc` docstring.

2. **Wire `compute-and-cache!`'s `add-on-dispose!` to walk `:inputs` and decrement each input's ref-count before clearing the parent slot.** Mechanically simple; brings the integer in line with the disposal model.

Option 2 is more work but closer to "what the integer says, the reality reflects." Mike's call.

## Scope

Internal to `re-frame.subs`. Likely a behavioral change for any test reading `:ref-count` directly.

Found by 2026-05-12 correctness review: ai/findings/correctness-review-2026-05-12.md §P3-2.
notes: Decision 2026-05-13: B = decrement on dispose. Pre-alpha green-light: 'what the integer says, reality reflects' invariant restored; Causa sub-cache panel + machine-inspector will read accurate counts; mechanical fix (one callback edit). Test behaviour changes for direct :ref-count reads are correct churn.
close_reason: PRs merged in batch landing wave 2026-05-13

title: interceptor chain :rf/interceptor-error overwrites prior errors
description:
## Problem

`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interceptor.cljc:46-62` — `invoke-before` and `invoke-after` both write `:rf/interceptor-error` to the context unconditionally on catch:

```clojure
(catch ... e
  (assoc context :rf/interceptor-error
         {:phase :before :id (:id interceptor) :exception e}))
```

If interceptor #2's `:before` fails and stamps an error, then interceptor #1's `:after` also fails, the second `assoc` overwrites the first. The router's downstream `:rf.error/handler-exception` trace surfaces only the LATER error; the original cause is lost.

Additionally, when a `:before` interceptor fails BEFORE a schema-validation interceptor (which sets `:rf/skip-handler?`), the handler-as-interceptor's skip check doesn't fire — the handler still runs against partial context, only to be reported as a generic interceptor-error later.

## Fix

1. Skip downstream `:before` stages once `:rf/interceptor-error` is set (mirror the existing `:rf/skip-handler?` short-circuit pattern in events.cljc / cofx.cljc). Continue running `:after` for proper teardown — that's the documented chain-continues guarantee.
2. Append errors to a `:rf/interceptor-errors` vector rather than overwrite. Keep `:rf/interceptor-error` for the FIRST error so existing tracing code reads "what went wrong first" without surprise.

## Scope

Internal to `re-frame.interceptor`. Test impact: any existing tests that assert on `:rf/interceptor-error` shape need to be updated to read the singleton (first-error) or the vector (all-errors) variant.

Found by 2026-05-12 correctness review: ai/findings/correctness-review-2026-05-12.md §P3-1.

  (let [m       (meta &form)
        ns-sym  (symbol (str (ns-name *ns*)))
        file    *file*]
    `(binding [source-coords/*pending-coords*
               (cond-> {:ns '~ns-sym}
                 ~file        (assoc :file ~file)
                 ~(:line m)   (assoc :line ~(:line m))
                 ~(:column m) (assoc :column ~(:column m)))]
       (TARGET-FN ~id ~@args)))

With the same 'metadata-free symbol' rationale comment x6.

ACTION: helper macro defmacro-with-coords that generates the binding shape from (target-fn id & args). The seven reg-* macros become one-liners.

OR: keep the defmacros but factor a build-pending-coords-form fn that returns the cond-> shape, and inline that.

Note: rf2-w1l0 (separate bead) addresses the duplicated rationale comment.

title: adapters: extract route-hook! helper to deduplicate rf2-0d35 routing pattern across 4 adapters
description:
Each CLJS adapter (reagent, reagent-slim, uix, helix) repeats the same 7-9 routed late-bind-hook installations at its bottom-of-file. Per-adapter ~150 lines; ~600 lines total of structural copy with near-identical comment blocks.

The pattern (rf2-0d35 routing — installed adapter's impl runs only when it is the (rf/init!)-installed one; otherwise chains to previously-registered reader):

  (let [previous (late-bind/get-fn :adapter/X)]
    (late-bind/set-fn! :adapter/X
      (fn adapter-X-routed [args]
        (if (identical? adapter (substrate-adapter/current-adapter))
          (impl args)
          (if previous (previous args) fallback)))))

Repeated for :adapter/current-frame, :adapter/current-component (where applicable), :adapter/ratom, :adapter/ratom?, :adapter/make-reaction, :adapter/add-on-dispose!, :adapter/dispose!, :adapter/reactive?, :adapter/after-render.

ACTION: extract a route-hook! helper into re-frame.substrate.adapter (preferred — alongside current-adapter) or re-frame.late-bind. Signature:

  (route-hook! adapter-spec :adapter/X impl-fn fallback-result)

Adapter ns bottom-of-file shrinks from ~150 to ~30 lines.

OPEN QUESTION: helper placement — substrate.adapter, late-bind, or new substrate.adapter.routing?

Discovered during clarity review 2026-05-12; see ai/findings/clarity-review-2026-05-12.md §F3 and §Q4.
close_reason: Closed

title: Realworld: replace repeated (current-time-ms) calls in handlers with a :rf/now coeffect

reg-event-fx handlers (e.g. :articles/loaded, :comments/loaded,

or realworld.time; have every handler that writes :loaded-at carry
:inject-cofx and read now from coeffects. Realworld is the canonical
SSR demo so the pure-handler discipline matters here in particular.

title: Replace js/setTimeout in demo-stub fxs with framework :dispatch-later path
description:
Four example demo-stub fxs use raw js/setTimeout to delay a canned
reply so the :loading UI state is observable:
- examples/reagent/realworld/core.cljs:255-258
- examples/reagent/boot/core.cljs:93-96
- examples/reagent/login/core.cljs:136-153
- examples/helix/login_helix/core.cljs:65-82 (and uix/login_uix
  /core.cljs:62- mirror)

The deferred work is an fx invocation (:rf.http/managed-canned-success),
not a dispatch, so :dispatch-later is not a 1:1 swap. But the timer
bypasses framework time controls (Tool-Pair time-travel, the
documented :dispatch-later nil-override seam used by timer.cljs tests)
and the pattern is replicated four times verbatim.

Fix options:
(a) Coin a small helper that internally :dispatch-later's to a private
    ::deliver-canned event whose handler calls the framework canned-
    success fx; reuse across the four examples.
(b) Accept current shape as a documented exception and add a comment
    naming the trade-off so readers don't copy js/setTimeout into

title: Decision: per-adapter start! convenience fns (e.g. reagent-adapter/start!) wrapping rf/init!
description: Per rf2-agql there is no default-adapter registry — every app must (rf/init! reagent/adapter). title: examples/counter_with_stories: prevent card reflow when 'hold to repeat' hint appears on -button hover
description:
In examples/reagent/counter_with_stories/views.cljs (counter-buttons Form-2 view, around line 43-60), hovering the '-' button triggers a Reagent local-atom toggle that conditionally renders a 'hold to repeat (not implemented — UI hint only)' span. The span's appearance widens the variant card on hover.

The behaviour itself is intentional (demonstrates Form-2 + the app-db / local-state boundary). The reflow is a cosmetic side-effect: when the span mounts, the inline-flex container grows; when it unmounts, it shrinks. Cards in :Workspace.counter/auto-grid all reflow.

Fix direction (pick whichever is smallest):
1. Reserve space for the hint via a non-rendered placeholder span at the same length (visibility: hidden when @hint? is false; visible when true). Keeps the card width stable.
2. Render the hint with position: absolute + a fixed-height parent so it overlays rather than displaces.
3. Use opacity transition (hint always rendered, opacity 0 vs 1) — simplest CSS-only fix; takes width permanently.

Recommend option 1 (placeholder reserve) — minimum visual impact, no new CSS animations.

Scope: examples/reagent/counter_with_stories/views.cljs only. Don't touch tools/story or anything outside the example.

Verify: hover the - button in a variant card. Card width should not change. Hint should still appear on hover, disappear on leave.

Discovered by Mike 2026-05-12 while running the Story playground interactively.
close_reason: Fixed inline: visibility-toggle instead of mount/unmount eliminates the reflow; hint text rewritten to be honest about the Form-2 demo it's actually doing.

Candidate inspirations:
- Storybook (the canonical reference) — JS-side; well-known stories/decorators/args/play/test
- Ladle (Vite-based Storybook alternative) — modern, similar model
- Histoire (Vue-side) — Storybook analogue
- Mintlify / Component playground (various) — for the docs-mode side

Scope: tools/re-frame2/reference/tooling/stories.md — add a tip near the top:
> **Tip**: stuck on how to model a story / variant / workspace shape? Ask yourself 'how would Storybook do it?' — Storybook is in your training data, and re-frame2's primitives map cleanly: reg-story ≈ Storybook story, reg-variant ≈ Storybook story variant (CSF), reg-decorator ≈ Storybook decorator, reg-workspace ≈ Storybook 'autodocs' / 'compose' (rough), reg-story-panel ≈ Storybook addon panel, play sequence ≈ Storybook play. Sketch in Storybook mentally, then translate.

Verify the mapping before committing — re-frame2's model isn't a direct copy of Storybook's; there are non-trivial differences (re-frame2 has workspaces as first-class composition; Storybook doesn't quite). Be honest about the limits in the tip.

One-liner. Same shape as the XState tip in reg-machine.md.

title: Beef up Playwright testing for examples/reagent/counter_with_stories — exercise the playground UI itself
description:

But the interactive playground surface (sidebar navigation, mode tabs, workspace cell mounting, time-travel panel, trace panel, a11y panel, layout-debug toggles, args editor, modes switcher, decorators visibility, save-layout button) is largely untested.

Mike (2026-05-12): 'I think this stories using counter needs some more serious testing via a background agent using playright so it can see what's going in.'

Direction: dispatch a Playwright-driven agent that:
1. Navigates between the variant URLs (/clicked-three-times, /empty, /loaded, /save-stubbed) directly — verifies each renders standalone (not just inside a workspace)
2. Navigates between workspaces (:Workspace.counter/all-states, :Workspace.counter/auto-grid) — verifies each renders all four variants
3. Toggles :dev/:docs/:test modes — verifies the canvas changes shape per mode
4. Interacts with the variant (clicks the +/- buttons) — verifies count updates

6. Switches modes (:Mode.app/dark / :Mode.app/light) — verifies the variant theme switches
7. Toggles layout-debug checkboxes — verifies the decorator outline / pseudo / measure overlays appear
8. Watches the trace panel — verifies events recorded after clicking '+'
9. Watches the time-travel panel — verifies epochs recorded
10. Clicks 'run' on the a11y panel — verifies axe-core scan runs

title: Suggestion: add agents/openai.yaml for re-frame-pair2 and align metadata surfaces
description:
## Problem

The two skills in `skills/` do not expose equivalent cross-agent metadata.

`re-frame-pair-improver2` ships `agents/openai.yaml` and includes `agents/` in its package payload. `re-frame-pair2` does not ship an `agents/` directory at all.

## Evidence from the current repo

- `skills/re-frame-pair-improver2/agents/openai.yaml` defines `display_name`, `short_description`, and `default_prompt`.
- `skills/re-frame-pair-improver2/package.json` includes `agents/` in `files`.
- `skills/re-frame-pair2/package.json` includes `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, `scripts/`, `.claude-plugin/`, and `docs/`, but no `agents/` entry.

## Suggested change

Add an `agents/openai.yaml` surface for `re-frame-pair2` and keep it in sync with the skill frontmatter.

Minimum shape:

- `display_name`
- `short_description`
- `default_prompt`

Also:

- include `agents/` in `skills/re-frame-pair2/package.json`
- document a regeneration path so the metadata can be refreshed when `SKILL.md` changes
- decide whether this repo wants a lightweight validation check that both skills keep their agent metadata aligned with the skill text

## Why this matters

`re-frame-pair2` is the flagship runtime skill in this folder. It should not be the least complete in terms of cross-agent discoverability metadata.

## Expected impact

- more consistent packaging across the repo's skills
- better discoverability on OpenAI/Codex-style skill surfaces
- less metadata drift between SKILL text and UI-facing prompts/descriptions

title: Impl drift: validate-at-boundary interceptor lacks CLJS production-mode coverage
description: The :spec/validate-at-boundary interceptor (rf2-r2uh, implementation/core/src/re_frame/spec.cljc) is exercised entirely on the JVM via implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_test.clj. The interceptor's whole value proposition is dev/prod gating — it no-ops in dev (debug-enabled? true) and runs inline schema validation in prod (debug-enabled? false). The JVM test rebinds the gate via with-redefs, but the gate's real-world behaviour is :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false where Closure constant-folds and DCEs the entire dev-side body. A CLJS smoke (in implementation/schemas/test/re_frame/schemas_cljs_test.cljs) under :node-test (DEBUG=true → no-op branch) and under :browser-test :advanced (DEBUG=false → validates inline) would pin the cross-substrate contract. Currently the prod branch is only proven to exist; the elision side is only proven via the boundary-without-spec warn-once cache.
close_reason: Resolved by PR https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/306. Adds CLJS production-mode coverage for :spec/validate-at-boundary via (1) two dev-mode no-op assertions in schemas_cljs_test.cljs and (2) a new browser-test-schemas-boundary-prod shadow-cljs build that compiles schemas_boundary_prod_test.cljs under :advanced + goog.DEBUG=false. All JVM + CLJS test suites green.

title: Impl drift: invoke-all conformance fixtures carry stale :id key in expect-effects
description: The conformance corpus fixtures invoke-all-join-all-completes.edn, invoke-all-join-any-fails-cancels.edn, and invoke-all-n-of-cancels-extras.edn assert the :rf.machine/spawn fx carries an :id key (e.g. {:machine-id :load-config :id :cfg ...}). title: Feature gap: Nine States needs XState-style orthogonal machine support, then pattern/example rewrite
description:
Problem statement

`spec/Pattern-NineStates.md` currently lands in an awkward middle ground:
- it correctly says not to mirror everything into a page-local enum;
- but the resulting pattern and worked example become fairly verbose, with many boolean discriminator subs and a root-level priority `cond`;
- and the example demonstrates that the named "nine states" are not a single exclusive FSM anyway (`Correct` can overlap with `One`, etc.).

This exposes a real modelling gap versus the XState-style solution.

Why the current shape is awkward

The Nine States UI is really multiple orthogonal axes:
- data axis: `Nothing | Loading | Empty | One | Some | Too Many | Error`
- form axis: `Neutral | Incorrect | Correct`
- mode axis: `Active | Done/Frozen`

Today the pattern composes those axes indirectly from separate slices (remote-data, form, machine/domain flag) and the example resolves overlaps by priority order in the root view. That works, but it is noisy and not very data-driven from the view's perspective.

XState has a cleaner answer for this family of problem:
- parallel / orthogonal regions to hold the independent axes in one machine without cross-product explosion;
- state tags / queryable labels so the UI can ask higher-level questions like `loading?`, `done?`, `invalid?` without matching exact nested state trees;
- selector-style subscription to a projection of the machine snapshot.

Recommended direction

Investigate adding the machine features needed to achieve practical parity with the XState solution for this problem shape:
- parallel regions (`:type :parallel` or equivalent) so data/form/mode can coexist in one machine cleanly;
- state tags (or an equivalent queryable classification surface) so views can derive render intent without a pile of boolean subs;
- a clear projection/subscription story for views reading a machine-derived render model.

Once the feature direction is decided and implemented, rewrite:
- `spec/Pattern-NineStates.md`
- `examples/reagent/nine_states/core.cljs`
- `examples/reagent/nine_states/README.md`

Rewrite goal

Replace the current many-sub + root-`cond` example with a more data-driven machine-oriented solution, where the UI subscribes to a single machine snapshot or derived render-model projection, while still preserving explicitness and testability.

Notes

This does NOT imply blindly copying XState wholesale. The design work is to decide which minimum machine features close the modelling gap for re-frame2's architecture. But Nine States is a concrete motivating case where the missing capability is visible today.
notes:
Nine States arc complete. All three stages shipped:
- Stage 1 (rf2-ee0d / PR #283) — :fsm/tags substrate.
- Stage 2 (rf2-l67o / PR #284) — :fsm/parallel-regions substrate.
- Stage 3 (rf2-c7wl / PR #285) — Pattern-NineStates.md + example + cross-refs rewritten around the new substrate.

Outcome matches the findings doc's hypothesis: parallel regions + state tags close the modelling gap; selector subs were already covered by Layer-3 :<- chained subs (no new primitive). The boolean-discriminator-sub variant lives in an Appendix on the pattern doc for apps that prefer it.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
Research draft: findings/nine-states-parallel-machines-design.md (~6,430 words).

Findings: the bead's three-feature hypothesis (parallel regions + state tags + selector subs) is two-thirds correct. Selector subs are already shipped — re-frame2's :<- chained subs are mechanically identical to XState's useSelector, so no new primitive is needed there. The real gap is (1) state tags as a queryable per-state label set, and (2) parallel regions as a third snapshot-shape arm (alongside flat keyword and compound vector path). Existing N-machines-per-region substitute (CP-5-MachineGuide.md) stays valid for axes that are independent features; parallel regions become the right choice when axes share a feature.

Proposed staging:
- Stage 1 — :fsm/tags (~250 LoC + ~150 lines spec + 4 fixtures). Strictly additive; useful on its own for hierarchical machines.
- Stage 2 — :fsm/parallel-regions (~680 LoC + ~450 lines spec + 10 fixtures). Capability claim TBD (suggest post-v1 unless Nine States is on v1 ship-list).
- Stage 3 — rewrite Pattern-NineStates + example (docs/example only, no new substrate). Worked rewrite in §5-6 of the findings doc; ~710 → ~540 LoC in the example, three orthogonal axes visible in the machine declaration, render priority becomes a data table consulted by one selector sub, root view becomes a single case.

Top open question (§9.6): does the v1 CLJS reference claim :fsm/parallel-regions, or does it stay post-v1? Tags should ship as v1; parallel regions are a bigger commitment and the substitute is already documented.

title: Suggestion: re-frame.registrar kind set is closed; Story needs own side-table
description:
While implementing Stage 2 (rf2-32dk), found a tension between two contracts:

1. AGENTS.md / IMPL-SPEC.md §1.1 / 'downstream-EPs-consume-foundation' rule: 'Story owns no new framework primitives. Every registry it uses (:story, :variant, :workspace, :story-panel, :tag, :mode, :decorator) registers via existing reg-* machinery.'

2. spec/007-Stories.md line 447: 'The framework registrar already supports new kinds via the existing reg- machinery (per 001-Registration.md); panels do not require a new framework primitive.'

3. implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc line 27-33: the 'kinds' set is CLOSED to #{:event :sub :fx :cofx :view :frame :route :app-schema :head :error-projector :flow}. register! THROWS on unknown kinds.

These three contracts conflict. Story needs the kinds: :story, :variant, :workspace, :story-panel, :tag, :mode, :decorator. None are in the closed set.

Resolution chosen for Stage 2: use a **Story-owned side-table** (atom under tools.story.registry) instead of the global registrar. This is consistent with IMPL-SPEC §5.1 which already names 'tools.story.registry/*variants*'. The side-table is internal to the tools/story/ artefact and never reaches a production bundle.

A bridge fn (story/handlers) provides spec/007 §Public-query-surfaces parity: '(story/handlers :story)' enumerates the side-table; the framework registrar stays closed.

Open question for future spec maintenance: should re-frame.registrar grow an 'open kinds' extension hook so downstream tools can register with the same machinery? OR should spec/007's wording change to acknowledge that Story's registrations live in a Story-owned side-table? The implementation has chosen the side-table path because it matches the closed-kinds discipline of spec/001 + the no-new-registries rule.
close_reason: Closed

title: Suggestion: revisit the mutation-heavy machine source-coord walker
description:
Tentative suggestion.

In `implementation/core/src/re_frame/source_coords.cljc`, `walk-machine-spec` / `walk-states-tree` build the per-element machine source-coordinate index via a mutation-heavy transient accumulator with nested `reduce-kv`, `doseq`, and side-effecting `assoc!` calls.

That may be fine, but this helper is compile-time metadata collection rather than hot runtime work, so the imperative shape seems harder to justify than it would be in a tight runtime loop. The current traversal also repeats a lot of slot-specific update logic inline, which makes the walker harder to extend or audit.

Possible direction:
- Recast the traversal as a more declarative visitor that returns collected entries and only materialises the final map at the edge.
- Or centralise the repeated slot-handling rules behind smaller helpers so the remaining mutation is clearly a deliberate implementation detail rather than the dominant shape.

Performance note:
- Transients may still be the right choice if macro-expansion cost matters and this walker is called often enough to notice.
- If so, keeping the imperative core is reasonable; it would just be worth documenting that compile-time performance is the reason for the less-functional style.
close_reason: Closed as docs-only: added an inline comment on walk-states-tree explaining why the mutation-heavy transient shape is deliberate (macro-expansion-time perf). Refactor to a declarative visitor is feasible but yak-shaving without benchmark data. Commit 519f38c.

title: Suggestion: unify machine guard/action validation under the recursive state walk
description:
RESHAPED 2026-05-12 (Mike's call): verify-the-gap-first, then act on the evidence.

Original observation (rf2-oz9t): in implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc, create-machine-handler validates keyword :guard / :action references via a manual top-level doseq over (:states machine), only walking :on transitions. walk-state-nodes (used just above for other registration-time validation) walks recursively but is NOT reused here. Spec text says registration-time validation should walk broadly (:on, :always, :entry, :exit), not just top-level :on. The narrow shape MIGHT miss nested-state guard/action refs and silently strand them as runtime-only errors.

What to do:
1. Write a small test: declare a reg-machine with a NESTED state whose :guard (and another whose :action) references an UNREGISTERED keyword. Register it.
2. Observe the result:
   - If registration succeeds silently (no exception, no warning) — the gap is real. The narrow pass is a correctness hole. Reshape the validator to drive off walk-state-nodes (or extend the existing recursive walker to also collect :guard / :action keyword refs).
   - If registration fails with a clear error pointing at the unregistered keyword — the gap is NOT real. Add a code comment in create-machine-handler explaining why the top-level :on pass is sufficient (e.g. it consults a separate index, or nested validation happens elsewhere). Close.
   - Spec/impl reconciliation: if the gap is NOT real, also check whether spec text needs softening — the current spec wording implies broader walking; if impl is sufficient, the spec is overspecified. File a small follow-up to update the spec doc.
3. Report which branch the test exercised + what action follows.

Performance note: registration-time, called once per machine on app startup. Readability + complete coverage matter more than imperative-loop speed.

OUT of scope: changing the narrow pass without evidence; refactoring source-coords walker (that's rf2-v25r, closed).
close_reason: Outcome A: gap was real. Probe test (12 cases) showed 10 silent failures: nested :on :guard/:action, top+nested :always :guard/:action, top+nested :entry/:exit action refs all bypassed the narrow top-level pass. Reshaped create-machine-handler to drive validation off walk-state-nodes and cover every transition-bearing slot (:on, :always, :entry, :exit). All 12 probe tests now throw at registration. PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/307

title: Spec 005 §Declarative :invoke — fn-form :data not invoked at spawn
description: Spec 005 line 1471 documents :invoke :data fn-form '(fn [snap event] data)' so the spawned child's :data can be derived from the parent's post-action snapshot + triggering event. apply-transition-once currently passes the spawn-args :data through verbatim — confirmed during rf2-ijm7 testing: literal-map :data works; fn-form :data results in the child's :data being the function itself, not the materialised map. Either implement fn-form invocation in spawn-fx (call the fn with [parent-snap event] before passing to the spawned machine) OR tighten the spec to drop the fn-form. Discovered during rf2-ijm7 (PR #260) — JVM tests worked around with literal-map only. Cross-ref: spec/005-StateMachines.md:1471, implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines.cljc spawn-fx :data path.
notes: PR #261 — https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/261. Path A (implement) per audit. Materialised :data fn-form in apply-transition-once :invoke + :invoke-all reductions, against the loop-evolving accumulator snapshot (post-action, includes prior sibling :on-spawn writes) and triggering event per Spec 005:1511. Throws route through existing ::action-failed short-circuit per Spec 005:1597. JVM tests in invoke_data_fn_form_test.clj (6 tests / 13 assertions); CLJS in machines_cljs_test.cljs. Full suite green: machines / core / http / ssr / routing / epoch / flows / schemas + elision + 419 CLJS tests. rf2-ijm7 had no fn-form workaround to revert.

title: Document Malli per-namespace bundle cost in Spec 010
description:
Per the rf2-qnxf Malli bundle-cost audit (findings/malli-bundle-cost-audit.md §3.2 / §4): add a §Bundle cost subsection to Spec 010 citing the audit's measured numbers and a rule of thumb on which Malli namespaces are safe in production paths.

## What to add

Subsection somewhere near §Why Malli, with content along these lines:

- Production bundle cost for a typical re-frame2 app with schemas: ~24 KB gzipped (just malli.core).
- Heavier surfaces add per-namespace: malli.error ~6 KB, malli.transform ~9 KB, malli.generator ~15 KB.
- Rule of thumb: `:require [malli.core]` only in production code paths; reserve `malli.error` / `malli.generator` / `malli.transform` / `malli.dev` for dev / test / 10x tiers.
- Cross-link to the rf2-qnxf audit findings document.

## Why

The 'Malli is hard to DCE' framing is half-right. Closure cannot DCE inside malli.core (the dynamic-dispatch internals defeat dataflow), but Closure DOES correctly DCE between Malli namespaces. Telling users where the boundary is reframes the cost story from 'Malli is 65 KB' (false for typical apps) to 'Malli is 24 KB' (accurate).

## Scope

- ~30-50 lines in Spec 010.
- Bundle-cost numbers from findings/malli-bundle-cost-audit.md §1.

## Out of scope

- The set-schema-validator! implementation (rf2-froe).

## References

- findings/malli-bundle-cost-audit.md §1 (measurement) and §3.2 (Strategy 2)

title: Frame-context corrupted-_currentValue silently falls through to :rf/default
description:
Per the rf2-22ds bead's Scenario 3: 'if the React-context boundary is corrupted (component rendered through an unwrapped portal? misuse case), the failure is observable + diagnostic — emits a structured error event, not a silent fallback.'

Today's behaviour: re-frame.adapter.context/coerce-context-value tolerates only keyword and non-empty string shapes. Anything else (nil, false, numeric, JS object, empty string) silently maps to nil and the resolution chain proceeds to :rf/default. There is no :rf.error/frame-context-corrupted (or similar) trace.

Real-world triggers for a corrupted _currentValue:
- A library that wraps the same React.createContext object externally and pushes a non-keyword value onto it.
- An incorrectly-authored React portal that renders a reg-view'd subtree outside the original Provider tree (in which case _currentValue is the createContext default :rf/default, which IS a valid keyword and the silent fallback IS arguably correct — but the misuse case is harder to diagnose without a trace).
- Tooling that pokes _currentValue directly (the adapter-context-current-frame-tolerates-prop-stringified-keyword test in cross_spec_cljs_test does this for coverage, demonstrating the seam).

Suggested shape: when coerce-context-value's input is non-nil and non-empty AND not a keyword AND not a coercible string, emit :rf.warning/frame-context-corrupted (op-type :warning) once per process per offending shape, with the observed value's pr-str and a hint to check Provider boundaries / external libs touching the shared context. Recovery: resolve to :rf/default (current behaviour). Per Spec 009 §Error categories.

The current rf2-22ds tests (scenario-3-context-corrupted-current-behaviour) pin the present behaviour as a regression guard; once this bead lands, those tests update to assert the structured-error event AND the :rf/default recovery.
notes: PR: https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/236 — structured :rf.error/frame-context-corrupted on function-component _currentValue reads of non-coercible shapes (nil/false/number/empty-string/JS-object). Recovery :replaced-with-default — apps still resolve to :rf/default. Spec 009 §error-categories + §recovery-table + §where-trace-emission-lives all updated. Scenario 3 of frame_provider_context_cljs_test rewritten to assert the trace event.

title: Sweep examples for best practice, code hygiene, and structure
description:
Mike's directive 2026-05-11: sweep the examples corpus for best practice, code hygiene, and structural consistency. Pairs with rf2-cyom (README sweep) which covers READMEs; this covers the actual code.

## Scope

All examples under examples/ — verify with glob at dispatch time. Stage 1 noted 17 example apps; verify count.

Per-example axes to check:

### 1. re-frame2 idiom adherence

- View registration via reg-view (not raw Reagent components where re-frame2 idiom applies)
- Subscribe + dispatch usage (not direct app-db reads/writes)
- Effect / cofx isolation (no side effects in handler bodies)
- Schema usage where appropriate (post-rf2-9qsk: schemas dev-only; boundary-validation interceptor for prod paths)
- Frame-provider usage in multi-frame examples (per rf2-sixo Path 1)
- :on-create / :on-destroy events for view-lifecycle side effects (not Form-2 closures)

### 2. Code hygiene

- Dead code removal
- Unused requires
- Stale comments referencing closed beads / old behavior
- Broken cross-doc links
- Inconsistent formatting

### 3. Structure consistency

- deps.edn — same dependency aliases / versions across examples (check for drift)
- shadow-cljs.edn — consistent build config shape
- README structure (verify with rf2-cyom; flag delta if rf2-cyom hasn't yet swept the example's README)
- Test file layout (per-example test/ dir conventions)
- Per-example src/ layout

### 4. Currency

- Stale references after the recent renames:
  - reagent-slim-and-fast → reagent-slim
  - day8/re-frame-2-reagent → day8/reagent-classic (when used as the thin-bridge artefact)
  - implementation/substrates/ → implementation/adapters/
- React 19 / Reagent 2 baseline awareness (where applicable; some examples may still use stock Reagent + React 18 — that's OK, but check if the example claims something else)
- Spec 005 :timeout-ms-on-:invoke (DROPPED in PR #223) — any example using it needs migration to state-level :after

### 5. Best practice

- Testing patterns: do examples have tests? Are they consistent?
- Error handling: re-frame2 conventions (interceptors, error events, etc.)
- Side-effect isolation: handlers pure; effects in fx/cofx layers
- Schema usage where load-bearing
- Source-coord / trace integration (when applicable to the example)

## Output

Per example:
- Issues found, categorised by axis
- Mechanical fixes applied inline (rename sweeps, dead-code removal, formatting nits)
- Substantive issues → follow-up bead

ONE batched PR titled 'examples: hygiene + best-practice sweep (rf2-XXXX)' OR per-example PRs if any single example's edits are substantial.

## Out of scope

- Don't add new examples.
- Don't add new tests beyond verifying refactors.
- Don't touch examples/<dir>/README.md if rf2-cyom is still in flight (avoid conflict; coordinate at PR-open time).
- Don't change spec/ or implementation/.
- Don't update decision-beads.md.

## Dispatchability

Direction-set; suitable for a background agent. No spec changes. Touches examples/* only — minimal hot-zone overlap.

If rf2-cyom (README sweep) is still in flight when this dispatches, coordinate by skipping README.md edits in the example dirs (rf2-cyom owns those).
