title: feat(test-react-adapter): re-frame2 substrate adapter that simulates React class-3 lifecycle for unit-testable lifecycle bug catching
description:
Placeholder follow-on filed per Mike directive 2026-05-19. Track as 'if we need it' — only build if React-lifecycle bugs prove recurrent beyond the rf2-4l7t2 unmount-during-render saga.

## Background
re-frame2 has 4 substrate adapters today: reagent, reagent-slim, uix, helix (all React-bound) + plain-atom (JVM/SSR/headless, no React). The plain-atom adapter is what Causa unit tests use today via test-support — exercises subs + dispatch + sub-chain reactivity, but NOT React class-3 lifecycle hooks.

The rf2-4l7t2 bug class — 'sync unmount during render' (caught by browser-Playwright + console-error gate) — depends on Reagent's class-3 hooks calling componentWillUnmount synchronously inside a render cycle. Can't be caught by plain-atom (no React) or by direct view-fn invocation (skips the class-3 wrap).

## Hypothetical new adapter (this bead's scope IF built)
 — a substrate adapter that:
- Mounts reg-view'd components into a captured hiccup tree
- Simulates React class-3 lifecycle (componentDidMount / componentDidUpdate / componentWillUnmount) in pure data
- Tracks 'currently rendering' state
- Throws on sync .unmount during render (mirroring React 18+ behaviour)
- Stores captured hiccup per mounted component
- Allows tests to assert lifecycle call ordering + counts
- ~300-500 LoC

Tests could then catch rf2-4l7t2-class bugs at unit-test speed without browser.

## Why deferred
- rf2-4l7t2 is the ONLY known React-lifecycle bug in this surface area as of 2026-05-19
- Playwright + console-error gate is acceptable for narrow lifecycle layer (Causa-embed mount/unmount cycle)
- Multi-frame e2e helper (rf2-7icrs in flight) covers 90% of bug classes at sub-second cost
- Building a faithful React-class-3 simulator is non-trivial and only pays off if many lifecycle bugs surface

## Trigger to build
- 2+ recurrent React-lifecycle bugs in causa_embed.cljs or future tools
- Playwright + console-error gate proving inadequate
- OR a strategic push to retire Playwright entirely

## Source
Mike directive 2026-05-19 ~midnight AUSEST after the multi-frame e2e testing analysis. 'Yes' to filing placeholder follow-on per mayor's recommendation.
notes: PR #1721 open: minimal viable skeleton shipped. New artefact at implementation/adapters/test-react/ (CLJC, JVM-runnable, opt-in). 4 tests pass (clojure -M:test); 3679 default-cljs tests still green. Mike to decide whether to expand or merge as-is.

title: feat(static): Events sub-tab — registered handlers + interceptor stack browser
description:
**Source:** ai/findings/2026-05-19-causa-explorer-mode.md §7.1 (Event handlers + Interceptors LOW v1.2) + parent epic rf2-o5f5f candidate 'Static Events catalog'.

## What
v1.2 Static sub-tab — browse registered event handlers (`reg-event-fx` / `reg-event-db`) and their interceptor chains. Single-step simulate verb (event-id + payload → simulated handler invocation, hermetic). Plus a separate Interceptors lens (pure-browse).

## Why (v1.2, not v1)
Per findings §7.1 explicitly marks both as LOW priority v1.2 — 'overlaps with the event-list in Runtime' (Events handlers) and 'power-user surface' (Interceptors). v1 Static ships Machines + Routes only; v1.1 adds Schemas + Flows + Subs; v1.2 picks up the denser surfaces.

## Scope (v1.2)

### Events sub-tab (handlers)
- Browse-all list of registered event handlers.
- Per row: event-id, handler-type (db/fx/ctx), source-coord chip, interceptor-count.
- Search by event-id + namespace.
- Sort: name / interceptor-count.
- Detail view (Shape A right pane):
  - Handler source-coord + jump-to-source.
  - Interceptor chain rendered top-to-bottom (per spec/004 Interceptor chain shape).
  - Single-step simulate-input: 'Fire event with payload [____] (hermetic)' — runs the handler in isolation, surfaces resulting cofx + db-mutations + fx-bundle WITHOUT real dispatch.

### Interceptors sub-tab (separate, denser)
- Browse-all registered interceptors (named + ad-hoc per spec/004).
- Per row: interceptor-id, type (before/after/both), source-coord.
- Pure-browse (no simulate-input — interceptors are composition; simulate fires through the handler-level simulate above).
- Detail view: before-fn + after-fn source + chain participants.

## Sub-tab mnemonics (per findings §7.3)
- Events handlers: `h` (Handlers)
- Interceptors: `i` (Interceptors — collision with Runtime Issues, but Static has no Issues so `i` is free)

## Out of scope
- Replay of past events (Runtime concern via Causa epoch buffer).
- Cross-event diffing (Runtime concern).
- Interceptor authoring / editing (read-only).
- Spec/019 authoring.

## Files
- `tools/causa/src/.../static/handlers/panel.cljs` (NEW)
- `tools/causa/src/.../static/handlers/simulate_input.cljs` (NEW) — reuse shared single-step simulate-input from Schemas/Flows beads.
- `tools/causa/src/.../static/interceptors/panel.cljs` (NEW)
- `tools/causa/src/.../static/shell.cljs` — register Handlers + Interceptors tabs.
- Tests: handlers list, simulate-input hermetic, interceptors list, jump-to-source.

## Size
L (300-450 LoC including tests). Two sub-tabs together; meaty simulate-handler logic.

## Dependencies
- BLOCKS-ON: rf2-o5f5f.1 (shell scaffold).
- BENEFITS-FROM: rf2-o5f5f.4 (Schemas v1.1) — shared simulate-input component.

## Sequencing
- v1.2 (after v1 + v1.1 ship).
- Filed at P4 to reflect explicit findings deferral; promote to P3 when v1.1 ships and Mike greenlights v1.2 cluster.

## Hot-zone
- tools/causa/src/.../static/shell.cljs — sequential with sibling sub-tab beads.

## Verify
- All registered events from `rf/event-registry` enumerate.
- Detail view shows interceptor chain.
- Simulate-input runs handler hermetically (no real dispatch).
- Interceptors sub-tab enumerates named + ad-hoc interceptors.

## Citations
- ai/findings/2026-05-19-causa-explorer-mode.md §7.1 (Event handlers + Interceptors v1.2 LOW)

title: feat(causa): View hierarchy fallback — data-attribute tagging in substrate adapters
description:
**Source:** ai/findings/2026-05-19-causa-machine-inspector-mode-s.md §12.1 + §11 Comments 4 + 5 (Mike, 2026-05-19 ~14:35 + 14:40 AUSEST).

## Status: FALLBACK ONLY
This is the deprecated-as-primary fallback for the View hierarchy capture work. The primary path (bead 5) reads Fiber links directly per Comment 6 LOCKED. This bead exists for v1.x scenarios where Fiber-reading breaks:

- Future React-version regression that the Fiber walker can't accommodate
- Substrates that don't use React (none today — all of Reagent / UIx / Helix mount through React; this is a forward-looking safety net)

## What to ship
1. Per-Reagent / UIx / Helix substrate adapter: ~30 LoC each. Each adapter inspects the hiccup return, locates the first concrete element (descending past nil / fragment / component-of-component as needed), and MUTATES that element's existing attribute map to add `data-rf-view="<name>"` (optionally `data-rf-source="<file:line>"`).
2. A `document.querySelectorAll('[data-rf-view]')` walker that infers parent-child by DOM containment.
3. Documented edge cases (fragment / nil-conditional / component-returning-component / portals / display:none) as known fidelity gaps.

## CRITICAL constraint (Comment 5)
MUST mutate the existing first element's attribute map. NEVER wrap with a synthetic `[:div]`. Wrapping breaks flexbox, CSS Grid, table layouts, `:nth-child` selectors, positioning ancestors, stacking contexts, and CSS containment. The wrap-with-div approach is a non-starter.

## Spec home
`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md` §View tagging contract — per-adapter contract.

## When to ship
- Phase 1 (now): nothing. Fiber-reading (bead 5) is the primary path.
- Phase 2 (if Fiber breaks): activate this bead.

## Citations
- Comments 4 + 5 (Mike, 2026-05-19 ~14:35 + 14:40 AUSEST) in §11 of Mode S findings.
- §12.1 of Mode S findings (post-iteration design).

title: perf(routing): match-against realises decoded lazy-seq twice (every? + zipmap)
description:
LOW severity from perf-sweep audit rf2-fzrav (ai/findings/perf-sweep-2026-05-15.md §L6).

implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc match-against (lines 309-319):

(let [groups  (if (sequential? m) (rest m) [])
      decoded (map (fn [g] (when g (safe-url-decode g))) groups)]
  (when (every? (fn [[g d]] (or (nil? g) (some? d)))
                (map vector groups decoded))
    (zipmap (map keyword names) decoded)))

decoded is a lazy seq that gets walked TWICE — once by every? (via map vector), once by zipmap. Head-holding of the lazy seq forces materialisation twice for the same elements.

Fix — switch to eager vector:

(let [groups  (if (sequential? m) (rest m) [])
      decoded (mapv (fn [g] (when g (safe-url-decode g))) groups)]
  (when (every? (fn [[g d]] (or (nil? g) (some? d)))
                (map vector groups decoded))
    (zipmap (map keyword names) decoded)))

(mapv instead of map.) One walk to build the vector; both later readers share the same eager values.

Fires on every URL match attempt against every route — so per nav, per route checked. Modest but unambiguous.

Files:
- implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing.cljc

Hot-zone: NO. Safe to parallel.

Pre-alpha.
close_reason: Landed via perf wave PR #1185-#1188 (admin-merged through unrelated slider testbed flake; fixed on main)

title: perf(schemas): walker/prefix? allocates take-seq + counts twice
description:
LOW severity from perf-sweep audit rf2-fzrav (ai/findings/perf-sweep-2026-05-15.md §L4).

implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc prefix? (lines 233-238):

(defn- prefix?
  [prefix path]
  (and (<= (count prefix) (count path))
       (= (seq prefix) (seq (take (count prefix) path)))))

Three issues:
1. (count prefix) called twice.
2. (take (count prefix) path) allocates a lazy seq.
3. (seq prefix) + (seq (take ...)) allocates two seq views over comparable elements.

Element-wise loop avoids all three:

(defn- prefix? [prefix path]
  (let [n (count prefix)]
    (and (<= n (count path))
         (loop [i 0]
           (cond
             (>= i n) true
             (not= (nth prefix i) (nth path i)) false
             :else (recur (inc i)))))))

Called once per sensitive-declaration on every schema-validation failure path (schema-sensitive-at? at line 277 — once for ancestor check, once for descendant). Failures are not in the steady-state hot path but the function is in walker.cljc which is loaded into the validation hot path.

Files:
- implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/walker.cljc

Hot-zone: NO. Safe to parallel.

Pre-alpha.
close_reason: Landed via perf wave PR #1185-#1188 (admin-merged through unrelated slider testbed flake; fixed on main)

title: perf(core): replace get-in for 2-level nested registry/frame reads with double get
description:
LOW severity from perf-sweep audit rf2-fzrav (ai/findings/perf-sweep-2026-05-15.md §L2+L3).

Both call sites allocate a path vector on every read; for 2-level reads (get (get m k1) k2) is faster.

L2: implementation/core/src/re_frame/registrar.cljc lookup (line 217):
  (get-in @kind->id->metadata [kind id])  →  (-> @kind->id->metadata (get kind) (get id))

  Called per dispatch (event handler), per fx (handler), per sub (handler).

title: docs(http): clarify :rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor map-args vs fn-form positional asymmetry
description:
Found by audit bead rf2-wui5v.

## Issue

`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_managed.cljc:179-184`:

```clojure
(fx/reg-fx :rf.fx/clear-http-interceptor
           {:doc "Spec 014 §Middleware (rf2-6y3q) — clear a request-side
                  interceptor by id as an fx. Args is `{:frame :id}`; `:frame`
                  defaults to `:rf/default`."}
           (fn [_ctx {:keys [frame id]}]
             (middleware/clear-http-interceptor (or frame :rf/default) id)))
```

The fx wraps `clear-http-interceptor` (the fn form), which takes positional
args `[id]` / `[frame id]`. The fx accepts a map `{:frame :id}` — different
shape from the fn. Both work; the fx unpacks via destructuring.

This is documented in the fx docstring, but it surprises code-readers
encountering both surfaces side-by-side.

## Options

1. **Documentation only**: add a one-liner in the fx doc — "args mirror the
   fn-form's two-arity (`:frame` optional, defaults to `:rf/default`)".
2. **Accept positionals too**: the fx's destructure could handle both
   `[id]` (vector → positional) and `{:id ...}` (map → keyed). More work,
   slightly more flexible.

Option 1 is the cheap fix; option 2 is for if we want strict symmetry.

## Surface

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_managed.cljc:179-184`

## Discovered through

Audit bead rf2-wui5v (http slice).

title: polish(http): interceptor :before non-map return — include id in ex-info cause string
description:
Found by audit bead rf2-wui5v.

## Issue

`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_middleware.cljc:160`:

```clojure
(throw (ex-info "interceptor :before did not return a ctx map"
                {:returned out}))
```

When a `:before` interceptor returns a non-map (nil, false, vector, ...), this
throw is caught by the surrounding `try` in `run-interceptor-chain!` and
re-thrown as `:rf.error/http-interceptor-failed`. The `:interceptor-id` rides
in the ex-data of the outer error, but the inner `:cause` string is the generic
"interceptor :before did not return a ctx map" with no id.

For a 10-interceptor chain whose failure prints a stack trace, the human reading
the trace has to also fish out ex-data to know WHICH interceptor returned wrong.

## Suggested fix

Include the id in the message:

```clojure
(throw (ex-info (str "interceptor " id " :before did not return a ctx map")
                {:id id :returned out}))
```

(Capture `id` from the surrounding `reduce` arity.)

## Surface

- `implementation/http/src/re_frame/http_middleware.cljc:154-184`

title: feat(epoch): emit :rf.epoch.cb/listener-exception trace when a listener throws
description:
## Finding

Parent audit: rf2-3391t (round-3 epoch audit). See `ai/findings/epoch-slice-audit-2026-05-15.md` §F5.

**Severity:** DEFER (post-v1.0 polish). Works as documented today; this is an observability improvement.

## Impl citation

`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch.cljc:309-318` — `notify-listeners!`:

```clojure
(defn- notify-listeners! [record]
  (let [frame-id (:frame record)]
    (doseq [[id f] @listeners]
      (record-observation! id frame-id)
      (try
        (f record)
        (catch #?(:clj Throwable :cljs :default) _
          ;; Per Spec 009 §Listener invocation rules: listener failures
          ;; are isolated. Continue notifying.
          nil)))))
```

## Problem

Exception isolation is correct — one broken listener cannot break the runtime or block other listeners (contract pinned by `listener-exception-isolation` test at `epoch_test.clj:310-328`). But the caught exception is silently dropped to `nil`. A tool wiring up a broken listener gets **no signal** that its callback failed.

## Fix

Emit a structured trace from the catch arm so devtools can surface the failure without breaking isolation:

```clojure
(catch #?(:clj Throwable :cljs :default) ex
  (trace/emit-error! :rf.epoch.cb/listener-exception
                     {:frame    frame-id
                      :cb-id    id
                      :epoch-id (:epoch-id record)
                      :message  (ex-message ex)
                      :recovery :no-recovery})
  nil)
```

Op-type `:rf.epoch.cb` (same op-type as `:rf.epoch.cb/silenced-on-frame-destroy` per `spec/Conventions.md:30`).

## Spec ask

This adds a new `:rf.epoch.cb/*` op so `spec/009-Instrumentation.md` §Op-type vocabulary needs the row added. Hot-zone file — sequence behind any in-flight 009 edits.

## Test

`epoch_test.clj` — extend `listener-exception-isolation` (or add a sibling test) to assert the `:rf.epoch.cb/listener-exception` trace fires once per broken-listener invocation, carrying the cb-id, frame, and epoch-id.

title: [story] Resolve :schema legacy alias on view-meta — accept formally or remove
description:

## Drift
`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/schema_validation.cljc` L308-312 schema-lookup order for the Schema-Validation panel:

```clojure
(or (:schema vb)                       ;; variant body
    (:schema sb)                       ;; story body
    (:spec   view-meta)                ;; framework :view meta (canonical)

```

Spec-Schemas `:rf/view-meta` (L213-223) only declares `:rf/props` for schema-shaped data; the Spec 010 canonical surface is `:spec`. Story falls back to `:schema` as a legacy alias — but `:schema` is NOT in any per-kind metadata schema.

## Effect

## Fix options

- (b) Spec-Schemas `:rf/view-meta` adds:

  ```clojure
  [:schema {:optional true} :any]  ;; legacy alias for :spec; accepted by Story (Spec 007 §Schema-validation panel)
  ```

  with a deprecation note pointing to the canonical `:spec`.

Mike's call. Both fine.

Wishlist alignment; no broken contract today. Worth doing before alpha when Story formalises its conformance surface (rf2-kxs6j follow-up area).

title: [spec] :rf/frame-meta should :merge :rf/registration-metadata for consistency with other per-kind shapes
description:
## Source
rf2-bc0k6 audit finding G6 (LOW severity).

## Drift
`spec/Spec-Schemas.md` L2108-2131 `:rf/frame-meta`:

```clojure
(def FrameMeta
  [:map
   [:id           :keyword]
   [:created-at   :any]
   [:preset       {:optional true} [:enum :default :test :story :ssr-server]]
   ...
   [:doc          {:optional true} :string]
   [:tags         {:optional true} [:set :keyword]]
   ...])
```

This is a standalone `[:map ...]`. Every other per-kind shape from rf2-kxs6j uses `[:merge RegistrationMetadata [:map ...kind-specific]]`. `FrameMeta` restates `:doc :tags` inline and OMITS `:spec :ns :line :file :platforms :sensitive?`.

But frames participate in source-coord capture — `implementation/core/test/re_frame/source_coords_test.clj` L23 lists `reg-frame` among the kinds with source-coords asserted. So `(frame-meta :foo)` returns include `:ns/:line/:file`. The schema doesn't reflect this.

## Effect
- A conformance validator using `:rf/frame-meta` rejects `:ns/:line/:file` keys (no slot defined).
- Open-shape semantics save correctness in practice; the schema just isn't as informative as the others.

## Fix
Rewrite `:rf/frame-meta` as:

```clojure
(def FrameMeta
  [:merge
   RegistrationMetadata
   [:map
    [:id           :keyword]
    [:created-at   :any]
    [:preset       {:optional true} [:enum :default :test :story :ssr-server]]
    [:on-create    {:optional true} [:vector :any]]
    [:on-destroy   {:optional true} [:vector :any]]
    [:fx-overrides {:optional true} [:map-of :keyword :any]]
    [:interceptor-overrides {:optional true} [:map-of :keyword :any]]
    [:interceptors {:optional true} [:vector :any]]
    [:drain-depth  {:optional true} :int]
    [:url-bound?   {:optional true} :boolean]
    [:platform     {:optional true} :keyword]
    [:on-error     {:optional true} :keyword]]])
```

Removes the duplicated `:doc :tags` keys; `:spec :ns :line :file :platforms` arrive via the merge. Doc-only Spec-Schemas edit. Single-file isolated.

## P4 reason
Not a breakage. Cleanup. Easy bead for a quick win.

title: [pair2-mcp] cheap O(1) runtime app-db-hash accessor (cache at mutation time)
description:
Follow-on from rf2-36xod.

rf2-36xod shipped the server-side precheck path: pair2-mcp sends one cheap nREPL eval — currently `(hash (re-frame-pair2.runtime/snapshot frame))` — and short-circuits the cache hit BEFORE running the tool eval. That saves the wire bytes AND the tool eval + transform pipeline.

The current `(hash …)` call is still O(n) over the app-db each precheck. For very large app-dbs this could itself become non-trivial. The headline optimisation per rf2-36xod's "Subtleties" section is:

> The runtime hash needs to be cheap to read. `(hash app-db)` on every dispatch is too expensive; better to cache it at the point of mutation (next-db wrap).

## What to ship

- A cached hash slot on each frame, updated at every mutation point — the dispatch-loop `next-db` wrap, `reset-frame-db!`, `restore-epoch`, `db-replaced` synthetic, etc.
- A `(re-frame-pair2.runtime/app-db-hash frame-id)` accessor that returns the cached integer in O(1).
- Path-aware variant for `get-path` precheck: `(re-frame-pair2.runtime/app-db-hash-at path frame-id)` — hash of the sub-tree at `path`. Not strictly required (the whole-db hash is a safe over-invalidation), but a perf win for slice-heavy callers.
- Update `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs` `precheck-form` to call the cheap accessor.

## Acceptance

- O(1) hash read. Verified by a micro-benchmark (`hash (snapshot)` vs the cached accessor on a 10k-key db).
- Mutation through `pair-dispatch!`, `reset-frame-db!`, `restore-epoch` all rotate the cached hash.
- pair2-mcp precheck still hits when state is unchanged; still misses after a mutation.
- No measurable per-dispatch latency increase from the cache-wrap.

## Touches

- `skills/re-frame-pair2/preload/re_frame_pair2/runtime.cljs` (new accessor, mutation hooks)
- Possibly `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc` if the per-frame hash slot lives there rather than in the preload.
- `tools/pair2-mcp/src/re_frame_pair2_mcp/tools.cljs` (switch `precheck-form` to the cheap accessor)
close_reason: Shipped O(1) per-frame app-db-hash accessor + cache-at-mutation via the epoch listener. precheck-form now emits (re-frame-pair2.runtime/app-db-hash <frame>) instead of (hash (snapshot <frame>)). New bb test covers lazy-compute, rotation, isolation.

title: [tools] Audit per-kind :rf/registration-metadata schemas (rf2-kxs6j) for tool consumption
description:
rf2-kxs6j (PR #563, merged this session) added 10 per-kind narrowed metadata schemas to spec/Spec-Schemas.md — :rf/event-handler-meta, :rf/sub-meta, :rf/fx-meta, :rf/cofx-meta, :rf/view-meta, :rf/machine-meta, :rf/flow-meta, :rf/app-schema-meta, :rf/head-meta, :rf/error-projector-meta.

These compose with :rf/registration-metadata (open shape with :doc, :spec, :ns/:line/:file, :tags, :platforms) so a tool introspecting (rf/handler-meta kind id) can now Malli-validate / drive UI off the per-kind shape rather than walking a single open map.

Current state: NO tool consumes the per-kind names. Story's Controls panel and Causa's panels work directly with declared schemas or the open registration-metadata. This isn't drift in the breakage sense — it's a wishlist alignment.

## Sites to consider
- tools/causa/spec/API.md L153 (handler-meta row) — could mention per-kind schemas exist as the introspection contract
- tools/story/src/re_frame/story/schemas.cljc — Controls panel; could narrow per kind for sharper UI

## Proposed work
Audit pass — surface the schemas in Causa's API.md as the canonical introspection types; consider whether Story Controls can use :rf/event-handler-meta to derive control widgets more accurately.

## Why P4
Wishlist; no broken contract today.

## Source
Sweep of tools-and-skills drift after rf2-kxs6j merge (2026-05-13 14:58 AUSEST).
notes:
## Audit verdict — 2026-05-15

10 per-kind schemas from rf2-kxs6j are well-shaped at the per-kind narrowing level. The drift is in the SHARED base (`:rf/registration-metadata`) and at the OUTER edges (kinds rf2-kxs6j didn't catalogue + tool surfaces that don't track the catalogue).

## 7 gaps surfaced

### High
- **G1 (rf2-44zpf):** pair2-mcp handler-meta/registry-list kind enum is 7 kinds; registrar's closed set is 11. Missing :route :flow :head :error-projector — agents forced to eval-cljs for introspection the registrar can answer.
- **G2 (rf2-t9166):** :sensitive? is documented in Spec 009 as 'every reg-* accepts it' but absent from the :rf/registration-metadata schema (and from Spec 001's metadata table). Schema-driven validation can't type-check the slot.

### Medium
- **G3 (rf2-4h8ny):** Spec-Schemas L342/L375 describe :source-coord as a 'sub-map of :rf/registration-metadata.' Impl emits flat :ns/:line/:file/:column at the top level. Tool-Pair and API.md describe the actual shape correctly — Spec-Schemas is the outlier. Doc-only fix.
- **G4 (rf2-87wee):** pair2-mcp handler-meta tool (a) never routes through wire-pipeline, (b) wouldn't decorate even if it did (source-uri walker matches sub-map shape, handler-meta returns flat keys). Promised :rf.source/uri jump-to-editor link never fires for handler-meta. Trace events / snapshot / watch-epochs are fine — those nest source-coord properly.
- **G5 (rf2-gsl5v):** reg-http-interceptor bypasses :rf/registration-metadata entirely. Stores {:id :before} in a frame-keyed atom, not the registrar. No :doc, source-coords, :tags, :spec. Spec 014 doesn't document metadata. No :rf/http-interceptor-meta schema.

### Low
- **G6 (rf2-xnutu):** :rf/frame-meta is a standalone [:map ...], not [:merge RegistrationMetadata ...]. Restates :doc/:tags and omits :spec/:ns/:line/:file/:platforms. Frames participate in source-coord capture so the schema is less informative than the others. Doc cleanup.
- **G7 (rf2-sjob2):** Story honours :schema as legacy alias for :spec on view-meta; spec doesn't acknowledge this. Either Story drops :schema or Spec-Schemas adds it with deprecation note.

## Slots without consumers (potential dead surface)
None found. :rf/sub-meta :rf/inputs/:rf/layer, :rf/view-meta :rf/args/:rf/form, :rf/app-schema-meta :frame all spec'd ahead of consumers per SA-3 invariant. No-action.

## Per-tool consumption notes
- **pair2-mcp:** raw passthrough of (rf/handler-meta) — agents see whatever the registrar stored. Constrained by kind-enum (G1) and by missing source-uri decoration (G4).
- **story:** consumes its OWN registrar (separate side-table for :variant/:story/:mode/etc.). Touches framework :view meta only via schema_validation panel's :spec/:schema fallback (G7).
- **story-mcp:** consumes Story registrar; no framework registration-metadata reads.
- **mcp-conformance:** handler-meta listed in NAMING.md L85 with 'Audit pending — added by rf2-cibp8' — no shape conformance pinned.
- **causa:** Routes panel reads :rf/route-metadata cleanly (:doc :path :tags :parent :on-match — all in schema). open-in-editor reads flat source-coord keys correctly.
- **causa-mcp:** spec-only artefact today; consumers don't exist yet.

## Findings doc
`ai/findings/registration-metadata-audit-2026-05-15.md` (local-only) carries the full inventory tables and file-line cites.

title: spec/001 line 185 claims machine actions/guards are 'new registry kinds' — contradicts §Registry model + line 101
description:
spec/001-Registration.md line 185 (the v1-reference blockquote in §Hot-reload semantics) asserts: 'machine actions/guards are new registry kinds'.

This contradicts:
- spec/001 §Registry model (line 81-101): the canonical kind set is {:event :sub :fx :cofx :view :frame :route :app-schema :head :error-projector :flow}. No :machine-action / :machine-guard.

title: reg-event-fx handler returning non-map silently no-ops
description:
## Problem

`implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:139-156` — `fx-handler->interceptor`:

```clojure
(let [effects (handler-fn cofx event)]
  (when (map? effects)
    (police-effect-map-shape! effects event))
  (cond-> ctx
    (and (map? effects) (contains? effects :db))
    (interceptor/assoc-effect :db (:db effects))

    (and (map? effects) (contains? effects :fx))
    (interceptor/assoc-effect :fx (:fx effects))))
```

If a `reg-event-fx` handler accidentally returns a non-map (vector, nil, number — typo or thinko), the body silently no-ops. `police-effect-map-shape!` doesn't fire (it's gated on `(map? effects)`), no warning, no error. The dispatch settles to a no-op.

## Fix

Emit `:rf.error/effect-handler-bad-return` when a `reg-event-fx`-registered handler returns a non-map / non-nil value. Recovery: `:no-recovery` (the handler's intent is unclear).

```clojure
(let [effects (handler-fn cofx event)]
  (cond
    (nil? effects) ctx  ;; no-op handlers are documented as legal
    (not (map? effects))
    (do (trace/emit-error! :rf.error/effect-handler-bad-return
                            {:event-id (first event)
                             :event event
                             :returned effects
                             :returned-type (type effects)
                             :reason "reg-event-fx handler returned a non-map; expected {:db ... :fx [...]}."
                             :recovery :no-recovery})
        ctx)
    :else
    (do
      (police-effect-map-shape! effects event)
      (cond-> ctx
        (contains? effects :db)
        (interceptor/assoc-effect :db (:db effects))
        (contains? effects :fx)
        (interceptor/assoc-effect :fx (:fx effects))))))
```

## Scope

Internal to `re-frame.events`. Add a Spec 009 entry for `:rf.error/effect-handler-bad-return` if not present.

Found by 2026-05-12 correctness review: ai/findings/correctness-review-2026-05-12.md §P4-2.
close_reason: Closed

title: dispatch-sync! cross-frame reentry not detected; cascade silently interleaves
description:
## Problem

`implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:414-415` — `dispatch-sync!`'s reentry check examines only the target frame's router state:

```clojure
(let [r @(:router frame-record)]
  (or (:in-sync-drain? r) (:in-drain? r)))
```

If frame `:a` is mid-drain and a handler in frame `:a` calls `(rf/dispatch-sync! [:foo] {:frame :b})` against a different frame, the check looks at frame `:b`'s router (idle), passes, and frame `:b`'s sync drain executes while frame `:a` is still mid-drain.

## Status

Arguably intentional — each frame's drain is independent and frame `:b`'s drain doesn't violate frame `:a`'s contract. But the cascade (frame `:b` runs to settled, then frame `:a` continues) is surprising to readers.

Spec 002 §dispatch-sync is silent on cross-frame.

## Fix — Mike-decision flagged

Two options:

1. **Loosen the error to cross-frame.** Any in-flight drain on any frame blocks `dispatch-sync!` everywhere.
2. **Emit `:rf.warning/cross-frame-dispatch-sync-during-drain`** so observability tools spot the pattern. Don't refuse.

P4 — pedantic. Either option is fine; current silent behavior is arguably correct.

Found by 2026-05-12 correctness review: ai/findings/correctness-review-2026-05-12.md §P4-1.
notes: Decision 2026-05-13: B = emit :rf.warning/cross-frame-dispatch-sync-during-drain trace event. Don't refuse. Pre-alpha green-light. Reasoning: frames are isolated state machines by design; cross-frame sync drain doesn't violate frame A contract; refusing breaks legitimate multi-frame coordination. Warning + trace surface = the right channel.

Event-handling pipeline atomicity (Mike CONFIRMED 2026-05-24). Architecture: interceptors (incl. the path std-interceptor) mutate the :db/:fx EFFECTS in interceptor context; app-db gets a SINGLE deferred install only after the ENTIRE chain (all :after interceptors + the flow transform) is done. Flows run at the OUTERMOST :after (framework-prepended :rf/flows, fires last) because flows read full-app-db :inputs and path's :after reshapes :db. CONTRACT: ANY throw BEFORE install (cofx, handler, interceptor :after, flow) => the deferred install simply does NOT happen => app-db UNCHANGED, NO :rf.event/db-changed, NO :fx. No partial commit (a flow throw must NOT commit prior flows' writes). The :db install is the atomic commit boundary. The ONLY post-commit stage is :fx: an fx throw surfaces an error but does NOT wind back app-db (fx side-effects http/nav/dispatch may already have fired and are irreversible). Uniform: flow-throw behaves like every other pre-install throw.

Cadence 'as you see fit' = after each dispatch pass / merge-close / decision batch, not every micro in_progress flip. Sequence: git add .beads/issues.jsonl; git commit -m 'chore(beads): ...'; git pull --rebase; git push. No AI attribution in the message.

Reagent's get-react-key (reagent2.impl.template L407) only reads :key meta from VECTORS. ^{:key k} attached to a function-call list form (e.g. ^{:key g} (group-section g …)) is lost on evaluation — the meta lives on the source list at READ time, not on the returned value. Two fixes: (a) put ^{:key k} on the vector literal returned by the function, or (b) wrap the result in (with-meta result {:key k}). Found in views_view.cljs PR #1471 fixing rf2-gphsi; same anti-pattern exists across several other panels (audit bead rf2-?? filed). Tell future test authors: a test that asserts :key meta on the rendered child reproduces the bug.
